In the beginning, God made the sky and the earth.
The earth was empty and had no shape. It was dark. Deep water covered everything. God's Spirit moved over the water.
God said, "Let there be light." And there was light.
God saw that the light was good. He separated the light from the dark.
God called the light "day." He called the dark "night." Evening came, and then morning came. That was the first day.
God said, "Let there be a sky in the middle of the water. Let it split the water in two."
God made the sky. He split the water below the sky from the water above the sky. And it was so.
God called the sky "heaven." Evening came, and then morning came. That was the second day.
God said, "Let the water under the sky come together in one place. Let dry land show." And it was so.
God called the dry land "earth." He called the water "seas." God saw that it was good.
God said, "Let the earth grow plants. Let plants make seeds. Let trees make fruit with seeds inside. Each kind should make its own kind." And it was so.
The earth grew plants and trees. Each kind made its own seeds. God saw that it was good.
Evening came, and then morning came. That was the third day.
God said, "Let there be lights in the sky. They will split the day from the night. They will be signs for special days, years, and seasons.
Let them shine on the earth." And it was so.
God made two big lights. The bigger light rules the day. The smaller light rules the night. He also made the stars.
God put them in the sky to shine on the earth.
They rule the day and the night. They split the light from the dark. God saw that it was good.
Evening came, and then morning came. That was the fourth day.
God said, "Let the water fill with living things. Let birds fly above the earth in the sky."
God made the big sea animals. He made every living thing that moves in the water. He made every kind of bird. God saw that it was good.
God blessed them and said, "Have many babies. Fill the seas. Let birds grow in number on the earth."
Evening came, and then morning came. That was the fifth day.
God said, "Let the earth make living things. Let there be animals, farm animals, and things that crawl." And it was so.
God made the wild animals, the farm animals, and everything that crawls on the ground. Each kind was its own kind. God saw that it was good.
God said, "Let Us make people in Our image. Let them rule the fish, the birds, the animals, and all the earth. Let them rule everything that crawls on the ground."
So God made people in His own image. He made them male and female.
God blessed them and said, "Have many children. Fill the earth and be in charge of it. Rule the fish, the birds, and every living thing on the earth."
God said, "Look, I give you every plant that makes seeds. I give you every tree that makes fruit with seeds. They will be food for you.
I give every green plant to the animals, the birds, and everything that crawls on the earth. It will be food for them." And it was so.
God saw all that He had made. It was very good. Evening came, and then morning came. That was the sixth day.
So the sky and the land and everything in them were finished.
By the seventh day, God had finished the work He had done. So on the seventh day He rested from all His work.
Then God blessed the seventh day and made it special. He did this because on that day He rested from all the work He had done to make everything.
This is the story of the sky and the land when they were made. It tells how the LORD God made the earth and the sky.
No bushes had grown on the earth yet. No plants had come up in the fields yet. This was because the LORD God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no man to work the ground.
But water came up from the earth and watered all the ground.
Then the LORD God made the man from dust from the ground. He breathed the breath of life into the man's nose, and the man became a living person.
The LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east. He put the man He had made there.
The LORD God made every tree grow from the ground. These trees were nice to look at and good to eat. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of knowing good and bad.
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden. From there it split into four rivers.
The first river is called Pishon. It goes through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
The gold of that land is pure. Bdellium and onyx stone are found there.
The second river is called Gihon. It goes through the whole land of Cush.
The third river is called Tigris. It flows east of Asshur. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
Then the LORD God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden. The man was to work it and take care of it.
The LORD God told the man, "You may eat from any tree in the garden.
But you must not eat from the tree of knowing good and bad. If you eat from it, you will die."
The LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper who is right for him."
The LORD God had made every wild animal and every bird from the ground. He brought them to the man to see what names he would give them. Whatever the man called each living thing became its name.
The man gave names to all the farm animals, to the birds, and to all the wild animals. But no helper was found who was right for the man.
So the LORD God made the man fall into a deep sleep. While he slept, He took one of the man's ribs and closed the place with flesh.
From the rib that the LORD God took from the man, He made a woman. He brought her to the man.
The man said, "This is someone from my own body. She will be called woman, because she was taken from man."
That is why a man leaves his father and mother and joins his wife. The two become one.
The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
The snake was trickier than any other wild animal the LORD God had made. He asked the woman, "Did God really say you must not eat fruit from any tree in the garden?"
The woman said to the snake, "We can eat fruit from the trees in the garden.
But God said we must not eat fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden. We must not even touch it, or we will die."
The snake said to the woman, "You will not die.
God knows that when you eat it, you will understand. You will be like God and know good from bad."

The woman saw that the tree was good for food. It was pretty to look at, and it could make a person wise. So she took some fruit and ate it. She gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it too.
Then they understood, and they knew they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made clothes for themselves.
The man and his wife heard the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool part of the day. They hid from the LORD God among the trees.
The LORD God called to the man, "Where are you?"
The man said, "I heard Your voice in the garden. I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid."
The LORD God said, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree I told you not to eat from?"
The man said, "The woman You gave to be with me gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it."
The LORD God said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" The woman said, "The snake tricked me, and I ate."
The LORD God said to the snake, "Because you did this, you are cursed more than all farm animals and wild animals. You will crawl on your belly and eat dust all your life.
I will make you and the woman hate each other. Your children and her children will be enemies. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel."
To the woman He said, "I will make your pain much worse when you have children. You will give birth in pain. You will want your husband, and he will be in charge of you."
To Adam He said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree I told you not to eat from, the ground is cursed because of you. You will have to work hard to eat from it all your life.
It will grow thorns and weeds for you, and you will eat plants from the field.
You will sweat to eat your bread until you go back to the ground. You were made from dust, and you will return to dust."
Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all living people.
The LORD God made clothes from animal skins for Adam and his wife, and He dressed them.
The LORD God said, "Look! The man has become like one of Us. He knows good and bad. Now he might reach out his hand, take fruit from the tree of life, eat it, and live forever."
So the LORD God sent him out of the garden of Eden to work the ground he came from.
He drove the man out. Then He put angels on the east side of the garden of Eden. He also put a flaming sword that turned every way to guard the way to the tree of life.
Adam slept with his wife Eve. She got pregnant and had a baby boy named Cain. She said, "With the the LORD's help, I have a baby boy."
Later she had another son. His name was Abel. Abel took care of sheep. Cain worked the ground.
After some time, Cain brought some food from the ground as a gift to the the LORD.
Abel brought the best parts from his first lambs. The The LORD was pleased with Abel and his gift.
But He was not pleased with Cain and his gift. Cain got very angry, and his face looked sad.
The The LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why does your face look sad?"
"If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is waiting at your door. It wants to control you, but you must control it."
Cain spoke to his brother Abel. When they were in the field, Cain attacked Abel and killed him.
Then the the LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" "I don't know," Cain said. "Am I supposed to watch over my brother?"
The The LORD said, "What did you do? Listen! Your brother's blood is crying to Me from the ground."
The The LORD said, "Now you are cursed and driven from the ground. It opened its mouth to drink your brother's blood from your hand.
When you work the ground, it will not give you good crops. You will wander around the earth."
Cain said to the the LORD, "My punishment is more than I can bear.
Today you are sending me away from the land. I will be hidden from you. I will wander on the earth, and anyone who finds me will kill me."
The The LORD said to him, "No! If anyone kills Cain, he will be punished seven times." Then the the LORD put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.
So Cain went out from the the LORD's presence and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Cain slept with his wife. She got pregnant and had a son named Enoch. Cain was building a city, and he named the city after his son Enoch.
Enoch had a son named Irad. Irad had a son named Mehujael. Mehujael had a son named Methushael. Methushael had a son named Lamech.
Lamech married two women. One was named Adah, and the other was named Zillah.
Adah had a son named Jabal. He was the father of people who live in tents and keep animals.
His brother was Jubal. He was the father of people who play harps and flutes.
Zillah had a son named Tubal-cain. He made tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah.
Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to me. Wives of Lamech, hear my words. I killed a man for hurting me. I killed a young man for hitting me."
If Cain is paid back seven times, then Lamech will be paid back seventy-seven times.
Adam slept with his wife again. She had a son and named him Seth. She said, "God has given me another child in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."
Seth had a son named Enosh. Then people began to call on the name of the the LORD.
This is the family line of Adam. God made man to look like God.
God made them male and female. God blessed them and called them Adam on the day they were made.
Adam was 130 years old when he had a son who looked like him. He named the boy Seth.
After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Adam lived 930 years in all. Then he died.
Seth was 105 years old when he had a son named Enosh.
After Enosh was born, Seth lived 807 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Seth lived 912 years in all. Then he died.
Enosh was 90 years old when he had a son named Kenan.
After Kenan was born, Enosh lived 815 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Enosh lived 905 years in all. Then he died.
Kenan was 70 years old when he had a son named Mahalalel.
After Mahalalel was born, Kenan lived 840 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Kenan lived 910 years in all. Then he died.
Mahalalel was 65 years old when he had a son named Jared.
After Jared was born, Mahalalel lived 830 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Mahalalel lived 895 years in all. Then he died.
Jared was 162 years old when he had a son named Enoch.
After Enoch was born, Jared lived 800 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Jared lived 962 years in all. Then he died.
Enoch was 65 years old when he had a son named Methuselah.
After Methuselah was born, Enoch lived close to God for 300 years. He had other sons and daughters.
Enoch lived close to God. Then he was gone, because God took him.
Methuselah was 187 years old when he had a son named Lamech.
After Lamech was born, Methuselah lived 782 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Methuselah lived 969 years in all. Then he died.
Lamech was 182 years old when he had a son.
He named the boy Noah. Lamech said, "This boy will give us rest from our hard work. The LORD cursed the ground."
After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 more years. He had other sons and daughters.
Lamech lived 777 years in all. Then he died.
Noah was 500 years old when he had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
People began to grow in number on the earth. Daughters were born to them.
The sons of God saw that the daughters of people were pretty. They married any women they wanted.
Then the LORD said, "My Spirit will not stay with people forever. They are only human. They will live 120 years."

In those days, and later too, there were Nephilim on the earth. The sons of God went to the daughters of people, and they had children. These children became the strong men of long ago. They were famous men.
The LORD saw that people were very bad on the earth. Every thought in their hearts was only bad all the time.
The LORD was sorry He had made people on the earth. He was sad in His heart.
So the LORD said, "I will wipe people off the earth. I made them, but now I will wipe out people, animals, bugs, and birds. I am sad that I made them."
But Noah found favor with the LORD.
This is the story of Noah's family. Noah was a good man. He did right in his time. He walked with God.
Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth was ruined in God's eyes. It was full of fighting.
God saw that the earth was ruined. All people had ruined their lives on the earth.
God said to Noah, "The time has come to end all living things. The earth is full of fighting because of them. I will destroy them and the earth. "
Make yourself an ark from gopher wood. Make rooms in it. Cover it inside and out with tar.
This is how you will make it: The ark will be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Make a window near the top. Finish it one cubit from the top. Put the door on the side. Make lower, second, and third floors. "
I am bringing a flood of water on the earth. It will destroy all living things under the sky. Everything on earth will die.
But I will make My promise with you. You, your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives will go into the ark with you. "
Bring two of every living thing into the ark. Bring them to keep them alive with you. They will be male and female.
Birds, animals, and all small things on the ground will come to you in pairs. This will keep them alive.
Take all the food that can be eaten. Gather it for yourself and for them. It will be food for you and for them."
Noah did all this. He did just what God told him to do.
The LORD said to Noah, "Come into the ark. You and your whole family come in, because I see that you are good.
Take seven pairs of every clean animal. Take a male and a female. Take one pair of every animal that is not clean.
Take seven pairs of birds too. This will keep life going on the earth.
In seven days I will make it rain for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe out every living thing I made from the earth."
Noah did everything the LORD told him.
Noah was 600 years old when the flood waters came on the earth.
Noah, his wife, his sons, and their wives went into the ark to get away from the flood water.
Clean animals and animals that are not clean came too. Birds and all small animals that move on the ground came.
They came to Noah in the ark two by two, male and female. This was just as God had told Noah.
After seven days, the flood water was on the earth.
Noah was 600 years old. It was the second month, day 17. On that day, springs under the earth burst open. The windows in the sky opened too.
Rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that same day, Noah went into the ark. His sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth went too. Noah's wife and the wives of his three sons went with them.
They went with every kind of wild animal, every kind of farm animal, every kind of small animal that moves on the ground, and every kind of bird.
They came to Noah in pairs, two of every living thing that breathes.
They came in as God told Noah. Then the LORD closed the door.
The flood lasted forty days. The water got higher and lifted the ark up off the ground.
The water kept rising. The ark floated on top of the water.
The water rose so high that it covered all the tall mountains under the sky.
The water rose about 22 feet above the mountains.
Every living thing on earth died. Birds, farm animals, wild animals, small creatures, and all people died.
Everything on dry land that breathed through its nose died.
Everything on the ground was wiped away. Only Noah and the people with him in the ark were left.
The water stayed high for 150 days.
But God remembered Noah. He remembered every living thing and all the animals in the boat with Noah. So God sent a wind over the earth. The water went down.
The springs under the earth and the windows in the sky closed. The rain stopped.
The water kept going down. After one hundred fifty days, there was less water.
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the boat came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
The water kept going down until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains could be seen.
After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the boat.
He sent out a raven. It flew back and forth until the water dried up on the earth.
Then he sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down.
The dove could not find a place to rest. So it came back to him in the boat. The water was still over the whole earth. Noah reached out his hand. He took the dove and brought it back into the boat.
He waited seven more days. Then he sent the dove out again.
In the evening, the dove came back. It had a fresh olive leaf in its mouth. Then Noah knew the water had gone down on the earth.
He waited seven more days. Then he sent the dove out again. This time it did not come back.
In the six hundred and first year of Noah's life, on the first day of the first month, the water had dried up. Noah took off the cover of the boat. He looked out and saw that the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was dry.
He said, "Come out of the boat. You and your wife, your sons and their wives, come out too.

Bring out every living thing that is with you. Bring out the birds, the animals, and all the small animals that move on the ground. They will spread out over the earth. They will have babies and grow in number."
So Noah came out with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.
All the animals, all the small animals that move, and all the birds came out of the boat. They came out by their families.
Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of the clean animals and some of the clean birds. He burned them on the altar as a gift to the LORD.

The LORD smelled the nice smell. The LORD said in His heart, "I will never put a curse on the ground again because of people. People's thoughts are evil from when they are young. I will never again destroy all living things the way I did."
As long as the earth is here, there will be planting time and harvest time. There will be cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night. They will not stop.
God blessed Noah and his sons. He said, "Have many children. Fill the whole earth.
All animals will be afraid of you. Every bird, every small animal, and all fish in the sea will fear you. I have put them in your hands.
You may eat any living thing that moves. I give you all of them, just like I gave you the green plants.
But do not eat meat that still has its lifeblood in it.
I will hold you responsible for your lives. I will demand an answer from every animal. I will also demand an answer from every person. If one person kills another, I will demand an answer.
If a person kills someone, people must put him to death. God made people like Himself.
Now you must have many children. Spread out over the earth and have many more."
God said to Noah and his sons, "I am making My promise with you and your children after you.
I am also making it with every living thing that is with you: the birds, the farm animals, and all the wild animals. Every animal that came out of the boat is included.
I promise that never again will all life be wiped out by a flood. Never again will a flood destroy the earth.
I promise that never again will all life be wiped out by a flood. Never again will a flood destroy the earth.
"This is the sign of My promise between Me and you and every living thing with you, for all time.
I have put My rainbow in the clouds. It will be the sign of My promise between Me and the earth.
When I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow shows in the clouds,
I will remember My promise between Me and you and all living things. The waters will never again become a flood to destroy all life.
Whenever the rainbow is in the clouds, I will see it. I will remember the promise that lasts forever between God and all living things on the earth.
This is the sign of the promise I have made between Me and all life on the earth."
Noah's sons who came out of the boat were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham became the father of Canaan.
These three sons became the fathers of all people on earth.
Noah was a farmer. He planted a grape garden.
He drank some of the wine. He got drunk. He lay without clothes in his tent.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father without clothes. He told his two brothers outside.
Shem and Japheth took a coat. They put it on their shoulders. They walked backward. They covered their father. They did not look at him.
Noah woke up. He knew what his youngest son had done.
He said, "May Canaan be cursed. He will be the lowest servant to his brothers.
Praise the the LORD, the God of Shem. May Canaan be his servant.
May God make Japheth great. May he live in the tents of Shem. May Canaan be his servant."
After the flood, Noah lived 350 more years.
Noah lived 950 years in all. Then he died.
These are the families of Noah's sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
From these men, the people of the nations spread into their lands. Each group had its own language and family.
Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah's sons were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was the father of Nimrod. Nimrod was the first great hero on earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the LORD. That is why people say, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD."
His kingdom began in Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh. These were in the land of Shinar.
From that land he went to Assyria. There he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah.
He also built Resen. It sits between Nineveh and Calah. Calah is the great city.
Mizraim was the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
He was also the father of Pathrusim, Casluhim, and Caphtorim. The Philistines came from Casluhim.
Canaan was the father of Sidon, his first son, and Heth.
He was also the father of the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites.
He was also the father of the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.
He was also the father of the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later the Canaanite families spread out.
The edge of the Canaanite land went from Sidon toward Gerar, all the way to Gaza. It went toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, all the way to Lasha.
These were Ham's sons. They are listed by their families, languages, lands, and nations.
Shem also had sons. He was Japheth's older brother. He was the father of all the sons of Eber.
Shem's sons were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
Aram's sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arphaxad was the father of Shelah. Shelah was the father of Eber.
Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
He was also the father of Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah.
He was also the father of Obal, Abimael, and Sheba.
He was also the father of Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were Joktan's sons.
They lived in the land from Mesha toward Sephar, in the eastern hills.
These were Shem's sons. They are listed by their families, languages, lands, and nations.
These are the families of Noah's sons, listed by their family lines and nations. From these, the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.
Everyone on earth spoke the same language and used the same words.
As people traveled east, they found a flat valley in Shinar and settled there.
They said to one another, "Come, let's make bricks and bake them well." They used bricks instead of stones, and tar for mortar.
Then they said, "Come, let's build a city and a tower with its top in the sky. Let's become famous, so we will not be scattered over the whole earth."
The LORD came down to see the city and the tower that people had built.
the LORD said, "Look, they are one people, and they all speak one language. This is only the start of what they will do. Soon nothing they plan will be too hard for them.
Come, let's go down and mix up their language. Then they will not understand one another."
So the LORD scattered them from there over the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.
That is why the city was called Babel. There the LORD mixed up the language of the whole earth, and from there the LORD scattered the people over the whole earth.
This is the family line of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he had a son named Arphaxad.
After Arphaxad was born, Shem lived 500 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he had a son named Shelah.
After Shelah was born, Arphaxad lived 403 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Shelah was 30 years old, he had a son named Eber.
After Eber was born, Shelah lived 403 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Eber was 34 years old, he had a son named Peleg.
After Peleg was born, Eber lived 430 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Peleg was 30 years old, he had a son named Reu.
After Reu was born, Peleg lived 209 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Reu was 32 years old, he had a son named Serug.
After Serug was born, Reu lived 207 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Serug was 30 years old, he had a son named Nahor.
After Nahor was born, Serug lived 200 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Nahor was 29 years old, he had a son named Terah.
After Terah was born, Nahor lived 119 more years and had other sons and daughters.
When Terah was 70 years old, he had sons named Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
This is the family line of Terah. Terah was the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran was the father of Lot.
Haran died while his father Terah was still alive, in the land where he was born, Ur of the Chaldeans.
Abram and Nahor both took wives. Abram's wife was Sarai. Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran. Haran was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.
But Sarai could not have children.

Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot (the son of Haran), and his daughter-in-law Sarai (the wife of Abram). They left Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. They came to Haran and stayed there.
Terah lived 205 years and died in Haran.
The LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, your people, and your father’s home. Go to the land I will show you.
I will make you into a big nation. I will bless you. I will make your name great. You will be a blessing.
I will bless anyone who blesses you. I will curse anyone who curses you. All people on earth will be blessed because of you.”
So Abram went, just as the LORD had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was 75 years old when he left Harran.
He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the things they owned, and the people who were with them in Harran. They left for Canaan and arrived there.
Abram traveled through the land to the big tree at Moreh, near Shechem. At that time, the Canaanites were living in the land.
The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your children.” So Abram built an altar there for the LORD, who had appeared to him.
From there he went to the hills east of Bethel and set up his tent. Bethel was to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar for the LORD and prayed to the LORD.
There was very little food in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to stay for a while, because the famine was very bad.
When he was almost in Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, “I know you are a very beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘She is his wife.’ Then they will kill me, but they will let you live.
Please say you are my sister. Then things will go well for me because of you, and I will live because of you.”
When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.
Pharaoh’s helpers saw her too. They told Pharaoh how beautiful she was. Then she was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
Pharaoh was good to Abram because of her. Abram got sheep, cattle, donkeys, servants, and camels.
But the LORD made Pharaoh and his family very sick because of Abram’s wife Sarai.
So Pharaoh called for Abram. He said, “What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so I took her as my wife? Now take your wife and go!”
Then Pharaoh told his men to send Abram away. They sent him and his wife and all he had.
Abram went up from Egypt to the south country. He took his wife and all he had. Lot went with him.
Abram was very rich. He had many animals, silver, and gold.
He traveled from place to place. He went from the south country to Bethel. He went to the place between Bethel and Ai. That was where his tent had been before.
It was where he had built an altar first. There Abram prayed to the LORD.
Lot went with Abram. Lot also had sheep, cows, and tents.
The land could not hold them both. They had too much stuff to live together.
The men who cared for Abram's animals and Lot's animals began to fight. At that time, Canaanites and Perizzites lived in the land.
Abram said to Lot, “Please do not let there be a fight between you and me. Do not let there be a fight between your workers and my workers. We are brothers.
Look, the whole land is before you. Please go your own way. If you go to the left, I will go to the right. If you go to the right, I will go to the left.”

Lot looked up and saw all the flat land by the Jordan River. It had water everywhere. This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. It looked like the garden of the LORD. It looked like the land of Egypt near Zoar.
So Lot chose all that flat land. He traveled east. The two men went their own ways.
Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. Lot stayed in the cities of the flat land. He put his tent near Sodom.
The men of Sodom were very bad. They sinned much against the LORD.
After Lot left, the LORD said to Abram, “Look up from where you are. Look north, south, east, and west.
All the land you see, I will give to you and your children forever.
I will make your children as many as the dust of the earth. If a man can count the dust, he can count your children.
Get up and walk through the land. Walk its length and width. I will give it to you.”
Abram moved his tent. He came and lived by the big trees at Mamre in Hebron. There he built an altar to the LORD.
In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
these kings made war with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
All these kings came together in the Valley of Siddim, which is the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they served Chedorlaomer. In the thirteenth year they turned against him.
In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came. They beat the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim.
They also beat the Horites in the hill country of Seir, all the way to El-paran near the desert.
Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat, which is Kadesh. They beat all the country of the Amalekites and the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar, went out. They set up for battle in the Valley of Siddim.
They fought against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar. It was four kings against five.
The Valley of Siddim had many tar pits. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ran away and fell into them. The rest ran to the hills.
The winners took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food. Then they left.
They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, and his things. Lot was living in Sodom. Then they left.
One man who got away came and told Abram the Hebrew. Abram was living near the big trees of Mamre the Amorite. Mamre's brothers were Eshcol and Aner. They had made a promise to help Abram.
Abram heard that his relative had been taken. He led out his trained men, 318 men born in his house. He chased the enemy as far as Dan.
At night Abram split his men into groups. He and his servants beat the enemy. They chased them to Hobah, north of Damascus.
Abram brought back all the goods. He brought back his relative Lot and Lot's things. He also brought back the women and the people.
After Abram came back from beating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, which is the King's Valley.
Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
He blessed Abram and said, "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth.
And blessed be God Most High, who gave your enemies into your hand." Abram gave him one tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people. You can keep the goods."
Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I promised the LORD, God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth.
I will not take a thread or a sandal strap or anything that is yours. You will not say, 'I made Abram rich.'
I will take nothing except what the young men ate and the share for the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their share."
After all this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision. The LORD said, "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield. Your reward will be very great."
But Abram said, "Lord the LORD, what will You give me? I have no children. The one who will get my house is Eliezer from Damascus."
Abram said, "Look, You have given me no child. So a servant in my house will get everything I own."
Then the word of the LORD came to him. He said, "This man will not get your things. A son of your own will get them."
The LORD took him outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can. So big will your family be."
Abram believed the LORD. The LORD said that Abram was right with Him.
The LORD also said to him, "I am the LORD. I brought you out of Ur in Chaldea to give you this land to own."
But Abram asked, "Lord the LORD, how will I know I will own it?"
The LORD said to him, "Bring Me a young cow, a goat, and a male sheep. Each should be three years old. Also bring a dove and a young pigeon."
So Abram brought all these animals to the LORD. He cut them in two and put the halves across from each other. But he did not cut the birds in half.
Birds that eat dead things came down on the pieces. Abram chased them away.
As the sun was going down, Abram fell into a deep sleep. A deep, scary darkness fell on him.
Then the LORD said to Abram, "Know for sure that your children will live in a land that is not theirs. They will be slaves and be treated badly for four hundred years.
But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. After that, they will leave with many good things.
"You, however, will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age.
After four generations, your children will come back here. The Amorites have not yet done all their wrong."
When the sun had set and it was dark, a smoking pot and a burning torch passed between the pieces.
On that day the LORD made a promise with Abram. He said, "I have given this land to your children. It goes from the river in Egypt to the great Euphrates River.
It is the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,
Abram's wife Sarai had no children. She had a servant girl from Egypt. Her name was Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram, "Look, the LORD has stopped me from having children. Please go to my servant girl. Maybe I can have a family through her." Abram listened to Sarai.
Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years. Then Sarai took Hagar, her Egyptian servant girl, and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
Abram went to Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar saw she was pregnant, she looked down on Sarai.
Sarai said to Abram, "This is your fault! I gave my servant to you. Now she is pregnant, and she treats me badly. May the LORD decide between you and me."
Abram said, "Your servant is in your hands. Do what you think is best." Then Sarai was mean to Hagar, and Hagar ran away.
The angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring in the desert. The spring was on the way to Shur.
The angel said, "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where did you come from? Where are you going?" Hagar said, "I am running away from Sarai, my boss."
The angel said, "Go back to your boss and obey her."
The angel also said, "I will give you so many children that no one can count them."
The angel said, "Look, you are pregnant. You will have a son. You will name him Ishmael, because the LORD heard your trouble."
He will be wild like a donkey. He will fight with everyone, and everyone will fight with him. He will not get along with his brothers.
Hagar called the the LORD who spoke to her, "You are the God who sees me." She said this because she thought she had seen the God who sees her.
So the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is between Kadesh and Bered.
Hagar had a son for Abram. Abram named him Ishmael.
Abram was 86 years old when Hagar had Ishmael.
When Abram was 99 years old, the LORD came to him and said, "I am God All-Powerful. Live for Me and do what is right.
I will make a special promise between Me and you. I will make your family very big."
Then God said, "Here is My promise with you. You will be the father of many nations.
Your name will not be Abram anymore. Your name will be Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.
I will give you many children. I will make you the father of many nations, and kings will come from you.
I will keep My promise with you and with your children and their children forever. I will be your God, and I will be their God too.
I will give you and your children after you the land where you are living now. I will give you all the land of Canaan to keep forever. I will be their God."
God said to Abraham, "You must keep My promise. You and your children and their children must keep it.
This is My promise that you must keep. It is between Me and you and your children after you: Every male among you must be circumcised.
You must be circumcised in your bodies. This will be the sign of My promise between Me and you.
Every baby boy must be circumcised when he is 8 days old. This rule lasts forever. It is for boys born in your homes and for boys bought with your money, even if they are not from your family.
Boys born in your home and boys bought with your money must be circumcised. My promise will be in your bodies forever.
Any male who is not circumcised has broken My promise. He will be sent away from his people."
God said to Abraham, "Do not call your wife Sarai anymore. Her name will be Sarah.
I will bless her. I will give you a son through her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of many nations. Kings will come from her."
Abraham fell face down and laughed. He said to himself, "Can a 100-year-old man have a baby? Can Sarah have a baby when she is 90?"
Abraham said to God, "I wish Ishmael could live and be blessed by You."
God said, "Your wife Sarah will have a son. You will name him Isaac. I will keep My promise with him forever. It will be for him and his children after him.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I have blessed him. I will give him many children, and his family will grow very big. He will be the father of 12 leaders, and I will make him a great nation.
But I will keep My promise with Isaac. Sarah will have him for you next year at this time."
When God finished talking with Abraham, God left him.
That same day, Abraham took his son Ishmael and all the males in his home. He took the boys born there and the men he had bought. He circumcised them, just as God had told him.
Abraham was 99 years old when he was circumcised.
Ishmael was 13 years old when he was circumcised.
Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on that same day.
All the men in his home were circumcised too. This included the men born there and the men bought with money.
The LORD appeared to Abraham by the big trees at Mamre. Abraham was sitting at the door of his tent in the hot part of the day.
He looked up and saw three men standing near him. He ran from the tent door to meet them and bowed down to the ground.
Abraham said, "My lord, if you are pleased with me, please do not go past me, your servant."
"Please let me bring a little water. Wash your feet and rest under the tree."
"I will get you some bread to eat. Then you can go on your way, because you came to me, your servant." "Do as you have said," they said.
Abraham hurried into the tent and said to Sarah, "Quick! Take three large bowls of fine flour, mix it, and make bread."
Abraham ran to the herd and took a young calf that was soft and good. He gave it to a servant, who hurried to cook it.
Abraham took cheese and milk and the calf he had cooked. He set them before the men. He stood by them under the tree while they ate.
They said to him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" "She is in the tent," he said.
The LORD said, "I will come back to you at this time next year. Your wife Sarah will have a son." Sarah was listening at the tent door behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were very old. Sarah could not have children anymore.
Sarah laughed to herself. She said, "I am too old to have a baby, and my husband is old too."
The LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh? She said, 'Can I really have a baby when I am old?'"
The LORD said, "Is anything too hard for the LORD? I will come back at the right time next year, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah was afraid, so she said, "I did not laugh." But the LORD said, "Yes, you did laugh."
Then the men got up to leave and looked toward Sodom. Abraham walked with them to send them off.
The LORD said, "Should I keep from Abraham what I am going to do?
Abraham will become a great and strong nation. All nations on earth will be blessed through him.
I chose him so he will teach his children and family to follow the LORD and do what is right and fair. Then the LORD can do for Abraham what He promised."
The LORD said, "The people of Sodom and Gomorrah have done so much wrong. Their sin is very bad.
I will go down and see if they have really done all the bad things people say. If not, I will know."
The men turned and went toward Sodom. Abraham stayed standing before the LORD.
Abraham came closer and said, "Will You really destroy good people along with bad people?
What if there are fifty good people in the city? Will You still destroy the place and not spare it for those fifty good people?
You would never do such a thing. You would never kill good people with bad people, as if they were the same. The Judge of all the earth will do what is right."
The LORD said, "If I find fifty good people in Sodom, I will spare the whole place for them."
Abraham said, "I am only dust and ashes, but I dare to speak to the Lord."
Abraham said, "What if there are five less than fifty good people? Will You destroy the whole city for that?" The LORD said, "If I find forty-five good people there, I will not destroy it."
Abraham said, "What if forty good people are found there?" The LORD said, "I will not destroy it for forty."
Abraham said, "Please do not be angry, Lord. What if thirty good people are found there?" The LORD said, "I will not destroy it if I find thirty."
Abraham said, "I dare to speak to the Lord. What if twenty good people are found there?" The LORD said, "I will not destroy it for twenty."
Abraham said, "Please do not be angry, Lord. I will speak just this once. What if ten good people are found there?" The LORD said, "I will not destroy it for ten."
When the LORD finished speaking with Abraham, He left. Abraham went back to his home.
Two angels came to Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the city gate. When Lot saw them, he stood up to meet them. He bowed with his face to the ground.
He said, "Please, sirs, come to my house. Wash your feet and stay the night. Then you can get up early and go on your way."They said, "No, we will stay in the town square."
But Lot asked them so much that they went with him. He made a meal for them and baked flat bread. They ate.
Before they went to bed, all the men of Sodom, young and old, came around the house.
They called to Lot, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us. We want to sleep with them."
Lot went out to them and shut the door behind him.
He said, "Please, my brothers, do not do this bad thing!
Look, I have two daughters. They have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you. You can do what you want with them. But do not hurt these men. They came under my roof."
They said, "Get out of the way! This man came here to live, and now he wants to be our judge! We will hurt you more than them." They pushed hard against Lot. They tried to break the door.
But the men inside reached out. They pulled Lot into the house and shut the door.
They made the men at the door blind. Young and old, they could not find the door.
The two men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here? A son-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here.
We are going to destroy this place. The cry to the the LORD against its people is so loud. He has sent us to destroy it."
Lot went out and talked to the men who were going to marry his daughters. He said, "Get up! Get out of this place. The the LORD is going to destroy the city!" But they thought he was joking.
At sunrise the angels pushed Lot. They said, "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here. If you do not, you will be swept away with the city."
Lot waited. But the men took his hand, his wife's hand, and his daughters' hands. They led them safely out of the city. The the LORD was kind to them.
When they were outside, one said, "Run for your life! Do not look back. Do not stop on the plain. Run to the mountains, or you will be swept away."
I have found favor with you. You have been very kind to me. You saved my life. But I cannot run to the mountains. The trouble will catch me, and I will die.
Look, there is a small city near here. Let me run there. It is small. Let me go there, and I will live."
He said, "All right. I will do this too. I will not destroy that city.
Hurry! Run there fast. I cannot do anything until you get there." That is why the city is called Zoar.
The sun had risen over the land when Lot reached Zoar.
Then the the LORD rained down burning sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. It came from the the LORD out of heaven.
He destroyed the cities of the plain. He destroyed all the people who lived there. He destroyed the plants of the land.
But Lot's wife looked back. She became a pillar of salt.
Early the next morning, Abraham got up. He went to the place where he had stood before the the LORD.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the plain. He saw smoke rising from the land like smoke from a hot oven.
When God destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abraham. He brought Lot out of the disaster. Lot had lived in those cities.
Lot and his two daughters left Zoar. They went up to the mountains. He was afraid to stay in Zoar. They lived in a cave.
The older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old. There is no man here to sleep with us. This is how people have children all over the world.
Come, let us give our father wine to drink. Then we will sleep with him. Then we can have children from our father."
That night they gave their father wine to drink. The older daughter went in and slept with her father. He did not know when she lay down or got up.
The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "I slept with our father last night. Let us give him wine again tonight. You go in and sleep with him. Then we can have children from our father."
That night they gave their father wine again. The younger daughter went in and slept with her father. He did not know when she lay down or got up.
So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter had a son. She named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites today.
The younger daughter had a son. She named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites today.
Abraham left that place. He went to the south country. He lived between Kadesh and Shur. He stayed in Gerar for a while.
Abraham said to his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." Abimelech, the king of Gerar, sent men, and they took Sarah.
That night God came to Abimelech in a dream. He said to him, "You are as good as dead. You took a married woman."
Abimelech had not gone near her. He said, "Lord, will You kill even people who did nothing wrong?
Did he not say to me, 'She is my sister'? And she herself said, 'He is my brother.' I did this with an honest heart. I did not mean to do wrong."
God said to him in the dream, "I know you did this with an honest heart. I also kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now give the man back his wife. He is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. If you do not give her back, know this: you and all who belong to you will surely die."
Early in the morning, Abimelech got up. He called all his servants. He told them everything. They were very afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham. He said to him, "What have you done to us? How did I sin against you, that you brought such a big sin on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done."
Abimelech said to Abraham, "What did you see? Why did you do this?"
Abraham said, "I thought, 'There is no fear of God in this place. They will kill me because of my wife.'
Besides, she really is my sister. She is my father's daughter, but not my mother's daughter. She became my wife.
When God made me leave my father's house, I said to her, 'Please be kind to me. Everywhere we go, say, "He is my brother."'"
Then Abimelech took sheep, cows, male and female servants. He gave them to Abraham. He gave Sarah back to him.
Abimelech said, "Look, my land is before you. Live where you like."
He said to Sarah, "Look, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. This proves to everyone with you that you did nothing wrong. You are cleared before everyone."
Abraham prayed to God. God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants. Then they had children.
For the LORD had closed every womb in Abimelech's house because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
The LORD came to Sarah, just like He said He would. The LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.
Sarah became pregnant and had a baby boy for Abraham when he was very old. It happened at the time God said it would.
Abraham named his son Isaac. Sarah had this baby for him.
Abraham had Isaac circumcised when he was eight days old, just like God told him to.
Abraham was one hundred years old when Isaac was born.
Sarah said, "God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."
She also said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would feed babies? But I have had a son when Abraham is old."
The boy grew up and was weaned. Abraham gave a big party on the day Isaac was weaned.
Sarah saw the son of Hagar, the woman from Egypt. Hagar had this son for Abraham. Sarah saw him making fun of Isaac.
Sarah said to Abraham, "Send away this slave woman and her son. The son of a slave woman will not share the family blessing with my son Isaac."
This made Abraham very sad because it was about his son.
God said to Abraham, "Do not be sad about the boy and your slave woman. Listen to Sarah. Do everything she tells you. Your family will be named through Isaac.
I will also make the son of the slave woman into a big group of people, because he is your son too."

Early the next morning, Abraham got up. He took bread and a bag of water and gave them to Hagar. He put them on her shoulder. He also sent the boy with her. Hagar left and walked in the desert near Beersheba.
When the water was gone, she put the boy under a bush.
She went and sat down far away, about as far as an arrow can fly. She said, "I cannot watch the boy die." She sat there and cried out loud.
God heard the boy crying. An angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said, "What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy where he is.
Get up, pick up the boy, and hold him with your hand. I will make him into a big group of people."
God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the bag with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy as he grew. He lived in the desert and became a hunter with a bow.
He lived in the desert of Paran. His mother found a wife for him from Egypt.
At that time, Abimelech and Phicol, the leader of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do."

Abimelech said, "Now promise me here before God that you will not lie to me, or to my children, or to their children. Be kind to me and to this land where you have lived, just as I have been kind to you."
Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water. Abimelech's workers had taken it.
Abimelech said, "I did not know who did this. You did not tell me. I had not heard about it until today."
Abraham took sheep and cows and gave them to Abimelech. The two men made an agreement.
Abraham set seven female lambs from the flock by themselves.
Abimelech asked, "What do these seven female lambs mean? Why did you put them by themselves?"
Abraham said, "Take these seven female lambs from my hand. They will show that I dug this well."
So that place was called Beersheba, because the two men swore an oath there.
They made an agreement in Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol, the leader of his army, got up and went back to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. He called on the name of the LORD, the God who lives forever.
Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines for many days.
After these things, God tested Abraham. He said, "Abraham!" "Here I am," Abraham said.
God said, "Take your son, your only son, whom you love. Take Isaac. Go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I will show you."

Early in the morning, Abraham got up. He put a saddle on his donkey. He took two young men with him and Isaac his son. He cut wood for the burnt offering. Then he got up and went to the place God had told him about.
On the third day, Abraham looked up and saw the place far away.
Abraham said to his young men, "Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there. We will worship, and then we will come back to you."
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering. He put it on Isaac his son. He took the fire and the knife in his hand. The two of them walked on together.
Isaac said to Abraham his father, "My father!" "Here I am, my son," Abraham said. Isaac said, "Look, we have fire and wood. But where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"
Abraham said, "God will give us the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." So the two of them walked on together.
They came to the place God had told him about. Abraham built an altar there. He put the wood in order. He tied up Isaac his son. He laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Abraham reached out his hand. He took the knife to kill his son.
The angel of the the LORD called to him from heaven. He said, "Abraham! Abraham!" "Here I am," Abraham said.
The angel said, "Do not hurt the boy. Do not do anything to him. Now I know you fear God. You have not held back your son, your only son, from Me."
Abraham looked up. He saw a ram behind him. Its horns were caught in a bush. Abraham went and took the ram. He offered it as a burnt offering instead of his son.
Abraham called that place "The LORD Will Provide." People still say today, "On the mountain of the the LORD it will be provided."
The angel of the the LORD called to Abraham a second time from heaven.
He said, "I make this strong promise by Myself, says the the LORD. I do this because you did this thing. You did not hold back your son, your only son.
I will bless you greatly. I will make your family as many as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the beach. Your family will defeat their enemies.
All nations on earth will be blessed through your family, because you obeyed Me."
Abraham went back to his young men. They got up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham stayed in Beersheba.
After these things, Abraham heard that Milcah had also had sons for Nahor, his brother.
Uz was the firstborn. His brothers were Buz and Kemuel, the father of Aram.
There were also Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight sons were born to Milcah and Nahor, Abraham's brother.
Nahor's other wife, Reumah, also had sons: Tebah, Gaham, Thahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lived to be 127 years old.
She died in Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to cry and mourn for her.
Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife. He spoke to the Hittites.
"I am a stranger here with you. Please sell me a place to bury my dead."
"Listen to us, sir. You are a great leader among us. Bury your dead in the best grave we have. None of us will keep our grave from you."
Abraham stood up. He bowed down to the people of that land, the Hittites.
He said, "If you are willing to let me bury my dead, listen to me. Ask Ephron son of Zohar for me.
Ask him to sell me the cave of Machpelah. It is at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me here with you for the full price. Then I will have a place to bury my dead."
Ephron was sitting with the Hittites. In front of all the Hittites who came to the city gate, Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham.
"No, sir. Listen to me. I give you the field and the cave in it. I give it to you in front of my people. Bury your dead."
Again Abraham bowed down to the people of the land.
He said to Ephron so everyone could hear, "Please listen to me. I will pay for the field. Take the money from me. Then I can bury my dead there."
"Sir, listen to me. The land is worth four hundred pieces of silver. What is that between us? Bury your dead."
Abraham agreed. He weighed out the silver Ephron had named. He did this in front of the Hittites. It was four hundred pieces of silver, the kind merchants use.
So Ephron's field in Machpelah near Mamre was Abraham's. The field, the cave in it, and all the trees around it became his.
This happened in front of all the Hittites at the city gate.
After that, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the field of Machpelah near Mamre. This is Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
The field and the cave in it became Abraham's burial place. The Hittites gave it to him.
Abraham was very old. The LORD had blessed him in every way.
Abraham said to his oldest servant, the one who ruled all he had, "Make a serious promise to me.
Promise by the LORD, the God of heaven and earth, that you will not get a wife for my son from the Canaanite girls who live near me.
Go to my old home and my family. Get a wife there for my son Isaac."
The servant said, "What if the woman will not come with me to this land? Should I take your son back to the land you came from?"
Abraham said, "No. Do not take my son back there.

The LORD, the God of heaven, took me from my father's house and my old home. He spoke to me and promised me, 'I will give this land to your family.' He will send His angel ahead of you. Get a wife for my son from there.
If the woman will not come with you, you are free from this promise. Only do not take my son back there."
So the servant promised Abraham he would do this.
The servant took ten of his master's camels and left. He took many good things from his master. He went to the city of Nahor in Mesopotamia.
In the evening, when women came to get water, he made the camels kneel by the well outside the city.
He prayed, "the LORD, God of my master Abraham, please help me today. Show kindness to my master Abraham.
I am standing by the spring. The young women of the city are coming out to get water.
Let the girl who says, 'Please give me a drink,' and then says, 'I will get water for your camels too,' be the one You have chosen for Isaac. Then I will know You have been kind to my master."
Before he finished praying, Rebekah came out. She had a jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel, who was the son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor.
The girl was very pretty and had never been married. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came back up.
The servant ran to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water from your jar."
She said, "Drink, my lord." She hurried and lowered her jar on her hand and gave him a drink.
When she finished giving him a drink, she said, "I will get water for your camels too, until they have all they need."
She hurried and poured the water into the water tub. Then she ran to the well again and got water for all his camels.
The man watched her quietly. He wanted to know if the LORD had made his trip a success.
When the camels finished drinking, the man took a gold nose ring and two gold bracelets. He put them on her hands.
He asked, "Whose daughter are you? Tell me. Is there room in your father's house for us to stay?"
She said, "I am the daughter of Bethuel. Milcah is his mother, and Nahor is his father.
We have plenty of straw and feed, and room for you to stay."
The man bowed down and worshiped the LORD.
He said, "Praise the LORD, the God of my master Abraham. He has not stopped being kind and true to my master. The LORD led me straight to my master's relatives."
The girl ran and told her mother's family what had happened.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban. Laban ran out to the man at the spring.
He had seen the ring and bracelets on his sister's hands. He had heard her say what the man said to her. So he went to the man, who was standing by the camels at the spring.
Laban said, "Come in, you who are blessed by the LORD. Why are you standing outside? I have made the house ready and a place for the camels."
So the man came into the house. Laban unloaded the camels. He gave them straw and feed. He gave water to wash the feet of the man and his helpers.
Food was set before him. But he said, "I will not eat until I tell why I came." Laban said, "Speak."
The LORD has blessed my master very much. He is now a great man. The LORD gave him sheep, cattle, silver, gold, servants, maids, camels, and donkeys.
Sarah, my master's wife, had a son for him when she was old. My master gave him everything he has.
"My master made me promise. He said, 'Do not get a wife for my son from the Canaanite girls in this land where I live.'
'Go to my father's house and my family. Get a wife there for my son.'
"I said to my master, 'What if the woman will not come with me?'
He said, 'The LORD, whom I follow, will send His angel with you. He will make your trip go well. You will get a wife for my son from my family.'
'Then you will be free from my promise if you go to my family and they will not give her to you. You will be free from my promise.'
"I came to the spring today and prayed, 'the LORD, God of my master Abraham, if You will make my trip go well,'
'I am standing by the spring. When a young woman comes out to get water, I will say, "Please give me a little water from your jar."'
'She will say, "I will drink, and I will get water for your camels too." Let her be the woman the LORD has chosen for my master's son.'
"Before I finished praying in my heart, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and got water. I said, 'Please give me a drink.'
She hurried and lowered her jar and said, 'Drink. I will water your camels too.' So I drank, and she watered the camels too.
I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'I am the daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor. Milcah is his mother.' Then I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.
"I bowed down and worshiped the LORD. I thanked the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, because He led me the right way to get a wife for my master's son from his family.
Now, if you will be kind and true to my master, tell me. If not, tell me, and I will go another way."
Laban and Bethuel answered, "This has come from the LORD. We cannot say yes or no to you.
Look, Rebekah is here. Take her and go. Let her be the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has said."
When Abraham's servant heard this, he bowed to the ground to worship the LORD.
The servant brought out silver and gold jewelry and clothes. He gave them to Rebekah. He also gave nice gifts to her brother and mother.
He and his men ate and drank and stayed the night. In the morning he said, "Send me back to my master."
Her brother and mother said, "Let the girl stay with us for a few days, at least ten. Then she can go."
He said, "Do not keep me. The LORD has made my trip go well. Send me back to my master."
They said, "We will call the girl and ask her."
They called Rebekah and asked, "Will you go with this man?" She said, "I will go."
So they sent Rebekah, her nurse, Abraham's servant, and his men on their way.
They blessed Rebekah and said, "Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands and thousands. May your children take over the cities of their enemies."
Rebekah and her maids got up and rode on the camels. They followed the man. The servant took Rebekah and left.
Isaac had come from Beer-lahai-roi. He was living in the south country.
In the evening, Isaac went out to the field to think and pray. He looked up and saw camels coming.
Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel.
She asked the servant, "Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?" The servant said, "He is my master." So she took her veil and covered herself.
The servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent. He married Rebekah. He loved her. Isaac was comforted after his mother died.
Abraham married another woman named Keturah.
She had Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah for him.
Jokshan had Sheba and Dedan. Dedan's sons were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were Keturah's sons.
Abraham gave everything he owned to Isaac.
While he was still alive, Abraham gave gifts to his other sons. He sent them east, away from Isaac, to the east country.
He died old and full of years. He had lived a long, good life. Then he died and went to rest with his people.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah. It was in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, east of Mamre.
Abraham had bought that field from the Hittites. Sarah, his wife, was buried there too.
After Abraham died, God blessed Isaac. Isaac lived near Beer Lahai Roi.
These are the children of Ishmael, Abraham's son. Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's servant, had Ishmael for Abraham.
These are the names of Ishmael's sons, by their family groups: Nebaioth, the firstborn, then Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam.
Also Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These were Ishmael's sons. They had towns and camps. There were twelve leaders over their tribes.
Ishmael lived 137 years. Then he died and was gathered to his people.
His family lived from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt, toward Asshur. They settled near all his brothers.
These are the children of Isaac, Abraham's son. Abraham was Isaac's father.
Isaac was 40 years old when he married Rebekah. She was the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan Aram. She was also the sister of Laban the Aramean.
Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she could not have children. The LORD answered Isaac, and Rebekah became pregnant.
The babies fought inside her. She said, "If this is how it is, why am I here?" So she went to ask the LORD.
The LORD said to her, "Two nations are in your womb. Two groups of people will come from your body. One will be stronger than the other. The older will serve the younger."
When her time came, she had twins.
The first baby came out red and hairy all over, like a coat. They named him Esau.
Then his brother came out. His hand held Esau's heel. They named him Jacob. Isaac was 60 years old when they were born.
The boys grew up. Esau became a skilled hunter and a man of the field. Jacob was a quiet man who stayed in the tents.
Isaac loved Esau, because Esau brought him food from hunting. Rebekah loved Jacob.
One day Jacob was cooking stew. Esau came in from the field. He was very tired.
Esau said to Jacob, "Let me eat some of that red stew. I am very tired." That is why he was called Edom.
Jacob said, "Sell me your right to be the first son today."
Esau said, "I am about to die. What good is that right to me?"
Jacob said, "Promise me today." Esau promised. So he sold his first son's right to Jacob.
Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. Esau ate and drank. Then he got up and left. In that way, Esau did not care about his first son's right.
There was a famine in the land. It was not the first one. There had been a famine when Abraham lived. Isaac went to Abimelech. Abimelech was king of the Philistines in Gerar.
The LORD appeared to Isaac. He said, "Do not go down to Egypt. Live in the land I tell you about.
Stay in this land. I will be with you and bless you. I will give all these lands to you and your children and grandchildren. I will keep the promise I made to your father Abraham.
I will make your children and grandchildren as many as the stars in the sky. I will give all these lands to them. All nations on earth will be blessed through them.
I will do this because Abraham obeyed Me. He kept My rules and My laws."
The men there asked about his wife. Isaac said, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say, "She is my wife." He thought, "The men here might kill me because of Rebekah." She was very pretty.
Isaac stayed there a long time. Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looked out a window. He saw Isaac holding his wife Rebekah close.
Abimelech called Isaac. He said, "She is your wife! Why did you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac said, "I thought I might die because of her."
Abimelech said, "What have you done to us? One of our men might have slept with your wife. Then we would be guilty."
Abimelech told all the people, "Anyone who hurts this man or his wife must be put to death."
Isaac planted crops in that land. That same year he got one hundred times as much. the LORD blessed him.
Isaac became rich. He got richer and richer until he was very rich.
He had many sheep, cows, and workers. The Philistines were jealous of him.
The Philistines had filled with dirt all the wells that Abraham's workers had dug.
Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from us. You are much stronger than we are."
So Isaac left. He camped in the Gerar Valley. He settled there.
Isaac dug again the wells from Abraham's time. The Philistines had filled them after Abraham died. Isaac gave them the same names Abraham had given them.
Isaac's workers dug in the valley. They found a well with fresh water.
The men of Gerar argued with Isaac's men. They said, "This water is ours." So Isaac named the well Esek because they argued with him.
They dug another well. They argued over that one too. Isaac named it Sitnah.
Isaac moved from there. He dug another well. No one argued over it. He named it Rehoboth. He said, "Now the LORD has made room for us. We will do well in this land."
Isaac went up to Beersheba from there.

The LORD appeared to Isaac that night. He said, "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid. I am with you. I will bless you. I will make your children and grandchildren many. I will do this because of Abraham, My servant."
Isaac built an altar there. He called on the name of the LORD. He put up his tent there. Isaac's workers dug a well there.
Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar. Ahuzzath, his friend, came too. Phicol, the army leader, came too.
Isaac said to them, "Why did you come to me? You hated me. You sent me away from you."
They said, "We see that the LORD has been with you. So we said, 'Let us make a promise between us and you.'
You will not hurt us. We did not touch you, and we only did good to you. We sent you away in peace. Now the LORD has blessed you."
Isaac made a feast for them. They ate and drank.
They got up early in the morning. They made a promise to each other. Isaac sent them away. They left in peace.
That same day, Isaac's workers came to him. They told him about the well they had dug. They said, "We found water."
Isaac named the well Shibah. That is why the city is called Beersheba to this day.
Esau was forty years old. He married Judith. She was the daughter of Beeri the Hittite. He also married Basemath. She was the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
These wives made life hard for Isaac and Rebekah.
Isaac was old, and his eyes were weak. He could not see. He called his older son, Esau. He said, "My son." Esau said, "Here I am."
Isaac said, "I am old now. I do not know when I will die."
"Now get your weapons. Take your bow and arrows. Go out to the field. Hunt some wild animal for me.
Cook me a tasty meal, the kind I like. Bring it to me. I will eat it. Then I will bless you before I die."
Rebekah was listening while Isaac talked to his son Esau. Esau went to the field to hunt. He would bring back the food.
Rebekah said to her son Jacob, "I heard your father say to your brother Esau,
'Bring me some wild animal and cook me a tasty meal. I will eat it. Then I will bless you before the LORD before I die.'
Now, my son, listen to me. Do what I tell you.
Go to the flock. Bring me two good young goats. I will cook them into a tasty meal for your father, the way he likes it.
Take it to your father. He will eat it. Then he may bless you before he dies."
Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "My brother Esau is a hairy man. I have smooth skin."
"What if my father touches me? He will think I am tricking him. Then I will get a curse, not a blessing."
His mother said, "My son, let the curse fall on me. Just listen to me. Go get the goats for me."
So Jacob went and got the goats. He brought them to his mother. She cooked a tasty meal, just the way his father liked it.
Rebekah took the best clothes of Esau, her older son. She had them in the house. She put them on Jacob, her younger son.
She put goat skins on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
Then she put the tasty meal and the bread she had made into Jacob's hands.
Jacob went to his father. He said, "My father." Isaac said, "Yes, my son. Who is it?"
Jacob said, "I am Esau, your first son. I did what you told me. Please sit up. Eat some of the food I hunted. Then you can bless me."
Isaac said, "How did you find it so fast, my son?" Jacob said, "The LORD your God helped me find it."
Isaac said, "Come near, my son. Let me touch you. I want to know if you are really my son Esau."
Jacob went close to his father Isaac. Isaac touched him. Isaac said, "The voice is Jacob's voice. But the hands are Esau's hands."
Isaac did not know him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau's hands. So Isaac blessed him.
Isaac said, "Are you really my son Esau?" Jacob said, "I am."
Isaac said, "My son, bring me some of the food you hunted to eat. Then I will bless you." Jacob brought it to him, and Isaac ate. Jacob also brought him wine, and Isaac drank.
Then Isaac said, "Come here, my son, and kiss me."
Jacob went to him and kissed him. Isaac smelled his clothes. Then Isaac blessed him. He said, "Ah, my son smells like a field that the LORD has blessed."
"May God give you dew from heaven and good things from the earth. May you have lots of grain and new wine."
"May countries serve you. May people bow down to you. Be the boss over your brothers. May your mother's sons bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed. May those who bless you be blessed."
After Isaac finished blessing Jacob, Jacob had just left. Then his brother Esau came in from hunting.
Esau also cooked a tasty meal. He brought it to his father. He said, "My father, please sit up. Eat some of the food I hunted. Then you can bless me."
Isaac said, "Who are you?" Esau said, "I am your son. I am your first son, Esau."
Isaac shook hard. He was very scared. He said, "Then who hunted the animal and brought it to me? I ate it before you came. I blessed him. He will stay blessed!"
When Esau heard his father's words, he cried out loud. It was a big, bitter cry. He said to his father, "Bless me too, my father!"
Isaac said, "Your brother came by tricking me. He took your blessing."
Esau said, "He is named Jacob for a reason. He has tricked me two times. He took my rights as the first son. Now he has taken my blessing." Then Esau said, "Have you not saved any blessing for me?"
Isaac said to Esau, "I made him boss over you. I gave all his relatives to him as servants. I gave him grain and new wine. So what can I do for you, my son?"
Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, my father!" Then Esau cried loudly.
Isaac said to him, "Your home will be away from the good things of the earth. Your home will be away from the dew of heaven above.
You will live by your sword. You will serve your brother. But when you get restless, you will break free from his control."
Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing his father gave him. Esau said to himself, "My father will die soon. Then I will kill my brother Jacob."
