Someone told Rebekah what her older son Esau had said. She sent for her younger son Jacob. She said to him, "Your brother Esau plans to kill you. He wants to get even with you.
Now, my son, do what I say. Run away fast to my brother Laban in Haran.
Stay with him for a while. Stay until your brother's anger goes away.
When your brother is not angry with you anymore, and he forgets what you did to him, I will send for you. I will bring you back. Why should I lose both of you in one day?"
Rebekah said to Isaac, "I am tired of living because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a wife from these women here, from these Hittite women, my life will not be worth living."
Isaac called Jacob and blessed him. He said, "Do not marry a woman from Canaan.
Go to Paddan Aram. Go to your mother's father Bethuel's house. Marry one of Laban's daughters. Laban is your mother's brother.
May God Almighty bless you. May He make you grow and have many children. May you become a big group of people.
May He give you Abraham's blessing. May it be for you and your children. Then you can take the land where you live. God gave that land to Abraham."
Isaac sent Jacob away. Jacob went to Paddan Aram, to Laban. Laban was Bethuel's son. Bethuel was an Aramean. Laban was the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan Aram to find a wife. Isaac had told Jacob not to marry a woman from Canaan.
Jacob listened to his father and mother. Then he went to Paddan Aram.
Esau saw that his father did not like the Canaanite women.
So Esau went to Ishmael. He married Mahalath. She was Ishmael's daughter. Ishmael was Abraham's son. Mahalath was the sister of Nebaioth. This was besides Esau's other wives.
Jacob left Beersheba and went toward Haran.
He came to a place and stayed there for the night, because the sun had gone down. He took a stone from that place. He put it under his head. Then he lay down to sleep.
He dreamed. He saw a ladder standing on the ground. Its top reached up to heaven. God's angels were going up and down on it.
The LORD stood above the ladder. He said, "I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your children the land you are lying on.
Your children will be like the dust of the earth. You will spread out to the west, east, north, and south. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your children.
I am with you. I will keep you safe wherever you go. I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I promised you."
Jacob woke up from his sleep. He said, "The LORD is in this place, and I did not know it!"
He was afraid. He said, "This place is so great and scary! This is God's house. This is the gate of heaven."
Early in the morning, Jacob got up. He took the stone he had put under his head. He set it up like a pillar. He poured oil on top of it.
He called that place Bethel. Before that, the town was called Luz.
Jacob made a promise. He said, "If God will be with me and keep me safe on this trip, and give me food to eat and clothes to wear,
then I will come back safely to my father's house. The LORD will be my God.
This stone pillar will be God's house. I will give You a tenth of everything You give me."
Then Jacob went on his way. He came to the land of the people in the east.
He looked and saw a well in a field. Three flocks of sheep lay by it. The flocks drank from that well. The stone on the top of the well was big.
When all the flocks came together there, the men rolled the stone from the top of the well. They gave water to the sheep. Then they put the stone back.
Jacob said to them, “My brothers, where are you from?” They said, “We are from Haran.”
He asked, “Do you know Laban, Nahor's son?” They said, “We know him.”
He asked, “Is he well?” They said, “He is well. Look, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.”
Jacob said, “It is still early in the day. It is not time to bring the animals home. Give water to the sheep and take them to eat grass.”
They said, “We cannot, until all the flocks come together and they roll the stone from the well. Then we water the sheep.”
While he was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep. She took care of them.
When Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and Laban's sheep, he went near. He rolled the stone from the well and watered Laban's flock.
Jacob kissed Rachel and cried out loud.
Jacob told Rachel that he was Rebekah's son, her father's nephew. She ran and told her father.
When Laban heard about Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him. He hugged him and kissed him. He brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.
Laban said, “You are my own family.” Jacob stayed with him a month.
Laban said, “Just because you are my relative, should you work for me for free? Tell me what your pay should be.”
Laban had two daughters. The older one was Leah. The younger one was Rachel.
Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was pretty and had a nice shape.
Jacob loved Rachel. He said, “I will work for you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”
Laban said, “It is better that I give her to you than to another man. Stay with me.”
Jacob worked seven years for Rachel. They seemed like a few days to him because he loved her.
Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife. My time is finished, and I want to be with her.”
Laban gathered all the men of that place and made a feast.
In the evening he took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob. Jacob slept with her.
Laban gave his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maid.
In the morning Jacob saw it was Leah. He said to Laban, “What have you done to me? Did I not work for Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
Laban said, “In our place we do not give the younger daughter before the older one.”
Laban said, “Finish this week with her. Then we will give you Rachel too, if you work for me seven more years.”
Jacob did so. He finished the week with Leah. Then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maid.
Jacob slept with Rachel too. He loved Rachel more than Leah. He worked for Laban seven more years.
The LORD saw that Leah was not loved. He let her have children. But Rachel could not have children.
Leah had a son. She named him Reuben. She said, “The LORD has seen my trouble. Now my husband will love me.”
She had another son. She said, “The LORD heard that I was not loved, so He gave me this son too.” She named him Simeon.
She had another son. She said, “Now my husband will stay close to me, because I have had three sons for him.” She named him Levi.
She had another son. She said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” She named him Judah. Then she stopped having children.
Rachel saw that she had no children for Jacob. She was jealous of her sister. She said to Jacob, "Give me children, or I will die."
Jacob got angry with Rachel. He said, "I am not God. He kept you from having children."
Rachel said, "Here is my servant Bilhah. Sleep with her. She can have children for me. Then I can have a family through her."
So she gave Bilhah to Jacob as his wife. He slept with her.
Bilhah became pregnant. She had a son for Jacob.
Rachel said, "God has helped me. He heard my voice and gave me a son." So she named him Dan.
Bilhah became pregnant again. She had a second son for Jacob.
Rachel said, "I have fought hard with my sister, and I won." She named him Naphtali.
Leah saw that she had stopped having children. She took her servant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as his wife.
Zilpah had a son for Jacob.
Leah said, "What good luck!" She named him Gad.
Zilpah had a second son for Jacob.
Leah said, "I am happy! Women will call me happy." She named him Asher.
During wheat harvest, Reuben found mandrake plants in a field. He brought them to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."
Leah said, "You took my husband. Now you want my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel said, "Then he can sleep with you tonight for the mandrakes."
Jacob came from the field in the evening. Leah went out to meet him. She said, "You must sleep with me tonight. I paid for you with my son's mandrakes." So he slept with her that night.
God listened to Leah. She became pregnant and had a fifth son for Jacob.
Leah said, "God has given me my reward, because I gave my servant to my husband." She named him Issachar.
Leah became pregnant again. She had a sixth son for Jacob.
Leah said, "God has given me a good gift. Now my husband will honor me, because I have given him six sons." She named him Zebulun.
Later she had a daughter. She named her Dinah.
Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb.
She became pregnant and had a son. She said, "God has taken away my shame."
She named him Joseph. She said, "May the LORD add another son to me."
After Rachel had Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me away. Let me go to my home and my land.
Give me my wives and children. I worked for you for them. Let me go. You know how hard I worked for you."
Laban said, "If you are pleased with me, stay. I know the LORD has blessed me because of you."
He said, "Name your pay, and I will pay it."
Jacob said, "You know how I worked for you and how your animals have done while with me.
You had little before I came. Now you have much more. The LORD has blessed you because of me. But when can I take care of my own family?"
Laban said, "What should I give you?" Jacob said, "Don't give me anything. If you do this one thing for me, I will keep taking care of your flocks.
Let me go through all your flocks today. I will take every spotted and speckled sheep, every dark lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. That will be my pay.
In the future, you can check my honesty. Any goat that is not spotted or speckled, or any lamb that is not dark, if it is with me, you can say I stole it."
Laban said, "Good. Let it be as you say."
That day Laban took out the male goats that were streaked or spotted. He took all the speckled or spotted female goats, every one with white on it, and all the dark lambs. He gave them to his sons.
Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob. Jacob took care of the rest of the flocks.
Jacob took fresh branches from poplar, almond, and plane trees. He peeled white stripes in them, so the white inside showed.
He put the branches in the water troughs where the flocks came to drink. They mated when they came to drink.
The flocks mated in front of the branches. They had young that were streaked, speckled, and spotted.
Jacob set the young animals apart. He made the flocks face the streaked and dark animals in Laban's flocks. He kept his own flocks separate. He did not put them with Laban's flocks.
Whenever the strong animals were ready to mate, Jacob put the branches in the troughs in front of them. They mated near the branches.
But when the animals were weak, he did not put the branches there. So the weak young belonged to Laban, and the strong ones belonged to Jacob.
Jacob became very, very rich. He had large flocks, female and male servants, camels, and donkeys.
Now Jacob heard what Laban's sons said. They said, "Jacob took all that was our father's. From our father's things he got all this wealth."
Jacob saw Laban's face. It was not kind to him like before.
Then the LORD said to Jacob, "Go back to the land of your fathers and to your family. I will be with you."
So Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah. He called them to the field where his sheep were.
He said to them, 'I see your father's face. It is not kind to me like before. But my father's God has been with me.
You know I worked hard for your father.
Your father tricked me. He changed my pay ten times. But God did not let him hurt me.
If he said, "Your pay will be the spotted sheep," then all the sheep had spotted babies. If he said, "Your pay will be the striped sheep," then all the sheep had striped babies.
So God took your father's animals and gave them to me.
When the sheep were ready to have babies, I looked up and saw a dream. The male sheep that jumped on the flock were striped, spotted, and mixed colors.
God's Angel spoke to me in the dream. He said, "Jacob." I said, "Here I am."
He said, "Look up now. See, the male sheep that jump on the flock are striped, spotted, and mixed colors. I have seen what Laban is doing to you."
"I am the God of Bethel. You poured oil on the stone there. You made a promise to Me. Now get up. Leave this land. Go back to the land where you were born."'
Rachel and Leah answered, 'Do we still have any share in our father's house?
He treats us like strangers. He sold us. He also used up our money.
All the wealth God took from our father is ours and our children's. Now do what God told you.'
Jacob got up. He put his sons and wives on camels.
He took all his animals and things. These were things he had gotten in Padan Aram. He went to his father Isaac in Canaan.
Laban had gone to cut the wool from his sheep. Rachel stole the small gods that were her father's.
Jacob did not tell Laban he was running away. He hid it from Laban.
He ran away with all he had. He crossed the river. He went toward the hills of Gilead.
On the third day, someone told Laban that Jacob had run away.
Laban took his relatives and chased him for seven days. He caught up to him in the hills of Gilead.
But God came to Laban in a dream at night. God said, "Be careful. Do not say anything good or bad to Jacob."
Laban caught up to Jacob. Jacob had put up his tent in the hills. Laban and his relatives put up their tents there too.
Laban said to Jacob, 'What have you done? You tricked me. You took my daughters away like prisoners taken in war.
Why did you sneak away? Why did you not tell me? I would have sent you away happy, with songs, a drum, and a harp.
You did not let me kiss my sons and daughters. You did a foolish thing.
I could hurt you. But your father's God spoke to me last night. He said, "Be careful. Do not say anything good or bad to Jacob."
Now you have gone because you miss your father's home. But why did you steal my gods?'
Jacob answered, 'I was afraid. I thought you might take your daughters from me by force.
If you find your gods with anyone, that person will not live. Let our relatives see what is yours with me, and take it.' Jacob did not know Rachel had stolen them.
Laban went into Jacob's tent, Leah's tent, and the two servant girls' tents. He did not find the gods. He left Leah's tent and went into Rachel's tent.
Rachel had taken the small gods. She put them in a camel saddle. She sat on them. Laban searched the whole tent, but did not find them.
She said to her father, 'Do not be angry, sir. I cannot get up. I am having my monthly time.' He searched, but did not find the gods.
Jacob was angry. He argued with Laban. Jacob said, 'What did I do wrong? What is my sin? Why did you chase me so hard?
You searched all my things. What did you find that is yours? Put it here before our relatives. Let them decide between us.
I have been with you twenty years. Your sheep and goats did not lose their babies. I did not eat your male sheep.
I did not bring you animals killed by wild animals. I paid for the loss myself. You made me pay for anything stolen by day or night.
I worked in the hot sun by day and the cold at night. Sleep left my eyes.
I have been in your house twenty years. I worked fourteen years for your two daughters. I worked six years for your sheep. You changed my pay ten times.
If my father's God, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, you would have sent me away with nothing. God saw my hard work and my trouble. He told you to stop last night.'
Laban answered, 'These daughters are my daughters. These children are my children. These sheep are my sheep. All you see is mine. But what can I do today to my daughters or to their children?
So come. Let us make an agreement, you and I. Let it be a witness between us.'
Jacob took a stone and set it up as a marker.
Jacob said to his relatives, 'Gather stones.' They gathered stones and made a pile. They ate there by the pile.
Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha. Jacob called it Galeed.
Laban said, 'This pile is a witness between us today.' So it was called Galeed.
It was also called Mizpah, because he said, 'May the LORD watch between us when we are apart.'
'If you hurt my daughters, or take other wives besides my daughters, no one may be with us. See, God is a witness between us.'
Laban said, 'Here is this pile. Here is this marker I set up between us.
This pile is a witness. This marker is a witness. I will not go past this pile to you. You will not go past this pile and marker to me, to hurt each other.'
'The God of Abraham, the God of Nahor, and the God of their father will judge between us.' Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain. He called his relatives to eat bread. They ate bread and stayed all night on the mountain.
Early in the morning, Laban got up. He kissed his sons and daughters and blessed them. Then Laban left and went home.
Jacob went on his way. God's angels met him.
When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is God's camp!" He named that place Mahanaim.
Jacob sent messengers ahead to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, in Edom.
He told them, "Say this to my lord Esau: 'Your servant Jacob says, I have been staying with Laban, and I have stayed until now.
I have oxen, donkeys, sheep, and servants. I am sending this to tell my lord, to find favor in your eyes.'"
The messengers came back to Jacob. They said, "We went to your brother Esau. He is coming to meet you, and 400 men are with him."
Jacob was very afraid and upset. He split the people with him into two groups. He did the same with the flocks, herds, and camels.
He thought, "If Esau comes and attacks one group, the other group may get away."
Then Jacob prayed, "God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, the LORD, who said to me, 'Go back to your country and your family, and I will do good to you,'
I do not deserve all the kindness and truth You have shown Your servant. I crossed this Jordan with only my stick, and now I have become two groups.
Please save me from my brother, from Esau. I am afraid he will come and hurt me and the mothers with their children.
But You said, 'I will surely do good to you and make your children like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted.'"
He stayed there that night. He took from what he had a gift for his brother Esau.
It was 200 female goats and 20 male goats, 200 female sheep and 20 male sheep,
30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows and 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys and 10 male donkeys.
He put them into the hands of his servants, herd by herd. He said to his servants, "Go ahead of me. Leave space between one herd and the next."
He told the first servant, "When my brother Esau meets you and asks who you are, where you are going, and whose these are in front of you,
then you are to say, 'They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift sent to my lord Esau. And Jacob is behind us.'"
He also told the second, the third, and all who followed the herds, "Say the same thing to Esau when you meet him.
You are also to say, 'Your servant Jacob is behind us.' He thought, 'I will make his face happy with the gift going before me. After that I will see his face. Maybe he will be kind to me.'"
So the gift went on ahead of him, but he stayed that night in the camp.
During the night he got up. He took his two wives, his two female servants, and his eleven sons. He crossed the river at the Jabbok.
He took them and sent them across the stream. He also sent over all that he had.
Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
When the man saw that he could not win against him, he touched the socket of Jacob's hip. Jacob's hip was put out of joint as they wrestled.
Then the man said, "Let me go, for the dawn is coming." But Jacob said, "I will not let You go unless You bless me."
The man asked him, "What is your name?" He said, "Jacob."
Then he said, "Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, because you have fought with God and with men and have won."
Jacob asked, "Please tell me Your name." He said, "Why do you ask my name?" And he blessed him there.
So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, "I have seen God face to face, and my life was saved."
The sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
So to this day the people of Israel do not eat the tough cord on the hip socket, because he touched Jacob's hip socket.
Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming with 400 men.
He split the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two female servants. He put the servants and their children first. He put Leah and her children next. He put Rachel and Joseph last.
Jacob went ahead of them. He bowed to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
Esau ran to meet him. He hugged Jacob and kissed him. They both cried.
Esau looked up and saw the women and children. He asked, "Who are these with you?" Jacob said, "They are the children God gave your servant."
The female servants and their children came near and bowed down.
Leah and her children came near and bowed down. Then Joseph and Rachel came near and bowed down.
Esau asked, "What do you mean by all this group I met?" Jacob said, "I sent them so you would be pleased with me."
Esau said, "I have enough, my brother. Keep what you have."
Jacob said, "No, please. If I found favor in your eyes, please take this gift from my hand. I saw your face, and it was like seeing God's face, and you welcomed me.
Please take the gift I brought you, because God has been kind to me. I have everything I need." Jacob kept asking, and Esau took it.
Esau said, "Let us travel together. I will go ahead of you."
Jacob said, "My lord knows the children are young and weak. The sheep and cows have new babies. If they are pushed too hard in one day, all the animals will die.
Please let my lord go ahead of his servant. I will travel slowly with the children and animals until I come to my lord in Seir."
Esau said, "Let me leave some of my people with you." Jacob said, "Why? I only want to find favor in my lord's eyes."
That day Esau went back to Seir.
Jacob traveled to Succoth. He built a house and made shelters for his animals. That is why the place is called Succoth.
Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan. He set up his camp near the city.
He bought the piece of land where he had set up his tent. He bought it from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, for 100 pieces of silver.
There he built an altar and called it "God, the God of Israel."
Dinah was Jacob's daughter. Her mother was Leah. She went out to see the women who lived in that land.
Shechem was the son of Hamor the Hivite. He was the leader of that land. He saw Dinah. He took her and hurt her.
He cared for Dinah, Jacob's daughter. He loved the girl. He spoke kindly to her.
Shechem said to Hamor his father, “Get me this girl to be my wife.”
Jacob heard that Shechem had hurt his daughter Dinah. His sons were in the fields with the animals. Jacob waited quietly until they came home.
Hamor, Shechem's father, went to Jacob to talk with him.
Jacob's sons came home from the fields. They heard what had happened. They were very sad and angry. Shechem had done a terrible thing. He had hurt Jacob's daughter. Such a thing should not be done.
Hamor talked with them. He said, “My son Shechem loves your daughter. Please give her to him to be his wife.
Let our families join. Give us your daughters. Take our daughters for yourselves.
You can live with us. The land is open to you. Live here, trade here, and own land here.”
Shechem said to her father and brothers, “Please be kind to me. I will give you whatever you ask.
Ask for a big bride price and gifts. I will pay what you say. Just give me the girl to be my wife.”
Jacob's sons answered Shechem and Hamor with a trick. They did this because Shechem had hurt their sister Dinah.
They said, “We cannot give our sister to a man who is not circumcised. That would shame us.
We will agree only if you become like us. Every man among you must be circumcised.
Then we will give our daughters to you and take your daughters. We will live together and become one people.
But if you will not be circumcised, we will take our daughter and leave.”
Hamor and Shechem liked what they heard.
The young man did not wait. He did it right away because he liked Jacob's daughter. He was the most honored man in his father's house.
Hamor and Shechem went to the city gate. They spoke to the men of the city.
“These men are peaceful with us. Let them live and trade in our land. The land is big enough for all of us. Let us take their daughters as wives, and let us give our daughters to them.
But they will live with us and become one people only if every man among us is circumcised, like they are.
Their animals and things will be ours. Let us agree, and they will live with us.”
All the men at the city gate listened to Hamor and Shechem. Every man was circumcised.
On the third day, the men were sore. Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers and Jacob's sons, took their swords. They came into the city without fear. They killed every man.
They killed Hamor and Shechem with the sword. They took Dinah from Shechem's house and left.
Jacob's sons came to the dead men. They took things from the city because their sister had been hurt.
They took sheep, cows, and donkeys. They took what was in the city and in the fields.
They took all the wealth, the wives, and the children. They took everything in the houses.

Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble on me. You made me look bad to the people who live here, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I do not have many people. They may join together and attack me. Then I and my family will be destroyed.”
They said, “Should he treat our sister with no respect?”
God said to Jacob, "Get up. Go up to Bethel and stay there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you ran away from your brother Esau."
Then Jacob said to his family and to all who were with him, "Get rid of the false gods you have with you. Make yourselves clean. Change your clothes."
He said, "Let us get up and go up to Bethel. I will build an altar there to God. He is the God who answered me when I was in trouble. He has been with me everywhere I went."
So they gave Jacob all the false gods they had and the rings in their ears. Jacob hid them under the oak tree near Shechem.
They left there. God made the people in the nearby towns afraid, so no one chased Jacob's sons.
Jacob and all the people with him came to Luz, which is Bethel, in the land of Canaan.
There he built an altar. He called the place El Bethel, because God had shown Himself to him there when he ran away from his brother.
Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died. She was buried under the oak tree below Bethel. Jacob called the tree Allon Bacuth, which means "oak of weeping."
When Jacob came back from Paddan Aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
God said to him, "Your name is Jacob. You will not be called Jacob anymore. Your name will be Israel." So God called him Israel.
God said to him, "I am God Almighty. Have many children and grow in number. Nations and groups of nations will come from you. Kings will be born from your family.
The land I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to you. I will give this land to you and to your children after you."
Then God went up from Jacob in the place where He had spoken with him.
Jacob set up a stone pillar where God had spoken with him. He poured a drink offering and oil on it.
Jacob named the place Bethel, because God had spoken to him there.
They left Bethel. While they were still a long way from Ephrath, Rachel began to have her baby. She had a hard time giving birth.
While Rachel was having a hard time, the woman helping her said, "Do not be afraid. You will have another son."
As Rachel was dying, she named her son Ben-Oni. But his father named him Benjamin.
Rachel died and was buried on the road to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
Jacob set up a pillar over her grave. It is still called Rachel's tomb today.
Israel moved on and put his tent past Migdal Eder.
While Israel lived there, Reuben went and slept with Bilhah, his father's servant wife. Israel heard about it. Jacob had twelve sons.
The sons of Leah were Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant, were Dan and Naphtali.
The sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant, were Gad and Asher. These were Jacob's sons who were born to him in Paddan Aram.
Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron. Abraham and Isaac had lived there.
Isaac lived to be 180 years old.
Isaac was very old when he died. Esau and Jacob buried him.
These are the family lines of Esau. Esau is also called Edom.
Esau married women from Canaan. His wives were Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
and Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.
Adah had a son named Eliphaz for Esau. Basemath had a son named Reuel.
Oholibamah had three sons: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These sons of Esau were born in Canaan.
Esau took his wives, sons, daughters, and everyone in his house. He took his animals and all he had gained in Canaan. Then he went to another land away from his brother Jacob.
They had too many things to live close together. The land where they stayed could not hold them all because of their animals.
So Esau, who is also called Edom, settled in the hill country of Seir.
These are the family lines of Esau, the father of Edom, in the hill country of Seir.
These are the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz, the son of Esau and Adah; and Reuel, the son of Esau and Basemath.
The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
Timna lived with Eliphaz, Esau's son. She had a son named Amalek. These grandsons came through Adah, Esau's wife.
The sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These sons came from Basemath, Esau's wife.
The sons of Oholibamah, Esau's wife and daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon, were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
These were the leaders among Esau's sons. From Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn son, came leaders named Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Kenaz.
Leaders named Korah, Gatam, and Amalek also came from Eliphaz. These leaders of Eliphaz lived in Edom. They came from Adah, Esau's wife.
From Reuel came leaders named Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These leaders of Reuel lived in Edom. They came from Basemath, Esau's wife.
From Oholibamah, Esau's wife, came leaders named Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
These were the sons of Esau, who is also called Edom, and these were their leaders.
These were the sons of Seir the Horite, who lived in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These were the leaders of the Horites. They were sons of Seir in Edom.
The sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam. Lotan's sister was Timna.
The sons of Shobal were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
The sons of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah. This Anah found hot springs in the desert while he was taking care of his father Zibeon's donkeys.
The children of Anah were Dishon and Oholibamah, Anah's daughter.
The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
The sons of Dishan were Uz and Aran.
These were the leaders of the Horites: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These leaders of the Horites led in Seir.
These were the kings who ruled Edom before Israel had a king.
Bela son of Beor ruled Edom. His city was Dinhabah.
When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah ruled after him.
When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites ruled after him.
When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad ruled after him. Hadad defeated Midian in the field of Moab. His city was Avith.
When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah ruled after him.
When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the river ruled after him.
When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor ruled after him.
When Baal-hanan died, Hadar ruled after him. His city was Pau. His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.
These were the names of Esau's leaders, by their families and places: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
Magdiel, and Iram. These leaders of Edom lived in the places they owned. He is Esau, the father of Edom.
Jacob lived in the land where his father had stayed. It was the land of Canaan.

These are the family stories of Jacob. Joseph was 17 years old. He helped his brothers take care of the sheep. He was still a boy. He worked with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father's wives. Joseph told his father about the bad things his brothers did.
Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons. This was because Joseph was born when Israel was old. Israel made Joseph a special robe.
When his brothers saw that their father loved Joseph more than them, they hated him. They could not speak kindly to him.
Joseph had a dream. He told it to his brothers. They hated him even more.
Joseph said, "Please listen to the dream I had.
We were tying up bundles of grain in the field. My bundle stood up. Your bundles gathered around and bowed down to mine."
His brothers said, "Do you think you will be our king? Do you think you will rule over us?" They hated him even more because of his dreams and words.
Then Joseph had another dream. He told it to his brothers. He said, "Listen. I had another dream. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me."
He told it to his father too. His father scolded him. He said, "What is this dream? Will I and your mother and your brothers really bow down to you?"
His brothers were jealous of him. But his father kept thinking about it.
His brothers went to take care of their father's sheep in Shechem.
Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers are taking care of the sheep in Shechem. Come, I will send you to them." Joseph said, "I am ready."
Israel said, "Go and see how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and tell me." So he sent Joseph from the valley of Hebron. Joseph went to Shechem.
A man found Joseph. He was lost in the field. The man asked, "What are you looking for?"
Joseph said, "I am looking for my brothers. Please tell me where they are taking care of the sheep."
The man said, "They have moved from here. I heard them say, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers. He found them in Dothan.
They saw him from far away. Before he came near, they made a plan to kill him.
They said to each other, "Look, here comes the dreamer.
Come on, let's kill him and throw him into one of the pits. We will say a wild animal ate him. Then we will see what happens to his dreams."
Reuben heard this. He saved Joseph from them. He said, "Let's not kill him.
Throw him into this pit in the desert. But don't hurt him." Reuben said this so he could save Joseph and take him back to his father.
When Joseph came to his brothers, they took off his robe, the special robe he was wearing.
They took him and threw him into the pit. The pit was empty. There was no water in it.
Then they sat down to eat. They looked up and saw a group of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and perfume. They were going to Egypt.
Judah said to his brothers, "What good is it to kill our brother and hide his blood?
Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites. Let's not hurt him. He is our brother. He is one of us." His brothers listened.
Some Midianite traders passed by. They pulled Joseph out of the pit. They sold Joseph for twenty pieces of silver to the Ishmaelites. The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt.
Reuben came back to the pit. Joseph was not there. Reuben tore his clothes.
He went back to his brothers. He said, "The boy is gone! Where can I go now?"
They took Joseph's robe. They killed a goat. They dipped the robe in the blood.
They sent the special robe to their father. They said, "We found this. Is it your son's robe? Please look at it."
Jacob knew it was Joseph's robe. He said, "It is my son's robe! A wild animal has eaten him. Joseph has been torn apart."
Jacob tore his clothes. He put on sackcloth. He mourned for his son for many days.
All his sons and daughters came to comfort him. But he would not be comforted. He said, "I will go down to the grave mourning for my son." So Jacob wept for him.
The Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar. Potiphar was one of Pharaoh's officers. He was the captain of the guard.
At that time, Judah left his brothers. He went down to stay with a man named Hirah. Hirah was from Adullam.
There, Judah saw a Canaanite woman. Her father was named Shua. Judah married her and slept with her.
She became pregnant and had a son. Judah named him Er.
She became pregnant again and had another son. She named him Onan.
She had one more son. She named him Shelah. He was born in Chezib.
Judah found a wife for Er, his oldest son. Her name was Tamar.
Er was very bad in the the LORD's eyes. So the The LORD put him to death.
Judah said to Onan, "Go and sleep with your brother's wife. Be a husband to her. Have children for your brother."
Onan knew the children would not be his own. So when he slept with his brother's wife, he made sure she did not get pregnant. He did not want to give children to his brother.
What Onan did was bad in the the LORD's eyes. So the The LORD put him to death too.

Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, "Live as a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up." He was afraid Shelah might die too, like his brothers. So Tamar went home and lived with her father.

After a long time, Judah's wife died. She was the daughter of Shua. Judah was comforted. Then he went up to Timnah with his friend Hirah from Adullam. They went to see the men cutting wool from his sheep.
Someone told Tamar, "Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to cut wool from his sheep."

Tamar took off her widow's clothes. She put on a veil and covered her face. Then she sat by the road at Enaim, on the way to Timnah. She did this because she saw that Shelah was grown, but Judah had not given her to him as a wife.
Judah saw her. He thought she was a prostitute, because she had covered her face.
Judah turned to her by the road and said, "Come, let me sleep with you." He did not know she was his daughter-in-law. She said, "What will you give me to sleep with me?"
Judah said, "I will send you a young goat from my flock." She said, "Will you give me something to keep until you send it?"
He said, "What should I give you?" She said, "Give me your seal, your cord, and the staff in your hand." He gave them to her. Then he slept with her, and she became pregnant.
Tamar got up and left. She took off her veil and put on her widow's clothes again.
Judah sent the young goat by his friend from Adullam. He wanted to get his things back from the woman. But he could not find her.
He asked the men who lived there, "Where is the prostitute who was by the road at Enaim?" They said, "No prostitute has been here."
He went back to Judah and said, "I could not find her. The men who live there said no prostitute has been there."
Judah said, "Let her keep the things. We do not want to be ashamed. I sent this goat, but you did not find her."
About three months later, someone told Judah, "Your daughter-in-law Tamar has been a prostitute. She is pregnant." Judah said, "Bring her out. Burn her!"
As she was being brought out, Tamar sent a message to her father-in-law. She said, "I am pregnant by the man who owns these things. Please see whose seal, cord, and staff these are."
Judah knew them. He said, "She is more right than I am. I did not give her to my son Shelah." He did not sleep with her again.
When it was time for her to have her babies, there were twins in her body.
While she was giving birth, one baby put out his hand. The woman helping her took a red thread and tied it on his hand. She said, "This one came out first."
But he pulled his hand back. Then his brother came out. The woman said, "You broke out!" So he was named Perez.
Then his brother came out. He had the red thread on his hand. He was named Zerah.

Joseph was taken down to Egypt. An Egyptian named Potiphar bought him. Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh and the captain of the guard. He bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites who had brought him there.
The LORD was with Joseph. Joseph became a successful man. He served in the house of his Egyptian master.
His master saw that the LORD was with Joseph. He also saw that the LORD made everything Joseph did turn out well.
Joseph found favor with his master. So his master made him his helper. Then he put Joseph in charge of his whole house. He gave Joseph control of everything he owned.

From the time Joseph was put in charge of the house and everything in it, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house because of Joseph. The LORD's blessing was on everything the Egyptian owned, both inside the house and out in the fields.
So the master left everything he owned in Joseph's care. He did not worry about anything except the food he ate. Joseph was very handsome.
After this, his master's wife looked at Joseph. She said, "Come to bed with me."
But Joseph refused. He said to his master's wife, "See, my master does not know what is in the house. He has put everything he has in my care.
No one in this house is more important than I am. He has not kept anything from me except you, because you are his wife. How could I do such an evil thing? It would be a great sin against God."
She kept asking Joseph day after day. But he would not listen to her. He would not sleep with her or even stay near her.
One day Joseph went into the house to do his work. None of the other men were in the house.
She grabbed his coat and said, "Come to bed with me." But Joseph left his coat in her hand. He ran away and went outside.
When she saw that he had left his coat in her hand and run outside,
she called the men of the house and said, "Look! My husband brought this Hebrew man here to make fun of us. He came in to sleep with me, but I screamed loudly.
When he heard me scream, he left his coat beside me and ran outside."
She kept his coat with her until his master came home.
Then she told her husband the same story. She said, "The Hebrew servant you brought us came in to make fun of me.
When I screamed, he left his coat beside me and ran outside."
When her husband heard what she said, "Your servant did this to me," he became angry.
So his master took Joseph and put him in prison. It was the place where the king's prisoners were kept. Joseph stayed there.
But the LORD was with Joseph. He showed Joseph kindness. He also caused the prison guard to like Joseph.
The prison guard put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners. Everything they did there was done under Joseph's care.
The prison guard did not check on anything Joseph was in charge of. This was because the LORD was with Joseph. The LORD made everything Joseph did turn out well.
After this, the king of Egypt's cupbearer and baker did wrong to their master, the king of Egypt.
The king of Egypt was angry with two of his helpers. He was angry with the head cupbearer and the head baker.
He put them in jail. It was in the house of the guard captain. It was the same jail where Joseph was held.
The guard captain put Joseph in charge of them. Joseph took care of them. They stayed in jail for a while.
The king's cupbearer and baker were in jail. One night, each man had a dream. Each dream had its own meaning.
In the morning, Joseph came to them. He saw they looked sad.
He asked the king's helpers who were in jail with him, "Why do you look so sad today?"
They said, "We had dreams, but no one can tell us what they mean." Joseph said, "Only God can tell what dreams mean. Please tell me your dreams."
The head cupbearer told Joseph his dream. He said, "In my dream, I saw a grapevine in front of me.
The vine had three branches. It seemed to bud and bloom. Then its clusters made ripe grapes.
Pharaoh's cup was in my hand. I took the grapes. I squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup. Then I put the cup in Pharaoh's hand."
Joseph said, "Here is what it means. The three branches are three days.
In three more days, Pharaoh will give you your job back. You will put Pharaoh's cup in his hand, like you did before.
But when things go well for you, please remember me. Be kind to me. Tell Pharaoh about me. Get me out of this place.
I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews. I have done nothing wrong here. But they put me in this prison."
The head baker saw that the meaning was good. He said to Joseph, "I also had a dream. In my dream, I had three baskets of bread on my head.
The top basket had all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh. But birds came and ate the food from the basket on my head."
Joseph said, "Here is what it means. The three baskets are three days.
In three days, Pharaoh will put you to death. He will hang you on a tree. Birds will eat your body."
Three days later was Pharaoh's birthday. He made a feast for all his servants. He brought out the head cupbearer and the head baker in front of them.
He gave the head cupbearer his job back. He put the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
But he hanged the head baker, just as Joseph had said.
The head cupbearer did not remember Joseph. He forgot him.
Two full years passed. Then Pharaoh dreamed he was standing by the Nile River.
Seven cows came up out of the Nile. They looked good and were fat. They ate grass by the river.
After them, seven other cows came up. They looked bad and were thin. They stood by the first cows on the riverbank.
The bad thin cows ate the seven good fat cows. Then Pharaoh woke up.
He went back to sleep and dreamed again. Seven heads of grain grew on one stalk. They were full and good.
After them, seven more heads grew. They were thin and dried by the east wind.
The thin heads swallowed the seven full good heads. Pharaoh woke up. It was a dream.
In the morning, Pharaoh was upset. He sent for all of Egypt's magic men and wise men. He told them his dreams. No one could explain them to Pharaoh.
Then the chief drink server said to Pharaoh, "Today I remember my sins.
Pharaoh was angry with his servants. He put me and the chief baker in prison. The prison was in the house of the captain of the guard.
One night we both dreamed. Each of us had a dream with its own meaning.
A young Hebrew man was there with us. He was a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams. He explained them to us. He told each man what his dream meant.
Things happened just as he said. Pharaoh put me back in my job, and he hanged the baker."
Pharaoh sent for Joseph. They rushed him out of the prison. He shaved and changed his clothes. Then he came to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I had a dream. No one can explain it. I heard that you can hear a dream and explain it."
Joseph answered Pharaoh, "It is not me. God will give Pharaoh a good answer."
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "In my dream I stood on the bank of the Nile.
Seven cows came up. They were fat and good-looking. They ate grass by the river.
After them, seven other cows came up. They were very ugly and thin. I have never seen such bad cows in all Egypt.
The thin ugly cows ate the seven fat cows that came up first.
But when they had eaten them, no one could tell. They still looked as thin as before. Then I woke up.
I also dreamed. Seven heads of grain grew on one stalk. They were full and good.
After them, seven more heads grew. They were thin and dried by the east wind.
The thin heads swallowed the seven good heads. I told this to the magic men, but no one could explain it to me."
Joseph said to Pharaoh, "Pharaoh's dreams are one dream. God has shown Pharaoh what He is going to do.
The seven good cows are seven years. The seven good heads are seven years. It is one dream.
The seven thin ugly cows that came up after them are seven years. The seven thin heads dried by the east wind are seven years of hunger.
This is what I told Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what He is going to do.
Seven years with lots of food are coming in all Egypt.
After them, seven years of hunger will come. All the extra food in Egypt will be forgotten. Hunger will ruin the land.
The extra food will not be remembered. The hunger after it will be so bad.
The dream came twice to Pharaoh because God has decided it. He will do it soon.
Now Pharaoh should look for a wise and understanding man. Put him in charge of Egypt.
Pharaoh should choose leaders over the land. Take one-fifth of Egypt's food during the seven good years.
They should gather all the good food that is coming. Store grain under Pharaoh's care. Keep food in the cities.
That food will be stored for the land for the seven years of hunger. Then Egypt will not be ruined by hunger."
The plan sounded good to Pharaoh and all his servants.
Pharaoh said to his servants, "Can we find a man like this? He has God's Spirit in him."
Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has shown you all this, no one is as wise and understanding as you.
You will be over my house. All my people will obey you. Only the throne will be greater than you.
See, I have put you over all Egypt."
Pharaoh took his signet ring from his hand. He put it on Joseph's hand. He dressed Joseph in fine linen clothes. He put a gold chain around his neck.
He had Joseph ride in his second chariot. Men called out before him, "Bow down!" He put him over all Egypt.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh. No one in all Egypt may lift a hand or foot without your permission."
Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as his wife. Joseph went out over Egypt.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from Pharaoh. He traveled through all Egypt.
During the seven good years, the land made lots of food.
Joseph gathered all the food in Egypt for seven years. He put food in the cities. He stored the food from the fields around each city in that city.
Joseph stored so much grain that it was like sand by the sea. He stopped counting it because there was too much.
Before the years of hunger came, Joseph had two sons with Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On.
Joseph named his first son Manasseh. He said, "God made me forget all my hard work and all my father's house."
He named his second son Ephraim. He said, "God made me do well in the land where I suffered."
The seven good years in Egypt ended.
The seven years of hunger began, just as Joseph had said. There was hunger in all lands. But in Egypt there was bread.
All Egypt was hungry. The people cried to Pharaoh for food. Pharaoh said to all Egypt, "Go to Joseph. Do what he says."
The hunger was over all the earth. Joseph opened all the storehouses. He sold grain to Egypt. The hunger got worse in Egypt.
People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the hunger was bad everywhere.
Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt. He said to his sons, "Why are you staring at each other?
I heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us. Then we can live and not die."
So ten of Joseph's brothers went down to buy grain in Egypt.
But Jacob did not send Joseph's brother Benjamin with them. He was afraid something bad might happen to him.
Israel's sons came with the others to buy grain, because there was no food in Canaan.
Joseph was the boss of the land. He sold grain to all the people. Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to him. Their faces touched the ground.
Joseph saw his brothers and knew them. But he acted like a stranger to them. He spoke harshly to them. He asked, "Where are you from?" They said, "From Canaan. We came to buy food."
Joseph knew his brothers, but they did not know him.
Joseph remembered the dreams he had about them. He said to them, "You are spies. You came to see the weak parts of our land."
They said, "No, my lord. Your servants came to buy food.
We are all sons of one man. Your servants are honest men. We are not spies."
He said, "No. You came to see the weak parts of our land."
They said, "Your servants are twelve brothers. We are sons of one man in Canaan. The youngest is with our father today. One brother is gone."
Joseph said, "I told you. You are spies.
I will test you this way. As Pharaoh lives, you will not leave here unless your youngest brother comes here.
Send one of you to get your brother. The rest will stay locked up. Then I will test your words. If they are not true, then, as Pharaoh lives, you are spies."
He put them in prison for three days.
On the third day, Joseph said to them, "Do this and live. I fear God.
If you are honest, let one brother stay in prison. The rest can go take grain home for your hungry families.
Bring your youngest brother to me. Then your words will be proven true, and you will not die." They did what he said.
They said to each other, "We are guilty about our brother. We saw how sad he was when he begged us, but we did not listen. That is why this trouble came to us."
Reuben said, "Did I not tell you not to hurt the boy? You did not listen. Now we must answer for his blood."
They did not know Joseph understood them. A man was translating for them.
Joseph turned away and cried. Then he came back and spoke to them. He took Simeon from them and tied him up while they watched.
Joseph told his men to fill their bags with grain. He also told them to put each man's money back in his sack. And he told them to give them food for the trip. They did so.
The brothers loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
At the place where they stopped for the night, one brother opened his sack to feed his donkey. He saw his money at the top of the sack.
He said to his brothers, "My money has been put back! Look, it is in my sack." Their hearts sank. They were afraid. They said to each other, "What has God done to us?"
They came to their father Jacob in Canaan. They told him everything that happened.
They said, "The man who is boss of that land spoke harshly to us. He treated us like spies.
We said, 'We are honest men, not spies.'
We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One brother is gone. The youngest is with our father in Canaan."
The man who is boss of that land said, "This is how I will know you are honest. Leave one brother with me. Take grain for your homes and go.
Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know you are not spies but honest. I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in that land."
As they emptied their sacks, each man found his bundle of money in his sack. They and their father saw the money bundles, and they were afraid.
Their father Jacob said, "You have taken my children from me. Joseph is gone. Simeon is gone. Now you want Benjamin too. Everything is against me."
Reuben said to his father, "You may kill my two sons if I do not bring him back. Put him in my care. I will bring him back to you."

Jacob said, "My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he is the only one left. If something bad happens on the trip you take, you will bring my gray head down to the grave in sorrow."
The famine was very bad in the land.
When the grain they had brought from Egypt was gone, their father said to them, "Go back and buy us a little more food."
Judah said to him, "The man warned us that we could not see his face unless our brother came with us.
If you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
But if you will not send him, we will not go down, because the man said we could not see his face unless our brother came with us."
Israel said, "Why did you treat me so badly by telling the man you have another brother?"

They said, "The man asked us about ourselves and our family. He asked if our father was still alive and if we had another brother. We told him what he asked. How could we know he would tell us to bring our brother down?"
Judah said to Israel his father, "Send the boy with me. We will go now. Then we will live and not die. We, you, and our children will all live.
I will be responsible for him. You can hold me to it. If I do not bring him back to you and show him to you, I will be to blame as long as I live.
If we had not waited, we could have gone and come back twice by now."

Their father Israel said to them, "If it must be so, then do this: Take some of the best things of the land in your bags. Carry down a gift to the man: a little balm, a little honey, spices, myrrh, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
Take twice as much money with you. Carry back the money that was put back in your sacks. Maybe it was a mistake.
Take your brother too. Go back to the man.
May God Almighty show you mercy before the man, so he sends your other brother and Benjamin back. As for me, if I lose them, I lose them."
So the men took the gift and twice as much money. They took Benjamin too. They went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the man over his house, "Bring the men into the house. Kill an animal and make it ready, because the men will eat with me at noon."
The man did as Joseph said. He brought the men to Joseph's house.

The men were afraid because they were brought into Joseph's house. They said, "We are brought in because of the money that was put back in our sacks the first time. He wants to blame us, attack us, and make us slaves, along with our donkeys."
They went up to the man who was over Joseph's house and spoke to him at the door of the house.
They said, "Please, sir, we came down the first time to buy food.
When we reached the place where we stayed, we opened our sacks. Each man's money was in his sack, all of it. We brought it back with us.
We also brought more money to buy food. We do not know who put our money in our sacks."
He said, "Peace to you. Do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasure in your sacks. I got your money." Then he brought Simeon out to them.
The man brought the men into Joseph's house. He gave them water to wash their feet and gave food to their donkeys.
They got the gift ready for Joseph to come at noon, because they heard they would eat there.
When Joseph came home, they brought him the gift in the house and bowed down to him on the ground.
He asked how they were. He said, "Is your old father well, the one you told me about? Is he still alive?"
They said, "Our father, your servant, is well. He is still alive." Then they bowed down.
He looked up and saw Benjamin, his mother's son. He said, "Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?" Then he said, "May God be kind to you, my son."
Joseph hurried away because he felt deep love for his brother. He looked for a place to cry. He went into his room and cried there.
Then he washed his face and came out. He got control of himself and said, "Serve the food."
They served Joseph by himself. They served his brothers by themselves. The Egyptians who ate with him sat by themselves. Egyptians will not eat with Hebrews. They think it is wrong.
They sat before him, the oldest first and the youngest last. The men were surprised.
He sent food to them from his table. But Benjamin got five times as much as any of them. They ate and drank and were happy with him.
Joseph told the man in charge of his house, "Fill the men's bags with food. Give them as much as they can carry. Put each man's money back in his bag.
Put my silver cup in the youngest brother's bag. Put his money for grain there too." The man did what Joseph said.
When morning came, the men were sent away with their donkeys.
They had not gone far from the city. Joseph said to the man in charge of his house, "Go after the men. Catch up to them. Say, 'Why did you pay back good with bad?
Isn't this the cup my master drinks from? He uses it to tell what will happen. You did a bad thing.'"
The man caught up to them and said these words to them.
They said to him, "Why does my lord say these things? We would never do such a thing.
We brought money back from Canaan. How could we steal silver or gold from your lord's house?
If the cup is found with any of us, that one will die. The rest of us will be your lord's slaves."
The man said, "Let it be as you say. The one who has the cup will be my slave. The rest of you can go free."
Each man quickly put his bag on the ground and opened it.
The man searched. He started with the oldest brother and ended with the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin's bag.
They tore their clothes. Each man loaded his donkey. They went back to the city.
Judah and his brothers went to Joseph's house. Joseph was still there. They fell to the ground in front of him.
Joseph said to them, "What is this you have done? Don't you know a man like me can find things out?"
Judah said, "What can we say to my lord? How can we prove we are right? God has found out our sin. We are all your slaves now. So is the one with the cup."
Joseph said, "No! Only the man with the cup will be my slave. The rest of you can go home in peace to your father."
Judah came close to him. He said, "Please, my lord, let your servant speak. Don't be angry with your servant. You are like Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'
We said to my lord, 'We have an old father. He has a young son. His brother died. This young son is the only child left from that mother. His father loves him.'
You said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me. I want to see him.'"
"We said to my lord, 'The boy cannot leave his father. If he leaves his father, his father will die.'
But you said to your servants, 'If your youngest brother does not come with you, you will not see my face again.'
When we went back to your servant, our father, we told him what my lord said.
Our father said, 'Go back and buy a little food for us.'
We said, 'We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, we will go. We cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.'"
"Your servant, our father, said to us, 'You know that my wife gave me two sons.
One son left me. I said he was surely torn apart. I have not seen him since.
If you take this one from me too, and something bad happens to him, I will die in sorrow.'
Now, if I go back to your servant, our father, and the boy is not with us, his life is tied to the boy's life.
When he sees the boy is not with us, he will die. Your servants will make our father die in sorrow.
I promised my father I would keep the boy safe. I said I would be guilty before my father all my life if I did not bring him back.
Now let me stay here as your slave instead of the boy. Let the boy go home with his brothers.
How can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I do not want to see the trouble that would come to my father."
Joseph could not control himself in front of all the people standing there. He called out, “Make everyone leave!” No one stayed with him when he told his brothers who he was.
He cried so loud that the Egyptians heard it. Pharaoh’s house heard it too.
Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” His brothers could not answer him. They were too scared.
Joseph said, “Come close to me.” They came close. “I am Joseph, your brother,” he said. “You sold me to Egypt.”
“Now do not be upset. Do not be angry with yourselves because you sold me here. God sent me ahead of you to save lives.”
“There has been no food in the land for two years. There are still five years with no planting or harvest.”
“God sent me ahead of you to keep your family alive on earth. He saved many lives in a big way.”
“So it was not you who sent me here. It was God. He made me like a father to Pharaoh. I am the boss of his whole house. I rule all of Egypt.”
“Hurry and go to my father. Tell him, ‘Your son Joseph says God made him boss of all Egypt. Come down to me. Do not wait.’”
“You will live in Goshen. You will be near me. You, your children, your grandchildren, your sheep, your cows, and all you own.”
“I will take care of you there. There are still five years with no food. I do not want you, your family, and all you own to have nothing.”
“You can see with your own eyes. My brother Benjamin can see too. I am the one talking to you.”
“Tell my father about all my good things in Egypt. Tell him all you have seen. Bring my father here fast.”
Then Joseph threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and cried. Benjamin cried too.
Joseph kissed all his brothers and cried over them. After that, his brothers talked with him.
The news reached Pharaoh’s house that Joseph’s brothers had come. Pharaoh and all his servants were happy.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers to do this: Load your animals and go back to Canaan.”
“Then bring your father and your families. Come to me. I will give you the best land in Egypt. You will eat the best food in the land.”
“You must also tell them, ‘Take wagons from Egypt for your little ones and your wives. Bring your father and come.’”
“Do not worry about your things. The best of all Egypt is yours.”
So Israel’s sons did as they were told. Joseph gave them wagons, just as Pharaoh had said. He gave them food for the trip.
He gave new clothes to each of them. But he gave Benjamin 300 pieces of silver and five sets of clothes.
He sent this to his father: ten donkeys carrying the best things from Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and food for the trip.
He sent his brothers away and said, “Do not fight on the way.”
They went up from Egypt and came to their father Jacob in Canaan.
They told him, “Joseph is still alive! He rules all of Egypt!” Jacob felt weak because he did not believe them.
But when they told him all that Joseph had said, and when he saw the wagons Joseph sent to carry him, Jacob felt better.
Then Israel said, “My son Joseph is still alive! I will go see him before I die.”
Israel and everyone with him traveled to Beersheba. There he gave gifts to God, the God of his father Isaac.
That night, God spoke to Israel in a dream. He said, "Jacob! Jacob!" Jacob answered, "Here I am."
God said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt. I will make you into a great nation there.
I will go down with you to Egypt. I will also bring you back again. Joseph will close your eyes."
Jacob left Beersheba. The sons of Israel took their father Jacob, the children, and the wives in the carts Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
They took their animals and the things they had gained in Canaan. Jacob and all his family went to Egypt.
He brought his sons, his grandsons, his daughters, and his granddaughters. He brought all his family with him to Egypt.
These are the names of Israel's sons and their families who came to Egypt. Reuben was Jacob's firstborn son.
Reuben's sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Simeon's sons were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul. Shaul's mother was a Canaanite woman.
Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Judah's sons were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Er and Onan died in Canaan. Perez's sons were Hezron and Hamul.
Issachar's sons were Tola, Puva, Job, and Shimron.
Zebulun's sons were Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These were the sons Leah had with Jacob in Paddan Aram. She also had a daughter named Dinah. All of Leah's sons and daughters made 33 people.
Gad's sons were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah. Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel.
These were the children of Zilpah. Laban gave Zilpah to his daughter Leah. Zilpah had 16 children for Jacob.
Rachel's children were Joseph and Benjamin.
In Egypt, Joseph had two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. Their mother was Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On.
Benjamin's sons were Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
Rachel had 14 children and grandchildren for Jacob.
Naphtali's sons were Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These were the children of Bilhah. Laban gave Bilhah to his daughter Rachel. Bilhah had 7 children for Jacob.
All of Jacob's direct family who came to Egypt were 66 people. This does not count his sons' wives.
With Joseph's two sons born in Egypt, Jacob's whole family in Egypt was 70 people.
Jacob sent Judah ahead to Joseph to show the way to Goshen. They came to Goshen.
Joseph got his chariot ready. He went to Goshen to meet his father Israel. He hugged him and cried on his neck for a long time.
Israel said to Joseph, "Now I can die happy. I have seen your face, and you are still alive."
Joseph said to his brothers and father, "I will go to Pharaoh and tell him, 'My brothers and my father's family from Canaan have come to me.
The men are shepherds. They care for animals. They brought their sheep, cattle, and all they own.
When Pharaoh calls you, he will ask, 'What is your work?'
You must say, 'Your servants have cared for animals since we were young, just like our fathers did.' Then you can live in Goshen, because Egyptians do not like shepherds."
Joseph went to Pharaoh and said, "My father and brothers came from Canaan with their sheep and cows and everything they own. They are now in Goshen."
He picked five of his brothers and brought them to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh asked his brothers, "What work do you do?" They said, "Your servants take care of sheep. We and our fathers have always done this."

Pharaoh will think the people of Israel are lost. He will think the desert has trapped them.
I will make Pharaoh's heart hard. He will chase them. I will show My glory through Pharaoh and all his army. Then the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD." And the people did as they were told.

Someone told the king of Egypt that the people had run away. Then Pharaoh and his servants changed their minds. They said, "What have we done? We let Israel go. They do not have to work for us anymore."
Pharaoh got his chariot ready. He took his army with him.
He took 600 of his best chariots. He took all the chariots of Egypt. Officers rode in each one.
The LORD made Pharaoh's heart hard. The king of Egypt chased the people of Israel. The people of Israel left proudly.

The Egyptians chased them. They had horses, chariots, and men on horses. They had a big army. They caught up with the Israelites. The Israelites were camped by the sea near Pi Hahiroth, in front of Baal Zephon.
Pharaoh came close. The people of Israel looked up. They saw the Egyptians coming after them. They were very afraid. They cried out to the LORD.
They said to Moses, "Are there no graves in Egypt? Did you bring us here to die in the desert? Why did you do this to us? Why did you bring us out of Egypt?
Didn't we tell you in Egypt to leave us alone so we could serve the Egyptians? It is better to serve the Egyptians than to die in the desert."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. Stand still. See how the LORD will save you today. Today you see the Egyptians. Never again will you see them.
The LORD will fight for you. Be quiet."
The LORD said to Moses, "Why are you crying to Me? Tell the people of Israel to move on.
Lift up your staff. Stretch out your hand over the sea. Split the sea open. Then the people of Israel can walk through the sea on dry ground.
I will make the hearts of the Egyptians hard. They will follow the people of Israel. I will show My glory through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.
Then the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD."
The angel of God had been going in front of the camp of Israel. Now he moved and went behind them. The pillar of cloud moved from in front of them and stood behind them.
It stood between the Egyptian camp and the Israelite camp. The cloud brought darkness to the Egyptians. It gave light to the Israelites. The two groups did not come near each other all night.
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The LORD pushed the sea back with a strong east wind all night. He made the sea dry land. The water split apart.
The people of Israel walked through the sea on dry ground. The water stood like a wall on their right and on their left.
All of Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and men on horses followed them into the sea.
Before dawn, the LORD looked down from the pillar of fire and cloud at the Egyptian camp. He made the camp panic. He took the wheels off their chariots. He made the chariots hard to drive.
The Egyptians said, "Let us run away from Israel! The LORD is fighting for them against us!"
The LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea. The water will come back over the Egyptians, their chariots, and their horsemen."
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. At daybreak, the sea went back to its normal place. The Egyptians tried to run from it. But the LORD threw them into the sea.
The water came back. It covered the chariots, the horsemen, and all of Pharaoh's army that had followed them into the sea. Not one of them was left.
The people of Israel had walked through the sea on dry ground. The water had stood like a wall on their right and on their left.
That day the LORD saved Israel from the Egyptians. Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore.
Israel saw the great thing the LORD had done in Egypt. The people feared the LORD. They believed in the LORD and in Moses, His servant.
Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD. They said, "I will sing to the LORD, because He is great and strong. He threw the horse and rider into the sea.
The LORD is my strength and my song. He saved me. This is my God, and I will praise Him. He is my father's God, and I will lift Him up.
The LORD fights in war. The LORD is His name. "
Pharaoh's war carts and his army, He threw into the sea. His best captains sank in the Red Sea.
Deep water covered them. They sank to the bottom like a stone.
Your right hand, the LORD, is strong and great. Your right hand, the LORD, breaks the enemy.
In Your great power, You knock down those who fight You. You send out Your anger, and it eats them up like dry grass.
With a strong breath from Your nose, the water piled up. The floods stood like a wall. The deep sea became solid in the middle of the sea. "
The enemy said, 'I will chase them. I will catch them. I will take their things. I will get what I want. I will pull out my sword. My hand will destroy them.'
You blew with Your wind. The sea covered them. They sank like lead in the deep water.
the LORD, which god is like You? Who is like You, great and holy? You are wonderful, and You do amazing things.
You reached out Your right hand. The ground swallowed them. "
In Your kind love, You led the people You saved. In Your strength, You guided them to Your holy home.
The nations heard and shook. Fear grabbed the people who live in Philistia.
The leaders of Edom were scared. The leaders of Moab shook with fear. All the people in Canaan melted away.
Great fear fell on them. By Your strong arm, they became as still as stone until Your people passed by, the LORD, until the people You bought passed by.
You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain You gave them. The LORD, You made a place for Your home, a holy place, the LORD, that Your hands made.
The LORD will rule forever and ever."
Pharaoh's horses, war carts, and men on horses went into the sea. The LORD brought the sea water back over them. But the people of Israel walked on dry ground in the middle of the sea.
Miriam, a woman prophet and Aaron's sister, took a drum in her hand. All the women went out after her with drums and dancing.
Miriam sang to them, "Sing to the LORD, because He is great and strong. He threw the horse and rider into the sea."
Moses led Israel away from the Red Sea. They went into the desert of Shur. They walked three days in the desert and found no water.
They came to Marah, but they could not drink the water there because it was bitter. That is why the place was called Marah.
The people complained to Moses. They said, "What will we drink?"
Moses cried out to the LORD. The LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the LORD made a rule and a law for them. There He tested them.

He said, "If you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and listen to His commands, and keep all His rules, I will not put on you any of the sicknesses I put on the Egyptians. I am the LORD who heals you."
They came to Elim. There were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They camped there by the water.
On the fifteenth day of the second month after they left Egypt, all the people of Israel traveled from Elim. They came to the Desert of Sin. It is between Elim and Sinai.
There in the desert, all the people of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron.
They said, "We wish the the LORD had killed us in Egypt! There we sat by pots of meat and ate all the bread we wanted. But you brought us out here to this desert to starve all of us to death!"

Then the the LORD said to Moses, "Look, I will make bread fall from the sky like rain for you. Each day the people will go out and gather enough for that day. This way I will test them. I will see if they follow My rules.
On the sixth day, they will get ready what they gather. It will be twice as much as they gather on other days."
So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, "Tonight you will know that the the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
In the morning you will see the glory of the the LORD, because He has heard your complaining against Him. Who are we, that you should complain against us?"

Moses also said, "When the the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread to fill you in the morning, it is because He has heard your complaining against Him. Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the the LORD."
Then Moses said to Aaron, "Tell all the people of Israel to come near to the the LORD, because He has heard your complaining."
When Aaron spoke to all the people, they looked toward the desert. There in a cloud, the glory of the the LORD appeared.
Then the the LORD spoke to Moses.
"I have heard the complaining of the Israelites. Tell them, 'In the evening you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be full of bread. Then you will know that I am the the LORD your God.'"
That evening, small birds called quail came and covered the camp. In the morning, dew was all around the camp.
When the dew dried up, thin flakes like frost were on the ground.
When the Israelites saw it, they asked each other, "What is it?" They did not know what it was. So Moses said to them, "It is the bread the the LORD has given you to eat."
Moses said, "This is what the the LORD has commanded: 'Each of you gather as much as you need. You may take an omer for each person in your tent.'"
The Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some gathered less.
When they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much had no extra. The one who gathered little had no lack. Each person gathered as much as he needed.
Moses said to them, "No one may keep any of it until morning."
But they did not listen to Moses. Some people left part of it until morning. It became full of worms and began to smell bad. So Moses was angry with them.
Every morning each person gathered as much as he needed. When the sun got hot, it melted away.
On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food. That was two omers for each person. All the leaders of the people came and told Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the the LORD has said: 'Tomorrow is a day of rest. It is a holy Sabbath to the the LORD. Bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then save what is left and keep it until morning.'"
