So they saved it until morning, as Moses had commanded. It did not smell bad, and there were no worms in it.
"Eat it today," Moses said, "because today is a Sabbath to the the LORD. Today you will not find it in the field.
For six days you may gather it. But on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none."
Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather. But they did not find any.
Then the the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep My commands and My teachings?
See, the the LORD has given you the Sabbath. That is why on the sixth day He gives you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is. No one may leave his place."
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The people of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like thin cakes made with honey.

Then Moses said, "This is what the the LORD has commanded: 'Keep an omer of manna for the people who come after you. Then they can see the bread I fed you in the desert when I brought you out of Egypt.'"
So Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put an omer of manna in it. Then place it before the the LORD to be kept for the people who come after you."
And Aaron placed it before the Testimony to be kept, just as the the LORD had commanded Moses.
The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they came to a land where people lived. They ate manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
An omer is a tenth of an ephah.
All the people of Israel left the desert of Sin. They traveled the way the the LORD told them. They camped at Rephidim. There was no water to drink.
The people argued with Moses. They said, "Give us water to drink." Moses said to them, "Why do you argue with me? Why do you test the the LORD?"
The people were thirsty. They complained to Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt? Did you bring us here to die of thirst, us and our children and our animals?"
Moses cried out to the the LORD. He said, "What should I do with these people? They are almost ready to throw stones at me."
The The LORD said to Moses, "Go ahead of the people. Take some leaders of Israel with you. Take the stick in your hand. It is the one you used to hit the Nile. Then go.
I will stand in front of you there on the rock at Horeb. Hit the rock. Water will come out of it. The people will drink." Moses did this while the leaders watched.
He named the place Massah and Meribah. That was because the people of Israel argued. It was also because they tested the the LORD. They said, "Is the the LORD with us or not?"
The Amalekites came and fought Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, "Pick some men for us. Go out and fight Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill. I will hold God's stick in my hand."
Joshua did what Moses said. He fought Amalek. Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
When Moses held up his hand, Israel was stronger. When he put his hand down, Amalek was stronger.

Moses' hands got tired. So they put a stone under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands. One stood on one side, and one on the other side. His hands stayed up until the sun went down.
Joshua beat Amalek and his people with the sword.
The The LORD said to Moses, "Write this in a book to remember it. Read it to Joshua. I will wipe out Amalek's name from under the sky."
Moses built an altar. He named it "The The LORD Is My Banner."
He said, "A hand was raised to the the LORD's throne! The The LORD will fight Amalek forever."
Jethro was a priest in Midian. He was Moses' father-in-law. He heard all that God had done for Moses and for His people, Israel. He heard that the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
Moses had sent his wife, Zipporah, away. Now Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took her back.
He also took her two sons. One son was named Gershom. Moses had said, "I have lived as a stranger in a foreign land."
The other son was named Eliezer. Moses had said, "The God of my father helped me. He saved me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro came to Moses in the desert. He brought Moses' wife and sons. Moses was camped at God's mountain.
Jethro sent a message to Moses. He said, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you. Your wife and her two sons are with me."
Moses went out to meet his father-in-law. He bowed down and kissed him. They greeted each other. Then they went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and Egypt for Israel. He told about the hard times they had on the way. He told how the LORD saved them.
Jethro was glad for all the good things the LORD had done for Israel. The LORD had saved them from Egypt.
Jethro said, "Praise be to the LORD. He saved you from Egypt and from Pharaoh. He saved the people from Egypt.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods. He did this when they were proud and mean to Israel."
Then Jethro brought a burnt offering and other gifts to God. Aaron and all the leaders of Israel came. They ate a meal with Moses' father-in-law in front of God.
The next day, Moses sat to settle problems for the people. They stood around him from morning until night.
His father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing. He asked, "What are you doing for the people? Why do you sit alone? All the people stand around you from morning until night."
Moses said to his father-in-law, "The people come to me to find out what God wants.
When they have a problem, they come to me. I decide who is right. I tell them God's rules and laws."
Moses' father-in-law said, "What you are doing is not good.
You and the people who come to you will get too tired. The work is too hard for you. You cannot do it alone.
Listen to me. I will give you advice. God will be with you. You should stand for the people before God. Bring their problems to Him.
Teach them God's rules and laws. Show them how to live and what work to do.

Choose good men from all the people. Choose men who fear God. Choose men who tell the truth and hate taking money to do wrong. Put them over the people. Make them leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

Let them settle problems for the people all the time. Let them bring the big problems to you. Let them settle the small problems themselves. This will make your work lighter. They will help carry the load.
If you do this, and if God tells you to, you can stand strong. All the people can go home in peace."
Moses listened to his father-in-law. He did everything Jethro said.
Moses chose good men from all Israel. He made them leaders over the people. They were leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They settled problems for the people all the time. They brought the hard problems to Moses. They settled the small problems themselves.
Then Moses sent his father-in-law away. Jethro went back to his own land.
Three months after the Israelites left Egypt, they came to the Sinai desert.
They left Rephidim and came to the Sinai desert. Israel camped there, near the mountain.
Moses went up to God. The LORD called to him from the mountain and said, "Say this to Jacob's family and to the people of Israel:
'You saw what I did to Egypt. I carried you safely to Myself, like an eagle lifting its young.
Now, if you listen to My voice and keep My agreement, you will be My special treasure among all nations. The whole earth is Mine.
You will be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation to Me. These are the words you must say to the people of Israel.'"
Moses came back. He called the leaders of the people and told them all the LORD's words.
All the people answered together, "We will do everything the LORD has said." Then Moses told the LORD what the people said.
The LORD said to Moses, "I will come to you in a thick cloud. Then the people will hear Me talk with you. They will always trust you." Moses told the LORD what the people had said.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people. Make them clean today and tomorrow. Have them wash their clothes.
Be ready on the third day. On that day, the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai. All the people will see Him.
Put a fence around the mountain for the people. Tell them, 'Be careful. Do not go up the mountain. Do not touch its edge. Anyone who touches the mountain must die.'
No one may touch them. They must be killed with stones or arrows. No person or animal may live. They may come up the mountain only when the trumpet blows a long sound."
Moses went down the mountain to the people. He made them clean, and they washed their clothes.
He told the people, "Be ready for three days. Do not sleep with a woman."
On the morning of the third day, there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain. A trumpet blew very loud. All the people in the camp were afraid.
Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God. They stood at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was covered with smoke. The LORD came down on it in fire. Smoke rose like smoke from a big oven. The whole mountain shook hard.
The trumpet sound grew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with a loud voice.
The LORD came down to the top of Mount Sinai. He called Moses to the top, and Moses went up.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people. Do not let them rush in to see the LORD. If they do, many will die.
The priests who come near the LORD must also make themselves clean. If they do not, the LORD may punish them."
Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai. You warned us. You said, 'Put a fence around the mountain and make it holy.'"
The LORD said, "Go down. Then come back up with Aaron. But do not let the priests and people break through to come up to the LORD. If they do, He may punish them."
So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
God spoke all these words. He said,
"I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of Egypt. I brought you out of the house where you were slaves.
"You must not have any other gods but Me.
Do not make for you any carved statue or picture of anything in the sky above, on the earth below, or in the water under the earth.

Do not bow down to them or serve them. I am the LORD your God. I am a jealous God. I punish children for the wrongs of their parents, even to the third and fourth generation after them, if they hate Me.
But I am kind to thousands who love Me and obey My rules.
You must not use the name of the LORD your God in a wrong way. The LORD will not let a person go free who uses His name in a wrong way.
"Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
You may work six days and do all your work.

But the seventh day is a Sabbath for the LORD your God. On that day you must not do any work. Not you, not your son, not your daughter, not your male servant, not your female servant, not your animals, and not the guest in your town.
The LORD made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them in six days. Then He rested on the seventh day. So the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
"Honor your father and your mother. Then you will live a long time in the land the LORD your God gives you.
Do not be unfaithful in marriage.
Do not lie about your neighbor.
Do not want what belongs to your neighbor. Do not want your neighbor's house, wife, servant, ox, donkey, or anything else that is your neighbor's."
All the people saw the thunder and lightning. They heard the trumpet. They saw the mountain covered with smoke. They were afraid and shook. They stood far away.
They said to Moses, "You must speak to us, and we will listen. But do not let God speak to us, or we will die."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. God came to test you. He wants you to respect Him, so you will not sin."
The people stood far away. Moses went near the dark cloud where God was.
The LORD said to Moses, "Tell the people of Israel: 'You have seen that I talked with you from heaven.
Do not make gods of silver to be with Me. Do not make gods of gold for you.
Make an altar of dirt for Me. On it, offer your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and cows. I will come to you and bless you in every place where I cause My name to be remembered.
If you make an altar of stone for Me, do not build it with cut stones. If you use a tool on it, you make it unclean.
Do not go up steps to My altar, so your nakedness is not seen.'"
These are the rules you must put before the people.
If you buy a Hebrew servant, he will work for six years. In the seventh year, he will go free. He will not pay anything.
If he came in alone, he will leave alone. If he had a wife, his wife will leave with him.
If his master gives him a wife, and she has sons or daughters for him, the wife and her children will belong to the master. The man will leave alone.
But if the servant says, “I love my master, my wife, and my children. I do not want to go free,”
then his master will take him to God. He will take him to the door or the door frame. Then his master will make a hole in his ear with a sharp tool. He will serve his master for life.
If a man sells his daughter to be a servant girl, she will not go free the same way the male servants go free.
If she does not please the master who chose her for himself, he must let someone buy her back. He must not sell her to people from another country, because he was not fair to her.
If he gives her to his son, he must treat her like a daughter.
If he marries another wife, he must still give her food, clothes, and time with him.
If he does not do these three things for her, she may go free. She will not pay anything.
Anyone who hits a person and kills him must be put to death.
But if he did not plan to kill him, and God let it happen, then I will give you a place where he can run for safety.
But if a man plans to kill his neighbor on purpose, you must take him away from My altar. He must die.
Anyone who hits his father or his mother must be put to death.
Anyone who kidnaps a person and sells him must be put to death. If the person is found with him, he must be put to death.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother must be put to death.
If two men fight and one hits the other with a stone or his fist, and the man does not die but must stay in bed,
and if the hurt man gets up and walks outside with a cane, the one who hit him is not guilty. But he must pay for the time the man could not work, and he must pay for the healing.
If a man hits his male or female servant with a stick and the servant dies, the man must be punished.
But if the servant lives for a day or two, the man will not be punished, because the servant belongs to him.

If men fight and hit a pregnant woman, and her baby is born early, but no one is badly hurt, the man who hit her must pay a fine. The woman's husband will decide the fine, and judges will set the amount.
But if someone is badly hurt, you must give life for life.
Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
Burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
If a man hits his male or female servant's eye and ruins it, he must let the servant go free because of the eye.
If he knocks out his male or female servant's tooth, he must let the servant go free because of the tooth.
If an ox kills a man or woman, the ox must be stoned to death. Its meat must not be eaten. The owner is not guilty.
But if the ox had hurt people before, and the owner knew but did not keep it tied up, and it kills a man or woman, the ox must be stoned. The owner must also be put to death.
If a price is put on his life, he must pay that price to save his life.
This same rule applies if the ox hurts a boy or a girl.
If the ox hurts a male or female servant, the owner must give the servant's master thirty pieces of silver. The ox must also be stoned.
If a man opens a pit, or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,
the man who owns the pit must pay for the animal. He must give money to the animal's owner, and he keeps the dead animal.
If one man's ox hurts another man's ox and it dies, they will sell the live ox and share the money. They will also share the dead ox.
But if people knew the ox had hurt animals before, and the owner did not keep it tied up, he must give an ox for the ox that died. He keeps the dead ox.
If a man steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, he must pay back five oxen for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking in and is hit so he dies, no one is guilty for his death.
But if the sun has come up, he is guilty. The thief must pay back what he stole. If he has nothing, he must be sold to pay for his theft.
If the stolen animal is found alive with him, whether it is an ox, a donkey, or a sheep, he must pay back two for one.
If a man lets his animals eat in another man’s field or vineyard, or lets them loose so they eat there, he must pay from the best of his own field or vineyard.
If a fire starts and burns thorns, and it burns up grain that is stacked or still growing, or the whole field, the person who started the fire must pay for all of it.
If a man gives his neighbor money or things to keep safe, and they are stolen from his house, the thief, if caught, must pay back two for one.
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must come before God. He must show that he did not take his neighbor’s things.

For any wrong about an ox, a donkey, a sheep, clothes, or any lost thing that someone says, “This is mine,” both sides must come before God. The one God says is wrong must pay back two for one to his neighbor.
If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep safe, and it dies, is hurt, or is taken while no one is watching,
the two men must make a promise before the LORD. They must find out if the keeper took his neighbor’s animal. The owner must accept the promise, and the keeper does not have to pay.
But if the animal was stolen, the keeper must pay the owner.
If a wild animal tore it up, he must bring the torn animal as proof. He does not have to pay for it.
If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is hurt or dies while the owner is not there, he must pay for it.
If the owner was there, he does not have to pay. If the animal was hired, the pay covers the loss.
If a man gets a young woman who is not promised to anyone to sleep with him, he must pay the price for a bride and marry her.
If her father refuses to give her to him, he must pay money equal to the price for a bride.
You must not let a woman who uses magic live.
Anyone who sleeps with an animal must be put to death.
Anyone who gives an offering to any god but the LORD alone must be destroyed.
You must not be mean to a foreigner or push him around. You were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You must not be mean to any widow or child with no father.
If you are mean to them and they cry out to Me, I will surely hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with a sword. Then your wives will become widows, and your children will have no father.
If you lend money to one of My people who is poor, you must not act like a money lender to him. You must not charge him interest.
If you take your neighbor’s coat as a promise to pay, you must give it back before the sun goes down.
That coat is his only cover. It is what he sleeps in. What else can he sleep in? If he cries out to Me, I will hear him, because I am kind.
You must not speak badly about God, and you must not curse a leader of your people.
You must not wait to give from your harvest and your wine. You must give Me your first son.
Do the same with your oxen and sheep. A new baby animal stays with its mother for seven days. On the eighth day, give it to Me.
You must be My holy people, because I am the LORD who makes you holy. You must not eat meat from an animal torn by wild animals in the field. Throw it to the dogs.
Do not tell a false story. Do not help bad people by being a false witness.
Do not do wrong just because many people do. When you speak in a case, do not twist the truth to follow the crowd.
Do not show special favor to a poor person in his case.
If you see your enemy's ox or donkey that got lost, take it back to him.
If you see the donkey of a man who hates you lying under its load, do not walk away. Help him get it up.
Do not keep a poor person from fair help in his case.
Stay away from false charges. Do not kill innocent and good people, because I will not let guilty people go free.
Do not take money to change what is right. Money can blind people who see well and twist the words of good people.
Do not be hard on a foreigner. You know how it feels to be a foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
For six years, plant your land and gather its crops.

But in the seventh year, let it rest and leave it alone. Then poor people among your people can eat from the field. Wild animals can eat what is left. Do the same with your grape field and your olive trees.
Work six days, but rest on the seventh day. This lets your ox and donkey rest. It also lets your servant's son and the foreigner rest.
Be careful to do all I have said to you. Do not even say the names of other gods.
Three times a year, celebrate a feast for Me.

Keep the Feast of Bread with No Yeast. Eat bread with no yeast for seven days, as I told you. Do this at the set time in the month of Abib, because that is when you came out of Egypt. No one should come to Me without a gift.
Celebrate the harvest feast with the first crops you grow in the field. Celebrate the gathering feast at the end of the year, when you bring in your crops from the field.
Three times a year, all your men must come before the Lord, the the LORD.
Do not offer the blood of My sacrifice with bread that has yeast. Do not let the fat from My feast stay until morning.
Bring the best first crops from your land to the house of the the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk. “
I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and bring you to the place I have made ready.
Pay attention to him and listen to what he says. Do not go against him, because he will not forgive your sins. My name is in him.
But if you truly listen to him and do all I say, then I will be an enemy to your enemies. I will oppose those who oppose you.
My angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites. I will wipe them out. “
Do not bow down to their gods. Do not serve them. Do not do the things they do. Instead, tear down their gods and break their stone pillars.
Serve the the LORD your God, and He will bless your food and water. I will take sickness away from you.
No woman in your land will lose her baby or be unable to have children. I will let you live out your days.
I will send fear of Me ahead of you. I will throw every nation you meet into confusion. I will make all your enemies turn and run. “
I will send hornets ahead of you to drive out the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites.
I will not drive them out in one year, because then the land would become empty, and wild animals would become too many for you.
Little by little I will drive them out, until you grow and take the land.
I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the Philistine sea, and from the desert to the River. I will hand over the people who live there, and you will drive them out. “
Do not make an agreement with them or with their gods.
They must not live in your land, or they will cause you to sin against Me. If you serve their gods, it will be a trap for you.”
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's leaders. Worship Him from far away."
Only Moses may come close to the LORD. The others must not come close, and the people must not go up with him.
Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all His rules. All the people answered together, "We will do everything the LORD has said."
Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. Early in the morning, he got up and built an altar at the foot of the mountain. He set up twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent some young men of Israel. They offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed bulls as peace offerings.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls. He sprinkled the other half on the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Agreement and read it aloud to the people. They said, "We will do everything the LORD has said, and we will obey."
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people. He said, "Look! This is the blood of the agreement the LORD has made with you, based on all these words."
Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's leaders went up the mountain.
They saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was something like a floor made of clear blue stone, as clear as the sky.
He did not hurt the leaders of Israel. They saw God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to Me on the mountain and stay there. I will give you stone tablets with the law and the commands I have written, so you can teach them."
Moses got up, and Joshua, who helped him, went with him. Then Moses went up to God's mountain.
He said to the leaders, "Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you. If anyone has a problem, he can go to them."
Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered it.
The glory of the LORD rested on Mount Sinai. The cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day, He called to Moses from inside the cloud.
To the people of Israel, the glory of the LORD looked like a fire that burns everything, on top of the mountain.
Moses went into the cloud and up the mountain. He stayed there forty days and forty nights.
"Tell the Israelites to bring Me an offering. Take it from every person whose heart wants to give.
This is the offering you shall take from them: gold, silver, and bronze.
blue, purple, and red thread; fine white cloth; and goat hair.
red sheepskins, other animal skins, and acacia wood.
oil for the lamps; spices for the special oil and for the sweet-smelling incense.
onyx stones and other stones to set in the special vest and the chest piece.
Make a holy place for Me. Then I will live among them.
Make the tent and everything in it just like the pattern I show you.
"Make a box of acacia wood. It shall be about 3 feet 9 inches long, 2 feet 3 inches wide, and 2 feet 3 inches high.
Cover it with pure gold inside and out. Put a gold rim around the top.
Cast four gold rings for it. Put them on its four corners. Put two rings on one side and two on the other side.
Make poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold.
Put the poles through the rings on the sides of the box to carry the box.
The poles must stay in the rings. Do not take them out.
Put the stone tablets with My rules in the box.
"Make a lid of pure gold. It shall be about 3 feet 9 inches long and 2 feet 3 inches wide.
Make two winged angels of hammered gold. Put them at the two ends of the lid.
Make one angel at one end and one at the other end. Make them from the lid.
The angels shall spread their wings up. Their wings shall cover the lid. They shall face each other, looking at the lid.
Put the lid on top of the box. Put the stone tablets inside the box.
I will meet you there, above the lid, between the two angels on the box of the law. I will tell you all the commands I have for the Israelites.
"Make a table of acacia wood. It shall be about 3 feet long, 1 foot 6 inches wide, and 2 feet 3 inches high.
Cover it with pure gold. Put a gold rim around it.
Make a rim around it about 4 inches wide. Put a gold edge around that rim.
Make four gold rings for it. Put them on the four corners near its legs.
Put the rings close to the rim. They are places for the poles to carry the table.
Make poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold. Carry the table with them.
Make its plates, dishes, bowls, and jars of pure gold. Use them for pouring out offerings.
Always put the special bread on the table before Me.
"Make a lampstand of pure gold. Hammer it out. Its base, stem, cups, buds, and flowers shall be one piece.
Six branches shall come out from its sides. Three branches from one side and three from the other side.
Each branch shall have three cups shaped like almond flowers, with a bud and a flower. Do the same for all six branches.
The lampstand shall have four cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and flowers.
Put a bud under each pair of branches that come out of the lampstand.
The buds and branches shall be one piece with it. All of it shall be one piece of pure gold, hammered out.
Make seven lamps for it. Light them so they shine in front of it.
Make its wick trimmers and trays of pure gold.
Make the lampstand and all these parts from about 75 pounds of pure gold.
Be careful to make everything just like the pattern I showed you on the mountain."
Make the tabernacle with ten curtains. Use fine linen. Use blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. Make cherubim on them with skill.
Each curtain must be 28 cubits long and 4 cubits wide. All the curtains must be the same size.
Join five curtains together. Join the other five curtains together.
Put blue loops on the edge of the last curtain in the first set. Do the same on the edge of the last curtain in the second set.
Make 50 loops on one curtain. Make 50 loops on the edge of the last curtain in the second set. The loops must match each other.
Make 50 gold hooks. Join the curtains with the hooks. Then the tabernacle will be one piece.
Make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle. Make 11 curtains in all.
Each of the 11 curtains must be 30 cubits long and 4 cubits wide.
Join five curtains into one set. Join the other six into another set. Fold the sixth curtain over the front of the tent.
Make 50 loops along the edge of the last curtain in the first set. Make 50 loops along the edge of the matching curtain in the second set.
Make 50 bronze hooks. Put them through the loops. Join the tent together as one piece.
Let the extra half curtain hang over the back of the tabernacle.
The extra cubit on one side and the extra cubit on the other side must hang over the sides of the tabernacle. This will cover it.
Make a cover for the tent from red ram skins. Make another cover over that from fine leather.
Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame must be 10 cubits long and 1.5 cubits wide.
Make two pegs on the side of each frame. Join them together. Make all the frames this way.
Make 20 frames for the south side of the tabernacle.
Make 40 silver bases for these frames. Put two bases under each frame. One base is for each peg.
Make 20 frames for the north side of the tabernacle.
Make 40 silver bases for these frames. Put two bases under each frame.
Make 6 frames for the back of the tabernacle, on the west side.
Make 2 frames for the two back corners of the tabernacle.
Join them from bottom to top. Fit them into one ring. Make both corner frames this way.
There must be 8 frames and 16 silver bases. Put two bases under each frame.
Make 5 crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle.
Make 5 crossbars for the frames on the other side. Make 5 crossbars for the frames on the back side, on the west.
The middle crossbar must go through the middle of the frames. It must run from one end to the other end.
Cover the frames with gold. Make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Cover the crossbars with gold too.
Set up the tabernacle the way you were shown on the mountain.
Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. Use fine linen. Make cherubim on it with skill.
Hang it on four posts of acacia wood. Cover the posts with gold. Use gold hooks. Put them on four silver bases.
Hang the veil from the hooks. Put the ark of the Testimony behind the veil. The veil will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
Put the mercy seat on the ark in the Most Holy Place.
Put the table outside the veil, on the north side of the tabernacle. Put the lampstand across from the table, on the south side.
For the entrance to the tent, make a curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. Use fine linen. Make it with skill, like an embroiderer.
Make five posts of acacia wood for the curtain. Cover them with gold. Make gold hooks. Make five bronze bases for them.
Make an altar from acacia wood. It should be square. Make it five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
Make horns on its four corners. The horns should be part of the altar. Cover the altar with bronze.
Make bronze tools for it: pots to carry away ashes, shovels, bowls, forks, and fire pans.
Make a bronze grate like a net. Put four bronze rings on its four corners.
Put the grate under the edge of the altar, halfway up.
Make poles from acacia wood and cover them with bronze.
Put the poles through the rings on two sides of the altar. Use them to carry the altar.
Make the altar hollow, out of boards. Make it just as it was shown on the mountain.
Make a courtyard around the holy tent. On the south side, put fine linen curtains one hundred cubits long.
Use twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The posts should have silver hooks and bands.
Do the same on the north side: curtains one hundred cubits long, twenty posts, twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands.
On the west side, put curtains fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
The east side should also be fifty cubits wide.
On one side of the gate, put curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
On the other side, put curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
For the gate, make a screen twenty cubits long. Use blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen. Four posts and four bases should hold it.
All the posts around the courtyard should have silver bands. Their hooks and bases should be bronze.
The courtyard should be one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide. The curtains should be five cubits high, with bronze bases.
All the tools used in the holy tent, and all the tent pegs for the holy tent and the courtyard, should be bronze.
Command the people of Israel to bring pure olive oil, pressed from olives, for the lamp. It should burn all the time.

In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain in front of the box that holds the law, Aaron and his sons should keep the lamp burning before the LORD from evening to morning. This is a rule for the people of Israel for all time.
Bring your brother Aaron and his sons to you from the Israelites. They are Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Aaron will serve Me as a priest.
Make holy clothes for your brother Aaron. They will show his honor and beauty.
Talk to all the wise men I have filled with a wise spirit. They will make Aaron's clothes. The clothes will set him apart to serve Me as a priest.
These are the clothes they will make: a chest piece, an ephod, a robe, a patterned coat, a turban, and a sash. Make holy clothes for your brother Aaron and his sons. They will serve Me as priests.
They will take gold, blue cloth, purple cloth, red cloth, and fine white cloth.
Make the ephod from gold thread, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen. Make it with skill.
It will have two shoulder pieces joined to its two ends.
The belt on it will be one piece with it. Make the belt like the ephod, from gold, blue, purple, red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
Take two onyx stones. Carve the names of Israel's sons on them.
Put six names on one stone and six names on the other stone. Put them in the order the sons were born.
A skilled worker will carve the names. Then set the stones in gold frames.

Put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod. They will help people remember Israel's sons. Aaron will carry their names on his two shoulders before the LORD. It will help people remember them.
Make two chains of pure gold. Make them like twisted cords. Put the chains on the frames.
Make a chest piece for decisions. Make it with skill, like the ephod. Make it from gold, blue, purple, red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It will be square and folded double. It will be one hand span long and one hand span wide.
Put four rows of stones in it. The first row will have a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald.
The second row will have a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond.
The third row will have a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
The fourth row will have a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Set them in gold frames.
There will be twelve stones. Each stone will have the name of one of Israel's sons. Carve each name like a seal. The stones will stand for the twelve tribes.
Make two gold chains for the chest piece. Make them like twisted cords.
Make two gold rings for the chest piece. Put them on the two upper corners.
Put the two gold chains through the two rings at the corners of the chest piece.
Fasten the other ends of the two chains to the two gold settings. Put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod in front.
Make two gold rings. Put them on the two lower corners of the chest piece, on the side that faces the ephod.
Make two more gold rings. Put them low on the two shoulder straps of the ephod, near the front. Put them close to where the pieces join, above the belt of the ephod.
Tie the chest piece to the ephod with blue cord. Tie it through the rings. Then the chest piece will not come loose from the ephod.
When Aaron goes into the holy place, he will carry the names of Israel's sons on his heart. The chest piece will help people remember them before the LORD.
Put the Urim and Thummim in the chest piece. They will be on Aaron's heart when he stands before the LORD. Aaron will always carry the means to make decisions for Israel's people before the LORD.
Make the robe of the ephod all of blue cloth.
Make an opening at the top for the head. Put a woven edge around the opening, like a collar. It must not tear.
Make shapes like pomegranates of blue, purple, and red yarn around the bottom edge. Put gold bells between them all around.
Put a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the bottom edge of the robe.
Aaron will wear it when he serves. People will hear the bells when he goes into the holy place before the LORD and when he comes out. Then he will not die.
Make a pure gold plate. Carve on it: Holy to the LORD.
Tie it to the turban with a blue cord. It will be on the front of the turban.

Aaron will wear it on his forehead. He will carry the guilt connected to the holy gifts Israel's people set apart. The gifts include all their holy offerings. The plate will help the LORD accept them.
Make the tunic of fine linen. Make the turban of fine linen. Make the sash with skilled needlework.
Make coats, sashes, and hats for Aaron's sons. Make them for honor and beauty.
Dress your brother Aaron and his sons in these clothes. Pour oil on them to set them apart. Give them authority to serve. Set them apart to serve Me as priests.
Make linen underclothes for them. They must cover from the waist to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons must wear them when they go into the tent of meeting or come near the altar to serve in the holy place. Then they will not be guilty and die. This is a law for Aaron and his family after him forever.
This is what you must do to make Aaron and his sons ready to serve Me as priests. Take one young bull and two rams that have no flaws.
Make bread with no yeast. Make flat cakes mixed with oil. Make thin wafers with oil on them. Use fine wheat flour.
Put all these in one basket. Bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the meeting tent. Wash them with water.
Take the clothes and put them on Aaron. Put on the long shirt, the robe, the special vest, and the chest piece. Tie the vest on him with its belt.
Put the head cloth on his head. Put the holy crown on the head cloth.
Take the oil used to make a priest. Pour it on his head to set him apart.
Bring his sons and put shirts on them.
Tie belts around Aaron and his sons. Put hats on them. They will be priests forever. This is the rule you must follow to make Aaron and his sons priests.
Bring the bull to the front of the meeting tent. Aaron and his sons must put their hands on its head.
Kill the bull in front of the LORD at the door of the meeting tent.
Take some of the bull's blood. Put it on the horns of the altar with your finger. Pour the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.
Take all the fat that covers the inside parts. Take the best part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. Burn them on the altar.
Burn the bull's meat, its skin, and its waste outside the camp. This is an offering to pay for sin.
Take one of the rams. Aaron and his sons must put their hands on its head.
Kill the ram. Splash its blood on all sides of the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces. Wash its inside parts and its legs. Put them with its head and the other pieces.
Then burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD. It smells good to Him. It is a fire offering to the LORD.
Take the second ram. Aaron and his sons must put their hands on its head.

Kill it. Take some of its blood and put it on the right ear of Aaron and his sons. Put it on the thumb of their right hand and the big toe of their right foot. Then splash the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.

Take some blood from the altar and some oil used to make a priest. Sprinkle them on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. Then he and his clothes will be made holy, and his sons and their clothes too.
Take the fat from the ram. Take the fat tail, the fat that covers the inside parts, the best part of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh. This ram is for making priests.
Take one loaf of bread, one cake made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of bread with no yeast that is before the LORD.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons. Wave them in front of the LORD. This is a wave offering.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar on top of the burnt offering. This smells good to the LORD. It is a fire offering to the LORD.
Take the chest of the ram used to make priests. Wave it in front of the LORD. It will be your share.
Make holy for Aaron and his sons the chest that was waved and the thigh that was lifted from the ram used to make priests.
This will belong to Aaron and his sons forever. It is the part the people of Israel give to the LORD from their peace offerings.
Aaron's holy clothes will belong to his sons after him. They will wear them when they are made priests.
The son who becomes priest after him must wear them for seven days when he goes into the meeting tent to serve in the holy place.
You must take the ram used to make priests and boil its meat in a holy place.
At the door of the meeting tent, Aaron and his sons must eat the meat of the ram and the bread in the basket.
They must eat the food that was used to pay for their wrongs and make them priests. No one else may eat it, because it is holy.
If any meat or bread is left until morning, you must burn it up. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.
Do for Aaron and his sons everything I have told you. Make them priests for seven days.
Each day, kill a bull as an offering to pay for sin. Clean the altar by paying for its wrongs. Pour oil on it to make it holy.
For seven days, pay for the altar's wrongs and make it holy. Then the altar will be most holy. Anything that touches it will be holy.
This is what you must offer on the altar all the time: two lambs one year old, each day, forever.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other in the evening.
With the first lamb, offer a small amount of fine flour mixed with oil, and a small cup of wine.
Offer the second lamb the same way in the evening. Offer the same flour and drink offering. This smells good to the LORD. It is a fire offering.
For all time to come, offer this burnt offering at the door of the meeting tent in front of the LORD. There I will meet with you and speak with you.
There I will meet with the people of Israel. That place will be made holy by My glory.
So I will make the meeting tent and the altar holy. I will make Aaron and his sons holy so they can serve Me as priests.
Then I will live among the people of Israel. I will be their God.
They will know that I am the LORD their God. I brought them out of Egypt so I could live among them. I am the LORD their God.
"Make an altar for burning incense. Make it from acacia wood.
Make it square. It should be one cubit long, one cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns should be one piece with it.
Cover it with pure gold on top, on all sides, and on the horns. Put a gold strip around it.
Make two gold rings under the strip, one on each of two sides. They will hold poles for carrying it.
Make the poles from acacia wood and cover them with gold.
Put the altar in front of the curtain that hangs over the box that holds the law. Put it in front of the lid that covers the law. That is where I will meet with you.
Aaron will burn sweet-smelling incense on it. He will burn it every morning when he takes care of the lamps.
He will also burn incense at sunset when he lights the lamps. This incense will burn before the the LORD always, for all your people to come.
Do not burn strange incense on it. Do not burn a burnt offering, a grain offering, or a drink offering on it.
Once a year, Aaron will use blood from the sin offering to make the altar right with God. He will do this on the horns of the altar once a year for all time. The altar is most holy to the the LORD."
The the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "
When you count the people of Israel, each man must give money to the the LORD to buy back his life. Do this when you count them. Then no sickness will come to them.
Everyone who is counted must give half a shekel of silver. Use the holy shekel. A shekel is 20 gerahs. So half a shekel is the gift to the the LORD.
Everyone 20 years old or older who is counted must give this gift to the the LORD.
The rich must not give more, and the poor must not give less than half a shekel. This gift pays for your lives.
Take this money from the people of Israel. Use it for the work of the tent of meeting. It will help the people of Israel remember before the the LORD. It will pay for your lives."
The the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "
Make a bronze bowl for washing. Make a bronze stand for it. Put it between the tent of meeting and the altar. Put water in it.
Aaron and his sons will wash their hands and feet with the water.
When they go into the tent of meeting, or when they come near the altar to serve, they must wash. If they do not wash, they will die. This is when they burn a gift to the the LORD.
They must wash their hands and feet so they will not die. This rule will last for all time for Aaron and his children."
The the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "
Take the best spices. Take 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, 250 shekels of sweet cinnamon, 250 shekels of sweet cane,
and 500 shekels of cassia. Use the holy shekel to weigh them. Take a hin of olive oil.
Make a holy oil for pouring. Mix it like a perfume maker would mix it. It will be holy oil for pouring.
Pour this oil on the tent of meeting and on the box that holds the law.
Pour it on the table and all its tools, on the lampstand and its tools, and on the altar for burning incense.
Pour it on the altar for burnt offerings and all its tools, and on the bowl and its stand.
Make these things holy. They will be most holy. Anyone who touches them will become holy.
Pour oil on Aaron and his sons. Make them holy so they can serve Me.
Tell the people of Israel that this oil is holy to Me. It is for all time.
Do not pour this oil on a normal person. Do not make oil like it. It is holy, and it must be holy to your.
Anyone who makes oil like it, or puts it on a stranger, will be cut off from his people."
The the LORD said to Moses, "Take spices: stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense. Use the same amount of each.
Make incense from them. Mix it like a perfume maker would mix it. Make it pure and holy.
Crush some of it into a fine powder. Put it in front of the law in the tent of meeting. That is where I meet with you. It is most holy for you.
Do not make incense like this for yourselves. It is holy to the the LORD.
Anyone who makes it to smell it will be cut off from his people."
"Look, I have chosen Bezalel. He is the son of Uri. Uri is the son of Hur. He is from the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with My Spirit. He has wisdom, understanding, and knowledge. He can do all kinds of work.
He can plan beautiful things. He can work with gold, silver, and bronze.
He can cut stones to set them. He can carve wood. He can do every kind of work.
I have also chosen Oholiab. He is the son of Ahisamach. He is from the tribe of Dan. I have given skill to all the workers. They have wise hearts. They will make everything I told you to make." "
They will make the holy tent. They will make the ark that holds God's law. They will make the cover on top of it. They will make all the things for the tent.
They will make the table and its dishes. They will make the pure gold lampstand and all its parts. They will make the altar for burning incense.
They will make the altar for burnt offerings and all its parts. They will make the wash basin and its stand.
They will make the special clothes for serving. They will make the holy clothes for Aaron the priest. They will make the clothes for his sons to serve as priests.
They will make the special oil. They will make the sweet-smelling incense for the holy place. They will make all these things, just as I told you."
"Tell the Israelites to keep My Sabbaths. The Sabbath is a sign between Me and you. It will last for all your families. It helps you know that I am the LORD. I make you holy.
Keep the Sabbath. It is holy for you. Anyone who does not keep it must be put to death. Anyone who works on that day will be cut off from the people.
People may work for six days. The seventh day is a Sabbath of rest. It is holy to the LORD. Anyone who works on the Sabbath day must be put to death.
The Israelites must keep the Sabbath. They must keep it forever. It is a lasting promise.
It is a sign between Me and the Israelites forever. The LORD made the heavens and the earth in six days. On the seventh day, He rested and felt refreshed."
When the LORD finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him two stone tablets. The law was written on them. God wrote the words with His finger.

The people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain. So they gathered around Aaron and said, "Come, make us gods who will go ahead of us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of Egypt, we don't know what has happened to him."
Aaron said to them, "Take off the gold earrings from your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."
All the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
He took the gold from their hands. He shaped it with a tool and made a gold calf. Then they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt."
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf. Aaron called out, "Tomorrow is a feast to the LORD."
The next day the people got up early. They offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings. Then the people sat down to eat and drink. They got up to have fun and dance.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down. Your people, whom you brought up out of Egypt, have done very wrong.

They have quickly turned away from what I told them to do. They have made a gold calf for themselves. They have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it. They said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "I have seen these people. They are very stubborn.
Now leave Me alone. My anger will burn against them and destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
Moses begged the LORD his God. He said, "The LORD, why are You so angry with Your people? You brought them out of Egypt with great power and strength.

Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out to hurt them, to kill them in the mountains, and to wipe them off the earth'? Turn from Your fierce anger. Change Your mind and do not bring disaster on Your people.

Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. You swore to them by Yourself. You said, 'I will make your children and grandchildren as many as the stars in the sky. I will give all this land to your children and grandchildren, and they will have it forever.'"
So the LORD changed His mind about the disaster He had said He would bring on His people.
Moses turned and went down the mountain. He had the two stone tablets with God's law in his hands. They were written on both sides, front and back.
The tablets were made by God. The writing was God's writing, cut into the stones.
Joshua heard the people shouting. He said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."
Moses said, "That is not the sound of winners shouting. It is not the sound of losers crying. I hear singing."
When Moses got close to the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. Moses was very angry. He threw the tablets from his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made. He burned it in the fire. He ground it into powder. He scattered it on the water. Then he made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What did these people do to you, that you brought such a big sin on them?"
Aaron said, "Don't let my lord's anger burn. You know these people. They are set on doing wrong.
They said to me, 'Make us gods who will go ahead of us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of Egypt, we don't know what has happened to him.'
So I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, take it off.' They gave it to me. I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."
Moses saw that the people were out of control, because Aaron had let them get out of control. This brought shame on them among their enemies.
Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Whoever is for the LORD, come to me." All the sons of Levi gathered around him.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD God of Israel says: 'Each man put his sword on his side. Go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate. Kill your brother, your friend, and your neighbor.'"
The sons of Levi did what Moses said. About three thousand men died that day.
Moses said, "Today you have given yourselves to the LORD. Each of you fought against his son and brother. So He will bless you today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have sinned a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD. Maybe I can make up for your sin."
Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Oh, these people have sinned a great sin. They have made gods of gold for themselves.
But now, if You will forgive their sin, forgive them. If You won't, please erase me from Your book that You have written."
The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against Me, I will erase from My book.
But now go. Lead the people to the place I told you. My angel will go ahead of you. But on the day I punish, I will punish them for their sin."
The LORD struck the people with a sickness because of what they did with the calf Aaron made.

Then the LORD said to Moses, "Leave this place. You and the people you brought up out of Egypt must go up to the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I said I would give it to their children.
I will send an angel ahead of you. I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Go up to a rich land with plenty of good things to eat. But I will not go with you, because you are stubborn. If I go with you, I might destroy you on the way."
The people heard this bad news. They were sad. No one wore jewelry.

The LORD said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites, 'You are stubborn people. If I stayed with you even for a moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your jewelry. Then I will decide what to do with you.'
So the Israelites took off their jewelry at Mount Horeb.

Moses used to take the tent and set it up outside the camp, far from the camp. He called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who wanted to ask the LORD something would go to the tent of meeting outside the camp.
When Moses went out to the tent, all the people got up. Each person stood at the door of his tent and watched Moses until he went into the tent.
When Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud came down and stood at the door of the tent. The LORD would speak with Moses.
All the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tent. Then all the people got up and bowed down. Each person stood at the door of his tent.
The LORD would speak to Moses face to face, like a man talks to his friend. Then Moses would go back to the camp. But his helper, Joshua son of Nun, stayed in the tent.
Moses said to the LORD, "Look, You told me, 'Lead these people up,' but You have not told me whom You will send with me. Yet You said, 'I know you by name, and I am pleased with you.'
Now if You are pleased with me, please teach me Your ways, so I may know You and please You. Remember that this nation is Your people."
The LORD replied, "I will go with you, and I will give you rest."
Then Moses said to Him, "If You do not go with us, do not lead us up from here.
For how will anyone know that You are pleased with me and Your people? It is only if You go with us. Then we will be different from all the other people on earth."
The LORD said to Moses, "I will do what you ask. You have pleased Me, and I know you by name."
Then Moses said, "Please let me see Your glory."
The LORD replied, "I will let all My goodness pass in front of you. I will say My name, the LORD, as I pass by. I will be kind to anyone I want. I will feel sorry for anyone I want."
But He added, "You cannot see My face. No one can see Me and live."
Then the LORD said, "Look, there is a place near Me where you may stand on a rock.
When My glory passes by, I will put you in a crack in the rock. I will cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take away My hand. You will see My back, but My face must not be seen."
Then The LORD said to Moses, “Cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready in the morning, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai. Stand before Me on top of the mountain.
No one may come with you. No one may be seen anywhere on the mountain. Not even the sheep and cows may eat grass in front of that mountain.”
So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had told him. He carried the two stone tablets in his hand.
The LORD came down in the cloud. He stood with Moses there and spoke His name, the LORD.
Then the LORD passed in front of Moses and called out, “The LORD, the LORD God, is kind and good. He is slow to get angry. He is full of love and truth.

He keeps His love for thousands. He forgives wrong, sin, and bad choices. But He will not let guilty people go free. He punishes children and grandchildren for their parents' wrongs, even to the third and fourth generation.”
Moses bowed down to the ground quickly and worshiped.
He said, “Lord, if I have found favor in Your eyes, please let the Lord go with us. These people are stubborn. Forgive our wrongs and our sins, and take us as Your own people.”

The LORD said, “I am making an agreement with you. I will do amazing things for all your people. No one in any nation has ever seen such things. The people around you will see what the LORD does, because it is an awesome thing I will do with you.
Do what I tell you today. I will drive out the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites ahead of you.
Be careful not to make an agreement with the people who live in the land you are entering. It could become a trap for you.
Instead, you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and cut down their poles for false gods. “
You must not worship any other god, for the LORD's name is Jealous. He is a jealous God.
Be careful not to make an agreement with the people who live in the land. They will worship their gods and sacrifice to them. They will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
If you take some of their daughters as wives for your sons, those daughters will worship their gods. Then they will lead your sons to do the same.
Do not make any metal gods for yourself. “
Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days at the set time in the month of Abib, eat bread without yeast, as I told you. You came out of Egypt in the month of Abib.
The first baby born to every mother belongs to Me. This includes all the firstborn males among your animals, both cows and sheep.
You must buy back the firstborn donkey with a lamb. If you do not buy it back, break its neck. You must buy back all the firstborn of your sons. No one may come before Me with nothing.
Work for six days, but rest on the seventh day. Even in plowing and harvest time, you must rest. “
Celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the first wheat you harvest. Celebrate the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year.
Three times a year, all your men must come before the Lord the LORD, the God of Israel.
I will drive out the nations before you. I will make your land bigger. No one will try to take your land while you go up three times a year to see the LORD your God.
Do not offer the blood of My sacrifice with anything that has yeast. Do not leave the Passover sacrifice until morning.
Bring the first and best crops from your land to the house of the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Write down these words. I have made an agreement with you and with Israel based on these words.”
Moses stayed with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He did not eat bread or drink water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the agreement, the Ten Commandments.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, he carried the two tablets of the agreement. He did not know that his face was shining because he had talked with the LORD.
Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses. His face was shining. They were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them. So Aaron and all the leaders of the people came back to him, and he talked with them.
After that, all the Israelites came near. He told them to do everything the LORD had said on Mount Sinai.
When Moses finished talking with them, he put a veil over his face.
But when Moses went in before the LORD to talk with Him, he took off the veil until he came out. When he came out, he told the Israelites what he had been told to do.
The Israelites saw that Moses' face was shining. So Moses put the veil back over his face until he went in to talk with the LORD.
Moses called all the people of Israel together. He said, "These are the things the LORD told us to do.
You may work for six days. But the seventh day must be holy. It is a day of rest for the LORD. Anyone who works on that day must die.
Do not light a fire in any of your homes on the Sabbath day."
Moses said to all the people, "This is what the LORD commanded.
Take an offering for the LORD from among you. Everyone who wants to give may bring the LORD's offering. Bring gold, silver, and bronze.
Bring blue, purple, and red yarn, fine linen, and goat hair.
Bring red ram skins, other animal skins, and acacia wood.
Bring oil for the light, spices for the special oil, and sweet spices for the incense.
Bring onyx stones and other stones to set in the special vest and the chest piece."
"Every skilled person among you must come and make all that the LORD commanded.
Make the tent, its cover, its hooks, its frames, its bars, its posts, and its bases.
Make the ark, its poles, its cover, and the curtain that hides it.
Make the table, its poles, all its tools, and the special bread.
Make the lamp holder, its tools, its lamps, and the oil for light.
Make the incense altar, its poles, the special oil, the sweet spices, and the curtain for the tent door.
Make the altar for burnt offerings, its bronze grate, its poles, all its tools, the wash bowl, and its stand.
Make the curtains for the yard, its posts, its bases, and the curtain for the yard gate.
Make the tent pegs, the yard pegs, and their ropes.
Make the special clothes for serving in the holy place. Make the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and for his sons to serve as priests."
Then all the people of Israel left Moses.
Everyone whose heart moved them came and brought a gift to the LORD. They brought things for the tent of meeting, for all its work, and for the holy clothes.
Men and women with willing hearts came. They brought pins, earrings, rings, and bracelets. They brought all kinds of gold. Each man brought gold to the LORD.
Everyone who had blue, purple, or red yarn, fine linen, goat hair, red ram skins, or other animal skins brought them.
Everyone who gave silver or bronze brought it to the LORD. Everyone who had acacia wood for the work brought it.
All the women who knew how to spin made yarn with their hands. They brought blue, purple, red, and fine linen yarn.
All the women whose hearts moved them in wisdom spun goat hair.
The leaders brought onyx stones and setting stones for the special vest and chest piece.
They also brought spices and oil for the light, for the special oil, and for the sweet incense.
The men and women of Israel whose hearts moved them brought a free gift to the LORD for all the work the LORD commanded through Moses.
Moses said to the people of Israel, "See, the LORD has called Bezalel by name. He is the son of Uri and the grandson of Hur, from the family of Judah.
The LORD filled him with the Spirit of God. He gave him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill in all kinds of work.
He can make designs and work with gold, silver, and bronze.
He can cut stones to set and carve wood. He can make all kinds of beautiful work.
The LORD put it in his heart to teach. He will teach Bezalel and Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, from the family of Dan.
The LORD filled them with skill to do all kinds of work. They can cut, design, and sew with blue, purple, red, and fine linen. They can weave. They can make all kinds of work and designs."
The LORD gave wisdom and understanding to Bezalel, Oholiab, and all the skilled workers. They knew how to do all the work for the holy place. They did everything the LORD commanded.
Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled worker whose heart the LORD had filled with skill. They came to do the work.
They took all the gifts the people of Israel had brought to Moses. The gifts were for the work of the holy place. But the people kept bringing more gifts every morning.
All the skilled workers who were doing the holy work came. Each man came from the work he was doing.
They said to Moses, "The people are bringing more than we need for the work the LORD commanded."
Moses gave a command. They told everyone in the camp, "No man or woman should bring any more gifts for the holy place." So the people stopped bringing gifts.
They had enough to do all the work. In fact, they had some left over.
All the skilled workers made the holy tent. They made ten curtains of fine linen. The curtains were blue, purple, and red. They had cherubim woven into them with skill.
Each curtain was 28 cubits long and 4 cubits wide. All the curtains were the same size.
They joined five curtains into one piece. They joined the other five curtains into another piece.
They made blue loops on the edge of the last curtain in the first set. They did the same on the edge of the last curtain in the second set.
They made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the other. The loops matched each other.
They made fifty gold hooks. They used the hooks to join the two sets of curtains. So the holy tent became one piece.
They made curtains of goat hair for a tent over the holy tent. They made eleven of these curtains.
Each curtain was 30 cubits long and 4 cubits wide. All of them were the same size.
They joined five curtains into one piece. They joined the other six curtains into another piece.
They made fifty loops on the edge of one curtain. They made fifty loops on the edge of the other curtain.
They made fifty bronze hooks. They used them to join the tent into one piece.
They made a covering for the tent from ram skins dyed red. They made another covering from fine leather skins on top.
They made frames of acacia wood for the holy tent.
Each frame was 10 cubits long and 1 1/2 cubits wide.
Each frame had two pegs joined to it. They did this for every frame.
They made twenty frames for the south side of the holy tent.
They made forty silver bases for the twenty frames. Each frame had two bases under it, one for each peg.
They made twenty frames for the north side of the holy tent.
These frames had forty silver bases, two under each frame.
They made six frames for the back of the holy tent, on the west side.
They made two frames for the two corners at the back.
These corner frames were joined at the bottom and the top with a ring. They did this for both corners.
So there were eight frames in all, with sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.
They made five bars of acacia wood for the frames on one side.
They made five bars for the frames on the other side. They made five bars for the frames at the back on the west side.
They made the middle bar to go all the way through the frames from one end to the other.
They covered the frames with gold. They made gold rings to hold the bars. They covered the bars with gold too.
They made the curtain that separated the rooms. It was blue, purple, and red fine linen. Cherubim were woven into it with skill.
They made four acacia pillars for it. They covered them with gold. They made gold hooks for them. They made four silver bases for them.
They made a screen for the entrance of the tent. It was blue, purple, and red fine linen, with pretty designs sewn into it.
They made five pillars for it. They put hooks on them. They covered the tops and bands with gold. They made five bronze bases for them.
Bezalel made the ark from acacia wood. It was two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one and a half cubits high.
He covered it with pure gold inside and out. He made a gold trim around it.
He made four gold rings. He put them on its four feet. He put two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
He made poles from acacia wood. He covered them with gold.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark. The poles were used to carry the ark.
He made the cover from pure gold. It was two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
He made two cherubim from hammered gold. He put them at the ends of the cover.
He made one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. The cherubim were made as one piece with the cover.
The cherubim had wings spread upward. Their wings covered the top. Their faces looked at each other. They looked down toward the cover.
He made the table from acacia wood. It was two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
He covered it with pure gold. He made a gold trim around it.
He made a frame around it one hand wide. He made a gold trim around the frame.
He made four gold rings. He put them on the four corners by its four legs.
The rings were near the frame. They held the poles for carrying the table.
He made poles from acacia wood. He covered them with gold. The poles were used to carry the table.
He made plates, dishes, bowls, and pitchers from pure gold. They were used on the table. Some were for pouring drink offerings.
He made the lampstand from pure gold. It was hammered work. The base, shaft, cups, buds, and flowers were all one piece.
Six branches came out from its sides. Three branches were on one side, and three were on the other side.
Each branch had three cups shaped like almond flowers. Each cup had a bud and a flower. This was true for all six branches.
The shaft had four cups shaped like almond flowers. They had buds and flowers.
A bud was under the first two branches. A bud was under the next two branches. A bud was under the last two branches.
The buds and branches were all one piece with the lampstand. It was hammered pure gold.
He made seven lamps. He also made wick trimmers and trays from pure gold.
He used one talent of pure gold for the lampstand and all its parts.
He made the altar of incense from acacia wood. It was square. It was one cubit long, one cubit wide, and two cubits high. The horns were made as one piece with it.
He covered the top, sides, and horns with pure gold. He made a gold trim around it.
He made two gold rings below the trim. They were on two opposite sides. They held the poles.
He made poles from acacia wood. He covered them with gold.
He made the holy anointing oil. He made pure incense with sweet spices. A perfume maker made them.
He made the altar for burnt offerings from acacia wood. It was square. It was 5 cubits long and 5 cubits wide. It was 3 cubits high.
He made horns on its four corners. The horns were part of the altar. He covered the altar with bronze.
He made all the altar's bronze tools. These were pots, shovels, bowls, forks, and fire pans. He made every tool for it.
He made a bronze grate like a net. It went under the ledge around the altar. It reached halfway up.
He put four bronze rings on the four corners of the grate. The rings held poles.
He made poles from acacia wood. He covered them with bronze.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar. The poles were used to carry it. He made the altar hollow. It was made with boards.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand. He made them from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
He made the courtyard. The south side was 100 cubits long. It had curtains of fine twisted linen.
It had 20 posts and 20 bronze bases. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver.
The north side was also 100 cubits long. It had 20 posts and 20 bronze bases. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver.
The west side was 50 cubits long. It had 10 curtains, 10 posts, and 10 bases. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver.
The east side, toward the sunrise, was 50 cubits long.
On one side of the entrance, the curtains were 15 cubits long. They had 3 posts and 3 bases.
On the other side, the curtains were also 15 cubits long. They had 3 posts and 3 bases.
All the curtains around the courtyard were made of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver. The tops of the posts were covered with silver. All the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.

The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was made with needlework. It was blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen. It was 20 cubits long and 5 cubits high. It was like the courtyard curtains.
It had 4 posts and 4 bronze bases. The hooks, bands, and tops of the posts were silver.
All the tent pegs for the holy tent and the courtyard were bronze.
This is the list of things for the holy tent, the holy tent where God's law was kept. Moses had them counted. The Levites did the work under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, made everything the the LORD commanded Moses.
Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, helped him. He was a skilled worker and designer. He worked with blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.
All the gold used for the work, the gold given as an offering, was 29 talents and 730 shekels. It was weighed by the holy shekel.
The silver from the people who were counted was 100 talents and 1,775 shekels. It was weighed by the holy shekel.
This was half a shekel for each person. It was for everyone 20 years old and older who was counted. There were 603,550 men.
The 100 talents of silver were used to make the bases for the holy tent and the bases for the inner curtain. There were 100 bases. Each base used one talent.
The 1,775 shekels were used to make hooks for the posts, to cover the tops of the posts, and to band them.
The bronze given as an offering was 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance to the tent of meeting, the bronze altar, the bronze grate for it, and all the altar's tools.
He also made the bases around the courtyard, the bases for the courtyard gate, and all the tent pegs for the holy tent and the courtyard.
They used blue, purple, and red yarn to make clothes for serving in the holy place. They also made holy clothes for Aaron, just as the LORD had told Moses.
He made the ephod from gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.
They hammered gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads. They worked the gold into the blue, purple, and red yarn, and the fine linen. A skilled worker did this.
They made shoulder pieces for the ephod. The pieces joined at its two ends.
The waistband of the ephod was made the same way. It was one piece with the ephod. It had gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen. They did this just as the LORD had told Moses.
They put onyx stones in gold settings. They carved the stones like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
They fastened the stones to the shoulder pieces of the ephod. They were memory stones for the sons of Israel. They did this just as the LORD had told Moses.
He made the breastpiece the same way as the ephod. It had gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.
It was square when folded. It was one span long and one span wide.
They put four rows of stones in it. The first row had carnelian, chrysolite, and emerald.
The second row had turquoise, sapphire, and diamond.
The third row had jacinth, agate, and amethyst.
The fourth row had beryl, onyx, and jasper. The stones were set in gold.
The twelve stones stood for the twelve sons of Israel. Each stone had one name carved on it like a seal. There was one name for each tribe.
They made braided chains of pure gold for the breastpiece. They were like cords.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings. They fastened the rings to the two corners of the breastpiece.
They put the two gold chains on the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece.
They fastened the other ends of the chains to the two settings. They put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod in front.
They made two more gold rings. They put them on the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the side next to the ephod.
They made two more gold rings. They put them on the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the front. They were near the seam, above the waistband of the ephod.

They tied the breastpiece to the ephod with a blue cord. The rings of the breastpiece joined the rings of the ephod. The breastpiece stayed above the waistband of the ephod. It did not swing away from the ephod. They did this just as the LORD had told Moses.
They made the robe for the ephod from blue cloth. A weaver made it.
The neck opening was in the middle of the top. It had a woven edge around it so it would not tear.
They made pomegranates from blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen. They put them around the bottom edge of the robe.
They made bells of pure gold. They put the bells between the pomegranates around the bottom edge of the robe.
The bells and pomegranates went around the bottom edge of the robe. This robe was for serving. They did this just as the LORD had told Moses.
They made tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons. A weaver made them.
They made the turban of fine linen. They made the headbands of fine linen. They made the linen underclothes of fine linen.
