They made the sash of fine linen with blue, purple, and red yarn. An embroiderer made it. They did this just as the LORD had told Moses.
They made the holy crown plate from pure gold. They carved on it like a seal: HOLY TO the LORD.
They put a blue cord on it. They used it to fasten the plate to the turban. They did this just as the LORD had told Moses.
So all the work on the holy tent, the meeting tent, was done. The Israelites did all this just as the LORD had told Moses.
Then they brought the holy tent to Moses. They brought the tent and all its things. They brought its hooks, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases.
They brought the red ram skin covering, the fine leather covering, and the curtain.
They brought the ark of the covenant with its poles and the lid.
They brought the table with all its tools and the special bread.
They brought the pure gold lampstand with its lamps. They brought the lamps on the branches and all its tools. They brought the oil for the light.
They brought the gold altar, the anointing oil, the sweet-smelling incense, and the curtain for the tent door.
They brought the bronze altar with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its tools. They brought the washbasin with its stand.

They brought the curtains for the courtyard with its posts and bases. They brought the curtain for the courtyard gate. They brought its ropes and tent pegs. They brought all the tools for serving in the holy tent, the meeting tent.
They brought the woven clothes for serving in the holy place. They brought the holy clothes for Aaron the priest. They brought the clothes for his sons to serve as priests.
The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had told Moses.
Moses looked at all the work. He saw that they had done it just as the LORD had told him. So he blessed them.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"On the first day of the first month, set up the tent where you meet with Me.
Put the box that holds the law inside. Cover it with the curtain.
Bring in the table and set out its bread. Bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.
Put the gold altar for sweet smoke in front of the box that holds the law. Put the curtain at the door of the tent."
"Put the altar for burnt gifts in front of the door of the tent.
Put the wash bowl between the tent and the altar. Put water in it.
Set up the yard all around. Put the curtain at the gate of the yard."
"Take the oil for pouring. Pour oil on the tent and everything in it. Make it holy. Make its things holy. It will be holy.
Pour oil on the altar for burnt gifts and all its things. Make the altar very holy.
Pour oil on the wash bowl and its base. Make it holy."
"Bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tent. Wash them with water.
Dress Aaron in the holy clothes. Pour oil on him and make him holy. Then he can serve Me as priest.
Bring his sons near. Dress them in shirts.
Pour oil on them like you poured oil on their father. They will serve Me as priests. This pouring of oil will make them priests forever, for all their children after them."
Moses did all this. He did just as the LORD told him.
The tent was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.
Moses set up the tent. He put in its bases, boards, bars, and pillars.
He spread the tent over it. He put the cover on top, just as the LORD had told Moses.
He took the law and put it in the box. He put the poles on the box. He put the cover on top of the box.
He brought the box into the tent. He hung the curtain. It covered the box that holds the law, just as the LORD had told Moses.
He put the table in the tent. It was on the north side, outside the curtain.
He set bread on it in a row before the LORD, just as the LORD had told Moses.
He put the lampstand in the tent. It was across from the table, on the south side.
He lit the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had told Moses.
He put the gold altar in the tent, in front of the curtain.
He burned sweet smoke on it, just as the LORD had told Moses.
He put the curtain at the door of the tent.
He put the altar for burnt gifts at the door of the tent. He offered the burnt gift and the grain gift on it, just as the LORD had told Moses.
He put the wash bowl between the tent and the altar. He put water in it for washing.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet from it.
They washed when they went into the tent and when they came near the altar, just as the LORD had told Moses.
Moses set up the yard all around the tent and the altar. He hung the curtain at the gate of the yard. Then Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent. The glory of the LORD filled the tent.
Moses could not go into the tent, because the cloud stayed on it. The glory of the LORD filled the tent.
When the cloud rose from the tent, the people of Israel moved on in all their trips.
If the cloud did not rise, they did not move until it rose.
The cloud of the LORD was over the tent by day. At night, fire was in it. All the people of Israel could see it on all their trips.
The LORD called to Moses. He spoke to him from the tent of meeting. He said,
"Tell the Israelites: When one of you brings an offering to the LORD, you must bring your offering from the animals. Use cattle or sheep.
"If his offering is a burnt offering from the cattle, he must bring a male animal without any flaw. He must bring it to the door of the tent of meeting. Then the LORD will accept him.
"He must put his hand on the head of the burnt offering. Then it will be accepted for him. It will make things right for him.
"He must kill the young bull in front of the LORD. Aaron's sons, the priests, will bring the blood. They will splash the blood all around the altar at the door of the tent of meeting.
"He must skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
"Aaron's sons, the priests, must put fire on the altar. They must stack wood on the fire.
"They must put the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood on the fire on the altar.
"He must wash the inside parts and the legs with water. The priest will burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering. It is a gift by fire. It has a smell the LORD likes.
"If his offering is from the sheep or goats for a burnt offering, he must bring a male animal without any flaw.
"He must kill it on the north side of the altar in front of the LORD. Aaron's sons, the priests, will splash its blood all around the altar.
"The priest must cut it into pieces, with its head and its fat. He must put them on the wood on the fire on the altar.
"He must wash the inside parts and the legs with water. The priest will bring all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering. It is a gift by fire. It has a smell the LORD likes.
"If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he must bring turtledoves or young pigeons.
"The priest will bring it to the altar. He will twist off its head and burn it on the altar. Its blood will be drained on the side of the altar.
"He must remove its food pouch with its feathers. He must throw it on the east side of the altar, where the ashes go.

"He must tear it open by the wings, but not tear it all the way apart. The priest will burn it on the altar on the wood on the fire. It is a burnt offering. It is a gift by fire. It has a smell the LORD likes."
When someone brings a grain offering to the the LORD, it must be fine flour. He must pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

He must bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests. One priest will take a full handful of the fine flour and oil, with all the frankincense, and burn it on the altar. This burned part is a reminder. It is a fire gift with a smell that pleases the the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy, from the fire gifts of the the LORD.
If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it must be fine flour. It can be cakes without yeast mixed with oil, or thin cakes without yeast brushed with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked on a pan, it must be fine flour mixed with oil, without yeast.
Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it must be made of fine flour with oil.
Bring the grain offering made from these things to the the LORD. Present it to the priest, and he will bring it to the altar.
The priest will take the reminder part from the grain offering and burn it on the altar. It is a fire gift with a smell that pleases the the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy, from the fire gifts of the the LORD.
Every grain offering you bring to the the LORD must have no yeast. You must not burn any yeast or honey as a fire gift to the the LORD.
You may bring them to the the LORD as a gift of first things, but they must not go up on the altar as a smell that pleases Him.
Season every grain offering with salt. Do not leave the salt of God's agreement out of your grain offering. Add salt to all your offerings.
If you bring a grain offering of first crops to the the LORD, bring fresh grain, crushed and roasted in fire, as your first-crop grain offering.
Put oil on it and add frankincense. It is a grain offering.
The priest will burn the reminder part from its crushed grain and oil, with all its frankincense. It is a fire gift to the the LORD.
If someone brings a peace offering from the cows, it can be a male or a female. It must have no flaws. Bring it before the LORD.
Put your hand on the head of the gift. Kill it at the door of the meeting tent. Aaron's sons, the priests, will splash the blood all around the altar.
From the peace offering, bring a burned gift to the LORD. Bring the fat that covers the inside parts. Bring all the fat on the inside parts.
Bring the two kidneys and the fat on them near the lower back. Also bring the covering on the liver. Take these off with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons will burn it on the altar. It goes on top of the burned gift on the wood fire. It is a sweet smell to the LORD.
If the peace offering comes from the flock, it can be a male or a female. It must have no flaws.
If someone brings a lamb, bring it before the LORD.
Put your hand on its head. Kill it before the meeting tent. Aaron's sons will splash the blood all around the altar.
From the peace offering, bring a burned gift to the LORD. Bring the whole fat tail. Cut it off near the backbone. Bring the fat that covers the inside parts. Bring all the fat on the inside parts.
Bring the two kidneys and the fat on them near the lower back. Also bring the covering on the liver. Take these off with the kidneys.
The priest will burn it on the altar. It is a food gift to the LORD.
If the offering is a goat, bring it before the LORD.
Put your hand on its head. Kill it before the meeting tent. Aaron's sons will splash the blood all around the altar.
From it, bring a burned gift to the LORD. Bring the fat that covers the inside parts. Bring all the fat on the inside parts.
Bring the two kidneys and the fat on them near the lower back. Also bring the covering on the liver. Take these off with the kidneys.
The priest will burn them on the altar. It is a food gift. It smells sweet. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a rule forever for all your family lines, wherever you live. Do not eat any fat or any blood.
He said, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When anyone sins without meaning to and breaks one of My commands, here is what must be done."
If the anointed priest sins, he brings guilt on the people. He must bring a young bull to the LORD. The bull must have no defect. It is a sin offering.
He must bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD. He must lay his hand on the bull's head. Then he must kill the bull before the LORD.
The anointed priest must take some of the bull's blood and bring it into the tent of meeting.
He must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD. He must do this in front of the curtain of the holy place.

He must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet-smelling incense before the LORD. This altar is in the tent of meeting. He must pour the rest of the bull's blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings. That altar is at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He must take all the fat from the bull of the sin offering. This is the fat that covers the insides and all the fat around the insides.
He must also take the two kidneys and the fat on them near the lower back. He must take the fatty part over the liver, with the kidneys. He must remove these.
The priest must burn them on the altar of burnt offerings, just as the fat is removed from an ox in a peace offering.
He must take the bull's skin, all its meat, its head, its legs, its insides, and its waste.
He must take the whole bull outside the camp. He must take it to a clean place where the ashes are poured out. He must burn it there on a wood fire. It must be burned where the ashes are poured out.
If all the people of Israel sin without meaning to, and they do not know they sinned, and they break one of the LORD's commands, they are guilty.
When they learn about their sin, the people must bring a young bull as a sin offering. They must bring it to the front of the tent of meeting.
The leaders of the people must lay their hands on the bull's head. They must kill the bull before the LORD.
The anointed priest must bring some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting.
He must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD. He must do this in front of the curtain.

He must put some of the blood on the horns of the altar before the LORD. This altar is in the tent of meeting. He must pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings. That altar is at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He must take all the fat from the bull and burn it on the altar.
He must do the same thing with this bull that he did with the sin offering bull. In this way the priest makes things right for them, and they are forgiven.
He must take the bull outside the camp and burn it. He must burn it the same way he burned the first bull. This is the sin offering for the whole people.
If a leader sins without meaning to and breaks one of the commands of the LORD his God, he is guilty.
When he learns about his sin, he must bring a male goat. The goat must have no defect.
He must lay his hand on the goat's head. He must kill the goat where the burnt offerings are killed, before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
The priest must take some of the blood with his finger. He must put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings. He must pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings.
He must burn all the fat on the altar. He must do it the same way the fat is burned in a peace offering. In this way the priest makes things right for him, and he is forgiven.
If one person from the people sins without meaning to and breaks one of the LORD's commands, he is guilty.
When he learns about his sin, he must bring a female goat. The goat must have no defect.
He must lay his hand on the goat's head. He must kill the goat where the burnt offerings are killed.
The priest must take some of the blood with his finger. He must put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings. He must pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

He must take all the fat away, just as the fat is taken away from a peace offering. The priest must burn it on the altar. It is a sweet smell to the LORD. In this way the priest makes things right for him, and he is forgiven.
If he brings a lamb for his sin offering, he must bring a female lamb. The lamb must have no defect.
He must lay his hand on the lamb's head. He must kill the lamb for a sin offering where the burnt offerings are killed.
The priest must take some of the blood with his finger. He must put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings. He must pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

He must take all the fat away. He must do it the same way the fat is taken from a lamb in a peace offering. The priest must burn the fat on the altar with the offerings burned for the LORD. In this way the priest makes things right for him, and he is forgiven.
If someone hears a curse and knows what happened, but does not tell what he saw or knew, he has sinned.
If someone touches something unclean, like a dead wild animal, a dead farm animal, or a dead small crawling thing, and does not know it, he becomes unclean and guilty.
If someone touches something unclean from a person and does not know it at first, but later knows, he is guilty.
If someone makes a promise without thinking, to do good or bad, and later remembers, he is guilty.
When he is guilty of one of these, he must say he did wrong.

He must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the wrong he did. It must be a female lamb or a female goat from the flock. It is a sin offering. The priest will make him right with God for that sin.
If he cannot afford a lamb, he must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the LORD for the wrong he did. One is for a sin offering. The other is for a burnt offering.
He must bring them to the priest. The priest will first offer the bird for the sin offering. He will break its neck, but not cut the head off all the way.
He will sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar. The rest of the blood will be poured out at the bottom of the altar. It is a sin offering.
He will prepare the second bird as a burnt offering, the way the law says. The priest will make him right with God for the sin he did, and he will be forgiven.

If he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he must bring one-tenth of a basket of fine flour for the sin he did. It is a sin offering. He must not put oil on it. He must not put sweet-smelling spice on it.
He must bring it to the priest. The priest will take a handful of it as a special part to remember God. He will burn it on the altar with the other gifts to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
The priest will make him right with God for the sin he did in any of these cases, and he will be forgiven. The rest of the flour will be for the priest, like a grain offering.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,

"If someone sins by mistake with the holy things of the LORD, he must bring a guilt offering to the LORD. It must be a perfect male sheep from the flock. It must be worth the right amount of silver, using the holy weight. This is a guilt offering.

He must pay back the value of the holy thing he harmed. He must also add one-fifth more. He must give it to the priest. Then the priest will make him right with God with the ram guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
If someone sins by doing something the LORD said not to do, even if he did not know it, he is still guilty.
He must bring a perfect male sheep from the flock to the priest as a guilt offering. The priest will make him right with God for the wrong he did without knowing, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering. He was truly guilty before the LORD."
"If a person sins against the LORD by lying to a neighbor about something given to him to keep, or something left with him, or something stolen, or by cheating a neighbor,
or if he finds something lost and lies about it, or swears a false promise about any of these sins,
then he has sinned and is guilty. He must give back what he stole or took by force, or the thing left with him, or the lost thing he found.
He must pay for whatever he lied about. He must pay the full amount plus one-fifth more. He must give it to the owner on the day he says he is guilty.
Then he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD through the priest: a ram from the flock with no flaw, worth the right amount.
The priest will make things right for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any of these things he has done."
"Command Aaron and his sons: This is the rule for the burnt offering. The burnt offering must stay on the fire on the altar all night until morning. The fire on the altar must keep burning.
The priest must put on his linen clothes and linen underclothes. He must take the ashes from the burnt offering off the fire and put them beside the altar.
Then he must take off those clothes and put on other clothes. He must carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar must keep burning. It must not go out. Each morning the priest must put wood on the fire. He must place the burnt offering on it. He must burn the fat parts of the peace offerings on it.
The fire must keep burning on the altar all the time. It must not go out. "
This is the rule for the grain offering. Aaron's sons must bring it before the LORD, in front of the altar.
The priest must take a handful of fine flour and oil from it, and all the sweet-smelling resin on it. He must burn this part on the altar. It is a sweet smell to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons must eat what is left. They must eat it as bread without yeast in a holy place. They must eat it in the yard of the meeting tent.
It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their share of My gifts burned by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Any male from Aaron's family may eat it. It is their share forever from the gifts burned by fire to the LORD for all time. Anything that touches these gifts will become holy."

"This is the offering Aaron and his sons must bring to the LORD on the day he becomes priest: a small amount of fine flour as a regular grain offering. They must bring half in the morning and half in the evening.
It must be made with oil on a flat pan. Bring it well mixed. Bring it as baked pieces of grain offering, a sweet smell to the LORD.
The priest who takes his place must make it. It is a rule forever for the LORD. It must be burned completely.
Every grain offering from a priest must be burned completely. It must not be eaten."
"Tell Aaron and his sons: This is the rule for the sin offering. The sin offering must be killed where the burnt offering is killed, before the LORD. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it must eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the yard of the meeting tent.
Anything that touches its meat will become holy. If any of its blood gets on a piece of clothing, you must wash that clothing in a holy place. "
The clay pot used to boil it must be broken. If it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and washed with water.
Any male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood was brought into the meeting tent to pay for sin in the holy place. It must be burned."
This is the rule for the guilt offering. It is very holy.
The guilt offering must be killed where the burnt offering is killed. The priest must splash its blood all around the altar.
He must bring all its fat. He must bring the fat tail and the fat that covers the inside parts.
He must bring the two kidneys and the fat on them near the lower back. He must bring the part of the liver near the kidneys. He must take it off.
The priest must burn these on the altar. They are a gift made by fire to the LORD. This is a guilt offering.
Every male priest may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is very holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering. The same rule is for both. The priest who uses it to make up for sin keeps it.
If a priest gives a burnt offering for someone, the skin of that burnt offering belongs to that priest.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, cooked in a pan, or made on a flat pan belongs to the priest who gives it.
Every grain offering, dry or mixed with oil, belongs to all of Aaron's sons in the same way.
This is the rule for the peace offering that a person may give to the LORD.

If he gives it to say thank you, he must bring flat bread with no yeast mixed with oil, thin bread with no yeast spread with oil, and cakes of good flour mixed with oil. He must bring them with the thank offering.
He must also bring bread with yeast with his peace offering of thanks.
He must bring one of these as a gift to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offerings.
The meat of the thank offering must be eaten on the day he gives it. None of it may be left until morning.
If the offering is a promise gift or a free gift, it may be eaten on the day he gives it. What is left may be eaten the next day.
But any meat left until the third day must be burned up.

If any meat from his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not count for the person who gave it. It will be a very bad thing. The person who eats it will be guilty.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten. It must be burned up. But meat that is clean may be eaten by anyone who is clean.
But if anyone who is unclean eats the meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person will be removed from his people.

If anyone touches anything unclean, whether a person's uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, gross thing, and then eats the meat of the LORD's peace offering, that person will be removed from his people.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses.
He said, "Speak to the Israelites and say, 'You must not eat the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.'"
The fat of an animal that died or was torn by wild animals may be used for other things. But you must not eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal given to the LORD as a gift by fire will be removed from his people.
You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal, anywhere you live.
Anyone who eats blood will be removed from his people.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses.
He said, "Speak to the Israelites and say, 'When anyone gives a peace offering to the LORD, he must bring to the LORD a gift from his peace offering.
He must bring it with his own hands. He must bring the fat and the breast. He must wave the breast before the LORD.
The priest must burn the fat on the altar. But the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
You must give the right thigh to the priest. It is a gift from your peace offerings.
The priest who gives the blood and fat of the peace offering gets the right thigh as his share.

I have taken the breast that is waved and the thigh that is given from the Israelites' peace offerings. I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons. This is their share from the Israelites forever.'"
This is the share of the gifts burned for the LORD for Aaron and his sons. It was given on the day they were brought to serve as priests to the LORD.
On the day oil was poured on them, the LORD commanded that the Israelites give this to them. It is a share that lasts forever for all the years to come.
This is the rule for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the offering when priests are set apart, and the peace offering.
The LORD commanded these to Moses on Mount Sinai. He commanded them on the day He told the Israelites to bring their gifts to the LORD in the Sinai desert.
He said, "Take Aaron and his sons with him. Bring the clothes, the special oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of bread without yeast.
Bring all the people together at the door of the meeting tent."
Moses did what the LORD told him to do. The people came together at the door of the meeting tent.
Moses said to them, "This is what the LORD said to do."
Moses brought Aaron and his sons near. He washed them with water.
He put a shirt on Aaron. He tied a belt around him. He put a robe on him. He put a special vest on him. He tied the vest's belt around him and fastened it.
He put the chest piece on him. He put the Urim and Thummim inside it.
He put the head wrap on Aaron's head. He put the gold plate, the holy crown, on the front of the head wrap. He did this as the LORD had told Moses.
Moses took the special oil. He poured it on the meeting tent and on everything in it. He made them holy for the LORD.
He sprinkled the oil on the altar seven times. He poured oil on the altar and on all its tools, and on the wash bowl and its stand, to make them holy.
He poured some of the oil on Aaron's head. He poured it on him to make him holy.
Moses brought Aaron's sons near. He put shirts on them. He tied belts around them. He put caps on them. He did this as the LORD had told Moses.
Moses brought the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on the bull's head.

Moses killed the bull. He took the blood. He put it on the corners of the altar with his finger. He put blood all around. He poured the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. This made the altar holy. It paid for sin.
Moses took all the fat from inside the bull, the best part of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat. He burned them on the altar.
He burned the bull, its skin, its meat, and its waste with fire outside the camp. He did this as the LORD had told Moses.
Moses brought the ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on the ram's head.
Moses killed it. He threw the blood all around the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces. He burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the inside parts and the legs with water. Then Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering. Its smell pleased the LORD. It was a gift burned for the LORD. He did this as the LORD had told Moses.
Moses brought the second ram. It was the ram used to make them priests. Aaron and his sons put their hands on the ram's head.
Moses killed it. He took some blood and put it on the tip of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

He brought Aaron's sons near. He put some blood on the tips of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Moses threw the blood all around the altar.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat from inside, the best part of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right leg.
From the basket of bread without yeast that was before the LORD, he took one loaf of bread without yeast, one loaf with oil, and one thin cake. He put them on the fat and on the right leg.
He put all of them on the hands of Aaron and on the hands of his sons. He waved them before the LORD.
Moses took them from their hands. He burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering. This was an offering to make them priests. Its smell pleased the LORD. It was a gift burned for the LORD.
Moses took the chest part. He waved it before the LORD. This part was for Moses. It came from the ram used to make them priests. He did this as the LORD had told Moses.

Moses took some of the special oil and some of the blood from the altar. He sprinkled them on Aaron and on his clothes. He sprinkled them on his sons and on their clothes. He made Aaron and his clothes holy. He made his sons and their clothes holy.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat at the door of the meeting tent. Eat it there. Eat the bread in the basket for making priests. I told you to do this. I said, 'Aaron and his sons must eat it.'
Burn what is left of the meat and the bread with fire.
You must not go out from the door of the meeting tent for seven days, until your time of being made priests is done. It takes seven days to finish.
Do this because the LORD told you to do it today. It pays for your sin.
Stay at the door of the meeting tent day and night for seven days. Keep the LORD's rule. Then you will not die. I was told to tell you this."
Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD told them to do through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the elders of Israel.
Moses said to Aaron, "Take a young bull for a sin offering. Take a ram for a burnt offering. They must have no flaws. Offer them to the LORD."
Moses said, "Tell the Israelites, 'Take a male goat for a sin offering. Take a calf and a lamb. They must be one year old. They must have no flaws. They are for a burnt offering.'
Take an ox and a ram for peace offerings. Sacrifice them to the LORD. Take a grain offering mixed with oil. Today the LORD will show Himself to you."
The people brought what Moses said. They came near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said, "This is what the LORD told you to do. Then the glory of the LORD will show itself to you."
Moses said to Aaron, "Go to the altar. Make your sin offering and burnt offering. Pay for your sins and the people's sins. Make the people's offering. Pay for their sins, just like the LORD said."
Aaron went to the altar. He killed the calf for his sin offering.
Aaron's sons brought him the blood. He dipped his finger in it. He put it on the horns of the altar. He poured the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.
He burned the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar. He did this just like the LORD told Moses.
He burned the meat and skin outside the camp.
He killed the burnt offering. Aaron's sons gave him the blood. He sprinkled it all around the altar.
They gave him the burnt offering cut into pieces, with the head. He burned them on the altar.
He washed the inside parts and legs. He burned them on the altar with the burnt offering.
He brought the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering. He killed it. He paid for sin with it, just like the first one.
He brought the burnt offering. He did it the right way.
He brought the grain offering. He filled his hand with it. He burned it on the altar, besides the morning burnt offering.
He killed the ox and ram for the people. They were peace offerings. Aaron's sons gave him the blood. He sprinkled it all around the altar.
He took the fat from the ox and ram. He took the fat tail, the covering fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
They put the fats on the chest pieces. He burned the fats on the altar.
Aaron lifted the chest pieces and the right thigh toward the LORD. He waved them, just like Moses said.
Aaron raised his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then he came down from making the sin offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the meeting tent. They came out and blessed the people. The glory of the LORD showed itself to all the people.
Fire came from the LORD. It burned up the burnt offering and the fats on the altar. All the people saw it. They shouted with joy and fell on their faces.
Nadab and Abihu were Aaron's sons. Each man took his pan. They put fire in the pans and added incense. They brought fire to the LORD that He did not ask for.
Fire came from the LORD. It burned them up. They died in front of the LORD.
Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD said: 'I will show that I am holy among those close to Me. I will be honored by all the people.'" Aaron said nothing.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan. They were sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle. Moses said, "Come here. Carry your relatives away from the holy place. Take them outside the camp."
They came and carried them in their shirts. They took them outside the camp, just as Moses said.

Moses said to Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar, "Do not mess up your hair. Do not tear your clothes. If you do, you will die. The LORD will be angry with all the people. But all the Israelites may cry for the men the LORD burned.
Do not leave the door of the meeting tent. If you do, you will die. The LORD's special oil is on you." They did as Moses said.
Then the LORD spoke to Aaron.
He said, "You and your sons must not drink wine or strong drink when you go into the meeting tent. If you do, you will die. This rule is for all time, for your family after you.
You must tell the difference between holy things and common things. You must tell the difference between clean things and unclean things.
You must teach the Israelites all the rules the LORD gave them through Moses."
Moses said to Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar, "Take the grain gift that is left from the food gifts given to the LORD. Eat it without yeast beside the altar. It is very holy.
Eat it in the holy place. It is your share and your sons' share from the LORD's food gifts. The LORD told me to do this.

But you, your sons, and your daughters may eat the breast meat that was waved and the thigh meat that was given. Eat it in a clean place. The LORD gave these to you and your sons. They are your share from the peace gifts of the Israelites.

The given thigh and the waved breast must be brought with the fat parts of the food gifts. Wave them before the LORD. This will be your share and your children's share forever. The LORD commanded this."
Moses asked about the goat for the sin gift. He found it had been burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's other sons. He asked, "
Why did you not eat the sin gift in the holy place? It is very holy. The LORD gave it to you to take away the people's wrong. You were to make things right for them before the LORD.
Its blood was not brought into the holy place. So you should have eaten the goat in the holy place, as I told you."
Aaron replied to Moses, "Today my sons gave their sin gift and burnt gift to the LORD. But bad things have happened to me. Would the LORD be happy if I ate the sin gift today?"
Moses heard this and was satisfied.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, "Speak to the Israelites.
Among all the animals on the land, these are the ones you may eat.
You may eat any animal that has a split hoof in two parts and chews its food again. "
But do not eat these animals. They chew their food again, but they do not have a split hoof. The camel is one. Its hoof is not split, so it is not clean for you.
The rock badger chews its food again, but it does not have a split hoof. It is not clean for you.
The hare chews its food again, but it does not have a split hoof. It is not clean for you.
The pig has a split hoof, but it does not chew its food again. It is not clean for you.
Do not eat their meat. Do not touch their dead bodies. They are not clean for you. "
You may eat anything that lives in the water. In the seas or in rivers, you may eat anything that has fins and scales.
But anything in the water that does not have fins and scales is gross to you. This includes the small living things in the water.
They are gross to you. Do not eat them. Their dead bodies are gross to you.
Anything in the water without fins and scales is gross to you. "
These birds are gross. Do not eat them: the eagle, the vulture, and the black vulture.
The kite and the falcon of any kind.
The ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, and the hawk of any kind.
The little owl, the cormorant, and the great owl.
The white owl, the desert owl, and the osprey.
The stork, the heron of any kind, the hoopoe, and the bat. "
All flying bugs that walk on four legs are gross to you.
But you may eat some flying bugs that walk on four legs. Eat the ones that have strong back legs for jumping on the ground.
You may eat these: the locust, the katydid, the cricket, and the grasshopper. Eat each kind.
All other flying bugs with four legs are gross to you. "
These animals make you not clean. Anyone who touches their dead bodies is not clean until evening.
Anyone who carries part of their dead body must wash his clothes. He is not clean until evening.
These animals are not clean for you: any animal that has a split hoof but not in two parts, or does not chew its food again. Anyone who touches them is not clean.
Any animal that walks on four legs and walks on its paws is not clean for you. Anyone who touches its dead body is not clean until evening.
Anyone who carries its dead body must wash his clothes. He is not clean until evening. These animals are not clean for you. "
These small animals that crawl on the ground are not clean for you: the mole, the mouse, and the great lizard of any kind.
The gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the sand lizard, and the chameleon.
These are not clean for you. Anyone who touches them when they are dead is not clean until evening. "

If one of these dead animals falls on something, that thing is not clean. It does not matter if it is wood, clothes, skin, or a sack. Any tool used for work must be put in water. It stays not clean until evening. Then it is clean.
If one falls into a clay pot, everything inside is not clean. You must break the pot.
Any food that water touches in that pot is not clean. Any drink in that pot is not clean. "
Anything their dead body falls on is not clean. An oven or a stove must be broken into pieces. They are not clean, and they are not clean for you.
A spring or a well with water in it stays clean. But anyone who touches the dead body in it is not clean.
If part of a dead body falls on seed that is planted, the seed is still clean.
But if water is put on the seed and part of the dead body falls on it, it is not clean for you. "
If an animal you may eat dies, anyone who touches its dead body is not clean until evening.
Anyone who eats part of its dead body must wash his clothes. He is not clean until evening. Anyone who carries the dead body must wash his clothes. He is not clean until evening. "
Every small animal that crawls on the ground is gross. Do not eat it.
You must not eat them, because they are gross. This includes any animal that crawls on its belly, walks on four legs, or has many legs.
Do not make yourselves gross with these crawling things. Do not make yourselves not clean with them. Do not let them make you not clean. "
I am the LORD your God. Make yourselves clean and holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves not clean with any crawling thing on the ground.
I am the LORD. I brought you out of Egypt to be your God. Be holy, because I am holy. "
This is the law for animals, birds, water animals, and all living things that crawl in the water or on the ground.
You must learn the difference between what is not clean and what is clean. You must learn the difference between animals you may eat and animals you may not eat."
"Speak to the people of Israel. Tell them: When a woman has a baby boy, she is not clean for seven days. This is like the time of her monthly bleeding.
On the eighth day, the boy must be circumcised.
Then the mother must wait thirty-three days to be made clean from her bleeding. She must not touch anything holy, and she must not go into the holy place until her days of cleaning are done.
"If she has a baby girl, she is not clean for two weeks, like her monthly bleeding. Then she must wait sixty-six days to be made clean from her bleeding.

When her days of cleaning are done, for a boy or a girl, she must bring these gifts to the priest at the meeting tent: a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or dove for a sin offering.
The priest will offer them before the LORD. He will pay for her sin, and she will be clean from her bleeding. This is the rule for a woman who has a baby, boy or girl.
If she cannot afford a lamb, she must bring two doves or two young pigeons. One is for a burnt offering, and one is for a sin offering. The priest will pay for her sin, and she will be clean."
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
“If a person has a raised spot, a scab, or a bright spot on the skin, and it may be a skin disease, he must be brought to Aaron the priest, or to one of his sons who is a priest.
The priest must look at the spot. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot looks deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease. The priest will say the person is not clean.
“If the bright spot is white but does not look deeper than the skin, and the hair has not turned white, the priest must keep the person away from others for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest must look again. If the spot has not changed and has not spread, the priest must keep him away for seven more days.
On the seventh day the priest must look again. If the spot has faded and has not spread, the person must wash his clothes. Then he is clean.
“But if the scab spreads on the skin after he was shown to the priest to be made clean, he must be shown to the priest again.
If the priest sees that the scab has spread, he must say the person is not clean. It is a skin disease.
“When a person has a skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.
The priest must look. If there is a white raised spot, and the hair has turned white, and there is raw flesh in the spot,
it is an old skin disease. The priest must say the person is not clean. He must not keep him away, because he is already not clean.
“If the skin disease spreads all over the skin, from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
the priest must look. If it covers all his skin, he must say the person is clean. It has all turned white, so he is clean.
But if raw flesh shows up, he is not clean.
The priest must look at the raw flesh and say the person is not clean. Raw flesh is not clean. It is a skin disease.
If the raw flesh turns white again, he must come to the priest.
The priest must look. If the spot has turned white, the priest must say the person is clean. Then he is clean.
“If a person has a boil on the skin and it heals,
and then a white raised spot or a reddish-white spot appears where the boil was, he must be shown to the priest.
The priest must look. If it looks deeper than the skin and the hair has turned white, it is a skin disease that has broken out in the boil. The priest must say the person is not clean.
If the hair has not turned white, and it is not deeper than the skin, but it is faded, the priest must keep him away for seven days.
If it spreads on the skin, the priest must say it is not clean. It is a skin disease.
If the spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil. The priest must say the person is clean.
“If a person has a burn on the skin, and the healed burn has a reddish-white or white spot,

the priest must look at it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and it looks deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must say the person is not clean. It is a skin disease.
If the hair has not turned white, and it is not deeper than the skin, but it is faded, the priest must keep him away for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest must look. If it has spread on the skin, the priest must say the person is not clean. It is a skin disease.
If the spot stays in its place and does not spread, and it is faded, it is only the scar from the burn. The priest must say the person is clean.
“If a man or a woman has a spot on the head or in the beard,
the priest must look at it. If it looks deeper than the skin, and the hair in it is yellow and thin, it is a scaly skin disease on the head or beard. The priest must say the person is not clean.
If the spot does not look deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest must keep the person away for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest must look. If the spot has not spread, and there is no yellow hair, and it does not look deeper than the skin,
the person must shave, but not the spot. The priest must keep him away for seven more days.
On the seventh day the priest must look. If the spot has not spread and does not look deeper than the skin, the priest must say the person is clean. He must wash his clothes, and he is clean.
“But if the spot spreads after he was made clean,
the priest must look. If it has spread, the priest must say the person is not clean. He does not need to look for yellow hair. The person is not clean.
If the spot stays the same and black hair grows in it, the spot has healed. The person is clean. The priest must say he is clean.
“If a man or a woman has white spots on the skin,
and the priest sees that the spots are dull white, it is only a rash on the skin. The person is clean.
“If a man loses his hair and becomes bald, he is clean.
If he loses hair at the front of his head, he is bald in front, but he is clean.
If there is a reddish-white spot on his bald head or forehead, it is a skin disease breaking out.
The priest must look at it. If the raised spot is reddish-white, like a skin disease on the skin of the body,
the man is sick with a skin disease. He is not clean. The priest must say he is not clean, because of the spot on his head.
“The person with the skin disease must wear torn clothes. His hair must be loose. He must cover the lower part of his face. He must call out, ‘Not clean! Not clean!’
He is not clean as long as he has the spot. He must live alone. He must stay outside the camp.
“If a garment has a spot that may be a skin disease, in wool or linen,
or in woven or knitted cloth of linen or wool, or in leather, or in anything made of leather,
and the spot is greenish or reddish, it must be shown to the priest.
The priest must look at the spot and keep the garment away from others for seven days.

On the seventh day the priest must look. If the spot has spread in the cloth, in the woven or knitted part, or in the leather, or in anything made of leather, it is a spreading mildew. It is not clean.
He must burn the garment, the woven or knitted cloth, the wool or linen, or any leather thing that has the spot. It is a spreading mildew, so it must be burned.
“If the priest sees that the spot has not spread in the cloth, in the woven or knitted part, or in the leather,
the priest must order the spot to be washed. Then he must keep the garment away for seven more days.
After it is washed, the priest must look. If the spot has not changed, even if it has not spread, it is not clean. It must be burned. It is a bad mildew, on the front or back.
If the priest sees that the spot has faded after washing, he must tear it out of the cloth, the leather, the woven part, or the knitted part.
If it shows up again in the cloth, in the woven or knitted part, or in the leather, it is spreading. The spot must be burned.
If the spot is gone after washing, the cloth, the woven or knitted part, or the leather must be washed again. Then it is clean.
This is the law for a spot that may be a skin disease in wool or linen cloth, in woven or knitted cloth, or in leather. It tells how to make it clean or not clean.”
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"These are the rules for a person with a skin disease when he is made clean. He must be brought to the priest.
The priest must go outside the camp and look at him. If the skin disease is healed,
the priest must order two clean birds, cedar wood, red yarn, and hyssop for the person who is being made clean.
"The priest must order one bird to be killed over fresh water in a clay pot.
He must take the live bird, the cedar wood, the red yarn, and the hyssop. He must dip them and the live bird in the blood of the bird that was killed. The blood must be mixed with the water.
He must sprinkle the person who is being made clean seven times. Then the priest must say the person is clean. He must let the live bird go in the open field.
"The person must wash his clothes. He must shave off all his hair. He must bathe in water. Then he is clean. After that, he may come into the camp. But he must stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day, he must shave all his hair again. He must shave his head, his beard, and his eyebrows. He must wash his clothes. He must bathe in water. Then he is clean.

"On the eighth day, he must take two male lambs with nothing wrong with them. He must take one young female sheep one year old with nothing wrong with it. He must take three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
The priest must bring the person who is being made clean and these offerings before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
The priest must take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering. He must take the log of oil. He must wave them before the LORD.
He must kill the lamb in the holy place where the sin offering and the burnt offering are killed. The guilt offering belongs to the priest, like the sin offering. It is most holy.

"The priest must take some of the blood of the guilt offering. He must put it on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest must take some of the oil from the log. He must pour it into the palm of his own left hand.
He must dip the finger of his right hand in the oil. He must sprinkle some of the oil before the LORD seven times.

He must put some of the oil left in his palm on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot. He must put it on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil in his palm must be put on the head of the person being made clean. The priest must make atonement for him before the LORD.
"Then the priest must offer the sin offering. He must make atonement for the person being made clean from his uncleanness. After that, he must kill the burnt offering.
The priest must burn the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. He must make atonement for the person. Then he is clean.

"If the person is poor and cannot afford these offerings, he must take one male lamb for a guilt offering. It must be waved to make atonement for him. He must take one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
He must take two doves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford. One must be a sin offering, and the other must be a burnt offering.
On the eighth day, he must bring them to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting, before the LORD, to be made clean.
"The priest must take the lamb for the guilt offering and the log of oil. He must wave them before the LORD.
He must kill the lamb. He must take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest must pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.
He must dip the finger of his right hand in the oil. He must sprinkle some of the oil before the LORD seven times.

He must put some of the oil on the right earlobe of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot. He must put it on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil must be put on the head of the person being made clean. The priest must make atonement for him before the LORD.

"He must offer one of the doves or pigeons, whichever the person can afford. One must be a sin offering, and the other a burnt offering, along with the grain offering. The priest must make atonement for the person before the LORD. Then he is clean.
These are the rules for a person with a skin disease who cannot afford the usual offerings for being made clean.
This is the law for a person who has a skin disease.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
"When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving to you, I will put a disease like mold in a house in the land you own.
"The owner of the house must come and tell the priest. He must say, "I see something like a disease in my house."

"Then the priest must order the house to be emptied before he comes to look at the disease. Then everything in the house will not become unclean. After that, the priest must come in to look at the house.
"He must look at the disease. If the disease is in the walls of the house, with green or red marks that look sunk in,
the priest must go out to the door of the house. He must shut up the house for seven days.
"On the seventh day, the priest must come back and look. If the disease has spread in the walls of the house,
the priest must order the stones with the disease to be taken out. They must be thrown outside the city in an unclean place.
He must have the inside of the house scraped all around. The dust that is scraped off must be thrown outside the city in an unclean place.
They must take other stones and put them in place of the old stones. They must take new clay and plaster the house.
"If the disease comes back and breaks out in the house after the stones are taken out and the house is scraped and plastered,
the priest must come and look. If the disease has spread, it is a bad mold in the house. It is unclean.
He must tear down the house. He must carry its stones, its wood, and all the broken pieces of the house outside the city to an unclean place.
"Anyone who goes into the house while it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps in the house or eats in the house must wash his clothes.
"If the priest comes back and sees that the disease has not spread after the house was plastered, he must say the house is clean. The disease is healed.
"To make the house clean, he must take two birds, cedar wood, red yarn, and hyssop.
He must kill one bird over fresh water in a clay pot.
"He must take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the red yarn, and the live bird. He must dip them in the blood of the bird that was killed and in the water. He must sprinkle the house seven times.
He must make the house clean with the blood of the bird, the water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the red yarn.
He must let the live bird go in the open field outside the city. He must make atonement for the house. Then it is clean.
"These are the rules for every kind of skin disease, for a scab,
for mold in clothing or in a house,
and for a swelling, a rash, or a bright spot.
They teach when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law for a skin disease."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If a man has a flow from his body, that flow is not clean.
This is how he is not clean from his flow: If the flow comes out or if it is stopped, he is not clean.
Any bed he lies on is not clean. Any seat he sits on is not clean.
Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will not be clean until evening.
Anyone who sits on a seat the man sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will not be clean until evening.
Anyone who touches the man's skin must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will not be clean until evening.
If the man spits on a clean person, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will not be clean until evening.
Any saddle he rides on is not clean.
Anyone who touches anything that was under him will not be clean until evening. Anyone who carries those things must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will not be clean until evening.
If the man touches someone without first washing his hands in water, the person he touched must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will not be clean until evening.
Any clay pot he touches must be broken. Any wood thing must be washed in water.
"When the man is clean from his flow, he must count seven days. Then he must wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water. Then he will be clean.
On the eighth day, he must take two doves or two young pigeons. He must come to the the LORD at the door of the meeting tent and give them to the priest.
The priest will make one bird a sin offering and the other a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make him right with the the LORD because of his flow.
"When a man has a flow of seed, he must bathe his whole body in water. He will not be clean until evening.
Any clothes or leather that have seed on them must be washed in water. They will not be clean until evening.
If a man lies with a woman and seed comes out, both must bathe in water. They will not be clean until evening.
"When a woman has a flow of blood from her body, she will not be clean for seven days because of her period. Anyone who touches her will not be clean until evening.
Anything she lies on during her period is not clean. Anything she sits on is not clean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will not be clean until evening.
Anyone who touches any seat she sits on must wash his clothes and bathe in water. That person will not be clean until evening.
If something on her bed or seat is touched, it will not be clean until evening.
If a man lies with her, he becomes not clean like her. He will not be clean for seven days. Every bed he lies on will not be clean.
"If a woman has blood flowing for many days outside her period, or if it flows past her regular period, she will not be clean all the days of her flow, just like during her period.
Any bed or seat she uses during her flow is not clean, just like during her period.
Anyone who touches these things will not be clean. He must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will not be clean until evening.
"When she is clean from her flow, she must count seven days. After that, she will be clean.
On the eighth day, she must take two doves or two young pigeons. She must bring them to the priest at the door of the meeting tent.
The priest will make one bird a sin offering and the other a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make her right with the the LORD because of her flow that made her not clean.
"You must keep the Israelites away from things that make them not clean. Then they will not die by making My holy tent not clean. It is among them.
"This is the law for a person with a flow. It is also for a man who has a flow of seed and becomes not clean.
It is also for a woman during her period, and for any man or woman who has a flow, or for a man who lies with a woman who is not clean."
The LORD spoke to Moses after two of Aaron's sons died. They had come too close to the LORD, and they died.

The LORD said to Moses, “Tell your brother Aaron not to go into the Holy Place behind the curtain at just any time. He must not go before the mercy seat on the ark, or he will die. I will appear in a cloud over the mercy seat.
This is how Aaron must come into the Holy Place. He must bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

“Aaron must put on the holy linen clothes. He must wear a linen shirt, linen underclothes, a linen belt, and a linen turban. These are holy clothes. He must wash his body with water and then put them on.
From the people of Israel, he must take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
“Aaron must bring the bull for his sin offering. He must make things right for himself and for his family.
He must take the two goats and bring them to the LORD at the door of the meeting tent.
“Aaron must draw lots for the two goats. One lot is for the LORD, and one lot is for Azazel.
Aaron must bring the goat that gets the lot for the LORD. He must offer it as a sin offering.
The goat that gets the lot for Azazel must be brought alive to the LORD. It will be used to make things right. Then it will be sent into the desert for Azazel.
“Aaron must bring the bull for his sin offering. He must make things right for himself and his family. Then he must kill the bull.
He must take a fire pan full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD. He must take two handfuls of fine incense. He must bring them behind the curtain.
He must put the incense on the fire before the LORD. The smoke from the incense must cover the mercy seat over the ark. Then he will not die.
“He must take some of the bull's blood. He must sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the mercy seat, on the east side. He must sprinkle the blood seven times in front of the mercy seat.

He must kill the goat for the people's sin offering. He must bring its blood behind the curtain. He must do with it as he did with the bull's blood. He must sprinkle it on the mercy seat and in front of the mercy seat.

“He must make things right for the Holy Place. The people of Israel have made it unclean with their sins. He must make things right for the meeting tent too. It stays among them even when they are unclean.

No person may be in the meeting tent when Aaron goes in to make things right in the Holy Place. He must stay out until Aaron comes out. Aaron must make things right for himself, his family, and all the people.

“Then Aaron must go out to the altar before the LORD. He must make things right for it. He must take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood. He must put it on the horns of the altar all around.
He must sprinkle some of the blood on the altar with his finger seven times. This will clean the altar and make it holy. It will clean it from the sins of the people of Israel.
“When Aaron has finished making things right for the Holy Place, the meeting tent, and the altar, he must bring the live goat.

Aaron must put both hands on the head of the live goat. He must tell God about all the wrong things the people of Israel have done. He must tell about all their sins. He must put their sins on the goat's head. Then he must send the goat into the desert with a man who is ready for this job.
The goat will carry all their wrongs to a faraway place. The man will let the goat go in the desert.
“Then Aaron must go into the meeting tent. He must take off the linen clothes he wore in the Holy Place. He must leave them there.

He must wash his body with water in a holy place. Then he must put on his own clothes. He must come out and offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering. He must make things right for himself and for the people.
“He must burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The man who sent the goat away for Azazel must wash his clothes. He must wash his body with water. Then he may come back into the camp.
“The bull and the goat for the sin offering must be taken outside the camp. Their blood was brought into the Holy Place to make things right. Their skin, meat, and waste must be burned with fire.
The person who burns them must wash his clothes. He must wash his body with water. Then he may come back into the camp.

“This is a rule that lasts forever. On the tenth day of the seventh month, you must make yourselves humble. You must not do any work. This is for people born among you and for strangers living among you.
On that day, I will make things right for you. I will make you clean. You will be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
It is a Sabbath day of complete rest. You must make yourselves humble. This is a rule that lasts forever.
“The priest who is chosen and set apart to serve in his father's place must make things right. He must wear the holy linen clothes.
He must make things right for the Most Holy Place, the meeting tent, and the altar. He must make things right for the priests and all the people.
This is a rule that lasts forever. Once a year, make things right for the people of Israel for all their sins.” Aaron did what the LORD told Moses.
"Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites. Tell them this is what the LORD commands.
If an Israelite kills an ox, a lamb, or a goat in the camp or outside the camp,
and does not bring it to the door of the meeting tent to offer it to the LORD, that man has spilled blood. He must be sent away from his people." "
This is so the Israelites will bring their sacrifices to the priest at the door of the meeting tent. They will not offer them in the open field. They will offer them as peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest will sprinkle the blood on the LORD's altar at the door of the meeting tent. He will burn the fat. It will smell sweet to the LORD.
They must not offer sacrifices to goat idols anymore. They used to follow them. This rule will last for them and their children forever." "
Also tell them: If an Israelite or a foreigner living with them offers a burned offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the door of the meeting tent to do it for the LORD, that man must be sent away from his people." "
If an Israelite or a foreigner living with them eats blood, I will turn against that person. I will send them away from their people.
The life of the body is in the blood. I gave it to you to pay for your lives on the altar. The blood pays for life because life is in it.
So I told the Israelites that no one among you may eat blood, and no foreigner living with you may eat blood." "
If an Israelite or a foreigner living with them hunts an animal or a bird that may be eaten, he must pour out its blood and cover it with dirt.
The life of every creature is in its blood. So I told the Israelites not to eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is in its blood. Anyone who eats it must be sent away." "

If any person, Israelite or foreigner, eats an animal that died on its own or was torn by another animal, he must wash his clothes and bathe in water. He will not be clean until evening. Then he will be clean.
If he does not wash his clothes or bathe his body, he will be guilty."
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Speak to the Israelites. Tell them: I am the LORD your God. "
Do not do what people in Egypt did, where you lived. Do not do what people in Canaan do. I am bringing you there. Do not follow their ways. "
You must follow My rules and keep My laws. Live by them. I am the LORD your God. "
Keep My rules and My laws. A person who does them will live by them. I am the LORD. "
No one may have sex with a close family member. I am the LORD. "
Do not have sex with your father or your mother. She is your mother. Do not have sex with her. "
Do not have sex with your father's wife. She is your father's wife. "
Do not have sex with your sister. She may be your father's daughter or your mother's daughter. She may have been born at home or somewhere else. Do not have sex with her. "
Do not have sex with your granddaughter, whether she is your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter. They are your own family. Do not have sex with them. "
Do not have sex with your father's wife's daughter if she was born to your father. She is your sister. Do not have sex with her. "
Do not have sex with your father's sister. She is your father's close family. "
Do not have sex with your mother's sister. She is your mother's close family. "
Do not have sex with your uncle's wife. She is your aunt. "
Do not have sex with your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife. Do not have sex with her. "
Do not have sex with your brother's wife. She belongs to your brother. "
Do not have sex with a woman and her daughter. Do not take her granddaughter, her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter, to have sex with her. They are her close family. That is very wrong. "
Do not marry a woman and her sister at the same time. Do not have sex with one while the other is alive. "
Do not have sex with a woman during her monthly period. "
Do not have sex with your neighbor's wife. That would make you unclean. "
Do not give any of your children to be burned for Molech. Do not misuse the name of your God. I am the LORD. "
Do not have sex with a man the way you would with a woman. That is a terrible sin. "
Do not have sex with any animal. That makes you unclean. A woman must not let an animal mate with her. That is wrong. "
Do not make yourselves unclean by doing any of these things. The nations I am sending away before you became unclean by doing them. "
The land became unclean. I punished it for its sin. The land spit out the people living there. "
You must keep My rules and My laws. Do not do any of these terrible things. This is for people born here and for strangers living among you. "
The people who lived in this land before you did all these terrible things. That made the land unclean. "
If you make the land unclean, it may spit you out too, just like it spit out the people before you. "
Anyone who does any of these terrible things will be removed from his people. "
So obey My command. Do not do these terrible customs that were done before you. Do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."
"Speak to all the people of Israel and tell them: Be holy, because I, the the LORD your God, am holy.
"Each person must respect his mother and father. Keep My special rest days. I am the the LORD your God.
"Do not turn to fake gods. Do not make metal gods for yourselves. I am the the LORD your God.
"When you give a peace offering to the the LORD, give it in a way that pleases Him.
"Eat it on the day you offer it, or the next day. Burn anything left on the third day.
"If someone eats it on the third day, it is bad and not accepted.
"The person who eats it will be guilty, because he made holy things unclean. That person must be removed from his people.
"When you gather your crops, do not take everything from the edges of your field. Do not pick up what falls.
"Do not strip your vineyard bare. Do not pick up fallen grapes. Leave them for poor people and for people from other lands. I am the the LORD your God.
"Do not steal. Do not lie. Do not trick each other.
"Do not swear a false promise in My name. Do not misuse the name of your God. I am the the LORD.
"Do not cheat your neighbor. Do not rob him. Do not keep a worker's pay until morning.
"Do not curse a deaf person. Do not put something in the way of a blind person. Fear your God. I am the the LORD.
"Do not be unfair in court. Do not favor poor people. Do not favor rich people. Judge your neighbor fairly.
"Do not spread stories about people. Do not stand by while your neighbor is in danger. I am the the LORD.
"Do not hate your brother in your heart. Correct your neighbor openly, so you do not sin because of him.
"Do not try to get even. Do not stay angry with your people. Love your neighbor as you love yourself. I am the the LORD.
"Keep My rules. Do not mate two kinds of animals. Do not plant two kinds of seeds in your field. Do not wear clothes made of two kinds of cloth.
"If a man sleeps with a slave woman who is promised to another man, but she has not been set free or paid for, they must be punished. But they must not be put to death, because she was not free.
"The man must bring a ram to the door of the Meeting Tent as a guilt offering to the the LORD.
"The priest will make peace for him before the the LORD with the ram. The sin he did will be forgiven.
"When you come to the land and plant fruit trees, do not eat the fruit for three years. It is not allowed.
"In the fourth year, all the fruit is holy. Give it as a praise offering to the the LORD.
"In the fifth year, you may eat the fruit. This will give you more crops. I am the the LORD your God.
"Do not eat meat with blood in it. Do not try to tell the future. Do not practice magic.
"Do not cut the hair at the sides of your head. Do not cut the edges of your beard.
"Do not cut your body for the dead. Do not put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the the LORD.
"Do not let your daughter become a prostitute. If you do, the land will be full of sin.
"Keep My special rest days. Respect My holy place. I am the the LORD.
"Do not ask spirits or mediums for help. Do not seek them, or you will become unclean. I am the the LORD your God.
"Stand up when an older person comes in. Honor old people. Fear your God. I am the the LORD.
"When a stranger lives with you in your land, do not hurt him.
"Treat the stranger who lives with you like a person born among you. Love him as you love yourself, because you were strangers in Egypt. I am the the LORD your God.
"Do not cheat when you measure length, weight, or amount.
"Use honest scales, honest weights, an honest basket measure, and an honest liquid measure. I am the the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt.
"Keep all My rules and laws. Do them. I am the the LORD."

"Tell the Israelites: If any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel gives one of his children to the false god Molech, that person must be put to death. The people of the land must throw stones at him.
"I will turn against that man and remove him from his people, because he gave his child to Molech. He made My holy place dirty. He also treated My holy name like it was not special.
"If the people of the land pretend not to see and do not put him to death when he gives his child to Molech,
then I will turn against that man and his family. I will remove them from their people. That includes him and all who follow him by being unfaithful to Me and worshiping Molech.
"If a person goes to mediums or to people who say they can talk to spirits, and is unfaithful to Me by following them, I will turn against that person and remove him from his people.
"Set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
Obey My rules and do them. I am the LORD. I am the one who makes you holy.
"If anyone curses his father or mother, he must be put to death. He cursed his father or mother, so his death is his own fault.
"If a man has sex with another man's wife—with his neighbor's wife—both the man and the woman must be put to death.
"If a man has sex with his father's wife, he has shamed his father. Both of them must be put to death. Their death is their own fault.
If a man has sex with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have done something terrible. Their death is their own fault.
If a man has sex with a man as he would with a woman, both of them have done something detestable. They must be put to death. Their death is their own fault.
"If a man marries a woman and her mother, that is wicked. The man and the women must be burned with fire, so that this wicked thing will not be among you.
"If a man has sex with an animal, he must be put to death. You must also kill the animal.
If a woman goes near an animal to have sex with it, you must kill the woman and the animal. They must be put to death. Their death is their own fault.

"If a man marries his sister, whether she is his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and he sees her private parts and she sees his, that is a disgrace. They will be separated from their people. He has shamed his sister, and he will be punished for his wrong.
If a man has sex with a woman during her monthly period, he has exposed her flow of blood. Both of them will be separated from their people.
"Do not have sex with your mother's sister or your father's sister, because that shames his close relative. They will be punished for their sin.
If a man has sex with his aunt, he has shamed his uncle. They will be punished for their sin, and they will die without children.
If a man marries his brother's wife, that is unclean. He has shamed his brother. They will have no children.
"So obey all My rules and all My laws. Do them. Then the land where I am bringing you to live will not throw you out.
"Do not follow the customs of the nations I am driving out before you. They did all these things, so I was disgusted with them.
"But I said to you, \"You will take their land. I will give it to you to own. It is a land full of good things.\" I am the LORD your God. I am the one who set you apart from the other nations.

"So you must tell the difference between clean and unclean animals and birds. Do not make yourselves disgusting with unclean animals, birds, or anything that crawls on the ground. I have set these apart as unclean for you.
"You must be holy to Me, because I, the LORD, am holy. I have set you apart from the other nations to be My own.
"If a man or woman among you is a medium or a person who says they can talk to spirits, they must be put to death. You must throw stones at them. Their death is their own fault."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron's sons, the priests. Tell them: A priest must not make himself unclean by touching a dead person among his people.
He may do it only for close family: his mother, father, son, daughter, or brother.
He may also do it for his unmarried sister who is close to him, since she has no husband.
But he must not make himself unclean for his wife's family. That would make him unclean.
