Priests must not shave their heads. They must not shave the edges of their beards. They must not cut their bodies.
They must be holy to their God. They must not ruin the name of their God. They bring gifts burned in fire to the LORD. They bring the food of their God. So they must be holy.
They must not marry a woman who sold herself for sex or a woman whose husband sent her away. A priest is holy to his God.
You must treat him as holy, because he brings the food of your God. He will be holy to you, because I, the LORD, am holy. I make you holy.
If a priest's daughter makes herself unclean by selling herself for sex, she brings shame on her father. She must be burned with fire.

"The high priest is the one above his brothers. Oil was poured on his head to make him priest. He was chosen to wear the holy clothes. He must not let his hair hang loose. He must not tear his clothes.
He must not go near any dead body. He must not make himself unclean, even for his father or mother.
He must not leave God's holy place. He must not make God's holy place unclean. The oil that made him priest is on him. It belongs to his God. I am the LORD.
"He must marry a woman who has never been married.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman who sold herself for sex. He may marry only a woman who has never been married, from his own people.
Then he will not make his children unclean among his people. I am the LORD, who makes him holy."
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to Aaron and tell him: For all the years to come, no man from your family who has a body problem may come near to bring the food of his God.
No man with a body problem may come near. Not a blind man, a lame man, a man with a scarred face, or a man with a body part that is too big or too small.
No man with a broken foot or hand.
No hunchback or dwarf. No man with a bad eye, a skin sore, scabs, or crushed private parts.
No priest from Aaron's family who has a body problem may come near to bring gifts burned in fire to the LORD. He has a body problem. He must not come near to bring the food of his God.
He may eat the most holy food of his God, and the holy food too.
But he must not go near the curtain or the altar, because he has a body problem. Then he will not make My holy places unclean. I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
So Moses told these things to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel.
"Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy things the people of Israel give to Me. They must not make My holy name common. I am the LORD.

Always, if any man in your family has something that makes him not clean, and he comes near the holy things that the people of Israel give to the LORD, that man must be sent away from Me. I am the LORD. "
No man from Aaron's family who has a skin disease or a flow may eat the holy food until he is clean. Also, no one who touches a dead body, or a man who has a flow from his body, may eat it.
No man who touches any unclean thing, like a bug that makes him not clean, or a person who is not clean, may eat it.
The person who touches these things will be not clean until evening. He may not eat the holy food unless he washes his body with water. "
When the sun goes down, he will be clean again. Then he may eat the holy food, because it is his food.
He must not eat an animal that died by itself or was killed by another animal. That would make him not clean. I am the LORD.
The priests must keep My rules. If they do not, they will be blamed and die, because they made the holy things common. I am the LORD. I make them holy. "
No one outside the priest's family may eat the holy food. A guest of the priest or a hired worker may not eat it.
But if the priest buys a person with his money, that person and the children born in his house may eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries a man who is not a priest, she may not eat the holy food that is given to the LORD.

But if she is a widow or is sent away, and she has no children, and she comes back to her father's house, she may eat her father's food like when she was young. No one outside the family may eat it. "
If a man eats the holy food by mistake, he must add one-fifth more to it and give the holy food to the priest.
The priests must not let the holy things of the people of Israel be made common.
They must not let the people carry the blame for eating the holy things. I am the LORD. I make them holy."
"Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel. Say: If any man of Israel or a foreigner living among you gives a gift to the LORD as a burnt offering, to keep a promise or as a free gift,
you must give a male animal with nothing wrong with it. It can be a bull, a sheep, or a goat. Then the LORD will accept it.
Do not bring an animal that has something wrong with it. The LORD will not accept it for you. "
If a man brings a peace offering to the LORD, from a bull or sheep or goat, to keep a promise or as a free gift, it must have nothing wrong with it.
Do not bring to the LORD an animal that is blind, hurt, cut, has a sore, a skin disease, or scabs. Do not put any of these on the altar as a gift burned to the LORD.
You may give a bull or sheep that has a part too long or too short as a free gift. But it will not be accepted as a promise gift. "
Do not bring to the LORD an animal whose body parts are crushed, broken, torn, or cut off. Do not do this in your land.
Do not take any of these from a foreigner to give as food to your God. They have something wrong with them, so they will not be accepted for you."
"When a bull, sheep, or goat is born, it must stay with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be accepted as a gift burned to the LORD.
Do not kill a cow or sheep and its young on the same day.
If you give a thank offering to the LORD, give it so the LORD will accept it.
Eat it the same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
Keep My rules and do them. I am the LORD.
Do not make My holy name common. I will be treated as holy among the people of Israel. I am the LORD. I make you holy.
I brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘These are My special times. They are the the LORD’s special times, and you are to call them holy meetings.
You may work for six days. But the seventh day is a Sabbath. It is a day of complete rest and a holy meeting. You must not do any work. No matter where you live, it is a Sabbath to the the LORD.
These are the the LORD’s special times. They are holy meetings that you must call at the right time.
The the LORD’s Passover starts at sunset on the fourteenth day of the first month.
On the fifteenth day of that month, the Feast of Bread Without Yeast to the the LORD begins. For seven days you must eat bread without yeast.
On the first day, you are to have a holy meeting. You must not do any regular work.
For seven days, you are to bring a fire offering to the the LORD. On the seventh day, you are to have a holy meeting. You must not do any regular work.’”
The the LORD also said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘When you come to the land I am giving you, and you gather its grain, you are to bring the first bundle of your grain to the priest.
The priest will lift up the bundle before the the LORD so He will accept it for you. He must lift it up on the day after the Sabbath.
On the day you lift up the bundle, you are to offer a one-year-old lamb that has no flaw. It is a burnt offering to the the LORD.

You must also bring a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. It is a fire offering to the the LORD. It has a smell that pleases Him. You must also bring a drink offering of one-fourth of a hin of wine.
You must not eat any bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until the very day you bring this offering to your God. This is a rule for all time for your families, no matter where you live.
Starting on the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the lifted bundle, you are to count seven full weeks.
You must count fifty days, until the day after the seventh Sabbath. Then you are to bring a new grain offering to the the LORD.
Bring two loaves of bread from where you live. They are a lifted offering. They are made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour and baked with yeast. They are first crops for the the LORD.

With the bread, you are to bring seven one-year-old male lambs with no flaw, one young bull, and two rams. They are a burnt offering to the the LORD. You must also bring their grain offerings and drink offerings. It is a fire offering with a smell that pleases the the LORD.
You are also to offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two one-year-old male lambs as a peace offering.
The priest will lift up the lambs before the the LORD with the first-crop bread. The bread and the two lambs are set apart for the the LORD for the priest.
On that same day, you are to call a holy meeting. You must not do any regular work. This is a rule for all time, no matter where you live, for your families.
When you gather the grain of your land, do not gather all the way to the edge of your field. Do not pick up what is left. Leave it for poor people and for outsiders. I am the the LORD your God.’”
The the LORD also said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘On the first day of the seventh month, you are to have a day of rest. It is a holy meeting announced with loud horn blasts.
You must not do any regular work. You are to bring a fire offering to the the LORD.’”
Then the the LORD said to Moses,
“The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day to Make Things Right. You are to have a holy meeting. You must make yourselves humble. You are to bring a fire offering to the the LORD.
On this day you must not do any work. It is the Day to Make Things Right. It makes things right for you before the the LORD your God.
If anyone does not make himself humble on this day, he must be cut off from his people.
I will wipe out anyone who does any work on this day.
You must not do any work at all. This is a rule for all time, no matter where you live, for your families.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you. You must make yourselves humble. You are to rest from the evening of the ninth day of the month until the next evening.”
The the LORD also said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the Feast of Tents to the the LORD begins. It lasts for seven days.
On the first day, you are to have a holy meeting. You must not do any regular work.

For seven days, you are to bring a fire offering to the the LORD. On the eighth day, you are to have a holy meeting. You are to bring a fire offering to the the LORD. It is a special meeting. You must not do any regular work.

These are the the LORD’s special times. You are to call them holy meetings. Bring fire offerings to the the LORD. Bring burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings, each on its own day.
These offerings are in addition to the the LORD’s Sabbaths. They are also in addition to your gifts, your promises, and your free gifts that you give to the the LORD.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered the crops of your land, you are to celebrate a feast to the the LORD for seven days. On the first day, you are to rest completely. On the eighth day, you are to rest completely.
On the first day, you are to take fruit from good trees, palm branches, leafy branches, and willow branches from the stream. You are to be glad before the the LORD your God for seven days.
You are to celebrate this feast to the the LORD for seven days each year. This is a rule for all time. You are to celebrate it in the seventh month.
You are to live in tents for seven days. Every Israelite born in the land must live in tents.
Do this so that your families will know that I made the Israelites live in tents when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the the LORD your God.’”
So Moses told the Israelites about the the LORD’s special times.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Command the Israelites to bring you clean oil from crushed olives for the lamp. This oil will keep the lamps burning all the time.
"Aaron must place it outside the curtain in the meeting tent. He must keep it burning before the LORD from evening to morning. This rule lasts for all time for your families.
"Aaron must keep the lamps burning on the clean lampstand before the LORD all the time."
"Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread. Use two-tenths of a basket of flour for each loaf.
"Put the loaves in two rows. Put six loaves in each row on the clean table before the LORD.
"Put pure incense on the row of loaves. It will be a reminder gift for the bread. It is a gift burned for the LORD.
"Every Sabbath day, Aaron must set the bread before the LORD. This is a lasting promise from the Israelites.
"The bread belongs to Aaron and his sons. They must eat it in a special place, because it is very holy. It comes from the gifts burned for the LORD. This rule lasts forever."
A man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian went out among the Israelites. He and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman spoke against God's name and cursed. The people brought him to Moses. His mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
They put him in jail until the LORD told them what to do.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Take the man who cursed outside the camp. Everyone who heard him must put their hands on his head. Then all the people must throw stones at him.
"Speak to the Israelites. Tell them: If anyone curses his God, he will be guilty.

"Anyone who speaks against the LORD's name must be put to death. All the people must throw stones at him. This is true for a foreigner or for someone born in the land. If he speaks against the LORD's name, he must die.
"If anyone kills a person, he must be put to death.
"If anyone kills an animal, he must pay for it. One life for another life.
"If a man hurts his neighbor, he must be hurt the same way.
"A broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. If he hurts a person, he must be hurt the same way.
"Whoever kills an animal must pay for it. Whoever kills a person must be put to death.
"You must have the same law for the foreigner and for the person born among you. I am the LORD your God."
Moses told the Israelites. They took the man who cursed outside the camp and threw stones at him. The Israelites did what the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He said,
"Speak to the people of Israel. Say this: When you come into the land I give you, the land must have a Sabbath rest for the the LORD.
For six years, plant your field. Trim your grapevines. Gather the crops.
But the seventh year is a Sabbath rest for the land. It is a Sabbath for the the LORD. Do not plant your field. Do not trim your grapevines.
Do not gather the grain that grows by itself. Do not pick grapes from vines no one trimmed. It will be a year of rest for the land."
"The land's rest will give food to you, your male servant, your female servant, your hired worker, and the stranger who lives with you.
Your livestock and the wild animals in your land may eat all its crops."
"Count seven groups of seven years. That is forty-nine years.
On the tenth day of the seventh month, on the Day of Forgiving Sins, blow a trumpet through all your land.
Make the fiftieth year holy. Call for freedom in the land for everyone who lives there. It is your Jubilee. Each person must go back to his own land. Each person must go back to his family.
The fiftieth year is your Jubilee. Do not plant. Do not gather grain that grows by itself. Do not pick grapes from vines no one trimmed.
It is holy. You may eat what the field grows by itself.
In this Jubilee year, each person must go back to his own land."
"When you sell land to your neighbor, or buy land from your neighbor, do not cheat each other.
Buy from your neighbor by counting the years after the Jubilee. He will sell to you by counting the years of crops.
If many years are left, pay more. If few years are left, pay less. He sells to you based on the number of harvests.
Do not cheat one another. Fear your God. I am the the LORD your God."
"Obey My rules and laws. Then you will live safely in the land.
The land will give its fruit. You will eat until you are full. You will live safely there."
"You may ask, 'What will we eat in the seventh year? We did not plant or gather our crops.'
I will send My blessing in the sixth year. The land will grow enough food for three years.
When you plant in the eighth year, you will still eat from the old crops. You will eat them until the ninth year, until the new crops come in."
"The land must not be sold forever. It is Mine. You are only strangers and guests with Me.
In all the land you own, you must allow the land to be bought back."
"If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his land, his nearest relative must come and buy it back for him.
If a man has no one to buy it back, but he gets enough money, he may buy it back himself.
He must count the years since he sold it. He must pay back the extra money to the man who bought it. Then he can go back to his land.
If he cannot get enough money to buy it back, the buyer keeps it until the Jubilee year. In the Jubilee, it is set free, and he goes back to his land."
"If a man sells a house in a walled city, he can buy it back until one year after he sold it.
If it is not bought back before the year is over, the house in the walled city belongs to the buyer and his family forever. It will not be set free in the Jubilee.
But houses in villages without walls are treated like fields. They can be bought back. They will be set free in the Jubilee."
"The Levites can always buy back the houses in their cities.
If a Levite buys back a house, it will be set free in the Jubilee. This is because the houses in Levite cities belong to them. They are among the people of Israel.
The fields around their cities must not be sold. They are theirs forever."
"If your brother becomes poor and cannot take care of himself, you must help him. Help him like a stranger or guest, so he can live with you.
Do not take interest or extra money from him. Fear your God, so your brother can live with you.
Do not lend him money for interest. Do not sell him food for profit.
I am the the LORD your God. I brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God."
"If your brother becomes poor and sells himself to you, do not make him work like a slave.
He will be with you like a hired worker or a guest. He will work with you until the Jubilee year.
Then he and his children will leave you. He will go back to his family and to his father's land.
They are My servants. I brought them out of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves.
Do not rule over him harshly. Fear your God."
"You may buy male and female slaves from the nations around you.
You may also buy them from the children of the strangers who live with you. You may buy their families who were born in your land. They will be your property.
You may leave them to your children after you. They can own them forever. But do not rule harshly over your brothers, the people of Israel."
"If a stranger or guest with you becomes rich, and your brother becomes poor and sells himself to that stranger or guest, or to a member of his family,
he may be bought back after he is sold. One of his brothers may buy him back.
His uncle or his cousin may buy him back. A close relative from his family may buy him back. Or if he gets enough money, he may buy himself back.
He and his buyer must count the years from the year he sold himself to the Jubilee year. The price will be like the pay of a hired worker for those years."
"If many years are left, he must pay back more of his price.
If few years are left until the Jubilee, he must pay back less.
He will be with the buyer like a hired worker year by year. The buyer must not rule over him harshly while you watch.
If he is not bought back in these ways, he and his children will be set free in the Jubilee year."
"The people of Israel are My servants. They are the servants I brought out of Egypt. I am the the LORD your God."
Do not make false gods for yourselves. Do not set up a cut-out shape or a stone pillar for yourselves. Do not put a carved stone in your land to bow down to it. I am the LORD your God.
Keep My rest days. Honor My holy place. I am the LORD.
If you walk in My rules and keep My commands and do them,
I will send rain at the right time. The land will grow food. The trees will give fruit.
Your grain will be so much that you will still be picking grain when it is time to pick grapes. Picking grapes will last until planting time. You will eat all you want and live safely in your land.
I will give peace in the land. You will lie down, and no one will scare you. I will take away wild animals from the land. No sword will go through your land.
You will chase your enemies. They will fall by the sword in front of you.
Five of you will chase a hundred. A hundred of you will chase ten thousand. Your enemies will fall by the sword in front of you.
I will look at you with favor. I will make you grow and have many children. I will keep My promise with you.
You will eat old grain from last year. You will bring out the old to make room for the new.
I will put My tent among you. I will not hate you.
I will walk among you. I will be your God. You will be My people.
I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of Egypt so you would not be slaves. I broke the heavy yoke on you. I let you walk tall.
If you do not listen to Me and do not do all these commands,
if you hate My rules and are sick of My laws, so you do not do any of My commands and break My promise,
then I will do this to you: I will bring sudden fear on you. I will bring sickness that makes you weak and sad. You will plant your seed for nothing. Your enemies will eat it.
I will turn My face against you. You will be beaten by your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you. You will run even when no one chases you.
If you still do not listen to Me, I will punish you seven times more for your sins.
I will break your strong pride. I will make the sky like iron and the ground like bronze.
Your strength will be used up for nothing. Your land will not grow food. The trees will not give fruit.
If you walk against Me and will not listen to Me, I will hit you seven times more, as your sins deserve.
I will send wild animals against you. They will take your children and kill your animals. There will be fewer of you. Your roads will be empty.
If these things do not teach you to obey Me, and you walk against Me,
then I will also walk against you in anger. I will punish you seven times more for your sins.
I will bring a sword against you that pays back My broken promise. You will gather in your cities. I will send sickness among you. You will be given into the hand of the enemy.
When I take away your bread, ten women will bake bread in one oven. They will weigh out your bread. You will eat but not be full.
If you still do not listen to Me, and you walk against Me,
I will walk against you in My burning anger. I will punish you seven times more for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters.
I will destroy your worship hills. I will cut down your idol poles. I will throw your dead bodies on the dead bodies of your idols. I will hate you.
I will make your cities empty. I will ruin your holy places. I will not accept your sweet gifts.
I will make the land empty. Your enemies who live there will be shocked by it.
I will scatter you among the nations. I will send enemies with swords after you. Your land will be empty. Your cities will be ruins.
Then the land will enjoy its rest. All the time it is empty, you will be in your enemies' land. Then the land will rest and enjoy its rest.
All the time it is empty, it will rest. It did not rest on your rest days when you lived there.
The people left among you will be scared in your enemies' lands. The sound of a leaf will make them run. They will run like running from a sword. They will fall even when no one chases them.
They will trip over each other like running from a sword, even though no one chases. You will not be able to stand before your enemies.
You will die among the nations. Your enemies' land will destroy you.
The people left among you will waste away because of their sin in your enemies' lands. They will waste away for their fathers' sins too.
They must tell about their sin and their fathers' sin. They were not faithful to Me. They walked against Me.
So I will also walk against them in anger. I will bring them into their enemies' land. Then if they stop being proud, they will pay for their sin.
Then I will remember My promise with Jacob. I will also remember My promise with Isaac and with Abraham. I will remember the land.
They will leave the land. It will enjoy its rest while it is empty. They will pay for their sin. This is because they hated My rules and were sick of My laws.
Even then, when they are in their enemies' land, I will not hate them or destroy them. I will not break My promise with them. I am the LORD their God.
I will remember My first promise. I brought them out of Egypt so all people could see. I did this to be their God. I am the LORD.
These are the rules, laws, and teachings the LORD gave between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
He said, "Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If you make a special promise to the LORD about a person's value, use these values."
A man twenty to sixty years old is worth fifty silver coins.
A woman that age is worth thirty.
A boy five to twenty years old is worth twenty. A girl that age is worth ten.
A child from one month to five years old is worth five silver coins for a boy and three for a girl.
A man sixty or older is worth fifteen. A woman that age is worth ten.
If you are too poor to pay the set value, bring the person to the priest. The priest will set a value you can afford.
If the promise is an animal that can be given to the LORD, the animal becomes holy.
Do not trade it for another animal. Do not swap a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If you do swap, both animals become holy.
If the animal is not clean and cannot be given to the LORD, bring it to the priest.
The priest will decide if it is good or bad. The value he sets will stand.
If you want it back, pay the value plus one fifth more.
If a person gives a house to the LORD, the priest will decide its value. The value he sets will stand.
If you want the house back, pay the value plus one fifth more. Then it is yours again.
If you give part of your family land to the LORD, its value is based on how much seed it takes. It is worth fifty silver coins for each large basket of barley seed.
If you give the field in the Jubilee year, the value stays the same.
If you give it after the Jubilee year, the priest counts the years left until the next Jubilee year. The value goes down for those years.
If you want the field back, pay the value plus one fifth more. Then it is yours again.
If you do not buy it back, or if you sell it to someone else, it can never be bought back.
When the field is set free in the Jubilee year, it becomes holy, like a field given fully to the LORD. It becomes the priests' land.
If you give a field you bought, not family land, to the LORD,
the priest counts its value up to the Jubilee year, and you pay that value that day as holy to the LORD.
In the Jubilee year, the field goes back to the person it was bought from, the first owner of the land.
Every value uses the holy coin weight: twenty small coins make one silver coin.
No one may give the firstborn of an animal, because the firstborn already belongs to the LORD. An ox or a sheep belongs to the LORD.
If the animal is not clean, it can be bought back at its set value plus one fifth. If you do not buy it back, it is sold at its set value.
But nothing a person owns and fully gives to the LORD can be sold or bought back. This includes a person, an animal, or family land. Everything fully given is most holy to the LORD.
No person who is fully given to be destroyed can be bought back. That person must be put to death.
A tenth of everything from the land belongs to the LORD. This includes grain from the ground and fruit from the trees. It is holy to the LORD.
If you want to buy back a tenth, pay its value plus one fifth more.
Every tenth animal from the herd or flock is holy to the LORD. It is every tenth animal that passes under the rod.
Do not pick out the good from the bad, and do not swap animals. If you swap, both the animal and the one swapped for it become holy. They cannot be bought back.
These are the commands the LORD gave Moses for the Israelites at Mount Sinai.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the tent of meeting. This was in the Sinai desert. It was the second month of the second year after the Israelites left Egypt. The LORD said,
"Take a census of all the Israelites. Count them by their families. Count every man by name.
You and Aaron must count the men who are twenty years old or older. Count all who can serve in the army. Count them by their groups.
One man from each tribe will help you. He will be the head of his family.
These are the names of the men who will stand with you to help: From Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur.
From Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
From Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab.
From Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar.
From Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.
From Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud. From Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
From Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.
From Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
From Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran.
From Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.
From Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
These men were chosen from the people. They were leaders of their tribes and heads of Israelite families."
Moses and Aaron took these named men.
On the first day of the second month, the whole community gathered. They were listed by their families and family groups. Men twenty years old or older were counted by name.
Moses counted them in the Sinai desert, just as the LORD had commanded.
The people of Reuben were counted by their families.
The people of Simeon were counted by their families.
The people of Gad were counted by their families.
The people of Judah were counted by their families.
The people of Issachar were counted by their families.
The people of Zebulun were counted by their families.
The people of Ephraim, from the family of Joseph, were counted by their families.
The people of Manasseh were counted by their families.
The people of Benjamin were counted by their families.
The people of Dan were counted by their families.
The people of Asher were counted by their families.
The people of Naphtali were counted by their families.
These were the men Moses and Aaron counted. The twelve leaders helped them. One leader came from each family.
All the Israelite men who were twenty years old or older and could serve in the army were counted by their families.
The Levites were not counted with the others.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Do not count the tribe of Levi with the other Israelites. Do not include them in the total.

You must put the Levites in charge of the holy tent where the sacred box is kept. They will care for it and all its things. They will carry the holy tent and its things. They will serve there. They will camp around the holy tent.
When the holy tent moves, the Levites will take it down. When it is set up, the Levites will put it up. Anyone else who comes near it must die.
The other Israelites will camp in their groups under their flags.
The Levites will camp around the holy tent. They will guard it. Then the LORD will not be angry with the Israelite people."
The Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
"The people of Israel must camp around the tent of meeting. They must stay a little way back from it. Each group must camp under its own flag, with the sign of its family group.
"On the east side, toward the sunrise, Judah must camp with its army. Nahshon son of Amminadab is the leader of Judah's people.
His army has seventy-four thousand six hundred men.
Issachar camps next to him. Nethanel son of Zuar is their leader.
His army has fifty-four thousand four hundred men.
Zebulun camps there too. Eliab son of Helon is their leader.
His army has fifty-seven thousand four hundred men.
All the men in Judah's camp total one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred. They must move out first.
"On the south side, Reuben must camp with its army. Elizur son of Shedeur is their leader.
His army has forty-six thousand five hundred men.
Simeon camps next to him. Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai is their leader.
His army has fifty-nine thousand three hundred men.
Gad camps there too. Eliasaph son of Reuel is their leader.
His army has forty-five thousand six hundred fifty men.
All the men in Reuben's camp total one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty. They must move out second.
"The tent of meeting, with the Levites, must travel in the middle of the camps. They must move out the same way they camp. Each group must stay in its place under its own flag.
"On the west side, Ephraim must camp with its army. Elishama son of Ammihud is their leader.
His army has forty thousand five hundred men.
Manasseh camps next to him. Gamaliel son of Pedahzur is their leader.
His army has thirty-two thousand two hundred men.
Benjamin camps there too. Abidan son of Gideoni is their leader.
His army has thirty-five thousand four hundred men.
All the men in Ephraim's camp total one hundred eight thousand one hundred. They must move out third.
"On the north side, Dan must camp with its army. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai is their leader.
His army has sixty-two thousand seven hundred men.
Asher camps next to him. Pagiel son of Ocran is their leader.
His army has forty-one thousand five hundred men.
Naphtali camps there too. Ahira son of Enan is their leader.
His army has fifty-three thousand four hundred men.
All the men in Dan's camp total one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They must move out last, under their flags.
"These are the people of Israel, counted by their families. All the people in the camps total six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
The Levites were not counted with the people of Israel, because the LORD told Moses not to count them.
The people of Israel did everything the LORD told Moses. They camped under their flags, and they moved out. Each man went with his family group and his father's house."
These are the family lines of Aaron and Moses. The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
Aaron's sons were Nadab, the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These sons were priests. They were chosen and set apart to serve.

Nadab and Abihu died in front of the LORD. They offered fire that was not allowed. This happened in the Sinai desert. They had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was alive.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "
Bring the Levites to Aaron the priest. They will help him.
They will care for his work and the work of all the people at the meeting tent. They will work in the holy tent.
They will care for all the things in the meeting tent. They will care for the duties of the Israelites. They will work in the holy tent.
Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. The Levites are given to him from the Israelites.
Appoint Aaron and his sons. They must do their priest work. Anyone else who comes near must die."
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "
Look, I have taken the Levites from the Israelites. They take the place of all the firstborn sons. So the Levites belong to Me.

This is because all firstborn sons belong to Me. On the day I killed the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart all the firstborn in Israel for Me. This includes people and animals. They are Mine. I am the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses in the Sinai desert. He said, "
Count the Levites by their family groups. Count every male who is one month old or older."
Moses counted them as the LORD had told him.
Levi had three sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei. These were the Gershonite families.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. These were the Kohathite families.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite families.
The Gershonites had two family groups: the Libnites and the Shimites.
They counted 7,500 males who were one month old or older.
The Gershonites camped behind the holy tent, on the west side.
Their leader was Eliasaph son of Lael.
The Gershonites took care of the holy tent. They took care of its cover and the curtain at the door of the meeting tent.
They also took care of the curtains around the courtyard, the curtain at the courtyard gate near the holy tent and altar, and the ropes used for all this work.
The Kohathites had four family groups: the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites.
They counted 8,600 males who were one month old or older. They took care of the holy things.
The Kohathites camped on the south side of the holy tent.
Their leader was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They took care of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the holy tools used with them. They also took care of the curtain and all the work for these things.
Eleazar son of Aaron the priest was the leader over the Levite leaders. He watched over those who took care of the holy things.
The Merarites had two family groups: the Mahlites and the Mushites.
They counted 6,200 males who were one month old or older.
Their leader was Zuriel son of Abihail. They camped on the north side of the holy tent.
They took care of the frames, bars, posts, bases, and all the tools of the holy tent, and all the work for it.
They also took care of the posts around the courtyard, their bases, tent pegs, and ropes.
Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons camped on the east side, in front of the holy tent. They took care of the holy place for the Israelites. Anyone else who came near had to die.
All the Levites that Moses and Aaron counted were 22,000 males who were one month old or older.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "Count all the firstborn males among the Israelites who are one month old or older. Write down their names and count them.
Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn Israelites. Take the Levites' animals instead of all the firstborn animals of the Israelites. The Levites belong to Me. I am the LORD."
Moses counted all the firstborn Israelites, just as the LORD had told him.
There were 22,273 firstborn males who were one month old or older.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "
Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn Israelites. Take the Levites' animals instead of the Israelites' animals. The Levites belong to Me. I am the LORD.
The Levites were 22,000, but there were 22,273 firstborn Israelites. So 273 more firstborn sons must be bought back.
Take five silver coins for each of the 273. Use the holy weight. One silver coin equals twenty small coins.
Give the silver to Aaron and his sons for the ones who are bought back."
Moses took the buy-back money for the extra firstborn sons.
He took 1,365 silver coins, using the holy weight.
Moses gave the silver to Aaron and his sons, just as the LORD had told him.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
"Count the Kohathite part of the Levites. Count them by their family groups.
Count men from 30 to 50 years old. These men will work in the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the Kohathites in the tent of meeting. They take care of the most holy things.
"When the camp moves, Aaron and his sons will go in. They will take down the curtain in front of the ark. They will cover the ark with it.
They will put a leather cover over it. Then they will spread a blue cloth over it. They will put the carrying poles in.
They will spread a blue cloth over the table that holds the special bread. They will put the bowls, pans, jars, and drink cups on it. The bread that is always there will stay on it.
They will spread a red cloth over these things. They will cover them with a leather cover. They will put the carrying poles in.
"They will take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand. They will cover its lamps, tongs, trays, and oil jars.
They will put the lampstand and all its tools in a leather cover. They will put it on a carrying frame.
They will spread a blue cloth over the gold altar. They will cover it with a leather cover. They will put its carrying poles in.
They will take all the tools used in the holy place. They will put them in a blue cloth. They will cover them with a leather cover. They will put them on a carrying frame.
"They will take the ashes off the altar. They will spread a purple cloth over it.
They will put all its tools on it: fire pans, forks, shovels, and bowls. They will cover it with a leather cover. They will put its carrying poles in.

Aaron and his sons will finish covering the holy place and its tools. Then the Kohathites will come to carry them. But they must not touch the holy things. If they do, they will die. These are the loads the Kohathites carry in the tent of meeting.

Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, will be in charge of the oil for the light, the sweet-smelling incense, the regular food gift, and the oil for special use. He will take care of the whole tent and everything in it, both the holy place and its tools."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
"Do not let the Kohathite family groups be cut off from the Levites.
Do this so they will live and not die when they come near the most holy place. Aaron and his sons will go in. They will give each man his work and his load.
But they must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment. If they do, they will die."
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Count the Gershonites too. Count them by their families and family groups.
Count men from 30 to 50 years old. These men will work in the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the Gershonite family groups. They will serve and carry things.
They will carry the curtains of the tent, the tent of meeting, its covering, the leather covering on top, and the curtain at the door of the tent of meeting.
They will carry the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain at the gate of the courtyard around the tent and altar, the ropes, and all their tools. They will do all the work for these things.
Aaron and his sons will be in charge of all the work of the Gershonites. Moses and Aaron will tell them what to carry and what to do. They will put them in charge of their loads.
This is the work of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting. They will work under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest."
Count the Merarites by their clans and family groups.
Count men from 30 to 50 years old. These men will work in the tent of meeting.
They will carry the frames of the tent, its bars, posts, and bases.
They will carry the posts around the courtyard, their bases, pegs, and ropes, and all their tools. Moses and Aaron will count these things by name and give them their loads.
This is the work of the Merarites in the tent of meeting. They will work under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders counted the Kohathites by their clans and family groups.
They counted men from 30 to 50 years old who would work in the tent of meeting.
These were the Kohathites who were counted. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had told Moses.
They also counted the Gershonites by their clans and family groups.
They counted men from 30 to 50 years old who would work in the tent of meeting.
These were the Gershonites who were counted. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had said.
They counted the Merarites by their clans and family groups.
They counted men from 30 to 50 years old who would work in the tent of meeting.
These were the Merarites who were counted. Moses and Aaron counted them as the LORD had told Moses.
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and family groups.
They counted men from 30 to 50 years old who would serve and carry loads in the tent of meeting.
Moses counted each man and gave him his work and load, as the LORD had told him.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the people of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with a bad skin disease, everyone with a body discharge, and everyone who touched a dead body.
Send out both men and women. Put them outside the camp so they do not make the camp unclean, because I live among you.
The Israelites did this. They sent them outside the camp. They did what the LORD said to Moses."
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the people of Israel: If a man or woman does any wrong that people do, and is not true to the LORD, that person is guilty.
He must tell about his sin. He must pay back for the wrong he did, and add one-fifth more. He must give it to the person he wronged.
If the man has no family member to pay back, the payback goes to the LORD for the priest. This is besides the ram used to make him right with God.
Every holy gift the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to the priest.
Each person keeps his own holy things. But whatever anyone gives to the priest belongs to the priest."
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the people of Israel: If a man's wife turns away and is not true to him,
and a man sleeps with her, and her husband does not know, and she becomes unclean in secret, with no one to speak against her, because she was not caught,
and if a jealous feeling comes over the husband, and he is jealous of his wife, whether she is unclean or not,

then the man must bring his wife to the priest. He must bring an offering for her: one-tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy. It helps people remember and shows guilt."
The priest must bring her near and stand her before the LORD.
The priest must take holy water in a clay jar. He must take dust from the floor of the holy tent and put it into the water.
The priest must stand the woman before the LORD. He must let her hair hang loose. He must put the grain offering for remembering in her hands. The priest holds the bitter water that brings a curse.

The priest must make her promise and say, "If no man has slept with you, and if you have not turned away to become unclean while married to your husband, then you will be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
But if you have turned away while married to your husband, and if you have made yourself unclean, and a man other than your husband has slept with you,
then the LORD will make you a curse and an oath among your people. He will make your leg shrink and your belly swell.
May this water that brings a curse go into your body, so your belly swells and your leg shrinks." And the woman must say, "Amen, Amen."
Then the priest must write these curses on a scroll and wash them into the bitter water.
He must make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse. The water will go into her and become bitter.
The priest must take the grain offering for jealousy from the woman's hand. He must wave it before the LORD and bring it to the altar.
The priest must take a handful of the offering as a special part and burn it on the altar. After that, he must make the woman drink the water.

When she drinks the water, if she has made herself unclean and was not true to her husband, the bitter water will go into her and become bitter. Her belly will swell and her leg will shrink. She will become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not made herself unclean, and she is clean, she will be free and will have children.
This is the law for jealousy. If a wife turns away while married to her husband and becomes unclean,
or if a jealous feeling comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife, then he must stand her before the LORD, and the priest must do all this law to her.
The man will be free from guilt, and the woman will carry her guilt.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Speak to the Israelites. Tell them, 'When a man or woman makes a special promise to the LORD as a Nazirite, to set himself or herself apart for the LORD, "'

he or she must not drink wine or strong drink. He or she must not drink vinegar made from wine or strong drink. He or she must not drink grape juice. He or she must not eat fresh grapes or dried grapes.
During all the days of this special time, he or she must not eat anything from a grapevine, not even the seeds or skins. "'

For all the days of this special promise, no razor may touch his or her head. The person must be holy until this special promise to the LORD is done. He or she must let the hair on the head grow long.
During all the days of this special promise to the LORD, he or she must not go near a dead body.
He or she must not make himself or herself unclean for a father, mother, brother, or sister when they die, because he or she has made a special promise to God.
All the days of this special promise, the person is holy to the LORD. "'
If someone dies suddenly near him or her, and the special promise on the head becomes unclean, the person must shave the head on the day he or she becomes clean. That is the seventh day.
On the eighth day, he or she must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest must offer one bird for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. This pays for the sin of being near a dead body. On that day the person must set the head apart again.
The person must start the special promise to the LORD again and bring a one-year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The first days do not count, because the special promise became unclean. "'
This is the law for the Nazirite when the days of the special promise are done. The person must be brought to the door of the Tent of Meeting.

He or she must bring an offering to the LORD: one perfect one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, one perfect one-year-old female lamb for a sin offering, and one perfect ram for a peace offering.
He or she must also bring a grain offering and a drink offering, and a basket of bread made without yeast. The bread should be fine flour mixed with oil, and thin cakes spread with oil.
The priest must bring them before the LORD and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He must offer the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, along with the basket of bread without yeast. The priest will also make the grain offering and the drink offering.
Then the Nazirite must shave the special hair at the door of the Tent of Meeting. He or she must take the hair and put it on the fire under the peace offering.
The priest must take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one piece of bread without yeast from the basket, and one thin cake. He must put them on the Nazirite's hands after the head is shaved.

The priest must wave them before the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy for the priest, along with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the gift. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law for the Nazirite who makes this offering to the LORD for the special promise. It is in addition to anything else the person can afford. The person must keep the promise he or she made, following the law of the special promise.'"
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Speak to Aaron and his sons. Say, 'This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them, "
The LORD bless you and keep you.
The LORD make His face shine on you and be kind to you.
The LORD lift up His face to you and give you peace."
So they will put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.'"
On the day Moses finished setting up the meeting tent, he poured oil on it and made it holy. He did the same to all its things, the altar, and all the altar's things.
The leaders of Israel brought gifts. They were the heads of their families. They were the leaders of the tribes who counted the people.
They brought their gifts to the LORD. They brought six covered carts and twelve oxen. Two leaders shared one cart. Each leader gave one ox. They brought them to the front of the meeting tent.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Take these gifts from them. Use them to work at the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites. Give each man what his work needs."
Moses took the carts and oxen. He gave them to the Levites.
He gave two carts and four oxen to the sons of Gershon. He gave them what their work needed.
He gave four carts and eight oxen to the sons of Merari. Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest, was in charge of them. He gave them what their work needed.
He gave none to the sons of Kohath. Their work was holy. They carried the holy things on their shoulders.
The leaders gave gifts for the altar on the day it was anointed. They brought their gifts before the altar.
The LORD said to Moses, "One leader will bring his gift each day. They will give gifts for the altar's special use."
On the first day, Nahshon son of Amminadab brought his gift. He was the leader of Judah.
His gift was one silver plate. It weighed 130 shekels. He also gave one silver bowl. It weighed 70 shekels. Both were by the holy shekel. They were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain gift.
He gave one gold dish. It weighed 10 shekels. It was full of incense.
He gave one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb one year old. These were for a burnt gift.
He gave one male goat for a sin gift.
For a peace gift, he gave two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs one year old. This was the gift of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar brought his gift. He was the leader of Issachar.
His gift was one silver plate. It weighed 130 shekels. He also gave one silver bowl. It weighed 70 shekels. Both were by the holy shekel. They were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain gift.
He gave one gold dish. It weighed 10 shekels. It was full of incense.
He gave one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb one year old. These were for a burnt gift.
He gave one male goat for a sin gift.
For a peace gift, he gave two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs one year old. This was the gift of Nethanel son of Zuar.

He gave one gold dish. It weighed 10 shekels. It was full of incense.
He gave one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb one year old. These were for a burnt gift.
He gave one male goat for a sin gift.
For a peace gift, he gave two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs one year old. This was the gift of Eliab son of Helon.

He gave one gold dish. It weighed 10 shekels. It was full of incense.

He gave one gold dish. It weighed 10 shekels. It was full of incense.
He gave one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb one year old. These were for a burnt gift.
He gave one male goat for a sin gift.
For a peace gift, he gave two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs one year old. This was the gift of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

His gift was one silver plate. It weighed 130 shekels. He also gave one silver bowl. It weighed 70 shekels. Both were by the holy shekel. They were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain gift.
He gave one gold dish. It weighed 10 shekels. It was full of incense.
He gave one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb one year old. These were for a burnt gift.

This is what the leaders of Israel gave when the altar was set apart. On the day it was anointed, twelve leaders gave gifts. They gave twelve silver plates, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed 130 shekels. Each silver bowl weighed 70 shekels. All the silver things weighed 2,400 shekels by the holy shekel.
Each gold dish weighed 10 shekels. All the gold dishes weighed 120 shekels.
For the burnt gift, they gave twelve young bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs one year old. They also gave grain gifts for them. They gave twelve male goats for sin gifts.
For peace gifts, they gave twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs one year old. This was the gift for the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the meeting tent to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him. The voice came from above the cover, between the two winged angels, on the ark of the law. The LORD spoke to him.
He said, "Speak to Aaron. Tell him, 'When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps should shine in front of the lampstand.'"
Aaron did this. He set up the lamps so they shone in front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had told Moses.
The lampstand was made of hammered gold. It had a base and flowers. It was made just the way the LORD showed Moses.
He said, "Take the Levites from among the Israelites. Make them clean.
Do this to make them clean: Sprinkle the water that washes away sin on them. Have them shave their whole body. Have them wash their clothes. Then they will be clean.
Then they must take a young bull and its grain offering. The grain offering is fine flour mixed with oil. You must also take a second young bull for a sin offering.
Bring the Levites to the front of the meeting tent. Gather all the Israelites there.
Bring the Levites to the LORD. The Israelites must put their hands on the Levites.
Aaron must lift the Levites up to the LORD as a wave offering from the Israelites. Then they can serve the LORD.
The Levites must put their hands on the heads of the bulls. Offer one bull for a sin offering. Offer the other as a burnt offering to the LORD. This will pay for the Levites' sin.
Stand the Levites in front of Aaron and his sons. Lift them up to the LORD as a wave offering.
This is how you set the Levites apart from the other Israelites. The Levites will be Mine.
After that, the Levites may come to serve in the meeting tent. You must make them clean first. You must lift them up as a wave offering.
They are given to Me fully from among the Israelites. I took them for Myself instead of the first baby boy born in every Israelite family.
Every firstborn Israelite belongs to Me, both people and animals. I made them holy for Myself on the day I killed every firstborn in Egypt.
So I took the Levites instead of all the firstborn Israelites.

I gave the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons. They come from the Israelites. They will serve for the Israelites in the meeting tent. They will pay for the Israelites' sin. Then no sickness will come on the Israelites when they come near the holy place."
Moses, Aaron, and all the Israelites did for the Levites just what the LORD told Moses. The Israelites did it.
The Levites made themselves clean. They washed their clothes. Aaron lifted them up to the LORD as a wave offering. Aaron paid for their sin to make them clean.
After that, the Levites came to serve in the meeting tent in front of Aaron and his sons. They did just as the LORD told Moses.
He said, "This is the rule for the Levites: A Levite who is 25 years old or older may come to work in the meeting tent.
When he is 50 years old, he must stop the hard work. He must not work anymore.
He may still help his brothers. He may watch over the meeting tent. But he must not do the hard work. This is how you care for the Levites in their jobs."
In the first month of the second year after the Israelites left Egypt, the the LORD spoke to Moses in the Sinai desert.
He said, “Tell the Israelites to keep the Passover at the right time.
Keep it on the fourteenth day of this month, in the evening. Keep it by all its rules.”
So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover.
They kept the Passover in the Sinai desert. They did it on the fourteenth day of the first month, in the evening. They did everything the the LORD had told Moses.
Some men could not keep the Passover that day because they were unclean from touching a dead body.
They came to Moses and Aaron that day. They said, “We are unclean because of a dead body. Why should we be kept from bringing the the LORD’s gift at the right time with the other Israelites?”
Moses said to them, “Wait here. I will find out what the the LORD tells us to do.”
Then the the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, “Speak to the Israelites.
If any man or any of his family in the future is unclean because of a dead body, or is far away on a trip, he may still keep the Passover for the the LORD.
He must keep it on the fourteenth day of the second month, in the evening. He must eat it with bread made without yeast and bitter herbs.
He must not leave any of it until morning. He must not break a bone. He must keep the Passover by all its rules.
But a man who is clean and not on a trip, but does not keep the Passover, must be cut off from his people. He did not bring the the LORD’s gift at the right time. He will be guilty.
If a foreigner living with you keeps the Passover to the the LORD, he must keep it by the same rules. There is one rule for the foreigner and for the person born in the land.”
On the day the meeting tent was set up, the cloud covered it. At night the cloud looked like fire over the tent. It stayed that way until morning.
The cloud always looked like that. At night it looked like fire.
When the cloud rose from the tent, the Israelites moved on. Where the cloud stayed, the Israelites camped.
The Israelites moved at the the LORD’s word, and they camped at the the LORD’s word. They camped as long as the cloud stayed over the tent.
Even if the cloud stayed over the tent for many days, the Israelites did what the the LORD said and did not move.
Sometimes the cloud stayed over the tent for only a few days. Then at the the LORD’s word they camped, and at the the LORD’s word they moved.
Sometimes the cloud stayed from evening to morning. When it rose in the morning, they moved. Whether by day or by night, when the cloud rose, they moved.
Whether the cloud stayed for two days, a month, or a longer time, the Israelites stayed camped and did not move. When it rose, they moved.
They camped at the the LORD’s word, and they moved at the the LORD’s word. They did what the the LORD said, just as the the LORD had told them through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Make two silver trumpets for yourself. Hammer them from one piece of silver. They will help you call the people together and tell the camps to move.
When both trumpets blow, all the people will meet with you at the door of the meeting tent.
If only one trumpet blows, the leaders of Israel's thousands will meet with you.
When you blow an alarm the first time, the camps on the east side will move.
When you blow a second alarm, the camps on the south side will move. They will blow an alarm when it is time to move.
"When you gather the people, blow the trumpets, but do not sound an alarm.
Aaron's sons, the priests, will blow the trumpets. This rule will last for all your families, forever.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who hurts you, sound an alarm with the trumpets. Then the LORD your God will remember you, and He will save you from your enemies.
Also, on your happy days, at your feasts, and at the start of your months, blow the trumpets over your burnt gifts and peace gifts. They will help the LORD remember you. I am the LORD your God."
On the twentieth day of the second month in the second year, the cloud rose from the sacred tent.
The people of Israel left the Sinai desert. They traveled in their groups. The cloud stopped in the Paran desert.
They moved first because the LORD told them to through Moses.
The camp of Judah moved first, by their groups. Nahshon son of Amminadab led its army.
Nethanel son of Zuar led the army of Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon led the army of Zebulun.
The sacred tent was taken down. The Gershonites and the Merarites carried it and moved.
The camp of Reuben moved next, by their groups. Elizur son of Shedeur led its army.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai led the army of Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Deuel led the army of Gad.
The Kohathites carried the holy things. They set up the sacred tent before the others arrived.
The camp of Ephraim moved next, by their groups. Elishama son of Ammihud led its army.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur led the army of Manasseh.
Abidan son of Gideoni led the army of Benjamin.
The camp of Dan moved last. It guarded all the other camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai led its army.
Pagiel son of Ocran led the army of Asher.
Ahira son of Enan led the army of Naphtali.
These were the ways the Israelites moved by their groups.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, who was Moses' father-in-law, "We are moving to the place the LORD promised to give us. Come with us. We will be good to you, because the LORD has promised good things to Israel."
Hobab said, "I will not go. I will go back to my own land and my family."
Moses said, "Please don't leave us. You know where we should camp in the desert. You can show us where to go.
If you come with us, we will share with you the good things the LORD gives us."
They traveled for three days from the mountain of the LORD. The box of the LORD's promise went ahead of them for three days to find a good place to rest.
The LORD's cloud was over them by day when they left the camp.
When the box moved, Moses said, "Rise up, the LORD! Let Your enemies scatter. Let those who hate You run away from You."
When it rested, he said, "Come back, the LORD, to Israel's many thousands."
The people complained, and it sounded bad to the LORD. He was angry. Fire from the LORD burned among them and burned the edge of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses. Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire stopped.
So they named that place Taberah, because the LORD's fire had burned among them.
A mixed group among them wanted better food. The Israelites cried too. They said, "Who will give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish we ate for free in Egypt, and the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now we are tired of this food. All we see is manna."
Manna looked like tiny seeds. It shone like a clear stone.
The people went around and picked it up. They ground it in mills or beat it in a bowl. They cooked it in a pot and made cakes from it. It tasted like cakes made with oil.
When the dew fell at night, the manna fell on it.
Moses heard the people crying at their tent doors, family by family. The LORD was very angry, and Moses was upset too.
Moses said to the LORD, "Why have You treated Your servant so badly? Why am I not pleasing to You? Why did You put the load of all these people on me?
Did I give birth to all these people? Did I bring them into the world? Why do You tell me to carry them in my arms, like a nurse carries a baby, to the land You promised their fathers?
Where can I get meat for all these people? They cry to me and say, 'Give us meat to eat!' "
I cannot carry all these people by myself. It is too much for me.
If You are going to treat me like this, please kill me now, if I have found favor in Your eyes. Then I will not see my trouble."

The LORD said to Moses, "Bring Me seventy men from the leaders of Israel. Choose men you know are leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the meeting tent and have them stand there with you.
I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will help you carry the load of the people, so you will not carry it alone. "
Say to the people, 'Get ready for tomorrow, because you will eat meat. You cried to the LORD and said life was better in Egypt. The LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.'
You will not eat meat for just one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days.

You will eat it for a whole month, until it comes out of your noses and makes you sick. This is because you turned away from the LORD, who is among you, and you cried before Him and said, 'Why did we leave Egypt?'"
Moses said to the LORD, "There are six hundred thousand foot soldiers here with me. Yet You say, 'I will give them meat to eat for a whole month'?
If we kill all the sheep and cows for them, will it be enough? If we catch all the fish in the sea for them, will it be enough?"
The LORD said to Moses, "Is the LORD too weak to do this? Now you will see whether My word comes true or not."
Moses went out and told the people the LORD's words. He gathered seventy men from the leaders of the people and put them around the tent.

The LORD came down in a cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy leaders. When the Spirit rested on them, they spoke God's words, and then they stopped.
Two men, Eldad and Medad, stayed in the camp. The Spirit rested on them too. They were among those chosen, but they had not gone out to the tent. They spoke God's words in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are speaking God's words in the camp."
Joshua son of Nun, who had served Moses since he was young, said, "Moses, my lord, stop them!"
Moses said, "Are you jealous for me? I wish all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would put His Spirit on them!"
Moses and the leaders of Israel went back to the camp.
A wind from the LORD brought quail from the sea and dropped them all around the camp. They were about three feet deep on the ground, in every direction as far as a day's walk.
The people got up and gathered quail all that day, all that night, and all the next day. The one who gathered the least gathered ten large baskets full. They spread them out around the camp.
While the meat was still between their teeth, before they chewed it, the LORD became angry with the people. He struck them with a very bad sickness.
So that place was called Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had wanted the meat.
The people traveled from Kibroth Hattaavah to Hazeroth and stayed at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of his wife from Cush. He had married her.
They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn't He also spoken through us?" And the LORD heard it.
Moses was a very humble man. He was more humble than anyone else on earth.
Right away the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, "Come out to the meeting tent, all three of you." So the three of them went out.
Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud. He stood at the door of the tent and called Aaron and Miriam. The two of them came forward.
He said, "Listen to My words. When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, show Myself to them in visions. I speak to them in dreams.
But it is not like that with My servant Moses. He is faithful in all My house.
I speak with him directly. I speak clearly, not in puzzles. He sees the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?"
The LORD was very angry with them, and He left.
When the cloud moved away from the tent, Miriam had a bad skin disease. Her skin was as white as snow. Aaron looked at her and saw that she had the skin disease.
Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not blame us for the sin we did so foolishly.
Do not let her be like a baby born dead, with half its body gone."
So Moses cried out to the LORD, "Please, God, heal her!"
The LORD replied to Moses, "If her father had shamed her, she would be ashamed for seven days. Keep her outside the camp for seven days. After that she can come back."
So Miriam was kept outside the camp for seven days. The people did not move on until she was brought back.
After that, the people left Hazeroth and camped in the Desert of Paran.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Send some men to look at the land of Canaan. I am giving this land to the people of Israel. Send one leader from each tribe."
So Moses sent them from the desert of Paran, just as the LORD said. The men were leaders of the Israelites.
From Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur.
From Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori.
From Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From Issachar: Igal son of Joseph.
From Ephraim: Hoshea son of Nun.
From Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu.
From Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi.
From Manasseh: Gaddi son of Susi.
From Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli.
From Asher: Sethur son of Michael.
From Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi.
From Gad: Geuel son of Machi.
These were the men Moses sent to look at the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun a new name. He called him Joshua.
Moses sent them to look at the land of Canaan. He said, "Go up through the Negev. Then go up into the hills.
See what the land is like. See if the people there are strong or weak. See if there are many people or few.
See if the land is good or bad. See if the towns have walls or not.
See if the land has good soil. See if there are trees. Be brave. Bring back some of the fruit of the land." It was the time when the first grapes were ready.
So the men went up and looked at the land. They went from the desert of Zin to Rehob near Hamath.
They went south and came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the people of Anak, lived there. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the Valley of Eshcol. There they cut a branch with one big bunch of grapes. Two men carried it on a pole. They also took some pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the Valley of Eshcol because of the grape bunch the Israelites cut there.
They came back after forty days.
They went to Moses and Aaron and all the Israelites at Kadesh in the desert of Paran. They told Moses and the people what they had seen. They showed them the fruit of the land.
They said, "We went to the land you sent us to. It is a very rich land. Here is some of its fruit.
But the people there are strong. The cities are big and have walls. We also saw Anak's people there.
The Amalekites live in the Negev. The Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hills. The Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan."
Caleb quieted the people before Moses. He said, "Let's go now and take the land. We can do it."
But the men who went with him said, "We cannot go up against those people. They are stronger than we are."
They spread a bad report about the land to the Israelites. They said, "The land we looked at is dangerous for the people who live there. All the people we saw there are very tall.
We saw giants there. Anak's people are giants too. We felt like tiny bugs next to them."
That night, all the people cried out loud.
All the people of Israel complained to Moses and Aaron. They said, "We wish we had died in Egypt! Or we wish we had died in this desert!"
They said, "Why did the LORD bring us to this land? We will die by the sword. Our wives and children will be taken. It would be better to go back to Egypt."
They said to each other, "Let's pick a leader and go back to Egypt."
Moses and Aaron fell on their faces in front of all the people.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh tore their clothes.
They said to all the people, "The land we went through is very, very good.
If the LORD is happy with us, He will bring us into this land. It is a land with plenty of milk and honey. He will give it to us.
Do not turn against the LORD. Do not be afraid of the people there. They will be easy for us to beat. They have no protection now. The LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them."
All the people said, "Stone them!" Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the meeting tent.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will these people turn against Me? How long will they not believe Me, even after all the signs I did among them?
I will hit them with sickness and take them away. I will make you into a big and strong nation."
Moses said to the LORD, "The Egyptians will hear about it. You brought these people out of Egypt by Your power.

The people who live in this land will hear about it. They have heard that You, the LORD, are with these people. They have seen You face to face. Your cloud stands over them. You go before them by day in a cloud and by night in fire.
If You kill all these people at once, the nations who heard about You will say that the LORD could not bring them into the land He promised. So He killed them in the desert.
Now let Your power be great, as You said.

The LORD is patient and full of love. He forgives sin and wrong. But He does not let guilty people go free. He brings punishment on children for their parents' sin, even to the third and fourth family.
Please forgive these people's sin, because Your love is great. You have forgiven them from Egypt until now."
The LORD said, "I have forgiven them, as you asked.
But as I live, all the earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD.
All the men who saw My glory and My signs in Egypt and the desert tested Me ten times. They did not obey Me.
They will not see the land I promised their fathers. None of the people who hated Me will see it."
But My servant Caleb had a different spirit. He followed Me all the way. I will bring him into the land he went to. His children will own it.
The Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow, turn around and go into the desert by the Red Sea.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
"How long will this bad group keep complaining against Me? I have heard the people of Israel complain against Me.
"As I live, says the LORD, I will do to you what you said in My hearing.
Your dead bodies will fall in this desert. All of you who were counted, twenty years old and older, who complained against Me,
will not go into the land I promised to give you. Only Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun will go in.
Your children, who you said would be taken, I will bring into the land you did not want.
Your dead bodies will fall in this desert.
Your sons will wander in the desert for forty years. They will suffer for your wrong until your bodies are gone.
You will carry your sin for forty years, one year for each day you explored the land. Then you will know I am angry with you.
I, the LORD, have spoken. I will do this to all this bad group that gathered against Me. They will be destroyed in this desert. They will die here.
The men Moses sent to explore the land came back. They made all the people complain against him by saying bad things about the land.
Those men who said bad things about the land died from a sickness in front of the LORD.
Only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh lived.
Moses told all the people these words. The people were very sad.
The next morning, they got up early and went to the top of the hill. They said, "We have sinned. But now we will go to the place the LORD told us about."
Moses said, "Why are you breaking the LORD's command? It will not work.
Do not go up. You will be beaten by your enemies, because the LORD is not with you.
The Amalekites and Canaanites are there. You will die by the sword, because you turned away from the LORD. The LORD will not be with you."
But they went up anyway. Moses and the chest of the LORD's promise did not leave the camp.
The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down. They beat the people and chased them to Hormah.
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land I am giving you to live in,
and you give a food gift to the the LORD from your cows or sheep, as a smell the the LORD likes, it may be a burnt gift or a gift to keep a promise, a free gift, or a gift at a special time.
The person who gives it must give to the the LORD a grain gift: a tenth of a basket of good flour mixed with a fourth of a jar of oil.
With each lamb that is burned or given, you are to get ready a fourth of a jar of wine as a drink gift.
With a ram, give a grain gift of two-tenths of a basket of good flour mixed with a third of a jar of oil.
