Give a third of a jar of wine as a drink gift, a smell the the LORD likes.
When you get ready a young bull as a burnt gift or gift to keep a promise, or a peace gift to the the LORD,
give with the bull a grain gift of three-tenths of a basket of good flour mixed with half a jar of oil.
Give half a jar of wine as a drink gift, a food gift with a smell the the LORD likes.
Do this for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.
You may make as many as you give.
"Every person born in Israel must do these things this way when he gives a food gift with a smell the the LORD likes.
If a visitor living with you gives a food gift to the the LORD, he must do it the way you do.
The whole group must have the same rule for you and the visitor living among you. It is a rule that lasts forever. You and the visitor are the same before the the LORD.
There is one law and one rule for you and the visitor living with you."
Then the the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land I am bringing you to,
and you eat food from that land, you must give a gift to the the LORD.
From the first of your dough, give a cake as a gift. Give it like a gift from the grain you gather.
For all time, give the the LORD a gift from the first of your dough.
"Now if you sin without meaning to and do not keep all these commands the the LORD has spoken to Moses,
all that the the LORD has commanded you through Moses from the day the the LORD gave them and on through the years to come,

and if it is done without the whole group knowing, then the whole group must get ready one young bull as a burnt gift, a smell the the LORD likes, with its grain gift and drink gift the right way, and one male goat as a sin gift.

The priest must make things right for the whole group of Israel, so they can be forgiven, because it was a mistake, and they brought their food gift to the the LORD and their sin gift before the the LORD for their mistake.
Then the whole group of Israel and the visitor living among them will be forgiven, because all the people acted without meaning to.
Also, if one person sins without meaning to, he must bring a one-year-old female goat as a sin gift.
The priest must make things right before the the LORD for the person who sinned without meaning to, to make things right for him, and he will be forgiven.
You must have the same law for the person born in Israel and for the visitor living among you.
"But the person who sins on purpose, whether born in Israel or a visitor, speaks against the the LORD. That person must be cut off from his people.
Because he hated the the LORD's word and broke His command, that person must be cut off. His wrong will stay on him."
While the Israelites were in the desert, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
The people who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and all the people.
They put him in a safe place because it had not been said what should be done to him.
Then the the LORD said to Moses, "The man must surely be put to death. All the people must stone him outside the camp."
So all the people took him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, just as the the LORD had told Moses.
Then the the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: For all time to come, they are to make tassels on the corners of their clothes, with a blue cord on each tassel.
It will be a tassel for you to see and remember all the the LORD's commands, so you will not follow your own wishes and what you see, which can lead you away from God.
Then you will remember and obey all My commands and be holy to your God.
I am the the LORD your God who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the the LORD your God."
Korah was the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi. Dathan and Abiram were sons of Eliab. On was the son of Peleth. They were from Reuben's family. They brought men with them.
They stood up against Moses. With them were 250 men from Israel. They were leaders the people knew well.
They came together against Moses and Aaron. They said, “You have gone too far! All the people are holy. the LORD is with them. Why do you put yourselves above the LORD's people?”
Moses heard this. He fell with his face to the ground.
Moses said to Korah and all his group, “In the morning the LORD will show who belongs to Him. He will show who is holy. He will bring that person near to Him. The one He chooses, He will bring near.
Do this. Take pans for burning sweet smoke. Korah and all his group, take them.
Tomorrow put fire and sweet smoke in them. Bring them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be holy. You Levites have gone too far!”
Moses said to Korah, “Listen, you Levites!
Isn't it enough for you that the God of Israel set you apart from the people of Israel? He brought you near to serve in the meeting tent. He set you to stand before the people and help them.
He brought you and all your fellow Levites near Him. But now you want the priest work too?
You and all your followers have joined together against the LORD. Who is Aaron that you complain about him?”
Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab. But they said, “We will not come!”
They said, “Isn't it enough that you brought us up from a rich land to kill us in the desert? And now you want to boss us around!
You have not brought us into a rich land. You have not given us fields and grape farms. Do you want to treat us like we cannot see? We will not come!”
Moses was very angry. He said to the LORD, “Do not accept their offering. I have not taken even one donkey from them. I have not hurt any of them.”
Moses said to Korah, “You and all your followers must come before the LORD tomorrow. You and they and Aaron must come.
Each man must take his pan and put sweet smoke in it. Bring all 250 pans before the LORD. You and Aaron must each bring a pan.”
So each man took his pan. He put fire and sweet smoke in it. The men stood with Moses and Aaron at the door of the meeting tent.
Korah brought all the people together against them at the door. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
“Separate yourselves from this group. Then I will destroy them in a moment.”
But Moses and Aaron fell with their faces to the ground. They cried out, “O God, God who gives breath to all living things, will You be angry with the whole group when only one man sins?”
“Tell the group, ‘Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram. The leaders of Israel followed him.
He warned the people, “Move back from the tents of these bad men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them. If you do, you will be swept away because of all their sins.”
So the people moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out. They stood at the doors of their tents. Their wives, children, and little ones stood with them.
Then Moses said, “By this you will know that the LORD sent me to do all these things. I did not plan them myself.
If these men die a normal death, and have only what all people have, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD makes something new happen, and the ground opens and swallows them and all that belongs to them, and they go alive into the grave, then you will know that these men did not respect the LORD.”
As soon as he finished speaking, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened its mouth. It swallowed them and their houses. It swallowed all the people with Korah and all their things.
They went alive into the grave. Everything they owned went with them. The earth closed over them. They were gone from the group.
All the Israelites around them ran away. They shouted, “The ground is going to swallow us too!”
Fire came out from the LORD. It burned up the 250 men who offered the sweet smoke.
“Tell Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, to take the pans out of the fire. Scatter the coals away. The pans are holy.
Make these pans, which belonged to men who sinned, into thin metal sheets to cover the altar. They brought them before the LORD, so they are holy. Let them be a sign to the people of Israel.”
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze pans. The men who were burned had brought them. He had them hammered into a cover for the altar.

This was what the LORD had told Moses. It was to remind the people of Israel that no one except a child of Aaron's family should burn sweet smoke before the LORD. If he does, he will be like Korah and his followers.
The next day all the people of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron. They said, “You have killed the LORD's people!”
The people gathered against Moses and Aaron. They looked toward the meeting tent. They saw the cloud cover it. The glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the meeting tent.
“Get away from this group. I will destroy them in a moment.” Then Moses and Aaron fell with their faces to the ground.
Then Moses said to Aaron, “Take your pan. Put fire from the altar in it. Add sweet smoke. Hurry to the group. Pay for their wrong. The LORD's anger has come out. The sickness has started.”
Aaron did what Moses said. He ran into the middle of the group. The sickness had already started among the people. He offered the sweet smoke and paid for their wrong.
He stood between the dead and the living. The sickness stopped.
The number of dead from the sickness was 14,700. This was besides those who died because of Korah.
Then Aaron went back to Moses at the door of the meeting tent. The sickness had stopped.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Speak to the people of Israel. Ask each family leader to give you a stick. There will be twelve sticks, one for each tribe. Write each man's name on his stick.
Write Aaron's name on the stick for the family of Levi. Each family leader gets one stick.
Put the sticks in the special tent where I meet with you.
The stick of the man I choose will grow. Then I will stop the people of Israel from complaining about you. They complain about you and Aaron."
Moses told the people of Israel. Each leader gave a stick. There were twelve sticks. Aaron's stick was with them.
Moses put the sticks in front of the LORD in the tent.
The next day, Moses went into the tent. Aaron's stick for the family of Levi had grown. It had buds, flowers, and ripe almonds.
Moses brought all the sticks out to the people. They looked at them. Each man took his own stick.

The LORD said to Moses, "Put Aaron's stick back in the tent. Keep it there as a sign for the rebels. Then their complaining against Me will stop. You can end their complaining, and they will not die."
Moses did what the LORD said.
The people of Israel said to Moses, "We are dying! We are lost! All of us are lost!"
"Anyone who comes near the tent of the LORD will die. Will all of us die?"
The LORD said to Aaron, "You and your sons must carry the blame for wrongs in the holy place. You and your sons must carry the blame for your priest work.
Bring your brothers too. They are from Levi's family, your father's family. They will join you and help you while you and your sons stand in front of the tent where God's rules are kept.
They will watch over you and the whole tent. But they must not come near the holy things or the altar. If they do, they and you will die.
They will join you and watch over the tent where people meet God. They will do all the work of the tent. No one else may come near you.
You must watch over the holy place and the altar. Then God's anger will not come on the people of Israel.
I have taken your brothers, the Levites, from among the people of Israel. I give them to you as a gift. They are given to the LORD to do the work of the tent where people meet God.
You and your sons must keep your priest work. You will care for the altar and the room behind the curtain. I give your priest work to you as a gift. Anyone else who comes near must die."
Then the LORD spoke to Aaron, "Look, I have given you charge of the gifts brought to Me. I give all the holy things of the people of Israel to you and your sons. This is a gift that lasts forever.

This is yours from the very holy gifts, kept from the fire: every gift they bring, every grain gift, every sin gift, and every guilt gift. They give these to Me. They are very holy for you and your sons.
Eat them in a very holy place. Every male may eat them. They are holy for you.

This is also yours: the gift from what they give, all the wave gifts of the people of Israel. I give them to you, your sons, and your daughters. This lasts forever. Anyone clean in your house may eat them.
I give you the best oil, the best wine, and the best grain. These are the first and best parts they give to the LORD.
The first ripe fruits from their land, which they bring to the LORD, will be yours. Anyone clean in your house may eat them.
Everything in Israel that is set apart fully for God will be yours.

The first baby born to a person or an animal, that they give to the LORD, will be yours. But you must buy back the firstborn son of a person. You must also buy back the firstborn of an animal that is not clean.
Buy them back when they are one month old. Pay five silver coins, by the holy weight. Twenty small coins make one shekel.
But do not buy back the firstborn of a cow, sheep, or goat. They are holy. Sprinkle their blood on the altar. Burn their fat as a gift that smells good to the LORD.
Their meat will be yours. It is like the breast that is waved and the right leg that is given.

All the holy gifts that the people of Israel bring to the LORD, I give to you, your sons, and your daughters. This lasts forever. It is a promise that lasts forever before the LORD, for you and your children after you."
The LORD said to Aaron, "You will not receive land in their country. You will not have a share among them. I am your share and your land among the people of Israel.
I give every tenth part in Israel to the Levites. It is their land share. It pays them for the work they do, the work of the tent where people meet God.
Then the people of Israel will not come near the tent where people meet God. If they do, they will carry blame and die.

The Levites will do the work of the tent where people meet God. They will carry their own blame. This rule will last for all time, for all your children after you. They will not receive land among the people of Israel.
I give the Levites the tenth part that the people of Israel bring to the LORD. That is why I said they will not receive land among the people of Israel."
The LORD spoke to Moses and said, "Speak to the Levites and tell them this:
When you take the tenth part from the people of Israel, the tenth part I gave you from them as your land share, you must give part of it to the LORD. Give a tenth part of the tenth part.
Your gift will count for you like grain that has just been gathered and like full jars from the grape press.
So from all your tenth parts, which you receive from the people of Israel, give the LORD's gift to Aaron the priest.
From all your gifts, give every part that belongs to the LORD. Give the best part of it. It is holy.
Tell them this: When you have set aside the best part, the rest will count for the Levites like grain that has just been gathered and like grapes from the grape press.
You and your families may eat it in any place. It is your pay for your work in the tent where people meet God.
You will not be blamed for it, if you give the best part. Do not treat the holy things of the people of Israel as if they are not holy. If you do, you will die."
Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
"This is the rule of the law that the LORD gives. Tell the Israelites to bring a red cow to Moses. It must have no spots or bad marks. It must never have been made to work.
Give the cow to Eleazar the priest. He must take it outside the camp and kill it while Eleazar watches.
Eleazar must take some blood on his finger. He must sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent where the LORD met them.
Then burn the cow while Eleazar watches. Burn its skin, meat, blood, and dung.
The priest must take cedar wood, a plant called hyssop, and red string. He must throw them into the fire where the cow is burning.
Then the priest must wash his clothes and wash his body in water. After that he may go back into the camp. But he will be not clean until evening.
The man who burns the cow must wash his clothes and wash his body in water. He will also be not clean until evening.

A clean man must gather the ashes of the cow. He must put them in a clean place outside the camp. The people of Israel must keep them. They use them in water that makes people clean. This water takes away sin.
The man who gathers the ashes must wash his clothes. He will be not clean until evening. This rule lasts forever for the Israelites and for the stranger who lives with them.
Anyone who touches a dead body will be not clean for seven days.
He must make himself clean with the water on the third day and on the seventh day. Then he will be clean. But if he does not make himself clean on those days, he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a dead body and does not make himself clean makes the LORD's tent dirty. That person must be sent away from Israel. He is still not clean, because the cleaning water was not sprinkled on him. His not-clean state is still on him.
This is the rule when a man dies in a tent. Everyone who goes into the tent, and everyone already in the tent, will be not clean for seven days.
Any open jar with no lid tied on it is not clean.
Anyone in an open field who touches a person killed by a sword, or a dead body, or a human bone, or a grave, will be not clean for seven days.
For the not-clean person, they must take some ashes from the burned gift for sin. They must put them in a jar. Then they must pour fresh water over them.

Then a clean person must take hyssop. He must dip it in the water. He must sprinkle it on the tent, on all the things in it, and on the people who were there. He must also sprinkle anyone who touched a bone, a dead person, or a grave.

The clean person must sprinkle the not-clean person on the third day and on the seventh day. After the not-clean person is clean on the seventh day, he must wash his clothes and wash in water. He will be clean by evening.
But if a person who is not clean does not make himself clean, he must be sent away from the group. He made the LORD's holy place dirty. The cleaning water was not sprinkled on him. He is not clean.
This rule lasts forever. The person who sprinkles the cleaning water must wash his clothes. Anyone who touches the cleaning water will be not clean until evening.
Anything a not-clean person touches will be not clean. Anyone who touches it will be not clean until evening."
In the first month, all the people of Israel came to the desert of Zin. They stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the people. So they came together against Moses and Aaron.
The people argued with Moses. They said, "If only we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
Why did you bring the people of the LORD into this desert? Did you bring us here to die? We and our animals will die here.
Why did you bring us up from Egypt? Why did you bring us to this bad place? It is not a place with grain, figs, grapes, or pomegranates. There is no water to drink."
Moses and Aaron left the people and went to the door of the meeting tent. They fell on their faces. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Take the staff. Bring the people together. You and your brother Aaron must speak to the rock while they watch. Water will come from the rock. Give water to the people and their animals."
Moses took the staff from in front of the LORD, just as He had told him.
Moses and Aaron brought the people together in front of the rock. Moses said to them, "Listen, you rebels! Must we bring water out of this rock for you?"
Moses lifted his hand. He hit the rock two times with his staff. A lot of water came out. The people and their animals drank.
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "You did not trust Me enough to honor Me before the people of Israel. So you will not lead this people into the land I gave them."
These waters are called Meribah. There the people of Israel argued with the LORD. There the LORD showed how holy He is.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom. He said, "Your brother Israel says this: You know all the trouble we have had.
Our fathers went down to Egypt. We lived there a long time. The Egyptians were bad to us and to our fathers.
We cried to the LORD. He heard us. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are in Kadesh, a city at the edge of your land.

Please let us pass through your land. We will not walk through fields or vineyards. We will not drink water from wells. We will stay on the king's road. We will not turn right or left until we pass through your land."
But Edom said to him, "You may not pass through my land. If you do, I will come out to fight you with a sword."
The people of Israel said to him, "We will go up on the road. If we or our animals drink your water, we will pay for it. Just let us pass through on foot. We want nothing else."
But Edom said, "You may not pass through." Then Edom came out to meet them with many people and a strong army.
So Edom would not let Israel pass through his land. Israel turned away from him.
All the people of Israel traveled from Kadesh. They came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, near the border of Edom, the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
"Aaron will die and join his ancestors. He will not enter the land I gave to the people of Israel. This is because you both went against My word at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar. Bring them up Mount Hor.
Take Aaron's clothes off. Put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will die there."
Moses did what the LORD commanded. He and Aaron and Eleazar went up Mount Hor while all the people watched.
Moses took Aaron's clothes off. He put them on Eleazar. Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down.
All the people saw that Aaron had died. All Israel cried for Aaron for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad lived in the south land. He heard that Israel was coming on the road to Atharim. He fought Israel and took some people captive.
Israel made a promise to the LORD. They said, "If You give these people to us, we will destroy their cities."
The LORD heard Israel. He gave the Canaanites to them. They destroyed them and their cities. They named that place Hormah.
The people left Mount Hor. They went toward the Red Sea to go around Edom. The people grew tired on the way.
They spoke against God and Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in this desert? There is no bread and no water. We hate this bad food."
So the LORD sent poisonous snakes among the people. The snakes bit them, and many Israelites died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We sinned. We spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make a snake and put it on a pole. Anyone who is bitten can look at it and live."
Moses made a bronze snake and put it on a pole. If a snake bit someone, that person looked at the bronze snake and lived.
The Israelites moved on and camped at Oboth.
Then they moved from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim. It was in the desert east of Moab.
They moved from there and camped in the Zered Valley.
Then they moved and camped beyond the Arnon River. It was in the desert that came from the Amorites. The Arnon was the border between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why the Book of the Wars of the LORD says, "Waheb in Suphah, and the streams of the Arnon,
and the slope of the streams that goes down to Ar, and leans toward Moab's border."
From there they went to Beer. That was the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
The leaders dug it. The important men of the people dug it with their sticks and staffs." Then they went from the desert to Mattanah.
From Mattanah they went to Nahaliel. From Nahaliel they went to Bamoth.
From Bamoth they went to the valley in the field of Moab. It was at the top of Pisgah, looking over the empty land.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites. They said,
"Let us pass through your land. We will not go into the fields or vineyards. We will not drink water from your wells. We will stay on the king's road until we pass through your land."
But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his land. He gathered all his people and went out to fight Israel in the desert. He came to Jahaz and fought Israel.
Israel beat him with the sword. They took his land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River, up to the border of the Ammonites. The border of the Ammonites was too strong.
Israel took all those cities. They lived in all the cities of the Amorites, including Heshbon and its towns.
Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amorites. He had fought the first king of Moab and took all his land up to the Arnon.
That is why the poets say, "Come to Heshbon! Let the city of Sihon be built and set up!
For fire came out of Heshbon. A flame came from the city of Sihon. It burned up Ar of Moab and the lords of the hilltops of the Arnon.
Oh, Moab! You are ruined! You people of Chemosh are lost! He gave his sons as runaways and his daughters as captives to Sihon, king of the Amorites.
We have shot at them. Heshbon is gone to Dibon. We laid waste to Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer. They captured its villages and took the land from the Amorites there.
Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out to fight them. He and all his people came to Edrei to battle.
The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him. I have given him, his people, and his land into your hand. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
They struck him, his sons, and all his people. They left no one alive. Then they took his land.
The people of Israel traveled and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was very afraid of the people, because there were so many of them. Moab dreaded the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, “This crowd will eat up everything around us, like an ox eats grass in a field.” Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

Balak sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor in Pethor by the river, in the land of his people. They were to call him. They said, “A people came out of Egypt. They cover the face of the earth, and they are staying near me.

Please come and curse this people for me, because they are too strong for me. Maybe I can beat them and push them out of the land. I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed.”
The elders of Moab and Midian went with money to pay for magic. They came to Balaam and spoke Balak's words to him.
Balaam said, “Stay here tonight. I will tell you what the LORD says to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men with you?”
Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent them to me.
Look, a people came out of Egypt. They cover the face of the earth. Now come and curse them for me. Maybe I can fight them and drive them out.”
God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them. Do not curse the people, because they are blessed.”
In the morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's princes, “Go back to your land, because the LORD will not let me go with you.”
So the princes of Moab got up and went to Balak. They said, “Balaam will not come with us.”
Then Balak sent more princes. They were greater and more important than the first ones.
They came to Balaam and said, “Balak son of Zippor asks you not to refuse to come to him.
He will honor you very much, and he will do whatever you say. Please come and curse this people for him.”
Balaam answered Balak's servants, “Even if Balak gave me his whole house full of silver and gold, I could not go past the word of the LORD my God, to do anything small or big.
Now please stay here tonight, so I can find out what else the LORD will say to me.”
That night God came to Balaam and said, “If the men came to call you, get up and go with them. But do only what I tell you.”
In the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
But God was angry because Balaam went. The angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a sword in his hand. The donkey turned off the road and went into a field. Balaam hit the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between vineyards, with a wall on each side.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pressed against the wall. She crushed Balaam's foot against the wall, and he hit her again.
Then the angel of the LORD moved ahead and stood in a tight place where there was no room to turn right or left.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and lay down under Balaam. Balaam got angry and hit the donkey with his stick.
Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you hit me these three times?”
Balaam said to the donkey, “You made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you now.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, the one you have ridden all your life? Have I ever done this to you before?” Balaam said, “No.”
Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a sword in his hand. Balaam bowed down and fell on his face.
The angel of the LORD said to him, “Why did you hit your donkey three times? Look, I came out to oppose you, because your way is wrong before me.
The donkey saw me and turned away three times. If she had not turned away, I would have killed you and let her live.”
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “I have sinned, because I did not know you were standing in the road against me. Now if it is bad in your eyes, I will go back.”
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but speak only the word I tell you.” So Balaam went with Balak's princes.
Balak heard that Balaam had come. He went out to meet him at a city of Moab on the border of the Arnon, at the edge of his land.
Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not send for you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to honor you?”
Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. But can I say anything? I will speak only the word God puts in my mouth.”
Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and he sent some to Balaam and to the princes who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there Balaam could see the edge of the Israelite camp.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here. Get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me.”
Balak did what Balaam said. Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand by your burnt offering. I will go away. Maybe the LORD will come to meet me. I will tell you what He shows me.” Then Balaam went to a high, quiet place.
God met Balaam. Balaam said, “I have set up seven altars. I offered a bull and a ram on each one.”
The LORD put a message in Balaam's mouth. He said, “Go back to Balak and say this to him.”
Balaam went back to Balak. Balak was standing by his burnt offering. All the leaders of Moab were with him.
“Balak brought me from Aram. The king of Moab brought me from the eastern hills. Balak wants me to curse Jacob and speak against Israel.
“How can I curse people God has not cursed? How can I speak against people the LORD has not spoken against?
“I see them from the top of the rocks. I look at them from the hills. Look, these people live alone. They are not counted with other nations.
“Who can count Jacob's dust? Who can count even a fourth of Israel? Let me die like good people. Let my end be like theirs.”
Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, but you have blessed them!”
Balaam answered, “I must say what the LORD puts in my mouth.”
Balak said, “Come with me to another place. You will see only part of them, not all. Curse them for me from there.”
Balak took Balaam to a field called Zophim, on top of Mount Pisgah. Balaam built seven altars there. He offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here by your burnt offering. I will go over there to meet the LORD.”
The LORD met Balaam. He put a message in Balaam's mouth. He said, “Go back to Balak and say this to him.”
Balaam went back to Balak. Balak was standing by his burnt offering. The leaders of Moab were with him. Balak said, “What did the LORD say?”
“Get up, Balak, and listen. Hear me, son of Zippor.
“God is not a man, so He does not lie. He is not a human, so He does not change His mind. If He says something, He does it. If He speaks, He makes it happen.
“Look, I was told to bless. He has blessed them, and I cannot change it.
“God has not seen wrong in Jacob. He has not seen trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them. They shout like a king is among them.
“God brought them out of Egypt. He is strong like a wild ox.
“No magic will work against Jacob. No tricks will work against Israel. People will say about Jacob and Israel, ‘Look what God has done!’
“Look, these people rise up like a lioness. They are like a lion that does not rest until it eats its food and drinks the blood of those it killed.”
Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all. Do not bless them at all.”
Balaam answered, “I told you I must do everything the LORD says.”
Balak said, “Come, I will take you to another place. Maybe God will be happy if you curse them for me from there.”
Balak took Balaam to the top of Mount Peor. It looks out over the empty land.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here. Get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me.”
Balak did what Balaam said. He offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam saw that the LORD was happy to bless Israel. He did not go to look for magic signs like before. He turned to face the wild land.
Balaam looked up and saw Israel camped by its family groups. The Spirit of God came on him.
Balaam spoke this message: "This is the word of Balaam son of Beor. This is the word of the man whose eyes are open.
This is the word of one who hears God's words. He sees what the Almighty shows him. He falls down, but his eyes stay open.
"How good your tents are, Jacob! How good your homes are, Israel!
They spread like valleys. They are like gardens by a river. They are like sweet-smelling trees the LORD planted. They are like cedar trees by water.
Water will pour from their buckets. Their crops will have plenty of water. Their king will be greater than Agag. Their kingdom will be lifted up.
God brought them out of Egypt. He is like strong horns of a wild ox for them. He will eat up enemy nations. He will crush their bones. He will shoot them with arrows.
They crouch and lie down like a lion, like a lioness. Who will wake them? Blessed are the ones who bless you. Cursed are the ones who curse you."
Balak got very angry at Balaam. He clapped his hands. He said to Balaam, "I called you to curse my enemies. But look, you have blessed them three times!
Now go home! I said I would honor you, but the LORD has kept you from honor."

Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell the messengers you sent me that if Balak gave me his whole house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything beyond what the LORD says, good or bad, on my own? I will say only what the LORD says.
Now I am going back to my people.
Come, let me warn you what this people will do to your people in the days to come."
Balaam spoke this message: "This is the word of Balaam son of Beor. This is the word of the man whose eyes are open.
This is the word of one who hears God's words. He knows what the Most High knows. He sees what the Almighty shows him. He falls down, but his eyes stay open.
"I see him, but not now. I look at him, but not near. A star will come from Jacob. A ruler's stick will rise from Israel. He will defeat Moab and all the sons of Sheth.
Edom will belong to him. Seir, his enemy, will belong to him too. But Israel will be strong and win.
A ruler will come from Jacob. He will destroy the people left in the city."
Balaam saw Amalek. He spoke this message: "Amalek was first among the nations, but in the end it will be destroyed."
Balaam saw the Kenites. He spoke this message: "Your home is strong, and your nest is set in a rock.
But the Kenites will be destroyed. How long until Assyria takes you captive?"
Balaam spoke this message: "Oh no! Who can live when God does this?
Ships will come from Kittim. They will trouble Assyria and Eber. But they will also be destroyed."
Then Balaam got up and went back to his home. Balak also went his way.
While Israel stayed in Shittim, the men started to sin with Moabite women.
The Moabite women invited the people to eat food offered to their gods. The people ate it and bowed down to those gods.
So Israel started worshiping Baal Peor. The LORD became very angry with Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and put them to death in the sun before the LORD. Then the LORD's anger will turn away from Israel."
Moses said to Israel's judges, "Each judge kill the men in his group who joined Baal Peor."
Then an Israelite man brought a Midianite woman to his fellow Israelites. He did this while Moses and all of Israel watched. They were crying at the door of the meeting tent.
Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest, saw this. He got up from among the people and took a spear in his hand.
He followed the Israelite man into the tent and stabbed both of them. He stabbed the Israelite man and the woman. Then the sickness stopped spreading among the Israelites.
But 24,000 people had already died from the sickness.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned My anger away from Israel. He was very jealous for Me, so I did not destroy all Israel in My jealousy.
So I am giving him My peace promise.
He and his children after him will always be priests, because he was jealous for his God and made things right for the Israelites."
The Israelite who was killed was Zimri son of Salu. He was a leader of a Simeonite family.
The Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur. Her father was the head of a Midianite family.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Treat the Midianites as enemies and attack them. They treated you like enemies. They tricked you at Peor and through Cozbi, a Midianite woman.
She was killed on the day of the sickness because of Peor."
After the sickness ended, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar, Aaron's son, the priest.
Count all the people of Israel by their families. Count every man who is 20 years old or older and can go to war.
Moses and Eleazar the priest told them this on the flat land of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho.
They counted the men who were 20 or older, just as the LORD had told Moses to do for the Israelites who came out of Egypt.
Reuben was the oldest son of Israel. His families were the Hanochites from Hanoch, the Palluites from Pallu,
the Hezronites from Hezron, and the Carmites from Carmi.
Eliab's sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram were the men who turned against Moses and Aaron in Korah's group. They turned against the LORD.
The ground opened and swallowed them and Korah. Fire killed 250 men. This was a warning sign.
But Korah's sons did not die.
Simeon's families were the Nemuelites from Nemuel, the Jaminites from Jamin, and the Jachinites from Jachin.
They were also the Zerahites from Zerah and the Shaulites from Shaul.
Gad's families were the Zephonites from Zephon, the Haggites from Haggi, and the Shunites from Shuni.
They were also the Oznites from Ozni and the Erites from Eri.
They were also the Arodites from Arod and the Arelites from Areli.
Judah's sons Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
Judah's families were the Shelanites from Shelah, the Perezites from Perez, and the Zerahites from Zerah.
Perez's families were the Hezronites from Hezron and the Hamulites from Hamul.
Issachar's families were the Tolaites from Tola and the Punites from Puvah.
They were also the Jashubites from Jashub and the Shimronites from Shimron.
Zebulun's families were the Sardites from Sered, the Elonites from Elon, and the Jahleelites from Jahleel.
Joseph's sons were Manasseh and Ephraim.
Manasseh's families were the Machirites from Machir. Machir was the father of Gilead, and the Gileadites came from Gilead.
Gilead's families were the Iezerites from Iezer and the Helekites from Helek.
They were also the Asrielites from Asriel and the Shechemites from Shechem.
They were also the Shemidaites from Shemida and the Hepherites from Hepher.
Zelophehad, Hepher's son, had no sons. He had only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
Ephraim's families were the Shuthalhites from Shuthelah, the Bachrites from Becher, and the Tahanites from Tahan.
Shuthelah's son Eran had the Eranite family.
These Ephraim families had 32,500 men. These were Joseph's sons by their families.
Benjamin's families were the Belaites from Bela, the Ashbelites from Ashbel, and the Ahiramites from Ahiram.
They were also the Shuphamites from Shupham and the Huphamites from Hupham.
Bela's sons were Ard and Naaman. Their families were the Ardites and the Naamites.
Dan's family was the Shuhamites from Shuham. These were Dan's families.
Asher's families were the Imnites from Imnah, the Ishvites from Ishvi, and the Beriites from Beriah.
Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel. Their families were the Heberites and the Malchielites.
Asher had a daughter named Serah.
Naphtali's families were the Jahzeelites from Jahzeel and the Gunites from Guni.
They were also the Jezerites from Jezer and the Shillemites from Shillem.
So the Israelites who were counted were 601,730 men.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said,
"Share the land among these people as their own land. Share it by the number of names.
Give more land to a big group and less land to a small group. Each group gets land based on how many people were counted.
But share the land by drawing lots. Share it by the names of the family groups of their fathers.
Share the land by drawing lots. Share it between big groups and small groups."
The Levites were counted by their families. They were the Gershonites from Gershon, the Kohathites from Kohath, and the Merarites from Merari.
These Levite families were the Libnites, the Hebronites, the Mahlites, the Mushites, and the Korahites. Kohath was the father of Amram.
Amram's wife was Jochebed. She was a daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. She had Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.
Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they brought wrong fire before the LORD.
The Levites who were counted were 23,000 males who were one month old or older. They were not counted with the other Israelites because they did not get land among the Israelites.
These are the people Moses and Eleazar the priest counted. They counted the Israelites on the flat land of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho.
None of these men were in the count that Moses and Aaron the priest made in the Sinai desert.
The LORD had said they would die in the desert. No one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the family groups of Manasseh son of Joseph, came forward. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood in front of Moses, in front of Eleazar the priest, in front of the leaders, and in front of all the people, at the door of the tent of meeting. They said,
"Our father died in the desert. He was not with Korah's group that turned against the the LORD. He died for his own sin. He had no sons.
Why should our father's name be taken away from his family because he has no son? Give us land with our father's relatives."
So Moses took their problem to the the LORD.
The the LORD said to Moses,
"The daughters of Zelophehad are right. Give them land to own with their father's relatives. Give them their father's land.
Tell the Israelites: If a man dies and has no son, give his land to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, give his land to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, give his land to his father's brothers.
If his father has no brothers, give his land to the closest relative in his family. He will own it. This is a rule for the Israelites, just as the the LORD told Moses."
Then the the LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain of Abarim and look at the land I gave to the Israelites.
After you see it, you will die and be with your people, just as your brother Aaron died.
For when the people turned against Me in the desert of Zin, you did not obey My command to show how holy I am to them at the water. These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the desert of Zin."
Then Moses spoke to the the LORD:
"The the LORD, God of the spirits of all people, please choose a man to lead the people.
He should lead them when they leave and when they return. He should lead them out and bring them in, so the the LORD's people will not be like sheep with no shepherd."
The the LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun. He is a man with the Spirit in him. Put your hand on him.
Stand him in front of Eleazar the priest and in front of all the people. Give him his job while they watch.
Put some of your honor on him, so all the Israelites will listen to him.

He will stand in front of Eleazar the priest. Eleazar will ask the the LORD for him by the Urim. At his word they will go out, and at his word they will come in—Joshua and all the Israelites with him, even all the people."
So Moses did what the the LORD commanded. He took Joshua and stood him before Eleazar the priest and before all the people.
He put his hands on him and gave him his job, just as the the LORD had said through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses. He said,
"Command the Israelites. Tell them to be careful to bring Me My offering—My food for My burnt offerings and My pleasing smell—at the right time."
"Tell them this is the burnt offering to give the LORD: two perfect male lambs, one year old, each day.
Offer one lamb in the morning. Offer the other in the evening."
"With each lamb, give a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with olive oil.
This regular burnt offering was set up at Mount Sinai. It is a fire offering with a pleasing smell to the LORD."
"For each lamb, pour out a drink offering of one-fourth of a hin of wine. Pour it in the holy place as an offering to the LORD.
Offer the second lamb in the evening. Make its grain and drink offerings like the morning ones. It is a burnt offering with a pleasing smell to the LORD."
"On the Sabbath, offer two perfect male lambs, one year old. Also offer a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, with its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for each Sabbath. It is in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering."
"At the start of each month, bring a burnt offering to the LORD. Bring two young bulls, one ram, and seven perfect male lambs one year old.
For each bull, offer a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. For the ram, offer two-tenths of an ephah.
For each lamb, offer one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. This burnt offering has a pleasing smell to the LORD."
"Their drink offerings are half a hin of wine for a bull, one-third of a hin for a ram, and one-fourth of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month, all year long.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering to the LORD to pay for your sins. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering."
"The Passover of the LORD is on day 14 of the first month.
On day 15 of that month is a feast. For seven days, eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day, have a holy meeting. Do not do your regular work."
"Bring a burnt offering to the LORD. Bring two young bulls, one ram, and seven perfect male lambs one year old.
Their grain offering is three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, and two-tenths for the ram.
Offer one-tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering to pay for your sins."
"Offer these in addition to the morning burnt offering, which is the regular burnt offering.
Do this every day for seven days. It is a fire offering with a pleasing smell to the LORD. It is in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day, have a holy meeting. Do not do your regular work."
"On the day you bring the first grain from your harvest to the LORD, at your Feast of Weeks, have a holy meeting. Do not do your regular work.
Bring a burnt offering with a pleasing smell to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old."
"Their grain offering is three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, and two-tenths for the ram.
Offer one-tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat to pay for your sins.
Do this in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. The animals must be perfect for you, with their drink offerings."
On the first day of the seventh month, you must have a holy meeting. Do not do your regular work. It is a day to blow trumpets.
As a pleasing smell to the LORD, bring one burnt offering: one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths with the ram,
and one-tenth with each of the seven lambs.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering to make things right for you.

These are in addition to the monthly burnt offering and its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings. They are a pleasing smell, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
On the tenth day of this seventh month, you must have a holy meeting. You must be humble and not do any work.
Bring to the LORD a burnt offering that smells good: one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Their grain offerings are three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths with the ram,
and one-tenth with each of the seven lambs.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the sin offering for forgiveness and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you must have a holy meeting. Do not do your regular work. Celebrate a feast to the LORD for seven days.
As a pleasing smell to the LORD, bring a burnt offering made by fire: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah with each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths with each of the two rams,
and one-tenth with each of the fourteen lambs.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the second day, you must bring twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, matching their number, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
On the third day, bring eleven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, matching their number, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the fourth day, bring ten young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, matching their number, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the fifth day, bring nine young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, matching their number, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the sixth day, bring eight young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, matching their number, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
On the seventh day, bring seven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, matching their number, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
On the eighth day, you must have a holy meeting. Do not do your regular work.
As a pleasing smell to the LORD, bring a burnt offering made by fire: one bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs. They must have nothing wrong with them.
Bring grain and drink offerings for the bull, the ram, and the lambs, matching their number, as the rules say.
Also bring one male goat as a sin offering. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

You must bring these to the LORD at your special feasts. This is in addition to your promised offerings and free-will offerings. These can be burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings.
So Moses told the Israelites everything the LORD had told him to do.
Moses told the leaders of Israel's tribes, "This is what the LORD commanded."
If a man makes a promise to the LORD, or makes a serious promise to do something, he must not break his word. He must do all he says.
If a young woman who still lives in her father's house makes a promise to the LORD, or makes a serious promise about what she will do,
and her father hears it and says nothing, then all her promises stay in place.
But if her father says no on the day he hears it, none of her promises stay in place. The LORD will forgive her, because her father said no.
If she gets married while she still has promises, or makes careless words that she must keep,
and her husband hears it and says nothing, then her promises stay in place.
But if her husband says no on the day he hears it, he cancels her promise and her careless promise. The LORD will forgive her.
Any promise made by a widow or a divorced woman stays in place for her.
If a woman makes a promise while in her husband's house, or makes a serious promise,
and her husband hears it and says nothing and does not stop her, then all her promises stay in place.
But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears them, then nothing she said in her promises stays in place. Her husband canceled them, and the LORD will forgive her.
A husband can say yes to or cancel any promise or serious promise his wife makes to give up something.
If her husband says nothing day after day, he says yes to all her promises. He says yes to them because he said nothing when he heard them.
But if he cancels them after he hears them, he is to blame.
These are the rules the LORD gave Moses for a man and his wife, and for a father and his young daughter.
He said, "Pay back the Midianites for what they did to Israel. After that, you will die and join your ancestors."
Moses spoke to the people. He said, "Get ready for war. Pick men from among you to fight Midian. They will carry out the the LORD's punishment on Midian.
Send one thousand men from each tribe of Israel to the war."
So twelve thousand men were chosen from Israel. They were ready to fight. One thousand came from each tribe.
Moses sent them to war. He sent one thousand men from each tribe. Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest went with them. He carried the holy things and the trumpets used to sound the alarm.
They fought against Midian, just as the the LORD had told Moses. They killed every man.
They killed the kings of Midian. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. These were the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with a sword.
The Israelites captured the Midianite women and children. They took all their animals and everything they owned.
They burned all the cities where the Midianites lived. They also burned their camps.
They took all the goods and the captives. This included people and animals.
They brought the captives, the goods, and the things they had taken to Moses, Eleazar, and the whole community. They were at the camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan River, near Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar, and all the leaders went out to meet them outside the camp.
Moses was angry with the officers and the leaders of the thousands and hundreds who came back from the war.
Moses said to them, "Why did you let all the women live?
These women led the Israelites to sin against the the LORD. They did it because Balaam told them to. This happened at Peor. That is why the the LORD's people became sick and many died.
Now kill every boy among the little children. Kill every woman who has been with a man.
But keep alive all the young girls who have not been with a man. You may keep them."

Moses said, "Stay outside the camp for seven days. Anyone who killed a person or touched a dead body must wash to be clean. Do this on the third day and on the seventh day. This is for you and the people you captured.
Wash every piece of clothing, every leather thing, everything made from goat hair, and every wooden thing."
Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone to war, "This is the rule of the law the the LORD gave Moses:
Only gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead can go through fire.
Put everything that can stand fire through the fire. Then it will be clean. But it must also be washed with the cleaning water. Everything that cannot stand fire must be washed with water.
On the seventh day, wash your clothes. Then you will be clean. After that, you may come into the camp."
"You and Eleazar the priest and the family leaders of the community must count the people and animals that were taken.
Divide the things taken between the soldiers who went to war and all the people.
From the soldiers who went to war, take one out of every five hundred people, cattle, donkeys, and sheep for the the LORD.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the the LORD.
From the people of Israel's half, take one out of every fifty people, cattle, donkeys, sheep, and all other animals. Give them to the Levites who take care of the the LORD's Holy Tent."
Moses and Eleazar did what the the LORD commanded.
The things the army took were 675,000 sheep.
And they took 32,000 women who had not been with a man.
The half given to the soldiers who went to war was 337,500 sheep, 36,000 cattle, 30,500 donkeys, and 16,000 people.
From the soldiers' half, the offering to the the LORD was 675 sheep.
Moses gave the offering to Eleazar the priest, just as the the LORD had commanded him.
The people of Israel's half, which Moses separated from the soldiers' half, was
From the people of Israel's half, Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals. He gave them to the Levites who take care of the the LORD's Holy Tent, just as the the LORD had commanded him.
The officers over the thousands and hundreds came to Moses.
They said to Moses, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our care. Not one man is missing.
So we bring a gift to the the LORD. It is gold from what each man found: arm bands, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces. We bring it to make up for our sins before the the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar took all the gold items.
All the gold from the commanders and captains was 16,750 shekels.
The soldiers had kept the things they took for themselves.
Moses and Eleazar brought the gold into the Tent of Meeting. It was a reminder for the Israelites before the the LORD.
The people of Reuben and Gad had many animals. They saw the land of Jazer and Gilead. That place was good for animals.
They came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the people.
They said, "Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon.
The land the LORD helped Israel take is good for animals. We, your servants, have animals.
If you are pleased with us, please give this land to us, your servants. Do not make us cross the Jordan River."
Moses said to the people of Gad and Reuben, "Will your brothers go to war while you stay here?
Why do you make the people of Israel not want to go to the land the LORD gave them?
Your fathers did this when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to see the land.
They went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land. Then they made the people of Israel not want to go to the land the LORD gave them.
That day the LORD was very angry. He made a promise.
He said, 'The men twenty years old and older who came out of Egypt will not see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. They did not follow Me all the way.'
Only Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun will see it, because they followed the LORD all the way.
The LORD was angry with Israel. He made them walk in the desert for forty years, until all the people who did evil in the LORD's eyes were gone.
Now you, a new group of sinful men, have taken your fathers' place. You are making the LORD even more angry with Israel.
If you turn away from following Him, He will leave them in the desert again. You will destroy all these people."
The men came near and said, "We will build sheep pens here for our animals and cities for our children.
But we will get ready and go in front of Israel's people. We will help them until they reach their land. Our children will stay in the safe cities, away from the people who live there.
We will not go back to our homes until every Israelite gets his land.
We will not share their land on the other side of the Jordan. Our land is here, east of the Jordan."
Moses said to them, "If you do this, if you get ready to fight for the LORD,
and every soldier crosses the Jordan in front of the LORD until He drives out His enemies,
and the land is taken for the LORD, then you may go back. You will be free from blame before the LORD and Israel. This land will be yours to keep before the LORD.
But if you do not do this, you have sinned against the LORD. Know that your sin will find you.
Build cities for your children and pens for your sheep. Do what you promised."
The people of Gad and Reuben said to Moses, "We, your servants, will do what you say.
Our children, our wives, and all our animals will stay in the cities of Gilead.
But your servants will cross over, ready for battle, to fight for the LORD, just as you said."
Moses told this to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the family leaders of Israel.
Moses said, "If the sons of Gad and Reuben cross the Jordan with you, ready for battle for the LORD, and the land is won for you, then give them Gilead to keep.
But if they do not cross over ready for battle, they must live with you in Canaan."
The people of Gad and Reuben answered, "We will do what the LORD has said.
We will cross into Canaan ready for battle for the LORD. Our land will stay here east of the Jordan."

Moses gave them the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan. He gave them the whole land with its cities and borders. He gave it to Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph.
The people of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran. These were strong cities and sheep pens.
The people of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo, Baal Meon (they changed its name), and Sibmah. They gave new names to the cities they built.
Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and took it. He drove out the Amorites who were there.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he lived there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and took their towns. He called them Havvoth Jair.
Nobah went and took Kenath and its towns. He called it Nobah after himself.
Here are the places where the Israelites went. They left Egypt in groups. Moses and Aaron led them.
Moses wrote down each place they left and each place they stopped. He did this because the the LORD told him to.
They left Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. That was the day after the Passover feast. The Israelites marched out bravely where all the Egyptians could see them.
The Egyptians were burying their firstborn sons, whom the the LORD had killed. The LORD had also punished their gods.
The Israelites left Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They left Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the desert.
They left Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, near Baal-zephon. They camped near Migdol.
They left Pi-hahiroth and crossed the sea into the desert. They walked three days in the desert of Etham and camped at Marah.
They left Marah and came to Elim. There were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees there. They camped there.
They left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They left the Red Sea and camped in the desert of Sin.
They left the desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They left Alush and camped at Rephidim. There was no water there for the people to drink.
They left Rephidim and camped in the desert of Sinai.
They left the desert of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They left Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They left Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shapher.
They left Mount Shapher and camped at Haradah.
They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They left Tahath and camped at Terah.
They left Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They left Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They left Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They left Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They left Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They left Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They left Ezion-geber and camped in the desert of Zin at Kadesh.
They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor because the the LORD told him to. He died there. This was in the fortieth year after the Israelites left Egypt. It was on the first day of the fifth month.
Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The king of Arad was a Canaanite. He lived in the south part of Canaan. He heard that the Israelites were coming.
The Israelites left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
They left Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They left Iye-abarim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They left Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They left Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, near Nebo.
They left the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan River from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho.

He said, "Tell the Israelites this: When you cross the Jordan into Canaan, you must make the people who live there leave. You must break their carved statues and their metal statues. You must tear down the places where people worshiped false gods. Then you will take the land and live there. I gave this land to you to own. You will divide the land by drawing lots for your families. You will give more land to a big family and less to a small family. Each family will get the land where its lot falls. But if you do not make the people leave, the ones you let stay will be like thorns in your eyes and sharp sticks in your sides. They will trouble you in the land where you live. Then I will do to you what I planned to do to them."
The LORD told Moses to tell the Israelites, “When you come into Canaan, this land will be yours. It is the land of Canaan with all its borders.
“Your southern border will start at the desert of Zin, near Edom. It will begin at the east end of the Salt Sea.
“It will turn south of the Scorpion Pass, go through Zin, and end south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it will go to Hazar Addar and cross to Azmon.
“The border will turn from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt. Its end will be at the Sea.
“Your western border will be the Great Sea. That will be your western border.
“This will be your northern border. From the Great Sea, mark out Mount Hor for yourselves.
“From Mount Hor, mark out toward Lebo Hamath. The border will end at Zedad.
“Then the border will go to Ziphron. Its end will be at Hazar Enan. This will be your northern border.
“Mark out your eastern border from Hazar Enan to Shepham.
“The border will go down from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain. It will go down and touch the slope east of the Sea of Chinnereth.
“Then it will go down to the Jordan. Its end will be at the Salt Sea. This is your land with its borders all around.”
Moses told the Israelites, “This is the land you will receive by drawing lots. The LORD commanded that it be given to the nine and a half tribes.
“The tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their land.
“The two and a half tribes received their land east of the Jordan, across from Jericho.”
The LORD spoke to Moses. The LORD said,
“These are the names of the men who will divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
“You will choose one leader from each tribe to divide the land.
“These are the men: from Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
from Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
from Dan, Bukki son of Jogli;
from Manasseh, Hanniel son of Ephod;
from Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
from Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan;
from Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi;
from Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud.”
These were the men the the LORD commanded to give the Israelites their land in Canaan.
The LORD spoke to Moses on the flat land of Moab. This was by the Jordan River near Jericho. He said,
"Tell the people of Israel to give the Levites cities to live in. The cities must come from the land you own. You must also give the Levites open land around the cities.
"The cities are for the Levites to live in. The open land is for their animals, their things, and all their livestock.
"The open land around the cities you give to the Levites must go out 1,000 cubits from the city wall all around.

"You must measure 2,000 cubits outside the city on the east side, 2,000 on the south side, 2,000 on the west side, and 2,000 on the north side. Put the city in the middle. This land will be pasture for the cities.
"You will give six cities to the Levites. These are cities of safety. A person who kills someone by mistake can run to one of them. You will also give the Levites 42 more cities.
"In all, you will give the Levites 48 cities, along with their open land.
"The cities you give must come from the land the people of Israel own. A big family group gives more cities. A small family group gives fewer. Give cities to match the land each group got."
The LORD spoke to Moses again. He said,
"Tell the people of Israel that you are about to cross the Jordan River into Canaan.
"Choose cities of safety for yourselves. A person who kills someone by mistake can run to one of them.
"These cities will be safe places from the person who wants to punish the killer. The killer will not die until he stands trial before the whole community.
"You will give six cities of safety.
"You must give three cities on the east side of the Jordan River. Give three cities in the land of Canaan. All six will be cities of safety.
"These six cities will be safe places for the people of Israel, for strangers, and for people living among you. Anyone who kills a person by mistake can run to one of them.
"But if a person hits someone with an iron tool and the person dies, the hitter is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
"If someone throws a stone and kills a person, the thrower is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
"If someone hits a person with a wooden tool and kills them, the hitter is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
"The person who punishes the killer must put the murderer to death. When he finds the murderer, he must kill him.
"If a person pushes someone because of hate, or throws something at them on purpose, and the person dies,
"or if he hits the person with his hand in hate and the person dies, the hitter is a murderer. The person who punishes the killer must put him to death when he finds him.
"But if a person pushes someone suddenly, without hate, or throws something without meaning to hurt,
"or drops a stone without seeing, and the stone kills someone, and he did not hate the person or try to hurt them,
"then the whole community must judge between the killer and the person who wants to punish him. They must use these rules.

"The community must save the killer from the person who wants to punish him. They must send the killer back to the city of safety he ran to. He must stay there until the high priest dies. The high priest was anointed with holy oil.
"But if the killer leaves the city of safety where he ran,
"and the person who punishes him finds him outside the city, that person may kill the killer. The killer's death is not murder.
"The killer must stay in his city of safety until the high priest dies. After that, he may go back to his own land.
"These rules are for you and your children forever, wherever you live.
"If someone kills a person, the killer may be put to death only if witnesses say so. One witness is not enough to put a person to death.
"Do not take money to spare the life of a murderer. The murderer is guilty and must be put to death.
"Do not take money to let a killer leave his city of safety early. He may not go home before the high priest dies.
"Do not make the land unclean where you live. Murder makes the land unclean. The land cannot be made clean again except by the blood of the murderer.
"Do not make the land unclean where you live, because I, the LORD, live among the people of Israel."

The leaders of Gilead's family group came to Moses. Gilead was the son of Machir, and Machir was the son of Manasseh. They were from Joseph's family. They spoke to Moses and to the leaders of Israel's family groups.
They said, "The LORD told you, our leader, to give the land to Israel's people by drawing lots. The LORD also told you to give our brother Zelophehad's land to his daughters.
But if his daughters marry men from another tribe of Israel, their land will be taken from our tribe. It will be added to the tribe they marry into. Then our tribe will lose that land.
When the special freedom year comes for Israel's people, their land will be added to the tribe they married into. It will be taken away from our tribe."
Moses told the people of Israel what the LORD said. He said, "The tribe of Joseph is right.
This is what the LORD commands about Zelophehad's daughters: They may marry anyone they want. But they must marry a man from their father's tribe.
Land in Israel must not move from one tribe to another. Each person must keep the land of his father's tribe.
Every girl who gets land in Israel must marry a man from her father's tribe. Then Israel's people can keep the land of their fathers.
So no land will move from one tribe to another. Each tribe of Israel must keep its own land."
Zelophehad's daughters did what the LORD told Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married their cousins on their father's side.
They married men from the family groups of Manasseh, who was Joseph's son. Their land stayed with their father's tribe.
These are the rules and laws the LORD gave Israel through Moses. He gave them on the flat land of Moab, by the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel. They were in the desert, east of the Jordan River. They were in the Arabah, near Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It takes eleven days to walk from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea by way of Mount Seir.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses spoke to the Israelites. He told them everything the the LORD had commanded him to say.
This was after he defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
East of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law. He said:
The the LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb. He said, "You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

Turn and travel on. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors. Go to the Arabah, the hills, the lowlands, the Negev, the coast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon. Go as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
See, I have given you this land. Go in and take it. It is the land the the LORD promised to give to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their children after them."
At that time I said to you, "I cannot carry you by myself.
The the LORD your God has made you grow. Today you are as many as the stars in the sky.
May the the LORD, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times more. May He bless you, just as He promised you.
How can I carry your troubles, your loads, and your arguments by myself?
Choose wise, understanding, and known men from your tribes. I will make them your leaders. They will be leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. They will be officers for your tribes."
You answered me and said, "What you said is good. We will do it."
So I took the wise and known men from your tribes and made them leaders over you. They were leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. They were officers for your tribes.
At that time I told your judges, "Listen to your brothers. Judge fairly between a man and his brother or a stranger.
