Do not favor one person over another in court. Listen to the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgment belongs to God. Bring me any case that is too hard for you, and I will hear it."
At that time I told you everything you should do.
Then we left Horeb, just as the the LORD our God commanded us. We traveled through the big and scary desert you saw. We came to Kadesh Barnea.
I said to you, "You have come to the hill country of the Amorites. The the LORD our God is giving it to us.

See, the the LORD your God has given you this land. Go up and take it. Do not be afraid or discouraged. The the LORD your God spoke to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He said He would give it to you."
Then all of you came to me and said, "Let us send men ahead of us. They can explore the land for us. They can bring back a report about the way we should go and the towns we will enter."
That seemed good to me. So I chose twelve men, one from each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country. They came to the Valley of Eshcol and spied it out.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. They reported, "The land the the LORD our God is giving us is good."
But you did not want to go up. You turned against the the LORD your God.
You grumbled in your tents and said, "The the LORD hated us. That is why He brought us out of Egypt. He wanted to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us.
Where can we go? Our brothers have scared us. They say, 'The people there are bigger and taller than we are. Their cities are big and have walls up to the sky. We even saw giants there.'"
Then I said to you, "Do not be afraid of them.
The the LORD your God goes ahead of you. He will fight for you. You saw everything He did for you in Egypt.
You saw how the the LORD your God carried you in the desert, like a man carries his son. He did this all along the way until you came to this place."
But even after this, you did not believe the the LORD your God.
He went ahead of you on the journey. At night He was in the fire, and during the day He was in the cloud. He looked for places for you to camp. He showed you the way you should go.
The the LORD heard your words. He was angry and took an oath. He said, "
Not one of these men from this evil generation will see the good land I promised to give to your fathers.
Only Caleb son of Jephunneh will see it. I will give him and his children the land he walked on, because he followed the the LORD fully."
The the LORD was angry with me too because of you. He said, "You will not go in there either."
But Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will go in. Encourage him, because he will give Israel the land as their share.
Your little ones, whom you said would be taken, and your children who do not yet know right from wrong, will go in. I will give them the land, and they will own it.
But as for you, turn around and go into the desert by way of the Red Sea.

Then you answered me, "We have sinned against the the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the the LORD our God commanded us." So each of you grabbed your weapons and thought it was easy to go up the hill.
But the the LORD said to me, "Tell them, 'Do not go up or fight. I am not with you. You will be beaten by your enemies.'"
I told you this, but you did not listen. You turned against the the LORD's command and went up the hill anyway.
The Amorites who lived in those hills came out to meet you. They chased you like bees. They beat you in Seir all the way to Hormah.
You came back and cried to the the LORD, but the the LORD did not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
So you stayed in Kadesh for many days, as long as you had stayed before.
Then we turned and traveled toward the desert along the Red Sea road, just as the LORD had told me. We went around Mount Seir for many days.
"You have gone around this hill country long enough. Turn north.
Command the people, 'You are about to pass through the land of your brothers, the people of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be very afraid of you. So be very careful.'"
"Do not fight with them. I will not give you any of their land, not even a small piece, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau to own.
You may buy food from them with money, and eat it. You may also buy water from them with money, and drink it.
The LORD your God has blessed you in all your work. He has watched over your trip through this big desert. For forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have not needed anything."
So we passed by our brothers, the people of Esau, who live in Seir. We went along the road through the desert valley, away from Elath and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and took the desert road to Moab.
The LORD said to me, "Do not trouble Moab. Do not start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land, because I have given Ar to the people of Lot to own."
The Emim used to live there. They were a big, strong people, as tall as the Anakites.
People thought they were Rephaim, just like the Anakites. But the Moabites called them Emim.
The Horites used to live in Seir. But the people of Esau chased them out, destroyed them, and settled there, just as Israel did in the land the LORD gave them.
"Now get up and cross the Zered Valley." We crossed it.
We traveled from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley. It took thirty-eight years. By then, all the soldiers of that generation had died, just as the LORD had promised.
The LORD worked against them. He troubled them until they were all gone.
When all the fighting men had died,
"Today you are to cross the border of Moab at Ar.
When you come near the people of Ammon, do not trouble them and do not start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land, because I have given it to the people of Lot to own."
That land was also thought to be Rephaim land. The Rephaim used to live there. The Ammonites called them Zamzummim.
They were a big, strong people, as tall as the Anakites. But the LORD destroyed them. The Ammonites took their place and settled there.
The LORD did the same thing for the people of Esau who live in Seir. He destroyed the Horites before them, and they took their place and settled there. They still live there today.
The Avvim lived in villages as far as Gaza. The Caphtorites came from Caphtor and destroyed them and settled there.
"Get up and move on. Cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have given you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Start to take his land, and fight him.
Today I will begin to make all people everywhere afraid of you. When they hear about you, they will shake and be scared."
From the desert of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon king of Heshbon with a message of peace.
I said, "Let me pass through your land. I will stay on the road and not turn right or left.
You can sell me food for money, and I will eat. You can give me water for money, and I will drink. Just let me pass through on foot.
Let me pass through, as the people of Esau in Seir and the Moabites in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land the LORD our God is giving us."
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through. The LORD your God had made him stubborn and hard-hearted, so He could give him to you.
The LORD said to me, "See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land to you. Now begin to take his land and own it."
Sihon and all his people came out to fight us at Jahaz.
The LORD our God gave him to us. We beat him, his sons, and all his people.
At that time we captured all his cities. We destroyed every city completely. We killed the men, women, and children. We did not leave anyone alive.
We took only the animals and the goods from the cities we captured.
From Aroer by the Arnon Valley to the city in the valley, all the way to Gilead, no city was too strong for us. The LORD our God gave them all to us.
But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites. You stayed away from the Jabbok River, the hill country cities, and everything the LORD our God told us to leave alone.
Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, came out with all his men to fight us at Edrei.
The LORD said to me, "Do not be afraid of him. I have given him, all his people, and his land to you. Do to him what you did to Sihon, the king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So the LORD our God gave Og, the king of Bashan, and all his people into our hands. We beat them until no one was left.
At that time we took all his cities. There was not one city we did not take. There were sixty cities in the whole area of Argob, in Og's kingdom in Bashan.
All these cities had high walls, gates, and bars. There were also many towns without walls.
We destroyed them just as we did to Sihon, the king of Heshbon. We destroyed every city, including the men, women, and children.
But we kept all the animals and the things from the cities for ourselves.
At that time we took the land from the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan. It went from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon.
The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion. The Amorites call it Senir.
We took all the cities on the flat land, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei in Og's kingdom.
Only Og, the king of Bashan, was left of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron. It was about 13 feet long and 6 feet wide. It is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.
At that time we took this land. I gave it to the Reubenites and Gadites. It went from Aroer by the Arnon River and half of the hill country of Gilead with its cities.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan to the half tribe of Manasseh. That was Og's kingdom, all the area of Argob and all Bashan. It was called the land of the Rephaim.
Jair, the son of Manasseh, took all the area of Argob up to the border of the Geshurites and Maachathites. He named the towns of Bashan after himself. They are called Havoth Jair to this day.
To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave land from Gilead to the Arnon River, with the middle of the river as the border. It went to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
The border also included the Jordan River and the Arabah. It went from Kinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, east of the hills of Pisgah.
At that time I told you, "The LORD your God has given you this land to have. All you strong men must cross over in front of your brothers, the Israelites.
Only your wives, your little ones, and your animals may stay in the cities I gave you. I know you have many animals.
Stay there until the LORD gives your brothers rest like He gave you. They will take the land the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you may go back to the land I gave you."
At that time I told Joshua, "You have seen all that the LORD your God did to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.
Do not be afraid of them. The LORD your God Himself fights for you."
At that time I begged the LORD.
"Lord the LORD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand. What god in heaven or on earth can do the things You do and the mighty acts You do?
Please let me go over and see the good land across the Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon."
But the LORD was angry with me because of you. He would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, "That is enough. Do not speak to Me about this again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and look west, north, south, and east. Look with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
But tell Joshua what to do. Make him strong and brave. He will go over before this people. He will help them take the land you see."
So we stayed in the valley across from Beth Peor.
Listen, Israel. I am teaching you the rules and laws to do. Then you may live and take the land the the LORD God of your fathers gives you.
Do not add to what I tell you. Do not take away from it. Keep the commands of the the LORD your God that I give you.
Your eyes saw what the the LORD did at Baal Peor. The LORD your God destroyed every man among you who followed Baal Peor.
But you who stayed close to the the LORD your God are alive today.
See, I taught you rules and laws, just as the the LORD my God told me. Do them in the land you are going to take.
Keep them and do them. They will be your wisdom and understanding before the nations. When they hear all these rules, they will say, “This great nation is wise and understanding.”
What great nation has a god so near as the the LORD our God whenever we call to Him?
What great nation has rules and laws as fair as all this law I set before you today?
Be very careful. Guard yourself, lest you forget the things your eyes saw, and lest they leave your heart all the days of your life. Teach them to your children and your grandchildren.

Remember the day you stood before the the LORD your God at Horeb, when the the LORD said to me, “Gather the people to Me. I will let them hear My words. They will learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth. They will teach their children.”
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain burned with fire up to the sky. There was darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
The LORD spoke to you from the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you did not see a form. You heard only a voice.
He told you His covenant. He commanded you to do the ten commands. He wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the the LORD commanded me to teach you rules and laws, so you can do them in the land you are crossing to take.
Guard yourselves carefully. You saw no form on the day the the LORD spoke to you from the fire at Horeb.
So do not corrupt yourselves. Do not make a carved idol. Do not make a picture of a man or a woman.
Do not make a picture of any animal on the earth, any bird that flies in the sky,
any thing that creeps on the ground, or any fish in the water under the earth.

Do not look up to the sky and see the sun, the moon, and the stars, all the armies of the sky, and be pulled away. Do not bow down to them or serve them. The LORD your God has given them to all the peoples under the sky.
The LORD took you and brought you out of the hard slavery in Egypt. He made you His own people, as you are today.
The LORD was angry with me because of your words. He swore that I would not cross the Jordan or enter the good land the the LORD your God gives you as your own.
I will not cross the Jordan. I will die in this land. But you will cross and take this good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant the the LORD your God made with you. Do not make a carved idol of anything the the LORD your God has forbidden you to make.
The LORD your God is a fire that burns up. He is a jealous God.

When you have children and grandchildren, and you grow old in the land, do not become corrupt. Do not make a carved idol of anything. Do not do evil in the eyes of the the LORD your God. Do not make Him angry.
Today I call heaven and earth to speak against you. You will quickly be destroyed from the land you are crossing the Jordan to take. You will not live there long. You will be completely destroyed.
The LORD will scatter you among the nations. Only a few of you will be left where the the LORD sends you.
There you will serve gods made by human hands, wood and stone. They cannot see, hear, eat, or smell.
But from there you will seek the the LORD your God, and you will find Him. You will search with all your heart and all your soul.
When all these things happen to you, in the last days, you will return to the the LORD your God and obey His voice.
The LORD your God is kind. He will not leave you or destroy you. He will not forget the covenant with your fathers that He promised them.
Ask about the days that were before you, since God made man on the earth. Ask from one end of the sky to the other. Has anything so great happened? Has anything like it been heard?
Has any people heard the voice of God speaking from the fire, as you heard, and lived?

Has any god tried to take a nation for himself from another nation, with tests, signs, wonders, war, great power, and terrible acts? That is what the the LORD your God did for you in Egypt, and you saw it.
You were shown this so you would know that the the LORD is God. There is no other.
From heaven He let you hear His voice to teach you. On earth He let you see His great fire. You heard His words from the fire.
Because He loved your fathers and chose their children after them, He brought you out of Egypt by His great power.
He drove out nations greater and stronger than you, so He could bring you in and give you their land as your own today.
Know today, and keep it in mind, that the the LORD is God in heaven above and on earth below. There is no other.
Keep His rules and commands that I give you today, so it may go well with you and your children after you. Then you will live long on the land the the LORD your God gives you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three cities east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
A person who killed his neighbor by accident, without hating him before, could run to one of these cities and live.
Bezer in the wilderness plateau was for the Reubenites. Ramoth in Gilead was for the Gadites. Golan in Bashan was for the Manassites.
This is the law Moses set before the people of Israel.
These are the rules, laws, and decisions Moses spoke to the people of Israel when they came out of Egypt.

This was east of the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon. Moses and the people of Israel defeated him when they came out of Egypt.
They took his land and the land of Og king of Bashan. These were the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan.
Their land went from Aroer by the Arnon Valley to Mount Sirion, that is, Hermon.
It also included all the Arabah east of the Jordan, to the Sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses called all Israel together and said, “Listen, Israel. Today I will tell you the rules and laws I speak to you. Learn them and do them.”
The LORD our God made an agreement with us at Horeb.
The LORD did not make this agreement with our fathers. He made it with us, with all of us who are alive here today.
The LORD spoke to you face to face from the fire on the mountain.
At that time I stood between the LORD and you to tell you what the LORD said. You were afraid of the fire, so you did not go up the mountain. Then the LORD said:
“I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of Egypt, out of the place where you were slaves.
You must not have other gods before Me.
You must not make a carved picture or statue of anything in the sky above, on the earth below, or in the water under the earth.

You must not bow down to them or serve them. I am the LORD your God. I want you to worship only Me. I punish children for the wrongs of their fathers, down to the third and fourth family after those who hate Me.
But I show love to a thousand families of those who love Me and obey My rules.
You must not use the name of the LORD your God in a wrong way. The LORD will not let anyone go free who uses His name in a wrong way.” “
Keep the Sabbath day holy. Rest on that day, as the LORD your God told you.
Work for six days and do all your work.

But the seventh day is a Sabbath for the LORD your God. On that day you must not work. You, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, and all your animals must rest. The stranger who lives in your town must rest too. Then your male and female servants can rest like you.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. The LORD your God brought you out with His strong hand and His power. So the LORD your God told you to keep the Sabbath day.” “
Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God told you. Then you will live a long time, and things will go well for you in the land the LORD your God gives you.
You must not cheat with someone else’s husband or wife.
You must not lie about your neighbor in court.
You must not want your neighbor’s wife. You must not want your neighbor’s house, field, male servant, female servant, ox, donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”

These are the words the LORD spoke in a loud voice to all your people from the fire, the cloud, and the thick dark cloud on the mountain. He did not say anything else. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice from the dark, and the mountain was burning with fire, the leaders of your tribes and your elders came to me.
You said, “Look! The LORD our God has shown us His glory and His great power. We heard His voice from the fire. Today we saw that a person can live even when God talks to him.
But now, why should we die? This big fire will burn us up, and we will die! If we hear the LORD our God’s voice any more, we will die.
What person has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking from the fire, like we did, and stayed alive?
You go near and listen to everything the LORD our God says. Then you tell us everything the LORD our God tells you. We will listen and do it.”
The LORD heard the words you spoke to me. He said to me, “I heard the words these people spoke to you. They spoke well. All they said was good.”
The LORD said, “If only they had a heart that wanted to fear Me and keep all My rules all the time! Then things would go well for them and their children forever.”
The LORD said, “Go and tell them, ‘Go back to your tents.’”
The LORD said, “But you, stand here with Me. I will speak to you all the commands, rules, and laws you must teach them. They must do them in the land I am giving them to own.”
So be careful to do what the LORD your God told you. Do not turn to the right or the left.
Walk in all the ways the LORD your God told you, so that you may live, do well, and live a long time in the land you will own.
These are the rules and laws the the LORD your God told me to teach you. You will follow them in the land you are going to take.
Then you and your children and grandchildren will respect the the LORD your God all the days of your life. You will keep all His rules that I give you. Then your days will last longer.
Listen, Israel! Be careful to obey these rules. Then things will go well for you. You will grow in number in a good land. The LORD, the God of your fathers, promised this to you.
Listen, Israel! The LORD our God is the one and only the LORD.
You must love the the LORD your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength.
These words that I command you today must stay in your heart.
Teach them carefully to your children. Talk about them when you sit at home, when you walk on the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Tie them on your hand as a sign. Wear them on your forehead.
Write them on the door frames of your house and on your gates.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land He promised to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He will give you big, good cities that you did not build.

You will live in houses full of good things that you did not fill. You will use wells that you did not dig. You will eat from vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant. You will eat and be full.
Be careful not to forget the the LORD. He brought you out of Egypt. He brought you out of slavery.
Respect the the LORD your God. Serve Him. Make promises using His name.
Do not follow other gods. Do not follow the gods of the people around you.
The the LORD your God is with you. He is a jealous God. Do not make Him angry, or He will destroy you from the land.
Do not test the the LORD your God. You tested Him at Massah.
Be careful to obey the commands of the the LORD your God. Obey His rules and laws that He gave you.
Do what the the LORD says is right and good. Then things will go well for you. You will go in and take the good land the the LORD promised to your fathers.
He will drive out all your enemies in front of you, as the the LORD said.
Later, your son will ask you, “What do these rules mean? The the LORD our God told you to obey them.”

Then you will say to your son, “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt. But the the LORD brought us out of Egypt with His strong hand. “We saw the the LORD do big and scary signs and wonders in Egypt. He did them against Pharaoh and all his family. “He brought us out of there. He led us to this land. He gave us the land He promised to our fathers. “The The LORD told us to obey all these rules. He told us to respect the the LORD our God. Then we will do well and live, like we do today. “If we are careful to obey all these commands before the the LORD our God, just as He told us, then it will count as doing right for us.”

When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are going to take, He will drive out many peoples before you. They are the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. These are seven peoples, and they are bigger and stronger than you.
The the LORD your God will give them to you. You must defeat them and destroy them completely. Do not make an agreement with them. Do not show them mercy.
Do not marry them. Do not give your daughter to their son. Do not take their daughter for your son.
They will turn your sons and daughters away from Me. They will serve other gods. Then the the LORD will be angry with you. He will quickly destroy you.
This is what you must do to them: tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved idols in fire.
You are a holy people to the the LORD your God. The the LORD your God chose you to be His special people. He chose you from all the peoples on the earth.
The the LORD did not choose you because you were many. You were the fewest of all peoples.

The the LORD chose you because He loved you. He kept the promise He made to your fathers. He brought you out with a strong hand. He saved you from slavery in Egypt. He saved you from Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
So know this: The the LORD your God is God. He is the faithful God. He keeps His agreement and His faithful love for a thousand generations. He does this for those who love Him and keep His commands.
But He pays back those who hate Him. He destroys them. He will not wait. He will pay them back.
So keep the commands, laws, and rules I give you today. Do what they say.
If you listen to these rules and keep them and do them, then the the LORD your God will keep His agreement and faithful love with you, as He promised your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, and make you grow. He will bless your children and your crops. He will bless your grain, wine, and oil. He will bless your young cows and sheep in the land He promised your fathers. He promised to give this land to you.
You will be blessed more than all peoples. No man or woman among you will be unable to have children. None of your animals will be unable to have young.
The the LORD will take away all sickness from you. He will not put the terrible diseases you knew in Egypt on you. He will put them on your enemies.
You will destroy all the peoples the the LORD your God gives you. Do not feel sorry for them. Do not serve their gods, because that would trap you.
You may think in your heart that these peoples are bigger than me. You may wonder how you can push them out.
Do not be afraid of them. Remember what the the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt.

Remember the great troubles, signs, and wonders you saw with your own eyes. Remember the the LORD your God's strong hand and outstretched arm. He brought you out. The the LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you fear.
The the LORD your God will also send hornets among them. He will do this until those left and those hiding from you are destroyed.
Do not be afraid of them. The the LORD your God is with you. He is great and fearsome.
The the LORD your God will drive out these peoples little by little. You will not be able to destroy them all at once. If you did, wild animals would grow too many and hurt you.
The the LORD your God will give them to you. He will throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will let you capture their kings. You will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will stand against you until you destroy them.
You must burn their carved gods in fire. Do not want their silver or gold. Do not take it for you, or it will trap you. It is hated by the the LORD your God.
Do not bring that hated thing into your house. You would become like it. Hate it completely. Hate it fully, because it is set apart to be destroyed.
Keep all the commands I give you today. Then you will live. You will grow. You will go in and take the land the the LORD promised to your fathers.

Remember how the the LORD your God led you through the desert for forty years. He did this to make you humble. He tested you. He wanted to know what was in your heart. He wanted to know if you would keep His commands or not.

He let you go hungry. Then He fed you with manna. You and your fathers had never seen this food before. He did this so you would learn that people do not live by bread alone. People live by every word that comes from the the LORD’s mouth.
Your clothes did not wear out. Your feet did not swell. This was true for forty years.
Know in your heart that the the LORD your God trains you, just like a man trains his son.
Keep the commands of the the LORD your God. Walk in His ways. Fear Him.
The The LORD your God is bringing you into a good land. It has streams and springs. Water comes from deep places in the valleys and hills.
It is a land with wheat and barley. It has vines, figs, and pomegranates. It has olive trees for oil and honey.
You will have plenty of bread there. You will not lack anything. The stones there are iron. You can dig copper from the hills.
When you have eaten and are full, praise the the LORD your God for the good land He has given you.
Be careful. Do not forget the the LORD your God. Do not stop keeping His commands, His rules, and His laws that I give you today.
When you have eaten and are full, when you have built good houses and live in them,
and when your herds and flocks grow, and your silver and gold grow, and everything you have grows,
do not let your heart get proud. Do not forget the the LORD your God. He brought you out of Egypt. He brought you out of slavery.
He led you through the big and scary desert. There were snakes and scorpions. There was no water. But He gave you water from hard rock.
He fed you with manna in the desert. Your fathers had not known this food. He did this to make you humble and to test you. In the end, He wanted to do good for you.
Do not say in your heart, “My own power and strength made me rich.”
Remember the the LORD your God. He is the One who gives you the power to get wealth. He does this to keep the promise He made to your fathers, just as He does today.
If you forget the the LORD your God, and go after other gods, and serve them and bow down to them, I tell you today that you will be destroyed.
The the LORD will destroy other nations for you. In the same way, you will be destroyed if you do not obey the the LORD your God.

Listen, people of Israel. Today you are crossing the Jordan River. You will go in and take land from nations that are bigger and stronger than you. Their cities are big, and their walls reach up to the sky.
These people are big and tall. They are the Anakites. You know about them. You have heard people say, "Who can fight the Anakites and win?"

But today you need to know this. The LORD your God is the One who goes before you. He is like a fire that burns everything up. He will destroy those people. He will make them fall before you. You will drive them out and destroy them fast, just like the LORD promised you.

The LORD your God will push them out before you. Do not say in your heart, "I am so good. That is why the LORD brought me here to take this land." It is because those nations are bad that the LORD is pushing them out before you.

You are not going in to take their land because you are good or have a clean heart. You are going in because those nations are bad. The LORD your God is pushing them out before you. He is keeping the promise He made to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know this. The LORD your God is giving you this good land. It is not because you do right. You are a stubborn people.
Remember this. Do not forget how you made the LORD your God angry in the desert. From the day you left Egypt until you came here, you kept saying no to the LORD.
At Mount Horeb you made the LORD angry. He was so angry He wanted to destroy you.

I went up the mountain to get the stone tablets. They were the tablets of the agreement the LORD made with you. I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I did not eat bread. I did not drink water.
The LORD gave me the two stone tablets. God wrote on them with His finger. They had all the words the LORD spoke to you from the fire on the mountain on the day you all came together.
After forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets. They were the tablets of the agreement.

The LORD said to me, "Get up. Go down from here fast. Your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have ruined themselves. They quickly turned away from what I told them to do. They made a metal god for themselves."
The LORD also said to me, "I have seen these people. They are very stubborn."
"Leave Me alone. I will destroy them. I will wipe out their name from under the sky. Then I will make you into a nation bigger and stronger than they are."
So I turned and went down the mountain. The mountain was on fire. I had the two tablets of the agreement in my hands.
I saw that you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made a metal calf for yourselves. You quickly turned away from what the LORD told you to do.
So I took the two tablets. I threw them down. I broke them in front of you.

Then I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, just like before. I did not eat bread. I did not drink water. I did this because of all the sin you did. You did bad things in front of the LORD. You made Him angry.
I was afraid of the LORD's anger. He was so angry He wanted to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me that time too.
The LORD was very angry with Aaron. He wanted to destroy him. But I prayed for Aaron at that time too.
I took the sinful calf you made. I burned it in the fire. I crushed it. I ground it into dust. Then I threw the dust into the stream that ran down the mountain.
You also made the LORD angry at Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth Hattaavah.
When the LORD sent you out from Kadesh Barnea, He said, "Go up and take the land I gave you." But you went against what the LORD your God told you. You did not believe Him. You did not listen to Him.
You have been going against the LORD since the day I met you.
So I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights. The LORD had said He would destroy you.
I prayed to the LORD. I said, "O Lord, the LORD, do not destroy Your people or the people You call Your own. You saved them with Your great power. You brought them out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Remember Your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at how stubborn these people are. Do not look at their bad ways or their sin.
"Otherwise the people in the land You brought us from will say, 'The LORD could not bring them into the land He promised. He hated them. So He brought them out to die in the desert.'
"But they are Your people. They are Your special treasure. You brought them out with Your strong hand and Your mighty arm."
At that time the LORD said to me, “Cut two stone tablets for yourself, like the first ones. Go up the mountain to Me. Make a wooden box.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, the ones you broke. Put them in the box.”
So I made a box of acacia wood. I cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Then I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.

The LORD wrote on the tablets the same words as before. They were the Ten Commandments. The LORD had spoken them to you on the mountain from the fire when all the people gathered. Then the LORD gave the tablets to me.
I turned and went down the mountain. I put the tablets in the box I had made, just as the LORD told me. They are there now.
The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene Jaakan to Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there. His son Eleazar became priest after him.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah and then to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi. They carry the box that holds the LORD's covenant. They stand before the LORD to serve Him. They bless people in His name. They still do this today.
That is why Levi did not get land like his brothers. The LORD is his share, just as the LORD your God said to him.
I stood on the mountain forty days and forty nights, like the first time. The LORD listened to me then too. The LORD did not want to destroy you.
Then the LORD said to me, “Get up and go. Travel ahead of the people. They will go in and take the land I promised to give their fathers.”

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? He asks you to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to love Him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
Keep His commands and His rules that I am giving you today. This is for your good.
Look, the sky and everything above it belong to the LORD your God. The earth and everything in it belong to Him too.
But The LORD cared for your fathers and loved them. He chose you, their children, after them. Out of all the peoples, He chose you. This is true today.
So change your hearts. Do not be stubborn anymore.
The LORD your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords. He is great, strong, and to be feared. He does not show favoritism. He does not take bribes.
He makes sure orphans and widows get justice. He loves foreigners and gives them food and clothes.
You must love foreigners too, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
Fear the LORD your God and serve Him. Stay close to Him. Swear by His name.
He is your praise. He is your God. He did these great and awesome things that your eyes saw.
Your fathers went down to Egypt with seventy people. Now the LORD your God has made you as many as the stars in the sky.
Love the LORD your God every day. Keep His rules and commands.

You need to know today that your children did not see what I am talking about. They did not see the LORD your God teach you. They did not see His great power, His strong hand, and His arm that He stretched out.
They did not see His signs and what He did in Egypt to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and to all his land.
They did not see what He did to Egypt's army, its horses, and its chariots. He made the Red Sea cover them when they chased you. The LORD destroyed them, and they are still gone today.
They did not see what He did for you in the desert until you came to this place.

They did not see what He did to Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, son of Reuben. The ground opened its mouth and swallowed them, their homes, their tents, and everything that was with them. This happened right in front of all Israel.
But your eyes saw all the great things the LORD did.
Keep all the command I give you today. Then you will be strong. You will go in and take the land you are crossing over to take.
Then you will live a long time on the land. The LORD promised it to your fathers and to their children after them. It is a land with plenty of milk and honey.
The land you are going to take is not like Egypt. You came out of Egypt. There you planted seeds and watered them by foot, like a garden.
But the land you are crossing into is a land of hills and valleys. It drinks rain from the sky.
It is a land the LORD your God cares for. His eyes are on it all the time, from the start of the year to the end.
If you listen carefully to my commands that I give you today, and love the LORD your God and serve Him with all your heart and all your soul,
then I will send rain on your land at the right time. I will send the early rain and the late rain. You will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.
I will give grass in your field for your animals. You will eat and be full.
Be careful. Do not let your heart be tricked. Do not turn away and serve other gods. Do not bow down to them.
If you do, the LORD's anger will burn against you. He will close the sky so there is no rain. The land will not give its crops. You will soon die off the good land the LORD is giving you.
Keep these words of mine in your heart and in your soul. Tie them on your hand as a sign. Let them be like bands between your eyes.
Teach them to your children. Talk about them when you sit at home, when you walk on the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Write them on the door frames of your house and on your gates.
Then your days and your children's days will be many on the land. The LORD promised to give it to your fathers. They will be as long as the sky is above the earth.
If you are careful to keep all these things I command you to do, and love the LORD your God, walk in all His ways, and stay close to Him,
then the LORD will drive out all these nations in front of you. You will take over nations that are bigger and stronger than you.
Every place where the bottom of your foot steps will be yours. Your border will stretch from the desert to Lebanon, and from the Euphrates River to the western sea.
No one will be able to stand against you. The LORD your God will make all the people in the land you walk on afraid of you. This is what He promised you.
Look, today I set before you a blessing and a curse.
You get the blessing if you obey the commands of the LORD your God that I give you today.
You get the curse if you do not obey the commands of the LORD your God. Do not turn from the way I command you today. Do not follow other gods you have not known.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are going to take, put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Those mountains are across the Jordan. They are west of the road, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the valley. They are near Gilgal, by the big trees of Moreh.
You are crossing the Jordan to go in and take the land the LORD your God is giving you. Take it and live in it.
Be careful to do all the rules and decisions I set before you today.
These are the rules and laws you must keep doing all the days you are alive on the land. The LORD God of your fathers gave it to you to own.
You must destroy all the places where the nations you will take over served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Break down their altars. Break their stone pillars. Burn their Asherah poles with fire. Cut down the carved images of their gods. Wipe out their names from that place.
Do not worship the the LORD your God like that.
Instead, look for the place the the LORD your God will choose from all your tribes to put His name there. Go there.
Bring there your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tenth parts, the gifts from your hand, your promises, your free gifts, and the firstborn of your cows and sheep.
There, before the the LORD your God, you and your families will eat and be glad in all the work your hands have done, because the the LORD your God blessed you.
Do not do as we do here today, each person doing what seems right to him.
For you have not yet come to the rest and the land the the LORD your God is giving you.
You will cross the Jordan and live in the land the the LORD your God gives you to own. He will give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you will live safely.

Then the place the the LORD your God chooses to put His name will be where you bring everything I command you: your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tenth parts, the gifts from your hand, and the best of your promises you make to the the LORD.
Be glad before the the LORD your God, you, your sons, your daughters, your male servants, your female servants, and the Levite in your towns, because he has no land or share with you.
Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in any place you see.
Offer your burnt offerings only in the place the the LORD will choose in one of your tribes. There do everything I command you.
But you may kill and eat meat in any of your towns, as much as you want, with the blessing of the the LORD your God. The clean and the unclean may eat it, like a deer or a gazelle.
But do not eat the blood. Pour it on the ground like water.
In your towns you may not eat the tenth part of your grain, wine, or oil, or the firstborn of your cows or sheep, or any of your promises or free gifts from your hand.

Eat them only before the the LORD your God in the place the the LORD your God chooses. You, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, and the Levite in your towns will eat them. Be glad before the the LORD your God in all the work your hands have done.
Be careful not to forget the Levite as long as you live in your land.
When the the LORD your God makes your land bigger, as He promised you, and you want to eat meat, you may eat meat whenever you want.

If the place the the LORD your God chooses to put His name is too far from you, then you may kill animals from your cows or your sheep that the the LORD has given you, as I commanded you. Eat them in your towns, as much as you want.
Eat them like you eat a deer or a gazelle. The unclean and the clean may eat them together.
But be strong and do not eat the blood, because the blood is the life. Do not eat the life with the meat.
Do not eat it. Pour it on the ground like water.
Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, because you do what is right in the eyes of the the LORD.
But take your holy things and your promises, and go to the place the the LORD chooses.
Offer the meat and blood of your burnt offerings on the altar of the the LORD your God. The blood of your sacrifices will be poured on the altar of the the LORD your God, and you may eat the meat.
Listen and obey all these words I command you, so that it may go well forever for you and your children after you, because you do what is good and right in the eyes of the the LORD your God.
When the the LORD your God removes the nations before you, and you take their land and you live in it,
be careful not to be trapped into following them after they are destroyed before you. Do not ask about their gods, saying, "How did these nations serve their gods? I will do the same."
Do not do that to the the LORD your God, because they did for their gods every terrible thing the the LORD hates. They even burned their sons and daughters in fire for their gods.
Be careful to do everything I command you. Do not add to it, and do not take away from it.
If a prophet or dreamer rises among you and gives you a sign or wonder,
and that sign or wonder happens, he may say, "Let us go after other gods you do not know and serve them."
Do not listen to that prophet or dreamer. the LORD your God is testing you to see if you love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
You must follow the LORD your God and fear Him. Keep His commands and obey His voice. Serve Him and stay close to Him.

That prophet or dreamer must be put to death, because he spoke against the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt and saved you from slavery. He tried to lead you away from the path the LORD your God commanded you to walk. Remove the evil from among you.
If your brother, your son or daughter, your wife, or your close friend secretly tries to lead you away, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods you and your fathers do not know,"
gods of people who live around you, from one end of the earth to the other,
do not give in to him or listen to him. Do not feel sorry for him. Do not spare him. Do not hide him.
You must kill him. You must be the first to put him to death. Then all the people must help.
Stone him to death, because he tried to pull you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt and out of slavery.
Then all Israel will hear and be afraid. They will not do such a bad thing again among you.
If you hear that in one of your cities the LORD your God gives you to live in,
bad men have gone out from among you and led the people of their city away, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods you do not know,"
then check it well. Ask and search carefully. If it is true that this terrible thing happened among you,
you must strike the people of that city with the sword. Destroy it completely, and all that is in it, even its animals.
Gather all its goods in the street and burn the city and all its goods with fire as a whole offering to the LORD your God. It must be a heap of ruins forever. It must not be rebuilt.
Do not keep anything that was set apart to be destroyed. Then the LORD may turn from His great anger and be kind to you. He will have mercy on you and make you many, as He promised your fathers.
Do this if you obey the LORD your God and keep all His commands that I give you today, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
You are the children of the LORD your God. Do not cut yourselves. Do not shave the front of your head for someone who died.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God. The LORD chose you to be His special people out of all the people on earth.
Do not eat anything that is unclean.
You may eat these animals: ox, sheep, and goat.
You may also eat deer, gazelle, roe deer, wild goat, ibex, antelope, and mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal with a split hoof that chews its cud.
But do not eat the camel, the rabbit, or the rock badger. They chew the cud, but their hooves are not split. So they are unclean for you.
Do not eat the pig. It has a split hoof, but it does not chew the cud. It is unclean for you. Do not eat its meat. Do not touch its dead body.
You may eat anything from the water that has fins and scales.
Do not eat anything from the water that does not have fins and scales. It is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But do not eat these birds: the eagle, the vulture, and the black vulture.
Do not eat the kite, the falcon, or any kind of hawk.
Do not eat any kind of raven.
Do not eat the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, or any kind of hawk.
Do not eat the little owl, the great owl, or the white owl.
Do not eat the desert owl, the osprey, or the cormorant.
Do not eat the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, or the bat.
All flying insects are unclean for you. Do not eat them.
You may eat any clean flying thing.

Do not eat an animal that dies on its own. Give it to the stranger who lives in your town. He may eat it. Or sell it to a foreigner. You are a holy people to the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Be sure to give one-tenth of all the crops your fields grow each year.

Eat the tenth of your grain, new wine, and oil before the LORD your God. Also eat the firstborn of your cattle and sheep. Do this in the place the LORD your God chooses for His name. Do this so you will learn to respect the LORD your God all your days.
If the trip is too long for you, and you cannot carry your tithe because the place the LORD your God chooses is too far away, and the LORD your God has blessed you, then...
trade your tithe for money. Carry the money in your hand. Go to the place the LORD your God chooses.
Spend the money on anything you want: cattle, sheep, wine, beer, or anything else you like. Eat it there before the LORD your God. You and your family should be happy.
Do not forget the Levite who lives in your town. He has no land like you do.
Every three years, bring a tenth of all your crops from that year. Store it in your towns.
Then the Levite, the stranger, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns can come and eat. They will be full. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all the work you do.
At the end of every seven years, you must cancel debts.
This is the rule for the release: If someone lent money to another person, let it go. Do not ask your neighbor or your brother to pay you back. This is the the LORD's special year to cancel debts.
You may ask a person from another country to pay you back, but you must let your brother's debt go.
There should not be poor people among you. The the LORD your God will bless you a lot in the land He is giving you to own.
You will be blessed if you listen carefully to the the LORD your God and obey all these rules I give you today.
The the LORD your God will bless you, just as He promised. You will lend money to many nations, but you will not borrow from them. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
If one of your brothers is poor in any town in the land the the LORD your God is giving you, do not be stubborn, and do not refuse to help him.
Instead, help him. Lend him what he needs.

Be careful. Do not let an evil thought grow in your heart. Do not say, "The seventh year is near, the year to cancel debts," and then look down on your poor brother and give him nothing. He may cry to the the LORD against you, and you will have sinned.
Give to him freely. Do not feel bad in your heart when you give. Because of this, the the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you do.
There will always be poor people in the land. That is why I command you to help your brother, your poor and needy people in your land.
If a Hebrew man or woman is sold to you, they must serve you for six years. In the seventh year, you must let them go free.
When you let them go free, do not send them away with nothing.
Give them gifts from your sheep, your grain, and your wine. Give to them as the the LORD your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the the LORD your God set you free. That is why I give you this command today.
But if your servant says, "I do not want to leave you," because he loves your family and has a good life with you,
then take a sharp tool and push it through his ear into the door. He will be your servant for the rest of his life. Do the same for your female servant.
Do not think it is hard to let them go free. They served you six years, which is worth twice as much as a hired worker. The the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
Set apart to the the LORD your God every firstborn male from your cattle and sheep. Do not make your firstborn ox work, and do not cut the wool from your firstborn sheep.
Each year, you and your family must eat them in the place the the LORD your God chooses.
If an animal has something wrong with it, such as being lame or blind or having another bad problem, do not sacrifice it to the the LORD your God.
You may eat it in your own towns. People who are clean and people who are not clean may eat it, like a gazelle or a deer.
But do not eat the blood. Pour it on the ground like water.
Watch for the month called Abib. Celebrate the Passover for the LORD your God. In that month, the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt at night.
Offer the Passover to the LORD your God. Use cattle or sheep. Do it at the place the LORD chooses for His name to stay.

Do not eat bread with yeast with it. For seven days eat flat bread with it. This bread is bread of hard times. You left Egypt fast. Eat it so you remember the day you left Egypt all the days of your life.
For seven days, no yeast should be seen anywhere in your land. Also, the meat you kill on the first evening must not stay until morning.
You cannot offer the Passover in just any town the LORD your God gives you.
Offer the Passover in the evening at the place the LORD your God chooses for His name. Do it at the set time you left Egypt.
Cook it and eat it at the place the LORD your God chooses. In the morning, go back to your tents.
Eat flat bread for six days. On the seventh day, have a special meeting for the LORD your God. Do no work that day.
Count seven weeks. Start counting when you first cut the grain.
Celebrate the Feast of Weeks for the LORD your God. Give a free gift from your hand. Give as much as the LORD your God has blessed you.

Be glad before the LORD your God at the place He chooses for His name. Be glad with your son and daughter, your servants, the Levite in your town, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow among you.
Remember you were a slave in Egypt. Keep and obey these laws.
Celebrate the Feast of Shelters for seven days. Do it after you gather your grain and your wine.
Be glad at your feast. Be glad with your son and daughter, your servants, the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow in your town.
Celebrate for seven days for the LORD your God at the place He chooses. The LORD your God will bless all your crops and all your work. You will be very glad.

Three times a year all your men must come before the LORD your God at the place He chooses. Come at the Feast of Flat Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Shelters. No one should come with empty hands.
Each man should give as he can, as the LORD your God has blessed him.
Appoint judges and officers for your tribes in all your towns the LORD your God gives you. They must judge the people fairly.
Do not twist justice. Do not favor one person over another. Do not take a bribe. A bribe blinds wise people and changes the words of good people.
Follow only what is right. Then you will live and keep the land the LORD your God gives you.
Do not plant a tree for a false god next to the altar you make for the LORD your God.
Do not set up a stone pillar. The LORD your God hates it.
Do not give the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has something wrong with it. That is very wrong to the LORD your God.
If a man or woman in one of your towns does something bad in the eyes of the LORD your God, and breaks His promise,
and goes to serve other gods, and bows down to them, or to the sun, or the moon, or all the stars in the sky, which I did not command,
and you are told about it and hear it, look into it well. If it is true that this bad thing happened in Israel,
take that man or woman to your city gate. Throw stones at them until they die.
The person who dies must be put to death because two or three people saw it. No one may be put to death because only one person saw it.
The witnesses must be the first to put him to death. Then all the people must help. Remove the bad from among you.
If a case is too hard for you to judge, like between one kind of blood and another, or one law and another, or one hurt and another, then go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
Go to the Levite priests and to the judge who is in office then. Ask them, and they will tell you the right answer.
Do what they say from that place the LORD chooses. Be careful to do all they teach you.
Follow the law they teach you and the decision they give you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left.
Anyone who proudly refuses to listen to the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or to the judge, must die. Remove the bad from Israel.
Then all the people will hear and be afraid. They will not be so proud again.
When you enter the land the LORD your God gives you and take it and live there, you may say, "Let us set a king over us like all the nations around us."
You must set over you the king the LORD your God chooses. He must be from your brothers. You may not set a foreigner over you, who is not your brother.
The king must not get many horses for himself. He must not send the people back to Egypt to get more horses, because the LORD has said to you, "You must not go back that way again."
He must not take many wives, or his heart will turn away. He must not get too much silver and gold.
When he sits on his king's seat, he must write a copy of this law on a scroll. He must do it in front of the Levite priests.
It must stay with him. He must read it all his life. Then he will learn to respect the LORD his God and keep all the words of this law and these rules. He will do them.
Then his heart will not be proud over his brothers, and he will not turn from the command to the right or to the left. Then he and his sons will rule a long time over Israel.
The priests from the tribe of Levi will not get land with the rest of Israel. They will eat the food offerings given to the the LORD. That is their share.
They will not have land with their brothers. The the LORD is their share, just like He said.
This is what the priests get from the people, from those who bring animals to offer: If it is an ox or a sheep, they give the priest the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.
Give him the first of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool from your sheep.
The the LORD your God chose him and his sons from all your tribes to stand and serve the the LORD all their lives.
If a Levite comes from one of your towns, from anywhere in Israel where he lives, and he wants to go to the place the the LORD chooses,
he may serve in the name of the the LORD his God, like all his brother Levites who stand there before the the LORD.
They will eat the same share. They can also keep money from selling their family things.
When you enter the land the the LORD your God gives you, do not learn to do the bad things those nations do.
No one among you may burn his son or daughter as an offering, or tell fortunes, or read signs, or do magic.
No one may cast spells, ask a medium or fortune-teller, or try to talk to the dead.
Anyone who does these things disgusts the the LORD. Because of these bad things, the the LORD your God will drive those nations out before you.
You must be blameless before the the LORD your God.
The nations you are taking the land from listen to fortune-tellers and sign readers. But the the LORD your God has not allowed you to do that.
The the LORD your God will raise up a prophet like me from among you, from your brothers. You must listen to him.

This is what you asked the the LORD your God for at Horeb on the day the people met together. You said, "Do not let me hear the voice of the the LORD my God again. Do not let me see this great fire again, or I will die."
The the LORD said to me, "They have spoken well.
I will raise up a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
Anyone who does not listen to My words that he speaks in My name, I will hold him responsible.
But a prophet who dares to speak a word in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die."
You may say in your heart, "How will we know if the the LORD did not speak?"
If a prophet speaks in the the LORD's name and it does not happen, the the LORD did not speak that word. The prophet spoke on his own. Do not be afraid of him.
When the LORD your God destroys the nations whose land the LORD your God gives you, you will take their place and live in their cities and houses.
Set apart three cities for yourself in the middle of the land the LORD your God gives you to own.
Make the road ready for yourself, and divide the land the LORD your God gives you into three parts, so anyone who kills a person can run there.
This is the rule for the person who kills someone and runs there to stay alive: He killed his neighbor by accident, and he did not hate him before.

For example, a man goes into the woods with his neighbor to cut wood. He swings his ax to cut a tree. The iron part flies off the handle and hits his neighbor, and his neighbor dies. That man may run to one of these cities and live.

If he does not, the one who takes revenge for the killing may chase the killer. He may be angry and catch him, because the road is long. Then he may kill him, even though the killer did not deserve to die, because he did not hate his neighbor before.
That is why I command you: Set apart three cities for yourself.
If the LORD your God makes your land bigger, as He promised your fathers, and gives you all the land He said He would give your fathers,
and if you keep all these commands I give you today—to love the LORD your God and walk in His ways all your days—then add three more cities to these three.
Do this so no innocent person is killed in the land the LORD your God gives you as your share. Then you will not be guilty of that death.
But if a man hates his neighbor, hides and waits for him, attacks and kills him, and then runs to one of these cities,
the leaders of his city must send men to bring him back from there. They must hand him over to the one who takes revenge for the killing, and he must die.
Do not feel sorry for him. Remove the guilt of an innocent person's death from Israel, so it will go well with you.
Do not move your neighbor's boundary marker. It was set in the land you will receive as your share in the land the LORD your God gives you to own.
One witness is not enough to prove a man guilty of any wrong or sin. A matter must be settled by two or three witnesses.
If a false witness stands up against a man and says he did wrong,
both men who have the argument must stand before the LORD, before the priests and judges who are serving then.
The judges must look into it carefully. If the witness is lying, and he lied about his brother,
do to him what he planned to do to his brother. Remove the evil from among you.
Then the rest will hear and be afraid. They will not do such an evil thing among you again.
Do not feel sorry. Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and people more than you, do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt, is with you.
When you come near the battle, the priest will go up and speak to the people.
He will say to them, "Hear, Israel, today you are coming near to fight your enemies. Do not let your heart be weak. Do not be afraid. Do not panic. Do not be scared of them.
"The LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you."
Then the officers will speak to the people. They will say, "Who is the man who built a new house but has not used it? Let him go home. He might die in battle, and another man might use it.
"Who is the man who planted a grape field but has not eaten from it? Let him go home. He might die in battle, and another man might eat from it.
"Who is the man who promised to marry a woman but has not married her? Let him go home. He might die in battle, and another man might marry her."
The officers will also speak to the people again. They will say, "Who is the man who is afraid and has a weak heart? Let him go home, so his brothers' hearts will not become weak like his."
When the officers finish speaking to the people, they will choose army leaders to lead the people.
When you come near a city to fight it, first offer peace to it.
If it answers with peace and opens to you, then all the people in it will be your workers and serve you.
But if it does not make peace with you, but fights you, then you must surround it.
The LORD your God will give it into your hand, and you will strike down all its men with the sword.

But you may take the women, children, animals, and all the other things in the city. You may take all of it for you. You may eat the things you took from your enemies, which the LORD your God gave you.
You must do this to all cities that are very far from you, cities that are not from these nations.
But in the cities of these people that the LORD your God gives you as your land, do not let anything that breathes live.
You must completely destroy them: the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, as the LORD your God commanded you.
Do this so they will not teach you to do the bad things they did for their gods. If you do those things, you will sin against the LORD your God.

When you surround a city for many days to fight it and take it, do not destroy its trees by cutting them with an axe. You may eat from them. Do not cut them down. The trees in the field are not people, so you should not fight them while you surround the city.
But you may destroy a tree that you know is not a food tree. You may cut it down and build war works against the city that fights you, until it falls.
If someone is found dead in a field in the land the LORD your God gives you to own, and no one knows who killed him,
your leaders and judges will go out. They will measure the distance from the dead body to the cities around it.
The city closest to the dead body will be found. The leaders of that city will take a young cow that has never worked. It has never pulled a heavy wooden bar.
The leaders of that city will bring the young cow down to a valley with running water. No one plows or plants there. They will break the cow's neck in the valley.
Then the priests, the sons of Levi, will come near. The LORD your God chose them to serve Him and to bless in the name of the LORD. They will settle every argument and every fight.
All the leaders of the city closest to the dead body will wash their hands over the young cow whose neck was broken in the valley.
They will say, "Our hands did not spill this blood. Our eyes did not see it happen.
Please, the LORD, forgive Your people Israel, whom You saved. Do not let innocent blood stay among Your people Israel. Then the guilt for this blood will be forgiven for them."
So you must remove the guilt of innocent blood from among you. Do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
When you go to war against your enemies, the LORD your God will put them in your power. You will take prisoners.
If you see a beautiful woman among the prisoners, and you want her, you may take her as your wife.
Bring her to your home. She will shave her head and cut her nails.
She will take off the clothes she wore as a prisoner. She will stay in your home and cry for her father and mother for one full month. After that, you may marry her, and she will be your wife.
But if you do not want her, let her go where she wants. Do not sell her for money. Do not treat her like a slave, because you have shamed her.
If a man has two wives, and he loves one but not the other, and both wives have sons for him, the oldest son is from the wife he does not love.
Then when he gives his sons what he owns, he must not give the son of the loved wife the special firstborn share instead of the son of the unloved wife. The unloved wife's son is the true oldest son.
Instead, he must give the oldest son, the son of the unloved wife, twice as much as the other sons. That son was the first proof of his strength. The oldest son's right stays with him.
If a man has a son who is stubborn and refuses to obey, who does not listen to his father or mother, and who will not listen even when they punish him,
his father and mother will grab him and take him to the leaders of his city, to the city gate.
They will say to the leaders, "This son of ours is stubborn and refuses to obey. He does not listen to us. He eats too much and drinks too much."
Then all the men of his city will throw stones at him until he dies. You must remove the evil from among you. All Israel will hear about it and be afraid.
If a man does a sin that deserves death, and he is put to death, and you hang his body on a tree,
do not leave his body on the tree overnight. Bury him that same day. Anyone who is hung is under God's curse. Do not make your land unclean. the LORD your God is giving it to you to own.
If you see your brother's ox or sheep wandering away, don't ignore them. Bring them back to your brother.
If your brother is not near, or you don't know him, take the animal to your home. Keep it until your brother looks for it, then give it back.
Do the same for his donkey, his clothes, or anything else he loses that you find. Don't ignore it.
If you see your brother's donkey or ox fall on the road, don't ignore it. Help him lift it up.
A woman must not wear a man's clothes, and a man must not wear a woman's clothes. This is because the LORD your God hates anyone who does this.
If you find a bird's nest with baby birds or eggs, and the mother is sitting on them, don't take the mother with the young.
You may take the young, but let the mother go. Then things will go well for you, and you will live a long time.
When you build a new house, put a low wall around the edge of the roof. Then no one will fall, and you won't be blamed for their death.
Don't plant your vineyard with two kinds of seed. If you do, both crops may be ruined.
Don't plow with an ox and a donkey together.
Don't wear clothes made of wool and linen mixed together.
Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
If a man takes a wife and sleeps with her, then hates her,
and he says bad things about her and gives her a bad name. He says, "I took this woman, but when I came near her, I did not find proof she had never been with a man."
Then the young woman's father and mother must take proof she had never been with a man to the city elders at the gate.
The father will say to the elders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, but he hates her.

Look, he has said bad things about her. He says, 'I did not find proof your daughter had never been with a man.' But here is proof my daughter had never been with a man." Then they will spread the cloth in front of the elders.
The elders of that city will take the man and punish him.

They will fine him one hundred pieces of silver and give the money to the young woman's father, because he gave a bad name to an Israelite girl who had never been with a man. She will stay his wife, and he can never divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the charge is true, and no proof she had never been with a man is found,

they must bring the young woman to the door of her father's house. The men of her city will stone her to death, because she did a wicked thing in Israel. She acted like a prostitute in her father's house. Remove the evil from among you.
If a man is found lying with a married woman, both the man and the woman must die. Remove the evil from Israel.
If a young woman is promised to a man, and a man finds her in the city and sleeps with her,

bring both of them to the gate of that city and stone them to death. Stone the young woman because she did not cry out in the city. Stone the man because he brought shame on his neighbor's wife. Remove the evil from among you.
But if a man finds a promised young woman in the field, and he grabs her and sleeps with her, only the man must die.
Do nothing to the young woman. She has done no sin that deserves death. This is like a man who attacks his neighbor and kills him.
He found her in the field. The promised young woman cried out, but no one was there to save her.
If a man finds a young woman who is not promised to anyone, grabs her, and sleeps with her, and people find out,
the man who slept with her must give the young woman's father fifty pieces of silver. She will become his wife, because he brought shame on her. He can never divorce her as long as he lives.
A man must not take his father's wife. He must not bring shame on his father.
A man whose private parts are crushed or cut off may not come into the the LORD's meeting place.
No child born from a wrong marriage may come into the the LORD's meeting place. Even after ten generations, that family may not come in.
No Ammonite or Moabite may come into the the LORD's meeting place. Even after ten generations, they may not come in forever.
This is because they did not meet you with bread and water on the road when you came out of Egypt. They also paid Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram Naharaim to curse you.
But the the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam. The the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the the LORD your God loves you.
Do not seek their peace or good for all your days. Never seek it.
Do not hate an Edomite, because he is your brother. Do not hate an Egyptian, because you lived as a stranger in his land.
Children born to them in the third generation may come into the the LORD's meeting place.
When you go out to fight your enemies, be careful to stay away from everything bad.
If a man among you is not clean at night, he must go outside the camp. He may not come into the camp.
When evening comes, he must wash with water. When the sun goes down, he may come back into the camp.
You must have a place outside the camp. Go there.
You must have a stick with your things. When you sit outside, dig with it. Then cover your waste.

For the the LORD your God walks in the middle of your camp. He is there to save you and to give your enemies to you. So your camp must be holy. He must not see anything shameful in you, or He will turn away from you.
Do not hand over a slave to his master if he runs away to you.
Let him live with you where he wants, in one of your towns. Do not treat him badly.
No Israelite man or woman may be a temple prostitute.
Do not bring money earned by a prostitute or by a dog into the the LORD's house to keep a promise to God. The the LORD your God hates both.
Do not charge interest to your brother on money, food, or anything else you lend.
You may charge interest to a person from another nation. But do not charge interest to your brother. Then the the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do in the land you are going to take.
If you make a promise to the the LORD your God, do not wait to keep it. The the LORD your God will ask you for it. If you do not keep it, it is a sin.
But if you do not make a promise, you will not sin.
Be careful to do what your mouth says, because you promised it to the the LORD your God.
If you go into your neighbor's grape field, you may eat grapes until you are full. But do not put any in your basket.
If you go into your neighbor's grain field, you may pick grain with your hand. But do not use a sickle on your neighbor's grain.
If a man marries a woman and he is not pleased with her because he found something wrong in her, he writes a paper to end the marriage. He gives it to her and sends her away from his home.
She leaves his home, goes away, and becomes another man's wife.
If that second man does not like her, he writes a paper to end the marriage, gives it to her, and sends her away. Or if that second man dies after he marries her,

her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back to be his wife after she has been made unclean. That is wrong before the LORD. Do not sin against the land the LORD your God gives you as a gift.
When a man takes a new wife, he must not go to war. He must not be given any other hard job for one year. He stays home and makes his new wife happy.
Do not take a millstone as a promise for a loan. That takes away a person's way to live.
If someone is caught stealing a person from the Israelites, working him hard, and selling him, that thief must die. Remove the evil from among you.
Be very careful about the skin disease leprosy. Do everything the priests and Levites teach you, just as I commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.
If you lend something to your neighbor, do not go into his house to take something as a promise.
You must stand outside. The man you lent to will bring the promise out to you.
If he is poor, do not keep his promise item overnight.
Give the promise back to him by sunset. Then he can sleep in his coat and bless you. That will be right for you before the LORD your God.
Do not cheat a poor worker, whether he is one of your people or a stranger living in your land or town.
