Pay him his wages the same day, before the sun goes down. He is poor and needs the money. If you do not, he may cry to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Fathers must not be put to death for their sons' sins. Sons must not be put to death for their fathers' sins. Each person must die for his own sin.
Do not be unfair to strangers, orphans, or widows. Do not take a widow's coat as a promise for a loan.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. The LORD your God saved you from there. That is why I command you to do this.
When you harvest your field and forget a bundle in the field, do not go back to get it. Leave it for the stranger, the orphan, and the widow. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all your work.
When you shake your olive tree, do not pick every olive. Leave some for the stranger, the orphan, and the widow.
When you pick grapes from your vine, do not go back over the vines. Leave some for the stranger, the orphan, and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
If two men have a fight and go to court, the judges will decide who is right and who is wrong. They must say the good man is right and the bad man is wrong.
If the bad man should be beaten, the judge will make him lie down. He will be beaten in front of the judge. The number of hits must match his wrong.
He may hit him up to forty times, but not more. If he hits him more, your brother would be put to shame before you.
Do not stop an ox from eating while it works.
If brothers live together and one of them dies and has no son, his wife must not marry someone outside the family. Her husband's brother must marry her and do what a brother should do for her.
The first son she has will carry the dead brother's name. Then his name will not be wiped out in Israel.

If the man does not want to marry his brother's wife, she must go to the elders at the city gate. She will say, "My husband's brother will not keep his brother's name alive in Israel. He will not do his duty for me."
The elders of his city will call him and talk to him. If he stands there and says, "I do not want to marry her,"

then his brother's wife will go to him in front of the elders. She will take off his sandal and spit in his face. She will say, "This is what happens to a man who will not build his brother's family."
In Israel, his family will be called "the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off."
If two men are fighting, and one man's wife comes to save her husband from the man hitting him, and she grabs the other man's private parts,
then cut off her hand. Do not feel sorry for her.
Do not keep two different weights in your bag, one big and one small.
Do not keep two different measures in your house, one big and one small.
You must use honest weights and measures. Then you will live a long time in the land the the LORD your God gives you.
The LORD your God hates everyone who does these wrong things.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt.
He met you on the way. He attacked you from behind when you were tired and weak. He killed the people who were falling behind you. He did not fear God.
When the the LORD your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land He gives you to own, you must wipe out the memory of Amalek from the earth. Do not forget.
When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you to own, and you take it over and live there,
take some of the first crops from all that your land grows. Put them in a basket and go to the place the LORD your God will choose for His Name.
Go to the priest who serves at that time and say to him, “I tell the LORD your God today that I have come to the land the LORD promised our fathers He would give us.”
The priest will take the basket from your hand and set it in front of the altar of the LORD your God.
Then you will say before the LORD your God, “My father was a wandering man from Aram. He went down to Egypt with a few people. He lived there, and his family grew into a great and strong nation.
But the Egyptians were mean to us. They hurt us and made us do hard work.
Then we called to the LORD, the God of our fathers. The LORD heard us and saw our trouble, our hard work, and our pain.
So the LORD brought us out of Egypt with great power and amazing signs and miracles.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land with plenty of good things.
And now I bring the first crops from the ground that You, the LORD, have given me.” Place the basket before the LORD your God and bow down before Him.
Then you and the Levites and the people from other lands who live among you will be happy with all the good things the LORD your God has given you and your family.

When you finish giving a tenth of all your crops in the third year, the year for giving a tenth, give it to the Levites, the people from other lands, the children with no father, and the women whose husbands have died. Then they can eat in your towns and have enough.

Then say to the LORD your God, “I have taken the holy part out of my house. I have given it to the Levites, the people from other lands, the children with no father, and the women whose husbands have died. I did all You commanded. I have not gone away from Your commands or forgotten them.

I did not eat any of the holy part while I was mourning. I did not take any of it while I was unclean. I did not give any of it to dead people. I listened to the LORD my God. I did everything You told me to do.
Look down from Your holy home in heaven. Bless Your people Israel and the land You gave us, just as You promised our fathers. It is a land with plenty of good things.”
The LORD your God commands you today to follow these rules and laws. Obey them carefully with all your heart and soul.
You have said today that the LORD is your God. You will live the way He wants. You will obey His rules, His commands, and His laws. You will listen to Him.
The LORD has said today that you are His people, His special treasure, just as He promised. You will obey all His commands.
He will make you the praise and glory and honor of all the nations He has made. You will be a holy people for the LORD your God, just as He promised.
Moses and the elders of Israel told the people, "Keep all the rules I give you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan River into the land the LORD your God gives you, set up big stones and cover them with plaster.

Write all these rules on them after you cross over. Then you can go into the land the LORD your God gives you. It is a land with lots of milk and honey. The LORD, the God of your fathers, promised it to you.
When you cross the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, like I tell you today, and cover them with plaster.
Build an altar there for the LORD your God. Make it from stones. Don't use iron tools on them.
Build the altar of the LORD your God with whole stones. Offer burnt gifts on it to the LORD your God.
Offer peace gifts there, eat them, and be happy before the LORD your God.
Write all the words of this law clearly on the stones.
Then Moses and the priests from Levi spoke to all Israel. They said, "Be quiet, Israel, and listen! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.
Obey the LORD your God. Do what He says. Keep His rules and laws. I am giving you these commands today."
That day Moses told the people,
"When you cross the Jordan, these tribes will stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
These tribes will stand on Mount Ebal to say the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali."
The priests from Levi will speak in a loud voice to all the men of Israel.
They will say, "Bad things will happen to the man who makes a carved or melted statue. The LORD hates it. It is made by a worker's hands. He sets it up in secret." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who does not honor his father or mother." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who moves his neighbor's boundary stone." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who leads a blind person the wrong way." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who is unfair to a stranger, an orphan, or a widow." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who sleeps with his father's wife. He has shamed his father." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who has sex with an animal." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who sleeps with his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who sleeps with his mother-in-law." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who hits his neighbor in secret." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who takes money to kill an innocent person." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
They will say, "Bad things will happen to anyone who does not obey all the words of this law." All the people will answer, "Amen!"
If you listen well to the voice of the the LORD your God and keep and do all His commands that I give you today, the the LORD your God will put you high above all nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come to you and catch up to you, if you listen to the voice of the the LORD your God.
You will be blessed in the city, and blessed in the field.
Your children, your crops, and your animals will be blessed. Your calves and lambs will grow.
Your basket and your bowl will be blessed.
You will be blessed when you come in, and blessed when you go out.
The the LORD will make your enemies who rise against you run away in fear before you. They will come out against you one way, but run away seven ways.
The the LORD will send blessing on your barns and on all you do. He will bless you in the land the the LORD your God gives you.
The the LORD will set you apart as His holy people, as He promised you, if you keep the commands of the the LORD your God and walk in His ways.
All the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the the LORD, and they will be afraid of you.
The the LORD will give you plenty of good things: children, animals, and crops in the land the the LORD promised your fathers to give you.

The the LORD will open the heavens, His good storage place, to give rain to your land at the right time, and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not need to borrow.
The the LORD will make you the head, not the tail. You will be only on top, not on the bottom, if you listen to the commands of the the LORD your God that I am giving you today, to keep and do them.
Do not turn away to the right or left from all the words I command you today, to follow other gods and serve them.
But if you do not listen to the voice of the the LORD your God, to keep and do all His commands and rules that I give you today, all these curses will come on you and catch up to you.
You will be cursed in the city, and cursed in the field.
Your basket and your bowl will be cursed.
Your children, your crops, your calves, and your lambs will be cursed.
You will be cursed when you come in, and cursed when you go out.
The the LORD will send on you trouble, panic, and punishment in all you do, until you are destroyed and quickly lost, because of the evil things you did when you left Him.
The the LORD will make sickness stick to you until He has removed you from the land you are going in to take.
The the LORD will hit you with wasting disease, fever, swelling, burning fever, war, blight, and mildew. They will chase you until you die.
The sky above your head will be like metal, and the ground under you will be like iron.
The the LORD will make the rain of your land turn to dust and powder. It will come down on you from the sky until you are destroyed.
The the LORD will let you be defeated by your enemies. You will go out against them one way, but run away seven ways. You will become a scary sight to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your dead body will be food for all the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, and no one will scare them away.
The the LORD will hit you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, rash, and itch that cannot be healed.
The the LORD will hit you with madness, blindness, and a confused heart.
At noon you will feel around like a blind man feels around in the dark. Nothing you do will go well. You will only be hurt and robbed all your life, with no one to save you.
You will promise to marry a woman, but another man will sleep with her. You will build a house, but not live in it. You will plant a grape field, but not use its fruit.
Your ox will be killed in front of you, but you will not eat it. Your donkey will be taken from you and not come back. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will save you.
Your sons and daughters will be given to another people. Your eyes will get tired looking for them all day, but you will have no power to help.
A people you do not know will eat the fruit of your land and all your hard work. You will only be hurt and crushed all your life.
You will go crazy from what your eyes see.
The the LORD will hit you with a bad sickness that cannot be healed, from the bottom of your foot to the top of your head.
The the LORD will lead you and your king, whom you set over you, to a nation you and your fathers have not known. There you will serve other gods made of wood and stone.
You will become a scary thing, a warning story people tell, and a joke among all the peoples where the the LORD sends you.
You will plant much seed in the field, but gather little, because locusts will eat it.
You will plant and care for grape fields, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees in all your land, but you will not get to use the oil, because your olives will drop off.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not stay with you, because they will be taken away.
Locusts will take over all your trees and the fruit of your land.
The stranger among you will rise higher and higher, and you will go lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
All these curses will come on you, chase you, and catch you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the the LORD your God, to keep His commands and rules that He gave you.
They will be a warning sign for you and your children forever.
Because you did not serve the the LORD your God with joy and a glad heart when you had plenty of everything,
you will serve your enemies whom the the LORD sends against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything. He will put a heavy iron collar on your neck until He destroys you.
The the LORD will bring a nation against you from far away, from the end of the earth, flying like an eagle. It will be a nation whose language you do not understand.
A fierce nation that will not respect the old or show mercy to the young.
It will eat the fruit of your animals and your land until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine, or oil, no calves or lambs, until it ruins you.

It will surround you in all your towns and all your land, until your high and strong walls that you trust in fall. It will surround you in all your towns and all your land that the the LORD your God gave you.
You will eat your own children, the sons and daughters the the LORD your God gave you, in the trouble your enemy brings when he traps you.
The tender and delicate man among you will turn against his brother, his wife, and his other children he has left.
He will not give any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he has nothing left in the trouble your enemy brings when he traps you in all your towns.
The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not even put her foot on the ground because she was so dainty, will turn against her husband, her son, and her daughter.
She will secretly eat her afterbirth and her children she gives birth to, because she has nothing left in the trouble your enemy brings when he traps you in your towns.
If you do not carefully keep all the words of this law written in this book, to fear this great and amazing name, the the LORD your God,
then the the LORD will make your plagues and your children's plagues terrible—great and lasting plagues, and bad and lasting sicknesses.
He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt that you feared, and they will stick to you.
The the LORD will also bring on you every sickness and every plague not written in this book of the law, until you are destroyed.
Because you were as many as the stars of heaven, but you will be left few, because you did not listen to the voice of the the LORD your God.

Just as the the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good and make you many, so the the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you and wipe you out. You will be pulled up from the land you are going in to take.
The the LORD will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods of wood and stone, which you and your fathers have not known.
Among those nations you will find no rest, and your foot will have no resting place. There the the LORD will give you a worried heart, weak eyes, and a sad heart.
Your life will always be in danger. You will be afraid night and day, and you will not feel safe about your life.
In the morning you will say, "If only it were evening!" and in the evening you will say, "If only it were morning!" because of the fear in your heart and what your eyes see.
The the LORD will send you back to Egypt by ship, by the way I said you would never see again. There you will try to sell yourselves to your enemies as slaves, but no one will buy.
These are the words of the promise that the the LORD told Moses to make with the people of Israel in the land of Moab. This was besides the promise He made with them at Horeb.
Moses called all Israel together and said to them, “You have seen all that the the LORD did in front of your eyes in Egypt. He did it to Pharaoh, to all his helpers, and to all his land.
Your eyes saw the hard times, signs, and amazing things.
But even today, the the LORD has not given you a heart to know Him, or eyes to see, or ears to hear.
I led you for forty years in the desert. Your clothes did not wear out, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You did not eat bread, and you did not drink wine or strong drink, so you would know that I am the the LORD your God.”
“When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight us, and we beat them.
We took their land and gave it to the families of Reuben, Gad, and half of the family group of Manasseh.
So obey the words of this promise. Do them, so you will do well in all you do.”
“All of you are standing today before the the LORD your God: your leaders, your family groups, your older men, and your officials—every man of Israel.
Your little ones, your wives, and the outsider living in your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who carries your water.
You are here to join the promise of the the LORD your God, and His vow, which the the LORD your God is making with you today.
He will make you His people today, and He will be your God, just as He said to you and promised your fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
I am not making this promise and this vow only with you.
I am making it with those standing here with us today before the the LORD our God, and also with those who are not here today.”
“You know how we lived in Egypt, and how we traveled through the nations you passed through.
You saw their hated things and their idols made of wood and stone, silver and gold, that were among them.”

“Be careful. Do not let any man or woman, family, or family group among you turn away today from the the LORD our God to serve the gods of those nations. Do not let a bitter root grow among you that makes poisonous, bitter fruit.
When a person hears these words of the vow, he may feel safe in his heart and say, ‘I will be okay, even if I keep doing what I want.’ This will bring ruin to both wet and dry land.

The the LORD will not want to forgive him. Instead, the the LORD’s anger and jealousy will burn against that man. All the curses written in this book will stay on him. The the LORD will wipe out his name from under heaven.
The the LORD will set him apart from all the family groups of Israel for harm, just like all the curses of the promise written in this Book of the Law.”
“The next generation, your children after you, and the outsider who comes from a far land, will say when they see the sickness of that land and the diseases the the LORD brought on it,

that the whole land is sulfur and salt, an empty, burned land. Nothing is planted, nothing grows, and no grass grows there. It is like Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the the LORD destroyed in His fierce anger.
All nations will ask, ‘Why did the the LORD do this to this land? What does this great anger mean?’
Then people will say, ‘It is because they left the promise of the the LORD, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of Egypt.
They went and served other gods and worshiped them—gods they did not know and that He did not give to them.
So the the LORD’s anger burned against that land, to bring all the curses written in this book on it.
The the LORD pulled them up from their land in anger and great fury, and threw them into another land, as it is today.’”
“The secret things belong to the the LORD our God. But the things He has shown belong to us and to our children forever, so we can do all the words of this law.”
When all these things happen to you—the good and the bad that I put before you—and you think about them in all the nations where the LORD your God sends you,
and you and your children turn back to the LORD your God and listen to His voice with all your heart and all your soul, doing all I tell you today,
then the LORD your God will bring you back from being held captive. He will be kind to you. He will gather you from all the nations where the LORD your God sent you.
Even if you are sent to the far edge of the sky, the LORD your God will gather you and bring you back from there.
The LORD your God will bring you to the land your fathers owned. You will own it. He will make you do well and make you many more than your fathers.
The LORD your God will change your heart and your children's hearts. Then you can love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul, so you can live.
The LORD your God will put all these bad things on your enemies, on those who hate you and chase you.
You will turn back and listen to the LORD's voice. You will do all His commands that I give you today.

The LORD your God will help you do well in all your work. He will bless the children you have, your animals, and your crops. The LORD will be happy to do good to you again, like He was happy to do good to your fathers.

This will happen if you listen to the LORD your God and keep His commands and rules written in this Book of the Law. It will happen if you turn back to the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
The command I give you today is not too hard for you. It is not far away.
It is not up in heaven. You should not say, "Who will go up to heaven to get it for us and tell it to us, so we can do it?"
It is not across the sea. You should not say, "Who will cross the sea to get it for us and tell it to us, so we can do it?"
The word is very close to you. It is in your mouth and in your heart, so you can do it.
Look, today I put before you life and good, and death and bad.

I command you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commands, rules, and laws. Then you will live and grow. The LORD your God will bless you in the land you are going to take.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are pulled away to bow down to other gods and serve them,
I tell you today that you will be destroyed. You will not live a long time in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take.
I call heaven and earth to speak against you today. I have put before you life and death, good and bad. So choose life, so you and your children can live.
Love the LORD your God. Listen to His voice. Stay close to Him. He is your life. He will give you many years in the land the LORD your God promised to give your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said, "I am 120 years old today. I can't lead you anymore. The LORD has told me, 'You will not cross the Jordan River.'
The LORD your God will go ahead of you. He will destroy these nations, and you will take their land. Joshua will go ahead of you too, just as the LORD said.
The LORD will do to them what He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites. He destroyed them and their land.
The LORD will give them to you. Then you must do to them everything I told you to do.
Be strong and brave. Don't be afraid of them. The LORD your God goes with you. He won't leave you or give up on you."
Moses called Joshua. In front of all Israel he said, "Be strong and brave. You will go with these people into the land the LORD promised their fathers. You will give them that land.
The LORD goes before you. He will be with you. He won't leave you or give up on you. Don't be afraid or worried."
Moses wrote down this law. He gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the LORD's agreement. He gave it to all the elders of Israel too.
Moses told them, "Every seven years, at the special time, the year debts are forgiven, during the Feast of Shelters,
all Israel must come to the place the LORD your God chooses. There, read this law out loud to all Israel.
Bring together the men, women, children, and the visitors in your towns. They need to hear it and learn it. Then they will respect the the LORD your God and obey all the words of this law.
Their children, who don't know it yet, must hear it and learn to respect the the LORD your God as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take."
The LORD said to Moses, "You will die soon. Call Joshua. Stand together in the tent of meeting. I will give him his orders." So Moses and Joshua went and stood in the tent of meeting.
The LORD showed Himself in the tent in a cloud pillar. The cloud stood at the door of the tent.
He said, "You are about to die. These people will get up and chase after other gods in the land they are going to. They will leave Me and break the agreement I made with them.

On that day I will be very angry with them. I will leave them and hide My face from them. Then many bad things and troubles will happen to them. On that day they will say, 'Haven't these bad things happened because our God is not with us?'
On that day I will surely hide My face because of all the bad things they did. They turned to other gods.
So now write this song. Teach it to the people of Israel. Put it in their mouths. This song will speak against them for Me.

I will bring them into the land I promised their fathers. It has plenty of milk and honey. They will eat and be full and get fat. Then they will turn to other gods and serve them. They will make Me angry and break My agreement.

When many bad things and troubles happen to them, this song will speak against them. It won't be forgotten by their children. I know what they want to do even now, before I bring them into the land I promised."
That day Moses wrote this song and taught it to the people of Israel.
He told Joshua son of Nun, "Be strong and brave. You will lead the people of Israel into the land I promised them. I will be with you."
When Moses finished writing all the words of this law in a book, until the end,
Moses told the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD's agreement,
"Take this book of the law. Put it beside the ark of the agreement of the LORD your God. It will be a witness against you.
I know how stubborn you are. You have fought against the the LORD while I have been alive with you. You will do it after I die too.
Bring all the elders and leaders of your tribes to me. I will speak these words to them. I will call heaven and earth to speak against them.

I know that after I die you will ruin yourselves. You will turn away from the way I told you to go. In the last days, bad things will happen to you because you did evil before the the LORD and made Him angry by what you did."
Moses spoke the words of this song to all Israel until the end.
Listen, heavens! I will speak. Earth, hear the words from my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain. Let my words drop like dew. They are like soft rain on new grass. They are like showers on young plants.
I will say the name of the the LORD. Give our God great praise!
God is like a strong Rock. What He does is perfect. All His ways are fair. He is a faithful God. He does no wrong. He is good and right.
But His people did wrong to Him. They are not His children anymore. They are a crooked and twisted group.
Is this how you pay back the LORD, you foolish people with no sense? Is He not your Father? Did He not make you and keep you?
Remember the old days. Think about the years long ago. Ask your father. He will tell you. Ask your older leaders. They will tell you.
When God Most High gave each nation its land, when He split people into groups, He set the borders for the nations. He did this for the people of Israel.
The LORD chose His people as His share. Jacob is His special gift.
God found His people in a dry desert. It was an empty, wild place. He took care of them. He taught them. He kept them safe like the center of His eye.
Like an eagle, He stirred up His nest and hovered over His young. He spread His wings and caught them. He carried them on His wings.
Only the LORD led His people. No false god was with them.
God let His people ride on the high places of the land. He fed them with food from the fields. He gave them honey from the rock. He gave them oil from hard stone.
He gave them butter from cows and milk from sheep. He gave them fat from lambs and rams from Bashan and goats. He gave them the best wheat. You drank the best wine from grapes.
But Israel grew rich and rebelled. You grew fat, thick, and smooth. Then he left God who made him. He turned away from the Rock who saved him.
They made God jealous with false gods. They made Him angry with terrible sins.
They gave gifts to demons, not to God. They worshiped gods they did not know. These gods were new. Your fathers did not know them.
You forgot the Rock who gave you birth. You forgot the God who made you.
The LORD saw this. He was angry with His sons and daughters. He pushed them away. "
I will turn My face away from them. I will see what happens to them at the end. They are a crooked people. They are children who cannot be trusted.

They made Me jealous with things that are not God. They made Me angry with their empty idols. So I will make them jealous with a people who are not a nation. I will make them angry with a foolish nation.
My anger is like a fire. It burns down to the grave. It eats up the earth and its crops. It sets the bases of the mountains on fire.
I will bring many troubles on them. I will use up My arrows on them.
Hunger will waste them. Sickness and bitter disease will eat them up. I will send wild animals to bite them. I will send snakes in the dust to sting them.
Outside, swords will kill their children. Inside, fear will rule. Young men and young women will die. Babies and old men will die. "
I said I would scatter them and erase their name from people.
But I held back. I did not want their enemies to brag. I did not want them to say that they won by their own power and that the LORD did not do this."
They are a people with no good plans. They have no sense.
If they were wise, they would understand this. They would see what will happen to them in the end.
How could one enemy chase a thousand of them? How could two chase ten thousand? Only because their Rock let their enemies have them. Only because the LORD gave them up.
Their rock is not like our Rock. Even our enemies agree.
Their vine comes from Sodom's vine. It comes from Gomorrah's fields. Their grapes are poison. Their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is like snake poison. It is like the deadly poison of cobras. "
I have kept this with Me. It is locked in My storehouse.
Payback is Mine. I will pay them back. Their time to fall is coming. Their day of trouble is near. What is coming for them will happen fast."
The LORD will stand up for His people. He will show mercy to His servants. He will see that their strength is gone. No one is left, slave or free. "
Where are their gods? Where is the rock they trusted?
Those gods ate the fat of their gifts. They drank the wine of their offerings. Let them rise up and help you. Let them be your protection.
See now that I am He. There is no God but Me. I bring death, and I give life. I wound, and I heal. No one can save people from My hand.
I lift My hand to heaven and say, as I live forever,
I will sharpen My flashing sword. My hand will take hold of justice. I will pay back My enemies. I will pay back those who hate Me.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood. My sword will eat flesh. It will eat the blood of the dead and the captives, even the heads of the enemy leaders."
Nations, be glad with His people! The LORD will pay back for the blood of His servants. He will take revenge on His enemies. He will make His land and His people clean.
Moses and Joshua son of Nun spoke all these words of this song to the people.
When Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, "Put your heart into all these words. I tell you today to teach them to your children. Then they will keep and do all the words of this law.
These words are not empty for you. They are your life. By these words you will live a long time in the land you are crossing the Jordan to own."
That same day the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, "
Go up to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, across from Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan. I am giving it to the people of Israel to own.
Die on the mountain you are going up. You will join your people, like your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.

This is because you and Aaron broke faith with Me among the people of Israel at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the desert of Zin. This is because you did not honor Me as holy among the people of Israel.
You will see the land from far away. But you will not go into the land I am giving to the people of Israel."
This is the blessing Moses, God's man, gave the people of Israel before he died.
The LORD came from Sinai. He rose like the sun for them from Seir. He shone from Mount Paran. He came with thousands of holy ones. Fire flashed from His right hand for them.
Yes, He loves His people. All His holy ones are in Your hand. They sit at Your feet. They receive Your words.
Moses gave us God's law. It is a gift for Jacob's people.
The LORD was King in Israel when the leaders met. All the tribes of Israel gathered together.
Let Reuben live and not die. Let his people be many.
Moses prayed, "LORD, hear Judah's voice. Bring him to his people. Let his hands be strong. Help him against his enemies."
About Levi he said: "LORD, Your Thummim and Urim belong to Your faithful servant. You tested him at Massah. You argued with him at Meribah's waters.
He said he did not know his father or mother, his brothers, or his children. He kept Your word and guarded Your covenant.
They will teach Your laws to Jacob. They will teach Your teachings to Israel. They will put incense before You. They will put whole burnt offerings on Your altar.
LORD, bless his strength. Accept the work of his hands. Break the backs of those who rise against him. Strike down those who hate him, so they cannot rise again."
About Benjamin he said: "The one the LORD loves lives safely with Him. The LORD covers him all day. He rests between the LORD's shoulders."
About Joseph he said: "May the LORD bless his land with heaven's dew and water from deep below.
May He bless it with the best fruit the sun gives and the best crops each month.
May He bless it with the best from the old mountains and the hills that last forever.

May He bless it with the best gifts of the earth and all it holds, and with the favor of the One who was in the burning bush. Let these blessings rest on Joseph's head. Let them crown the leader among his brothers.

He has the strength of a firstborn bull. His horns are like a wild ox's horns. With them he will push nations to the ends of the earth. These are the many thousands of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh."
About Zebulun he said: "Be happy, Zebulun, when you go out. Be happy, Issachar, in your tents.
They will call people to the mountain. There they will offer good sacrifices. They will enjoy the wealth of the seas and treasures hidden in the sand."
About Gad he said: "Praise God, who makes Gad's land bigger. Gad lives like a lion and tears his enemies apart.
He chose the best land for himself. He received the leader's share. He came with the leaders of the people. He did what is right and fair for the LORD and for Israel."
About Dan he said: "Dan is a young lion. He leaps from Bashan."
About Naphtali he said: "Naphtali has plenty of favor. He is full of the LORD's blessing. He will take the west and the south."
About Asher he said: "Asher is blessed with children. His brothers favor him. He has plenty of oil.
your shoes will be iron and bronze. your strength will last as long as you live."
There is no God like the God of Israel. He rides through the heavens to help you. He rides on the clouds in His greatness.
The God who lives forever is your safe home. His arms hold you up forever. He will drive your enemies out before you. He will say, "Destroy them!"
So Israel lives safely. Jacob's land has grain and new wine. Even the sky drops dew.

You are happy, Israel! Who is like you? You are a people saved by the LORD. He is your shield and help. He is your sword of victory. Your enemies will come crawling to you. You will walk on their high places.
Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo. He stood on top of Pisgah, across from Jericho.
The LORD showed him the whole land. He saw from Gilead to Dan. He saw all of Naphtali. He saw the land of Ephraim and Manasseh. He saw all of Judah to the sea in the west.
He saw the south land and the valley near Jericho, the city of palm trees. He saw as far as Zoar.
The LORD said to him, "This is the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I said I would give it to your family. I have let you see it with your eyes. But you will not cross over into it."
Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in Moab. This was just as the LORD had said.
The LORD buried him in a valley in Moab, across from Beth-peor. No one knows where his grave is, even now.
Moses was 120 years old when he died. His eyes were still good. He was still strong.
The Israelites were very sad for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days. Then their time of sadness was over.
Joshua, the son of Nun, was full of wisdom. Moses had put his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him. They did what the LORD had told Moses.
No prophet like Moses has come in Israel since then. The LORD knew him in a very close way.
Moses did all the signs and wonders the LORD sent him to do in Egypt. He did them for Pharaoh, for all his helpers, and for all his country.
He did all the great and powerful things that all Israel saw.
After Moses, the servant of the LORD, died, the LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun. Joshua had helped Moses. The LORD said:
"Moses My servant is dead. Now get up. You and all the people must cross the Jordan River. Go to the land I am giving to the people of Israel.
I will give you every place where your feet walk, just as I told Moses.
Your land will go from the desert and Lebanon to the great Euphrates River. It will include all the land of the Hittites and reach to the great sea in the west.
"No one will be able to stand against you all your life. I will be with you, just as I was with Moses. I will not leave you or give up on you.
Be strong and brave. You will help these people take the land I promised to give their fathers.
"Be very strong and brave. Obey all the law that Moses My servant gave you. Do not turn away from it, to the right or to the left. Then you will do well wherever you go.
Keep this Book of the Law with you. Think about it day and night. Then you can obey all that is written in it. You will do well and succeed.
I have told you to be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or worried. I, the LORD your God, am with you wherever you go."
Then Joshua gave orders to the leaders of the people. He said,
"Go through the camp and tell the people to get food ready. In three days you will cross the Jordan River. You will go in and take the land the LORD your God is giving you."
Then Joshua spoke to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh. He said,
"Remember what Moses, the servant of the LORD, told you. The LORD your God is giving you rest. He is giving you this land.

Your wives, your children, and your animals may stay in the land Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan. But all your fighting men, ready for war, must cross ahead of your brothers. You must help them.

You must help them until the LORD gives your brothers rest, just like He gave you. Then they will take the land the LORD your God is giving them. After that, you may go back to your own land. You will take the land Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you east of the Jordan."
The people answered Joshua. They said, "We will do everything you tell us to do. We will go wherever you send us.
We obeyed Moses in everything. We will obey you in the same way. May the LORD your God be with you, just as He was with Moses.
Anyone who does not obey your words, or does not listen to everything you command, will be put to death. Just be strong and brave."

Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men from Shittim to spy on the land. He told them, "Go, look over the land, and especially Jericho." So they went and stayed at the house of a woman named Rahab.
Someone told the king of Jericho, "Men from Israel have come here tonight to spy on the land."
So the king sent a message to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to your house. They came to spy on the whole land."
But Rahab had already hidden the two men. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
They left when it was getting dark, and the city gate was about to close. I do not know where they went. Chase them fast, and you may catch them."
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under stalks of flax that she had laid out there.
The men chased them toward the road to the shallow places in the Jordan River. As soon as the chasers had left, the city gate was shut.
Before the spies went to sleep, Rahab went up to the roof.
She said to them, "I know that the LORD has given you this land. We are very afraid of you. Everyone who lives here is scared and weak because of you.
"We heard how the LORD dried up the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt. We heard what you did to Sihon and Og, the two Amorite kings across the Jordan. You destroyed them completely.
"When we heard that, we were very scared. Everyone lost courage because of you. The LORD your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.
"Now please promise me by the LORD that you will be kind to my father's family, just as I was kind to you. Give me a sure sign.
"Promise to save my father, mother, brothers, sisters, and all their people. Keep us alive and do not let us die."
The men said to her, "We will protect you with our lives! If you do not tell about our plan, then when the LORD gives us this land, we will be kind and faithful to you."
So Rahab let them down by a rope through the window. Her house was built into the city wall.
She said, "Go to the hills so the men chasing you will not find you. Hide there for three days until they come back. Then go on your way."
The men said to her, "We will keep the promise you made us swear.
When we come into the land, tie this red rope in the window you let us down from. Bring your father, mother, brothers, and all your father's family into your house.
If anyone goes out of your house into the street, he will be responsible for his own death, and we will not be blamed. But if anyone in your house is hurt, we will be blamed.
But if you tell about our plan, we will not have to keep our promise to you."
Rahab said, "I agree. Let it be as you say." Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope in the window.
The spies went to the hills and stayed there three days, until the men chasing them came back. The chasers looked all along the road but did not find them.
Then the two spies came down from the hills, crossed the river, and went to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened.
They said to Joshua, "The LORD has surely given the whole land to us. Everyone who lives there is very afraid of us."
Early in the morning, Joshua got up. He and all the people of Israel left Shittim. They went to the Jordan River. They stayed there before they crossed.
After three days, the leaders went through the camp.
They told the people, "When you see the priests from Levi carrying the ark of the the LORD your God, leave your place and follow it.
But stay far away. Keep about two thousand cubits between you and the ark. Do not go near it. Then you will know which way to go. You have never been this way before."
Joshua told the people, "Make yourselves clean. Tomorrow the the LORD will do amazing things among you."
Joshua said to the priests, "Pick up the ark of the covenant and go ahead of the people." So they picked it up and went ahead of the people.
The The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will make you great in the eyes of all Israel. Then they will know that I am with you, just as I was with Moses."
The the LORD said, "You must tell the priests who carry the ark, 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan, stand in the river.'"
Joshua said to the people of Israel, "Come close and listen to the words of the the LORD your God.
This is how you will know that the living God is among you. He will drive out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites from before you.
Look! The ark of the the LORD of all the earth will go into the Jordan ahead of you.
Choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.
As soon as the priests who carry the ark of the the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, put their feet in the Jordan, the water flowing down from above will be cut off. It will stand up in a heap."
When the people broke camp to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark went ahead of them.
The Jordan was full over all its banks during harvest time. When the priests reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water,

the water coming down from upstream stopped. It piled up in a heap far away at Adam, near Zarethan. The water flowing down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, was completely cut off. The people crossed over opposite Jericho.
The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All Israel passed by on dry ground until the whole nation had crossed the Jordan.
After all the people crossed the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,
"Take twelve men for yourselves from the people. Pick one man from each tribe.
Tell them, 'Take twelve stones for yourselves from the middle of the Jordan. Take them from where the priests stood. Carry them with you. Put them down where you camp tonight.'"
Joshua called the twelve men he had chosen from the Israelites. He picked one man from each tribe.

Joshua said to them, "Cross over in front of the ark of the LORD your God. Go into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you lift one stone for yourselves onto his shoulder. There should be one stone for each tribe of Israel.
This will be a sign for you. Tomorrow your children may ask, 'What do these stones mean to you?'
Tell them, 'The Jordan's water stopped flowing. It stopped in front of the ark of the LORD's promise when the ark crossed the Jordan. These stones will remind the people of Israel forever.'"

The people of Israel did what Joshua told them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan. They took one stone for each tribe, just as the LORD had told Joshua. They carried the stones to their camp and put them there.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan. He put them where the priests stood while carrying the ark of the promise. The stones are still there today.

The priests stood in the middle of the Jordan. They stayed there until Joshua finished telling the people all that the LORD had told him to say. This was what Moses had told Joshua to say. Then the people hurried across.
After all the people had crossed, the ark of the LORD crossed too. The priests went in front of the people.
The men from Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed first. They were ready for battle. About 40,000 men went in front of the other Israelites, just as Moses had told them.
They crossed in front of the LORD to the plains of Jericho.
That day the LORD made Joshua a great leader for all Israel. The people respected him all his life, just as they had respected Moses.
Then the LORD said to Joshua,
"Tell the priests who carry the ark of the promise to come up from the Jordan."
Joshua told the priests, "Come up from the Jordan."

When the priests came up from the middle of the Jordan, the water returned. As soon as the priests' feet touched dry ground, the Jordan's water went back to its place and overflowed its banks, just like before.
The people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month. They camped at Gilgal, on the east side of Jericho.
Joshua set up the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan at Gilgal.
He said to the Israelites, "In the future, your children will ask their fathers, 'What do these stones mean?'
Tell them, 'The people of Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground.'
For the LORD your God dried up the Jordan in front of you until you crossed over. He did the same thing at the Red Sea. He dried it up in front of us until we crossed over.
He did this so all the people on earth would know the LORD is very strong. He did this so you would respect the LORD your God forever."

All the Amorite kings west of the Jordan heard the news. All the Canaanite kings by the sea heard it too. They heard that the LORD had dried up the Jordan for the Israelites. The Israelites crossed over. The kings were very afraid. They lost all courage because of the Israelites.
At that time, the LORD said to Joshua, "Make knives from sharp stone. Circumcise the sons of Israel again."
So Joshua made knives from sharp stone. He circumcised the sons of Israel at Gibeath-haaraloth.
This is why Joshua circumcised them. All the men who came out of Egypt were soldiers. They died on the way in the desert after they left Egypt.
All the people who came out had been circumcised. But the people born in the desert on the trip from Egypt had not been circumcised.

The people of Israel walked in the desert for forty years. All the soldiers who came out of Egypt died. They did not obey the LORD. The LORD had sworn that He would not let them see the land. He had promised their fathers He would give us this land. It is a rich land with plenty of good food.
So He raised up their sons in their place. Joshua circumcised them. They had not been circumcised on the way.
After all the men were circumcised, they stayed in the camp until they were healed.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have taken away the shame of Egypt from you." So that place was called Gilgal. It is still called that today.
On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, the Israelites camped at Gilgal. They were on the plains of Jericho. They kept the Passover.
The day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate bread without yeast. They also ate roasted grain from the food of the land.
The day after they ate from the food of the land, the manna stopped. There was no more manna for the Israelites. That year they ate from the harvest of the land of Canaan.

When Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up. He saw a man standing in front of him. The man had a sword in his hand. It was pulled out. Joshua went to him. He asked, "Are you for us or for our enemies?"
"Neither," he replied. "I have now come as commander of the the LORD's army." Then Joshua fell facedown on the ground. He worshiped. He asked, "What does my Lord have to say to His servant?"
The commander of the the LORD's army replied, "Take off your sandals. The place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
Jericho was locked tight because of the Israelites. No one went out, and no one came in.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Look, I have given Jericho to you. I have also given you its king and its strong soldiers.
You must walk around the city. All the fighting men will go around the city one time. Do this for six days.

Seven priests will carry seven trumpets made from ram horns. They will walk in front of the ark of the the LORD. On the seventh day, you will go around the city seven times. The priests will blow the trumpets.

When the priests blow the trumpets for a long time, and you hear the sound, all the people will shout loudly. Then the city wall will fall down. After that, the people will go straight into the city."
Joshua called the priests. He said, "Pick up the ark of the the LORD. Seven priests will carry seven trumpets in front of the ark of the the LORD."
Then he said to the people, "Go! March around the city. The armed men will go in front of the ark of the the LORD."
After Joshua spoke, the seven priests carried the seven trumpets. They walked ahead and blew them. The ark of the the LORD followed them.
The armed men walked in front of the priests who blew the trumpets. The men at the back walked behind the ark. The priests kept blowing the trumpets.
Joshua told the people, "Do not shout. Do not make any noise. Do not say a word until I tell you to shout. Then shout!"
They carried the ark of the the LORD around the city one time. Then they went back to camp and stayed there for the night.
Joshua got up early in the morning. The priests carried the ark of the the LORD.

The seven priests carried the seven trumpets. They walked in front of the ark of the the LORD and blew them. The armed men walked in front of the priests. The men at the back walked behind the ark of the the LORD. The priests kept blowing the trumpets.
On the second day, they went around the city one time. Then they went back to camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day, they got up early at sunrise. They went around the city seven times, just as before. That day, they went around the city seven times.
The seventh time, the priests blew the trumpets. Joshua said to the people, "Shout! The LORD has given you the city."
"The city and all in it must be destroyed completely for the the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute and all who are with her in her house will live. She hid the men we sent.
But you must stay away from the things that are to be destroyed. If you take any of them, you will bring trouble to all of Israel.
All the silver, gold, bronze, and iron things are holy to the the LORD. They will go into the treasure room of the the LORD's house."
The people shouted when the priests blew the trumpets. When the people heard the trumpet sound, they shouted loudly. The wall fell down. Then the people went straight into the city and took it.
They destroyed everything in the city. They killed men and women, young and old. They killed oxen, sheep, and donkeys with swords.
Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the prostitute's house. Bring out the woman and all who belong to her, just as you promised her."
The young spies went in and brought out Rahab. They brought out her father, mother, brothers, and all who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and left them outside Israel's camp.
They burned the city and everything in it. But they put the silver, gold, bronze, and iron into the treasure room of the the LORD's house.
Joshua let Rahab the prostitute live. He also let her father's family and all who belonged to her live. She still lives among the Israelites today. She hid the men Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua made them promise. He said, "Anyone who tries to rebuild Jericho will be cursed by the the LORD. He will lose his oldest son when he lays the foundation. He will lose his youngest son when he sets up the gates."
The the LORD was with Joshua. People all over the land heard about him.

The Israelites did not obey God. Achan took some of the things that had to be destroyed. He was from the tribe of Judah. His family line was Zerah, then Zabdi, then Carmi, then Achan. The the LORD was very angry with the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai. Ai was near Beth Aven, east of Bethel. He said to them, "Go up and look at the land." So the men went up and looked at Ai.
They came back to Joshua and said, "Do not send all the people. Send about two or three thousand men to attack Ai. Do not make all the people tired, because Ai has only a few men."
So about three thousand men went up. But they ran away from the men of Ai.
The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them. They chased them from the city gate to Shebarim. They killed them as they ran down the hill. Then the people of Israel were very afraid.
Joshua tore his clothes. He fell to the ground in front of the ark of the the LORD. He stayed there until evening. The leaders of Israel did the same. They put dust on their heads.
Joshua said, "Oh, Lord the the LORD, why did You bring us across the Jordan? Did You bring us here so the Amorites could destroy us? I wish we had stayed on the other side of the Jordan!
O Lord, what can I say now? Israel has turned and run from its enemies.
The Canaanites and all the people who live in this land will hear about this. They will come against us and destroy us completely. Then what will You do for Your great name?"
The the LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying on your face?
Israel has sinned. They broke My covenant, the one I gave them. They took some of the things that had to be destroyed. They stole. They lied. They put those things with their own things.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They will run from their enemies, because they themselves are now set apart to be destroyed. I will not be with you anymore unless you destroy what is set apart from among you.

Get up and make the people holy. Tell them, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow. The the LORD, the God of Israel, says this: There are things set apart to be destroyed among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove those things from among you.'

In the morning, you must come near tribe by tribe. The tribe the the LORD chooses will come forward family group by family group. The family group the the LORD chooses will come forward family by family. The family the the LORD chooses will come forward man by man.
The one who is caught with the things set apart must be burned with fire. Everything he has must be burned too. He broke the the LORD's covenant and did a very bad thing in Israel."
Joshua got up early in the morning. He brought Israel forward tribe by tribe. The tribe of Judah was chosen.
He brought the family groups of Judah forward. The family group of the Zerahites was chosen. He brought the Zerahites forward family by family. The family of Zabdi was chosen.
He brought the family of Zabdi forward man by man. Achan was chosen. He was the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah.
Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give honor to the the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession to Him. Tell me what you did. Do not hide it from me."
Achan answered, "It is true. I sinned against the the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.

I saw a beautiful coat from Shinar among the things taken. I saw two hundred pieces of silver and a gold bar that weighed fifty pieces. I wanted them, so I took them. They are hidden in the ground in my tent. The silver is under them."
Joshua sent men. They ran to the tent. There they found the hidden things. The silver was under them.
They took the things out of the tent and brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites. They laid them out before the the LORD.

Then Joshua and all Israel took Achan, son of Zerah. They took the silver, the coat, and the gold bar. They took his sons and daughters, his ox, his donkey, his sheep, his tent, and everything he owned. They brought them to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "You have brought trouble on us. Today the the LORD will bring trouble on you." Then all Israel stoned him. They burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
They piled a big heap of stones over him. It is still there today. Then the the LORD stopped being so angry. So that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid. Do not give up. Take all the fighting men with you, and go up to Ai. See, I have given the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land into your hand.
Do to Ai and its king what you did to Jericho and its king. But you may take the things and animals. Set a trap behind the city."
Joshua and all the fighting men got up to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand brave men and sent them out at night.
He told them, "See, you are the hidden men behind the city. Do not go far from the city. All of you stay ready.
I and all the people with me will go near the city. When they come out to meet us, as before, we will run away from them.
They will chase us until we draw them away from the city. They will think we are running from them, as before. Then we will run away.
Then you will get up from your hiding place and take the city. the LORD your God will give it into your hand.
When you take the city, burn it. Do as the LORD told you."
Joshua sent them to the hidden place. They stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. Joshua stayed that night with the people.
Joshua got up early in the morning. He counted the people. He and the leaders of Israel went up in front of the people to Ai.
All the fighting men with him went up. They came near the city and camped north of Ai. There was a valley between them and Ai.
Joshua took about five thousand men and set them in the hidden place between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
They set all the army north of the city and the men at the back west of the city. That night Joshua went into the middle of the valley.

When the king of Ai saw this, he hurried. Early in the morning, the men of the city went out to meet Israel in battle. The king and all his people went to the place in front of the open plain. He did not know that hidden men were behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel let the men of Ai push them back. They ran toward the desert.
All the people in the city were called to chase them. They chased Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
No man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go after Israel. They left the city open and chased Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Hold out the spear in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." Joshua held out the spear in his hand toward the city.
As soon as he held out his hand, the hidden men got up quickly from their place. They ran into the city, took it, and hurried to set it on fire.

The men of Ai turned and looked. They saw smoke rising from the city into the sky. They had no strength to run this way or that. The people who had run toward the desert turned back against those who chased them.
Joshua and all Israel saw that the hidden men had taken the city and that smoke was rising. They turned back and struck the men of Ai.
The men who came out of the city were now in the middle of Israel. Israel struck them until no one was left alive.
They caught the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

Israel finished killing all the people who lived in Ai. They chased them in the fields and in the desert. All of them fell by the sword until they were gone. Then Israel went back to Ai and struck it with the sword.
All the people of Ai who fell that day were twelve thousand, both men and women.
Joshua did not pull back his hand that held the spear until all the people of Ai were completely destroyed.
Israel took only the animals and the things of the city, as the LORD had told Joshua.
Joshua burned Ai and made it a pile of ruins that is still there today.

He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua told them to take his body down from the tree. They threw it at the gate of the city and put a big pile of stones over it. It is still there today.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

He did this as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had told the people of Israel. The altar was made of whole stones that no iron tool had touched. On it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.
There, in front of the people of Israel, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law of Moses.

All Israel stood on both sides of the covenant box of the LORD. The priests and the men who carried the box stood there too. Half of the people faced Mount Gerizim, and half faced Mount Ebal. This was as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had first commanded, to bless the people of Israel.
After that, Joshua read all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, just as they were written in the book of the law.
Joshua read every word that Moses had commanded. He read it in front of all the people of Israel, the women, the little children, and the foreigners who lived among them. Not one word was left out.

When all the kings on the other side of the Jordan heard what Joshua did, they came together. They lived in the hills, in the lowlands, and along the big sea near Lebanon. They were Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
They agreed to fight Joshua and Israel together.
The people of Gibeon heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai.
The Gibeonites used a trick. They went and got old, worn sacks for their donkeys. They took old wine skins that were torn and tied up.
Their sandals were old and patched. Their clothes were old. All their food was dry and moldy.
They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal. They said to him and to the men of Israel, "We come from a far country. Please make a peace agreement with us."
The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Maybe you live near us. How can we make an agreement with you?"
They said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua asked, "Who are you? Where do you come from?"
They said to him, "Your servants have come from a very far country. We came because of the name of the the LORD your God. We heard about Him. We heard all He did in Egypt.
We heard all He did to the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan. He beat Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
Our leaders and all the people in our land told us to take food for the trip and go meet you. They told us to say, 'We are your servants. Please make an agreement with us.'"
"Look at our bread. It was warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. Now it is dry and moldy.
These wine skins were new when we filled them. Now they are torn. Our clothes and sandals are very worn from the long trip."
The men took some of their food. But they did not ask the the LORD what to do.
Joshua made a peace agreement with them. He promised to let them live. The leaders of the people swore an oath to them.
Three days later, the Israelites heard that the Gibeonites lived nearby.
The Israelites traveled and reached their cities: Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.
But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders had sworn an oath to them by the the LORD, the God of Israel. All the people grumbled against the leaders.
All the leaders told all the people, "We swore an oath to them by the the LORD, the God of Israel. Now we cannot hurt them."
"This is what we will do. We will let them live. Then the the LORD will not be angry with us for breaking the oath we made."
The leaders said, "Let them live." So they became woodcutters and water carriers for all the people, just as the leaders said.
Joshua called the Gibeonites and said to them, "Why did you trick us? You said, 'We live very far from you,' but you live near us.
Now you are cursed. You will never stop being servants. You will cut wood and carry water for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "We were told clearly that the the LORD your God commanded His servant Moses to give you all this land and to destroy all the people living in it before you. We were very afraid for our lives, so we did this.
Now we are in your hands. Do to us what seems good and right to you."
So Joshua saved them from the Israelites. He did not let them kill the Gibeonites.
That day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the people and for the altar of the the LORD. They serve there to this day, at the place the the LORD chooses.

Adoni-Zedek was the king of Jerusalem. He heard that Joshua had taken Ai and destroyed it. He heard that Joshua did to Ai and its king what he did to Jericho and its king. He also heard that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and now lived with them.
He was very afraid. Gibeon was a big city, like a royal city. It was bigger than Ai, and all its men were strong fighters.
So Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon.
He said, "Come up to me and help me. Let's attack Gibeon. It made peace with Joshua and Israel."

So these five Amorite kings, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gathered together. They went up with all their armies. They camped near Gibeon and fought against it.

The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal. They said, "Don't stop helping us, your servants. Come up to us fast and save us and help us. All the Amorite kings in the hills have gathered against us."
So Joshua went up from Gilgal. All his army went with him. They were strong fighters.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Don't be afraid of them. I have given them to you. No one can stand against you."
Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and came to them by surprise.
The LORD confused them before Israel. Israel killed many of them at Gibeon. Israel chased them down the road to Upper Beth Horon. Israel killed them all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.
As they ran from Israel down the hill from Beth Horon, the LORD threw big hailstones from the sky. More men died from the hail than from the sword.
On that day the LORD gave the Amorites to Israel. Joshua prayed to the LORD while Israel watched. He said, "Sun, stand still over Gibeon. Moon, stand still over the valley of Aijalon."
The sun stopped. The moon stood still until Israel beat its enemies. This is written in the Book of Jashar. The sun stayed in the middle of the sky. It did not go down for about a whole day.
There has never been a day like that before or since. The LORD listened to a man. The LORD fought for Israel.
Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.
The five kings ran away. They hid in a cave at Makkedah.
Someone told Joshua, "The five kings are hiding in a cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said, "Roll big stones to the mouth of the cave. Put men there to guard them."
Joshua said to his men, "Don't you stay here. Chase the enemy. Attack them from behind. Don't let them get to their cities. The LORD your God has given them to you."
Joshua and Israel killed almost all of them. The ones left ran to safe cities.
Then all the people went back safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah. No one said a bad word against the Israelites.
Joshua said, "Open the cave. Bring the five kings out to me."
So they did. They brought out the five kings: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

When they brought the kings to Joshua, he called all the men of Israel. He said to the army leaders who went with him, "Come here. Put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came and put their feet on their necks.
Then Joshua said to them, "Don't be afraid. Don't give up. Be strong and brave. The LORD will do this to all your enemies you fight."
Then Joshua killed them. He hung them on five trees. They hung there until evening.
At sunset Joshua told them to take the bodies down. They threw them into the cave where they had hidden. They put big stones at the mouth of the cave. The stones are still there today.
That day Joshua took Makkedah. He killed everyone in it. He destroyed it, just like he did to Jericho. He did the same to its king. No one was left alive.
Then Joshua and all Israel went from Makkedah to Libnah. They fought against it.
The LORD gave Libnah and its king to Israel. Israel killed everyone there. No one was left alive. Joshua did to its king what he did to Jericho's king.
Then Joshua and all Israel went from Libnah to Lachish. They camped there and fought.
The LORD gave Lachish to Israel. Israel took it on the second day. They killed everyone there, just like they did to Libnah.
Then Horam, king of Gezer, came to help Lachish. Joshua killed him and his army. No one was left alive.
Then Joshua and all Israel went from Lachish to Eglon. They camped and fought.
They took it that day. They killed everyone there. They destroyed it, just like they did to Lachish.
Then Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron. They fought against it.
They took it. They killed the king, the nearby towns, and all the people. No one was left alive. Joshua destroyed it and all its people, just like he did to Eglon.
Then Joshua and all Israel went back to Debir. They fought against it.
They took it. They killed the king and the nearby towns. They killed everyone there. No one was left alive. Joshua treated Debir and its king the same way he treated Hebron and Libnah.

Joshua took all the land: the hills, the south country, the lowlands, and the slopes. He killed all the kings. No one was left alive. He destroyed every living thing, just as the LORD God of Israel had told him to do.
Joshua fought from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza. He took all the land of Goshen up to Gibeon.
Joshua took all these kings and their land at one time, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.
Then Joshua and all Israel went back to the camp at Gilgal.
When Jabin, king of Hazor, heard the news, he sent word to Jobab, king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph.
He also sent word to the kings in the north who lived in the hills, in the dry valley south of the Sea of Galilee, in the lowlands, and by the sea near Dor.
He sent word to the Canaanites in the east and west, to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hills, and to the Hivites under Mount Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
They came out with all their armies. There were so many people that they were like sand on the beach. They had many horses and war carts.
All these kings joined together. They came and set up camp by the waters of Merom to fight Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. Tomorrow at this time, I will hand all of them over to Israel to be killed. You must make their horses unable to run and burn their war carts."
Joshua and all his soldiers came upon them suddenly by the waters of Merom and attacked them.
The LORD gave them into Israel's hands. Israel struck them and chased them to Greater Sidon, to Misrephoth-maim, and east to the Valley of Mizpah. They struck them until no one was left alive.
Joshua did what the LORD said. He made their horses unable to run and burned their war carts.
At that time Joshua turned back and took Hazor. He killed its king with a sword. Hazor had been the most important of all those kingdoms.
They killed everyone in Hazor with swords. They destroyed them completely. No one was left alive. Then Joshua burned Hazor.
Joshua took all the cities of those kings. He killed the people and kings with swords. He destroyed them completely, just as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had told him to do.
But Israel did not burn the cities that were still standing on their old hills. Joshua burned only Hazor.
The Israelites took all the treasures and animals from those cities. But they killed every person with swords until no one was left alive.
Joshua did everything just as the LORD had told Moses, and Moses had told Joshua. He did not leave out anything the LORD had told Moses to do.
So Joshua took all that land. He took the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowlands, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel, and its lowlands.
He took land from Mount Halak, which goes up toward Seir, all the way to Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and killed them.
Joshua fought with all these kings for a long time.
No city made peace with Israel except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon. Israel took all the rest in battle.
The LORD had made them stubborn. He did this so they would fight Israel and be destroyed completely. He did not show them mercy. He wanted to destroy them, just as He had told Moses.

At that time Joshua went and destroyed the Anakites from the hill country, from Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and Israel. He destroyed them and their cities completely.
No Anakites were left in Israel except in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua took the whole land, just as the LORD had told Moses. He gave it to Israel to own, by their tribes. Then the land had peace from war.
These are the kings of the land that the people of Israel beat. They took the land east of the Jordan River. It went from the Arnon River valley to Mount Hermon. It also went east to the dry plain.

Sihon was king of the Amorites. He lived in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer by the Arnon River, through the middle of that river, up to the Jabbok River. That was the border of the Ammonites. He also ruled half of Gilead.
He ruled the dry plain east to the Sea of Galilee and the Salt Sea. He ruled the road to Beth-jeshimoth and the south under the slopes of Pisgah.
Og was king of Bashan. He was one of the last of a giant people called the Rephaim. He lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
He ruled Mount Hermon, Salecah, and all of Bashan. His land went to the borders of the Geshurites and Maacathites. It also reached half of Gilead, next to Sihon, king of Heshbon.
Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites beat these kings. Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave their land to the people of Reuben, Gad, and half of the family group of Manasseh to live on.
