These are the kings of the land Joshua and the Israelites beat west of the Jordan River. Their land went from Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which goes up toward Seir. Joshua gave this land to the people of Israel to share.
It included the hill country, the lowlands, the dry plain, the slopes, the desert, and the south country. The people there were Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
The king of Jericho, one. The king of Ai, near Bethel, one.
The king of Jerusalem, one. The king of Hebron, one.
The king of Jarmuth, one. The king of Lachish, one.
The king of Eglon, one. The king of Gezer, one.
The king of Debir, one. The king of Geder, one.
The king of Hormah, one. The king of Arad, one.
The king of Libnah, one. The king of Adullam, one.
The king of Makkedah, one. The king of Bethel, one.
The king of Tappuah, one. The king of Hepher, one.
The king of Aphek, one. The king of Lasharon, one.
The king of Madon, one. The king of Hazor, one.
The king of Shimron-meron, one. The king of Achshaph, one.
The king of Taanach, one. The king of Megiddo, one.
The king of Kedesh, one. The king of Jokneam in Carmel, one.
The king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one. The king of Goiim in Gilgal, one.
The king of Tirzah, one. All together there were thirty-one kings.
Joshua was old. He had lived many years. The LORD said to him, “You are old and have lived many years. But much land still needs to be taken.”
This is the land that is left: all the land of the Philistines and the Geshurites.

It goes from the Shihor River near Egypt to the border of Ekron in the north. This land counts as Canaanite land. It has the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. It also has the Avvites.
To the south is all the land of the Canaanites. It goes from Mearah of the Sidonians to Aphek, up to the border of the Amorites.
It has the land of the Gebalites and all Lebanon to the east. It goes from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.
“All the people who live in the hills from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, and all the Sidonians, I will drive out before the Israelites. Just give the land to Israel as a gift, as I have told you.
Now divide this land as a gift among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
The other half of Manasseh, the Reubenites, and the Gadites had already received their land. Moses gave it to them east of the Jordan. He was the servant of the LORD.
Their land went from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, including the city in the middle of the valley, and all the flat land of Medeba up to Dibon.
It included all the cities of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, up to the border of the Ammonites.
It also included Gilead, the land of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan up to Salecah.
It included all the kingdom of Og in Bashan. Og ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the last of the Rephaim. Moses beat them and took their land.
But the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacah still live among the Israelites today.
But to the tribe of Levi, Moses gave no land. The gifts burned for the LORD, the God of Israel, are their land, just as He had promised them.
This is what Moses gave to the family groups of the tribe of Reuben:
Their land went from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, including the city in the middle of the valley, and all the flat land near Medeba.
It had Heshbon and all its cities on the flat land—Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, and Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth.

It had all the cities of the flat land and all the kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Moses had beaten Sihon and the leaders of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. These were the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.
The Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the fortune teller, with the sword, along with the others they killed.
The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan. This was the land given to the family groups of Reuben, including the cities and towns.
This is what Moses gave to the family groups of the tribe of Gad:
Their land was Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites up to Aroer, near Rabbah.
It went from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir.
In the valley, it had Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon. It also had the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon. The Jordan was its border on the east.
This was the land given to the family groups of Gad, including the cities and towns.
This is what Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, that is, to the family groups of the half-tribe of Manasseh:
Their land went from Mahanaim through all Bashan—all the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan. It included all the towns of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities.
It had half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan. This was for the family groups of Machir son of Manasseh, for half of the family groups of Machir.
These are the lands Moses gave on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan, across from Jericho.
But to the tribe of Levi, Moses gave no land. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their land, just as He had promised them.
These are the parts of land the people of Israel got in Canaan. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the tribes gave out the land.
They gave out the land by drawing lots to the nine and a half tribes. The LORD had told Moses to do this.
Moses had already given land to two and a half tribes on the other side of the Jordan. He did not give land to the Levites among them.
Joseph's family became two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites did not get a piece of land. They got cities to live in and fields for their animals.
So the people of Israel did what the LORD told Moses. They split up the land.
Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh, a Kenizzite, said to him, "You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh-barnea about you and me.
I was 40 years old when Moses, the servant of the LORD, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to look at the land. I came back and gave him an honest report.
My brothers who went with me scared the people. But I followed the LORD my God with all my heart.
That day Moses promised me, 'Surely the land your foot walked on will be yours and your children's forever, because you followed the LORD my God with all your heart.'
Now look, the LORD has kept me alive for 45 years since He spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the desert. Today I am 85 years old.
I am still as strong today as I was when Moses sent me. I am as strong now as I was then, for war and for all I do.

So give me this hill country the LORD talked about that day. For you heard then that the Anakites were there, with big cities that had strong walls. Maybe the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, just as the LORD said."
Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron for his land.
So Hebron belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as his land to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart.
Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba, after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakites. Then the land was at peace.
The land share for the family groups of Judah went down to the land of Edom and to the Desert of Zin in the far south.
Their south border started at the far end of the Dead Sea.
It crossed south of Scorpion Pass, went to Zin, and went up to Kadesh Barnea. Then it passed Hezron, went up to Addar, and curved around to Karka.
Then it passed Azmon and joined the stream of Egypt. It ended at the sea. This was their south border.
The east border was the Dead Sea all the way to where the Jordan River ends. The north border started at the bay of the sea where the Jordan River ends.
It went up to Beth Hoglah and passed north of Beth Arabah. Then it went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
The border went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor. It turned north to Gilgal, across from the Pass of Adummim south of the stream. It passed the waters of En Shemesh and ended at En Rogel.

Then it ran up the Valley of Ben Hinnom on the south side of the Jebusite city. That city is Jerusalem. Then it climbed to the top of the hill west of the Hinnom Valley, at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the top of the hill, the border went toward the spring of Nephtoah. It came out at the towns of Mount Ephron and went down toward Baalah. Baalah is Kiriath Jearim.
Then it curved west from Baalah to Mount Seir. It ran along the north side of Mount Jearim. That is Kesalon. It went down to Beth Shemesh and crossed to Timnah.
It went to the north side of Ekron. It turned toward Shikkeron, passed Mount Baalah, and reached Jabneel. The border ended at the sea.
The west border was the sea. These were the borders around the family groups of Judah.
The LORD told Joshua to give Caleb son of Jephunneh a share in Judah. So Joshua gave him Kiriath Arba. That is Hebron. Arba was the father of Anak.
Caleb drove out three sons of Anak from Hebron: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there he went up against the people living in Debir. Before, it was called Kiriath Sepher.
Caleb said, "I will let the man who attacks and takes Kiriath Sepher marry my daughter Achsah."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it. So Caleb gave his daughter Achsah to him to marry.
When Achsah came to Othniel, she told him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
She said, "Please give me a blessing. You gave me land in the Negev. Please give me springs of water too." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This was the land share for the tribe of Judah, by family groups.
The towns in the far south were Kabzeel, Eder, and Jagur.
Hazor Hadattah and Kerioth Hezron (that is, Hazor).
Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, and Beth Pelet.
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon. That is twenty-nine towns and their villages.
Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, and Enam.
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim. That is fourteen towns and their villages.
Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah. That is sixteen towns and their villages.
Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah. That is nine towns and their villages.
Ekron and its nearby towns and villages.
West of Ekron, all the towns near Ashdod and their villages.
Ashdod and its nearby towns and villages. Gaza and its nearby towns and villages, as far as the stream of Egypt and the sea.
Dannah and Kiriath Sannah (that is, Debir).
Goshen, Holon, and Giloh. That is eleven towns and their villages.
Humtah, Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron), and Zior. That is nine towns and their villages.
Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah. That is ten towns and their villages.
Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon. That is six towns and their villages.
Kiriath Baal (that is, Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah. That is two towns and their villages.
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi. That is six towns and their villages.
But the people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, who lived in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites live there with the people of Judah to this day.
The land for Joseph's family started at the Jordan River near Jericho. It went east to the water of Jericho. It went through the dry land that goes up from Jericho to the hills near Bethel.
It went from Bethel to Luz. Then it crossed to the border of the Archites at Ataroth.
It went down west to the border of the Japhletites. That was as far as lower Beth Horon and Gezer. It ended at the sea.
So Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, got their land.
This was the land for Ephraim's family groups. Their border went from Ataroth Addar in the east to upper Beth Horon.
It went out toward the sea. From Michmethath on the north, it turned east to Taanath Shiloh. Then it passed by it to Janoah on the east.
It went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah. It touched Jericho and came out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border went west to the Brook of Kanah. It ended at the sea. This was the land for Ephraim's family groups.
Ephraim also had cities and towns set apart for them inside the land of Manasseh's people.
But they did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. So the Canaanites live among Ephraim's people even now. They are forced to work.
The family group of Manasseh got its land. Manasseh was Joseph's oldest son. Machir was Manasseh's oldest son and Gilead's father. Machir was a soldier, so he got Gilead and Bashan.
The rest of Manasseh's family groups also got land. They were Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the sons of Manasseh, son of Joseph.

Zelophehad was Hepher's son. Hepher was Gilead's son. Gilead was Machir's son. Machir was Manasseh's son. Zelophehad had no sons. He had only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

The daughters came to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders. They said, "The LORD told Moses to give us land with our brothers." So Joshua gave them land with their father's brothers, just as the LORD said.
So Manasseh got ten shares of land. This was besides Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan River.
Manasseh's daughters got land with his sons. The land of Gilead went to the rest of Manasseh's sons.
Manasseh's border went from Asher to Michmethath, east of Shechem. Then it turned south to the people of En Tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh. But the town of Tappuah, on Manasseh's border, belonged to Ephraim.
The border went down to the Kanah Valley. The towns south of the valley, among Manasseh's towns, belonged to Ephraim. Manasseh's border was north of the valley and reached the sea.
Ephraim's land was to the south. Manasseh's land was to the north. The sea was their border. They touched Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
In Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also had Beth Shan, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo, with their towns.
But Manasseh's people could not take these towns. The Canaanites wanted to stay in that land.
Later, when the Israelites got stronger, they made the Canaanites work for them. But they did not drive them out completely.
The sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua. They said, "Why did you give us only one share of land? We are many people. The LORD has blessed us a lot."
Joshua said to them, "If you are many people, go up into the forest. Clear a place for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and Rephaim. The hill country of Ephraim is too small for you."
The sons of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us. All the Canaanites in the valley have iron chariots. They are in Beth Shan and its towns. They are also in the Jezreel Valley."
Joshua said to the family of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are many people. You are very strong. You will not have just one share.
The hill country will be yours. It is a forest. You will clear it. Its far borders will be yours. The Canaanites have iron chariots. But you will drive them out."
All the people of Israel came together at Shiloh. They set up the tent of meeting there. The land was now under their control.
Seven tribes of Israel still had no land of their own.
Joshua said to the Israelites, “How long will you wait to take the land the the LORD God of your fathers gave you?
Pick three men from each tribe. I will send them. They will go through the land and write it down. They will bring it back to me.
Then divide the land into seven parts. Judah will stay in the south. Joseph’s family will stay in the north.
You write down the seven parts of the land and bring them to me. I will cast lots for you here before the the LORD our God.

The Levites do not get a part of the land like the rest of you. Serving the the LORD is their share. Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh already got their land east of the Jordan River. Moses, the servant of the the LORD, gave it to them.”
The men got up and went. Joshua told the men who went to write the land, “Go through the land and write it down. Then come back to me. I will cast lots for you here before the the LORD in Shiloh.”
The men went through the land. They wrote it in a book. They divided it into seven parts by cities. Then they came back to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
Joshua cast lots for them before the the LORD in Shiloh. There Joshua divided the land among the Israelites by their groups.
The lot came up for the tribe of Benjamin, by its families. Its land was between Judah and Joseph.
Their north border started at the Jordan River. It went up on the north side of Jericho. It went up west through the hill country. It ended at the desert of Beth-aven.
From there the border passed south of Luz, also called Bethel. It went down to Ataroth-addar on the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.
The border turned west and south from the mountain before Beth-horon. It ended at Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim), a city of Judah. This was the west side.
The south side started at the end of Kiriath-jearim. It went west to the spring of Nephtoah.
It went down to the end of the mountain near the Valley of Ben Hinnom, north of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Valley of Hinnom south of the Jebusite city. It went down to En-rogel.
It turned north to En-shemesh. It went to Geliloth, across from the road to Adummim. It went down to the stone of Bohan, Reuben’s son.
It passed on the north side of the Arabah. It went down into the Arabah.
It passed north of Beth-hoglah. It ended at the north end of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan River. This was the south border.
The Jordan River was the east border. This was Benjamin’s land, by its families, with towns all around.
The cities of Benjamin, by families, were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, and Emek-keziz.
They also included Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, and Bethel.
They also included Avvim, Parah, and Ophrah.
They also included Chephar-ammoni, Ophni, and Geba. That is twelve cities with their villages.
They also included Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth.
They also included Mizpah, Chephirah, and Mozah.
They also included Rekem, Irpeel, and Taralah.
They also included Zelah, Eleph, the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath. That is fourteen cities with their villages. This was Benjamin’s land, by families.
The second lot was for the families of Simeon. Their land was inside Judah's land.
They got Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah.
They got Hazar-shual, Balah, and Ezem.
They got Eltolad, Bethul, and Hormah.
They got Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah.
They got Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen. That was thirteen towns and their villages.
They got Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan. That was four towns and their villages.
They also got all the villages around these towns, all the way to Baalath-beer, which is Ramah in the south. This was Simeon's land.
Simeon's land came from Judah's part, because Judah had too much land. So Simeon lived inside Judah's land.
The third lot was for the families of Zebulun. Their border reached to Sarid.
It went west to Maralah and touched Dabbesheth. It met the stream east of Jokneam.
From Sarid it turned east, toward the sunrise, to the border of Chisloth-tabor. Then it went to Daberath and up to Japhia.
From there it went east to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin. It reached Rimmon and turned toward Neah.
Then the border went north around Hannathon. It ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el.
It had Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem. That was twelve towns and their villages.
This was Zebulun's land, with these towns and villages.
The fourth lot was for the families of Issachar.
Their land had Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shunem.
It had Hapharaim, Shion, and Anaharath.
It had Rabbith, Kishion, and Abez.
It had Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez.
The border touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh. It ended at the Jordan River. That was sixteen towns and their villages.
This was Issachar's land, with these towns and villages.
The fifth lot was for the families of Asher.
Their land had Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph.
It had Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. On the west it touched Carmel and Shihor-libnath.
Then it turned east to Beth-dagon. It touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el. It went north to Beth-emek and Neiel. It reached Cabul on the left.
It went to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah. It reached as far as big Sidon.
Then the border turned to Ramah. It went to the strong city of Tyre. It turned to Hosah. It ended at the sea near Achzib.
It had Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob. That was twenty-two towns and their villages.
This was Asher's land, with these towns and villages.
The sixth lot was for the families of Naphtali.
Their border started at Heleph and the big tree at Zaanannim. It passed Adami-nekeb and Jabneel. It went to Lakkum and ended at the Jordan River.
Then the border turned west to Aznoth-tabor. It went to Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and the Jordan River on the east.
The strong towns were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth.
It had Adamah, Ramah, and Hazor.
It had Kedesh, Edrei, and En-hazor.
It had Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh. That was nineteen towns and their villages.
This was Naphtali's land, with these towns and villages.
The seventh lot was for the families of Dan.
Their land had Zorah, Eshtaol, and Ir-shemesh.
It had Shaalabbin, Aijalon, and Ithlah.
It had Elon, Timnah, and Ekron.
It had Eltekeh, Gibbethon, and Baalath.
It had Jehud, Bene-berak, and Gath-rimmon.
It had Me-jarkon and Rakkon, near Joppa.
The Danites could not take all their land, so they went up and fought Leshem. They took it and killed its people. They lived there and named it Dan, after their father Dan.
This was Dan's land, with these towns and villages.
When they finished dividing the land, the people of Israel gave Joshua son of Nun a share among them.
As the LORD had said, they gave him the city he asked for: Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He built the city and lived there.

These are the lands that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the family leaders gave out by lot to the tribes of Israel at Shiloh, in front of the LORD, at the door of the Tent of Meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
"Tell the people of Israel to choose safe cities for themselves. I told them about these cities through Moses.
A person who kills someone by accident can run there. These cities will keep him safe from the relative who wants revenge.
He will run to one of these cities. He will stand at the city gate. He will tell the city leaders what happened. Then they will let him come inside. They will give him a place to live with them.
"If the relative who wants revenge comes after him, the city leaders must not give him up. The killer did not mean to kill his neighbor. He did not hate him before.
He must live in that city until he goes to court in front of the people. He stays until the high priest dies. Then he can go back home to the city he ran from."
So they chose Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

On the east side of the Jordan near Jericho, they gave Bezer in the desert on the flat land from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the cities chosen for all the people of Israel and for strangers living among them. Anyone who killed a person by accident could run there. He would not be killed by the relative who wanted revenge until he went to court in front of the people.
The leaders of the Levite families came to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the Israelite tribes.
They were at Shiloh in Canaan. They said, "The LORD told Moses to give us cities to live in and fields for our animals."
So the Israelites gave the Levites cities and fields from their own land, just as the LORD had said.
The Kohathite families got their share first. The sons of Aaron the priest got thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
The rest of Kohath's sons got ten cities by lot from Ephraim, Dan, and half of Manasseh.
The sons of Gershon got thirteen cities by lot from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and half of Manasseh in Bashan.
The sons of Merari got twelve cities for their families from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
The Israelites gave these cities and fields to the Levites by lot, just as the LORD had told Moses.
From Judah and Simeon, they gave cities by name to Aaron's sons.
These were the Kohathites, and they got the first share.
They gave them Kiriath-arba, also called Hebron, in the hills of Judah, with its fields. Arba was the father of Anak.
But the fields and villages around the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To Aaron's sons, the priests, they gave Hebron, a safe city for someone who killed by accident, along with Libnah and its fields.
They also gave Jattir, Eshtemoa, and their fields.
They gave Holon, Debir, and their fields.
They gave Ain, Juttah, and Beth-shemesh. That was nine cities from these two tribes, with their fields.
From Benjamin they gave Gibeon, Geba,
Anathoth, and Almon—four cities with their fields.
All the cities for Aaron's priest sons were thirteen, with their fields.
The rest of the Kohathite families got cities by lot from Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem, a safe city in the hills of Ephraim, along with Gezer and its fields.
They gave Kibzaim and Beth-horon, with their fields.
From Dan they gave Eltekeh and Gibbethon.
They gave Aijalon and Gath-rimmon. That was four cities from Dan, with their fields.
From half of Manasseh they gave Taanach and Gath-rimmon. That was two cities with their fields.
All together, the Kohath families got ten cities with their fields.
From half of Manasseh they gave the Gershon families Golan in Bashan, a safe city, and Beeshterah, with their fields. That was two cities.
From Issachar they gave Kishion and Daberath.
They gave Jarmuth and En-gannim. That was four cities with their fields.
From Asher they gave Mishal and Abdon.
They gave Helkath and Rehob. That was four cities with their fields.
From Naphtali they gave Kedesh in Galilee, a safe city, Hammoth-dor, and Kartan. That was three cities with their fields.
All together, the Gershon families got thirteen cities with their fields.
From Zebulun they gave the Merari families Jokneam and Kartah.
They gave Dimnah and Nahalal. That was four cities with their fields.
From Reuben they gave Bezer and Jahzah.
They gave Kedemoth and Mephaath. That was four cities with their fields.
From Gad they gave Ramoth in Gilead, a safe city, and Mahanaim.
They gave Heshbon and Jazer. That was four cities with their fields.
All together, the Merari families got twelve cities with their fields.
The Levites had forty-eight cities in all among the Israelites, with their fields.
Every one of these cities had fields around it.
The LORD gave Israel all the land He had promised to their fathers. They took it and lived there.
The LORD gave them rest on every side, just as He had promised their fathers. None of their enemies could stand against them. the LORD gave all their enemies into their hands.
Not one of the good promises the LORD made to Israel failed. Everything came true.
Then Joshua called the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, “You have kept all that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, told you to do. You have listened to my voice in all that I told you.
For a long time you did not leave your brothers. You kept the command of the the LORD your God.

Now the the LORD your God has given your brothers rest, just as He said. Now turn and go to your tents. Go to the land you own. Moses, the servant of the the LORD, gave it to you on the other side of the Jordan.

But be very careful to do the law and the commands that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, gave you. Love the the LORD your God. Walk in all His ways. Keep His commands. Stay close to Him. Serve Him with all your heart and all your soul.”
Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away. They went to their tents.
Moses had given half the tribe of Manasseh land in Bashan. Joshua gave the other half land west of the Jordan. When Joshua sent them to their tents, he blessed them too.
He said, “Go home with great riches. You have much cattle, silver, gold, bronze, and iron. You have many clothes. Share the things you took from your enemies with your brothers.”

So the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh left the people of Israel at Shiloh in the land of Canaan. They went back to their own land of Gilead, which they had received by the word of the the LORD through Moses.

When they came to Geliloth near the Jordan in the land of Canaan, the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh built a big altar there by the Jordan. It could be seen from far away.

Then the people of Israel heard, “Look, the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh have built an altar on the edge of the land of Canaan. It is at Geliloth near the Jordan, on our side.”
When the people of Israel heard this, the whole group came together at Shiloh to go to war against them.
The people of Israel sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the land of Gilead. He went to the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh.
They also sent ten leaders. There was one leader from each tribe of Israel. Each man was head of a family group among the clans of Israel.
They went to the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead. They said to them, “
This is what the whole group of the the LORD says: ‘Why did you turn away from the God of Israel by building an altar for yourselves today?
Was the sin at Peor not enough for us? We have not made ourselves clean from it to this day. A bad sickness came on the group of the the LORD then.
And now you would turn away from the the LORD? If you turn against the the LORD today, He will be angry with all the people of Israel tomorrow.

If your land is not clean, come over to the the LORD’s land. The the LORD’s tent is there. Take land among us. But do not turn against the the LORD or against us by building an altar for yourselves other than the altar of the the LORD our God.
Did not Achan son of Zerah sin against the things set apart for God? Anger came on all the people of Israel. He was not the only one who died for his sin.’”
Then the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of Israel. “
The LORD, God of gods, the LORD, God of gods, He knows, and Israel will know too. If we did this to turn against the the LORD or to be unfaithful to Him, do not save us today.
If we built this altar to turn away from the the LORD, or to burn gifts or grain on it, or to make peace gifts on it, may the the LORD Himself ask us to pay for it.
But we did this because we were worried. We thought that someday your children might say to our children, ‘What do you have to do with the the LORD, the God of Israel?’
For the the LORD made the Jordan a border between us and you. You people of Reuben and Gad have no share in the the LORD. Then your children might make our children stop fearing the the LORD. “
So we said, ‘Let us build an altar. It is not for burnt gifts or sacrifices.

It is a witness between us and you, and for the children after us. We want to serve the the LORD in front of Him with our burnt gifts, sacrifices, and peace gifts. Then your children will not say to our children, “You have no share in the the LORD.”’

And we thought, ‘If they say this to us or to our children later, we will say, “Look at the copy of the the LORD’s altar that our fathers made. It is not for burnt gifts or sacrifices. It is a witness between us and you.”’

We would never turn against the the LORD or turn away from Him today by building an altar for burnt gifts, grain gifts, or sacrifices other than the altar of the the LORD our God, which is in front of His tent.”
When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the group heard what the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh said, they were pleased.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the people of Reuben, the people of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh, “Today we know that the the LORD is with us. You have not been unfaithful to the the LORD in this. Now you have saved the people of Israel from the the LORD’s anger.”
Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders went back from the people of Reuben and Gad in the land of Gilead to the people of Israel in the land of Canaan. They brought back a report.
The people of Israel were pleased with the report. They praised God. They did not talk about going to war against them or destroying the land where the people of Reuben and Gad lived.
So the people of Reuben and Gad named the altar Witness. They said, “It is a witness between us and you that the the LORD is God.”
A long time passed. The LORD had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them. Joshua was very old.
Joshua called all Israel together. He called the elders, leaders, judges, and officers. He said, "I am old. I am very old.
"You have seen all that the LORD your God did to these nations for you. The LORD your God fought for you.
"Look, I gave your tribes these nations that are still left. I also gave you all the nations I destroyed. This land goes from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.
"The LORD your God will push them out before you. He will drive them out before you. You will take their land. The LORD your God promised this to you.
"Be very strong. Keep and do all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses. Do not turn left or right from it.
"Do not mix with these nations still among you. Do not say the names of their gods. Do not swear by them. Do not serve them. Do not bow down to them.
"Hold close to the LORD your God, like you have done until today.
"The LORD drove out big and strong nations before you. No one has stood against you to this day.
"One of you can chase a thousand. The LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.
"So be very careful to love the LORD your God.
"But if you turn away and hold to the rest of these nations still among you, and if you marry them and join them,

"then know for sure that the LORD your God will not drive these nations out before you anymore. They will be traps and snares for you. They will be like whips on your sides and thorns in your eyes. You will die and lose this good land the LORD your God gave you.
"Now I am going to die, like all people do. You know in your heart and soul that not one good thing the LORD your God promised you has failed. Everything has come true.
"Just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come true, so the LORD will bring every bad thing on you. He will destroy you from this good land the LORD your God gave you.
"If you break the agreement the LORD your God made with you, and go serve other gods and bow to them, then the LORD will be angry with you. You will quickly lose the good land He gave you."
Joshua brought all the tribes of Israel to Shechem. He called the elders, judges, and leaders of Israel. They stood before God.

Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Long ago, your fathers lived on the other side of the Euphrates River. Terah was the father of Abraham and Nahor. They served other gods.
I took your father Abraham from the other side of the river. I led him through all the land of Canaan. I gave him many children. I gave him Isaac.
I gave Isaac Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Seir to own. Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
"I sent Moses and Aaron. I punished Egypt with trouble. After that, I brought you out.
I brought your fathers out of Egypt. You came to the sea. The Egyptians chased your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.
Your fathers cried to the LORD. He put darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. You lived in the desert for many days.
"Then I brought you to the land of the Amorites. They lived on the other side of the Jordan. They fought you. I gave them into your hands. You took their land. I destroyed them before you.
Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But I would not listen to Balaam. He blessed you instead. I saved you from his hand.
"You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought you. So did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites. I gave them into your hands.
I sent hornets ahead of you. They drove out the two Amorite kings before you. It was not by your sword or your bow.
I gave you land you did not work for. I gave you cities you did not build. You eat from vineyards and olive trees you did not plant.
"So now, respect the LORD. Serve Him with all your heart and with truth. Get rid of the gods your fathers served on the other side of the river and in Egypt. Serve the LORD.

If it seems bad to you to serve the LORD, choose today whom you will serve. You may serve the gods your fathers served on the other side of the river. Or you may serve the gods of the Amorites, whose land you live in. But my family and I will serve the LORD."
The people answered, "We would never leave the LORD and serve other gods!

The LORD our God brought us and our fathers up from Egypt. He brought us out of slavery in Egypt. He did great miracles we could see. He kept us safe on the whole road we traveled. He kept us safe among all the peoples we passed through.
The LORD drove out all the peoples before us. He drove out the Amorites who lived in the land. So we will serve the LORD too, for He is our God."
Joshua said to the people, "You cannot serve the LORD. He is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your sins and wrongs if you turn away.
If you leave the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn against you. He will hurt you and destroy you, even after He has been good to you."
The people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the LORD."
Joshua said, "You are witnesses against yourselves. You have chosen the LORD to serve." The people said, "We are witnesses."
Joshua said, "Then get rid of the foreign gods among you. Give your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel."
The people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God. We will obey His voice."
That day Joshua made an agreement with the people at Shechem. He set rules for them.
Joshua wrote these words in God's Law Book. He took a large stone and set it up there under the oak tree near the LORD's holy place.
Joshua said to all the people, "This stone will be a reminder for us. It heard all the words the LORD spoke to us. It will be a reminder for you, so you will not deny your God."
Then Joshua sent the people away. Each man went to his own land.
After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died. He was 110 years old.
They buried him at Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua. They also served the LORD all the days of the elders who lived after Joshua. These elders knew all the things the LORD had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the people of Israel brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem. They were buried in the piece of land Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father. Jacob paid 100 pieces of silver for it. It became the land of Joseph's children.
Eleazar son of Aaron died. They buried him at Gibeah, which belonged to his son Phinehas, in the hill country of Ephraim.
After Joshua died, the Israelites asked the LORD, "Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?"
The LORD said, "Judah will go first. I have given the land to him."
Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come with me to fight the Canaanites in my part of the land. Then I will go with you to fight in your part." So Simeon went with him.
Judah went to fight. The LORD gave them victory over the Canaanites and Perizzites. They killed ten thousand men at Bezek.
They found Adoni-Bezek in Bezek. They fought him and beat the Canaanites and Perizzites.
Adoni-Bezek ran away, but they chased and caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes.

Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings had their thumbs and big toes cut off. They picked up food scraps under my table. I did the same to others, and now God has paid me back." Then they took him to Jerusalem, where he died.
The men of Judah fought Jerusalem. They took the city, killed people with swords, and burned it.
Later, Judah's men went to fight Canaanites in the hills, the southern desert, and the lowlands.
Judah went to Hebron, which used to be called Kiriath-arba. They beat Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
Then they went to Debir, which used to be called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Achsah in marriage to the man who takes Kiriath-sepher."
Othniel, son of Kenaz and Caleb's younger brother, took the city. So Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah to marry.
When she came, she told her husband to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
She said, "Please bless me. You gave me dry land in the south, so give me springs of water too." Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.
The Kenites, from Moses' father-in-law's family, went with Judah's men from the city of palm trees to the desert of Judah near Arad. They went to live among the people there.
Judah and his brother Simeon fought the Canaanites in Zephath. They destroyed the city completely and called it Hormah.
Judah also took Gaza and its land, Ashkelon and its land, and Ekron and its land.
The LORD was with Judah. They took the hills, but they could not push out the people in the valleys, because those people had iron chariots.
As Moses had said, they gave Hebron to Caleb. He drove out the three sons of Anak from there.
The people of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites still live there with them today.
The family of Joseph also went to fight Bethel, and the the LORD was with them.
They sent scouts to spy on Bethel, which used to be called Luz.
The scouts saw a man leaving the city. They said, "Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you well."
He showed them the way in. They killed the people of the city with swords, but they let the man and his whole family go free.
The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city. He called it Luz, and it still has that name today.
Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, and Megiddo, or their nearby towns, because the Canaanites were set on staying in that land.
When Israel grew strong, they made the Canaanites work as slaves, but they never drove them out completely.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites in Gezer, so the Canaanites kept living among them there.
Zebulun did not drive out the people of Kitron and Nahalol. The Canaanites lived among them and were made to work.
Asher did not drive out the people of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
So the people of Asher lived among the Canaanites, the people already in the land, because they did not drive them out.
Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. They lived among the Canaanites, the people already in the land. The people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath were made to work.
The Amorites pushed the people of Dan into the hills and would not let them go down into the valley.
The Amorites were set on staying in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when Joseph's family grew strong, they made them work.
The Amorites' border ran from the pass of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.
The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim. He said, "I brought you out of Egypt. I led you into the land I promised to your fathers. I said, 'I will never break My promise to you.'
You must not make a promise with the people who live in this land. You must tear down their altars. But you did not listen to Me. What have you done?
So now I say I will not drive them out in front of you. They will cause you trouble. Their gods will trap you."
After the angel of the LORD said these words to all the people of Israel, they cried loudly and wept.
They named that place Bochim. There they gave offerings to the LORD.
Joshua sent the people of Israel away. Each man went to his own land to take it.
The people served the LORD while Joshua lived. They also served Him while the older leaders lived after Joshua. Those leaders had seen all the great things the LORD did for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun was the the LORD's servant. He died at 110 years old.
They buried him in his land at Timnath-heres, in the hills of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
After that whole group died, a new group grew up. They did not know the LORD. They did not know the things He had done for Israel.
Then the people of Israel did what was wrong in the eyes of the LORD. They served gods called Baal.
They left the LORD, the God of their fathers. He had brought them out of Egypt. They followed other gods, the gods of the people around them. They bowed down to them. They made the LORD angry.
They left the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.
The LORD was very angry with Israel. He let raiders rob them. He let their enemies capture them. They could not beat their enemies anymore.
Everywhere Israel went, the LORD worked against them and brought trouble, just as He had promised. So they were very upset.
Then the LORD raised up judges. The judges saved them from the raiders.

But the people would not listen to their judges. They ran after other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly left the way their fathers had walked. Their fathers had obeyed the the LORD's commands. They did not do the same.

When the LORD raised up a judge for them, He was with that judge. The judge saved them from their enemies while the judge lived. The LORD felt sorry for them when they cried out because their enemies hurt them.
But when the judge died, the people did even worse than their fathers. They went after other gods to serve and bow down to them. They did not stop their bad ways. They stayed stubborn.
The LORD was very angry with Israel. He said, "This group broke My promise. I told their fathers to keep it. They did not listen to Me.
So I will not drive out the nations that Joshua left when he died.
I will use them to test if Israel will follow the LORD's way, like their fathers did."
So the LORD let those nations stay. He did not drive them out quickly. He did not give them to Joshua.
These are the nations the LORD left. He left them to test Israel. He tested all the people who had not fought in the wars in Canaan.
He did this to teach war to the new groups of Israel who had not fought before.
There were the five rulers of the Philistines. There were also the Canaanites, Sidonians, and Hivites. They lived in the Lebanon mountains, from Mount Baal Hermon to Lebo Hamath.
They were left to test Israel. The LORD wanted to see if Israel would obey His rules. Moses had given these rules to their fathers.
The people of Israel lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
They married the daughters of those people. They gave their own daughters to the sons of those people. They served the gods of those people.
The people of Israel did wrong in the eyes of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God. They served the false gods named Baal and Asherah.
The LORD was very angry with Israel. He let Cushan-Rishathaim, king of Aram Naharaim, rule over them. Israel served him for eight years.
Then the people of Israel cried out to the LORD. The LORD gave them a helper. His name was Othniel. He was the son of Kenaz. He was Caleb's younger brother. He saved Israel.
The Spirit of the LORD came on Othniel. He became Israel's judge. He went to war. The LORD let Othniel beat Cushan-Rishathaim, king of Aram.
Then the land had peace for forty years. After that, Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Again the people of Israel did wrong in the eyes of the LORD. So The LORD let Eglon, king of Moab, become strong against Israel. This was because Israel did wrong in the eyes of the LORD.
Eglon got the Ammonites and Amalekites to join him. He came and attacked Israel. They took the City of Palms.
The people of Israel served Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.

Again the people of Israel cried out to the LORD. He gave them a helper named Ehud. Ehud was the son of Gera. He was from Benjamin. He was left-handed. Israel sent Ehud to Eglon, king of Moab, with a gift.
Ehud made a sword with two sharp sides. It was about a foot and a half long. He tied it to his right leg under his clothes.
Ehud gave the gift to Eglon, king of Moab. Eglon was a very fat man.
After Ehud gave the gift, he sent home the men who carried it.
But at the stone statues near Gilgal, Ehud turned back. He said, “I have a secret message for you, King.” The king said, “Quiet!” Then all the men standing near him left.
Ehud came to the king. The king was sitting alone in the cool room upstairs. Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you.” The king stood up from his chair.
Ehud reached with his left hand. He took the sword from his right side. He pushed it into the king's stomach.
The handle went in too. The king's body emptied. Ehud did not pull the sword out. The king's helpers went out the back.
Then Ehud went out to the porch. He shut and locked the doors of the room upstairs.
After Ehud left, the king's helpers came. They saw the doors were locked. They said, “He is probably using the bathroom in the cool room.”
They waited a long time. He did not open the doors. So they took a key and opened them. They saw their king dead on the floor.
While they waited, Ehud got away. He passed the stone statues and went to Seirah.
When he got there, he blew a trumpet in the hills of Ephraim. The people of Israel came down with him from the hills. He led them.
He said, “Follow me. The LORD has given Moab, your enemy, into your hands.” So they went down after him. They took the crossings of the Jordan River near Moab. They did not let anyone cross.
At that time they killed about ten thousand men of Moab. All were strong men. Not one man got away.
That day Moab was brought under Israel's rule. The land had peace for eighty years.
After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. He killed six hundred Philistines with a sharp stick used to drive oxen. He also saved Israel.
After Ehud died, the people of Israel did wrong again. They did what the LORD saw as bad.
So the LORD let Jabin, king of Canaan, rule over them. Jabin ruled in Hazor. His army boss was Sisera. Sisera lived in Harosheth Haggoyim.
The people of Israel cried out to the LORD. Jabin had 900 iron war carts. He was very mean to Israel for 20 years.
At that time, Deborah was a leader for Israel. She was a woman who spoke for God. She was the wife of Lappidoth.
She sat under Deborah's palm tree. It was between Ramah and Bethel, in the hills of Ephraim. The people of Israel came to her to settle their problems.

She sent for Barak, the son of Abinoam. He was from Kedesh in Naphtali. She said to him, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has told you to go. Take 10,000 men from Naphtali and Zebulun. Go up to Mount Tabor.
I will bring Sisera, Jabin's army boss, with his war carts and his men to the Kishon River. I will give him to you."
Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go. If you do not go with me, I will not go."
"I will go with you," Deborah said. "But the way you are going, you will not get the praise. The LORD will let a woman beat Sisera." Then Deborah went with Barak to Kedesh.
There Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali. Ten thousand men went up with him. Deborah went up too.
Heber the Kenite had left the other Kenites. They came from Hobab, Moses' father-in-law. Heber put his tent by the big tree in Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
People told Sisera that Barak, son of Abinoam, had gone up to Mount Tabor.
So Sisera called all his war carts. There were 900 iron carts. He called all his men from Harosheth Haggoyim to the Kishon River.
Deborah said to Barak, "Get up! Today the LORD has given Sisera to you. The LORD has gone ahead of you." So Barak went down Mount Tabor. Ten thousand men followed him.
The LORD threw Sisera's army into a panic. Barak's men beat them with swords. Sisera got down from his war cart and ran away on foot.
Barak chased the war carts and the army to Harosheth Haggoyim. All of Sisera's men fell by the sword. Not one was left.
But Sisera ran on foot to Jael's tent. She was Heber's wife. Jabin, king of Hazor, and Heber's family had a peace deal.
Jael went out to meet Sisera. She said, "Come in, my lord. Come in. Do not be afraid." He went into her tent. She covered him with a blanket.
He said, "I am thirsty. Please give me a little water." She opened a bottle of milk. She gave him a drink. Then she covered him again.
He told her, "Stand at the tent door. If a man comes and asks you, 'Is anyone here?' say, 'No.'"
But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and a hammer. She went to him quietly. He was fast asleep and very tired. She hit the peg into the side of his head. It went into the ground. He died.

Just then Barak came by. He was chasing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him. She said, "Come. I will show you the man you want." He went in with her. There was Sisera, dead. The tent peg was in the side of his head.
That day God brought down Jabin, king of Canaan, for the people of Israel.
The people of Israel kept getting stronger against Jabin, king of Canaan. They destroyed him.
On that day, Deborah and Barak, son of Abinoam, sang this song.
“The leaders in Israel led the way. The people gave themselves freely. Praise the the LORD!”
“Hear this, kings! Listen, rulers! I will sing to the the LORD. I will sing. I will make music to the the LORD, the God of Israel.”
“The LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from Edom, the earth shook. The sky poured. The clouds poured water.
The mountains shook before the the LORD. Even Mount Sinai shook before the the LORD, the God of Israel.”
“In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the roads were empty. Travelers took crooked paths.
Life in the villages stopped. It stopped until I, Deborah, stood up. I stood up to care for Israel like a mother.
They chose new gods. Then war came to the city gates. Not one shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.
My heart is with the leaders of Israel. It is with the people who gave themselves freely. Praise the the LORD!”
“Those who ride white donkeys, sitting on saddle blankets, and those who walk on the road, listen.
Listen to the singers by the wells. They sing about the the LORD’s good deeds. They sing about His good deeds for His fighters in Israel. Then the the LORD’s people went down to the city gates.”
“Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up, sing a song! Get up, Barak! Son of Abinoam, take your prisoners!
Then the rest of the people came down to the leaders. The the LORD’s people came down to me to fight the strong enemy.”
“Some came from Ephraim, from Amalek’s land. Benjamin came with his people after you. Leaders came down from Makir. From Zebulun came men who carry the leader’s staff.
The leaders of Issachar were with Deborah. Issachar was with Barak. They were sent into the valley under his lead. The men of Reuben thought hard about what to do.”
“Why did you stay among the sheep pens? Why did you listen to the whistles for the flocks? The men of Reuben thought hard about what to do.
Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan. Dan, why did you stay by the ships? Asher stayed by the sea. He stayed in his bays.
The people of Zebulun risked their lives. Naphtali did too on the high places of the field.”
“Kings came and fought. The kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo. But they took no silver.
The stars in the sky fought. From their paths they fought against Sisera.
The Kishon River swept them away. The old river, the Kishon River. March on, my soul, with strength!
Then the horses’ hooves pounded. They pounded from the running of his strong horses.”
“Curse Meroz,” said the angel of the the LORD. “Curse its people hard. They did not come to help the the LORD. They did not help the the LORD against the strong enemy.”
“Jael is most blessed among women. She is the wife of Heber the Kenite. She is most blessed of women in the tent.
He asked for water. She gave him milk. She brought him butter in a bowl fit for leaders.
Her hand reached for the tent peg. Her right hand reached for the worker’s hammer. She hit Sisera. She crushed his head. She broke and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he bent down. He fell. He lay still. Between her feet he bent down. He fell. Where he bent down, there he fell, dead.”
Sisera’s mother looked through the window. She cried from the lattice. “Why is his chariot so late? Why do his chariot wheels wait?”
Her wise ladies answered her. She kept saying to herself,
“They must be finding and sharing the things they took. A girl or two for each man. Pretty clothes for Sisera. Pretty clothes with fancy work. Fancy clothes for the winner’s neck.”
“So may all your enemies die, the the LORD! But may those who love You be like the sun when it rises in its strength.” Then the land had peace for forty years.
The Israelites did wrong in the the LORD's eyes. So the the LORD let Midian rule them for seven years.
Midian was stronger than Israel. The Israelites hid in caves, dens, and safe places in the mountains to get away from Midian.
When the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and people from the east came to fight them.
They camped against Israel. They ruined the crops. They left no food for Israel. They took sheep, oxen, and donkeys.
They came with many animals and tents. They were like a swarm of locusts. Their camels could not be counted. They came to ruin the land.
Israel became very poor because of Midian. The Israelites cried out to the the LORD.
When the Israelites cried out to the the LORD because of Midian,
the the LORD sent a man to speak to the Israelites. He said, "This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up from Egypt. I brought you out of the land where you were slaves.
I saved you from the Egyptians. I saved you from all who hurt you. I drove them out before you. I gave you their land.
I said, I am the the LORD your God. Do not be afraid of the gods of the Amorites, whose land you live in. But you did not listen to Me."

The angel of the the LORD came and sat under the oak tree in Ophrah. It belonged to Joash, who was from the family of Abiezer. His son Gideon was beating out wheat in a winepress to hide it from Midian.
The angel of the the LORD appeared to him and said, "The LORD is with you, strong and brave man."

Gideon said, "Please, my lord, if the the LORD is with us, why has all this happened? Where are all the wonderful things our fathers told us about? They said the the LORD brought us up from Egypt. But now the the LORD has left us. He has let Midian rule us."
The LORD turned to him and said, "Go with the strength you have. Save Israel from Midian. Have I not sent you?"
Gideon said, "Please, Lord, how can I save Israel? My family is the weakest in Manasseh. I am the youngest in my father's house."
The LORD said, "I will be with you. You will beat Midian as if they were one man."
Gideon said, "If I have found favor with you, give me a sign that it is really you speaking to me."
"Please do not go away until I come back with my offering and set it before you." The The LORD said, "I will stay until you return."
Gideon went in and cooked a young goat. He made bread without yeast. He put the meat in a basket. He put the broth in a pot. He brought them out to the angel under the oak tree and gave them to him.
The angel of God said, "Take the meat and the bread. Put them on this rock. Pour out the broth." Gideon did so.
The angel of the the LORD touched the meat and bread with the end of his staff. Fire came up from the rock and burned up the meat and bread. Then the angel of the the LORD went away.
Gideon saw that it was the angel of the the LORD. He cried out, "Oh no, Lord, the LORD! I have seen the angel of the the LORD face to face!"
The LORD said to him, "Peace be with you. Do not be afraid. You will not die."
Gideon built an altar to the the LORD there. He called it "The LORD Is Peace." It is still in Ophrah, which belongs to the family of Abiezer.

That night the the LORD said to Gideon, "Take your father's young bull. Take the second bull, the one that is seven years old. Pull down your father's altar to Baal. Cut down the Asherah pole beside it.
Build an altar to the the LORD your God on top of this strong place. Use the wood from the Asherah pole you cut down. Take the second bull and burn it as an offering to the the LORD."
Gideon took ten of his servants. He did what the the LORD said. But he was afraid of his father's family and the men of the town. So he did it at night.
In the morning the men of the town got up. They saw that the altar to Baal was broken down. The Asherah pole was cut down. The second bull was offered on the new altar.
They asked each other, "Who did this?" They looked into it and found out. They said, "Gideon son of Joash did this."
The men of the town said to Joash, "Bring out your son. He must die. He broke down the altar to Baal. He cut down the Asherah pole."

Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you fight for Baal? If Baal is a god, let him fight for himself. If anyone fights for Baal, that person must die before morning. If Baal is a god, let him fight, because his altar was broken down."
So that day they called Gideon "Jerubbaal." They said, "Let Baal fight against him, because he broke down Baal's altar."
The Midianites, the Amalekites, and people from the east gathered together. They crossed over and camped in the Jezreel Valley.
The Spirit of the the LORD came upon Gideon. He blew a trumpet. The people of Abiezer followed him.
He sent messengers to all of Manasseh. He sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali too. They came to join him.
Gideon said to God, "If You will save Israel by my hand, as You said,
I will put a piece of wool on the ground where grain is beaten. If there is dew only on the wool, and all the ground is dry, then I will know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You said."
That is what happened. The next morning Gideon got up early. He squeezed the wool. He got a bowl full of water from it.
Gideon said to God, "Do not be angry with me. Let me ask one more time. Let the wool be dry this time, and let all the ground have dew."
That night God did it. The wool was dry, but there was dew on all the ground.
Early in the morning, Gideon (also called Jerubbaal) and all his men got up. They camped by the spring of Harod. The Midian camp was north of them in the valley, near Moreh hill.
The LORD said to Gideon, "There are too many men with you. I will not give Midian into their hands, or Israel may brag and say, 'I saved myself.'
So call out to the men, 'Anyone who is afraid may go home from Mount Gilead.'" Then 22,000 men went home, and 10,000 stayed.
The LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many men. Take them to the water. I will test them for you there. The men I say can go with you will go. The men I say cannot go will not go."
So Gideon took the men to the water. The LORD said, "Separate the men who lap water with their tongues, like a dog. Also separate the men who kneel down to drink."
300 men lapped water with their hands to their mouths. The rest knelt down to drink.
The LORD said to Gideon, "I will save you with the 300 men who lapped. I will give Midian into your hand. Let everyone else go home."
So the men took food and trumpets. Gideon sent everyone else home. The 300 men stayed. The Midian camp was below them in the valley.
That night the LORD said to Gideon, "Get up and go down to the camp. I have given it into your hand.
But if you are afraid to go down, take your helper Purah with you.
Listen to what they say. Then you will feel strong and brave, and you can go down to the camp." So Gideon and Purah went to the edge of the enemy camp.
Midian, Amalek, and the people from the east were spread out in the valley. There were so many of them, like locusts. Their camels were too many to count, like sand by the sea.

Gideon came close. A man was telling his friend a dream. He said, "I had a dream. A loaf of barley bread rolled into the Midian camp. It hit a tent. The tent fell down, turned upside down, and fell flat."
His friend answered, "This can only be the sword of Gideon son of Joash, an Israelite. God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hand."
When Gideon heard the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to worship. Then he went back to the Israel camp and said, "Get up! The LORD has given the Midian camp into your hand."
He divided the 300 men into three groups. He gave each man a trumpet and an empty jar. Inside each jar was a torch.
Gideon said to them, "Watch me and do what I do. When I get to the edge of the camp, do just as I do.
I and everyone with me will blow our trumpets. Then you blow your trumpets all around the camp. Shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"
Gideon and 100 men with him came to the edge of the camp late at night, just as the guards were changing. They blew their trumpets and broke the jars in their hands.
All three groups blew their trumpets and broke their jars. They held torches in their left hands and trumpets in their right hands. They shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
Each man stood in his place around the camp. The whole enemy camp ran away, shouting and crying out.

The 300 men kept blowing their trumpets. The LORD made the enemy soldiers turn their swords on each other all through the camp. The army ran away to Beth Shittah, toward Zererah, and to the border of Abel Meholah by Tabbath.
Men from Israel, Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh were called out. They chased the Midianites.

Gideon sent messengers all through the hill country of Ephraim. He said, "Come down and fight Midian. Take control of the Jordan River all the way to Beth Barah." So the men of Ephraim were called out. They took control of the Jordan River all the way to Beth Barah.

They caught two Midian leaders, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. They kept chasing Midian. They brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
The men of Ephraim said to Gideon, "What have you done to us? Why didn't you call us when you went to fight Midian?" They argued with him very hard.
Gideon said, "What have I done now that is like what you did? Aren't the small grapes Ephraim picked better than all the grapes my family picked?
God gave you Oreb and Zeeb, the leaders of Midian. What could I do like you?" When he said this, their anger went away.
Gideon and his 300 men came to the Jordan River. They were tired, but they kept chasing.
Gideon said to the men of Succoth, "Please give some bread to the men with me. They are tired. I am chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
The leaders of Succoth said, "Do you already have Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand? Why should we give bread to your soldiers?"
Gideon said, "When the LORD gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your skin with thorns and briers from the desert."
Gideon went up to Penuel and spoke the same way. The men of Penuel answered him like the men of Succoth did.
He also said to the men of Penuel, "When I come back safely, I will tear down this tower."
Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their camp. About 15,000 men were left from all the people of the east. 120,000 swordsmen had died.
Gideon went up by the road of the tent dwellers, east of Nobah and Jogbehah. He attacked the camp while it felt safe.
Zebah and Zalmunna ran away. Gideon chased them and caught the two Midian kings, Zebah and Zalmunna. The whole camp panicked.
Gideon son of Joash came back from the battle by the road that goes up to Heres.
He caught a young man from Succoth and asked him questions. The young man wrote down the leaders and elders of Succoth for him. There were 77 men.

Gideon came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. You made fun of me. You said, 'Do we already have Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand? Why should we give food to your tired men?'"
Gideon took the elders of the city and desert thorns and briers. He used them to punish the men of Succoth.
He tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of that city.
Gideon said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Where are the men you killed at Tabor?" They said, "They looked like you, like sons of a king."
Gideon said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. I promise by the LORD, if you had kept them alive, I would not kill you."
Gideon said to Jether, his oldest son, "Get up and kill them." But the boy did not pull out his sword, because he was afraid. He was still young.
Zebah and Zalmunna said, "You do it. You are strong like a man." So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna. He took the crescent ornaments from their camels' necks.
The men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us. You and your son and your grandson can rule, because you saved us from Midian."
Gideon said, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."
Gideon said to them, "I ask one thing from you: each man give me an earring from what he took." They had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.
They said, "We will give them." They spread out a coat, and each man threw an earring from what he had taken onto it.
The gold earrings Gideon asked for weighed 1,700 shekels. This was besides the crescent ornaments, purple cloth, and clothes from the Midian kings, and besides the chains from the camels' necks.
Gideon made an ephod from it and put it in his town, Ophrah. All Israel worshiped it there. It became a trap for Gideon and his family.
Midian was beaten down before Israel. They did not become strong again. The land had peace for 40 years while Gideon lived.
Jerubbaal son of Joash went home and lived there.
Gideon had 70 sons, because he had many wives.
His concubine in Shechem also had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age. He was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of Abiezer.
After Gideon died, the people of Israel turned back and worshiped the Baals. They made Baal-Berith their god.
Israel did not remember the LORD their God, who had saved them from all their enemies around them.
They did not show kindness to Gideon's family for all the good he had done for Israel.
Abimelech was Jerubbaal's son. He went to Shechem to see his mother's brothers. He talked to them and to all his mother's family.

He said, "Please tell all the leaders of Shechem: Which is better for you? Should seventy men, all sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you? Or should one man rule over you? Remember, I am your own flesh and blood."
His mother's brothers told all these words to the leaders of Shechem. The leaders' hearts turned to Abimelech. They said, "He is our brother."
They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baal-berith. Abimelech used the money to hire worthless, reckless men. They followed him.
He went to his father's house in Ophrah. He killed his seventy brothers, Jerubbaal's sons, on one stone. But Jotham, Jerubbaal's youngest son, was left alive because he hid.
All the leaders of Shechem and all the people of Beth-millo met together. They went to the oak tree at Shechem and made Abimelech king.
When Jotham heard this, he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim. He raised his voice and cried out. He said, "Hear me, leaders of Shechem, that God may hear you.
"The trees went to choose a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, 'Be our king.'
But the olive tree said, 'Should I give up my oil that honors God and men, and go rule over the trees?'
The trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, be our king.'
The fig tree said, 'Should I give up my sweet fruit, and go rule over the trees?'
The trees said to the grapevine, 'Come, be our king.'
The grapevine said, 'Should I give up my wine that makes God and men glad, and go rule over the trees?'
Then all the trees said to the thornbush, 'Come, be our king.'
The thornbush said to the trees, 'If you truly make me king over you, come and rest in my shade. But if not, fire will come out of the thornbush and burn up the cedar trees of Lebanon.
"Now, if you have acted true and good in making Abimelech king, and if you have done good to Jerubbaal and his house, and have paid him back for what he did—
for my father fought for you. He risked his life and saved you from Midian.

But you rose up against my father's house today. You killed his seventy sons on one stone. You made Abimelech, the son of his slave woman, king over the leaders of Shechem, because he is your brother—
if you have acted true and good with Jerubbaal and his house today, then be glad with Abimelech, and let him be glad with you.
"But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and burn up the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo. Let fire come out from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and burn up Abimelech."
Jotham ran away and fled. He went to Beer and lived there because of Abimelech, his brother.
Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem. The leaders of Shechem turned against Abimelech.

This happened so the wrong done to Jerubbaal's seventy sons would come back on them. Their blood would be on Abimelech, their brother, who killed them, and on the leaders of Shechem, who helped him kill his brothers.
The leaders of Shechem put men in hiding on the hills. They robbed everyone who passed by. Someone told Abimelech.
Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and moved to Shechem. The leaders of Shechem trusted him.
They went out to the fields and picked grapes. They made wine and had a party. They went into their god's house. They ate and drank. They cursed Abimelech.

Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech? Who is Shechem? Why should we serve him? Is he not Jerubbaal's son? Is Zebul not his helper? Serve the men of Hamor, Shechem's father. Why should we serve Abimelech?"
"If only I had these people under my hand! I would remove Abimelech." Then he said to Abimelech, "Build up your army and come out."
Zebul, the city ruler, heard Gaal's words. He was very angry.
He sent men secretly to Abimelech. He said, "Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem. They are turning the city against you.
Come by night with your men. Hide in the fields.
In the morning, when the sun comes up, get up early and attack the city. When Gaal and his men come out to fight you, do what you can."
Abimelech and all his men got up at night. They hid around Shechem in four groups.
Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the city gate. Abimelech and his men got up from hiding.
Gaal saw the men and said to Zebul, "Look! Men are coming down from the hills." Zebul said, "You are seeing the shadows of the hills. They look like men."
Gaal spoke again, "Look! Men are coming down from the middle of the land. One group is coming from the oak tree of the fortune tellers."
Zebul said to him, "Where is your big talk now? You said you should not serve Abimelech. Are these not the men you looked down on? Go out now and fight them."
Gaal went out in front of the leaders of Shechem and fought Abimelech.
Abimelech chased him. Gaal ran away. Many men fell dead all the way to the city gate.
Abimelech stayed in Arumah. Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem. They could not live there.
The next day the people went out to the fields. Someone told Abimelech.
He took his men and split them into three groups. They hid in the fields. He saw the people coming out of the city. He got up and attacked them.
Abimelech and his group rushed and stood at the city gate. The other two groups rushed at everyone in the fields and killed them.
Abimelech fought the city all day. He took the city. He killed the people in it. He tore down the city and spread salt on it.
All the leaders of the tower of Shechem heard this. They went into the strong room of their god's temple.
Someone told Abimelech that all the leaders of the tower of Shechem had gathered.
Abimelech and all his men went up Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took an ax. He cut a branch from a tree. He put it on his shoulder. He said to his men, "Hurry! Do what you see me do."
Each man cut a branch too. They followed Abimelech. They put the branches against the strong room. They set it on fire. All the people in the tower of Shechem died—about a thousand men and women.
Then Abimelech went to Thebez. He camped there and took it.
There was a strong tower in the city. All the men, women, and leaders ran there. They shut themselves in. They went up to the roof of the tower.
Abimelech came to the tower and fought it. He went up to the door to burn it with fire.
A woman threw a piece of a millstone down on Abimelech's head. It broke his skull.
He quickly called his helper who carried his weapons. He said, "Draw your sword and kill me. I do not want people to say that a woman killed me." His helper stabbed him, and he died.
When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they went home.
God paid back Abimelech for the evil he did to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
God also paid back the men of Shechem for their evil. The curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came true for them.
After Abimelech, a man from Issachar named Tola came to save Israel. Tola was the son of Puah and the grandson of Dodo. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judged Israel for twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.
After him, Jair from Gilead came up. He judged Israel for twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons. They rode on thirty donkeys. They had thirty towns in Gilead. People still call those towns Havvoth Jair today.
Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

The Israelites did wrong again in the eyes of the LORD. They served the Baals and the Ashtoreths. They also served the gods of Aram, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia. They left the LORD and did not serve Him.
The LORD was angry with Israel. He let the Philistines and the Ammonites take charge of them.
For eighteen years, they crushed and hurt the Israelites who lived east of the Jordan River in Gilead, in the land of the Amorites.
The Ammonites crossed the Jordan River to fight Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. The people of Israel were very upset.
The Israelites cried to the LORD and said, "We have sinned against you. We have left our God and served the Baals."
The LORD said to the Israelites, "Didn't I save you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines?
The Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites also hurt you. You cried to Me, and I saved you from their power.
But you left Me and served other gods. So I will not save you again.
Go and cry to the gods you chose. Let them save you when you are in trouble."
