The Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned. Do to us whatever you think is best. But please save us today."
They put away the foreign gods from among them. They served the LORD. He felt sorry for Israel because they were hurting.
The Ammonites were called together and camped in Gilead. The Israelites gathered and camped at Mizpah.
The leaders of Gilead said to each other, "Who will start the fight against the Ammonites? He will be the leader of all who live in Gilead."
Jephthah was a strong fighter from Gilead. His mother was a woman who sold her body. Gilead was his father.
Gilead had other sons by his wife. When they grew up, they sent Jephthah away. They said, "You will not get any of our father's land. You are the son of another woman."
Jephthah ran away from his brothers. He lived in the land of Tob. Bad men came to him. They joined him.
After a while, the Ammonites fought against Israel.
When the Ammonites fought Israel, the leaders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from Tob.
They said to him, "Come and be our leader. Then we will fight the Ammonites."
Jephthah said to the leaders of Gilead, "Didn't you hate me and send me away from my father's house? Why do you come to me now, when you are in trouble?"
The leaders said, "That is why we come back to you now. Come with us and fight the Ammonites. Then you will be the leader of all who live in Gilead."
Jephthah said, "If you bring me back to fight the Ammonites, and the the LORD gives them to me, then I will be your leader."
The leaders said, "The The LORD is listening to what we say. We will do what you say."
So Jephthah went with the leaders of Gilead. The people made him their leader and captain. Jephthah said all these words before the the LORD in Mizpah.
Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites. He said, "What do you have against me? Why are you fighting in my land?"

The king of the Ammonites said to Jephthah's messengers, "Israel took my land when they came up from Egypt. It was from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River and to the Jordan River. Give it back to me in peace."
Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the Ammonites.
He said, "Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
When Israel came up from Egypt, they went through the desert to the Red Sea. Then they came to Kadesh.
Israel asked the king of Edom to let them pass through his land, but he would not listen. Israel also asked the king of Moab, but he would not agree. So Israel stayed at Kadesh."

"Then Israel went through the desert. They went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab. They came from the east to the land of Moab. They camped on the other side of the Arnon River. They did not go into Moab, because the Arnon River was the border of Moab.
Israel asked Sihon, king of the Amorites in Heshbon, to let them pass through his land to their home.
But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his land. He gathered all his people. They camped at Jahaz. Then they fought against Israel."
"The The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into Israel's hands. Israel beat them. Israel took all the land of the Amorites who lived there.
They took all the land of the Amorites from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River. They took it from the desert to the Jordan River.
Now the the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites for His people Israel. Should you take it?"
"Aren't you to take what Chemosh, your god, gives you? We will take what the the LORD our God gives us.
Are you better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever fight against Israel?
Israel has lived in Heshbon and its towns, in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities along the Arnon River for three hundred years. Why didn't you take them back then?
I have not sinned against you. But you are doing wrong to me by fighting me. Let the the LORD judge today between the people of Israel and the people of Ammon."
But the king of the Ammonites did not listen to Jephthah's words.
The Spirit of the the LORD came on Jephthah. He passed through Gilead and Manasseh. He passed through Mizpah in Gilead. From Mizpah he crossed over to the Ammonites.
Jephthah made a promise to the the LORD. He said, "If You give the Ammonites into my hands,
then whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I come home safe from the Ammonites will be the the LORD's. I will give it as a burnt offering."
Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight them. The The LORD gave them into his hands.
He beat them very badly. He took twenty cities from Aroer to Minnith and to Abel-keramim. The Ammonites were beaten by Israel.
Jephthah came to his house in Mizpah. His daughter came out to meet him. She was playing a tambourine and dancing. She was his only child. He had no other son or daughter.
When he saw her, he tore his clothes. He said, "Oh no, my daughter! You have made me very sad. You have brought trouble on me. I made a promise to the the LORD, and I cannot take it back."
She said to him, "My father, you made a promise to the the LORD. Do to me what you said. The The LORD has punished your enemies, the Ammonites, for you.
Let me do this one thing. Leave me alone for two months. Let me go into the hills with my friends. I will cry because I will never marry."
He said, "Go." He sent her away for two months. She and her friends went into the hills and cried because she would never marry.
After two months, she came back to her father. He did what he had promised. She had never been with a man. This became a rule in Israel.
Every year, the young women of Israel went for four days to sing sad songs for the daughter of Jephthah from Gilead.
The men of Ephraim came together. They went north and said to Jephthah, "Why did you go fight the Ammonites and not call us to go with you? We will burn your house down!"
Jephthah said to them, "I and my people had a big fight with the Ammonites. I called you, but you did not save me from them.
I saw that you would not save me. So I risked my life and went to fight the Ammonites. The LORD gave them to me. Why are you coming to fight me today?"

Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead. They fought Ephraim. The Gileadites beat them, because the men of Ephraim had said, "You Gileadites are just runaway Ephraim people living among Ephraim and Manasseh."

The Gileadites took the crossing places of the Jordan River that led to Ephraim. When an Ephraim man who had escaped tried to cross, the Gilead men asked him, "Are you from Ephraim?" If he said no, they told him, "Say 'Shibboleth.'"
He said, "Sibboleth," because he could not say it right. Then they grabbed him and killed him at the Jordan crossing. At that time, 42,000 men from Ephraim died.
Jephthah led Israel for six years. Then he died and was buried in a town in Gilead.
After him, Ibzan from Bethlehem led Israel.
He had 30 sons and 30 daughters. He sent his daughters away to marry, and he brought in 30 young women from outside for his sons. He led Israel for seven years.
Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After him, Elon from Zebulun led Israel. He led Israel for ten years.
Then Elon from Zebulun died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him, Abdon son of Hillel from Pirathon led Israel.
He had 40 sons and 30 grandsons. They rode on 70 donkeys. He led Israel for eight years.
Then Abdon son of Hillel from Pirathon died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, on the hill country of the Amalekites.
The people of Israel did wrong again. The LORD saw it. So He let the Philistines rule them for forty years.
A man named Manoah lived in Zorah. He was from the family of Dan. His wife could not have children.
The angel of the LORD came to the woman. He said, “You cannot have children now, but you will have a baby boy.”
“Be careful. Do not drink wine or beer. Do not eat anything unclean.”
“You are going to have a baby. No one may cut his hair. The boy will be a Nazirite for God from birth. He will begin to save Israel from the Philistines.”
The woman went to her husband. She said, “A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God. He was very frightening. I did not ask where he came from. He did not tell me his name.”
“He told me, ‘You are going to have a baby boy. Do not drink wine or beer. Do not eat anything unclean. The boy will be a Nazirite for God from birth until he dies.’”
Manoah prayed to the LORD. He said, “Please, Lord, send the man of God back to us. Teach us what to do for the boy who will be born.”
God heard Manoah. The angel of God came to the woman again. She was sitting in a field. Her husband was not with her.
The woman ran quickly to her husband. She said, “The man who came to me before has appeared to me again.”
Manoah got up and followed his wife. He came to the man. He said, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” “I am,” the man said.
Manoah said, “When your words come true, what should the boy’s life be like? What should he do?”
The angel of the LORD said to Manoah, “Your wife must be careful to do all I told her.”
“She must not eat anything from a grapevine. She must not drink wine or beer. She must not eat anything unclean. She must obey all I commanded her.”
Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “Please stay with us. We will make a young goat for you.”
The angel of the LORD said to Manoah, “If you keep me here, I will not eat your bread. If you make a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” Manoah did not know he was the angel of the LORD.
Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “What is your name? We want to honor you when your words come true.”
The angel of the LORD said to him, “Why do you ask my name? It is too wonderful to tell.”
Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering. He offered them on a rock to the LORD. The LORD did a wonderful thing while Manoah and his wife watched.
The flame went up from the altar toward heaven. The angel of the LORD went up in the flame. Manoah and his wife saw it. They fell with their faces to the ground.
The angel of the LORD did not appear to Manoah or his wife again. Then Manoah knew he was the angel of the LORD.
Manoah said to his wife, “We will die! We have seen God.”
His wife said to him, “If the LORD wanted to kill us, He would not have accepted our burnt offering and grain offering. He would not have shown us these things. He would not have told us this now.”
The woman had a baby boy. She named him Samson. The boy grew. The LORD blessed him.
The Spirit of the LORD began to move him. This was in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
Samson went down to Timnah. There he saw a young woman. She was from the Philistines who lived in Timnah.
He went back and told his father and mother. He said, "I saw a young woman from the Philistines in Timnah. Get her for me to be my wife."

His father and mother said, "Are there no young women among our own people? Why do you go to the Philistines, who are not God's people, to get a wife?" Samson said to his father, "Get her for me. She is the one I want."
His father and mother did not know this was from the LORD. The LORD was looking for a chance to fight the Philistines. At that time, the Philistines ruled over Israel.
Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. They came to the grape fields near Timnah. A young lion roared at Samson.
The Spirit of the LORD came on Samson with power. He tore the lion apart with his bare hands, like a young goat. He did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
Then Samson went down and talked to the woman. She was the one he wanted.
After some days, Samson went back to get her. On the way, he turned to look at the lion's body. He saw a swarm of bees and honey in it.
He scraped the honey into his hands and ate it. He gave some to his father and mother, and they ate it. He did not tell them the honey came from the lion's body.
Samson's father went down to the woman. Samson gave a big party there. Young men did that in those days.
When the people saw Samson, they brought thirty young men to be his friends.
Samson said to them, "Let me tell you a riddle. If you can solve it in the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen shirts and thirty sets of clothes."
"If you cannot tell me, then you must give me thirty linen shirts and thirty sets of clothes." They said, "Tell us your riddle. We want to hear it."
Samson said, "Out of the eater came food. Out of the strong came something sweet." For three days they could not solve the riddle.
On the seventh day, they said to Samson's wife, "Trick your husband into telling you the answer. If you do not, we will burn you and your father's house. Did you ask us here to rob us?"

Samson's wife cried to him. She said, "You hate me. You do not love me. You gave a riddle to my people, but you did not tell me the answer." He said, "I did not even tell my father and mother. Should I tell you?"
She cried before him for the seven days of the feast. On the seventh day he told her the answer, because she kept asking. Then she told it to her people.

Before the sun went down on the seventh day, the men of the city said to Samson, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" Samson said, "If you had not used my wife to get the answer, you would not have solved my riddle."

The Spirit of the LORD came on Samson with power. He went down to Ashkelon and killed thirty of their men. He took their clothes and gave them to the men who had answered the riddle. He was very angry, and he went back to his father's house.
Samson's wife was given to his friend, the man who had been with him.
Later, when people were picking wheat, Samson took a young goat to visit his wife. He said, "I will go to my wife's room." But her father would not let him go in.
Her father said, "I thought you hated her. So I gave her to your friend. Isn't her younger sister nicer? You can have her instead."
Samson said to them, "This time I can pay them back. I will really hurt them."
Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. He tied them tail to tail in pairs. He tied a torch to each pair.
He lit the torches and let the foxes go in the Philistines' grain fields. He burned the piles of grain, the growing grain, and the grape fields and olive trees.
The Philistines asked, "Who did this?" They were told, "Samson did. He is from Timnah. His wife was given to his friend." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
Samson said to them, "Since you did this, I will not stop until I pay you back."
He fought them hard and killed many of them. Then he went down and stayed in a cave in the rock of Etam.
The Philistines went up and camped in Judah. They spread out near Lehi.
The people of Judah asked, "Why have you come up against us?" The Philistines answered, "We have come to tie up Samson. We want to do to him what he did to us."

Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cave in the rock of Etam. They said to Samson, "Don't you know the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?" Samson answered, "I only did to them what they did to me."
They said to him, "We have come to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines." Samson said, "Promise me you will not kill me yourselves."
They said, "We will only tie you up and hand you over to them. We will not kill you." So they tied him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.
As he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted to meet him. Then the Spirit of the the LORD came on him with power. The ropes on his arms became like burned cloth. The ties fell off his hands.
He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey. He picked it up and hit a thousand men.
Then Samson said, "With a donkey's jawbone I have piled them into heaps. With a donkey's jawbone I have killed a thousand men."
When he finished speaking, he threw the jawbone away. That place was called Ramath Lehi.
He was very thirsty. He called to the the LORD, "You have given Your servant this big win. Now must I die of thirst and fall into the hands of people who do not belong to the the LORD?"
Then God opened the hollow place in Lehi. Water came out. Samson drank, and his strength came back. He lived. So he called the place En Hakkore. It is in Lehi even now.
Samson led Israel for twenty years during the time of the Philistines.
Samson went to Gaza. There he saw a woman who sold herself, and he went in to her.

The people of Gaza heard, "Samson is here!" So they surrounded the city and hid to catch him. They waited all night at the city gate. They were quiet all night and said, "We will kill him when morning comes."

Samson slept until the middle of the night. Then he got up. He took hold of the city gate doors and the two posts. He pulled them up with the bar. He put them on his shoulders and carried them to the top of the hill facing Hebron.
Later, Samson loved a woman in the Valley of Sorek. Her name was Delilah.

The Philistine rulers came to her and said, "Trick him. Find out where his great strength comes from. Find out how we can beat him. Then we can tie him up and hurt him. Each of us will give you 1,100 pieces of silver."
Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me where your great strength comes from. Tell me how someone can tie you up and hurt you."
Samson said to her, "If they tie me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not dried, I will be weak like any other man."
The Philistine rulers brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not dried. She tied him with them.
Men were hiding in the inner room. She said, "Samson, the Philistines are attacking you!" He broke the strings like a thread of flax burns in a fire. No one knew where his strength came from.
Delilah said to Samson, "You tricked me. You lied to me. Now tell me how someone can tie you up."
He said, "If they tie me with new ropes that have never been used, I will be weak like any other man."
Delilah took new ropes and tied him. She said, "Samson, the Philistines are attacking you!" Men were hiding in the inner room. He broke the ropes off his arms like a thread.
Delilah said to Samson, "You have tricked me again. You lied to me. Tell me now how someone can tie you up." He said, "If you weave the seven braids of my hair into the cloth on the loom."
She fastened it with a pin and said, "Samson, the Philistines are attacking you!" He woke up and pulled out the pin, the loom, and the cloth.
She said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have tricked me. You have not told me where your great strength comes from."
She kept asking him every day. She pushed him so hard that he felt like he would die.

So he told her all his heart. He said, "No one has ever cut my hair. I have been set apart for God since I was in my mother's womb. If my head is shaved, my strength will leave me. I will be weak like any other man."

Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart. She sent for the Philistine rulers and said, "Come back this time. He has told me all his heart." The Philistine rulers came to her. They brought the money with them.
She made him sleep on her knees. She called a man. He shaved off the seven braids of Samson's head. She began to hurt him, and his strength left him.
She said, "Samson, the Philistines are attacking you!" He woke up and said, "I will go out like before and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had left him.
The Philistines grabbed him. They took out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza. They tied him with bronze chains. He ground grain in the prison.
But the hair on his head began to grow again.
The Philistine rulers gathered to offer a big sacrifice to their god Dagon. They were happy. They said, "Our god has given our enemy Samson into our hands."
When the people saw him, they praised their god. They said, "Our god has given our enemy into our hands. He destroyed our land. He killed many of us."
When they were happy, they said, "Call Samson so he can make us laugh." They called Samson from the prison. He made them laugh. They stood him between the pillars.
Samson said to the boy who held his hand, "Let me feel the pillars that hold up the house. I want to lean on them."
The house was full of men and women. All the Philistine rulers were there. About 3,000 men and women were on the roof watching Samson make them laugh.
Samson called to the LORD and said, "Lord, the LORD, remember me. Make me strong just this once, O God. Let me get back at the Philistines for my two eyes."
Samson took hold of the two middle pillars that held up the house. He leaned on them. He put one hand on one pillar and the other hand on the other pillar.
Samson said, "Let me die with the Philistines." He pushed with all his strength. The house fell on the rulers and on all the people. More people died when he died than he had killed while he lived.
His brothers and all his father's family came down. They carried him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. He had judged Israel for twenty years.
There was a man named Micah. He lived in the hill country of Ephraim.
He said to his mother, "You had 1,100 pieces of silver taken from you. You cursed about it. You said, 'I have the silver.' But I took it." His mother said, "May the LORD bless my son!"
Micah gave the silver back to his mother. She said, "I set this silver apart for the LORD for my son. It was to make a carved statue and a metal idol. Now I give it back to you."
So Micah gave the silver back to his mother. She took 200 pieces of silver and gave them to a man who worked with silver. He made a carved statue and a metal idol. They were kept in Micah's house.
Micah had a small place to worship. He made an ephod and some household gods. He picked one of his sons to be his priest.
In those days Israel had no king. Everyone did what he thought was right.
There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah. He was a Levite. He was living among the people of Judah.
He left Bethlehem in Judah to find a place to live. He came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim.
Micah asked him, "Where do you come from?" The man said, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah. I am looking for a place to live."
Micah said, "Stay with me. Be like a father to me and be my priest. I will give you ten pieces of silver each year, clothes, and food." So the Levite went with him.
The Levite agreed to stay with the man. The young man became like one of his sons.
Micah made the young Levite his priest. The Levite lived in Micah's house.
Micah said, "Now I know the LORD will be good to me. I have a Levite as my priest."
In those days there was no king in Israel. The tribe of Dan was looking for land to live in. Up to that day, they had not received land among the tribes of Israel.

So the Danites sent five men from their families. They were strong men from Zorah and Eshtaol. They went to spy out the land and look it over. They told them, "Go and explore the land." The men came to the hill country of Ephraim, to Micah's house, and stayed there.
While they were near Micah's house, they heard the young Levite's voice. They turned aside and asked him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing here?"
He said, "Micah did this and that for me. He hired me, and I became his priest."
They said to him, "Please ask God if our trip will succeed."
The priest said, "Go in peace. The LORD is with you on your way."

Then the five men went on. They came to Laish. They saw the people living there safely, like the people of Sidon. They were quiet and safe. No one took their land. They were far from Sidon, and they had no help from anyone.
They came back to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol. Their brothers asked, "What did you see?"
They said, "Get up! Let us go up and attack them. We saw the land, and it is very good. Do not be slow. Go and take the land.
When you get there, you will find a safe people. The land is large. God has given it to you. There is nothing you lack there."
So 600 men from the Dan tribe left Zorah and Eshtaol. They carried weapons.
They went up and camped at Kiriath Jearim in Judah. That is why people call that place Mahaneh Dan even today. It is near Kiriath Jearim.
From there they passed through the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah's house.

The five men who had spied out the land of Laish said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there are a priest's vest, family idols, a carved image, and a metal image? Think about what you should do."
They turned aside and went to the young Levite's house at Micah's place. They greeted him.
The 600 Danite men stood at the gate, wearing their weapons.
The five men went in and took the carved image, the priest's vest, the family idols, and the metal image. The priest stood at the gate with the 600 armed men.
When those men went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the priest's vest, the family idols, and the metal image, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
They said to him, "Be quiet. Come with us. Be a father and priest to us. Is it better to be priest for one man's house, or priest for a whole tribe and family in Israel?"
The priest was glad. He took the priest's vest, the family idols, and the carved image, and went with the people.
They put the children, the animals, and their goods in front. Then they turned and left.
They had gone far from Micah's house. The men who lived near Micah gathered and chased the Danites.
They called out to the Danites. The Danites turned around and said to Micah, "Why are you shouting?"
Micah said, "You took the gods I made and my priest. What do I have left? How can you ask me what is wrong?"
The Danites said to him, "Do not let us hear your voice. Angry men might attack you, and you and your household could die."
Then the Danites went on their way. Micah saw they were too strong for him, so he turned back and went home.
The Danites took what Micah had made and the priest who had been his. They came to Laish, to a quiet and safe people. They killed them with swords and burned the city.
No one came to help them. The city was far from Sidon. They had no ties with anyone. It was in the valley near Beth Rehob. The Danites rebuilt the city and lived there.
They named the city Dan, after their father Dan, who was born to Israel. Before that, the city was called Laish.
The Danites set up the carved image for themselves. Jonathan, son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, and his sons were priests for the Dan tribe until the land was taken into captivity.
They kept Micah's carved image the whole time God's house was at Shiloh.
In those days, Israel had no king. A Levite lived in the far hills of Ephraim. He took a woman to live with him from Bethlehem in Judah.
His woman was not faithful to him. She left him and went to her father's house in Bethlehem in Judah. She stayed there four months.
Her husband went after her to speak kindly to her and bring her back. He had his servant and two donkeys with him. Her father saw him and was glad to meet him.
His father-in-law, the young woman's father, held on to him. He stayed three days. They ate and drank and slept there.
On the fourth day they got up early. He was ready to go. The young woman's father said to his son-in-law, "Eat a piece of bread to give you strength. Then you can go."
So the two men sat and ate and drank. The young woman's father said to the man, "Please stay another night. Let your heart be happy."
The man got up to go, but his father-in-law urged him. So he stayed there.
On the fifth day he got up early to go. The young woman's father said, "Eat something to give you strength. Wait until the day is late." So the two men ate together.

The man got up to go, with his woman and his servant. His father-in-law said, "Look, the day is almost over. Please stay tonight. Look, the day is ending. Stay here and let your heart be happy. Tomorrow get up early and go home."
But the man did not want to stay. He got up and went. He came near Jebus, which is Jerusalem. He had two donkeys with loads on them, and his woman was with him.
The day was very late. The servant said to his master, "Come, let's turn aside to this city of the Jebusites and spend the night there."
His master said, "We will not turn aside into a city of people who are not Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah."
He said to his servant, "Come, let's go near one of these places. We will spend the night in Gibeah or Ramah."
So they went on. The sun set near Gibeah in Benjamin.
They turned aside to spend the night in Gibeah. He sat in the city square. No one took them into a house to spend the night.
An old man was coming from his work in the field at evening. He was from the hills of Ephraim, but he lived in Gibeah. The people of that place were Benjaminites. He saw the traveler in the square.
The old man said, "Where are you going? Where did you come from?"

He said, "We are passing from Bethlehem in Judah to the far side of the hills of Ephraim. I am from there. I went to Bethlehem in Judah, and now I am going to the house of the the LORD. No one has taken me into his house.
We have straw and feed for our donkeys. We have bread and wine for me, your servant, and the young man with us. We do not lack anything."
The old man said, "Peace to you. Let me take care of all your needs. Only do not spend the night in the square."
He brought him to his house. He fed the donkeys. They washed their feet. They ate and drank.

While they were having a good time, some bad men of the city surrounded the house. They beat on the door. They said to the old man, the owner of the house, "Bring out the man who came to your house. We want to know him."
The owner of the house went out to them. He said, "No, my brothers, do not do this evil thing. This man came into my house. Do not do this foolish thing.
Look, here is my unmarried daughter, and his woman. Let me bring them out. You can hurt them and do what you think is good. But do not do this thing to this man."
But the men would not listen. The man took his woman and brought her out to them. They hurt her all night until morning. At dawn they let her go.
As the morning was breaking, the woman came to the door of the man's house where her lord was. She fell down there until it was light.
In the morning her lord got up. He opened the doors of the house. He went out to go on his way. He saw the woman, his woman, fallen at the door. Her hands were on the doorstep.
He said to her, "Get up. Let's go." But she did not answer. He put her on the donkey. The man got up and went to his home.
He came to his house. He took a knife. He took hold of his woman. He cut her into twelve pieces, part by part. He sent her to all the land of Israel.
Everyone who saw it said, "Nothing like this has ever happened or been seen since the people of Israel came up from Egypt until today. Think about it. Talk it over. Speak."
All the Israelites from Dan to Beersheba, and from Gilead too, came out. The whole group gathered as one man before the LORD at Mizpah.
The leaders of all the people stood in God's meeting. There were 400,000 foot soldiers with swords.
The Benjamites heard that Israel had gone up to Mizpah. The Israelites said, "Tell us how this bad thing happened."
The Levite, the husband of the woman who was killed, answered, "I and my second wife came to Gibeah in Benjamin to stay the night.
The men of Gibeah came against me. They surrounded the house. They wanted to kill me. They hurt my second wife, and she died.
I took my second wife, cut her into pieces, and sent the pieces to all parts of Israel. They did a terrible, foolish thing in Israel.
Look, all you Israelites, tell me what to do here."
All the people stood up as one man. They said, "None of us will go home. None of us will go to his house.
Now this is what we will do to Gibeah. We will go against it by drawing lots.

We will take ten men from every hundred, from all the tribes of Israel. We will take a hundred from every thousand, and a thousand from every ten thousand. They will get food for the people. They will go to Geba of Benjamin. They will punish the foolish thing done in Israel."
All the men of Israel came together as one man.
The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin. They said, "What is this bad thing among you?
Hand over the bad men in Gibeah. We will kill them and remove the evil from Israel." But the Benjamites would not listen to their brothers, the Israelites.
The Benjamites gathered from their cities to Gibeah to fight the Israelites.
That day they had 26,000 swordsmen from the cities, plus 700 chosen men from Gibeah.
Among them were 700 left-handed men. Each one could throw a stone at a hair and not miss.
The Israelites, not counting Benjamin, had 400,000 swordsmen. All of them were fighters.
The Israelites went up to Bethel and asked God, "Who should go first to fight Benjamin?" The LORD said, "Judah first."
The Israelites got up in the morning and camped near Gibeah.
The men of Israel went out to fight Benjamin. They lined up against them at Gibeah.
Benjamin came out of Gibeah and killed 22,000 Israelites that day.
The Israelites got stronger and set up for battle again in the same place.
The Israelites went up and cried before the LORD until evening. They asked, "Should we go again to fight our brother Benjamin?" The LORD said, "Go up against him."
The second day the Israelites came near Benjamin.
Benjamin came out from Gibeah and killed 18,000 more Israelites. All of them were swordsmen.
All the Israelites went up to Bethel. They sat and cried before the LORD. They did not eat until evening. They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD.
The Israelites asked the LORD a question. In those days the ark of God's promise was there.

Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, stood before it. He asked, "Should I go out again to fight my brother Benjamin, or should I stop?" The LORD said, "Go up. Tomorrow I will give them into your hand."
The Israelites put hidden men all around Gibeah.
The third day the Israelites went up against Benjamin. They lined up at Gibeah as before.
Benjamin came out to meet them. The Israelites drew them away from the city. Benjamin began to kill Israelites, about 30 men, as before. This happened on the roads to Bethel and Gibeah.
The Benjamites said, "They are running from us as before." The Israelites said, "Let us run and draw them from the city to the roads."
All the Israelites got up from their place and lined up at Baal Tamar. The hidden men of Israel burst out from their place near Geba.
Then 10,000 chosen men from all Israel came opposite Gibeah. The battle was heavy. Benjamin did not know that trouble was near.
The LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel. The Israelites killed 25,100 Benjamites that day. All of them were swordsmen.
Benjamin saw that they were beaten. The Israelites moved back because they trusted the hidden men at Gibeah.
The hidden men hurried and rushed into Gibeah. They spread out and killed the whole city with the sword.
The Israelites and the hidden men had agreed on a signal. They would make a cloud of smoke rise from the city.
The Israelites turned back in the battle. Benjamin had begun to kill about 30 Israelites. They thought, "Surely they are running from us as before."
But the smoke began to rise from the city. Benjamin looked back and saw the whole city going up in smoke to the sky.
The Israelites turned back. Benjamin was afraid because they saw that trouble had come on them.
They ran from Israel toward the desert. But the battle followed them. Men from the cities destroyed them along the way.
They surrounded Benjamin. They chased them without rest and trampled them down east of Gibeah.
They turned and ran to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites killed 5,000 more along the roads. They chased them to Gidom and killed 2,000.
That day 25,000 brave Benjamites who used swords fell.
But 600 men turned and ran to the rock of Rimmon. They stayed there four months.
The Israelites went back to Benjamin. They killed with the sword every living thing in the cities, even the animals. They burned every city they found.
The men of Israel made a promise at Mizpah. They said, "None of us will let our daughters marry the men of Benjamin."
So the people went to Bethel. They sat there before God until evening. They cried loudly and sadly.
They said, "Why, O the LORD, God of Israel, did this happen in Israel? Today one tribe is gone from Israel."
The next day the people got up early. They built an altar there. They gave burnt offerings and peace offerings.
Then the Israelites asked, "Which tribe did not come to the meeting before the LORD?" They had made a big promise. Anyone who did not come to the LORD at Mizpah would be put to death.
The Israelites were sad for their brothers in Benjamin. They said, "Today one tribe is gone from Israel."
They asked, "What will we do for wives for the men who are left? We swore to the LORD that we would not let our daughters marry them."
So they asked, "Which tribe of Israel did not come to the LORD at Mizpah?" They found that no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp for the meeting.
When they counted the people, no one from Jabesh-gilead was there.
So the people sent 12,000 brave men. They told them, "Go and kill the people of Jabesh-gilead with swords. Kill the women and children too.
This is what you must do: Kill every man, and kill every woman who has slept with a man."
They found 400 young women in Jabesh-gilead who had not slept with a man. They brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.
Then the whole group sent a peaceful message to the men of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon.
At that time the men of Benjamin came back. The Israelites gave them the women they had saved from Jabesh-gilead. But there were not enough women for all of them.
The people were sad for Benjamin. The LORD had made a break among the tribes of Israel.
Then the elders of the group said, "What will we do for wives for the men who are left? The women of Benjamin have been destroyed."
They said, "The men left in Benjamin must have their own land, so one tribe is not lost from Israel."
But we cannot give them our daughters as wives. The Israelites had sworn, "Anyone who gives a wife to a man from Benjamin is cursed."
So they said, "Look, every year there is a feast to the LORD in Shiloh. It is north of Bethel, east of the road from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
So they told the men of Benjamin, "Go and wait in the grape fields."

They said, "Watch. When you see the young women of Shiloh come out to dance, each man must come out of the grape fields. Grab a wife for himself from the young women of Shiloh. Then go to the land of Benjamin."
They said, "If their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we will say, 'Be kind to them. We did not take a wife for each man in the war. You did not give them wives, so you are not guilty.'"
So the men of Benjamin did this. They took the number of wives they needed from the women who were dancing. Then they went back to their own land. They rebuilt the cities and lived in them.
At that time the Israelites went home, each to his own tribe and family. They left and went to their own land.
In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what he thought was right.
Long ago, when Israel had judges, there was no food in the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live in the fields of Moab. He went with his wife and his two sons.
The man's name was Elimelech. His wife was Naomi. His sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to Moab and lived there.
Then Elimelech died. Naomi was left with her two sons.
The sons married women from Moab. One was named Orpah, and the other was named Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
Then Mahlon and Chilion died too. Naomi was left without her husband and without her two sons.
In Moab, Naomi heard that the LORD had helped His people. He gave them food. So Naomi and her sons' wives got up to go back from Moab.
Naomi and her two sons' wives left the place where they had been. They started down the road to Judah.
Naomi said to her two sons' wives, "Go back, each of you, to your mother's house. May the LORD be kind to you, as you were kind to the men who died and to me.
May the LORD give you rest in the home of a new husband." Then she kissed them. They cried.
They said, "No, we will go with you to your people."
Naomi said, "Go back, my daughters. Why come with me? Do I have more sons who could be your husbands?
Go back, my daughters. I am too old to have a husband. Even if I had hope, and even if I had a husband tonight and had sons,
would you wait for them to grow up? Would you stay single for them? No, my daughters. It is much harder for me than for you. The LORD has turned against me."
They cried again. Orpah kissed Naomi and left. But Ruth held on to Naomi.
Naomi said, "Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and her gods. Go back with her."
But Ruth said, "Do not make me leave you. Do not make me turn back. Where you go, I will go. Where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people. Your God will be my God.
Where you die, I will die. There I will be buried. May the LORD punish me if anything but death keeps us apart."
Naomi saw that Ruth would not change her mind. So she stopped talking to her.
The two women walked until they came to Bethlehem. When they got there, the whole town was stirred up. The women said, "Is this Naomi?"
Naomi said, "Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara. The Almighty has made my life very bitter.
I went away full, but the LORD brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? The LORD has spoken against me. The Almighty has hurt me."
So Naomi came back from Moab. Her son's wife Ruth, the woman from Moab, came with her. They got to Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest.
Now Naomi had a relative. He was a strong man from Elimelech’s family. His name was Boaz.
Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Let me go to the fields. I will pick up leftover grain. Maybe someone will be kind to me.” Naomi said, “Go, my daughter.”
So Ruth went to the fields. She picked up grain behind the workers. By chance, she came to a field that belonged to Boaz. He was from Elimelech’s family.
Just then Boaz came from Bethlehem. He said to the workers, “The LORD be with you!” The workers said, “The LORD bless you!”
Boaz asked the boss of the workers, “Who is that young woman?”
The boss answered, “She is the Moabite woman who came back with Naomi from Moab.”
She asked, “Please let me pick up grain and tie it into bundles behind the workers.” She has worked since morning. She only rested a little in the house.
Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Do not go to another field to pick grain. Do not leave this field. Stay close to my young women.
Watch the field where they cut grain. Follow them. I told the young men not to bother you. When you are thirsty, go to the water jars. Drink the water the men drew.”
Ruth bowed down to the ground. She said, “Why are you so kind to me? Why do you notice me? I am a foreigner.”
Boaz answered, “I have heard all you did for your mother-in-law after your husband died. You left your father and mother and your home country. You came to a people you did not know.
May the LORD repay you for what you have done. May the LORD, the God of Israel, give you a full reward. You have come to Him for safety under His wings.”
Then Ruth said, “My lord, you have comforted me. You have spoken kindly to me, your servant. I am not even like one of your servant girls.”

At mealtime, Boaz said to her, “Come here. Eat some bread. Dip your piece in the vinegar.” So she sat with the workers. Boaz gave her roasted grain. She ate until she was full. She had some left over.
When Ruth got up to gather grain, Boaz told his workers, “Let her gather even among the bundles. Do not shame her.
Also pull out some grain from the bundles for her. Leave it so she can pick it up. Do not scold her.”
So Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening. Then she beat the grain out of the stalks. She had about a big basket of barley.
She carried it to town. Her mother-in-law saw what she had gathered. Ruth also gave her the food left from her meal.

Her mother-in-law asked, “Where did you gather today? Where did you work? Blessed is the man who noticed you!” Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the man she worked with. She said, “The man I worked with today is named Boaz.”

Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “The LORD bless him! He has not stopped showing kindness to the living and the dead.” Naomi also said, “That man is a close relative of ours. He is one of our family redeemers.”
Then Ruth the Moabite said, “He also told me to stay close to his workers until they finish all his harvest.”
Naomi said to Ruth, “It is good, my daughter, that you go with his young women. Then no one will bother you in another field.”
So Ruth stayed close to Boaz’s young women. She gathered grain until the barley and wheat harvests were done. Then she lived with her mother-in-law.
Naomi said to Ruth, "My daughter, I want to find a safe home for you. I want things to go well for you."
"Boaz is a relative of ours. He is the man whose workers you have been with. Tonight he will clean barley at the grain floor."
"Wash up and put on perfume. Put on your nice clothes. Then go down to the grain floor. But do not let him know you are there until he is done eating and drinking."
"Watch where he lies down. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down. He will tell you what to do."
Ruth said, "I will do everything you say."
So Ruth went down to the grain floor. She did everything Naomi told her to do.
Boaz ate and drank. He felt good. He went to lie down at the end of the grain pile. Ruth came quietly. She uncovered his feet and lay down.
In the middle of the night, the man woke up with a start. He turned over. He saw a woman lying at his feet.
"Who are you?" Boaz asked. "I am your servant Ruth," she said. "Please spread your coat over me. You are a family helper."
"The LORD bless you, my daughter," Boaz said. "This kindness is greater than the first one. You did not run after young men, rich or poor."
"Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you all you ask. All the people in my town know you are a good woman."
"It is true that I am a family helper. But there is another man who is a closer relative than I am."
"Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he wants to help you, good. Let him help you. But if he does not want to, as surely as the the LORD lives, I will help you. Lie here until morning."
So Ruth lay at his feet until morning. She got up before anyone could recognize her. Boaz said, "No one must know that a woman came to the grain floor."
He also said, "Bring me the shawl you are wearing. Hold it out." She held it out. He measured six measures of barley and put them on her. Then he went back to town.
When Ruth came to Naomi, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" Then Ruth told her everything Boaz had done for her.
Ruth said, "He gave me these six measures of barley. He said, 'Do not go back to Naomi with nothing.'"
Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you find out what happens. The man will not rest until this is settled today."
Boaz went up to the city gate and sat down. The family member Boaz had talked about walked by. Boaz said, "Come here and sit down, friend." The man came and sat down.
Boaz asked ten town leaders to sit there too. They sat down.
Boaz said to the family member, "Naomi came back from Moab. She is selling the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

I wanted to tell you about it. Buy it here in front of the people and leaders. If you will buy it back, buy it. If you will not, tell me. I know no one else who can buy it, and I am the next one who can buy it." The man said, "I will buy it."
Boaz said, "When you buy the field from Naomi, you also get Ruth from Moab. She was the wife of the man who died. You must buy her so the dead man's name can stay on his land."
The man said, "I cannot buy it for myself. It might hurt my own land. You buy it back. I cannot."
This is how people in Israel made a land deal sure. A man took off his shoe and gave it to the other man. This showed everyone the deal was true.
So the family member said to Boaz, "Buy it for yourself," and took off his shoe.
Boaz said to the town leaders and all the people, "You are witnesses today. I bought from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.

I also bought Ruth from Moab. She was Mahlon's wife. She will be my wife. This keeps the dead man's name on his land. His name will not be lost among his family or at the city gate. You are witnesses today."
All the people and leaders said, "May the LORD make the woman coming into your house like Rachel and Leah. They built the family of Israel. Do well in Ephrathah. Be well known in Bethlehem.
May your family be like the family of Perez. Tamar had him for Judah. May the LORD give you children through this young woman."
Boaz married Ruth. He slept with her. The LORD gave her a baby, and she had a son.
The women said to Naomi, "Praise the LORD! He has not left you without a family helper today. May his name be well known in Israel.
He will give you new life. He will take care of you when you are old. Your daughter-in-law loves you. She is better to you than seven sons. She has given you this baby."
Naomi took the baby and held him in her arms. She took care of him.
The women living nearby said, "Naomi has a son!" They named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, and Jesse became the father of David.
This is the family line of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron.
Hezron was the father of Ram, and Ram was the father of Amminadab.
Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
Salmon was the father of Boaz, and Boaz was the father of Obed.
Obed was the father of Jesse, and Jesse was the father of David.

There was a man named Elkanah. He lived in Ramathaim-zophim in the hills of Ephraim. He was the son of Jeroham. Jeroham was the son of Elihu. Elihu was the son of Tohu. Tohu was the son of Zuph. Elkanah was from Ephraim.
He had two wives. One was named Hannah. The other was named Peninnah. Peninnah had children. Hannah had none.
Every year, this man went up from his town to Shiloh. He went there to worship and give gifts to the LORD of Hosts. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD there.
On the day he gave his gift, Elkanah gave parts to his wife Peninnah. He gave parts to all her sons and daughters too.
But he gave Hannah two parts. He did this because he loved Hannah. The LORD had kept her from having children.
The LORD had kept Hannah from having children. So Peninnah made fun of her. She bothered her again and again.
This happened every year. When Hannah went to the house of the LORD, Peninnah made her sad. Hannah cried and did not eat.
Her husband Elkanah said to her, "Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
After they ate and drank in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Eli the priest was sitting by the door of the LORD's house.
Hannah was very sad. She prayed to the LORD and cried hard.

She made a promise to God. She said, "O LORD of Hosts, please look at me. I am Your servant. Please remember me. Do not forget me. Give me a son. Then I will give him to the LORD for all his life. No razor will ever touch his head."
Hannah kept praying to the LORD. Eli watched her mouth.
She was praying in her heart. Only her lips moved. No one could hear her voice. So Eli thought she was drunk.
Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!"
"No, my lord," Hannah said. "I am a woman with a sad heart. I have not had wine or strong drink. I have poured out my heart to the LORD.
Do not think I am a bad woman. I have been praying because I am so sad and upset."
Eli said, "Go in peace. May the God of Israel give you what you asked for."
Hannah said, "May I find favor in your eyes." Then she went on her way. She ate. Her face was not sad anymore.
Early the next morning, they got up and worshiped the LORD. Then they went home to Ramah. Elkanah and Hannah were together as husband and wife. The LORD remembered her.
In time, Hannah had a baby boy. She named him Samuel. She said, "I asked the LORD for him."
Elkanah and his whole family went up to Shiloh. They went to give their yearly gift to the LORD. They also kept their promise.
But Hannah did not go. She said to her husband, "After the boy is weaned, I will take him. I will bring him to see the LORD. He will stay there forever."
Her husband Elkanah said, "Do what seems best to you. Stay here until you have weaned him. May the LORD keep His promise." So Hannah stayed. She nursed her son until he was weaned.
When she had weaned him, she took the boy with her. She took three bulls, some flour, and a bottle of wine. She brought him to the LORD's house in Shiloh.
They killed the bull. They brought the boy to Eli.
Hannah said, "Please, my lord, as sure as you live, I am the woman who stood here praying to the LORD.
I prayed for this boy. The LORD gave me what I asked for.
So I am giving him to the LORD. He will belong to the LORD all his life." Then he worshiped the LORD there.
My heart is happy in the the LORD. My power is high in the the LORD. I can brag over my enemies, because I am glad for Your help.
No one is holy like the the LORD. No one is like You. No one is as strong as our God.
Don't talk so proud. Don't let proud words come from your mouth. The LORD knows everything, and He checks what people do.
Strong men's bows break. People who fall get strong again.
People who had food now work for bread. Hungry people are full now. The woman with no children has seven. The woman with many children is weak.
The LORD can make people die or live. He sends people down to the grave and brings them up.
The LORD makes people poor or rich. He brings people down and lifts them up.
He lifts poor people from the dust. He lifts needy people from the trash heap to sit with leaders. He gives them a place of honor. The LORD holds up the earth.
He keeps His loyal people from falling. Wicked people are quiet in the dark. No one wins by strength alone.
People who fight the the LORD will break apart. He will thunder from heaven against them. The LORD will judge the whole earth. He will give strength to His king and make His chosen leader strong.
Elkanah went home to Ramah. The boy served the the LORD in front of Eli the priest.
Eli's sons were bad men. They did not know the the LORD.
This was the priests' rule for the people. When a man brought a sacrifice, the priest's helper came with a fork that had three points. He put it into the meat while it boiled.
He stuck it into the pot, the kettle, the pan, or the pot. The priest took all the meat the fork brought up. They did this to all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.
Even before the fat was burned, the priest's helper came. He said to the man who was giving the offering, "Give meat to the priest to roast. He will not take boiled meat from you. He wants raw meat."
The man said, "Let them burn the fat first. Then take what you want." But the helper said, "No. Give it now. If you do not, I will take it by force."
The young men's sin was very bad before the the LORD. They treated the the LORD's offering with no respect.
Samuel served before the the LORD. He was a boy wearing a linen vest.
Each year his mother made him a little coat. She brought it when her husband went to give the yearly sacrifice.
Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife. He said, "May the the LORD give you children from this woman. She gave one child to the the LORD." Then they went home.
The LORD cared for Hannah. She had three more sons and two daughters. Samuel grew up with the the LORD.
Eli was very old. He heard all that his sons did to Israel. He heard that they slept with the women who served at the tent of meeting.
He said to them, "Why do you do these things? I hear about your bad deeds from all the people.
No, my sons. The news I hear is not good. You make the the LORD's people sin.

If one person sins against another, God can help. But if a person sins against the the LORD, who can pray for him?" But they would not listen to their father. The LORD had decided to put them to death.
Samuel kept growing. He was liked by the the LORD and by people.
A man of God came to Eli and said, "This is what the the LORD says: 'Did I not clearly show Myself to your father's house when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh?

I chose your father's family from all the tribes of Israel to be My priests. They were to go up to My altar, burn incense, and wear the special vest before Me. I gave your father's family all the fire gifts from Israel.
Why do you look down on My sacrifice and offering that I set for My home? Why do you honor your sons more than Me? You get fat from the best parts of My people's offerings.

So the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "I did say your family and your father's family would serve Me forever." But now the the LORD says: "No! I will honor those who honor Me. I will not honor those who disrespect Me."
Look, days are coming when I will take away your strength and your father's strength. No old man will be left in your family.
You will see trouble in My home while good is done for Israel. There will never be an old man in your family.
But I will not take every man from your family away from My altar. Still, your eyes will grow weak, and your heart will hurt. All your family's young men will die in their best years.
This will be the sign to you. It will come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. Both will die on the same day.
I will choose a faithful priest for Myself. He will do what is in My heart and mind. I will build him a lasting family. He will serve before My chosen king forever.
Then everyone left in your family will come and bow to him. They will ask for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread. They will say, "Please give me a priest's job so I can eat bread."'"
Samuel was a young helper of the the LORD. He served the the LORD near Eli. Back then, the the LORD's word was rare. People did not have many visions.
One day, Eli's eyes were weak. He could not see well. He was lying in his room.
Before God's lamp went out, Samuel was lying in the the LORD's house. The ark of God was there.
Then the the LORD called Samuel. Samuel said, “Here I am.”
Samuel ran to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “You called me.” “I did not call you,” Eli said. “Go back and lie down.” So Samuel went back and lay down.
The the LORD called again, “Samuel!” Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “You called me.” “My son, I did not call you,” Eli said. “Go back and lie down.”
Samuel did not know the the LORD yet. The the LORD had not shown him His word.
The the LORD called Samuel a third time. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “You called me.” Then Eli knew the the LORD was calling the boy.
Eli said to Samuel, “Go and lie down. If He calls you, say, ‘Speak, the LORD, for Your servant is listening.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
The the LORD came and stood there. He called as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” Samuel said, “Speak, for Your servant is listening.”
The the LORD said to Samuel, “Look, I am about to do something in Israel. It will make both ears of everyone who hears it ring.
“On that day, I will do to Eli's family all that I said about his house. I will start it and finish it.
“I told him I would judge his family forever. He knew his sons were speaking against God, but he did not stop them.
“So I swore to Eli's family that their wrong will never be forgiven by sacrifices or offerings.”
Samuel lay until morning. Then he opened the doors of the the LORD's house. Samuel was afraid to tell Eli what he had seen.
Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son.” Samuel said, “Here I am.”
Eli said, “What did He say to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do to you and more if you hide any word from me that He said to you.”
So Samuel told him everything. He did not hide anything. Eli said, “He is the the LORD. Let Him do what seems good to Him.”
Samuel grew up. The the LORD was with him. None of his words failed.
All Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was a true prophet of the the LORD.
The the LORD kept showing Himself to Samuel at Shiloh, because the the LORD spoke to Samuel there.
Samuel's words came to all Israel. The Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They camped at Ebenezer. The Philistines camped at Aphek.
The Philistines lined up to fight Israel. Israel lost and ran away. The Philistines killed about four thousand men in the field.

When the people came back to camp, the leaders of Israel said, "Why did the the LORD let us lose today to the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the the LORD's promise from Shiloh. It can be with us and save us from our enemies."

So the people sent men to Shiloh. They brought back the ark of the promise of the the LORD of heaven's armies. He sits between the angels. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of God.
When the ark of the the LORD's promise came into camp, all Israel shouted so loud that the ground shook.
The Philistines heard the shout. They asked, "What is this loud shout in the Hebrew camp?" Then they learned that the ark of the the LORD had come into camp.
The Philistines were afraid. They said, "God has come into camp! Oh no! This has never happened before.
Oh no! Who will save us from these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the desert.
Be strong and act like men, Philistines! Do not let the Hebrews rule you as you ruled them. Be men and fight!"
The Philistines fought. Israel lost again. Every man ran home. The loss was very great. Thirty thousand soldiers from Israel fell.
The ark of God was taken. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
A man from Benjamin ran from the battle line. He came to Shiloh that same day. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head.
When he came, Eli was sitting on a seat by the road. He was watching, because his heart was afraid for the ark of God. The man came into the city to tell the news. The whole city cried out.
Eli heard the cry and asked, "What is this noise?" The man hurried and told Eli.
Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes were weak, and he could not see.
The man said to Eli, "I am the one who came from the battle. I ran from the battle today." Eli asked, "What happened, my son?"
The messenger said, "Israel ran from the Philistines. Many people died. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead. The ark of God has been taken."
When the man spoke about the ark of God, Eli fell backward off his chair by the gate. His neck broke, and he died. He was old and heavy. He had led Israel for forty years.

His daughter-in-law, Phinehas's wife, was about to have a baby. When she heard that the ark of God was taken and that her father-in-law and husband were dead, she knelt down and gave birth. Her pain came fast.
As she was dying, the women beside her said, "Do not be afraid. You have a son." But she did not answer. She did not pay attention.
She named the baby Ichabod. She said, "Glory has left Israel," because the ark of God was taken and because of her father-in-law and husband.
She said, "Glory has left Israel, for the ark of God has been taken."
The Philistines took God's ark. They carried it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
They brought the ark into Dagon's temple. They set it next to Dagon.
The people of Ashdod got up early the next day. They saw Dagon lying face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD. They picked up Dagon and put him back in his place.

The next morning, they got up early again. They saw Dagon lying face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD. Dagon's head and both hands were broken off at the doorstep. Only his body was left.
That is why Dagon's priests and everyone who comes into Dagon's house in Ashdod still do not step on Dagon's doorstep to this day.
The the LORD's hand was heavy on the people of Ashdod. He ruined them. He struck them with painful lumps. This happened to Ashdod and the land around it.
When the men of Ashdod saw this, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay with us. His hand is too hard on us and on our god Dagon."
They sent for all the Philistine rulers. They asked, "What should we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" The rulers said, "Move the ark of the God of Israel to Gath." So they moved it there.
After they moved it, the the LORD's hand was against that city. There was a great fear. He struck the men of the city, young and old. Painful lumps broke out on them.
They sent the ark of God to Ekron. When it got there, the people of Ekron cried out, "They brought the ark of the God of Israel here to kill us and our people!"

They gathered all the Philistine rulers. They said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel. Let it go back to its place. It must not kill us and our people." Death and fear filled the whole city. God's hand was very heavy there.
The men who did not die were struck with painful lumps. The cry of the city went up to heaven.
The ark of the LORD had been in the land of the Philistines for seven months.
The Philistines called their priests and people who tell the future. They said, "What should we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how to send it back home."
They said, "If you send back the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it empty. Send a gift to show you are sorry. Then you will get better. You will know why God has not stopped punishing you."
The Philistines asked, "What gift should we send?" They said, "Make five gold sores and five gold rats. Make one for each Philistine leader. The same sickness hit you and your leaders.
Make models of your sores and models of your rats that are ruining the land. Give honor to the God of Israel. Maybe He will stop punishing you, your gods, and your land.
Why should you be stubborn like the Egyptians and Pharaoh? God punished them. Then they let the people go."
"Now get a new cart. Hitch two mother cows that have never pulled a load. Tie the cows to the cart. Take their calves away and keep them in a pen.
Put the ark of the LORD on the cart. Put the gold things you send back to God as a sorry gift in a box beside it. Then let it go.
Watch. If it goes up the road to Beth-shemesh, then God did this bad thing to us. If not, then we will know God did not hurt us. It was just chance."
So the men did it. They took two mother cows, hitched them to the cart, and kept the calves in a pen.
They put the ark of the LORD on the cart. They also put the box with the gold rats and models of their sores on it.
The cows went straight toward Beth-shemesh. They stayed on the road and mooed as they walked. They did not turn right or left. The Philistine leaders followed them to the edge of Beth-shemesh.
People in Beth-shemesh were gathering wheat in the valley. They looked up and saw the ark. They were glad to see it.
The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh. It stopped by a big rock. The men split the wood of the cart and burned the cows as a gift to the LORD.
The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box with the gold things. They put them on the big rock. That day the men of Beth-shemesh burned gifts and made sacrifices to the LORD.
The five Philistine leaders saw this. They went back to Ekron that same day.
These are the gold sores the Philistines sent back to the LORD as a sorry gift: one each for Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.

The number of gold rats matched the number of Philistine cities of the five leaders. It included strong cities and country towns. The big rock where they put the ark of the LORD is still there today in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.

But God struck down some men of Beth-shemesh because they looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck down seventy men and fifty thousand men. The people were sad because the LORD had hit them with a big blow.
The men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who can stand before the LORD, this holy God? Where should the ark go from here?"
So they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim. They said, "The Philistines have sent back the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it to your home."
The men of Kiriath-jearim came and took the ark of the the LORD. They brought it to Abinadab's house on the hill. They set apart his son Eleazar to watch over the ark of the the LORD.
The ark stayed in Kiriath-jearim for a long time—twenty years. All the people of Israel were sad and wanted the the LORD.

Then Samuel said to all Israel, "If you want to come back to the the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtoreth statues from among you. Get your hearts ready for the the LORD. Serve Him only. Then He will save you from the Philistines."
So the Israelites put away the Baals and the Ashtoreths. They served the the LORD only.
Then Samuel said, "Gather all Israel at Mizpah. I will pray to the the LORD for you."
They gathered at Mizpah. They drew water and poured it out before the the LORD. That day they did not eat. They said, "We have sinned against the the LORD." Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
The Philistines heard that Israel had gathered at Mizpah. The Philistine leaders went up to fight Israel. The Israelites heard about it and were afraid.
The Israelites said to Samuel, "Do not stop praying to the the LORD our God for us. Ask Him to save us from the Philistines."
Samuel took a baby lamb and burned it all as an offering to the the LORD. He prayed to the the LORD for Israel. The the LORD answered him.

While Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the Philistines came near to fight Israel. But that day the the LORD thundered with a loud voice against the Philistines. He confused them. They were beaten by Israel.
The men of Israel marched out of Mizpah. They chased the Philistines. They beat them all the way to a place below Beth-car.
Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer. He said, "So far the the LORD has helped us."
The Philistines were beaten down. They did not come into Israel's land again. The the LORD worked against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
The cities the Philistines had taken from Israel, from Ekron to Gath, were given back. Israel took their land back from the Philistines. There was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
Samuel judged Israel all his life.
Every year he traveled from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah. He judged Israel in all these places.
Then he went back to Ramah. His home was there. He judged Israel there. He built an altar to the the LORD there.
When Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
His first son was Joel, and his second son was Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
But his sons did not follow his ways. They chased money. They took bribes. They did not judge fairly.
All the leaders of Israel came together. They came to Samuel at Ramah.
They said to him, "You are old. Your sons do not live the way you do. Now give us a king to judge us, like all the other nations."
But Samuel did not like it when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." So Samuel prayed to the LORD.
The LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to the people in all they say to you. They have not turned away from you. They have turned away from Me. They do not want Me to be their king.
They have done this since the day I brought them out of Egypt. They left Me and served other gods. Now they are doing the same thing to you.
Listen to them. But warn them. Tell them what a king will do to them."
Samuel told all the LORD's words to the people who asked for a king.
He said, "This is what a king will do to you. He will take your sons and put them in his chariots and make them his horsemen. They will run in front of his chariots.
He will make some of them leaders of thousands and leaders of fifties. He will make them plow his fields and cut his grain. He will make them build his weapons and his chariots.
He will take your daughters to make perfume, cook food, and bake bread.
He will take your best fields, vineyards, and olive trees. He will give them to his servants.
He will take one tenth of your grain and your vineyards. He will give it to his officers and servants.
He will take your servants, your best young men, and your donkeys. He will put them to work for him.
He will take one tenth of your sheep. You will be his servants.
On that day, you will cry out because of the king you chose. But the LORD will not answer you then."
But the people would not listen to Samuel. They said, "No. We want a king over us.
We want to be like all the other nations. We want a king to judge us, to go out before us, and to fight our battles."
Samuel heard all the people's words. He told them to the LORD.
The LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to them. Make them a king." Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go home, each of you to your own city."

There was a man named Kish. He was a strong man from the family of Benjamin. Kish was the son of Abiel. Abiel was the son of Zeror. Zeror was the son of Becorath. Becorath was the son of Aphiah. They were Benjamites.
Kish had a son named Saul. Saul was young and handsome. No one in Israel was better looking than he was. He was taller than everyone else.
Some donkeys that belonged to Kish were lost. Kish said to Saul, "Take one helper and go look for the donkeys."
Saul and his helper went through the hill country of Ephraim. They went through Shalishah. They went through Shaalim. They went through the land of Benjamin. They could not find the donkeys.
When they came to Zuph, Saul said to his helper, "Let's go home. my father may stop worrying about the donkeys. He may start worrying about us."
The helper said, "Look, there is a man of God in this town. He is an important man. Everything he says comes true. Let's go there. Maybe he can tell us which way to go."
Saul said to his helper, "If we go, what will we bring the man? We have no bread left. We have no gift for the man of God. What do we have?"
The helper answered, "I have a little silver. I can give it to the man of God. He can tell us which way to go."
In the past, people in Israel called a prophet a seer. When they wanted to ask God something, they said, "Let's go to the seer."
Saul said, "That is a good idea. Let's go." So they went to the town where the man of God was.
As they went up the hill to the town, they met some young women. The women were getting water. Saul and his helper asked, "Is the seer here?"
The women said, "Yes, he is. He is right here. Hurry, because he came to town today. The people have a sacrifice at the high place."

They said, "As soon as you go into the town, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes. He blesses the sacrifice first. Then the invited guests eat. Go now. You will find him at this time of day."
They went up to the town. As they came into the middle of the town, Samuel came out. He was going to meet them. He was going up to the high place.
The day before Saul came, the LORD told Samuel,
"Tomorrow at this time I will send you a man from Benjamin. Anoint him as leader over My people Israel. He will save My people from the Philistines. I have seen My people. Their cry has come to Me."
When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD said, "Look, this is the man I told you about. He will rule over My people."
Saul went up to Samuel at the gate. He said, "Please tell me where the seer's house is."
Samuel said, "I am the seer. Go up to the high place ahead of me. Eat with me today. In the morning I will send you on your way. I will tell you everything in your heart.
Do not worry about the donkeys you lost three days ago. They have been found. Also, who is all Israel looking for? Is it not you and your father's family?"
Saul answered, "I am from the smallest tribe in Israel, Benjamin. my family is the least important family in Benjamin. Why are you talking to me like this?"
Samuel took Saul and his helper. He brought them into the big room. He gave them the best seats with the invited guests. There were about thirty men.
Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the special portion I gave you to keep."

The cook brought the thigh and what was on it. He set it in front of Saul. Samuel said, "Look, this is the part saved for you. Eat it. It was kept for you for this special time. I invited the people." So Saul ate with Samuel that day.
They went down from the high place to the town. Samuel talked with Saul on the roof.
They got up early. At dawn, Samuel called Saul on the roof. He said, "Get up. I will send you away." Saul got up. Both of them went outside.
As they went down to the edge of the town, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell your helper to go ahead of us. You stand here today, so I can tell you God's word." The helper went on ahead.
Samuel took a jar of oil and poured it on Saul's head. He kissed him. Then he said, "The LORD has chosen you to lead His people.

When you leave me today, you will meet two men near Rachel's grave, at Zelzah in Benjamin. They will tell you the donkeys you went to find are found. They will say your father stopped worrying about them. Now he worries about you. He asks what he should do about his son.

Go on from there. You will come to the oak tree at Tabor. There you will meet three men going up to God at Bethel. One will carry three young goats. One will carry three loaves of bread. One will carry a jar of wine.
They will say hello to you. They will give you two loaves of bread. Take the bread from them.

After that, go to Gibeah, where God is worshiped. A Philistine camp is there. When you go into the town, you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the hill. They will have harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres. They will be speaking for God.
The Spirit of the LORD will come on you in a strong way. You will speak for God with them. You will become like a new person.
When these things happen, do what you need to do. God is with you.
Go down ahead of me to Gilgal. I will come down to you. I will give offerings to God. Wait seven days until I come to you. Then I will tell you what to do.
As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed his heart. All these signs happened that day.
When Saul and his helper came to Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God came on him in a strong way. He spoke for God with them.
People who knew Saul before saw him speaking for God with the prophets. They said to each other, "What has happened to Kish's son? Is Saul a prophet too?"
A man who lived there said, "Who is the father of these prophets?" So people began to say, "Is Saul a prophet too?"
When Saul finished speaking for God, he went up to the hill.
Saul's uncle asked him and his helper, "Where have you been?" Saul said, "We went to look for the donkeys. But we did not find them. So we went to see Samuel."
His uncle said, "Tell me, what did Samuel say to you?"
Saul said, "He told us the donkeys were found." But Saul did not tell his uncle what Samuel said about being king.
Then Samuel called all the people to come to the LORD at Mizpah.
He said to the people of Israel, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you out of Egypt. I saved you from the Egyptians and from all the kings who hurt you."

"But today you turned away from your God. He saves you from all your troubles. You told Him you did not want Him. You asked for a king to rule you. Now stand before the LORD by your tribes and your family groups."
So Samuel brought all the tribes near. The tribe of Benjamin was chosen.
