The sea's deep places showed. The world's base was seen. This happened when the LORD spoke strongly and blew with angry breath.
"He reached down from high up and took me. He pulled me out of deep water.
He saved me from my strong enemy and from enemies too strong for me.
They came at me on my bad day, but the LORD held me up.
He brought me to a wide open place. He saved me because He was pleased with me.
"The LORD paid me back for doing right. He gave me what my clean hands earned.
I followed the ways of the LORD. I did not do wrong against my God.
All His rules were in front of me. I did not ignore His laws.
I was without blame before Him. I kept myself from sin.
So the LORD paid me back for doing right, for being clean before His eyes.
"To the faithful, You are faithful. To the one without blame, You are without blame.
To the pure, You are pure. To the crooked, You are clever.
You save people who are hurting, but You bring down proud people.
"For You are my lamp, the LORD. You make my darkness bright.
With You I can run through an army. With my God I can jump over a wall.
God's way is perfect. The word of the LORD is pure. He is a shield to all who hide in Him.
Who is God besides the LORD? Who is a rock except our God?
God is my strong fort. He makes my way clear.
He makes my feet like a deer's feet. He sets me on high places.
He trains my hands for war. My arms can bend a bronze bow.
You gave me Your saving shield. Your right hand holds me up. Your kindness lifts me high.
You make a wide path for me, so my feet do not slip.
"I chased my enemies and destroyed them. I did not turn back until they were gone.
I crushed them. They could not get up. They fell under my feet.
You gave me strength for the fight. You made my enemies fall under me.
You made my enemies turn and run. I destroyed those who hated me.
They looked, but no one saved them. They called to the LORD, but He did not answer them.
I ground them like dust. I crushed and stomped them like mud in the streets.
"You saved me from my people's fights. You kept me as head of nations. People I did not know serve me.
People from other lands give in to me. When they hear me, they obey me.
People from other lands lose courage. They come shaking out of their strong places.
"The LORD lives! Praise my Rock! May the God who saves me be lifted high!
He is the God who pays back my enemies and brings nations under me.
He brings me out from my enemies. You lift me above my enemies. You save me from violent men.
So I will praise You, the LORD, among the nations. I will sing to Your name.
He gives great saving to His king. He shows kindness to His chosen one, to David and his family forever."
These are David's last words. David, son of Jesse, said this. He was the man God lifted up. He was chosen by the God of Jacob. He wrote songs for Israel.
The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me. His word was on my tongue.
The God of Israel spoke. The Rock of Israel said to me, "A good leader rules people fairly and shows respect for God.
He shines like the morning sun. He is like rain that makes the grass grow."
My family is not perfect with God. But God made a promise to me. It lasts forever. It is safe and sure. He will give me help and everything I hope for.
But bad men are like thorns. They are thrown away. No one can pick them up with bare hands.
A man who touches them needs iron or wood. They are burned in the fire.
These are the names of David's mighty men. Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahkemonite was the leader of the Three. He killed eight hundred men in one battle.
Next was Eleazar son of Dodo, the Ahohite. He was one of the three brave men with David. The men of Israel ran away when the Philistines came to fight. But Eleazar stood and fought.
He fought the Philistines until his hand was so tired he could not let go of his sword. The LORD gave a great victory that day. The people came back only to take things from the dead.
Next was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered at a field full of lentils. The people ran away from the Philistines.
But Shammah stood in the middle of the field and saved it. He struck down the Philistines. The LORD gave a great victory.
At harvest time, three of the thirty leaders went down to David at the cave of Adullam. A Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was in a safe place. Philistine soldiers were in Bethlehem then.
David wanted water. He said, "I wish I could drink water from the well by the gate in Bethlehem!"
The three brave men broke through the Philistine camp. They drew water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem. They brought it to David. But David would not drink it. He poured it out to the LORD.
David said, "The LORD, I would never drink this! It is like the blood of men who risked their lives." So David did not drink it. These three brave men did this.
Abishai, Joab's brother and son of Zeruiah, was the leader of the Three. He swung his spear at three hundred men and killed them. He was famous among the Three.
He was the most honored of the Three. So he became their leader. But he was not one of the first Three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was from Kabzeel. He did many brave things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
He killed a big Egyptian man. The Egyptian had a spear. Benaiah went down to him with a stick. He took the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with it.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada did these things. He was famous among the three brave men.
He was more honored than the thirty. But he did not reach the first Three. David made him leader of his guards.
Asahel, Joab's brother, was one of the thirty. Elhanan son of Dodo was from Bethlehem.
Shammah the Harodite and Elika the Harodite.
Helez the Paltite and Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa.
Abiezer from Anathoth and Mebunnai the Hushathite.
Zalmon the Ahohite and Maharai the Netophathite.
Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite and Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin.
Benaiah the Pirathonite and Hiddai from the valleys of Gaash.
Abi-albon the Arbathite and Azmaveth the Barhumite.
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, and Jonathan.
Shammah the Hararite and Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite.
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite and Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite.
Hezro the Carmelite and Paarai the Arbite.
Igal son of Nathan from Zobah and Bani the Gadite.
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, and the men who carried weapons for Joab son of Zeruiah.
Ira the Ithrite and Gareb the Ithrite.
Uriah the Hittite was also one of them. There were thirty-seven in all.
The LORD was angry with Israel again. He caused David to count the people of Israel and Judah.
The king said to Joab, the army leader, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. Count the people so I will know how many there are."
Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God make the people a hundred times more. May my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do this?"
The king's word won over Joab and the army leaders. So Joab and the leaders left the king and went to count the people of Israel.
They crossed the Jordan River. They camped near Aroer, south of the city in the middle of the valley of Gad, toward Jazer.
Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi. Then they went to Dan and around to Sidon.
Then they went to the strong city of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Then they went out to the south of Judah at Beersheba.
After nine months and twenty days, they came back to Jerusalem.
Joab told the king how many people there were. Israel had eight hundred thousand brave men who used swords. Judah had five hundred thousand men.
After that, David felt bad in his heart. He said to the LORD, "I have sinned a lot by doing this. Now, LORD, please take away my sin. I have acted foolishly."
The next morning, the LORD spoke to Gad the prophet.
He said, "Go tell David, 'The LORD says: I am giving you three choices. Pick one, and I will do it to you.'"

Gad went to David and told him. He said, "Should seven years of hunger come to your land? Or should you run for three months while your enemies chase you? Or should three days of sickness come to your land? Now think and choose what answer I should take back to the One who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in big trouble. Let us fall into the LORD's hands, because He is very kind. But do not let me fall into people's hands."
So the LORD sent sickness on Israel from morning until the set time. Seventy thousand men died from Dan to Beersheba.

When the angel reached out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD felt sorry and stopped the trouble. He said to the angel who was hurting the people, "Stop! Put your hand down." The angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
When David saw the angel hurting the people, he said to the LORD, "I am the one who sinned. I did wrong. These sheep, what did they do? Please let Your hand be against me and my family."
That day Gad came to David and said, "Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
David went up, just as Gad had said, as the LORD had told him.
Araunah looked and saw the king and his servants coming. He went out and bowed with his face to the ground before the king.
Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so the sickness will stop hurting the people."
Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take what he likes and offer it. Here are oxen for the offering. Here are the sledges and yokes for wood."
Araunah gave all of it to the king. Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD your God be pleased with you."

The king said to Araunah, "No, I will buy it from you for a price. I will not give the LORD my God an offering that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty pieces of silver.
David built an altar there to the LORD. He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. The LORD answered the prayer for the land, and the sickness stopped hurting Israel.
King David was very old. His servants covered him with blankets, but he could not get warm.
His servants said to him, "Let us find a young woman who has never married. She can stand before you, our king, and take care of you. She can lie beside you and keep you warm."
They looked all over Israel for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag from Shunem and brought her to the king.
The young woman was very beautiful. She took care of the king and served him, but the king did not sleep with her.
Adonijah son of Haggith made himself important. He said, "I will be king." He got chariots and horsemen, and fifty men ran ahead of him.
His father never told him no. He never asked, "Why did you do that?" Adonijah was very handsome, and he was born after Absalom.
He talked with Joab son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest, and they helped him.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's mighty men were not with Adonijah.
Adonijah killed sheep, cows, and fat calves. He did this near the stone of Zoheleth by En Rogel. He invited all the king's sons and all the men of Judah who served the king.
But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.
Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has made himself king? Our lord David does not know it.
Now let me give you some advice. It can save your life and your son Solomon's life.
Go to King David and tell him that he promised you your son Solomon would be king after him and sit on his throne. Ask him why Adonijah has become king.
While you are still there talking with the king, I will come in after you. I will say the same things you said."
Bathsheba went to the king in his room. The king was very old, and Abishag from Shunem was serving him.
Bathsheba bowed down to the king. The king said, "What do you want?"
She said, "My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to me that my son Solomon would be king after you and sit on your throne.
But now Adonijah has made himself king. My lord the king, you do not know it.
He killed many cows and fat calves and sheep. He invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the army leader. But he did not invite your servant Solomon.
My lord the king, all Israel is watching you. They want to know who will sit on your throne after you.
If you do not tell them, then when you die, I and my son Solomon will be treated like we did wrong."
While she was still talking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
They told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." He came in and bowed with his face to the ground.
Nathan said, "My lord the king, did you say Adonijah would be king after you and sit on your throne?

Today he went down and killed many cows and fat calves and sheep. He invited all the king's sons, the army leaders, and Abiathar the priest. Now they are eating and drinking with him and shouting for King Adonijah.
But he did not invite me, your servant, or Zadok the priest, or Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.
Did my lord the king do this? You did not tell your servants who would sit on your throne after you."
King David answered, "Call Bathsheba to me." She came and stood before the king.
The king made a promise. He said, "As the LORD lives, Who saved my life from all trouble,
just as I promised you by the LORD, the God of Israel, that your son Solomon would be king after me and sit on my throne in my place, I will do it today."
Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground. She honored the king and said, "May my lord King David live forever."
King David said, "Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." They came to the king.
The king said to them, "Take my servants with you. Put my son Solomon on my own mule. Take him down to Gihon.
There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet will pour oil on him and make him king over Israel. Blow the trumpet and say that King Solomon should live long.
Then come back up with him. He will come and sit on my throne. He will be king in my place. I have chosen him to lead Israel and Judah."
Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so too.
As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon. May He make Solomon's throne greater than my lord the king's throne."
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down. They put Solomon on King David's mule and took him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent. He poured it on Solomon. Then they blew the trumpet. All the people said, "Long live King Solomon!"
All the people went up after him. They played flutes and were very happy. The noise was so loud that the ground shook.
Adonijah and all his guests heard it as they finished eating. When Joab heard the trumpet, he said, "Why is the city so noisy?"
While Joab was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came. Adonijah said, "Come in. You are a brave man. You bring good news."
Jonathan answered, "No! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
The king sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites. They put Solomon on the king's mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet poured oil on him at Gihon. They came back up happy. The whole city is excited. That is the noise you heard.
Solomon now sits on the royal throne.

The king's servants came to bless our lord King David. They said that the king's God should make Solomon's name greater than the king's name, and make his throne greater than the king's throne. Then the king bowed on his bed.
The king also blessed the LORD, the God of Israel. He said that today God has given someone to sit on his throne, and his eyes have seen it."
All of Adonijah's guests were afraid. They got up and went home.
Adonijah was afraid of Solomon. He got up and went to the altar. He grabbed the horns of the altar.
Someone told Solomon, "Adonijah is afraid of you, King Solomon. He has grabbed the horns of the altar. He asks you not to kill him with a sword."
Solomon said, "If he is a good man, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground. But if he does wrong, he will die."
King Solomon sent men. They brought Adonijah down from the altar. He came and bowed to King Solomon. Solomon said to him, "Go home."
When David was close to death, he told his son Solomon what to do.
"I am going to die, like everyone does. So be strong. Be a man.

Keep what the LORD your God asks you to do. Walk in His ways. Keep His rules, His commands, His laws, and His teachings. They are written in the Law of Moses. Then you will do well in all you do, wherever you go.

Then the LORD will keep His promise to me. He said, 'If your sons walk in truth before Me with all their heart and all their soul, then you will always have someone from your family on Israel's throne.'

You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me. He killed Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. They were the leaders of Israel's armies. He killed them when there was peace. Their blood stained the belt around his waist and the sandals on his feet.
So use your wisdom. Do not let him die peacefully in old age.
But be kind to the sons of Barzillai from Gilead. Let them eat with you. They helped me when I ran from your brother Absalom.

Watch Shimei son of Gera. He is from Benjamin and lives in Bahurim. He said awful things about me when I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Jordan River. I promised him by the LORD, 'I will not kill you with a sword.'
So do not let him go free. You are a wise man, and you will know what to do to him. Make sure he is killed."
Then David died. He was buried in the City of David.
David ruled Israel for forty years. He ruled seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
Solomon sat on his father David's throne. His kingdom was strong.
Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She asked, "Do you come in peace?" "Yes, in peace," he said.
"I have something to say to you." "Speak," she said.
"You know the kingdom was mine. All Israel wanted me to be king. But the kingdom went to my brother. The LORD gave it to him."
"Now I have one request. Please do not say no." "Speak," she said.
"Please ask King Solomon to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife. He will not say no to you."
"Very well. I will speak to the king for you."

Bathsheba went to King Solomon to talk about Adonijah. The king stood up to meet her and bowed to her. Then he sat on his throne. He had a throne brought for his mother, and she sat at his right hand.
"I have one small request. Please do not say no." "What is it, my mother? I will not say no to you."
"Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife."
"Why do you ask for Abishag for Adonijah? You might as well ask for the kingdom for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!"
Then King Solomon promised by the LORD, "May God punish me, and even more, if Adonijah does not pay with his life for this request!"
"Now, as sure as the LORD lives, He made me strong and set me on my father David's throne. He gave me a family, as He promised. So Adonijah will die today!"
So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada. Benaiah killed Adonijah, and he died.

The king said to Abiathar the priest, "Go to your fields in Anathoth. You deserve to die. But I will not kill you now. You carried the ark of the Lord the LORD before my father David. You shared in all my father's troubles."
So Solomon removed Abiathar from being the LORD's priest. This happened just as the LORD had said at Shiloh about Eli's family.
Joab had joined Adonijah but not Absalom. When he heard the news, he ran to the LORD's tent and held on to the altar's horns.
King Solomon heard that Joab had run to the LORD's tent and was by the altar. So he sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada and said, "Go kill him."
Benaiah went to the LORD's tent and said to Joab, "The king says, 'Come out!'" "No, I will die here!" Benaiah went back and told the king what Joab said.
The king said, "Do what he said. Kill him and bury him. Then I will be free from the blame for the innocent blood Joab spilled.

The LORD will make Joab pay for the blood he spilled. He killed two good men better than himself. My father David did not know about it. The men were Abner son of Ner, leader of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, leader of Judah's army.
Their blood will come back on Joab and his children forever. But the LORD will give peace to David, his children, his family, and his throne forever."
So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and killed Joab. Joab was buried at his own house in the desert.
The king made Benaiah son of Jehoiada leader of the army in Joab's place. He made Zadok the priest in Abiathar's place.
The king sent for Shimei and said, "Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem. Live there. Do not leave and go anywhere else."
"On the day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, you will surely die. Your blood will be on your own head."
Shimei said to the king, "That is good. Your servant will do what my lord the king says." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.
After three years, two of Shimei's slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Someone told Shimei, "Look, your slaves are in Gath."
So Shimei saddled his donkey and went to Gath to look for his slaves. He found them and brought them back from Gath.
Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and come back.

The king sent for Shimei and said, "Did I not make you promise by the LORD? Did I not warn you, 'On the day you leave and go anywhere, you will surely die'? And you said, 'That is good. I have heard.'"
"So why did you not keep your promise to the LORD and the command I gave you?"
The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your heart all the bad things you did to my father David. Now the LORD will bring that bad back on your own head."
But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will stand before the LORD forever.
Then the king ordered Benaiah son of Jehoiada. Benaiah went out and killed Shimei, and he died. So Solomon's kingdom was safe.

Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. He brought her to the City of David. She stayed there until he finished building his house, the house of the the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem.
The people still burned offerings on the high hills. They did that because no house had been built for the the LORD yet.
Solomon loved the the LORD. He followed the rules of his father David. But he still burned offerings and incense on the high hills.
The king went to Gibeon to give offerings there. It was the most important high place. Solomon gave one thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
That night at Gibeon, the the LORD came to Solomon in a dream. God said, "Ask for anything. I will give it to you."

Solomon said, "You showed great kindness to Your servant, my father David. He walked with You in truth and did what was right. His heart was right with You. You kept this great kindness for him. You gave him a son to sit on his throne, just like today.
And now, the LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in place of my father David. But I am only a little child. I do not know how to lead.
Your servant is among Your people, whom You chose. They are a great people. No one can count them all.
So give Your servant a heart that listens. Then he can judge Your people. Help him know right from wrong. Who can judge this great people of Yours?"
The Lord was pleased that Solomon asked for this.
God said to him, "Because you asked for this, and did not ask for a long life, or riches, or the death of your enemies, but asked for wisdom to make fair choices, I will give it to you.
I will do what you asked. I give you a wise and understanding heart. No one before you or after you will be like you.
I also give you what you did not ask for: riches and honor. No king will be like you all your life.
If you walk in My ways and keep My rules and commands, like your father David did, I will give you a long life."

Solomon woke up. He saw it was a dream. He went to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the the LORD. He gave burnt offerings and peace offerings. He also made a feast for all his servants.
Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king. They stood before him.
One woman said, "Please, sir, this woman and I live in the same house. I had a baby while she was there.
Three days after my baby was born, she had a baby too. We were alone in the house. No one else was there, just the two of us.
During the night, this woman's baby died because she lay on it.
She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while I was sleeping. She put him in her arms and put her dead baby in my arms.
When I got up in the morning to feed my baby, he was dead. But when I looked closely, I saw he was not my baby."
The other woman said, "No! The living baby is mine, and the dead one is yours." But the first woman said, "No! The dead baby is yours, and the living one is mine." They argued in front of the king.
The king said, "One woman says her baby is alive and the other woman's baby is dead. The other woman says the opposite."
The king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword to him.
The king said, "Cut the living baby in two. Give half to one woman and half to the other."

The woman whose baby was alive loved her son very much. She said to the king, "Please, sir, give her the living baby. Do not kill him." But the other woman said, "He will not be mine or yours. Cut him in half."
The king answered, "Give the living baby to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is his mother."
All Israel heard about the king's decision. They respected the king, because they saw God's wisdom in him to make fair choices.
These were his leaders. Azariah son of Zadok was the priest.
Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, were writers. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud wrote down what happened.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada led the army. Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
Azariah son of Nathan led the officers. Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's friend.
Ahishar ran the palace. Adoniram son of Abda was over the workers who had to work for the king.
Solomon had twelve helpers over all Israel. They fed the king and his house. Each helper did this one month each year.
Their names were these. Ben-Hur was in the hills of Ephraim.
Ben-Deker was in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, Aijalon, and Beth-hanan.
Ben-Hesed was in Arubboth. He also had Socoh and all the land of Hepher.
Ben-Abinadab was in all of Naphath-dor. Taphath, Solomon's daughter, was his wife.
Baana son of Ahilud was in Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth-shean near Zarethan, below Jezreel. His land went from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and past Jokneam.

Ben-Geber was in Ramoth Gilead. He also had the towns of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead. He had Gilead and the land of Argob in Bashan. There were sixty big cities there with strong walls and bronze gates.
Ahinadab son of Iddo was in Mahanaim.
Ahimaaz was in Naphtali. He also married Basemath, Solomon's daughter.
Baana son of Hushai was in Asher and Bealoth.
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in Issachar.
Shimei son of Ela was in Benjamin.
Geber son of Uri was in the land of Gilead. This was the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan. One helper was in charge of that land.
Judah and Israel were many. They were like sand by the sea. They ate, drank, and were happy.
Solomon ruled all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt. They brought gifts and served Solomon all his life.
Solomon's food for one day was thirty large baskets of fine flour and sixty large baskets of meal.
It also had ten fat oxen, twenty oxen from the field, and one hundred sheep. This was besides deer, gazelle, and fattened birds.
He ruled all the land west of the River. He ruled all the kings west of the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza. He had peace all around.
All the days of Solomon, Judah and Israel lived safely. They lived from Dan to Beersheba. Each man sat under his vine and under his fig tree.
Solomon had forty thousand stalls for chariot horses. He had twelve thousand horsemen.
The helpers fed King Solomon and all who came to the king's table. Each helper did this one month. They made sure nothing was missing.
They brought barley and straw for the horses and chariot horses. They brought it to the place where it was needed. Each helper did this as needed.
God gave Solomon wisdom. It was very great. His understanding was wide like the sand on the seashore.
Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the sons of the east. It was greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
He was wiser than all men. He was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, sons of Mahol. His name was known in all the nations around.
He spoke three thousand proverbs. He had one thousand and five songs.
He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop on the wall. He spoke about animals, birds, crawling things, and fish.
People came from all nations to hear Solomon's wisdom. All the kings of the earth who heard of his wisdom came too.
Hiram, king of Tyre, heard that Solomon was made king in place of his father. Hiram had always been David's friend. So Hiram sent his servants to Solomon.
Solomon sent this message to Hiram:
"You know that my father David could not build a house for the the LORD his God. He had wars all around him. The The LORD did not let him rest until He put his enemies under his feet.
But now the the LORD my God has given me peace on every side. There is no enemy and no trouble.
So I plan to build a house for the the LORD my God. The The LORD promised my father David: 'I will put your son on your throne after you. He will build a house for My name.'

So please command your men to cut cedar trees for me from Lebanon. My servants will work with your servants. I will pay your servants whatever wage you set. You know we do not have anyone who can cut wood like the people of Sidon."
Hiram was very glad when he heard Solomon's words. He said, "Praise the the LORD today! He gave David a wise son to rule this great people."
Hiram sent this message to Solomon: "I heard what you sent to me. I will do all you ask for cedar and cypress wood.

My servants will bring the wood down from Lebanon to the sea. I will tie it into rafts and float it to the place you choose. There I will break it apart, and you can take it. You can pay me back by giving food for my house."
So Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar and cypress wood he wanted.
Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand baskets of wheat for food for his house, and twenty jars of pure oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram every year.
The The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as He promised. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they made an agreement.
King Solomon made thirty thousand men from all Israel work for him.
He sent them to Lebanon in shifts. Ten thousand men went each month. They worked one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of this work.
Solomon also had seventy thousand men who carried loads and eighty thousand men who cut stone in the hills.
He had three thousand three hundred bosses who watched the workers.
The king told his workers to cut large, expensive stones to lay the foundation of the temple.
Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the men from Gebal cut and prepared the wood and stones to build the temple.
It was 480 years after the Israelites left Egypt. In the fourth year of Solomon's rule over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month, Solomon began to build the the LORD's house.
The house King Solomon built for the the LORD was 60 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
The front porch was 20 cubits long across the width of the house. It was 10 cubits wide in front of the house.
He made windows with narrow slats for the house.
Against the wall of the house, he built a side building around the walls. It went around the main hall and the holiest room. He made side rooms all around.

The lowest floor was 5 cubits wide. The middle floor was 6 cubits wide. The third floor was 7 cubits wide. He made ledges around the outside of the house so the beams would not be fastened into the walls.
The house was built with finished stones cut at the stone yard. No hammer, axe, or iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
The door to the middle floor was on the right side of the house. Winding stairs led up to the middle floor, and from the middle floor to the third floor.
So he built the house and finished it. He covered it with beams and cedar boards.
He built the side building all around the house. Each floor was 5 cubits high. He fastened it to the house with cedar beams.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Solomon. He said,
"This house you are building—if you walk in My rules, do what is right, and keep all My commands by living by them, then I will do what I promised your father David.
I will live among the Israelites. I will not leave My people Israel."
So Solomon built the house and finished it.
He lined the inside walls of the house with cedar boards. He covered the walls from the floor to the ceiling with wood. He covered the floor with cypress boards.
He set apart 20 cubits at the back of the house with cedar boards from floor to ceiling. This made the inner room, the holiest room.
The main hall in front of the inner room was 40 cubits long.
The inside of the house was cedar. It was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar. No stone could be seen.
He got the inner room ready inside the house. He put the ark of the the LORD's promise there.
The inner room was 20 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 20 cubits high. He covered it with pure gold. He also covered the cedar altar with gold.
Solomon covered the inside of the house with pure gold. He put gold chains across the front of the inner room and covered it with gold.
He covered the whole house with gold until it was finished. He also covered with gold the whole altar in the inner room.
In the inner room, he made two winged creatures from olive wood. Each was 10 cubits high.
One wing of the first creature was 5 cubits. The other wing was 5 cubits. From the tip of one wing to the tip of the other was 10 cubits.
The second creature was also 10 cubits. Both creatures had the same size and shape.
The first creature was 10 cubits high, and so was the second.

He put the creatures in the inner room. Their wings were spread out. The wing of one touched one wall. The wing of the other touched the other wall. Their wings touched each other in the middle of the room.
He covered the creatures with gold.
He carved all the walls of the house all around. He carved winged creatures, palm trees, and open flowers. He did this in the inner and outer rooms.
He covered the floor of the house with gold. He did this in the inner and outer rooms.
For the door of the inner room, he made doors of olive wood. The doorframe was one-fifth of the wall.
On the two olive-wood doors, he carved winged creatures, palm trees, and open flowers. He covered them with gold. He spread gold over the creatures and palm trees.
He made olive-wood doorposts for the door of the main hall. They were one-fourth of the wall.
He made two doors of cypress wood. Each door had two folding parts.
He carved winged creatures, palm trees, and open flowers on them. He covered them with gold. The gold was spread evenly over the carved work.
He built the inner courtyard with three rows of cut stone and one row of cedar beams.
The foundation of the the LORD's house was laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.
In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the eighth month, the house was finished. It was finished in all its parts and plans. He spent seven years building it.
Solomon built his own house. It took thirteen years to finish all of it.
He also built the House of the Forest of Lebanon. It was 100 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high. It stood on four rows of cedar pillars. Cedar beams rested on the pillars.
Cedar covered the rooms above the pillars. There were 45 rooms. There were 15 rooms in each row.
The windows were in three rows. They faced each other.
All the doorways and posts were square. The windows faced each other in three rows.
He made a porch of pillars. It was 50 cubits long and 30 cubits wide. There was another porch in front of them. It had pillars and a roof in front.
He made a porch for the throne where he judged. It was called the porch of judgment. Cedar covered it from the floor to the ceiling.
His own house was in the other court behind the porch. It was built the same way. He also built a house for Pharaoh's daughter, his wife. It was like the porch.

All these buildings used costly stones. The stones were cut to size. They were sawed with saws. This was true inside and outside. They went from the foundation to the top. They also went outside to the big court.
The foundation had large, costly stones. Some were 10 cubits long. Some were 8 cubits long.
Above them were costly stones cut to size. There was also cedar wood.
The big court all around had three rows of cut stone. It had one row of cedar beams. This was for the inner court of the the LORD's house. It was also for the porch of the house.
King Solomon sent for Hiram. He brought him from Tyre.

Hiram was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a man from Tyre. His father worked with bronze. Hiram was filled with wisdom, understanding, and skill. He could do all kinds of bronze work. He came to King Solomon. He did all the work.
He cast two bronze pillars. Each pillar was 18 cubits high. Each was 12 cubits around.
He made two bronze capitals. They went on top of the pillars. Each capital was 5 cubits high.
He made a network of chains for the capitals. The capitals were on top of the pillars. There were seven chains for one capital. There were seven chains for the other.
He made pomegranates in two rows around the network. They covered the capitals on top of the pillars. He did the same for the other pillar.
The capitals on top of the pillars in the porch were shaped like lilies. They were 4 cubits high.
There were also two hundred pomegranates in rows around each capital. They were just above the rounded part next to the network.
He set up the pillars at the porch of the temple. He set up the right pillar. He called it Jachin. He set up the left pillar. He called it Boaz.
The top of the pillars had lily work. So the work on the pillars was finished.
He made the Sea of cast metal. It was round. It was 10 cubits across from rim to rim. It was 5 cubits high. It was 30 cubits around.
Under the rim, gourds went all around it. There were ten gourds for every cubit. The gourds were in two rows. They were cast with the Sea.
It stood on twelve oxen. Three faced north. Three faced west. Three faced south. Three faced east. The Sea was on top of them. Their backs pointed inward.
The Sea was a handbreadth thick. Its rim was like the rim of a cup. It was shaped like a lily flower. It held two thousand baths of water.
He made ten bronze stands. Each stand was 4 cubits long. Each was 4 cubits wide. Each was 3 cubits high.
The stands had panels between the frames.
On the panels were lions, oxen, and cherubim. Above and below were lions and oxen. Hanging pieces went down from them.
Each stand had four bronze wheels. It had bronze axles. It had four feet. Under the basin, supports were cast at its four corners. These supports were beside the hanging pieces.
The top had a round opening. It was one cubit across. The capital above it was one and a half cubits high. The opening had carvings. The frames were square, not round.
Four wheels were under the frames. The wheel axles were part of the stand. Each wheel was one and a half cubits high.
The wheels were like chariot wheels. Their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all cast metal.
Each stand had four supports at its four corners. The supports were part of the stand.
The top of the stand was round. It was half a cubit high. The supports and panels were part of it.
He carved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the plates, supports, and panels. Wreaths went all around.
He made all ten stands the same way. They were cast the same. They were measured the same. They were the same size.
He made ten bronze basins. Each basin held forty baths of water. Each basin was four cubits across. There was one basin on each stand.
He put five stands on the right side of the house. He put five on the left side. He put the Sea at the southeast corner.
Hiram made the basins, shovels, and bowls. Hiram finished all the work he did for King Solomon for the the LORD's house.
There were two pillars. There were two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars. There were two networks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals.
There were four hundred pomegranates for the two networks. Each network had two rows of pomegranates. They covered the two bowl-shaped capitals in front of the pillars.
There were ten stands and ten basins on the stands.
There was one Sea and twelve oxen under the Sea.
There were pots, shovels, and bowls. All the vessels Hiram made for Solomon for the the LORD's house were polished bronze.
The king had them cast in clay molds. This was in the Jordan Valley. It was between Succoth and Zarethan.
Solomon did not weigh all the vessels. There were so many. The weight of the bronze was too great to measure.
Solomon made all the vessels for the the LORD's house. He made the gold altar. He made the gold table for the special bread.
He made lampstands of pure gold. Five were on the right. Five were on the left. They were in front of the inner room. The flowers, lamps, and tongs were also gold.
The cups, snuffers, bowls, spoons, and censers were pure gold. The hinges for the doors of the inner room, the Most Holy Place, and for the doors of the temple were gold.

All the work King Solomon did for the the LORD's house was finished. Solomon brought in the holy things his father David had set apart. He put the silver, gold, and vessels into the treasuries of the the LORD's house.

Then Solomon gathered the elders of Israel and all the leaders of the tribes. These were the family leaders of the Israelites. They came to King Solomon in Jerusalem. They were to bring the ark of the LORD's covenant from the City of David, which is Zion.
All the men of Israel came to King Solomon for the feast. It was the seventh month, the month called Ethanim.
All the elders of Israel came, and the priests carried the ark.
They brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy things in the tent. The priests and Levites carried them.
King Solomon and all the people of Israel were there in front of the ark. They sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that no one could count them.
The priests brought the ark of the LORD's covenant to its place. They put it in the inner room of the temple, the Most Holy Place. They set it under the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark. They covered the ark and its poles.
The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the holy place in front of the inner room. But they could not be seen from outside. They are still there today.
There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets. Moses had put them there at Horeb. That is where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
When the priests came out of the Holy Place, a cloud filled the LORD's temple.
The priests could not stand and serve because of the cloud. The glory of the LORD filled the temple.
The LORD said He would live in thick darkness. I have built a house for You. It is a place where You can live forever.”
Then the king turned around and blessed all the people of Israel while they stood. He said, “
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel. He spoke with His mouth to my father David. He did what He promised with His hand.
He said, ‘Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel to build a house for My name. But I chose David to rule over My people Israel.’
My father David wanted to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, ‘You wanted to build a house for My name. You did well to want that.
But you will not build the house. Your son, who comes from your own body, will build the house for My name.’
Now the LORD has done what He said. I have taken my father David's place. I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I have put the ark there. It holds the LORD's covenant. He made it with our fathers when He brought them out of Egypt.”
Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of all the people. He spread his hands toward heaven.
He prayed, “O the LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth below. You keep Your covenant and show love to Your servants. They walk before You with all their heart.
You have kept what You promised to Your servant my father David. You spoke with Your mouth, and You did it with Your hand. It is as it is today.

Now, O the LORD, God of Israel, keep the promise You made to Your servant my father David. You said, ‘You will never fail to have a man sit before Me on the throne of Israel. But your sons must guard their way and walk before Me, as you have walked before Me.’
And now, O God of Israel, let Your words come true. You spoke them to Your servant my father David.
But will God really live on earth? Look, the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot hold You. How much less this house I have built! “
Yet please listen to the prayer of Your servant and to his plea, O the LORD my God. Hear the cry and the prayer that Your servant prays before You today.
May Your eyes be open toward this house night and day. This is the place You said would have Your name. Hear the prayer Your servant prays toward this place.
Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, where You live. Hear and forgive.
When a man sins against his neighbor and must take an oath, and he comes to swear before Your altar in this house,
then hear from heaven and act. Judge Your servants. Show the wicked person he is wrong by bringing his guilt on his own head. Show the good person he is right by giving him what is right. “
When Your people Israel lose to an enemy because they sinned against You, and they come back to You and praise Your name and pray and plead with You in this house,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel. Bring them back to the land You gave their fathers.
When the sky is shut and there is no rain because they sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and praise Your name and turn from their sin because You punished them,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel. Teach them the good way to live. Send rain on Your land that You gave Your people to own. “
When there is hunger or sickness in the land, or plant disease, or locusts, or enemies attacking their cities, or any trouble or sickness,
then hear every prayer and plea that any man or all Your people Israel may bring. Each one knows his own pain. He spreads out his hands toward this house.
Then hear from heaven, where You live, and forgive and act. Give each man what he deserves, for You know his heart. You alone know the hearts of all people.
Do this so they will fear You all the days they live in the land You gave our fathers. “
Also, for the foreigner who is not one of Your people Israel but comes from far away because of Your name—
they will hear of Your great name and strong hand and outstretched arm. When he comes to pray toward this house,

then hear from heaven, where You live, and do what the foreigner asks. Do this so all the peoples of the earth may know Your name and fear You, just as Your people Israel do. Then they will know that this house I built is called by Your name. “
When Your people go out to fight their enemies, wherever You send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city You chose and the house I built for Your name,
then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and help them.
When they sin against You—for no one does not sin—and You are angry with them and let an enemy take them captive to a far or near land, “
and when they think about it in the land where they are held, and they turn back and plead with You, saying, ‘We have sinned. We have done wrong. We have been wicked,’

and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and they pray to You toward the land You gave their fathers, the city You chose, and the house I built for Your name,
then hear from heaven, where You live, their prayer and plea, and help them.
Forgive Your people who sinned against You. Forgive all the wrongs they did against You. Make their captors show them mercy. “
For they are Your people and Your own special people. You brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace.
May Your eyes be open to the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel. Listen to them whenever they call on You.
For You set them apart as Your own people from all the peoples of the earth. You spoke this through Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord, the LORD.”
When Solomon finished praying, he got up from before the altar of the LORD. He had been kneeling with his hands spread toward heaven.
He stood and blessed all the people of Israel in a loud voice. He said, “
Blessed be the LORD. He has given rest to His people Israel, just as He promised. Not one of all His good promises has failed. He spoke them through His servant Moses.
May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He not leave us or give up on us.
May He turn our hearts to Him. Then we can walk in all His ways and keep His commands, rules, and laws that He gave our fathers.
May these words of mine, which I have prayed before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night. May He help His servant and His people Israel, as each day needs.
Then all the peoples of the earth will know that the LORD is God. There is no other.
And may your hearts be fully given to the LORD our God. Walk in His rules and keep His commands, as you do today.”
Then the king and all Israel offered sacrifices to the LORD.
Solomon offered peace offerings to the LORD. He offered 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. The king and all the people dedicated the temple of the LORD.

That same day the king made the middle of the courtyard holy. It was in front of the temple. He did this because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small. It could not hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and fat of the peace offerings.

Solomon and all Israel with him made a large crowd. They came from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt. They celebrated the feast before the LORD our God for seven days. Then they celebrated seven more days. That was fourteen days in all.

On the eighth day he sent the people home. They blessed the king. They went to their tents. They were happy and glad in heart. They were glad because of all the good things the LORD had done for His servant David and for His people Israel.
Solomon finished building the house of the the LORD, the king's house, and everything he wanted to do.
Then the the LORD appeared to Solomon again, like He did at Gibeon.
The The LORD said, "I heard your prayer. I made this house you built holy. My name will be here forever. My eyes and My heart will be here always.
If you live for Me like your father David did, with a true heart and doing right, and do all I tell you, and keep My rules,
then I will keep your family on Israel's throne forever. I promised your father David that his family would always rule Israel.
But if you or your sons stop following Me and do not keep My commands and rules I gave you, and if you serve and worship other gods,
then I will remove Israel from the land I gave them. I will also send away this house I made holy for My name. Israel will become a joke and a shame to all nations.
This house will become a pile of stones. Everyone who passes by will be shocked and hiss. They will ask why the the LORD did such a thing to this land and this house.

Others will answer that they left the the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of Egypt. They held to other gods, worshiped them, and served them. That is why the the LORD brought all this trouble on them."
Solomon took twenty years to build the two houses: the house of the the LORD and his own house.
King Solomon gave twenty towns in Galilee to Hiram, king of Tyre. Hiram had given him cedar wood, cypress wood, and gold for all his building plans.
Hiram left Tyre to see the towns Solomon gave him, but he did not like them.
He asked, "What are these towns you gave me, my brother?" He called them the land of Cabul. They still call them that today.
Hiram sent the king one hundred twenty talents of gold.
This is the list of forced workers King Solomon used to build the house of the the LORD, his own house, the terraces, Jerusalem's wall, and the towns of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
Pharaoh, king of Egypt, had attacked Gezer and burned it. He killed the Canaanites who lived there. Then he gave the city to his daughter, Solomon's wife, as a wedding gift.
Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth-horon.
He also built Baalath and Tamar in the desert.
He built store cities, cities for his chariots and horses, and everything else he wanted to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and all his land.
Solomon forced the people still left in the land to work. They were Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, not Israelites.
They still work as forced labor today.
Solomon did not force Israelites to work as slaves. They were his soldiers, helpers, leaders, captains, chariot leaders, and horsemen.
Solomon had five hundred fifty bosses over his workers.
After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the City of David to the house Solomon built for her, Solomon built the terraces.
Three times each year Solomon gave burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he built for the the LORD. He burned incense to the the LORD. In this way he finished the temple.
King Solomon built ships at Ezion-geber, near Eloth in Edom.
Hiram sent sailors who knew the sea to work with Solomon's men.
They sailed to Ophir and brought back four hundred twenty talents of gold for King Solomon.
The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon. People said he was famous because of the the LORD. So she came to test him with hard questions.
She came to Jerusalem with a very big group. Her camels carried spices, much gold, and precious stones. She went to Solomon and told him everything on her mind.
Solomon answered all her questions. Nothing was too hard for him to explain.
The queen saw Solomon’s wisdom and the house he built.
She saw his food, his servants, his helpers, their clothes, his drink servers, and his burnt offering at the the LORD’s house. After that, she was so amazed she could hardly speak.
She said, “What I heard in my own land about your words and wisdom is true.
I did not believe it until I came and saw it with my own eyes. People did not even tell me half of it. Your wisdom and good life are much greater than the stories I heard.
“How happy your people are! How happy are the servants who stand before you all the time and hear your wisdom!
Praise be to the the LORD your God. He was pleased with you and put you on Israel’s throne. Because the the LORD loves Israel forever, He made you king to do what is right and fair.”
She gave the king 120 talents of gold. She also gave many spices and precious stones. No one ever brought so many spices again.
Hiram’s ships brought gold from Ophir. They also brought much rare wood called almug and precious stones from Ophir.
The king used the almug wood to make supports for the the LORD’s house and for his own house. He also made lyres and harps for the singers. No one had seen such wood before or since.
King Solomon gave the queen everything she wanted. He also gave her gifts from his royal treasure. Then she and her servants went back to her land.
Each year Solomon got 666 talents of gold.
This was besides money from traders, merchants, and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land.
Solomon made 200 large shields of gold. Each one used 600 shekels of gold.
He made 300 small shields of gold. Each one used 3 minas of gold. He put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a big throne of ivory and covered it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps. The back was round. There were armrests on both sides. Two lions stood by the armrests.
Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one on each side of each step. No other kingdom had a throne like it.
All of Solomon’s drinking cups were gold. The cups in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were gold too. In Solomon’s time, silver was not worth much.
The king had a fleet of ships. Every three years they brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
Solomon became greater than all the kings on earth in riches and wisdom.
People from all over the world came to see Solomon. They wanted to hear the wisdom God put in his heart.
Every year each man brought a gift. The gifts were silver and gold things, clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. He kept them in chariot cities and in Jerusalem.
In Jerusalem, silver was as common as stones. Cedar wood was as common as sycamore trees in the lowlands.
Solomon got horses from Egypt and Kue. His traders bought them from Kue.
A chariot from Egypt cost 600 pieces of silver. A horse cost 150 pieces of silver. Solomon’s traders sold them to the Hittite and Aramean kings.
King Solomon loved many foreign women. He loved Pharaoh’s daughter. He also loved women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the Hittites.

They were from nations the LORD had told Israel about: “Do not marry them. Do not let them marry you. They will turn your hearts to their gods.” But Solomon stayed close to them because he loved them.
He had seven hundred wives who were princesses. He had three hundred other wives. His wives turned his heart away.
When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart to other gods. His heart was not fully with the LORD his God, like his father David’s heart.
Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians. He also followed Milcom, the hated god of the Ammonites.
Solomon did what was bad in the eyes of the LORD. He did not follow the LORD fully, like his father David did.
Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the hated god of Moab. He built it on the hill east of Jerusalem. He also built one for Molech, the hated god of the Ammonites.
He did the same for all his foreign wives. They burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
The LORD was angry with Solomon. His heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel. The LORD had appeared to him two times.
The LORD had commanded him not to follow other gods. But Solomon did not keep what the LORD commanded.
So the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you did this, you did not keep My covenant and My rules that I gave you. I will tear the kingdom away from you. I will give it to your servant.
But I will not do it while you are alive. I will tear it away from your son.
Yet I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give one tribe to your son. I do this for My servant David and for Jerusalem, the city I chose.”
Then the LORD raised up an enemy against Solomon. It was Hadad the Edomite. He was from the royal family of Edom.
This happened when David was king. Joab, the leader of the army, went to bury the dead. He killed every male in Edom.
Joab and all Israel stayed there six months. They killed every male in Edom.
But Hadad ran away. He was still a young boy. Some of his father’s Edomite servants went with him to Egypt.
They left Midian and came to Paran. They took men from Paran with them. Then they came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, land, and food.
Hadad found great favor with Pharaoh. Pharaoh gave him a wife. She was the sister of his own wife, Queen Tahpenes.
The sister of Tahpenes had a son named Genubath. Tahpenes raised him in Pharaoh’s house. Genubath grew up among Pharaoh’s children.
In Egypt, Hadad heard that David had died. He also heard that Joab, the army leader, had died. Then Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Let me go back to my own country.”
Pharaoh said to him, “What do you lack here with me? Why do you want to go to your country?” Hadad said, “Just let me go.”
God also raised up another enemy. It was Rezon son of Eliada. He had run away from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
David had killed some of Hadadezer’s men. Rezon gathered men around him. He became the leader of a group of fighters. They went to Damascus and lived there. Rezon ruled in Damascus.
Rezon was Israel’s enemy all the days of Solomon. He caused trouble, along with Hadad. Rezon ruled over Aram.
Jeroboam son of Nebat rebelled against the king. He was from Zeredah in Ephraim. His mother was Zeruah, a widow. Jeroboam was Solomon’s servant.
This is why he rebelled: Solomon was building the Millo. He was closing a gap in the wall of his father David’s city.
Jeroboam was a strong and able man. Solomon saw that the young man worked hard. So Solomon put him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
At that time, Jeroboam left Jerusalem. The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak. The two men were alone in the field.
Ahijah took the new cloak he was wearing. He tore it into twelve pieces.
Ahijah said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself. The LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am tearing the kingdom from Solomon’s hand. I will give you ten tribes.
One tribe will stay with Solomon’s family. This is for My servant David and for Jerusalem, the city I chose from all the tribes of Israel.

They left Me. They bowed down to Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians. They bowed to Chemosh, the god of Moab. They bowed to Milcom, the god of the Ammonites. They did not walk in My ways. They did not do what is right in My eyes. They did not keep My rules and My laws, like David, Solomon’s father, did.”
“But I will not take the whole kingdom from Solomon’s hand. I will make him ruler all his life. I do this for My servant David, whom I chose. David kept My commands and My rules.
I will take the kingdom from his son’s hand. I will give you ten tribes.
I will give one tribe to his son. Then My servant David will always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem. That is the city I chose for My name.”
“I will take you, and you will rule over all you want, and you will be king over Israel.

If you listen to all I command you, and walk in My ways, and do what is right in My eyes, and keep My rules and commands like My servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting house, like I built for David. I will give Israel to you.
I will make David’s family suffer because of this. But not forever.”
Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam ran away to Egypt. He went to Shishak king of Egypt. He stayed in Egypt until Solomon died.
The rest of Solomon’s deeds and his wisdom are written in the book of Solomon’s deeds.
Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
Then Solomon died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam became king after him.
Rehoboam went to Shechem. All Israel had gone there to make him king.
Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this. He was still in Egypt. He had run away from King Solomon. He had been living there.
The people sent for Jeroboam. He and all Israel came to Rehoboam. They said,
"Your father made our work very hard. Please make it lighter. Make his hard rules easier. Then we will serve you."
Rehoboam said, "Go away for three days. Then come back to me." So the people left.
King Rehoboam asked the older men. They had served his father Solomon. He asked, "How do you say I should answer these people?"
They said, "If you are kind to these people today, and serve them, and speak good words to them, they will serve you always."
But Rehoboam did not listen to the old men. He asked the young men who grew up with him. They were near him.
He said, "What do you say? We need to answer the people. They said to make the load lighter that your father put on us."
The young men who grew up with him said, "Tell these people who spoke to you that your father made our load heavy and you should make it lighter. Tell them that I am stronger than my father."
My father put a heavy load on you. I will make it even heavier. My father hit you with whips. I will hit you with sharp whips."
On the third day, Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam. This was what the king had said: "Come back to me on the third day."
The king answered the people in a harsh way. He did not follow the old men's advice.
He spoke to them the way the young men said. He said, "My father made your load heavy. I will make it even heavier. My father hit you with whips. I will hit you with sharp whips."
The king did not listen to the people. This happened because the LORD planned it. He wanted to keep His word. He had spoken this word to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh.

All Israel saw that the king did not listen to them. So they answered the king, "What part do we have with David? We have no share with Jesse's son. Go home, Israel! David, take care of your own family." Then Israel went home.
But Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Adoram. Adoram was in charge of forced work. All Israel stoned him, and he died. King Rehoboam quickly got into his chariot. He ran away to Jerusalem.
So Israel turned away from David's family. They are still against David's family today.
All Israel heard that Jeroboam had come back. They sent for him and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah stayed with David's family.

Rehoboam came to Jerusalem. He gathered all Judah and the tribe of Benjamin. There were 180,000 chosen men. They were ready to fight. They wanted to fight Israel. They wanted to give the kingdom back to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
But God's word came to Shemaiah, a man of God.
He said, "Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah. Speak to all Judah and Benjamin. Speak to the rest of the people.

Say that the LORD says not to go up. Do not fight your brothers, the Israelites. Each man should go home, because the LORD planned it." The people listened to the LORD's word. They went home, just as the LORD said.
Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim. He lived there. Then he left and built Penuel.
Jeroboam said in his heart, "The kingdom may go back to David's family.

If these people go up to the LORD's house in Jerusalem to give gifts, their hearts may turn back to their king. They may turn back to Rehoboam, king of Judah. Then they may kill me and go back to Rehoboam, king of Judah."
So the king asked for advice. Then he made two gold calves. He said to the people, "It is too far for you to go up to Jerusalem. Look! These are your gods, Israel. They brought you up out of Egypt."
He put one calf in Bethel. He put the other in Dan.
This became a sin. The people went to worship the calf in Dan.
Jeroboam built places to worship on the hills. He made priests from all kinds of people. They were not from Levi's family.

Jeroboam made a feast. It was on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. It was like the feast in Judah. He offered gifts on the altar. He did this in Bethel. He gave gifts to the calves he had made. He put priests on the hill altars he had made.
On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month he chose for himself, he offered gifts on the altar he made in Bethel. He made a feast for Israel. He went up to the altar to burn sweet smoke.
Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense. A man of God came from Judah to Bethel because the the LORD sent him.

He cried out against the altar by the word of the the LORD. He said, "Altar, altar! The the LORD says this: A boy named Josiah will be born in David's family. He will burn on you the priests of the high places who burn incense on you. He will burn human bones on you."
That day the man of God gave a sign. He said, "This is the sign the the LORD has spoken: The altar will split apart. The ashes on it will spill out."
When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God said about the altar, he reached out his hand from the altar. He said, "Grab him!" But his hand dried up. He could not pull it back.
The altar split apart. The ashes spilled out, just as the man of God had said by the word of the the LORD.

The king said to the man of God, "Please ask the the LORD your God to pray for me. Ask Him to make my hand well again." So the man of God prayed to the the LORD. The king's hand became well again, like before.
The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me. Eat with me. I will give you a gift."
The man of God said to the king, "Even if you gave me half your house, I would not go with you. I will not eat bread or drink water here."
"The the LORD told me not to eat bread or drink water here. He told me not to go back the same way I came."
So he went another way. He did not go back the way he came to Bethel.
An old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and told him everything the man of God had done that day in Bethel. They told him the words he had said to the king.
Their father asked, "Which way did he go?" His sons showed him the way the man of God from Judah had gone.
The old prophet said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." They saddled it. He rode on it.
He went after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak tree. He asked, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" The man said, "I am."
The old prophet said, "Come home with me and eat bread."
The man of God said, "I cannot go back with you or come in with you. I will not eat bread or drink water with you here."
"The the LORD told me not to eat bread or drink water there. He told me not to go back by the way I came."
The old prophet said, "I am a prophet too, like you. An angel spoke to me by the word of the the LORD and said, 'Bring him back to your house. Let him eat bread and drink water.'" But he lied to him.
So the man of God went back with him. He ate bread in his house. He drank water.
While they sat at the table, the word of the the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back.
He cried out to the man of God from Judah, "The the LORD says this: You did not obey the the LORD. You did not keep the command the the LORD your God gave you.
You came back. You ate bread and drank water in the place where He said, 'Do not eat bread or drink water.' So your body will not be buried with your fathers."
After he ate bread and drank water, the old prophet saddled the donkey for the man of God.
The man of God left. A lion found him on the road and killed him. His body lay on the road. The donkey stood by it. The lion stood by the body too.
Some men passed by. They saw the body on the road and the lion standing by it. They went and told the city where the old prophet lived.

When the prophet who brought him back heard this, he said, "He is the man of God who did not obey the the LORD. The the LORD gave him to the lion. It tore him and killed him, just as the the LORD had said."
He said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." They saddled it.
He went and found the body on the road. The donkey and the lion were standing by it. The lion had not eaten the body. It had not hurt the donkey.
The prophet picked up the body of the man of God. He put it on the donkey. He brought it back. The old prophet came to the city to cry for him and bury him.
He laid the body in his own tomb. They cried over him, "Oh, my brother!"
After he buried him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the same tomb where the man of God is buried. Put my bones next to his bones."
The words he spoke by the word of the the LORD will come true. He spoke them against the altar in Bethel and against all the high places in the cities of Samaria.
After this, Jeroboam still did not turn from his evil way. He made priests from the people. Anyone who wanted to be a priest could become one.
This became a sin for Jeroboam's family. It led to them being wiped out from the earth.
At that time, Jeroboam's son Abijah got sick.

Jeroboam said to his wife, "Please get up and change how you look. No one must know you are Jeroboam's wife. Go to Shiloh. The prophet Ahijah is there. He is the one who said I would be king over this people.
Take ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey with you. Go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."
Jeroboam's wife did what he said. She got up and went to Shiloh. She came to Ahijah's house. Ahijah could not see, because his eyes were weak from old age.
The LORD had told Ahijah, "Look, Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her son, because he is sick. Say this and that to her. When she comes in, she will pretend to be someone else."
When Ahijah heard her footsteps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why do you pretend to be someone else? I have a hard message for you."
"Go and tell Jeroboam that the LORD, the God of Israel, says this: I picked you up from among the people. I made you ruler over My people Israel.

I tore the kingdom away from David's family and gave it to you. But you have not been like My servant David. He obeyed My commands. He followed Me with all his heart. He did only what was right in My eyes.
You have done more evil than all who came before you. You went and made other gods for yourself. You made metal gods to make Me angry. You turned your back on Me.

"So I will bring trouble to Jeroboam's family. I will destroy every male in Jeroboam's family, both slave and free, in Israel. I will burn up Jeroboam's family and sweep it away like trash until it is gone.
Dogs will eat anyone from Jeroboam's family who dies in the city. Birds of the sky will eat anyone who dies in the field. The LORD has spoken.
"As for you, get up and go home. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.

All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He is the only one of Jeroboam's family who will be buried. This is because the LORD, the God of Israel, found something good in him among Jeroboam's family.
"The LORD will raise up a king over Israel who will destroy Jeroboam's family. That will happen even today. Yes, even now.

The LORD will strike Israel. They will be like a reed shaking in the water. He will pull Israel up from this good land He gave their ancestors. He will scatter them beyond the Euphrates River. This is because they made poles for the false goddess Asherah. They made the LORD angry.
He will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam. Jeroboam sinned and made Israel sin too."
Then Jeroboam's wife got up and left. She went to Tirzah. As she stepped over the doorstep of the house, the boy died.
They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him. This happened just as the LORD had said through His servant Ahijah the prophet.
The rest of the things Jeroboam did, including his wars and his rule, are written in the records of the kings of Israel.
Jeroboam ruled for twenty-two years. Then he died and was buried with his fathers. his son Nadab became king after him.

Rehoboam son of Solomon ruled in Judah. he was forty-one years old when he became king. he ruled seventeen years in Jerusalem. This is the city the LORD chose from all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD. They sinned more than their fathers had done. They made the LORD jealous.
They also built high places, stone pillars, and poles for the false goddess Asherah on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were also men who sold sex at the worship places in the land. The people did all the terrible things the other nations did, the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
he took the treasures from the LORD's temple and the king's palace. he took everything. he took all the gold shields Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields to take their place. he put them in the care of the guards who watched the entrance to the king's palace.
Whenever the king went to the LORD's temple, the guards carried the shields. Then they brought them back to the guard room.
The rest of Rehoboam's acts and all he did are written in the records of the kings of Judah.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
Rehoboam died and was buried with his fathers. his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. his son Abijam became king after him.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam began to rule over Judah.
He ruled in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
He did the same bad things his father did. His heart was not fully for the LORD his God, like David's heart was.
But because David served the LORD, the LORD let David's family keep ruling in Jerusalem. He let David's son rule after him, and He kept Jerusalem strong.
David did what was right in the LORD's eyes. He did not turn from any command all his life, except the wrong he did with Uriah the Hittite.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all through Abijam's life.
The rest of what Abijam did is written in the book of the kings of Judah. There was also war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam died and was buried in the city of David. His son Asa became king after him.
In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
He ruled in Jerusalem forty-one years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, like David his father.
He sent away the men who served false gods in the temple. He took away all the idols his fathers had made.
He also removed his mother Maacah from being queen mother. She had made a horrible idol for Asherah. Asa cut down the idol and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The hilltop worship places were not taken away. But Asa's heart was fully for the LORD all his life.
He brought into the house of the LORD the silver, gold, and vessels that he and his father had set apart for God.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Baasha king of Israel attacked Judah. He built up Ramah. He wanted to stop people from going to or coming from Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa took all the silver and gold left in the treasures of the house of the LORD and the king's house. He gave them to his servants. He sent them to Ben-Hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus. He said,

"There is an agreement between me and you. There was one between my father and your father. I have sent you silver and gold. Go and break your agreement with Baasha king of Israel. Then he will leave me alone."
