Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa. He sent his army leaders against the cities of Israel. He struck Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, and all the land of Chinnereth and Naphtali.
When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah. He stayed in Tirzah.
Then King Asa called all Judah. No one was excused. They carried away the stones and wood of Ramah that Baasha had built. King Asa used them to build Geba in Benjamin and Mizpah.
The rest of all that Asa did, his power, and the cities he built are written in the book of the kings of Judah. In his old age he got sick in his feet.
Asa died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. His son Jehoshaphat became king after him.
Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah. He ruled over Israel two years.
He did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He walked in his father's way and in his sin, which made Israel sin.
Baasha son of Ahijah, from the family of Issachar, made a plan against him. Baasha struck him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines. Nadab and all Israel were attacking Gibbethon.
Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of Asa king of Judah. He became king in his place.
When Baasha became king, he struck down all the house of Jeroboam. He did not leave Jeroboam anyone who breathed. He destroyed them, as the LORD had said through His servant Ahijah the Shilonite.
This happened because of Jeroboam's sins and the sin he made Israel do. He made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.
The rest of what Nadab did is written in the book of the kings of Israel.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah in the third year of Asa king of Judah. He ruled twenty-four years.
He did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin, which made Israel sin.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Jehu, the son of Hanani, against Baasha. It said,
"I lifted you up from the dust. I made you a leader over My people Israel. But you walked in the way of Jeroboam. You made My people Israel sin. You made Me angry with their sins.
So I will wipe out Baasha and his family. I will make your family like the family of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Dogs will eat the ones from Baasha who die in the city. Birds in the sky will eat the ones who die in the fields."
The rest of the things Baasha did, and his power, are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Baasha died and was buried with his fathers in Tirzah. His son Elah became king after him.

The word of the the LORD also came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his family. It was because of all the evil he did in the eyes of the the LORD. He made the the LORD angry with what he did. He became like the family of Jeroboam. He also struck down Jeroboam's family.
Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah. This was in the 26th year of Asa, king of Judah. He ruled two years.
He was in Tirzah. He got drunk in the house of Arza. Arza was in charge of the palace in Tirzah.
Zimri was the leader of half the chariots. He made a plan against Elah. In the 27th year of Asa, king of Judah, Zimri came and struck Elah and killed him. Then Zimri became king.
As soon as Zimri sat on the throne, he killed all of Baasha's family. He did not leave one man. He did not even leave a relative or a friend.
Zimri wiped out all of Baasha's family. This happened just as the the LORD had said through the prophet Jehu.
This was for all the sins of Baasha and his son Elah. They sinned. They made Israel sin. They made the the LORD, the God of Israel, angry with their worthless idols.
The rest of what Elah did is written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Zimri became king in Tirzah. This was in the 27th year of Asa, king of Judah. He ruled seven days. The army was camped at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
The army in the camp heard that Zimri had made a plan and killed the king. So all Israel made Omri king that day. Omri was the army commander.
Omri and all Israel went up from Gibbethon. They surrounded Tirzah.
Zimri saw that the city was taken. He went into the strong part of the king's house. He set the king's house on fire around him. He died in the fire.
This happened because of the sins Zimri committed. He did evil in the eyes of the the LORD. He walked in the way of Jeroboam. He made Israel sin.
The rest of what Zimri did, and the plan he made, is written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Then the people of Israel split into two groups. Half followed Tibni son of Ginath and wanted him to be king. The other half followed Omri.
The people who followed Omri were stronger than the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died. Then Omri became king.
Omri became king over Israel in the 31st year of Asa, king of Judah. He ruled twelve years. He ruled six years in Tirzah.
He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver. He built on the hill. He named the city he built Samaria. He named it after Shemer, who owned the hill.
Omri did evil in the eyes of the the LORD. He did worse than all who came before him.
He walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat. He made Israel sin. He made the the LORD, the God of Israel, angry with their worthless idols.
The rest of what Omri did, and his power, is written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Omri died and was buried in Samaria. His son Ahab became king after him.
Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the 38th year of Asa, king of Judah. Ahab son of Omri ruled over Israel in Samaria for twenty-two years.
Ahab son of Omri did evil in the eyes of the the LORD. He did more evil than all who came before him.
It was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. He married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. He went and served Baal and worshiped him.
He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he built in Samaria.
Ahab made a wooden pole for Asherah. He did more to make the the LORD, the God of Israel, angry than all the kings of Israel before him.

In Ahab's days, Hiel from Bethel built Jericho again. He laid its foundation with his oldest son, Abiram. He set up its gates with his youngest son, Segub. This happened just as the the LORD had said through Joshua son of Nun.
Elijah was from Tishbe in Gilead. He said to King Ahab, "I serve the LORD, the God of Israel. He is alive! There will be no dew or rain for years, unless I say so."
Then the LORD spoke to him. He said,
"Go away from here. Turn east and hide by the Brook Cherith, east of the Jordan.
You will drink from the brook. I have told the ravens to feed you there."
So Elijah went and did what the LORD said. He stayed by the Brook Cherith, east of the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.
After a while, the brook dried up because no rain fell in the land.
Then the LORD spoke to him again. He said,
"Get up and go to Zarephath near Sidon. Stay there. I have told a widow there to feed you."
So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he came to the city gate, a widow was there picking up sticks. He called to her and said, "Please bring me a little water in a cup so I can drink."
As she went to get it, he called, "Please bring me a piece of bread too."

She said, "I swear by the LORD your God, I have no bread. I only have a little flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am picking up two sticks so I can go home and make food for me and my son. We will eat it, and then we will die."
Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go and do what you said. But first make a small bread cake for me from what you have, and bring it to me. Then make some for yourself and your son.
For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not be empty, until the day the LORD sends rain on the land.'"
She went and did what Elijah said. Then she, her family, and Elijah ate for many days.
The jar of flour did not run out, and the jug of oil did not become empty, just as the LORD had said through Elijah.
Later, the son of the woman who owned the house got very sick. He got so sick that he stopped breathing.
The woman said to Elijah, "What do you have against me, man of God? Did you come here to remind me of my sin and kill my son?"
Elijah said, "Give me your son." He took the boy from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he stayed, and laid him on his bed.
Elijah prayed to the LORD, "the LORD my God, did You bring trouble on this widow I am staying with by killing her son?"
He stretched himself over the boy three times and cried out to the LORD, "the LORD my God, let this boy's life come back to him!"
The LORD heard Elijah, and the boy's life came back to him, and he lived.
Elijah took the boy and brought him down from the upper room into the house. He gave him to his mother and said, "Look, your son is alive."
The woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is true."
After many days, in the third year, the word of the the LORD came to Elijah. He said, "Go show yourself to Ahab. I will send rain on the earth."
So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine was strong in Samaria.
Ahab called Obadiah, who was over the house. Obadiah feared the the LORD very much.
When Jezebel was killing the prophets of the the LORD, Obadiah took one hundred prophets. He hid fifty in a cave. He gave them bread and water.
Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs and streams. Maybe we can find grass for the horses and mules. Then we will not have to kill any of our animals."
They split the land between them. Ahab went one way by himself. Obadiah went the other way by himself.
As Obadiah was on the way, Elijah met him. Obadiah knew him. He fell on his face. He said, "Are you my lord Elijah?"
Elijah said, "I am. Go tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"
Obadiah said, "What sin did I do? Why are you giving your servant to Ahab to be killed?
As the the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent someone to look for you. When they said you were not there, he made them promise they could not find you.
"And now you say, 'Go tell your lord, "Elijah is here."'

I do not know where the Spirit of the the LORD will take you when I leave you. If I go tell Ahab and he does not find you, he will kill me. But I, your servant, have feared the the LORD since I was young.
Did no one tell my lord what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of the the LORD? I hid one hundred prophets of the the LORD. I put fifty in a cave. I gave them bread and water.
And now you say, 'Go tell your lord, "Elijah is here."' He will kill me!"
Elijah said, "As the the LORD of all armies lives, before whom I stand, I will show myself to Ahab today."
Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him, "Are you the one who troubles Israel?"
Elijah said, "I have not troubled Israel. But you and your father's family have. You left the commands of the the LORD. You followed the Baals."
Elijah said, "Now call all Israel to me on Mount Carmel. Also bring the four hundred fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table."
So Ahab called all the people of Israel. He gathered the prophets on Mount Carmel.
Elijah came near to all the people and said, "How long will you go back and forth? If the the LORD is God, follow Him. If Baal is God, follow him." The people did not answer.
Elijah said to the people, "I am the only prophet of the the LORD left. But Baal has four hundred fifty prophets."

Elijah said, "Let us have two bulls. Let them choose one bull. They will cut it up and put it on the wood. They will not light the fire. I will get the other bull. I will put it on the wood. I will not light the fire."
Elijah said, "Then you will call on the name of your god. I will call on the name of the the LORD. The God who answers by fire, He is God." All the people said, "That is good."
Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "You are many. Choose one bull. Make it ready first. Call on the name of your god. Do not light the fire."

They took the bull that was given to them. They made it ready. They called on the name of Baal from morning until noon. They said, "Baal, answer us!" But there was no voice and no answer. They danced around the altar they had made.
At noon Elijah made fun of them. He said, "Call louder! He is a god. Maybe he is thinking. Maybe he is busy. Maybe he is on a trip. Maybe he is asleep and must wake up."
They called louder. They cut themselves with swords and spears. This was their way. Blood ran on them.
After noon they kept on prophesying until the time for the evening gift. But there was no voice. No one answered. No one listened.
Elijah said to all the people, "Come near to me." All the people came near to him. He fixed the altar of the the LORD that had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones. There was one stone for each tribe of Jacob's sons. The the LORD had said, "Your name will be Israel."
With the stones he built an altar in the name of the the LORD. He dug a ditch around the altar. It was big enough to hold two baskets of seed.
He laid the wood in order. He cut up the bull. He put it on the wood.
He said, "Fill four jars with water. Pour it on the offering and on the wood." They did. He said, "Do it again." They did it again. He said, "Do it a third time." They did it a third time.
The water ran around the altar. It even filled the ditch.

At the time of the evening gift, Elijah the prophet came near. He said, "O the LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that You are God in Israel. I am Your servant. I have done all these things by Your word."
"Answer me, the LORD! Answer me, so these people may know that You are the the LORD their God, and that You have turned their hearts back."
Then the fire of the the LORD fell. It burned up the offering, the wood, the stones, the dust, and the water in the ditch.
All the people saw it. They fell on their faces. They said, "The the LORD, He is God! The the LORD, He is God!"
Elijah said to them, "Catch the prophets of Baal! Do not let one of them get away." They caught them. Elijah brought them down to the Kishon Valley. He killed them there.
Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up. Eat and drink. I hear the sound of much rain."
Ahab went up to eat and drink. Elijah went up to the top of Carmel. He bent down to the ground. He put his face between his knees.
Elijah said to his servant, "Go up and look toward the sea." The servant went up and looked. He said, "There is nothing." Elijah said, "Go back." He did this seven times.
The seventh time, the servant said, "Look! A small cloud, like a man's hand, is rising from the sea." Elijah said, "Go tell Ahab, 'Hitch up your chariot and go down. The rain must not stop you.'"
The sky grew dark with clouds and wind. There was a heavy rain. Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.
The hand of the the LORD was on Elijah. He tied up his coat. He ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done. He told her how Elijah had killed all the prophets with a sword.
Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah. The messenger said, "I swear by the gods that by this time tomorrow you will be dead like those prophets."
Elijah was afraid. He got up and ran to save his life. He went to Beersheba in Judah. There he left his servant.
Elijah walked one day into the desert. He sat under a bush. He asked to die. He said, "I have had enough, the LORD. Take my life. I am no better than my fathers."
Elijah lay down under the bush and slept. An angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."
Elijah looked up. He saw bread baked on hot stones and a jar of water by his head. He ate and drank. Then he lay down again.
The angel of the LORD came a second time. He touched Elijah and said, "Get up and eat. The journey is too long for you."
Elijah got up. He ate and drank. Then he walked for forty days and forty nights. He reached Mount Horeb, the mountain of God.
There Elijah went into a cave and stayed. The LORD spoke to him. He said, "Elijah, what are you doing here?"

Elijah said, "I have served You faithfully, the LORD God of armies. The people of Israel have left Your agreement. They have torn down Your altars. They have killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left. Now they are trying to kill me too."

The LORD said, "Go out and stand on the mountain before Me." Then the LORD passed by. A very strong wind tore the mountains and broke the rocks. But the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake. But the LORD was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake came fire. But the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire came a soft, quiet voice.
When Elijah heard it, he pulled his cloak over his face. He went out and stood at the mouth of the cave. Then a voice said to him, "Elijah, what are you doing here?"

Elijah said, "I have served You faithfully, the LORD God of armies. The people of Israel have left Your agreement. They have torn down Your altars. They have killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left. Now they are trying to kill me too."
The LORD said to him, "Go back the way you came. Go to the desert near Damascus. When you get there, make Hazael king over Aram.
Also make Jehu son of Nimshi king over Israel. And choose Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah to be prophet after you.
Jehu will kill anyone who escapes from Hazael. Elisha will kill anyone who escapes from Jehu.
But I will leave seven thousand people in Israel. They have not bowed down to Baal. They have not worshiped him."
Elijah left there. He found Elisha son of Shaphat. Elisha was plowing with twelve teams of oxen. He was with the last team. Elijah walked by him and threw his cloak on him.
Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah. He said, "Let me say goodbye to my father and mother. Then I will follow you." Elijah said, "Go back. I did not force you to come."

Elisha went back. He took his team of oxen and killed them. He cooked the meat over a fire made from the yokes. He gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he got up and followed Elijah. He helped Elijah.
Ben-Hadad was the king of Aram. He brought all his army. Thirty-two kings came with him. He also had horses and chariots. He went up, surrounded Samaria, and fought against it.
He sent messengers into the city to Ahab, the king of Israel.
The message said, "Ben-Hadad says, 'Your silver and gold are mine. Your best things, your wives, and your children are mine too.'"
The king of Israel answered, "As you say, my lord the king, I am yours, and all I have is yours."
The messengers came back and said, "Ben-Hadad says, 'I sent word to you. I said you must give me your silver, gold, wives, and children.'"
"But tomorrow at this time, I will send my servants to you. They will search your house and your servants' houses. They will take everything you like best."
The king of Israel called all the elders of the land. He said, "Please see how this man wants trouble. He sent for my wives, children, silver, and gold. I did not refuse him."
All the elders and the people said to him, "Do not listen to him. Do not agree."
So Ahab said to Ben-Hadad's messengers, "Tell my lord the king, 'I will do all you asked at first. But I cannot do this new thing.'" The messengers left and told him.
Ben-Hadad sent another message: "I swear by the gods that I will make Samaria into dust. There will not be enough dust for all my men to carry."
The king of Israel answered, "Tell him, 'A man should not brag while putting on his armor. He can brag only after he wins.'"
When Ben-Hadad heard this message, he was getting drunk in the tents with the kings. He said to his servants, "Get ready." They got ready to attack the city.
A prophet came to Ahab, the king of Israel. He said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Do you see this big crowd? Today I will give them into your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

Ahab asked, "Who will start the fight?" The prophet answered, "This is what the LORD says: 'The young leaders of the regions will start it.'" Then Ahab asked, "Who will lead the army?" The prophet said, "You will."
Ahab counted the young leaders of the regions. There were 232. After them, he counted all the people of Israel. There were 7,000.
They went out at noon. Ben-Hadad was getting drunk in the tents with the 32 kings who helped him.
The young leaders went out first. People told Ben-Hadad, "Men have come out from Samaria."
Ben-Hadad said, "If they come for peace, take them alive. If they come for war, take them alive too."
Those young leaders and the army behind them came out of the city.
Each man killed his enemy. The army of Aram ran away. Israel chased them. Ben-Hadad, the king of Aram, escaped on a horse with some horsemen.
The king of Israel went out and struck the horses and chariots. He killed many men in Aram.
Then the prophet came to the king of Israel and said, "Go, make yourself strong. Think about what you must do. Next year the king of Aram will come back against you."
The servants of the king of Aram said to him, "Their gods are gods of the hills. That is why they were stronger than us. But if we fight them on the flat land, we will be stronger than them."
"Do this: Take the kings away from their places. Put governors in their places instead."
"Get an army as big as the one you lost. Get the same number of horses and chariots. Then fight them on the flat land. We will be stronger than them." Ben-Hadad listened to them and did it.
The next year, Ben-Hadad counted the men of Aram. He went up to Aphek to fight Israel.
The people of Israel were counted and fed. They marched out to meet them. They camped across from them. They looked like two small flocks of goats. But the army of Aram filled the land.

A man of God came to the king of Israel and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'The Arameans said, "The LORD is a god of the hills, not a god of the valleys." So I will give all this big crowd into your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"
They camped across from each other for seven days. On the seventh day the battle started. The Israelites killed 100,000 Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
The rest ran into the city of Aphek. The wall fell on 27,000 men who were left. Ben-Hadad ran into the city and hid in an inner room.

His servants said to him, "We have heard that the kings of Israel are kind. Let us go to the king of Israel with sackcloth around our waists and ropes around our heads. Maybe he will spare your life."

They put sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads. They went to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad says, 'Please let me live.'" The king said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
The men watched Ahab's words. They quickly said, "Yes, your brother Ben-Hadad!" Ahab said, "Go get him." Ben-Hadad came out. Ahab had him ride in his chariot.

Ben-Hadad said to him, "I will give back the cities my father took from your father. You can have streets in Damascus, as my father had in Samaria. Then I will let you go." Ahab made a peace treaty with him and let him go.
At the LORD's word, one of the prophets said to his friend, "Hit me, please." But the man would not hit him.
The prophet said, "Because you did not obey the LORD's voice, a lion will attack you as soon as you leave me." Then he left. A lion found him and killed him.
The prophet found another man and said, "Hit me, please." The man hit him and wounded him.
Then the prophet went and stood by the road. He waited for the king. He disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes.

As the king passed by, the prophet cried out to him. He said, "Your servant went into the battle. A man brought another man to me and said, 'Guard this man. If he gets away, you will die, or you will pay a large amount of silver.'"
"While your servant was busy here and there, the man got away." The king of Israel said to him, "That is your sentence. You decided it."
The prophet quickly took the bandage off his eyes. The king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.
The prophet said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Because you let go the man I set apart for destruction, your life will be taken instead of his life, and your people instead of his people.'"
The king of Israel went home to Samaria. He was angry and upset.
After these things, Naboth the man from Jezreel had a grape field in Jezreel. It was next to the palace of Ahab, king of Samaria.

Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your grape field. I want to make it a garden for vegetables. It is close to my house. I will give you a better grape field for it. Or, if you like, I will pay you money for it."
Naboth said to Ahab, "The LORD forbid that I give you the land my fathers left me."
Ahab went home. He was sad and angry because of what Naboth said. He lay on his bed, turned his face to the wall, and would not eat.
His wife Jezebel came in and said, "Why are you so sad? Why won't you eat?"
He said, "I asked Naboth for his grape field. I offered money or another grape field. He said no."
Jezebel said, "Are you not the king of Israel? Get up, eat, and be happy. I will get you Naboth's grape field."
She wrote letters in Ahab's name. She used his seal. She sent them to the leaders and important men who lived in Naboth's city.
In the letters she wrote, "Call a fast. Put Naboth in a high place among the people.
Bring two bad men to sit across from him. Have them say that he cursed God and the king. Then take him out and kill him with stones."
The men of his city, the leaders and important men, did what Jezebel sent. They did what the letters said.
They called a fast. They put Naboth at the head of the people.
Two bad men came in and sat across from him. They accused Naboth in front of the people. They said, "Naboth cursed God and the king." Then they took him outside the city and killed him with stones.
They sent word to Jezebel: "Naboth has been killed with stones and is dead."
When Jezebel heard that Naboth was killed with stones and was dead, she said to Ahab, "Get up and take Naboth's grape field. He would not sell it to you, but now he is dead."
When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up to go down and take Naboth's grape field.
Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the man from Tishbe.
It said, "Go meet Ahab king of Israel in Samaria. He is in Naboth's grape field, where he went down to take it."
"Say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Did you kill a man and take his land? In the place where dogs licked Naboth's blood, dogs will lick your blood too.'"
Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" Elijah said, "I have found you, because you sold yourself to do evil in the LORD's eyes.
I will bring trouble on you. I will destroy your family. I will remove every male in Ahab's family from Israel, whether slave or free.
I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah. You made Israel sin, and you made Me angry.
The LORD also says about Jezebel: Dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.
Anyone of Ahab's family who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs. Anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by birds of the sky."
No one was like Ahab. He sold himself to do evil in the LORD's eyes, because his wife Jezebel led him to do it.
He did very bad things by going after fake gods, like the Amorites did. The LORD had driven them out before the people of Israel.
When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes. He put rough cloth on his skin. He did not eat. He lay in rough cloth and walked slowly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the man from Tishbe.
It said, "Have you seen how Ahab is sorry before Me? Because he is sorry before Me, I will not bring this trouble in his days. I will bring it on his house in his son's days."
For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.
In the third year, Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, went to see the king of Israel.
The king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth-gilead is ours? We have not taken it back from the king of Aram."
Then he said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to fight at Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat said, "I am like you. My people are like your people. My horses are like your horses."
Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please ask the the LORD what to do today."

The king of Israel gathered about four hundred prophets. He asked them, "Should I go to war at Ramoth-gilead, or should I wait?" The prophets said, "Go up. The Lord will give it into the king's hand."
Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not another prophet of the the LORD here? Let us ask him too."

The king of Israel said, "There is still one man who can ask the the LORD for us. But I hate him, because he never says good things about me. He only says bad things. His name is Micaiah son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat said, "Please do not say that."
The king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, sat on their thrones. They wore royal clothes. They were at the threshing floor by the gate of Samaria. All the prophets were speaking in front of them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made iron horns. He said, "This is what the the LORD says: 'With these you will push Aram until they are destroyed.'"
All the prophets said the same thing: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and win. The the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
The messenger who went to call Micaiah said to him, "Look, all the prophets are saying the same good thing to the king. Please say a good thing too."
Micaiah said, "As surely as the the LORD lives, I will say only what the the LORD tells me."
Micaiah came to the king. The king said, "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead to fight, or should we not?" Micaiah said, "Go up and win. The The LORD will give it into the king's hand."
The king said, "How many times must I make you promise to tell me only the truth in the name of the the LORD?"
Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep with no shepherd. The The LORD said, 'They have no master. Let each one go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you he would not say good things about me? He would only say bad things."

Micaiah said, "So listen to the the LORD's word. I saw the the LORD sitting on His throne. All the armies of heaven stood around Him, on His right and on His left. The The LORD said, 'Who will trick Ahab into going up and dying at Ramoth-gilead?' One said one thing, and one said another. Then a spirit came out and stood before the the LORD. It said, 'I will trick him.' The The LORD asked, 'How?' The spirit said, 'I will go out and put false words in the mouths of all his prophets.' The The LORD said, 'You will trick him. Go and do it.' So now the the LORD has put false words in the mouths of all these prophets. The The LORD has said bad things will happen to you."
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came close and hit Micaiah on the cheek. He said, "Which way did the the LORD's Spirit leave me to speak to you?"
Micaiah said, "You will see on that day when you go into a back room to hide."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah. Send him back to Amon, the city leader, and to Joash, the king's son."
He said, "Say, 'The king says: Put this man in prison. Give him only bread and water until I come home safe.'"
Micaiah said, "If you come home safe, then the the LORD did not speak through me." He also said, "Listen, everyone!"
The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will dress like someone else and go into battle. But you wear your royal clothes." Then the king of Israel dressed like someone else and went into battle.
The king of Aram ordered thirty-two chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, big or small. Fight only with the king of Israel."
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, "That must be the king of Israel." They turned to fight him. Jehoshaphat cried out.
When they saw he was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.
A man shot an arrow without aiming. It hit the king of Israel between parts of his armor. The king said to his chariot driver, "Turn around and get me out of the battle. I am hurt."
The battle got worse that day. The king stood in his chariot facing Aram. Blood ran from his wound into the bottom of the chariot. He died that evening.
At sunset, a shout went through the army: "Every man go to his city. Every man go to his land."
The king died. They brought him to Samaria and buried him there.
They washed his chariot at the pool of Samaria. Dogs licked his blood. Prostitutes washed there. This happened just as the the LORD had said.
The rest of Ahab's acts and all he did are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel. This includes the ivory house he built and the cities he built.
Ahab died and was buried with his fathers. His son Ahaziah became king after him.
Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king. He ruled twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

He followed the way of his father Asa. He did not turn away from it. He did what was right in the the LORD's eyes. But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
The rest of Jehoshaphat's acts, his power, and his wars are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
He removed the rest of the male temple prostitutes who were left from his father Asa's time.
There was no king in Edom. A governor ruled there.
Jehoshaphat built ships to go to Ophir for gold. But they did not go, because the ships were broken at Ezion-geber.
Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants go with your servants." But Jehoshaphat would not.
Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, his father. His son Jehoram became king after him.
Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He ruled two years over Israel.
He did evil in the the LORD's eyes. He followed the way of his father and mother, and the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
He served Baal and worshiped him. He made the the LORD, the God of Israel, angry, just like his father had done.
After King Ahab died, Moab broke away from Israel.
King Ahaziah fell through the screen in his upstairs room in Samaria. He was badly hurt. He sent messengers to ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, "Will I get well from this sickness?"

But an angel of the the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Go and meet the messengers of the king of Samaria. Say to them, 'Is there no God in Israel? Why are you going to ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron?'"
"So this is what the the LORD says: You will not get up from the bed you went to. You will die for sure." Then Elijah went.
The messengers went back to the king. He asked them, "Why did you come back?"

They said, "A man came to meet us. He told us, 'Go back to the king who sent you. Tell him, "This is what the the LORD says: Is there no God in Israel? Why do you send men to ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? So you will not get up from the bed you went to. You will die for sure."'"
The king asked, "What did the man look like?"
They said, "He was a hairy man with a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "That is Elijah the Tishbite."
Then the king sent a captain with fifty men to Elijah. Elijah was sitting on top of a hill. The captain said, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down.'"
Elijah said, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and burn you and your fifty men." Then fire came down from heaven and burned him and his fifty men.
The king sent another captain with fifty men. He said, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down right away.'"
Elijah said, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and burn you and your fifty men." Then God's fire came down from heaven and burned him and his fifty men.
The king sent a third captain with fifty men. He went up and fell on his knees in front of Elijah. He begged, "Man of God, please let my life and the lives of your fifty servants matter to you.
Fire came down from heaven and burned the first two captains and their fifty men. Now please let my life matter to you."
An angel of the the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him. Do not be afraid of the king." So Elijah got up and went down with him to the king.

Elijah said to the king, "This is what the the LORD says: 'Is there no God in Israel? You sent men to ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron. So you will not get up from the bed you went to. You will die for sure.'"
So Ahaziah died, just as the the LORD had said through Elijah. He had no son, so his brother Jehoram became king after him. This was in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
The other things Ahaziah did are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a storm, Elijah and Elisha left Gilgal.
Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here. The LORD has sent me to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.
The young prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha. They said, "Do you know that the LORD will take your master from you today?" Elisha said, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."
Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here. The LORD has sent me to Jericho." Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.
The young prophets at Jericho came to Elisha. They said, "Do you know that the LORD will take your master from you today?" He said, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."
Elijah said, "Please stay here. The LORD has sent me to the Jordan River." Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them walked on.
Fifty men from the young prophets went too. They stood far away and watched. Elijah and Elisha stood by the Jordan River.
Elijah took his cloak and rolled it up. He hit the water with it. The water split to the right and left. The two men walked across on dry ground.
After they crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I can do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said, "Please let me have a double share of your spirit."
Elijah said, "You have asked a hard thing. But if you see me when I am taken from you, it will happen. If not, it will not."
As they kept walking and talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire came between them. Elijah went up to heaven in a storm.
Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father! My father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!" Then he could not see Elijah anymore. He grabbed his clothes and tore them in two.
Elisha picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah. He went back and stood by the Jordan River.
He took Elijah's cloak that had fallen. He hit the water and said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" He hit the water again. The water split to the right and left. Elisha crossed over.
The young prophets from Jericho saw Elisha from far away. They said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed to the ground.

They said to him, "Look, we have fifty strong men. Please let them go look for your master. Maybe the Spirit of the LORD carried him away and threw him on a mountain or in a valley." Elisha said, "Do not send them."
They kept asking until he gave in. Then he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men. They looked for three days but did not find Elijah.
When they came back to him in Jericho, he said to them, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"
The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, sir, this city is a good place to live, as you can see. But the water is bad, and the land does not grow crops."
Elisha said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." They brought it to him.
He went out to the spring of water and threw salt into it. He said, "This is what the LORD says: I have healed this water. It will not cause death or bad land anymore."
The water was healed, just as Elisha had said. It is still good today.
He left there and went up to Bethel. As he walked up the road, some young boys came out of the city. They made fun of him and said, "Go up, bald head! Go up, bald head!"
He turned around and looked at them. He cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two female bears came out of the woods and attacked forty-two of the boys.
He went from there to Mount Carmel. Then he went back to Samaria.
In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel. He ruled in Samaria for twelve years.
He did what was wrong to the LORD. But he was not as bad as his father and mother. He took away the stone pillar of Baal that his father had made.
But he held on to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin. He did not stop.
Mesha, king of Moab, raised sheep. He gave the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool of 100,000 rams.
When Ahab died, the king of Moab stopped obeying the king of Israel.
King Jehoram left Samaria that day and gathered all Israel.

He sent a message to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He said, "The king of Moab has turned against me. Will you go with me to fight Moab?" Jehoshaphat said, "I will go. I am like you. My people are like your people. My horses are like your horses."
Jehoram asked, "Which way should we go?" Jehoshaphat said, "Through the desert of Edom."
So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went. They traveled seven days. There was no water for the army or for the animals with them.
The king of Israel said, "Oh no! The LORD has brought us three kings together so Moab can beat us."
Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here? We can ask the LORD through him." One of the king of Israel's servants said, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He helped Elijah."
Jehoshaphat said, "The LORD speaks through him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to see Elisha.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do you want from me? Go to your father's prophets and your mother's prophets." The king of Israel said, "No! The LORD has brought us three kings together so Moab can beat us."
Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD of Armies lives, I would not even look at you if I did not respect Jehoshaphat, king of Judah."
Elisha said, "But now bring me someone who can play music." While he played, the LORD's power came on Elisha.
Elisha said, "This is what the LORD says: Dig many ditches in this valley.
You will not see wind or rain. But this valley will fill with water. You and your animals can drink it.
This is easy for the LORD. He will also give Moab to you.
You will attack every strong city and every good city. You will cut down every good tree. You will stop all the water springs. You will ruin the good land with stones."
In the morning, at offering time, water came from the direction of Edom. The land filled with water.
All Moab heard that the kings had come to fight. So every man who could fight, and even older men, were called together. They stood at the border.
They got up early. The sun shone on the water. To Moab, the water looked red like blood.
They said, "This is blood! The kings must have fought and killed each other. Now, Moab, let's take their things!"
When they came to Israel's camp, Israel's army got up and fought Moab. The Moabites ran away. The Israelites chased them and kept fighting them in the land.

They destroyed the cities. They threw stones on the good land until it was full. They stopped up the water springs. They cut down every good tree. Only the city of Kir Hareseth was left, with its stones. Men with slings surrounded it and attacked it.
The king of Moab saw the battle was too strong for him. He took 700 men with swords to break through to the king of Edom. But they could not.
Then he took his oldest son, who would be king after him. He offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. The Israelites were shocked. They left and went back to their own land.

A woman whose husband was one of the young prophets cried out to Elisha. She said, "My husband, your servant, is dead. You know he feared the LORD. Now the man we owe money to has come to take my two sons as slaves."
Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me what you have in your house." She said, "I have nothing in my house but a little oil."
He said, "Go ask all your neighbors for empty jars. Don't ask for just a few."
He said, "Then go inside and shut the door behind you and your sons. Pour the oil into all those jars. When one jar is full, put it aside."
She left him and shut the door behind her and her sons. Her sons brought jars to her, and she poured the oil.
When the jars were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another jar." He said, "There are no more jars." Then the oil stopped.
She went to the man of God and told him. He said, "Go sell the oil. Pay what you owe. Then you and your sons can live on what is left."
One day Elisha went to Shunem. An important woman lived there. She asked him to eat with her. So whenever he passed by, he stopped there to eat.
She said to her husband, "I know he is a holy man of God. He passes by us all the time."
She said, "Let's make a small room on the roof. Let's put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp there for him. Then when he comes, he can stay there."
One day he came and went up to the room and lay down.
He said to his servant Gehazi, "Call the woman from Shunem." He called her, and she stood before him.
Elisha said, "Tell her, 'You have taken good care of us. What can we do for you? Should we speak to the king or the army leader for you?'" She answered, "I live among my own people."
Elisha asked, "What can we do for her?" Gehazi said, "She has no son, and her husband is old."
He said, "Call her." He called her, and she stood in the doorway.
He said, "At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms." She said, "No, my lord, man of God, please don't lie to me, your servant."
The woman became pregnant. At that time the next year, she had a son, just as Elisha had said.
The boy grew up. One day he went out to his father, who was with the workers in the field.
The boy said to his father, "My head! My head!" His father said to a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
The servant carried him to his mother. He sat on her lap until noon, then he died.
She went up and laid him on the man of God's bed. She shut the door and went out.
She called her husband and said, "Send me one servant and one donkey. I want to go to the man of God and come back."
He said, "Why go today? It is not a new moon or Sabbath." She said, "It's all right."
She saddled the donkey. She told her servant, "Go fast. Don't slow down for me unless I tell you."
She went to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When he saw her far off, he said to Gehazi, "Look, the woman from Shunem is coming."
He said, "Run to meet her. Ask her, 'Are you well? Is your husband well? Is the child well?'" She said, "We are well."

When she reached the man of God on the hill, she grabbed his feet. Gehazi came to push her away. But the man of God said, "Leave her alone. She is very sad. The LORD has kept this from me. He did not tell me."
She said, "Did I ask you for a son, my lord? Didn't I say, 'Don't trick me'?"
He said to Gehazi, "Tuck in your clothes, take my staff, and go. Don't stop to greet anyone. If someone greets you, don't answer. Put my staff on the boy's face."
The boy's mother said, "As surely as the LORD lives and you live, I will not leave you." So he got up and went with her.
Gehazi went ahead and put the staff on the boy's face. But there was no sound and no sign of life. He went back to meet Elisha and said, "The boy has not woken up."
Elisha went into the house. The boy was dead and lying on the bed.
He went in and shut the door behind them both. Then he prayed to the LORD.
He went up and lay on the child. He put his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. The boy's body became warm.
Then he got up and walked back and forth in the house once. Then he went up again and stretched himself over the boy. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
He called Gehazi and said, "Call the woman from Shunem." He called her, and she came. Elisha said, "Take your son."
She came in and fell at his feet. She bowed to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.
Elisha went back to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land. The young prophets sat before him. He told his servant, "Put on the big pot and make stew for the young prophets."

One man went out to the field to gather herbs. He found a wild vine and picked wild gourds. He filled his coat with them. He came back and cut them into the pot of stew. They did not know what they were.
They served the stew to the men. As they ate, they cried out, "The stew is poisoned, man of God!" They could not eat it.
He said, "Bring flour." He threw it into the pot. He said, "Serve it to the people so they can eat." There was nothing wrong with it.
A man from Baal-shalishah brought bread. He had twenty loaves of barley bread and fresh grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."
His servant said, "How can I feed a hundred men with this?" Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat. The LORD says they will eat and have some left."
He set it before them. They ate and had some left, just as the LORD had said.
Naaman was the leader of the army for the king of Aram. He was a great man. His master liked him very much. The LORD had used him to help Aram win. He was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
Bands of soldiers from Aram had taken a young girl from Israel. She worked for Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, "I wish my master could go to the prophet in Samaria. He could heal him of his leprosy."
Naaman went to his master and told him what the girl had said.
The king of Aram said, "Go. I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So Naaman went. He took ten bags of silver, six thousand gold coins, and ten sets of clothes.
He took the letter to the king of Israel. It said, "I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Please heal him of his leprosy."

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes. He said, "Am I God? Can I kill people and make them alive again? Why does he send a man to me to heal his leprosy? He must be trying to start a fight with me."
Elisha, the man of God, heard that the king tore his clothes. He sent a message to the king: "Why did you tear your clothes? Send him to me. Then he will know there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and chariots. He stood at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger to him. The messenger said, "Go wash in the Jordan River seven times. Your skin will be like new, and you will be clean."

But Naaman was angry. He left and said, "I thought he would come out to me. I thought he would stand and call on the name of the the LORD His God. I thought he would wave his hand over the spot and heal the leprosy."
"Are not the rivers of Damascus, the Abana and the Pharpar, better than all the water in Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" He turned and left in anger.
His servants came to him. They said, "Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something big, would you not do it? So you should do this. He only said, 'Wash and be clean.'"
So Naaman went down. He dipped in the Jordan River seven times, just as the man of God said. His skin became like a little child's skin. He was clean.
He went back to the man of God. He and all his men stood before him. Naaman said, "Now I know there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. Please take a gift from your servant."
Elisha said, "As the the LORD lives, I will not take anything." Naaman urged him to take it, but Elisha said no.
Naaman said, "If you will not take it, please let me take two loads of dirt. I will not burn gifts or give sacrifices to other gods anymore. I will give them only to the the LORD."

"May the the LORD forgive me for this one thing. When my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship, he leans on my arm. I have to bow there too. May the the LORD forgive me when I bow in the temple of Rimmon."
Elisha said, "Go in peace." So Naaman left him and went a short way.
Gehazi, Elisha's helper, said, "My master let Naaman go. He did not take what Naaman brought. As the the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him."
So Gehazi chased Naaman. Naaman saw him running. He got down from his chariot to meet him. He said, "Is everything all right?"

Gehazi said, "Everything is all right. My master sent me. He said, 'Two young men from the group of prophets came from the hills of Ephraim. Please give them one large piece of silver and two sets of clothes.'"
Naaman said, "Please take two pieces of silver." He urged him. He tied two pieces of silver in two bags. He gave them and two sets of clothes to two of his servants. They carried them for Gehazi.
When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the things from the servants. He put them in the house. Then he sent the men away, and they left.
Then Gehazi went in and stood before his master. Elisha said, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" Gehazi said, "I did not go anywhere."
Elisha said, "My heart went with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you. Is this a time to get money, clothes, olive fields, vineyards, sheep, cows, and servants?"
"So Naaman's leprosy will stick to you and your children forever." Gehazi left. His skin was white like snow.
The group of prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we live with you is too small for us."
They said, "Let us go to the Jordan River. Each of us can take one log. We will build a place to live there." Elisha said, "Go."
One of them said, "Please come with your servants." Elisha said, "I will go."
So he went with them. They came to the Jordan and cut down trees.
As one man was cutting a log, the iron axe head fell into the water. He cried out, "Oh no, my master! It was borrowed!"
Elisha asked, "Where did it fall?" The man showed him the place. Elisha cut a stick and threw it there. The iron floated.
Elisha said, "Pick it up." The man reached out his hand and took it.
The king of Aram was at war with Israel. He talked with his servants. He said, "We will camp at a certain place."
But the man of God sent a message to the king of Israel. He said, "Be careful. Do not pass by that place, because the Arameans are coming down there."
The king of Israel sent men to the place the man of God warned him about. He kept watch there. This happened more than once or twice.
The king of Aram was upset about this. He called his servants and said, "Tell me! Which of us is on the side of the king of Israel?"
One servant said, "None of us, my lord the king. Elisha the prophet in Israel tells the king of Israel the words you say in your bedroom."
The king said, "Go and see where he is. I will send men to get him." They told him, "He is in Dothan."
So he sent horses, chariots, and a strong army there. They came at night and surrounded the city.
Elisha's helper got up early. He went out and saw an army with horses and chariots all around the city. He said, "Oh no, my master! What shall we do?"
Elisha said, "Do not be afraid. Those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
Elisha prayed, "The LORD, please open his eyes so he can see." The LORD opened the young man's eyes. He saw the hill full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
When the Arameans came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD. He said, "Please strike this nation with blindness." The LORD struck them with blindness, just as Elisha said.
Elisha said to them, "This is not the right road, and this is not the right city. Follow me. I will lead you to the man you are looking for." He led them to Samaria.
When they reached Samaria, Elisha said, "The LORD, open their eyes so they can see." The LORD opened their eyes. They saw they were in the middle of Samaria.
The king of Israel saw them. He said to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down?"
Elisha said, "Do not strike them. You would not strike men you captured with your sword and bow. Put bread and water in front of them. Let them eat and drink. Then let them go back to their master."
The king made a big feast for them. They ate and drank. Then he sent them back to their master. After that, small groups of Arameans did not come into Israel again.
Later, Ben-Hadad king of Aram gathered all his army. He went up and surrounded Samaria.
There was a terrible famine in Samaria. The city was under attack. A donkey's head cost 80 pieces of silver. A small cup of dove droppings cost 5 pieces of silver.
The king of Israel was walking on the wall. A woman cried out to him, "Help, my lord the king!"
He said, "If the LORD does not help you, how can I help you? I have no food from the threshing floor and no wine from the winepress."
The king asked her, "What is wrong?" She said, "The other woman told me to give her my son. She said we could eat him today and eat her son tomorrow."
She said, "So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I asked her to give me her son so we could eat him, but she hid her son."
When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his clothes. He was walking on the wall. The people saw he wore sackcloth under his clothes.
He said, "May God punish me if Elisha son of Shaphat still has his head today!"

Elisha was sitting in his house. The elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man ahead. Before the messenger came, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent someone to cut off my head? When the messenger comes, shut the door. Hold him at the door. Don't you hear his master's feet behind him?"
While he was still speaking, the messenger came down to him. The messenger said, "This trouble is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

Elisha said, "Listen to the word of the the LORD. The The LORD says, 'Tomorrow at this time, a basket of fine flour will cost one coin. Two baskets of barley will cost one coin. This will happen at the gate of Samaria.'"

The officer who helped the king said to the man of God, "Look! Even if the the LORD opened windows in heaven, could this happen?" Elisha said, "You will see it with your eyes. But you will not eat it."
Four men had a bad skin disease. They sat at the city gate. They said to each other, "Why are we sitting here until we die?
If we go into the city, we will die because there is no food. If we stay here, we will die too. Let's go to the Syrian camp. If they let us live, we live. If they kill us, we die anyway."
They got up when it was dark. They went to the Syrian camp. When they got to the edge of the camp, no one was there.

The The LORD had made the Syrian army hear a loud noise. It sounded like chariots, horses, and a big army. They said to each other, "The king of Israel hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack us!"
So they got up and ran away in the dark. They left their tents, horses, and donkeys. The camp was just as it was. They ran to save their lives.

The sick men came to the edge of the camp. They went into one tent. They ate and drank. They took silver, gold, and clothes. They hid them. Then they went into another tent. They took things and hid them too.
They said to each other, "We are not doing right. Today is a good news day. We should not keep quiet. If we wait until morning, trouble will come to us. Let's go and tell the king's family."

They came to the city gate. They called to the gatekeeper. They said, "We went to the Syrian camp. No one is there. We did not hear a person. The horses and donkeys are tied up. The tents are still there."
The gatekeeper called out. He told the king inside.

The king got up at night. He said to his servants, "I will tell you what the Syrians did to us. They know we are hungry. So they left the camp to hide in the field. They think, 'When the people come out of the city, we will catch them alive. Then we will get into the city.'"
One servant said, "Please let us take five of the horses still in the city. They are few, like the people left. Let us send them to look."
So they took two chariot horses. The king sent men after the Syrian camp. He said, "Go and look."
They went after them to the Jordan River. The whole road was full of clothes and things. The Syrians had thrown them away when they ran fast. The messengers came back and told the king.
The people went out. They took things from the Syrian camp. Then a basket of fine flour cost one coin. Two baskets of barley cost one coin. This happened just as the the LORD had said.
The king had put the officer who leaned on his arm in charge of the gate. The people walked on him at the gate, and he died. This happened just as the man of God had said when the king came to him.
The man of God had said to the king, "Tomorrow at this time, two baskets of barley will cost one coin. A basket of fine flour will cost one coin. This will be at the gate of Samaria."

The officer had answered the man of God. He said, "Look! Even if the the LORD opened windows in heaven, could this happen?" The man of God said, "You will see it with your eyes. But you will not eat it."
That is what happened to him. The people walked on him at the gate, and he died.
Elisha said to the woman whose son he brought back to life, “Get up. Take your family and go live where you can. The LORD says there will be no food in this land for seven years.”
The woman got up and did what God’s man said. She took her family and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
After seven years, the woman came back from the land of the Philistines. She went to the king to ask for her house and her land back.
The king was talking to Gehazi, the helper of God’s man. He said, “Tell me all the big things Elisha has done.”

While Gehazi told the king how Elisha brought a dead man back to life, the woman came to ask the king for her house and land. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman. This is her son. Elisha brought him back to life.”
The king asked the woman about it. She told him. Then the king told one of his officers, “Give back everything that was hers. Give back all the food from her fields from the day she left until now.”
Elisha went to Damascus. Ben-hadad, the king of Aram, was sick. People told him, “God’s man has come here.”
The king said to Hazael, “Take a gift with you. Go meet God’s man. Ask the LORD through him, ‘Will I get better from this sickness?’”

Hazael went to meet him. He took a gift with him: forty camel loads of the best things from Damascus. He stood in front of Elisha and said, “Your son Ben-hadad, king of Aram, sent me to you. He asks, ‘Will I get better from this sickness?’”
Elisha said to him, “Go tell him, ‘You will get better.’ But the LORD has shown me that he will die.”
Elisha stared at Hazael until Hazael felt ashamed. Then God’s man cried.

Hazael said, “Why are you crying, my lord?” Elisha said, “Because I know the bad things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn their strong towns. You will kill their young men with swords. You will kill their little children and hurt their pregnant women.”
Hazael said, “I am only a dog. How could I do such a big thing?” Elisha said, “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram.”
Hazael left Elisha and went back to his master. The king asked, “What did Elisha say to you?” Hazael said, “He told me you would get better.”
The next day Hazael took a blanket, dipped it in water, and put it over Ben-hadad’s face. Ben-hadad died. Then Hazael became king.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah. Jehoshaphat was king of Judah then.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.
He followed the bad ways of the kings of Israel, like Ahab’s family. He married Ahab’s daughter. He did what was wrong in the eyes of the LORD.
But the LORD did not want to destroy Judah. He kept His promise to David. He promised that someone from David’s family would always be king.
While Jehoram was king, Edom broke free from Judah’s rule. They chose their own king.
Jehoram went to Zair with all his war carts. The Edomites surrounded him and his army leaders. But he attacked at night and beat them. Then his army ran home.
Edom is still free from Judah today. At that time, Libnah also broke free.
The rest of what Jehoram did is written in the book of the kings of Judah.
Jehoram died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. His son Ahaziah became king.
Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for one year. His mother was Athaliah. She was the granddaughter of Omri, king of Israel.
He followed the bad ways of Ahab’s family. He did what was wrong in the eyes of the LORD, like Ahab’s family did. He was married into Ahab’s family.
He went with Joram son of Ahab to fight Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth-gilead. The men of Aram hurt Joram.

King Joram went back to Jezreel to heal from the wounds the men of Aram gave him at Ramah. He was fighting Hazael, king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went to Jezreel to see Joram son of Ahab, because Joram was sick.
The prophet Elisha called one of the younger prophets. He said, "Tie up your clothes and take this little jar of oil in your hand. Go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you get there, look for Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Bring him away from his friends. Take him to a private room.
Pour the oil on his head. Say, 'The LORD says, "I have chosen you to be king of Israel."' Then open the door and run. Do not wait."
The young prophet went to Ramoth-gilead. He found the army leaders sitting together. "Captain, I have a message for you." Jehu asked, "For which one of us?"
Jehu stood up and went inside. The prophet poured oil on his head. He said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says, 'I have chosen you to be king over the LORD's people, over Israel.'"
The prophet said, "You must destroy the family of Ahab, your king. I will punish them for killing My prophets and all the LORD's servants. Jezebel is to blame.
Every man and boy in Ahab's family will die. I will destroy every one of them, slave or free, in Israel.
I will make Ahab's family like the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah.
Dogs will eat Jezebel in the field at Jezreel. No one will bury her." Then he opened the door and ran away.
Jehu went out to his lord's servants. They asked, "Is everything all right? Why did this crazy man come to you?" Jehu said, "You know the man and his talk." They said, "That is not true! Tell us."
Jehu said, "He said this to me: 'The LORD says, "I have chosen you to be king of Israel."'"
They hurried. Each man took off his coat and put it under Jehu on the steps. They blew a trumpet and shouted, "Jehu is king!"
Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, had joined together against Joram. Joram and all Israel had been guarding Ramoth-gilead from Hazael, king of Aram.

King Joram had gone back to Jezreel to get well from wounds the army of Aram gave him while fighting Hazael, king of Aram. Jehu said, "If you are with me, do not let anyone leave the city to carry news to Jezreel."
Jehu rode to Jezreel, because Joram was there. Ahaziah, king of Judah, had come down to see Joram.
The watchman on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's men coming. He said, "I see a group coming." Joram said, "Send a horseman to meet them. Ask if they come in peace."

A horseman rode out and said, "The king asks, 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu said, "This is not your business. Fall in behind me." The watchman said, "The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back."
Joram sent a second horseman. He came to them and said the same thing. Jehu answered, "Fall in behind me."
The watchman said, "He reached them too, but he is not coming back. The way the chariot is driven looks like Jehu, son of Nimshi. He drives like a crazy man."
Joram said, "Get ready." His chariot was made ready. Joram, king of Israel, and Ahaziah, king of Judah, each rode out in his chariot to meet Jehu. They met him at the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.

When Joram saw Jehu, he asked, "Do you come in peace, Jehu?" Jehu answered, "How can there be peace while your mother Jezebel keeps sinning and using evil magic?" Joram turned his chariot to run. He shouted to Ahaziah, "It's a trap, Ahaziah!"
Jehu pulled his bow as hard as he could and shot Joram between his shoulders. The arrow went out through his heart. Joram sank down in his chariot.
Jehu said to Bidkar, his officer, "Pick him up and throw him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember when you and I rode together behind Ahab, his father.

The LORD said this against him: 'I saw the blood of Naboth and his sons yesterday,' says the LORD. 'I will pay you back in this same field,' says the LORD. Now throw him into the field, just as the LORD said."

Ahaziah, king of Judah, saw what happened. He ran toward Beth-haggan. Jehu chased him and said, "Shoot him too!" They shot him in his chariot on the road up to Gur near Ibleam. He got away to Megiddo and died there.
His servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem. They buried him with his fathers in the city of David.
Ahaziah became king of Judah in the eleventh year of Joram, son of Ahab.
Jehu came to Jezreel. Jezebel heard about it. She painted her eyes, fixed her hair, and looked out the window.
When Jehu came through the gate, she said, "Do you come in peace, Zimri, killer of his master?"
He looked up at the window and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three servants looked out at him.
He said, "Throw her down!" They threw her down. Her blood splashed on the wall and on the horses. The horses ran over her.
He went in, ate, and drank. Then he said, "Take care of this cursed woman and bury her, for she was a king's daughter."
They went to bury her, but they found only her skull, her feet, and her hands.
They came back and told him. He said, "This is the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah the Tishbite: In the plot of Jezreel dogs will eat Jezebel's flesh.
Jezebel's body will be like waste on the field in the plot of Jezreel, so no one can say, 'This is Jezebel.'"
Ahab had 70 sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters. He sent them to Samaria to the leaders of Jezreel, the old men, and the men who cared for Ahab's sons. The letter said:
When this letter comes to you, your master's sons are with you. You also have chariots, horses, a strong city, and weapons.
Pick the best and right son of your master. Put him on his father's throne. Then fight for your master's family.
But the leaders were very afraid. They said, "Two kings could not stand against Jehu. How can we stand?"

The palace boss, the city leaders, the old men, and the caregivers sent a message to Jehu. They said, "We are your servants. We will do all you say. We will not make anyone king. Do what you think is good."

Jehu wrote again: "If you are on my side, and if you listen to me, take the heads of your master's men. Bring them to me in Jezreel tomorrow at this time." The king's sons were 70 men. The great men of the city had raised them.
When the letter came, they took the king's sons and killed them. They put the heads in baskets. They sent them to Jehu in Jezreel.
A messenger came and told Jehu, "They brought the heads of the king's sons." Jehu said, "Put them in two piles at the gate until morning."
In the morning, Jehu went out. He stood before all the people. He said, "You are not guilty. I made a plan against my master and killed him. But who killed all these men?
Know this: None of the the LORD's words against Ahab's family will fail. The The LORD did what He said through His servant Elijah."
Jehu killed all who were left of Ahab's family in Jezreel. He killed his great men, his close friends, and his priests. He did not leave one.
Then Jehu went to Samaria. On the way he came to Beth-eked of the shepherds.
There Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah, king of Judah. He asked, "Who are you?" They said, "We are brothers of Ahaziah. We are going down to greet the king's sons and the queen mother's sons."
Jehu said, "Take them alive!" They took them alive. Then they killed them at the pit of Beth-eked. There were 42 men. They did not leave one.

Jehu left there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu blessed him. He asked, "Is your heart right with me, as my heart is with you?" Jehonadab said, "Yes." Jehu said, "Give me your hand." He gave his hand. Jehu helped him up into the chariot.
Jehu said, "Come with me. See how I care for the the LORD." They rode in his chariot.
Jehu came to Samaria. He killed all who were left of Ahab's family in Samaria. He destroyed them, just as the the LORD had said through Elijah.
Then Jehu gathered all the people. He said, "Ahab served Baal a little. Jehu will serve him much.

Now call all prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests. Do not miss anyone. I have a big offering for Baal. Anyone who is missing will not live." But Jehu was tricking them. He wanted to destroy the people who served Baal.
Jehu said, "Set apart a special meeting for Baal." So they called it.
Jehu sent word through all Israel. All who served Baal came. Not one was missing. They came into the house of Baal. The house was full from one end to the other.
Jehu said to the man in charge of the clothes room, "Bring out clothes for all who serve Baal." He brought out the clothes.
Jehu and Jehonadab went into the house of Baal. Jehu said to the servants of Baal, "Look around. Make sure no servant of the the LORD is here with you. Only people who serve Baal should be here."
They went in to make offerings. Jehu had placed 80 men outside. He said, "If any man lets one of these men escape, he will die."

When Jehu finished the burnt offering, he said to the guards and officers, "Go in and kill them. Do not let anyone escape." They killed them with swords. They threw the bodies out. Then they went into the inner room of the house of Baal.
They brought out the sacred stones from the house of Baal and burned them.
They tore down the sacred stone of Baal. They tore down the house of Baal. They made it a toilet. It is still that way today.
So Jehu got rid of Baal worship in Israel.
But Jehu did not stop following the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. Jeroboam had led Israel to sin. Jehu kept the golden calves in Bethel and Dan.
The The LORD said to Jehu, "You have done well. You did what is right in My eyes. You did to Ahab's family all that was in My heart. So your sons will be kings of Israel for four generations."
But Jehu did not follow the law of the the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not stop the sins that Jeroboam led Israel into.
In those days the the LORD began to take land from Israel. Hazael hurt Israel in all its land.
He took the land east of the Jordan. He took all the land of Gilead, the land of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh. He took it from Aroer by the Arnon Valley through Gilead and Bashan.
The rest of the things Jehu did, and all his power, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Jehu died and was buried with his fathers in Samaria. his son Jehoahaz became king after him.
Jehu ruled over Israel in Samaria for 28 years.
Athaliah was the mother of King Ahaziah. She saw that her son had died. Then she got up and killed all the king’s family.

But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash, Ahaziah’s son. She stole him from the king’s sons who were being killed. She hid him and his nurse in a bedroom. They hid him from Athaliah, and he was not killed.
Joash was hidden with Jehosheba in the the LORD’s house for six years. Athaliah ruled the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada sent for the captains of the hundreds. They were Carites and guards. He brought them to him at the the LORD’s house. There he made an agreement with them. He made them promise. Then he showed them the king’s son.
He told them, “Here is what you must do. One third of you who come on the Sabbath will guard the king.
One third will be at the Sur Gate. One third will be at the gate behind the guards. You will guard the house and keep it safe.
The rest of you will guard the the LORD’s house around the king.
Stay around the king. Each man must have his weapon in his hand. Anyone who comes near your group must be killed. Stay with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.”
The captains did all that Jehoiada the priest told them. Each man took his own men. Some were coming on the Sabbath, and some were leaving the Sabbath. They came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave the captains the spears and shields that had belonged to King David. They were in the the LORD’s house.
The guards stood with weapons in hand around the king. They stood from the right side of the house to the left side, by the altar and the house.
Jehoiada brought out the king’s son. He put the crown on him. He gave him the law. They made him king and anointed him. They clapped their hands and said, “Long live the king!”
Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people. She went to the people in the the LORD’s house.

She saw the king standing by the pillar, as was the custom. The captains and trumpeters were by the king. All the people were happy and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, “Treason! Treason!”
Jehoiada the priest gave an order to the captains who were in charge of the army. He said, “Take her out past the soldiers. Kill anyone who follows her. Do not kill her in the the LORD’s house.”
They grabbed her. She went by the way the horses go into the king’s house. There they killed her.
Jehoiada made an agreement between the the LORD and the king and the people. They would be the the LORD’s people. He also made an agreement between the king and the people.

All the people went to the house of Baal. They tore it down. They broke his altars and idols into pieces. They killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars. Then the priest set guards over the the LORD’s house.

Jehoiada took the captains, the Carites, the guards, and all the people. They brought the king down from the the LORD’s house. They went by the guards’ gate to the king’s house. Joash sat on the king’s throne.
All the people were happy. The city was quiet. They killed Athaliah with a sword at the king’s house.
Joash was seven years old when he became king.
In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother’s name was Zibiah. She was from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days Jehoiada the priest taught him.
But the high places were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.

Joash said to the priests, “Collect all the money brought as holy gifts into the house of the LORD. This includes the money people paid to be counted, money promised to God, and any money people choose to bring to the the LORD’s house.
