Each priest should take the money from the people he knows and use it to fix any damage found in the temple.”
But by the twenty-third year of King Joash’s rule, the priests still had not fixed the damage to the temple.

So King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests. He asked, “Why have you not fixed the damage to the temple? From now on, do not take money from the people you know. Give it for the repair of the temple.”
The priests agreed not to take money from the people or to fix the temple themselves.

Then Jehoiada the priest took a box. He made a hole in its lid. He put it beside the altar, on the right side as you enter the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the door put all the money brought into the the LORD’s house into the box.
When they saw a lot of money in the box, the king’s writer and the high priest went up. They counted the money in the the LORD’s house. They put it in bags.
They gave the counted money to the men in charge of the work on the the LORD’s house. They paid the carpenters and builders who worked there.
They also paid stone workers and bought wood and cut stone to fix the damage. They paid for everything needed to make the house strong again.
But the money brought into the the LORD’s house was not used to make silver bowls, lamp trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any other gold or silver things for the house.
Instead, they paid the workers, who used it to repair the the LORD’s house.
Also, they did not ask the men who handled the money to show records. Those men were honest and faithful.
Money from guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought into the the LORD’s house. It belonged to the priests.
At that time, Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath. He captured it. Then he decided to attack Jerusalem.

So King Joash of Judah took all the holy things his fathers had given: Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, kings of Judah. He also took his own holy things and all the gold in the storehouses of the the LORD’s house and the king’s palace. He sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then Hazael left Jerusalem.
The rest of what Joash did is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
His servants made a plan against him. They killed Joash at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.
His servants Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer struck him, and he died. They buried him with his fathers in the City of David. His son Amaziah became king after him.
In the twenty-third year of Joash, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for seventeen years.
He did what was wrong in the eyes of the LORD. He followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel to sin. Jehoahaz did not turn away from those sins.
So The LORD was very angry with Israel. He let Hazael, king of Aram, and Ben-Hadad, Hazael’s son, hurt them for a long time.
Then Jehoahaz begged the LORD for help. The LORD listened to him, because He saw how hard the king of Aram was on Israel.
The LORD gave Israel a rescuer. The people got free from Aram’s power. They went back to their tents, like before.
But Israel still did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam’s family. They kept doing the same wrong things. A pole for a false god also stayed in Samaria.
Jehoahaz had only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers left. The king of Aram had killed the rest and crushed them like dust.
The rest of Jehoahaz’s story, and his brave deeds, are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria. His son Joash became king after him.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash, king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for sixteen years.
He did what was wrong in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel to sin.
The rest of Jehoash’s story, and his brave deeds, and his war with Amaziah, king of Judah, are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. Then his son Jeroboam became king.
Elisha was sick with the illness that would kill him. Jehoash, king of Israel, came down to see him. He cried over Elisha and said, "My father, my father! You are Israel’s strength and protection!"
Elisha said to him, "Get a bow and some arrows." So Jehoash got a bow and arrows.
Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." The king put his hand on it. Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands.

Elisha said, "Open the east window." The king opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" The king shot. Then Elisha said, "This is the arrow of victory from the LORD. It is the arrow of victory over Aram. You will beat Aram at Aphek until it is finished."
Then Elisha said, "Take the arrows." The king took them. Elisha said, "Hit the ground." The king hit the ground three times and stopped.
The man of God was angry with him. He said, "You should have hit the ground five or six times. Then you would have beaten Aram until it was finished. But now you will beat Aram only three times."
Elisha died and was buried. At the start of a new year, groups of men from Moab came into the land.
Some people were burying a man. They saw a raiding group coming. They threw the man into Elisha’s tomb. When the man touched Elisha’s bones, he came back to life and stood up.
Hazael, king of Aram, had been hard on Israel all during Jehoahaz’s life.
But the LORD was kind to Israel. He felt sorry for them. He turned back to them because of His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He did not want to destroy them or push them away from Him.
Hazael died. His son Ben-Hadad became king after him.
Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz, took back the cities that Ben-Hadad had taken from his father Jehoahaz in the war. Jehoash beat Ben-Hadad three times and got Israel’s cities back.
In the second year that Joash son of Jehoahaz was king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
He was 25 years old when he began to rule. He ruled 29 years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
Amaziah did what was right in the eyes of the the LORD. But he was not like David his father. He did what his father Joash did.
But he did not take away the high places. The people still gave offerings and burned incense there.
When his power was strong, he killed the servants who had killed his father the king.

But he did not kill their children. He followed what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses. The the LORD had told them, "Fathers must not die for their children. Children must not die for their fathers. Each person dies for his own sin."
Amaziah killed 10,000 men from Edom in the Salt Valley. He took the city of Sela in war. He named it Joktheel. That name is still used today.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel. He said, "Come. Let us meet face to face."
Jehoash king of Israel sent a message back to Amaziah king of Judah. He said, "You are like a small thorn bush, and I am like a big cedar tree. A wild animal can crush a small bush.
You beat Edom, and now your heart is proud. Enjoy your win and stay home. Why start trouble? You will fall, and Judah will fall with you."
But Amaziah did not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up. He and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth Shemesh in Judah.
Judah lost the battle. Every man ran home.

Jehoash king of Israel caught Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash and grandson of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh. He took him to Jerusalem. He broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate. That was about 400 cubits.
He took all the gold and silver. He took all the things found in the house of the the LORD and in the king's store rooms. He took people captive too. Then he went back to Samaria.
The rest of what Jehoash did is written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel. It tells about his power and his war with Amaziah king of Judah.
Jehoash died and was buried with his fathers in Samaria. His son Jeroboam became king after him.
Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived 15 years after Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel died.
The rest of what Amaziah did is written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Some men made a plan against Amaziah in Jerusalem. He ran to Lachish. They sent men after him, and they killed him there.
They carried his body on horses. He was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
All the people of Judah took Azariah. He was 16 years old. They made him king instead of his father Amaziah.
Azariah built the town of Elath and took it back for Judah. This happened after King Amaziah died.
Amaziah son of Joash was king of Judah for 15 years when Jeroboam son of Joash became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled 41 years.
He did evil in the eyes of the the LORD. He did not stop doing the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. That Jeroboam had led Israel to sin.

Jeroboam took back the land of Israel from Lebo Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah. He did this as the the LORD God of Israel said through His servant Jonah son of Amittai. Jonah was the prophet from Gath Hepher.
The The LORD saw how much Israel suffered. Everyone was in trouble. No one was left to help Israel.
The The LORD had not said He would wipe out Israel's name from under heaven. So He saved them through Jeroboam son of Joash.
The rest of what Jeroboam did is written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel. It tells about his power, his wars, and how he took back Damascus and Hamath for Israel.
Jeroboam died and was buried with the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah became king after him.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam, king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.
He was sixteen years old when he became king. He was king in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.
But the hilltop worship places were not taken away. The people still gave gifts and burned incense there.
The LORD made the king sick with leprosy. He had it until he died. He lived in a separate house. His son Jotham was in charge of the palace and judged the people of the land.
The other things Azariah did are written in the book of the kings of Judah.
Azariah died and was buried with his family in the City of David. His son Jotham became king after him.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Samaria. He was king for six months.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his fathers had done. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel to sin.
Shallum son of Jabesh made a secret plan against him. He struck him down and killed him in front of the people. Then he became king in his place.
The other things Zechariah did are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
This was the word the LORD had spoken to Jehu: “Your sons will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.” And it happened.
In the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah, king of Judah, Shallum son of Jabesh became king. He was king in Samaria for one month.
Menahem son of Gad went up from Tirzah to Samaria. He attacked Shallum son of Jabesh and killed him. Then he became king in his place.
The other things Shallum did, and the plan he made, are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah and everyone in it and its borders. They would not open the city gates, so he attacked it. He killed everyone in the city, even women who were going to have babies.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Menahem son of Gad became king of Israel in Samaria. He was king for ten years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel to sin.
Pul, the king of Assyria, came into the land. Menahem gave Pul one thousand talents of silver so that Pul would help him keep his kingdom.
Menahem got the silver from all the rich men of Israel. He made each man give fifty pieces of silver to the king of Assyria. Then the king of Assyria went back and did not stay in the land.
The other things Menahem did are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
Menahem died and was buried with his family. His son Pekahiah became king after him.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king of Israel in Samaria. He was king for two years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel to sin.

Pekah son of Remaliah, one of his officers, made a secret plan against him. With Argob, Arieh, and fifty men from Gilead, he struck him down and killed him in the palace in Samaria. Then he became king in his place.
The other things Pekahiah did are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in Samaria. He was king for twenty years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not stop the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah, king of Israel, Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, came. He took Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali. He carried the people away to Assyria.
Hoshea son of Elah made a secret plan against Pekah son of Remaliah. He struck him down and killed him. Then he became king in his place. This was in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
The other things Pekah did are written in the book of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king. He was king in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother was Jerusha, the daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done.
But the hilltop worship places were not taken away. The people still gave gifts and burned incense there. He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD.
The other things Jotham did are written in the book of the kings of Judah.
In those days the LORD began to send Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham died and was buried with his family in the City of David, his father's city. His son Ahaz became king after him.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king. He ruled sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel. He even sacrificed his son in fire. This was like the terrible things the nations did. The LORD had driven those nations out before the people of Israel.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense on high places, on hills, and under every green tree.
Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came to fight Jerusalem. They surrounded Ahaz, but they could not win against him.
At that time Rezin king of Aram took back Elath for Aram. He drove the people of Judah out of Elath. The men of Aram came to Elath and lived there to this day.
Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. He said, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the king of Aram and from the king of Israel. They are attacking me."
Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the house of the LORD and in the king's treasure rooms. He sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listened to him. He went up to Damascus and took the city. He sent the people away to Kir. He also killed Rezin.
King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. He saw an altar there in Damascus. King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a copy of the altar and a pattern for making it.
Uriah the priest built the altar. He made it just like King Ahaz had sent from Damascus. Uriah the priest finished it before King Ahaz came back from Damascus.
When the king came back from Damascus, he saw the altar. He went to it and offered sacrifices on it.
He burned his burnt offering and his grain offering. He poured out his drink offering. He sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
He moved the bronze altar that stood before the LORD. It had been in front of the temple, between the other altar and the house of the LORD. He put it on the north side of the other altar.

King Ahaz told Uriah the priest, "Burn the morning burnt offering and the evening burnt offering on the large altar. Burn the king's burnt offering and grain offering. Burn the burnt offering and grain offering for all the people of the land. Pour out their drink offerings. Sprinkle on it all the blood from the burnt offerings and all the blood from the sacrifices. But I will use the bronze altar to ask God for guidance."
Uriah the priest did everything King Ahaz had told him to do.
King Ahaz cut the panels off the stands. He took the bowls from them. He took the large bronze bowl down from the bronze bulls under it. He put it on a stone floor.
He moved the covered walkway used on the Sabbath. It had been built in the temple. He also moved the king's outside entrance to the house of the LORD. He did this because of the king of Assyria.
The other things Ahaz did are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Ahaz died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Hezekiah became king after him.
Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in Samaria. This was in the twelfth year that Ahaz was king of Judah. Hoshea ruled for nine years.
He did what was wrong in the eyes of the the LORD. But he was not as bad as the kings of Israel before him.
Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, came against him. Hoshea served him and paid him a yearly payment.

But the king of Assyria found out that Hoshea had a secret plan. Hoshea had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt. He also stopped paying the yearly payment to Assyria. So the king of Assyria arrested him and put him in prison.
The king of Assyria attacked the whole land. He went up to Samaria and surrounded it for three years.

In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria took Samaria. He carried the people of Israel away to Assyria. He settled them in Halah, in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
This happened because the people of Israel sinned against the the LORD their God. He had brought them out of Egypt. He saved them from Pharaoh, king of Egypt. But they worshiped other gods.
They followed the ways of the nations that the the LORD had driven out ahead of them. They also followed the ways that the kings of Israel had made.

The people of Israel did things in secret that were not right against the the LORD their God. They built altars on high places in all their cities. They built them from the watchtower to the walled city.
They set up stone pillars and wooden poles for the goddess Asherah on every high hill and under every green tree.
They burned incense on all the high places. They did this like the nations the the LORD had sent away before them. They did evil things that made the the LORD angry.
They served idols, even though the the LORD had said, "Do not do this."

The LORD warned Israel and Judah. He used all His prophets. He said, "Turn from your evil ways. Keep My commands and rules. Obey all the law I gave your fathers. I sent it to you through My servants the prophets."
But they did not listen. They were stubborn, like their fathers. Their fathers had not believed in the the LORD their God.

They rejected His rules and the agreement He made with their fathers. They ignored His warnings. They followed worthless idols and became worthless themselves. They copied the nations around them, even though the the LORD had told them not to do those things.
They left all the commands of the the LORD their God. They made two metal calves. They made an Asherah pole. They bowed down to all the stars in the sky. They served Baal.
They even made their sons and daughters pass through fire. They used magic and spells. They sold themselves to do evil in the eyes of the the LORD. They made Him angry.
So the the LORD was very angry with Israel. He took them away from His sight. Only the tribe of Judah was left.
But Judah also did not keep the commands of the the LORD their God. They followed the ways that Israel had made.
So the the LORD rejected all the people of Israel. He punished them. He handed them over to robbers. At last, He threw them out of His sight.
He had torn Israel away from the family of David. The people made Jeroboam son of Nebat their king. Jeroboam led Israel away from following the the LORD. He made them sin a great sin.
The people of Israel kept doing all the sins of Jeroboam. They did not stop.
At last, the the LORD removed Israel from His sight, just as He had said through all His servants the prophets. Israel was carried away from their own land to Assyria, and they are still there today.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim. He settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the people of Israel. They took over Samaria and lived in its cities.
At first, they did not fear the the LORD. So the the LORD sent lions among them. The lions killed some of them.

The settlers said to the king of Assyria, "The nations you moved and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the rules of the God of this land. That is why He sent lions among them. The lions are killing them, because they do not know the rules of the God of this land."
Then the king of Assyria gave this order: "Take one of the priests you carried away from there. Let him go back and live there. Let him teach them the rules of the God of this land."
So one of the priests who had been carried away from Samaria came back. He lived in Bethel. He taught them how to fear the the LORD.
But each nation still made its own gods. They put them in the high places that the people of Samaria had made. Each nation did this in the cities where they lived.
The men of Babylon made Succoth Benoth. The men of Cuth made Nergal. The men of Hamath made Ashima.
The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak. The Sepharvites burned their children in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
They also feared the the LORD. But they chose priests from among themselves. These priests offered sacrifices for them in the houses on the high places.
They feared the the LORD, but they also served their own gods. They followed the ways of the nations they had come from.

To this day, they still do as they did at first. They do not truly fear the the LORD. They do not follow the rules, laws, teachings, or commands that the the LORD gave to the children of Jacob. He named them Israel.
The LORD had made an agreement with them. He commanded them, "Do not fear other gods. Do not bow down to them. Do not serve them. Do not offer sacrifices to them."
Instead, fear the the LORD. He is the One who brought you up out of Egypt with great power and a strong arm. Bow down to Him. Offer sacrifices to Him.
Keep the rules, laws, teachings, and commands that He wrote for you. Do them always. Do not fear other gods.
Do not forget the agreement He made with you. Do not fear other gods.
Fear the the LORD your God. He will save you from the hand of all your enemies.
But they did not listen. They kept doing what they had done before.
So these nations feared the the LORD, but they also served their carved idols. Their children and grandchildren did the same. They still do it today, just as their fathers did.
In the third year that Hoshea son of Elah was king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah.
He was 25 years old when he became king. He ruled 29 years in Jerusalem. His mother was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. He did what King David did.

He took away the high places. He broke the stone pillars. He cut down the Asherah poles. He smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. He called it Nehushtan. Up to that time, the people of Israel had burned incense to it.
He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. No king of Judah before him or after him was like him.
He stayed close to the LORD. He did not turn away from Him. He kept the commands the LORD gave through Moses.
The LORD was with him. He did well in everything he did. He said no to the king of Assyria and did not serve him.
He fought the Philistines and won, all the way to Gaza. He took their land from the watchtower to the walled city.
In Hezekiah's fourth year, which was Hoshea's seventh year, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and surrounded it.
After three years, they took the city. This was Hezekiah's sixth year and Hoshea's ninth year.
The king of Assyria took the people of Israel to Assyria. He put them in Halah, by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.
This happened because they did not listen to the LORD their God. They broke His agreement. They did not do what Moses, the LORD's servant, told them. They did not listen or obey.
In Hezekiah's fourteenth year, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the strong cities of Judah and took them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent a message to the king of Assyria at Lachish. He said, "I did wrong. Please go away from me. I will pay whatever you ask." The king of Assyria asked Hezekiah to pay 300 large pieces of silver and 30 large pieces of gold.
Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the LORD's house and in the king's treasure rooms.
At that time, Hezekiah stripped the gold from the doors and doorposts of the LORD's house. He gave it to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria sent Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem. They came with a large army. They went up to Jerusalem and stood by the upper pool, on the road to the washer's field.
They called for the king. Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the house, Shebna the writer, and Joah son of Asaph, who kept the records, came out to them.
Rabshakeh said, "Tell Hezekiah that the great king of Assyria asks what you are trusting in.
He says you say you have plans and power for war, but those are only words. Now who are you trusting in, since you turned against me?
Look, you are trusting in Egypt. Egypt is like a broken stick. If you lean on it, it breaks and cuts your hand. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like to all who trust in him.
If you say, 'We trust in the LORD our God,' isn't He the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah took away? Hezekiah told Judah and Jerusalem, 'Bow down only at this altar in Jerusalem.'
Make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses if you can put riders on them.
How can you turn back even one small officer of my master? You trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen.
Did I come up to destroy this place without the LORD? The LORD said to me, 'Go up and destroy this land.'"
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic. We understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew where the people on the wall can hear."
Rabshakeh said, "Did my master send me to speak these words to your king and to you leaders, and not to the men on the wall? They will suffer and starve with you."
Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew, "Listen to the word of the great king of Assyria!
Do not let Hezekiah fool you. He cannot save you from my hand.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD. He says, 'The LORD will save us. This city will not be given to the king of Assyria.'
Do not listen to Hezekiah. The king of Assyria says, 'Make peace with me. Come out to me. Then each of you will eat from your own vine and fig tree and drink from your own well.'

I will come and take you to a land like your own land. It is a land of grain and new wine, bread and vineyards, olive oil and honey. You will live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he tells you, 'The LORD will save us.'
Did the gods of the nations save their lands from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they save Samaria from me?
Which of all the gods of these lands saved their land from me? So how can the LORD save Jerusalem from me?"
The people were quiet. They did not answer him at all. This was because the king had said, "Do not answer him."

Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the house, Shebna the writer, and Joah son of Asaph, who kept the records, came to Hezekiah. Their clothes were torn. They told him what Rabshakeh had said.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the writer, and the leading priests. They all wore sackcloth. They went to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, "King Hezekiah says this: Today is a day of trouble, correction, and shame. Children are ready to be born, but there is no strength to bring them out.

Maybe the LORD your God heard all the words of the Rabshakeh. His master, the king of Assyria, sent him to make fun of the living God. Maybe the LORD your God will correct him for the words He heard. So pray for the people who are left."
So King Hezekiah's servants went to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master this: The LORD says, 'Do not be afraid of the words you heard. The servants of the king of Assyria insulted Me.
Look, I will put a spirit in him. He will hear a report and go back to his own land. There I will have him killed by the sword.'"
When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he went back and found the king fighting against Libnah.
Now Sennacherib heard a report that Tirhakah, king of Cush, was coming to fight him. So he sent messengers to Hezekiah again. He said:
"Tell Hezekiah king of Judah this: 'Do not let your God, whom you trust, trick you. Do not believe Him when He says Jerusalem will not be given to the king of Assyria.
You have heard what the kings of Assyria did to all the lands. They destroyed them completely. Will you be saved?
Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed save them? Did they save Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'"
Hezekiah took the letters from the messengers and read them. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread them out before the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed before the LORD: "O the LORD, God of Israel, who sits above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
Please listen, O the LORD, and hear. Please open Your eyes, O the LORD, and see. Listen to the words Sennacherib sent to insult the living God.
It is true, O the LORD. The kings of Assyria destroyed the nations and their lands.
"They threw their gods into the fire and destroyed them. Those gods were not really gods. They were only wood and stone, made by human hands.
And now, O the LORD our God, please save us from his hand. Then all the kingdoms of the earth will know that You alone, O the LORD, are God."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Because you prayed to Me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is what the LORD has said against him: The people of Zion hate you and laugh at you. The people of Jerusalem shake their heads at you.
Whom have you insulted and spoken bad things about? Who have you shouted at? You proudly raised your eyes against the Holy One of Israel!

"Through your messengers you insulted the Lord. You said, 'With my many chariots I went up to the high mountains, to the far parts of Lebanon. I cut down its tallest cedar trees and its best cypress trees. I went to its farthest places, to its thickest forest.
I dug wells and drank foreign water. With the bottoms of my feet I dried up all the rivers of Egypt.'
"Have you not heard? Long ago I made this plan. In the old days I planned it. Now I have carried it out. I let you crush strong cities into piles of stones.
So their people, with no strength, are scared and ashamed. They are like plants in a field, like fresh green grass, like grass on a roof that dries up before it grows.
But I know when you sit and when you go out and when you come in. I know how angry you are at Me.
"Because you are angry at Me, and because I have heard your proud talk, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth. I will send you back the way you came.

"This will be a sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself. Next year you will eat what grows from that. But in the third year you will plant and harvest. You will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The people of Judah who are left will grow roots below and bear fruit above.
For out of Jerusalem will come people who are left. Out of Mount Zion will come people who escape. The strong care of the LORD will do this.

"So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not come into this city. He will not shoot an arrow here. He will not come against it with a shield. He will not build a ramp to attack it.
He will go back the way he came. He will not come into this city. The LORD says this.
I will protect this city and save it. I will do it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.'"
That night the angel of the LORD went out and killed 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. In the morning, people saw that they were all dead.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria left. He went back to Nineveh and stayed there.

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword. They ran away to the land of Ararat. Then his son Esarhaddon became king after him.
In those days Hezekiah got sick and was near death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "Put your house in order. You are going to die, and you will not live."
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
He said, "Please, the LORD, remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart. I have done what is good in Your eyes." Then Hezekiah cried and wept bitterly.
Before Isaiah left the middle of the city, the LORD spoke to him.

He said, "Go back and tell Hezekiah, the leader of My people, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. I will heal you. On the third day you will go up to the house of the LORD.
I will add fifteen years to your life. I will save you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will protect this city for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.'"
Isaiah said, "Take a lump of figs." They took it and put it on the boil, and Hezekiah got well.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"
Isaiah said, "This is the sign from the LORD that the LORD will do what He said: The shadow will move ten steps forward, or it will go back ten steps."
Hezekiah said, "It is easy for the shadow to go down ten steps. Let it go back ten steps instead."
Isaiah the prophet prayed to the LORD, and the LORD made the shadow go back ten steps on the steps of Ahaz.
At that time, Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, because he heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

Hezekiah welcomed them and showed them all his treasures: silver, gold, spices, fine oil, his whole storehouse, and everything in his kingdom. There was nothing in his house or in all his rule that he did not show them.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and asked, "What did these men say? Where did they come from?" Hezekiah said, "They came from a far country, from Babylon."
Isaiah asked, "What did they see in your house?" Hezekiah said, "They saw everything in my house. There was nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them."
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Listen to the word of the LORD.
The days are coming when everything in your house, and everything your fathers saved up until now, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
Some of your own sons, who will be born to you, will be taken away. They will become servants in the palace of the king of Babylon."
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD you spoke is good. Will there not be peace and truth in my days?"
The rest of Hezekiah's deeds, and all his power, and how he made the pool and the tunnel and brought water into the city, are written in the book of the kings of Judah.
Hezekiah died and was buried with his fathers. His son Manasseh became king after him.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king. He ruled fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother was named Hephzibah.
He did evil things that the the LORD hated. He acted like the other nations. The The LORD had driven those nations out before the people of Israel.
He rebuilt the hilltop altars his father Hezekiah had destroyed. He set up altars for Baal. He made a wooden Asherah idol, like King Ahab of Israel did. He bowed down to them and served them.
He built altars in the the LORD’s temple. The The LORD had said, “I will put My name in Jerusalem.”
He built altars for all the stars in the sky in both courtyards of the the LORD’s temple.
He even made his son pass through fire. He practiced magic and fortune-telling. He used mediums and spirit readers. He did many evil things that made the the LORD angry.

He put the carved Asherah idol into the the LORD’s temple. The The LORD had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.”
The The LORD said, “I will not make Israel leave the land I gave their fathers, if they are careful to do all I commanded them and all the law My servant Moses gave them.”
But they did not listen. Manasseh led the people to do more evil than the nations the the LORD had destroyed before Israel.
The The LORD spoke through His servants the prophets. He said, “Manasseh, king of Judah, has done these terrible things.
He has done more evil than the Amorites before him. He has led Judah to sin with his idols.
“So the the LORD God of Israel says: I am bringing trouble on Jerusalem and Judah. Everyone who hears about it will be shocked.
“I will treat Jerusalem like I treated Samaria. I will judge it the way I judged Ahab’s family. I will wipe out Jerusalem, like wiping a dish and turning it upside down.
“I will leave the rest of My people. I will give them to their enemies. Their enemies will rob them and take their things.
“They have done evil in My eyes. They have made Me angry since the day their fathers left Egypt. They still do it today.”
Manasseh also killed many innocent people. He filled Jerusalem with blood from one end to the other. Besides this, he led Judah to sin. Judah did evil in the eyes of the the LORD.
The rest of the things Manasseh did, and all his sins, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Manasseh died and was buried with his fathers in the garden of his house, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon became king after him.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king. He ruled two years in Jerusalem. His mother was Meshullemeth. She was the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.
He did evil in the eyes of the the LORD, just like his father Manasseh.
He walked in all the ways his father walked. He served the idols his father served, and he bowed down to them.
He left the the LORD, the God of his fathers. He did not walk in the the LORD’s way.
Amon’s servants made a plan against him. They killed the king in his own house.
The people of the land killed all who had made the plan against King Amon. Then they made his son Josiah king after him.
The rest of the things Amon did are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
They buried him in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. His son Josiah became king after him.
Josiah was eight years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-one years. His mother was Jedidah. She was the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.
Josiah did what pleased the LORD. He followed all the ways of David, his father. He never turned away from them.
In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan to the LORD's temple. Shaphan was the son of Azaliah and the grandson of Meshullam. He was the secretary.
The king said, "Go up to Hilkiah the high priest. Have him count the money brought into the LORD's temple. The guards at the door collected it from the people.
Give it to the men in charge of the work in the LORD's temple. They will pay the workers who fix the temple.
Give it to the woodworkers, the builders, and the stone workers. They will buy wood and stone to fix the temple.
Do not ask them to show how they spend it, because they are honest."
Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "I found the Book of the Law in the LORD's temple." Then Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and Shaphan read it.
Shaphan went to the king and told him what happened. He said, "Your servants took the money found in the temple and gave it to the men in charge of the work in the LORD's temple.
Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." Then Shaphan read it to the king.
When the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes.
The king gave orders to Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the king's servant. He said,

"Go and ask the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah. Ask about the words of this book that was found. The LORD is very angry with us, because our fathers did not obey the words of this book. They did not do all that is written for us."

Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophet. She was the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas. He took care of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in Jerusalem, in the second part of the city. They spoke to her.
She said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says. Tell the man who sent you to Me,
'I will bring trouble on this place and on the people who live here. I will do all the bad things written in the book the king of Judah read.
They left Me and burned incense to other gods. They made Me angry by all they did. So My anger will burn against this place, and it will not go out.'
"But tell the king of Judah who sent you to ask the LORD this: 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says. You heard My words.

Your heart was soft, and you were sorry before the LORD. You heard what I said about this place and its people. I said it would be ruined and cursed. You tore your clothes and cried before Me. So I have heard you, says the LORD.
I will let you die in peace. You will be buried with your fathers. Your eyes will not see all the trouble I will bring on this place.'" Then they brought the answer back to the king.
The king sent for all the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem. They came to him.

The king went up to the house of the the LORD with all the men of Judah. All the people of Jerusalem went with him. The priests and prophets went too. All the people, young and old, were there. He read aloud all the words of the Book of the Agreement that had been found in the house of the the LORD.

The king stood by a pillar. He made an agreement before the the LORD. He promised to follow the the LORD and to keep His rules, His laws, and His commands with all his heart and all his soul. He promised to do what this agreement said. All the people agreed to keep the agreement.

The king told Hilkiah the high priest, the other priests, and the doorkeepers to bring out of the the LORD's temple all the things made for Baal, for Asherah, and for everything in the sky. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron. He carried their ashes to Bethel.

He stopped the false priests. Judah's kings had chosen them to burn incense on the high places in Judah's towns and around Jerusalem. He also stopped those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the stars, and to everything in the sky.

He brought the wooden idol of Asherah out of the the LORD's house. He took it to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem. He burned it there. He ground it to dust. He threw the dust on the graves of the common people.
He tore down the rooms in the the LORD's house where men sold themselves for false worship. Women wove cloth there for the Asherah idol.

He brought all the priests from Judah's towns. He ruined the high places where priests had burned incense. This was from Geba to Beersheba. He also broke down the high places at the gates. These were at the entrance of Joshua's gate. Joshua was the city leader. The high places were on the left side of the city gate.
But the priests of the high places did not serve at the the LORD's altar in Jerusalem. They ate bread without yeast with their fellow priests.
He made Topheth unclean. Topheth was in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He did this so no one would burn his son or daughter as a sacrifice to Molech.

He took away the horses that Judah's kings had given to the sun god. They were at the entrance to the the LORD's house. They were near the room of Nathan-Melech, an officer in the courtyard. He burned the sun chariots.

The kings of Judah had made altars on the roof of Ahaz's upper room. Manasseh had made altars in the two courtyards of the the LORD's house. The king broke them down and crushed them. He threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.

The king made unclean the high places east of Jerusalem. They were south of the Mount of Corruption. Solomon king of Israel had built them for Ashtoreth, the false god of the Sidonians. He also built them for Chemosh, the false god of Moab, and for Milcom, the false god of the Ammonites.
He broke the stone pillars. He cut down the wooden idols. He filled their places with human bones.

He also broke down the altar at Bethel and the high place. Jeroboam son of Nebat had made them. Jeroboam led Israel to sin. Josiah broke down the altar and the high place. He burned the high place and crushed it to dust. He burned the Asherah pole.

Josiah turned and saw tombs on the mountain. He sent men to take bones from the tombs. They burned them on the altar. This made the altar unclean. It happened just as the the LORD had said through the man of God. That man had said these words long ago.

Josiah said, “What tombstone is this that I see?” The men of the city told him, “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah. He said these things would happen to the altar at Bethel. You have done them.”
Josiah said, “Leave him alone. Do not move his bones.” So they left his bones alone, along with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
Josiah also took away all the shrines of the high places in Samaria's towns. Israel's kings had made them to make the the LORD angry. He did to them the same things he had done in Bethel.
He killed all the priests of the high places there on the altars. He burned human bones on them. Then he went back to Jerusalem.
The king told all the people, “Celebrate the Passover for the the LORD your God. Do it the way this Book of the Agreement says.”
No Passover like this had been held since the days of the judges who led Israel. It had not been held in all the days of Israel's kings or Judah's kings.
In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, this Passover was held for the the LORD in Jerusalem.

Josiah also got rid of people who talked to spirits and mediums. He got rid of household gods, idols, and all the terrible things seen in Judah and Jerusalem. He did this to obey the words of the law written in the book. Hilkiah the priest had found that book in the the LORD's house.
No king before him or after him was like him. He turned to the the LORD with all his heart, all his soul, and all his strength. He followed all the Law of Moses.
But the the LORD did not stop being angry. His great anger burned against Judah because of all the things Manasseh had done to make Him angry.

The The LORD said, “I will take Judah away from My sight, just as I took Israel away. I will reject this city of Jerusalem that I chose. I will reject the house where I said, ‘My name will be there.’”
The rest of what Josiah did is written in the book of the history of Judah's kings.
While Josiah was king, Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt went up to fight the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah went to meet him. Pharaoh Necho killed Josiah at Megiddo.

Josiah's servants carried him in a chariot from Megiddo. They brought him to Jerusalem. They buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land took Jehoahaz, Josiah's son. They anointed him and made him king after his father.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king. He ruled three months in Jerusalem. His mother was Hamutal. She was the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did evil in the the LORD's eyes. He did what his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Necho put Jehoahaz in prison at Riblah in the land of Hamath. This kept him from ruling in Jerusalem. Pharaoh also made the land pay one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
Pharaoh Necho made Eliakim, Josiah's son, king instead of Jehoahaz. He changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz to Egypt, and Jehoahaz died there.
Jehoiakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh. But he taxed the land to get the money. He made the people of the land pay silver and gold, each man by his own value, to give to Pharaoh Necho.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother was Zebidah. She was the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
He did evil in the the LORD's eyes. He did what his fathers had done.
While Jehoiakim was king, Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, came to attack. Jehoiakim served him for three years. Then he turned against him.
The LORD sent groups of soldiers from Babylon, Aram, Moab, and Ammon to destroy Judah. This happened just like the LORD said through His prophets.
This happened to Judah because the LORD commanded it. He wanted to take them away from Him. This was because of the sins of King Manasseh and all the bad things he did.
He also killed innocent people. He filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. The LORD would not forgive.
Everything else King Jehoiakim did is written in the book of the kings of Judah.
King Jehoiakim died and was buried with his ancestors. His son Jehoiachin became king after him.
The king of Egypt did not leave his land again. The king of Babylon had taken all the land that belonged to Egypt, from the stream of Egypt to the Euphrates River.
Jehoiachin was 18 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for three months. His mother was Nehushta. She was the daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.
He did what was wrong in the LORD's eyes, just like his father had done.
At that time, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. They surrounded the city.
Nebuchadnezzar himself came to the city while his men kept it surrounded.

King Jehoiachin of Judah, his mother, his servants, his leaders, and his palace workers went out to the king of Babylon. The king of Babylon took them captive. This was in the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's rule.

He took all the treasures from the LORD's house and from the king's house. He cut up all the gold things that King Solomon of Israel had made for the LORD's temple. This happened just as the LORD had said.

He took all the people of Jerusalem away. He took the leaders, the strong soldiers, the craftsmen, and the metal workers. There were ten thousand captives. Only the poorest people were left in the land.
He took King Jehoiachin to Babylon. He also took the king's mother, the king's wives, the officials, and the important men of the land. He led them away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
The king of Babylon took seven thousand strong soldiers and one thousand craftsmen and metal workers. They were all strong men who could fight. He brought them to Babylon.
The king of Babylon made Mattaniah king in Jehoiachin's place. Mattaniah was Jehoiachin's uncle. The king changed Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 11 years. His mother was Hamutal. She was the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
He did what was wrong in the LORD's eyes, just like Jehoiakim had done.
Because of the LORD's anger, He let this happen to Jerusalem and Judah. He sent them away from Him. Zedekiah also turned against the king of Babylon.

Zedekiah had been king for nine years. On the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. He brought all his army. They set up camp around the city and built walls against it.
The city was under attack until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth day of the month, the famine in the city was bad. There was no bread for the people.

Then the city wall was broken. All the soldiers ran away at night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden. The Chaldeans were all around the city. Zedekiah went toward the Arabah.
The Chaldean army chased the king. They caught him on the plains of Jericho. All his soldiers ran away from him.
They took the king to the king of Babylon at Riblah. There they judged him.
They killed Zedekiah's sons while he watched. Then they put out Zedekiah's eyes. They tied him with bronze chains and took him to Babylon.
In the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, on the seventh day of the fifth month, Nebuzaradan came to Jerusalem. He was the captain of the guard and a servant of the king of Babylon.
He burned the house of the LORD, the king's house, and all the houses in Jerusalem. He burned every large house with fire.
All the Chaldean army with the captain of the guard broke down the walls around Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan took the rest of the people who were left in the city. He also took the people who had joined the king of Babylon and the rest of the crowd.
But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest people in the land. They were to take care of the grape fields and farms.
The Chaldeans broke the bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze sea in the house of the LORD. They took the bronze to Babylon.
They took the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, spoons, and all the bronze tools used there.
The captain of the guard took the fire pans and bowls. Some were gold and some were silver.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon made for the house of the LORD had more bronze than anyone could weigh.
One pillar was about 27 feet tall. Its bronze top was about 4.5 feet tall. It had a net of bronze and fruit shapes all around the top. The second pillar was like the first one, with a net.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three doorkeepers.

From the city he took one man who worked in the palace and was in charge of the soldiers. He also took five men who advised the king and were found in the city. He took the army writer who gathered the people. He took sixty men from the people who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan took them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken away from its land.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon chose Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan to rule over the people left in Judah.

When all the army leaders heard this, they and their men came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, Jaazaniah son of Maacath, and their men.
Gedaliah promised them and their men. He said, "Do not be afraid of the Chaldean servants. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon. Then it will go well with you."
In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, from the king's family, came with ten men. They killed Gedaliah, the Jews, and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, small and great, and the army leaders got up and went to Egypt. They were afraid of the Chaldeans.

In the first year of Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, he let Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison. This was in the thirty-seventh year after King Jehoiachin of Judah was taken away.
He spoke kindly to him. He gave him a seat above the seats of the other kings with him in Babylon.
Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes. He ate bread in front of the king all the days of his life.
The king gave him food every day, all the days of his life.
Adam was the father of Seth. Seth was the father of Enosh.
Enosh was the father of Kenan. Kenan was the father of Mahalalel. Mahalalel was the father of Jared.
Jared was the father of Enoch. Enoch was the father of Methuselah. Methuselah was the father of Lamech.
Lamech was the father of Noah. Noah had three sons. Their names were Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Japheth had these sons: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer had these sons: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
Javan had these sons: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
Ham had these sons: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush had these sons: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah had these sons: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was the father of Nimrod. Nimrod became a mighty hero on earth.
Mizraim was the father of the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
He was also the father of the Pathrusim, Casluhim, and Caphtorim. The Philistines came from the Casluhim.
Canaan's first son was Sidon. He also had Heth.
Canaan had these people groups: the Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites.
He had the Hivites, Arkites, and Sinites.
He had the Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.
Shem had these sons: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arphaxad was the father of Shelah. Shelah was the father of Eber.
Eber had two sons. One was Peleg, because the earth was split in his time. The other was Joktan.
Joktan had these sons: Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
He had Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah.
He had Ebal, Abimael, and Sheba.
He had Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were Joktan's sons.
Shem was the father of Arphaxad. Arphaxad was the father of Shelah.
Shelah was the father of Eber. Eber was the father of Peleg. Peleg was the father of Reu.
Reu was the father of Serug. Serug was the father of Nahor. Nahor was the father of Terah.
Terah was the father of Abram. Abram is Abraham.
Abraham had two sons. They were Isaac and Ishmael.
Here are Ishmael's sons: Nebaioth was the first. Then Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam.
Then Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema.
Then Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were Ishmael's sons.
Abraham also had sons by Keturah, another wife. Their sons were Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan had Sheba and Dedan.
Midian had Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these came from Keturah.
Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac had two sons. They were Esau and Israel.
Esau had these sons: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
Eliphaz had these sons: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
Reuel had these sons: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
Seir had these sons: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
Lotan had Hori, Homam, and Timna. Lotan's sister was Timna.
Shobal had Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon had Aiah and Anah.
Anah had Dishon. Dishon had Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
Ezer had Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan had Uz and Aran.
These kings ruled in Edom before Israel had a king. Bela was the son of Beor. His city was Dinhabah.
Bela died. Then Jobab, the son of Zerah from Bozrah, ruled.
Jobab died. Then Husham from the land of Teman ruled.
Husham died. Then Hadad, the son of Bedad, ruled. He beat Midian in the field of Moab. His city was Avith.
Hadad died. Then Samlah from Masrekah ruled.
Samlah died. Then Shaul from Rehoboth by the river ruled.
Shaul died. Then Baal-Hanan, the son of Achbor, ruled.
Baal-Hanan died. Then Hadad ruled. His city was Pau. His wife was Mehetabel. She was the daughter of Matred, and Matred was the daughter of Mezahab.
Hadad died. These were the leaders of Edom: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
Magdiel, and Iram. These were the leaders of Edom.
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three were born to him by the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite woman. Er, Judah's oldest son, was bad in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD killed him.
Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, had Perez and Zerah by him. So Judah had five sons.
The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five in all.
The son of Carmi was Achar, who brought trouble on Israel by taking things set apart for God.
The son of Ethan was Azariah.
The sons born to Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, the leader of the people of Judah.
Nahshon was the father of Salmon, and Salmon was the father of Boaz.
Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse.
Jesse was the father of Eliab, his oldest son; Abinadab, the second; and Shimea, the third.
He was also the father of Nathanel, the fourth; Raddai, the fifth.
Ozem was the sixth, and David was the seventh.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah had three sons: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
Abigail had Amasa. Amasa's father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb, Hezron's son, had children by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth. Her sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath. She had Hur.
Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.
Later, Hezron married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead. He was sixty years old, and she had Segub.
Segub was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead.
But Geshur and Aram took the towns of Jair, along with Kenath and its sixty villages. All these men came from Machir, the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, his wife Abijah had Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, were Ram, the oldest; Bunah; Oren; Ozem; and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram, Jerahmeel's oldest son, were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur's wife was Abihail, and she had Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim. Seled died without children.
The son of Appaim was Ishi. The son of Ishi was Sheshan. The son of Sheshan was Ahlai.
The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother, were Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without children.
The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. These came from Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. He had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter to his servant Jarha. She had Attai.
Attai was the father of Nathan. Nathan was the father of Zabad.
Zabad was the father of Ephlal. Ephlal was the father of Obed.
Obed was the father of Jehu. Jehu was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Helez. Helez was the father of Eleasah.
Eleasah was the father of Sismai. Sismai was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Jekamiah. Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, were Mesha, his oldest son, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema was the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.
Shammai's son was Maon. Maon was the father of Beth-zur.
Caleb's servant wife Ephah had Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.
The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Caleb's servant wife Maacah had Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also had Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Sheva, the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
These were the sons of Caleb. The sons of Hur, Ephrathah's oldest son, were Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim,
Salma, the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph, the father of Beth-gader.
Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, had sons: Haroeh, and half of the Manahathites.
The families of Kiriath-jearim were the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. From these came the Zorathites and Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma were Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.
The families of writers who lived at Jabez were the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
These were David's sons born to him in Hebron. The first son was Amnon. His mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel. The second son was Daniel. His mother was Abigail from Carmel.
The third son was Absalom. His mother was Maacah, daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur. The fourth son was Adonijah. His mother was Haggith.
The fifth son was Shephatiah. His mother was Abital. The sixth son was Ithream. His mother was David's wife Eglah.
Six sons were born to David in Hebron. He ruled there seven years and six months. He also ruled in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
These sons were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. Their mother was Bathshua, daughter of Ammiel.
Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet were born there too.
Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia were also born there.
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet were born there as well. Those nine sons were in addition to the first four.
All these were David's sons. He also had sons by his other wives. Tamar was their sister.
Solomon's son was Rehoboam. Rehoboam's son was Abijah. Abijah's son was Asa. Asa's son was Jehoshaphat.
Jehoshaphat's son was Joram. Joram's son was Ahaziah. Ahaziah's son was Joash.
Joash's son was Amaziah. Amaziah's son was Azariah. Azariah's son was Jotham.
Jotham's son was Ahaz. Ahaz's son was Hezekiah. Hezekiah's son was Manasseh.
Manasseh's son was Amon. Amon's son was Josiah.
Josiah's sons were Johanan, the firstborn; Jehoiakim, the second; Zedekiah, the third; and Shallum, the fourth.
Jehoiakim's sons were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.
Jeconiah, the captive, had a son named Shealtiel.
Jeconiah's other sons were Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
Pedaiah's sons were Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's sons were Meshullam and Hananiah. Shelomith was their sister.
Five more of his sons were Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed.
Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. The sons of Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah are also named.
Shecaniah's son was Shemaiah. Shemaiah's sons were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat. That was six in all.
Neariah's sons were Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam. That was three in all.
Elioenai's sons were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani. That was seven in all.
The sons of Judah were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah was Shobal's son. Reaiah's son was Jahath. Jahath's sons were Ahumai and Lahad. These were the Zorathite family groups.
Etam's sons were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was Gedor's father. Ezer was Hushah's father. These were Hur's sons. Hur was Ephrathah's oldest son and Bethlehem's father.
Ashhur was Tekoa's father. He had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah's sons were Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari.
Helah's sons were Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan.
Koz was Anub's father and Zobebah's father. He was also father of the family groups of Aharhel. Aharhel was Harum's son.
Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez. She said, "I gave birth to him in pain."
Jabez prayed to the God of Israel. He said, "If only You would bless me and make my land bigger! Let Your hand be with me. Keep me from harm, so I will not be in pain." God answered his prayer.
Chelub was Shuhah's brother. Chelub was Mehir's father. Mehir was Eshton's father.
Eshton was father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. Tehinnah was father of Ir-nahash. These were the men of Recah.
Kenaz's sons were Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel's son was Hathath.
Meonothai was Ophrah's father. Seraiah was Joab's father. Joab was father of Ge-harashim. They were craftsmen.
Caleb was Jephunneh's son. Caleb's sons were Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.
Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
Ezra's sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered's wife Bithiah had Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah. Ishbah was father of Eshtemoa.
These were the sons of Pharaoh's daughter Bithiah. Mered married her. His wife from Judah had Jered, Gedor's father; Heber, Soco's father; and Jekuthiel, Zanoah's father.
Hodiah's wife was Naham's sister. Her sons were the father of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's sons were Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
Shelah was Judah's son. Shelah's sons were Er, Lecah's father; Laadah, Mareshah's father; and the family groups of linen workers at Beth-ashbea.
Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph ruled in Moab and Jashubi-lehem. These names come from old records.
They were potters. They lived in Netaim and Gederah. They stayed there and worked for the king.
Simeon's sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shaul's son was Shallum. Shallum's son was Mibsam. Mibsam's son was Mishma.
Mishma's sons were Hammuel, Zaccur, and Shimei.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters. His brothers did not have many children. So their whole family group was not as big as Judah's family group.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, and Hazar-shual.
They also lived in Bilhah, Ezem, and Tolad.
They lived in Bethuel, Hormah, and Ziklag.
They lived in Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim. These were their towns until David was king.
Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan. That is five towns.
They also had all the villages around them, as far as Baal. These were their homes. They kept their family records.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah son of Seraiah son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah,
Ziza son of Shiphi son of Allon son of Jedaiah son of Shimri son of Shemaiah.
These men were leaders in their family groups. Their families grew very big.
They went to the entrance of Gedor, on the east side of the valley. They went to find grass for their sheep.
They found rich, good grass. The land was wide, quiet, and peaceful. Hamites had lived there before.

These men were listed by name. They came in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah. They attacked the Hamites' tents and the Meunites who were there. They destroyed them completely, and they are still gone today. Then they lived there, because there was grass for their sheep.
Five hundred of these Simeonites went to Mount Seir. Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel led them. These four were sons of Ishi.
They defeated the rest of the Amalekites who had escaped. They still live there today.

Reuben was the first son born to Israel. But Reuben lost his first son rights because he slept with his father's wife. So his first son rights went to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel. Reuben was not counted as the first son.
Judah was the strongest of his brothers. A leader came from him. But Joseph got the first son rights.
The sons of Reuben, Israel's first son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Joel's son was Shemaiah. Shemaiah's son was Gog. Gog's son was Shimei.
Shimei's son was Micah. Micah's son was Reaiah. Reaiah's son was Baal.
Baal's son was Beerah. Beerah was the leader of the Reubenites. The king of Assyria, Tiglath-pileser, took him away.
Their relatives were listed by family groups. Jeiel was the leader, and Zechariah was with him.
Bela was the son of Azaz. Azaz was the son of Shema. Shema was the son of Joel. Bela lived in Aroer, Nebo, and Baal-meon.
He lived eastward to the edge of the desert, starting from the Euphrates River. His animals were many in Gilead.
In Saul's time, they fought the Hagrites. The Hagrites lost to them. Then they lived in tents across the east side of Gilead.
The Gadites lived across from them in Bashan, as far as Salcah.
Joel was the leader. Shapham was second. Janai and Shaphat were in Bashan.
Their brothers by father's houses were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber. That is seven.
They were sons of Abihail, son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
Ahi was the son of Abdiel, son of Guni. He was the leader of their fathers' houses.
They lived in Gilead, Bashan, and its towns. They also lived in all the pasture lands of Sharon.
They were all listed in the time of Jotham, king of Judah, and Jeroboam, king of Israel.
The Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh had 44,760 soldiers. They were brave men. They carried shields and swords. They could use bows. They knew how to fight.
They fought the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
They cried to God in the war. They trusted in Him. God listened to them and helped them. The Hagrites and all with them were given into their hands.
They took 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 people as prisoners.
Many died because God helped them win the war. Then they lived there until they were taken away.
Half of Manasseh was very large. They lived in Bashan, Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
Their fathers' leaders were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were brave, famous men.
But they sinned against the God of their fathers. They worshiped the gods of the people in that land. God had destroyed those people before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up Pul, king of Assyria, and Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. They carried away the Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh. They took them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river Gozan. They are still there today.
The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Amram were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar was the father of Phinehas. Phinehas was the father of Abishua.
Abishua was the father of Bukki. Bukki was the father of Uzzi.
Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah was the father of Meraioth.
Meraioth was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah. Azariah was the father of Johanan.
Johanan was the father of Azariah. This Azariah served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah was the father of Amariah. Amariah was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Hilkiah. Hilkiah was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Seraiah. Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak.
Jehozadak was taken away when the the LORD let Nebuchadnezzar carry Judah and Jerusalem into exile.
The sons of Levi were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Gershom were Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite families by their fathers' lines.
Gershom's family line was Libni, then Jahath, then Zimmah.
Then came Joah, then Iddo, then Zerah, then Jeatherai.
Kohath's family line was Amminadab, then Korah, then Assir.
Then came Elkanah, then Ebiasaph, then Assir.
Then came Tahath, then Uriel, then Uzziah, then Saul.
Elkanah had two sons, Amasai and Ahimoth.
Elkanah's family line was Elkanah, then Zophai, then Nahath.
Then came Eliab, then Jeroham, then Elkanah.
Samuel had two sons. Joel was the firstborn, and Abijah was the second.
Merari's family line was Mahli, then Libni, then Shimei, then Uzzah.
Then came Shimea, then Haggiah, then Asaiah.
These are the men David put in charge of music in the the LORD's house after the ark had a resting place.
They sang before the meeting tent until Solomon built the the LORD's house in Jerusalem. Then they did their work in their right order.
Here are the men who stood with their sons. From the Kohathites came Heman the singer. He was the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,
the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,
the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,
the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.
His brother Asaph stood at his right hand. Asaph was the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchijah,
the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,
the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,
the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
On the left stood their brothers, the sons of Merari. Ethan was the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
Their brothers the Levites were given to all the work of the tent, the house of God.

Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place. They burned gifts on the altar for burnt offerings and on the incense altar. They did the work to make Israel right with God, as Moses, God's servant, had told them.
These were Aaron's sons: Eleazar, then Phinehas, then Abishua,
then Bukki, then Uzzi, then Zerahiah,
then Meraioth, then Amariah, then Ahitub,
These were their towns with their borders. The sons of Aaron, the Kohathites, got these towns by lot.
They were given Hebron in Judah, with its fields around it.
But the fields of the city and its villages were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron they gave Hebron, a safe city, and Libnah with its fields, and Jattir and Eshtemoa with their fields.
They also gave Hilen with its fields, Debir with its fields,
Ashan with its fields, and Beth-shemesh with its fields.
From Benjamin's tribe they gave Geba with its fields, Alemeth with its fields, and Anathoth with its fields. That was thirteen towns for their families.
The rest of Kohath's families got ten towns by lot from half of Manasseh's tribe.
The sons of Gershom got thirteen towns from Issachar's tribe, Asher's tribe, Naphtali's tribe, and half of Manasseh's tribe in Bashan.
The sons of Merari got twelve towns by lot from Reuben's tribe, Gad's tribe, and Zebulun's tribe.
The people of Israel gave these towns and their fields to the Levites.
They gave by lot these towns named here from Judah's tribe, Simeon's tribe, and Benjamin's tribe.
Some Kohath families got towns from Ephraim's tribe.
They gave them Shechem, a safe city, in Ephraim's hill country, and Gezer with its fields,
Jokmeam with its fields, Beth-horon with its fields,
