Aijalon with its fields, and Gath-rimmon with its fields.
From half of Manasseh's tribe, they gave Aner with its fields and Bileam with its fields to the rest of Kohath's families.
To Gershom's sons from half of Manasseh's tribe, they gave Golan in Bashan with its fields and Ashtaroth with its fields.
From Issachar's tribe, they gave Kedesh with its fields, Daberath with its fields,
Ramoth with its fields, and Anem with its fields.
From Asher's tribe, they gave Mashal with its fields, Abdon with its fields,
Hukok with its fields, and Rehob with its fields.
From Naphtali's tribe, they gave Kedesh in Galilee with its fields, Hammon with its fields, and Kiriathaim with its fields.
To the rest of Merari's sons from Zebulun's tribe, they gave Rimmono with its fields and Tabor with its fields.
From Reuben's tribe, across the Jordan east of Jericho, they gave Bezer in the desert with its fields, Jahzah with its fields,
Kedemoth with its fields, and Mephaath with its fields.
From Gad's tribe, they gave Ramoth in Gilead with its fields, Mahanaim with its fields,
Heshbon with its fields, and Jazer with its fields.
Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel. They were leaders of their families. In David's time, Tola's family had 22,600 strong soldiers.
Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. These five men were leaders.
Their families had 36,000 soldiers ready for war. They had many wives and children.
The other families of Issachar had 87,000 strong soldiers. All were listed by family records.
Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
Bela's sons were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. These five were family leaders. By family records, Bela's family had 22,034 strong soldiers.
Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.
By family records, their family leaders had 20,200 strong soldiers.
Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
These men were family leaders and strong soldiers. They had 17,200 men ready to fight in war.
Shuppim and Huppim were sons of Ir. Hushim was the son of Aher.
Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were the sons of Bilhah.
Manasseh's sons were Asriel, whom his Aramean second wife bore. She also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife for Huppim and Shuppim. His sister's name was Maacah. Another descendant was Zelophehad, who had daughters.
Machir's wife Maacah had a son named Peresh. His brother was Sheresh. Sheresh's sons were Ulam and Rakem.
Ulam's son was Bedan. These men were from Gilead, the son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh.
Machir's sister Hammoleketh had sons named Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Ephraim's line was Shuthelah, Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, and Tahath.
Zabad was his son, then Shuthelah. Ezer and Elead were also sons. Men from Gath, born in that land, killed them because they came to take their animals.
Ephraim was very sad for a long time. His brothers came to comfort him.
Later, Ephraim went to his wife. She became pregnant and had a son. He named the boy Beriah because trouble came to his home.
His daughter Sheerah built Lower Beth-horon, Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah.
Rephah was his son. Resheph was Rephah's son. Telah was Resheph's son. Tahan was Telah's son.
Ladan was Tahan's son. Ammihud was Ladan's son. Elishama was Ammihud's son.
Nun was Elishama's son. Joshua was Nun's son.
Ephraim's family lived in Bethel and its towns. To the east was Naaran. To the west were Gezer and its towns, Shechem and its towns, and Ayyah and its towns.
Near Manasseh's border were Beth-shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, and Dor and its towns. The sons of Joseph, son of Israel, lived in these places.
Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel. Malchiel was the father of Birzaith.
Heber had sons named Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham. Their sister was Shua.
Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
Shemer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
Shemer's brother Helem had sons named Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Zophah's sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, and Imrah.
Also Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
Jether's sons were Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
Ulla's sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were sons of Asher. They were family leaders and brave soldiers. They were chief leaders. By family records, 26,000 men were ready for war.
Benjamin had Bela as his first son. Ashbel was his second son. Aharah was his third son.
Nohah was his fourth son. Rapha was his fifth son.
Bela's sons were Addar, Gera, and Abihud.
He also had Abishua, Naaman, and Ahoah.
He also had Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These were Ehud's sons. They were leaders of families who lived in Geba. They were taken to Manahath.
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera took them away. Gera was the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim had children in Moab after he sent his wives Hushim and Baara away.
From Hushim he had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, and Malcam.
He also had Jeuz, Sakiah, and Mirmah. These sons were leaders of families.
From Hushim he had Abitub and Elpaal.
Elpaal's sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed. Elpaal built Ono and Lod and the nearby towns.
Beriah and Shema were leaders of families in Aijalon. They chased away the people of Gath.
Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth were leaders too.
Zebadiah, Arad, and Eder were leaders too.
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were sons of Beriah.
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, and Heber were also leaders.
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were sons of Elpaal.
Jakim, Zichri, and Zabdi were leaders.
Elienai, Zillethai, and Eliel were leaders too.
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were sons of Shimei.
Ishpan, Eber, and Eliel were leaders.
Abdon, Zichri, and Hanan were leaders.
Hananiah, Elam, and Anthothijah were leaders.
Iphdeiah and Penuel were sons of Shashak.
Shamsherai, Shehariah, and Athaliah were leaders.
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were sons of Jeroham.
All these men were leaders of families. They lived in Jerusalem with their families.
Gibeon's father lived in Gibeon. His wife was Maacah.
His first son was Abdon. Then came Zur, Kish, Baal, and Nadab.
He also had Gedor, Ahio, and Zechar.
Mikloth was the father of Shimeah. They lived near their brothers in Jerusalem.
Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal. Merib-baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz was the father of Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea. Raphah was his son. Eleasah was his son. Azel was his son.
Azel had six sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were Azel's sons.
His brother Eshek had sons too. Ulam was the first son. Jeush was the second son. Eliphelet was the third son.
Ulam's sons were strong men who used bows. They had many sons and grandsons. There were 150 of them. All these were Benjamin's sons.
All the people of Israel were listed by family. Their names were written in the book of the kings of Israel. Judah was taken to Babylon because they did wrong.
The first people to live again in their own towns were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
Some people from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.
Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, came from Perez, who was a son of Judah.
From the people of Shiloh came Asaiah, the firstborn son, and his sons.
From the family of Zerah came Jeuel and his relatives. There were 690 of them.
From Benjamin came Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah.
Also Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.
These men were family leaders. They and their relatives numbered 956.
From the priests came Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
Also Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub. He was the leader in God's house.
Also Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer.
They and their relatives were family leaders. There were 1,760 of them. They were strong men who did the work in God's house.
From the Levites came Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah. He was from the family of Merari.
Also Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph.
Also Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah. He lived in the villages of Netophah.
The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was the leader.
Until then they were at the king's gate on the east. They were gatekeepers for the Levite camps.

Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his relatives from the family of Korah, were in charge of the work. They guarded the entrances to the tent. Their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the camp of the LORD.
Long ago Phinehas son of Eleazar had been their leader, and the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

All these chosen men were gatekeepers at the doorways. There were 212 of them. They were listed by family in their villages. David and Samuel the prophet had chosen them because they could be trusted.
They and their sons guarded the gates of the LORD's house, the tent.
The gatekeepers were on the four sides: east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives came from their villages at set times to help them for seven days.
The four chief gatekeepers were Levites. They were trusted to be over the rooms and treasures of God's house.
They stayed around God's house because they had to guard it. They had the key and opened it every morning.
Some of them were in charge of the tools used in worship. They counted them when they came in and when they went out.
Others were in charge of the holy things, and of the flour, wine, oil, incense, and spices.
Some priests' sons mixed the spices.
Mattithiah, a Levite and firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was trusted to make the flat bread.
Some people from the family of Kohath, their relatives, were in charge of the bread set out each Sabbath.
The singers, leaders of the Levites, stayed in the rooms and were free from other work, because they worked day and night.
These men were leaders of the Levites by their families. They lived in Jerusalem.
In Gibeon lived Jeiel, father of Gibeon. His wife's name was Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab.
Also Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner was the father of Kish, Kish the father of Saul, and Saul the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.
Ahaz was the father of Jarah; Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea; Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
Azel had six sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel's sons.
The Philistines fought against Israel. The men of Israel ran away from the Philistines. Many fell dead on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines went after Saul and his sons. They killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, who were Saul's sons.
The battle got hard for Saul. The archers caught up to him. They shot at him, and he was badly hurt.

Saul said to the man who carried his armor, "Draw your sword and kill me with it. I do not want those men who do not follow God to come and hurt me." But the man was very afraid, so he would not do it. Then Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
When the man who carried his armor saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died.
So Saul died. His three sons died too. All of his family died with him.
All the men of Israel in the valley saw that Israel ran away. They saw that Saul and his sons were dead. So they left their towns and ran away too. The Philistines came and lived in those towns.
The next day, the Philistines came to take things from the dead men. They found Saul and his sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
They took his armor and his head. They sent them all around the land of the Philistines. They wanted to tell their idols and their people.
They put his armor in the house of their gods. They put his head in the house of Dagon.
The people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul.
All the brave men got up. They took the bodies of Saul and his sons. They brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under a big tree in Jabesh. Then they did not eat for seven days.
Saul died because he turned away from the the LORD. He did not obey the the LORD's word. He also asked a person who talked to spirits for help.
Saul did not ask the the LORD for help. So the the LORD put him to death. The the LORD gave the kingdom to David, the son of Jesse.
All Israel came together to David at Hebron. They said, "Look, we are your own family.
Even when Saul was king, you led Israel out and brought them back. The the LORD your God said to you, 'You will take care of My people Israel. You will be the leader over My people Israel.'"

All the leaders of Israel came to King David at Hebron. David made an agreement with them before the the LORD. They poured oil on David to make him king over Israel. This happened just as the the LORD had said through Samuel.
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem. It was called Jebus then. The Jebusites lived there.
The people living there said to David, "You will not come in here." But David took the strong place of Zion. That place is called the City of David.
David said, "The first man to hit the Jebusites will be the leader and commander." Joab, son of Zeruiah, went up first. So he became the leader.
David lived in the strong place. That is why people call it the City of David.
David built the city all around. He built from the Millo to the wall around it. Joab fixed the rest of the city.
David became greater and greater. The LORD of armies was with him.
These were the leaders of David's brave men. They helped make him strong in his kingdom. All Israel helped make him king. This happened as the the LORD had said about Israel.
This is how many brave men David had. Jashobeam, son of Hachmoni, was leader of the thirty. He raised his spear and killed three hundred men at one time.
After him came Eleazar, son of Dodo. He was from Ahoah. He was one of the three brave men.
He was with David at Pas-dammim. The Philistines gathered there for war. The field was full of barley. The people ran away from the Philistines.
But they stood in the middle of the field. They saved it. They hit the Philistines. The LORD helped them win a great battle.
Three of the thirty leaders went down to David. He was at the rock by the cave of Adullam. The Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was in the strong place. The Philistines had soldiers in Bethlehem.
David wanted water. He said, "I wish someone would give me water to drink from the well in Bethlehem by the gate!"
So the three men broke through the Philistine camp. They got water from the well in Bethlehem by the gate. They carried it to David. But David would not drink it. He poured it out to the the LORD.

David said, "No! I will not do that. My God, it would be wrong. This water is like the blood of these men. They risked their lives to bring it." So he would not drink it. These three brave men did this.
Abishai, brother of Joab, was leader of the three. He raised his spear and killed three hundred men. He was famous among the three.
He was honored more than the thirty. He became their leader. But he was not one of the three.
Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, was a brave man from Kabzeel. He did great things. He killed two sons of Ariel from Moab. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

He killed a big Egyptian man. The Egyptian was about seven and a half feet tall. He had a spear like a weaver's beam. Benaiah went down to him with a stick. He took the spear from the Egyptian's hand. Then he killed the Egyptian with his own spear.
Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, did these things. He was famous among the three brave men.
He was honored more than the thirty. But he was not one of the three. David put him in charge of his guards.
Here are other brave soldiers: Asahel, brother of Joab; Elhanan, son of Dodo, from Bethlehem;
Shammoth the Harorite; Helez the Pelonite;
Ira, son of Ikkesh, from Tekoa; Abiezer from Anathoth;
Sibbecai the Hushathite; Ilai the Ahohite;
Maharai from Netophah; Heled, son of Baanah, from Netophah;
Ithai, son of Ribai, from Gibeah of the Benjaminites; Benaiah from Pirathon.
Hurai from the valleys of Gaash; Abiel the Arbathite;
Azmaveth from Bahurim; Eliahba from Shaalbon;
the sons of Hashem from Gizon; Jonathan, son of Shagee, the Hararite;
Ahiam, son of Sacar, the Hararite; Eliphal, son of Ur;
Hepher from Mecherah; Ahijah the Pelonite;
Hezro from Carmel; Naarai, son of Ezbai.
Joel, brother of Nathan; Mibhar, son of Hagri;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai from Beeroth, who carried Joab's armor;
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad, son of Ahlai;
Adina, son of Shiza, from Reuben, leader of the Reubenites, with thirty men with him;
Hanan, son of Maacah; Joshaphat the Mithnite.
Uzzia from Ashterath; Shama and Jeiel, sons of Hotham from Aroer;
Jediael, son of Shimri; his brother Joha, the Tizite;
Eliel from Mahavah; Jeribai and Joshaviah, sons of Elnaam; Ithmah the Moabite;
Eliel; Obed; and Jaasiel from Mezobah.
These are the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was still hiding from Saul son of Kish. They were strong helpers in war.
They could shoot arrows and throw stones with either hand. They were from Benjamin, Saul's tribe.
Ahiezer was the leader, and Joash, sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; and Jehu the Anathothite.
Ishmaiah the Gibeonite was a strong fighter among the thirty and their leader. Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite.
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite.
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam the Korahites.
Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

Some Gadites joined David at the stronghold in the desert. They were strong soldiers, ready for war. They could use shields and spears. Their faces were like lions' faces, and they were as fast as deer on the mountains.
Ezer was first, Obadiah second, Eliab third.
These Gadites were army leaders. The least could fight one hundred men, and the greatest one thousand.
These are the men who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it was full and overflowed its banks. They chased away everyone in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
Some Benjaminites and Judahites came to David at the stronghold.

David went out to meet them and said, "If you come in peace to help me, my heart will be one with yours. But if you come to trick me and hand me over to my enemies, even though I have done no wrong, may the God of our fathers see it and judge."

Then the Spirit came on Amasai, the leader of the thirty, and he said, "We are yours, David! We are with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you! For your God helps you." So David welcomed them and made them leaders of his army.

Some men from Manasseh joined David when he went with the Philistines to fight Saul. But they did not help the Philistines, because the Philistine leaders sent David away. They said, "He may turn against us and go back to his master Saul."
When David went to Ziklag, these men from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, leaders of thousands in Manasseh.
They helped David fight the raiders, because they were all strong, brave men and leaders in the army.
Day after day men came to help David until his camp was as big as God's camp.
These are the numbers of the leaders who came to David at Hebron to turn Saul's kingdom over to him, as the LORD had said.
From Judah: 6,800 men ready for war, carrying shields and spears.
Jehoiada, leader of Aaron's family, came with 3,700 men.
Zadok, a brave young man, came with 22 leaders from his father's family.
From Benjamin, Saul's relatives: 3,000. Most of them had stayed loyal to Saul's family until then.
From Ephraim: 20,800 strong soldiers, famous men in their families.
From the half tribe of Manasseh: 18,000 men chosen by name to make David king.
From Issachar: 200 leaders who understood the times and knew what Israel should do. All their relatives followed their advice.
From Zebulun: 50,000 soldiers ready for war, with all kinds of weapons. They were loyal and not divided.
From Naphtali: 1,000 leaders, with 37,000 men carrying shields and spears.
From Dan: 28,600 men ready for war.
From Asher: 40,000 soldiers ready for war.
From east of the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh: 120,000 men with all kinds of weapons.
All these soldiers came to Hebron with one heart to make David king over all Israel. The rest of Israel also agreed with one heart to make David king.
They stayed there three days, eating and drinking, because their relatives had prepared food for them.

Also, people near them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. They brought flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep. There was great joy in Israel.
David talked with the leaders of thousands and hundreds and with every chief.

Then David said to all the people of Israel, "If you think this is good, and if it comes from the LORD our God, let us send word to our brothers who are left in all the lands of Israel. Let us also send word to the priests and Levites in their towns with fields. Ask them to come join us.
Let us bring back the ark of our God to us. We did not ask about it in the days of Saul."
All the people said it was good. The whole group wanted to do it.
David gathered all Israel from the Shihor in Egypt to Hamath. He did this to bring the ark of God from Kiriath Jearim.
David and all Israel went up to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim, in Judah. They went to bring up the ark of God, the LORD, who sits between the winged angels. His name is called there.
They put the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab. Uzzah and Ahio were driving the cart.
David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their strength. They sang and played harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
When they came to the grain floor of Kidon, the oxen stumbled. Uzzah put out his hand to hold the ark.
The LORD was angry with Uzzah. He struck him because he put his hand on the ark. Uzzah died there before God.
David was angry because the LORD had punished Uzzah. So that place is called Perez Uzzah to this day.
David was afraid of God that day. He said, "How can I bring the ark of God to me?"
So David did not take the ark to the City of David. He took it instead to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
The ark of God stayed with the family of Obed-Edom in his house for three months. The LORD blessed Obed-Edom and all that he had.
Hiram was king of Tyre. He sent messengers to David. He also sent cedar logs, stone workers, and wood workers to build a house for David.
David knew that the the LORD had made him king over Israel. The the LORD had made his kingdom great for His people Israel.
In Jerusalem, David took more wives. He had more sons and daughters.
These are the names of his children born in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
The Philistines heard that David had been made king over all Israel. They all went up to find him. But David heard about it and went out to meet them.
The Philistines came and attacked the Valley of Rephaim.
So David asked God, "Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You give them to me?" The the LORD said, "Go. I will give them to you."
So David went up to Baal-perazim. He beat them there. He said, "Like water breaking through, God has broken through my enemies for me." So that place was called Baal-perazim.
There the Philistines left their idols. David had them burned in the fire.
The Philistines came again and attacked the valley.
David asked God again. God said, "Do not go straight after them. Go around them. Attack them in front of the balsam trees."
God said, "When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, go out to fight. Then God will have gone out before you to beat the Philistine camp."
David did what God told him. They beat the Philistine army from Gibeon to Gezer.
David became famous in all the lands. The the LORD made all the nations afraid of him.
David built houses for himself in the City of David. He made a place for the ark of God. He set up a tent for it.
Then David said, "Only the Levites should carry the ark of God. The LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD. They will serve Him forever."
David called all Israel to Jerusalem. They would bring the ark of the LORD to the place he made for it.
David gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites.
For the Kohathites, Uriel was the leader. He had 120 brothers.
For the Merarites, Asaiah was the leader. He had 220 brothers.
For the Gershonites, Joel was the leader. He had 130 brothers.
For the Elizaphanites, Shemaiah was the leader. He had 200 brothers.
For the Hebronites, Eliel was the leader. He had 80 brothers.
For the Uzzielites, Amminadab was the leader. He had 112 brothers.
David called the priests Zadok and Abiathar. He also called the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levite families. You and your brothers must make yourselves clean. Bring the ark of the LORD God of Israel to the place I made for it.
You did not carry it the first time. The LORD our God punished us. We did not follow His rules."
So the priests and Levites made themselves clean. They would bring up the ark of the LORD God of Israel.
The Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders. They used poles, just as Moses had told them to do. This was what the LORD had said.
David told the Levite leaders to choose their brothers to sing. They would sing with joy. They would play harps, lyres, and cymbals. The music would be loud.
The Levites chose Heman son of Joel. From his brothers they chose Asaph son of Berechiah. From the Merarites they chose Ethan son of Kushaiah.

With them were their brothers in the next group: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel. They were gatekeepers.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan played bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played harps.
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah played lyres. They led the music.
Chenaniah was the leader of the Levites. He was in charge of carrying the ark. He knew how to do it well.
Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer were priests. They blew trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark.
David, the elders of Israel, and the leaders of thousands went to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-Edom. They were happy.
God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD. They offered seven bulls and seven rams.

David wore a robe of fine linen. All the Levites who carried the ark wore linen too. The singers wore linen too. Chenaniah, the leader of the carrying singers, wore linen. David also wore a linen ephod.
All Israel brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD up with shouts. They sounded horns, trumpets, and cymbals. They played harps and lyres.

When the ark of the covenant of the LORD came to the City of David, Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating. She did not like him for it in her heart.
They brought the Ark of God and put it in the tent David had set up. They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.
David finished giving the burnt and peace offerings. Then he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
He gave every man and woman in Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake.
David chose some Levites to serve before the Ark of the LORD. They were to remember, thank, and praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
Asaph was the leader. Zechariah was second. Then came Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel. They played harps and lyres. Asaph played cymbals.
The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blew trumpets all the time before the Ark of the Covenant of God.
That day David first gave this song of thanks to Asaph and his brothers to sing to the LORD.
“Give thanks to the LORD. Call on His name. Tell the nations what He has done.
Sing to Him. Make music to Him. Talk about all His wonderful works.
Be proud of His holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD be glad.
Look to the LORD and His strength. Seek His face always.
Remember the wonderful things He did. Remember His miracles and His fair decisions.
You are from Israel, His servant. You are Jacob’s children, the ones He chose.
“He is the LORD our God. His rules are for the whole world.
Remember His agreement forever. Remember the word He gave for a thousand generations.
It is the agreement He made with Abraham, and His promise to Isaac.
He made it a law for Jacob. It lasts forever for Israel.
He said, ‘I will give you the land of Canaan. It will be your share of land.’
You were only a few people then. You lived there as strangers.
“They walked from nation to nation. They went from one kingdom to another.
He did not let anyone hurt them. He warned kings about them.
He said, ‘Do not touch My chosen people. Do not hurt My prophets.’
Sing to the LORD, all the earth. Tell His saving power every day.
Tell all nations about His glory. Tell all people about His wonderful works.
The LORD is very great. People praise Him. He is feared more than all gods.
All the gods of the nations are false. But the LORD made the heavens.
“Honor and beauty are before Him. Strength and joy are in His place.
Families of nations, give the LORD glory and strength.
Give the LORD the glory His name deserves. Bring an offering and come to Him. Worship the LORD in holy beauty.
All the earth, shake before Him. The world is set and will not move.
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice. Let people say among the nations, ‘The LORD rules.’
“Let the sea roar and everything in it. Let the fields be glad and everything in them.
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, because He is coming to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the LORD, because He is good. His love lasts forever.
Say, ‘Save us, God of our salvation. Gather us and rescue us from the nations. Then we will thank Your holy name and praise You.’”
Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Then all the people said, ‘Amen,’ and praised the LORD.
David left Asaph and his brothers there before the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD. They served before the Ark every day.
Obed-Edom and his 68 relatives served as gatekeepers. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers too.
Zadok the priest and his brothers served before the tent of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon.
They offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering every morning and evening. They did everything written in the Law of the LORD that He gave Israel.
Heman and Jeduthun were with them, and the rest of those chosen and named. They thanked the LORD because His love lasts forever.
Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments for sacred songs. The sons of Jeduthun were gatekeepers.
Then all the people went home. David went home to bless his family.
David was living in his house. He said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I live in a house made of cedar. But the ark of the LORD’s agreement is in a tent.”
Nathan said to David, “Do everything you want to do, because God is with you.”
That night God spoke to Nathan.
He said, “Go and tell My servant David what the LORD says: You will not build a house for Me to live in.
“I have not lived in a house since the day I brought Israel up. I have moved from tent to tent and from place to place.
Wherever I went with all Israel, I never asked one of Israel’s judges, whom I told to take care of My people, why he had not built Me a house of cedar.
“Now tell him what the LORD of Armies says: I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to rule over My people Israel.
I was with you wherever you went. I defeated all your enemies in front of you. I made your name great, like the names of the great people on earth.
I will give My people Israel a place to live. I will plant them there. They will live in their own place and not be afraid anymore. Wicked people will not hurt them again, as they did before.
“For the days when I gave judges over My people Israel, I brought down all your enemies. I tell you that the LORD will build you a house.
When your days are over and you go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your child after you, one of your sons. I will make his kingdom strong.
“He will build a house for Me. I will make his throne last forever.
I will be his Father, and he will be My son. I will not take My faithful love away from him, as I took it away from the one before you.
I will put him in My house and in My kingdom forever. His throne will be set up forever.”
Nathan told David all these words and this vision.
King David went in and sat before the LORD. He said, “Who am I, O the LORD God, and what is my family, that You have brought me this far?
“This was a small thing in Your eyes, God. You have spoken about Your servant’s family far into the future. You have treated me as a person of high rank, O the LORD God.
“What more can David say to You about Your servant? You know Your servant.
“The LORD, You did all this great thing for Your servant, following Your own heart, to make all these great things known.
“The LORD, there is no one like You. There is no God but You. We have heard it with our own ears.

“And who is like Your people Israel? They are the one nation on earth that God went to rescue as His own people. You made Your name great and wonderful by driving out nations before Your people, whom You rescued from Egypt.
“You made Your people Israel Your own people forever. And You, the LORD, became their God.
“Now, the LORD, let the word You spoke about Your servant and his family come true forever. Do as You have said.
“Let Your name be strong and great forever. People will say, ‘The LORD of Armies is the God of Israel. He is God to Israel.’ And the house of Your servant David will be set up before You.
“You, my God, have shown Your servant that You will build him a house. That is why Your servant has found courage to pray to You.
“Now, the LORD, You are God. You have promised this good thing to Your servant.
“Now You have been pleased to bless Your servant’s house, so it will last forever before You. For You, the LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever.”
After this, David attacked the Philistines. He beat them and took Gath and its nearby towns from them.
David beat Moab. The Moabites became David's servants and paid him gifts.
David beat King Hadadezer of Zobah near Hamath. Hadadezer was on his way to set up his power at the Euphrates River.
David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers. He hurt all the horses that pulled the chariots so they could not run, but he kept 100.
When the Arameans from Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them.
David put soldiers in Damascus in Aram. The Arameans became his servants and paid him gifts. The LORD helped David win everywhere he went.
David took the gold shields from Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
David took a lot of bronze from Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer. Solomon later used it to make the bronze sea, the pillars, and other bronze things.
King Tou of Hamath heard that David had beaten all the army of King Hadadezer of Zobah.

King Tou sent his son Hadoram to King David. He asked David for peace and blessed him, because David had fought and beaten Hadadezer. Hadadezer had often fought Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of gold, silver, and bronze things.
King David gave these things to the LORD. He also gave silver and gold he had taken from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
Abishai son of Zeruiah killed 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
David put soldiers in Edom. All of Edom became his servants. The LORD helped David win everywhere he went.
David ruled over all Israel. He was fair and did right for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah led the army. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the record keeper.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Shavsha was the writer.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada led the Cherethites and Pelethites. David's sons were his top helpers.
After this, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died. His son Hanun became king.

David said, "I want to be kind to Hanun son of Nahash. His father was kind to me." So David sent men to comfort him about his father. David's servants came to the land of the Ammonites to Hanun to comfort him.
The leaders of the Ammonites said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honoring your father by sending men to comfort you? Did his servants come here to look around, spy, and destroy our land?"
So Hanun took David's servants. He shaved them. He cut their clothes in half up to their hips. Then he sent them away.
Some men went and told David about this. He sent men to meet them, because they were very ashamed. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then come home."
The Ammonites saw they had made David angry. Hanun and the Ammonites sent 1,000 talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram Naharaim, Aram Maacah, and Zobah.
They hired 32,000 chariots. They also hired the king of Maacah and his troops. They came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites came from their towns and got ready for war.
When David heard this, he sent Joab and all his strong soldiers.
The Ammonites came out and lined up for battle at the city gate. The kings who came stayed by themselves in the open field.
Joab saw that the battle was in front of him and behind him. He chose the best soldiers in Israel and lined them up against the Arameans.
He put the rest of the army under his brother Abishai. They lined up against the Ammonites.
Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, you will help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will help you.
Be strong. Let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the the LORD do what is good in His sight."
Joab and his men moved forward to fight the Arameans. The Arameans ran away from him.
When the Ammonites saw the Arameans running away, they also ran away from Abishai. They went back into the city. Then Joab went back to Jerusalem.
The Arameans saw they had lost to Israel. They sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates River. Shophach, the leader of Hadadezer's army, led them.
David was told about this. He gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan River. He came to them. David lined up his army for battle. They fought.
The Arameans ran away from Israel. David killed 7,000 chariot drivers and 40,000 foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach, the army leader.
When Hadadezer's servants saw they had lost to Israel, they made peace with David. They became his servants. The Arameans did not want to help the Ammonites anymore.
In spring, when kings go to war, Joab led the army and ruined the land of the Ammonites. He surrounded their city, Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and tore it down.
Then David took the crown from their king's head. It weighed a lot of gold, and it had a pretty stone in it. David put it on his own head. He also took a lot of treasure from the city.
David brought out the people who lived there. He made them work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He did the same thing in all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his men went back to Jerusalem.
Later, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, who was from the giants. After that, the Philistines were beaten.
There was another war with the Philistines. Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath from Gath. Goliath's spear was very big.
There was still another battle at Gath. A very tall man was there. He had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. That made 24 in all. He also came from the giants.
He made fun of Israel. Jonathan, the son of David's brother Shimea, killed him.
So these giant men from Gath were killed by David and his men.
Satan turned against Israel. He made David want to count the people of Israel.
David said to Joab and the leaders, "Go and count the people of Israel from Beersheba to Dan. Bring me the number so I will know how many there are."
Joab said, "May the LORD make His people a hundred times more than they are. But, my lord the king, are they not all your servants? Why do you want this? Why should Israel be blamed?"
But the king's word was stronger than Joab's. So Joab left and went all over Israel. Then he came back to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the number of the people. There were 1,100,000 men in all Israel who could fight with a sword. Judah had 470,000 men who could fight with a sword.
But Joab did not count the people of Levi and Benjamin, because he hated what the king asked.
God was not pleased with this. He punished Israel.
David said to God, "I have sinned very much by doing this. Please forgive me. I was very foolish."
The LORD spoke to Gad, David's prophet. He said,
"Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I will give you three choices. Pick one, and I will do it to you.'"
So Gad came to David and said, "This is what the LORD says: Choose one.

You may choose three years of famine. Or you may choose three months of running from your enemies while their swords chase you. Or you may choose three days of the sword of the LORD and sickness in the land, with the angel of the LORD destroying all over Israel. Now think about what answer I should give to the One who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in great trouble. Let me fall into the LORD's hands, because His mercy is very great. Do not let me fall into human hands."
So the LORD sent a sickness on Israel, and 70,000 men died.

God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But while he was destroying it, the LORD saw and stopped the trouble. He said to the angel, "That is enough. Stop now." The angel of the LORD was standing at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth. The angel held a sword in his hand, ready to strike Jerusalem. David and the leaders wore rough sackcloth and fell face down.

David said to God, "Wasn't it I who told them to count the people? I have sinned and done wrong. These people are like sheep. What did they do? The LORD my God, let Your hand be against me and my family, not against Your people, so they will not be sick."
The angel of the LORD told Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD at Ornan's threshing floor.
So David went up, because Gad had spoken in the LORD's name.
Ornan was beating wheat. He turned and saw the angel. His four sons hid.
When David came to Ornan, Ornan saw him and came out of the threshing floor. He bowed down to David.
David said to Ornan, "Let me have this threshing floor. I want to build an altar to the LORD here. Sell it to me for the full price, so the sickness will stop for the people."
Ornan said, "Take it, my lord the king. Do what seems good to you. Look, I give you the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all."
But King David said, "No. I will buy it for the full price. I will not take what is yours to give to the LORD. I will not offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing."
So David gave Ornan 600 shekels of gold for the place.
David built an altar to the LORD there. He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called on the LORD, and the LORD answered him with fire from heaven on the altar.
Then the LORD told the angel to put his sword back in its sheath.
At that time, David saw that the LORD had answered him at Ornan's threshing floor. So he offered sacrifices there.
The tent of the LORD, which Moses made in the desert, and the altar for burnt offerings were at the high place in Gibeon.
But David could not go there to ask God, because he was afraid of the angel's sword.
David said, "This is the house of the the LORD God. This is the altar for burnt offerings for Israel."
David gave orders to gather the foreigners living in Israel. He chose stonecutters to cut smooth stones for building God's house.
David got ready a lot of iron for nails for the doors and gates, and for the clamps. He also got so much bronze that no one could weigh it.
He got so many cedar logs that no one could count them. The people from Sidon and Tyre brought many cedar logs to David.

David said, "My son Solomon is young and weak. The house to be built for the the LORD must be very great. It must be famous and beautiful in all the lands. So I will get things ready for it." David got many things ready before he died.
David called for his son Solomon. He told him to build a house for the the LORD, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, "My son, I wanted to build a house for the name of the the LORD my God.
But the the LORD spoke to me. He said, 'You have spilled much blood. You have fought big wars. you must not build a house for My name, because you have spilled much blood on the earth before Me.
Look, you will have a son. He will be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies around him. His name will be Solomon. I will give Israel peace and quiet in his days.
He will build a house for My name. He will be My son, and I will be his Father. I will set up the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.' "
Now, my son, may the the LORD be with you. May you succeed and build the house of the the LORD your God, as He has spoken concerning you.
May the the LORD give you wisdom and understanding. May He put you in charge of Israel, so you keep the law of the the LORD your God.
Then you will do well if you obey the rules and laws the the LORD gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or give up. "

Now look, I have worked hard and saved 100,000 talents of gold and 1,000,000 talents of silver for the house of the the LORD. I have also saved so much bronze and iron that no one can weigh it. I have saved wood and stone too. You may add more.
You have many workers with you. There are stonecutters, builders, and woodworkers, and workers skilled in every kind of work.
There is so much gold, silver, bronze, and iron that no one can count it. Get up and work, and may the the LORD be with you."
David also told all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon.
He said, "The the LORD your God is with you, isn't He? He has given you peace on every side. He gave the people of the land into my hands, and the land has been won for the the LORD and His people.

Now set your heart and soul to seek the the LORD your God. Get up and build the holy place of the the LORD God. Bring the ark of the covenant of the the LORD and the holy things of God into the house built for the name of the the LORD."
David was very old. He made his son Solomon king over Israel.
David gathered all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites.
The Levites who were 30 years old or older were counted. There were 38,000 men.
Of these, 24,000 were to oversee the work of the house of the LORD. Six thousand were officers and judges.
Four thousand were gatekeepers. Four thousand praised the LORD with instruments David made for praise.
David divided them into groups for the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Gershon's sons were Laadan and Shimei.
Laadan's sons were Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel. There were three.
Shimei's sons were Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. There were three. These men were leaders of Laadan's family groups.
Shimei also had four sons: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah.
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one family group.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. There were four.
Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart forever to be most holy. He was to burn incense before the LORD, serve Him, and bless in His name forever.
Moses was a man of God. His sons were counted with the tribe of Levi.
Moses' sons were Gershom and Eliezer.
Gershom's son was Shebuel the chief.
Eliezer's sons were Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons. But Rehabiah had many sons.
Izhar's son was Shelomith the chief.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah the chief, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, and Jekameam fourth.
Uzziel's sons were Micah the chief and Isshiah second.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died and had no sons, only daughters. Their relatives, the sons of Kish, married them.
Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth. There were three.
These were Levi's descendants, grouped by family. Their leaders were counted by name. All the men were 20 years old or older. They did the work for the house of the LORD.
David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people. He lives in Jerusalem forever."
So the Levites did not need to carry the tent and all its things for service anymore.
For by David's last words, the Levites were counted from 20 years old and up.
Their job was to help Aaron's sons serve in the house of the LORD. They worked in the courtyards and rooms. They helped make all holy things clean. They did the work of the house of God.
They also cared for the holy bread, fine flour for grain offerings, bread without yeast, food cooked in pans, mixed dough, and all measuring tools.
They stood every morning to thank and praise the LORD. They did the same in the evening.
They helped with all burnt offerings given to the LORD on Sabbaths, new moons, and special days. They did this by number, as the rules said, always before the LORD.
They kept watch over the tent of meeting, the holy place, and their brothers, Aaron's sons. They served in the house of the LORD.
These were the groups of Aaron's sons. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died before their father. They had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
David split them into groups with Zadok from Eleazar's family and Ahimelech from Ithamar's family. They did set jobs.
More leaders came from Eleazar's family than from Ithamar's. Eleazar's family had sixteen leaders. Ithamar's family had eight leaders.
They picked the groups by a random draw. Both families had leaders for God's holy work.

Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite and writer, wrote their names before the king, the leaders, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites. One family group was chosen for Eleazar, and one for Ithamar.
The first group was Jehoiarib. The second was Jedaiah.
The third was Harim. The fourth was Seorim.
The fifth was Malchijah. The sixth was Mijamin.
The seventh was Hakkoz. The eighth was Abijah.
The ninth was Jeshua. The tenth was Shecaniah.
The eleventh was Eliashib. The twelfth was Jakim.
The thirteenth was Huppah. The fourteenth was Jeshebeab.
The fifteenth was Bilgah. The sixteenth was Immer.
The seventeenth was Hezir. The eighteenth was Happizzez.
The nineteenth was Pethahiah. The twentieth was Ezekiel.
The twenty-first was Jachin. The twenty-second was Gamul.
The twenty-third was Delaiah. The twenty-fourth was Maaziah.
These were their work times. They went to the house of the the LORD to serve, as the rules said. Aaron had set this. The The LORD God of Israel had told him to do it.
The rest of Levi's family was listed too. From Amram's family came Shubael. From Shubael's family came Jehdeiah.
From Rehabiah's family, the leader was Isshiah.
From the Izhar family came Shelomoth. From Shelomoth's family came Jahath.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah first, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, and Jekameam fourth.
From Uzziel's family came Micah. From Micah's family came Shamir.
Micah's brother was Isshiah. From Isshiah's family came Zechariah.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Jaaziah's son was Beno.
From Merari's family through Jaaziah came Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Mahli had a son named Eleazar, but Eleazar had no sons.
Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth. These were the Levite families.

They drew lots too, just like Aaron's sons. King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites were there. The older family group and the younger group were treated the same.
David and the army leaders chose some of Asaph's, Heman's, and Jeduthun's sons to serve. They spoke God's words and played harps, lyres, and cymbals. They were counted as workers for this job.
From Asaph's sons were Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah. Asaph led them. He spoke God's words as the king told him.
From Jeduthun's sons were Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah. There were six in all. Their father Jeduthun led them. He sang thanks and praise to the the LORD and played the harp.
From Heman's sons were Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman, the king's prophet. He spoke God's words to make God's power great, as God said. God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
All these men were under their fathers' lead. They made music in the the LORD's house with cymbals, harps, and lyres for God's house work. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman were under the king's lead.
With their brothers, all trained and good at singing to the the LORD, there were 288 of them.
They drew lots for their jobs. Young and old took part together. Teachers and students took part together.
The first lot was for Asaph. It went to Joseph. The second lot went to Gedaliah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The third lot went to Zaccur, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The fourth lot went to Izri, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The fifth lot went to Nethaniah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The sixth lot went to Bukkiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The seventh lot went to Jesharelah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The eighth lot went to Jeshaiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The ninth lot went to Mattaniah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The tenth lot went to Shimei, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The eleventh lot went to Azarel, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The twelfth lot went to Hashabiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The thirteenth lot went to Shubael, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The fourteenth lot went to Mattithiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The fifteenth lot went to Jeremoth, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The sixteenth lot went to Hananiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The seventeenth lot went to Joshbekashah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The eighteenth lot went to Hanani, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The nineteenth lot went to Mallothi, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The twentieth lot went to Eliathah, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The twenty-first lot went to Hothir, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The twenty-second lot went to Giddalti, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The twenty-third lot went to Mahazioth, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
The twenty-fourth lot went to Romamti-ezer, with his sons and brothers—twelve men.
These were the groups of gate guards. The Korahites had Meshelemiah. He was the son of Kore. He came from Asaph's family.
Meshelemiah's sons were Zechariah, the firstborn, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel,
Obed-edom's sons were Shemaiah, the firstborn, Jehozabad, Joah, Sacar, Nethanel,
Ammiel, Issachar, and Peulthai. God had blessed Obed-edom.
Shemaiah had sons who led their family. They were strong men.
Shemaiah's sons were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad. His brothers were Elihu and Semachiah.
All these men came from Obed-edom. They and their sons and brothers were strong men. They could work hard. There were sixty-two from Obed-edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and brothers. They were strong men. There were eighteen of them.
Hosah was from Merari's family. His sons were Shimri, the chief. Shimri was not the firstborn. But his father made him chief.
Hilkiah was second, Tebaliah was third, and Zechariah was fourth. Hosah had thirteen sons and brothers.
These groups of gate guards had jobs. The leaders of the men served in the house of the LORD. They served like their brothers.
They drew lots for every gate. Both small and large families took part.
The east gate lot fell to Shelemiah. They drew lots for Zechariah, his son. He was a wise helper. His lot fell to the north.
Obed-edom got the south gate. His sons got the storehouse.
Shuppim and Hosah got the west gate. They were at the Shalleketh gate on the road. One group watched across from the other.
Each day, six Levites were at the east gate. Four were at the north gate. Four were at the south gate. Two at a time were at the storehouse.
At Parbar on the west, four were on the road. Two were at Parbar.
These were the groups of gate guards for the Korahites and Merarites.
The Levites were in charge of the treasures of God's house. They were also in charge of the treasures of the holy things.
Ladan came from Gershon's family. The family leaders from Ladan were Jehieli.
Jehieli's sons were Zetham and Joel, his brother. They were in charge of the treasures of the LORD's house.
The Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites also served.
Shebuel was the son of Gershom. Gershom was the son of Moses. Shebuel was the leader over the treasures.
Eliezer's family line was Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomoth.

This Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the treasures of the holy things. King David and the family leaders had given these things. The leaders were army leaders over thousands and hundreds.
They gave things taken in war to make the house of the LORD strong.
Samuel the prophet, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah also gave things. All these gifts were under the care of Shelomith and his relatives.
Chenaniah and his sons from the Izharites worked outside. They were officers and judges over Israel.
Hashabiah and his relatives from the Hebronites were 1,700 strong men. They served west of the Jordan River. They did all the work for the LORD and the king.
Jerijah was the leader of the Hebronites. Family records showed their family lines. In David's fortieth year as king, they looked for strong men. They found them at Jazer in Gilead.
Jerijah's relatives were 2,700 strong men and family leaders. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh. They handled all matters for God and the king.

This is the list of the people of Israel. It names the family leaders and the army leaders over thousands and hundreds. It also names the officers who helped the king. They served in groups that worked each month all year. Each group had 24,000 men.
Jashobeam son of Zabdiel led the first group. This group worked in the first month. It had 24,000 men.
He was from Perez's family. He was the chief army leader for the first month.
Dodai the Ahohite led the second group. This group worked in the second month. Mikloth was the leader of his group. It had 24,000 men.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest led the third group. This group worked in the third month. It had 24,000 men.
This Benaiah was a strong fighter among the Thirty. He was over the Thirty. His son Ammizabad led his group.
Asahel, Joab's brother, led the fourth group. This group worked in the fourth month. His son Zebadiah took his place after him. It had 24,000 men.
Shamhuth the Izrahite led the fifth group. This group worked in the fifth month. It had 24,000 men.
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite led the sixth group. This group worked in the sixth month. It had 24,000 men.
Helez the Pelonite, from Ephraim, led the seventh group. This group worked in the seventh month. It had 24,000 men.
Sibbecai the Hushathite, from Zerah's family, led the eighth group. This group worked in the eighth month. It had 24,000 men.
Abiezer the Anathothite, from Benjamin, led the ninth group. This group worked in the ninth month. It had 24,000 men.
Maharai the Netophathite, from Zerah's family, led the tenth group. This group worked in the tenth month. It had 24,000 men.
Benaiah the Pirathonite, from Ephraim, led the eleventh group. This group worked in the eleventh month. It had 24,000 men.
Heldai the Netophathite, from Othniel's family, led the twelfth group. This group worked in the twelfth month. It had 24,000 men.
These men led the tribes of Israel. For Reuben, Eliezer son of Zichri. For Simeon, Shephatiah son of Maacah.
For Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel. For Aaron, Zadok.
For Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers. For Issachar, Omri son of Michael.
For Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah. For Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel.
For Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah. For half of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah.
For the other half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah. For Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner.
For Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
David did not count the men who were 20 years old or younger. This was because the LORD had said He would make Israel as many as the stars in the sky.
Joab son of Zeruiah started to count the people, but he did not finish. Because of this, God was angry with Israel. The number was not written in King David's history book.
Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king's storehouses. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the country, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers.
Ezri son of Kelub was in charge of the field workers who farmed the land.
Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the fruit from the vineyards for the wine cellars.
Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive trees and sycamore trees in the low hills. Joash was in charge of the olive oil stores.
Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds in Sharon. Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the herds in the valleys.
Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.
Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the sheep. All these men were officials who took care of King David's things.
Jonathan, David's uncle, gave advice. He was a wise man and a writer. Jehiel son of Hachmoni helped teach the king's sons.
Ahithophel was the king's advisor. Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.
After Ahithophel, Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar advised the king. Joab was the leader of the king's army.

King David called all of Israel’s leaders to Jerusalem. He called the leaders of the tribes, the army leaders who served the king, the leaders of thousands and hundreds, and the men in charge of the king’s and his sons’ things and animals. He also called the palace workers, the strong men, and all the brave soldiers.

King David stood up and said, “Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I wanted to build a home where the box of God’s promise could rest. It would be a place for our God’s feet. I got ready to build it.”
But God said to me, “You are not to build a house for My name, because you are a man who fought wars and spilled blood.”

David said, “Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father’s family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah to lead. From Judah’s family He chose my father’s family. From my father’s sons He was happy to make me king over all Israel.”
“Of all my sons—for the LORD has given me many sons—He chose my son Solomon to sit on the throne over the LORD’s kingdom in Israel.”
God said to me, “Solomon your son is the one who will build My house and My yards. I chose him to be My son, and I will be his Father.”
“I will make his kingdom last forever, if he is strong to do My commands and My rules, like he does today.”

David said, “So now, with all Israel watching and with our God listening, keep and look for all the commands of the LORD your God. Then you may own this good land and leave it to your children after you, forever.”

“And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father. Serve Him with a whole heart and a willing mind. The LORD looks at all hearts and understands every thought. If you look for Him, you will find Him. But if you leave Him, He will leave you forever.”
“See now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the holy place. Be strong and do it.”
Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the front porch of the temple, its buildings, its storage rooms, its upper rooms, its inner rooms, and the room for the cover of the box.
The plans had everything he had in mind for the yards of the LORD’s house, for all the rooms around it, for the storage rooms of God’s house, and for the storage rooms for the holy things.
They also had plans for the groups of priests and helpers, for all the work in the LORD’s house, and for all the tools used in the LORD’s house.
He set the weight of gold for all gold tools used in every kind of work, and the weight of silver for all silver tools.
He set the weight of gold for the gold lampstands and their lamps, and the weight of silver for the silver lampstands and their lamps, for the work each one did.
He also set the weight of gold for the tables that held the special bread, and the weight of silver for the silver tables.
He gave pure gold for the forks, the sprinkling bowls, and the pitchers. He set the weight of gold for each of these. For the silver things, he set their weight of silver.
He set the weight of pure gold for the altar where sweet spices were burned, and for the gold seat with angels whose wings spread out and cover the box of God’s promise.
David said, “All of this is written down for me. The LORD gave me these plans. He helped me understand every part.”

Then David said to his son Solomon, “Be strong and brave. Do the work. Do not be afraid or sad. The LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or leave you until the LORD’s house is finished.”
“The groups of priests and helpers are ready to work in God’s house. Every skilled worker who wants to help will be there for you. The leaders and all the people will follow your orders.”
King David said to all the people, "My son Solomon, whom God has chosen, is still young and tender. The work is big. The temple is not for people. It is for the the LORD God."

I have used all my strength to get things ready for God's house. I got gold for gold things, silver for silver things, bronze for bronze things, iron for iron things, and wood for wood things. I also got onyx stones and other stones to set in place. I got stones of antimony and colorful stones. I got many kinds of precious stones and marble stones.
I also give my own gold and silver to God's house, because I love it. I give more than what I already got ready for the holy house.
I give 3,000 talents of gold from Ophir and 7,000 talents of pure silver. It is to cover the walls of the buildings.
I give gold and silver for all the work that skilled workers will do. Who will give himself to the the LORD today?"
Then the leaders of the family groups, the leaders of Israel's tribes, the leaders of thousands and hundreds, and the king's officials gave gifts freely.
They gave for God's house: 5,000 talents and 10,000 gold coins of gold, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.
People who had precious stones gave them to the the LORD's house treasury. Jehiel the Gershonite took care of them.
The people were happy because they gave freely. They gave to the the LORD with all their heart. King David was also very happy.
David praised the the LORD in front of everyone. He said, "Praise You, the LORD, God of our father Israel, forever and ever.
The LORD, greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty are Yours. Everything in heaven and on earth is Yours. The LORD, the kingdom is Yours. You are lifted up above all.
Riches and honor come from You. You rule over everything. Power and strength are in Your hand. In Your hand is the power to make people great and strong.
Now, our God, we thank You and praise Your glorious name.
But who am I, and what are my people, that we can give like this? Everything comes from You. We have given You only what is Yours.
We are strangers and travelers before You, like our fathers were. Our days on earth are like a shadow. We have no hope.
The LORD our God, all this plenty we got ready to build a house for You and Your holy name comes from Your hand. All of it is Yours.
I know, my God, that You test the heart and like what is right. I have given all these things freely because my heart is right. Now I see with joy Your people here giving freely to You.
The LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep these thoughts in Your people's hearts forever. Turn their hearts to You.
Give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep Your commands, laws, and rules, and to do them all. Let him build the temple I have prepared."
David said to all the people, "Bless the the LORD your God." All the people blessed the the LORD, the God of their fathers. They bowed down and worshiped the the LORD and the king.
The next day they offered sacrifices and burnt offerings to the the LORD: 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs, with their drink offerings. They also offered many sacrifices for all Israel.
They ate and drank before the the LORD that day with great joy. They made David's son Solomon king again. They anointed him before the the LORD as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
Then Solomon sat on the the LORD's throne as king in place of his father David. He did well, and all Israel listened to him.
All the leaders and mighty men, and even all of King David's sons, gave their support to King Solomon.
The the LORD made Solomon very great before all Israel. He gave him royal honor that no king in Israel had before.
So David, Jesse's son, ruled over all Israel.
He ruled over Israel for forty years. He ruled seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor. His son Solomon ruled after him.
King David's deeds, from first to last, are written in the book of Samuel the seer, in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer.
It tells about his whole reign and his power, and the times that came upon him, upon Israel, and upon all the kingdoms of the lands.
Solomon was David's son. He grew strong as king. The LORD his God was with him. He made Solomon very great.
Solomon spoke to all Israel. He spoke to leaders of thousands and hundreds. He spoke to judges. He spoke to every leader in Israel. He spoke to the heads of the family groups.
Solomon and all the people went to the high place at Gibeon. They went there because God's tent of meeting was there. Moses, the LORD's servant, had made it in the desert.
David had already brought God's holy box from Kiriath-jearim. He put it in the place he made in Jerusalem. He had set up a tent for it there.
The bronze altar was there too. Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, had made it. It stood in front of the LORD's tent. Solomon and the people went there to worship the LORD.
Solomon went up to the LORD at the bronze altar. It was by the tent of meeting. He gave 1,000 burnt offerings on it.
That night God came to Solomon in a dream. God said, "Ask Me what I should give you."
Solomon said to God, "You showed great love to my father David. You made me king after him.
Now, the LORD God, keep Your promise to my father David. You made me king over many people. They are as many as the dust of the earth.
Give me wisdom and knowledge. Then I can lead these people. Who can judge this great people of Yours?"

God said, "You asked for this from your heart. You did not ask for riches, wealth, or honor. You did not ask for the lives of your enemies. You did not ask to live a long time. You asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge My people. I made you king over them.
So I give you wisdom and knowledge. I will also give you riches, wealth, and honor. No king before you or after you will have as much."
Solomon went from the high place at Gibeon. He went from the tent of meeting to Jerusalem. Then he ruled over Israel.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. He kept them in chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold as common as stones in Jerusalem. He made cedar wood as common as sycamore trees in the lowlands.
Solomon's horses came from Egypt and Kue. The king's traders bought them from Kue for a price.

They brought a chariot from Egypt for 600 pieces of silver. They brought a horse for 150 pieces of silver. They did the same for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram. Their hands brought them out.
Solomon decided to build a house to honor the name of the the LORD. He also decided to build a royal house for himself.
He counted 70,000 men to carry loads. He counted 80,000 men to cut stone in the mountains. He counted 3,600 men to watch over them.
Solomon sent a message to Hiram, king of Tyre. He said, “You did this for David my father. You sent him cedar wood to build a house to live in. Please do the same for me.

Look, I am building a house to honor the name of the the LORD my God. I set it apart for Him. I will burn sweet-smelling smoke in front of Him. I will keep the special bread out all the time. I will bring burnt offerings in the morning and evening. I will bring them on Sabbath days, on new moon days, and on the special days of the the LORD our God. This will be a rule for Israel forever.
The house I build is big, because our God is bigger than all other gods.
But who can build a house for Him? Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot hold Him. Who am I to build a house for Him? I only want to burn offerings in front of Him. “

Now send me a man who knows how to work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, red, and blue cloth. He should know how to carve designs. He will work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem. My father David chose them.
Also send me cedar, cypress, and algum wood from Lebanon. I know your workers know how to cut trees in Lebanon. My workers will help your workers.
Send me lots of wood, because the house I build is big and amazing.
I will give your workers who cut wood 20,000 baskets of wheat, 20,000 baskets of barley, 20,000 jars of wine, and 20,000 jars of oil.”
Hiram, king of Tyre, wrote back to Solomon. He said, “Because the the LORD loves His people, He made you king over them.

Praise the the LORD, the God of Israel! He made heaven and earth. He gave King David a wise son. This son knows how to think and understand. He will build a house for the the LORD and a royal house for himself.
Now I send you a smart man who understands. His name is Huram. He is my best worker. “

He is the son of a woman from Dan. His father was from Tyre. He knows how to work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood. He knows how to work with purple, blue, red, and white cloth. He can carve any design. He can plan any work given to him. He will work with your skilled men and with the skilled men of my lord David, your father.
Now send the wheat, barley, oil, and wine that my lord spoke about to his servants.
We will cut wood from Lebanon as much as you need. We will bring it to you on rafts by sea to Joppa. Then you will carry it up to Jerusalem.”
Solomon counted all the foreigners in Israel. This was after his father David had counted them. He found 153,600 men.
He made 70,000 of them carry loads. He made 80,000 cut stone in the mountain. He made 3,600 watch over the people and make them work.

Then Solomon started to build the the LORD's house in Jerusalem. He built it on Mount Moriah. That was where the the LORD had shown Himself to his father David. David had picked that spot. It was the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
Solomon started building on the second day of the second month. This was in his fourth year as king.
These are the sizes Solomon set for God's house. It was 60 cubits long. It was 20 cubits wide.
The porch in front was 20 cubits long across the width of the house. It was 120 cubits high. He covered the inside with pure gold.
He covered the main room with cypress wood. He covered it with fine gold. He put palm trees and chains on it for beauty.
He made the temple pretty with special stones. The gold was gold from Parvaim.
He covered the beams, door frames, walls, and doors with gold. He cut angel statues into the walls.
He made the Most Holy Room. Its length matched the width of the house. It was 20 cubits. Its width was 20 cubits too. He covered it with 600 talents of fine gold.
The nails weighed 50 shekels of gold. He also covered the top rooms with gold.
In the Most Holy Room, he made two angel statues. They were carved work. He covered them with gold.

The angel statues had 20 cubits of wings in all. One wing of the first statue was 5 cubits long. It touched the wall of the house. Its other wing was 5 cubits long. It touched the wing of the other statue.
The other statue's wing was 5 cubits long. It touched the wall of the house. Its other wing was 5 cubits long. It touched the first statue's wing.
Their wings spread out 20 cubits. They stood on their feet. They faced the main room.
He made the curtain from blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen. He wove angel statues into it.
In front of the house, he made two pillars. Each was 35 cubits high. Each had a top piece 5 cubits high.
He made chains and put them on top of the pillars. He made 100 pomegranates. He put them on the chains.
He set up the pillars in front of the temple. One was on the south. One was on the north. He named the south one Jachin. He named the north one Boaz.
Solomon made a bronze altar. It was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
He also made the Sea out of cast metal. It was round. It was ten cubits from one side to the other. It was five cubits high. A line thirty cubits long went all the way around it.
