Below the rim, there were bulls all around it. There were ten bulls in each cubit. The bulls were in two rows. They were cast as part of the Sea.
The Sea stood on twelve bulls. Three bulls faced north. Three faced west. Three faced south. Three faced east. The Sea was on top of them. Their backs faced the middle.
The Sea was as thick as a hand is wide. Its rim was like the rim of a cup. It looked like a lily flower. It held three thousand baths.
Solomon made ten basins for washing. He put five on the right side and five on the left side. The priests washed things for burnt offerings in them. The priests washed in the Sea.
He made ten gold lampstands. They were made the way they should be. He put them in the temple. Five were on the right side and five on the left side.
He made ten tables. He put them in the temple. Five were on the right side and five on the left side. He also made one hundred gold bowls for sprinkling.
He made the priests' courtyard. He also made the big courtyard and its doors. He covered the doors with bronze.
He put the Sea on the southeast side. It was on the south side toward the east.
Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. Huram finished the work he had started for King Solomon in the house of God.
He made two pillars. He made two bowl-shaped tops for the pillars. He made two sets of net-like work to cover the two bowl-shaped tops on the pillars.
He made four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of net-like work. There were two rows of pomegranates on each net. They covered the two bowl-shaped tops on the pillars.
He made the stands and the basins that went on them.
He made the Sea and the twelve bulls under it.
Huram-abi made the pots, shovels, forks, and all their tools for King Solomon for the house of the LORD. They were made of polished bronze.
The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of Jordan. This was between Succoth and Zeredah.
Solomon made so many of these things that no one could weigh all the bronze.
Solomon made all the things for the house of God. He made the gold altar. He made the tables for the Bread of the Presence.
He made the lampstands of pure gold. They had lamps to burn in front of the Most Holy Place. They were made the way they should be.
He made the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs. They were made of the purest gold.

He made the gold wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, small bowls, and incense holders. He made the gold doors for the inner room, the Most Holy Place. He also made the gold doors for the main hall of the temple.

All the work Solomon did for the LORD’s house was finished. Solomon brought in the holy things his father David had set apart. He put the silver, gold, and all the vessels in the treasuries of God’s house.

Then Solomon called together the leaders of Israel in Jerusalem. He called the elders, the heads of the tribes, and the family leaders. They were to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant from the city of David, which is Zion.
All the men of Israel met with the king during the feast in the seventh month.
All the elders of Israel came. The Levites carried the ark.
They also carried the tent of meeting and all the holy things that were in it. The priests and Levites brought them up.
King Solomon and all the people of Israel who were there stood before the ark. They sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that no one could count them.
The priests brought the ark of the LORD’s covenant to its place. They put it in the inner room of the temple, the Most Holy Place. They put it under the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim spread their wings over the ark and its carrying poles. They covered them from above.
The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the front of the inner room. But they could not be seen from outside. They are still there today.
There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets Moses had put there at Mount Horeb. That was where the LORD made His covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
All the priests who were there made themselves holy. They did not have to stay in their groups. When they came out of the holy place,

the Levites who sang stood east of the altar. They were Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and brothers. They wore fine linen. They had cymbals, harps, and lyres. One hundred twenty priests stood with them and blew trumpets.

The trumpeters and singers made one sound. They praised and thanked the LORD. They lifted their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments. They sang, “He is good! His faithful love lasts forever!” Then the house of the LORD was filled with a cloud.
The priests could not stand and serve because of the cloud. The glory of the LORD had filled God’s house.
Then Solomon said, “The LORD has said He will live in the dark cloud.
But I have built You a big house. It is a place for You to live forever.”
Then the king turned around. He blessed all the people of Israel. All the people were standing there. “
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel. He kept His word. He said it with His mouth to my father David. Now He has done it with His hands.

He said, ‘From the day I brought My people out of Egypt, I did not choose any city from the tribes of Israel. I did not choose a city to build a house for My name. I did not choose a man to rule My people Israel.’
‘But I chose Jerusalem for My name to be there. I chose David to rule My people Israel.’ “
My father David wanted to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, ‘You wanted to build a house for My name. That was good. You had that in your heart.’
‘But you will not build the house. Your son, your own child, will build the house for My name.’ “
The LORD has done what He said. I took my father David’s place. I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I put the ark there. In it is the LORD’s promise. He made it with the people of Israel.”
Then Solomon stood before the LORD’s altar. He was in front of all the people of Israel. He spread out his hands.

Solomon had made a bronze stand. It was about seven and a half feet long and wide. It was about four and a half feet high. He put it in the middle of the yard. He stood on it. He knelt down before all the people of Israel. He spread his hands toward heaven. “
O the LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven or on earth. You keep Your promise. You show love to Your servants who follow You with all their hearts.
You kept what You promised to Your servant David, my father. You said it with Your mouth. You did it with Your hand today.

Now, O the LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant David, my father, what You promised him. You said, ‘you will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if your sons guard their ways and walk in My law as you have walked before Me.’
Now, O the LORD, God of Israel, let Your word to Your servant David come true.” “
But will God really live with people on earth? Heaven, even the highest heaven, cannot hold You. How much less this house I built!
Yet listen to the prayer of Your servant. Listen to his plea, O the LORD my God. Hear the cry and the prayer he prays to You.
May Your eyes be open to this house day and night. You said You would put Your name here. Hear the prayer Your servant prays toward this place.
Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel. They pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, where You live. Hear and forgive.” “
When a man sins against his neighbor and must take an oath, and he comes to take that oath before Your altar in this house,
then hear from heaven. Do what is right. Judge Your servants. Punish the bad man for his bad ways. Show the good man is right by giving him a good reward.” “
When Your people Israel lose to an enemy because they sinned against You, and they come back to You and praise Your name, and pray to You in this house,
then hear from heaven. Forgive the sin of Your people Israel. Bring them back to the land You gave them and their fathers.” “
When the sky is shut and there is no rain because they sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and praise Your name, and turn from their sin because You punished them,
then hear from heaven. Forgive the sin of Your servants and Your people Israel. Teach them the good way to walk. Send rain on Your land, which You gave Your people to own.” “
When there is no food in the land, or sickness, or plant disease, or bugs, or enemies attack their cities, or any other trouble or sickness comes,
then any man or all Your people Israel may pray. Each one knows his own hurt and pain. He spreads out his hands toward this house.
Then hear from heaven, where You live. Forgive. Give each man what he deserves. You alone know the hearts of all people.
Then they will fear You. They will walk in Your ways all their lives in the land You gave our fathers.” “
And for the stranger who is not Your people Israel but comes from a far land because of Your great name and Your strong hand and Your power—when he comes and prays toward this house,

then hear from heaven, where You live. Do what he asks. Then all people on earth will know Your name and fear You, like Your people Israel do. They will know that this house I built is called by Your name.” “
When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and they pray to You toward this city You chose and the house I built for Your name,
then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea. Help them.” “
When they sin against You—no one is without sin—and You are angry with them and let an enemy take them away to a far or near land,
and when they think about it in the land where they were taken, and they are sorry and pray to You there, saying, ‘We sinned. We did wrong. We were bad,’
and when they come back to You with all their heart and soul in that land, and pray toward the land You gave their fathers, toward the city You chose, and toward the house I built for Your name,
then hear from heaven, where You live, their prayer and their plea. Help them. Forgive Your people who sinned against You.” “
Now, my God, may Your eyes be open and Your ears listen to the prayer made in this place.
Now get up, O the LORD God. Come to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your power. May Your priests, O the LORD God, be saved. May Your faithful people be happy with what is good.
O the LORD God, do not turn away the king You chose. Remember Your love for Your servant David.”
When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven. It burned up the burnt offering and the sacrifices. The glory of the LORD filled the temple.
The priests could not go into the LORD’s temple, because the glory of the LORD filled it.

All the Israelites saw the fire come down. They saw the glory of the LORD on the temple. They knelt with their faces to the ground. They worshiped and praised the LORD. They said He is good. His loving kindness lasts forever.
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices to the LORD.
King Solomon offered 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. He and all the people dedicated God’s temple.
The priests stood at their stations. The Levites played instruments David had made to praise the LORD. They said His loving kindness lasts forever. The priests blew trumpets. All Israel stood there.

Solomon made the middle of the courtyard holy. It was in front of the LORD’s temple. He offered burnt offerings and fat from peace offerings there. The bronze altar he made was too small. It could not hold the food offering, the burnt offering, and the fat.
At that time Solomon and all Israel with him kept the festival for seven days. A very large crowd came from Lebo-hamath to the stream of Egypt.
On the eighth day they held a special meeting. They had kept the altar dedication for seven days. They had kept the festival for seven days.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he sent the people to their tents. They were happy and glad. They were glad because of the good things the LORD had done for David, Solomon, and Israel His people.
Solomon finished the LORD’s temple and the king’s house. He did well in all he planned to do in both.
The LORD appeared to Solomon at night. He said, “I have heard your prayer. I have chosen this place for Myself. It will be a house where people give sacrifices.
If I close the sky so no rain falls, or tell locusts to eat the land, or send sickness among My people,
and if My people who are called by My name are humble, pray, look for Me, and turn from their bad ways, then I will hear them from heaven. I will forgive their sin and heal their land.”
“Now My eyes will be open. My ears will listen to the prayer made in this place.
I have chosen and made holy this temple. My name will be here forever. My eyes and My heart will be here always.”
“As for you, if you walk before Me as David your father walked, and do all I commanded you to do, and keep My rules and My laws,
then I will make your kingdom last. I promised David your father that no one from your family would stop ruling over Israel.”
“But if you turn away and leave My rules and commands I gave you, and if you go serve and worship other gods,
then I will pull Israel out of the land I gave them. I will throw away this temple I made holy for My name. I will make it a warning and a joke to all nations.”
“This temple is great now, but all who pass by will be shocked. They will ask why the LORD did this to this land and temple.

People will answer that they left the LORD, the God of their fathers. He brought them out of Egypt. They held on to other gods, worshiped them, and served them. So He brought all this trouble on them.”
After twenty years, Solomon finished building the the LORD’s house and his own house.
Solomon built again the cities Hiram gave him. He moved Israel people to live in them.
Then Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and took it over.
He built Tadmor in the desert. He also built cities to store things in Hamath.
He built Upper and Lower Beth-horon again. He made them strong cities with walls, gates, and bars.
He built Baalath too. He built cities to store things, cities for his chariots and horses, and all he wanted to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and his whole land.
Some people were left from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. They were not Israel people.
Their children stayed in the land after them. Israel had not destroyed them. Solomon made them work hard. They still do this today.
But Solomon did not make Israel people work like that. They were his soldiers, leaders, and chariot and horse captains.
King Solomon had 250 leaders. They watched over the people.

Solomon brought Pharaoh’s daughter from David’s City to the house he built for her. He said, “My wife will not live in David’s house, king of Israel. The places where the the LORD’s holy box came are holy.”
At that time, Solomon gave burnt gifts to the the LORD on the the LORD’s altar. He had built it in front of the porch.
He gave them each day, as Moses said. He did this on rest days, new moon days, and three special times each year: the Feast of Bread Without Yeast, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tents.

Like his father David’s plan, Solomon put priests in groups to serve. He put Levites in groups to sing praise and help the priests each day. He also put gate guards in groups at each gate. David, the man of God, had told him to do this.
They did not turn away from the king’s words about the priests, Levites, or treasure rooms.
So all Solomon’s work was done. It started when they laid the base of the the LORD’s house. It ended when the the LORD’s house was finished. The The LORD’s house was done.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and Eloth on the coast of Edom.
There, Hiram sent him ships with his servants. Sailors who knew the sea went too. They went with Solomon’s servants to Ophir. They brought back 450 talents of gold to King Solomon.

The queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was. She came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions. She brought a very large group with her. Camels carried spices, gold, and precious stones. She met Solomon and told him everything on her mind.
Solomon answered every question she asked. Nothing was too hard for him to explain.
The queen saw Solomon's wisdom. She also saw the house he built.

She saw the food on his table. She saw his servants and how they stood. She saw their clothes. She saw his drink servers and their clothes. She saw the steps he took up to the house of the the LORD. She was so amazed she could hardly breathe.
She said to the king, "What I heard in my country about your words and your wisdom is true.
I did not believe it until I came and saw it with my own eyes. People did not tell me even half of it. You are even wiser than the report I heard.
How happy your people must be! How happy these servants of yours must be, who stand before you all the time and hear your wisdom!

Praise be to the the LORD your God, who was pleased with you and put you on His throne as king for the the LORD your God. Because the the LORD loved Israel forever, He made you king over them. He made you king to do what is fair and right."
She gave the king 120 talents of gold. She also gave him many spices and precious stones. No spice was ever like the spice the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
The servants of Hiram and Solomon brought gold from Ophir. They also brought valuable wood.
The king used that wood to make steps for the house of the the LORD and for his own house. He also made harps and lyres for the singers. Nothing like them had been seen before in Judah.
King Solomon gave the queen everything she wanted and asked for. This was besides what she had brought him. Then she turned and went back to her country with her servants.
Solomon received 666 talents of gold in one year.
This was besides the gold and silver brought by traders, merchants, all the kings of Arabia, and the governors of the land.
King Solomon made 200 large shields of hammered gold. Each shield used 600 pieces of gold.
He made 300 smaller shields of hammered gold. Each used 300 pieces of gold. The king put them in the building called the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a great throne of ivory. He covered it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps. A footrest of gold was attached to it. There were armrests on each side. Two lions stood beside the armrests.
Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one on each side. No other kingdom had a throne like it.
All of Solomon's drinking cups were gold. All the dishes in the building called the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. In Solomon's time, silver was not worth much.
The king had ships that went to Tarshish with Hiram's servants. Once every three years the ships came back. They brought gold, silver, ivory, monkeys, and peacocks.
Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
All the kings of the earth came to see Solomon. They wanted to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
Every year each visitor brought gifts: silver and gold items, clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
Solomon had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots. He had 12,000 horsemen. He kept some in chariot cities and some with him in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the river to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem. He made cedar wood as common as fig trees in the lowlands.
Horses were brought to Solomon from Egypt and from every land.

The rest of what Solomon did, from first to last, is written in the records of Nathan the prophet. It is also in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite and in the visions of Iddo the prophet about Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for 40 years.
Then Solomon died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam became king after him.
Rehoboam went to Shechem. All Israel had come there to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard this, he came back from Egypt. He had run away there from King Solomon.
The people sent for Jeroboam. He and all Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
“Your father made our work very hard. Now make his hard work and heavy load lighter, and we will serve you.”
Rehoboam said, “Come back to me in three days.” So the people left.
King Rehoboam asked the older men who had served his father Solomon while he was alive, “How do you say I should answer these people?”
They said, “If you are kind to these people and please them and speak good words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
But Rehoboam did not listen to the older men’s advice. He asked the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
He asked them, “What do you say? How should I answer these people who say, ‘Make the hard work your father gave us easier’?”
The young men who had grown up with him said, “Tell the people who said to you, ‘Your father made our load heavy, but you make it lighter,’ ‘I am even stronger than my father.’
Say, ‘My father put a heavy load on you, but I will make your load even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you much worse.’”
On the third day, Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam, as the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
The king answered them in a harsh way. He did not listen to the older men’s advice.
He spoke to them the way the young men told him. He said, “My father made your load heavy, but I will make it heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you much worse.”
The king did not listen to the people. This happened because God planned it. The LORD wanted to keep His word, which He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, they said, “We have no share in David! We have no part in Jesse’s son! Israel, go home! David, take care of your own kingdom!” Then all Israel went home.
But Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was in charge of forced work. The Israelites threw stones at him, and he died. King Rehoboam got into his chariot and escaped to Jerusalem.
Israel has been against David’s family to this day.
Rehoboam went to Jerusalem. He called together the men of Judah and Benjamin. There were 180,000 chosen fighters. They were ready to fight Israel. They wanted to win back the kingdom for Rehoboam.
The word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, a man of God.
God said, "Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and all the people of Israel in Judah and Benjamin this:
'This is what the LORD says: You must not go up. You must not fight your brothers. Go home. This is from Me.'" The people listened to the LORD's words. They went back and did not attack Jeroboam.
Rehoboam stayed in Jerusalem. He built cities in Judah to keep them safe.
He built Bethlehem, Etam, and Tekoa.
He built Beth-zur, Soco, and Adullam.
He built Gath, Mareshah, and Ziph.
He built Adoraim, Lachish, and Azekah.
He built Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. These were strong cities in Judah and Benjamin.
He made the strong places stronger. He put leaders in them. He stored food, oil, and wine there.
He put shields and spears in every city. He made them very strong. Judah and Benjamin were on his side.
The priests and Levites from all over Israel came to Rehoboam.
The Levites left their fields and homes. They came to Judah and Jerusalem. Jeroboam and his sons had not let them serve the LORD.
Jeroboam chose his own priests. They served at the high places. They served the goat idols and the calves he had made.
People from every tribe of Israel wanted to follow the LORD, the God of Israel. They came to Jerusalem after the Levites. They came to give offerings to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
They made Judah strong. They helped Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years. They followed the ways of David and Solomon for three years.
Rehoboam married Mahalath. She was the daughter of Jerimoth son of David. Her mother was Abihail, daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
She had sons named Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
Later he married Maacah, daughter of Absalom. She had sons named Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Maacah more than his other wives and servant wives. He had 18 wives and 60 servant wives. He had 28 sons and 60 daughters.
He chose Abijah, Maacah's son, to be the leader. Abijah would be king after him.
Rehoboam was wise. He sent some of his sons to cities in Judah and Benjamin. He gave them plenty of food. He found many wives for them.
After Rehoboam became strong as king, he and all the people of Israel with him left the law of the LORD.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, they were not faithful to the LORD. So Shishak, king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem.
He had 1,200 war carts, 60,000 men on horses, and many people with him from Egypt. They were Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites.
He took the strong cities of Judah and came to Jerusalem.

Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah. They had gathered in Jerusalem because they were afraid of Shishak. He said to them, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have left Me, so I will leave you to Shishak.'"
The leaders of Israel and the king made themselves humble. They said, "The LORD is right."

When the LORD saw that they made themselves humble, He spoke to Shemaiah. He said, "They made themselves humble, so I will not destroy them. I will soon save them. My anger will not pour out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
But they will serve him, so they can learn the difference between serving Me and serving the kings of other lands."
Shishak, king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem. He took the treasures of the LORD's house and the treasures of the king's house. He took everything. He even took the gold shields that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place. He gave them to the leaders of the guards who watched the door of the king's house.
When the king went to the LORD's house, the guards went with him. They carried the shields. Then they took them back to the guard room.
Because Rehoboam made himself humble, the LORD's anger turned from him. He was not destroyed all the way. Also, some good things were in Judah.

King Rehoboam became strong in Jerusalem and stayed king. He was 41 years old when he became king. He ruled 17 years in Jerusalem. This was the city the LORD chose from all the tribes of Israel. He put His Name there. Rehoboam's mother was Naamah. She was an Ammonite.
He did wrong because he had not set his heart to look for the LORD.

The things Rehoboam did first and last are written in the books of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the man who saw visions. They also wrote family lists. There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the time.
Rehoboam died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Abijah became king after him.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king of Judah.
He ruled in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah. She was the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah went to war with 400,000 brave soldiers. Jeroboam got ready to fight him with 800,000 brave soldiers.
Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim. He said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel.
You know the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom to David and his sons forever. He made a lasting promise with them. "
Jeroboam son of Nebat was a servant of Solomon son of David. But Jeroboam turned against his master and took power.
Some worthless men joined him. They grew strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon. Rehoboam was young and soft-hearted, so he could not stop them. "

Now you think you can stand against the kingdom of the LORD. That kingdom is in the hands of David's sons. You have many people, and you have the gold calves Jeroboam made for you. He made them to be your gods.

You drove away the LORD's priests, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites. You made your own priests, like other countries do. Anyone who brings a young bull and seven rams can become a priest for gods that are not real.
But we serve the LORD our God. We have not left Him. The priests who serve the LORD are Aaron's sons, and the Levites help them.

Every morning and evening they burn offerings and sweet incense to the LORD. They set out bread on the clean table. They light the gold lampstand each evening. We do the LORD's work. But you left Him.
God is with us. He leads us. His priests blow the trumpets to warn you. People of Israel, do not fight the LORD, the God of your fathers. You will not win."
Jeroboam sent men to sneak around behind them. His army stood in front of Judah, and the hidden men stood behind them.
Judah turned around and saw they were trapped front and back. They cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
The men of Judah shouted. When they shouted, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel in front of Abijah and Judah.
The Israelites ran away from Judah. God gave them into Judah's hands.
Abijah and his people hit them hard. Five hundred thousand chosen men from Israel died.
At that time the Israelites were brought low. The men of Judah won because they trusted the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Abijah chased Jeroboam and took cities from him. He took Bethel and its towns, Jeshanah and its towns, and Ephron and its towns.
Jeroboam never got his strength back while Abijah lived. The LORD struck him, and he died.
Abijah grew strong. He married fourteen wives. He had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of Abijah's story, his ways and words, is written in the book of the prophet Iddo.
Abijah died and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa became king after him. During Asa's time, the land was at peace for ten years.
Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He took away the foreign altars and the high places. He broke the stone pillars and cut down the Asherah poles.
He told Judah to look for the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to keep the law and the command.
He took away the high places and the sun images from all the cities of Judah. The kingdom was at peace under him.
Because the land was at peace, Asa built strong cities in Judah. There was no war in those years, because the LORD gave him rest.

Asa said to Judah, "Let us build these cities. Let us put walls around them, with towers, gates, and bars. The land is still open before us, because we looked for the LORD our God. We looked for Him, and He gave us rest all around." So they built and did well.
Asa had an army. From Judah there were 300,000 men with large shields and spears. From Benjamin there were 280,000 men with shields and bows. All of them were strong fighters.
Zerah, a man from Cush, came against them with an army of one million men and three hundred chariots. He came as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him. They set up for battle in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

Asa cried out to the LORD his God. He said, "the LORD, no one can help like You, whether someone is strong or weak. Help us, the LORD our God, because we trust in You. We came in Your name against this big crowd. the LORD, You are our God. Do not let people win against You."
The LORD struck the men from Cush before Asa and Judah. The men from Cush ran away.
Asa and his people chased them to Gerar. The men from Cush fell until they could not get up again. They were broken before the LORD and His army. Asa's men took a lot of things.
They struck all the cities around Gerar, because they were afraid of the LORD. They took things from all the cities, because there was much to take.
They also struck the tents where people kept their animals. They took many sheep and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
Now God’s Spirit came on Azariah son of Oded.

He went out to meet Asa. He said, “Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you when you are with Him. If you look for Him, He will let you find Him. But if you leave Him, He will leave you. “
For many days, Israel did not have the true God. They did not have a priest to teach them. They did not have God’s law.
But when they were in trouble, they turned back to the LORD, the God of Israel. They looked for Him, and He let them find Him.
In those days, people who went out or came in had no peace. There were many fights among the people who lived in those lands.
One nation crushed another nation. One city crushed another city. God made trouble for them in every way.
But you, be strong. Do not give up. Your work will be rewarded.”

When Asa heard these words and the message from Oded the prophet, he became brave. He took away the hated idols from all Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had taken in the hills of Ephraim. He fixed the altar of the LORD that was in front of the porch of the LORD’s house.

Then he gathered all Judah and Benjamin. He also gathered people from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who lived with them. Many people had come to him from Israel. They came because they saw that the LORD, his God, was with him.
They gathered in Jerusalem in the third month. This was in the fifteenth year of Asa’s rule.
At that time, they gave the LORD seven hundred bulls and seven thousand sheep. These came from the things they had taken in battle.
Then they made a promise to look for the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and all their soul.
Anyone who would not look for the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death. This was for small and great, man or woman.
They shouted to the LORD with a loud voice. They shouted and blew trumpets and horns.
All Judah was happy about the promise. They had sworn it with all their heart. They looked for Him with all their strength, and He let them find Him. So the LORD gave them rest on every side.
King Asa also took away his grandmother Maacah from being queen mother. She had made a hated Asherah pole. Asa cut down the pole. He chopped it up. He burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The high places were not taken away from Israel. But Asa’s heart was fully given to the LORD all his days.
He brought into God’s house the silver and gold things and the tools that he and his father had set apart for God.
There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s rule.
In the thirty-sixth year of King Asa's rule, Baasha, king of Israel, went up against Judah. He built the town of Ramah. He did this so no one could go in or out to King Asa of Judah.
King Asa took silver and gold from the LORD's house and from his own house. He sent it to Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus. He said,
"There is a deal between me and you, and between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you silver and gold. Go and break your deal with Baasha, king of Israel. Then he will leave me alone."
Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa. He sent his army leaders to the towns of Israel. They attacked Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the storage places in the towns of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah. He ended his work.
King Asa took all of Judah. They carried the stones and wood from Ramah that Baasha had built. They used them to build Geba and Mizpah.
At that time, Hanani the seer came to King Asa of Judah. He said to him, "You trusted the king of Aram. You did not trust the LORD your God. So the army of the king of Aram got away from you.
"Were not the Cushites and Libyans a very big army with many chariots and horsemen? Yet when you trusted the LORD, He gave them into your hand.
"The LORD's eyes look all over the earth. He wants to help people whose hearts are fully His. You did a foolish thing. So from now on, you will have wars."
Asa got angry with the seer. He put him in jail, because he was very angry at him for this. At that time, Asa was mean to some of the people.
The other things Asa did, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, Asa got sick in his feet. His sickness was very bad. But even then, he did not ask the LORD for help. He asked doctors instead.
In the forty-first year of his rule, Asa died. He was buried with his family.

They buried him in the tombs he had dug for himself in the city of David. They laid him on a bed full of spices and many kinds of perfume oil. Skilled workers made the perfume. They made a very big fire for him.
Jehoshaphat, Asa's son, became king after him. He grew strong in Israel.
He put soldiers in all the strong cities of Judah. He also put leaders in charge of the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he followed the good ways of his father David. He did not worship the Baals.
He looked to the God of his father. He walked in God's commands. He did not act like Israel.
So the LORD made his kingdom strong. All the people of Judah gave gifts to Jehoshaphat. He had great riches and honor.
His heart was set on following the LORD. He also removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.
In the third year of his rule, he sent his leaders to teach in the cities of Judah. Their names were Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah.
The Levites with them were Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah. The priests with them were Elishama and Jehoram.
They taught in Judah. They had the book of the law of the LORD with them. They went through all the cities of Judah and taught the people.
Fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms around Judah, so they did not fight Jehoshaphat.
Some Philistines brought gifts and silver to Jehoshaphat. The Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats.
Jehoshaphat kept growing greater. He built forts and store cities in Judah.
He had much work in the cities of Judah. Strong, brave soldiers were in Jerusalem.
Here is the count of them by their family groups in Judah. The leaders of thousands were Adnah the leader, with 300,000 mighty men.
Next was Jehohanan the leader, with 280,000 men.
Next was Amasiah son of Zichri, who gave himself to the LORD. He had 200,000 mighty men.
From Benjamin there was Eliada, a mighty man, with 200,000 men armed with bows and shields.
Next was Jehozabad, with 180,000 men ready for war.
These men served the king. This was in addition to the men the king had placed in the strong cities all over Judah.
Jehoshaphat had a lot of riches and honor. He joined his family to Ahab's family.
After some years, he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab killed many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him. Ahab urged him to go up to Ramoth Gilead.
Ahab, king of Israel, said to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth Gilead?" Jehoshaphat said, "I am like you. My people are like your people. I will be with you in the war."
Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please ask what the the LORD says today."
The king of Israel gathered four hundred prophets. He said to them, "Should we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or should I stay home?" They said, "Go up. God will give it to the king."
Jehoshaphat said, "Is there still a prophet of the the LORD here? We should ask him."

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is one more man. We can ask the the LORD through him. But I hate him. He never says good things about me. He always says bad things. His name is Micaiah son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said, "Don't say that, king."
The king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imla quickly."
The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, each sat on his throne. They wore royal robes. They sat at the threshing floor by the gate of Samaria. All the prophets spoke in front of them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself. He said, "This is what the the LORD says: 'With these horns you will push the Arameans until they are destroyed.'"
All the prophets said the same thing: "Go up to Ramoth Gilead and win. The the LORD will give it to the king."
The messenger who went to get Micaiah said to him, "Look, all the prophets say the same good thing to the king. Please say the same thing they say. Speak good words too."
Micaiah said, "As surely as the the LORD lives, I will speak only what my God says."
When Micaiah came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or should I stay home?" Micaiah said, "Go up and win. They will be given into your hand."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me only the truth in the name of the the LORD?"
Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. The the LORD said, 'These people have no master. Let each one go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you he would not say good things about me, but bad things?"
Micaiah said, "So listen to the word of the the LORD. I saw the the LORD sitting on His throne. All the armies of heaven stood on His right and on His left."
The the LORD said, "Who will trick Ahab, king of Israel, into going up and dying at Ramoth Gilead?" One said one thing. Another said another.
Then a spirit came out and stood before the the LORD. He said, "I will trick him." The the LORD said to him, "How?"
The spirit said, "I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets." The the LORD said, "You will trick him. You will also succeed. Go out and do it."
Micaiah said, "Now look, the the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours. The the LORD has said bad things will happen to you."
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came close and hit Micaiah on the cheek. He said, "Which way did the the LORD's Spirit go from me to speak to you?"
Micaiah said, "You will see. On that day you will hide in an inner room."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon, the ruler of the city, and to Joash the king's son."
He said, "Say this: 'The king says, Put this man in prison. Feed him only a little bread and water until I come back safe.'"
Micaiah said, "If you come back safe, the the LORD did not speak through me. Listen, everyone!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, went up to Ramoth Gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will dress like someone else and go into battle. But you wear your own clothes." So the king of Israel dressed like someone else, and they went into battle.
The king of Aram had told his chariot captains, "Don't fight the small soldiers or the big leaders. Fight only the king of Israel."
When the chariot captains saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That is the king of Israel." They turned to fight him. Jehoshaphat shouted for help. The the LORD helped him. God made them turn away from him.
When the chariot captains saw it was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.
A man shot an arrow without aiming. He hit the king of Israel between the pieces of his armor. The king said to his driver, "Turn around and take me out of the battle. I am hurt."
The battle got worse that day. The king of Israel stayed in his chariot facing Aram until evening. He died at sunset.
King Jehoshaphat of Judah went home in peace. He went to his house in Jerusalem.

Jehu was the son of Hanani. He was a prophet. He went out to meet the king. He said, "King Jehoshaphat, should you help bad people? Should you love people who hate the LORD? Because of this, the LORD is angry with you.
But some good things are found in you. You took away the poles used to worship a false god. You made your heart ready to look for God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out among the people. He went from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim. He brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
He put judges in the land. He put them in every strong city of Judah.
He said to the judges, "Look at what you are doing. You do not judge for people. You judge for the LORD. He is with you when you decide a case.
Now let the fear of the LORD be on you. Be careful and do it. With the LORD our God, there is no wrong. There is no playing favorites. There is no taking bribes."
Jehoshaphat also put Levites, priests, and leaders of Israel in Jerusalem. They were there to judge for the LORD. They were there to settle arguments. They came back to Jerusalem.
He told them, "Do this with faith. Do it with a whole heart. Do it in fear of the LORD.

If your brothers in their cities bring a case to you, it may be about blood, or about God's law, or about rules and decisions, warn them. Then they will not be guilty before the LORD. Then anger will not come on you and your brothers. Do this, and you will not be guilty.

Look, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all things about the LORD. Zebadiah son of Ishmael is the leader of Judah in all things about the king. The Levites and officers are before you. Be strong and do it. May the LORD be with those who do good."
After this, the people of Moab and Ammon came, along with some Meunites, to make war against Jehoshaphat.
Some men came and told Jehoshaphat, "A big army is coming against you from Aram, from across the sea. They are already at Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi."
Jehoshaphat was afraid. He decided to ask the LORD for help. He told all Judah to go without food.
People from all the towns of Judah came together to ask the LORD for help.
Jehoshaphat stood up in the crowd of Judah and Jerusalem in the LORD's house. He was in the new courtyard.
He said, "LORD, God of our fathers, are You not God in heaven? You rule all the kingdoms of the nations. Power and strength are in Your hand. No one can stand against You.
Our God, did You not drive out the people who lived in this land before Your people Israel? You gave it to the children of Abraham, Your friend, for all time.
They lived there and built a holy place for Your name. They said,

'If trouble comes on us—sword, punishment, sickness, or hunger—we will stand before this house and before You, because Your name is in this house. We will cry to You in our trouble, and You will hear and save us.'
Now look! The men of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir are here. You did not let Israel enter their land when Israel came from Egypt. Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them.
See how they pay us back. They come to drive us out of the land You gave us.
Our God, will You not judge them? We have no strength against this big army that comes against us. We do not know what to do. But our eyes are on You."
All Judah stood before the LORD, with their wives and children and little ones.
Then the Spirit of the LORD came on Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah. He was a Levite from Asaph's family. He was in the middle of the crowd.
He said, "Listen, all Judah and people of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat! The LORD says to you, 'Do not be afraid. Do not be scared of this big army. The battle is not yours. It is God's.'
Tomorrow go down against them. They are coming up by the hill of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the valley, before the desert of Jeruel.

You do not need to fight in this battle. Stand still and see how the LORD saves you. People of Judah and Jerusalem, do not be afraid. Do not be scared. Go out against them tomorrow, and the LORD will be with you."
Jehoshaphat bowed low with his face to the ground. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem fell before the LORD to worship Him.
Then Levites from the Kohathites and Korahites stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

Early in the morning they got up and went out to the desert of Tekoa. As they left, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, people of Judah and Jerusalem! Trust in the LORD your God, and you will be safe. Trust His prophets, and you will do well."
After asking the people, he chose singers for the LORD. They praised the LORD for His holy beauty. They went out ahead of the army and said, "Give thanks to the LORD, for His love lasts forever."
When they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah. They were defeated.
The men of Ammon and Moab turned against the people of Mount Seir. They destroyed them completely. When they finished with Seir, they turned on each other and destroyed themselves.
When Judah came to the watchtower in the desert, they looked at the army. They saw dead bodies on the ground. No one had escaped.

Jehoshaphat and his people came to take the goods. They found many bodies and valuable things. They took so much that they could not carry it all. They spent three days taking the goods, because there was so much.
On the fourth day they met in the Valley of Blessing. There they praised the LORD. That is why the place is called the Valley of Blessing to this day.
Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem went back. Jehoshaphat led them. They were happy as they returned to Jerusalem, because the LORD had made them glad over their enemies.
They came to Jerusalem, to the house of the LORD, with harps, lyres, and trumpets.
Fear of God came on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against Israel's enemies.
Then Jehoshaphat's kingdom was at peace. His God gave him rest on every side.
Jehoshaphat ruled over Judah. He was 35 years old when he became king. He ruled 25 years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
He followed the ways of his father Asa. He did not turn from them. He did what was right in the LORD's eyes.
But the high places were not taken away. The people still had not set their hearts on the God of their fathers.
The rest of Jehoshaphat's deeds, first and last, are written in the book of Jehu son of Hanani. That book is mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel.
Later, Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined with Ahaziah king of Israel. Ahaziah did many bad things.
They agreed to build ships to go to Tarshish. They built the ships in Ezion-geber.

Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah spoke against Jehoshaphat. He said, "Because you joined with Ahaziah, the LORD will break up what you have made." The ships were wrecked and could not sail to Tarshish.
Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. His son Jehoram became king after him.
Jehoram had brothers. They were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. They were all sons of Jehoshaphat, king of Israel.
Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold, and other valuable things. He also gave them strong cities in Judah. But he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because Jehoram was the firstborn son.
When Jehoram took power, he made himself strong. He killed all his brothers with a sword. He also killed some leaders of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, just as Ahab’s family had done. He married Ahab’s daughter. He did what was evil in the eyes of the the LORD.
But the LORD did not want to destroy David’s family. He had made a promise to David. He had promised to keep David’s family line alive forever.
In Jehoram’s time, Edom broke away from Judah’s rule. They chose their own king.
Jehoram went with his officers and all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him and his chariot leaders. But he got up and attacked them at night.
Edom is still free from Judah today. At that time, Libnah also broke away from his rule. This happened because Jehoram had left the LORD, the God of his fathers.
He also made high places on the hills of Judah. He led the people of Jerusalem away from the LORD. He led Judah down the wrong path.

Then a letter came to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet. It said, "This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: You have not followed the ways of your father Jehoshaphat. You have not followed the ways of Asa, king of Judah.

Instead, you have followed the ways of the kings of Israel. You have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem away from the LORD, just like Ahab’s family did. You have also killed your brothers. They were your father’s family, and they were better than you.
So the LORD will bring a terrible sickness on your people, your sons, your wives, and all your things.
You yourself will be very sick in your stomach. Your sickness will get worse day after day, until your insides come out."
Then the LORD made the Philistines and the Arabs angry at Jehoram. These Arabs lived near the Cushites.
They came into Judah and broke in. They took all the things they found in the king’s house. They also took his sons and his wives. The only son left was Jehoahaz, his youngest son.
After all this, the LORD made Jehoram very sick in his stomach. The sickness could not be cured.
After two years, his sickness got so bad that his insides came out. He died in great pain. His people did not burn spices for him, as they had done for his fathers.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eight years. No one was sad when he died. They buried him in the City of David, but not with the other kings.
The people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king. He was the youngest son of Jehoram, king of Judah. The older sons had been killed by a group of raiders who came with the Arabs to the camp.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to rule. He ruled one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah. She was the daughter of Omri.
He followed the bad ways of Ahab's family. His mother told him to do wrong.
He did what the the LORD saw as bad, like Ahab's family did. After his father died, they gave him bad advice. That advice ruined him.
He listened to their advice. He went with Joram, the son of Ahab and king of Israel, to fight Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth Gilead. The people of Aram hurt Joram.

Joram went back to Jezreel to get well. He had been hurt at Ramah while fighting Hazael, king of Aram. Ahaziah, son of Jehoram and king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to see Joram, because Joram was sick.
God caused Ahaziah to be destroyed when he went to see Joram. When he got there, he went out with Joram to meet Jehu, the son of Nimshi. The the LORD had chosen Jehu to destroy Ahab's family.
While Jehu was punishing Ahab's family, he found the leaders of Judah. He also found the sons of Ahaziah's relatives who helped Ahaziah. He killed them.

Jehu's men looked for Ahaziah. They caught him while he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu and killed him. They buried him because they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who followed the the LORD with all his heart." After that, Ahaziah's family had no strength to rule.
When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw that her son was dead, she took over. She killed all the royal family of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash, Ahaziah's son. She hid him while the other royal children were being killed. She put him and his nurse in a bedroom. Jehoshabeath was King Jehoram's daughter and the wife of Jehoiada the priest. She was Ahaziah's sister. She hid Joash from Athaliah so Athaliah would not kill him.
Joash stayed hidden with them in God's house for six years. During that time, Athaliah ruled the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada grew strong and made a promise with the captains of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
They went all through Judah. They brought the Levites from every city in Judah and the family leaders of Israel to Jerusalem.
The whole group made a promise with the king at God’s house. Jehoiada said, “Look, the king’s son will rule. The LORD said this would happen for David’s family.”
“This is what you must do. One third of you priests and Levites who come to work on the Sabbath will guard the doors.
One third will be at the king’s house. One third will be at the Foundation Gate. All the people will be in the yards of the LORD’s house.
No one may go into the LORD’s house except the priests and Levites who are working. They may go in because they are holy. All the people must follow the LORD’s rules.
The Levites must stand around the king. Each man must hold his weapon. Anyone who goes into the temple must die. You must stay close to the king wherever he goes.”

The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest told them. Each man brought his group. Some were just starting work for the Sabbath, and some were ending. Jehoiada did not send any group away.
Jehoiada the priest gave the captains of hundreds the spears, shields, and small shields that had belonged to King David. They were in God’s house.
He put all the people in place. Each man held his weapon. They stood all around the king, from the south side of God’s house to the north side, near the altar and the temple.
They brought out the king’s son. They put the crown on him. They gave him the law book. They made him king. Jehoiada and his sons poured oil on him. They said, “Long live the king!”
Athaliah heard the noise of people running and praising the king. She came to the people at the LORD’s house.

She looked and saw the king standing by his pillar at the door. The leaders and trumpet players stood by the king. All the people were happy. They blew trumpets. The singers sang and played music and led the praise. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and yelled, “You are turning against the king! You are turning against the king!”

Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds who led the army. He said, “Take her out between the rows. Anyone who follows her must die by the sword.” He had already said, “Do not kill her in the LORD’s house.”
They grabbed her. She went to the entrance of the Horse Gate at the king’s house. They killed her there.
Jehoiada made a promise between himself, all the people, and the king. They would be the LORD’s people.
All the people went to Baal’s temple and tore it down. They smashed its altars and statues. They killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars.

Jehoiada put the priests and Levites in charge of the LORD’s house. They followed David’s groups. They gave burnt offerings to the LORD, as Moses’ law says. They did it with joy and singing, as David had ordered.
He put gatekeepers at the gates of the LORD’s house. No one who was unclean in any way could go in.

He took the captains of hundreds, the leaders, the rulers of the people, and all the people. They brought the king down from the LORD’s house. They went through the Upper Gate to the king’s house. They sat the king on the throne.
All the people were happy. The city was quiet, because Athaliah had been killed with a sword.
Joash was seven years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother's name was Zibiah. She was from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the the LORD during all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Jehoiada picked two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.
Later, Joash wanted to fix the the LORD's house.
He gathered the priests and Levites. He said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah. Collect money each year from all Israel to fix the house of your God. Hurry." But the Levites did not hurry.

The king called Jehoiada the chief priest. He asked, "Why didn't you make the Levites bring from Judah and Jerusalem the money that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, and the people of Israel gave for the tent of meeting?"
The sons of Athaliah, that bad woman, had broken into God's house. They had also used the holy things from the the LORD's temple for the Baals.
The king gave an order. They made a chest and put it outside, at the gate of the the LORD's temple.
They told the people of Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the the LORD the tax that Moses, the servant of God, had asked Israel to give in the desert.
All the leaders and all the people were happy. They brought money and put it in the chest until it was full.

When the Levites brought the chest to the king's men, they saw there was a lot of money. The king's secretary and the chief priest's officer would empty the chest. They would carry it back to its place. They did this every day. They gathered a lot of money.

The king and Jehoiada gave the money to the men who did the work on the the LORD's house. They hired stonecutters and carpenters to fix the the LORD's house. They also hired men who worked with iron and bronze to make the the LORD's house strong.
The workers did the work. The repair went well. They made God's house like it was before, and they made it strong.

When they finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada. They made things for the the LORD's temple: serving things, things for burnt offerings, bowls, and gold and silver things. They offered burnt offerings in the the LORD's temple every day while Jehoiada lived.
Jehoiada grew very old. He died at one hundred thirty years old.
They buried him with the kings in the City of David. He had done good in Israel, and for God and His house.
After Jehoiada died, the leaders of Judah came to the king and bowed down to him. The king listened to them.
They left the house of the the LORD, the God of their fathers. They served Asherah poles and idols. So God's anger came on Judah and Jerusalem because of their guilt.
God sent prophets to bring them back to the the LORD. The prophets warned them, but they would not listen.

The Spirit of God came on Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood in front of the people and said, "This is what God says: Why do you break the the LORD's commands? You will not do well. You have left the the LORD, so He has left you."
They made a plan against him at the king's command. They threw stones at him in the courtyard of the the LORD's temple.
King Joash did not remember the kindness that Jehoiada, his father, had shown him. He killed Jehoiada's son. As Zechariah died, he said, "May the the LORD see this and punish them."
At the end of the year, the army of Aram came against him. They came to Judah and Jerusalem. They destroyed all the leaders of the people. They sent all the things they took to the king of Damascus.
The army of Aram came with only a few men. But the the LORD gave a very large army into their hands, because Judah had left the the LORD, the God of their fathers. So Joash was punished.

When they left, they left Joash badly hurt. His servants made a plan against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest. They killed him on his bed. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
The men who made the plan against him were Zabad, son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad, son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
Many things were said against Joash. The work on God's house was written in the book of the kings. His son Amaziah became king after him.
Amaziah was 25 years old when he became king. He ruled 29 years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not with all his heart.
When his kingdom was strong, he killed the servants who had killed his father, the king.

But he did not kill their sons. The book of the law of Moses says what the LORD commanded: "Parents must not die for their children. Children must not die for their parents. Each person must die for his own sin."

Amaziah gathered the people of Judah. He chose leaders for groups of 1,000 and 100. He counted all the men of Judah and Benjamin who were 20 years old or older. He found 300,000 strong men who could fight. They held spears and shields.
He hired 100,000 brave soldiers from Israel. He paid 100 talents of silver.
A man of God came to him and said, "King, do not let the army of Israel go with you. The LORD is not with Israel. He is not with the people of Ephraim.
But if you go, be strong for the fight. God will make you fall before your enemies. God can help or make you fall."
Amaziah said to the man of God, "What about the 100 talents of silver I gave to the Israel troops?" The man of God said, "The LORD can give you much more than that."
So Amaziah sent the troops from Ephraim home. They were very angry with Judah. They went home in a rage.
Amaziah became strong. He led his people to the Valley of Salt. He killed 10,000 men from Seir.
The men of Judah captured 10,000 men alive. They brought them to the top of a rock. They threw them down. All of them died.
The troops that Amaziah had sent home raided cities in Judah. They went from Samaria to Beth-horon. They killed 3,000 people. They took many valuable things.
After Amaziah came back from killing the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir. He set them up as his own gods. He bowed down to them. He burned incense to them.
The LORD was angry with Amaziah. He sent a prophet to him. The prophet said, "Why do you look for gods that could not save their own people from you?"

While he spoke, the king said to him, "Did we make you an adviser to the king? Stop! Why should you be hit?" The prophet stopped. Then he said, "I know that God has planned to destroy you. You did this, and you did not listen to my advice."
Amaziah, king of Judah, asked for advice. Then he sent a message to Joash, son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel. It said, "Come. Let us fight."

Joash, king of Israel, sent a message back to Amaziah, king of Judah. It said, "A small thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a big cedar tree in Lebanon. It said, 'Give your daughter to my son for a wife.' A wild animal in Lebanon walked by and stepped on the thistle.
You say, 'I beat Edom.' Your heart makes you proud. Now stay home. Why stir up trouble? You and Judah will fall."
Amaziah did not listen. This was from God. God wanted to let the enemy win. They had looked for the gods of Edom.
Joash, king of Israel, went up. He and Amaziah, king of Judah, fought each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
Judah was beaten by Israel. Every man ran home.

Joash, king of Israel, captured Amaziah, king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh. He brought him to Jerusalem. He broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate. That was 400 cubits.
He took all the gold, silver, and things in God's house that were with Obed-edom. He took the treasures from the king's house. He took hostages. Then he went back to Samaria.
Amaziah, son of Joash, king of Judah, lived 15 years after the death of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
The rest of the things Amaziah did, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
From the time Amaziah turned away from the LORD, people in Jerusalem made a plan against him. He ran to Lachish. They sent men after him to Lachish. They killed him there.
They brought him back on horses. They buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.
All the people of Judah picked Uzziah. He was sixteen years old. They made him king after his father Amaziah.
He built the town of Eloth. He brought it back to Judah. This was after the king died and was laid to rest with his family.
Uzziah was sixteen when he became king. He ruled 52 years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. He did what his father Amaziah had done.
He asked God for help while Zechariah was alive. Zechariah understood God's messages. As long as Uzziah looked for the LORD, God helped him do well.
He went out and fought the Philistines. He broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod. He built towns in Ashdod and in Philistine land.
God helped him fight the Philistines, the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
The Ammonites paid Uzziah money. His fame spread all the way to Egypt. He became very strong.
Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem. They were at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the Angle. He made them strong.
He built towers in the desert. He dug many wells. He had much livestock in the low hills and the flat land. He had farmers and grape growers in the mountains and in Carmel. He loved the land.
Uzziah had an army ready for war. They went out in groups. Jeiel the writer and Maaseiah the officer counted them. Hananiah, one of the king's leaders, was over them.
The number of family leaders, the strong men, was 2,600.
Under them was an army of 307,500 men. They fought with great power. They helped the king against his enemies.
Uzziah gave all the army shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones for slings.

In Jerusalem he made machines. Skilled men made them. They were put on the towers and corners. They shot arrows and big stones. His name spread far away. God helped him in a wonderful way until he became strong.
But when he became strong, his heart became proud. He did wrong against the LORD his God. He went into the temple of the LORD. He wanted to burn incense on the incense altar.
Azariah the priest went in after him. Eighty brave priests of the LORD went with him.

They said, “Uzziah, it is not for you to burn incense to the LORD. Only the priests, the sons of Aaron, may do that. They are set apart to burn incense. Get out of the holy place. You have done wrong. The LORD God will not give you honor for this.”

Uzziah was angry. He had a pan of incense in his hand. While he was angry with the priests, in front of the priests in the house of the LORD, by the incense altar, a skin disease broke out on his forehead.
Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him. They saw that he had a skin disease on his forehead. They hurried him out. He hurried to leave too, because the LORD had struck him.
King Uzziah had the skin disease until the day he died. He lived in a house by himself. He was kept away from the house of the LORD. His son Jotham ruled the people.
The other things Uzziah did, from first to last, were written by the prophet Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
Uzziah died and was buried with his family. They buried him in the field where the kings were buried. People said he had a skin disease. His son Jotham became king after him.
Jotham was 25 years old when he became king. He was king in Jerusalem for 16 years. His mother was Jerusha. She was the daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the the LORD's eyes, just like his father Uzziah. But he did not go into the the LORD's temple. The people kept doing wrong.
Jotham built the Upper Gate of the the LORD's temple. He also did a lot of work on the wall at the Hill of Ophel.
He built towns in the hill country of Judah. He built forts and towers in the woods.

Jotham fought the king of the Ammonites and beat them. That year, the Ammonites paid him 100 talents of silver, 10,000 baskets of wheat, and 10,000 baskets of barley. They paid the same in the second and third years.
Jotham became strong because he walked the right way before the the LORD his God.
The rest of what Jotham did, and his wars, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was 25 years old when he became king. He was king in Jerusalem for 16 years.
Jotham died and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king after him.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, like his father David.
He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel. He also made metal statues for the Baals.
He burned incense in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He burned his sons in the fire. This was like the terrible things the nations did. The LORD had driven those nations out before the people of Israel.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

So the LORD his God let him fall into the hands of the king of Aram. The Arameans beat him. They took many people away to Damascus. He was also given into the hands of the king of Israel, who hit him hard.
Pekah son of Remaliah killed one hundred twenty thousand people in Judah in one day. They were all strong soldiers. This happened because they had left the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Zichri, a strong man from Ephraim, killed Maaseiah, the king's son. He killed Azrikam, the leader of the palace. He killed Elkanah, who was second to the king.
The Israelites took two hundred thousand of their brothers as prisoners. They took women, sons, and daughters. They also took many things. They brought the things to Samaria.

But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army that was coming to Samaria. He said to them, "Look, the LORD God of your fathers was angry with Judah. So He gave them into your hand. You killed them in a rage that reached up to heaven.
And now you plan to make the people of Judah and Jerusalem your male and female slaves. Are you not also guilty before the LORD your God?
Now hear me. Send back the captives you took from your brothers. The LORD's fierce anger is on you."
Then some leaders of Ephraim stood against the men coming back from war. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.

They said to them, "You must not bring the captives here. You are trying to bring guilt on us from the LORD. That would add to our sins and guilt. Our guilt is already great, and the the LORD's fierce anger is on Israel."
So the armed men left the captives and the things they had taken in front of the leaders and the whole group.

The men named above stood up. They took the captives. From the things taken, they clothed all who had no clothes. They gave them clothes and sandals. They gave them food and drink. They put oil on them. They put all the weak ones on donkeys. They brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, near their brothers. Then they went back to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
The Edomites had come again. They struck Judah and carried away captives.

The Philistines raided the cities in the lowlands and in the south of Judah. They captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco and its nearby towns, Timnah and its nearby towns, and Gimzo and its nearby towns. Then they settled there.
The LORD had brought Judah low because of Ahaz, king of Israel. He led Judah to do wrong, and he had been very unfaithful to the LORD.
Tilgath-pilneser, king of Assyria, came against him. He troubled him instead of helping him.
Ahaz took part of the the LORD's house, part of the king's house, and part from the leaders. He gave it to the king of Assyria. But it did not help him.
In the time of trouble, King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to the LORD.

He offered sacrifices to the gods of Damascus, the ones that had beaten him. He said, "The gods of the kings of Aram help them. I will sacrifice to them so they will help me." But they caused his ruin, and the ruin of all Israel.
Ahaz gathered the things from God's house. He cut up the things from God's house. He shut the doors of the the LORD's house. He made altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods. This made the LORD, the God of his fathers, angry.
The rest of his acts and his ways, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz died and was buried with his fathers in the city in Jerusalem. But they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah became king after him.
Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother was Abijah. She was the daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. He did all the things David his father had done.
In the first month of his first year as king, Hezekiah opened the doors of the LORD's house. He fixed them.
He brought the priests and the Levites. He gathered them in the east side of the city.
"Listen to me, Levites. Make yourselves clean now. Make the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers, clean. Take the dirty things out of the holy place.
Our fathers did wrong. They did evil in the eyes of the LORD our God. They left Him. They turned away from the LORD's house. They turned their backs.
They shut the doors of the porch. They put out the lamps. They did not burn incense. They did not give burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
"So the LORD's anger was on Judah and Jerusalem. He made them a terrible sight. He made them ruined and laughed at. You can see this with your own eyes.
Our fathers died in war. Our sons, daughters, and wives were taken away.
"Now I want to make a promise to the LORD, the God of Israel. I want His anger to leave us.
Now, my sons, do not be lazy. The LORD chose you to stand before Him. He chose you to serve Him. He chose you to be His helpers and to burn incense.

The Levites stood up. They were Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohathites. They were Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel from the Merarites. They were Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershonites.
They were Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaphites. They were Shimei and Jehiel from the Hemanites. They were Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthunites.
They gathered their brothers. They made themselves clean. They went to clean the the LORD's house. They did what the king said by the the LORD's word.

The priests went deep inside the the LORD's house to clean it. They brought out all the dirty things they found in the the LORD's temple. They brought them to the courtyard. The Levites took them out to the Kidron Valley.

They began to make the holy place clean on the first day of the first month. On the eighth day they reached the porch. They made the the LORD's house clean for eight more days. They finished on the sixteenth day of the first month.

Then they went to King Hezekiah. They said, "We have cleaned all of the the LORD's house. We cleaned the altar for burnt offerings and all its tools. We cleaned the table for the bread and all its tools.
We also got ready all the tools King Ahaz had thrown away when he did wrong.
We made them clean. See, they are in front of the the LORD's altar.
King Hezekiah got up early. He gathered the city leaders. They went up to the the LORD's house.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats. These were a sin offering for the kingdom, the holy place, and Judah. Hezekiah told the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them on the the LORD's altar.
They killed the bulls. The priests took the blood and threw it on the altar. They killed the rams and threw the blood on the altar. They killed the lambs and threw the blood on the altar.
They brought the male goats for the sin offering to the king and the people. They put their hands on them.
The priests killed them. They used the blood to pay for sin on the altar. They did this for all Israel. The king said the burnt offering and the sin offering were for all Israel.

Hezekiah put the Levites in the the LORD's house. They had cymbals, harps, and lyres. They did this as David, Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet had said. The the LORD gave this command through His prophets.
The Levites stood with David's instruments. The priests stood with trumpets.

Hezekiah said to offer the burnt offering on the altar. When the burnt offering began, the song to the the LORD began too. The trumpets played. They used David's instruments. David was king of Israel.
All the people bowed down. The singers sang. The trumpeters played. They did this until the burnt offering was done.
When the offering was done, the king and all the people there bowed down and worshiped.
