King Hezekiah and the leaders told the Levites to praise the the LORD. They used the words of David and Asaph the seer. The Levites praised with joy. They bowed down and worshiped.

Hezekiah said, "Now you have given yourselves to the the LORD. Come near. Bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the the LORD's house." The people brought sacrifices and thank offerings. Everyone with a willing heart brought burnt offerings.
The people brought seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs. These were burnt offerings to the the LORD.
There were also six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep that were made holy.

There were not enough priests to skin all the burnt offerings. So the Levites helped their brothers. They helped until the work was done and the priests were clean. The Levites were more ready in heart to make themselves clean than the priests.
There were also many burnt offerings. There was fat from the peace offerings. There were drink offerings. The work of the the LORD's house was set in order.
Hezekiah and all the people were glad. God had made the people ready so fast.

King Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah. He also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh. He asked them to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. They were to keep the Passover for the LORD, the God of Israel.
The king, his leaders, and all the people in Jerusalem decided to keep the Passover in the second month.
They could not keep it at the usual time. The priests had not made themselves ready, and the people had not come together in Jerusalem.
This plan looked good to the king and all the people.

So they decided to send word through all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan. They told people to come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover for the LORD, the God of Israel. Many people had not kept it the way God's Law said.

The king sent runners with letters. They went through all Israel and Judah. The letters said, "People of Israel, come back to the LORD. He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Come back to Him. Then He may bring back the people who are left. They got away from the kings of Assyria.
"Do not be like your fathers and brothers. They were not faithful to the LORD, the God of their fathers. So He let them be destroyed. You can see it.
"Now do not be stubborn like your fathers. Give your hearts to the LORD. Come to His holy place. He made it holy forever. Serve the LORD your God. Then He will not be angry with you.

"If you come back to the LORD, your brothers and children will find mercy. Their captors will show them mercy. The LORD your God is kind and caring. He will not turn away from you if you come back to Him."
The runners went from town to town in Ephraim, Manasseh, and Zebulun. People laughed at them and made fun of them.
But some men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun were sorry for their sin. They came to Jerusalem.
God's hand was on Judah. He gave the people one mind. They did what the king and leaders asked, because the LORD had spoken.
A very large crowd came to Jerusalem in the second month. They came to keep the Feast of Bread Without Yeast.
They got up and took away the altars in Jerusalem. They took away all the altars for burning incense too. They threw them into the Kidron Valley.
They killed the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites felt ashamed. They made themselves ready. Then they brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
They stood in their places, the way they were supposed to. They followed the Law of Moses, the man of God. The priests sprinkled the blood. The Levites handed it to them.
Many people in the crowd had not made themselves ready. So the Levites killed the Passover for everyone who was not clean. This made them ready for the LORD.

Many people came from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun. They had not cleaned themselves. Still, they ate the Passover, which was not the usual way. But Hezekiah prayed for them. He said, "May the good the LORD forgive everyone
who sets his heart to look for God, the LORD, the God of his fathers. Even if he is not clean the right way."
The LORD heard Hezekiah. He made the people well.

The people of Israel who were in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Bread Without Yeast for seven days. They were very happy. The Levites and priests praised the LORD every day. They used loud instruments for the LORD.
Hezekiah spoke kindly to all the Levites. They knew how to serve the LORD well. For seven days they ate the feast food. They offered peace offerings. They thanked the LORD, the God of their fathers.
All the people agreed to keep the feast for seven more days. So they kept it for seven more days with joy.
King Hezekiah of Judah gave 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep for the people. The leaders gave 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep. Many priests made themselves ready.

All the people of Judah were happy. The priests and Levites were happy too. So were all the people who came from Israel. People from other lands who came from Israel and people living in Judah were happy too.
There was great joy in Jerusalem. Nothing like it had happened in Jerusalem since the time of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel.
Then the priests and Levites stood up. They blessed the people. Their voice was heard. Their prayer went up to His holy home in heaven.

After all this, the Israelites who were there went to the towns of Judah. They broke the stone pillars. They cut down the Asherah poles. They tore down the high places and altars in Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh. They destroyed all of them. Then the Israelites went back to their own towns and land.

Hezekiah put the priests and Levites into groups. Each group had its own work. They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. They served, thanked, and praised God at the gates of the LORD’s house.
The king gave some of his own things for the morning and evening burnt offerings. He also gave for burnt offerings on Sabbath days, new moon days, and feast days. This was written in the LORD’s Law.
He told the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the priests and Levites their share. Then they could give their time to the LORD’s Law.
When the people heard this, the Israelites brought a lot of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and all the food from the fields. They brought a large amount. They also brought a tenth of everything.

The people of Israel and Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought a tenth of their cows and sheep. They brought a tenth of the holy things given to the LORD their God. They piled them in big heaps.
They started making the heaps in the third month. They finished in the seventh month.
Hezekiah and his leaders came and saw the heaps. They praised the LORD. They blessed His people Israel.
Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps.
Azariah the chief priest from Zadok’s family said, “Since the people started bringing gifts to the LORD’s house, we have had plenty to eat. There is much left over. The LORD has blessed His people.”
Then Hezekiah said to get rooms ready in the LORD’s house. They did.
They brought the gifts, tithes, and holy things in faithfully. Konaniah the Levite was in charge. His brother Shimei was next in charge.
Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were helpers under Konaniah and Shimei. King Hezekiah and Azariah, the leader of God’s house, chose them.
Kore son of Imnah was a Levite. He kept the east gate. He was in charge of the free gifts given to God. He handed out the LORD’s gifts and the holy things.

Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah helped him. They faithfully gave food to the priests in the towns. They gave to their fellow priests in each group, to the great and the small.
This was besides the males three years old and older whose names were written down. They came to the LORD’s house each day to do their daily work in their groups.
The priests were counted by their family groups. The Levites twenty years old and older were counted by their groups and duties.
They also gave to all their little children, wives, sons, and daughters in the whole group. They set themselves apart for God faithfully.
For the priests, the sons of Aaron, who lived in the fields near their towns, men were named in every city. They gave shares to every male priest and to every Levite on the list.
Hezekiah did this in all Judah. He did what was good, right, and true before the LORD his God.
In all the work he started for God’s house, and in obeying the Law and commands, he looked for his God with all his heart. He did well and had success.
After all this, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, came to Judah. He camped near its strong cities. He wanted to take them.
Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come. He knew Sennacherib wanted to fight Jerusalem.
Hezekiah talked with his leaders and brave men. They decided to stop the water from the springs outside the city. The men helped him.
Many people came together. They stopped all the springs. They also stopped the stream that ran through the land. They said, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find lots of water?"
Hezekiah worked hard. He fixed the broken wall. He built towers. He built another wall outside. He made the Millo strong in the City of David. He made many spears and shields.
He put army leaders over the people. He brought them together in the city square by the gate. He encouraged them.
He said, "Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid. Do not be scared of the king of Assyria or his big army. There are more with us than with him."
The Assyrian king had only human strength. But the people had the the LORD their God. He would help them. He would fight their battles. The people trusted what Hezekiah said.
Later, Sennacherib was attacking Lachish. He sent his servants to Jerusalem. They went to King Hezekiah and to all the people of Judah there.
Sennacherib said, "Why do you trust? Why do you stay in Jerusalem while it is under attack?
Hezekiah is tricking you. He will let you die of hunger and thirst. He says, 'The The LORD our God will save us from the king of Assyria.'
Hezekiah took away the hill altars and the other altars. He told Judah and Jerusalem, 'Worship at one altar. Burn incense there.'
Don't you know what I and my fathers did to other nations? Their gods could not save their lands from me.
No god of those nations saved their people from me. So your God cannot save you from me.
So do not let Hezekiah fool you. Do not believe him. No god of any nation saved its people from me or my fathers. Your God will not save you from me either."
His servants said even more bad things against the the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.

He wrote letters to insult the the LORD God of Israel. He spoke against Him. He said, "The gods of other nations did not save their people from me. So Hezekiah's God will not save His people from me."
They shouted in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem on the wall. They wanted to scare them. They wanted to take the city.
They talked about the God of Jerusalem like He was a man-made god, like the gods of other nations.
King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, prayed. They cried out to heaven.

The The LORD sent an angel. The angel killed all the strong soldiers, leaders, and commanders in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib went home in shame. He went into his god's temple. There his own sons killed him with a sword.
The The LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem. He saved them from Sennacherib and from everyone else. He took care of them on every side.
Many people brought gifts to the the LORD in Jerusalem. They brought valuable things to King Hezekiah. After this, all nations honored him.
In those days, Hezekiah became very sick. He prayed to the the LORD. The The LORD answered him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah did not thank God for the good things. His heart became proud. God was angry with him, Judah, and Jerusalem.
Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem were sorry for their pride. So the the LORD did not punish them while Hezekiah was alive.
Hezekiah had great wealth and honor. He made storage rooms for silver, gold, jewels, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable things.
He had storehouses for grain, wine, and oil. He had barns for animals and large flocks.
He got many animals and built cities. God gave him great wealth.
Hezekiah blocked the upper spring of Gihon. He sent the water down to the west side of the City of David. He did well in all his work.
When the leaders of Babylon sent men to ask about the sign in the land, God let Hezekiah be tested. God wanted to know what was in his heart.
The rest of Hezekiah's story and his kind acts are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz. They are also in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

Hezekiah died and was buried with his ancestors. They buried him in the upper tombs of David's family. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him when he died. His son Manasseh became king after him.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-five years.
He did what was wrong in the LORD's eyes. He did the bad things that the nations did. The LORD had driven those nations out before the people of Israel.
He built again the high places that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He made altars for the Baals. He made poles for Asherah. He bowed down to all the stars in the sky and served them.
He built altars in the LORD's temple. The LORD had said, "My name will be in Jerusalem forever."
He built altars in the two courtyards of the LORD's temple for all the stars in the sky.

He burned his sons in the fire in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He used magic and guessed the future. He did witchcraft. He asked mediums and people who spoke to spirits. He did much wrong in the LORD's eyes. He made the LORD angry.

He put the carved idol he made in God's temple. God had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.
I will not make Israel leave the land I gave their fathers. But they must keep all I told them through Moses. They must obey all the law, rules, and decisions."
Manasseh led Judah and the people of Jerusalem away from the right path. They did more wrong than the nations the LORD had destroyed before the people of Israel.
The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people. But they did not listen.
So the LORD brought the army leaders of the king of Assyria against them. They caught Manasseh. They put hooks in him. They tied him with bronze chains. They took him to Babylon.
When he was in trouble, he asked the LORD his God for help. He was very sorry and bowed before the God of his fathers.
He prayed to the LORD. The LORD listened to him. The LORD heard his prayer. The LORD brought him back to Jerusalem and gave him back his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.

After that, he built the outer wall of the City of David. It was on the west side of Gihon in the valley. It went to the Fish Gate. It went around the hill. He made it very high. He put army leaders in all the strong cities of Judah.
He took away the foreign gods and the idol from the LORD's temple. He took away all the altars he had built on the temple hill and in Jerusalem. He threw them out of the city.
He fixed the LORD's altar. He gave peace offerings and thank offerings on it. He told Judah, "Serve the LORD God of Israel."
The people still gave offerings at the high places. But they gave them only to the LORD their God.

The rest of what Manasseh did is written down. So is his prayer to his God. So are the words of the prophets who spoke to him in the name of the LORD God of Israel. They are in the records of the kings of Israel.

His prayer and how the LORD listened to him are written down. So are all his sins and wrong ways. So are the places where he built high places. So are the places where he set up poles for Asherah and idols before he was sorry. They are in the records of Hozai.
Manasseh died and was buried with his fathers in his palace. His son Amon became king after him.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for two years.
He did what was wrong in the LORD's eyes, like his father Manasseh did. Amon gave sacrifices to all the carved idols Manasseh had made. He served them.
He did not bow before the LORD, like his father Manasseh did. Instead, Amon added to his wrong.
His servants made a plan against him. They killed him in his palace.
The people of the land killed all who had planned against King Amon. Then they made his son Josiah king.
Josiah was 8 years old when he became king. He ruled 31 years in Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the the LORD. He followed the ways of his father David. He did not turn right or left.

In the eighth year of his rule, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his father David. In the twelfth year, he began to clean Judah and Jerusalem. He removed hill altars, Asherah poles, carved idols, and metal idols.

He had the altars of Baal torn down. He cut down the incense altars above them. He broke the Asherah poles, carved idols, and metal idols. He ground them to dust and scattered the dust on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He burned the bones of the priests on their altars. He cleaned Judah and Jerusalem.
He did the same in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and Naphtali, and in the ruins around them.
He tore down the altars and Asherah poles. He smashed the idols to dust. He cut down all the incense altars in all Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of his rule, when he was cleaning the land and the temple, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city leader, and Joah son of Joahaz the record keeper to fix the temple of the the LORD his God.

They came to Hilkiah the high priest. They gave him the money brought into God's house. The Levites who guarded the door had collected it from Manasseh, Ephraim, all the rest of Israel, all Judah and Benjamin, and the people of Jerusalem.
They gave it to the men in charge of the work on the the LORD's house. The workers used it to fix and make the temple strong.
They gave money to the carpenters and builders. They bought cut stone and wood to fix the buildings that the kings of Judah had let fall apart.
The men did the work well. The Levites in charge were Jahath and Obadiah from Merari's family, and Zechariah and Meshullam from Kohath's family. The Levites were skilled with music.
They led the carriers and all the workers. Some Levites were writers, officers, and gatekeepers.
When they brought out the money for the the LORD's house, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law of the the LORD given by Moses.
Hilkiah said to Shaphan the writer, "I found the Book of the Law in the the LORD's house." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan brought the book to the king. He said, "Your servants are doing all they were told. They melted down the money found in the the LORD's house and gave it to the men in charge of the work."
They melted down the money found in the the LORD's house. They gave it to the men in charge and to the workers.
Shaphan the writer told the king, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." Then Shaphan read from it before the king.
When the king heard the words of the Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
The king told Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the writer, and Asaiah the king's servant,

"Go and ask the the LORD for me. Ask for the people still left in Israel and Judah. Ask about the words in this book that was found. The the LORD is very angry with us. He has poured out His anger on us because our fathers did not obey the the LORD's word. They did not do all that is written in this book."

Hilkiah and the men the king sent went to Huldah the woman prophet. She was the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, who took care of the clothes. She lived in Jerusalem in the Second District. They spoke to her.
She said to them, "The The LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me,
The The LORD says: I will bring trouble on this place and on the people who live here. I will bring all the curses written in the book they read to the king of Judah.
They left Me. They burned incense to other gods. They made Me angry with all they did. So My anger will pour out on this place. It will not stop.
"But to the king of Judah who sent you to ask the the LORD, say this: The The LORD, the God of Israel, says: You heard these words.
Your heart was soft. You humbled yourself before God when you heard His words against this place and its people. You tore your clothes and cried before Me, so I heard you, says the the LORD.
I will let you die in peace. You will be buried with your fathers. Your eyes will not see all the trouble I bring on this place and its people."
The king sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem. He gathered them together.

The king went up to the the LORD's house. All the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, young and old, went with him. He read to them all the words of the Book of the Agreement found in the the LORD's house.

The king stood by his place. He made an agreement before the the LORD. He promised to follow the the LORD and keep His commands, rules, and laws with all his heart and all his soul. He promised to do the words of the agreement written in this book.
He made all the people in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand and agree. The people of Jerusalem did what the agreement with God, the God of their fathers, said.

Josiah took away all the hated idols from all the lands of the Israelites. He made all the people in Israel serve the the LORD their God. As long as he lived, they did not stop following the the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Josiah kept the Passover for the LORD in Jerusalem. They killed the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He put the priests in their work groups and helped them serve in the house of the LORD.

He said to the Levites, who taught all Israel and were holy to the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the house Solomon built. You do not have to carry it on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel."
Get ready by your family groups, by your divisions. Follow what King David wrote and what his son Solomon wrote.
Stand in the holy place with the groups of your brothers, the sons of the people, and with the family groups of the Levites.
Kill the Passover lamb. Clean yourselves. Get ready to help your brothers do what the LORD said through Moses."
Josiah gave the people thirty thousand lambs and young goats, and three thousand bulls. These were for the Passover for all the people who were there.

His leaders also gave gifts to the people, the priests, and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the leaders of God's house, gave the priests two thousand six hundred lambs for the Passover and three hundred bulls.
Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah, Nethanel, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, gave the Levites five thousand lambs for the Passover and five hundred bulls.
The work was ready. The priests stood where they should stand, and the Levites stood in their groups, just as the king had said.
They killed the Passover lamb. The priests sprinkled the blood. The Levites skinned the animals.
They took away the burnt offering parts to give to each family group of the people. They offered them to the LORD, as Moses' book says. They did the same with the bulls.
They roasted the Passover lamb over the fire, as the rule says. They cooked the holy parts in pots, pans, and bowls. Then they hurried and gave them to all the people.

After that, they got things ready for themselves and the priests. The priests, Aaron's sons, were busy offering burnt offerings and fat until night. The Levites got things ready for themselves and for the priests, Aaron's sons.

The singers, Asaph's sons, stood where they should stand, as King David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, the king's prophet, had said. The gatekeepers stood at each gate. They did not have to leave their work, because their brothers the Levites got things ready for them.
So all the work of the LORD was ready that day. They kept the Passover and offered burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, just as King Josiah had said.
The Israelites who were there kept the Passover then. They also kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. None of Israel's kings had kept a Passover like the one Josiah kept, with the priests, the Levites, all Judah and Israel who were there, and the people of Jerusalem.
This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule.
After all this, Josiah had fixed up the temple. Neco, the king of Egypt, went up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates River. Josiah went out to meet him.

Neco sent men to Josiah with this message: "King of Judah, this is not your fight. I am not coming against you today. I am going to fight another group. God told me to hurry. Stop fighting against God, who is with me, or He will destroy you."
But Josiah did not turn away. He went out in disguise to fight. He did not listen to Neco's words, which came from God. He went to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
Archers shot King Josiah. He said to his servants, "Carry me away. I am badly hurt."
His servants took him out of his chariot. They put him in his second chariot. They brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried with his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem were sad for Josiah.
Jeremiah was sad for Josiah. All the men and women who sang made sad songs about Josiah. They made these songs a rule in Israel. They are written in the book of Laments.
The rest of what Josiah did, and his good deeds, are written in the law of the LORD.
His first and last acts are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
The people of the land took Josiah’s son Jehoahaz. They made him king in Jerusalem after his father died.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for three months.
The king of Egypt took him off the throne. He made the land pay a big tax: one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
Then Neco, king of Egypt, made Jehoahaz’s brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem. He changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. He did bad things that the LORD his God did not like.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, attacked him. He tied him up with bronze chains and took him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar took some special things from the LORD’s house. He brought them to Babylon and put them in his own temple.
The rest of what Jehoiakim did is written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. This includes the bad things he did and what was found against him. His son Jehoiachin became king after him.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for three months and ten days. He did bad things that the LORD did not like.
Later, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him. He brought him to Babylon with the valuable things from the LORD’s house. He made Zedekiah, Jehoiachin’s brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years.
He did bad things that the LORD his God did not like. He would not show respect to Jeremiah the prophet. Jeremiah spoke the LORD’s words.

He also turned against King Nebuchadnezzar. Nebuchadnezzar had made him promise by God to be faithful. But Zedekiah was stubborn. He made his heart hard. He would not turn back to the LORD, the God of Israel.
All the leaders of the priests and the people also did more and more wrong. They followed the bad things other nations did. They made the LORD’s house dirty. The LORD had set it apart in Jerusalem.
The LORD, the God of their fathers, kept sending them messages through His messengers. He did this because He cared about His people and His home.
But they made fun of God’s messengers. They hated His words. They laughed at His prophets. The LORD’s anger grew against His people. At last there was no way to fix it.

So He brought the king of Babylon against them. The king killed their young men with swords in the holy house. He did not spare young men or young women. He did not spare old people or very old people. God gave all of them to him.
He took to Babylon all the things, big and small, from God’s house. He took the treasures of the LORD’s house. He took the king’s treasures and the treasures of his leaders.
They burned down God’s house. They broke down Jerusalem’s wall. They burned all its palaces. They destroyed everything of value.
The people who did not die by the sword were taken to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar made them his servants. They served him and his sons until the kingdom of Persia became strong.
The land finally got its rest. All the time it was empty, it rested. This lasted until seventy years were done. It happened just as the LORD had said through Jeremiah.

In the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, the LORD’s word spoken by Jeremiah came true. The LORD moved Cyrus, king of Persia, to act. Cyrus sent a message through all his kingdom. He also wrote it down.

“This is what Cyrus, king of Persia, says: ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. He has chosen me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever among you belongs to His people, may the LORD his God be with him. Let him go to Jerusalem.’”

In the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, the LORD did what He promised through Jeremiah. The LORD stirred up Cyrus, the king of Persia. Cyrus told everyone in his land and wrote it down too. He said:
"This is what Cyrus, king of Persia, says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the lands of the earth. He has told me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, in Judah.
If any of you belong to His people, may his God be with him. Go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.
People who live near those who are left should help them. Give them silver, gold, things, and animals. They should also give gifts for God's house in Jerusalem."
So the family leaders of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and Levites, got ready. God had stirred their hearts to go up and build the LORD's house in Jerusalem.
All the people around them helped too. They gave silver and gold things, other things, animals, and nice gifts. They also gave extra gifts.
King Cyrus brought out the things from the LORD's house. Nebuchadnezzar had taken them from Jerusalem and put them in his god's house.
Cyrus had Mithredath, the money keeper, bring them out. He counted them and gave them to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.
There were 30 gold dishes, 1,000 silver dishes, and 29 silver tools.
There were 30 gold bowls, 410 silver bowls, and 1,000 other things.
In all, there were 5,400 gold and silver things. Sheshbazzar brought all of them when the people came back from Babylon to Jerusalem.

These are the people from the land who came back from being held captive in Babylon. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had carried them away. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah. Each person went to his own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. This is the list of the men of Israel.
The family of Parosh had 2,172 people.
The family of Shephatiah had 372 people.
The family of Arah had 775 people.
The family of Pahath-moab, from the sons of Jeshua and Joab, had 2,812 people.
The family of Elam had 1,254 people.
The family of Zattu had 945 people.
The family of Zaccai had 760 people.
The family of Bani had 642 people.
The family of Bebai had 623 people.
The family of Azgad had 1,222 people.
The family of Adonikam had 666 people.
The family of Bigvai had 2,056 people.
The family of Adin had 454 people.
The family of Ater, from Hezekiah, had 98 people.
The family of Bezai had 323 people.
The family of Jorah had 112 people.
The family of Hashum had 223 people.
The family of Gibbar had 95 people.
Kiriath Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth had 743 people.
The family of Nebo had 52 people.
The family of Magbish had 156 people.
The other family of Elam had 1,254 people.
The family of Harim had 320 people.
Lod, Hadid, and Ono had 725 people.
The priests: the family of Jedaiah, from the house of Jeshua, had 973 people.
The family of Immer had 1,052 people.
The family of Pashhur had 1,247 people.
The family of Harim had 1,017 people.
The Levites: the families of Jeshua and Kadmiel, from the family of Hodaviah, had 74 people.
The singers: the family of Asaph had 128 people.
The gatekeepers: the families of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai had 139 people in all.
The temple servants included the families of Ziha, Hasupha, and Tabbaoth.
The families of Keros, Siaha, and Padon.
The families of Lebanah, Hagabah, and Akkub.
The families of Hagab, Shamlai, and Hanan.
The families of Giddel, Gahar, and Reaiah.
The families of Rezin, Nekoda, and Gazzam.
The families of Uzza, Paseah, and Besai.
The families of Asnah, Meunim, and Nephusim.
The families of Bakbuk, Hakupha, and Harhur.
The families of Bazluth, Mehida, and Harsha.
The families of Barkos, Sisera, and Temah.
The families of Neziah and Hatipha.
The sons of Solomon’s servants included the families of Sotai, Hassophereth, and Peruda.
The families of Jaalah, Darkon, and Giddel.
The families of Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim, and Ami.
The temple servants and the sons of Solomon’s servants had 392 people in all.
These people came up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer. They could not show their family or family line, or prove they were from Israel.
The families of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda had 652 people.
Among the priests were the families of Habaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai. Barzillai had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite, so he was called by that name.
They looked for their family records but could not find them. So they were not allowed to serve as priests.
The governor told them not to eat the most holy food until a priest could use the Urim and Thummim.
Besides these, there were 7,337 male and female servants and 200 male and female singers.
When they came to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some family leaders gave freely to build God’s house again in its place.
They gave as much as they could: 61,000 gold coins, 5,000 pieces of silver, and 100 priest clothes.
The priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, and some of the people settled in their towns. All Israel lived in their towns.
In the seventh month, the people of Israel were in their towns. They came together in Jerusalem like one person.

Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, the priests, stood up. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers stood up too. They built the altar of the God of Israel. They wanted to give burnt offerings on it. This is what the Law of Moses, the man of God, said to do.
They put the altar on its old base. They gave burnt gifts on it to the LORD, morning and evening. They were afraid of the people in the lands around them.
They also kept the Feast of Shelters. They gave the daily burnt offerings. They gave the right number for each day, as the rules said.
After that, they gave the regular burnt offering. They also gave offerings for the new moons and for the LORD's special feasts. People also gave gifts they chose to give to the LORD.
They started giving burnt offerings to the LORD on the first day of the seventh month. But the LORD's temple had not been built yet.

They gave money to stonecutters and builders. They gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre. Those people brought cedar wood from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. King Cyrus of Persia had said they could do this.

In the second month of the second year, after they came to God's house in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of their brothers began the work. The priests and Levites helped too. All who had come back from captivity to Jerusalem helped. They chose Levites who were twenty years old or older to lead the work on the LORD's house.
Jeshua and his family stood together with Kadmiel and his family. The sons of Judah and the sons of Henadad stood with them too. All these Levites led the builders in God's house.

When the builders laid the foundation of the LORD's temple, the priests stood there. They wore their special clothes and had trumpets. The Levites, who were Asaph's family, had cymbals. They stood to praise the LORD. This was like what King David of Israel had done.

They sang to the LORD. They praised Him and thanked Him. They said, "He is good. His love for Israel lasts forever." Then all the people shouted with joy. They praised the LORD because the foundation of His house was laid.
Many older priests, Levites, and family leaders cried. They had seen the first temple. When they saw the new foundation, they cried loudly. But many others shouted with joy.
The people shouted so loudly that no one could tell the happy shouts from the sad cries. The sound was heard far away.
The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people who had come back were building a temple for the the LORD, the God of Israel.

They came to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders. They said, “Let us build with you. We want to worship your God too. We have worshiped Him since the time of King Esarhaddon of Assyria. He brought us here.”

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other family leaders said, “You cannot help us build a temple for our God. We will build it for the the LORD, the God of Israel. King Cyrus of Persia told us to do this.”
Then the people of that land made the people of Judah weak. They scared them so they would not build.
They paid people to work against them. This went on during the time of King Cyrus and until King Darius ruled Persia.
They wrote a letter against the people of Judah and Jerusalem when King Ahasuerus ruled.
Later, in the time of King Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their friends wrote to him. The letter was written in the Aramaic language.
Rehum the leader and Shimshai the writer wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes.
Rehum, Shimshai, and their friends wrote it. Their friends were judges and leaders from many lands.
The great and famous Osnappar had moved them to live in Samaria and in other places west of the Euphrates River. Now they wrote to the king.
This is a copy of the letter they sent: “To King Artaxerxes, from your servants who live west of the Euphrates River.
King, we want you to know that the Jews who left you and came to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that city. It has been a bad city. They are fixing the walls and the bases.
King, if they finish this city and the walls, they will stop paying taxes and money to kings. It will hurt the kings.
We work for you, and we do not want to see you lose honor. So we tell you.

Look in the records of your fathers. You will see that this city has been a bad city. It has hurt kings and lands. People have fought against the king there for a long time. That is why the city was destroyed.
King, if this city is built again and the walls are finished, you will have no land left west of the Euphrates River.”
King Artaxerxes sent this answer to Rehum, Shimshai, and their friends in Samaria and west of the Euphrates: “Peace to you. I read the letter you sent.
I told men to search. They found that this city has fought against kings for a long time. People there have turned against kings and caused trouble.
Strong kings have ruled Jerusalem. They ruled all the land west of the Euphrates. People paid taxes and money to them.
Now tell these men to stop. Do not let them build the city until I say so.
Be careful and do this right. Do not let the damage grow and hurt the kings.”
When Rehum, Shimshai, and their friends read the king's letter, they hurried to Jerusalem. They used their power to make the Jews stop building.
So the work on God's temple in Jerusalem stopped. It did not start again until the second year of King Darius of Persia.
The prophets Haggai and Zechariah, the son of Iddo, spoke God's message to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem. They spoke in the name of the God of Israel, who watched over them.
Then Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, got up and started to rebuild God's house in Jerusalem. God's prophets were with them and helped them.
At that time, Tattenai, the governor of the land across the river, and Shethar-bozenai and their friends came to them. They said, "Who told you to build this house and finish it?
What are the names of the men building this building?"
But God watched over the Jewish leaders, and they did not stop the work until a report went to Darius and an answer came back by letter.
This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor of the land across the river, and Shethar-bozenai and his friends, the officials there, sent to King Darius.
They sent a report to him. It said, "To King Darius: Peace to you.
Let the king know that we went to Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with big stones, and wood is put in the walls. The work is going fast and doing well in their hands.
Then we asked those leaders, 'Who told you to build this house and finish it?'
We also asked their names, so we could tell you and write down the names of their leaders.
"They answered us, 'We are servants of the God of heaven and earth. We are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago. A great king of Israel built it and finished it.
But our fathers made the God of heaven angry, so He let Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, the Chaldean, rule over them. Nebuchadnezzar destroyed this house and took the people to Babylon.
But in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, King Cyrus gave an order to rebuild this house of God.

The gold and silver things from God's house were taken by Nebuchadnezzar from the temple in Jerusalem to the temple in Babylon. King Cyrus took them from the temple in Babylon and gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he made governor.
King Cyrus told him, 'Take these things, go, and put them in the temple in Jerusalem. Let God's house be rebuilt in its place.'

Then Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of God's house in Jerusalem. From that time until now they have been building it, and it is not finished yet.' "Now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the king's records in Babylon. See if King Cyrus gave an order to rebuild God's house in Jerusalem. Then let the king tell us what he wants to do about this."
King Darius made a rule. Men searched the records kept in Babylon's treasure house.
They found one scroll in the fort at Ecbatana in Media. The scroll said:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus made this order: God's house in Jerusalem must be rebuilt. It is the place where offerings are made. Its base must be strong. It must be about 90 feet high and 90 feet wide.
It will have three rows of big stones and one row of wood. The king will pay for it.
Also bring back the gold and silver dishes from God's house. Nebuchadnezzar took them from the temple in Jerusalem and carried them to Babylon. Put them back in God's house in Jerusalem."
"Now, Tattenai, governor of the land beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their friends, stay away from there.
Let the Jewish elders build God's house in its place.
"I also order this: Help these Jewish elders build God's house. Pay them in full from the king's money and from taxes in the land beyond the River, so the work does not stop.
Give them what they need: young bulls, rams, and lambs for burned offerings to the God of heaven; wheat, salt, wine, and oil, as the priests in Jerusalem ask. Give it every day without fail.
Then they can offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the king and his sons.
If anyone changes this order, a beam will be pulled from his house, and he will be hung on it. His house will be made a trash pile.
May the God who put His name there destroy any king or people who try to change or destroy this house in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have made this order. Do it fully."
Then Tattenai, Shethar-bozenai, and their friends did exactly as King Darius had sent.

The Jewish elders built and did well. They were helped by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the house by the command of the God of Israel and by the orders of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, king of Persia.
The house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of King Darius.
The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the returned captives joyfully celebrated the opening of God's house.
For the celebration they offered 100 bulls, 200 rams, 400 lambs, and 12 male goats as a sin offering for all Israel. There was one goat for each tribe.
The priests and Levites were set in their groups to serve God in Jerusalem, just as Moses' book says.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, the returned people kept the Passover.
The priests and Levites had all become clean. They killed the Passover lamb for all the returned people, for their priest brothers, and for themselves.
The Israelites who came back from exile ate it. So did everyone who had turned from the unclean ways of other nations to seek the the LORD God of Israel.
They kept the Feast of Bread Without Yeast for seven days with joy, because the the LORD had made them joyful. He made the king of Assyria want to help them build the house of God, the God of Israel.
After this, while Artaxerxes was king of Persia, there was a man named Ezra. He was the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest.

This Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe who knew the Law of Moses well. The LORD, the God of Israel, had given that Law. The king gave Ezra everything he asked for, because the the LORD his God was helping him.
In the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, Ezra went up to Jerusalem. Some people of Israel went with him. There were priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
He got to Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king.
Ezra left Babylon on the first day of the first month. He got to Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month. His God was good to him and helped him on the way.
Ezra had made up his mind to study the Law of the the LORD, to obey it, and to teach its rules and laws to the people of Israel.
This is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and scribe. Ezra was a scribe of the the LORD's commands and laws for Israel.
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the Law of the God of heaven: Peace! Now I make this rule:
Any of the people of Israel, priests, and Levites in my kingdom who want to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
You are sent by the king and his seven helpers to check on Judah and Jerusalem. Use the Law of your God that you hold.
You are to take the silver and gold that the king and his helpers freely gave to the God of Israel, whose home is in Jerusalem.
Take all the silver and gold you find in the land of Babylon. Take the gifts that the people and priests freely give for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
Use this money to buy bulls, rams, and lambs. Buy grain and drink for offerings. Offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
You and your brothers may do what seems good to you with the rest of the silver and gold. Do it the way your God wants.
Give the items that were given to you for the house of your God to the God in Jerusalem.
If you need anything else for the house of your God, take it from the king's treasury.
I, King Artaxerxes, make this rule for all the treasurers beyond the river: Give Ezra, the priest and scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, everything he asks for. Do it quickly.
Give up to 100 talents of silver, 100 baskets of wheat, 100 jars of wine, 100 jars of oil, and as much salt as is needed.
Do everything the God of heaven commands for the house of the God of heaven. Then no anger will come on the king's kingdom or his sons.
We also tell you that no tax, fee, or toll may be taken from the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or workers of this house of God.
And you, Ezra, use the wisdom God gives you to choose judges and leaders. They will judge all the people beyond the river who know God's Laws. Teach those who do not know.
Anyone who does not obey the Law of your God or the king's law must be punished. They may be put to death, sent away, lose their things, or be put in prison."
Ezra said, "Praise the the LORD, the God of our fathers!

He put this in the king's heart to make the the LORD's house in Jerusalem beautiful. He was kind to me before the king, his helpers, and all the king's powerful leaders. I was strong because the the LORD my God was helping me. I gathered the leaders of Israel to go with me."
These are the family leaders who came back with me from Babylon. This was when King Artaxerxes was king.
From Phinehas' family came Gershom. From Ithamar's family came Daniel. From David's family came Hattush.
From Shecaniah's family, from Parosh's family, came Zechariah. 150 men came with him.
From Pahath-moab's family came Elihoenai son of Zerahiah. 200 men came with him.
From Shecaniah's family came the son of Jahaziel. 300 men came with him.
From Adin's family came Ebed son of Jonathan. 50 men came with him.
From Elam's family came Isaiah son of Athaliah. 70 men came with him.
From Shephatiah's family came Zebadiah son of Michael. 80 men came with him.
From Joab's family came Obadiah son of Jehiel. 218 men came with him.
From Shelomith's family came the son of Josiphiah. 160 men came with him.
From Bebai's family came Zechariah son of Bebai. 28 men came with him.
From Azgad's family came Johanan son of Hakkatan. 110 men came with him.
From the last of Adonikam's family came Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah. 60 men came with them.
From Bigvai's family came Uthai and Zabbud. 70 men came with them.
I gathered the people by the river that goes to Ahava. We camped there three days. I looked at the people and the priests. I did not find any Levites there.
Then I sent leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. They could understand God's law. I also sent Joiarib and Elnathan.
I sent them to Iddo, the leader, at Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and his brothers, the temple helpers at Casiphia. They were to bring us helpers for God's house.
God's hand was good to us. They brought us Sherebiah. He was a wise man from Mahli's family. Mahli was from Levi, who was from Israel. Sherebiah came with his sons and brothers. There were 18 men.
They also brought Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from Merari's family. With them came their brothers and sons. There were 20 men.
They also brought 220 temple helpers. David and the leaders had given them to help the Levites. All of them were named.
There by the Ahava River, I called for a fast. We were to be humble before our God. We asked Him for a safe trip for us, our children, and all our things.

I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to help us on the road. We had told the king, "The hand of our God is good to all who seek Him, and His power and anger are against all who leave Him."
So we fasted and asked our God for help. He heard us.
Then I set apart twelve of the priest leaders. I chose Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers.
I weighed out the silver, gold, and things for God's house. The king, his advisors, his leaders, and the Israelites who were there had given these gifts.
I weighed out 650 talents of silver, silver things worth 100 talents, and 100 talents of gold.
I also weighed out 20 gold bowls worth 1,000 coins. I weighed two fine bronze things that were as precious as gold.
I said to them, "You are holy to the LORD. These things are holy too. The silver and gold are a free gift to the LORD, the God of your ancestors."

Watch these things and keep them safe. Do not lose them until you weigh them in the rooms of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. Weigh them before the leaders of the priests, the Levites, and the family leaders of Israel.
So the priests and Levites took the weighed silver, gold, and things. They were to bring them to God's house in Jerusalem.
On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River. We went to Jerusalem. God's hand was on us. He kept us safe from enemies and robbers on the way.
We got to Jerusalem. We rested there three days.

On the fourth day, we weighed the silver, gold, and things in God's house. We gave them to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was there. Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui, who were Levites, were also there.
Everything was counted and weighed. The total weight was written down.

The people who came back from being captives gave burnt offerings to the God of Israel. They gave 12 bulls for all Israel, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and 12 male goats for sin. All of these were burnt offerings to the LORD.
They gave the king's orders to the governors west of the river. The governors helped the people and God's house.

After this, the leaders came to me. They said, "The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not kept away from the people of the lands. They have copied the bad things those people do. They have mixed with the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites."
They have taken some of their daughters to be wives for themselves and their sons. So the holy family line has mixed with the people of the land. The leaders and officials led the way in this wrong.
When I heard this, I tore my clothes. I pulled hair from my head and beard. I sat down, stunned.
Then everyone who was afraid of the words of the God of Israel came to me. They came because of the wrong the people had done. I sat there, stunned, until the evening sacrifice.
At the time of the evening sacrifice, I got up from where I was sitting. My clothes were still torn. I fell on my knees. I spread out my hands to the LORD my God.
I said, "O my God, I am ashamed. I feel disgraced. I cannot even look up to You, my God. Our wrongs are more than we can count. Our guilt has reached up to heaven.

"Since the time of our fathers until today, our guilt has been great. Because of our wrongs, we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over to other kings. We have been killed by the sword. We have been taken away. We have been robbed. We are ashamed, just like today.

"But now, for a short time, the LORD our God has been kind to us. He left us a few people. He gave us a safe place in His holy place. Even while we were slaves, our God gave us new life. He gave light to our eyes.

"Even though we are slaves, our God has not left us. He has shown us His kind love before the kings of Persia. He gave us new life to build God's house again. He let us fix its broken parts. He gave us safety in Judah and Jerusalem.
"And now, our God, what can we say after this? We have turned away from Your commands.

You gave these commands through Your servants the prophets. They said, 'The land you are going to take is made dirty by the people who live there. They have filled it with bad things from one end to the other.

So do not give your daughters to their sons. Do not take their daughters for your sons. Do not look for their peace or good. Then you will be strong. You will eat the good things of the land. You will leave it to your sons forever.'
"After all the bad things that happened to us because of our wrongs and great guilt, You, our God, have not punished us as much as we deserve. You have left us a few people like this.
"Should we break Your commands again? Should we marry these people who do bad things? Would You not be so angry with us that You would destroy us? Then no one would be left.
"The LORD, God of Israel, You are right. That is why a few of us are still here today. Here we are before You in our guilt. Because of this, no one can stand before You."
While Ezra prayed and said he was sorry, he cried and fell down in front of God's house. A very big crowd of Israel's men, women, and children came to him. The people cried a lot.
Shecaniah son of Jehiel, from the family of Elam, said to Ezra, “We have not been faithful to our God. We married women from other lands. But there is still hope for Israel.

Now let’s make a promise to our God. We will send away all these foreign wives and their children. We will do this the way you, my lord, and those who obey God's commands say. We will follow God's Law.
Get up! This is your job, and we are with you. Be strong and do it.”
So Ezra got up. He made the priests, the Levites, and all Israel promise to do this. They promised.
Then Ezra left God's house. He went to the room of Johanan son of Eliashib. He did not eat bread or drink water. He was sad because the people who had come back had done wrong.
They sent out a message all through Judah and Jerusalem. It told all the people who had come back to meet in Jerusalem.
If anyone did not come in three days, he would lose everything he owned. He would also be kept away from the group of people who had come back. The leaders and elders decided this.

In three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem. It was the twentieth day of the ninth month. All the people sat in the open area in front of God's house. They shook because of this problem and because of the rain.
Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have not been faithful. You married women from other lands. This made Israel's guilt even bigger.
Now say you are sorry to the LORD, the God of your fathers. Do what He wants. Stay away from the people of the land and from these foreign wives.”
All the people answered in a loud voice, “You are right! We will do what you said.
But there are many people. It is the rainy time, and we cannot stand outside. This work will take more than one or two days. We have done a very wrong thing.

Let our leaders stand for all of us. Let every man in our towns who married a foreign wife come at set times. Let the elders and judges of each town come with them. We will do this until God stops being so angry with us about this.”
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were against this. Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.
The people who had come back did this. Ezra the priest chose men who were leaders of their families. He chose them by name. They sat down on the tenth day of the tenth month to look into this.
They finished with all the men who had married foreign wives by the first day of the first month.
Here are the priests who had married foreign wives: From the family of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
They promised to send their wives away. They also brought a ram as a guilt offering because they were guilty.
From the family of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
From the family of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
From the family of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Eleasah.
From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also called Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
From the people of Israel: From the family of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
From the family of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
From the family of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
From the family of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
From the family of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth.
From the family of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
From the family of Harim: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, and Shimeon.
From the family of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
From the family of Bani: Maadai, Amram, and Uel.
From the family of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these men had married women from other lands. Some of them had children with these wives.
These are the words of Nehemiah, son of Hachaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the city of Susa.
My brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who were left from the people taken away, and about Jerusalem.
They said to me, "The people left in that land are in big trouble and shame. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates are burned with fire."
When I heard these words, I sat down and cried. I was sad for days. I did not eat, and I prayed to the God of heaven.
I said, "Please, the LORD God of heaven, great and mighty God, who keeps His promise and is kind to those who love Him and keep His commands.

Please let Your eyes be open and Your ears listen to the prayer of Your servant today. I pray day and night for Your servants, the people of Israel. I say sorry for the sins of the people of Israel. We sinned against You. I and my family have sinned.
We did very wrong against You. We did not keep Your commands, Your rules, and Your laws that You gave to Your servant Moses.
Please remember the word You told Your servant Moses: 'If you are not faithful, I will spread you among the nations.'
But if you come back to Me and keep My commands and do them, even if you are pushed far away, I will bring you together from there. I will bring you to the place I chose for My name.
They are Your servants and Your people. You saved them with great power and a strong hand.

Please, the LORD, let Your ear listen to the prayer of Your servant and of Your servants who want to honor Your name. Help Your servant today, and let this man show him kindness. I served drinks to the king."
In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, wine was in front of him. I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had not been sad in front of him.
The king said to me, "Why is your face sad? You are not sick. This is only sadness inside." I was very afraid.
I said to the king, "Long live the king! Why should I not look sad? The city where my fathers are buried is in ruins, and its gates were burned by fire."
The king said to me, "What do you want?" Then I prayed to the God of heaven.
I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, and if you are happy with me, your servant, send me to Judah, to the city where my fathers are buried, so I can rebuild it."
The king and the queen sitting beside him said to me, "How long will your trip be, and when will you come back?" The king was pleased to send me, and I told him a time.
I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, please give me letters for the governors west of the River, so they will let me pass until I reach Judah."

I also asked for a letter to Asaph, who takes care of the king's forest. He should give me wood to make beams for the gates of the strong building by the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will live in. The king gave me these things because my God was helping me.
I went to the governors west of the River and gave them the king's letters. The king had sent army captains and horsemen with me.
Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about it. They were very upset that someone had come to help the people of Israel.
I came to Jerusalem and stayed there three days.
I got up at night with a few men. I did not tell anyone what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one I rode.
I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward the Dragon Spring and the Dung Gate. I looked at the walls of Jerusalem that were broken down, and at the gates that had been burned.
Then I went to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal I was riding to get through.
So I went up the valley at night and looked at the wall. Then I turned around and came back in through the Valley Gate.
The leaders did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. I had not yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the leaders, or the other workers.
Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem is in ruins, and its gates are burned. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem so we will not be shamed anymore."
I told them how my God had helped me, and what the king had said to me. They said, "Let us get up and build." So they got ready to do good work.

But Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it. They laughed at us and looked down on us. They said, "Are you rebuilding the wall? Are you going to turn against the king?"
I answered them, "The God of heaven will help us succeed. We are His servants, and we will get up and build. But you have no share, no right, and no claim in Jerusalem."

Eliashib the high priest and the other priests got to work. They rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They made it holy. They put in its doors. They built up to the Tower of the Hundred. They made that tower holy too. They built up to the Tower of Hananel.
The men of Jericho built the next part. Zakkur son of Imri built next to them.
The sons of Hassenaah rebuilt the Fish Gate. They put in its beams, doors, locks, and bars.
Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, fixed the wall next to them. Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, fixed it next to him. Zadok son of Baana fixed it next to him.
The men of Tekoa fixed the wall next to them. But their leaders would not help with the work.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah fixed the Old Gate. They put in its beams, doors, locks, and bars.
Men from Gibeon and Mizpah fixed the wall next to them. Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite were among them. They worked for the governor of the land across the Euphrates River.
Next to them, Uzziel son of Harhaiah, a goldsmith, fixed the wall. Next to him, Hananiah, a perfume maker, fixed it. They rebuilt Jerusalem up to the Broad Wall.
Next to them, Rephaiah son of Hur fixed the wall. He was the leader of half of an area of Jerusalem.
Next to them, Jedaiah son of Harumaph fixed the wall across from his house. Next to him, Hattush son of Hashabneiah fixed it.
Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab fixed another part. They also fixed the Tower of the Ovens.
Next to them, Shallum son of Hallohesh fixed the wall. He was the leader of the other half of an area of Jerusalem. His daughters helped him.
Hanun and the people of Zanoah fixed the Valley Gate. They rebuilt it. They put in its doors, locks, and bars. They also fixed about 1,500 feet of wall up to the Dung Gate.
Malkijah son of Rechab fixed the Dung Gate. He was the leader of the area of Beth-haccerem. He rebuilt it. He put in its doors, locks, and bars.

Shallun son of Col-hozeh fixed the Fountain Gate. He was the leader of the area of Mizpah. He rebuilt it. He put a roof on it. He put in its doors, locks, and bars. He also fixed the wall by the Pool of Siloam, by the king’s garden, up to the stairs that go down from David’s city.

After him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk fixed the wall. He was the leader of half of an area of Beth-zur. He fixed it up to a spot across from David’s tombs. He fixed it up to the man-made pool and the House of the Warriors.
Next to him, the Levites fixed the wall under Rehum son of Bani. Next to him, Hashabiah fixed it. He was the leader of half of the area of Keilah. He fixed it for his area.
Next to him, the other Levites fixed the wall under Binnui son of Henadad. He was the leader of the other half of the area of Keilah.
Next to him, Ezer son of Jeshua fixed another part. He was the leader of Mizpah. He fixed it from a spot across from the road up to the weapons house to the corner.
Next to him, Baruch son of Zabbai worked hard. He fixed another part. He fixed it from the corner to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
Next to him, Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, fixed another part. He fixed it from the door of Eliashib’s house to the end of it.
Next to him, the priests from the nearby area fixed the wall.
Next to them, Benjamin and Hasshub fixed the wall in front of their house. Next to them, Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, fixed it next to his house.
Next to him, Binnui son of Henadad fixed another part. He fixed it from Azariah’s house to the corner.

Palal son of Uzai fixed the wall across from the corner and the tower that sticks out from the king’s upper palace. This was by the guard’s courtyard. Next to him, Pedaiah son of Parosh fixed the wall.
The temple servants living on the hill called Ophel fixed the wall up to a spot across from the Water Gate to the east and the tower that sticks out.
Next to them, the men of Tekoa fixed another part. They fixed it from the big tower that sticks out to the wall of the hill called Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate, the priests fixed the wall. Each one fixed it in front of his own house.
Next to them, Zadok son of Immer fixed the wall across from his house. Next to him, Shemaiah son of Shecaniah fixed it. He was the guard at the East Gate.
Next to him, Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, fixed another part. Next to them, Meshullam son of Berechiah fixed the wall across from his room.
Next to him, Malkijah, a goldsmith, fixed the wall up to the house of the temple servants and the merchants. This was across from the Inspection Gate and up to the upper room at the corner.
Between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants fixed the wall.
When Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he got very mad. He made fun of the Jews.

He spoke to his brothers and the army of Samaria. He said, "What are these weak Jews doing? Can they make the city strong again? Will they give gifts to God? Will they finish in one day? Can they make good stones from piles of burned stones?"
Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him. He said, "Even a fox could knock down their stone wall."
Hear us, our God, for we are treated badly. Make them pay for their mean words. Let them be carried off as prisoners in another land.
Do not hide their sin. Do not take away their guilt from before You, because they made the builders angry.
So we built the wall. We joined all of it together up to half its height, because the people wanted to work.
When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that the wall of Jerusalem was being fixed and the gaps were closing, they got very angry.
They all made a plan to come and fight against Jerusalem and cause trouble.
We prayed to our God, and we set guards day and night to watch for them.
The people of Judah said, "The workers are getting tired. There is too much broken stone. We cannot build the wall."
Our enemies said, "They will not know or see us coming. Then we will kill them and stop the work."
The Jews who lived near them came ten times and said, "Wherever you go, they will attack us."
So I put people behind the lower parts of the wall, at the open spots. I put them in family groups, with swords, spears, and bows.

I looked around, stood up, and said to the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord. He is great and amazing. Fight for your brothers, sons, daughters, wives, and homes."
When our enemies heard that we knew their plan, God ruined it. Then we all went back to work on the wall.
From that day on, half of my servants worked on the building, and half held the spears, shields, bows, and armor. The leaders stood behind all the people of Judah.
The builders and the carriers worked with one hand, and held a weapon in the other hand.
Each builder had a sword tied at his side. The man with the trumpet stayed beside me.
I said to the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, "The work is big and spread out. We are far apart on the wall.
Wherever you hear the trumpet sound, run to us there. Our God will fight for us."
So we worked from early morning until the stars came out. Half of us held spears.
At that time I said to the people, "Let every man and his servant stay in Jerusalem at night. Then they can be guards at night and work during the day."
Neither I, nor my brothers, nor my servants, nor the guards with me took off our clothes. Each man kept his weapon, even when he went for water.
The people and their wives cried out loudly against their Jewish brothers.
Some said, "We have many sons and daughters. We need grain to eat so we can live."
Some said, "We have given up our fields, vineyards, and houses to get grain during the famine."
Others said, "We borrowed money to pay the king's tax on our fields and vineyards.

We are the same kind of people as our brothers. Our children are as good as theirs. But we have to sell our sons and daughters as slaves. Some of our daughters are already slaves. We have no power to stop it. Our fields and vineyards belong to other people now."
I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.
I thought about it. Then I argued with the leaders. I said to them, "You are charging your brothers too much interest!" I called a big meeting about them.
I said, "We have bought back our Jewish brothers who were sold to other nations. Now you are selling your brothers, and they may be sold to us!" They were quiet. They had nothing to say.
I also said, "What you are doing is not good. Shouldn't you live with respect for our God? Then our enemies will not make fun of us.
I, my brothers, and my servants are lending them money and grain. Please, let us stop charging this extra money.
Please give back to them today their fields, vineyards, olive trees, and houses. Also give back the extra money, grain, new wine, and oil you took from them."
They said, "We will give everything back. We will not ask them for anything. We will do what you say." Then I called the priests. I made the leaders swear to do this.

I also shook out my coat. I said, "May God shake out of his house and out of his work every man who does not keep this promise. May he be shaken out and left with nothing." The whole group said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. The people did what they promised.
From the time King Artaxerxes made me governor of Judah, from his twentieth year to his thirty-second year, I and my brothers did not eat the food given to the governor.

The governors before me made the people carry a heavy load. They took bread and wine from them, plus forty pieces of silver. Even their servants ruled over the people. But I did not do this, because I feared God.
I worked hard on this wall. All my servants were gathered there to work. We did not buy any land.
Also, one hundred fifty Jewish men and leaders ate at my table. Visitors from the nations around us came too.

Each day I prepared one ox, six good sheep, and some birds. Every ten days I had all kinds of wine in large amounts. But I did not ask for the governor's food, because the work was very hard for these people.
Remember me, my God, for good. Remember all I have done for these people.
Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and our other enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall. There were no gaps left in it. But I had not put doors in the gates yet.
Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message. They said, "Come, let us meet in one of the villages on the plain of Ono." But they wanted to hurt me.
I sent messengers back to them. I said, "I am doing a big job. I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and go down to you?"
Four times they sent me the same message. Each time I gave them the same answer.
The fifth time, Sanballat sent his helper to me. The helper had an open letter in his hand.

The letter said, "People everywhere are talking. Geshem says it is true. You and the Jews are planning to turn against the king. That is why you are building the wall. People also say you want to be their king.
You even set up prophets in Jerusalem to say about you, 'There is a king in Judah!' The king will hear this. So come, let us meet together."
I sent back this answer: "Nothing you are saying is true. You are making it up."
They all wanted to scare us. They thought, "Their hands will get weak, and the work will not be done." But I prayed, "God, give me strength."

I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah son of Mehetabel. He could not leave his home. He said, "Let us meet at God's house, inside the temple. Let us close the temple doors. Men are coming to kill you. They are coming to kill you at night."
I said, "Should a man like me run away? Should someone like me go into the temple just to stay alive? No, I will not go in."
I knew God had not sent him. He had spoken against me because Tobiah and Sanballat paid him.
They paid him to scare me. They wanted me to sin by going into the temple. Then they could shame me.
My God, remember what Tobiah and Sanballat have done. Also remember Noadiah, a woman prophet, and the other prophets who tried to scare me.
We finished the wall on the twenty-fifth day of Elul. It took fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard about it, the nations around us were afraid. They lost their courage. They knew God had helped us do this work.
In those days, the leaders of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah. Tobiah sent letters back to them.

Many people in Judah had promised to help him. Tobiah was connected to them by marriage. He was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah. His son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They also told me about the good things Tobiah did. Then they told Tobiah what I said. Tobiah sent letters to scare me.
After the wall was built and I put the doors in place, I chose gatekeepers, singers, and Levites.
Then I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem. I also put Hananiah in charge. He was the leader of the fort. I chose him because he could be trusted, and he feared God more than most people.

I told them, "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot. While the guards are on duty, keep the doors shut and locked. Also choose people who live in Jerusalem to guard. Some can stand at their posts, and some can guard near their homes."
The city was big and wide, but few people lived there. The houses had not been rebuilt yet.

Then my God put it in my heart to gather the leaders, the officials, and the people so they could be listed by family. I found the list of the first people who came back. I found these words written in it:
These are the people from the area who came back from being captives in Babylon. King Nebuchadnezzar had taken them away. They came back to Jerusalem and Judah. Each person went to his own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the men of Israel:
The family of Parosh had 2,172 people.
The family of Pahath-moab, through Jeshua and Joab, had 2,818.
The family of Ater, through Hezekiah, had 98.
