The people from Bethlehem and Netophah had 188.
The people from Beth Azmaveth had 42.
The people from Kiriath Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth had 743.
The people from Ramah and Geba had 621.
The people from Bethel and Ai had 123.
The people from the other Nebo had 52.
The people from the other Elam had 1,254.
The people from Lod, Hadid, and Ono had 721.
The family of Jedaiah, through Jeshua, had 973 priests.
The Levite family of Jeshua, through Kadmiel and Hodevah, had 74 people.
The singers from the family of Asaph had 148.
The gatekeepers from the families of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai had 138.
The temple servants were from these families: Ziha, Hasupha, and Tabbaoth.
They were also from Keros, Siaha, and Padon.
They were from Lebanah, Hagabah, and Shalmai.
They were from Hanan, Giddel, and Gahar.
They were from Reaiah, Rezin, and Nekoda.
They were from Gazzam, Uzza, and Paseah.
They were from Besai, Meunim, and Nephisim.
They were from Bakbuk, Hakupha, and Harhur.
They were from Bazluth, Mehida, and Harsha.
They were from Barkos, Sisera, and Temah.
They were from Neziah and Hatipha.
The servants of Solomon were from these families: Sotai, Sophereth, and Perida.
They were also from Jaala, Darkon, and Giddel.
They were from Shephatiah, Hattil, Pokereth-hazzebaim, and Amon.
In all, the temple servants and the servants of Solomon numbered 392.
The following people came from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer. They could not prove that their families came from Israel.
They were from the families of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, and they numbered 642.
Some of the priests were from the families of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai. Barzillai had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and took his name.
These men looked for their family records, but they could not find them. So they were not allowed to serve as priests.
The governor told them not to eat the most holy food until a priest could ask God using the Urim and Thummim.
This did not include their 7,337 male and female servants and 245 male and female singers.
Some family leaders gave money for the work. The governor gave 1,000 gold coins, 50 bowls, and 530 sets of clothes for the priests.
Other family leaders gave 20,000 gold coins and 2,200 pieces of silver for the work.
The rest of the people gave 20,000 gold coins, 2,000 pieces of silver, and 67 sets of clothes for the priests.
So the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and all the rest of Israel settled in their own towns. By the seventh month, the people of Israel had settled in their towns.

All the people came together as one in the open place in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the teacher to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses. The LORD had told Moses to give this law to Israel.
On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the Law to the people. Men, women, and all who could listen and understand were there.

He read from it from early morning until noon. He stood in the open place in front of the Water Gate. Men, women, and those who could understand listened. Everyone paid attention to the Book of the Law.

Ezra the teacher stood on a wood platform made for this. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah stood on his right. Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam stood on his left.
Ezra opened the book where everyone could see. He was above all the people. When he opened it, all the people stood up.
Ezra praised the LORD, the great God. All the people lifted their hands and said, "Amen, Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

The Levites—Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the other Levites—helped the people understand the Law. The people stayed where they stood.
They read from the Book of the Law of God. They explained it and helped people understand. So the people understood what was read.

Nehemiah the leader, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who helped the people spoke to all the people. They said, "This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not be sad. Do not cry." All the people were crying when they heard the words of the Law.
Then he said to them, "Go and eat good food. Drink sweet drinks. Send food to people who have nothing ready. This day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad. The joy of the LORD is your strength."
The Levites quieted all the people. They said, "Be quiet. This day is holy. Do not be sad."
Then all the people went to eat and drink. They sent food to others. They had a big, happy party. They did this because they understood the words that were taught to them.
On the second day, the leaders of the families, the priests, and the Levites came to Ezra the teacher. They wanted to learn more about the Law.
They found a rule in the Law. The LORD had told Moses that the people of Israel should live in booths during the seventh month feast.

They told everyone in all their towns and in Jerusalem, "Go out to the hills and bring back branches from olive trees, wild olive trees, myrtle trees, palm trees, and other leafy trees. Make booths with them, as the Law says."
So the people went out and brought branches back. They made booths on their roofs, in their yards, in the yards of God's house, and in the open places near the Water Gate and the Gate of Ephraim.
All the people who came back from being taken away made booths and lived in them. Since the time of Joshua son of Nun, the people of Israel had not celebrated like this. Everyone was very happy.
Day by day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God. They celebrated the feast for seven days. On the eighth day, they had a special meeting, as the rules said.
On the 24th day of that month, the people of Israel came together. They did not eat. They wore rough cloth. They put dirt on their heads.
The Israelites stayed away from people from other nations. They stood up and told God their sins and the sins of their parents.

They stood where they were and read from the Book of the Law of the the LORD their God for one fourth of the day. For another fourth of the day, they told God they were sorry and worshiped the the LORD their God.
The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the steps. They cried out loudly to the the LORD their God.

The Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, “Stand up and bless the the LORD your God forever and ever. May Your glorious name be blessed. May it be lifted up higher than all blessing and praise.

You alone are the the LORD. You made the heavens, even the highest heavens, and all their stars. You made the earth and everything on it. You made the seas and everything in them. You give life to everything. All the stars in the sky worship You. “
You are the the LORD God. You chose Abram. You brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans. You gave him the name Abraham.

You found his heart true to You. You made an agreement with him to give the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites to his children and their children. You kept Your promise, because You do what is right. “
You saw how our ancestors suffered in Egypt. You heard their cry at the Red Sea.
You did powerful signs and wonders against Pharaoh, his servants, and all the people of his land. You knew they treated our ancestors badly. You made a great name for Yourself that lasts to this day.
You split the sea in front of them. They walked through the sea on dry ground. You threw their enemies into the deep water. They sank like a stone in rushing water. “
You led them with a cloud pillar by day and a fire pillar by night. The pillars showed them the way to go.
You came down on Mount Sinai. You spoke to them from heaven. You gave them fair rules and true teaching. You gave them good laws and commands. “
You told them about Your holy Sabbath. You gave them commands, rules, and teaching through Your servant Moses.
When they were hungry, You gave them bread from heaven. When they were thirsty, You brought water out of the rock. You told them to go in and take the land You had promised to give them. “
But they and our ancestors acted proudly. They became stubborn. They did not obey Your commands.

They refused to listen. They forgot the miracles You did for them. They became stubborn. In their rebellion, they chose a leader to take them back to slavery. But You are a forgiving God. You are kind and caring. You are slow to anger. You love with great love. You did not leave them.
Even when they made a metal calf and said, ‘This is your god, who brought you out of Egypt,’ and when they insulted You so much. “

You did not leave them in the desert because of Your great kindness. By day the cloud pillar did not leave them. It led them on their way. By night the fire pillar did not leave them. It gave them light to show the way to go.
You gave Your good Spirit to teach them. You did not keep Your manna from them. You gave them water when they were thirsty.
For forty years You took care of them in the desert. They had everything they needed. Their clothes did not wear out. Their feet did not swell. “
You gave them kingdoms and nations. You gave them land on every side. They took the land of Sihon, king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, king of Bashan.
You made their children as many as the stars in the sky. You brought them to the land You had told their ancestors to take and live in.
Their children went in and took the land. You put the Canaanites who lived there under their power. You gave them the Canaanite kings and people, so they could do with them what they wanted.

They captured strong cities and good land. They took houses full of good things, wells already dug, vineyards, olive trees, and many fruit trees. They ate and were full. They became fat and happy because of Your great goodness. “
But they turned against You. They rebelled. They ignored Your law. They killed Your prophets, who had warned them to come back to You. They said very bad things about You.

So You let their enemies have power over them. Their enemies hurt them. But when they were in trouble, they cried out to You. You heard them from heaven. Because of Your great kindness, You sent people to save them. Those people saved them from their enemies.

But as soon as they were safe, they did evil again in Your sight. Then You let their enemies rule over them. When they cried out to You again, You heard them from heaven. Many times You saved them because of Your kindness. “

You warned them to come back to Your law. But they acted proudly. They did not obey Your commands. They broke Your rules, even though a person can live by following them. They turned away and would not listen.
For many years You were patient with them. By Your Spirit, You warned them through Your prophets. But they did not listen. So You let other nations have power over them.
But because of Your great kindness, You did not destroy them completely. You did not leave them. You are a kind and caring God. “

So now, our God, You are great, strong, and awesome. You keep Your promise of love. Please do not think it is too small a thing that all this trouble has come to us, our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all Your people. It has been this way since the days of the kings of Assyria until today.
In all that happened to us, You are right. You have been faithful, but we have done wrong. “
Our kings, leaders, priests, and ancestors did not keep Your law. They did not listen to Your commands and warnings You gave them.
Even in their own kingdom, with all the good things You gave them, and in the wide, rich land You set before them, they did not serve You. They did not stop doing evil. “
Here we are today, slaves in the land You gave our ancestors. You gave it to them so they could eat its fruit and enjoy its good things. But now we are slaves here.
Its big harvest goes to the kings You put over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and our animals however they want. We are in great trouble.
Because of all this, we are making a strong promise. We are writing it down. Our leaders, Levites, and priests are putting their seals on it.”
These people signed the agreement: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah.
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
The Levites were Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the family of Henadad, and Kadmiel.
Their brothers were Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, and Hanan.
The leaders of the people were Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, and Bani.

The rest of the people joined too. This included the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and all who had turned away from the peoples of the lands to obey God's Law. Their wives, sons, and daughters joined as well, if they were old enough to understand.

They joined their brothers and leaders. They promised with a curse and an oath to follow God's Law, which God gave through Moses, His servant. They also promised to obey carefully all the commands, rules, and laws of the LORD our God.
We will not give our daughters to marry people from other lands. We will not take their daughters to marry our sons.
If people from other lands bring things to sell on the Sabbath or on a holy day, we will not buy from them. We will let the land rest every seventh year, and we will cancel all debts.
We will give one-third of a shekel each year to help with the work in the house of our God.

This money is for the holy bread, the regular grain offering, the regular burnt offering, the Sabbath offerings, the new moon offerings, the feast day offerings, the holy gifts, and the sin offerings that make things right for Israel. It is also for all the work in the house of our God.
We used lots to choose who will bring wood to God's house. Each family will bring wood at set times every year. It will be burned on the altar of the LORD our God, as the Law says.
We will bring the first crops from our land and the first fruit from every tree to the house of the LORD every year.
We will bring our firstborn sons and our firstborn animals to the house of our God. We will bring the firstborn of our herds and flocks to the priests who serve in God's house, as the Law says.

We will bring the first part of our dough, our gifts, the fruit of every tree, new wine, and olive oil to the priests in the rooms of God's house. We will bring a tenth of our crops to the Levites, because they collect the tenth in all the towns where we work.
A priest from Aaron's family must be with the Levites when they collect the tenth. Then the Levites must bring one-tenth of that tenth to the rooms of the storehouse in God's house.

The people of Israel and the Levites will bring the grain, new wine, and olive oil to the rooms where the holy tools are kept. The priests who serve, the gatekeepers, and the singers are there. We will not forget the house of our God.
The leaders lived in Jerusalem. The rest of the people drew lots. One out of every ten would live in Jerusalem, the holy city. The other nine stayed in their towns.
The people blessed all the men who chose to live in Jerusalem.

These are the heads of the areas who lived in Jerusalem. In the towns of Judah, each person lived on his own land. This included the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the sons of Solomon's servants.
Some of the sons of Judah and Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. From Judah's sons: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, from Perez's family.
Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, from Shelah's family.
The sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were 468 brave men.
From Benjamin's sons: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah.
After him were Gabbai and Sallai. There were 928 men.
Joel son of Zichri was their leader. Judah son of Hassenuah was in charge of the second part of the city.
From the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib; Jachin.
Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub. He was the leader of the house of God.
Their helpers who worked in the temple were 822 men. Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah was also there.
His helpers, who were family leaders, were 242 men. Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer was also there.
Their helpers were 128 brave men. Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was their leader.
From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni.
Shabbethai and Jozabad were two leaders of the Levites. They were in charge of the outside work for the house of God.
Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph led the thanks and prayer. Bakbukiah was second among his helpers. Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun was also there.
The Levites in the holy city were 284.
The gatekeepers were Akkub, Talmon, and their helpers. They guarded the gates. There were 172 men.
The rest of the Israelites, with the priests and Levites, lived in all the towns of Judah. Each lived on his own land.
The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel. Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of them.
The leader of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica. He was from Asaph's family, the singers who served in the house of God.
The king had given a command about them. The singers got food each day.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel was the king's helper. He was from Zerah's family, from Judah. He spoke for the people in all matters.
Some people of Judah lived in villages with their fields. They lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages, Dibon and its villages, Jekabzeel and its villages,
Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its villages. They settled from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.
The sons of Benjamin lived from Geba to Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its villages,
Lod, Ono, and the Valley of Craftsmen.
Some Levites from Judah settled in Benjamin.
These are the priests and Levites who came back with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. He and his brothers led the songs of thanks.
Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, stood across from them in the work.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim. Joiakim was the father of Eliashib. Eliashib was the father of Joiada.
Joiada was the father of Jonathan. Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim, these were the leaders of the priest families. For Seraiah, Meraiah. For Jeremiah, Hananiah.
For Ezra, Meshullam. For Amariah, Jehohanan.
For Malluchi, Jonathan. For Shebaniah, Joseph.
For Harim, Adna. For Meraioth, Helkai.
For Iddo, Zechariah. For Ginnethon, Meshullam.
For Abijah, Zichri. For Miniamin and Moadiah, Piltai.
For Bilgah, Shammua. For Shemaiah, Jehonathan.
For Joiarib, Mattenai. For Jedaiah, Uzzi.
For Sallai, Kallai. For Amok, Eber.
For Hilkiah, Hashabiah. For Jedaiah, Nethanel.
In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the leaders of the Levite and priest families were written down. The priests were written down too, during the rule of Darius the Persian.
The family leaders of Levi were written in the Book of the Chronicles up to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their brothers. They stood across from each other to praise and thank God. One group answered the other, as David the man of God had commanded.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers. They guarded the storerooms at the gates.
These men served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak. They also served in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and writer.
When the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated, the Levites were found in all their towns. They were brought to Jerusalem to celebrate with joy, thanks, and song. They used cymbals, harps, and lyres.
The singers came from the area around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,
from Beth-gilgal, and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth. The singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites made themselves clean. Then they made the people, the gates, and the wall clean.
I brought the leaders of Judah up on the wall. I set up two large choirs to give thanks and walk along the wall. One choir went to the right, toward the Dung Gate.
Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed,
and some priests with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan son of Shemaiah son of Mattaniah son of Micaiah son of Zaccur son of Asaph,
and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played the musical instruments of David the man of God. Ezra the writer led them.
At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the stairs of the City of David to the wall. They passed above David's house to the Water Gate on the east.
The second choir went to the left. I followed them, with half the people, on the wall. We went from the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,
past the Gate of Ephraim, the Old Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate. They stopped at the Guard Gate.
The two choirs stood in the house of God. I stood there with half the officials.
The priests with trumpets were Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, Hananiah,
Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loudly under Jezrahiah, who led them.
That day they offered big sacrifices and were happy. God had given them great joy. The women and children were happy too. The joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.

That day men were chosen to be in charge of the storerooms. They collected gifts, first crops, and tenths. They brought in the shares the Law said to give to the priests and Levites. The fields around the towns gave these shares. Judah was happy about the priests and Levites who served.
They took care of the work of their God and the work of making things clean. The singers and gatekeepers did this too, as David and his son Solomon had commanded.
Long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were leaders of song. They sang praise and thanks to God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel gave shares to the singers and gatekeepers. They gave what was needed each day. They set apart shares for the Levites. The Levites set apart shares for the sons of Aaron.
That day the people read from the Book of Moses. They heard that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever join God's people.
This was because they did not help Israel with food and water. They paid Balaam to curse Israel. But our God turned the curse into a blessing.
When the people heard the law, they sent away everyone who was not from Israel.
Before this, Eliashib the priest was close to Tobiah.

He gave Tobiah a big room in God's house. Before that, people kept grain gifts, incense, temple things, and the tenth part of grain, new wine, and oil there. These were for the Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and gifts for the priests.
All this time I was not in Jerusalem. I had gone to the king of Babylon in the thirty-second year of his rule. Later I asked to leave and came back.
I came to Jerusalem. I saw the bad thing Eliashib did for Tobiah. He made a room for him in the yards of God's house.
This made me very angry. I threw all of Tobiah's things out of the room.
I told them to clean the rooms. They cleaned God's house. I brought back the grain gifts and incense.
I also learned that the Levites had not been given their share. The Levites and singers who did the work had gone back to their fields.
I argued with the leaders. I said, "Why has God's house been left empty?" I brought them together and put them back in their places.
Then all Judah brought the tenth part of grain, new wine, and oil into the store rooms.

I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the writer, Pedaiah the Levite, and Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah in charge of the store rooms. They were trusted men. They were to share the gifts with their brothers.
"Remember me, my God, for this. Do not wipe out the good things I did for Your house and its work."

In those days I saw people in Judah pressing grapes on the Sabbath. They brought big piles of grain and loaded donkeys. They also brought wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. I warned them not to sell food on that day.
Men from Tyre who lived there brought fish and all kinds of goods. They sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
I argued with the leaders of Judah. I said to them, "What bad thing are you doing? You are ruining the Sabbath.
Didn't your fathers do this? Our God brought all this trouble on us and on this city. Now you bring more anger on Israel by ruining the Sabbath."

When the gates of Jerusalem began to get dark before the Sabbath, I told them to shut the doors. I said they should not open them until after the Sabbath. I put some of my men at the gates so no load could come in on the Sabbath.
Sellers of all kinds of goods stayed outside Jerusalem once or twice.
I warned them. I said, "Why do you stay outside the wall? If you do it again, I will use force against you." After that, they did not come on the Sabbath.
I told the Levites to make themselves clean and come guard the gates. They were to keep the Sabbath holy. "Remember me, my God, for this. Spare me because of Your great love."
In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod. They could not speak the language of Judah. They spoke the language of many peoples.

I argued with them. I cursed them. I hit some of them. I pulled out their hair. I made them promise by God, "You will not give your daughters to their sons. You will not take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves."
"Didn't King Solomon of Israel sin because of this? There was no king like him among many nations. He was loved by his God. God made him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women made him sin.
Should we listen to you and do all this great evil? Should we be unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?"
One son of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was married to a daughter of Sanballat the Horonite. I chased him away from me.
"Remember them, my God, because they have made the priesthood and the promise of the priests and Levites unclean."
So I cleaned them from everything foreign. I set the priests and Levites in their jobs. Each man had his work.
I also set times for wood for the altar and for the first crops. "Remember me, my God, for good."
This happened in the days of King Ahasuerus. He ruled 127 lands, from India to Cush.
At that time, King Ahasuerus sat on his royal seat in the strong city of Susa.
In his third year as king, he made a big dinner for all his leaders and helpers. The army leaders of Persia and Media, and the important men from the lands, stood before him.
For 180 days, he showed how rich and great his kingdom was.
After those days, the king made a seven-day party in the garden of the king's palace. It was for all the people in the city of Susa, from the least important to the most important.
White and blue cloth hung there. Fine linen and purple cloth were tied with cords to silver rings on stone pillars. Gold and silver couches sat on a floor made of pretty, expensive stones.
They served drinks in gold cups. The king gave plenty of wine, because he was very generous.
No one had to drink. The king told the men who ran his house to let each man choose for himself.
Queen Vashti also made a dinner for the women in the king's palace.
On the seventh day, the king was happy from wine. He called seven men who helped him. Their names were Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas.
He told them to bring Queen Vashti to him. She was to wear the royal crown. He wanted to show the people and leaders how beautiful she was.
But Queen Vashti would not come. The king had sent the men with his message. The king became very angry, and his anger burned inside him.
Then the king talked to the wise men. They knew the right times to do things. He usually asked men who knew the law and what was fair.

The men closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. They were seven leaders of Persia and Media. They saw the king often and were very important in the kingdom.
The king asked, "What does the law say we should do to Queen Vashti? She did not obey the king's command that came through the helpers."
Memucan answered in front of the king and the leaders. He said, "Queen Vashti did wrong. She hurt not only the king, but all the leaders and all the people in the lands of King Ahasuerus.
All the women will hear what the queen did. Then they will look down on their husbands. They will say that King Ahasuerus told Queen Vashti to come, but she did not come.
Today the important women of Persia and Media will hear about this. They will tell all the king's leaders. Then there will be no end to disrespect and anger.

"If it pleases the king, send out a royal rule. Write it in the laws of Persia and Media, so it cannot be changed. Queen Vashti must never come before King Ahasuerus again. Give her royal place to a woman better than she is.
Then the king's rule will be heard in all his big kingdom. All women, from the least to the most important, will honor their husbands."
The king and the leaders liked this advice. The king did what Memucan said.

He sent letters to all the lands in his kingdom. Each land got the letter in its own writing, and each people got it in its own language. The letter said that every man should be the boss in his own home.
After these things, King Xerxes was not angry anymore. He remembered Queen Vashti, what she had done, and what he had decided about her.
The king's helpers said, "Let us look for pretty young girls for the king. They should never have been married.

Let the king choose leaders in every part of his kingdom. They can bring all the pretty young girls to the women's rooms in the fort of Susa. Put them with Hegai, the king's servant who takes care of the women. Give them things to make them beautiful.
Then the girl who makes the king happy can be queen instead of Vashti." This idea made the king happy, so he did it.
In the fort of Susa there was a Jewish man named Mordecai. He was the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish. He was from the family of Benjamin.
He had been taken from Jerusalem to Babylon. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon took him when he carried away Jeconiah, the king of Judah, and other people.
Mordecai took care of his cousin Hadassah, also called Esther. She had no father or mother. She was lovely and beautiful. When her parents died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.
When the king's order was heard, many young girls were brought to the fort of Susa to Hegai. Esther was also taken to the king's palace and put with Hegai, who took care of the women.
She pleased him and won his favor. He quickly gave her beauty care, her food, and seven special helpers from the king's palace. He moved her and her helpers to the nicest place in the women's rooms.
Esther did not tell anyone about her people or her family, because Mordecai had told her not to.
Every day Mordecai walked in front of the courtyard of the women's rooms. He wanted to know how Esther was and what was happening to her.
Before a young woman went in to King Xerxes, she had to have twelve months of beauty care. She had six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and makeup.
When she went in to the king, she could take anything she wanted from the women's rooms to the king's palace.

She went in the evening and came back in the morning to the second women's rooms. Shaashgaz, the king's servant who took care of the other women, was in charge there. She did not go to the king again unless he liked her and called her by name.
When it was Esther's turn to go in to the king, she did not ask for anything except what Hegai, the king's servant who took care of the women, told her to ask for. Everyone who saw Esther liked her.
She was taken to King Xerxes in his palace in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his rule.
The king loved Esther more than all the other women. She won his favor and kindness more than all the other young girls. He put the royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.
The king gave a big party for Esther. He invited all his leaders and servants. He gave a holiday to the lands he ruled. He gave gifts generously.
When the young girls were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
Esther still did not tell her family or people, just as Mordecai had told her. She kept doing what Mordecai said, just as she did when he raised her.
In those days, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate. Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's servants who guarded the door, got angry. They planned to hurt King Xerxes.
Mordecai heard about the plan. He told Queen Esther, and she told the king that Mordecai had heard it.
The plan was checked and found true. Both men were hanged on a pole. This was written in the book of the king's records.
After these things, King Ahasuerus made Haman very important. Haman was the son of Hammedatha. He was an Agagite. The king gave him a high seat. It was above all the other leaders with the king.
All the king's workers at the gate bowed down to Haman. They did this because the king said to do it. But Mordecai did not bow down or worship Haman.
The king's workers at the gate said to Mordecai, "Why do you disobey the king's rule?"
Day after day they said this to him. He did not listen. So they told Haman. They wanted to see if Mordecai would keep refusing. Mordecai had told them he was a Jew.
Haman saw that Mordecai did not bow down or worship him. Haman was very angry.
They told Haman who Mordecai's people were. Haman did not want to hurt only Mordecai. He wanted to destroy all the Jews in King Ahasuerus's land.

In the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, in the first month, Nisan, they cast lots. This was called Pur. They cast them before Haman. They did this day after day and month after month. The lot chose the twelfth month, Adar.

Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is one people. They are spread out among the people in all your lands. Their laws are different from all other people. They do not obey the king's laws. It is not good for you to let them stay.
If it pleases the king, write an order to destroy them. I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the king's treasury. The king's workers can take it."
The king took his special ring from his hand. He gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite. Haman was the enemy of the Jews.
The king said to Haman, "The silver is given to you. The people are given to you too. Do with them what seems good to you."

On the thirteenth day of the first month, the king's writers were called. They wrote all that Haman told them to write. They sent it to the rulers of each land. They wrote to each land in its own writing. They wrote to each people in its own language. They wrote it in the name of King Ahasuerus. They sealed it with the king's ring.

Letters were sent by messengers to all the king's lands. They told the people to destroy, kill, and wipe out all the Jews. This included young and old, women and children. It was to happen in one day. That day was the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. The people could take the Jews' things.
A copy of the writing was given as a law in every land. It was shown to all the people. They were to be ready for that day.
The messengers went out quickly. They did what the king said. The law was given in Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink. The city of Susa was confused.
When Mordecai learned what had happened, he tore his clothes. He put on rough cloth and ashes. He went into the city. He cried out with a loud and bitter cry.
He went up to the king's gate. But he could not go in, because no one in rough cloth could enter the king's gate.
In every part of the land, the king's order made the Jews very sad. They fasted, cried, and wailed. Many lay in rough cloth and ashes.
Esther's helpers and servants came and told her about Mordecai. The queen was very upset. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear instead of his rough cloth. But he would not take them.
Then Esther called Hathach. He was one of the king's helpers who served her. She told him to find out why Mordecai was so upset.
So Hathach went out to Mordecai. Mordecai was in the city square in front of the king's gate.
Mordecai told him all that had happened. He also told how much money Haman had promised to pay into the king's money room to destroy the Jews.

Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the king's order. It said the Jews would be destroyed. He told Hathach to show it to Esther and explain it. He also told Esther to go to the king. She should beg for mercy and ask for her people.
Hathach went back and told Esther what Mordecai had said.
Then Esther told him to give this answer to Mordecai:

"All the king's officials and the people in his lands know the rule. Anyone who goes to the king in the inner room without being called must die. Only if the king holds out his gold scepter will that person live. But I have not been called to go to the king for thirty days."
Esther's words were told to Mordecai.
He sent back this answer: "Do not think you will escape in the king's house while all the other Jews die.
If you stay quiet now, help and rescue will come to the Jews from somewhere else. But you and your family will die. Who knows? Maybe you became queen for a time like this."
Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:

"Go and gather all the Jews in Susa. Fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my helpers will fast too. Then I will go to the king, even though it is against the rule. If I die, I die."
So Mordecai went away and did everything Esther had told him.

On the third day, Esther put on her royal clothes. She stood in the inner courtyard of the king's house. She faced the king's house. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house. He faced the gate of the house.

On the third day, Esther put on her royal clothes. She stood in the inner courtyard of the king's house. She faced the king's house. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house. He faced the gate of the house.
When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard, he was pleased with her. The king held out the gold scepter in his hand to Esther. Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter.
When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard, he was pleased with her. The king held out the gold scepter in his hand to Esther. Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter.
The king said to her, "What do you want, Queen Esther? What is your request? It will be given to you, even up to half of my kingdom."
The king said to her, "What do you want, Queen Esther? What is your request? It will be given to you, even up to half of my kingdom."
Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast I have made for him."
Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast I have made for him."
The king said, "Hurry! Bring Haman so we can do what Esther said." So the king and Haman came to the feast Esther had made.
The king said, "Hurry! Bring Haman so we can do what Esther said." So the king and Haman came to the feast Esther had made.
While they drank wine, the king said to Esther, "What is your wish? It will be given to you. What is your request? I will do it, even up to half of my kingdom."
While they drank wine, the king said to Esther, "What is your wish? It will be given to you. What is your request? I will do it, even up to half of my kingdom."
Esther answered, "This is my wish and my request:
Esther answered, "This is my wish and my request:
"If you are pleased with you is not needed? wait"
"If you are pleased with me, and if it pleases you to grant my wish and do what I ask, then let the king and Haman come to the feast I will make for them. Tomorrow I will do what you say."
Haman left that day happy and glad. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and Mordecai did not stand up or move for him, Haman was very angry with Mordecai.
But Haman held back his anger. He went home and sent for his friends and his wife, Zeresh.
Haman told them about his great riches, his many children, and all the ways the king had honored him. He told how the king had made him greater than the other leaders and servants.
Haman also said, "Queen Esther did not let anyone come with the king to the feast she made, except me. And tomorrow I am invited again with the king.
"But all of this does not make me happy, because I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."

His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a tall pole made, about 75 feet high. In the morning, ask the king to hang Mordecai on it. Then go happily with the king to the feast." Haman liked this idea, and he had the pole made.
That night the king could not sleep. He said, "Bring the book that tells what happened in the past." They read it to the king.
They found where Mordecai had told about Bigthana and Teresh. They were two of the king's helpers who guarded the door. They had tried to hurt King Ahasuerus.
The king asked, "What did we do to honor Mordecai for this?" His helpers said, "Nothing was done for him."
The king asked, "Who is in the yard?" Haman had come into the outer yard of the king's house. He wanted to ask the king to hang Mordecai on the tall post he had set up.
The king's helpers said, "Haman is standing in the yard." The king said, "Bring him in."
Haman came in. The king said, "What should be done for the man the king wants to honor?" Haman thought, "Who would the king want to honor more than me?"
Haman said to the king, "For the man the king wants to honor,
bring a royal robe the king has worn, and a horse the king has ridden. Put a royal crown on its head.

Give the robe and horse to one of the king's important leaders. Have him dress the man the king wants to honor. Then have him lead him on the horse through the city square. Have people shout before him, 'This is what is done for the man the king wants to honor!'"
The king said to Haman, "Hurry! Take the robe and horse, just as you said. Do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Do not leave out anything from all that you said."
So Haman took the robe and horse. He dressed Mordecai and led him on horseback through the city square. He shouted before him, "This is what is done for the man the king wants to honor!"
Then Mordecai went back to the king's gate. Haman hurried home. He was sad and covered his head.

Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends what had happened to him. His wife Zeresh and his wise friends said to him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is one of the Jews, you will not win against him. You will surely fall before him."
While they were still talking, the king's helpers came. They hurried to bring Haman to the dinner Esther had made.
The king and Haman went to eat with Queen Esther.

While they drank wine at the second dinner, the king asked Esther again, "What do you want, Queen Esther? It will be given to you. What are you asking for? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be done."
Queen Esther answered, "If you are pleased with me, King, and if it pleases you, please save my life. That is what I ask. And save my people. That is what I want.
I and my people have been sold to be destroyed, killed, and wiped out. If we had only been sold as slaves, I would have kept quiet, because the enemy is not worth the harm he brings to the king."
King Xerxes asked Queen Esther, "Who is he, and where is he, who has dared to do such a thing?"
Esther replied, "The man who hates us and is our enemy is this bad Haman!" Haman was scared in front of the king and queen.
The king was so angry that he got up from the dinner and went into the palace garden. Haman stayed to beg Queen Esther to spare his life. He saw the king had decided to destroy him.

When the king came back from the garden to the dinner hall, Haman was falling on the bed where Esther was. The king said, "Would he dare attack the queen while I am in the house?" As soon as the king said this, they covered Haman's face.

Then Harbonah, one of the king's servants, said, "Look, there is a very tall pole for hanging at Haman's house. He had it built for Mordecai, who helped save the king's life. Hang him on it!" The king said, "Hang him on it!"
So they hanged Haman on the pole he had made for Mordecai. Then the king's anger went away.
On that day, King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther Haman's house. Haman was the enemy of the Jews. Mordecai came to the king. Esther had told the king who Mordecai was to her.
The king took off his ring. He had taken it from Haman. He gave it to Mordecai. Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's house.
Esther spoke to the king again. She fell at his feet and cried. She begged him to stop Haman's bad plan. Haman the Agagite had planned to hurt the Jews.
The king held out his gold scepter to Esther. She stood up and stood before the king.

She said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor with him, and if this seems right to the king and good to him, then write a new letter. Take back the letters Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite wrote. He wrote them to kill the Jews in all the king's lands.
I cannot bear to see my people hurt. I cannot bear to see my family ruined."
The king said to Esther and Mordecai, "I have given Esther Haman's house. They hanged Haman on a pole because he hurt the Jews.
Now you may write a letter in my name about the Jews. Write what seems right to you. Seal it with my ring. A letter written in my name and sealed with my ring cannot be changed."

On the 23rd day of the third month, Sivan, the king's writers were called. They wrote everything Mordecai told them. They sent it to the Jews and to the rulers in all 127 lands, from India to Ethiopia. Each land got the message in its own writing. Each people got it in their own language. The Jews got it in their own writing and language.
The letters were written in the name of King Ahasuerus. They were sealed with the king's ring. Messengers on fast horses carried them. They rode the king's best horses.
The king let the Jews in every city gather together. They could fight to save their lives. They could destroy any army that attacked them. They could also take the enemy's things.
This was to happen on one day in all the lands. It was the 13th day of the 12th month, called Adar.
A copy of the letter was sent to every land. It was made known to all people. The Jews were to be ready on that day to fight back against their enemies.
The messengers hurried out because the king commanded it. The law was also given in the city of Susa.
Mordecai left the king wearing royal clothes. He wore blue and white. He had a big gold crown and a purple robe made of fine cloth. The city of Susa shouted with joy.
The Jews had light, joy, and honor.
In every land and city where the king's order reached, the Jews were happy. They had parties and special days. Many people became Jews, because they were afraid of the Jews.

On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, called Adar, the king's order was to happen. On that day, the enemies of the Jews wanted to rule them. But it turned around. The Jews ruled those who hated them.

In every part of King Ahasuerus's land, the Jews came together in their towns. They stood against people who wanted to hurt them. No one could stand against them, because all the people were afraid of them.
All the leaders, helpers, and workers for the king helped the Jews. They did this because they were afraid of Mordecai.
Mordecai was great in the king's house. People in every land heard about him. Mordecai kept getting greater.
The Jews hit all their enemies with swords. They killed and destroyed them. They did what they wanted to their enemies.
In the strong city of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed 500 men.
They killed these sons of Haman: Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
These ten were the sons of Haman, son of Hammedatha. He had hated the Jews. The Jews did not take their things.
That day, the number of dead in Susa was told to the king.

The king said to Queen Esther, "In Susa, the Jews killed 500 men. They also killed Haman's ten sons. What have they done in the rest of the land? What do you want? It will be given. What else do you ask? It will be done."
Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa do tomorrow what they did today. Also, hang Haman's ten sons on poles."
The king said, "Yes. Do it." The order was given in Susa. They hanged Haman's ten sons.
On the fourteenth day of Adar, the Jews in Susa came together again. They killed 300 men in Susa. They did not take their things.
The other Jews in the king's lands came together. They stood up for their lives. They rested from their enemies. They killed 75,000 people who hated them. They did not take their things.
This was on the thirteenth day of Adar. They rested on the fourteenth day. They made it a day of feasts and joy.
The Jews in Susa came together on the thirteenth and fourteenth days. They rested on the fifteenth day. They made it a day of feasts and joy.
So the Jews who lived in small towns make the fourteenth day of Adar a day of joy, feasts, and good times. They send food to each other.
Mordecai wrote these things down. He sent letters to all the Jews in King Ahasuerus's lands, near and far.
He told them to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar every year.

These were the days the Jews rested from their enemies. Their sad month turned into a happy month. Their crying turned into a good day. They were to make these days into feasts and joy. They were to send food to each other and gifts to poor people.
The Jews agreed to do what they had started. They also agreed to do what Mordecai wrote to them.
Haman, son of Hammedatha, was from Agag. He hated all the Jews. He planned to destroy them. He cast lots to pick a day to crush and destroy them.
When Esther went to the king, he wrote that Haman's bad plan should come back on Haman. Haman and his sons were hanged on poles.
So these days are called Purim, after the word Pur. This is because of all the words in this letter, and because of what the Jews saw and what happened to them.
The Jews set these days for themselves, their children, and all who joined them. They would not skip them. They would do these two days every year, at the right time, the way it was written.
These days are remembered and done in every family and every town, in every age. The days of Purim will not pass from the Jews. Their memory will not end for their children.
Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with full power to make the second letter about Purim strong.
He sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 parts of Ahasuerus's land. The letters had words of peace and truth.

They set up these days of Purim at their times. Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther set them up. They set them up for themselves and their children. They also set up the times of fasting and crying out.
Esther's command made these words about Purim strong. They were written in a book.
King Ahasuerus made the land and the islands in the sea pay a tax.
All of Mordecai's power and strength, and the story of how great the king made him, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Media and Persia.
Mordecai the Jew was next in rank to King Ahasuerus. He was great among the Jews, and many of his people liked him. He worked for the good of his people and spoke peace to all his family.
There was a man in the land of Uz. His name was Job. He was good and honest. He respected God and stayed away from bad things.
He had seven sons and three daughters.
He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pairs of oxen, and 500 donkeys. He had many workers. He was the greatest man in the east.
His sons took turns having parties at their homes. They invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

After the parties, Job would call his children and make them clean. He got up early and gave burnt offerings for each one. He thought, "Maybe my children did wrong. Maybe they cursed God in their hearts." Job did this every time.
One day God's angels came to stand before the LORD. Satan came with them.
The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered, "I have been walking all over the earth."
The LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed My servant Job? There is no one like him on earth. He is good and honest. He respects God and stays away from bad things."
Satan answered the LORD, "Does Job respect God for no reason?
You have kept him safe on every side. You have kept his family and all he has safe. You have blessed his work. His animals have grown in the land.
But stretch out Your hand and touch all he has. He will curse You right to Your face."
The LORD said to Satan, "All he has is under your control. But do not hurt him." Then Satan left the LORD.
One day Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother's house.
A messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing. The donkeys were eating grass nearby.
Then the Sabeans attacked and took them. They killed the workers with swords. I am the only one who got away to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "Fire from God fell from the sky. It burned up the sheep and the workers. I am the only one who got away to tell you."

While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "The Chaldeans came in three groups. They took the camels and killed the workers with swords. I am the only one who got away to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother's house.
A big wind came from the desert. It hit all four corners of the house. The house fell on the young people, and they died. I am the only one who got away to tell you."
Then Job stood up. He tore his robe. He shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped.
He said, "I was born with nothing. I will go back with nothing. The LORD gave, and the LORD took away. May the LORD's name be praised."
In all this, Job did not sin. He did not blame God.
One day, God's sons came to stand before the LORD. Satan came too, to stand before the LORD.
The LORD asked Satan, "Where did you come from?" Satan said, "I have been going all over the earth."

The LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed My servant Job? No one on earth is like him. He is good and honest. He respects God and stays away from evil. He still holds to his good name, even though you pushed Me to hurt him for no reason."
Satan answered, "A man will give up one thing to save another. He will give all he has to stay alive.
But reach out Your hand and hurt his body. Then he will curse You to Your face."
The LORD said to Satan, "All right. He is in your power, but do not kill him."
So Satan left the LORD's presence. He gave Job painful sores all over, from his feet to his head.
Job sat in ashes. He took a piece of broken clay pot and scratched himself.
His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your good name? Curse God and die!"
Job said to her, "You talk like a foolish woman. Should we take good things from God, but not bad things?" Job did not sin with his words.

Job had three friends: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuh, and Zophar from Naamah. They heard about all the bad things that happened to Job. So they came from their homes and met together. They went to feel sad with him and help him feel better.
They looked at him from far away and did not know him. They cried loudly. Each man tore his clothes and put dust on their heads.
Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one spoke to him, because they saw he hurt very much.
After this, Job opened his mouth. He cursed the day he was born.
May the day I was born be lost. May the night that said, 'A boy is born,' be lost too.
May that day be dark. May God above not care about it. May no light shine on it.
May darkness and deep gloom take it. May a cloud cover it. May blackness fill it.
May thick dark take that night. May it not be counted in the days of the year. May it not be counted in any month.
May that night be empty. May no happy shout be heard in it.
Let those who know how to curse a day curse it. Let those who can wake the sea monster do it.
May its stars go dark. May it wait for light but not get it. May it not see the morning light.
For it did not close the doors of my mother's body. It did not hide trouble from my eyes." "
Why did I not die when I was born? Why did I not die as I came from my mother?
Why were there knees to hold me? Why were there breasts to feed me?
Now I would lie down and be quiet. I would sleep and rest.
I would rest with kings and leaders of the earth. They built places that are now in ruins.
Or with princes who had gold. They filled their houses with silver.
Or why was I not hidden like a baby who died before birth? Like a baby who never saw light.
There the bad people stop making trouble. There tired people rest.
Prisoners rest together. They do not hear the boss shout.
The small and the great are there. The slave is free from his master." "
Why is light given to people in pain? Why is life given to people who are bitter?
They wait for death, but it does not come. They look for it more than for hidden treasure.
They are glad and happy when they find the grave.
Why is life given to a man who cannot see his way? God has shut him in.
My sighs are my food. My groans pour out like water.
What I feared has come to me. What I dreaded has happened.
I have no peace. I have no quiet. I have no rest, only trouble."
“If someone tries to talk to you, will you get tired? But who can keep from speaking?
In the past, you taught many people. You made weak hands strong.
Your words held up people who were falling. You made weak knees strong.
But now trouble comes to you, and you are tired. It touches you, and you are scared.
Isn’t your fear of God your safety? Isn’t living right your hope?
“Think now. Who has ever died while innocent? Where were good people wiped out?
As I have seen, people who do wrong and cause trouble get back what they gave.
God’s breath destroys them. His angry wind ends them.
The lion may roar. The fierce lion may growl. But the young lions’ teeth are broken.
The old lion dies with no food. The young lions scatter.
“A secret word came to me. My ear caught a whisper of it.
It came in scary thoughts at night, when deep sleep falls on people.
Fear and shaking came over me. They made all my bones shake.
A spirit passed by my face, and the hair on my body stood up.
It stood still, but I could not see its shape. A form was before my eyes. Then I heard a quiet voice:
“‘Can a person be right before God? Can a man be clean before his Maker?
Look, He does not trust His servants. He finds fault with His angels.
How much more people who live in clay houses, whose base is dust! They are crushed more easily than a moth.
From morning to night they are beaten down. Without anyone noticing, they are gone forever.
Their life is pulled up like a tent. They die without wisdom.’”
Call out now. Will anyone answer you? Which holy one will you turn to?
For anger kills a fool, and jealousy kills a simple person.
I have seen a fool take root, but then I cursed his home right away.
His sons are far from safety. They are crushed at the city gate, and no one saves them.
Hungry people eat his crops, even from thorn bushes. Thirsty people long for his riches. “
For hardship does not come from the dust. Trouble does not grow from the ground.
But people are born to trouble, just like sparks fly up. “
But I would ask God for help. I would bring my case to God.
He does great things we cannot find out. His wonders have no number.
He gives rain to the earth and sends water on the fields.
He lifts humble people up high, and sad people are lifted to safety.
He stops the plans of sneaky people, so their hands do not succeed. “
He catches wise people in their own tricks. The plans of sneaky people fail fast.
They meet darkness in the day and feel around at noon like it is night.
He saves poor people from cruel words and from the hand of strong people.
So poor people have hope, and wrong is silenced. “
Happy is the man God corrects, so do not hate the lessons of the Almighty.
For He hurts, but He also bandages. He strikes, but His hands heal.
He will save you from six troubles. No harm will touch you in seven.
In hunger He will save you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
You will be safe from cruel words, and you will not fear ruin when it comes. “
You will laugh at ruin and hunger, and you will not fear wild animals.
For you will have an agreement with the stones of the field, and wild animals will be at peace with you.
You will know your tent is safe, and you will check your home and find nothing wrong.
You will know your children will be many, and your family will be like grass on the earth.
You will go to the grave at a good old age, like grain brought in at the right time.
We have checked this, and it is true. So listen and know it for yourself.”
"If only my sadness could be weighed, and all my trouble put on a scale together!
It would be heavier than the sand of the sea. That is why my words have been rough.
The arrows of the Almighty are in me. Their poison fills my spirit. God's terrors line up against me.
Does a wild donkey cry out when it has grass? Does an ox make noise when it has food?
Is tasteless food eaten without salt? Is there flavor in the white of an egg?
I do not want them. They make me sick."
"I wish I could have what I ask. I wish God would give me what I hope for.
I wish God would be pleased to crush me, to let go His hand and cut me off.
Then I would still have comfort. I would be glad in pain without holding back, because I have not hidden the words of the Holy One.
What strength do I have to keep going? What is left for me to wait for?
Is my strength like stone? Is my body made of bronze?
I have no help in myself. Good sense has left me."
"A hurting person should get kindness from a friend, or he may turn away from fearing the Almighty.
But my brothers have been untrue, like a stream that dries up. They pass by like rushing streams.
They are dark with ice. Snow hides on them.
When it gets warm, they melt away and disappear from their place.
Travelers turn off their path. They go into empty land and die.
The travelers from Tema look. The travelers from Sheba hope for them.
They are ashamed because they trusted. They come and are disappointed."
"Now you have become nothing. You see trouble and are afraid.
Did I ever say, 'Give me something'? Did I say, 'Pay for me with your money'?
Did I ask you to save me from an enemy? Did I ask you to buy me back from cruel men?
Teach me, and I will be quiet. Show me where I was wrong.
Honest words can hurt, but what does your arguing show?
Do you think you can fix words? The words of a sad man are like wind.
You would even throw dice for an orphan. You would sell your friend.
But now please look at me. I will not lie to your face.
Please turn back. Let there be no wrong. Turn again, and my good name is still there.
Is there wrong on my tongue? Can my mouth not tell trouble?"
Life on earth is hard work.
A slave wants shade. A worker hopes to get paid. "
So I have months of empty days. I have nights of trouble.
When I lie down, I ask, 'When will morning come?' I toss and turn until daylight. "
Worms cover my body. Dust is on me. My skin breaks open and looks bad.
My days go by fast, like thread on a loom. They end with no hope. "
Remember that my life is short, like a breath. My eyes will not see good again.
The person who sees me now will not see me again. Your eyes look at me, and then I am gone. "
A cloud fades and is gone. In the same way, a person who goes down to the grave does not come back.
He will not return to his house. His place will not know him anymore. "
So I will not be quiet. I will speak because I am upset. I will complain because I am sad. "
Am I the sea or a sea monster? Why do You guard me?
When I say, 'My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my pain,' "
then You scare me with dreams. You frighten me with visions.
So I would rather choke and die than keep this body. "
I hate this life. I will not live forever. Leave me alone, because my days are just a breath. "
What is a person that You make him so important? Why do You care so much about him?
You check on him every morning. You test him every moment. "
How long will You not look away from me? Will You not leave me alone even for a moment?
I have sinned. What can I do to You, You who watch over people? Why have You made me Your target? Am I a burden to You? "
Why not take away my sin? Why not forgive my wrong? Soon I will lie in the dust. You will look for me, but I will not be there."
"How long will you talk like this? Your words are like a big wind.
Does God make things unfair? Does the Almighty twist what is right?
Your sons sinned against Him, so He let them face the trouble they made.
If you look to God and ask the Almighty for help,
if you are clean and good, then He will come to help you and make your home good again.
You started small, but your future will grow big. "
Ask the old people. Listen to what their fathers learned.
We are new here and know little. Our days on earth pass like a shadow.
Won't they teach you and tell you what they know in their hearts? "
Can a water plant grow without a swamp? Can reeds grow without water?
While they are still growing, they dry up before other plants do.
That is what happens to people who forget God. The hope of people who do not follow God will die.
His trust is weak. His safety is like a spider's web.
He leans on his house, but it falls. He holds it tight, but it does not last.
He is like a plant with lots of water in the sun. Its branches spread over the garden.
Its roots wrap around rocks. It tries to find a place among the stones.
If it is pulled up, it is gone. Its place does not remember it.
This is how his life goes. But others will grow from the dust. "
Look, God does not turn away a good man. He will not help bad people.
He will fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.
Your enemies will be covered with shame. The home of bad people will be gone."
"I know this is true. But how can a person be right with God?
If someone wanted to argue with God, he could not answer even one question out of a thousand.
God is wise and strong. Who has stood against Him and won?
"He moves mountains, and they do not even know it. He turns them over when He is angry.
He shakes the earth out of its place. What holds it up trembles.
He tells the sun not to shine, and He hides the stars.
He alone spreads out the sky. He walks on the waves of the sea.
He made the stars named the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the stars in the south.
He does great things we cannot understand. He does more wonders than we can count.
"If He passes by me, I do not see Him. If He moves on, I do not notice Him.
If He takes something away, who can stop Him? Who can ask Him, 'What are You doing?'
God does not hold back His anger. Even strong helpers bow down to Him.
"So how can I answer Him? How can I choose my words with Him?
Even if I were right, I could not answer Him. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
If I called Him and He answered, I still would not believe He listened to me.
He crushes me in a storm. He gives me many wounds for no reason.
He will not let me catch my breath. He fills me with bitter pain.
If this is about strength, He is strong! If this is about justice, who can call Him into court?
Even if I were right, my own words would show me wrong. Even if I had no blame, He would say I am guilty.
I have done no wrong, but I do not know myself. I hate my life.
"It is all the same. So I say, 'He destroys both good people and bad people.'
When sudden trouble kills, He laughs at the pain of innocent people.
The earth is given to wicked people. He covers the eyes of its judges. If it is not Him, then who is it?
"My days are faster than a runner. They run by without any good.
They pass like boats made of reeds, like an eagle diving for food.
"If I say, 'I will forget my trouble and smile again,'
I still fear all my pain. I know You will not clear me.
If I am guilty, why work so hard for nothing? It is useless.
Even if I wash with snow water and make my hands clean with soap,
You will throw me into a pit. Even my clothes will hate me.
"He is not a man like me, so I cannot answer Him. We cannot go to court together.
There is no one between us to put a hand on us both.
Let Him take away His punishment, so I am not afraid of Him.
Then I would speak without being afraid of Him. But now I cannot."
I am tired of living. I will say what is wrong. I will speak from my sad heart.
I will ask God not to call me bad. I will ask Him to show me why He fights me.
Is it good for You to hurt me? Do You hate what You made? Do You help bad people's plans? "
Do You have human eyes? Do You see like a person sees?
Are Your days like a person's days? Are Your years like a man's years?
Why do You look for my wrong? Why do You search for my sin?
You know I am not bad. No one can save me from Your power. "
Your hands made me and put me together. But now You destroy me.
Please remember that You made me like clay. Will You turn me back to dust?
Did You not make me from a tiny drop, like milk that turns to cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh. You covered me with bones and muscles.
You gave me life and kindness. You watched over my spirit.
You kept all this in Your heart. I know it was Your plan. "
If I do wrong, You see it. You will not clear me of my wrong.
If I am bad, I am in trouble. If I am good, I still feel too ashamed to look up. I am full of shame. Please see my pain.
You hunt me like a fierce lion. You keep showing Your power against me.
You bring new witnesses against me. You get more angry with me. Hard times and war come against me. "
Why did You bring me out of my mother's womb? I wish I had died before anyone saw me.
It would be like I never lived. I would go straight from the womb to the grave.
My days are short. Please leave me alone for a little while. Let me have a little peace.
Before I go to a place I cannot come back from, the land of darkness and death.
It is a dark land, like black night. Nothing is in order there. Even the light looks dark."
"Should so many words go without an answer? Should a man who talks a lot be called right?
Do your proud words make people stay quiet? You laugh at others, and no one tells you to stop.
You say, 'My teaching is right, and I am clean in His sight.'
"I wish God would speak. I wish He would open His mouth and answer you.
He would show you hidden wisdom. True wisdom is much bigger than you think. Know this: God does not punish you as much as your sin deserves.
"Can you understand God's deep ways? Can you find out how far the Almighty goes?
God's ways are higher than the sky. What can you do? They are deeper than the grave. What can you know?
They are longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
"If God passes by and locks someone up, or calls a court, who can stop Him?
He knows false people. When He sees wrong, He does not ignore it.
But a silly man cannot become wise, just like a wild donkey cannot become a person.
"If you set your heart on God and lift your hands to Him,
if you put away the wrong in your hand and do not let sin stay in your home,
"then you can lift your face without shame. You will stand strong and not be afraid.
You will forget your trouble, like water that has flowed away.
Your life will be bright like noon. Even your dark times will be like morning.
"You will be safe, because there is hope. You will look around and rest in peace.
You will lie down, and no one will scare you. Many people will come to you for help.
But the eyes of bad people will grow weak. They will not escape. Their hope will be like a last breath."
"You think you are the only smart people. You think wisdom will die with you.
But I have a mind like yours. I am not less than you. Everyone knows these things.
My friends laugh at me. I called to God, and He answered me. I am a good and honest man, but they still laugh at me.
"People who feel safe look down on people in trouble. Trouble is waiting for people who slip.
Robbers live in peace. People who make God angry feel safe. They trust their own power.
"But ask the animals. They will teach you. Ask the birds in the sky. They will tell you.
Or talk to the earth. It will teach you. The fish in the sea will tell you too.
All of them know that the the LORD did this.
"He holds the life of every living thing. He holds the breath of all people.
Ears test words, just like mouths taste food.
Old people are wise. Long life brings understanding.
"God has wisdom and power. He has good advice and understanding.
If He tears something down, no one can build it back. If He locks someone in, no one can open it.
If He holds back the water, it dries up. If He sends it out, it floods the earth.
He has strength and true wisdom. Both the tricked and the trickster belong to Him.
"He leads advisors away with nothing. He makes judges look foolish.
He takes power from kings. He makes them weak.
He leads priests away with nothing. He knocks down strong men.
He takes away the words of trusted people. He takes away the wisdom of old leaders.
He brings shame on leaders. He takes strength from strong men.
"He shows things hidden in darkness. He brings dark secrets to light.
He makes nations great, then destroys them. He grows nations, then leads them away.
He takes away the sense of the leaders. He makes them wander in a place with no path.
They feel around in the dark with no light. He makes them stagger like a drunk person."
“My eyes have seen all this. My ears have heard and understood it.
What you know, I know too. I am not less than you.
But I want to speak to the Almighty. I want to argue my case with God.
But you cover me with lies. You are all bad doctors.
I wish you would be quiet. That would be wise for you.
Listen to my side. Hear my words.
Will you say wrong things for God? Will you lie for Him?
Will you take His side? Will you fight for God?
Will it go well when He checks you? Can you trick Him like you trick people?
He will surely scold you if you secretly take His side.
His greatness would scare you. Fear of Him would fall on you.
Your sayings are like ashes. Your defenses are like clay.
Be quiet and let me speak. Then let happen what will happen.
Why do I risk my life? Why do I hold my life in my hands?
Even if He kills me, I will still hope in Him. But I will argue my ways to His face.
This will save me. A bad man cannot come to Him.
Listen closely to my words. Let your ears hear what I say.
Look, I have made my case ready. I know I am right.
Who can argue with me? If someone could, I would be quiet and die.
God, give me only these two things. Then I will not hide from You:
Take Your hand far from me. Do not let Your fear scare me.
Then call me, and I will answer. Or let me speak, and You answer me.
How many wrong things and sins do I have? Show me my wrong and my sin.
Why do You hide Your face? Why do You treat me like an enemy?
Will You scare a leaf blown by wind? Will You chase dry straw?
You write bitter things against me. You make me pay for the sins of my youth.
You put my feet in chains. You watch all my ways. You mark the bottoms of my feet.
So people waste away like rotten cloth, like clothes eaten by moths.”
"A man born to a woman lives only a short time and has lots of trouble.
He grows like a flower and then fades away. He is like a shadow that quickly goes away.
Do You look at someone like that? Will You bring me to court with You?
"No one can make something clean from something dirty. Not even one person.
You decide how many days he will live. You know his months. You set his time, and he cannot go past it.
Please look away from him and leave him alone. Then he can have some peace in his day, like a worker at the end of his job.
"There is hope for a tree. If it is cut down, it can grow again. Its new shoots will not stop.
Even if its roots are old in the ground and its stump dies in the dirt,
it can grow again when water is near. It grows branches like a new plant.
"But a man dies and is laid low. He takes his last breath, and then where is he?
Water can leave a sea. A river can dry up and be gone.
So a man lies down and does not get up again. He will not wake up until the sky is gone. He will not rise from his sleep.
"I wish You would hide me in the grave. Keep me there until Your anger is gone. Set a time for me, and remember me.
If a man dies, will he live again? I will wait through my hard days until I am made new.
You would call, and I would answer You. You would want the work of Your hands.
Then You would count my steps. You would not watch over my sin.
You would seal up my wrong in a bag. You would cover my sin.
"But a mountain can fall and crumble. A rock can be moved from its place.
Water wears away stones. Floods wash away the dirt of the earth. In the same way, You destroy a person's hope.
You win against him forever, and he is gone. You change his face and send him away.
His sons may come to honor him, but he does not know it. They may be brought low, but he does not see them.
He feels only the pain in his own body. He mourns only for himself."
Then Eliphaz, the man from Teman, answered and said:
"Should a wise man answer with empty words and fill his belly with hot air?
Should he argue with words that help no one?
But you are pushing away the fear of God. You are stopping people from thinking about God.
Your sin teaches your mouth what to say. You choose the words of a sneaky person.
Your own mouth says you are wrong, not me. Your own lips speak against you.
"Were you the first man ever born? Were you born before the hills?
Have you heard God's secret plans? Do you think you are the only wise one?
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not?
We have old and gray-haired men here. They are older than your father.
Are God's comfort words too small for you? Are His gentle words not enough for you?
Why does your heart pull you away? Why do your eyes flash with anger?
You turn your spirit against God. You bring these words from your mouth.
"What person can be pure? Who born of a woman can be right with God?
Look, God does not even trust His holy ones. The heavens are not pure to Him.
So how much less a person who is awful and dirty? He does wrong as easily as drinking water!
