"I will show you. Listen to me. I will tell what I have seen.
Wise men told this. They did not hide it from their fathers.
The land was given to them alone. No stranger lived among them.
"Wicked people hurt all their days. The years meant for cruel people are full of pain.
Scary sounds fill his ears. Even when things go well, trouble comes to him.
He does not think he will get out of the dark. He is marked to die by the sword.
He walks around looking for bread and says, 'Where is it?' He knows a dark day is near.
Fear and pain scare him. They beat him down like a king ready for battle.
He raised his hand against God. He fights the Almighty.
He runs hard against Him with a strong shield.
He has let pride cover his face, and fat grow on his sides.
He lived in ruined towns, in houses no one should live in. They were ready to become piles of stones.
He will not stay rich. His money will not last. His things will not spread over the earth.
He will not get out of the dark. Fire will dry up his branches. God's breath will blow him away.
He should not trust in empty things. He fools himself. Empty things will be his pay.
It will be paid before his time. His branch will not stay green.
He will drop his unripe grapes like a vine. He will drop his flowers like an olive tree.
The group of people who do not care about God is empty. Fire burns the tents of those who take bribes.
They plan trouble and do wrong. They get ready to lie."
"I have heard many things like these. You are all terrible comforters.
"Will your long speeches never end? Why do you keep talking?
"I could talk like you if you were in my place. I could say many things against you and shake my head at you.
"But I would cheer you up with my words. My kind words would help you feel better.
"Even if I talk, my pain does not go away. If I stay quiet, it still does not leave.
"Now He has worn me out. You have ruined everyone around me.
"You have made me thin and weak. My weak body shows my trouble. It speaks against me.
"God's anger has torn me apart. He hates me. He grinds His teeth at me. My enemy stares hard at me.
"They open their mouths to speak against me. They hit my face and shame me. They all join together against me.
"God has put me in the hands of bad people. He has given me to bad people.
"I was safe and calm, but God broke me. He grabbed me by the neck and crushed me. He made me His target.
"His arrows surround me. He cuts me deep with no mercy. He spills my pain on the ground.
"He breaks me again and again. He attacks me like a strong soldier.
"I put rough cloth on my skin to show my sadness. I have lost my strength.
"My face is red from crying. Deep darkness covers my eyes.
"My hands have done no wrong. My prayer is pure.
"Earth, do not hide my blood. Do not let my cry be quiet.
"Even now, my Witness is in heaven. My Helper is up above.
"My friends make fun of me. My eyes pour out tears to God.
"I wish someone could speak to God for me, like a person speaks for a friend.
"In a few years, I will go away and not come back."
My spirit is broken. My days are cut short. The grave is ready for me.
People who make fun of me are all around me. My eyes have to watch their mean words.
Please, God, promise to help me. Who else will stand up for me?
You have kept their hearts from understanding, so You will not lift them up.
A person who turns in friends for money will see his children's eyes grow weak.
He has made me a laughingstock to everyone. I am someone people spit on.
My eyes are weak from sadness. My whole body is just a shadow.
Good people are shocked by this. Innocent people get angry at those who do wrong.
But good people will keep doing right. Those who are innocent will get stronger.
But all of you, come back. I will not find one wise person among you.
My days are over. My plans are broken. The things I hoped for in my heart are gone.
They make the night seem like day. "Light is near," they say, "even in the dark."
If I think the grave will be my home, if I make my bed in the dark,
if I say to the pit, "You are my father," and to the worm, "You are my mother and sister,"
then where is my hope? Who can see hope for me?
Will my hope go down with me to the grave? Will we sink into the dust together?
Then Bildad, a man from Shuh, spoke.
"How long will you keep talking? Think first, then we can talk.
Why do you treat us like animals? Why do you think we are not smart?
You are tearing yourself apart in anger. Should the whole world be left empty just for you? Should a big rock be moved from where it sits?
"The light of bad people goes out. The fire they make does not shine.
The light in his tent gets dark. The lamp above him goes out.
"His strong steps get shorter. His own bad plans make him fall.
His feet get caught in a net. He walks right into its ropes.
A trap grabs his heel. A snare holds him tight.
A rope is hidden in the ground for him. A trap waits on his path.
"Fears scare him all around. They chase him with every step.
He has no strength left. Trouble is waiting right beside him.
Trouble eats pieces of his skin. Death eats the rest of him.
He is pulled from his safe tent. He is led away to death.
"Fire stays in his tent. Burning sulfur is thrown over his home.
His roots dry up below. His branches die above.
He is forgotten on earth. He has no name in the land.
He is pushed from light into darkness. He is chased out of the world.
"He has no children or grandchildren among his people. No one is left in his home.
People in the west are shocked at what happened to him. People in the east shake with fear.
This is how bad people end up. This is the home of one who does not know God."
"How long will you make me sad? You hurt me with words.
You have blamed me again and again. You are not ashamed to attack me.
If I really did go wrong, that is my own trouble.
"If you make yourselves bigger than me and use my shame against me,
then know that God has been unfair to me. He has trapped me.
"I cry out, 'Someone hurt me!' but no one answers. I call for help, but there is no justice.
"He has blocked my path, so I cannot pass. He has covered my roads with darkness.
He has taken my honor away. He has taken the crown off my head.
He breaks me down on every side until I am gone. He pulls up my hope like a tree.
"His anger burns against me. He counts me as His enemy.
His soldiers come together. They build a ramp to attack me. They set up camp all around my tent.
"He has pushed my brothers away from me. My friends have become strangers to me.
My relatives have left. My close friends have forgotten me.
My guests and my female servants treat me like a stranger. They see me as someone from another land.
"I call my servant, but he does not answer. I beg him with my own mouth.
My breath is bad to my wife. I am disgusting to my own family.
"Even little boys make fun of me. When I get up, they talk against me.
All my close friends hate me. The people I loved have turned against me.
"I am only skin and bones. I have barely escaped.
Have pity on me, my friends. Have pity, because God has hurt me.
"Why do you chase me like God does? Can you never be satisfied with hurting me?
"I wish my words were written down. I wish they were written in a book.
I wish they were cut into rock with an iron pen and lead, so they would last forever.
"I know my Redeemer lives. In the end He will stand on the earth.
After my skin is destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
I myself will see Him with my own eyes. I, and not someone else. My heart aches inside me.
"If you say, 'We will hunt him down,' and, 'He is the cause of his trouble,'
you should fear the sword. Anger brings punishment with a sword, so you will know there is a judge."
Then Zophar, a man from Naamah, answered.
"So my worried thoughts make me answer. I feel upset inside.
I heard words that shame me. My mind makes me reply.
Do you not know this has been true since people were put on earth?
Bad people win for a short time. People who do not care about God are happy for only a moment.
"Even if his pride reaches the sky and his head touches the clouds,
he will be gone forever, like his own dirt. People who saw him will say, 'Where is he?'
He will fly away like a dream, and no one will find him. He will be chased away like a bad dream at night.
The eye that saw him will not see him again. His home will not see him again.
"His sons will pay back the poor. His hands will give back his money.
His bones were strong when he was young, but he will lie down in the dust.
"Even if evil tastes sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,
even if he holds it and will not let it go, and keeps it in his mouth,
his food will turn to poison in his stomach. It will be like snake poison inside him.
"He swallows riches, but he will throw them up. God will make him spit them out.
He will suck poison from snakes. A snake's fangs will kill him.
He will not enjoy rivers flowing with honey and cream.
He must give back what he gained without enjoying it. He will not enjoy the money from his work.
"For he crushed poor people and left them. He took houses he did not build.
Because he was never happy with what he had, he will not keep his treasure.
Nothing is left for him to eat. So his good things will not last.
When he has plenty, he will be in trouble. Hard times will come to him.
"When he has filled his stomach, God will show His anger. He will rain trouble on him while he eats.
If he runs from an iron weapon, a bronze arrow will hit him.
It will come out of his back. The shiny point will come out of his liver. Great fear will come over him.
Darkness is saved for his treasures. A fire no one fans will burn him and eat up what is left in his tent.
"The sky will show his sin. The earth will rise up against him.
The good things in his house will be carried away. They will be dragged away on the day of God's anger.
This is what God gives a bad person. This is the part God gives him."
Listen closely to my words. Let this be your comfort.
Bear with me, and I will speak. After I speak, mock me.
Am I arguing with a person? If so, why should I not be upset?
Look at me and be shocked. Put your hand over your mouth.
When I think about it, I am scared. Fear grabs my body.
Why do wicked people keep living? They grow old and get strong.
Their children are safe with them. Their grandchildren are right before their eyes.
Their homes are safe. They are not afraid. God does not punish them.
Their bulls breed well. Their cows do not lose their calves.
They send their little ones out like sheep. Their children dance.
They sing with tambourines and harps. They are happy when they hear the flute.
They live in comfort. Then they die in peace.
They say to God, “Go away from us. We do not want to know Your ways.
What is the Almighty, that we should serve Him? What do we gain if we pray to Him?”
Look, their good things are not in their own hands. I do not follow the plans of wicked people.
How often does the light of wicked people go out? Does trouble come on them? In His anger, does God give them pain?
They are like straw in the wind. They are like dust blown away by a storm.
God saves up their wrong for their children. He pays them back, so they will know.
They will see their own ruin. They will drink the anger of the Almighty.
What good is their house to them after they die, when their time is cut short?
Can anyone teach God? He judges even the great ones.
One person dies strong and well. He is safe and calm.
His body is full of good food. His bones are full of marrow.
Another person dies sad and bitter. He never enjoyed good things.
They both lie in the dust. Worms cover them.
I know what you are thinking. I know your plans against me.
You say, “Where is the house of the great man? Where is the tent of the wicked?”
Have you not asked people who travel? Do you not know what they say?
Wicked people are kept for the day of trouble. They are brought out on the day of anger.
Who will tell him his wrong to his face? Who will pay him back for what he did?
He is carried to the grave. Someone watches over his tomb.
He rests in the grave in the valley. Many people follow him. Countless go before him.
So how can you comfort me with empty words? Your answers are false.
Then Eliphaz from Teman answered Job.
“Can a person help God? A wise person helps only himself.
Does the Almighty care if you are good? Does He gain if you do right?
Does He correct you because you fear Him? Does He take you to court for that?”
“Your wrongs are big. Your sins never stop.
You took things from your brothers for no reason. You took clothes from people who had none.
You gave no water to tired people. You kept bread from hungry people.
The strong man took the land. The important man lived there.
You sent widows away with nothing. You hurt children who had no father.”
“So traps are all around you. Fear comes fast.
It is dark, so you cannot see. A flood of water covers you.”
“God is high in heaven. Look at the stars. They are very high.
But you say, ‘What does God know? Can He judge through the dark clouds?
Thick clouds hide Him. He cannot see. He walks on the sky.’”
“Will you keep the old road that bad men walked?
They were taken away before their time. Their foundation was washed away like a river.
They said to God, ‘Leave us alone! What can the Almighty do to us?’
Yet He filled their houses with good things. But I stay far from the plans of bad men.”
“Good people see it and are glad. Clean people laugh at them.
They say, ‘Our enemies are gone. Fire has eaten what was left.’”
“Make peace with God now. Then good things will come to you.
Take His teaching from His mouth. Keep His words in your heart.
If you come back to the Almighty, you will be built up again. Push wrong away from your tent.
Put gold in the dust. Put Ophir gold with the stones in the stream.
Then the Almighty will be your gold and your silver.
Then you will enjoy the Almighty. You will lift up your face to God.
You will pray to Him, and He will hear you. You will keep your promises.
You will decide something, and it will happen. Light will shine on your road.
When people are brought low, you will say, ‘There is a way up.’ God will save the humble person.
He will even save a guilty person. Yes, that person will be saved because your hands are clean.”
"Even today my complaint is bitter. My hand feels heavy with my groaning.
Oh, if I only knew where to find Him! If I could come to His place!
I would lay my case before Him. I would fill my mouth with my reasons.
I would know what words He would answer me. I would understand what He would say to me.
"Would He argue with me with His great power? No, He would listen to me.
There a good person could talk with Him. I would be saved forever from my Judge.
"Look, I go forward, but He is not there. I go back, but I cannot see Him.
He works on the left, but I do not find Him. He turns to the right, but I do not see Him.
"But He knows the way I take. When He has tested me, I will come out like gold.
My foot has followed His steps. I have kept His way and have not turned away.
I have not left the words He told me to keep. I have kept His words like treasure, more than my daily bread.
"But He never changes. Who can make Him change? He does what He wants.
He will finish what He has planned for me. He has many plans like these.
"So I am afraid of Him. When I think about Him, I am scared.
God has made my heart weak. The Almighty has scared me.
But the dark has not silenced me. The thick dark has not covered my face."
Why doesn't the Almighty set times for things? Why do people who know Him not see His days?
They move land markers. They graze stolen sheep.
They chase away the donkey of a child with no father. They take a widow's ox as a promise to pay.
They push poor people off the road. They make the poor hide. "
Poor people go out to work like wild donkeys in the desert. They look for food. The dry land gives food to their children.
They gather grass in the fields. They pick leftover grapes from bad people's vineyards.
They sleep with no clothes. They have nothing to keep them warm.
Mountain rains soak them. They hide by rocks because they have no shelter. "
They snatch babies from their mothers. They take a poor baby as a promise to pay.
They walk around with no clothes. They carry grain but still go hungry.
They press olives for oil. They press grapes, but they are thirsty.
People in the city groan. Hurt people cry out. But God does not blame anyone for it. "
Some people turn away from the light. They do not know its ways. They do not walk in its paths.
When the sun goes down, a killer gets up to kill poor people. At night he is like a thief.
A man who is not faithful to his wife watches for evening. He thinks, 'No one will see me.' He hides his face.
In the dark they break into houses. By day they stay inside. They never see the light.
To them, deep dark is like morning. They are friends with scary dark. "
They are like foam on water. Their part of the land is cursed. They do not go to the vineyards.
Just as dry heat melts snow water, the grave takes sinners.
Their mothers forget them. Worms eat them. No one remembers them. So wrong is snapped like a tree.
They hurt women who cannot have children. They are not kind to widows. "
But God drags away strong people by His power. When He stands up, no one feels safe.
He lets them feel safe, and they trust it. But His eyes watch their ways.
They are high for a short time, then they are gone. They are brought low and gathered like all others. They are cut off like heads of grain.
If this is not true, who can prove me wrong? Who can show my words are empty?"
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered. He said,
"God has power, and people fear Him. He makes peace in heaven.
No one can count all His armies. His light shines on everyone.
So how can a person be right with God? How can someone born from a woman be clean?
Even the moon is not bright enough for Him. The stars are not clean in His eyes.
How much less a person, who is only a worm!"
"How you helped the weak! You saved a person with no strength.
How you advised someone with no wisdom! You shared much good advice.
Who did you speak to? Whose breath came from you?
The dead shake under the waters, with all who live there.
The grave is open before Him. The place of ruin has no cover.
He stretches out the north over empty space. He hangs the earth on nothing.
He wraps water in His clouds. The clouds do not break under the water.
He covers the face of the full moon. He spreads His cloud over it.
He drew a circle on the waters, where light and dark meet.
The pillars of heaven shake. They are amazed at His warning.
By His power He calmed the sea. By His wisdom He broke the sea monster Rahab.
By His breath the sky became clear. His hand struck the fleeing snake.
These are only the edges of His ways. We hear only a faint whisper of Him. Who can understand His mighty thunder?"
God is alive, but He took away my rights. The Almighty made my heart sad.
While I still breathe, and God's breath is in my nose,
my lips will not say wrong things, and my tongue will not tell lies. "
I will never say you are right. I will never give up my good name.
I will hold on to my right ways. I will not let them go. My heart will not blame me as long as I live.
Let my enemy be like bad men. Let the one who fights me be like a wrongdoer. "
What hope does a man who does not care about God have when he is cut off, when God takes his life?
Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?
Will he be happy with the Almighty? Will he call on God all the time? "
I will teach you about God's power. I will not hide what the Almighty has planned.
You have all seen this. Why do you talk nonsense? "
This is what bad men get from God. This is what cruel men get from the Almighty:
If he has many sons, they will die by the sword. His children will not have enough food.
The ones left after him will be buried. Their widows will not cry. "
He may pile up silver like dust. He may save clothes like clay.
But good people will wear what he got ready. Innocent people will share his silver.
The house he builds is weak, like a moth's nest. It is like a small tent a watchman makes.
He goes to bed rich, but he will not stay that way. He opens his eyes, and he is gone. "
Fear comes on him like a flood. A storm carries him away at night.
The east wind picks him up and takes him away. It blows him from his place.
It hits him hard with no mercy. He runs from its power in fear.
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from where it is."
People can find silver in mines. They can find gold and clean it.
Iron comes from the dust. Copper is poured from stone.
People put an end to the dark. They search to the farthest place, where black rock and deep shadow are.
They break open a tunnel far from where people live. The place is forgotten by feet. People hang and swing there.
The ground gives food. Under it, fire changes the rock.
Its rocks hold sapphires. Its dust holds gold.
No bird of prey knows that path. No falcon has seen it.
Proud animals have not walked there. No lion has gone over it.
People put their hands on hard rock. They turn mountains over from the roots.
They cut tunnels through rock. Their eyes see every precious thing.
They hold back streams so water does not drip. They bring hidden things out into the light.
But where can wisdom be found? Where is the place to get good sense?
No one knows how much it is worth. It is not found where living people are.
The deep says, “It is not in me.” The sea says, “It is not with me.”
It cannot be bought with gold. No amount of silver can pay for it.
It cannot be valued with gold from Ophir, with costly onyx or sapphire.
Gold and glass cannot equal it. It cannot be traded for fine gold.
No one talks about coral or crystal. Wisdom costs more than pearls.
The topaz of Cush cannot equal it. It cannot be valued with pure gold.
So where does wisdom come from? Where is the place to get good sense?
It is hidden from all living eyes. It is kept from the birds of the sky.
Destruction and Death say, “We have only heard about it.”
God understands the way to it. He knows where it is.
He looks to the ends of the earth. He sees under the whole sky.
He made a weight for the wind. He measured the water.
He made a rule for the rain. He made a path for the thunderbolt.
Then He saw it and told about it. He set it up and studied it.
And He said to man, “Look, the fear of the Lord is wisdom. To turn away from evil is good sense.”
“I wish I could go back to the months before, like the days when God watched over me.
His lamp shone over my head, and by His light I walked through the dark.
I was like I was in my best days, when God was my close friend and blessed my home.
The Almighty was still with me, and my children were around me.
My path was like it was washed in butter, and rocks gave me streams of oil.
“When I went out to the city gate and sat down in the square,
young men saw me and hid, and old men stood up and stayed standing.
Leaders stopped talking and put their hand over their mouth.
Important people stayed quiet, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouth.
When ears heard me, they called me happy. When eyes saw me, they spoke well of me.
“I saved poor people who cried for help. I helped children with no father and no helper.
The dying person blessed me. I made the sad widow's heart sing.
I put on right living like clothes. Fair choices were my robe and turban.
I was eyes for blind people and feet for people who could not walk.
I was like a father to poor people. I looked into their problems.
I stopped bad men and took back what they stole.
“I thought I would die old, with my family, after many days.
My roots reached the water, and dew stayed on my branches all night.
People still honored me, and my bow was strong in my hand.
“People listened to me and waited. They were quiet for my advice.
After I spoke, they did not speak again. My words fell on them like rain.
They waited for me like rain. They opened their mouths wide for spring rain.
I laughed with them, and they could not believe it. They did not make my face sad.
I chose their way and sat as leader. I lived like a king among soldiers, like one who comforts sad people.”
But now young men laugh at me. They are younger than I am. I would not even let their fathers work with my sheep dogs.
Their strong hands were no help to me. Their strength was gone.
They are thin from hunger. They wander in dry, empty land. They look for food in ruined places.
They pick salty weeds among the bushes. They eat roots to stay alive.
People chase them away. They shout at them as if they were thieves.
They live in holes in the ground and in rocks. They cry out among the rocks.
They make loud noises among the bushes. They gather under thorn plants.
They are foolish people. They have no good name. They were chased out of the land. “
Now I am the song they sing. I am the joke they tell.
They hate me. They stay away from me. They even spit in my face.
He let them loose and hurt me. They act wild in front of me.
On my right side, the crowd rises up. They trip my feet. They bring trouble to me.
They block my path. They help my trouble. No one stops them.
They rush in through a big break. They roll around in the ruins.
Fear comes over me. My honor is blown away like the wind. My help is gone like a cloud. “
Now my life feels poured out inside me. Days of pain have taken hold of me.
Night cuts into my bones. My pain never rests.
My clothes are changed by His great power. They wrap around me like a collar.
He has thrown me into the mud. I am like dust and ashes.
I cry to You, but You do not answer me. I stand up, and You just look at me.
You have become cruel to me. You fight me with Your strong hand.
You lift me into the wind. You toss me around. You melt me in the storm.
I know You will bring me to death. That is the home for all who live. “
Yet doesn't He reach out His hand against a broken man, even when he cries for help in his trouble?
Did I not cry for people in hard times? Did I not feel sad for the poor?
I hoped for good, but evil came. I waited for light, but darkness came.
My stomach is upset and does not rest. Days of pain come to me.
I walk in black without the sun. I stand in the crowd and cry for help.
I am like a brother to wild dogs. I am a friend to ostriches.
My skin turns black and falls off. My bones burn with heat.
My harp is used for sad songs. My flute is for sounds of crying.”
I made a promise with my eyes. I would not look at a young woman in a wrong way.
What does God give from above? What does the Almighty give from high up?
Doesn't trouble come to bad people? Doesn't disaster come to people who do wrong?
Doesn't He see my ways? Doesn't He count all my steps? "
If I walked with lies, or my feet hurried to cheat,
then let God weigh me on fair scales. Let Him know I am not guilty.
If I left the right path, if my heart followed my eyes, or if I did wrong with my hands,
then let others eat what I planted. Let my crops be pulled up. "
If I let a woman pull my heart away, or if I waited by my neighbor's door,
then let my wife work for another man. Let other men sleep with her.
That would be a shameful sin. It would be a crime to punish.
It is like a fire that burns to ruin. It would destroy all I have. "
If I was not fair to my male or female servants when they had a problem with me,
what could I do when God comes? What could I say when He asks me?
Did not God make me and them before birth? Did not the same One form us both? "
If I kept the poor from what they needed, or let a widow's eyes grow tired,
if I ate my food alone and did not share with the orphan,
but from my youth I cared for them like a father. From birth I helped the widow.
If I saw someone dying without clothes, or a needy person with no covering,
and they did not thank me for warming them with wool from my sheep,
if I raised my hand against an orphan, knowing I had power with the judges,
then let my arm fall from my shoulder. Let it be broken at the joint.
For I was afraid of God's punishment. I could not do such things because of His greatness. "
If I trusted in gold, or said to pure gold, 'You are my safety,'
if I was glad I had great wealth, or because my hand found much money,
if I saw the sun shining, or the moon moving in beauty,
and my heart was secretly drawn to them, and I worshiped them,
then that would be a sin to punish, because I would have been untrue to God above. "
If I was glad when my enemy had trouble, or was happy when bad things happened to him,
I did not let my mouth sin by cursing him and asking for his death. "
If the people in my home did not say, 'Who has not had enough of Job's food?'
No stranger had to sleep outside. I opened my doors to travelers. "
If I hid my sins like other people do, and kept my wrong inside my heart,
because I was afraid of the crowd, and families made fun of me, so I stayed quiet and did not go out— "
Oh, if someone would hear me! Here is my mark. Let the Almighty answer me. Let the man who sues me write it down.
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder. I would wear it like a crown.
I would tell him every step I took. I would go to him like a leader. "
If my land cries out against me, and its rows weep together,
if I ate its crops without paying, or wore out its workers,
then let weeds grow instead of wheat, and thorns instead of barley." Job's words are done.
These three men stopped answering Job because Job thought he was right.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, became very angry. He was angry at Job because Job said he was right instead of God.
He was also angry at Job’s three friends. They had no answer, but they still blamed Job.
Elihu waited to speak to Job because the other men were older than him.
When Elihu saw that the three men had no answer, he became very angry. "
I am young, and you are old. So I was afraid to tell you what I know.
I thought older people should speak. I thought many years should teach wisdom.
But it is the spirit in people. The breath of the Almighty gives understanding.
Not all people are wise. Not all old people understand what is right.
So listen to me. I will tell you what I know. "
I waited for your words. I listened to your ideas until you were done talking.
I listened closely. None of you proved Job wrong. None of you answered his words.
Don't say, 'We found wisdom. God will push him down, not a person.'
Job has not spoken against me. So I will not answer him with your words.
They are shocked and have no more words. They stopped talking.
I waited because they stopped talking. They stood there and did not answer again. "
Now I will answer too. I will tell what I know.
I have so many words. The spirit inside me pushes me to speak.
I feel like I will burst with words. It is like new wine ready to spill.
I will speak so I can feel better. I will open my mouth and answer.
I will not favor anyone. I will not flatter any person.
I do not know how to flatter. If I did, my Maker would soon take me away."
But now, Job, listen to my words. Hear all my words.
Look, I open my mouth. My tongue speaks.
My words show my heart is right. My lips speak what I know.
God's Spirit made me. The breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me if you can. Put your words in order. Stand before me.
Look, I am like you to God. I was also made from clay.
Do not be afraid of me. I will not press hard on you.
I heard what you said. I heard your words.
You said, “I am clean. I have not sinned. I have no wrong in me.
He finds reasons to be against me. He counts me as His enemy.
He puts my feet in chains. He watches all my ways.”
But you are not right in this. I will answer you, because God is greater than man.
Why do you argue with God? You say, “He will not answer people's words.”
God speaks in one way, and even in two ways, but people do not notice.
In a dream, in a vision at night, when deep sleep falls on people, while they lie on their beds,
then He opens people's ears and scares them with warnings.
He does this to turn people from what they do and to hide pride from them.
He keeps their soul from the grave. He keeps them from dying by the sword.
A man may be corrected with pain in bed. His bones may hurt all the time.
He may hate bread. He may not want good food.
His body wastes away until no one can see it. His bones stick out.
His soul comes near the grave. His life comes near those who kill.
If there is an angel for him, one messenger out of a thousand, to tell the man what is right,
then God is kind to him and says, “Save him from going down to the grave. I have found a price.”
His body becomes fresh like a child's. He goes back to his young days.
Then the man prays to God. God accepts him. He sees God's face with joy. God gives back his right standing.
Then he sings before people and says, “I sinned. I did wrong. But it was not paid back to me.
God saved my soul from the grave. My life will see the light.”
Look, God does all these things two or three times with a man.
He does this to bring his soul back from the grave, so he can shine with the light of life.
Pay attention, Job. Listen to me. Be quiet, and I will speak.
If you have words, answer me. Speak, because I want to show you are right.
If not, listen to me. Be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.
"Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who know things.
The ear tests words, like the mouth tastes food.
Let us choose what is right. Let us know among us what is good.
"Job said, 'I am right. God took away my fair chance.
People call me a liar, but I have not sinned. I am hurt bad, but I did no wrong.'
What man is like Job? He takes in mean words like water.
He goes with bad men and walks with people who do wrong.
He said, 'It does not help a man to be good to God.'
"So listen to me, you men with good hearts. God would never do wrong. The Almighty would never do bad.
He pays a man for his work. He lets a man find what his road brings.
Truly, God will not do wrong. The Almighty will not twist what is right.
Who told Him how to run the earth? Who put the whole world in place?
If He set His heart on it, He would take back His spirit and breath.
All people would die together, and man would go back to dust.
"If you understand, hear this. Listen to my words.
Can someone who hates what is right rule? Would you say the good and mighty God is bad?
Is it right to call a king worthless, or leaders bad?
How much less to God. He does not favor princes. He does not treat rich people better than poor people. They are all made by His hands.
They can die in a moment. At night, people shake and pass away. Strong men are taken away without anyone's hand.
"His eyes are on a man's ways. He sees all his steps.
There is no dark place or deep shadow where bad men can hide.
God does not need to watch a man longer before bringing him to court.
He breaks strong men without asking questions. He puts other men in their place.
So He knows what they do. He turns night on them, and they are crushed.
He hits them like bad men where people can see.
This is because they turned away from Him and did not think about His ways.
So the cry of poor people comes to Him. He hears the cry of people who hurt.
"When He is quiet, who can blame Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? It is the same for a nation or a man.
This keeps bad men from ruling and trapping the people.
Has anyone said to God, 'I have paid for my wrong. I will not do wrong again;
teach me what I do not see. If I did wrong, I will not do it again'?
Should He pay you back your way, just because you do not like it? You choose, not I. So say what you know.
"Men who understand will say to me, and a wise man who hears me will say:
'Job speaks without knowing. His words show no sense.'
Job should be tested to the end, because he answers like bad men.
He adds sin to his sin. He mocks us, and says many words against God."
"Do you think this is fair? You say, 'I am more right than God.'
But you ask, 'What good is it for me? What do I gain if I do not sin?'
I will answer you, and your friends too.
Look up at the sky and see. Look at the clouds high above you.
"If you sin, does it hurt God? If you sin many times, what does it do to Him?
If you do right, what do you give Him? What does He take from your hand?
Your sin hurts people like you. Your good helps people like you.
"People cry out when they are pushed down. They call for help when strong people hurt them.
But no one says, 'Where is God, my Maker, who gives songs at night?'
He teaches us more than the animals. He makes us wiser than the birds.
"There they cry out, but He does not answer. This is because bad men are proud.
Surely God does not listen to empty cries. The Almighty does not pay attention to them.
How much less will He hear you when you say you cannot see Him! Your case is before Him, and you must wait for Him.
"Now, because He does not punish in anger, and He does not pay much mind to foolish talk,
Job opens his mouth for nothing. He says many words with no knowledge."
Elihu also kept speaking. He said: "
Wait a little. I will show you. I still have words to say for God.
I will bring my knowledge from far away. I will say my Maker is right.
My words are true. A person with true knowledge is with you. "
God is very strong. He does not reject people. He is strong in power and wisdom.
He does not let evil people live on. He gives fair help to poor people.
He always watches over good people. He puts them with kings on thrones. He lifts them up forever. "
If people are tied up in chains, caught by trouble,
He tells them what they did. He shows them their sins, because they were proud.
He helps them listen to correction. He tells them to stop doing wrong.
If they listen and serve Him, they live good days. Their years are happy.
But if they do not listen, they die by the sword. They die without understanding. "
People who pretend to be good store up anger. They do not ask for help when God ties them up.
They die while young. Their life ends among bad people.
He saves poor people through their trouble. He helps them listen when life is hard. "
He would lead you out of trouble to a wide, calm place. Your table would be full of good food.
But you have received the punishment meant for wicked people. Punishment and justice have caught you.
God is angry. Be careful, or He may take you away with one blow. No big payment can save you.
Will your cry for help save you from trouble? Will all your strength save you?
Do not wish for the night, when people are taken away from their homes.
Be careful. Do not turn to sin. You have chosen this instead of trouble. "
God is great in power. Who can teach like Him?
Who told Him what to do? Who can say He did wrong?
Remember to praise His work. People see it.
Everyone can see it. People look at it from far away.
God is great. We do not fully know Him. His years cannot be counted. "
He makes water drops small. Rain pours down from the mist.
The clouds pour it out. Rain falls hard on people.
Who can understand the clouds? Who can understand His thunder?
He spreads His light on it. He covers the bottom of the sea.
By these things He judges people. He gives plenty of food.
He covers His hands with lightning. He tells it where to strike.
His thunder shows His power. Even animals know a storm is coming."
"My heart pounds and jumps from its place when I think about this.
Listen closely to the roar of His voice and the rumble that comes from His mouth.
He sends His lightning under the whole sky and to the ends of the earth.
After that, a voice roars. He thunders with His great voice. He does not hold back when people hear it.
God thunders in wonderful ways with His voice. He does great things we cannot understand.
"He tells the snow, 'Fall on the earth.' He tells the rain, 'Pour down hard.'
He stops people from working, so everyone can know what He is doing.
Then wild animals go into their dens and stay in their caves.
The storm comes from its room, and the cold comes with the strong winds.
God's breath makes ice, and the wide waters freeze.
He fills the clouds with water, and He scatters His lightning through them.
The clouds turn around to do what He tells them, all over the earth.
He may send it to punish people, to help the land, or to show His love.
"Listen to this, Job. Stand up and think about God's wonders.
Do you know how God controls the clouds and makes His cloud shine with lightning?
Do you know how the clouds hang in the sky, the wonders of Him who knows everything?
Your clothes get hot when the land is still because of the south wind.
Can you, with Him, spread out the sky, strong like a bronze mirror?
"Teach us what we should say to Him. We cannot get our words ready because of the dark.
Should I tell Him that I want to speak? If a man speaks, will he be swallowed up?
Now people do not see the light. It is bright in the sky, but the wind blows by and clears the clouds.
"Out of the north comes gold, and God is clothed in wonderful greatness.
The Almighty—we cannot find Him. He is great in power. He does not twist justice, and He does not stop doing what is right.
So people fear Him. He does not look at those who think they are wise in their own hearts."
Then the LORD answered Job from the storm and said:
“Who is this who makes things dark with words that have no knowledge?
“Get ready like a man. I will ask you questions, and you will answer Me.
“Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell Me, if you understand.
“Who set its size, since you know? Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
“What holds up its bases? Or who laid its corner stone,
“when the morning stars sang together and all God's sons shouted for joy?
“Who shut up the sea behind doors when it burst out at birth,
“when I made clouds its clothes and thick darkness its blanket?
“When I set My rule for it and put bars and doors on it,
“and said, ‘You may come this far, but no farther. Here your proud waves must stop’?
“Have you ever told the morning what to do since your days began? Have you shown the dawn where to be,
“so it could grab the earth's edges and shake the wicked out of it?
“The earth turns like clay under a stamp, and its parts stand out like clothes.
“The light of the wicked is taken away, and their strong arm is broken.
“Have you gone to the springs of the sea? Have you walked in the deep parts of the ocean?
“Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
“Have you understood how wide the earth is? Tell Me, if you know all of it.
“Where is the road to where light lives? And where does darkness stay,
“so you can take it to its land and know the paths to its home?
“Surely you know, because you were born then, and your days are many!
“Have you gone into the storehouses of snow? Have you seen the storehouses of hail,
“which I keep for hard times, for the day of battle and war?
“Where is the road where light is split, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth?
“Who cut a channel for the heavy rain and a path for the thunder?
“to rain on land where no one lives, on the empty desert,
“to fill empty and ruined places and make the grass grow?
“Does rain have a father? Or who made the drops of dew?
“Who is the mother of ice? Who gave birth to the frost from the sky?
“Water becomes hard like stone, and the deep sea freezes over.
“Can you tie up the Pleiades? Can you untie Orion's belt?
“Can you bring out the stars in their time? Can you lead the Bear and her cubs?
“Do you know the rules of the sky? Can you set their power over the earth?
“Can you shout to the clouds so a flood of water covers you?
“Can you send out lightning so it goes and says to you, ‘Here we are’?
“Who put wisdom in people's hearts? Who gave understanding to their minds?
“Who can count the clouds with wisdom? Who can tip over the sky's water jars,
“when the dust becomes mud and the clods stick together?
“Can you hunt food for the lion? Can you feed the young lions,
“when they hide in their dens and wait in the bushes?
“Who feeds the raven when its babies cry to God and wander around hungry?”
"Do you know when mountain goats have their babies? Do you watch the deer have her fawn?
Do you count the months they carry? Do you know when they give birth?
They crouch down and have their young. They send their babies away.
Their young get strong. They grow up in the wild. They leave and do not come back."
"Who let the wild donkey go free? Who untied its ropes?
I gave it the dry land for its home. I gave it the salty flats for its place.
It laughs at the noise of the town. It does not hear the driver shout.
It looks for food in the hills. It follows every green plant."
"Will the wild ox work for you? Will it stay by your feeding trough?
Can you tie it with a rope to make it plow? Will it plow the fields for you?
Will you trust it because it is strong? Will you leave your hard work to it?
Will you trust it to bring your grain home and pile it up for you?"
"The ostrich flaps its wings with joy. But its wings are not like a stork's feathers.
It leaves its eggs on the ground. It warms them in the dust.
It forgets that a foot may crush them. A wild animal may step on them.
It is hard on its young, as if they were not its own. Its work is wasted. It is not afraid.
God did not give it wisdom. He did not give it understanding.
But when it runs with its wings spread, it laughs at the horse and rider."
"Do you give the horse its strength? Do you put a mane on its neck?
Do you make it jump like a grasshopper? Its proud snorting scares people.
It paws the ground in the valley. It is glad in its strength. It runs into battle.
It is not afraid. It does not turn back from the sword.
Arrows rattle against it. The spear and javelin flash.
It runs so fast it seems to eat the ground. It cannot stand still when it hears the trumpet.
When the trumpet sounds, it says, 'Ha!' From far away it smells war. It hears the thunder of leaders and shouting."
"Does the hawk fly because you are wise? Does it spread its wings to the south?
Does the eagle fly high because you tell it to? Does it build its nest up high?
It lives on the cliff. It stays on the rock.
From there it looks for food. Its eyes see far away.
Its young drink blood. Where dead bodies are, there it is."
Then the LORD answered Job. He said,
"Will a person who finds fault fight with the All-Powerful God? Let the one who argues with God answer Him."
"Look, I am not important. What can I say to You? I put my hand over my mouth.
I spoke once, but I have no answer. I spoke twice, but I will not say more."
Then the LORD answered Job from the storm. He said,
"Now get ready like a man. I will ask you questions, and you must answer Me.
Will you say I am not fair? Will you blame Me so you can be right?
Do you have power like God? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
Then dress yourself in greatness and beauty. Wear honor and glory.
Show your strong anger. Look at every proud person and bring him down.
Look at every proud person and humble him. Step on the wicked where they stand.
Bury them all in the dust. Lock them in the grave.
Then I will praise you too, because your right hand can save you.
"Look at Behemoth. I made him, and I made you. He eats grass like a cow.
See how strong his hips are. See the power in his belly muscles.
His tail is like a big tree. The muscles in his legs are tight and strong.
His bones are like bronze tubes. His legs are like iron bars.
He is one of God's best works. Only His Maker can fight him.
The hills give him food, and the wild animals play near him.
He lies under the big plants, hidden by reeds and in the swamp.
The big plants shade him. The trees by the stream grow around him.
Even if the river rushes, he is not afraid. He stays calm even if the Jordan River pushes against his mouth.
Can anyone catch him by looking at him? Can anyone put a hook in his nose?"
“Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook? Can you tie his tongue with a rope?
Can you put a rope through his nose? Can you hook his jaw?
Will he ask you to be kind? Will he speak soft words to you?
Will he make a deal with you to be your slave forever?
Can you make him a pet like a bird? Can you tie him up for your girls?
Will traders try to buy him? Will they split him up to sell?
Can you fill his skin with sharp spears? Can you stick fishing spears in his head?
If you touch him, you will remember the fight and not do it again!
Look, hoping to catch him is useless. Just seeing him scares people.
“No one is fierce enough to wake him. So who can stand against Me?
Who gave Me something first, so I must pay them back? Everything under the sky is Mine.
“I will not be quiet about his body parts, his strength, and his fine shape.
Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can come close with a bridle?
Who can open the doors of his face? His teeth are scary all around.
His back has rows of shields. They are shut tight together.
They are so close that no air can pass between them.
They stick to each other. They hold tight and cannot be pulled apart.
“When he sneezes, light flashes. His eyes are like the first light of morning.
Burning sticks leap from his mouth. Sparks of fire shoot out.
Smoke comes from his nose like a pot boiling over burning reeds.
His breath sets coals on fire. A flame pours from his mouth.
“Strength lives in his neck. Fear jumps up in front of him.
The folds of his flesh stick together. They are firm and will not move.
His heart is hard like a stone, even like a heavy grinding stone.
When he rises up, even strong men are afraid. They step back in fear.
“A sword that reaches him does no good. Neither does a spear, dart, or javelin.
He thinks iron is like straw. He thinks bronze is like rotten wood.
Arrows cannot make him flee. Stones from a sling are like dust to him.
A club is like straw to him. He laughs at the sound of a javelin.
His underside is like sharp pieces of broken pots. He leaves a trail in the mud like a heavy sled.
“He makes the deep water boil like a pot. He turns the sea into a boiling pot.
He leaves a glowing path behind him. The deep water looks white, like foam.
Nothing on earth is like him. He is a creature with no fear.
He looks down on proud people. He is king over all who are proud.”
Job answered the LORD and said,
"You know that You can do all things. No plan of Yours can be stopped.
Who is this who hides plans without knowing? So I spoke about things I did not understand. They were too wonderful for me. I did not know them.
Please listen, and I will speak. I will ask You, and You will teach me.
I had heard about You with my ears, but now my eye has seen You.
So I take back my words. I am sorry in dust and ashes."

After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My anger is hot against you and your two friends, because you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has.

Now take seven bulls and seven rams. Go to My servant Job and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you. I will accept him so that I do not punish you for your foolish talk. You did not speak of Me what is right, as My servant Job did."
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what the LORD told them. The LORD accepted Job.
After Job prayed for his friends, the LORD gave Job back twice as much as he had before.

All his brothers and sisters and old friends came. They ate with him in his house. They felt sorry for him and comforted him for all the trouble the LORD had brought on him. Each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
So the LORD blessed Job's later life more than his early life. He had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
He also had seven sons and three daughters.
He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.
No women in all the land were as beautiful as Job's daughters. Their father gave them a share of the family land along with their brothers.
After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
Then Job died. He was old and had lived a long life.
Happy is the man who does not go with bad people. He does not stand where sinners stand. He does not sit with people who make fun of others.
But he loves the the LORD's rules. He thinks about them day and night.
He is like a tree by a stream. It gives fruit at the right time. Its leaves do not dry up. Everything he does goes well.
Bad people are not like that. They are like dry bits of wheat that the wind blows away.
So bad people will not stand when God judges. Sinners will not stand with good people.
The LORD knows how good people live. But bad people will be lost forever.
Why do the nations get so mad? Why do people make empty plans?
The kings of the earth stand ready, and the rulers join together. They stand against the the LORD and against His Chosen King.
They say, "Let us break their chains and throw off their ropes."
The One who sits in heaven laughs. The Lord makes fun of them.
Then He speaks to them in anger and scares them with His great anger.
He says, "I have put My King on Zion, My holy mountain."
I will tell what God decided. The the LORD said to Me, "You are My Son. Today I have become Your Father.
Ask Me, and I will give You the nations to own. You will own the ends of the earth.
You will break them with an iron rod. You will smash them like a clay pot."
So be wise, kings. Be warned, judges of the earth.
Serve the the LORD with fear, and be glad while trembling.
Honor the Son, or He may get angry and you may die on the way. His anger can burn in a moment. Happy are all who trust in Him.
The LORD, how many enemies I have! Many people are rising up against me.
But you, the LORD, are a shield around me. You are my honor, and You lift me up.
I call to the LORD, and He answers me from His holy hill.
I lie down and sleep. I wake up again, because the LORD keeps me safe.
I will not be afraid of thousands of people all around me.
Rise up, the LORD! Save me, my God! You hit all my enemies on the cheek. You break the teeth of bad people.
The LORD saves people. Please bless Your people.
Answer me when I call, God who does what is right. You helped me when I was in trouble. Be kind to me and hear my prayer.
How long will you people turn my good name into shame? How long will you love empty things and look for lies? Selah
Know that the the LORD has chosen good people for Himself. The the LORD will hear me when I call to Him.
Be angry, but do not sin. On your bed, think in your heart and be still. Selah
Offer right sacrifices, and trust in the the LORD.
Many are asking, "Who can show us the good?" Shine the light of Your face on us, O the LORD.
You have filled my heart with more joy than when they have lots of food and drink.
In peace I will lie down and sleep, for You alone, O the LORD, keep me safe.
Listen to my words, the LORD. Understand my thoughts.
Listen to my cry, my King and my God. I pray to You.
In the morning, the LORD, You hear my voice. In the morning I bring my prayer to You and wait.
You are not a God who likes bad things. Evil cannot stay with You.
Proud people cannot stand before You. You hate everyone who does wrong.
You destroy people who tell lies. The LORD hates people who kill and cheat.
But I will come into Your house because of Your great love. I will bow toward Your holy temple with respect.
Lead me, the LORD, on the right path because of my enemies. Make Your way straight in front of me.
They do not speak the truth. Their hearts are full of evil. Their throats are like open graves. They use smooth words to trick people.
Punish them, God. Let them fall because of their own plans. Push them away because they have sinned so much. They have turned against You.
But let everyone who trusts in You be happy. Let them sing with joy forever. Keep them safe, because they love Your name. Let them be glad in You.
You bless those who do right, the LORD. You cover them with Your kindness like a shield.
For the music leader. Use stringed instruments. This is a song of David. The LORD, do not scold me when You are angry. Do not punish me when You are very angry.
Be kind to me, the LORD, because I am weak. Heal me, the LORD, because my bones hurt.
I am very upset. How long, the LORD? How long?
Come back, the LORD, and save me. Save me because You are kind.
No one remembers You when they die. Who can praise You from the grave?
I am tired from crying. All night I cry in bed, and my bed is wet with tears.
My eyes are weak from sadness. They are tired because of all my enemies.
Go away from me, all you who do wrong. The LORD has heard my crying.
The LORD has heard my cry for help. The LORD will listen to my prayer.
May all my enemies be ashamed and very afraid. May they turn and run away in shame.
The LORD my God, I run to You for safety. Save me and keep me safe from all who chase me.
If You do not, they may tear me apart like a lion, and no one can save me.
The LORD my God, if I did this wrong, if my hands are guilty,
if I hurt a friend for no reason or took things from someone who did nothing wrong,
then let my enemy chase me and catch me. Let him step on me and push me into the dust.
Get up, the LORD, in Your anger. Rise up against those who hate me. Wake up and help me, for You said You would judge.
Let people from all nations gather around You. Rule over them from heaven.
The LORD judges all people. Judge me, the LORD, by my right doing and by my honest heart.
Stop the bad things bad people do. Help good people stand strong. You test what is in our hearts.
God is my shield. He saves people whose hearts are good.
God is a fair judge. He is angry with bad people every day.
If a bad person does not change, God will sharpen His sword. He will get His bow ready.
He has made deadly weapons. He sets His arrows on fire.
Look, bad people make trouble. They carry sin and bring lies into the world.
They dig a hole, but they fall into it themselves.
The trouble they make comes back on them. The harm they do falls on their own heads.
I will thank the LORD because He is right. I will sing to the name of the LORD, the Most High.
The LORD, our Lord, how great is Your name in all the world! You put Your glory above the sky.
From the mouths of babies and little children, You made strong praise. This stops Your enemies and those who want revenge.
When I look at Your sky, the work of Your hands, I see the moon and stars You put there.
What is a person that You think about him? What is a human being that You care for him?
You made people a little lower than God. You crowned them with glory and honor.
You put people in charge of all You made. You put everything under their feet:
all sheep and cows, and the wild animals too;
birds in the sky, fish in the sea, and all that travels through the ocean.
The LORD, our Lord, how great is Your name in all the world!
I will thank the LORD with all my heart. I will tell of all Your wonderful works.
I will be glad and happy in You. I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High.
When my enemies turn and run, they trip and die before You.
For You did what was fair for me. You sat on Your throne and judge fairly.
You spoke sharply to the nations. You destroyed the wicked. You wiped out their name forever and ever.
The enemy is gone forever. Their cities lie in ruins. People no longer remember them.
But the LORD sits on His throne forever. He has set up His throne to judge.
He will judge the world fairly. He will rule the nations with what is right.
The LORD is a safe place for people who are hurt. He is a strong tower in times of trouble.
Those who know Your name trust in You. For You, the LORD, have not left the people who look for You.
Sing praise to the LORD, who lives in Zion. Tell the nations what He has done.
He remembers people who were killed. He does not forget their cries for help.
Be kind to me, the LORD. See how my enemies hurt me. Save me from death.
Then I can tell everyone in Zion how great You are. I will be glad because of Your help.
The nations fell into the hole they dug. Their feet got caught in the net they hid.
The LORD showed that He is fair. The wicked are caught in their own traps. Think about this.
Wicked people will go down to the grave. So will all nations that forget God.
But God will not forget poor people forever. The hope of hurt people will not die.
Rise up, the LORD. Do not let people win. Let the nations be judged in front of You.
Put fear in them, the LORD. Let the nations know they are only people. Think about this.
Why does the the LORD stand so far away? Why does He hide when trouble comes?
The wicked man is proud. He hunts poor people. He traps them with his plans.
He brags about what he wants. He praises greedy people. He says bad things about the the LORD.
He is too proud to look for God. God is not in any of his thoughts.
He always gets his way. Your laws are far from him. He laughs at all his enemies.
He says to himself, “I will never fall. I will never be in trouble.”
His mouth is full of curses, lies, and threats. Trouble and sin hide under his tongue.
He hides near towns. In secret he kills innocent people. He watches for helpless people.
He hides like a lion in the bushes. He waits to catch poor people. He pulls them into his trap.
The helpless are crushed and beaten down. They fall under his power.
He says to himself, “God forgot. He hides His face. He will never see.”
The LORD, please get up! Lift Your hand, God! Do not forget the poor.
Why does the wicked man say bad things about God? He says to himself, “God will never punish me.”
But You have seen the trouble and sadness. You will pay them back with Your hand. Helpless people trust in You. You help children without parents.
Break the power of wicked and evil people. Search for their bad deeds until You find none.
The LORD is King forever. The countries will disappear from His land.
The LORD, You have heard what poor people want. You will make their hearts strong. You will listen to them.
You will be fair to children without parents and to people who are hurt. Then people on earth will not scare them anymore.
I trust the LORD to keep me safe. Why do you say to me, "Run away to safety"?
Look, bad people bend their bows. They put arrows on the string. They shoot from hiding at good people.
If everything falls apart, what can a good person do?
The LORD is in His holy temple. His throne is in heaven. He sees everyone. He looks closely at people.
The LORD tests good people and bad people. He hates those who do wrong and love hurting others.
The LORD will rain fire and burning sulfur on bad people. A hot wind will be their share.
For the LORD is good. He loves good deeds. Good people will see Him.
Help, the LORD, because good people are gone. People who can be trusted are gone from us.
People lie to each other. They use nice words, but they do not mean them.
May the LORD stop all smooth talkers and every proud tongue.
They say, “Our words will make us strong. Our lips are ours. Who is our master?”
“Because poor people are treated badly and needy people cry out, now I will get up,” says the LORD. “I will keep safe the one who wants help.”
The LORD’s words are pure. They are like silver cleaned in a fire on the ground, made pure seven times.
You, the LORD, will keep them. You will guard us from these people forever.
Wicked people walk around everywhere when bad things are praised among people.
For the music leader. A song by David. The LORD, how long will You forget me? Will it be forever? How long will You look away from me?
How long must I worry alone? My heart is sad all day. How long will my enemy win over me?
Look at me and answer me, the LORD my God. Give me strength, or I will die.
Then my enemy will say, "I won!" The people who hurt me will be glad because I failed.
But I trust in Your kind love. My heart will be glad because You save me.
I will sing to the LORD, because He has been good to me.
The foolish person says in his heart, "There is no God." They have done wrong. They do evil things. No one does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven at people. He wants to see if any understand and seek God.
Everyone has turned away. Everyone has become evil. No one does good, not even one.
Will the people who do wrong never learn? They hurt my people without care. They do not call on the the LORD.
Then they will be very afraid, because God is with those who do right.
You ruin the plans of poor people, but the the LORD keeps them safe.
Oh, I wish someone would save Israel from Zion! When the the LORD brings His people back, Jacob will be happy, and Israel will be glad.
The LORD, who can stay in Your tent? Who can live on Your holy hill?
He does what is right. He lives the right way. He tells the truth from his heart.
He does not talk bad about people. He does not hurt his neighbor. He does not say mean things about his friends.
He does not respect bad people. He honors people who fear the LORD. He keeps his promise, even when it hurts.
He does not lend money to make extra money. He does not take money to hurt an innocent person. A person who does these things will never fall.
Keep me safe, God, because I trust in You.
I said to the LORD, "You are my Lord. Without You, nothing is good for me."
As for God's holy people in the land, they are the best ones. I like them very much.
People who run after other gods will have more and more trouble. I will not pour their blood offerings. I will not say their names.
The LORD is my share and my cup. You keep my place safe.
My land is in a good place. My home is nice to me.
I will praise the LORD, because He gives me advice. Even at night, my heart teaches me.
I keep the LORD in front of me always. Because He is beside me, I will not fall.
So my heart is glad, and I praise Him with my tongue. My body will live in peace.
For You will not leave me in the grave. You will not let Your Holy One rot.
You will show me the way to live. In Your presence, there is so much joy. At Your right hand, happy things last forever.
Please hear my honest prayer, the LORD. Listen to my cry. Please hear my prayer from lips that do not lie.
Let my good name come from You. Let Your eyes see what is fair.
You tested my heart. You came to me at night. You tried me and found no wrong. I promised not to sin with my mouth.
People do many things, but by Your words I stayed away from cruel people.
My steps stayed on Your paths. My feet did not slip.
I call on You, God, because You will answer me. Please listen to me and hear my words.
Show Your great love. You save those who trust in You. Keep them safe from those who fight them.
Keep me like the most precious part of Your eye. Hide me under the safe cover of Your wings.
The wicked hurt me. My enemies surround me.
They have hard hearts. Their mouths speak proud words.
They follow me and surround me now. Their eyes look down to throw me to the ground.
They are like a hungry lion. They are like a young lion hiding and waiting.
Rise up, the LORD. Face them and make them fall. Save me from the wicked with Your sword.

Use Your hand, the LORD, to save me from these people. They belong to this world, and this world is all they get. You fill their stomachs with good things. Their children have plenty, and they leave extra to their little ones.
But I will see Your face because I am right with You. When I wake up, I will be happy to be with You.

For the music leader. A song of David, who served the LORD. David sang these words to the LORD on the day the LORD saved him from all his enemies and from Saul. I love You, the LORD. You are my strength.
The LORD is my rock, my safe place, and the One who saves me. My God is my rock. I hide in Him. He is my shield and my strength. He saves me and keeps me safe.
I will call to the LORD. He is worth praising. Then He will save me from my enemies.
Death tied me up like ropes. Bad floods scared me.
The grave closed in on me. Death set traps for me.
When I was in trouble, I called to the LORD. I cried to my God for help. He heard my voice from His holy house. My cry reached His ears.
The earth shook and quaked. The bottoms of the mountains trembled. They shook because He was angry.
Smoke came from His nose. Fire came from His mouth and burned. Hot coals came from it.
He pushed the sky apart and came down. Dark clouds were under His feet.
He rode on a winged creature and flew. He flew on the wings of the wind.
He hid in the dark. Dark clouds covered Him.
Bright light shone before Him. His clouds passed by. There was hail and hot coals of fire.
The LORD thundered in the sky. The Most High spoke. There was hail and hot coals.
He shot His arrows and scattered His enemies. He sent lightning and confused them.
The sea pulled back. The bottom of the world showed. You, the LORD, spoke sharply. The wind from Your nose blew.
He reached down from high up and took me. He pulled me out of deep water.
He saved me from my strong enemy. My enemies were too strong for me.
They came after me when I was in trouble. But the LORD helped me.
He brought me to a safe, wide place. He saved me because He was happy with me.
The LORD paid me back for doing right. He rewarded me for keeping my hands clean.
I kept the LORD's ways. I did not turn away from my God to do wrong.
I kept all His rules in front of me. I did not ignore His laws.
I was honest with Him. I stayed away from sin.
So the LORD paid me back for doing right. He saw that my hands were clean.
You are loyal to loyal people. You are good to people who do right.
You are pure to pure people. You are clever with crooked people.
You save people who are hurting. You bring down people who are proud.
You, the LORD, light my lamp. My God makes my dark place bright.
With You I can run through an army. With my God I can jump over a wall.
God's way is perfect. the LORD's words are pure. He is a shield to all who hide in Him.
Who is God besides the LORD? Who is the Rock except our God?
God gives me strength. He makes my way safe.
He makes my feet like a deer's feet. He helps me stand on high places.
He teaches my hands to fight. My arms can bend a bow made of hard metal.
You gave me the shield of Your help. Your right hand holds me up. Your kindness lifts me up.
You made my path wide under me. My feet did not slip.
I chased my enemies and caught them. I did not stop until they were gone.
I hit them so they could not get up. They fell under my feet.
You gave me strength for the fight. You made my enemies fall under me.
You made my enemies run away. I destroyed my foes.
They cried for help, but no one saved them. They cried to the LORD, but He did not answer them.
I crushed them like dust in the wind. I threw them out like mud in the street.
You saved me from fighting with my own people. You made me the leader of nations. People I did not know serve me.
As soon as they hear me, they obey me. People from other lands obey me.
People from other lands give up. They come out of their forts shaking.
The LORD is alive! Praise my Rock! May the God who saves me be praised!
He is the God who pays back my enemies. He puts nations under me.
He saves me from my enemies. You lift me up above my foes. You save me from cruel men.
So I will thank You, the LORD, among the nations. I will sing to Your name.
He gives great help to His king. He shows love to His chosen one, to David and his children forever.
This song is for the music leader. David wrote it. The sky tells how great God is. The wide space above shows what His hands made.
Each day speaks to the next day. Each night shows what God knows.
There are no words. We cannot hear their voice.
But their message goes all over the earth. Their words reach the ends of the world. God put a tent for the sun in the sky.
The sun is like a groom leaving his room. It is like a strong man who is happy to run.
It rises at one end of the sky. It travels to the other end. Nothing can hide from its heat.
The law of the LORD is perfect. It gives new life to people. The the LORD's words can be trusted. They make a simple person wise.
The the LORD's rules are right. They make the heart happy. The the LORD's command is pure. It makes the eyes see clearly.
Respect for the LORD is pure. It lasts forever. The the LORD's decisions are true and right.
They are worth more than lots of gold. They are sweeter than honey from the honeycomb.
They warn Your servant. Keeping them brings a big reward.
Who can know his own mistakes? Wash me clean from hidden sins.
Keep Your servant from sins I do on purpose. Do not let them rule me. Then I will be blameless. I will be free from big sin.
Let the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be pleasing to You. O the LORD, You are my Rock and my Savior.
May the LORD answer you when you have trouble. May the God of Jacob keep you safe.
May He send you help from His holy place. May He hold you up from Zion.
May He remember all your gifts. May He be pleased with the gifts you burn. Selah.
May He give you what your heart wants. May He make all your plans work.
We will shout with joy when you win. We will raise our flags for our God. May the LORD give you all you ask for.
Now I know that the LORD saves His chosen king. He answers him from His holy heaven. He saves him with the power of His right hand.
Some trust in war carts. Some trust in horses. But we trust in the LORD our God.
They fall down and lose. But we stand up and stay strong.
The LORD, save the king! Answer us when we call!
The LORD, the king is happy because of Your strength. He is very glad because You save him.
You gave him what his heart wanted. You did not keep back the words he asked for.
You go to meet him with good gifts. You put a gold crown on his head.
He asked You for life, and You gave it to him. He will live forever.
His honor is great because You save him. You give him glory and power.
You bless him forever. You make him happy with the joy of being near You.
The king trusts in the LORD. Because the Most High loves him faithfully, he will not fall.
Your hand will find all Your enemies. Your right hand will find the people who hate You.
You will make them like a hot oven when You come. The LORD will destroy them in His anger, and fire will burn them up.
You will destroy their children from the earth. Their family will be gone from the people.
They plan evil against You and make bad plans, but they will not win.
You will make them run away. You will aim Your arrows at their faces.
The LORD, show how great You are with Your strength! We will sing and praise Your power.
My God, my God, why have You left me? You are far from saving me. My cries are loud.
My God, I call to You day and night, but You do not answer. I cannot be quiet.
But You are holy. You sit on the praises of Israel.
Our fathers trusted in You. They trusted, and You saved them.
They cried to You and were saved. They trusted in You and were not ashamed.
But I am like a worm, not a man. People make fun of me. Everyone looks down on me.
All who see me laugh at me. They shake their heads.
“He trusts in the LORD. Let the LORD save him. Let Him help him, since He cares for him.”
But You brought me into the world. You made me trust in You while I was still nursing.
From birth I was put in Your care. From the start You have been my God.
Do not stay far from me, because trouble is near and no one helps.
Many bulls surround me. Strong bulls from Bashan circle me.
They open their mouths at me like a roaring lion that tears its food.
I am poured out like water. All my bones are out of place. My heart is like wax. It melts inside me.
My strength is dry like a broken pot. My tongue sticks to my mouth. You bring me down to death.
Dogs surround me. A crowd of evil men circles me. They have pierced my hands and feet.
I can count all my bones. People look at me and stare.
They divide my clothes among them. They throw dice for my robe.
But You, the LORD, do not stay far. You are my strength. Hurry to help me.
Save my life from the sword. Save my only life from the dogs.
Save me from the lion's mouth. You have answered me from the horns of wild bulls.
I will tell Your name to my brothers. I will praise You in the middle of the crowd.
You who fear the LORD, praise Him. All you children of Jacob, honor Him. All you children of Israel, fear Him.
For He has not looked down on the suffering of the poor. He has not hidden His face from him. When he cried to Him, He heard.
My praise comes from You in the great crowd. I will keep my promises to You where those who fear You can see.
Poor people will eat and be full. Those who look for the LORD will praise Him. May your hearts live forever.
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD. All the families of the nations will bow down before You.
For the kingdom belongs to the LORD. He rules over the nations.
All the rich people of the earth will eat and bow down. All who go down to the dust will kneel before Him. No one can keep himself alive.
Future children will serve Him. They will belong to the Lord for generations to come.
They will come and tell about His goodness to people not yet born, because He has done it.
The LORD is my shepherd. I will not need anything.
He makes me lie down in green fields. He leads me by quiet water.
He gives me new strength. He leads me on the right path to show His goodness.
Even when I walk through the darkest valley, I will not be afraid, because You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.
You set a table for me where my enemies can see. You pour oil on my head. My cup is full and running over.
Goodness and love will follow me all my life. I will live in the LORD's house forever.
A song by David. The earth and everything in it belong to the the LORD. The world and all the people who live in it belong to Him.
He built the earth on the seas. He made it strong on the rivers.
Who can go up the the LORD's hill? Who can stand in His holy place?
A person with clean hands and a pure heart. He does not worship false gods. He does not lie when he makes a promise.
He will get a blessing from the the LORD. God, who saves him, will make him right.
These are the people who look for Him. They look for You, God of Jacob. Selah.
Lift your heads, you gates! Lift up, you old doors! The King of Glory will come in.
Who is this King of Glory? The LORD is strong and mighty. The LORD wins in battle.
Lift your heads, you gates! Lift them up, you old doors! The King of Glory will come in.
Who is this King of Glory? The LORD of armies. He is the King of Glory. Selah.
I give my whole heart to You, the LORD.
My God, I trust in You. Do not let me be embarrassed. Do not let my enemies win over me.
People who trust in You will not be embarrassed. But people who turn against You for no reason will be embarrassed.
the LORD, teach me Your ways. Show me Your paths.
Lead me in Your truth and teach me. You are the God who saves me. I trust in You all day long.
Remember Your kindness and faithful love, the LORD. They have been there since long ago.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my wrong ways. Remember me because of Your faithful love, the LORD, because You are good.
The LORD is good and right. So He teaches sinners the right way.
He leads people who are humble in what is right. He teaches them His way.
All the LORD's paths are faithful love and truth for those who keep His promise and His rules.
the LORD, because of who You are, forgive my sin, because it is great.
Who is the person who fears the LORD? The LORD will teach him the way he should choose.
He will live in peace, and his children will receive the land.
The LORD shares His secrets with those who fear Him. He shows them His promise.
My eyes are always on the LORD, because He will pull my feet out of the trap.
Turn to me and be kind to me, because I am alone and hurting.
