You will feel like someone sleeping on a stormy sea or lying on top of a ship's ropes.
"They hit me," you will say, "but I'm not hurt! They beat me, but I don't feel it! When will I wake up so I can find another drink?"
Do not be jealous of bad people. Do not want to be with them.
Their hearts think about hurting others. Their lips talk about trouble.
By wisdom a house is built. By understanding it is made strong.
By knowledge the rooms are filled with things that are special and nice.
A wise man is strong. A man who knows things grows stronger.
By wise plans you fight a war. You win when you have many helpers who give advice.
Wisdom is too hard for a fool to understand. He does not speak at the gate.
A person who plans to do bad will be called a troublemaker.
Foolish plans are sin. People do not like a person who makes fun of others.
If you are weak in trouble, your strength is small.
Save those who are being led to die. Hold back those who are stumbling toward being killed.
If you say, "We did not know," doesn't He know? He keeps your soul. He pays back each person for what he does.
Eat honey, my son, because it is good. Sweet honey tastes good in your mouth.
Learn wisdom for your soul. If you find it, you will have a future. Your hope will not end.
Do not set a trap, you wicked person, against the home of a good person. Do not ruin his resting place.
A good person may fall seven times and get up. But wicked people stumble into trouble.
Do not be glad when your enemy falls. Do not let your heart be happy when he stumbles.
The LORD may see it and be unhappy. He may turn His anger away from him.
Do not be upset because of people who do bad. Do not be jealous of wicked people.
A bad person has no future. The lamp of wicked people goes out.
My son, fear the LORD and the king. Do not join people who cause trouble.
Their trouble comes suddenly. Who knows what trouble will come to them?
These are also sayings for wise people: It is not good to be unfair in court.
Whoever says to a bad person, "You are good," will be cursed by people. Nations will hate him.
But those who correct bad people will be happy. A good blessing will come on them.
An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
Get your work ready outside. Get your field ready. Then build your house.
Do not be a false witness against your neighbor. Do not lie with your lips.
Do not say, "I will do to him what he did to me. I will pay back the man for what he did."
I walked past the field of a lazy man and the vineyard of a man with no sense.
Thorns had grown all over it. Weeds covered its face. Its stone wall was broken down.
I saw it and thought about it. I learned a lesson from what I saw.
A little sleep, a little rest, a little folding of the hands,
and being poor will come on you like a robber. You will be in need like a man with a weapon.
These are more wise sayings from Solomon. Men who worked for King Hezekiah of Judah copied them.
It is a great honor for God to keep a thing secret. It is a great honor for kings to find things out.
The sky is high, and the earth is deep. In the same way, a king's heart is hard to understand.
Take the junk out of silver. Then the metal worker can make something good.
Take bad people away from the king. Then his rule will be fair and strong.
Do not act big in front of the king. Do not stand where great people stand.
It is better to hear, "Come up here," than to be put down in front of a leader.
Do not rush into a fight. What will you do later if your neighbor shames you?
Talk out your problem with your friend. Do not share another person's secret.
Someone may hear it and shame you. Then your bad name will stay.
A word said at the right time is like gold apples in a silver dish.
A wise warning to a listening ear is like gold earrings or fine gold jewelry.
A faithful messenger is like cool snow on a hot harvest day. He brings joy to those who sent him.
A person who brags about gifts he does not give is like clouds and wind with no rain.
With patience, a ruler can be won over. Gentle words can win over a stubborn person.
If you find honey, eat just enough. If you eat too much, you will throw up.
Do not go to your friend's house too often. He may get tired of you and hate you.
A person who tells lies about a friend is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Trusting a person who turns on you in trouble is like a bad tooth or a sore foot.
Singing happy songs to a sad person does not help. It is like taking off a coat in the cold.
If your enemy is hungry, give him food. If he is thirsty, give him water.
In this way, you will make him feel ashamed. And the LORD will reward you.
The north wind brings rain. A gossiping tongue brings angry faces.
It is better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a wife who always argues.
Like cold water to a tired person is good news from far away.
A good person who gives in to a bad person is like a muddy spring or a dirty well.
It is not good to eat too much honey. It is not good to brag about yourself.
A person who cannot control himself is like a city with broken walls.
Honor does not fit a fool. It is as odd as snow in summer or rain at harvest time.
A curse with no reason will not come true. It is like a bird that flies by and does not land.
A whip is for a horse, and a bit is for a donkey. A rod is for the back of a fool.
Do not answer a fool in his foolish way, or you will be like him.
Answer a fool in his foolish way, or he will think he is wise.
Sending a message with a fool is like hurting your own feet and drinking trouble.
A wise saying in the mouth of a fool is like the legs of a lame person that hang weak and useless.
Giving honor to a fool is like putting a stone in a sling. It does not help and can only cause harm.
A wise saying in the mouth of a fool is like a thorn in the hand of a drunk person.
Hiring a fool or just anyone is like a person shooting arrows with no aim. It can hurt people.
A dog goes back to what it threw up. In the same way, a fool goes back to his foolish ways.
Do you see a person who thinks he is wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
A lazy person says, "There is a lion in the street! There is a lion in the town square!"
A door swings back and forth. A lazy person just turns in his bed.
A lazy person puts his hand in the dish, but he is too tired to bring it back to his mouth.
A lazy person thinks he is wiser than seven people who give good answers.
Grabbing a dog by the ears is dangerous. So is jumping into someone else's fight.
A crazy person who shoots fire and causes death is like
a person who tricks his neighbor and says, "I was only joking!"
Without wood, a fire goes out. Without a gossip, a fight stops.
Charcoal keeps coals hot, and wood keeps a fire burning. In the same way, a person who likes to argue keeps fights going.
The words of a gossip are like tasty food. They go deep inside a person.
Sweet words with an evil heart are like shiny silver painted on a clay pot.
A person who hates hides it with his words and keeps lies hidden inside.
When he speaks kindly, do not believe him, because seven terrible things are in his heart.
His hate may be covered by lies, but his evil will be shown to everyone.
A person who digs a hole may fall into it. A person who rolls a stone may have it roll back on him.
A lying tongue crushes people, and the liar hates them. Smooth words bring trouble.
Do not brag about tomorrow. You do not know what tomorrow will bring.
Let someone else praise you. Do not praise yourself.
A stone is heavy. Sand is heavy too. But a fool's anger is heavier than both.
Anger is mean. Rage is wild. But who can stand up to jealousy?
It is better for someone to correct you openly than to love you in secret.
A true friend may hurt you with honest words. An enemy may say too many nice things to you.
A full person does not want honey. A hungry person thinks even bitter food tastes sweet.
A person who leaves home is like a bird that leaves its nest.
Oil and perfume make the heart glad. Good advice from a friend is sweet too.
Do not leave your friend or your father's friend. Do not go to your brother's house when trouble comes. A close neighbor is better than a brother far away.
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad. Then I can answer those who make fun of me.
A wise person sees trouble and hides. A foolish person keeps going and gets hurt.
If someone promises to pay a stranger's debt, take his coat as a promise. If he does it for a woman he does not know, hold him to it.
If you shout a blessing to your neighbor early in the morning, it will seem like a curse.
A wife who always argues is like a leaky roof on a rainy day.
Trying to stop her is like trying to stop the wind or hold oil in your hand.
Just as iron makes iron sharp, one person can help another grow.
If you take care of a fig tree, you eat its fruit. If you serve your master well, you will be honored.
Water shows your face. In the same way, your heart shows who you are.
Death and ruin are never full. People's eyes are never full either.
Silver is tested by fire. Gold is tested by fire too. A person is tested by praise.
Even if you grind a fool like grain, his foolishness will not go away.
Know how your sheep are doing. Pay attention to your herds.
Money does not last forever. A crown does not last forever either.
When the grass is gone, new plants grow. The plants on the mountains are gathered.
Your lambs will give you clothes. Your goats will help you buy a field.
There will be enough goat milk for your food, your family's food, and your servant girls.
Bad people run away even when no one chases them. But good people are very brave.
When a country does wrong, it has many rulers. But a wise leader helps it stay strong longer.
A poor person who is mean to other poor people is like a hard rain that ruins the crops.
People who leave God's law praise bad people. But people who keep God's law stand up to them.
Bad people do not understand what is fair. But people who follow the the LORD understand it well.
It is better to be poor and honest than rich and crooked.
A son who keeps the law is smart. But a boy who hangs around with greedy eaters brings shame to his dad.
A person who gets rich by charging high interest will end up giving it to someone kind to poor people.
If a person will not listen to God's law, God hates even his prayer.
A person who leads good people into a bad path will be caught in his own trap. But honest people will get good things.
A rich person thinks he is wise. But a poor person with good sense knows he is not truly wise.
When good people win, there is great joy. When bad people take charge, people hide.
A person who hides his sins will not do well. But a person who says he is sorry and stops doing wrong will be forgiven.
Happy is the person who always shows respect for the the LORD. But a person with a hard heart falls into trouble.
A bad ruler over poor people is fierce and scary.
A leader with no good sense hurts many people. But a leader who hates cheating will live a long time.
A person who has killed someone will run away for life. Do not help him.
A person who lives an honest life will be safe. But a person who lives a crooked life will fall fast.
A person who works his land will have plenty of food. But a person who chases empty dreams will be very poor.
A person who keeps his word will be blessed a lot. But a person who rushes to get rich will not escape trouble.
It is not good to treat people unfairly. But some people will do wrong for a piece of bread.
A greedy person rushes after money and does not know that poverty is coming.
A person who corrects someone will be liked more later than a person who only says sweet things.
A person who steals from his mom or dad and says, "I did nothing wrong," is a friend to a person who destroys things.
A greedy person starts fights. But a person who trusts in the the LORD will be blessed.
A person who trusts his own heart is a fool. But a person who lives with wisdom will be saved.
A person who gives to poor people will not be in need. But a person who looks away will receive many curses.
When bad people take power, people hide. But when bad people die, good people will do well.
A man who is stubborn and will not take advice will suddenly be destroyed, and no one can help him.
When good people do well, everyone is happy. When bad people rule, people are sad and complain.
A man who loves wisdom makes his father glad. But a man who spends time with bad women wastes his money.
A fair king makes the land strong and steady. But a man who takes extra money from people tears it down.
A man who flatters his neighbor sets a trap for him.
A bad man gets caught in his own sin. But a good man can sing and be happy.
A good man thinks about what poor people need. A bad man does not understand.
People who make fun of others stir up a city. Wise people calm anger.
If a wise man goes to court with a fool, the fool gets mad and laughs, and there is no peace.
Men who want to hurt others hate an honest man. They try to kill good people.
A fool lets out all his anger. A wise man holds it back.
If a ruler listens to lies, all his helpers are bad.
Poor people and mean people have one thing in common: the LORD gives life to both.
A king who judges poor people fairly will have a throne that lasts forever.
Discipline and correction give wisdom. But a child who is left alone shames his mother.
When bad people grow strong, sin grows too. But good people will see them fall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest. He will make you happy.
Without God's guidance, people run wild. But people who keep His law are happy.
A servant cannot be corrected by words alone. Even if he understands, he will not answer.
Do you see a man who speaks too fast? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
A servant who is spoiled from youth will cause trouble later.
An angry man stirs up fights. A hot-tempered man does many wrong things.
A man's pride will bring him down. But a humble person will be honored.
A man who helps a thief puts his own life in danger. He hears the curse but does not tell.
Being afraid of people is a trap. But a person who trusts in the LORD is safe.
Many people want a leader to like them. But true justice for a person comes from the LORD.
Good people cannot stand a bad man. Bad people cannot stand a good man.
These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh. This is his message. The man says to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
I am not as smart as other people. I do not understand like a person.
I did not learn wisdom. I do not know the Holy One.
Who went up to heaven and came back down? Who held the wind in His hands? Who wrapped the water in a cloth? Who made the whole earth? What is His name? What is His Son's name? You know this is true.
Every word of God is pure. He is a shield for those who trust in Him.
Do not add to His words. If you do, He will correct you, and you will be shown to be a liar.
I ask You for two things. Please do not say no before I die.
Keep lies and false words far from me. Do not give me poverty or riches. Give me just enough food for each day.
If I have too much, I might forget You and say, "Who is the LORD?" If I am poor, I might steal and bring shame to God's name.
Do not tell lies about a servant to his master. If you do, he may curse you, and you will be guilty.
Some people curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
Some people think they are pure, but they are still dirty.
Some people look down on others with proud eyes.
Some people have teeth like swords and jaws like knives. They eat up poor and needy people.
The leech has two daughters. They say, "Give! Give!" Three things are never full. Four things never say, "Enough!"
They are the grave, a woman who cannot have a baby, dry ground that wants more water, and fire that never says, "Enough!"
An eye that makes fun of a father or hates to obey a mother will be picked out by ravens in the valley and eaten by young eagles.
Three things are too amazing for me. Four things I do not understand:
how an eagle flies in the sky, how a snake moves on a rock, how a ship sails on the sea, and how a man loves a young woman.
This is how a woman who cheats acts: She eats, wipes her mouth, and says, "I did nothing wrong."
The earth shakes under three things. It cannot stand four:
a servant who becomes king, a foolish person who has too much food,
a woman who was not loved but gets married, and a servant girl who takes her boss's place.
Four things on earth are small, but very wise.
Ants are not strong, but they save food for summer.
Small animals that live in rocks are not powerful, but they make safe homes there.
Grasshoppers have no king, but they march together.
A lizard can be caught by hand, but it lives in kings' palaces.
Three things walk with pride. Four things look proud when they walk:
a lion, the strongest animal, who does not back away from anything;
a rooster that walks proudly, a male goat, and a king with his army.
If you have been foolish and proud, or if you planned to do wrong, stop talking.
Just as shaking milk makes butter, and twisting a nose makes it bleed, stirring up anger causes fights.
These are the words of King Lemuel. His mother taught him this message.
"What, my son? What, child of my body? What, child I prayed for?
Do not give your strength to women. Do not give your ways to those who ruin kings.
"It is not right for kings, Lemuel, to drink wine. It is not right for leaders to want strong drink.
They may drink and forget the law. They may take away the rights of poor people.
"Give strong drink to someone who is dying. Give wine to someone who is very sad.
Let them drink and forget they are poor. Let them not remember their hard times.
"Speak up for people who cannot speak. Speak up for those who have no one to help.
Speak up and judge fairly. Stand up for poor and needy people."
Who can find a very good wife? She is worth more than jewels.
Her husband trusts her. He will have all he needs.
She does him good, not harm, all her life.
She looks for wool and flax. She works with willing hands.
She is like trading ships. She brings food from far away.
She gets up while it is still night. She gives food to her family and work to her servants.
She looks at a field and buys it. She plants a vineyard with what her hands earn.
She works with strength. Her arms are strong.
She knows her work is good. Her lamp does not go out at night.
She spins thread with her hands. She holds the spinning tool.
She opens her hand to poor people. She reaches out to needy people.
She is not afraid of snow for her family. All her family wear warm clothes.
She makes blankets for herself. Her clothes are fine linen and purple.
Her husband is known at the city gate. He sits with the leaders of the land.
She makes linen cloth and sells it. She gives belts to traders.
She wears strength and honor. She smiles at the future.
She speaks with wisdom. Kind words are on her tongue.
She watches over her home. She does not waste time being lazy.
Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband praises her:
"Many women have done well, but you are better than all of them."
Charm can fool people. Beauty fades. But a woman who honors the LORD should be praised.
Give her the reward of her work. Let her deeds praise her in the city.
These are the words of the Teacher. He was David's son. He was king in Jerusalem.
The Teacher says, "Everything is empty! Yes, everything is empty!"
What good does a person get from all his hard work under the sun?
One group of people comes, and another goes. But the earth stays forever.
The sun rises. The sun goes down. Then it hurries back to where it rises.
The wind blows south. Then it turns north. It goes around and around. Then it comes back again.
All rivers run to the sea, but the sea is never full. The water goes back to where rivers start. Then it flows again.
Everything is tiring. No one can say it all. The eye is never full from seeing. The ear is never full from hearing.
What happened before will happen again. What was done before will be done again. Nothing is new under the sun.
Someone may say, "Look! This is new!" But it was already here long ago, before we lived.
No one remembers people from long ago. People later on will not be remembered by those who come after them.
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I decided to use my mind to seek and search out wisdom about everything done in the world. God gave people a hard job. They must work at it.
I have seen everything done under the sun. It is all empty. It is like chasing the wind.
A bent thing cannot be made straight. A missing thing cannot be counted.
I said in my heart, "I have grown in wisdom more than anyone who ruled Jerusalem before me. My mind has learned much wisdom and knowledge."
I set my mind to know wisdom. I also wanted to know foolish and silly things. I saw that this too is like chasing the wind.
Much wisdom brings much trouble. More knowledge brings more sadness.
I said to myself, "Let me try being happy. Let me enjoy good things." But that was useless too.
I said, "Laughing is silly. What good is fun?"
I tried to cheer myself with wine. My mind still used wisdom. I tried foolish things. I wanted to see what good people can do on earth in their short lives.
I made my work bigger. I built houses for myself. I planted vineyards.
I made gardens and parks. I planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
I made pools of water to water a forest of growing trees.
I bought slaves, men and women. I had servants born in my house. I had more cows, sheep, and goats than anyone before me in Jerusalem.
I gathered silver and gold. I gathered treasures from kings and lands. I got singers, men and women. I got many wives, which men enjoy.
I became great. I had more than anyone in Jerusalem before me. My wisdom stayed with me.
I did not keep my eyes from anything they wanted. I did not keep my heart from any joy. My heart was glad from all my work. That was my share from all my work.
Then I looked at all the work my hands had done. I looked at the hard work I had done. But all of it was useless. There was no real gain on earth.
Then I turned to look at wisdom, madness, and foolishness. What can the next king do? Only what has already been done.
I saw that wisdom is better than foolishness, like light is better than dark.
The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in the dark. Yet I saw that the same thing happens to both.
I said to myself, "What happens to the fool will happen to me too. So why was I so wise?" I said to myself, "That is useless too."
No one remembers the wise man or the fool forever. In the days to come, all will be forgotten. The wise man dies just like the fool.
So I hated life. The work done on earth was bad to me. All was useless.
I hated all the work I did on earth. I must leave it to the person who comes after me.
Who knows if that person will be wise or foolish? Yet he will rule over all my work. I worked and used wisdom on earth. That is useless too.
So I gave up. My heart was sad about all the work I did on earth.
A person may work with wisdom, knowledge, and skill. But he must give his share to someone who did not work for it. That is useless. It is a great wrong.
What does a person get from all his work and worry on earth?
All his days are pain. His work is sad. Even at night his heart does not rest. That is useless too.
There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and find joy in his work. I saw that this too comes from God.
For who can eat or feel joy without Him?
God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the person who pleases Him. But to the sinner He gives the work of gathering and storing up, to give to the one who pleases God. That is useless.
There is a time for everything. There is a time for every thing people do on earth.
A time to be born, and a time to die. A time to plant, and a time to pull up what was planted.
A time to kill, and a time to heal. A time to tear down, and a time to build.
A time to cry, and a time to laugh. A time to grieve, and a time to dance.
A time to throw stones, and a time to gather stones. A time to hug, and a time to let go.
A time to look for things, and a time to lose them. A time to keep, and a time to throw away.
A time to tear, and a time to sew. A time to be quiet, and a time to speak.
A time to love, and a time to hate. A time for war, and a time for peace.
What good does a worker get from all his hard work?
I saw the hard work God gave people to do.
God made everything beautiful at the right time. He put the idea of forever in people's hearts. But people cannot fully understand what God does from start to finish.
I know there is nothing better for people than to be happy and do good while they live.
It is God's gift when a person can eat, drink, and enjoy good things from all his hard work.
I know that everything God does lasts forever. No one can add to it, and no one can take away from it. God does this so people will honor Him.
What is now has already happened. What will happen has already happened. God brings back what has passed.
I also saw something on earth. In the place where fairness should be, there was evil. In the place where right should be, there was evil.
I said to myself that God will judge good people and bad people. There is a time for everything, and for everything people do.
I said to myself about people that God is testing them. He wants them to see that they are like animals.
People and animals have the same end. One dies, and so does the other. They all breathe the same air. People are no better than animals. Everything is like a breath that quickly fades.
Everything goes to the same place. Everything came from dust, and everything goes back to dust.
Who knows if the spirit of people goes up, and the spirit of animals goes down into the earth?
So I saw that there is nothing better for a person than to be happy in his work. That is his share. Who can bring him to see what will happen after him?
Then I looked at all the wrongs people do in this world. I saw the tears of people who were hurt. No one helped them. The people who hurt them had power, but no one helped the hurt people.
I said the dead are better off than the living who are still alive.
But even better is someone who has never lived. That person never saw the bad things people do in this world.
I saw that people work hard and do good work because they are jealous of each other. This is also useless and pointless.
A fool does nothing and ruins himself.
A little peace is better than a lot of hard work that means nothing.
Then I looked again and saw another useless thing in this world.

A man works alone. He has no partner, no son, and no brother. He works all the time, but he is never happy with his money. He asks, "Who am I working for? Why am I not enjoying good things?" This is also useless and a heavy burden.
Two people are better than one, because they get more from their work.
If one falls, the other can help him up. But if a person is alone and falls, no one is there to help him up.
If two people sleep near each other, they keep warm. But one person alone cannot get warm.
If one person is attacked, two can stand together. And three people together are even stronger.
A poor young person who is wise is better than an old king who is foolish and will not listen to advice.
He came out of prison to become king, even though he was born poor in that land.
I saw all the people living in this world follow the young man who would take the king's place.
There is no end to the people who came before him. And the people who come after will not be happy with him either. This is also useless and pointless.
Watch your steps when you go to God's house. It is better to listen than to give a foolish offering. Fools do not know they do wrong.
Do not rush to speak. Do not let your heart be quick to say a word to God. God is in heaven, and you are on earth. So let your words be few.
Dreams come from having too much to do. A fool talks too much.
If you make a promise to God, do not wait to keep it. God is not pleased with fools. Keep your promise.
It is better not to promise than to promise and not keep it.
Do not let your mouth make you sin. Do not say to the temple worker, "I made a mistake." Why should God be angry at your words and ruin the work of your hands?
Dreams and empty words are many. Fear God.
If you see poor people treated badly, and fairness and good things taken away in a land, do not be surprised. One leader is watched by a higher leader, and there are even higher leaders above them.
The land gives food to everyone. Even the king eats from the fields.
People who love money are never satisfied with money. People who love having lots of things are never happy with what they get. This is also empty.
When you have more stuff, more people use it up. What good is it to the owner, except to look at it?
A worker sleeps well, whether he eats a little or a lot. But a rich person has so much that he cannot sleep.
I have seen a bad thing in this life: a person saves up money, and it hurts him.
That money is lost in a bad deal. Then he has a son, but nothing is left for him.
Everyone comes into the world with nothing. Everyone leaves the same way. They take nothing from their hard work.
This is also a bad thing: people come with nothing, and leave with nothing. What good is working so hard for nothing?
All his life he eats in the dark. He has much trouble, sickness, and anger.

I have seen what is good and right: It is good for a person to eat, drink, and enjoy the good things from all his hard work in this life. God gives him a certain number of days to live. That is his share.
God also gives some people wealth and things. He lets them eat from it, take their share, and be happy in their work. This is a gift from God.
They do not think much about their life, because God keeps them busy with joy in their heart.
I saw something bad in this world. It is a heavy load for people.
God gives a man money, things, and respect. He has all he wants. But God does not let him enjoy them. Someone else enjoys them instead. This is empty and very sad.
A man may have a hundred children and live many years. But if he is not happy with good things and does not get a good burial, I say a baby who dies before birth is better off than he.
That baby comes into the world with no life and goes away in darkness. His name is hidden in darkness.
He never saw the sun or knew anything. But he has more peace than the man who lived long.
Even if a man lives two thousand years but does not enjoy his good things, all people still go to the same place.
A man works to eat, but he is never full.
What good is a wise man more than a foolish man? What does a poor man gain by knowing how to act among living people?
It is better to enjoy what the eyes see than to chase what the heart wants. This is also empty and useless.
What is has already been named. What a person is has been known. No one can fight the One who is stronger.
Many words make things more empty. What good does that do for a person?
Who knows what is good for a person in life, in the few days that pass like a shadow? Who can tell him what will happen after him in this world?
A good name is better than perfume.

The day a person dies is better than the day a person is born. It is better to go to a house where people are sad than to go to a party. Death comes to every person. The living should think about that.
Being sad is better than laughing, because a sad face can make the heart better.
Wise people think about sad things. Foolish people think about fun.
It is better to listen to a wise person correct you than to listen to fools sing.
A fool's laugh is like thorns crackling under a pot. It means nothing.
Being treated badly can make a wise person act like a fool. A bribe can ruin the heart.
The end of a thing is better than the start. Being patient is better than being proud.
Do not be quick to get angry. Anger stays in the heart of a fool.
Do not say, "Why were the old days better than now?" That is not a wise question.
Wisdom is as good as money you get from your family. It is even better for people who are alive.
Wisdom keeps you safe, like money does. But knowing things is better, because wisdom helps you live.
Look at what God does. No one can fix what He bends.
On a good day, be happy. On a bad day, think about it. God made both days. People cannot know what will happen next.
I have seen strange things in my life. A good person can die even while doing right. A bad person can live a long time while doing wrong.
Do not try to be too good. Do not try to be too wise. Why would you ruin yourself?
Do not do too much wrong. Do not be a fool. Why would you die too soon?
Hold on to both. Do not let go of either one. People who fear God stay away from both extremes.
Wisdom makes a wise person stronger than ten leaders in a city.
No one on earth always does good and never sins.
Do not listen to every word people say. You might hear your worker curse you.
You know in your heart that you have cursed other people many times.
I tested all this with wisdom. I said, 'I will be wise.' But it was too hard for me.
What is real is far away and very deep. Who can find it?
I turned my mind to learn and search for wisdom and how things fit together. I wanted to know why being wicked is foolish and why being foolish is crazy.
I found something more bitter than death. It is a woman whose heart is like traps and nets. Her hands are like chains. A man who pleases God will escape her. A sinner will get caught by her.
The Teacher says, "Look, I found this. I put one thing with another to find an answer.
I looked for it with all my heart, but I did not find it. I found one good man among a thousand. But I did not find one good woman among them all.
Look, I found only this: God made people good, but they have looked for many tricks."
Who is like a wise person? Who knows what things mean? Wisdom makes a person's face shine. It also softens a hard face.
Obey the king's command. I say this because you made a promise to God.
Do not hurry to leave the king. Do not join a bad plan. He does what he wants.
A king's word has power. No one can ask him, "What are you doing?"
Whoever obeys his command will not get hurt. A wise heart knows the right time and way.
There is a right time and way for every thing. But people have much trouble.
No one knows what will happen next. Who can tell someone what is coming?
No one can hold back the wind. No one can stop the day they die. No one can leave a war early. Doing wrong will not save the people who do it.
I saw all this. I thought about everything done on earth. Sometimes one person rules another and hurts them.
I also saw bad people buried. They used to come and go from the holy place. People forgot them in the city where they did this. This too is empty.
When a bad act is not punished fast, people's hearts fill with plans to do wrong.
A bad person may do many wrong things and live a long time. But I know it will go better for people who fear God and respect Him.
Bad people do not fear God, so things will not go well for them. Their days will not last long like a shadow.
There is something empty that happens on earth. Good people get what bad people deserve. Bad people get what good people deserve. I say this too is empty.
So I praise joy. There is nothing better for a person on earth than to eat, drink, and be glad. Joy will stay with them in their work all the days of life that God gives them on earth.
I decided to learn wisdom and to see the work done on earth. Some people cannot sleep day or night.
Then I saw all that God has done. No one can understand what happens on earth. People work hard to find it, but they cannot. Even if a wise person says they know, they cannot really understand.
I thought about all these things. I saw that good people and wise people, and the things they do, are in God's hands. No one knows if love or hate will come to them.

Everyone has the same end. It does not matter if a person is good or bad, clean or unclean, or gives offerings or not. The person who does right and the person who sins end the same way. The person who makes a promise and the person who fears making one end the same way.
This is a bad thing in all that happens on earth. Everyone has the same end. Also, people's hearts are full of evil and wild thoughts while they live. Then they die.
Anyone who is alive still has hope. It is better to be a poor person who is alive than a great person who is dead.
Living people know they will die. Dead people know nothing. They have no more reward. People forget them.
Their love, their hate, and their jealousy are gone. They will never again share in anything done on earth.
So go and eat your bread with joy. Drink your wine with a happy heart, for God is already pleased with your work.
Always wear your bright clothes, and always have oil on your head, to show joy.
Enjoy life with the wife you love. Enjoy all the days of your short life, for God gave you this life on earth. This is your share in life and in the work you do on earth.
Do whatever your hand finds to do. Do it with all your strength. There is no work or planning or knowing or wisdom in the grave, where you are going.

I saw another thing on earth. The fastest runner does not always win the race. The strongest fighter does not always win the battle. Wise people do not always get bread. Smart people do not always get money. People who know a lot do not always get good things. Time and chance happen to all of them.
No one knows when his time will come. People are like fish caught in a net or birds caught in a trap. Trouble comes on them suddenly.
I also saw this wisdom on earth. It seemed great to me.
There was a small city with few people in it. A great king came against it. He surrounded it and built big towers to attack it.
A poor wise man lived in the city. He saved the city with his wisdom. But no one remembered that poor man.
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But people looked down on the poor man's wisdom, and no one listened to his words.
The quiet words of wise people are better heard than the shouts of a foolish ruler.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war. But one sinner can destroy much good.
Dead flies can make perfume smell bad. A little foolishness can count more than wisdom and honor.
A wise person tends to do right. A foolish person tends to do wrong.
Even when a foolish person walks along the road, his heart has no sense. He says to everyone, “I am a fool!”
If a ruler gets angry with you, do not leave your place. Being calm can make big wrongs better.
I have seen something bad under the sun. It is a mistake that comes from a ruler.
Foolishness is put in high places, while rich people sit in low places.
I have seen slaves riding horses, while princes walk on the ground like slaves.
Anyone who digs a hole may fall into it. Anyone who breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
A person who cuts stones may get hurt by them. A person who cuts wood may be in danger from them.
If an ax is dull and not sharp, more strength is needed. But skill brings success.
If a snake bites before it is charmed, the snake charmer gets no reward.
A wise person’s words are kind. A fool’s words can ruin him.
His words start with foolishness and end with wicked madness.
A fool also says many words. No one knows what will happen. Who can tell him what will come after?
A fool’s hard work makes him tired, because he does not know the way to the city.
How sad for you, land, if your king is a child and your leaders eat a big meal in the morning.
How good for you, land, if your king comes from a good family and your leaders eat at the right time—for strength, not to get drunk!
Because of laziness, the roof caves in. Because of lazy hands, the house leaks.
People get food ready for fun. Wine makes life happy. Money can solve everything.
Do not curse the king, even in your mind. Do not curse a rich person in your bedroom. A bird may carry your words. A flying creature may tell what you said.
Share your food with others. After many days, you will find it again.
Give part to seven people, and even to eight. You do not know what trouble will come to the land.
If clouds get full, they pour rain on the earth. If a tree falls to the south or north, it stays where it fell.
If you wait for the wind, you will not plant. If you watch the clouds, you will not harvest.
You do not know how the wind moves. You do not know how bones grow before a baby is born. In the same way, you do not know the work of God, who makes everything.
Plant your seeds in the morning. Do not stop working in the evening. You do not know which will do well—this one or that one—or if both will be good.
Light is sweet. It is good to see the sun.
If a man lives many years, let him be happy in all of them. But let him remember the dark days. They will be many. Everything that comes is like a puff of smoke.
Young man, be happy in your youth. Let your heart cheer you in your young days. Walk in the way your heart wants and in what your eyes see. But know that God will judge you for all these things.
Take sorrow out of your heart. Put bad things away from your body. Youth and young days are like a puff of smoke.
Remember your Creator while you are young. Do it before bad days come. Do it before years come when you will say, “I do not enjoy them.”
Do it before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars grow dark. Do it before clouds come back after rain.
When you are old, your hands may shake. Your strong legs may bend. You may stop chewing well, because there are few teeth. Your eyes may see dimly.
Your lips may close. You may not chew loudly. You may wake when a bird sings. Your voice may grow weak.
You may be afraid of high places. You may be scared on the road. Your hair may turn white. You may move slowly. Your desire may fade. Then you go to your forever home. People mourn in the streets.
Do this before your life ends. It is like a silver cord snapping. It is like a gold bowl breaking. It is like a jar breaking at a spring. It is like a wheel breaking at a well.
The dust goes back to the earth. The spirit goes back to God, who gave it.
The Teacher says, “Everything is like a breath. It all passes away.”
The Teacher was wise. He also taught people. He thought about things. He studied them. He put many wise sayings in order.
The Teacher tried to find helpful words. He wrote true and right words.
Wise words are like sharp sticks. They push you to do right. Collected sayings are like strong nails. One Shepherd gives them.
My son, be careful about more than this. People make many books. There is no end to them. Too much study makes the body tired.
Here is the end of it all. We have heard everything. Fear God. Keep His rules. This is what people should do.
God will bring every act into court. He will judge even secret things. He will judge good and bad.
"Kiss me with your lips. Your love is better than wine.
Your oils smell sweet. Your name is like perfume poured out. So young women love you.
Pull me along with you, and let's run. The king brought me into his rooms. We will be glad and happy in you. We will praise your love more than wine. It is right that they love you.
I am dark and beautiful, young women of Jerusalem. I am like Kedar's tents and Solomon's curtains.
Do not stare at me because I am dark. The sun has burned me. My mother's sons were angry at me. They made me guard the grape fields, but I did not guard my own.
Tell me, my love, where you feed your flock. Where do you let them rest at noon? Why should I be like someone hiding her face near your friends' sheep?"
"If you do not know, most beautiful of women, follow the sheep's tracks. Feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
My love, you are like Pharaoh's horse among chariots.
Your cheeks are pretty with earrings. Your neck is pretty with bead necklaces.
We will make gold earrings for you with silver beads."
"While the king rests on his bed, my perfume gives its sweet smell.
My love is like a little bag of sweet perfume resting on my chest.
My love is like a bunch of flowers from the gardens of En Gedi."
"Look, you are beautiful, my love. Look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves."
"Look, you are beautiful, my beloved. You are so pleasant. Our bed is fresh and green.
The beams of our house are cedar. Our roof is made of pine."
I am a flower from Sharon. I am a lily in the valleys.
"Like a lily among thorns, so is my dear among the young women."
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my love among the young men. I wanted to sit in his shade. His fruit tasted sweet to me.
He brought me to the wine house. His flag over me was love."
"Hold me up with raisin cakes. Make me comfortable with apples. I am weak with love.
His left hand is under my head. His right arm holds me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise by the gazelles and the wild deer. Do not wake up love until it is ready."
"I hear my love's voice! Look, he is coming. He jumps over the mountains. He skips over the hills.
My love is like a gazelle or a young deer. Look, he stands behind our wall. He looks through the windows. He peeks through the openings."
"Get up, my dear. Come with me, my beautiful one.
Winter is gone. The rain has passed.
Flowers are seen in the land. It is time to sing. The dove's voice is heard in our land.
The fig tree has green figs. The grapevines give a sweet smell. Get up, my dear. Come with me, my beautiful one.
"My dove, in the rock's cracks, in the secret place of the cliff, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice. Your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely."
"Catch the little foxes for us. They ruin the grape fields. Our grape fields are in bloom.
My love is mine, and I am his. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
Until the day starts and the shadows run away, come back to me, my love. Be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of Bether."
On my bed at night, I looked for the one I love. I looked for him, but I did not find him.
I will get up now and walk around the city. I will look in the streets and squares. I will look for the one I love. I looked for him, but I did not find him.
The watchmen who walk around the city found me. "Have you seen the one I love?"
I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and did not let him go. I brought him to my mother's house, to the room where I was born.
"Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise by the deer and does of the field: do not wake love until it is ready."
"Who is this coming up from the desert like smoke? She smells like myrrh and frankincense, and like all the spices a seller has."
Look, it is Solomon's carriage. Sixty strong men stand around it. They are the strong men of Israel.
They all hold swords. They know how to fight. Each man has his sword on his thigh because they are afraid at night.
King Solomon made a carriage for himself from the wood of Lebanon.
He made its posts silver. He made its base gold. He made its seat purple. Its inside was made with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
"Daughters of Zion, go out and see King Solomon. He wears the crown his mother put on him on his wedding day, on the day his heart was glad."
"You are beautiful, my darling. Yes, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep that just got a haircut and a bath. They all match in pairs, and none is missing.
Your lips are like a red thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks are like a piece of pomegranate behind your veil.
"Your neck is like David's tower, built in rows of stone. A thousand shields hang there, shields of brave soldiers.
Your breasts are like two young deer, twins of a gazelle, eating among lilies.
"I will stay until day breaks and the shadows run away. Then I will go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.
You are beautiful in every way, my darling. There is no flaw in you.
"Come away with me from Lebanon, my bride. Come away from Lebanon. Look down from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions' dens and the leopards' mountains.
You have won my heart, my sister, my bride. You won my heart with one look from your eyes, with one bead from your necklace.
"How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is better than wine, and the smell of your oils is better than any spice.
Your lips, my bride, drip honey. Honey and milk are under your tongue. Your clothes smell like Lebanon.
"You are like a locked garden, my sister, my bride. You are like a locked spring, a sealed fountain.
Your garden grows pomegranates and all kinds of good fruit, with henna and nard.
There is nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all kinds of incense trees, myrrh and aloes, and all the best spices.
You are a garden fountain, a well of fresh water, streams flowing from Lebanon."
"Wake up, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow on my garden so its spices spread out. Let my love come into his garden and eat its best fruit."
"I came into my garden, my sister, my bride. I picked my myrrh with my spice. I ate my honeycomb with my honey. I drank my wine with my milk. Eat, friends. Drink and be happy, loved ones."
"I am asleep, but my heart is awake. I hear my loved one knocking:" "Open the door for me, my sister, my dear one, my dove, my perfect one. My head is wet with dew. My hair is wet with night rain."
"I took off my robe. How can I put it on again? I washed my feet. How can I get them dirty?
My loved one put his hand through the hole in the door. My heart beat fast for him.
I got up to open the door for my loved one. My hands dripped with myrrh. My fingers dripped with myrrh on the lock.
I opened the door for my loved one, but he had gone. My heart sank when he spoke. I looked for him, but I could not find him. I called him, but he did not answer.
The guards found me while they walked around the city. They hit me and hurt me. They took my veil from me. These were the guards on the walls."
"Girls of Jerusalem, I beg you: If you find my loved one, tell him I am weak with love."
"What makes your loved one better than others, most beautiful woman? Why do you ask us to promise?"
"My loved one is bright and red. He stands out among ten thousand.
His head is pure gold. His hair is wavy and black like a raven.
His eyes are like doves by streams of water. They are washed in milk and set in their sockets.
His cheeks are like beds of spice, like towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies that drip with myrrh.
His arms are like gold rods set with jewels. His body is like smooth ivory decorated with blue stones.
His legs are like marble pillars on gold bases. He looks like Lebanon, like its tall cedar trees.
His mouth is very sweet. He is all lovely. This is my loved one. This is my friend, girls of Jerusalem."
"Where did your loved one go, most beautiful of women? Which way did he turn? We want to look for him with you."
"My loved one went down to his garden, to the spice beds. He feeds in the gardens and picks lilies."
"I belong to my loved one, and my loved one belongs to me. He feeds among the lilies."
"You are beautiful, my darling, like the city of Tirzah. You are lovely like Jerusalem. You are amazing like an army with flags."
"Turn your eyes away from me. They are too much for me. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down from Gilead."
"Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the wash. Each one has a twin, and none is missing."
"The sides of your face are like a piece of pomegranate behind your veil."
"There are sixty queens and eighty other wives, and young women too many to count."

"But my dove, my perfect one, is the only one. She is the only daughter of her mother. She is the favorite of the one who gave birth to her. The young women saw her and called her blessed. The queens and other wives praised her."
"Who is this looking down like the morning light? She is beautiful like the moon. She is bright like the sun. She is amazing like an army with flags."
"I went down to the nut grove to see the flowers in the valley. I wanted to see if the vines had buds or if the pomegranates were flowering."
"Before I knew it, my heart put me with the royal chariots of my people."
"Come back, come back, dear Shulammite. Come back, come back, so we can look at you. Why would you look at the Shulammite like the dance of two armies?"
How pretty are your feet in sandals, daughter of a prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, made by a master's hands.
Your belly button is like a round cup. It never runs out of mixed wine. Your belly is like a pile of wheat, ringed with lilies.
Your breasts are like two young deer, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are pools of water in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, looking toward Damascus.
Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel. The hair of your head is like purple cloth. A king is caught in your hair.
How pretty and sweet you are, my love, with all your delights!
Your height is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters.
I said, 'I will climb the palm tree and hold its fruit.' May your breasts be like grape clusters, and may the smell of your nose be like apples.
Your mouth is like the best wine. It flows smoothly to my love and makes sleeping lips talk.
I belong to my love, and he longs for me.
Come, my love, let's go to the country. Let's stay the night in the villages.
Let's go early to the vineyards. We will see if the vines have budded, if the flowers have opened, and if the pomegranates are blooming. There I will give you my love.
The mandrakes give off their smell. At our door are all kinds of good things, new and old, that I saved for you, my love.
"If only you were like a brother to me, one who drank milk from my mother! Then if I found you outside, I would kiss you, and no one would look down on me.
I would lead you and bring you to my mother's house. She taught me there. I would give you spiced wine to drink, and sweet juice from my fruit.
His left arm holds my head, and his right arm hugs me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I ask you to promise: do not wake up love until it is ready."
"Who is this coming up from the desert, leaning on the one she loves?" "Under the apple tree I woke you up. There your mother became pregnant with you. There she gave birth to you."
"Put me like a seal on your heart, like a seal on your arm. Love is as strong as death. Jealousy is as hard as the grave. It burns like a big fire, like a strong flame.
Many waters cannot put out love. Rivers cannot wash it away. If a man gave all the money in his house for love, people would look down on him."
"We have a little sister, and her breasts are not grown yet. What should we do for our sister when someone asks to marry her?
If she is a wall, we will build silver towers on her. If she is a door, we will cover her with cedar boards."
"I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So I have become in his eyes like one who brings peace."
"Solomon had a grape field in Baal Hamon. He let farmers use it. Each one had to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
But my grape field is mine to give. The thousand pieces of silver are for you, Solomon, and two hundred are for the men who care for the fruit."
"You who live in the gardens, with friends listening for your voice, let me hear it."
"Come quickly, my love, and be like a deer or a young deer on the mountains of spices."
This is the vision Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem. It happened in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, heavens! Listen, earth! The LORD has spoken: "I raised children and brought them up, but they turned against Me.
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey knows its master's food bowl, but Israel does not know. My people do not understand."

Oh, what a sinful nation! You are a people heavy with sin. You come from people who do wrong. You are children who ruin things. You left the LORD. You looked down on the Holy One of Israel. You turned your backs on Him.
Why do you want more beatings? Will you keep turning away? Your whole head is sick. Your whole heart is weak.
From the bottom of your foot to the top of your head, nothing is healthy. You have cuts, bruises, and fresh wounds. No one has cleaned them, bandaged them, or softened them with oil.
Your land is empty. Your cities are burned. Strangers eat your food right in front of you. Your land is ruined, like a land turned upside down by strangers.
The city of Zion is left like a little hut in a vineyard, like a small shelter in a field, like a city surrounded by enemies.
If the LORD of Armies had not left us a few survivors, we would be like Sodom. We would be like Gomorrah.
Hear the LORD's word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to our God's teaching, you people of Gomorrah!
The LORD says, "What are all your sacrifices to Me? I have had enough of your burnt rams and the fat of your fat cows. I do not want the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats.
When you come to stand before Me, who asked you to trample My courtyards?
"Stop bringing worthless gifts. Your incense makes Me sick. I cannot stand your new moon meetings, your Sabbath meetings, and your special meetings. They are full of sin.
I hate your new moons and your special days. They are a heavy load to Me. I am tired of carrying them.
When you raise your hands to pray, I will look away. Even if you pray many times, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood.
"Wash yourselves and make yourselves clean. Take your bad deeds away from My eyes. Stop doing wrong.
Learn to do good. Look for what is fair. Help people who are hurt. Stand up for children with no parents. Speak for women whose husbands have died.
The LORD says, "Come now, let us talk this out. Even if your sins are bright red, they will become white like snow. Even if they are deep red, they will become like clean wool.
If you are willing and listen, you will eat the good food of the land.
But if you refuse and turn against Me, you will be killed by the sword." The LORD has spoken.
How did the faithful city become like a woman who sells herself? It was full of fair choices. Right living stayed there. But now it is full of murderers.
Your silver has become junk. Your wine is mixed with water.
Your leaders do not obey. They are friends of thieves. Everyone loves bribes and chases gifts. They do not stand up for children with no parents. They do not listen to a woman whose husband died.
So the Lord, the LORD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says, "Ah! I will get relief from My enemies. I will pay back those who hate Me.
I will turn My hand against you. I will clean away your junk metal. I will remove all your tin.
I will bring back your judges like before. I will bring back your helpers like at the start. After that, you will be called the City of Fairness, the City That Can Be Trusted."
Zion will be saved by fair choices. The people who come back to her will be saved by doing right.
But people who turn against God and people who sin will be broken together. People who leave the LORD will be destroyed.
You will be ashamed of the special oak trees you wanted. You will be embarrassed by the gardens you chose.
You will be like an oak tree whose leaves dry up, and like a garden with no water.
Strong people will be like dry grass, and their work will be like a spark. Both will burn together, and no one will put out the fire.
This is the message Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days to come, the mountain where the the LORD's house stands will be the most important mountain. It will stand higher than all the hills. People from all countries will come to it.

Many people will come and say, "Let's go up to the mountain of the the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways, so we can walk in His paths." For teaching will go out from Zion, and the word of the the LORD from Jerusalem.

Then He will judge between the countries. He will settle fights for many people. They will turn their swords into farm tools and their spears into garden knives. Countries will not fight each other anymore. They will not learn how to fight wars anymore.
Come, family of Jacob. Let's walk in the light of the the LORD.
For You have left Your people, the family of Jacob. They are full of ways from the east. They follow fortune-tellers like the Philistines. They make deals with people from other lands.
Their land is full of silver and gold. There is no end to their treasure. Their land is full of horses. There is no end to their war carts.
Their land is full of false gods. They bow down to things they made with their own hands.
So people are brought down low. Do not forgive them.
Go into the rocks. Hide in the dust. Get away from the fear of the the LORD and from His great glory.
The proud look on people's faces will be brought down. The proud ways of people will be made low. On that day, the the LORD alone will be lifted high.
The Day of the the LORD of Heaven's Armies will come against all proud and lifted-up people. Everything that is raised high will be brought low.
It will come against the tall cedar trees of Lebanon and against the oak trees of Bashan.
It will come against all the high mountains and all the raised hills.
It will come against every high tower and every strong wall.
It will come against every ship from Tarshish and every beautiful boat.
So the pride of people will be brought down. The proud ways of people will be made low. On that day, the the LORD alone will be lifted high.
The false gods will disappear completely.
People will run into caves in the rocks and holes in the ground. They will run away from the fear of the the LORD and from His great glory, when He stands up to shake the earth.
On that day, people will throw away their silver and gold idols. They made them to worship them. They will throw them to the moles and bats.
They will run into caves in the rocks and cracks in the cliffs. They will run away from the fear of the the LORD and from His great glory, when He stands up to shake the earth.
Stop trusting people. They only have a breath in their noses. They are worth nothing.
Look! The Lord, the LORD of hosts, is taking away help from Jerusalem and Judah. He is taking away all the food and water they need.
He is taking away strong men, soldiers, judges, prophets, people who tell the future, and old leaders.
He is taking away captains of fifty, important men, advisors, smart builders, and people who know secret charms.
I will make boys their leaders. Little children will rule over them.
People will be hard on each other. One person will fight with another. Young people will be rude to old people. People no one respects will boss around people who are respected.
A man will grab his brother in his father's house and say, "You have a coat. Be our leader. Take care of this ruined place."
But that day he will say, "I will not fix things. I have no food and no clothes at home. Do not make me the leader of the people."
Jerusalem has stumbled, and Judah has fallen. They speak and act against the LORD. They go against His glory.
The look on their faces shows they are guilty. They brag about their sin like the people of Sodom did. They do not hide it. How sad for them! They have brought trouble on themselves.
Tell good people that it will go well for them. They will enjoy the good they have done.
How sad for bad people! Things will go badly for them. They will be paid back for what they did.
My people are ruled by children. Women lead them. My people, your leaders lead you the wrong way. They have ruined your path.
The LORD stands to argue His case. He stands to judge the nations.
The LORD will come to judge the old leaders and rulers of His people. He will say, "You have ruined the vineyard. The things you took from poor people are in your houses."
"Why do you crush My people? Why do you hurt poor people?" says the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
The LORD said, "Because the women of Zion are proud. They walk with their necks held high. They flirt with their eyes. They take small steps as they walk. They make noise with their feet.
So the Lord will put sores on the heads of Zion's women. The LORD will show their private parts."
On that day the Lord will take away their fancy ankle chains, headbands, and moon-shaped necklaces.
He will take away their dangling earrings, bracelets, and veils.
He will take away their pretty hats, arm bands, belts, perfume boxes, and charms.
He will take away their rings and nose rings.
He will take away their party dresses, capes, coats, and purses.
He will take away their mirrors, fine linen clothes, head wraps, and shawls.
Instead of perfume, there will be a bad smell. Instead of a belt, a rope. Instead of nice hair, baldness. Instead of a fine dress, a rough cloth dress. Instead of beauty, a burn mark.
Your men will fall by the sword. Your strong men will die in battle.
Her gates will cry out and be sad. She will be empty and sit on the ground.
On that day, seven women will hold on to one man. They will say, "We will eat our own bread. We will wear our own clothes. Just let your name be on us. Take away our shame."
In that day, the LORD's Branch will be beautiful and great. The fruit of the land will be the joy and honor of Israel's people who are left.
Everyone left in Zion and Jerusalem will be called holy. This is for everyone whose name is written down for life in Jerusalem.
The Lord will wash away the dirt of Zion's daughters. He will clean the blood from Jerusalem. He will do this with fairness and fire.
Then the LORD will make a cloud and smoke by day over every home on Mount Zion and over their groups. At night, there will be a shining fire. Over all the glory, there will be a cover.
It will be a shade from the hot sun by day. It will be a safe place and a hiding place from storm and rain.
I will sing for my dear friend a song about his grape garden. My dear friend had a grape garden on a very good hill.
He dug it up and took out the stones. He planted the best grape plants. He built a watchtower in it. He cut out a wine press in it. He hoped for good grapes, but it made bad grapes.
"Now, you people who live in Jerusalem and in Judah, please decide between Me and My grape garden.
What more could I have done for My grape garden? Why did I hope for good grapes, but it made bad grapes?
Now I will tell you what I will do to My grape garden. I will take away its fence. It will be burned. I will break down its wall. It will be walked on.
I will make it a waste place. It will not be trimmed or dug. Thorns and weeds will grow. I will tell the clouds not to rain on it."

The grape garden of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel. The men of Judah are the plant He loved. He looked for right and fair ways, but saw people getting hurt. He looked for people doing right, but heard cries for help.
How sad for people who join house to house and field to field until no place is left. Then you will live alone in the land.
The LORD of Hosts has said in my ears, "Surely many houses will be empty. Great and good houses will have no one living in them.
Ten acres of grape garden will make only one small jar of wine. A big basket of seed will make only a little grain."
How sad for people who get up early to drink strong drink. They stay up late at night, and wine makes them wild.
Their parties have harps, lyres, drums, and flutes. They have wine too. But they do not look at the work of the LORD. They do not see what His hands have made.
So My people will be taken away because they do not know Me. Their great men will be hungry. Their crowds will be thirsty.
The grave has made its mouth big. It opens wide with no end. Their glory, their crowds, their noise, and their happy people will go down into it.
People will be brought low. Proud men will be brought down. The eyes of proud people will be brought down.
But the LORD of Hosts will be lifted up by right and fair ways. The Holy God will show He is holy by doing right.
Then lambs will eat grass like in a field. Strangers will eat the broken places of rich men.
How sad for people who drag sin along with lies. They pull wrong like heavy cart ropes.
They say, "Let Him hurry and do His work fast so we can see it. Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come near and happen, so we can know it."
How sad for people who call bad good and good bad. They make dark into light and light into dark. They make bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter.
How sad for people who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.
How sad for people who are strong at drinking wine and brave at mixing strong drink.
They make the bad man look right for money. They take right away from good people.

So fire will burn them like dry grass and straw. Their roots will rot. Their flowers will blow away like dust. This is because they said no to the law of the LORD of Hosts. They made fun of the word of the Holy One of Israel.

So the LORD was very angry with His people. He raised His hand and hit them. The mountains shook. Their dead bodies were like trash in the streets. But even then, His anger did not stop. His hand was still raised.
The LORD will lift up a flag for far-away nations. He will whistle for them from the ends of the earth. Look, they come fast.
None of them is tired. None of them falls. None sleeps or rests. Their belts are tight. Their shoe straps do not break.
Their arrows are sharp. Their bows are ready. Their horses' feet are like hard rock. Their wheels are like a windstorm.
They roar like lions. They growl like young lions. They grab their catch and carry it off. No one saves it.
In that day they will roar over them like the sea. Anyone who looks at the land sees dark and trouble. The sky is dark with clouds.
In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord. He was sitting on a high throne. His robe filled the temple.
Seraphs stood above Him. Each had six wings. With two wings they covered their faces. With two they covered their feet. With two they flew.
They called to each other and said, "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of His glory."
The doorways shook when they spoke. The temple filled with smoke.
I said, "Oh no! I am ruined! I am a man who says bad things. I live with people who say bad things. I have seen the King, the LORD of Armies!"
One of the seraphs flew to me. He had a hot coal in his hand. He took it with tongs from the altar.
He touched my mouth with it. He said, "See! This has touched your lips. Your sin is taken away. Your wrong is forgiven."
I heard the voice of the Lord. He said, "Who should I send? Who will go for Us?" I said, "Here I am. Send me!"
He said, "Go and tell these people, 'You will hear, but you will not understand. You will see, but you will not know.'"

"Make their hearts hard. Make their ears dull. Make their eyes blind. Then they will not see with their eyes. They will not hear with their ears. They will not understand with their hearts. They will not turn back to Me. I will not heal them."
I said, "Lord, how long?" He said, "Until cities are empty. No one lives in them. Houses are empty. No people are in them. The land is empty and destroyed."
The LORD will send people far away. The land will be very empty.
But one tenth will be left. Even that will be burned again. But like a tree stump, God's holy people will stay.
In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram went to fight Jerusalem. Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel joined him, but they could not take the city.
David's family heard, "Aram and Ephraim have joined together." The king and his people were scared. Their hearts shook like trees in a strong wind.
The LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out with your son Shear-jashub. Meet King Ahaz at the end of the upper pool, by the road to the washer's field.

Say to him, 'Be careful. Stay calm. Do not be afraid. Do not let your heart get weak because of these two rulers. They are like two sticks that are almost burned out. They are angry, but they will not last. They are Rezin of Aram and Remaliah's son.'"
They have made an evil plan against you. They say,
"Let us attack Judah. Let us scare the people. Let us break in and put Tabeel's son on the throne."
But this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: "It will not happen. It will not come true."
Damascus is the capital of Aram, and Rezin rules Damascus. In 65 years, Ephraim will be broken. It will no longer be a people.
Samaria is the capital of Ephraim, and Remaliah's son rules Samaria. If you do not believe this, you will not last.
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again.
He said, "Ask the LORD your God for a sign. You can ask for something deep in the ground or high in the sky."
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask. I will not test the LORD."
Isaiah said, "Listen, family of David. Is it not enough to tire out people? Do you also want to tire out my God?
So the Lord Himself will give you a sign. Look! A young woman is going to have a baby. She will have a son. She will call His name Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey. He will know how to say no to bad and yes to good.
Before the boy knows how to say no to bad and yes to good, the land of the two kings you fear will be left empty."
The LORD will bring hard times to you, your people, and your family. Hard times like these have not come since Israel left Judah. The LORD will bring the king of Assyria.
On that day, the LORD will whistle for flies from the rivers of Egypt and for bees from Assyria.
They will all come and rest in the valleys, in the cracks of rocks, in the thorn bushes, and in the pastures.
On that day, the Lord will use a razor from across the River. He will shave the head, the leg hair, and the beard.
On that day, a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep.
Because there will be so much milk, he will eat curds. Everyone left in the land will eat curds and honey.
On that day, every place where a thousand grapevines grew, worth a thousand silver coins, will be full of thorns and briers.
People will go there with bows and arrows, because the whole land will be thorns and briers.
No one will go to the hills that people used to hoe. They will be afraid of the thorns and briers. But oxen will be sent there, and sheep will walk over them.
The LORD said to me, "Take a big piece of paper and write on it with a common pen: 'Quick to take things, fast to steal.'"
I will have two trusted men watch this. They are Uriah the priest and Zechariah, the son of Jeberechiah.
Then I went to the woman who spoke for God. She became pregnant and had a son. The LORD said to me, "Name him 'Quick to take things, fast to steal.'"
Before the boy can say "Dad" or "Mom," the good things of Damascus and the things taken from Samaria will be carried away by the king of Assyria.
The LORD spoke to me again.
"These people do not want the calm waters of Shiloah. They are happy with Rezin and the son of Remaliah.
So the Lord will bring a strong flood against them. It is the king of Assyria and all his power. It will rise over every river and every bank.
It will move through Judah and cover it. The water will reach up to the neck. Its wings will spread over the whole land. God is with us."
"Be broken, you nations! Listen, you far countries! Get ready, and you will be broken. Get ready, and you will be broken.
Make your plans, but they will come to nothing. Speak your words, but they will not stand. God is with us."
The LORD spoke to me with a strong hand. He warned me not to walk like these people. He said,
"Do not say, 'It is a trap,' when these people say, 'It is a trap.' Do not be afraid of what they fear. Do not be scared of them.
Honor the LORD of All as holy. Let Him be the one you fear. Let Him be the one you dread.

He will be a safe place. But He will also be a stone that makes people trip and a rock that makes them fall. This will happen to both parts of Israel. He will be a trap and a snare to the people of Jerusalem.
Many will trip over Him. They will fall and be broken. They will be caught and taken away."
"Tie up the words of God's truth. Keep His teaching safe for my followers."
I will wait for the LORD. He turns away from Jacob's family. I will put my hope in Him.
Look! I and the children the LORD gave me are special signs in Israel. They come from the LORD of All, who lives on Mount Zion.
People may say to you, "Ask the people who talk to spirits. Ask the ones who whisper and mumble." But should a people ask their God? Should they ask dead people for the living?
Go to God's teaching and His words of truth. If they do not speak like this, they have no light.
They will walk through the land. They will be in pain and hungry. When they are hungry, they will be angry. They will speak bad words about their king and their God. They will look up.
They will look at the earth. But they will see trouble and darkness. They will be pushed into thick darkness.

People in trouble will not stay sad forever. Long ago, God made the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali sad. But later, He will bring honor to the land by the sea, across the Jordan, and to Galilee, where many nations live.
The people who walked in the dark have seen a great light. A light has shone on those who live in a very dark land.
You made the nation bigger and gave them more joy. They are happy in front of You, like people happy at harvest time, like soldiers happy when they share things they won in war.
For, just like when Midian was beaten, You broke the heavy load on them. You broke the bar on their shoulders and the stick of the one who pushed them down.
Every soldier's boot from battle and every coat covered in blood will be burned. They will be food for the fire.

A child is born to us. A son is given to us. He will be the ruler, and the job of ruling will be on His shoulders. People will call Him Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

His rule and peace will never end. He will sit on David's throne and rule over His kingdom. He will make it strong and fair, and He will keep it right, from now on and forever. The LORD who rules over all will make this happen because He cares so much.
The Lord sent a word against Jacob. It will come down on Israel.
All the people will know it—Ephraim and the people who live in Samaria. They speak with pride and a proud heart. They say,
"The bricks fell down, but we will build with cut stone. The fig trees were cut down, but we will put cedars in their place."
But the LORD made Rezin's enemies strong against them. He stirred up their enemies.
People from Aram in the east and Philistines in the west have eaten up Israel. But even after all this, His anger is not gone. His hand is still raised.
But the people did not turn back to God, who punished them. They did not look for the LORD who rules over all.
So the LORD will take away from Israel the head and the tail, the palm branch and the reed, all in one day.
The leaders and important people are the head. The prophets who tell lies are the tail.
The ones who lead these people lead them the wrong way. The ones who follow are lost.

So the Lord will not be happy with the young men. He will not feel sorry for the children without fathers or the women whose husbands have died. Everyone is evil and does wrong. Everyone says foolish things. But even after all this, His anger is not gone. His hand is still raised.
Evil burns like a fire. It eats up thorns and weeds. It sets the thick woods on fire, and smoke rises up.
