Because of the LORD's anger, the land will be burned. The people will be like wood for the fire. They will not be kind to each other.
They will grab food on the right, but still be hungry. They will eat on the left, but not be full. Each person will attack his own people.
Manasseh will attack Ephraim, and Ephraim will attack Manasseh. Together they will turn against Judah. But even after all this, His anger is not gone. His hand is still raised.
Trouble is coming for leaders who make bad laws! They write rules that hurt people.
They push poor people away from what is fair. They take what belongs to My poor people. They take things from widows. They rob children whose fathers have died.
What will you do when God punishes you? What will you do when trouble comes from far away? Who will help you? Where will you leave your money?
You will have no choice but to bow like prisoners. You will fall with people who are killed. Even after all this, the LORD is still angry. His hand is still raised.
Trouble is coming, Assyria! You are the stick I use when I am angry. The club in your hand shows My anger.
I will send you to a nation that does not follow God. I will send you against people I am angry with. You will take their things and rob them. You will walk on them like mud in the street.
But Assyria does not think like that. It does not plan like that. In its heart, it wants to destroy and wipe out many nations.
Assyria's leaders say, "Are not all my commanders like kings?
Isn't Calno like Carchemish? Isn't Hamath like Arpad? Isn't Samaria like Damascus?
my hand has taken kingdoms that worship false gods. Their carved statues were more than those in Jerusalem and Samaria.
I did this to Samaria and its false gods. I will do the same to Jerusalem and its idols."
When the Lord finishes all His work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He will punish the king of Assyria for his proud words and proud look.
The king says, "I did this by my own power. I did this by my wisdom. I am smart. I moved the borders of nations. I took their treasures. I brought down their leaders like a strong bull.
my hand found the wealth of nations like a bird finds a nest. I gathered their things like someone gathers eggs. No bird flapped a wing or made a sound."
Can an axe brag about the person who swings it? Can a saw think it is better than the person who uses it? A stick cannot swing the person who holds it. A club cannot lift the person who uses it.
So the Lord GOD of Hosts will make His strong soldiers sick and weak. Under His glory, a fire will burn like a big fire.
The light of Israel will be a fire. His Holy One will be a flame. In one day it will burn and destroy Assyria's thorns and weeds.
It will destroy the beauty of Assyria's forest and good land. It will destroy body and soul. It will be like a sick person getting weaker and weaker.
So few trees will be left in Assyria's forest that a child could count them.
In that day, the leftover people of Israel and the survivors of Jacob's family will not depend on the one who hit them anymore. They will depend on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
A small group will come back. The rest of Jacob's people will come back to the Mighty God.
Even if Israel's people are as many as sand by the sea, only a small group will come back. God has decided to destroy them, but He will do what is right.
The Lord GOD of Hosts will finish the destruction He has planned for the whole earth.
So the Lord GOD of Hosts says, "My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of Assyria. Assyria will hit you with a rod and lift a club against you, like Egypt did."
In a very short time, My anger will end. Then My anger will be against Assyria and destroy them.
The LORD of Hosts will whip Assyria. He will punish them like He punished Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise His stick over the sea, like He did in Egypt.
In that day, Assyria's heavy load will leave your shoulders. Its yoke will leave your neck. The yoke will break because you are strong and well-fed.
Assyria has come to Aiath. It has passed through Migron. At Michmash it stores its supplies.
They crossed the pass. They stayed at Geba for the night. Ramah is afraid. Gibeah of Saul ran away.
Cry out, people of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth, cry for help!
Madmenah runs away. The people of Gebim run for safety.
Today Assyria stops at Nob. It shakes its fist at the mountain of Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord GOD of Hosts will chop off the branches with a loud crash. The tall trees will be cut down. The proud ones will be brought low.
He will cut down the thick bushes with iron. Lebanon will fall by the power of the Mighty One.
A new branch will grow from Jesse's family. From his roots, it will bear fruit.
The Spirit of the LORD will rest on Him. He will have wisdom and understanding. He will have good plans and strength. He will know things and honor the the LORD.
He will not judge by what He sees. He will not decide by what He hears.
He will judge poor people fairly. He will help humble people. He will strike the earth with words from His mouth. He will kill evil people with just a breath.
He will wear right living like a belt. He will wear faithfulness like a band around His waist.
Wolves will live with lambs. Leopards will lie down with young goats. Calves, lions, and young farm animals will be together. A little child will lead them.
Cows and bears will eat together. Their babies will lie down together. Lions will eat straw like cows.
Babies will play near snake holes. Young children will put their hands into snake nests.
They will not hurt or destroy on the the LORD's holy mountain. Everyone on earth will know the the LORD, like the sea is full of water.
On that day, Jesse's root will stand like a flag for all people. Nations will come to Him. His resting place will be wonderful.
On that day, the Lord will reach out His hand a second time. He will bring back the rest of His people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Babylonia, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He will raise a flag for the nations. He will gather Israel's people who were sent away. He will bring together Judah's scattered people from all over the earth.
Ephraim will no longer be jealous. Judah's enemies will be destroyed. Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, and Judah will not attack Ephraim.
They will fly down on Philistia in the west. Together they will take things from people in the east. They will rule Edom and Moab. The Ammonites will obey them.
The LORD will dry up the sea of Egypt. With a hot wind, He will wave His hand over the Euphrates River. He will split it into seven streams. People will walk across in sandals.
There will be a road for the rest of His people coming from Assyria. It will be like the road Israel had when they came up from Egypt.
On that day, you will say, “I will praise You, the LORD. You were angry with me, but You stopped being angry, and You make me feel better.”
See, God saves me. I will trust and not be afraid. The LORD God is my strength and my song. He saved me.
With joy, you will get water from the wells that save.
On that day, you will say, “Give thanks to the LORD. Call on His name. Tell the nations what He has done. Say that His name is high.”
Sing to the LORD, because He has done great things. Let everyone on earth know it.
Shout and sing with joy, people of Zion, because the Holy One of Israel is great among you.
This is a message about Babylon. Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saw it.
Raise a flag on a bare hill. Call out to them. Wave your hand so they can go through the gates of the leaders.
I have told My holy ones to come. I called My strong fighters to show My anger. They are happy to win for Me.
Listen! There is a loud noise on the mountains, like a big crowd. Listen! There is a loud roar among the kingdoms, like nations gathered together. the LORD of Armies is getting an army ready for war.
They come from far away, from the ends of the sky. the LORD and His angry weapons come to destroy the whole earth.
Cry out! The Day of the LORD is near. It will come like ruin from the Almighty.
So all hands will go weak, and every heart will melt.
Fear, panic, and pain will grab them. They will twist and turn like a woman having a baby. They will look at each other, and their faces will turn red with fear.
Look! The Day of the LORD is coming. It will be cruel. It will bring fury and burning anger. It will make the earth empty, and it will destroy the sinners in it.
The stars and their groups in the sky will not shine. The sun will be dark when it rises, and the moon will not give its light.
I will punish the world for its bad ways. I will punish the wicked for their wrongs. I will end the pride of proud people, and I will bring down the pride of cruel rulers.
I will make people harder to find than pure gold. People will be rarer than the gold of Ophir.
I will shake the sky, and the earth will shake out of its place. This will happen because of the anger of the LORD of Armies and His burning anger on that day.
They will be like a scared deer. They will be like sheep with no shepherd. Each person will turn to his own people. Each will run to his own land.
Anyone who is caught will be stabbed. Anyone who is caught will die by the sword.
Their babies will be killed in front of them. Their houses will be robbed. Their wives will be attacked.
Look! I will stir up the Medes against them. The Medes do not care about silver. They do not want gold.
Their bows will kill the young men. They will not feel sorry for the babies. They will not spare the children.
Babylon is the jewel of kingdoms. It is the pride of the Chaldeans. But God will destroy it like Sodom and Gomorrah.
No one will live there ever again, for generation after generation. No Arab will put up a tent there. No shepherd will make his sheep lie down there.
Wild animals of the desert will lie there. Its houses will be full of owls. Ostriches will live there. Wild goats will jump around.
Hyenas will howl in its strong forts. Jackals will howl in its fine palaces. Babylon's time is near. Its days will not last long.
The LORD will be kind to Jacob. He will choose Israel again. He will put them in their own land. People from other lands will join them. They will stay with Jacob’s family.
Other nations will take them and bring them home. Israel’s people will have them as servants. They will make slaves of the people who made them slaves. They will rule over the ones who hurt them.
On the day the LORD gives you rest, you will be free from your pain and fear. You will not do the hard work they forced on you. “
On that day you will sing this song about the king of Babylon: “How the cruel ruler has stopped! How his angry power has stopped!
The LORD has broken the stick of bad people. He has broken the rod of rulers.
The cruel ruler hit nations in anger many times. He ruled people with angry power and did not stop.
Now all the earth is quiet and at rest. People sing for joy.
Even the cypress and cedar trees of Lebanon are glad because of you. They say, ‘Since you are down, no one comes to cut us down.’ “
The grave below wakes up to meet you when you come. It stirs up dead leaders for you. It makes all kings of nations stand up from their thrones.
They all speak to you. They say, ‘You are weak like us now. You are just like us.’
Your pride has gone down to the grave. The sound of your harps has stopped. Worms are spread under you. Bugs cover you. “
How you have fallen from heaven, O bright morning star, son of the dawn! You are cut down to the ground, you who hurt the nations. “
You said in your heart, ‘I will go up to heaven. I will set my throne above God’s stars. I will sit on the mountain where God meets, in the far north.
I will rise above the high clouds. I will be like the Most High.’ “
But you are brought down to the grave, to the deep pit. “
People who see you stare at you. They think, ‘Is this the man who shook the earth and made kingdoms shake?
He made the world like a desert. He tore down its cities. He did not let his prisoners go home.’ “
All kings of nations lie in honor, each in his own tomb.
But you are thrown out of your grave like a hated branch. You are covered with the dead. You are like a body that was walked on.
You will not be buried with them, because you ruined your land and killed your people. The children of bad people will not be named.
Get ready to kill his children for what their fathers did wrong. Then they will not rise and take the earth or fill cities with people.”
The LORD of hosts says, “I will rise against them. I will cut off Babylon’s name and all who are left. I will cut off its children and grandchildren.
I will make Babylon a home for wild animals and pools of water. I will sweep it away with a broom of ruin.”
The LORD of hosts has sworn, “What I planned will happen. What I decided will stand.
I will break Assyria in My land. I will crush him on My mountains. His yoke will leave My people. His heavy load will leave their shoulders.”
This is the plan for the whole earth. This is the LORD’s hand stretched out over all nations.
The LORD of hosts has planned it. Who can stop it? His hand is stretched out. Who can turn it back?
In the year King Ahaz died, this heavy message came:
“Do not be glad, all Philistia, because the stick that hit you is broken. From the root of the snake will come a viper. Its fruit will be a flying, fiery snake.
The poor will have food. The needy will lie down in safety. I will kill your root with hunger. I will kill those who are left.
Cry out at your gates! Cry out in your city! Melt away, all Philistia! Smoke comes from the north. No one will be left alone in his place.”
What will people answer the messengers of the nations? “The LORD has built Zion. The poor of His people will be safe there.”
A message about Moab. The city of Ar in Moab is ruined. It is destroyed in one night. The city of Kir in Moab is ruined. It is destroyed in one night too.
The people of Dibon go up to their temple to cry. They cry at the high places. Moab cries loudly over Nebo and Medeba. All the men shave their heads. All the men cut off their beards.
In the streets they wear rough cloth. On the roofs and in the squares, everyone cries loudly. They fall down and weep.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out. Their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. So the soldiers of Moab cry out. They are scared deep inside.

My heart cries out for Moab. Her people who run away go as far as Zoar. They go as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. On the road up to Luhith, they cry as they walk. On the road to Horonaim, they shout that they are being destroyed.
The water in Nimrim is dried up. The grass is dry. The plants are gone. The green is no more.
So now they carry their things over the Brook of the Willows.
A cry is heard all around Moab. The crying reaches Eglaim. The crying reaches Beer-elim.
The water at Dimon is full of blood. But I will bring even more trouble on Dimon. I will send a lion after the people running from Moab and the people left in Admah.
Send a lamb to the ruler of the land. Send it from Sela through the desert to Mount Zion.
The women of Moab are like birds driven from their nests. They wait at the river crossings of Arnon.
Give good advice. Do what is right. Be like cool shade at noon. Hide the people who are chased away. Do not tell where they are.

Let Moab's people who were chased away stay with you. Be a safe place for them from the one who destroys. The one who takes by force is gone. The ruin is over. The one who hurts people is gone from the land.
Then a king's seat will be set up in loving care. One will sit on it and be true. He will be in David's tent. He will judge fairly and look for what is right. He will be quick to do right.
We heard how proud Moab is. He is very proud. We heard his anger and his proud words. But his words are not true.
So Moab will cry for Moab. Everyone will cry. You will be sad for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth. You will be very sad.

The fields of Heshbon are weak. The grapevines of Sibmah are weak. The rulers of other nations hit their branches. Those branches reached to Jazer. They spread into the desert. Its new growth spread far, even over the sea.
So I will cry like Jazer cries for Sibmah's grapevines. I will cry tears for Heshbon and Elealeh. The happy shouts have stopped for your summer fruit and your harvest.
Joy is taken from the good fields. In the vineyards no one sings or shouts. No one steps on grapes to make wine. I stopped the happy shout at the wine presses.
So my heart aches for Moab like a sad song. My deep feelings ache for Kir-hareseth.
When people see Moab is tired on the high place, he will go to his holy place to pray. But he will not be able.
This is the word the LORD spoke about Moab long ago.
But now the LORD says, "In three years, like a worker's years, Moab's glory will be brought down. Its large crowd will be small. The few left will be very weak."
This is a message about Damascus. Look! Damascus will stop being a city. It will become a pile of broken stones.
The towns of Aroer will be empty. They will be for sheep. The sheep will lie down, and no one will scare them.
The strong city will be taken from Ephraim. The kingdom will be taken from Damascus. The few people left in Syria will be like the greatness of the people of Israel, says the LORD of Hosts.
In that day, Jacob's greatness will be small. His body will get thin.
It will be like when a worker cuts ripe grain. His arm cuts the heads of grain. It will be like picking grain in the Valley of Rephaim.

A few olives will be left. It will be like shaking an olive tree. Two or three olives will be on the top branch. Four or five will be on the other branches. This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says.
In that day, a man will look to his Maker. His eyes will look to the Holy One of Israel.
He will not look at the altars his hands made. He will not look at the Asherah poles or the incense altars his fingers made.
In that day, his strong cities will be like empty woods and empty hilltops. People left those places because of the people of Israel. The land will be empty.
You forgot the God who saves you. You did not remember Him. You did not remember the Rock who keeps you safe. So you plant pretty plants. You plant grapevines from a faraway land.
On the day you plant them, you make them grow. In the morning, your seeds bloom. But the harvest will be a sad pile on a day of grief and pain that cannot be healed.
Oh no! Many, many people are loud. They sound like the sea. Nations rush like mighty water.
Nations rush like many waters. But He will tell them to stop. They will run far away. They will be blown away like dust on hills before the wind. They will be like a rolling leaf before a storm.
In the evening, look! There is fear. Before morning, they are gone. This is what happens to those who steal our things. This is what happens to those who rob us.
Trouble is coming to the land with buzzing wings, far past the rivers of Cush!

That land sends messengers by sea in boats made of reeds. Go, fast messengers, to a tall people with smooth skin. They are feared far and wide. They are a strong nation with a strange language. Rivers split their land.
All you people of the world, you who live on the earth, when a flag is raised on the mountains, you will see it. When a horn blows, you will hear it.
This is what the LORD says to me: "I will stay quiet and watch from My home. I will be like heat waves in the sun, and like a cloud of dew in the hot harvest time."
Before the harvest, when the flowers are gone and the grapes are growing, He will cut the new shoots with pruning knives and cut away the spreading branches.
They will be left for the mountain birds and the wild animals. The birds will eat them all summer. The wild animals will eat them all winter.

At that time, gifts will be brought to the LORD Almighty from that tall people with smooth skin. They are feared far and wide. They are a strong nation with a strange language. Rivers split their land. The gifts will go to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD Almighty.
This is a message about Egypt. Look! The LORD rides on a fast cloud and comes to Egypt. Egypt's false gods shake with fear. The Egyptians' hearts melt inside them.
The LORD says, "I will make Egyptians fight each other. They will fight brother against brother and friend against friend. City will fight city, and kingdom will fight kingdom."
The Egyptians will lose their courage. Their plans will come to nothing. They will ask their false gods, fortune tellers, and people who talk to spirits for help.
The LORD says, "I will hand Egypt over to a hard master. A strong, mean king will rule them." This is what the Lord, the LORD of Armies, says.
The water in the sea will dry up. The river will become dry and cracked.
The canals will smell bad. The streams of Egypt will get low and dry up. The reeds and tall grass will die.
Grass along the Nile will dry up. All the seeds planted by the Nile will dry up and blow away. They will be gone.
The fishermen will be sad. Everyone who throws a hook in the Nile will cry. The people who spread nets on the water will feel weak.
The people who work with flax will be upset. The people who weave fine cloth will be upset too.
The people who hold up the land will be crushed. Everyone who works for pay will be sad.
The leaders of Zoan are very foolish. Pharaoh's wise men give bad advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am the son of wise men. I come from old kings"?
Where are your wise men? Let them tell you what the the LORD of Armies has planned against Egypt. They should know.
The leaders of Zoan are fools. The leaders of Memphis are tricked. The leaders who should guide Egypt's people have led Egypt the wrong way.
The The LORD put a spirit of confusion in Egypt. Egypt staggers in all it does, like a drunk man staggering in his own mess.
No one in Egypt can help—not the rich or the poor, not the strong or the weak.
In that day, the Egyptians will be weak and afraid. They will tremble at the the LORD of Armies' hand when He shakes it over them.
The land of Judah will scare Egypt. Everyone who hears about it will be afraid because of what the the LORD of Armies planned against Egypt.
In that day, five cities in Egypt will speak the language of Canaan. They will promise to follow the the LORD of Armies. One city will be called the City of Destruction.
In that day, there will be an altar to the the LORD in the middle of Egypt. There will be a stone pillar to the the LORD near its border.
It will be a sign and a witness for the the LORD of Armies in Egypt. When the Egyptians cry out to the the LORD because of people who hurt them, He will send a savior to rescue them.
The the LORD will show Himself to the Egyptians. They will know the the LORD that day. They will worship Him with gifts and offerings. They will make promises to the the LORD and keep them.
The the LORD will hit Egypt and then heal it. The Egyptians will come back to the the LORD. He will listen to their prayers and heal them.
In that day, there will be a road from Egypt to Assyria. Assyrians will go to Egypt, and Egyptians will go to Assyria. Egyptians and Assyrians will worship the the LORD together.
In that day, Israel will be the third nation with Egypt and Assyria. They will be a blessing in the middle of the earth.
The the LORD of Armies will bless them. He will say, "Egypt is My people. Assyria is the work of My hands. Israel is My own land."
In the year when Tartan came to Ashdod, Sargon, the king of Assyria, sent him. Tartan fought Ashdod and took it.

At that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz. He said, "Go take off the rough cloth from your waist and your sandals from your feet." Isaiah did it. He went without clothes and without shoes.
The LORD said, "Just as My servant Isaiah has gone without clothes and without shoes for three years, this is a sign and warning for Egypt and Cush.
So the king of Assyria will take the people of Egypt and Cush away as prisoners. Young and old will go without clothes and shoes. Egypt will be put to shame.
The people who hoped in Cush and bragged about Egypt will be afraid and ashamed.
"On that day, the people who live by the sea will say, 'Look! This is what happened to the people we hoped in. We ran to them for help to get away from the king of Assyria. How can we get away now?'"
Like strong winds in the dry south, an enemy comes from the desert. It comes from a scary land.
A hard message was shown to me. The traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Attack Media! I will end all her crying.
So my body is full of pain. Pain grabs me like a woman having a baby. I am mixed up when I hear it. I am scared when I see it.
My heart is weak. Fear shakes me. The evening I wanted has become a fear to me.
Set the table. Watch the tower. Eat and drink. Rise up, leaders! Get your shields ready.
For this is what the Lord says to me: “Go, stand a lookout. Have him report what he sees.
When he sees chariots with two horses, riders on donkeys, and riders on camels, let him watch very closely.”
The lookout shouted, “My lord, I stand on the watchtower every day. I stay at my post every night.”
Then the lookout said, “Look! A chariot with men is coming, with two horses.” Someone answered, “Babylon has fallen! It has fallen! All the statues of her gods are broken on the ground.”
My people, you are like grain being crushed. I tell you what I heard from the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel.
A message about Dumah: Someone calls to me from Seir, “Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?”
The watchman said, “Morning is coming, but night is coming too. If you want to ask, ask. Come back again.”
A message about Arabia: In the woods of Arabia you will sleep, travelers from Dedan.
Bring water for the thirsty. People of Tema, give bread to the runaway.
They run from swords, from a sword pulled out, from a bow ready to shoot, and from the heavy trouble of war.
For this is what the Lord says to me: “In one year, like a worker counts his time, all the greatness of Kedar will end.”
Only a few of Kedar’s brave men with bows will be left. For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
What is wrong with you? Why did you all go up to the roofs?
The city is full of noise. The town is in an uproar. It used to be a happy city. Your dead did not die by the sword. They did not die in battle.
All your leaders ran away together. They were caught without a fight. Everyone who was found was caught too. They ran far away.
So I said, "Leave me alone so I can cry hard. Do not rush to comfort me about the trouble of my people."
The Lord, the LORD of Hosts, has a day of noise, trouble, and confusion in the Valley of Vision. Walls are broken down. People cry to the mountain.
Elam took up its quiver. It came with chariots and horsemen. Kir got ready with shields.
Your best valleys were full of chariots. Horsemen stood at the gate.
The LORD took away Judah's protection. That day, you looked at the weapons in the Forest House.
You saw the broken walls of David's city. You gathered water from the lower pool.
You counted the houses in Jerusalem. You tore down houses to make the wall stronger.
You made a pool between the walls for the old water. But you did not look to its Maker. You did not see its Creator from far away.
That day, the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, called for crying, sadness, shaved heads, and rough clothes.
But instead, there was joy and gladness. People killed cows and sheep. They ate meat and drank wine. They said, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
The LORD of Hosts spoke in my ears: "This wrong will not be forgiven. You will die for it," says the Lord, the LORD of Hosts.
This is what the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, says: "Go to Shebna, the man in charge of the palace.
What are you doing here? Who gave you the right to dig a grave here? You cut a grave high up. You carved a resting place for yourself in the rock.
The LORD will throw you away with force. He will wrap you up.
He will roll you up like a ball and throw you into a wide land. There you will die. There your fine chariots will stay. They will shame your master's house.
I will push you out of your job. He will pull you down from your place."
That day, I will call my servant Eliakim, son of Hilkiah.
I will give him your robe. I will tie your belt on him. I will put your power in his hand. He will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and Judah.
I will put the key of David's house on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.
I will make him like a strong peg in a safe place. He will be a seat of honor for his family.
All the honor of his family will hang on him. His children and relatives will depend on him. Even small things, from bowls to jars, will hang on him.
That day, says the LORD of Hosts, the peg in the safe place will be pulled out. It will be cut down and fall. The load on it will be cut off. The LORD has spoken.
This is a sad message about Tyre. Cry out, ships of Tarshish! Tyre is destroyed. Its houses are broken, and no one can go in. People from Kittim heard the news.
Be quiet, people who live by the sea. Merchants from Sidon crossed the sea and filled your land.
By many waters came grain from Shihor and crops from the Nile. Tyre became a market for the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, you strong place by the sea. The sea says, "I have not had labor pains. I have not had a baby. I have not raised young men or brought up young women."
When Egypt hears this news, they will hurt, just as Tyre did.
Go across to Tarshish. Cry out, people who live by the sea.
Is this the city you used to cheer for? It is very old. Its people traveled far to live there.
Who planned this against Tyre? Tyre was a city that wore a crown. Its sellers were like rulers. Its traders were honored on earth.
The LORD of Hosts planned it. He will bring down all proud beauty. He will put all honored people to shame.
Daughter of Tarshish, cross your land like the Nile. There is no more harbor.
He stretched out His hand over the sea. He shook the kingdoms. The LORD gave a command about Canaan: destroy its strong places.
He said, "You will not be happy anymore, crushed young woman of Sidon. Get up and go to Kittim. Even there you will find no rest."
Look at the land of the Chaldeans. They are now a weak people. Assyria made it a home for wild animals. They built war towers. They tore down its palaces. They made it a ruin.
Cry out, ships of Tarshish, for your strong place is destroyed.
In that day, Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years. It will be like one king's whole life. After seventy years, Tyre will be like a song about a woman who sells herself.
Take a harp. Walk around the city, like a forgotten woman. Play well and sing many songs, so you will be remembered.
After seventy years, the LORD will visit Tyre. She will go back to her pay. She will sell herself to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Her trade and her pay will be set apart for the LORD. It will not be saved or stored. Her trade will be for the people who live with the LORD. It will give them food to eat and good clothes to wear.
Look! The LORD is making the earth empty. He is ruining it. He is twisting the ground. He is scattering the people who live there.
Everyone will be the same. People and priests will be the same. Workers and bosses will be the same. Buyers and sellers will be the same. Lenders and borrowers will be the same.
The earth will be completely emptied. It will be robbed clean. the LORD has said this.
The earth is sad and dying. The whole world is weak and fading. Even the proud leaders of the earth are weak.
The earth is dirty because of the people who live on it. They broke the LORD's laws. They changed His rules. They broke His promise that lasts forever.
So a curse is eating up the earth. The people who live there are guilty. That is why earth people are burned up, and only a few are left.
The new wine is sad. The grapevines are weak. All happy people are groaning.
The happy sound of drums stops. The noise of party people stops. The joy of the harp stops.
They do not sing while they drink wine. Strong drink tastes bitter to those who drink it.
The broken city is in ruins. Every house is closed. No one can enter.
People cry in the streets because there is no wine. All joy has turned sad. Happiness has left the earth.
The city is left empty. Its gate is broken down.
So it will be in the middle of the earth among the nations. It will be like shaking an olive tree. It will be like picking the last grapes.
They lift up their voices. They shout for joy. From the west they praise the LORD's greatness.
So praise the LORD in the east. Honor the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, in the faraway islands.
From the ends of the earth we heard songs of praise to the Good One. But I said, “I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Oh, no! Traitors have been bad! Traitors have been very bad!”
Terror, a pit, and a trap are waiting for you who live on the earth.

The person who runs from the sound of terror will fall into the pit. The person who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. The windows of heaven are opened. The foundations of the earth shake.
The earth is broken into pieces. The earth is split apart. The earth shakes hard.
The earth wobbles like a drunk person. It sways like a small hut. Its sins are heavy on it. It falls and does not get up again.
On that day the LORD will punish the armies in heaven above and the kings on earth below.
They will be gathered like prisoners in a pit. They will be shut in a cell. After many days they will be punished.
The moon will be ashamed. The sun will be embarrassed. This is because the LORD of Armies will rule on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem. His leaders will see His glory.
O the LORD, You are my God. I will lift You up. I will praise Your name. You have done amazing things. You planned them long ago. They are true and sure.
You turned the city into a pile of rocks. You made the strong city a ruin. The palace of strangers is gone. It will never be built again.
So strong people will honor You. Cities of cruel nations will fear You.

You have been a safe place for poor people. You have been a safe place for needy people in trouble. You are like a shelter from the storm. You are like shade from the hot sun. The breath of cruel people is like a storm hitting a wall.
You quiet the noise of strangers like heat in a dry place. You stop the song of cruel people like heat under a cloud.
On this mountain, the LORD of Hosts will make a big feast for all people. It will have rich food and fine wine. The food will be full of good meat. The wine will be old and clear.
On this mountain, He will take away the cover over all people. He will remove the blanket over all nations.
He will end death forever. The Lord, the LORD, will wipe away tears from every face. He will take away the shame of His people from all the earth. The LORD has spoken.
On that day people will say, “Look! This is our God. We waited for Him, and He saved us. This is the LORD. We waited for Him. Let us be glad and happy because He saved us.”
The hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain. Moab will be crushed like straw in a trash pile.
Moab will stretch out its arms in the middle of it, like a swimmer stretches out his arms to swim. But the LORD will bring down its pride and stop what its hands can do.
He will bring down your high walls and strong towers. He will knock them to the ground, down to the dust.
On that day, people will sing this song in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city. He makes walls and safe places to keep us safe."
Open the gates. Let the good nation come in. They keep their promises.
You will keep in full peace the person whose mind stays on You, because he trusts You.
Trust in the LORD forever, because GOD the LORD is the Rock that lasts forever.
He brought down the people who live high up. He made the proud city low. He brought it down to the ground. He pushed it into the dust.
Feet walked on it. The feet of poor people. The steps of needy people.
The road of good people is straight. You make the path smooth for good people.
Yes, the LORD, we wait for You on the road of Your fair rules. Your name and Your fame are what our souls want.
At night my soul wants You. My spirit in me looks for You early. When Your fair rules come to the earth, people learn to do right.
Even if bad people are treated kindly, they do not learn to do right. In a land where people do right, they still do wrong. They do not see the great power of the LORD.
The LORD, Your hand is high up, but they do not see. Let them see Your strong care for Your people, and let them be ashamed. Let fire eat up Your enemies.
The LORD, You will give us peace. You have done all our work for us.
The LORD our God, other rulers ruled us. But we remember only Your name.
Dead people will not live again. Spirits will not rise. So You punished them and wiped them out. You erased all memory of them.
The LORD, You made the nation bigger. You made the nation bigger. You are honored. You made all the borders of the land far.
The LORD, they looked for You when they were in trouble. When You punished them, they whispered a quiet prayer.
Like a woman about to have a baby twists and cries in pain, so we were before You, the LORD.
We were like a woman with a baby, but nothing came of it. We did not bring safety to the earth. No new people were born.
Your dead people will live. Their bodies will rise. Wake up and sing, you who live in the dust! For Your dew is like morning dew. The earth will bring out her dead.
"Go, My people. Go into your rooms and close your doors behind you. Hide for a short time until the anger passes."
Look, the LORD is coming out of His place to punish the people of the earth for their wrong. The earth will show her killed people. She will not hide her dead people anymore.
In that day, the LORD will punish Leviathan, the snake that runs away, with His strong sword. He will kill the dragon in the sea.
“In that day, sing about a vineyard full of fruit.
I am the LORD. I take care of it. I water it all the time. I keep it safe day and night, so no one can hurt it.
I am not angry. I wish thorns and weeds were here for Me to fight! I would go against them. I would burn them all up.
Or let them hold on to My strength. Then they can make peace with Me. Yes, let them make peace with Me.”
Later, Jacob will grow roots. Israel will bloom and bud. It will fill the whole world with fruit.
Did the LORD punish Israel like He punished her enemies? Was she killed like those who killed her?
By war and being sent away, You fought with her. You took her away with a strong wind on a hot day.
So Jacob's sin will be forgiven. This is the full fruit of taking away his sin: he will crush all the altar stones into small pieces. No poles for Asherah and no incense altars will be left.
The strong city is empty. It is like a deserted home in the desert. A calf eats grass there. It lies down there and eats the branches.

When the branches dry up, they break off. Women come and burn them for firewood. This is because the people do not understand. So their Maker will not have pity on them. Their Creator will not be kind to them.
In that day, the LORD will gather you, children of Israel, one by one. He will gather you from the Euphrates River to the stream in Egypt.
In that day, a loud trumpet will sound. The people lost in Assyria will come. The people scattered in Egypt will come. They will worship the LORD on His holy mountain in Jerusalem.
How sad for the proud crown of Ephraim's people who get drunk! How sad for the fading flower that shows their beauty! It sits on the head of a rich valley. The people there are drunk with wine.
Look! The Lord has someone strong and mighty. He is like a hailstorm, a storm that destroys. He is like floodwaters that rush and overflow. He will throw it down to the ground with His hand.
The proud crown of Ephraim's people who get drunk will be trampled underfoot.
The fading flower of its beauty, which is on the head of a rich valley, will be like a ripe fig before summer. As soon as someone sees it, he eats it up.
In that day, the LORD of Armies will be a beautiful crown and a lovely headband for His people who are left.
He will give a spirit of fairness to the one who judges. He will give strength to those who fight back at the city gate.

These leaders also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink. The priest and the prophet stumble from strong drink and are confused by wine. They stumble because of strong drink. They see things wrong, and they judge wrong.
All their tables are covered with vomit. There is no clean spot.
Who will He teach? Who will understand His message? Babies who just stopped drinking milk? Little ones just taken from their mother's breast?
For they say, "Rule after rule, rule after rule. Line after line, line after line. A little here, a little there."
So He will speak to these people with strange, mocking words and a foreign tongue.
He said to them, "This is the place to rest. Let tired people rest here. This is a calm place." But they would not listen.

So the LORD's word to them will be, "Rule after rule, rule after rule. Line after line, line after line. A little here, a little there," so that they may go and fall backward. They will be broken. They will be trapped and caught.
So listen to the LORD's word, you mockers who rule these people in Jerusalem.
You said, "We made a deal with death. We made an agreement with the grave. When the terrible trouble comes, it will not reach us. We made lies our safe place. We hid in false words."
So the Lord, the LORD, says, "Look! I am putting a stone in Jerusalem. It is a tested stone. It is a precious cornerstone. It is a strong base. The one who trusts will not panic."
I will make fairness like a measuring line. I will make right living like a straight line. Hail will wash away the safe place made of lies. Water will flood the hiding place.
Your deal with death will be canceled. Your agreement with the grave will not last. When the terrible trouble passes through, it will trample you.
Each time it passes, it will grab you. It will come morning after morning, day and night. Understanding the news will bring only fear.
The bed is too short to lie down on. The blanket is too small to cover you.
The LORD will stand up like He did at Mount Perazim. He will be angry like He was in the Valley of Gibeon. He will do His work, a strange work. He will do His job, a strange job.
So now do not make fun. Your chains may get stronger. I heard the Lord, the LORD of Armies, say He will destroy the whole land.
Listen to me. Hear my voice. Pay attention and hear my words.
Does a farmer plow all day just to plant? Does he keep turning the dirt?
When the ground is smooth, doesn't he plant dill and scatter cumin? Doesn't he plant wheat in rows, barley where it belongs, and rye along the edge?
His God teaches him and shows him the right way.
Dill is not beaten with a sharp farm tool. A cart wheel is not rolled over cumin. Dill is beaten with a stick. Cumin is beaten with a rod.
Grain is crushed, but not forever. The cart wheel rolls over it, but it does not turn it to dust.
This also comes from the the LORD of Armies. He gives wonderful advice and great wisdom.
Oh no, Ariel! Ariel is the city where David stayed. Count year after year. Let the feasts come back.
But I will bring trouble to Ariel. She will cry and be sad. To Me, she will be like a fire on an altar.
I will camp all around you. I will put towers around you. I will build walls to trap you.

You will be brought low. You will speak from the ground. Your words will come out like a whisper from the dust. Your voice will sound like a spirit from the ground. Your words will chirp from the dust.
But your many enemies will be like fine dust. The cruel crowd will be like straw that blows away. It will happen fast, in a moment.
The LORD of Armies will visit you with thunder and a big shake of the ground. There will be loud noise, a storm, and a wind. Fire will burn everything.
Then the crowd of all the nations that fight Ariel will be like a dream at night. All who attack her, her fort, and trouble her will be like a night dream.

It will be like a hungry man who dreams he is eating, but wakes up and is still hungry. It will be like a thirsty man who dreams he is drinking, but wakes up and is tired, and his soul still wants water. So it will be for all the nations that fight Mount Zion.
Be amazed and shocked. Make yourselves blind and unable to see. Be drunk, but not with wine. Stagger, but not with strong drink.
For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes—the prophets. He has covered your heads—the prophets who see visions.
For you, this whole vision is like words in a sealed book. If someone who can read gets it, he says, "I cannot read it, because it is sealed."
If someone who cannot read gets it, he says, "I do not know how to read."
Then the LORD said, "Because these people come near Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their fear of Me is only rules that men taught.
So I will do something amazing again to these people. I will do one wonder after another. The wise men's wisdom will die. The smart men's understanding will be hidden."
Oh no to those who go deep to hide their plans from the LORD. They do their work in the dark. They say, "Who sees us? Who knows us?"
You have turned things upside down. It is like the pot maker is counted as clay. Can the pot say to the pot maker, "You did not make me"? Can the jar say to the pot maker, "He does not understand"?
In a very short time, Lebanon will become good farm land. Good farm land will be like a forest.
On that day, deaf people will hear the words of the book. Blind people's eyes will see out of the dark and gloom.
The humble will have more joy in the LORD. The poor will be glad in the Holy One of Israel.
The cruel will be gone. The mockers will end. All who look for evil will be stopped.
They make a person sin with words. They trap the one who speaks for what is right at the gate. They take away justice from an innocent person with empty charges.
So the LORD, who saved Abraham, says, "Jacob will not be ashamed anymore. His face will not turn pale anymore.
For when he sees his children, the work of My hands among them, they will honor My name. They will honor the Holy One of Jacob. They will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Then people who go the wrong way in spirit will learn. People who complain will learn the lesson."
How sad for the stubborn children, says the the LORD. You make plans that are not Mine. You trust in help that is not from My Spirit. You add sin to sin.
They go down to Egypt without asking Me. They go there to be safe under Pharaoh. They want Egypt to protect them.
But Pharaoh's help will bring you shame. Egypt's protection will bring you disgrace.
Their leaders are at Zoan. Their messengers have reached Hanes.
Everyone will be ashamed because they trusted in people who cannot help them. Those people bring no help or good. They bring only shame and disgrace.

This is a message about the animals in the south. The road goes through a hard and scary land. There are lions and young lions. There are snakes and flying snakes. People carry their money on donkeys' backs. They carry their treasures on camels' backs. They go to a nation that cannot help them.
Egypt's help is useless and empty. That is why I call Egypt 'Rahab who does nothing.'
Go now and write this on a tablet. Write it in a book. It will be a witness for the days to come, forever.
These people are stubborn. They are children who lie. They do not want to listen to the the LORD's teaching.
They say to the seers, "Do not see." They say to the prophets, "Do not tell us what is right. Speak nice words to us. Tell us false hopes."
They say, "Leave the road. Turn away from the path. Stop bringing the Holy One of Israel before us."
So the Holy One of Israel says: "You have rejected this message. You trust in force and lies. You lean on them.
So your sin will be like a crack in a high wall. It bulges out and is ready to fall. Its crash will come all at once.
It will break like a clay jar. It will shatter so much that no piece will be left to carry coals from a fire or to get water from a well."
For the Lord, the the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: "You would be saved if you turned back to God and rested. Your strength would be quiet trust. But you did not want it."
You said, "No, we will run away on horses." So you will run away. You said, "We will ride fast horses." So your enemies will be fast too.
One enemy will make a thousand of you run. Five enemies will make you all run. You will be left alone like a flag on a mountain, like a banner on a hill.
Yet the the LORD wants to be kind to you. So He gets up to show you mercy. The the LORD is a fair God. Happy are all who wait for Him.
People in Zion, who live in Jerusalem, you will not cry anymore. He will be kind when you cry for help. When He hears you, He will answer.
The Lord will give you hard bread and bitter water. But your Teacher will not hide anymore. You will see Him with your own eyes.
When you go right or left, you will hear a voice behind you say, "This is the way. Walk in it."
Then you will make your silver idols dirty. You will throw away your gold statues. You will throw them away like dirty rags and say, "Get out!"
Then He will send rain on the seeds you plant. The food from the land will be rich and full. On that day, your animals will eat in open fields.
The oxen and donkeys that work the land will eat food mixed with salt. It will be cleaned with shovels and forks.
On every high mountain and hill, streams of water will flow. On the day when many are killed and towers fall,
the moon will shine like the sun. The sun will be seven times brighter, like seven days of light. This will be on the day the the LORD binds up His people's hurts and heals their wounds.
Look! The name of the the LORD comes from far away. His anger burns. His load is heavy. His lips are full of anger. His tongue is like a fire that burns everything.
His breath is like a rushing flood. It rises to the neck. He comes to sift the nations in a sieve of ruin. A bit in the mouths of the peoples makes them go the wrong way.
You will sing like on a holy festival night. Your heart will be glad like someone walking with a flute. You will go up to the mountain of the the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
The the LORD will make His mighty voice heard. He will show His arm in anger, with strong anger, burning fire, storms, and hailstones.
For the voice of the the LORD will break Assyria. He will hit them with His rod.
Every blow from the rod the the LORD brings down on them will be with tambourines and harps. He will fight them with His weapons.

Topheth has been ready for a long time. It was made ready for the king. Its fire pit is deep and wide. It has much fire and wood. The breath of the the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, sets it on fire.

Oh no! Some people go down to Egypt for help. They trust in horses. They trust in many war carts. They trust in horse riders because they are very strong. But they do not look to the Holy One of Israel. They do not ask the LORD for help.
But God is wise. He brings trouble. He does not take back His words. He will stand against the homes of bad people. He will stand against those who help people do wrong.
But Egypt has people, not God. Their horses are just flesh, not spirit. When the LORD holds out His hand, the helper and the one helped will both stumble. They will all fall and die together.

The LORD said to me, "A lion growls over its food. A young lion does too. Many shepherds may call out to it. But it is not scared by their voices. It does not care about their noise. In the same way, the LORD of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill."
Like birds flying overhead, the LORD of Armies will protect Jerusalem. He will guard it. He will save it. He will pass over it and keep it safe.
Come back to the One you all have turned far away from, children of Israel.
On that day, each of you will throw away your silver idols and gold idols that your own hands made.
Then Assyria will fall. No man's sword will kill him. A sword not made by man will destroy him. He will run away from the sword. His young men will be forced to work hard.
His strong rock will pass away in fear. His leaders will panic at the battle flag," says the LORD. "His fire is in Zion, and His furnace is in Jerusalem."
Look! A king will rule in a fair way.
Leaders will rule with fairness. Each one will be like a safe place from wind and from a storm, like streams of water in dry land, like shade from a big rock in a tired land.
Then people who see will keep their eyes open. People who hear will listen.
A person who is quick to act will learn and understand. People who stutter will speak clearly.
No longer will a foolish person be called good. No longer will a selfish person be called kind.
A foolish person talks nonsense. His mind plans bad things. He does bad things. He lies about the LORD. He leaves hungry people with nothing. He keeps thirsty people from drink.
A selfish person's ways are bad. He makes bad plans to hurt poor people with lies. He does this even when needy people ask for what is right.
But a good person makes good plans. He stands up for good things.
“Get up, you women who feel safe! Listen to my voice. Pay attention to my words, you daughters who feel safe.
In a little more than a year, you safe women will shake with fear. The grape harvest will fail. There will be no new wine.
“Shake with fear, you women who feel safe! Tremble, you women who are too sure! Take off your clothes and put on rough cloth.
Beat your chests in sadness for the good fields, for the vines that gave fruit.”
Thorns and weeds will grow on My people's land. They will grow on all the happy homes in the joyful city.
The palace will be left empty. The city full of people will be left alone. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever. Wild donkeys will enjoy them. Flocks of sheep will eat there.
This will last until the Spirit is poured out on us from above. Then the dry land will become good land. Good land will seem like a forest.
Then what is right will live in the wild land. What is good will stay in the good land.
Doing what is right will bring peace. Serving what is right will bring calm trust forever.
Then My people will live in a peaceful place. They will live in safe tents and safe homes.
But hail will knock down the forest. The city will sink down to low places.
You will be happy if you plant seeds by all the water and let the ox and donkey walk free.

Oh no, you destroyer! You have not been destroyed yet. You traitor! No one has turned on you yet. But when you stop destroying, you will be destroyed. When you stop being a traitor, people will turn on you.
The LORD, be kind to us. We wait for You. Be our strength each morning. Save us when we are in trouble.
When You speak, people run away. When You stand up, nations scatter.
Your things that were taken will be gathered up like caterpillars gather. People will rush on them like locusts swarm.
The LORD is great. He lives high above. He filled Zion with what is fair and right.
He will be a strong base for your times. He gives much salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Honoring the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
Look! Their brave fighters cry in the streets. The messengers of peace cry hard.
The roads are empty. Travelers stop going. The agreement is broken. Cities are hated. People are not respected anymore.
The land is sad and weak. Lebanon is ashamed and dries up. Sharon is like a desert. Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.
“Now I will stand up,” says the LORD. “Now I will raise Myself. Now I will be great.”
You make empty plans. You bring forth useless straw. Your own breath is like fire that will burn you up.
People will be burned like lime. Cut thorns will be set on fire.
You who are far away, listen to what I did. You who are near, know My power.
Sinners in Zion are scared. Shaking grabs the people who pretend to be good. They ask, “Who can live with a fire that eats? Who can live with flames that never end?”
The one who lives right and speaks truth refuses money from cheating. He will not take bribes. He closes his ears to plans to kill. He shuts his eyes so he does not look at evil.
He will live high up. His safe place will be strong rocks. His food will be given. His water will be sure.
Your eyes will see the King in His beauty. They will see a land far away.
Your mind will think about the old fear: “Where is the one who keeps records? Where is the one who weighs? Where is the one who counts the towers?”
You will not see the mean people anymore. They speak a language you do not understand. They stammer in words you cannot figure out.

Look at Zion, the city of our festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem. It will be a safe place to live. It will be like a tent that is not moved. Its stakes will never be pulled up. None of its ropes will break.
But there the the LORD, who is great, will be for us. It will be a place of rivers and wide waters. No boat with oars will go there. No big ship will pass by.
The LORD is our judge. the LORD makes our laws. the LORD is our King. He will save us.
Your ropes are loose. They cannot hold the mast up. They cannot spread the sail. Then a lot of treasure will be shared. Even people who cannot walk will take stolen things.
No one living in Zion will say, “I am sick.” The people living there will be forgiven for their sins.
Come near, you nations. Listen. Pay attention, you peoples. Let the earth hear. Let all that fills it hear. Let the whole world hear, and all its people.
The LORD is angry with all the nations. He is furious with all their armies. He will destroy them all. He will give them over to be killed.
Their dead will be left on the ground. The smell of their bodies will rise up. The mountains will be soaked with their blood.
All the stars in the sky will fade away. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll. All the stars will fall like dry leaves from a grapevine. They will fall like leaves from a fig tree.
My sword has been used in heaven. Now it will come down on Edom. It will bring judgment on the people I set apart to be destroyed.

The sword of the LORD is covered with blood. It is full of fat. It has blood from lambs and goats. It has fat from the kidneys of rams. For the LORD will make a sacrifice in Bozrah. It will be a great killing in Edom.
Wild cattle will fall with them. Young bulls will fall with the strong bulls. Their land will be soaked with blood. Their soil will be rich with fat.
For the LORD has a day of payback. It is the year He pays back those who hurt Zion.
Edom’s streams will turn to tar. Its soil will turn to sulfur. Its land will keep burning.
The fire will not go out day or night. Its smoke will rise forever. From one generation to the next, the land will stay empty. No one will ever walk through it again.
Owls and other night birds will live there. Ravens will live there too. He will mark the land to make it empty and ruined.
Its leaders will have no kingdom left to rule. All its princes will be gone.
Thorns will grow over its forts. Weeds and thorny plants will grow in its strong places. It will be a home for wild dogs and a place for ostriches.
Wild animals of the desert will meet hyenas there. One wild goat will call to another. A night animal will rest there and find a safe place.
The owl will build a nest there and lay eggs. She will hatch them and keep them in her shade. Hunting birds will gather there, each with its mate.
Look in the book of the LORD and read. Not one of these animals will be missing. Not one will be without its mate. His mouth has commanded it. His Spirit has gathered them.
He has chosen their places. His hand has measured it out for them. They will own it forever. From one generation to the next, they will live there.
The desert and dry land will be happy. The empty land will be happy and bloom like a flower.

It will bloom and be very happy. It will sing with joy. The beauty of Lebanon will be given to it. The beauty of Carmel and Sharon will be given to it. People will see the the LORD's great beauty, the beauty of our God.
Make weak hands strong. Make weak knees strong.
Say to people with scared hearts, "Be strong. Do not be afraid. Look, your God will come to punish. He will pay back what is owed, and He will save you."
Then blind people will see, and deaf people will hear.
Then people who cannot walk will jump like deer. People who cannot speak will sing with joy. Water will pour out in the desert. Streams will flow in the dry land.
Hot sand will become a pool. Dry ground will have springs of water. Where jackals live, grass and tall plants will grow.
A road will be there. It will be called the Way of Holiness. People who are not clean will not walk on it. It is for people who walk that way. Even people who do not know much will not get lost.
No lion will be there. No wild animal will walk on it. They will not be found there. But saved people will walk there.

The people the the LORD has set free will come back. They will enter Zion singing. They will be crowned with joy that never ends. Joy and gladness will catch up with them. Sorrow and sighing will run away.
In the 14th year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, attacked all the strong towns in Judah. He took them.
The king of Assyria sent his leader, Rabshakeh, from Lachish to Jerusalem. He brought a big army. Rabshakeh stood by the upper pool on the road to the field where clothes were washed.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah was in charge of the palace. Shebna was the writer. Joah son of Asaph wrote things down. They came out to meet him.
Rabshakeh said, "Tell Hezekiah this. The great king, the king of Assyria, says, 'What are you trusting in?'
I say your plans and your power for war are just talk. Who do you trust? Why did you turn against me?
Look, you trust in Egypt. But Egypt is like a broken stick. If a man leans on it, it will break and cut his hand. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is like that to all who trust in him.
Maybe you will say, 'We trust in the LORD our God.' But isn't He the God whose hilltop altars Hezekiah took away? Hezekiah told Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship at this altar.'
Now make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you 2,000 horses if you can find riders for them.
How could you turn back even one of my master's smallest officers? Yet you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen.
I did not come here without the LORD to destroy this land. The LORD told me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to us in Aramaic. We understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew where the people on the wall can hear."
Rabshakeh said, "My master did not send me to speak only to your master and to you. He sent me to speak to the men on the wall too. They will eat their own waste and drink their own urine with you."
Then Rabshakeh stood and shouted in Hebrew, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
The king says, 'Do not let Hezekiah trick you. He cannot save you.'
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD. He says, 'The LORD will save us. This city will not be given to the king of Assyria.'
Do not listen to Hezekiah. The king of Assyria says, 'Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own grapevine and fig tree and drink from his own well.'
I will come and take you to a land like your own land. It will have grain, new wine, bread, and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah fool you. He says, 'The LORD will save us.' Has any god of any nation saved his land from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they save Samaria from me?
None of the gods of these lands saved their countries from me. So The LORD will not save Jerusalem from me."
The people stayed quiet and did not answer him, because the king had said, "Do not answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the writer, and Joah son of Asaph, who wrote things down, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn. They told him what Rabshakeh had said.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the writer, and the older priests. They were wearing sackcloth. He sent them to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
They said to him, "Hezekiah says today is a day of trouble, blame, and shame. We are like a mother ready to have a baby, but she has no strength to push.

Maybe the the LORD your God heard what Rabshakeh said. The king of Assyria sent him to make fun of the living God. Maybe the the LORD your God will show he is wrong. So pray for the people who are left."
King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master the the LORD says this: Do not be afraid of the words you heard. The servants of the king of Assyria made fun of Me.
Look, I will put a spirit in him. He will hear news and go home. Then I will make him die by a sword in his own land."
Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish. He went back and found the king fighting against Libnah.
He heard that Tirhakah, king of Cush, was coming to fight him. So he sent messengers to Hezekiah.
They said, "Tell Hezekiah, king of Judah: Do not let your God fool you. You trust in Him, but He says Jerusalem will not be given to the king of Assyria. Do not believe Him.
Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria did to all the lands. They destroyed them. Do you think you will be saved?
Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed save them? Did they save Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath? Where is the king of Arpad? Where is the king of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?"
Hezekiah took the letters from the messengers and read them. Then he went up to the house of the the LORD and spread them out before the the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed to the the LORD. He said,
"the the LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, You sit above the cherubim. You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Please listen, the the LORD, and hear. Please look, the the LORD, and see. Hear all the words Sennacherib sent to mock the living God.
It is true, the the LORD. The kings of Assyria have destroyed all the nations and their lands.
They threw their gods into the fire. Those were not gods at all. They were made by people. They were made of wood and stone. So the Assyrians destroyed them.
Now, the the LORD our God, save us from his hand. Then all the kingdoms of the earth will know that You alone are the the LORD."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah. He said, "This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you prayed to Me about Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard you.
This is what the the LORD says about him: The young woman of Zion looks down on you and laughs at you. The people of Jerusalem shake their heads at you.
Who have you mocked and made fun of? Who did you shout at? You raised your eyes against the Holy One of Israel!

By your servants you mocked the Lord. You said you took your many chariots up to the high mountains, to the far sides of Lebanon. You said you cut down its tallest cedars and its best cypress trees. You said you went to its farthest height and its thickest forest.
You said you dug wells and drank water. You said that with the soles of your feet you dried up all the rivers of Egypt.
Have you not heard? I did this long ago. I planned it long ago. Now I have made it happen. You turned strong cities into piles of rocks.
The people who lived there were weak. They were afraid and put to shame. They were like grass in a field and green plants. They were like grass on a roof and grain burned before it grows.
But I know when you sit down, when you go out, and when you come in. I know how angry you are at Me.
Because you are angry at Me and your proud words reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bridle in your lips. I will make you go back the same way you came."

"This will be a sign for you: This year you will eat what grows on its own. The second year you will eat what grows from that. But in the third year you will plant and harvest. You will plant grapevines and eat their fruit.
The people left in Judah will grow roots down and bear fruit up.
For a people will go out from Jerusalem. Survivors will come from Mount Zion. The the LORD of Hosts will do this."

"So this is what the the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not come into this city. He will not shoot an arrow here. He will not come near it with a shield. He will not build a ramp against its walls.
He will go back the same way he came. He will not come into this city," says the the LORD.
"I will protect this city and save it. I will do it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David."
Then the angel of the the LORD went out. He struck 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. In the morning, people got up early. They saw that all of them were dead.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria left. He went home and stayed in Nineveh.
While he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword. They ran away to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon became king after him.

In those days, Hezekiah got very sick. The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, came to him and said, "This is what the the LORD says: Get your things in order, because you are going to die and will not get well."
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the the LORD.
He said, "Please, the LORD, remember how I have lived for You with a true heart. I have done what is good in Your eyes." Then Hezekiah cried very hard.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Isaiah.
He said, "Go and tell Hezekiah that the the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I heard your prayer. I saw your tears. I will give you fifteen more years to live.
I will save you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will keep this city safe.
This will be a sign for you from the the LORD that the the LORD will do what He said. I will make the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz."
So the sun moved back ten steps on the stairway where it had gone down.
This is what Hezekiah, king of Judah, wrote after he was sick and got well again:
"I said, 'In the middle of my life, I must go to the gates of the grave. I am losing the rest of my years.'
I said, 'I will not see the the LORD in the land of the living. I will not look at people in this world anymore.'
My home is taken from me, like a tent is taken down. My life is rolled up like cloth by a weaver. He cuts me off from the loom. From day to night, You bring me to an end.
"I waited until morning. Like a lion, He breaks all my bones. From day to night, You bring me to an end.
I cried out like a bird. I moaned like a dove. My eyes grew weak as I looked up. Lord, I am in trouble. Please help me.
What can I say? He spoke to me and did this. I will live quietly all my years because my heart is bitter.
"Lord, people live by these things. All these things give life to my spirit. You will make me well and let me live.
Look, I had bitter pain, but it brought me peace. You loved me and saved my soul from the deep pit. You threw all my sins behind Your back.
The grave cannot praise You. Death cannot sing to You. Those who go down to the pit cannot hope in Your truth.
"The living, the living, they praise You, as I do today. Fathers tell their children about Your truth.
The LORD saved me, so we will sing and play music all our lives in the house of the the LORD."
Isaiah said, "Take a lump of figs and put it on the sore, and he will get well."
Hezekiah asked, "What sign will show that I will go up to the house of the the LORD?"
At that time, Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah. He had heard that Hezekiah was sick and got well.

Hezekiah was happy to see them. He showed them his treasure room. He showed them silver, gold, spices, and fine oil. He also showed them his weapons and everything in his storage rooms. He did not hide anything in his house or in all his land.
Then Isaiah the prophet went to King Hezekiah. He asked, "What did those men say? Where did they come from?" Hezekiah said, "They came from far away. They came from Babylon."
Isaiah asked, "What did they see in your house?" Hezekiah said, "They saw everything in my house. I did not keep anything back from them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Listen to what the LORD of Armies says.
Days are coming. Everything in your house will be carried to Babylon. So will the things your fathers saved up until now. Nothing will be left," says the LORD.
"Some of your children, your own sons who will be born to you, will be taken away. They will be servants in the palace of the king of Babylon."
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you spoke is good." He thought, "There will be peace and safety while I live."
“Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.
“Speak kindly to Jerusalem. Tell her that her hard work is done. Her sin is forgiven. She got twice the punishment from the LORD for all her sins.”
A voice calls out, “Get the road ready for the LORD in the wild land. Make a straight path for our God in the desert.”
Every valley will be raised up. Every mountain and hill will be lowered. The crooked ground will be made straight. The rough places will be made flat.
The LORD's glory will be shown. All people will see it together. The LORD has spoken.
A voice says, “Cry out!” I asked, “What should I cry?” “All people are like grass. All their beauty is like a flower in the field.
“The grass dries up. The flower fades when the LORD's breath blows on it. Yes, people are like grass.
The grass dries up. The flower fades. But the word of our God stands forever.”

Go up on a high mountain, O Zion, you who bring good news. Raise your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, you who bring good news. Raise it. Do not be afraid. Say to the towns of Judah, “Here is your God!”
See, the Lord the LORD comes with power. His arm rules for Him. His reward is with Him. His payment goes before Him.
He will feed His flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in His arm and hold them close to His heart. He will gently lead the mother sheep.
Who measured the water in the hollow of His hand? Who marked off the sky with His hand? Who held the dust of the earth in a small cup? Who weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills on a balance?
Who has told the LORD's Spirit what to do? Who has given the LORD advice?
Who did He ask for help? Who taught Him what is right? Who taught Him what He knows? Who showed Him the way to understand?
The nations are like a drop in a bucket. They are like dust on the scales. See, He lifts up the islands like fine dust.
Lebanon is not enough wood for a fire. Its animals are not enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are nothing to Him. They are like nothing and empty.
Who can you compare God to? What picture can you compare Him to?
To an idol? A worker makes it. A goldsmith covers it with gold and makes silver chains for it.
A poor man who cannot give a big gift chooses wood that will not rot. He finds a good worker to set up an idol that will not fall.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been told to you from the start? Have you not understood since the world was made?
He sits above the circle of the earth. The people on it are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the sky like a cloth. He spreads it like a tent to live in.
He makes leaders come to nothing. He makes the judges of the earth useless.
They are planted and sown. They take root in the ground. But He blows on them, and they dry up. A storm carries them away like straw.
“To whom will you compare Me? Or who is My equal?” asks the Holy One.
Look up at the sky. Who made all these? He brings out the stars and calls each one by name. Because He is so strong and powerful, not one is missing.
Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you speak, O Israel, “my way is hidden from the LORD, and my God ignores my case”?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the God who lives forever. He made the ends of the earth. He does not get tired or weary. No one can understand His wisdom.
He gives power to tired people. He gives strength to people with no power.
Even young people get tired and weary. Young men trip and fall.
But people who wait on the LORD will get new strength. They will fly high like eagles. They will run and not get tired. They will walk and not get weary.
“Be quiet before Me, O islands. Let the people get strong again. Let them come near and speak. Let us meet together and decide who is right.
Who called a man from the east to serve Him the right way? God gives nations to him and beats kings. He makes them like dust with his sword, like straw blown by the wind with his bow.
He chases them and keeps going safely. He barely touches the ground as he walks.
Who did this and made it happen? Who called people from the start? I am the LORD—the first and the last. I am He.”
The islands see this and are afraid. The far ends of the earth shake. They come closer and gather.
Each person helps the next one and says to his brother, “Be strong!”
The worker helps the gold worker. The one who smooths metal with a hammer helps the one who hits the anvil. He says about the solder, “It is good.” Then he nails it so it will not move.
“But you, Israel, are My servant. Jacob, I chose you. You come from Abraham, who is My friend.
I brought you from the far ends of the earth. I called you from its far corners. I said to you, ‘You are My servant. I chose you and did not turn away from you.’
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. Do not be upset, for I am your God. I will make you strong. I will help you. I will hold you up with My right hand that does right.”
“See, all who are angry at you will be ashamed. Those who argue with you will come to nothing and die.
You will look for them but not find them. Those who fight you will become nothing, like they never lived.
For I am the LORD your God. I hold your right hand. I say to you, ‘Do not be afraid. I will help you.’”
“Do not be afraid, O Jacob, you worm, O Israel. I will help you,” declares the LORD. “Your Savior is the Holy One of Israel.”
“See, I will make you like a new, sharp threshing tool with many teeth. You will crush the mountains and grind them down. You will turn the hills into straw.
You will toss them, and the wind will carry them away. The storm will scatter them. But you will be glad in the LORD. You will praise the Holy One of Israel.”
“Poor people and needy people look for water, but there is none. Their tongues are dry with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not leave them.
I will open rivers on the dry hills. I will make springs in the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water. I will turn the dry land into flowing springs.
I will plant cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive trees in the desert. I will put pine, fir, and cypress trees together in the dry valley.
Then all will see and know. They will think and understand that the hand of the LORD did this. The Holy One of Israel made it.”
