Jerusalem, wash the bad from your heart, so you may be saved. How long will you keep bad thoughts?
A voice tells from Dan. It tells of trouble from Mount Ephraim.
Tell the nations. Tell Jerusalem that enemies are coming from a far land. They shout against the cities of Judah.
They surround her like men who guard a field, because she turned against Me, says the LORD.
"Your ways and your deeds brought this on you. This is your punishment. It is bitter. It has reached your heart!"
My pain! My pain! I hurt inside. My heart pounds. I cannot be quiet. I heard the horn. I heard the war alarm.
One trouble comes after another. The whole land is ruined. My tents are broken. My curtains are torn in a moment.
How long must I see the flag of war and hear the horn?
"My people are foolish. They do not know Me. They are silly children. They do not understand. They are smart at doing bad. They do not know how to do good."
I looked at the earth. It was empty and bare. I looked at the sky. Its light was gone.
I looked at the mountains. They were shaking. All the hills moved.
I looked. There was no person. All the birds of the sky had flown away.
I looked. The good land was a desert. All its cities were broken before the LORD, before His fierce anger.
This is what the LORD says: "The whole land will be empty. But I will not destroy it all.
So the earth will be sad. The sky above will grow dark. I have spoken, and I will not change My mind. I have decided, and I will not turn back."
At the sound of the horseman and the bowman, all the people run away. They hide in thick bushes and climb on rocks. Every city is left empty. No one lives in them.
And you, ruined one, what will you do? You may wear red. You may wear gold. You may paint your eyes. But it is for nothing. Your lovers hate you. They want to kill you.

I hear a cry like a woman having a baby. It is a cry of pain like a woman having her first baby. It is the cry of Zion's daughter. She gasps for breath. She holds out her hands. "Oh no! I am weak. Murderers are killing me!"

Run back and forth through the streets of Jerusalem. Look and learn. Search the town squares. If you find even one man, if one person does what is right and wants to be faithful, then I will forgive the city.
Even when they say, "I swear by the LORD," they are lying.

O the LORD, don't Your eyes look for truth? You struck them, but they did not feel pain. You wore them out, but they would not take correction. They made their faces harder than rock. They would not turn back.
I said, "Surely they are only poor. They have acted foolishly, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the law of their God."
I will go to the great ones and speak to them, for they know the way of the LORD, the law of their God. But these people have thrown off God's rule together. They have broken free from His control.

So a lion from the forest will attack them. A wolf from the desert will destroy them. A leopard will wait near their cities. Everyone who goes out will be torn apart, because their sins are many and they keep turning away from God.
"How can I forgive you? Your children have left Me and sworn by gods that are not real. I gave them what they needed, but they were not faithful to Me. They crowded into a prostitute's house.
They were like well-fed horses. Each one wanted his neighbor's wife.
"Should I not punish them for this? Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?" says the LORD.
Go up through her vineyards and destroy them, but do not destroy everything. Cut off her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.
"For the family of Israel and the family of Judah have been very unfaithful to Me," says the LORD.
They have lied about the LORD and said, "He will not do anything. No trouble will come to us. We will not see war or hunger."
The prophets are just wind. God's word is not in them. So may what they say happen to them.
So this is what the LORD God of Armies says: "Because you have spoken this word, look, I will make My words in your mouth like fire. This people will be like wood, and the fire will burn them up.
Look, I am bringing a nation from far away against you, people of Israel," says the LORD. "It is a very old nation. You do not know its language, and you will not understand what it says."
Their arrows are like an open grave. All their soldiers are strong.

They will eat your harvest and your food. They will eat your sons and daughters. They will eat your flocks and herds. They will eat your vines and fig trees. With the sword they will destroy the strong cities you trust in.
"Yet even in those days," says the LORD, "I will not destroy you completely."

"When you ask why the the LORD our God did all this to us, you are to tell them that just as you left Me and served other gods in your land, you will serve foreign people in a land that is not yours."
Tell this in the family of Jacob. Announce it in Judah.
"Listen to this, foolish people, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear."

"Do you not fear Me?" says the LORD. "Do you not shake before Me? I made the sand a wall for the sea. It is a limit that lasts forever, and the sea cannot cross it. Its waves may crash, but they cannot win. They may roar, but they cannot cross it.
But these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts. They have turned away and gone.
They do not say in their hearts that they should fear the the LORD our God, who gives rain at the right time, both fall and spring rain, and keeps the harvest time for us.
Your sins have turned these good things away. Your sins have kept good from you.
For wicked men are found among My people. They hide like bird catchers. They set traps and catch people.
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of tricks. That is why they became great and rich.
They are fat and smooth. They do very bad things. They do not help orphans, and they do not stand up for poor people.
"Should I not punish them for this? Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?" says the LORD.
A terrible and shocking thing has happened in the land.
The prophets say false things. The priests rule by their own power. My people love it that way. But what will you do in the end?
People of Benjamin, run for safety! Leave Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa! Raise a signal at Beth-haccerem! Great trouble is coming from the north.
I compare the daughter of Zion to a beautiful, gentle woman.
Shepherds and their flocks will come to her. They will set up tents all around her. Each man will feed in his own place.
"Get ready for war against her! Get up! Let's attack at noon! Oh no, the day is fading! The evening shadows are stretching out."
"Get up! Let's attack at night! Let's destroy her big houses!"
The LORD of Armies says, "Cut down trees and pile up dirt against Jerusalem. This city must be punished. It is full of trouble inside."
Just as a well pours out fresh water, she pours out fresh evil. People hear about violence and stealing there. Sickness and wounds are always before Me.
The LORD says, "Jerusalem, let this be a warning to you. If not, I will turn away from you. I will make you an empty land where no one lives."
The LORD of Armies says, "The enemy will pick Israel clean like a vine. Go back and pick the branches again, like someone picking grapes."
Who can I talk to and warn? They will not listen. Their ears are closed. They cannot hear. They make fun of the the LORD's word. They do not want it.

But I am full of the the LORD's anger. I am tired of holding it back. So I will pour it out on children in the street and on groups of young men. Husbands and wives will be caught too. Old people and those who have lived long will be caught.
Their houses, fields, and wives will go to other people. I will punish the people who live in this land, says the the LORD.
From the small to the great, all want money. From prophet to priest, all tell lies.
They have treated My people's hurt like it is no big deal. They say, "Peace, peace," but there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they did terrible things? No, they were not ashamed at all. They did not even know how to blush. So they will fall with others who fall. When I punish them, they will trip, says the the LORD.
The LORD says, "Stand where roads meet and look. Ask for the old ways. Ask which way is good. Walk in it. Then your souls will find rest." But they said, "We will not go."
The LORD says, "I put guards over you. Listen to the trumpet sound." But they said, "We will not listen."
So listen, nations. Know, people, what will happen to them.
Listen, earth! I am bringing trouble on these people. It comes from their own plans. They did not listen to My words. They turned away from My law.
Why do you bring Me sweet smoke from Sheba and sweet cane from far away? Your burned gifts do not please Me. Your gifts do not make Me happy.
The LORD says, "I will put things that make these people trip. Fathers and sons will trip over them together. Neighbors and friends will die."
The LORD says, "Look! People are coming from the north. A great nation is coming from far away.
They carry bows and spears. They are mean and show no mercy. Their sound is like the sea. They ride horses. They are ready for war against you, daughter of Zion."
We heard the news. Our hands are weak. Trouble has grabbed us. Pain has grabbed us like a woman giving birth.
Do not go out to the field. Do not walk on the road. The enemy has a sword. Fear is all around.
Daughter of My people, wear rough cloth. Roll in ashes. Mourn like you lost your only child. Cry loudly, because the destroyer will suddenly come against us.
I have made you a tester of metals among My people. You will know and test their ways.
They are all stubborn. They go around telling lies. They are like bronze and iron. They all destroy.
The air pump blows hard. The lead melts. The fire burns for nothing. The bad people are not taken away.
They are called rejected silver, because the the LORD has rejected them.
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD.
The LORD said, "Stand at the gate of the LORD's house. Say this message there: 'Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who come through these gates to worship the LORD.'"
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says, "Make your ways and your actions better. Then I will let you live in this place.
Do not trust in false words and say, 'This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD.'
If you really make your ways and actions better, and if you really do what is right between a person and his neighbor,

if you do not hurt the stranger, the child with no father, or the woman whose husband died, and if you do not kill innocent people in this place, and if you do not follow other gods and hurt yourselves,
then I will let you live in this place, in the land I gave to your fathers long ago and forever."
But look, you trust in false words that do not help.
Will you steal, kill, cheat on your husband or wife, lie in court, burn incense to Baal, and follow gods you do not know?
Then you come and stand in front of Me in this house that has My name on it. You say, "We are safe now," but then you go and do all these bad things again.
Has this house, which has My name on it, become a cave for robbers to you? Look, I have seen it, says the LORD.
Go to My place in Shiloh. That is where I first put My name. See what I did to it because of the bad things My people Israel did.
Now, because you have done all these things, says the LORD, and because I spoke to you again and again but you did not listen, and I called you but you did not answer,
I will do to this house, which has My name on it, the same thing I did to Shiloh. I will do it to the place you trust in. I will do it to the place I gave to you and your fathers.
I will throw you out of My sight, just as I threw out all your brothers, all the children of Ephraim.
As for you, do not pray for these people. Do not cry out or pray for them. Do not ask Me to help them, because I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The sons gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women mix dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven. They pour out drinks for other gods to make Me angry.
But are they making Me angry? says the LORD. They are hurting themselves and bringing shame on themselves.
So this is what the Lord GOD says: My anger and My great anger will pour out on this place. It will hit people and animals. It will hit trees and crops. It will burn and will not go out.
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves."
When I brought your fathers out of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices.
But I gave them this command: "Obey My voice. Then I will be your God, and you will be My people. Walk in all the ways I command you, so it may go well with you."
But they did not listen. They did not pay attention. They followed the stubborn thoughts of their evil hearts. They got worse, not better.
From the day your fathers left Egypt until now, I have sent you all My servants, the prophets. I sent them again and again.
But they would not listen to Me. They would not pay attention. They were stubborn. They did worse than their fathers.
When you tell them all this, they will not listen to you. When you call them, they will not answer you.
So you are to tell them, "This is the nation that would not listen to the LORD their God. They would not take correction. Truth is gone. It is not in their mouths anymore."
Cut off your hair and throw it away. Sing a sad song on the bare hills, because the LORD has rejected and left the people He is angry with.
The sons of Judah have done evil in My sight, says the LORD. They have put their bad things in the house that has My name on it, and made it unclean.
They built places to worship at Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom. There they burned their sons and daughters in the fire. I did not command this. It never came into My mind.

So the days are coming, says the LORD, when people will not call it Topheth or the Valley of Hinnom. They will call it the Valley of Slaughter. They will bury people in Topheth until there is no room.
The dead bodies of these people will be food for birds and wild animals. No one will scare them away.
I will take away the happy sounds in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. No one will hear the voice of the bridegroom or the bride. The land will become an empty land.
"At that time," says the the LORD, "they will take the bones of Judah's kings, leaders, priests, prophets, and the people of Jerusalem out of their graves.

They will spread them in the sun, moon, and stars. They loved and served these things. They followed, asked them for help, and bowed down to them. No one will pick them up or bury them. They will be like waste on the ground.
Wherever I have sent them away, the people left from this bad family will want to die more than live," says the the LORD of Hosts.
"You must tell them this is what the the LORD says: 'Do people fall down and not get up? If someone turns away, do they not come back?'
Why then do these people turn away? Why does Jerusalem keep turning away? They hold tight to lies. They will not come back.
I listened and heard. They do not say what is right. No one is sorry for his bad ways. No one says, 'What did I do?' Everyone runs his own way, like a horse running into battle.
"Even the stork in the sky knows her times. The dove, swallow, and crane know when to go. But My people do not know what the the LORD wants.
How can you say, 'We are wise, and we have the the LORD's rules'? But the writers' pens have made lies.
The wise will be ashamed. They will be scared and trapped. They turned away from the the LORD's word. So what wisdom do they have?
"So I will give their wives to other men. I will give their fields to new owners. From the least to the greatest, all want money. From prophet to priest, all tell lies.
They act like My people's hurt is small. They say, 'Peace, peace,' but there is no peace.

Were they ashamed of the bad things they did? No, they were not ashamed at all. They did not even know how to blush. So they will fall with others who fall. When I punish them, they will fall down," says the the LORD.

"I will take away their harvest," says the the LORD. "There will be no grapes on the vines. There will be no figs on the trees. Even the leaves will dry up. I gave them things, but I will take them away."

"Why do we sit here? Come, let us go to the strong cities and die there. The the LORD our God has let bad things happen to us. He gave us poison water to drink, because we sinned against the the LORD.
We hoped for peace, but nothing good came. We hoped for healing, but there was only fear."
We hear the horses snort in Dan. The whole land shakes at the sound of the strong horses. They come to eat up the land and all in it, the city and the people in it.
"I will send snakes among you. They are snakes no one can charm. They will bite you," says the the LORD.
My joy is gone. I am full of grief. My heart is sick.
Listen to the cry of my people from far away: "Is the the LORD not in Zion anymore? Is her King not there anymore?" "Why did they make Me angry with their carved statues and empty idols?"
"The harvest is past. Summer is over. But we are not saved."
I am hurt because my people are hurt. I am sad. Fear holds me.
Is there no medicine in Gilead? Is there no doctor there? Why then are my people not healed?
I wish my head were full of water. I wish my eyes made tears like a spring. Then I could cry day and night for my people who were killed.
If I had a small house in the desert, I would leave my people. They all break their promises. They are not true to God.
"They use their words like bows to shoot lies. Lies win over truth in the land. They go from one bad thing to another. They do not know Me.
Be careful with your friends. Do not trust your brothers. Every brother tricks people. Every friend tells lies about others.
Each person tricks the person next door. They do not tell the truth. They have taught their tongues to lie. They work hard to do wrong.
You live among lies. In their tricks, they refuse to know Me," says the LORD.
So the LORD of Armies says: "Look, I will clean them like metal in fire. I will test them. What else can I do for My people?
Their tongues are like deadly arrows. They speak lies. With their mouths they say peace to a friend, but in their hearts they plan a trap.
Should I not punish them for these things? Should I not pay them back, this nation?" says the LORD.

I will cry and wail for the mountains. I will sing a sad song for the grass in the wild places. They are burned, so no one walks there. No cows are heard. The birds and animals have run away. They are gone.
"I will make Jerusalem a pile of rocks. Wild dogs will live there. I will make the cities of Judah empty. No one will live there," says the LORD.
Who is wise enough to understand this? Who has heard the LORD speak, so he can tell it? Why is the land ruined and burned like a desert, so no one walks through?
The LORD says, "They left My law, which I gave them. They did not live by it. They did not obey My voice.
Instead, they followed their own stubborn hearts. They worshiped the false gods called Baal. Their fathers taught them to do this."
So the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I will feed these people bitter food. I will give them poisoned water to drink.
I will scatter them among nations they and their fathers did not know. I will send war after them until they are gone," says the LORD.
The LORD of Armies says: "Think about this. Call the women who cry at funerals. Send for them. Let them come.
Let them come fast. Let them cry for us. Then our eyes will fill with tears. Our eyelids will pour water.
A crying voice is heard from Jerusalem: 'We are ruined! We are very ashamed! We had to leave the land because our homes were torn down.'"
Now, women, listen to the word of the LORD. Let your ears hear what He says. Teach your daughters to cry. Teach each other to sing sad songs.
Death has climbed in through our windows. It has come into our big houses. It takes children from the streets and young men from the town squares.
Say this: "The LORD says, 'Dead bodies will fall like waste in the open field. They will be like cut grain left behind the worker. No one will pick them up.'"
The LORD says, "Do not let a wise man brag about his wisdom. Do not let a strong man brag about his strength. Do not let a rich man brag about his money.

But if someone brags, let him brag about this: He understands Me and knows Me. I am the LORD. I show love, do what is right, and make things fair on earth. I am happy with these things," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD. "I will punish all who have the outside mark but not the inside change.
Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and all who live in the desert and cut the corners of their hair. All the nations are not truly changed. All Israel is not changed in heart."
Listen to the word the the LORD speaks to you, people of Israel.
This is what the the LORD says: "Do not learn the ways of other nations. Do not be scared by signs in the sky. Other nations are scared by them.
The customs of the nations are worthless. They cut down a tree from the forest. A worker shapes it with his tool.
They decorate it with silver and gold. They nail it down with a hammer and nails so it will not fall over.
They are like a scarecrow in a field. They cannot talk. They must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them. They cannot hurt anyone, and they cannot help anyone."
No one is like You, the LORD. You are great, and Your name is strong and powerful.
Everyone should fear You, King of the nations. You deserve it. Among all the wise men of the nations and in all their kingdoms, no one is like You.
They are all foolish. They learn from worthless idols made of wood.
People bring silver from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz. A worker and a goldsmith make the idols. They cover them with blue and purple cloth. Skilled men make all of this.
But the the LORD is the true God. He is the living God and the King forever. The earth shakes when He is angry. The nations cannot stand up to His anger.
So you must tell them this: "The gods who did not make the sky and the earth will disappear from the earth and from under the sky."
God made the earth with His power. He set the world in place with His wisdom. He stretched out the sky with His understanding.
When He thunders, the waters in the sky roar. He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain. He brings the wind out of His storehouses.
Every person is foolish and knows nothing. Every goldsmith is ashamed of his idols. His metal images are a lie. They have no breath.
They are worthless. They are made to trick people. When the time comes for them to be punished, they will be destroyed.
The Portion of Jacob is not like them. He made everything. Israel is the people He chose to be His own. The LORD of Hosts is His name.
Gather your things, people of Zion. You live under attack.
For this is what the the LORD says: "I will throw out the people who live in this land. I will bring trouble on them so they can be caught."
I am so sad because I am broken. My wound hurts. But I said, "This is my sickness, and I must carry it."
My tent is destroyed. All its ropes are cut. My children have left me and are gone. No one is left to set up my tent or hang my curtains.
The leaders are foolish. They do not look for the the LORD. So they have not done well, and all their sheep are scattered.
Listen! News is coming. There is a loud noise from the north. It will make the cities of Judah empty. They will become homes for wild animals.
I know, the LORD, that people cannot choose their own way. No one who walks can direct his own steps.
Correct me, the LORD, but be fair. Do not correct me in Your anger, or You will destroy me.
Pour out Your anger on the nations that do not know You. Pour it on the families that do not pray to You. They have destroyed Jacob. They have wiped him out. They have ruined his home.
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD.
The LORD said, "Listen to the words of this agreement. Tell them to the men of Judah and to the people who live in Jerusalem.
Tell them that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Bad things will happen to the person who does not obey the words of this agreement.

I gave this command to your fathers when I brought them out of Egypt. That place was like a hot iron furnace. I said, "Obey Me. Do everything I tell you to do. Then you will be My people, and I will be your God."
I made this promise to your fathers. I promised to give them a land with plenty of milk and honey. That is still true today.'" Then I answered, "Amen, the LORD."
Then the LORD said to me, "Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Say, 'Listen to the words of this agreement and obey them.'
From the time I brought your fathers out of Egypt until today, I have warned them again and again. I said, 'Obey My voice.'

But they did not listen. They did not pay attention. Each person followed his own stubborn and evil heart. So I brought on them all the curses of this agreement that I commanded them to keep, but they did not keep them."
The LORD said to me, "The men of Judah and the people who live in Jerusalem have made a secret plan against Me.

They have gone back to the sins of their fathers. Their fathers refused to listen to My words. These people followed other gods and served them. The family of Israel and the family of Judah have broken the agreement I made with their fathers."
So the LORD says, "I am going to bring trouble on them. They will not be able to escape it. They will cry out to Me, but I will not listen to them.
Then the cities of Judah and the people who live in Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods they burn spices to. But those gods will not save them when trouble comes.
Judah, you have as many gods as you have cities. You people have set up as many altars to burn spices to Baal as Jerusalem has streets."
The LORD said to me, "Do not pray for these people. Do not cry out or pray for them, because I will not listen when they cry out to Me in their time of trouble."
The LORD says, "Why should My dear people be in My house? They have done many evil things. Can holy meat keep trouble away from you? You do evil, and then you are glad."
The LORD once called you a green olive tree. It was beautiful and full of fruit. But now, with a loud roar, He will set fire to it. Its branches will burn up.
The LORD of Heaven's Armies planted you. But He has said He will bring trouble on you. This is because of the evil of the families of Israel and Judah. They made Him angry by burning spices to Baal.
The LORD told me what was happening, so I knew. Then He showed me what they were doing. "

I was like a gentle lamb being led to be killed. I did not know they had made plans against me. They said they would destroy me like a tree with its fruit. They said they would cut me off from the land of the living, so no one would remember my name.
But the LORD of Heaven's Armies judges fairly. He tests people's hearts and minds. The LORD, let me see You punish them, because I have trusted You with my case."
So the LORD says this about the men of Anathoth who are trying to kill you: They say you must not prophesy in the LORD's name, or you will die by their hands.
So the LORD of Heaven's Armies says, "I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword. Their sons and daughters will die from hunger.
No one will be left among them. I will bring trouble on the men of Anathoth in the year I punish them."
"You are right, the LORD, when I talk with You. But I want to ask You about what is fair. Why do bad people do well? Why do people who break trust feel safe?
You planted them, and they took root. They grow and bear fruit. You are always on their lips, but far from their hearts.
But You know me, the LORD. You see me and test my heart for You. Drag them off like sheep to be killed. Set them apart for the day they will be killed.
How long will the land be sad and all the grass in the fields dry up? The bad things people do have caused this. Even the animals and birds are gone, because they say, 'He will not see how we end.'"
"If you ran with men on foot and they wore you out, how can you race with horses? If you trip in a safe land, how will you do in the thick woods by the Jordan?
Even your brothers and your father's family have turned against you. They have called out after you. Do not trust them, even if they say good things to you."
"I have left My house. I have given up My land. I have put the one I love into the hands of her enemies.
My land has become like a lion in the forest to Me. She roared against Me. So I hate her.
"Is My land like a spotted bird to Me? Birds of prey all around are against her. Come, gather all the wild animals. Bring them to eat her.
Many shepherds have ruined My vineyard. They trampled My field. They turned My special land into a dry, empty place.
"They made it a ruin. It is sad before Me. The whole land is ruined, because no one thinks about it.
Destroyers have come to all the bare hills in the desert. The sword of the LORD destroys from one end of the earth to the other. No one is safe.
They planted wheat but picked thorns. They worked hard for nothing. Be ashamed of your crops because of the LORD's fierce anger."
"The LORD says: 'All My bad neighbors touch the land I gave to My people Israel. I will pull them up from their land. I will pull the people of Judah out from among them.'
After I pull them up, I will come back and show mercy to them. I will bring each one back to his own land.
"If they learn My people's ways and promise by My name, 'As the LORD lives,' just like they taught My people to promise by Baal, then they will be built up among My people.
But if they do not listen, I will pull up that nation and destroy it, says the LORD."
The LORD said to me, "Go buy a cloth belt. Put it around your waist. Do not put it in water."
So I bought the belt, just as the the LORD said. I put it around my waist.
Then the word of the the LORD came to me again.
He said, "Take the belt you bought, the one around your waist. Go to the Euphrates River and hide it in a crack in the rocks."
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, just as the the LORD told me.
After many days, the the LORD said to me, "Go to the Euphrates and get the belt I told you to hide there."
So I went to the Euphrates and dug up the belt. I took it from the place where I had hidden it. But it was ruined. It was no good for anything.
Then the word of the the LORD came to me.
He said, "This is what the the LORD says: 'In the same way, I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
These wicked people will not listen to My words. They follow their stubborn hearts. They go after other gods to serve and worship them. They will be like this belt—useless for anything.

For as a belt clings to a man's waist, so I made all the people of Israel and all the people of Judah cling to Me,' says the the LORD. 'They were to be My people. They were to bring Me praise, glory, and honor. But they did not listen.'"
"Say to them, 'This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every jar will be filled with wine.' They will say to you, 'Do we not know that every jar will be filled with wine?'

Then say to them, 'This is what the the LORD says: I will make everyone in this land drunk. I will make the kings who sit on David's throne drunk, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people in Jerusalem.
I will smash them against each other, fathers and sons together,' says the the LORD. 'I will not pity them. I will not spare them. I will not have mercy on them. I will destroy them.'"
Listen and pay attention. Do not be proud, for the the LORD has spoken.
Give glory to the the LORD your God before He brings darkness, before your feet stumble in the dark. While you hope for light, He will turn it into deep darkness and thick clouds.
But if you will not listen, I will cry in secret because of your pride. My eyes will cry hard tears, because the the LORD's flock will be taken away.
Say to the king and the queen mother: "Come down from your throne. Your beautiful crown has fallen from your heads."
The cities in the south are shut up, and no one opens them. All the people of Judah are carried away. They are all taken away.
Look up and see the people coming from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you? Where are your beautiful sheep?
What will you say when He puts over you the leaders you taught to be your friends? Will pain grab you like a woman having a baby?
If you ask in your heart, "Why did this happen to me?" it is because of your great sin. Your skirts are lifted, and your feet are bare.
Can a person change the color of his skin? Can a leopard change its spots? Then you also cannot do good, because you are used to doing evil.
I will scatter them like straw blown by the wind in the desert.
"This is your share. This is what I have set aside for you," says the the LORD. "You forgot Me, and you trusted in lies."
I will pull your skirts up over your face, and your shame will show.
I have seen your cheating and your wild cries. I have seen your shameful acts on the hills and in the fields. How terrible for you, Jerusalem! How long will you stay unclean?
This is the message the LORD gave to Jeremiah about the dry time.
Judah is sad. Its gates are weak. People bow their heads to the ground. Jerusalem cries out.
The leaders send their helpers to get water. They go to the water holes, but find no water. They come back with empty jars. They are ashamed and upset. They cover their heads in shame.
The ground is cracked and dry because there is no rain. The farmers are ashamed. They cover their heads.
Even the mother deer in the field leaves her baby, because there is no grass to eat.
The wild donkeys stand on the bare hills. They gasp for air like wild dogs. Their eyes grow weak, because there is no grass.
Our sins speak against us. the LORD, do something good to honor Your name. We have turned away from You many times. We have sinned against You.
You are Israel's hope. You save us in hard times. Why are You like a stranger in the land? Why are You like a traveler who stays for one night?
Why are You like a man who is confused? Why are You like a strong man who cannot save? But You are with us, the LORD. Your name is on us. Do not leave us!
This is what the LORD says about these people: "They love to wander. They do not hold back their feet. the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their wrongs and punish their sins."
the LORD said to me, "Do not pray for good for these people.
When they go without food, I will not listen to their cry. When they bring burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will end them with war, hunger, and sickness."
Then I said, "Oh, Lord, the LORD, the prophets say to them, 'You will not see war. You will not be hungry. I will give you true peace here.'"

the LORD said to me, "The prophets lie and use My name. I did not send them. I did not command them. I did not speak to them. They give you false visions. They tell you lies that come from their own hearts."

So this is what the LORD says about the prophets who speak in His name but whom He did not send. They say, "There will be no war or hunger in this land." But those prophets will die by war and hunger.

The people they speak to will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem. They will die from hunger and war. No one will bury them—not them, their wives, their sons, or their daughters. I will punish them for their evil.
You will say this to them: "Let my eyes cry tears day and night. Do not let them stop. For the young women of my people are broken. They have a very bad hurt.
If I go out to the field, I see people killed by war. If I go into the city, I see people sick from hunger. Even the prophet and the priest wander in a land they do not know."
Have You completely turned away from Judah? Do You hate Zion? Why did You hurt us so we cannot be healed? We hoped for peace, but nothing good came. We hoped for healing, but there was only trouble.
We know our wrongs, the LORD. We know the sins of our fathers. We have sinned against You.
For Your name's sake, do not hate us. Do not bring shame to Your glorious throne. Remember Your promise to us. Do not break it.
Do any of the false gods of the nations bring rain? Do the skies give showers? Are You not the LORD our God? We hope in You, because You made all these things.
Then the The LORD said to me, "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before Me, I would not feel sorry for this people. Send them away from Me, and let them go.

If they ask you, 'Where should we go?' tell them, 'This is what the the LORD says: Those meant for death will die; those meant for the sword will be killed by the sword; those meant for hunger will starve; and those meant to be taken away will be taken away.'"
The LORD says, "I will send four kinds of trouble on them. The sword will kill some. Dogs will drag away some. Birds in the sky and animals on the ground will eat and destroy the rest.
I will make them a scary sight to all the kingdoms of the earth. This is because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem."
The LORD says, "Who will feel sorry for you, Jerusalem? Who will be sad for you? Who will stop and ask how you are?
You left Me. You turned your back on Me. So I reached out My hand against you and destroyed you. I am tired of being kind."
"I will scatter them at the gates of the land. I will take away their children and destroy My people, because they did not turn from their bad ways.
Their widows will be more than the sand by the sea. I will bring an enemy at noon to hurt them. I will suddenly bring fear and trouble on mothers and their children.

The mother with seven children will be weak and die. Her life will end before the day is over. She will be shamed and disgraced. The rest of them I will kill with the sword in front of their enemies," says the the LORD.
"Oh, how sad I am, my mother, that you gave birth to me! I am a man who argues with everyone in the land. I have not loaned or borrowed money, but everyone curses me."
The LORD said, "I will help you and do good for you. I will make your enemies beg you for help when trouble comes.
Can iron break iron from the north? Can bronze break it?
I will let your wealth and treasures be taken for free, because of all your sins, all over your land.
I will make you go with your enemies to a land you do not know. My anger is like a fire that burns against you."
"You know me, the LORD. Remember me and take care of me. Pay back those who hurt me. Do not stay angry with me for long. Know that I suffer shame because of You.
I found Your words and took them to heart. They made me happy and glad, because I am called by Your name, the LORD God of all armies.
I did not join people who party and laugh, and I did not have fun. I stayed alone, because Your hand was on me. You made me angry at wrong.
Why does my pain never stop? Why is my hurt so bad it will not heal? Will You let me down like a stream that dries up? Will Your help fail like water that is not there?"

The LORD says, "If you come back to Me, I will bring you back. You will stand before Me. If you choose good words over bad words, you will speak for Me. People will come to you, but you will not go to them.
I will make you a strong wall of bronze for these people. They will fight you, but they will not win. I am with you to save you and rescue you," says the the LORD.
"I will save you from bad people and set you free from mean people."
The word of the the LORD came to me.
The LORD said, “Do not get married. Do not have sons or daughters here.
This is what the the LORD says about the children born here, and about their mothers and fathers in this land:
They will die of bad sickness. They will not be cried for or buried. They will be like waste on the ground. They will die by war and by hunger. Their bodies will be food for birds and wild animals.”

The LORD says, “Do not go into a house where people are sad for someone who died. Do not go to cry for them. Do not feel sorry for them. I have taken away My peace, My faithful love, and My mercy from these people, says the the LORD.
Both important and unimportant people will die in this land. They will not be buried. No one will cry for them. No one will cut their skin or shave their heads for them.
No one will bring food to comfort them because someone died. No one will give them a drink to comfort them for their father or mother.
Do not go into a house where people are having a party to eat and drink.”
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “While you watch, I will stop the happy sounds in this place. You will not hear the groom or the bride.”
When you tell the people all this, they will ask you, “Why did the the LORD say such a big trouble will come to us? What have we done wrong? What sin have we done against the the LORD our God?”
Then say to them, “Your fathers left Me, says the the LORD. They followed other gods. They served them and bowed to them. They left Me and did not obey My law.
You have done worse than your fathers. Each of you follows his own stubborn, evil heart. You do not listen to Me.”
The LORD says, “So I will throw you out of this land into a land you and your fathers did not know. There you will serve other gods day and night. I will not be kind to you.”
“So the days are coming, says the the LORD, when people will no longer say, ‘As surely as the the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up from Egypt.’

Instead, they will say, ‘As surely as the the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up from the north and from all the lands where He drove them.’ Then I will bring them back to their own land, which I gave to their fathers.”
The LORD says, “Look, I am sending many fishermen. They will catch the people. After that, I will send many hunters. They will hunt them from every mountain, hill, and crack in the rocks.”
“For My eyes see all their ways. They cannot hide from Me. Their sin cannot hide from My eyes.
First, I will pay them back double for their sin and guilt. They made My land unclean. They filled My land with dead bodies of their hated idols and their disgusting things.”

“The LORD, You are my strength and my safe place. You are my help in trouble. Nations will come to You from the ends of the earth. They will say, ‘Our fathers only had lies. Their idols were worthless and could not help.’”
“Can people make gods for themselves? They are not real gods.
So I will make them know. This time I will show them My power and My strength. Then they will know that My name is the the LORD.”
Judah's sin is written with an iron pen. It is cut with a diamond point on the tablet of their heart. It is also on the horns of their altars.
Even their children remember their altars and the wooden poles for a false god. They stand by green trees and on high hills.
My mountain in the field, I will let enemies take your wealth and all your treasures. I will also let them take your high places, because of sin all through your land.
You will let go of the land I gave you. I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know. You made Me angry. My anger will burn forever.
This is what the the LORD says: "Cursed is the man who trusts in people. He relies on human power. He turns his heart away from the the LORD."
He will be like a bush in the desert. He will not see good come. He will live in dry places in the desert, in a salty land where no one lives.
But blessed is the man who trusts in the the LORD. The the LORD is his safe place.
He is like a tree planted by water. Its roots reach the stream. It does not fear when heat comes. Its leaves stay green. It does not worry in a dry year. It does not stop making fruit.
The heart is more tricky than anything else. It is very sick. Who can know it?
I, the the LORD, search the heart. I test the mind. I give each person what he has earned by his ways, and by the fruit of his deeds.
A bird that sits on eggs it did not lay is like a man who gets rich in a wrong way. In the middle of his life, his riches will leave him. In the end, he will look foolish.
A glorious throne, high from the beginning, is the place of our temple.
O the LORD, You are the hope of Israel. All who leave You will be put to shame. Those who turn away from You will be written in the dust, because they left the the LORD, the spring of living water.
Heal me, O the LORD, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved. You are my praise.
Look, they keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the the LORD? Let it come now!"
But I did not run away from being a shepherd after You. I did not want the day of trouble. You know. What came from my lips was open before You.
Do not be a terror to me. You are my safe place in the day of trouble.
Let those who chase me be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be afraid, but do not let me be afraid. Bring the day of trouble on them. Break them with double trouble.
This is what the the LORD said to me: "Go and stand at the gate where the people go. It is the gate the kings of Judah use to go in and out. Stand at all the gates of Jerusalem too."
Say to them, "Hear the word of the the LORD, you kings of Judah, all Judah, and all who live in Jerusalem and come in through these gates."
This is what the the LORD says: "Be careful. Do not carry a load on the Sabbath day. Do not bring it through the gates of Jerusalem.
Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day. Do not do any work. Keep the Sabbath day holy, as I told your fathers."
But they did not listen. They did not pay attention. They were stubborn. They would not listen or learn.
"But if you listen carefully to Me," says the the LORD, "and do not bring a load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and keep the Sabbath day holy by not doing any work on it,

then kings and princes who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this city. They will ride in chariots and on horses. They and their princes, the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem, will come. This city will be lived in forever.

People will come from the cities of Judah and from around Jerusalem. They will come from the land of Benjamin, from the lowlands, from the hill country, and from the south. They will bring burnt gifts and sacrifices, grain gifts and incense. They will bring thank-you gifts to the house of the the LORD.

But if you do not listen to Me and keep the Sabbath day holy, and if you carry a load as you go through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will start a fire in its gates. It will burn up the palaces of Jerusalem. It will not be put out."
This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Get up and go to the potter's house. I will speak to you there."
So I went there. The potter was working at his wheel.
The pot he was making broke in his hands. So he made it into another pot, the way he wanted.
Then the the LORD spoke to me again:
The The LORD says, "House of Israel, can I not do with you what the potter does? Look, you are like clay in the potter's hand. You are in My hand, house of Israel.
At any time I can speak about a nation or kingdom. I can pull it up, tear it down, and destroy it.
But if that nation I warned turns from its wrong ways, I will change My mind. I will not bring the trouble I planned.
At another time I can speak about a nation or kingdom. I can build it up and help it grow.
But if it does wrong in My eyes and does not listen to Me, I will not give the good I planned for it."

So tell the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem, "The LORD says this: Look, I am planning trouble for you. I have a plan against you. Each of you, turn from your wrong ways. Make your ways and your actions good."
But they will say, "No, it is no use. We will follow our own plans. Each of us will do what his stubborn, bad heart wants."
So the the LORD says, "Ask the nations: Has anyone ever heard of anything like this? Israel has done a very bad thing.
Does the snow on the rocks of Lebanon ever leave? Do the cold waters from a faraway place ever stop flowing?
"But My people forgot Me. They burn incense to false gods. This made them trip on their way, on the old paths. They walk on rough side paths, on roads that are not smooth.
They made their land empty and ruined. People hiss at it all the time. Everyone who passes by is shocked and shakes his head.
Like the east wind, I will scatter them in front of their enemies. On the day of trouble, I will turn My back to them, not My face."

Then they said, "Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah. The law will not be lost from the priest. The wise will still have advice. The prophet will still have words. Come, let us hurt him with our words. Let us not listen to anything he says."
"Listen to me, O the the LORD. Hear what my enemies say.
Should good be paid back with evil? They dug a hole to trap me. Remember that I stood before You and spoke good for them. I tried to turn Your anger away from them.
"So let their children starve. Let their children be killed by the sword. Let their wives lose their children and become widows. Let their men die. Let their young men be killed in war.
Let a cry be heard from their houses when You suddenly send attackers against them. They dug a hole to catch me. They hid traps for my feet.
But You, O the the LORD, know all their plans to kill me. Do not forgive their wrong. Do not wipe away their sin from before You. Let them fall in front of You. Punish them when You are angry."
The LORD said, "Go and buy a clay jar from a man who makes pots. Take some of the leaders of the people and some of the leaders of the priests."
"Go out to the Valley of Ben Hinnom, near the Gate of Broken Pots. Say there the words I tell you."

"Listen to the word of the the LORD, kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem. The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says He is bringing trouble on this place. Anyone who hears about it will be shocked.

They turned away from Me and made this place unholy. They burned sweet-smelling smoke to other gods that they, their fathers, and their kings did not know. They filled this place with the blood of people who did nothing wrong.
They built places to worship Baal. They burned their sons in the fire as gifts to Baal. I did not tell them to do this. It never came to My mind."
"The LORD says that soon this place will not be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom. It will be called the Valley of Killing.
Here I will ruin the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will let their enemies kill them with swords. I will give their dead bodies to the birds and wild animals to eat.
I will make this city a ruin. People will hiss when they see it. Everyone who walks by will be shocked and hiss because of all its hurts.
I will make them eat their own sons and daughters. They will eat each other when their enemies surround them and make life hard."
The LORD said, "Then break the jar in front of the men who came with you."

Jeremiah told the people, "The LORD of Armies says He will break this people and this city like a jar maker breaks a jar. It cannot be put back together. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no room left.
The LORD says He will do this to this place and to the people who live here. He will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be unclean like Topheth. This is because on their roofs they burned sweet-smelling smoke to all the stars and poured out drinks to other gods."
Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where the the LORD had sent him to speak His message. He stood in the courtyard of the house of the the LORD. He said to all the people,
"The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says He is bringing on this city and all its nearby towns all the trouble He said He would. The people were stubborn and would not listen to His words."
Pashhur was a priest. He was Immer's son. He was in charge of the LORD's house. He heard Jeremiah say these things.
He had Jeremiah the prophet beaten. Then he put him in the stocks. This was at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, at the LORD's house.
The next day, Pashhur let Jeremiah out of the stocks. Jeremiah said to him, "The LORD does not call you Pashhur. He calls you Fear All Around.

This is what the LORD says: 'I will make you a fear to yourself and to all your friends. With your own eyes, you will see them fall by the sword of their enemies. I will give all of Judah to the king of Babylon. He will take them to Babylon or kill them with the sword.

I will give all the wealth of this city to its enemies. I will give its goods and its valuable things. I will give all the treasures of the kings of Judah. The enemies will take them and carry them to Babylon.
And you, Pashhur, and all who live in your house, will go away as captives. You will go to Babylon. There you will die and be buried. So will all your friends. You told them lies.'"
O the LORD, You tricked me, and I was tricked. You are stronger than me, and You won. All day long, people laugh at me. Everyone makes fun of me.
Every time I speak, I cry out. I say, "There is trouble and ruin!" So the LORD's word brings me shame and mean words all day long.
But if I say, "I will not say His name or speak for Him anymore," His word is like a fire burning in my heart. It is shut up in my bones. I am tired of holding it in. I cannot keep it in.
I hear many people whisper, "Fear All Around! Tell on him! Let's tell on him!" All my close friends watch for me to fall. They say, "Maybe he will be fooled. Then we can beat him and pay him back."
But the LORD is with me like a strong soldier. So the people who chase me will trip and not win. They will fail and be very ashamed. People will never forget their shame.
The LORD of All, You test good people. You look at hearts and minds. Let me see You pay them back. I have given my case to You.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! He saves the life of a person in need from bad people.
I curse the day I was born! May no one bless the day my mother had me!
I curse the man who told my father, "A boy is born to you!" He made my father very happy.
May that man be like the towns the LORD destroyed without pity. May he hear crying in the morning and a war cry at noon.
I was not killed before I was born. So my mother's womb became my grave, and it stayed full forever.
Why was I born? I only see trouble and sadness. My days end in shame.
This is the word the LORD gave Jeremiah. King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah the priest, son of Maaseiah, to him. They said,
"Please ask the the LORD to help us. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is fighting against us. Maybe the the LORD will do His great works for us, and Nebuchadnezzar will leave."
Jeremiah said to them, "Tell Zedekiah this:

"This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I will make your weapons useless. You are using them to fight the king of Babylon and the Babylonians who are around your city walls. But I will bring those enemies into the middle of this city.
"'I will fight against you with a strong hand and a mighty arm. I will be very angry.
"'I will strike the people and animals in this city. They will die from a bad sickness.

"'After that,' says the the LORD, 'I will give Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, and the people left in this city after sickness, war, and hunger to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to their enemies. Those enemies want to kill them. The enemy will kill them with swords. They will not spare them or feel sorry for them.'
"And tell these people, 'This is what the the LORD says: I am putting before you the way to live and the way to die.

"'Anyone who stays in this city will die by sword, hunger, and sickness. But anyone who goes out and gives up to the Babylonians who are around you will live. He will keep his life like a prize taken in war.
"'I have turned My face against this city to hurt it, not to help it,' says the the LORD. 'It will be given to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.'
"Also tell the family of the king of Judah, 'Listen to the word of the the LORD!'

"House of David, this is what the the LORD says: 'Do what is right each morning. Save the person who was robbed from the robber. If you do not, My anger will go out like fire and burn. No one will put it out. This will happen because of their evil deeds.'
"'I am against you, you who live in the valley, you who are like a rock on the flat land,' says the the LORD. 'You say, "Who can come down against us? Who can come into our homes?"'
"'I will punish you for what you have done,' says the the LORD. 'I will start a fire in your forest. It will burn up everything around it.'"
The LORD said, "Go to the king of Judah's house. Speak this word there.
Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah. You sit on David's throne. You and your servants and your people come through these gates.

"Do what is fair and right. Help the person who was robbed. Save him from the one who hurts him. Do not be mean. Do not crush people. Do not kill innocent people. Do not hurt the stranger, the child with no father, or the widow in this place.

"If you do these things, then kings will sit on David's throne. They will come through the gates of this house. They will ride in chariots and on horses. The king, his servants, and his people will come too.
"But if you do not listen to these words, I swear by Myself, says the LORD, this house will become a ruin."
The LORD says about the house of the king of Judah, "You are very special to Me, like the best land. But I will make you a desert. Your cities will be empty.
"I will send men to destroy you. Each man will have his weapons. They will cut down your best cedar trees. They will throw them into the fire.
"Many nations will pass by this city. Each person will say to his friend, 'Why did the LORD do this to this great city?'
People will answer, 'Because they left the LORD their God. They bowed down to other gods and served them.'"
Do not weep for the dead. Do not feel sorry for him. Weep hard for the one who is taken away. He will not come back. He will not see his home land again.
The LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah. He became king after his father Josiah. He left this place. He will not come back here.
He will die where they took him. He will not see this land again.
It is bad for the one who builds his house by doing wrong. He builds upper rooms by being unfair. He makes his neighbor work for free. He does not pay him.
He says, "I will build a big house for myself. It will have large rooms. I will cut windows in it. I will cover it with cedar wood. I will paint it red."
The LORD says, "Do you think you are a king because you use cedar wood? Did your father not eat and drink? He did what was fair and right. Then things went well for him.
He helped poor and needy people. Then things went well. Is that not what it means to know Me? says the LORD.
But your eyes and your heart look only for money. You want to hurt innocent people. You want to push people down and be mean."
So the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, "No one will cry for him. No one will say, 'Oh, my brother!' or 'Oh, my sister!' No one will cry, 'Oh, my lord!' or 'Oh, his glory!'
"He will be buried like a donkey. He will be dragged away and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem."
"Go up to Lebanon and cry. Lift your voice in Bashan. Cry from Abarim. All your friends are broken.
"I spoke to you when you were safe. But you said, 'I will not listen.' You have been like this since you were young. You did not listen to My voice.
The wind will blow away your leaders. Your friends will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed. You will feel bad because of all your wrong.
"You live in Lebanon. You live among cedar trees. How you will groan when pain comes. It will be like pain for a woman having a baby.
"As I live, says the LORD, even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a ring on My right hand, I would pull you off.
I will give you to those who want to kill you. I will give you to those you fear. I will give you to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
I will throw you and your mother, who gave birth to you, into another land. You were not born there. You will die there.
They will not come back to the land they want so much."
Is this man Coniah like a broken pot that no one wants? Why are he and his children thrown into a land they do not know?
Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the LORD.
The LORD says, "Write this man down as having no children. He will not do well in his life. None of his children will sit on David's throne or rule in Judah."
How sad for the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep I care for! says the the LORD.

So the the LORD, the God of Israel, says to the shepherds who lead My people: You scattered My flock. You drove them away. You did not take care of them. So now I will punish you for the bad things you did, says the the LORD.
I will gather the rest of My flock from all the lands where I sent them. I will bring them back to their own land. They will have many children and grow.
I will give them new shepherds. The new shepherds will take care of them. Then My people will not be afraid or upset. Not one will be missing, says the the LORD.
Look, the days are coming, says the the LORD. I will give David a good and fair king. He will be like a new branch. He will rule well. He will do what is right and fair in the land.
In his time, Judah will be safe, and Israel will live in peace. His name will be “The LORD Is Our Righteousness.”
So look, the days are coming, says the the LORD. People will not say anymore, “As sure as the the LORD is alive, who brought Israel up from Egypt.”
Instead they will say, “The The LORD is alive! He brought Israel home from the north and from all the lands where He sent them.” Then they will live in their own land.
My heart is broken inside me. All my bones shake. I am like a drunk man, like a man full of wine. This is because of the the LORD and His holiness.
The land is full of people who are not faithful in marriage. The The LORD’s curse makes the land sad. The fields are dry. The people do wrong, and their strength is not used for good.
The prophets and priests are not living for God. I found their evil even in My house, says the the LORD.
So their path will be slippery. They will be pushed into the dark and fall. I will bring trouble on them in the year I punish them, says the the LORD.
I saw something foolish in the prophets of Samaria. They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel the wrong way.

I saw a terrible thing in the prophets of Jerusalem. They are not faithful in marriage, and they live by lies. They make bad people stronger, so no one stops doing wrong. To me they are all like Sodom, and the people there are like Gomorrah.

So the the LORD All-Powerful says about these prophets: I will make them eat bitter food and drink poisoned water, because ungodly ways came from Jerusalem’s prophets and spread through the whole land.
The The LORD All-Powerful says: “Do not listen to the prophets who speak to you. They are filling your heads with empty things. They tell you their own ideas, not words from the the LORD.”
They keep telling people who do not like the the LORD, “The The LORD says you will have peace.” They tell everyone who follows their own stubborn heart, “No bad thing will come to you.”
But who has been close to the the LORD? Who has seen and heard His words? Who has listened to His words and obeyed?
Look, the the LORD’s storm is coming. His anger is like a strong wind. It will hit the heads of bad people.
The The LORD’s anger will not turn back until He has done what He planned in His heart. In the days to come, you will understand this clearly.
I did not send these prophets, but they ran to speak. I did not speak to them, but they prophesied.
If they had stood with me, they would have told My people My words. Then My people would have turned from their bad ways and bad actions.
Am I a God who is only near? says the the LORD. Am I not also a God far away?
Can anyone hide in a secret place so I cannot see him? says the the LORD. Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the the LORD.
I have heard what the prophets say. They prophesy lies in My name. They say, “I had a dream! I had a dream!”
How long will these lying prophets keep false ideas in their hearts?
They think their dreams can make My people forget My name, just as their fathers forgot My name and served Baal.
A prophet who has a dream may tell the dream. A prophet who has My word must speak My word faithfully. Empty talk is not the same as God’s true word, says the the LORD.
My word is like fire, says the the LORD. It is like a hammer that breaks rock.
So I am against the prophets, says the the LORD, who steal My words from each other.
I am against the prophets, says the the LORD, who use their tongues and say, “The The LORD says this.”

I am against prophets who tell false dreams, says the the LORD. They tell them and lead My people the wrong way with lies and foolish talk. I did not send them or command them. They do not help My people at all, says the the LORD.
When these people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, “What is the the LORD’s heavy load?” You must say to them, “You are the heavy load! I will throw you away, says the the LORD.”
I will punish any prophet, priest, or person who says, “This is the the LORD’s heavy load.” I will punish him and his family.
This is what each person says to his neighbor and to his brother: “What did the the LORD answer?” and “What did the the LORD say?”
Do not say “the the LORD’s heavy load” anymore. That phrase is just a person’s own words. You are changing the words of the living God, the the LORD All-Powerful, our God.
This is what you say to the prophet: “What did the the LORD answer you?” and “What did the the LORD say?”
If you say, “This is the the LORD’s heavy load,” the the LORD says this: Because you said, “The the LORD’s heavy load,” even though I told you not to say that,
I will make you forget completely. I will throw you away from Me. I will throw away the city I gave to you and your fathers.
I will bring lasting shame on you. People will never forget it.

After Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, took Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and the leaders of Judah, and the skilled workers and metalworkers from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs. They were in front of the temple of the LORD.
One basket had very good figs, like figs that ripen early. The other basket had very bad figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
Then the LORD asked me, "Jeremiah, what do you see?" I said, "Figs. The good ones are very good, but the bad ones are so bad they cannot be eaten."
Then the word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"This is what The LORD, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, I will treat the people of Judah who were taken away to Babylon as good. I sent them there for their good.
I will watch over them for good. I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up, not tear them down. I will plant them, not pull them up.
I will give them a heart that knows Me. They will be My people, and I will be their God. They will come back to Me with all their heart."
"This is what the LORD says: I will treat Zedekiah, king of Judah, and his leaders, and the people left in Jerusalem, and the people living in Egypt, like the bad figs that are too bad to eat.
I will make them a terrible thing and a bad example to all the kingdoms of the earth. People will shame them, make fun of them, and curse them everywhere I send them.
I will send war, hunger, and sickness on them until they are gone from the land I gave to them and their fathers."

This is the message that came to Jeremiah about all the people of Judah. It was in the fourth year that Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, was king of Judah. That was the first year Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
Jeremiah spoke to all the people of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem. He said, "
For twenty-three years, since the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until today, the the LORD's word has come to me. I have spoken to you again and again, but you did not listen.
The The LORD sent you all His servants, the prophets. He sent them again and again, but you did not listen or pay attention.
He told you to turn from your evil ways and stop doing bad things. Then you could live in the land the the LORD gave you and your fathers forever.
He told you not to follow other gods or bow down to them. He told you not to make Him angry by what you do, so He would not hurt you.
But the the LORD says you did not listen to Him. You made Him angry by what you did, and it hurt you."
The The LORD of armies says, "Because you did not listen to My words,

look, I will send for all the families from the north. I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. I will bring them against this land and its people and all the nations around it. I will wipe them out completely. I will make this place empty and scary forever.
I will take away happy sounds and joy. I will take away the voices of brides and grooms. I will take away the sound of mills and the light of lamps.
This whole land will become empty and ruined. These nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
After seventy years, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their wrongs. I will make their land empty forever.
I will bring on that land all My words that I spoke against it. I will do everything written in this book that Jeremiah said would happen to all the nations.
Many nations and great kings will make them slaves too. I will pay them back for what they have done."
The The LORD, the God of Israel, said to me, "Take this cup of wine from My hand. It is full of My anger. Make all the nations I send you to drink it.
They will drink and stagger and go crazy because of the sword I am sending among them."
So I took the cup from the the LORD's hand. I made all the nations drink it, the nations the the LORD sent me to.
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah drank it. Their kings and officials drank it. This made them empty, ruined, scary, and cursed, as they are today.
Pharaoh king of Egypt drank it, along with his servants, his leaders, and all his people.
All the mixed people drank it. All the kings of the land of Uz drank it. All the kings of the Philistines drank it—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the rest of Ashdod.
Edom drank it. Moab drank it. The Ammonites drank it.
All the kings of Tyre drank it. All the kings of Sidon drank it. The kings of the coastlands across the sea drank it.
Dedan drank it. Tema drank it. Buz drank it. All who cut the corners of their hair drank it.
All the kings of Arabia drank it. All the kings of the mixed tribes who live in the desert drank it.
All the kings of Zimri drank it. All the kings of Elam drank it. All the kings of Media drank it.
All the kings of the north drank it, near and far, one after another. All the kingdoms of the world on the earth drank it. After them, the king of Sheshach will drink too.

Then tell them that the the LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says they must drink until they are drunk. They will vomit, fall down, and not get up again. This is because of the sword He is sending among them.
If they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, then say to them that the the LORD of armies says they must drink.

The The LORD of armies says, "Look, I am starting to bring trouble on the city that bears My name. Do you think you will go free? You will not go free, because I am calling for a sword against everyone on earth."

Then Jeremiah prophesied these words: "The The LORD will roar from high above. He will thunder from His holy home. He will roar loudly against His own land. He will shout like people stomping grapes, against everyone on earth.
Noise will reach the ends of the earth, because the the LORD has a case against the nations. He will judge all people. He will hand the wicked over to the sword, says the the LORD."
The The LORD of armies says, "Look, trouble is going out from nation to nation. A great storm is rising from the ends of the earth.
On that day, those killed by the the LORD will lie from one end of the earth to the other. No one will cry for them. No one will gather them or bury them. They will be like dung on the ground.
Cry out, you shepherds! Roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock! Your time to be killed has come. You will fall and break like a fancy jar.
The shepherds will have no way to run. The leaders of the flock will have no way to escape.
Listen to the shepherds cry! Listen to the leaders of the flock wail! The The LORD is destroying their pasture.
Their peaceful homes are cut down because of the the LORD's fierce anger.
He has left His hiding place like a lion. Their land is empty because of the cruel sword and His fierce anger."
At the start of King Jehoiakim's rule, this message came from the LORD. Jehoiakim was the son of King Josiah of Judah.
The LORD said, “Stand in the courtyard of the LORD's house. Speak to all the cities of Judah that come to worship there. Tell them all the words I tell you to say. Do not leave out a word.
Maybe they will listen and turn from their bad ways. Then I will not bring the trouble I planned for them. I planned it because of their bad deeds.
Say to them, ‘This is what the LORD says: If you do not listen to Me and follow My law that I gave you,
and if you do not listen to the prophets who serve Me—whom I send to you again and again—though you have not listened,
then I will make this temple like Shiloh. I will make this city a curse to all the nations.’”
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah say these things in the the LORD's house.
When Jeremiah finished saying all that the the LORD told him to say to the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people grabbed him. They said, “You must die!”

They said, “Why did you say in the the LORD's name that this house will be like Shiloh? Why did you say this city will be empty and ruined?” All the people gathered around Jeremiah in the the LORD's house.
The leaders of Judah heard this. They came from the king's house to the the LORD's house. They sat down at the entrance to the New Gate.
The priests and prophets said to the leaders and all the people, “This man should die. He spoke against this city. You heard it with your own ears.”
Jeremiah said to all the leaders and all the people, “The the LORD sent me to speak against this temple and this city. I said all the words you heard.
Now change your ways and your actions. Listen to the the LORD your God. Then the the LORD will not bring the trouble He said He would bring.
As for me, I am in your hands. Do to me what you think is right.
But you should know this: If you kill me, you will bring guilt on yourselves, on this city, and on the people who live here. The the LORD truly sent me to say all these words to you.”
The leaders and all the people said to the priests and prophets, “This man should not die. He spoke to us in the name of the the LORD our God.”
Some of the older leaders stood up. They spoke to all the people. They said, “Micah from Moresheth prophesied in the days of King Hezekiah of Judah.
He said, ‘This is what the the LORD of Armies says: Zion will be plowed like a field. Jerusalem will become a pile of rocks. The hill where the temple stands will become a forest.’

Did King Hezekiah and all Judah kill him? No. Hezekiah feared the the LORD. He prayed to the the LORD. The the LORD did not bring the trouble He had said He would bring. But we are about to bring great trouble on ourselves.”
There was also a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath Jearim. He prophesied in the the LORD's name. He said the same things about this city and this land that Jeremiah said.
King Jehoiakim and his soldiers and leaders heard his words. The king wanted to kill him. Uriah heard about it. He was afraid. He ran away to Egypt.
King Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men to Egypt.
They brought Uriah out of Egypt. They took him to King Jehoiakim. The king killed him with a sword. He threw his body into the common people's graves.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan helped Jeremiah. So Jeremiah was not given to the people to be killed.
At the start of King Jehoiakim's rule, this message came to Jeremiah from the LORD. He said,
"Make a wooden yoke with straps, and put it on your neck."
Send these yokes to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Their messengers are coming to Jerusalem to see King Zedekiah of Judah.
Tell them, "The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Give this message to your masters:
I made the earth, the people, and the animals on it. I did this with My great power and strong arm. I give it to anyone I choose.
Now I have given all these lands to My servant, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. I have even given him the wild animals to serve him.
All nations will serve him, and then his son, and then his grandson. This will last until the time for his own land comes. Then many nations and great kings will make him serve them.

Any nation or kingdom that will not serve King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and will not put its neck under his yoke, I will punish with war, hunger, and sickness, says the LORD. I will destroy them by his power."
So do not listen to your prophets, fortune-tellers, dreamers, magic workers, or sorcerers. They tell you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon."
They are telling you lies. They want to take you far from your land. I will drive you out, and you will be destroyed.
But any nation that puts its neck under the king of Babylon's yoke and serves him, I will let stay in its own land, says the LORD. They can farm it and live there.
I also spoke to Zedekiah, king of Judah. I said, "Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon. Serve him and his people, and you will live."
Why should you and your people die by war, hunger, and sickness? The LORD has said this will happen to any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon.
Do not listen to the prophets who tell you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon." They are lying to you.
I did not send them, says the LORD. They are telling lies in My name. They want to drive you out, and you will be destroyed. You and the prophets who speak to you will be destroyed.

I also spoke to the priests and all the people. I said, "The LORD says: Do not listen to your prophets. They tell you that soon the things from the LORD's temple will be brought back from Babylon. They are lying to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and you will live. Why should this city be destroyed?"

If they are prophets, and if they really have the LORD's word, let them ask the LORD of Hosts not to let the rest of the holy things in the LORD's temple, the king's house, and Jerusalem be taken to Babylon.
The LORD of Hosts says this about the pillars, the big bowl, the stands, and the rest of the things left in this city.
