King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon did not take them when he took King Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim of Judah from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem.
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says this about the things left in the LORD's temple and in the king's house in Jerusalem:
They will be carried to Babylon and stay there until I come for them, says the LORD. Then I will bring them back to this place.

In the fifth month of that year, early in King Zedekiah’s rule over Judah, the prophet Hananiah, son of Azzur from Gibeon, spoke to me in the the LORD’s house. The priests and all the people were there.
He said, “This is what the the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
In two years I will bring back to this place all the things from the the LORD’s house that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon took away and carried to Babylon.
I will also bring back Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the people of Judah who were taken to Babylon,’ says the the LORD. ‘I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.’”
Then the prophet Jeremiah answered the prophet Hananiah in front of the priests and all the people standing in the the LORD’s house.

He said, “Amen! May the the LORD do it! May the the LORD make your words come true. May He bring back the things from the the LORD’s house and all the people who were taken, from Babylon to this place.
But please listen to what I say to you and to all the people.
Long ago, prophets who came before us said there would be war, trouble, and sickness for many lands and big kingdoms.
But a prophet who says there will be peace is known to be truly sent by the the LORD only when his words come true.”
Then Hananiah took the yoke off Jeremiah’s neck and broke it.

He said before all the people, “This is what the the LORD says: ‘In the same way, I will break the yoke of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon off the necks of all the countries in two years.’” Then Jeremiah went on his way.
After Hananiah broke the yoke off Jeremiah’s neck, the the LORD’s word came to Jeremiah.
The LORD said, “Go and tell Hananiah, ‘This is what the the LORD says: You broke a wooden yoke, but now you will have an iron yoke.
I have put an iron yoke on the necks of all these countries. They must serve King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and they will serve him. I will even give him the wild animals.’”
Then Jeremiah said to Hananiah, “Listen, Hananiah! The the LORD did not send you. But you have made these people trust in lies.
So the the LORD says: ‘I am about to take you away from the earth. You will die this year, because you spoke against the the LORD.’”
In the seventh month of that year, the prophet Hananiah died.

These are the words of the letter Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem. He sent it to the older leaders, the priests, the prophets, and all the people Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the royal officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, and the skilled workers had left Jerusalem.
Jeremiah sent the letter with Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah. King Zedekiah of Judah had sent them to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. The letter said:
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the people I took from Jerusalem to Babylon:
"Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Get married and have sons and daughters. Find wives for your sons, and give your daughters to men to marry. Let them have sons and daughters too. Grow in number there. Do not become few.
Look for peace in the city where I sent you. Pray to the LORD for that city, because when it is at peace, you will be at peace."
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says:
"Do not let your prophets and those who tell the future trick you. Do not listen to the dreams you dream. They prophesy lies to you in My name. I did not send them, says the LORD."
The LORD says: "After seventy years in Babylon are over, I will come to you. I will keep My good promise to you and bring you back to this place.
I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD. They are plans for peace, not for harm. I want to give you a good future and hope.
You will call to Me and come and pray to Me, and I will listen to you.
You will look for Me and find Me when you look for Me with all your heart.

I will be found by you, says the LORD. I will bring you back from captivity. I will gather you from all the nations and places where I sent you, says the LORD. I will bring you back to the place I sent you away from."
The LORD says: "You say, 'The LORD has given us prophets in Babylon.'
But this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people who live in this city. They are your brothers who did not go with you to Babylon."
The LORD of Hosts says: "I am sending war, hunger, and sickness on them. I will make them like bad figs that are too bad to eat.

I will chase them with war, hunger, and sickness. I will make them a terrible warning to all kingdoms on earth. People will curse them, be shocked by them, mock them, and shame them among all the nations where I sent them.
This is because they did not listen to My words, says the LORD. I sent My servants the prophets to them again and again, but you did not listen, says the LORD."
But you, listen to the word of the LORD. All of you who were taken from Jerusalem to Babylon, listen.

The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah: "They prophesy lies to you in My name. I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them while you watch."

The LORD says: "Because of them, all the captives from Judah in Babylon will use a curse. They will say that the LORD should make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire.

This is because they did a terrible thing in Israel. They were not faithful to their neighbors' wives. They also said false words in My name, words I did not tell them to say. I know what they did, and I am a witness, says the LORD."
The LORD also told Jeremiah to send a message to Shemaiah the Nehelamite.
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Because you sent letters in your name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying:"
"The LORD has made you priest instead of Jehoiada the priest. You are to be in charge in the LORD's house. You must arrest any person who acts crazy and says he is a prophet. Put him in chains.
Why have you not stopped Jeremiah from Anathoth? He says he is a prophet for you.
He sent us a letter in Babylon. He said it will be a long time. He told us to build houses and live in them, plant gardens, and eat their fruit."
Zephaniah the priest read this letter to Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah. He said, "Send this message to all the people who were taken away:
'This is what the LORD says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite. He prophesied to you, but I did not send him. He made you trust a lie.
So I will punish Shemaiah and his family. None of his family will live among these people. He will not see the good I will do for My people, says the LORD, because he spoke against the LORD.'"
This is the message the LORD gave to Jeremiah.
The LORD, the God of Israel, says, "Write in a book all the words I have spoken to you.
A time is coming when I will bring My people Israel and Judah back home. I will give them the land I gave their fathers. They will live there again."
These are the words the LORD spoke about Israel and Judah.
The LORD says, "We have heard cries of fear. There is no peace.
Ask and see: Can a man have a baby? Why do I see every man with his hands on his stomach, like a woman in labor? Why is every face white with fear?
That day will be terrible. Nothing will be like it. It will be a hard time for Jacob, but he will be saved."
The LORD of heaven's armies says, "I will break the heavy load off your neck. I will set you free. No one from another land will make you a slave again.
They will serve the LORD their God and a king from David's family. I will raise up that king for them."

The LORD says, "Do not be afraid, Jacob, My servant. Do not be scared, Israel. I will save you from far away. I will save your children from the land where they are held. Jacob will come home and rest. No one will scare him.
I am with you to save you. I will destroy the nations where I scattered you. But I will not destroy you. I will punish you the right amount. I will not let you go without punishment."
The LORD says, "Your hurt is too deep to heal. Your wound is very bad.
No one will stand up for you. There is no medicine for your wound. You cannot be healed.
All your friends have forgotten you. They do not care about you. I punished you like a cruel enemy would, because your guilt is great. Your sins are many.
Why do you cry about your wound? Your pain cannot be healed. I did this to you because your guilt is great. Your sins are many."
The LORD says, "So all who hurt you will be hurt. All your enemies will become prisoners. Those who rob you will be robbed. I will punish those who attack you.
I will make you well again. I will heal your wounds. People called you someone no one wants. They said no one cares about Zion."
The LORD says, "I will bring Jacob's homes back. I will be kind to his tents. The city will be built again on its hill. The palace will stand where it was.
Songs of thanks will come from them. People will celebrate. I will make them many. They will not be few. I will make them great. They will not be small.
Their children will be like before. Their group will be set up before Me. I will punish all who hurt them.
Their leader will be one of them. Their ruler will come from among them. I will bring him near to Me. He will come to Me. No one would dare come to Me on his own.
You will be My people, and I will be your God."
The LORD's storm goes out in anger. It is a strong storm. It will hit the heads of bad people.
The LORD's great anger will not stop until He does what He plans. In the last days, you will understand this.
"At that time," declares the LORD, "I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be My people."
This is what the LORD says: "The people who lived through war found help in the desert. Israel, when I go to give him rest,
the LORD showed Himself to me from far away. He said, 'I have loved you with a love that lasts forever. So I have pulled you close with kind love.'"
"I will build you again, and you will be built again, O young woman Israel. You will again play your tambourines and dance with joy.
You will plant grape fields again on the hills of Samaria. The farmers will plant and eat the fruit."
"For a day will come when watchmen on Ephraim's hills call out, 'Get up! Let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!'"
For this is what the LORD says: "Sing with joy for Jacob. Shout among the leading nations. Let your praise be heard. Say, 'O the LORD, save Your people, the rest of Israel!'"

"Look, I will bring them from the north land and gather them from the ends of the earth. The blind and the lame will be with them. So will women who are expecting and women in labor. A big group will come back!"
"They will come crying. I will lead them with prayer. I will make them walk by streams of water. They will walk on a straight path and not trip. For I am Israel's Father. Ephraim is My Firstborn."
Listen to the LORD's word, O nations. Tell it far away by the sea: "The One who scattered Israel will gather him. He will keep him like a shepherd keeps his sheep."
For the LORD has paid to free Jacob. He has saved him from the hand that was too strong for him.

They will come and shout for joy on Zion's high places. They will shine because of the LORD's good gifts—grain, new wine, oil, and young sheep and cows. Their life will be like a watered garden. They will not be weak again.
Then the young women will dance with joy. Young men and old men will too. I will turn their sadness into joy. I will comfort them and make them glad instead of sad.
"I will fill the priests with plenty. My people will be full with My good things," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "A voice is heard in Ramah. It is crying and loud weeping. Rachel cries for her children. She will not be comforted, because they are gone."
This is what the LORD says: "Stop your crying. Stop your tears. You will be paid for your work," says the LORD. "Your children will come back from the enemy's land.
There is hope for your future," says the LORD. "Your children will come back to their own land."
"I have heard Ephraim crying." "You corrected me, and I was corrected like a young cow that is not trained. Bring me back, and I will come back, for You are the LORD my God.
After I came back, I was sorry. After I learned, I hit my leg in grief. I was ashamed and embarrassed, because I carried the shame of my youth."
"Is Ephraim not My dear son? Is he not My joy? I speak against him, but I still remember him. So My heart wants him. I have deep pity for him," says the LORD.
"Put up road signs for yourself. Make signposts. Remember the road you traveled. Come back, O young woman Israel. Come back to your cities.
How long will you wander, you stubborn daughter? For the LORD has made something new on earth: a woman will surround a man."
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "When I bring them back, they will say this again in Judah and its cities:" "The LORD bless you, O good home, O holy mountain."
"Judah and all its cities will live together in the land. So will farmers and people who move with their sheep.
For I have given rest to the tired soul. I have filled every sad soul."
Then I woke up and looked around. My sleep was very sweet to me.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will fill Israel and Judah with people and animals.
Just as I watched over them to pull up and tear down, to destroy and ruin, and to bring trouble, so I will watch over them to build and plant," says the LORD.
"In those days, people will not say, 'Fathers ate sour grapes, and children's teeth hurt.'
Instead, each person will die for his own sin. The person who eats sour grapes will have his own teeth hurt."
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will make a new promise with Israel and Judah.
It will not be like the promise I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt. They broke that promise, even though I was like a husband to them," says the LORD.
"But this is the promise I will make with Israel after those days," says the LORD. "I will put My law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be My people.

No one will need to teach his neighbor or brother, saying, 'Know the LORD,' because all of them will know Me, from the small to the great," says the LORD. "For I will forgive their wrongs and not remember their sins anymore."
This is what the LORD says: "He gives the sun for light in the day. He sets the moon and stars for light at night. He stirs the sea so its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is His name."
"Only if these rules stop before My eyes," says the LORD, "will Israel's children stop being a nation before Me."
This is what the LORD says: "Only if the sky above can be measured and the earth's base below can be found out will I turn away from all of Israel's children for all they have done," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will stretch out straight to Gareb hill and then turn toward Goah.

The whole valley of dead bodies and ashes, and all the fields to the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate in the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will never be pulled up or torn down again."
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah. This was in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah. It was also the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
At that time, the army of the king of Babylon was all around Jerusalem. Jeremiah the prophet was locked up in the prison yard of the king's palace.
Zedekiah king of Judah had put him there. He asked, "Why do you say the LORD says He will give this city to the king of Babylon? He will capture it."
Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape the Babylonians. He will be given to the king of Babylon. He will speak to him face to face. He will see him with his own eyes.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon. Zedekiah will stay there until I come to him, says the LORD. You may fight the Babylonians, but you will not win.
Jeremiah said, "The LORD spoke to me."
The LORD said, "Look, your cousin Hanamel, son of Shallum, is coming to you. He will ask you to buy his field in Anathoth. You have the right to buy it back."

Then my cousin Hanamel came to me in the prison yard, just as the LORD had said. He said, "Please buy my field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin. You have the right to own it, and you can buy it back. Buy it for yourself." Then I knew this was the LORD's word.
So I bought the field from my cousin Hanamel in Anathoth. I weighed out seventeen pieces of silver.
I wrote it down and sealed it. I had people watch. I weighed the silver on a scale.
I took the deed. One copy was sealed, and one copy was open. It had the rules for buying land.
I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah. My cousin Hanamel, the witnesses who signed it, and all the Jews in the prison yard saw me do it.
While they watched, I told Baruch what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, said.
The LORD said, "Take these deeds, the sealed one and the open one, and put them in a clay jar. They will last a long time."
The LORD also said, "People will again buy houses, fields, and vineyards in this land."
After I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
"Oh, Lord, the LORD, You made the sky and the earth by Your great power and strong help. Nothing is too hard for You.
You show love to thousands, but You pay back the wrong of fathers to their children after them. You are the great and powerful God. The LORD Almighty is Your name.
Your plans are great, and You do mighty things. Your eyes see all people. You give each person what they deserve for how they live.
You did signs and wonders in Egypt long ago. You still do them in Israel and among all people. You made Yourself famous, as You have today.
You brought Your people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders. You used Your strong hand and great power. You made people afraid.
You gave them this land. You promised it to their fathers. It is a land full of good things.
They came and took the land. But they did not listen to You. They did not follow Your law. They did not do what You told them. So You brought all this trouble on them.
Now the enemy has built ramps to take the city. The city will be given to the Babylonians who fight it. There is war, hunger, and sickness. What You said has happened. You can see it.
But You told me to buy the field with money and have people watch. Yet the city is being given to the Babylonians."
Then the LORD spoke to Jeremiah. He said,
"Look, I am the LORD, the God of all people. Nothing is too hard for Me.
So I am giving this city to the Babylonians and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will take it.

The Babylonians who are fighting this city will come in and set it on fire. They will burn it down. They will burn the houses where people burned incense to Baal on the roofs. They also poured out drinks to other gods to make Me angry.
The people of Israel and Judah have done only evil in My sight since they were young. The people of Israel have only made Me angry with what they do.
This city has made Me angry and mad since it was built. I will get rid of it.
The people of Israel and Judah did many wrong things. They made Me angry. Their kings, leaders, priests, and prophets did it. The people of Judah and the people of Jerusalem did it too.
They turned their backs to Me, not their faces. I taught them again and again, but they did not listen. They would not learn.
They put their horrible idols in the house where My name is. They made it unclean.

They built places to worship Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. They burned their sons and daughters in the fire for Molech. I did not tell them to do this. It never came to My mind. They did this terrible thing and made Judah sin."
Now the LORD, the God of Israel, says this about the city you talk about. You say it is being given to the king of Babylon by war, hunger, and sickness.
But I will bring them back from all the lands where I sent them when I was angry. I will bring them back to this place. They will live in safety.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way. They will respect Me all their days. This will be good for them and their children after them.
I will make a promise with them that lasts forever. I will not stop doing good to them. I will put respect for Me in their hearts. They will not leave Me.
I will be happy to do good for them. I will plant them in this land with all My heart and all My soul.
Just as I brought all this big trouble on these people, I will bring all the good things I promised them.
People will buy fields in this land you call empty. You say no people or animals live there. It is given to the Babylonians.

People will buy fields with money. They will write deeds and seal them. They will have people watch. This will happen in Benjamin, around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, the hill country, the lowlands, and the south. I will bring My people back, says the LORD.
Jeremiah was still in the prison yard.
The LORD said, "I made the world. I shaped it and set it firm.
The LORD is His name. Call to Me. I will answer you. I will tell you great things you do not know."
The LORD, the God of Israel, said, "This is about the houses in this city and the kings' houses in Judah. They were torn down to help the enemy.
The enemy is coming to fight. The houses will be full of dead people. I struck those people down because I was angry. I turned away from this city because of all its evil."
The LORD said, "But I will bring health and healing to this city. I will heal My people. I will give them much peace and truth.
I will bring Judah and Israel back from being taken away. I will build them up like before.
I will make them clean from all the wrong they did against Me. I will forgive all their sins.

Then this city will be a reason for joy and praise and honor to all nations on earth. They will hear about all the good I do for My people. They will be amazed and afraid because of all the good and peace I give."

The LORD said, "In this place you say is empty, with no people or animals, in Judah's towns and Jerusalem's streets that are empty, with no one living there and no animals, people will hear sounds again.

People will hear joy and gladness. People will hear the bride and groom. People will hear others thank the LORD in His house. They will say, 'Give thanks to the LORD of all armies. The LORD is good. His faithful love lasts forever.' "For I will make this land good again like before," says the LORD.
The LORD of all armies said, "This empty place, with no people or animals, and all its towns, will have shepherds again. Their sheep will rest there.
In the hill towns, the lowland towns, the south towns, Benjamin's land, around Jerusalem, and Judah's towns, sheep will walk past the one who counts them," says the LORD.
The LORD said, "Days are coming when I will keep My good promise to Israel and Judah.
In those days, I will make a good and fair king grow from David's family. He will do what is right in the land.
In those days, Judah will be saved. Jerusalem will be safe. People will call her, 'The LORD is the One who makes us right.'"
The LORD said, "David will never run out of sons to sit on Israel's throne.
The priests from Levi's family will never run out of men to bring offerings to Me," says the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah again.
He said, "If you can break My promise of day and night, so day and night do not come at the right time,
then you can break My promise to David and the priests. That would mean David has no son to rule.
But just as no one can count the stars or measure the sand by the sea, I will make David's family and the Levites who serve Me very many," says the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah again.
He said, "Have you seen what these people say? They say, 'The LORD chose two families, but He threw them away.' "They look down on My people. They say My people are not a nation anymore.
But if I did not set day and night and the rules for sky and earth,

then I would also throw away Jacob's children and David My servant. I would not let David's children rule over Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob's children. But I will bring My people back and show them mercy," says the LORD.

This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD. It came when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, all his army, all the kingdoms he ruled, and all the people were fighting against Jerusalem and its cities.
The LORD, the God of Israel, says, "Go and tell Zedekiah king of Judah that I will give this city to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.
You will not get away from him. You will be caught and given to him. You will see the king of Babylon in person, and you will talk with him. Then you will go to Babylon.
But listen to the LORD's word, Zedekiah king of Judah. The LORD says about you, 'You will not die by the sword.
You will die in peace. People will burn spices for you, like they did for your fathers, the kings before you. They will mourn for you and call you their king. For I have said this, says the LORD.'"
Jeremiah the prophet told all this to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.
At that time, the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and the other cities left in Judah, Lachish and Azekah. These were the only strong cities left in Judah.
After King Zedekiah made a promise with all the people in Jerusalem to set slaves free,
each person was to set free his Hebrew slave, man or woman. No one was to make a fellow Jew work as a slave.
All the leaders and all the people who joined the promise agreed to set free their male and female slaves. They obeyed and let them go. They did not make them work as slaves anymore.
But later they changed their minds. They took back the men and women they had set free and made them slaves again.
Then the LORD spoke to Jeremiah again.
The LORD, the God of Israel, says, "I made a promise with your fathers when I brought them out of Egypt, out of the land where they were slaves.

I said, 'At the end of seven years, you must set free a Hebrew brother who sold himself to you. He will work for you six years, and then you must set him free.' But your fathers did not listen to Me. They did not pay attention.
Recently you turned back and did what is right in My eyes. You set your neighbors free, and you made a promise before Me in the place that has My name.
But now you have turned back. You have dishonored My name. Each of you took back your male and female slaves after you set them free. You forced them to be slaves again.

So the LORD says, 'You did not obey Me. You did not set your brothers and neighbors free. So now I set you free, says the LORD. I will let war, disease, and hunger come to you. I will make you a terrible thing to all the kingdoms of the earth.'"
I will treat people who broke My promise like the calf they cut in two and walked between. They did not keep the words of the promise they made before Me.
The leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people who walked between the pieces of the calf,
I will give them to their enemies who want to kill them. Their dead bodies will be food for birds and animals.
I will give Zedekiah king of Judah and his leaders to their enemies who want to kill them, and to the Babylonian army that has pulled back from you.

I am going to give the command, says the LORD. I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, take it, and burn it down. I will make the cities of Judah empty, with no one living in them.
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah. This was when Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, was king of Judah.
The LORD said, "Go to the Rechabites. Talk to them. Bring them to one of the rooms in the house of the LORD. Give them wine to drink."
So Jeremiah took Jaazaniah. He was the son of Jeremiah and the grandson of Habazziniah. Jeremiah also took Jaazaniah's brothers and all his sons. He took all the Rechabites.

He brought them to the house of the LORD. They went to the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah. He was a man of God. This room was next to the room of the leaders. It was above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, who guarded the door.
Jeremiah put bowls full of wine and cups in front of the Rechabites. He said, "Drink some wine."
But they said, "We will not drink wine. Our father, Jonadab son of Rechab, told us not to drink wine. He said we and our children must never drink it.

He also said we must not build houses. We must not plant seeds. We must not plant grapevines. We must not own them. We must live in tents all our lives. Then we will live a long time in the land where we live.
We listened to our father, Jonadab son of Rechab. We do not drink wine. This is true for us, our wives, our sons, and our daughters.
We do not build houses to live in. We have no grapevines, fields, or seeds.
We live in tents. We listen to our father, Jonadab. We do what he told us.
When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to this land, we said, 'Let us go to Jerusalem. The armies of Babylon and Aram are coming.' So we came to Jerusalem and stayed there."
Then the LORD spoke to Jeremiah again.
The LORD of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, said, "Go and tell the people of Judah and the people in Jerusalem, 'Will you not learn to listen to My words?' says the LORD."

"Jonadab son of Rechab told his sons not to drink wine. They have not drunk wine to this day. They obeyed their father's command. But I have spoken to you again and again. You have not listened to Me."

"I sent all My servants, the prophets, to you. I said, 'Turn from your bad ways. Do good things. Do not follow other gods. Serve them no more. Then you can stay in the land I gave you and your fathers.' But you did not listen to Me. You did not pay attention."
"The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab kept their father's command. But these people have not listened to Me."

So the LORD of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, says, "I will bring on Judah and on everyone in Jerusalem all the bad things I said I would bring. I spoke to them, but they did not listen. I called them, but they did not answer."
Jeremiah said to the Rechabites, "The LORD of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, says, 'You obeyed your father, Jonadab. You kept all his commands. You did what he told you.
So Jonadab son of Rechab will always have someone from his family to serve Me.'"
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came to Jeremiah from the LORD.
"Get a scroll. Write on it all the words I have spoken to you about Israel, Judah, and all the other nations. Write from the day I first spoke to you in Josiah's time until now.
Maybe the people of Judah will hear about all the bad things I plan to do to them. Then each person may stop doing bad things. Then I will forgive their sin."
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah. Baruch wrote on the scroll all the words the LORD had spoken to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah told Baruch, "I am stuck here. I cannot go to the LORD's house."
"So you go to the LORD's house on the fast day. Read the LORD's words from the scroll. Read them to all the people of Judah who come from their towns.
Maybe they will pray to the LORD. Maybe each person will stop doing bad things. The LORD is very angry with these people."
Baruch did everything Jeremiah the prophet told him. He read the LORD's words from the book in the LORD's house.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the towns of Judah said they would not eat before the LORD.

Then Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the book. He read them to all the people in the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe. This room was in the upper courtyard, by the New Gate of the LORD's house.
Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the LORD from the book.

He went down to the king's house, to the scribe's room. All the officials were sitting there. They were Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
Micaiah told them all the words he heard Baruch read to the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch. They said, "Bring the scroll you read to the people, and come here." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll and came to them.
They said to him, "Sit down and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
When they heard all the words, they were afraid. They looked at one another. They said to Baruch, "We must tell the king all these words."
Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you write all these words? Did he tell you to write them?"
Baruch said, "He spoke all these words to me. I wrote them with ink on the book."
The officials said to Baruch, "Go and hide. You and Jeremiah must hide. Do not let anyone know where you are."
Then they went to the king in the courtyard. They left the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe. They told the king all the words.
The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll. Jehudi took it from Elishama's room. He read it to the king and to all the officials standing by the king.
The king was sitting in his winter house. It was the ninth month. A fire burned in a pot in front of him.
As Jehudi read three or four parts, the king cut them with a knife. He threw them into the fire. He did this until the whole scroll was burned in the fire.
The king and all his servants who heard these words were not afraid. They did not show any sorrow.
Even Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah begged the king not to burn the scroll. But he would not listen to them.
The king told Jerahmeel son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD hid them.
After the king burned the scroll and the words Baruch wrote at Jeremiah's mouth, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
"Take another scroll. Write on it all the words that were on the first scroll. Jehoiakim, king of Judah, burned that scroll."

"Say to Jehoiakim, king of Judah, 'This is what the LORD says: You burned this scroll. You did not want the words that said the king of Babylon will come and destroy this land and kill people and animals.'"
"So this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim, king of Judah: No one from his family will rule as king after him. His dead body will be left outside in the heat by day and the cold by night."
"I will punish him, his children, and his servants for their sin. I will bring on them, on the people of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah all the bad things I spoke about. They did not listen."

Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe. Baruch wrote on it, at Jeremiah's mouth, all the words from the book that Jehoiakim, king of Judah, had burned in the fire. Many more words like them were added.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made Zedekiah son of Josiah king of Judah. Zedekiah ruled instead of Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim.
But Zedekiah, his helpers, and the people did not listen to the words the the LORD had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the priest, son of Maaseiah, to Jeremiah the prophet. They said, "Please pray to the the LORD our God for us."
Jeremiah could walk freely among the people, because he had not been put in prison yet.
Pharaoh's army came out of Egypt. When the Babylonians who were attacking Jerusalem heard about them, they left Jerusalem.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet.
The the LORD, the God of Israel, said, "Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to ask Me, 'Pharaoh's army that came to help you will go back to Egypt.'
Then the Babylonians will come back and fight this city. They will take it and burn it down."
The the LORD said, "Do not fool yourselves. You may say, 'The Babylonians will leave us.' But they will not!
Even if you beat the whole Babylonian army, so that only hurt men are left in their tents, they would still get up and burn this city down."
After the Babylonian army left Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah started to leave the city. He was going to the land of Benjamin to get his share of the land among the people there.
When he reached the Benjamin Gate, Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, the guard captain, arrested him. Irijah said, "You are running away to the Babylonians!"
Jeremiah said, "That is not true! I am not running away to the Babylonians." But Irijah would not listen to him. Instead, he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the leaders.
The leaders were angry with Jeremiah. They beat him and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the secretary. They had made that house into a prison.
Jeremiah was put in a deep cell in a dungeon. He stayed there many days.

King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah and had him brought to the palace. He asked him privately, "Is there any word from the the LORD?" Jeremiah answered, "Yes. You will be handed over to the king of Babylon."
Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What wrong did I do to you, your helpers, or these people, that you put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who said to you, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or this land'?
But now, my lord the king, please listen to me. Let my request come before you. Do not send me back to Jonathan's house, or I will die there."

King Zedekiah ordered that Jeremiah be put in the courtyard of the guard. He was to get a loaf of bread each day from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.
Four men named Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashhur heard what Jeremiah was saying to all the people.

He said, "This is what the LORD says: Anyone who stays in this city will die by sword, hunger, or sickness. But anyone who goes out to the Babylonians will live. He will keep his life like something taken in war, and he will live.
This is what the LORD says: This city will be given to the army of the king of Babylon. They will take it."

Then the officials said to the king, "This man should be put to death. He is making the soldiers and the people lose heart by saying these things. He does not want good for the people. He wants to hurt them."
The king said, "He is in your hands. I cannot stop you."

So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the pit of Malchijah, the king's son. It was in the courtyard of the guards. They let him down with ropes. There was no water in the pit, only mud, and Jeremiah sank in the mud.
Ebed-Melech the Cushite was a servant in the king's palace. He heard that they had put Jeremiah in the pit. The king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
Ebed-Melech went out from the palace and spoke to the king.
He said, "My lord the king, these men did wrong to Jeremiah the prophet. They threw him into the pit to die there of hunger, because there is no more bread in the city."
The king told Ebed-Melech, "Take thirty men from here and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the pit before he dies."
So Ebed-Melech took the men with him. He went to a room under the storehouse in the palace. He took old rags and old clothes and lowered them on ropes to Jeremiah in the pit.
He called down, "Put these rags and old clothes under your arms to pad the ropes." Jeremiah did so.
They pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and lifted him out of the pit. Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guards.
King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to the third entrance of the the LORD's house. The king said to Jeremiah, "I want to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me."
Jeremiah said, "If I tell you, you will kill me. And if I give advice, you won't listen to me."
But King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah secretly, "As sure as the LORD lives, who gave us breath, I will not kill you or hand you over to those men who want to kill you."

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD, the LORD All-Powerful, the God of Israel, says: If you go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, you will live. This city will not be burned. You and your family will live.
But if you do not go out, this city will be given to the Babylonians. They will burn it, and you will not escape."
Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who joined the Babylonians. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they might hurt me."
Jeremiah said, "They will not hand you over. Obey the LORD's voice in what I say. Then things will go well for you, and you will live.
But if you refuse to go out, this is what the LORD has shown me:

All the women left in the king's palace in Judah will be brought out to the Babylonian officials. Those women will say about you, 'Your friends tricked you and got the best of you. Your feet sank in the mud, and they turned away.'
All your wives and children will be led out to the Babylonians. You will not escape. You will be caught by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned."
Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not tell anyone about this talk, or you will die.
If the officials hear that I talked with you, they may come and say, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what he said to you. Do not hide it, or we will kill you.'
Then you are to say, 'I was just asking the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"
When all the officials came to Jeremiah and asked him questions, he told them everything the king had told him to say. They said nothing more to him, because no one had heard the talk.
Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guards until Jerusalem was taken. That is how it happened when Jerusalem was taken.

In the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came with all his army to Jerusalem. They surrounded the city and kept people from going in or out.
On the ninth day of the fourth month of Zedekiah's eleventh year, the city wall was broken through.

Then all the leaders of the king of Babylon came in and sat at the Middle Gate. They were Nergal-Sharezer, Samgar-Nebu, Sarsechim, Nergal-Sharezer the Rabmag, and all the other leaders of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah, king of Judah, and all his soldiers saw them, they ran away. They left the city at night through the king's garden. They went out through the gate between the two walls and headed toward the desert.

But the Babylonian army chased them. They caught Zedekiah on the flat land near Jericho. They took him to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, at Riblah in the land of Hamath. There the king decided his punishment.
At Riblah, the king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons while Zedekiah watched. He also killed all the important men of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes. He tied him with bronze chains and took him to Babylon.
The Babylonians burned the king's house and the people's houses. They also tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took the rest of the people who were left in the city to Babylon. This included the people who had gone over to the Babylonians.
But Nebuzaradan left some of the poor people in the land of Judah. They had nothing. That day he gave them grape fields and other fields.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had given orders about Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard. He said,
"Take him. Keep him safe. Do not hurt him in any way. Do for him whatever he asks you."
So Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, and Nebushazban, Nergal-Sharezer the Rabmag, and all the other chief officers of the king of Babylon sent men.
They took Jeremiah out of the courtyard of the guard. They gave him to Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. So Jeremiah stayed with the people.
While Jeremiah was still held in the courtyard of the guard, the LORD spoke to him.

"Go and tell Ebed-Melech, a man from Cush, that I, the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, say this: I am about to do what I said I would do to this city. It will bring trouble, not good. In that day these things will come true before your eyes.
"But I will save you that day, says the LORD. You will not be given to the men you fear.
I will surely save you. You will not die by the sword. You will keep your life, because you trusted in Me, says the LORD."

This is the message the the LORD gave Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan, the guard captain, set him free at Ramah. He had found Jeremiah in chains with the people from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken to Babylon.
The guard captain found Jeremiah and said, “The The LORD your God said this trouble would come to this place.
And now the the LORD has done it, just like He said. This happened because you sinned against the the LORD and did not listen to His voice. That is why this trouble came to you.

But now I am setting you free today from the chains on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will take care of you. But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, then don't come. Look, the whole land is in front of you. Go wherever seems good and right to you.”

But before Jeremiah could turn to leave, Nebuzaradan added, “Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan. The king of Babylon put him in charge of the cities of Judah. Stay with him among the people. Or go anywhere else that seems right to you.” Then the guard captain gave him food and a gift, and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. He stayed with him among the people left in the land.

All the army leaders in the fields and their men heard that the king of Babylon had put Gedaliah son of Ahikam in charge of the land. He was also in charge of the men, women, and children who were the poorest in the land. They had not been taken to Babylon.

So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai from Netophah, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, along with their men.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, took an oath before them and their men. He said, “Do not be afraid to serve the Babylonians. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.
As for me, I will stay in Mizpah to speak for you to the Babylonians who come to us. You gather wine, summer fruit, and oil. Put them in your jars. Live in the cities you have taken.”
All the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left some people in Judah. They heard he had put Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over them.
So they came back from all the places where they had been scattered. They came to Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They gathered a lot of wine and summer fruit.
Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the army leaders in the fields came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
They said to him, “Do you know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?” But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah in private at Mizpah. He said, “Let me go kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No one will know. Why should he kill you and scatter all the Jews who are gathered to you? Then the rest of the people of Judah would die.”
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, “Do not do this. You are telling lies about Ishmael.”
In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, came to Mizpah. He was from the king's family. Ten men came with him. They ate with Gedaliah son of Ahikam.
Then Ishmael and his ten men stood up. They killed Gedaliah with a sword. Gedaliah was the man the king of Babylon had put in charge of the land.
Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah. He killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there too.
The next day, no one yet knew Gedaliah was dead.
Eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They had shaved their beards and torn their clothes. They were sad and had cut themselves. They brought gifts and incense to the house of the LORD.
Ishmael went out from Mizpah to meet them. He was crying. He walked toward them and said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
When they came into the town, Ishmael and his men killed them. They threw the bodies into a deep hole in the ground.
But ten men said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us! We have wheat, barley, oil, and honey hidden in a field." So he did not kill them.
The deep hole was one King Asa had made long ago. He made it to hide from Baasha, king of Israel. Ishmael filled it with dead bodies.

Ishmael took all the people left in Mizpah as captives. This included the king's daughters and the other people. Nebuzaradan, the guard leader, had put Gedaliah in charge of them. Ishmael took them and started to go to the Ammonites.
Johanan son of Kareah and the army leaders with him heard what Ishmael had done.
They took their men and went to fight Ishmael. They caught up with him near the big pool in Gibeon.
The people with Ishmael saw Johanan and his leaders. They were glad.
All the people Ishmael had taken turned and went to Johanan.
Ishmael and eight of his men got away from Johanan. They ran to the Ammonites.
Then Johanan and his leaders took all the survivors from Mizpah. These were the people he had saved from Ishmael. They were soldiers, women, children, and servants. He brought them from Gibeon.
They went and stayed at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem. They were on their way to Egypt.
They were afraid of the Babylonians. This was because Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had put in charge of the land.
All the army leaders came to Jeremiah. They were Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
They said, "Please listen to our request. Pray to the the LORD your God for us. Pray for this small group that is left. We are only a few left from many, as you can see.
May the the LORD your God show us the way to go and what to do."
Jeremiah the prophet said, "I have heard you. I will pray to the the LORD your God, just as you asked. I will tell you everything the the LORD answers you. I will not keep back any word."
Then they said, "May the the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not do all the word the the LORD your God sends you to tell us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the the LORD our God. We are sending you to Him so that things may go well for us. We will obey the the LORD our God."
After ten days, the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah.
So he called Johanan son of Kareah, all the army leaders with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
He said to them, "This is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says. You sent me to bring your request to Him.
"If you stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down. I will plant you and not pull you up. I am sorry for the trouble I brought on you.
"Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon. You are afraid of him now, but do not be afraid of him, says the the LORD. I am with you to save you and rescue you from his power.
"I will make him show you mercy. He will be kind to you and bring you back to your own land.
"But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and you do not obey the the LORD your God,
and you say, 'No, we will go to Egypt. There we will not see war. We will not hear the trumpet. We will not be hungry for food. We will live there,'
"then listen to the word of the the LORD, you who are left of Judah. The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'If you decide to go to Egypt and live there,
then the sword you fear will catch up with you there in Egypt. The hunger you worry about will follow you there. You will die there.
"All the people who decide to go to Egypt to live there will die by war, hunger, and sickness. Not one of them will be left. No one will escape the trouble I will bring on them.'

"The The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'Just as My anger was poured out on the people of Jerusalem, so My anger will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become a curse, a shock, a bad example, and a shame. You will not see this place again.'
"The The LORD has spoken to you, you who are left of Judah: 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for sure that I have warned you today.
"You have fooled yourselves. You sent me to the the LORD your God and said, 'Pray to the the LORD our God for us. Tell us everything the the LORD our God says, and we will do it.'
"I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the the LORD your God. You have not done anything He sent me to tell you.
"So know for sure that you will die by war, hunger, and sickness in the place you want to go and live."
Jeremiah finished telling all the people all the words the LORD their God had sent him. These were all words from the LORD for them.
Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the proud men said to Jeremiah, "You are telling a lie. the LORD our God did not send you to say, 'Do not go to Egypt to live there.'
But Baruch son of Neriah is turning you against us. He wants the Chaldeans to kill us and take us to Babylon."
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the army leaders, and all the people did not obey the LORD. They did not stay in the land of Judah.
Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army leaders took all the people left in Judah. These people had come back from many nations to live in Judah.

They took the men, the women, the children, the king's daughters, and every other person. Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left these people with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan. They also took Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to Egypt because they did not obey the LORD. They came to Tahpanhes.
Then the LORD spoke to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes.
He said, "Take some big stones in your hand. Hide them in the cement in the brick floor at the entrance to Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes. Do this while the men of Judah watch.

Say to them, 'This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am going to send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. I will set his throne over these stones I hid. He will spread his royal tent over them.
He will come and attack Egypt. Some will die. Some will be taken captive. Some will be killed with swords.
I will set fire to the houses of Egypt's gods. He will burn them and carry the people away. He will wrap himself in Egypt like a shepherd wraps his coat. Then he will leave in peace.
He will break the stone pillars at Beth-shemesh in Egypt. He will burn the houses of Egypt's gods.'"
This message came to Jeremiah for all the Jews living in Egypt—in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph, and Pathros.
The LORD said, "You have seen all the trouble I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah. Look, they are empty today. No one lives there.
This happened because of the bad things they did. They made Me angry. They burned incense and served other gods. Those gods were not known by them or by their fathers.
I sent all My servants, the prophets. I sent them again and again. I said, 'Do not do this terrible thing that I hate.'
But they did not listen. They did not pay attention. They did not turn from their bad ways. They kept burning incense to other gods.
So My anger flared up. It burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. They became empty ruins, as they are today."
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, "Why are you doing such a bad thing to yourselves? Why are you cutting off the men and women, children and babies of Judah? Then no one will be left.

You make Me angry with what your hands do. You burn incense to other gods in Egypt, where you have come to live. You do this so you will be cut off. You will become a curse and a shame among all the nations.

Have you forgotten the bad things your fathers did? Have you forgotten the bad things the kings of Judah did? Have you forgotten the bad things their wives did? Have you forgotten your own bad things and your wives' bad things? They did these things in Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem.
To this day they have not been sorry. They have not shown respect. They have not followed My law and My rules that I gave to you and your fathers."
So the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, "I am turning against you for trouble. I will cut off all of Judah.

I will take the rest of Judah who decided to go to Egypt to live there. They will all die in Egypt. They will die by the sword and by hunger. From the least to the greatest, they will die. They will become a curse, a horror, and a shame.
I will punish the people who live in Egypt, just as I punished Jerusalem. They will die by the sword, by hunger, and by disease.
None of the rest of Judah who came to Egypt to live there will escape or survive. No one will go back to Judah, except a few who escape."
Then all the men who knew their wives burned incense to other gods, and all the women standing there in the large crowd, and all the people living in Egypt in Pathros, answered Jeremiah. They said,
"We will not listen to you or to the word you spoke to us in the name of the LORD.

We will do everything we said we would do. We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven. We will pour out drink offerings to her. We and our fathers, our kings and our leaders, did this in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of bread. We were well off, and we saw no trouble.
But since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything. We have been killed by the sword and by hunger."
The women said, "When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make her cakes and pour out drink offerings without our husbands knowing?"
Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and women who had answered him,

"The incense you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings, your leaders, and all the people—did not the LORD remember it? Did it not come to His mind?

The LORD could not stand it anymore because of your evil deeds and the terrible things you did. So your land became empty ruins and a horror. It became a curse, with no one living there, as it is today.

This happened because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD. You did not obey the LORD. You did not follow His law, His rules, or His teachings. So this trouble came on you, as it has today."
Jeremiah said to all the people and to the women, "Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah in Egypt."

The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, "You and your wives have said with your mouths and done with your hands what you promised. You said, 'We will keep our promises. We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' So go ahead. Keep your promises. Do what you said.

But now hear the word of the LORD, all Judah living in Egypt. I have sworn by My great name, says the LORD, that no one in Judah living in Egypt will ever again use My name to make a promise. No one will say, 'As the Lord the LORD lives.'
I am watching over them for trouble, not for good. All the men of Judah in Egypt will die by the sword and by hunger until they are gone.
Only a few will escape the sword and return from Egypt to Judah. Then all the rest of Judah who came to Egypt to live will know whose word is true—Mine or theirs.
This will be a sign to you that I will punish you in this place. Then you will know that My words will come true and bring trouble.

I will give Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, to his enemies and to those who want to kill him. I did the same thing to Zedekiah, king of Judah. I gave him to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy who wanted to kill him."

This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah. Baruch wrote these words on a scroll as Jeremiah said them. This was in the fourth year of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah. He said:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
You said, 'I am so sad! The LORD has added sorrow to my pain. I am tired from crying, and I have found no rest.'
So you must tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: I will tear down what I built. I will pull up what I planted. This is for the whole earth.'
And you? Do you look for big things for yourself? Do not look for them. I will bring trouble on all people, says the LORD. But I will give you your life wherever you go."
This is the message from the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet about the nations.

It is about Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt. His army was by the Euphrates River at Carchemish. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, beat them in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Get your shields ready. Get your armor ready. Get ready to fight.
Tie up the horses. Ride, horsemen! Stand in your helmets. Shine your spears. Put on your armor.
Why do I see them scared? They run away. Their strong men are beaten. They run fast and do not look back. Fear is all around them, says the LORD.
Do not let the fast runner get away. Do not let the strong man escape. In the north, by the Euphrates River, they trip and fall.
Who is rising like the Nile, with water like rushing rivers?
Egypt rises like the Nile. Its water rushes like rivers. Egypt says, "I will rise. I will cover the earth. I will destroy cities and the people in them."
Horses, go forward! Chariots, rush in! Strong men, go out to fight. Soldiers from Cush and Put carry shields. Soldiers from Lud use bows.

That day belongs to the Lord, the LORD of heaven's armies. It is a day when He punishes His enemies. The sword will eat and drink its fill of their blood. The Lord, the LORD of heaven's armies, has a sacrifice in the north by the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get medicine, young woman of Egypt. You used many medicines for nothing. There is no healing for you.
The nations heard about your shame. Your cry fills the earth. Strong men trip over each other. They both fall.
This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah the prophet. It is about Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, coming to attack Egypt.
Tell it in Egypt. Announce it in Migdol. Announce it in Memphis and Tahpanhes. Say, "Get ready. Be prepared. The sword will destroy all around you."
Why are your brave men swept away? They did not stand, because the LORD pushed them down.
He made many trip and fall on each other. They said, "Get up. Let us go back to our people and our home land. Let us get away from the sword of the cruel enemy."
People called Pharaoh, king of Egypt, Noise. He let his chance pass.
"As surely as I live, says the King. His name is the LORD of heaven's armies. Someone will come like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea."
Get your things ready to leave, people of Egypt. Memphis will become empty and burned. No one will live there.
Egypt is like a pretty young cow. But a biting fly from the north is coming, coming.
Her hired soldiers are like fat calves. They also turn and run. They do not stand, because their bad day has come. It is time for them to be punished.
She hisses like a snake. They march with an army and come with axes, like men cutting wood.
They will cut down her thick forest, says the LORD. It is too thick to search. They are more than grasshoppers. They cannot be counted.
The people of Egypt will be put to shame. They will be given to the people of the north.
The LORD of heaven's armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I will punish Amon of No, Pharaoh, Egypt, her gods, her kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.
I will give them to those who want to kill them. I will give them to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and his men. After that, Egypt will be lived in again like before, says the LORD."

"But you, Jacob My servant, do not be afraid. Do not be scared, Israel. Look, I will save you from far away. I will save your children from the land where they are captives. Jacob will come back. He will be quiet and safe. No one will scare him.

You, My servant Jacob, do not be afraid, says the LORD. I am with you. I will completely destroy all the nations where I sent you. But I will not completely destroy you. I will punish you fairly. I will not leave you without punishment."
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet. It was about the Philistines. This was before Pharaoh attacked Gaza.

This is what the LORD says: "An army is coming from the north. It will be like a big flood. It will cover the land and everything in it. It will cover the city and the people living there. The people will cry out. Everyone in the land will wail.
They will hear the loud sound of horses' hoofs. They will hear chariots rushing and wheels rumbling. Fathers will not even look back to help their children. They will be too weak.
"This will happen on the day the LORD destroys all the Philistines. He will cut off Tyre and Sidon and every helper left. The LORD is destroying the Philistines, the people left from Caphtor.
Gaza will be ruined. Ashkelon will be destroyed. You who are left in the valley, how long will you keep mourning?
"Oh, sword of the LORD! How long until you stop? Go back into your sheath. Rest and be still!
How can it be quiet when the LORD has given it a job? He has set it against Ashkelon and the coast."
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says about Moab: "Oh no! Nebo is ruined! Kiriathaim is taken and put to shame. The strong place is put to shame and broken."

"Moab will not be praised anymore. In Heshbon, people made bad plans against Moab. They said, "Come, let's cut Moab off so it is not a nation anymore." "Madmen, you will be quiet too. The sword will come after you."
A cry comes from Horonaim: "Everything is ruined! It is a big breakdown!"
"Moab is destroyed. Its little ones cry out.
They go up the hill to Luhith, crying. On the way down to Horonaim, they hear cries of trouble."
"Run! Save your lives! Be like a bush in the desert.
You trusted in your own work and treasures, so you will be caught too. Chemosh will be taken away. His priests and leaders will go with him."
The destroyer will come to every city. No city will get away. The valley will die, and the flat land will be ruined, just as the LORD said.
"Give Moab wings, so it can fly away and get free. Its cities will be empty, with no one living in them."
A person who does the the LORD's work in a lazy way will be cursed. A person who keeps his sword from blood will be cursed.
"Moab has been safe since it was young. It stayed calm and did not move. It was not poured from jar to jar. It did not go away. So its old ways stayed in it, and its smell did not change."
The LORD says, "Days are coming when I will send men to pour Moab out. They will empty its jars and break its pots."
"Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just like Israel was ashamed of Bethel, the thing they trusted.
How can you say that you are strong men and brave men for war?"
"Moab is ruined. Its cities are taken. Its best young men are going down to be killed. This is what the King says. His name is the LORD of Armies.
Moab's trouble is near. Its bad time is coming very fast."
"All of you around Moab, cry for it. All of you who know Moab's name, say this:" "How the strong stick is broken! How the beautiful rod is broken!"
"Come down from your glory and sit thirsty, you who live in Dibon. The destroyer of Moab has come up against you. He has ruined your strong places.
Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer. Ask those who run away and escape what happened."
"Moab is ashamed, for it is broken. Cry out and wail! Tell it by the Arnon River that Moab is ruined."
Judgment has come to the flat land: to Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
to Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the cities of Moab, far and near.
The LORD says, "Moab's power is cut off, and its strength is broken.
Make Moab drunk, because it made itself bigger than the the LORD. Moab will roll in its own sick. People will laugh at it too."
"Was Israel not a joke to you? Was Israel found with thieves? Every time you talked about Israel, you shook your head.
Leave the cities and live in the rocks, you people of Moab. Be like a dove that makes its nest in the sides of a deep hole."
"We have heard how proud Moab is. Moab is very proud. We have heard about its high place, its pride, its bragging, and its proud heart.
I know Moab's pride, says the LORD, but it is not right. Its bragging has not done what it says."
"So I will cry for Moab. I will cry out for all of Moab. I will be sad for the people of Kir-heres.
I will cry for you more than for Jazer's vine, you vine of Sibmah. Your branches went over the sea. They reached the sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your summer fruit and your grapes."
"Joy and gladness are taken away from the good land and from Moab. I have stopped the wine in the presses. No one steps on grapes with a happy shout. The happy shout is gone.
From the cry of Heshbon to Elealeh, and to Jahaz, they lift up their voices. From Zoar to Horonaim, and to Eglath-shelishiyah. The waters of Nimrim will become dry and ruined."
The LORD says, "I will stop in Moab the one who offers sacrifice on the high place and the one who burns incense to his god.
So my heart is sad for Moab like flutes. My heart is sad for the people of Kir-heres like flutes, because the rich things Moab had are gone."
Every head is shaved. Every beard is cut. Every hand has cuts. Every person wears rough cloth around the waist.
"On every roof in Moab and in its streets, there is crying. I have broken Moab like a jar no one likes, says the LORD.
How it is broken! They wail. How Moab has turned its back in shame! Moab will be a joke and a scare to all around it."
The LORD says, "Look! Someone will fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth is taken. The strong places are seized. In that day, the hearts of Moab's brave men will be like the heart of a woman in pain."
"Moab will be destroyed and not be a people anymore, because it made itself bigger than the the LORD.
Terror, pit, and trap are on you, you who live in Moab, says the LORD."
"The one who runs from terror will fall into the pit. The one who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. I will bring on Moab the year it must be punished, says the LORD.
Those who ran away stand in the shadow of Heshbon, with no strength. Fire came out from Heshbon. A flame came from Sihon. It has eaten the edge of Moab and the top of the noisy people."
"Trouble is coming to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh are gone. Your sons are taken away. Your daughters are taken away too."
"But in the last days, I will bring Moab back from being taken away, says the LORD. This is the end of the judgment on Moab."
This is what the LORD says about the Ammonites: "Does Israel have no children? Does Israel have no one to take his place? Then why did Milcom take Gad? Why do his people live in Gad's towns?

So listen. The days are coming. I will make a loud battle cry against Rabbah, the main city of Ammon. It will become a pile of ruins. Its small towns will burn. Then Israel will take back what was taken from him.
Cry out, Heshbon, because Ai is ruined! Cry out, women of Rabbah! Put on rough cloth and be sad. Run along the walls. Milcom will be carried away, and his priests and leaders will go with him."
"Why do you brag about your valleys? You turn away, but you trust your stored treasures. You say, 'Who can come against me?'

I will bring fear on you. Fear will come from all around you. You will be pushed out. Each person will run straight ahead. No one will gather the ones who run away," says the Lord the LORD of Armies. "But later I will bring the Ammonites back from being captives."
This is what the LORD of Armies says about Edom: "Is there no wisdom in Teman? Has good advice died? Has their wisdom gone?
Turn and run! Live deep in the caves, people of Dedan. I am bringing trouble on Esau. It is time to punish him.
If grape pickers came, would they leave a few grapes? If thieves came at night, would they take only what they need?
But I will strip Esau bare. I will uncover his hiding places. He cannot hide. His children, his brothers, and his neighbors will be ruined. Then he will be no more.
Leave your orphans. I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in Me."
"This is what the LORD says: Even those who should not have to drink the cup must drink it. You will not go free. You will drink it.
I have sworn by Myself that Bozrah will become a ruined place. People will laugh at it. It will be empty and cursed. All its towns will be ruins forever.
I have heard a message from the LORD. A messenger is sent to the nations: Gather together and attack Edom! Get ready for war!
I will make you small among the nations. People will look down on you.
Your pride has tricked you. You live in the cracks of the rocks. You hold the high hill. But even if you build your nest high like an eagle, I will bring you down."
"Edom will be a ruined place. Everyone who passes by will be shocked. They will whistle at all its wounds.
Edom will be like Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them. No one will live there. No person will stay there.

Like a lion coming from the bushes by the Jordan to a green field, I will chase Edom away fast. Then I will choose a young leader for it. Who is like Me? Who can stand against Me? What shepherd can stand before Me?
So listen to the LORD's plan for Edom. Listen to what He plans for the people of Teman. Even the little sheep will be dragged away. Their home will be destroyed.
At the sound of their fall the earth will shake. Their cry will be heard at the Red Sea.
Look! Someone will fly up like an eagle and swoop down. He will spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day, the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in pain."
"Hamath and Arpad are ashamed. They heard bad news and melted with fear. They are worried like the sea that cannot be quiet.
Damascus has become weak. It turned to run. Fear has taken hold. Pain and sorrow have grabbed it, like a woman having a baby.
How can the city that was praised be left alone? It was the city I loved.
So its young men will fall in its streets. All the soldiers will be silent on that day.
I will set fire to the wall of Damascus. It will burn the palaces of Ben-Hadad," says the LORD of Armies.
This is what the LORD says: "Get up and attack Kedar. Destroy the people of the east.
They will take their tents and sheep. They will take their curtains and all their things. They will take their camels. They will shout, 'Fear is all around!'
Run away! Get far away! Live deep in the caves, people of Hazor," says the LORD. "The king of Babylon has made a plan against you. He has thought of a plan.
Get up and attack a nation that feels safe. It lives alone. It has no gates and no bars. It lives by itself.
Their camels will be taken. Their many animals will be taken. I will scatter them to the wind. I will bring trouble from every side.
Hazor will be a home for wild dogs. It will be empty forever. No one will live there. No person will stay there."
This is the LORD's message to Jeremiah the prophet about Elam. It came at the start of Zedekiah's rule over Judah.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "I will break the bow of Elam. It is the best of their power.
I will bring the four winds from the four corners of heaven against Elam. I will scatter them to all these winds. People from Elam will go to every nation.
I will make Elam afraid before their enemies and before those who want to kill them. I will bring trouble on them. My anger will burn. I will send the sword after them until I have destroyed them.
I will set up My throne in Elam. I will destroy the king and leaders there.
But in the last days, I will bring Elam back from being captives," says the LORD.
This is the message the LORD gave to Jeremiah the prophet. It was about Babylon and the land of the people of Babylon.
"Tell the nations. Let them hear. Raise a flag. Do not hide it. Say, 'Babylon is caught. Bel is put to shame. Merodach is scared. Babylon's false gods are shamed. Their statues are scared.'
A nation from the north will attack her. It will make her land empty. No one will live there. People and animals will run away."
The LORD says, "In those days, the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together. They will go and cry. They will look for the LORD their God.
They will ask the way to Zion. They will look that way. They will say, 'Come, let us join the LORD. Let us make a promise that lasts forever. It will not be forgotten.'"
"My people were like lost sheep. Their leaders led them the wrong way. They made them wander in the hills. They went from hill to hill. They forgot their safe place."
Everyone who found them hurt them. Their enemies said, "We are not guilty. They sinned against the LORD. He is the home of what is right. He is the hope their fathers trusted."
"Run away from Babylon. Leave the land of the people of Babylon. Be like strong goats that lead the flock."
"I will bring a big group of nations from the north to attack Babylon. They will line up against her. They will take her. Their arrows will be like a skilled fighter's arrows. None will miss.
The people of Babylon will be taken like treasure. Everyone who takes from her will have enough," says the LORD.
"You were happy. You were glad. You took what was Mine. You were like a fat young cow in the grass. You made noise like strong bulls.
Your mother will be very ashamed. The one who had you will be confused. See, Babylon will be the last of the nations. It will be a dry, empty place."
"Because of the LORD's anger, no one will live there. It will be empty. Everyone who passes by will be shocked. They will make fun of all her hurts.
Line up against Babylon all around. Everyone with a bow, shoot at her. Do not hold back arrows. She sinned against the LORD.
Shout against her all around. She has given up. Her walls have fallen down. It is the LORD's payback. Pay her back. Do to her what she did.
Stop the farmers in Babylon. Stop the people who cut the grain. Because of the enemy's sword, everyone will turn to their own people. Everyone will run to their own land."
Israel is like a sheep that was scattered. Lions chased it away. First the king of Assyria hurt it. Now Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has broken its bones.
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, "I will punish the king of Babylon and his land. I punished the king of Assyria the same way.
I will bring Israel back home. He will eat in Carmel and Bashan. He will be full on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.
In those days, says the LORD, people will look for Israel's wrongs, but find none. They will look for Judah's sins, but not find them. I will forgive the people I leave.
