Go up against the land of Merathaim. Attack the people of Pekod. Destroy them completely, says the LORD. Do all I tell you."
A sound of war is in the land. There is big destruction.
Babylon was like a hammer for the whole earth. Now it is broken. Babylon is empty among the nations.
"I set a trap for you, Babylon. You were caught, and you did not know it. You were found and caught because you fought against the LORD."
The LORD opened His storehouse. He brought out His angry weapons. This is the work of the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, in the land of the people of Babylon.
"Come against her from far away. Open her storehouses. Pile her up like heaps of ruins. Destroy her completely. Leave nothing of her.
Kill all her young bulls. Trouble is coming for them. Their time has come."
People run away and escape from Babylon. They tell in Zion that the LORD our God has paid Babylon back. He has paid back for His temple.
"Call the bowmen against Babylon. Set up camp around her. Let no one escape. Pay her back for what she did. Do to her what she did. She was proud against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel.
So her young men will fall in her streets. All her soldiers will be killed that day," says the LORD.
The Lord, the LORD of Hosts, says, "Look, I am against you, proud one. Your day has come. I will punish you.
The proud one will trip and fall. No one will help him up. I will start a fire in his cities. It will burn all around him."
The LORD of Hosts says, "The people of Israel and Judah are hurt together. Everyone who took them keeps them. They will not let them go."
Their Savior is strong. His name is the LORD of Hosts. He will fight for them. He will give rest to the land. He will shake up the people of Babylon.
"A sword is coming for the people of Babylon, says the LORD. It is coming for their leaders and their wise men.
A sword is coming for the braggers. They will act like fools. A sword is coming for her strong men. They will be scared.
A sword is coming for their horses, chariots, and all the mixed people inside her. They will be weak. A sword is coming for her treasures. They will be stolen.
Her waters will dry up. It is a land of carved idols. The people are crazy for their idols.
Wild animals will live there. Ostriches will live there. It will never be lived in again. No one will live there from family to family.
I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities near them, says the LORD. In the same way, no one will live there."
The LORD says, "Look, a people is coming from the north. It is a big nation. Many kings will come from faraway places.
They will hold bows and spears. They are mean and will not show mercy. Their noise will roar like the sea. They will ride horses. They will line up for war against you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon heard about them. His hands became weak. Fear took hold of him. Pain came on him like a woman having a baby.
Look, he will come up like a lion from the thick bushes by the Jordan River to the safe place. I will chase them away from her quickly. Who can stand before Me?"
So listen to the LORD's plan against Babylon. Listen to His thoughts against the land of the people of Babylon. Even the smallest sheep will drag them away. He will make their home empty.
When Babylon is taken, the earth will shake. The nations will hear the cry.
The LORD says, "I am stirring up a destroying wind against Babylon and against the people of Leb-kamai.
I will send strangers to Babylon. They will scatter her and empty her land. They will be all around her on the day of trouble.
Let the archer bend his bow. Let the soldier put on his armor. Do not spare her young men. Destroy all her army.
Her dead will fall in the land of the Chaldeans. Her wounded will fall in her streets.
Israel and Judah have not been left by their God, the LORD of Hosts. Their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel."
Run away from Babylon! Save your lives! Do not be destroyed when she is punished. This is the time for the LORD's payback. He will pay her back.
Babylon was a gold cup in the LORD's hand. It made all the earth drunk. The nations drank its wine. So the nations went wild.
Babylon fell suddenly and broke. Cry for her! Bring medicine for her pain. Maybe she can be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Leave her. Let us go home. Her punishment has reached the sky. It is as high as the clouds.
The LORD has shown that we are right. Come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done.
Sharpen the arrows! Fill the arrow bags! The LORD has stirred up the kings of Media. He wants to destroy Babylon. This is the LORD's payback. It is payback for His temple.
Hold up a flag against Babylon's walls. Keep watch strong. Set guards. Get ready to ambush. The LORD planned this and did what He said to Babylon's people.
You who live by many waters and have many treasures, your time is up. Your greedy gain is measured.
The LORD of Hosts has made a strong promise. He said, "I will fill you with people like locusts. They will shout for victory over you."
God made the earth with His power. He set the world in place with His wisdom. He stretched out the heavens with His understanding.
When He thunders, water pours in the sky. He brings clouds from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain. He brings wind from His storehouses.
Every person is foolish and knows nothing. Every gold worker is ashamed of his idol. His metal god is a lie. It has no breath.
They are worthless. They are tricks. When God comes to punish, they will be destroyed.
Jacob's God is not like them. He made everything. Israel is His own people. His name is the LORD of Hosts.
"You are My hammer and weapon of war. With you I smash nations. With you I destroy kingdoms.
With you I smash horse and rider. With you I smash war cart and driver.
With you I smash man and woman. With you I smash old and young. With you I smash young man and young woman.
With you I smash shepherd and flock. With you I smash farmer and oxen. With you I smash leaders and officials.
Before your eyes I will pay back Babylon and all the people of Chaldea for all the bad things they did in Zion," declares the LORD.

"I am against you, you destroying mountain," declares the LORD. "You destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out My hand against you and roll you down from the rocks. I will make you a burned-up mountain.
No one will take a stone from you for a corner or for a foundation. You will be empty forever," declares the LORD.

Hold up a flag in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Get the nations ready to fight her. Call the kingdoms against her: Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Pick a leader against her. Bring up horses like locusts.
Get the nations ready to fight her, the kings of Media, their leaders and all their officials, and every land they rule.
The land shakes and twists. The LORD's plans against Babylon stand. He will make Babylon an empty land with no one living in it.
Babylon's strong men stop fighting. They stay in their safe places. Their strength is gone. They are like women. Her houses are set on fire. Her gate bars are broken.
One runner runs to meet another. One messenger meets another. They tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken from every side.
The river crossings are seized. The wet lands are burned. The soldiers are scared.
"For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor when it is trampled. In a little while, her harvest time will come."
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, ate us up. He crushed us. He made us like an empty jar. He swallowed us like a sea monster. He filled his stomach with our good food. He drove us out.
"Let the violence done to me and my body come back on Babylon," says the person who lives in Zion. "My blood come back on the people of Chaldea," says Jerusalem.
"So this is what the LORD says: I will plead your case. I will pay you back. I will dry up her sea and make her spring dry.
Babylon will become a pile of broken stones. Wild dogs will live there. People will be scared of her and mock her. No one will live there.
They will all roar like lions. They will growl like young lions.
While they are hot with wine, I will set out their feast. I will make them drunk so they are happy. Then they will sleep a sleep that never ends. They will not wake up.
I will bring them down like lambs to be killed, like rams with goats," declares the LORD.
Sheshach is taken! The pride of the whole earth is seized! Babylon has become a scary place to all nations.
The sea has come up over Babylon. She is covered by many waves.
Her cities are empty. They are dry and bare. No one lives in them. No person walks through them.
"I will punish Bel in Babylon. I will make him spit out what he swallowed. The nations will not flow to him anymore. Yes, Babylon's wall has fallen."
"Come out of her, My people! Save your lives from the LORD's hot anger.

Do not let your heart get weak. Do not be scared by the news you hear in the land. News will come one year. More news will come the next year. There will be violence in the land. One ruler will fight another."
"So days are coming when I will punish Babylon's false gods. The whole land will be put to shame. All her dead will fall inside her.
Then heaven and earth and everything in them will sing for joy over Babylon. Attackers will come from the north to hurt her," declares the LORD.
Babylon must fall because of Israel's dead. Babylon's dead have fallen because of all the earth.
You who escaped the sword, go! Do not stand still! Remember the LORD from far away. Let Jerusalem come into your mind.
We are ashamed because we heard insults. Shame covered our faces because strangers came into the holy places of the LORD's house.
"So days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will punish her false gods. Hurt people will cry out in all her land.
Even if Babylon climbs to the sky and makes her strong place higher, attackers from Me will come to her," declares the LORD.
Listen! A cry from Babylon! Great ruin from the land of the Chaldeans!
The LORD is laying Babylon waste. He is destroying her loud voice. Her waves roar like many waters. The sound of their voice is loud.
An attacker has come against her, against Babylon. Her strong men are taken. Their bows are broken. The LORD is the God of payback. He will surely pay back.

"I will make her leaders and wise men drunk. I will make her helpers and strong men drunk. They will sleep a sleep that never ends and not wake up," declares the LORD, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Babylon's wide walls will be knocked down. Her high gates will be burned with fire. People work for nothing. Nations tire themselves out for the fire."

This is the message Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah. Seraiah was in charge of the resting place. He went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his rule.
Jeremiah wrote in one book all the bad things that would come to Babylon. He wrote all these words about Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words.

Say, 'O the LORD, You have spoken about this place. You said You would cut it off, so that no person or animal will live in it. It will be empty forever.' "When you finish reading this book, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates River.
Say, 'This is how Babylon will sink. It will not rise again, because of the trouble I am bringing on it. Its people will be worn out.' These are the words of Jeremiah."
Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for 11 years. His mother was Hamutal. She was the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
He did what was bad in the eyes of the LORD. He did like Jehoiakim had done.
The LORD was angry with Jerusalem and Judah. He would send them away from Him. Zedekiah also turned against the king of Babylon.
In the ninth year of his rule, in the tenth month, on the tenth day, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came with all his army. They camped around Jerusalem. They built ramps against the city.
The city was under attack until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth day of the fourth month, there was no food in the city. The people were starving.

Then the city wall was broken through. The Babylonian soldiers were all around. At night, the king and his soldiers ran away through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden. They went toward the desert.
The Babylonian army chased King Zedekiah. They caught him on the plains of Jericho. All his soldiers ran away from him.
They took the king to Riblah in the land of Hamath. There the king of Babylon judged him.
At Riblah, the king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons while Zedekiah watched. He also killed all the leaders of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes. He tied him with bronze chains. He took him to Babylon. Zedekiah stayed in prison until he died.
In the fifth month, on the tenth day, in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan came to Jerusalem. He was the captain of the guard who worked for the king of Babylon.
He burned the house of the LORD. He burned the king's house. He burned all the big houses in Jerusalem.
The Babylonian soldiers with him tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan took away the rest of the people who were still in the city. He took the people who had given up to the king of Babylon. He took the rest of the workers.
But Nebuzaradan left some of the poor people. They were to take care of the grape fields and farms.
The Babylonians broke the bronze pillars in the house of the LORD. They broke the bronze stands and the big bronze bowl called the Sea. They took all the bronze to Babylon.
They took the pots, shovels, bowls, and all the bronze tools used for the temple.
They took the cups, fire pans, bowls, pots, lampstands, pans, and small bowls. Some were gold and some were silver.
The two pillars, the Sea, the twelve bronze bulls under the stands, and all the things King Solomon made for the house of the LORD were too heavy to weigh. There was so much bronze.
Each pillar was 18 cubits high. It was 12 cubits around. It was four fingers thick and hollow.
The bronze top on each pillar was 5 cubits high. There was bronze lattice and pomegranates all around the top. Both pillars were the same.
There were 96 pomegranates on the outside. There were 100 pomegranates all around the lattice.
Nebuzaradan took Seraiah the chief priest. He took Zephaniah the second priest. He took the three men who guarded the door.

From the city he took one officer who was in charge of the soldiers. He took seven of the king's advisors who were found there. He took the army commander's secretary. He took 60 other men from the city.
Nebuzaradan took them to Riblah. They went to the king of Babylon.
There the king of Babylon killed them in Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken away from its land.
This is how many people Nebuchadnezzar took away: In the seventh year, 3,023 Jews.
In the eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem.
In the twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan took 745 Jews. In all, 4,600 people.

In the thirty-seventh year after Jehoiachin, king of Judah, was taken away, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Evil-Merodach, king of Babylon, showed kindness to Jehoiachin. He brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to him. He gave him a seat above the other kings in Babylon.
Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes. He ate bread every day for the rest of his life.
Every day, the king of Babylon gave him food until he died.
How lonely is the city that once had many people! She was great among the nations, but now she is like a widow. She was a princess among the lands, but now she must work like a slave.
She cries hard at night. Tears run down her cheeks. None of the people she loved come to comfort her. All her friends turned against her and became her enemies.
Judah was taken away because she was poor and had to work hard. Now she lives far away among other nations. She can't find rest. Her enemies caught her in a tight place.
The roads to Zion are sad. No one comes for the feasts. Her gates are empty. Her priests groan. Her young women are sad. She is very bitter.
Her enemies won. They are in charge now, because the LORD punished her for many sins. Even her little children were taken away by the enemy.
The people of Zion lost all their beauty. Her leaders are like deer with no grass to eat. They are weak, and they run from the one chasing them.
In her trouble, Jerusalem remembered all the good things she once had. Her people fell into enemy hands, and no one helped her. Her enemies saw her and laughed at her fall.
Jerusalem sinned badly. So she became unclean. Everyone who honored her now looks down on her, because they saw her shame. She groans and turns away.
Her sin is clear, but she did not think about what would happen. She fell in a terrible way. No one comforts her. "Look, the LORD, at how much I hurt! The enemy has become great."
The enemy reached out and took all her treasures. She saw foreign nations go into her holy place. You said they could not join Your people.
All her people groan as they look for bread. They gave their treasures for food to stay alive. "Look, the LORD, and see! I am hated." "
Does my pain mean nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look and see if there is pain like mine. The LORD caused it on the day He was very angry.
From heaven He sent fire down into my bones. He spread a net for my feet. He turned me back. He left me empty and weak all day. "
My sins are like a heavy load around my neck. His hand tied them on. They weigh on my neck. The Lord has taken my strength. He put me in the hands of people I cannot fight. I cannot get up.
The Lord crushed all my strong men. He called a crowd to break my young men. The Lord crushed Judah's young women like grapes in a press.
I cry because of these things. Tears run from my eyes. No one is near to comfort me or give me new life. My children are left empty, because the enemy won."
Zion held out her hands, but no one comforted her. The LORD told Jacob's enemies to surround her. Jerusalem became unclean among them. "
The LORD is right. I went against Him. Listen, all you people, and look at my pain. My young men and young women were taken away.
I called to my friends, but they tricked me. My priests and leaders died in the city while they looked for food to save their lives. "
Look, the LORD, I am in trouble! My stomach turns. My heart is upset inside me. I was very rebellious. Outside, the sword kills. Inside, it is like death.
They heard me groan, but no one comforted me. All my enemies heard about my trouble and were glad, because You did it. You brought the day You promised. May they become like me. "
Let all their evil come before You. Do to them what You did to me for all my sins. I groan so much, and my heart is weak."
How the Lord has covered Zion with a cloud of anger! He has thrown Israel's glory from heaven to earth. He forgot His footstool on the day He was angry.

The Lord did not feel sorry. He destroyed all of Jacob's homes. In His anger He tore down Judah's strong cities. He brought them to the ground and made them unclean. He ended the kingdom and its leaders.
In fierce anger He took away all of Israel's strength. He pulled back His helping hand when the enemy came. He burned through Jacob like a fire that eats everything around.
He bent His bow like an enemy. His right hand stood like a foe. He killed all their loved ones. In Zion's homes He poured out His anger like fire.
The Lord became like an enemy. He destroyed Israel. He destroyed all her big houses and tore down her strong forts. He made much sadness and crying in Judah.
He ruined His meeting tent like a garden. He destroyed His place to meet. The LORD made Zion forget her special days and Sabbaths. In fierce anger He rejected the king and the priest.
The Lord rejected His altar. He left His holy place. He let the enemy take the walls of her palaces. They shouted in the LORD's house like on a special day.
The LORD planned to destroy Zion's wall. He stretched a measuring line and did not stop destroying. The wall and the fort both grew weak and wasted away.
Her gates sank into the ground. He destroyed and broke their bars. Her king and leaders are among other nations. There is no law, and her prophets find no message from the the LORD.
The leaders of Zion sit on the ground and say nothing. They put dust on their heads and wore rough clothes. The young women of Jerusalem bowed their heads to the ground.
My eyes are worn out from crying. My insides hurt. My heart is poured out on the ground because my people are broken. Little children and babies faint in the city streets.
They ask their mothers, "Where is food and drink?" They faint in the city streets like hurt people. Their lives slip away in their mothers' arms.
What can I say to you? What can I compare you to, Jerusalem? What can I say you are like, so I can comfort you, Zion? Your hurt is as big as the sea. Who can heal you?
Your prophets told you false and empty things. They did not show your sin so you could come back home. They told you false and misleading things.
All who walk by clap their hands at you. They hiss and shake their heads at Jerusalem. They say, "Is this the city they called the most beautiful, the joy of the whole earth?"
All your enemies open their mouths against you. They hiss and grind their teeth. They say, "We destroyed her. This is the day we waited for. We lived to see it!"
The LORD did what He planned. He kept His word from long ago. He tore you down and did not feel sorry. He let your enemies be happy over you. He made your enemies strong.
Their hearts cried out to the Lord. Zion's wall, let your tears run like a river day and night. Do not rest. Let your eyes overflow with tears.

Get up and cry out in the night. At the start of the night watch, pour out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift your hands to Him for your children who faint from hunger on every street corner.
Look, the LORD, and see. Have You ever done this to anyone? Should mothers eat their own children, the little ones they care for? Should priests and prophets be killed in the Lord's holy place?
Young and old lie together in the streets. My young men and girls fell by the sword. You killed them in the day of Your anger. You slaughtered them and did not feel sorry.
You brought fears on me from every side, like on a special day. On the day of the LORD's anger, no one escaped or lived. My enemy destroyed the children I cared for and raised.
I am the man who has seen trouble from God's anger.
He led me into dark places with no light.
He turns His hand against me all day long.
He made my body weak. He broke my bones.
He built walls around me with trouble and hard work.
He put me in dark places like people who died long ago.
He walled me in so I cannot get out. He made my chains heavy.
Even when I cry out and ask for help, He shuts out my prayer.
He blocked my roads with stone walls. He made my paths crooked.
He is like a bear waiting to attack me, like a lion hiding in secret places.
He led me off my path and tore me apart. He made me empty.
He bent His bow and made me a target for His arrows.
He shot arrows into my heart.
I became a joke to all my people. They sing mean songs about me all day.
He filled me with bitter things. He made me drink poison.
He broke my teeth with gravel. He pushed me in the dust.
I lost all peace. I forgot what good is.
I said, "My strength is gone. My hope in the the LORD is gone."
The LORD, remember my trouble and my wandering. Remember the bitter poison.
I remember these things, and my soul is sad.
But I bring this to my heart, and so I still hope.
the LORD's faithful love never ends. His mercy never stops.
Every morning it is new. Your faithfulness is very great.
My soul says, "The LORD is my share." So I hope in Him.
The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that looks for Him.
It is good to wait quietly for the LORD to save us.
It is good for a man to carry a heavy load when he is young.
He should sit alone and be quiet, because God gave him this load.
He should put his mouth in the dust. Maybe there is hope.
He should give his cheek to the one who hits him. He should accept shame.
The Lord will not push us away forever.
Even if He brings trouble, He will show mercy. He has great faithful love.
He does not make trouble from His heart. He does not like to hurt people.
He does not crush prisoners under His feet.
He does not take away a man's rights before the Most High.
He does not cheat a man in court. The Lord does not see this as good.
Who can speak and make it happen unless the Lord commands it?
Both good and bad come from the Most High.
Why should a living person complain? Each person should look at his own sin.
Let us look at our ways and test them. Let us turn back to the LORD.
Let us lift our hearts and hands to God in heaven.
We have sinned and turned against You. You have not forgiven us.
You covered Yourself with anger and chased us. You killed and did not pity.
You hid behind a cloud so prayer could not pass.
You made us trash and garbage among the nations.
All our enemies open their mouths against us.
We feel fear and traps, ruin and destruction.
My eyes pour out tears because my people are hurt.
My eyes will not stop crying. They will not rest
until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
My eyes hurt my heart because of what happened to the girls in my city.
My enemies hunted me like a bird for no reason.
They shut me in a pit and threw stones at me.
Water rose over my head. I said, "I am finished."
I called on Your name, O LORD, from the bottom of the pit.
You heard my voice. Do not hide Your ear from my cry for help.
You came near when I called You. You said, "Do not be afraid."
Lord, You fought my case. You saved my life.
O LORD, You saw the wrong done to me. Judge my case.
You saw all their revenge and all their plans against me.
O LORD, You heard their insults and all their plans against me.
My enemies talk about me all day.
Watch when they sit and when they stand. I am the song they mock.
Pay them back, O LORD, for what their hands have done.
Give them a sad heart. Your curse be on them.
Chase them in Your anger and wipe them out from under the LORD's sky.
How the gold has lost its shine! The best gold is changed. The holy stones are thrown in every street.
The sons of Zion were very valuable. Now people treat them like clay pots made by a potter.
Even wild animals feed their babies. But my people have become cruel, like birds in the desert that do not care for their young.
Babies' tongues stick to their mouths because they are thirsty. Little children ask for bread, but no one gives them any.
People who once ate rich food are now poor in the streets. People raised in fine clothes now sit in piles of ashes.
My people have been punished more than Sodom. Sodom was destroyed in a moment, and no one helped her.
Her leaders were brighter than snow and whiter than milk. Their bodies were redder than red jewels. They looked like blue jewels.
Now they look blacker than dirt. No one knows them in the streets. Their skin sticks to their bones. It is dry like a stick.
People killed by a sword are better off than people who die of hunger. Hungry people waste away, hurt by pain, because the fields have no food.
Kind women have cooked their own children. The children became food for them when my people were destroyed.
The LORD used up all His anger. He poured out His fierce anger. He set fire to Zion. It burned the city to the ground.
The kings of the earth did not believe it. No one in the world believed it. They thought no enemy could get into Jerusalem's gates.
But it happened because of the sins of the prophets and the wrongs of the priests. They killed good people in the city.
They wandered blind in the streets. They were covered with blood. No one could touch their clothes.
People shouted to them, "Go away! You are unclean! Go away! Go away! Do not touch us!" So they ran and wandered. People in other lands said, "They cannot stay here."
The LORD Himself scattered them. He does not look at them with favor anymore. The priests get no honor. The leaders get no kindness.
Our eyes grew tired from watching for help that never came. We watched for a nation that could not save us.
They followed our steps, so we could not walk in our streets. Our end was near. Our days were counted, because our end had come.
Our enemies chased us faster than eagles in the sky. They chased us over the mountains. They waited to trap us in the desert.
The king the the LORD chose was caught in their traps. He was our very life. We had said, "We will live among the nations under his protection."
People of Edom, be happy now. You live in the land of Uz. But the cup of trouble will come to you too. You will get drunk and be shamed.
People of Zion, your punishment is finished. He will not make you stay away any longer. People of Edom, He will punish you for your wrongs. He will show your sins.
The LORD, remember what happened to us. Look and see our shame.
Our land now belongs to strangers. Our homes now belong to foreigners.
We have no father. Our mothers are like women whose husbands have died.
We have to pay for water to drink. We have to pay for wood.
People chase us. We are tired and get no rest.
We turned to Egypt and Assyria for food.
Our fathers did wrong. Now we carry their trouble.
Slaves rule over us. No one saves us from them.
We risk our lives to get bread because of danger in the desert.
Our skin is hot like an oven because of hunger.
Women are hurt in Zion. Young girls are hurt in Judah towns.
Leaders are hung by their hands. Old men are not honored.
Young men grind grain. Boys fall while carrying wood.
Old men no longer sit at the gate. Young men no longer sing.
Our joy is gone. Our dancing turned to crying.
Our crown fell from our head. We sinned, and now we are in trouble.
Because of this, our hearts are weak. Because of these things, our eyes are dim.
Mount Zion is empty. Foxes walk on it.
You, the LORD, rule forever. Your throne lasts for all time.
Why do You forget us forever? Why do You leave us so long?
Bring us back to You, the LORD, so we can return. Make our days new like before.
Have You completely turned away from us? Are You very angry with us?
In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, I was among the people taken away by the Kebar River. The sky opened, and I saw visions from God.
It was the fifth day of the month. That was the fifth year after King Jehoiachin was taken away.
The LORD spoke to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, in the land of Babylon by the Kebar River. The LORD's power was on him.
I looked, and I saw a strong wind coming from the north. There was a big cloud with fire flashing in it. Bright light shone all around it. In the middle of the fire, it looked like glowing metal.
In the middle of the cloud, I saw four living creatures. They looked like people.
Each one had four faces and four wings.
Their legs were straight. Their feet were like a calf's feet. They shone like shiny metal.
They had human hands under their wings on all four sides. All four of them had faces and wings.
Their wings touched each other. They did not turn when they moved. Each one went straight ahead.
Each one had a human face. On the right was a lion's face. On the left was an ox's face. Each one also had an eagle's face.
Their wings spread out above. Two wings touched the one next to it. Two wings covered their bodies.
Each one went straight ahead. They went where the Spirit wanted them to go. They did not turn as they moved.
The living creatures looked like burning coals of fire. They moved back and forth like torches. Bright lightning came out of the fire.
The creatures moved quickly back and forth, like flashes of lightning.
As I looked at the creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each one. Each wheel faced all four ways.
The wheels looked like shiny stone. All four wheels looked the same. It was like a wheel inside a wheel.
They could move in any of the four directions. They did not turn as they moved.
The edges of the wheels were tall and frightening. They were full of eyes all around.
When the creatures moved, the wheels moved with them. When the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose too.
The creatures went where the Spirit wanted to go. The wheels went with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
When the creatures moved, the wheels moved. When they stopped, the wheels stopped. When they rose from the ground, the wheels rose too, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Over the heads of the creatures was something like a great, scary sky. It shone like ice.
Under the sky, their wings were straight. Each one had two wings touching the one next to it, and two wings covering its body.

When they moved, I heard the sound of their wings. It sounded like rushing water. It sounded like the voice of God. It was a loud noise, like an army camp. When they stopped, they lowered their wings.
A voice came from above the sky over their heads. When they stopped, they lowered their wings.
Above the sky over their heads was something that looked like a throne. It looked like a blue stone. On the throne was a figure that looked like a man.
From His waist up, He looked like glowing metal, like fire with light all around. From His waist down, He looked like fire with light all around.
He looked like a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day. This was the glory of the LORD. I saw it, and I bowed down to the ground. Then I heard a voice speaking.
He said to me, “Son of man, stand up on your feet. I will speak to you.”
As He spoke, the Spirit came into me and set me on my feet. Then I heard Him speaking to me.
He said, “Son of man, I am sending you to the people of Israel. They are a nation that keeps turning away from Me. They and their fathers have turned away from Me to this very day.
They are stubborn and mean. I am sending you to them, and you must say to them, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says.’
They may listen, or they may not. They are a stubborn family. But they will know that a prophet was with them.”

“And you, Son of man, do not be afraid of them or their words. Do not be afraid. They are like thorns and sharp weeds around you, and you live among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words. Do not be scared by how they look. They are a stubborn family.
But speak My words to them. They may listen, or they may not. They are stubborn.”
“But you, Son of man, listen to what I say. Do not be stubborn like that stubborn family. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.”
Then I looked. I saw a hand reaching out to me. In it was a scroll.
He opened it in front of me. It was written on the front and the back. It had words of sadness, crying, and trouble.
He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll. Then go speak to the people of Israel."
So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll.
Then He said, "Son of man, eat this scroll I am giving you. Fill your stomach with it." So I ate it, and it tasted sweet like honey in my mouth.
Then He said, "Son of man, go to the people of Israel and speak My words to them.
You are not being sent to people who talk in a strange, hard language. You are being sent to the people of Israel.
You are not being sent to many nations that speak strange, hard languages you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
But the people of Israel will not want to listen to you, because they do not want to listen to Me. All the people of Israel are stubborn. They will not change their minds.
Look, I have made your face as strong as their faces. I have made your forehead as strong as their foreheads.
I have made your forehead like a diamond, harder than rock. Do not be afraid of them. Do not be upset by them, because they are a stubborn people."
Then He said, "Son of man, listen well to all the words I say to you. Take them to heart.
Go to your people who were taken away. Speak to them. Tell them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: They may listen, or they may not.'"
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard a loud rumbling behind me. It said, "Praise the glory of the the LORD where He is!"
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching each other. It was also the sound of the wheels beside them. It was a loud rumbling.
So the Spirit lifted me up and carried me away. I went with a bitter and angry heart. The strong hand of the the LORD was on me.
I came to the people who were taken away at Tel Abib, by the River Kebar. I sat there with them for seven days. I was very upset.
At the end of seven days, the word of the the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, I have made you a lookout for the people of Israel. When you hear a word from My mouth, warn them for Me.
If I say to a bad person, 'You will die,' and you do not warn him to turn from his bad ways so he can live, that bad person will die because of his sin. But I will blame you for his death.
But if you warn the bad person and he does not turn from his bad ways, he will die because of his sin. But you will have saved your life.

If a good person turns from doing good and does wrong, and I put something in his way that makes him fall, he will die. Since you did not warn him, he will die for his sin. The good things he did will not be remembered. But I will blame you for his death.
But if you warn the good person not to sin, and he does not sin, he will live. He listened to your warning. You will have saved your life."
Then the hand of the the LORD was on me there. He said, "Get up and go out to the open field. I will speak to you there."
So I got up and went out to the open field. I saw the glory of the the LORD standing there. It looked like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar. I fell facedown.
Then the Spirit came into me and stood me on my feet. He spoke to me. He said, "Go and shut yourself inside your house.
You, son of man, people will tie ropes on you. They will bind you with them. You will not be able to go out among them.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth. You will not be able to talk. You will not be able to tell them they are wrong, because they are a stubborn people.

But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth. You will say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Whoever wants to listen, let him listen. Whoever refuses, let him refuse. They are a stubborn people.'"
“You, son of man, take a brick. Put it in front of you. Draw a picture of Jerusalem on it.
Build a wall around it to show a siege. Pile up dirt against it. Put army camps around it. Put big poles all around it to break the wall.
Take an iron pan. Put it between you and the city like a wall. Turn your face toward the city. It will be under attack. Attack it. This is a sign for the people of Israel.”
“Lie on your left side. Put the sin of Israel on it. You will carry their sin.
I give you 390 days. That is the same number as the years of their sin. You will carry the sin of Israel.
When you finish those days, lie on your right side. Carry the sin of Judah. I give you 40 days. One day stands for one year.
Turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem. Show your bare arm. Speak against the city.
I will tie you with ropes. You will not turn from one side to the other until your days of attack are done.”
“Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Put them in one jar. Make bread from them. Eat it for the 390 days you lie on your side.
Eat only a small piece of bread each day.
Measure the water you drink. Drink it at set times.
Eat the bread like barley cakes. Bake it over human waste while people watch.”
“The LORD says, ‘This is how the people of Israel will eat unclean bread among the nations where I send them.’”
“Oh, Lord the LORD! I have never made myself unclean. From my youth until now, I have not eaten meat that died on its own or was torn by animals. No unclean meat has ever entered my mouth.”
“Look, I will let you use cow dung instead of human dung. Bake your bread over that.”
“Look, I will take away the bread in Jerusalem. The people will eat bread by weight and worry. They will drink water by measure and be afraid.
They will not have enough bread or water. They will waste away because of their sin.”
You, son of man, take a sharp sword. Use it like a barber's razor. Shave your head and your beard. Then get scales and weigh the hair. Divide it into parts.

When the siege is done, burn one third of the hair in the fire in the city. Take another third and cut it with the sword all around the city. Scatter the last third to the wind. I will send a sword after them.
Take a few hairs from there. Tie them in the edge of your robe.
Then take some of those hairs and throw them into the fire. Burn them up. A fire will come from them to all the people of Israel. "
This is what the Lord the LORD says: This is Jerusalem. I put her in the middle of the nations. Lands are all around her.
She turned My laws into wrong. She was worse than the nations around her. She did not follow My laws. She did not keep My rules.
Because you were more trouble than the nations around you, you did not follow My laws. You did not keep My rules. You did not even act like the nations around you. "
So now I am against you. I will punish you right among you, where the nations can see.
Because of all your bad things, I will do to you what I have never done. I will never do it again.
So fathers will eat their sons among you. Sons will eat their fathers. I will punish you. I will scatter all that is left of you to every wind. "
This is what the Lord the LORD says: As I live, you have made My holy place dirty with all your bad things and your ugly idols. So I will cut you down. I will not look away. I will not show you pity.

One third of you will die from sickness. One third will die from hunger among you. One third will fall by the sword all around you. I will scatter one third to every wind. I will chase them with a sword.
I will use up My anger on them. Then My anger will rest. I will be calm when My anger is done. Then they will know that I am the LORD. I said this in My jealousy. "
I will make you a ruin. The nations around you will shame you. Everyone who passes by will see.
You will be shamed and mocked. You will be a warning and a shock to the nations around you. I will punish you in anger and fury. I am the LORD. I have spoken. "
I will send bad arrows of hunger to destroy you. I will bring more hunger on you. I will break your food supply.
I will send hunger and wild animals against you. They will take your children. Plague and blood will pass through you. I will bring a sword against you. I am the LORD. I have spoken."
The word of the LORD came to me.
He said, "Son of man, look toward the mountains of Israel and speak against them.

Say, 'Mountains of Israel, listen to the word of the Lord the LORD. This is what the Lord the LORD says to the mountains and hills, to the valleys and low places: I will bring war against you, and I will destroy the places where you worship false gods.
Your altars will become empty ruins. Your places for burning incense will be broken. I will throw your dead bodies down in front of your false gods.
I will put the dead bodies of Israel's people in front of their false gods. I will scatter your bones around your altars.

Wherever you live, your cities will be destroyed and your hilltop worship places ruined. Your altars will be destroyed and ruined. Your false gods will be broken and gone. Your places for burning incense will be cut down. The things you made will be wiped out.
Dead people will fall among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'
"But I will let some of you live. Some of you will escape being killed in war and live among other nations. You will be scattered through many countries.

Then the ones who escape will remember Me among the nations where they are taken. They will remember how I was hurt because their hearts left Me and followed false gods with their eyes. They will feel sick about the bad things they did and all their terrible sins.
Then they will know that I am the LORD. I did not say this for nothing. I really will bring this trouble on them."

This is what the Lord the LORD says: "Clap your hands and stamp your foot and say, 'Oh no! Because of all the evil, terrible sins of the people of Israel, they will fall by war, by hunger, and by sickness.'
People far away will die from sickness. People close by will be killed in war. People who are left and trapped will die from hunger. In this way, I will use up My anger on them.

Then you will know that I am the LORD. You will see their dead bodies lying among their false gods and around their altars. This will happen on every high hill, on every mountaintop, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak. It will happen wherever they burned sweet-smelling offerings to their false gods.
I will reach out My hand against them. I will make the land empty and ruined, from the desert to Diblah. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
You, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: The end has come! The end is here for all four corners of the land. “
The end is here for you. I will send My anger on you. I will judge you by your ways. I will punish you for all your sinful things. “
I will not feel sorry for you. I will not hold back. I will pay you back for your ways. Your sinful things will stay among you. Then all of you will know that I am the LORD. “
This is what the Lord GOD says: Bad trouble is coming, one after another. Look, it is coming. “
The end has come. The end has come. It has woken up against you. Look, it is coming. “
Your time is up, people in the land. The time has come. The day is near. It will be a day of noise and trouble, not a happy day on the mountains. “
Soon I will pour out My anger on you. I will use up My anger on you. I will judge you by your ways. I will punish you for all your sinful things. “
I will not feel sorry. I will not hold back. I will pay you back for your ways. Your sinful things will stay among you. Then all of you will know that I am the LORD who punishes. “
Look, the day is here! Look, it is coming! The end has come. The stick has budded. Pride has bloomed. “
Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. None of them will be left. Their money and things will not stay. No one will cry for them. “
The time has come. The day is here. The buyer should not be glad. The seller should not be sad. My anger is on all the crowd. “
The seller will not get back what he sold, as long as he lives. The warning is for all the people. It will not turn back. Because of their sin, no one will stay alive. “
They blew the trumpet and got everything ready. But no one goes to war. My anger is on all the people. “
Outside is the sword. Inside are sickness and hunger. Anyone in the field dies by the sword. Anyone in the city is eaten by hunger and sickness. “
The ones who get away will run to the mountains. They will be like sad doves in the valleys. They will all cry, each for his own sin. “
All hands will be weak. All knees will feel like water. “
They will put on rough cloth. Fear will cover them. Shame will be on all faces. All heads will be shaved. “

They will throw their silver into the streets. Their gold will be like trash. Their silver and gold cannot save them on the day of the LORD's anger. They will not fill their stomachs. They will not be happy in their souls. Their sin made them trip and fall. “
They used their pretty things to show off. They made horrible statues and bad gods from them. So I will make those things dirty to them. “
I will give those things to strangers to take. I will give them to the wicked people of the earth to steal. They will ruin them. “
I will turn My face away from them. Bad men will come in and ruin My special place. “
Make a chain! The land is full of bloody crimes. The city is full of violence. “
I will bring the worst nations to take their houses. I will stop the pride of the strong. Their holy places will be ruined. “
When trouble comes, they will look for peace. But there will be none. “

One disaster will come after another. One rumor will follow another. They will look for a vision from the prophet. But the teaching from the priest will be lost. The advice from the elders will be lost. “

The king will cry. The prince will be filled with fear. The people's hands will shake. I will do to them what they deserve. I will judge them by their own rules. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day, I sat in my house. The leaders of Judah sat in front of me. Then the hand of the Lord GOD came on me there.
I looked and saw a shape like a man. From His waist down, He looked like fire. From His waist up, He shone like bright metal.

He reached out what looked like a hand and took me by the hair of my head. The Spirit lifted me between the ground and the sky. He brought me in a vision to Jerusalem. He brought me to the north gate of the inner yard. There was a false god there that makes God jealous.
There I saw the glory of the God of Israel. It looked like the vision I saw in the valley.
He said to me, “Son of Man, look toward the north.” I looked north. By the altar gate, at the entrance, stood that false god that makes God jealous.
He said to me, “Son of Man, do you see what they are doing? The people of Israel are doing terrible sins here. They drive Me away from My holy place. But you will see even worse sins than these.”
Then He brought me to the entrance of the yard. I looked and saw a hole in the wall.
He said to me, “Son of Man, dig through the wall.” I dug through the wall and found a door.
He said, “Go in and see the terrible things they do here.”
I went in and looked. I saw all kinds of crawling things and gross animals. I also saw all the false gods of Israel carved all around the wall.
Seventy leaders of Israel stood in front of them. Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stood among them. Each man held a small pan. Sweet-smelling smoke rose up.
He said to me, “Son of Man, do you see what the leaders of Israel do in the dark? Each man is in his own private room. They say, ‘The The LORD does not see us. The the LORD has left the land.’
You will see them do even worse sins.”
Then He brought me to the north gate of the the LORD’s house. I saw women sitting there, crying for Tammuz, a false god.
He said to me, “Son of Man, do you see this? You will see even worse sins than these.”

Then He brought me into the inner yard of the the LORD’s house. At the entrance to the the LORD’s temple, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men. Their backs were toward the the LORD’s temple. Their faces looked east. They bowed down to the sun.
He said to me, “Son of Man, have you seen this? Is it a small thing for Judah to do these terrible sins here? They fill the land with hurt and keep making Me angry. Look! They are insulting Me.
So I will act in anger. I will not feel sorry for them. I will not spare them. Even if they shout loudly to Me, I will not listen.”
Then I heard a loud voice say, “Bring the men who will punish the city. Each one has a weapon that can destroy in his hand.”

Six men came from the upper gate that faces north. Each one had a weapon to kill in his hand. One man among them wore linen clothes and had a writer’s case at his waist. They came and stood by the bronze altar.
The glory of Israel’s God had moved from the winged creature above it to the doorway of the house. He called to the man in linen clothes who had the writer’s case at his waist.
The LORD said to him, “Go through the city, through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry because of all the bad things done there.”
Then He said to the other men while I listened, “Follow him through the city and strike. Do not let your eye feel sorry, and do not pity anyone.
Kill old men, young men, young women, women, and children, but do not touch anyone who has the mark. Start at My holy place.” So they started with the older men who were in front of the house.
Then He said to them, “Make the house unclean and fill the courtyards with dead people. Go out!” So they went out and hit people in the city.
While they were killing, I was left alone. I fell on my face and cried out, “Ah, Lord the LORD! Will You destroy all the people left in Israel when You pour out Your anger on Jerusalem?”

He said to me, “The people of Israel and Judah have done very, very bad things. The land is full of blood, and the city is full of violence. They say that the LORD has left the land and that the LORD does not see.
So I will not look with pity or show mercy. I will let what they did come back on them.”
Then the man in linen clothes who had the writer’s case at his waist came back and said, “I have done what You told me.”
I looked up. I saw above the sky over the cherubim's heads something like a throne. It looked like a blue stone.

The LORD said to the man in white clothes, "Go in among the wheels, between the cherubim. Fill your hands with hot coals from among the cherubim. Throw them over the city." He went in while I watched.
The cherubim stood on the south side of the temple. When the man went in, a cloud filled the inner yard.
Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherub to the door of the temple. The temple filled with the cloud. The yard filled with the bright light of the glory of the LORD.
The sound of the cherubim's wings could be heard as far as the outer yard. It sounded like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.
When the LORD told the man in white clothes, "Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim," the man went in and stood by a wheel.
Then one cherub reached out his hand to the fire among them. He took some and put it into the hands of the man in white clothes. The man took it and went out.
The cherubim looked like they had a person's hand under their wings.
Then I looked and saw four wheels by the cherubim. One wheel was by each cherub. The wheels shone like a bright stone.
They all looked the same. Each one looked like a wheel inside a wheel.
When they moved, they could go in any of four directions. They did not turn as they went. They followed where the head faced.
Their whole bodies, backs, hands, and wings were full of eyes all around. Their four wheels were full of eyes too.
I heard the wheels being called "the spinning wheels."
Each one had four faces. The first face was a cherub's face. The second was a person's face. The third was a lion's face. The fourth was an eagle's face.
Then the cherubim rose up. These were the living creatures I had seen by the Kebar River.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved with them. When the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not leave their side.
When they stood still, the wheels stood still. When they rose, the wheels rose with them. The spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Then the glory of the LORD left the door of the temple and stood above the cherubim.
The cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the ground. The wheels were beside them. They stopped at the east gate of the LORD's house. The glory of the God of Israel was above them.
These were the living creatures I had seen under the God of Israel by the Kebar River. I knew they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and four wings. They had what looked like a person's hands under their wings.
Their faces looked like the faces I had seen by the Kebar River. Each creature moved straight ahead.

Then the Spirit lifted me up. He brought me to the east gate of the house of the LORD. It faces east. At the gate, I saw twenty-five men. I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah. They were leaders of the people.
He said to me, "Son of man, these men plan to do wrong. They give bad advice in this city.
They say, 'Isn't it time to build houses? This city is like a pot, and we are the meat inside.'
So speak against them. Speak, son of man."
Then the Spirit of the LORD came on me. He said, "Speak. Tell them this is what the LORD says: You have said these things, people of Israel. I know what you think.
You have killed many people in this city. You filled its streets with dead bodies.
So this is what the Lord GOD says: The dead you put in the city are the meat. The city is the pot. But I will take you out of it.
You are afraid of the sword, so I will bring the sword on you, says the Lord GOD. "
I will take you out of the city. I will put you in the hands of strangers. I will punish you.
You will die by the sword. I will judge you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
This city will not be your pot. You will not be the meat in it. I will judge you at the border of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the LORD. You did not follow My rules. You did not keep My laws. You lived like the nations around you."
While I was speaking, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell on my face. I cried out, "O Lord GOD, will You destroy the rest of Israel?"
Then the word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, your brothers, your family, and all Israel are the ones the people in Jerusalem talk about. They say, 'They are far from the LORD. This land is ours to keep.' "
So tell them this is what the Lord GOD says: I sent them to many nations. I spread them in other lands. But for a short time I have been a safe place for them where they went.
So tell them this is what the Lord GOD says: I will gather you from the nations. I will bring you together from the countries where you were scattered. I will give you the land of Israel.
They will go there. They will take away all the bad idols and wrong things. "
I will give them one heart. I will put a new spirit in them. I will take away their hard heart. I will give them a soft heart.
Then they will follow My rules and keep My laws and do them. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
But those who want their bad idols and wrong things, I will bring their bad ways back on their own heads, says the Lord GOD."
Then the angels lifted their wings. The wheels were beside them. The glory of the God of Israel was above them.
The glory of the LORD went up from the city. It stood on the mountain east of the city.
The Spirit lifted me up. He carried me in a vision by the Spirit of God to the people taken away to Babylon. Then the vision ended.
I told the people taken away everything the LORD had shown me.
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, you are living among a stubborn people. They have eyes to see, but they do not see. They have ears to hear, but they do not hear. They are a stubborn people.
So you, son of man, pack your bags to go away. In their sight, go away by day. From your place, move to another place in their sight. Maybe they will see, even though they are a stubborn people.
Bring out your things packed to go away by day in their sight. Then in the evening, in their sight, go out like people who are sent away.
In their sight, dig through the wall and bring your things out through it.
In their sight, lift your bag on your shoulder and take it out in the dark. Cover your face so you cannot see the land. For I have made you a sign to the people of Israel.

So I did as I was told. I brought out my things packed to go away by day. Then in the evening I dug through the wall with my hands. I took out my things in the dark, carrying them on my shoulder, in their sight.
In the morning, the word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, did not the stubborn people of Israel ask you, 'What are you doing?'"
"Say to them, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: This message is about the prince in Jerusalem and all the people of Israel who are there.
I am a sign to you. As I have done, so it will be done to them. They will go away as prisoners.
The prince among them will carry his things on his shoulder in the dark and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out. He will cover his face so that he cannot see the land.
I will catch him in My net, and he will be trapped. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Babylonians, but he will not see it. There he will die.
I will scatter to every wind all who are around him. I will scatter his helpers and all his soldiers. I will chase them with swords.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I scatter them among the nations and spread them through the countries.
But I will spare a few of them from the sword, hunger, and sickness. They can tell of all their bad ways among the nations where they go. Then they will know that I am the LORD.'"
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, eat your food with shaking. Drink your water with fear and worry.

Say to the people of the land, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says about those who live in Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They will eat their bread in worry and drink their water in fear. This is because their land will be empty of everything in it. That is because of the wrong done by all who live there.
The cities where people live will be destroyed, and the land will become empty. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, what is this saying you have in the land of Israel: 'The days go by, and the visions never come true'?"

"So say to them, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will put an end to this saying in Israel. They will not say it anymore. Instead, they will say, "The days are near, and every vision will come true."
For there will be no more false visions or sweet lies in Israel.
For I am the LORD. I will speak, and what I speak will happen. It will not be put off any longer. In your days, you stubborn people, I will speak a word and do it, says the Lord the LORD.'"
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Look! The people of Israel say, 'The vision he sees is for far in the future.'
So say to them, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: None of My words will be put off any longer. The word I speak will be done, says the Lord the LORD.'"
The word of the LORD came to me.
He said, "Son of man, speak against the prophets of Israel. They make up messages from their own hearts. Say to them to listen to the word of the LORD."
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: Trouble is coming for the foolish prophets. They follow their own thoughts and have seen nothing.
O Israel, your prophets are like foxes in ruined places.
"You did not fix the broken places. You did not build a wall for Israel's house to stand in battle on the day of the LORD.
They see false visions and tell lies. They say the LORD sent them, but the LORD did not send them. Still they hope their words come true.
"Did you not see a false vision? Did you not speak a lying message? You claimed the LORD said it, but I did not say it.
So this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you spoke lies and saw false visions, I am against you, says the Lord the LORD.

"My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and tell lies. They will not be in the meeting of My people. Their names will not be written in Israel's family list. They will not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord the LORD.
"This is because they led My people the wrong way. They said there was peace, but there was no peace. When someone builds a weak wall, they cover it with plaster.
Tell the people who cover it with plaster that it will fall. Heavy rain will come. Great hailstones will fall. A strong wind will break it open.
When the wall falls, people will ask you where the plaster is that you spread on it.
"So this is what the Lord the LORD says: In My anger I will send a strong wind. In My anger I will send heavy rain and hailstones to destroy it.
I will tear down the wall you covered with plaster. I will bring it to the ground. Its base will show. It will fall. You will be destroyed in it. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
I will finish My anger against the wall and against the people who covered it with plaster. I will say to you that the wall is gone and the people who covered it are gone.
These are the prophets of Israel. They spoke about Jerusalem. They saw visions of peace for her, but there was no peace, says the Lord the LORD."
He said, "Son of man, turn your attention to the women of your people. They prophesy from their own hearts. Speak against them."

"This is what the Lord the LORD says: Trouble is coming for the women who sew magic charms on their wrists. They make veils for people of every size to catch souls. Will you catch the souls of My people and keep your own souls alive?

"You dishonored Me among My people for a few handfuls of barley and pieces of bread. You killed people who should live. You let people live who should die. You lied to My people, and they listened to lies.
So I am against your magic charms. You use them to catch souls like birds. I will tear them from your arms. I will let the souls go free. They are the souls you hunt like birds.
"I will tear off your veils. I will save My people from your hands. They will not be caught by you anymore. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
You made good people sad with lies. I did not make them sad. You made bad people strong so they would not turn from their bad ways to save their lives.
"So you will no longer see false visions. You will no longer tell fortunes. I will save My people from your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
Some leaders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.
Then the word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, these men have brought their idols into their hearts. They have put their sin right in front of them. Should I let them ask Me anything?

"So speak to them. Tell them, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: When any man of Israel brings his idols into his heart and puts his sin and the thing that makes him fall right in front of him, and then he comes to a prophet, I, the LORD, will answer him. I will answer him because of his many idols.'
I will do this to grab the hearts of the people of Israel. They have turned away from Me because of their idols.
"So tell the people of Israel, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: Turn back! Turn away from your idols and from all your bad things.'

For any man of Israel, or any foreigner living in Israel, who turns away from Me and brings his idols into his heart and puts his sin and the thing that makes him fall right in front of him, and then comes to a prophet to ask Me something, I, the LORD, will answer him Myself.
"I will turn against that man. I will make him a warning sign to others. People will point at him and talk about him. I will cut him off from My people. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
If a prophet is tricked and says something, I, the LORD, have tricked that prophet. I will reach out My hand against him and destroy him from among My people Israel.
"They will carry their guilt. The person who asked will be guilty just like the prophet.

I will do this so the people of Israel will stop wandering away from Me. They will stop making themselves dirty with all their sins. Then they will be My people, and I will be their God, says the Lord the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me again. He said,
"Son of man, if a land sins against Me by not being faithful, I will reach out My hand against it. I will break its food supply. I will send hunger into it. I will cut off people and animals from it.
"Even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in that land, they could save only themselves because they did right, says the Lord the LORD.
"Or if I send wild animals through the land, and they kill the children, and the land becomes empty so no one walks through it because of the animals,
as surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, even if those three men were in it, they could not save their sons or daughters. They would save only themselves, and the land would be empty.
"Or if I bring a sword against that land and say, 'Sword, go through the land,' and I cut off people and animals from it,
as surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, those three men could not save their sons or daughters. They would save only themselves.
"Or if I send sickness into that land and pour out My anger on it with blood, to cut off people and animals from it,
as surely as I live, says the Lord the LORD, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they could not save a son or a daughter. They would save only themselves because they did right.

"For this is what the Lord the LORD says: How much worse it will be when I send My four terrible punishments against Jerusalem—sword, hunger, wild animals, and sickness—to cut off people and animals from it!

"But look, some people will be left in it. Sons and daughters will be brought out to you. When you see how they live and what they do, you will feel better about the trouble I brought on Jerusalem. You will see that I brought all of it on the city.
"They will comfort you when you see how they live and what they do. Then you will know that I did not do all this for no reason, says the Lord the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, what makes vine wood better than other wood from branches in the forest?
"Can people use its wood to make useful things? Can they take a peg from it to hang things on?
Look, it is thrown into the fire for fuel. The fire burns both ends and blackens the middle. Can it be used for anything?
Even before it was burned, it could not be used for work. How much less now that the fire has burned and blackened it!
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: As I have given vine wood among forest trees to be burned, I will do the same to the people living in Jerusalem.
I will turn against them. They got out of the fire, but the fire will still burn them up. When I turn against them, you will know that I am the LORD.
I will make the land empty because they were not faithful to Me, declares the Lord the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me.
He said, "Son of man, tell Jerusalem about her bad ways."
"This is what the Lord, the LORD, says to Jerusalem: You come from Canaan. That is where you were born. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
On the day you were born, no one cut your cord. No one washed you with water. No one rubbed you with salt. No one wrapped you in cloth.
No one felt sorry for you or did any of these things to care for you. You were thrown into a field. You were hated on the day you were born.
"I passed by you and saw you kicking in your blood. I said to you, 'Live!' Yes, I said to you, 'Live!'
I made you grow like a plant in a field. You grew up and became a young woman. Your breasts were formed, and your hair grew. But you were still naked.

"I passed by again and saw that it was time for love. I spread My cloak over you and covered your nakedness. I made a promise to you and made an agreement with you, and you became Mine, says the Lord, the LORD.
I washed you with water. I washed your blood off you. I put oil on you.
I dressed you in pretty clothes. I put fine leather shoes on your feet. I wrapped you in fine linen. I covered you with silk.
I gave you jewelry. I put bracelets on your arms and a chain around your neck.
I put a ring on your nose and earrings in your ears. You wore a beautiful crown on your head.
You wore gold and silver. Your clothes were fine linen, silk, and pretty cloth. You ate the best flour, honey, and oil. You were very beautiful, and you became a queen.
People in other nations heard about your beauty. Your beauty was perfect, because I gave it to you, says the Lord, the LORD.
"But you trusted in your beauty. You were not faithful to Me. You gave your love to everyone who passed by. You were ready to give yourself away.
You took some of your clothes and made altars on high places. You were not faithful there either. This should not happen.
You took your beautiful jewelry made of My gold and silver that I gave you. You made statues of men and were not faithful to them.
You took your pretty clothes and covered them. You gave them My oil and My perfume.
You gave them My bread, fine flour, oil, and honey that I gave you to eat. This happened, says the Lord, the LORD.
You took your sons and daughters, whom you had for Me, and killed them. Was that not enough?
You killed My children and sent them through fire for those gods.
In all your bad ways, you did not remember when you were young. You were naked and bare, covered in blood.
"How terrible for you! says the Lord, the LORD. After all your evil,
you built a raised place for yourself. You made a high place in every street.
You built high places at the top of every road. You made your beauty dirty. You gave yourself to everyone who passed by.
You were not faithful to the Egyptians, your neighbors. You did this more and more, and you made Me angry.
So I reached out My hand against you. I took away your food. I gave you to your enemies, the Philistine women, who were ashamed of your bad ways.
You were not faithful to the Assyrians. Still you were not satisfied.
You did it even more with the Chaldeans, the land of traders. Still you were not satisfied.
How weak your heart is, says the Lord, the LORD, because you did all these things like a woman who sells herself.
You built your high places at the top of every road. You made high places in every street. But you were not like a prostitute, because you did not even ask for pay.
You are like a wife who takes other men instead of her husband.
Men pay prostitutes. But you gave gifts to all who loved you. You paid them to come to you from all around because you were not faithful.
You were the opposite of other women. No man came to you for pay; you paid them. So you were different.
"So, you prostitute, listen to the word of the LORD.
This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Because you showed your bad ways and uncovered yourself to your lovers and your idols, and because you gave them your children's blood,
I will gather all your lovers you were happy with, and all those you loved, and all those you hated. I will gather them around you. Then I will uncover you for them to see all your nakedness.
I will punish you like women who are not faithful and who kill. I will bring on you blood and anger.
I will give you into their hands. They will tear down your high places and break your altars. They will strip off your clothes and take your jewelry. They will leave you naked and bare.
They will bring a crowd against you. They will throw stones at you and cut you with their swords.
They will burn your houses and punish you in front of many women. I will stop you from selling yourself. You will not give gifts to lovers again.
Then My anger will rest. My jealousy will leave you. I will be quiet and not be angry anymore.
Because you forgot your youth and made Me angry in all these things, I will bring your ways on your own head, says the Lord, the LORD. You added this wrong to all your other wrongs.
"Everyone who speaks in sayings will say this about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'
You are your mother's daughter. You hate your husband and your children. You are like your sisters, who hated their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father was an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria. She and her daughters live to your left. Your younger sister is Sodom. She and her daughters live to your right.
You did not just follow their ways. You did their bad things. In a short time, you became worse than they were.
As I live, says the Lord, the LORD, your sister Sodom and her daughters did not do as much wrong as you and your daughters.
This was Sodom's sin: She and her daughters were proud. They had plenty of food and lived in peace and comfort. But they did not help the poor and needy.
They were proud and did terrible things in front of Me. So I took them away, as you saw.
Samaria did not sin even half as much as you. You did more bad things than she did. You made your sisters look good by all the bad things you did.
You must carry your shame, because you made your sisters look better. Because of your sins, which are worse than theirs, they look better than you. So be ashamed and carry your shame.
"I will bring back Sodom and her daughters and Samaria and her daughters from being captives. I will also bring back your captives with them.
Then you will carry your shame. You will be ashamed for all you did. You will comfort them.
Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters and Samaria and her daughters, will go back to what they were before. You and your daughters will go back to what you were before.
You did not even speak of your sister Sodom when you were proud.
Before your bad ways were seen, you were laughed at by the daughters of Aram and those around them, and by the daughters of the Philistines all around.
You must carry your bad ways and your terrible acts, says the the LORD.
"This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I will do to you just as you did. You broke your promise and ignored your agreement.
But I will remember My agreement with you from when you were young. I will make an agreement with you that lasts forever.
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your older and younger sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of your agreement.
I will keep My agreement with you. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.
Then you will remember and be ashamed. You will not open your mouth again because of your shame, when I forgive you for all you did, says the Lord, the LORD."
The word of the the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, tell the people of Israel this riddle and story.
"Say to them: This is what the Lord the the LORD says. A big eagle with big wings and long feathers came to Lebanon. It took the top of a cedar tree.
It broke off the top shoot and carried it to a land of traders. It planted it in a city of traders.
It also took a seed and planted it in good soil. It put it by plenty of water, like a willow tree.
The seed grew into a low vine. Its branches turned toward the eagle. Its roots stayed under it. It became a vine and grew branches and shoots.
"But another big eagle with big wings and many feathers came. This vine turned its roots toward him. It sent its branches to him. It wanted him to water it.
It was planted in good soil by plenty of water. It could grow branches and fruit. It could become a fine vine.

"Say: This is what the Lord the the LORD says. Will it grow well? No. He will pull up its roots. He will take off its fruit. It will dry up. All its leaves will dry up. It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by the roots.
It is planted, but will it grow well? No. The east wind will hit it, and it will dry up. It will dry up where it grew."
Then the word of the the LORD came to me again. He said,
"Tell the stubborn people: Do you not know what these things mean? Tell them: The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem. He took its king and its leaders. He brought them to Babylon.
He took a man from the king's family. He made an agreement with him. He made him promise to be faithful. He also took the leaders of the land.
He did this so the kingdom would stay weak. It could not rise up again. The king had to keep the agreement to stay alive.
"But the king turned against Babylon. He sent men to Egypt to get horses and many soldiers. Will he succeed? Will a man who does this get away? Can he break the agreement and still get away?
