As surely as I live, says the Lord the the LORD, he will die in Babylon. He will die in the land of the king who made him king. He did not respect that king's promise. He broke his agreement.
Pharaoh and his big army will not help him in war. They will build ramps and walls to attack the city and kill many people.
He broke his promise. He said he would keep it, but he did all these things. He will not get away.
"So the Lord the the LORD says: As surely as I live, I will punish him for the promise he did not respect and the agreement he broke.
I will spread My net over him. He will be caught in My trap. I will bring him to Babylon. I will judge him there for turning against Me.
All his soldiers who run away will die by the sword. The rest will be scattered everywhere. Then you will know that I am the the LORD. I have spoken."
"This is what the Lord the the LORD says: I will take a small branch from the top of a cedar tree and plant it. I will break off a soft shoot from its top branches and plant it on a high mountain.

I will plant it on the high mountains of Israel. It will grow branches and fruit. It will become a great cedar tree. Birds of every kind will nest under it. They will rest in the shade of its branches.

Then all the trees in the field will know that I am the the LORD. I bring the tall tree down and make the short tree tall. I dry up the green tree and make the dry tree grow. I, the the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it."
The word of the the LORD came to me. “
What do you mean by using this saying in Israel: ‘Parents do wrong, and their children get hurt’?
As surely as I live, declares the Lord the LORD, you will not use this saying in Israel anymore. “
Look, every person belongs to Me. Fathers and sons both belong to Me. The person who sins is the one who will die. “
Suppose a man does what is right and fair.
He does not eat at altars on the hills. He does not look to Israel's false gods. He does not sleep with another man's wife. He does not go near a woman during her period.
He does not hurt anyone. He gives back what he borrowed. He does not steal. He gives food to the hungry. He gives clothes to people with no clothes.
He does not lend money to make extra money from it. He stays away from wrong. He makes fair choices between people.
He follows My rules and keeps My laws. He is a good man. He will live, declares the Lord the LORD. “
But suppose he has a son who hurts people and kills. This son does one of these bad things.
The father did not do these things. But the son eats at altars on the hills. He sleeps with another man's wife.
He hurts poor and needy people. He steals. He does not give back what he took. He looks to false gods. He does very wrong things.
He lends money to make extra money. He will not live. He did all these bad things, so he will die. His death is his own fault. “
Now suppose this son has a son. This grandson sees all the sins his father did. But he does not do the same things.
He does not eat at altars on the hills. He does not look to Israel's false gods. He does not sleep with another man's wife.
He does not hurt anyone. He does not keep what he borrowed. He does not steal. He gives food to the hungry. He gives clothes to people with no clothes.
He stays away from wrong. He does not lend money to make extra money. He follows My laws. He will not die for his father's wrong. He will live.
His father hurt people and stole from his brother. He did wrong among his people. So he will die for his wrong. “
But you ask, ‘Why doesn't the son pay for the father's wrong?’ Since the son did what is right and fair, and kept My laws, he will live.
The person who sins will die. A son will not pay for his father's wrong. A father will not pay for his son's wrong. Good people get credit for their good. Bad people get blame for their bad. “
But if a bad man stops doing all his sins and keeps My laws and does what is right and fair, he will live. He will not die.
None of his past wrongs will be remembered. Because he did right, he will live. “
Do I want bad people to die? declares the Lord the LORD. No. I want them to stop their bad ways and live. “
But if a good man stops doing right and does wrong, like the bad man does, will he live? No. None of his good will be remembered. He will die because he was not faithful and because he sinned. “
But you say, ‘The Lord's way is not fair.’ Listen, people of Israel: Is My way unfair? No. Your ways are unfair.
If a good man stops doing right and does wrong, he will die. He will die because of the wrong he did. “
But if a bad man stops his bad ways and does what is right and fair, he will save his life.
He thought about his wrongs and stopped. He will live. He will not die. “
But the people of Israel say, ‘The Lord's way is not fair.’ Are My ways unfair? No. Your ways are unfair. “
So I will judge you, people of Israel. Each of you will be judged by what you do, declares the Lord the LORD. Turn back. Stop all your sins, so sin will not ruin you.
Throw away all the sins you have done. Get a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, people of Israel?
I do not want anyone to die, declares the Lord the LORD. So turn back and live!”
You, sing a sad song for the leaders of Israel.
Say, "What was your mother like? She was like a lioness among lions. She lay down with young lions and raised her cubs."
One of her cubs grew into a young lion. He learned to hunt. He attacked people.
Other countries heard about him. They caught him in a trap. They dragged him with hooks to Egypt.
When she saw her hope was gone, she took another cub and raised him to be a young lion.
He walked among lions. He became a young lion. He learned to hunt. He attacked people.
He broke their strong places and ruined their cities. The land and everything in it shook at his roar.
Countries from all around came against him. They spread a net over him. They caught him in a trap.
They put him in a cage with hooks and took him to the king of Babylon. They kept him in prison so he could never roar again in the hills of Israel.
Your mother was like a grapevine planted by the water. It grew well and had many branches.
Its branches were strong enough to be rulers' staffs. It grew tall among the thick branches. People saw how tall and full it was.
Then it was pulled up in anger and thrown to the ground. A hot east wind dried its fruit. Its strong branch broke and dried up. Fire burned it up.
Now it is planted in a dry and empty land.
Fire came from its own branch and burned its fruit. Now there is no strong branch to be a ruler's staff. This is a sad song, and people will sing it as a sad song.
It was the seventh year. On the tenth day of the fifth month, some leaders of Israel came to ask the the LORD for help. They sat in front of me.
Then the the LORD spoke to me.
"Son of man, speak to the leaders of Israel. Say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: Are you coming to ask Me for help? As I live, I will not answer you, says the Lord the LORD.'
Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Tell them about the bad things their fathers did."

"Say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: On the day I chose Israel, I raised My hand to the family of Jacob. I made Myself known to them in Egypt. I raised My hand and said, "I am the the LORD your God." '
On that day I raised My hand to bring them out of Egypt. I would take them to a land I found for them. It had milk and honey. It was the best land of all.
I said to them, "Each of you throw away the bad things you look at. Do not make yourselves dirty with Egypt's idols. I am the the LORD your God."
But they did not obey Me. They would not listen. They did not throw away their bad things. They did not leave Egypt's idols. So I said I would pour out My anger on them in Egypt.
But I did it for My name's sake. I did not let My name be made dirty in front of the nations. They saw Me bring Israel out.
So I brought them out of Egypt. I led them into the desert.
I gave them My rules and laws. A person who follows them will live.
I also gave them My Sabbaths. They were a sign between Me and them. They would know that I am the the LORD who makes them holy.

But the people of Israel did not obey Me in the desert. They did not follow My rules. They said no to My laws. They made My Sabbaths dirty. So I said I would pour out My anger to destroy them in the desert.
But I did it for My name's sake. I did not let My name be made dirty in front of the nations. They saw Me bring Israel out.
I also raised My hand to them in the desert. I said I would not bring them into the land I gave them. It had milk and honey and was the best land.
I did this because they said no to My rules. They did not follow My laws. They made My Sabbaths dirty. Their hearts went after their idols.
But I felt sorry for them. I did not destroy them all in the desert.
I said to their children in the desert, "Do not follow your fathers' rules. Do not keep their laws. Do not make yourselves dirty with their idols."
"I am the the LORD your God. Follow My rules. Keep My laws and do them."
"Keep My Sabbaths holy. They are a sign between Me and you. Then you will know that I am the the LORD your God."
But the children did not obey Me. They did not follow My rules. They did not keep My laws. They made My Sabbaths dirty. So I said I would pour out My anger on them in the desert.
But I held back My hand. I did it for My name's sake. I did not let My name be made dirty in front of the nations. They saw Me bring Israel out.
I also raised My hand to them in the desert. I said I would scatter them among the nations. I would send them to other lands.
I did this because they did not keep My laws. They said no to My rules. They made My Sabbaths dirty. Their eyes went after their fathers' idols.
So I gave them rules that were not good. I gave them laws they could not live by.
I let them become dirty by their gifts. They offered all their first babies. I did this to make them guilty. Then they would know that I am the the LORD.'"
"So, son of man, speak to the people of Israel. Say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: Your fathers also spoke bad about Me. They were not faithful to Me.

I brought them to the land I promised. They saw high hills and green trees. They gave sacrifices there. They gave gifts that made Me angry. They burned sweet smells there. They poured out drink offerings.
Then I said, "What is this high place where you go?" So it is called High Place to this day.'"
"So say to Israel, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: Will you make yourselves dirty like your fathers? Will you chase after bad things?

When you bring gifts and burn your children, you make yourselves dirty with all your idols. And I will not be asked by you, people of Israel. As I live, says the Lord the LORD, I will not be asked by you.
You may think, "Let us be like other nations. Let us be like the families of the lands. Let us serve wood and stone." But that will not happen.'"
"As I live, says the Lord the LORD, I will rule over you with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured-out anger.
I will bring you out from the nations. I will gather you from the lands where you are scattered. I will do it with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured-out anger.
I will bring you into the desert of the nations. There I will judge you face to face.
I will judge you like I judged your fathers in the desert of Egypt, says the Lord the LORD.
I will make you pass under the stick. I will bring you into the promise of the agreement.
I will take out the rebels and sinners among you. I will send them away from where they live. They will not come into the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the the LORD."

"As for you, people of Israel, this is what the Lord the LORD says: Go, serve your idols, each of you. But after that, if you will not listen to Me, do not make My holy name dirty again with your gifts and idols.

For on My holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord the LORD, all the people of Israel will serve Me in the land. There I will accept them. There I will ask for your gifts and first crops. I will ask for all your holy things.

I will accept you like a sweet smell. I will do this when I bring you from the nations. I will gather you from the lands where you are scattered. I will show Myself holy through you in front of the nations.
Then you will know that I am the the LORD. I will bring you into the land of Israel. I raised My hand to give this land to your fathers.
There you will remember your ways and all the things you did. You became dirty by them. You will hate yourselves for all the bad things you did.
Then you will know that I am the the LORD. I will do this for My name's sake. I will not do it like your bad ways or your ruined acts, people of Israel, says the Lord the LORD."
Then the the LORD spoke to me.
"Son of man, look toward the south. Speak to the south. Prophesy against the forest in the south.

Say to the forest in the south, 'Hear the word of the the LORD. This is what the Lord the LORD says: I am about to set you on fire. It will burn every green tree and every dry tree. The bright flame will not go out. Every face from south to north will be burned.'
All people will see that I, the the LORD, started the fire. It will not go out."
Then I said, "Oh, Lord the LORD! People say I just tell stories."
The word of the LORD came to me.
He said, "Son of man, turn your face toward Jerusalem. Speak against the holy places. Speak God's message against the land of Israel.
Say to the land of Israel, 'This is what the LORD says: I am against you. I will pull My sword from its case. I will cut off both good people and bad people from you.'
Because I cut off both, My sword will come out of its case against all people, from the south to the north.
Then all people will know that I am the LORD. I pulled My sword from its case. It will not go back."
You, son of man, groan in front of them. Groan with a broken heart and bitter pain.

When they ask why you groan, say, 'Bad news is coming. Everyone will lose courage. All hands will become weak. Every spirit will faint. Every knee will shake like water. It is coming. It will happen,' says the Lord, the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me again.
He said, "Son of man, speak for God. Say, 'This is what the Lord says: A sword! A sword! It is sharpened and polished.'
It is sharpened to kill. It is polished to flash like lightning. Should we be glad about My son's stick? The sword cuts down every tree.
The sword is given to the sharpener to hold. It is sharpened and polished, so it can be put in the killer's hand.
Cry and wail, son of man, for this sword is against My people. It is against all the leaders of Israel. They are given to the sword with My people. So show how sad you are.
This is a test. What if the stick that hates all wood does not last? says the Lord, the LORD."
"Son of man, speak for God and clap your hands. Let the sword strike two times, even three times. It is a sword for people who are killed. It is a big sword that cuts deep into them.
So people will lose courage and many will stumble. I set the sword against all their gates. It is made to flash like lightning. It is sharpened to kill.
Gather together. Turn to the right. Turn to the left. Go where your face is set.
I too will clap My hands. I will calm My anger. I, the LORD, have spoken."
The word of the LORD came to me again.
He said, "Son of man, draw two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to follow. Both roads start from the same land. Make a sign where the road splits at the city.
Make one road for the sword to go to Rabbah, the city of the Ammonites. Make the other road go to Judah, to the strong city of Jerusalem.
The king of Babylon stands where the two roads split. He uses magic to choose. He shakes arrows. He asks his false gods. He looks at an animal's liver.

In his right hand is the sign for Jerusalem. He will set up big logs to break the walls. He will give the order to kill. He will shout a war cry. He will set the logs against the gates. He will pile up dirt against the wall. He will build a wall to attack.
To them, it looks like a false sign. They have sworn many oaths. But he remembers their guilt, so they will be caught.
So the Lord, the LORD, says: Because you bring your guilt to mind by showing your sins, your sins are seen in all your deeds. Because you are remembered, you will be caught."
"And you, sinful and bad prince of Israel, your day has come. The time to punish you is here.
This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Take off the turban. Remove the crown. Things will not stay the same. The lowly will be lifted up. The proud will be brought down.
I will ruin it, ruin it, ruin it. It will not be fixed until the One comes who has the right to judge. Then I will give it to Him."
"Son of man, speak for God. Say, 'This is what the Lord, the LORD, says to the Ammonites and their insults: A sword! A sword is drawn to kill. It is polished to destroy. It is made to flash.'
They see false visions about you. They tell lies when they use magic. They want to use the sword to kill bad people. Their day has come. The time to punish them is here.
Put the sword back in its case. I will judge you where you were made, in the land where you were born.
I will pour out My anger on you. I will blow the fire of My great anger on you. I will give you into the hands of cruel men, skilled destroyers.
You will be fuel for the fire. Your blood will be in the middle of the land. You will not be remembered, because I, the LORD, have spoken."
The word of the LORD came to me.
He said, “Son of man, will you judge? Will you judge the city of blood? Then show her all her terrible sins.”
He said, “Say this to the city:” “This is what the Lord the LORD says: O city, you shed blood in your own city. You make idols that make you dirty.
You are guilty because of the blood you spilled. You are dirty because of the idols you made. Your time is up. Your day has come. So I will make you a shame to the nations and a joke to all lands.
Near and far lands will laugh at you. You are dirty and full of trouble.
Look, the leaders of Israel in you use their power to spill blood.
In you, people look down on fathers and mothers. They cheat strangers. They hurt orphans and widows.
You hate My holy things. You make My Sabbath days dirty.
In you, people tell lies to spill blood. In you, people eat on the hills and do bad things.
In you, men slept with their father's wife. In you, they slept with women during their monthly time.
In you, one man sleeps with his neighbor's wife. Another sleeps with his daughter-in-law. Another sleeps with his sister.
In you, people take money to spill blood. You charge interest and make unfair profit. You cheat your neighbors. You have forgotten Me, says the Lord the LORD.
Look, I am very angry about the money you made by cheating. I am angry about the blood in you.
Can your heart stay strong? Can your hands stay strong when I punish you? I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
I will scatter you among the nations. I will spread you through the lands. I will take away your dirt from you.
You will be shamed in front of the nations. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me.
He said, “Son of man, the people of Israel have become like useless metal to Me. They are all bronze, tin, iron, and lead in a furnace. They are like silver waste.”
“So this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because all of you became like junk, I will gather you into Jerusalem.
“I will gather you like silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into a furnace. I will blow on it with fire to melt you. In My anger and wrath I will put you there and melt you.
“I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of My anger. You will melt inside it.
“You will melt like silver in a furnace. Then you will know that I, the LORD, poured out My anger on you.”
The word of the LORD came to me.
He said, “Son of man, say this to the land:” “You are a land that is not clean. No rain falls on you in your day of anger.
“Her prophets in her are like a roaring lion tearing its food. They eat people. They take treasure and good things. They make many widows in her.

“Her priests break My law and make My holy things dirty. They do not show the difference between holy and common. They do not teach clean and dirty. They forget My Sabbath days, and I am treated badly among them.
“Her leaders in her are like wolves tearing their food. They spill blood and kill people to make unfair money.
“Her prophets cover them with lies. They see false visions. They tell lies. They say, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says,’ but the LORD did not speak.
“The people of the land cheat others and steal. They hurt the poor and needy. They treat strangers unfairly.
“I looked for one man among them who would build a wall and step in for Me, to keep the land from being destroyed. But I found none.
“So I poured out My anger on them. I destroyed them with the fire of My wrath. I made them pay for what they did, says the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me. He said, "
Son of man, two women were born to one mother.
They cheated in Egypt. They cheated when they were young. There men touched their chests, and there they lost their purity.
Their names were Oholah, the older sister, and Oholibah. They became Mine. They had sons and daughters. Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem." "
Oholah cheated while she was Mine. She wanted her lovers, the Assyrians, who were near.
They wore blue clothes. They were leaders and officials. They were all handsome young men. They rode horses.
She gave herself to them. They were the best men of Assyria. She made herself dirty with all their idols. She wanted them.
She did not stop cheating from Egypt. When she was young, men slept with her. They took her purity. They poured their cheating on her.
So I gave her to her lovers. I gave her to the Assyrians she wanted.
They showed her nakedness. They took her sons and daughters. They killed them with swords. She became a bad name among women. They punished her." "
Her sister Oholibah saw this. She cheated even more. Her cheating was worse than her sister's.
She wanted the men of Assyria: leaders and officials who were near. They wore beautiful clothes. They were horsemen on horses. They were all handsome young men.
I saw that both sisters were dirty. They went the same bad way." "
She cheated even more. She saw men carved on a wall. They were pictures of Chaldeans carved in red.
They wore belts around their waists. They had long hats on their heads. They all looked like officers. They looked like Babylonians, the Chaldeans, from their home land.
She wanted them when she saw them. She sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
The sons of Babylon came to her bed of love. They made her dirty by cheating. She was dirty because of them. Then she turned away from them in disgust.
She showed her cheating. She showed her nakedness. Then I turned away from her, like I turned away from her sister.
Still she cheated more. She remembered her young days when she cheated in Egypt.
She wanted men whose bodies were like donkeys and whose strength was like horses.
You remembered your cheating from when you were young. The Egyptians touched your chest when you were young." "
So, Oholibah, this is what the Lord, the LORD says: 'I will stir up your lovers against you. You are sick of them. I will bring them against you from all sides.
They are Babylonians and all the Chaldeans: Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them. They are handsome young men, leaders and officials, officers and famous men. They all ride horses.
They will come against you with weapons, chariots, and wagons, and with many people. They will put shields and helmets around you. I will let them judge you by their own rules.

I will be jealous for you. They will hurt you in anger. They will cut off your nose and ears. Your people left alive will fall by swords. They will take your sons and daughters. Your people left alive will burn in fire.
They will strip off your clothes and take your pretty things.
So I will stop your cheating and your Egypt cheating. You will not look at them again. You will not remember Egypt anymore." "
This is what the Lord, the LORD says: 'I will give you to people you hate. I will give you to people you are sick of.
They will hurt you with hate. They will take all you worked for. They will leave you naked and bare. Your cheating will be seen. Your bad ways and cheating will be shown.
This will happen because you cheated after other nations. You made yourself dirty with their idols.
You walked your sister's way. So I will put her cup in your hand.
This is what the Lord, the LORD says: 'You will drink your sister's cup. It is deep and wide. It holds a lot. People will laugh at you and make fun of you.
You will be full of drunkenness and sadness. It is a cup of horror and ruin. It is the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and empty it. You will bite its broken pieces and tear your chest. I have spoken, says the Lord, the LORD.'
So this is what the Lord, the LORD says: 'Because you forgot Me and turned your back on Me, you must carry your bad ways and your cheating.'"
The LORD said to me, "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then tell them their terrible sins.
They cheated on their husband. Blood is on their hands. They cheated with their idols. They even passed their sons, whom they had for Me, through fire as food for their idols.
They did this to Me too: They made My holy place dirty. They treated My Sabbath days as not holy.
On the day they killed their children for their idols, they came into My holy place to make it dirty. See, they did this in My house.
They even sent for men from far away. A messenger was sent to them. They came. For those men you bathed, painted your eyes, and put on jewelry.
You sat on a fancy bed with a table set before it. On it you put My incense and My oil.
A noisy crowd was with her. Men from the desert came, drunk men from many people. They put bracelets on the women's wrists and pretty crowns on their heads.
Then I said that the woman worn out by cheating would now cheat with men, and they with her.
They went to her like men go to a prostitute. So they went to Oholah and Oholibah, those wicked women.
But good men will judge them. They will judge them like cheating wives and like women who kill. They are cheating wives, and blood is on their hands." "
This is what the Lord, the LORD says: 'Bring a crowd against them. Give them to fear and to being robbed.
The crowd will stone them and cut them down with swords. They will kill their sons and daughters. They will burn their houses with fire.
So I will make cheating stop in the land. All women will learn a lesson and not cheat like yours.
They will pay you back for your cheating. You will carry the sin of your idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord, the LORD.'"
On the tenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year, the LORD spoke to me.
He said, "Son of man, write down today's date. Today the king of Babylon has surrounded Jerusalem."
Tell this stubborn people a story. Say, "Put the pot on the fire. Pour water into it.
Put in the meat pieces—all the best pieces, the thigh and shoulder. Fill it with the best bones.
Take the best sheep. Pile bones under the pot. Boil it well. Cook the bones in it too."
So this is what the Lord GOD says: "Oh, city full of blood! You are like a pot with grime stuck inside. The grime has not come out. Take the meat out piece by piece. No one chose the pieces.
Her blood is in her. She poured it on bare rock. She did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust.
To make Me angry and pay her back, I put her blood on bare rock, so it would not be covered."
This is what the Lord GOD says: "Oh, city full of blood! I too will make the fire big.
Pile on the wood. Light the fire. Boil the meat well. Mix in the spices. Burn the bones.
Then set the empty pot on the coals. Heat it until its bronze glows. Let its grime melt inside. Let its grime be burned away.
She worked hard, but her grime stayed. The fire did not take it out."
He also says, "Your grime holds sin. I tried to clean you, but you would not be clean. You will not be clean from your grime until My anger is done with you.
I, the LORD, have spoken. It will happen. I will do it. I will not hold back. I will not feel sorry. I will not change My mind. They will judge you by what you have done, says the Lord GOD."
The word of the LORD came to me again.
He said, "Son of man, I am about to take away the one you love most. She will die from sickness. But do not cry. Do not weep. Do not let tears fall.
Sigh quietly. Do not mourn for the dead. Tie your turban on your head. Put your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your upper lip. Do not eat food brought by others."
In the morning I spoke to the people. That evening my wife died. The next morning I did what I was told.
The people asked me, "Won't you tell us what this means for us? Why are you acting this way?"
I said to them, "The LORD spoke to me. He told me to say this to you:
"'I am about to make My holy place unclean. It is your pride and strength. It is what you love to see. It is what your heart wants. Your sons and daughters that you left behind will die by the sword.
You will do as I have done. You will not cover your upper lip. You will not eat food brought by others.
You will keep your turbans on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not cry or weep. You will waste away because of your sins. You will groan to each other.
Ezekiel will be a sign for you. You will do everything he did. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.'"
"And you, Son of man, on the day I take away their strong place—the joy of their pride, what they love to see, and what their hearts want—their sons and daughters too—
on that day a man who escapes will come to you with news.
On that day your mouth will open when the man comes. You will speak and not be silent anymore. You will be a sign to them. They will know that I am the LORD."
The word of the the LORD came to me.
“Son of man, turn your face toward the Ammonites and speak against them.

Say to the Ammonites, ‘Hear the word of the Lord, the the LORD. This is what the Lord, the the LORD, says: Because you said, “Aha!” when My holy place was made unclean, when the land of Israel was empty, and when the people of Judah were taken away,
I will give you to the people of the East. They will camp among you and make homes there. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
I will make Rabbah a place for camels, and the Ammonites a place for sheep to rest. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.
For this is what the Lord, the the LORD, says: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and were glad with all your heart to see Israel hurt,

I have reached out My hand against you. I will give you to other nations as things they take in war. I will cut you off from the peoples, and you will die in other lands. I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.’”
“This is what the Lord, the the LORD, says: Because Moab and Seir said, ‘Look, the family of Judah is like all the other nations,’
I will open Moab to attack, starting from its border towns. I will take away its best land, including Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim.
I will give that land to the Ammonites, and the Ammonites will not be remembered among the nations.
I will punish Moab. Then they will know that I am the the LORD.”
“This is what the Lord, the the LORD, says: Because Edom took revenge on the family of Judah and did wrong by paying them back,
I will reach out My hand against Edom. I will cut off people and animals from it. I will make it empty from Teman, and Dedan will fall by the sword.
I will let My people Israel punish Edom. They will deal with Edom with My anger and My fierce anger. Then they will know My punishment, says the Lord, the the LORD.”
“This is what the Lord, the the LORD, says: Because the Philistines took revenge with hate in their hearts and tried to destroy Israel forever,
I will reach out My hand against the Philistines. I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy those left on the coast.
I will punish them greatly in My anger and correct them. Then they will know that I am the the LORD when I punish them.”
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"Son of man, Tyre said about Jerusalem, 'Ha! The door for all nations is broken. It swings open to me. Now that she is ruined, I will be full.'"
"So the Lord the LORD says: 'Look, I am against you, Tyre. I will bring many nations against you, like the sea brings its waves.'
'They will break down your walls and tear down your towers. I will scrape your dust from you and make you a bare rock.'
'You will be a place to spread nets in the sea, because I have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD. You will be taken by the nations.'
'Your daughters in the field will be killed by the sword. Then they will know that I am the LORD.'"
"For the Lord the LORD says: 'Look, I am bringing Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, king of kings, from the north. He comes with horses, chariots, horsemen, and many people.'
'He will kill your daughters in the field with the sword. He will set up a siege wall against you. He will pour out a ramp against you. He will lift up shields against you.'
'He will hit your walls with his battering rams. He will break down your towers with his axes.'
'His many horses will cover you with dust. He will come through your gates like men break through a broken wall. Your walls will shake at the sound of horsemen, wheels, and chariots.'
'With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets. He will kill your people with the sword. He will bring down your strong forts to the ground.'"
"They will take your riches and steal your goods. They will break down your walls and tear down your nice houses. They will throw your stones, wood, and dust into the water.
I will stop your happy songs. No one will hear your harps again.
I will make you a bare rock. You will be a place to spread nets. You will never be built again, because I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD.'"
"The Lord the LORD says to Tyre: 'Will not the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and people are killed inside you?'

'Then all the leaders of the sea will step down from their thrones. They will take off their robes and their fine clothes. They will put on shaking fear. They will sit on the ground. They will shake every moment and be shocked at you.'

'They will sing a sad song about you. They will say, "How you are destroyed, famous city, where sailors lived! You were strong on the sea, you and your people. You made everyone who lived there afraid."'
'Now the islands will shake on the day you fall. The islands in the sea will be scared because you are gone.'"
"For the Lord the LORD says: 'I will make you a ruined city, like cities no one lives in. I will bring the deep water over you, and the great waters will cover you.'

'I will send you down with those who go down to the deep hole, to the people of long ago. I will put you in the lowest parts of the earth, like old ruins, with those who go down to the deep hole. You will never live there again. I will bring beauty to the land of the living.'
'I will make you a terror, and you will be gone. People will look for you, but they will never find you again, declares the Lord the LORD.'"
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, sing a sad song about Tyre. "
Say to Tyre, who lives by the sea and trades with many lands. This is what the Lord the LORD says: You, Tyre, have said, 'I am perfect in beauty.'
Your borders are in the heart of the sea. Your builders made you very beautiful. "
They built your ship boards from pine trees of Senir. They took cedar from Lebanon to make your mast.
They made your oars from oak trees of Bashan. They made your deck from ivory and wood from the coasts of Cyprus.
Your sail was fine linen from Egypt. It was your flag. Your cover was blue and purple cloth from the coasts of Elishah. "
Men from Sidon and Arvad rowed for you. The wise men of Tyre were your sailors and ship guides.
Old men from Gebal and their skilled workers fixed your leaks. Ships from all over the sea and their sailors came to trade with you.
Men from Persia, Lud, and Put served in your army. They hung shields and helmets on your walls. They made you look great.
Men from Arvad and your army stood on your walls all around. Men from Gammad stood in your towers. They hung their shields on your walls all around. They made you beautiful. "
Tarshish traded with you because you had so much wealth. They gave silver, iron, tin, and lead for your goods.
Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you. They brought people and bronze tools to trade.
From Beth-togarmah they gave horses, war horses, and mules for your goods.
The men of Dedan traded with you. You traded with many lands. They brought ivory and dark wood to pay you.
Aram traded with you because you made so many things. They gave blue-green stone, purple cloth, fine sewing, linen, coral, and red stones for your goods. "
Judah and Israel traded with you. They gave wheat, cakes, honey, oil, and sweet oil for your trade.
Damascus traded with you because you had so much wealth and so many goods. They gave wine from Helbon and white wool.
Dan and Greece brought iron, sweet spice, and cane for your trade.
Dedan traded with you for saddle blankets.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar traded with you. They traded in lambs, rams, and goats. "
Traders of Sheba and Raamah traded with you. They gave gold, the best spices, and precious stones for your goods.
Haran, Canneh, Eden, and traders from Sheba, Asshur, and Kilmad traded with you.
They traded with you in beautiful clothes, blue and purple cloth, colorful rugs, and strong ropes. "
Ships of Tarshish carried your goods. You were full and very heavy on the sea.
Your rowers took you into deep water. The east wind broke your ship in the middle of the sea.
Your money, goods, trade, sailors, ship guides, repairers, traders, soldiers, and everyone with you will sink in the sea on the day you fall. "
The lands by the sea will shake when your ship guides cry out.
All who row, all sailors, and all ship guides of the sea will come down from their ships and stand on the land.
They will cry loudly over you and cry with pain. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads for you and put on rough cloth. They will cry for you with bitter hearts and deep sadness.
They will sing a sad song for you and cry over you: 'Who was like Tyre, now quiet in the sea?' "
When your goods went out over the seas, you made many people rich. Your wealth and trade made the kings of the earth rich.
Now you are broken by the seas in deep water. Your trade and all your people have fallen with you.
All who live by the sea are shocked at you. Their kings are afraid and shake.
The traders among the nations hiss at you. You have become a terrible thing, and you will be no more forever."
The word of the LORD came to me.

"Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre this message from the Lord GOD: Because your heart is proud, you said, "I am a god. I sit on a god's throne in the middle of the seas." But you are only a man, not a god, even though you think you are as wise as a god."
Look, you are wiser than Daniel. No secret is hidden from you. "
By your wisdom and understanding, you made wealth for yourself. You gathered gold and silver in your storehouses.
By your great skill in trade, you grew your wealth. Your heart became proud because of your riches. "
So the Lord GOD says: Because you think your heart is like a god's heart,
I will bring strangers against you. They are the meanest of nations. They will draw their swords against your beauty and wisdom. They will ruin your shine.
They will bring you down to the grave. You will die a violent death in the middle of the seas. "
Will you still say, "I am a god," when those who kill you stand before you? You will be just a man, not a god, in the hands of those who hurt you.
You will die like people who are not part of God's family. Foreigners will kill you. For I have spoken, says the Lord GOD."
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, sing a sad song for the king of Tyre. Tell him this message from the Lord GOD: You were a perfect example, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

You were in Eden, God's garden. Every precious stone covered you: ruby, topaz, diamond, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald. They were set in gold. They were ready on the day you were created. "
You were a chosen guardian angel. I placed you on God's holy mountain. You walked among stones of fire.
You were good in all your ways from the day you were created, until bad was found in you. "
Through your great trade, you were filled with hurt, and you sinned. So I drove you out from God's mountain. I destroyed you, the covering angel, from among the stones of fire.
Your heart became proud because of your beauty. You ruined your wisdom because of your shine. I threw you to the ground. I made you a show before kings. "
By your many sins and cheating in trade, you made your holy places dirty. So I brought fire from inside you. It ate you up. I turned you to ashes on the earth in front of everyone who saw you.
All the nations who knew you are shocked at you. You have become something scary, and you will be gone forever."
The word of the LORD came to me.
"Son of man, look toward Sidon and speak against it.
Say this message from the Lord GOD: I am against you, Sidon. I will show My greatness among you. They will know that I am the LORD when I carry out punishments in her and show My holy power in her. "
I will send sickness into her and blood in her streets. Dead people will fall inside her from swords on every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD. "
Israel will no longer suffer painful problems from the people around them who look down on them. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD."

"This is what the Lord GOD says: When I bring together the people of Israel from the nations where they were sent away, I will show how holy I am through them so other nations can see. Then they will live in their own land, the land I gave to My servant Jacob.

They will live there in peace. They will build houses and plant grape gardens. They will live in peace when I punish all the nations around them who were mean to them. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God."
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day, the word of the LORD came to me.
“Son of man, turn your face toward Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Speak against him and against all Egypt.

“Speak and tell him, ‘This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I am against you, Pharaoh, king of Egypt. You are like a big monster lying in your rivers. You said the Nile is yours and that you made it.’
“But I will put hooks in your mouth. The fish in your rivers will stick to your scales. I will pull you out of your rivers, and all the fish that stick to your scales will come out too.

“I will leave you in the desert, you and all the fish from your rivers. You will fall on the open field. No one will pick you up or gather you. I have given you as food to the wild animals and the birds.
“Then all the people of Egypt will know that I am the LORD. They have been like a weak stick for the people of Israel.
“When Israel held your hand, you broke and hurt their shoulders. When they leaned on you, you broke, and their backs shook.
“So this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I will bring a sword against you. I will destroy people and animals in your land.
“The land of Egypt will become empty and ruined. Then they will know that I am the LORD. You said the Nile is yours and that you made it.
“So I am against you and your rivers. I will make the land of Egypt a ruined, empty place from Migdol to Syene, all the way to the border of Cush.
“No person or animal will walk through it. It will not be lived in for forty years.
“I will make Egypt the emptiest land among ruined lands. Its cities will be empty for forty years among ruined cities. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations. I will send them to other lands.
“For this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: After forty years, I will bring the Egyptians back from the nations where they were scattered.
“I will bring Egypt back from being captured. I will bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land where they started. There they will be a small kingdom.
“It will be the smallest kingdom. It will never again lift itself above other nations. I will make them so small that they will never again rule over other nations.
“Egypt will no longer be a place Israel trusts. Instead, it will remind Israel of its sin when Israel turned to Egypt. Then they will know that I am the Lord, the LORD.”
In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day, the word of the LORD came to me.

“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made his army work hard against Tyre. Every head was made bald, and every shoulder was rubbed bare. But he and his army got no pay from Tyre for the work they did.

“So this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He will carry off its wealth. He will take its treasure and its goods. It will be pay for his army.
“I have given him the land of Egypt as a reward for his work, because he and his army did it for Me, says the Lord, the LORD.
“On that day I will make the people of Israel strong again. I will let you speak among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
The LORD spoke to me. He said, "
Son of man, prophesy. Tell the people this message from the Lord, the LORD: Cry out, 'Oh no for that day!'
For the day is near. The Day of the LORD is near. It will be a day of clouds. It will be a time of trouble for the nations. "
A sword will come to Egypt. Cush will have great fear when many die in Egypt. Egypt's riches will be taken away. Its strong places will be torn down.
Cush, Put, Lud, and all the mixed people will die by the sword. Kub and the people of the covenant land will die too. "

This is what the LORD says: The people who help Egypt will fall. Egypt's proud strength will come down. From Migdol to Syene, they will die by the sword inside Egypt. This is what the Lord, the LORD, says.
They will be empty like empty lands. Their cities will be among ruined cities. "
Then they will know that I am the LORD. I will set fire to Egypt. All who help her will be broken.
On that day, messengers will go out from Me in ships. They will scare Cush so it does not feel safe. Great fear will come on the day Egypt is judged. Yes, it is coming. "
This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I will stop the crowds of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
He and his people will come. They are the most cruel nation. They will come to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt. They will fill the land with dead people. "
I will dry up the streams of the Nile. I will give the land to bad men. I will ruin the land and all in it by the hand of strangers. I, the LORD, have spoken.
This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I will destroy the false gods. I will stop the idols in Memphis. There will be no more prince in Egypt. I will put fear in the land of Egypt. "
I will ruin Pathros. I will set fire to Zoan. I will punish Thebes.
I will pour out My anger on Pelusium, the strong place of Egypt. I will cut off the crowds of Thebes.
I will set fire to Egypt. Pelusium will shake in pain. Thebes will be split open. Memphis will have trouble every day. "
The young men of On and Pi-beseth will die by the sword. Those cities will be taken away.
In Tehaphnehes, the day will be dark. I will break Egypt's power there. Then Egypt's proud strength will stop. A cloud will cover her. Her daughters will be taken away.
So I will judge Egypt. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, the LORD spoke to me. He said, "
Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. It has not been wrapped to heal. It has not been bandaged to make it strong enough to hold a sword.
So this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I am against Pharaoh, king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the strong one and the weak one. I will make the sword fall from his hand. "
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations. I will spread them out in the lands.
I will make the arms of the king of Babylon strong. I will put My sword in his hand. I will break the arms of Pharaoh. He will cry out in pain before him, like a wounded man. "

I will make the arms of the king of Babylon strong. But the arms of Pharaoh will fall. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I put My sword into the hand of the king of Babylon. He will use it against the land of Egypt.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations. I will spread them out in the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, the the LORD spoke to me.
He said, "Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his people: Who are you like in your greatness? "
Look, Assyria was like a cedar tree in Lebanon. It had beautiful branches. It gave shade like a forest. It grew very tall. Its top rose high among the thick branches.
Water made it grow. The deep water made it tall. Rivers ran around the place where it was planted. Channels sent water to all the trees in the field.
So it grew taller than all the trees in the field. Its branches grew many and long because it had lots of water.
All the birds in the sky made nests in its branches. All the wild animals had babies under its branches. Many nations lived in its shade.
It was beautiful because it was big. Its branches were long. Its roots reached down to lots of water.
The cedar trees in God's garden could not hide it. The cypress trees were not like its branches. The plane trees were not like its branches. No tree in God's garden was as pretty as it.
I made it pretty with many branches. All the trees in Eden, in God's garden, were jealous of it. "
So the Lord the LORD says, Because you grew so tall, and your top reached into the thick branches, and you became proud because of your height,
I will hand you over to a strong ruler of the nations. He will treat you the way your wrongs deserve. I have thrown you out.

Strangers, mean nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in all the valleys. Its branches broke in every part of the land. All the people of the earth went down from its shade and left it.
All the birds in the sky settled on its fallen tree. All the wild animals were on its branches.

This is so no tree with lots of water will grow proud and tall. No tree will put its top among the thick branches. No tree that drinks water will stand tall in pride. They all must die and go down to the earth below, to be with people who go down to the grave.

The Lord the LORD says, On the day it went down to the grave, I made people sad. I covered the deep water over it. I stopped its rivers. I held back the great waters. I made Lebanon dark because of it. All the trees in the field were weak for it.

I made nations shake when they heard it fall. I brought it down to the grave with those who go down to the grave. All the trees of Eden, the best and finest of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the earth below.
They also went down to the grave with it, to join those killed by the sword. The people who lived in its shade among the nations also went down.

Who are you like in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? You will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the earth below. You will lie among people who are not circumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his people, says the Lord the LORD."
In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, the word of the the LORD came to me.

The The LORD said, "Son of man, sing a sad song for Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Say to him: You are like a young lion among the nations. But you are like a sea monster in the seas. You splash in your rivers. You stir up the water with your feet. You make their rivers muddy.
"The Lord GOD says, I will throw My net over you. Many people will gather around you. They will pull you up in My net.
I will throw you on the land. I will leave you in the open field. Birds of the sky will settle on you. Wild animals will eat their fill from you.
I will spread your flesh on the mountains. I will fill the valleys with your body.
I will water the land with your blood, even to the mountains. The streams will be full of you.
"When you die, I will cover the sky. I will make the stars dark. I will cover the sun with a cloud. The moon will not shine.
I will make all the bright lights in the sky dark over you. I will put darkness over your land, says the Lord GOD.
"I will trouble the hearts of many people. I will bring news of your ruin to the nations, to lands you did not know.
Many people will be shocked when they see you. Kings will shake with fear. I will wave My sword in front of them. On the day you fall, each one will shake with fear for his own life.
"The Lord GOD says, The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.
I will make your people fall by the swords of mighty men. They are the most scary men of all nations. They will destroy the greatness of Egypt and all her people.
"I will destroy all her animals near the many waters. No human foot will muddy them again. No animal hoof will muddy them again.
Then I will make their waters settle. I will make their rivers flow like oil, says the Lord GOD.
"When I make the land of Egypt empty and ruined, when I take away all who live there, then they will know that I am the the LORD.
This is a sad song. The daughters of the nations will sing it. They will sing it for Egypt and all her people, says the Lord GOD."
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the the LORD came to me.
The The LORD said, "Son of man, cry for Egypt's people. Send them down. Send Egypt and the daughters of mighty nations down to the world below, to those who go down to the grave.
You are not better than them. Go down and lie with those not circumcised.
They will fall among those killed by the sword. The sword is ready. Drag Egypt and all her people away.
The mighty men in the grave will speak to him. They will say that his helpers have gone down too. They lie with those not circumcised, killed by the sword.
"Assyria is there with all her people. Graves are all around her. All of them are dead, killed by the sword.
Her graves are in the deepest part of the grave. Her people are all around her grave. All of them are dead, killed by the sword. They once spread fear in the land of the living.

Elam is there with all her people. They are all around her grave. All of them are dead, killed by the sword. They went down not circumcised to the grave. They spread fear in the land of the living. Now they carry their shame with those who go down to the grave.

A place is made for Egypt among the dead, with all her people. Graves are all around her. All of them were not circumcised and were killed by the sword. They spread fear in the land of the living. Now they carry their shame with those who go down to the grave. She is put among the dead.
"Meshech and Tubal are there with all their people. Graves are all around them. All of them were not circumcised and were killed by the sword. They spread fear in the land of the living.

They will not lie with the fallen mighty men who went down to the grave with their weapons. Those men put their swords under their heads, but their sins stayed on their bones. They were feared as mighty men in the land of the living.
But you will be broken among those not circumcised. You will lie with those killed by the sword.
Edom is there with her kings and princes. In their strength they were put with those killed by the sword. They lie with those not circumcised and with those who go down to the grave.

All the princes of the north are there, and all the Sidonians. They went down in shame with those killed by the sword. Even though they spread fear by their strength, they lie with those not circumcised, killed by the sword. They carry their shame with those who go down to the grave.
"Pharaoh will see them and be comforted about all his people—Pharaoh and all his army, killed by the sword, says the Lord GOD.
I put fear of him in the land of the living. Pharaoh and all his people will be laid among those not circumcised, with those killed by the sword, says the Lord GOD."
The The LORD spoke to me.
He said, "Son of man, speak to your people. Say to them, 'When I bring war to a land, the people of that land choose one man from among them and make him their watchman.
If he sees the enemy coming into the land, he blows a horn and warns the people.
If someone hears the horn but does not listen to the warning, and the enemy kills him, his death is his own fault.
He heard the horn, but he did not listen. His death is his own fault. If he had listened, he would have lived.

But if the watchman sees the enemy coming and does not blow the horn to warn the people, and someone is killed, that person dies for his own sin. But I will hold the watchman responsible for his death.'"
"As for you, Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel. When you hear a message from Me, you must warn them for Me.
When I say to a wicked person, 'You will die,' and you do not warn him or tell him to stop doing wrong, that wicked person will die for his sin. But I will hold you responsible for his death.
But if you warn the wicked person to turn from his wrong ways, and he does not turn, he will die for his sin. But you will have saved your own life."
He said, "Now, Son of man, say to the people of Israel, 'You have said, "Our sins are on us. We are wasting away because of them. How can we live?"'"

"Say to them, 'As surely as I live, says the Lord, the LORD, I do not want wicked people to die. I want them to turn from their wrong ways and live. Turn back! Turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, people of Israel?'"

"So, Son of man, say to your people, 'A good person's right living will not save him when he sins. A bad person's past sins will not make him fall when he turns from them. And a good person cannot live by his good deeds when he sins.
If I say a good person will live, but he trusts in his good deeds and then does wrong, none of his good deeds will be remembered. He will die for the wrong he did.
But if I say to a bad person, "You will die," and he turns from his sin and does what is right and fair—
if he gives back what he took, pays back what he stole, and follows the rules that lead to life, without doing wrong, he will live. He will not die.
None of his past sins will be remembered. He has done what is right and fair, so he will live.'"
"But your people say, 'The Lord's way is not fair.' But it is their way that is not fair.
If a good person turns from doing right and does wrong, he will die for it.
But if a bad person turns from his wrong ways and does what is right and fair, he will live.
Still you say, 'The Lord's way is not fair.' But I will judge each of you by what you do, people of Israel."
In the twelfth year after we were taken from home, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a man who escaped from Jerusalem came to me. He said, "The city has been taken!"
The evening before he arrived, the LORD's power came on me. He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So I could speak again, and I was not silent anymore.
Then the LORD spoke to me.
He said, "Son of man, those who live in the ruined cities in the land of Israel are saying, 'Abraham was only one man, but he got the land. We are many, so the land is given to us to own.'"
"So tell them, 'This is what the Lord, the LORD says: You eat meat that still has blood in it. You look to your false gods. You kill people. Should you then own the land?
You trust in your swords. You do terrible things. Each of you has been with another man's wife. Should you then own the land?'

Tell them that this is what the Lord, the LORD says: 'As surely as I live, those in the ruined cities will be killed by the sword. Those in the open fields I will give to wild animals to eat. Those in the forts and caves will die of sickness.'"
"I will make the land empty and ruined. The pride in its power will end. The mountains of Israel will be empty, so no one will walk through them.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I make the land empty and ruined because of all the terrible things they did."
"As for you, Son of man, your people talk about you near the walls and at the doors of their houses. They say to one another, 'Come, let's hear the message that comes from the LORD.'"
"So they come to you like a crowd. They sit in front of you and hear your words, but they do not do them. They say sweet things with their mouths, but their hearts chase money.
To them, you are like a singer with a beautiful voice who plays music well. They hear your words, but they do not do them.
When all this happens—and it will happen—then they will know that a prophet was among them."
The LORD gave me a message.

"Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and say to them: This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: How terrible for the shepherds of Israel who only take care of themselves! Should not shepherds take care of the flock?
You eat the best food. You wear the wool. You kill the fat animals. But you do not feed the flock.

You have not helped the weak. You have not healed the sick. You have not tied up the hurt ones. You have not brought back the lost ones. You have not looked for the missing ones. You have ruled them with force and cruelty.
"So they were scattered because there was no shepherd. They became food for all the wild animals.
My sheep wandered on all the mountains and on every high hill. They were scattered all over the earth. No one looked for them. No one searched for them.
"So, you shepherds, listen to the word of the LORD:
As surely as I live, says the Lord, the LORD, My sheep became food for wild animals because no one led them. My shepherds did not look for them. They fed only themselves. They did not feed My sheep.
So, you shepherds, listen to the word of the LORD.

This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I am against the shepherds. I will take My sheep back from them. I will stop them from tending the flock, so they will not feed themselves anymore. I will rescue My sheep from their mouths. They will not be food for them anymore.
"For this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I Myself will search for My sheep and look after them.
As a shepherd looks after his scattered flock when he is with them, so will I look after My sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a cloudy and dark day.

I will bring them out from the nations. I will gather them from the countries. I will bring them into their own land. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in all the places where people live.
I will feed them in a good pasture. The high mountains of Israel will be their grazing land. There they will lie down in good grazing land. They will eat rich food on the mountains of Israel.
I Myself will feed My sheep and make them lie down, says the Lord, the LORD.
I will look for the lost ones and bring back the strays. I will tie up the hurt ones and make the weak ones strong. But I will destroy the fat and strong ones. I will shepherd them with fairness.
"As for you, My flock, this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: I will judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and goats.
Is it not enough for you to eat the good grass? Must you also trample the rest of the grass with your feet? Is it not enough for you to drink clean water? Must you also muddy the rest with your feet?
My sheep must eat what you have trampled. They must drink what you have muddied with your feet.
"So this is what the Lord, the LORD, says to them: I Myself will judge between the fat sheep and the thin sheep.
Because you push with your side and shoulder. You hit the weak sheep with your horns until you scatter them away.
I will save My flock. They will no longer be prey. I will judge between one sheep and another.
"I will place one shepherd over them. He will be My servant David. He will feed them. He will be their shepherd.
I, the LORD, will be their God. My servant David will be a leader among them. I, the LORD, have spoken.
"I will make an agreement of peace with them. I will remove dangerous animals from the land. Then they will live safely in the desert. They will sleep in the woods.
I will bless them and the places around My hill. I will send rain at the right time. The rains will be a blessing.

The trees will give fruit. The land will give crops. They will be safe in their land. They will know that I am the LORD when I break the heavy bars from their necks and save them from those who made them slaves.
They will no longer be prey for the nations. Wild animals will not eat them. They will live in safety, and no one will make them afraid.
I will give them a famous garden. They will not starve in the land. They will not be shamed by the nations anymore.
Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them. They are the people of Israel, My people, says the Lord, the LORD.
You are My sheep. You are the sheep I feed. You are My people, and I am your God, says the Lord, the LORD."
The LORD gave me a message.
He said, "Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and speak against it."
Then He said to Mount Seir, "This is what the Lord the LORD says: Look, I am against you, Mount Seir. I will reach out My hand against you. I will make you a wasteland.
I will wreck your cities. You will become a wasteland. Then you will know that I am the LORD. "
You have hated for a long time. You let Israel's people be killed by the sword when they were in trouble, at their final punishment.
So, as sure as I live, says the Lord the LORD, I will let you be killed. Killing will chase you. Because you did not hate killing, killing will chase you. "
I will make Mount Seir a wasteland, a total wasteland. I will stop anyone from passing through it or coming back.
I will fill its mountains with dead people. Those killed by the sword will fall on your hills, in your valleys, and in all your low places.
I will make you a lasting wasteland. Your cities will not be lived in. Then you will know that I am the LORD. "
Because you said these two nations and two lands would be yours, and that you would take them. But the LORD was there.
So, as sure as I live, says the Lord the LORD, I will deal with you the way your anger and jealousy led you to deal with them. I will make Myself known among them when I judge you. "
Then you will know that I, the LORD, heard all the mean things you said against the mountains of Israel. You said they were empty and given to you to eat.
You bragged against Me with your mouth. You said many things against Me. I heard it all. "
This is what the Lord the LORD says: While the whole earth is happy, I will make you a wasteland.
You were happy when Israel's land was empty. So I will do the same to you. You will become a wasteland, Mount Seir and all Edom, yes, all of it. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
"Son of man, speak to the mountains of Israel and tell them to listen to the word of the LORD.
The Lord the LORD says this: The enemy said about you that the old hills were theirs now.
"So speak for Me and say this: They ruined you and hurt you from all sides. You became a thing other nations took. People talked about you and made fun of you.

So, mountains of Israel, listen to the word of the Lord the LORD. The Lord the LORD says this to the mountains and hills, to the valleys and dry riverbeds, to the empty ruins and left-behind cities. They became things for other nations around to steal and laugh at.

"So the Lord the LORD says this: I spoke against the other nations in My hot anger. I spoke against Edom too. They took My land and were glad and mean about it. They thought its grasslands were theirs to steal.

So speak about the land of Israel. Say to the mountains and hills, to the valleys and dry riverbeds, that the Lord the LORD says this: Look, I spoke in My hot anger. I was angry because you took insults from the nations.
So the Lord the LORD says this: I raised My hand and made a promise. The nations around you will be ashamed.
"But you, mountains of Israel, will grow branches and fruit for My people Israel. They will come home soon.
Look, I am on your side. I will turn to you. You will be planted and grown.
"I will put many people on you. All Israel will live there. The cities will have people again, and the ruins will be built again.
I will put many people and animals on you. They will grow and have young. I will make you lived-in like before. I will make you do better than before. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
I will let My people Israel walk on you. They will own you. You will be their land to keep. You will not take their children from them anymore.
"The Lord the LORD says this: People say to you that you destroy people and take children from your nation.
So you will not destroy people or take children from your nation anymore, says the Lord the LORD.
I will not let other nations make fun of you. You will not be ashamed anymore. You will not make your nation fall, says the Lord the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me again. It said,
"Son of man, when Israel lived in their land, they made it dirty by how they acted. They were as unclean as a woman during her monthly time.
So I poured out My anger on them. They had spilled blood on the land. They had made it dirty with false gods.
I sent them to live among other nations. They spread out in many lands. I judged them for what they did.
"Wherever they went, they made My holy name look bad. People said that these are the LORD's people, but they had to leave His land.
But I cared about My holy name. Israel had made it look bad among the nations where they went.
"So tell Israel that the Lord the LORD says this: I am not doing this for you. I am doing it for My holy name. You made My name look bad among the nations where you went.

I will make My great name holy again. The nations made it look bad. You made it look bad too. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, says the Lord the LORD. They will see that I am holy because of you.
"I will take you out of the nations. I will gather you from all the lands. I will bring you back to your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water on you. You will be clean. I will wash you from all your dirt and all your false gods.
I will give you a new heart. I will put a new spirit in you. I will take out your hard heart of stone. I will give you a soft heart.
"I will put My Spirit in you. I will help you follow My rules and keep My laws.
Then you will live in the land I gave your fathers. You will be My people, and I will be your God.
"I will save you from all your dirt. I will call for the grain and make it grow. You will not go hungry again.
I will make the fruit trees and fields grow more. You will not be shamed by hunger in front of other nations.
Then you will remember your bad ways and your bad deeds. You will hate what you did because of your sins and wrong things.
"I am not doing this for you, says the Lord the LORD. Know this. Be ashamed and disgraced for your ways, Israel.
"The Lord the LORD says this: On the day I clean you from all your sins, I will let people live in the cities again. The ruins will be built again.
The empty land will be farmed. It will not stay empty for everyone to see.
"Then people will say that this empty land is now like the garden of Eden. The ruined, empty, broken cities are now strong and lived in.
"Then the nations around you that are left will know that I, the LORD, rebuilt what was broken. I planted again what was empty. I, the LORD, said it, and I will do it.
"The Lord the LORD says this: I will let Israel ask Me for this again. I will make their people grow like a flock of sheep.
Like the holy flock, like the flock in Jerusalem at its special feasts, the ruined cities will be full of people. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
The power of the LORD came on me. The LORD took me away by His Spirit and set me down in the middle of a valley. The valley was full of bones.
He led me all around them. I saw many, many bones on the ground in the valley. They were very dry.
He said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" I said, "Lord the LORD, You know."
He said, "Speak to these bones. Tell them: Dry bones, listen to what the LORD says!"
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will put My breath in you, and you will live.
I will put muscles and skin on you. I will cover you with skin. I will put My breath in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
I spoke as He told me. While I spoke, I heard a loud noise. The bones shook. They came together, bone to bone.
I looked. Muscles and flesh were on them. Skin covered them. But they had no breath.
He said, "Speak to the breath. Tell it: This is what the Lord the LORD says: Come from all four winds, breath, and breathe life into these dead people, so they will live."
So I spoke as He told me. Breath came into them. They lived. They stood on their feet. It was a huge army.
He said, "Son of man, these bones are all the people of Israel. They say their bones are dry. They say they have no hope. They say they are cut off."
He said, "Speak to them. This is what the Lord the LORD says: My people, I will open your graves. I will bring you up from your graves. I will bring you to the land of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the LORD. I will open your graves and bring you up from them. You are My people.
I will put My Spirit in you, and you will live. I will give you a home in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and done this, says the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,

"Son of man, take one stick. Write on it: For Judah and the people of Israel who are with him. Take another stick. Write on it: For Joseph. This is the stick of Ephraim and all the people of Israel who are with him.
Hold them together in your hand so they become one stick."
When your people ask you, "What does this mean?"

Say to them, "This is what the Lord the LORD says: I will take the stick of Joseph in Ephraim's hand and the tribes of Israel with him. I will put them with the stick of Judah. I will make them one stick. They will be one in My hand.
Hold the sticks you wrote on in your hand where they can see them."
"Tell them this is what the Lord the LORD says: I will take the people of Israel from the nations. I will gather them from all around. I will bring them to their own land.
I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will be king over all of them. They will not be two nations anymore. They will not be split into two kingdoms anymore.
They will not worship idols or do bad things or sin anymore. I will save them from the places where they sinned. I will make them clean. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
My servant David will be king over them. He will be the one shepherd for all of them. They will follow My rules and keep My laws.

"They will live in the land I gave to My servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They, their children, and their children's children will live there forever. My servant David will be their leader forever.
I will make a peace agreement with them. It will last forever. I will place them and make them grow. I will put My holy place among them forever.
My home will be with them. I will be their God, and they will be My people.
The nations will know that I am the LORD, who makes Israel holy. My holy place will be with them forever."
The LORD gave me a message.
"Man, turn your face toward Gog. He is from the land of Magog. He is the top leader of Meshech and Tubal. Speak against him.
Say, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: I am against you, Gog. You are the top leader of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around. I will put hooks in your jaws. I will bring you out with all your army. They will ride horses. They will wear full armor. They will carry shields and swords.
Persia, Cush, and Put will be with them. They will carry shields and wear helmets.
Gomer and all his troops will come. Beth Togarmah will come from the far north with all his troops. Many nations will be with you.
Get ready. Stay ready. You and all your troops must be ready. Be a guard for them.

After many days, you will be gathered. In the last years, you will go to a land that is safe again after war. Its people came from many nations. They live on the mountains of Israel. That land was empty for a long time. Now those people live there in safety.
You will come like a storm. You will cover the land like a cloud. Your troops and many nations will come with you.'"
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: On that day, you will think bad thoughts. You will plan something evil.
You will say, 'I will attack a land of open towns. I will attack quiet people who live in safety. They have no walls or gates.'

You will want to take their stuff and steal their things. You will attack places that were empty but now have people. Those people came from many nations. They have animals and goods. They live in the middle of the world.

"Sheba, Dedan, and the traders from Tarshish, and all their leaders, will say to you, 'Did you come to steal? Did you bring your troops to take things? Are you taking silver and gold, animals and goods? Are you taking a big prize?'"
"So, man, speak My words. Tell Gog, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: On that day, My people Israel will live in safety. Won't you know it?
You will come from your home in the far north. Many nations will come with you. They will ride horses. It will be a big, strong army.

You will come against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the last days, I will bring you to My land. Then the nations will know Me. Through you, Gog, I will show them that I am holy.'"
"This is what the Lord the LORD says: Are you the one I told about long ago? My servants, the prophets of Israel, said for many years that I would bring you against them.
But on that day, when Gog comes against Israel, the Lord the LORD says My anger will rise.
Because I am jealous and very angry, I say there will be a big earthquake in Israel.

Fish, birds, wild animals, and all small animals on the ground will shake because of Me. All people on earth will shake too. Mountains will fall. High rocks will fall. Every wall will fall to the ground.
I will bring war against Gog on all My mountains, says the Lord the LORD. Each man will fight his brother with a sword.
I will judge him with sickness and bloodshed. I will rain on him, his troops, and the nations with him. I will send heavy rain, hail, fire, and burning rock.
So I will show how great and holy I am. Many nations will know Me. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
You, son of man, tell what will happen to Gog. Say, “This is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Look, I am against you, Gog, leader of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around. I will lead you. I will bring you up from the far north. I will bring you against the mountains of Israel.
