Then I will knock the bow out of your left hand. I will knock the arrows out of your right hand.
You will fall on the mountains of Israel. You and all your troops and the people with you will fall. I will give you to the birds and wild animals to eat.
You will fall in the open field. I have said it, says the Lord, the LORD.
I will send fire on Magog and on people who live safely on the islands. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
I will make My holy name known among My people Israel. I will not let My holy name be shamed again. The nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
It is coming. It will happen, says the Lord, the LORD. This is the day I spoke about.

Then people who live in the cities of Israel will go out. They will gather the weapons and burn them. They will burn shields, small shields, bows, arrows, clubs, and spears. They will burn them for seven years.
They will not gather wood from the fields or cut wood from the forests. They will burn the weapons. They will take back what was taken from them. They will rob the robbers, says the Lord, the LORD.

On that day I will give Gog a grave in Israel. It will be in the valley where travelers pass, east of the sea. It will block the path. There they will bury Gog and all his army. They will call that place the Valley of Gog's Army.
The people of Israel will bury them. It will take seven months to make the land clean.
All the people of the land will help bury them. That day will bring Me honor, says the Lord, the LORD.
Men will be chosen to walk through the land all the time. They will bury the bodies left on the ground to make the land clean. After seven months, they will search for more.
When they walk through the land, if someone sees a bone, he will put a marker next to it. Then the buriers will bury it in the Valley of Gog's Army.
There will also be a city called Hamonah. In this way they will make the land clean.

You, son of man, this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Tell every bird and wild animal, “Gather around for the big sacrifice I am making for you on the mountains of Israel. You will eat meat and drink blood.”
You will eat the meat of strong men. You will drink the blood of the leaders of the land. You will eat rams, lambs, goats, and bulls. All of them are fat animals from Bashan.
You will eat fat until you are full. You will drink blood until you are drunk. This is from My sacrifice that I made for you.
You will be full at My table with horses and chariots, with strong men and all kinds of soldiers, says the Lord, the LORD.
I will show My glory among the nations. All the nations will see My punishment that I gave. They will see My hand that I put on them.
From that day on, the people of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.
The nations will know that the people of Israel were taken away because of their sin. They turned against Me. So I hid My face from them. I gave them to their enemies, and they all died by the sword.
I did this because of their unclean ways and their sins. I hid My face from them.
So this is what the Lord, the LORD, says: Now I will bring back Israel's people. I will be kind to all the people of Israel. I will care about My holy name.
They will forget their shame and all the wrong they did against Me. They will live safely in their own land. No one will scare them.
I will bring them back from the nations. I will gather them from the lands of their enemies. I will show Myself holy through them in front of many nations.
Then they will know that I am the LORD their God. I brought them to their own land. I did not leave any of them among the nations.
I will not hide My face from them anymore. I will pour out My Spirit on the people of Israel, says the Lord, the LORD.

It was twenty-five years after we were taken away. It was the start of the year, on the tenth day of the month. It was fourteen years after the city fell. On that day, the LORD's power came on me. He brought me there.
In visions from God, He brought me to Israel. He set me on a very high mountain in the south. There was something like a city there.
He brought me there. I saw a man who looked like bronze. He stood at the gate. He had a linen cord and a measuring rod.

The man said to me, “Son of man, look with your eyes. Listen with your ears. Pay attention to all I show you. I brought you here so I can show you these things. Tell the people of Israel all that you see.”
I saw a wall around the house. The man had a measuring rod six cubits long. A cubit is about 18 inches. He measured the wall. It was one rod thick and one rod high.
He went to the east gate. He walked up its steps. He measured the doorstep. It was one rod wide. He measured the other doorstep. It was one rod wide too.
Each side room was one rod long and one rod wide. The space between side rooms was five cubits. The porch that faced inside had a doorstep one rod wide.
He measured the porch from inside. It was one rod.
The porch was eight cubits long. Its door posts were two cubits. The porch faced the house.
The east gate had three side rooms on each side. They were all the same size. The door posts on both sides were the same size too.
He measured the gate opening. It was ten cubits wide. The gate was thirteen cubits long.
In front of the side rooms was a low wall one cubit high. Each side room was six cubits across. The low wall on the other side was one cubit high too.
He measured the gate from roof to roof of the side rooms. It was twenty-five cubits wide. One door faced the other door.
The door posts were sixty cubits high. The yard reached the gate all around.
The porch at the inside gate was fifty cubits long.
The side rooms and door posts had windows all around. The porch had windows all around inside. Palm trees were on the door posts.
He brought me to the outer yard. I saw a stone floor all around. There were thirty rooms on the floor.
The floor was next to the gates. It was as long as the gates. It was the lower floor.
He measured from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner yard. It was one hundred cubits to the east and to the north.
There was a gate on the north side of the outer yard. He measured its length and width.
It had three side rooms on each side. Its door posts and porch were like the first gate. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, porch, and palm trees were like the east gate. Seven steps led up to it. The porch was in front of them.
The inner yard had a gate facing the north gate and the east gate. It was one hundred cubits from gate to gate.
He led me south. I saw a south gate. He measured its door posts and porch. They were like the others.
It had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Seven steps led up to it. Its porch was in front. Palm trees were on its door posts, one on each side.
The inner yard had a south gate. It was one hundred cubits from gate to gate.
He brought me to the inner yard through the south gate. He measured the south gate. It was like the others.
Its side rooms, door posts, and porch were like the others. It had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
There were porches all around. They were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
Its porch faced the outer yard. Palm trees were on its door posts. Eight steps led up to it.
He brought me to the east gate of the inner yard. He measured it. It was like the others.
Its side rooms, door posts, and porch were like the others. It had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its porch faced the outer yard. Palm trees were on its door posts, one on each side. Eight steps led up to it.
He brought me to the north gate. He measured it. It was like the others.
Its side rooms, door posts, and porch were like the others. It had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its door posts faced the outer yard. Palm trees were on them, one on each side. Eight steps led up to it.
There was a room by the door posts of the gate. There they washed the burnt offering.
In the porch of the gate there were two tables on each side. On them they killed the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
Outside the porch, on the north side, there were two tables. On the other side of the porch there were two more tables.
So there were four tables on one side and four on the other. That made eight tables. They killed the sacrifices on them.
There were four tables of cut stone for the burnt offering. Each was one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one cubit high. They put the tools on them.
Hooks about three inches long were fastened around. The meat of the offering was put on the tables.
Outside the inner gate were rooms for singers. One was on the north side, facing south. The other was on the south side, facing north.
The man said to me, “The room that faces south is for the priests who take care of the temple.
The room that faces north is for the priests who take care of the altar. These priests are sons of Zadok. They are Levites who come near the LORD to serve Him.”
He measured the yard. It was one hundred cubits square. The altar was in front of the house.
He brought me to the porch of the house. He measured the porch. It was five cubits on each side. The gate was three cubits wide on each side.
The porch was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide. Steps led up to it. There were pillars by the door posts, one on each side.
Then the man brought me to the outer room. He measured the door posts. The door was six cubits wide on each side.
The door was ten cubits wide. The sides of the door were five cubits wide on each side. He measured the outer room. It was forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
Then he went into the inner room. He measured the door posts. They were two cubits wide. The door was six cubits wide. The opening was seven cubits wide.
He measured the inner room. It was twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. It was across from the outer room. He said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
He measured the wall of the temple. It was six cubits thick. The side rooms around the temple were four cubits wide.
The side rooms were in three floors. There were thirty rooms on each floor. There were ledges around the temple wall. They held up the side rooms. They were not fastened into the temple wall.
The side rooms got wider on each higher floor. The building around the temple got wider as it went up. A stairway went from the lowest floor to the top floor through the middle floor.
I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it. This base held up the side rooms. It was six cubits high.
The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick. The open space between the side rooms of the temple and the outer rooms was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
This open space was all around the temple.
The side rooms had a door on the north and a door on the south. The open space was five cubits wide all around.
The building facing the separate area on the west was seventy cubits wide. Its wall was five cubits thick all around. It was ninety cubits long.
He measured the temple. It was one hundred cubits long. The separate area, the building, and its walls were also one hundred cubits long.
The front of the temple and the separate area on the east were one hundred cubits wide.
He measured the building facing the separate area on the west. It was one hundred cubits long, with porches on each side. The inner room and the porches of the court were measured too.
The doorways, the windows, and the porches around all three were covered with wood. The floor was wood from the doorway to the windows. The windows were covered.
Above the door, all the way to the inner room, and on the outside and on all the walls, inside and outside, there were measurements.
It was carved with cherubim and palm trees. A palm tree was between each cherub. Each cherub had two faces.
One face was a man’s face. It looked toward the palm tree on one side. The other face was a lion’s face. It looked toward the palm tree on the other side. This carving went all around the temple.
From the floor to above the door, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the temple wall.
The outer room had a square doorframe. The front of the Most Holy Place looked the same.
The altar was made of wood. It was three cubits high and two cubits square. It had corners, a base, and sides made of wood. He said to me, “This is the table that is before the the LORD.”
The outer room and the Most Holy Place had double doors.
Each door had two parts. There were two swinging doors for each. There were two doors for one side and two for the other.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the outer room, like those on the walls. There was a wooden cover over the front of the porch outside.
There were windows and palm trees on both sides of the porch. The side rooms of the temple had overhangs.
He took me out through the north way to the outer yard. He brought me to a room. It was across from the special place and across from the building on the north side.
The front of the north door was 100 cubits long. It was 50 cubits wide.
Rooms faced rooms on three levels. They were across from the twenty cubits of the inner yard. They were across from the stone floor of the outer yard. There were covered walks, one above another.
In front of the rooms was a walk. It was ten cubits wide. It went to the inner yard. Their doors faced north.
The top rooms were shorter. The covered walks took space from them. They took space from the middle and bottom rooms too.
The rooms were on three levels, like pillars in the yards. But there were no pillars. So the top rooms were smaller than the lower and middle rooms.
Outside, a wall stood in front of the rooms. It was fifty cubits long. It ran beside the rooms toward the outer yard.
The rooms on the outer yard side were fifty cubits long. The building was one hundred cubits long in front of them.
Below these rooms was a door. It was on the east side. People used it to enter from the outer yard.
On the east side, the wall of the yard had rooms. They were across from the special place and across from the building.
There was a walk in front of them. It looked like the rooms on the north side. They were as long and as wide. Their doors and rules were the same.
The south rooms had doors like the north rooms. There was a door at the start of the walk. The walk was in front of the wall. People entered from the east.

He said to me, "The north and south rooms across from the special place are holy rooms. The priests who are close to the LORD will eat the holy food there. They will put the holiest offerings there. They are the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. This place is holy."

When the priests go in, they must not go out to the outer yard in their holy clothes. They must leave those clothes there, because they are holy. They must put on other clothes before they go near the people.
He finished measuring the inner house. Then he brought me out through the east gate. He measured all around.
He measured the east side with a measuring reed. It was 500 reeds long.
He measured the north side. It was 500 reeds long.
He measured the south side. It was 500 reeds long.
He measured the west side. It was 500 reeds long.
He measured all four sides. There was a wall around it. It was 500 reeds long and 500 reeds wide. It separated the holy place from the common place.
He led me to the gate that faces east.
I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the sound of many waters. The earth shone with His glory.
It looked like the vision I saw when He came to destroy the city. It also looked like what I saw by the Kebar River. So I fell on my face.
The glory of the the LORD came into the temple through the east gate.
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court. The glory of the the LORD filled the temple.
A man stood beside me. I heard someone speak to me from the temple.

He said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place where My feet rest. I will live here among the people of Israel forever. The house of Israel and their kings will no longer make My holy name unclean by their unfaithful ways or by the dead bodies of their kings on their hilltop altars.

When they put their doorstep next to My doorstep, and their door frame next to My door frame, with only a wall between us, they made My holy name unclean by the bad things they did. So I destroyed them in My anger.
Now let them put their unfaithful ways and the dead bodies of their kings far from Me. Then I will live among them forever.
"You, son of man, tell the people of Israel about this temple. Then they will be ashamed of their sins. Let them measure its plan.

If they are ashamed of everything they have done, then show them the design of the temple. Show them its exits and entrances. Show them all its shapes and rules. Write it down where they can see it. Then they will keep all its rules and do them.
This is the law of the temple: The whole area around it on top of the mountain is most holy. Yes, this is the law of the temple."

These are the measurements of the altar in cubits. One cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth. The gutter is one cubit deep and one cubit wide. It has a rim one span wide around its edge. This is the height of the altar.
From the gutter on the ground to the lower ledge is two cubits. The ledge is one cubit wide. From the lower ledge to the upper ledge is four cubits. That ledge is one cubit wide.
The top of the altar is four cubits high. Four horns stick up from it.
The top is square. It is twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.
The ledge around it is also square. It is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide. It has a rim half a cubit wide all around. Its gutter is one cubit wide all around. Its steps face east.
He said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord the LORD says: These are the rules for the altar on the day it is built. Offer burnt offerings on it, and sprinkle blood on it.
Give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levite priests from Zadok's family who come near to serve Me, says the Lord the LORD.
Take some of the blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the border. This will clean the altar and pay for its sin.
Take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the place set aside for the temple, outside the holy place.
"On the second day, offer a male goat with no flaws as a sin offering. Clean the altar the same way it was cleaned with the bull.
When the cleaning is finished, offer a young bull and a ram from the flock. Both must have no flaws.
Bring them to the the LORD. The priests will throw salt on them and offer them as a burnt offering to the the LORD.
"For seven days, make a goat as a sin offering each day. Also offer a young bull and a ram from the flock. Both must have no flaws.
For seven days, the priests will pay for the altar's sin, clean it, and set it apart for God.
When the days are over, on the eighth day and after that, the priests may offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar. Then I will accept you, declares the Lord the LORD."
He brought me back to the outer gate of God's holy place. It faced east. The gate was shut.
The LORD said to me, "This gate will stay shut. It must not be opened. No one may come in through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, came in through it. So it must stay shut.
Only the leader may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He will come in through the porch of the gate and go out the same way."
He brought me to the front of God's house by the north gate. I looked and saw the LORD's bright glory fill God's house. I fell face down.

The LORD said to me, "Person, pay attention. Look closely with your eyes. Listen closely with your ears to everything I say to you. Remember all the rules and laws of the LORD's house. Pay close attention to the way in and the ways out of God's house.
Tell the stubborn people of Israel, 'This is what the Lord the LORD says: You have done enough bad things, people of Israel.

You let people from other lands come in. They do not follow God in their hearts or bodies. They made My house not holy. You gave Me fat and blood as offerings. You broke My promise with all your bad things.
You did not take care of My holy things. You let other people take care of My holy place for you.'
The Lord the LORD says, 'No person from another land may come into My holy place. Not even one who lives with Israel's people. No one whose heart and body are not right with Me may come in.'"
The Levites who left Me when Israel went the wrong way will pay for their sin. They left Me to follow false gods.

But they will still work in My holy place. They will guard the gates of God's house and work there. They will prepare the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people. They will stand and help the people.
They served false gods. They caused Israel to sin. So I made a serious promise that they will pay for their sin, says the Lord the LORD.
They must not come near Me to be priests. They must not come near My holy things or the most holy things. They will carry their shame and their bad sins.
But I will put them in charge of all the work in God's house and everything done there.

But the priests who are Levites and come from Zadok's family stayed faithful. They took care of My holy place when Israel went the wrong way. They may come near to serve Me. They will stand before Me and give Me fat and blood offerings, says the Lord the LORD.
Only they may come into My holy place. Only they may come to My table to serve Me. They will do what I ask.
When they come into the inner court, they must wear linen clothes. They must not wear wool when they work at the inner gates or inside God's house.
They must wear linen hats on their heads and linen underclothes around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them sweat.

When they go out to the outer court to be with the people, they must take off those clothes. They must leave them in the holy rooms and put on other clothes. Then they will not make the people holy with their clothes.
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long. They must trim their hair neatly.
No priest may drink wine when he goes into the inner court.
They must not marry a woman whose husband died or a divorced woman. They must marry a woman who has never been married, from Israel's people. Or they may marry the widow of a priest.
They must teach My people the difference between what is holy and what is not holy. They must show them the difference between what is clean and what is not clean.
When people do not agree, the priests must judge them. They must judge by My rules. They must keep My laws and My rules for all My special days. They must keep My Sabbaths holy.
A priest must not make himself unclean by going near a dead person. But he may do so for his father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or sister who never married.
After he is clean again, he must wait seven days.
On the day he goes into the holy place, into the inner court, to serve there, he must bring a sin offering, says the Lord the LORD.
I am what they receive from Me. Do not give them land in Israel, because I am their land.
They will eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. Everything in Israel given to the LORD will belong to them.
The best of all first crops and every gift from all your offerings will belong to the priests. You must also give the priests the first of your dough, so a blessing may rest on your house.
The priests must not eat any animal that was found dead or torn by wild animals.

When you divide the land for your families, you must give a special gift to the LORD. It will be a holy part of the land. It will be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. It will be holy all around.
From this, a square piece 500 by 500 cubits will be for the holy place. There will be 50 cubits of open land around it.
From this measured land, measure 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. The holy place and the Most Holy Place will be there.
This holy part of the land will be for the priests who serve in the holy place and come near to serve the LORD. It will be a place for their homes and a holy space for the temple.
An area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide will be for the Levites who serve in the temple. It will be their land, with twenty rooms.
You will give the city land 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, next to the holy part. It will be for all the people of Israel.
The prince will have land on both sides of the holy part and the city land. One part will reach the west edge, and the other will reach the east edge. Both will run the full length from west to east.
This land in Israel will be his. My princes will not treat My people badly anymore. They will share the land with the people of Israel by their tribes.
This is what the Lord GOD says: “Enough, princes of Israel! Stop hurting people and stealing. Do what is right and fair. Stop taking land from My people, declares the Lord GOD.”
You must use fair scales, fair ephahs, and fair baths.
The ephah and the bath must be the same size. The bath is one tenth of a homer. The ephah is one tenth of a homer. Their size will follow the homer.
The shekel will be twenty gerahs. Your mina will be sixty shekels: twenty, twenty-five, and fifteen.
This is the gift you will give: one sixth of an ephah from a homer of wheat, and one sixth of an ephah from a homer of barley.
The rule for oil is this: give one tenth of a bath for each cor. A cor is ten baths.

Give one sheep from every two hundred sheep from Israel's good fields. This is for the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering. It will help make things right for the people, says the Lord GOD.
All the people of the land will give this gift to the prince in Israel.

The prince will give the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the drink offerings at the feasts, the new moons, the Sabbath days, and all the special days of the people of Israel. He will give the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering to help make things right for the people of Israel.
This is what the Lord GOD says: “On the first day of the first month, take a young bull with no bad spot. Use it to clean the holy place.”
The priest will take some blood from the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the altar court, and on the doorposts of the inner gate.
You will do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins by mistake or without knowing. This will help make things right for the temple.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, you will have the Passover. It is a feast of seven days. People will eat bread with no yeast.
On that day, the prince will give a bull for himself and for all the people as a sin offering.
For the seven days of the feast, he will give seven bulls and seven rams with no bad spots each day as a burnt offering to the LORD. He will also give a male goat each day as a sin offering.
He will give a grain offering: one ephah for the bull, one ephah for the ram, and one hin of oil for each ephah.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, at the feast, he will do the same for seven days. He will give the sin offering, the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the oil.
The Lord the LORD says, "The inner gate that faces east must stay shut on the six work days. But it must be open on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon."

The prince comes in from outside through the porch of the gate. He stands by the gatepost. The priests get his burnt offering and his peace offerings ready. He bows down at the doorstep of the gate. Then he goes out. The gate stays open until evening.
On the Sabbath days and on the New Moons, the people of the land bow down before the LORD at the door of that gate.
On the Sabbath day, the prince gives the LORD a burnt offering. It is six lambs without a mark and one ram without a mark.
He gives a grain offering with it. He gives an ephah of grain for the ram. For the lambs, he gives as much as he can. He also gives a hin of oil for each ephah.
On the day of the New Moon, he gives a young bull without a mark, six lambs, and a ram. They must have no mark.
He gives a grain offering with them. He gives an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram. For the lambs, he gives as much as he can. He also gives a hin of oil for each ephah.
When the prince comes in, he comes through the porch of the gate. He goes out the same way.

When the people come before the LORD at the special times, the one who comes in by the north gate goes out by the south gate. The one who comes in by the south gate goes out by the north gate. No one goes back out the same gate. They go out by the other gate.
The prince is with them. When they come in, he comes in. When they go out, he goes out.
At the feasts and special times, the grain offering is an ephah for a bull, an ephah for a ram, and as much as he can for the lambs. He also gives a hin of oil for each ephah.

When the prince gives a free gift to the LORD, a burnt offering or peace offerings, the east gate is opened for him. He gives his burnt offering and his peace offerings the same way he does on the Sabbath day. Then he goes out. After he goes out, the gate is shut.
You shall give a lamb one year old without a mark as a burnt offering to the LORD every morning. You shall give it every morning.

And you shall get a grain offering ready with it every morning. It is one sixth of an ephah of fine flour. It is one third of a hin of oil to wet the fine flour. It is a grain offering to the LORD. This rule lasts forever.
They get the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil ready every morning. It is a regular burnt offering.
The Lord the LORD says, "If the prince gives a gift of land to one of his sons, it is his land. It belongs to his sons. It is their land to keep.
But if he gives a gift of land from his family land to one of his servants, it is his until the year of freedom. Then it goes back to the prince. But the family land belongs to his sons.
The prince must not take any of the people's land to push them out. He must give his sons land from his own land, so that none of My people are scattered from their land."
He brought me through the entrance by the side of the gate to the holy rooms for the priests. They faced north. There was a place at the far west end.

He said to me, "This is the place where the priests boil the guilt offering and the sin offering. They bake the grain offering here. They do not take them out to the outer court, so the people are not made holy."
He brought me out to the outer court. He led me past the four corners of the court. There was a small court in each corner.
In the four corners of the outer court were closed-in courts. They were 40 cubits long and 30 cubits wide. All four were the same size.
A wall went around all four. Cooking places were built under the walls all around.
He said to me, "These are the kitchens. The temple workers boil the people's sacrifices here."
He brought me back to the door of the house. I saw water coming out from under the door. It flowed east. The house faced east. The water ran down from the right side of the house, south of the altar.
He led me out by the north gate and around to the outside gate that faces east. Water was trickling from the right side.
The man went east. He had a measuring line in his hand. He measured one thousand cubits. Then he led me through the water. It was up to my ankles.
He measured another thousand and led me through the water. It was up to my knees. He measured another thousand and led me through the water. It was up to my waist.
He measured another thousand. It was a river I could not cross. The water was too deep. I would have to swim. No one could cross it.
He said to me, "Son of man, do you see this?" Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
When I got back, I saw many trees on both sides of the river.
He said to me, "This water flows to the east country. It goes down to the Arabah. It enters the sea. When it reaches the sea, the water will be healed.
Wherever the river flows, living things will live. There will be many fish. The water that comes there makes things well. Everything will live where the river goes.
"Men will fish by the sea. They will stand from En-gedi to En-eglaim. They will spread nets. The fish will be many kinds, like the fish of the great sea.
But the swamps and marshes will not be healed. They will be left for salt.

By the river, on both sides, trees will grow for food. Their leaves will not dry up. Their fruit will not stop. They will make new fruit every month, because the water comes from the holy place. The fruit will be for food. The leaves will be for healing."
The Lord the LORD says this: "This is the border of the land you will take for the twelve tribes of Israel. Joseph will get two parts.
You will share it equally. I promised to give it to your fathers. This land will be yours.
"Here is the north border. It goes from the great sea by the road to Lebo-hamath, to Zedad.
It goes through Hamath, Berothah, and Sibraim, between Damascus and Hamath. It reaches Hazar-hatticon by the border of Hauran.
So the border goes from the sea to Hazar-enan, north of Damascus and Hamath. This is the north side.
"On the east side, the border runs from between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan, between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the eastern sea. Measure this to the east.
On the south side, it goes from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, along the Brook of Egypt, to the great sea. This is the south side.
On the west side, it is the great sea, from the border to across from Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
"Divide this land among the tribes of Israel.
Share it for your own and for the strangers who live among you and have children. Treat them like people born in Israel. They will share the land with you among the tribes of Israel.
Give the stranger his share in the tribe where he lives," says the Lord the LORD.

These are the names of the tribes. Dan will get one share. It will be on the far north side, by the road to Hethlon, up to the way into Hamath, and as far as Hazar Enan, near the border of Damascus and Hamath. It will run from the east side to the west side.
Asher will get one share next to Dan's border, from east to west.
Naphtali will get one share next to Asher's border, from east to west.
Manasseh will get one share next to Naphtali's border, from east to west.
Ephraim will get one share next to Manasseh's border, from east to west.
Reuben will get one share next to Ephraim's border, from east to west.
Judah will get one share next to Reuben's border, from east to west.

Next to Judah's border, from east to west, will be the special land you set apart. It will be 25,000 wide and as long as one share. It will run from the east side to the west side. The holy place will be in the middle.
The special land you set apart for the the LORD will be 25,000 long and 10,000 wide.

This holy land will be for the priests. It will be 25,000 long on the north side, 10,000 wide on the west side, 10,000 wide on the east side, and 25,000 long on the south side. The the LORD's holy place will be in the middle.
It will be for the priests who are set apart from Zadok's sons. They kept My rules. They did not go wrong like the Levites did when Israel went wrong.
This very holy land set apart for them will be next to the Levites' land.
Next to the priests' land, the Levites will get a share. It will be 25,000 long and 10,000 wide. The whole length will be 25,000. The width will be 10,000.
They must not sell or trade any of it. They must not give away this special part of the land, because it is holy to the the LORD.
The rest of the land will be 5,000 wide and 25,000 long. It will be common land for the city. It will be for homes and open fields. The city will be in the middle.
The city will measure 4,500 on the north side, 4,500 on the south side, 4,500 on the east side, and 4,500 on the west side.
The city's open fields will reach 250 to the north, 250 to the south, 250 to the east, and 250 to the west.
The rest of the land next to the holy land will run east and west. It will be 10,000 on each side. Its crops will give food to the city workers.
The city workers will farm it. They will come from all the tribes of Israel.
The whole piece will be a square. It will be 25,000 by 25,000. You are to set apart the holy land, along with the city's land.

The rest of the land on both sides of the holy land and the city's land will belong to the ruler. It will go east from the 25,000 of the holy land to the east border. It will go west from the 25,000 to the west border. The holy land and the temple will be in the middle.
So the Levites' land and the city's land will be in the middle of the ruler's land. The ruler's land will be between Judah's border and Benjamin's border.
The rest of the tribes: Benjamin will get one share, from east to west.
Simeon will get one share next to Benjamin's border, from east to west.
Issachar will get one share next to Simeon's border, from east to west.
Zebulun will get one share next to Issachar's border, from east to west.
Gad will get one share next to Zebulun's border, from east to west.
Along Gad's border, from east to west, will be the south part. It will reach from Tamar to the waters of Meribah Kadesh, then to the Brook of Egypt and the Great Sea.
This is the land you will give to the tribes of Israel as their share. These are their parts, says the Lord the LORD.
These are the city's exits. On the north side, it will be 4,500 long.
There will be three gates on the north side. They are the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
On the east side, it will be 4,500 long. There will be three gates. They are the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
On the south side, it will be 4,500 long. There will be three gates. They are the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
On the west side, it will be 4,500 long. There will be three gates. They are the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The city will measure 18,000 all around. From that day on, the name of the city will be: The LORD Is There.
In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to Jerusalem. He surrounded the city and attacked it.
The Lord let him take King Jehoiakim of Judah. He also took some things from God's house. He carried them to the land of Shinar, to his god's house, and put them in his god's treasure room.
Then the king told Ashpenaz, his top helper, to bring some people of Israel. He wanted boys from the king's family and from important families.

They had to be young men with no marks on them. They had to look good. They had to be smart in all kinds of learning. They had to know things and understand things. They had to be strong enough to serve in the king's palace. They also had to learn the books and language of the Chaldeans.
The king gave them food from his own table each day. He also gave them the wine he drank. They were to learn for three years. After that, they would stand before the king.
Some of these young men were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. They were from Judah.
The top helper gave them new names. He called Daniel Belteshazzar. He called Hananiah Shadrach. He called Mishael Meshach. He called Azariah Abednego.
But Daniel decided in his heart that he would not make himself unclean with the king's food or wine. So he asked the top helper to let him not make himself unclean.
God helped Daniel. He made the top helper kind and caring toward Daniel.

The top helper said to Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king. He gave you your food and your drink. Why should he see you looking weak? You might look worse than the young men your age. Then I could be in trouble with the king."
Then Daniel said to the helper that the top helper had put over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
"Please test us, your servants, for ten days. Give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then look at us and at the young men who eat the king's food. After that, do with us, your servants, what you think is best."
The helper listened to them about this. He tested them for ten days.
After ten days, they looked better and stronger than all the young men who ate the king's food.
So the helper took away the king's food and wine. He gave them vegetables instead.
God gave these four young men learning and skill in all books and wisdom. Daniel could understand all visions and dreams.
At the end of the time the king had set, the top helper brought them to King Nebuchadnezzar.
The king talked with them. No one was like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they stood before the king.
In every question about wisdom and understanding, the king found them ten times better than all the magicians and wise men in his whole kingdom.
Daniel stayed there until the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's rule, he had dreams. His spirit was upset, and he could not sleep.
The king called for the wise men, the magicians, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans. He wanted them to tell him his dreams. They came and stood before the king.
The king said, "I had a dream. My spirit is upset. I want to know what it means."
The Chaldeans answered the king, "O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will explain it."
The king answered the Chaldeans, "This is my decision. If you do not tell me the dream and what it means, I will have you cut into pieces. I will make your houses into piles of rubble.
But if you tell me the dream and what it means, I will give you gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and what it means."
They answered again, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain it."
The king answered, "I know for sure that you are trying to get more time. You see that I have made my decision.

If you do not tell me the dream and what it means, there is only one law for you. You have agreed to tell me lies and bad things until things change. So tell me the dream and what it means. Then I will know you can explain it."
The Chaldeans answered the king, "No one on earth can do what the king asks. No great and powerful king has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
What the king asks is too hard. No one can show it to the king except the gods. But they do not live with people."
Because of this, the king became very angry. He ordered that all the wise men of Babylon be killed.
The law went out. The wise men were to be killed. Men looked for Daniel and his friends to kill them too.
Then Daniel spoke wisely and carefully to Arioch, the king's captain. Arioch had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel asked Arioch, "Why did the king make such a harsh law?" Then Arioch told Daniel what had happened.
Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time. Then he would tell the king the dream and what it means.
Daniel went home. He told his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what had happened.
He asked them to pray for mercy from the God of heaven. They prayed so that Daniel and his friends would not die with the other wise men of Babylon.
During the night, the secret was shown to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel praised the God of heaven.
Daniel said, "Praise be to God's name forever and ever! Wisdom and power belong to Him.
He changes times and seasons. He removes kings and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to wise people. He gives knowledge to people who understand.
"He shows deep and hidden things. He knows what is in the dark. Light lives with Him.
"I thank You and praise You, God of my fathers. You gave me wisdom and power. Now You have told me what we asked of You. You have shown us the king's problem."

Then Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had chosen to kill the wise men of Babylon. Daniel said, "Do not kill the wise men of Babylon. Take me to the king. I will tell the king what the dream means."
Arioch quickly took Daniel to the king. He said, "I found a man from the captives of Judah. He can tell the king what the dream means."
The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Can you tell me the dream I saw and what it means?"
Daniel answered the king, "No wise man, magician, or reader of dreams can tell the king this secret.
But there is a God in heaven who shows secrets. He has told King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the last days. This is your dream. These are the visions you saw while you were in bed.
"As you lay in bed, O king, your thoughts turned to what will happen after this. The One who shows secrets has told you what will happen.
"This secret was shown to me, but not because I am wiser than anyone else. It was shown so that you, O king, may know what it means. Then you will know the thoughts of your heart.
"You, O king, were looking. You saw a huge statue. It was very big and bright. It stood in front of you. It looked scary.
The head of the statue was pure gold. Its chest and arms were silver. Its belly and thighs were bronze.
Its legs were iron. Its feet were part iron and part clay.
While you watched, a stone was cut out, but not by human hands. It hit the statue on its feet of iron and clay. It broke them.

Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were crushed together. They became like dust on a summer field. The wind blew them away. No one could find them again. But the stone that hit the statue became a huge mountain. It filled the whole earth.
"This is the dream. Now I will tell you what it means.
"You, O king, are the greatest king. The God of heaven gave you a kingdom, power, strength, and honor.
He gave you power over people, animals, and birds. He made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.
After you, another kingdom will rise. It will not be as strong as yours. Then a third kingdom, made of bronze, will rule over all the earth.
The fourth kingdom will be strong like iron. Iron breaks and crushes everything. Like iron, it will break and crush all these kingdoms.
"You saw the feet and toes. Some were clay and some were iron. This means the kingdom will be divided. It will have some of the strength of iron, because you saw iron mixed with clay.
The toes were part iron and part clay. So this kingdom will be partly strong and partly weak.
You saw iron mixed with clay. People will try to join together by marriage, but they will not stay together. Iron does not mix with clay.
"In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed. No other people will take it. It will crush and end all these kingdoms. It will stand forever.

You saw a stone cut from a mountain, but not by human hands. It crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God has shown the king what will happen after this. The dream is true, and its meaning can be trusted."
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face. He worshiped Daniel. He ordered that an offering and incense be brought for him.
The king said to Daniel, "Truly, your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings. He shows secrets. That is why you could show this secret."
Then the king gave Daniel a high position. He gave him many great gifts. He made him ruler over all of Babylon. He made him chief over all the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel asked the king, and the king put Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in charge of the work of Babylon. But Daniel stayed at the king's gate.
King Nebuchadnezzar made a gold statue. It was about 90 feet tall and 9 feet wide. He set it up in the flat land of Dura in Babylon.

King Nebuchadnezzar sent for all the leaders in his land. He wanted the top leaders, bosses, governors, helpers, money keepers, judges, and all other officials. They were to come to the special day for the statue.
All these leaders came. They stood in front of the statue.
A man shouted, "Listen, all you people, nations, and languages!
When you hear horns, flutes, harps, and all kinds of music, you must fall down. You must worship the gold statue that the king set up.
Anyone who does not fall down and worship will be thrown right away into a hot, burning fire."
So when all the people heard the music, they fell down. They worshiped the gold statue.
Then some Babylonian men came forward. They accused the Jewish men.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "Long live the king!
You, O king, made a rule. You said that every person who hears the music must fall down and worship the gold statue.
You also said that anyone who does not fall down and worship will be thrown into the hot fire.

There are some Jewish men you put in charge of Babylon. Their names are Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men do not listen to you, O king. They do not serve your gods. They do not worship your gold statue."
Then King Nebuchadnezzar became very angry. He ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought to him. They brought the men to the king.
Nebuchadnezzar said to them, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is it true that you do not serve my gods? Is it true that you do not worship the gold statue I set up?

Now, when you hear the music, be ready to fall down and worship the statue I made. If you do, all is well. But if you do not, you will be thrown into the hot fire. And what god can save you from my hand?"
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, "O King Nebuchadnezzar, we do not need to answer you about this.
If our God can save us from the hot fire and from your hand, O king, He will save us.
But if He does not, you must know this, O king: We will not serve your gods. We will not worship your gold statue."
Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of anger. His face changed. He ordered the fire made seven times hotter than usual.
He told some strong soldiers in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He told them to throw the men into the fire.
So the men were tied up. They still had on their coats, pants, hats, and other clothes. Then they were thrown into the fire.
The king's order was harsh, and the fire was very hot. The flames killed the soldiers who took Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to the fire.
The three men fell into the fire. They were still tied up.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was shocked. He jumped up. He asked his helpers, "Did we not throw three tied-up men into the fire?" "Yes, O king," they answered.
He said, "Look! I see four men. They are walking in the fire. They are not hurt. The fourth looks like a son of the gods."
Nebuchadnezzar went near the door of the fire. He said, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out!" Then they came out of the fire.

The leaders, bosses, governors, and the king's helpers came together. They saw that the fire had not hurt the men. Their hair was not burned. Their clothes were not changed. They did not even smell like fire.

Nebuchadnezzar said, "Praise the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego! He sent His angel. He saved His servants who trusted in Him. They did not obey the king's order. They gave up their bodies instead of serving or worshiping any god except their God.

So I make this rule: If any person, from any people, nation, or language, says anything bad against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that person will be cut to pieces. His house will be torn down. No other god can save like this."
Then the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego more honor in Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar sends this to all nations and people who speak every language and live everywhere. May you have much peace!
I am glad to tell you about the great signs and wonders the Most High God did for me.
His signs are great. His wonders are strong. His kingdom lasts forever. His rule goes on and on.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was resting in my house. I was doing well in my palace.
I had a dream that scared me. In bed, thoughts and pictures in my head scared me.
So I sent for all the wise men of Babylon. I wanted them to tell me what the dream meant.
The magicians, wise men, star readers, and fortune tellers came in. I told them the dream, but they could not tell me what it meant.
At last, Daniel came to me. He is called Belteshazzar, after my god's name. God's Spirit is in him. I told him the dream.
I said, "Belteshazzar, you are the leader of the magicians. I know God's Spirit is in you. No secret is too hard for you. Tell me what I saw in my dream and what it means.
"In my dream, I was lying in bed. I saw a tree in the middle of the earth. It was very tall.
The tree grew big and strong. Its top reached the sky. People everywhere could see it.
Its leaves were pretty. It had lots of fruit. It gave food to all. Wild animals rested under it. Birds lived in its branches. Every living thing got food from it.
"While I was lying in bed, I saw a holy messenger come down from heaven.
"He shouted in a loud voice, 'Cut down the tree! Cut off its branches! Pull off its leaves! Scatter its fruit! Make the animals run away from under it! Make the birds leave its branches!
"'But leave the stump and its roots in the ground. Put a band of iron and bronze around it. Let it stay in the grass. Let the man be wet with dew from heaven. Let him eat grass with the wild animals.
"'Let his mind change from a man's mind to an animal's mind. Let seven years go by.

"'This order comes from the holy messengers. It is a command from the holy ones. It is so that all living people may know that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of men. He gives them to anyone He wants. He can put the lowest man in charge.'
"This is the dream I saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means. The wise men of my kingdom could not tell me. But you can, because God's Spirit is in you."

Then Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, was quiet for a while. His thoughts scared him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning scare you." Belteshazzar answered, "My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its meaning for your enemies!
"The tree you saw grew big and strong. Its top reached the sky. It could be seen everywhere.
Its leaves were pretty. Its fruit was plenty. It gave food to all. Wild animals lived under it. Birds lived in its branches.
That tree is you, O king! You have grown great and strong. Your greatness has reached the sky. Your rule reaches the ends of the earth.

"You also saw a holy messenger come down from heaven. He said, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it. But leave the stump and roots in the ground. Put a band of iron and bronze around it. Let it stay in the grass. Let the man be wet with dew from heaven. Let him live with wild animals until seven years go by.'
"This is what it means, O king. This is the order from the Most High that has come to you, my lord the king.

"You will be sent away from people. You will live with wild animals. You will eat grass like an ox. You will be wet with dew from heaven. Seven years will go by. This will last until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of men. He gives them to anyone He wants.
"The command said to leave the stump and roots. This means your kingdom will be given back to you. It will happen when you know that Heaven rules.
"So, O king, please listen to my advice. Stop sinning. Do what is right. Stop doing wrong. Be kind to poor people. Then maybe your good life will last longer."
All of this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Twelve months later, he was walking on the roof of his palace in Babylon.
He said, "Look at this great Babylon! I built it with my strong power. It shows my glory and greatness."
While the words were still in his mouth, a voice came from heaven. It said, "King Nebuchadnezzar, your kingdom has been taken from you.

"You will be sent away from people. You will live with wild animals. You will eat grass like an ox. Seven years will go by. This will last until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of men. He gives them to anyone He wants."

Right away, the words came true. Nebuchadnezzar was sent away from people. He ate grass like an ox. Dew from heaven made his body wet. His hair grew like eagle feathers. His nails grew like bird claws.

At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven. My mind came back to me. I praised the Most High. I honored Him and gave Him glory. He lives forever. His rule lasts forever. His kingdom lasts from one family line to the next.
All the people on earth are like nothing next to Him. He does what He wants with the armies of heaven and the people of earth. No one can stop Him. No one can say to Him, "What have You done?"

At that same time, my mind came back to me. My honor and beauty came back to me. They were for the glory of my kingdom. My leaders came looking for me. I was put back on my throne. I became even greater than before.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and lift up and honor the King of heaven. All His works are true. All His ways are fair. He can bring down proud people.
King Belshazzar gave a big dinner for one thousand of his important men. He drank wine with them.

While he drank, Belshazzar said to bring the gold and silver cups. These were the cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from God's house in Jerusalem. The king wanted to drink from them with his important men, his wives, and his other women.
So they brought the gold cups from God's house in Jerusalem. The king, his important men, his wives, and his other women drank from them.
They drank wine and praised gods made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
Right then, fingers of a human hand came out and wrote on the wall. The wall was near the lampstand in the king's palace. The king saw the hand writing.
The king's face changed. He was scared. His thoughts troubled him. His legs felt weak, and his knees hit together.

The king called loudly for the wise men, the Chaldeans, and the star readers. He said to Babylon's wise men, "Whoever reads this writing and tells what it means will wear purple. He will get a gold chain for his neck. He will be third in charge of the kingdom."
All the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or tell the king what it meant.
Then King Belshazzar was very scared. His face changed more. His important men were confused.
The queen came into the banquet hall because of the king's words and his important men. She said, "O king, live forever! Do not be scared. Do not let your face change.

There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods. In your father's days, he was found to have light, understanding, and wisdom like the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, made him chief of the wise men, the magicians, the Chaldeans, and the star readers.

His name is Daniel, but the king called him Belteshazzar. He has a very great spirit. He knows things and understands things. He can explain dreams and tell hard things. He can untie knots. Call Daniel now. He will tell you what the writing means."
Then Daniel was brought to the king. The king said to Daniel, "Are you Daniel, one of the Jewish people my father the king brought from Judah?
I heard that the spirit of the gods is in you. You have light, understanding, and great wisdom.
The wise men and magicians were brought to me. They could not read this writing or tell me what it means.

But I heard you can give meanings and untie knots. If you can read the writing and tell me what it means, you will wear purple. You will get a gold chain for your neck. You will be third in charge of the kingdom."
Daniel answered the king, "Keep your gifts. Give your rewards to someone else. But I will read the writing for the king and tell what it means.
O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar his kingdom, greatness, honor, and glory.

Because of the greatness God gave him, all people, nations, and languages were very afraid of him. He killed people when he wanted. He gave power to people when he wanted. He took power away when he wanted.
But when his heart became proud and his spirit became hard, he was taken from his throne. His glory was taken from him.

He was driven away from people. His mind became like an animal's mind. He lived with wild donkeys. He ate grass like an ox. Dew from heaven made him wet until he knew that the Most High God rules over people's kingdoms. He sets over them whom He wants. "
But you, Belshazzar, his son, have not made your heart humble, even though you knew all this.

You lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven. You had the cups from His house brought to you. You and your important men, your wives, and your other women drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone. Those gods cannot see, hear, or know anything. But you did not honor the God who holds your breath and all your ways in His hand.
So a hand was sent from God. This writing was written.
This is the writing that was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.
Here is what it means. MENE means God has counted the days of your kingdom and ended it.
TEKEL means you have been weighed on the scales and found too light.
PERES means your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
Then Belshazzar said to dress Daniel in purple. They put a gold chain on his neck. They announced that he would be third in charge of the kingdom.
That same night, Belshazzar, the king of the Chaldeans, was killed.
Darius the Mede took the kingdom. He was about sixty-two years old.
It made King Darius happy to choose 120 rulers to help run the whole kingdom.
He put three leaders over them. Daniel was one of them. These leaders checked the rulers' work so the king would not lose anything.
Daniel did so well that the king planned to put him in charge of the whole kingdom.

The other leaders and rulers tried to find something wrong with Daniel in his work for the king. But they could not find any wrong or bad thing. He was faithful. No careless or bad thing was found in him.
So they said, "We will never find anything wrong with Daniel unless we find something against him about the law of his God."
Then these men went to the king together. They said, "O King Darius, live forever!

All the king's top helpers, rulers, and leaders have agreed. The king should make a new law. For thirty days, anyone who prays to any god or man, except you, O king, will be thrown into the pit with lions.
Now, O king, make this law and sign it. Then it cannot be changed, like the laws of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be taken back."
So King Darius signed the written law.

When Daniel learned that the law was signed, he went to his house. His upstairs room had windows that opened toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he got down on his knees. He prayed and thanked his God, just as he had done before.
Then these men went as a group and found Daniel praying and asking his God for help.

So they went to the king and said, "O King, did you not sign a law? For thirty days, no one may pray to any god or man except you, O king. If someone does, he will be thrown into the pit with lions." The king answered, "This is true. It is the law of the Medes and Persians, and it cannot be changed."
Then they said to the king, "Daniel, who is one of the people taken from Judah, does not care about you, O king. He does not care about the law you signed. He still prays three times a day."
When the king heard this, he was very upset. He wanted to save Daniel. He worked until sunset to rescue him.
Then the men went to the king together. They said, "Remember, O king, that no law the king makes can be changed. That is the law of the Medes and Persians."
So the king gave the order. Daniel was brought and thrown into the pit with lions. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve all the time, save you!"
A stone was brought and put over the mouth of the pit. The king sealed it with his own ring and with the rings of his important men. This was so nothing could be changed about Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace. He did not eat. No music or fun was brought to him. He could not sleep.
At the first light of morning, the king got up. He hurried to the pit with lions.
When he got near the pit, he called out in a worried voice, "O Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve all the time, been able to save you from the lions?"
Then Daniel spoke to the king: "O king, live forever!
My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths. They did not hurt me. I was found not guilty before Him. I have not done anything wrong against you, O king."
The king was very happy. He ordered Daniel to be lifted out of the pit. When Daniel was lifted out, no hurt was found on him. He had trusted in his God.

Then the king ordered the men who had told lies about Daniel to be brought. They were thrown into the pit with lions, along with their children and wives. Before they reached the bottom, the lions grabbed them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to all the people, nations, and languages in the land: "May your peace and plenty grow!
I order that in every part of my kingdom, people must fear and respect the God of Daniel. He is the living God. He lives forever. His kingdom will never be destroyed. His power will never end.
He saves and rescues. He does amazing things in heaven and on earth. He saved Daniel from the power of the lions."
So Daniel did well during the rule of Darius and during the rule of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year that Belshazzar was king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream. He saw pictures in his mind while he lay in bed. Then he wrote the dream down. He told the main parts.
Daniel said he looked in his dream at night. He saw the four winds of the sky stirring up the big sea.
Four big animals came up out of the sea. Each one was different.
The first animal was like a lion. It had eagle wings. Daniel watched until its wings were pulled off. It was lifted from the ground. It stood on two feet like a man. It was given a man's heart.
Another animal came next. It was like a bear. It rose up on one side. It had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. Someone said to it, "Get up! Eat a lot of meat!"
Then Daniel looked and saw another animal. It was like a leopard. It had four bird wings on its back. It had four heads. It was given power to rule.

Then he saw a fourth animal in his night dream. It was scary and very strong. It had big iron teeth. It ate and crushed things. It stomped on what was left with its feet. It was different from all the other animals. It had ten horns.

Daniel looked at the horns. Then a small horn grew up among them. Three of the first horns were pulled out to make room for it. This horn had eyes like a person's eyes. It had a mouth that spoke proud words.

Daniel watched until thrones were set up. Then the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothes were white like snow. The hair on His head was like clean wool. His throne was like fire. Its wheels were burning fire.
A river of fire flowed out from in front of Him. Thousands and thousands served Him. Millions stood before Him. The court sat to judge, and the books were opened.
Daniel kept looking because of the loud proud words the horn was saying. He saw the animal killed. Its body was destroyed and thrown into the fire.
The other animals lost their power to rule. But they were allowed to live for a while.
Daniel saw in his night dream. He saw someone who looked like a man coming with the clouds of heaven. He came to the Ancient of Days. He was brought before Him.
He was given power to rule, honor, and a kingdom. All people, all nations, and all languages will serve Him. His rule will last forever. It will never end. His kingdom will never be destroyed.
I, Daniel, felt upset deep inside. The pictures in my head troubled me.
I went up to one of the people standing there. I asked him to tell me the truth about all this. He told me what it meant.
He said, "These four big animals are four kings. They will rise up from the earth.
But God's holy people who belong to the Most High will receive the kingdom. They will own it forever and ever."

Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth animal. It was different from all the others. It was very scary. It had iron teeth and bronze claws. It ate, crushed, and stomped on what was left with its feet.

I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head. I wanted to know about the other horn that grew up. Three horns fell before it. That horn had eyes and a mouth that spoke proud words. It looked stronger than the others.
I saw that horn fight against God's holy people. It won against them for a time.
This lasted until the Ancient of Days came. He gave justice to God's holy people who belong to the Most High. Then the time came for God's people to own the kingdom.
He said, "The fourth animal means a fourth kingdom on earth. It will be different from all other kingdoms. It will eat up the whole earth. It will stomp on it and crush it.
The ten horns mean ten kings. They will come from this kingdom. After them, another king will come. He will be different from the first ones. He will bring down three kings.

He will speak against the Most High. He will wear out God's holy people who belong to the Most High. He will try to change the set times and the law. God's people will be given into his hand for three and a half years.
But the court will sit to judge. His power will be taken away. It will be destroyed forever.

The kingdom, power, and greatness of all the kingdoms under heaven will be given to the people who are God's holy people of the Most High. Their kingdom will last forever. Every ruler will serve and obey them."
This is the end of the matter. I, Daniel, was very troubled in my thoughts. My face changed. But I kept these things in my heart.
In the third year that King Belshazzar ruled, I, Daniel, saw another vision. It came after the first one I had seen.
In the vision, I saw myself in the strong city of Susa, in the land of Elam. I was standing by the Ulai River.
I looked up and saw a ram with two horns. It stood by the river. Both horns were high, but one was higher than the other. The higher one grew up last.
I saw the ram push to the west, north, and south. No animal could stand against it. No one could save them from its power. It did what it wanted and became very strong.
While I watched, a male goat came from the west. It moved so fast across the whole earth that its feet did not touch the ground. It had one big horn between its eyes.
It came to the ram with two horns that I had seen by the river. It charged at the ram in great anger.
I saw it reach the ram. It was furious. It hit the ram and broke its two horns. The ram was too weak to fight back. The goat threw the ram to the ground and trampled it. No one could save the ram.
The goat became very powerful. But when it was at its strongest, its big horn broke. Four horns grew in its place. They pointed toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of those horns, a small horn grew. It grew very strong toward the south, the east, and the beautiful land.
It grew so much that it reached the army of heaven. It threw some of the army and some of the stars to the ground. Then it trampled them.
It even grew up to the Prince of the army of heaven. It stopped the daily offering. It threw down the holy place where God's people worshiped.
Because people sinned, the army and the daily offering were given to it. Truth was thrown to the ground. It did all this and succeeded.

Then I heard one holy being speak. Another holy being asked him, “How long will this vision last? How long will the daily offering be stopped? How long will the holy place be ruined? How long will the army be trampled?”
He said, “It will last for 2,300 evenings and mornings. Then the holy place will be made clean.”
I, Daniel, saw the vision and wanted to understand it. Then I saw someone who looked like a man standing in front of me.
I heard a person’s voice from the Ulai River. It said, “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”
Gabriel came near to where I stood. I was afraid and fell on my face. He said to me, “Son of man, understand this. The vision is about the time of the end.”
While he was speaking, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground. Then he touched me and helped me stand up.
He said, “I will tell you what will happen near the end of God’s anger. The vision is for the time that has been set.
The ram with two horns stands for the kings of Media and Persia.
The male goat stands for the king of Greece. The big horn between its eyes is the first king.
The horn that broke stands for four kingdoms that will come from his nation. But they will not be as strong as he was.
When those kingdoms are almost finished, and the people have sinned very much, a fierce king will rise. He will be very clever.
His power will be great, but not from his own strength. He will destroy in shocking ways. He will succeed in what he does. He will destroy strong people and God’s holy people.

He will use his clever plans to make lies succeed. He will think he is very great. While people feel safe, he will destroy many. He will even stand against the Prince of princes. But he will be broken, and no human hand will do it.
The vision about the evenings and mornings is true. But keep the vision secret for now, because it is for many days from now.”
I, Daniel, was weak and sick for several days. Then I got up and did the king’s work. I was amazed by the vision, but no one could explain it to me.
In the first year that Darius ruled, he was king over Babylon. Darius was the son of Ahasuerus. He was from Media.
In that first year, I, Daniel, was reading. I learned from the books how many years the LORD had said through Jeremiah the prophet. Jerusalem would be empty for seventy years.
I turned to the Lord God to pray and beg Him. I did not eat. I wore rough cloth and put ashes on myself.
I prayed to the LORD my God and said I was wrong. I said, "Lord, You are great and awesome. You keep Your promise. You show love to those who love You and obey Your commands.
We sinned. We did wrong. We did bad things. We turned against You. We did not follow Your commands and Your rules.
We did not listen to Your servants, the prophets. They spoke in Your name to our kings, our leaders, and our fathers. They spoke to all the people too.

Lord, You are right. We are ashamed today. This is true for the men of Judah, the people in Jerusalem, and all Israel. It is true for those near and far, in all the lands where You sent them. They were not faithful to You.
the LORD, we are ashamed. Our kings, leaders, and fathers are ashamed. We sinned against You.
Lord our God, You are kind and forgiving. We turned against You.
We did not listen to the LORD our God. We did not follow His laws. He gave those laws to us through His servants, the prophets.
All Israel broke Your law and turned away. They would not listen to You. So the trouble God promised in the Law of Moses, His servant, came on us. We sinned against Him.
You did what You said You would do to us and our rulers. You brought a big trouble on us. Nothing like this has happened anywhere under heaven. Nothing like what happened to Jerusalem.
All this trouble came on us, just like it is written in the Law of Moses. But we did not ask the LORD our God for help. We did not turn from our wrong ways. We did not learn Your truth.
So the LORD kept the trouble ready and brought it on us. the LORD our God is right in all He does. But we did not listen to Him.
Now, Lord our God, You brought Your people out of Egypt with strong power. You made Your name great, even today. We sinned. We did bad things.

Lord, You do what is right. Please turn Your anger away from Your city, Jerusalem. It is Your holy mountain. Our sins and our fathers' sins made Jerusalem and Your people a shame to everyone around us.
Now, our God, hear the prayer of Your servant. Hear his request. Lord, for Your own sake, shine on Your holy place that is now empty.
Listen, my God. Hear me. Open Your eyes and see. We are ruined. See the city that has Your name. We are not asking You because we are good. We ask because You are very kind.
Lord, hear me. Lord, forgive me. Lord, listen and act. My God, do not wait. Do this for Your own sake. Your city and Your people have Your name."
While I was still talking and praying, I told God I was wrong. I told Him my people Israel were wrong. I asked the LORD my God to help His holy mountain.
While I was still praying, Gabriel came. I had seen him before in a vision. He flew quickly to me at the time of the evening offering.
He taught me and talked with me. He said, "Daniel, I came now to help you understand.
When you first prayed, an answer came. I came to tell you, because you are very loved. So think about the message and understand the vision.

Seventy weeks are set for your people and your holy city. They will end sin. They will pay for wrong. They will bring lasting good. They will finish the vision and the prophet's words. They will make the Most Holy Place holy.

Know and understand this. From the time the order is given to bring the Jews back and rebuild Jerusalem, until the Chosen Ruler comes, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. The city will be rebuilt with streets and a ditch, but in hard times.

After the sixty-two weeks, the Chosen Ruler will be killed. He will have nothing. Then the people of the ruler who is coming will destroy the city and the holy place. The end will come like a flood. Until the end there will be war. God has set the ruin.

He will make a strong promise with many for one week. In the middle of the week, he will stop the offerings and gifts. With horrible things, one who ruins will come. This will last until the set ruin is poured out on the one who ruins."

In the third year that Cyrus was king of Persia, a message was shown to Daniel. People called him Belteshazzar. The message was true. It was about a big war. Daniel understood the message and what he saw in the vision.
At that time, I, Daniel, was sad for three whole weeks.
I did not eat tasty food. I did not eat meat or drink wine. I did not put oil on myself. I did this for three weeks.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I stood by the great river, the Tigris.
I looked up and saw a man. He wore linen clothes. A belt of pure gold from Uphaz was around his waist.
His body was like a bright gem. His face was bright like lightning. His eyes were like fire. His arms and feet shone like polished brass. His voice sounded like a big crowd.
I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men with me did not see it. They were very afraid and ran to hide.
So I was alone. I saw this great vision. I had no strength left. My face looked weak and sick. I had no power.
Then I heard his voice. When I heard it, I fell into a deep sleep with my face on the ground.
A hand touched me. It made me shake on my hands and knees.
He said, "Daniel, you are greatly loved. Understand what I say to you. Stand up. I was sent to you." When he said this, I stood up shaking.
He said, "Do not be afraid, Daniel. From the first day you decided to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard. I came because of your words."
But the prince of Persia stopped me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the top leaders, came to help me. I stayed there with the kings of Persia.
