Now I came to help you understand what will happen to your people in the last days. The vision is for many days.
When he said these words, I looked down and could not speak.
Then someone who looked like a man touched my lips. I opened my mouth and spoke to the one standing in front of me. I said, "My lord, this vision has made me very sad. I have no strength left.
How can I, your servant, talk with you, my lord? I can hardly breathe."
Then someone who looked like a man touched me again and gave me strength.
He said, "Peace to you. Do not be afraid. Be strong. Yes, be strong." When he spoke to me, I felt strong again. I said, "Speak, my lord, because you have made me strong."
He said, "Do you know why I came to you? Now I will go back to fight the prince of Persia. After I go, the prince of Greece will come.
But first I will tell you what is written in the book of truth. No one helps me with these things except Michael, your prince."
In the first year that Darius the Mede ruled, I stood by to help and strengthen him.
Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will rule Persia. The fourth king will be richer than all of them. He will use his money to make everyone fight the kingdom of Greece.
Then a strong king will rise up. He will rule with great power and do what he wants.

But when he becomes strong, his kingdom will break apart. It will be split into four parts, like the four winds. It will not go to his children. It will not be ruled the way he ruled. His kingdom will be pulled up and given to others.
The king of the south will grow strong. But one of his leaders will grow even stronger and rule a bigger kingdom.

After some years, they will join together. The daughter of the king of the south will go to the king of the north to make peace. But she will not keep her power. His power will not last. She will be given up, along with the people who brought her, her child, and the one who helped her at that time.
But one from her family will take her place. He will come with an army. He will go into the strong place of the king of the north. He will fight them and win.
He will also take their gods to Egypt, along with their statues and valuable things of silver and gold. For some years he will leave the king of the north alone.
Then the king of the south will go into the land of the king of the north. But he will go back to his own land.
His sons will start a war. They will gather many soldiers. An army will come, sweep through, and go back. It will keep fighting up to his strong place.
Then the king of the south will get very angry. He will go out and fight the king of the north. The king of the north will raise a big army, but it will be given to the king of the south.
When the army is taken away, he will become proud. He will kill many thousands, but he will not win.
The king of the north will raise another army. It will be bigger than the first. After some years, he will come with a big army and many supplies.
At that time many will rise up against the king of the south. Also, some violent men from your people will try to make the vision come true, but they will fail.

Then the king of the north will come. He will build a ramp to attack. He will capture a strong city. The armies of the south will not be able to stand. Even their best soldiers will not have the strength to stand.
The one who comes will do what he wants. No one will stand against him. He will stand in the Beautiful Land, and destruction will be in his hand.

He will decide to come with all the power of his kingdom. He will make peace with the king of the south. He will give him his daughter to marry, to destroy the kingdom. But she will not stand with him or help him.
Then he will turn to the coastlands and capture many. But a leader will stop his pride and turn his pride back on him.
Then he will turn to the strong places of his own land. But he will stumble and fall, and he will be no more.
After him, another king will rise. He will send a tax collector through the splendid kingdom. But in a few days he will be broken, not in anger or in war.
Then a worthless man will take his place. He will not be given royal honor. He will come when people feel safe. He will take the kingdom by trickery.
Then the strong armies will be swept away before him and broken. The leader of the agreement will also be broken.
After an agreement is made with him, he will act with lies. He will rise to power with only a few people.

When things are calm, he will invade the richest parts of the land. He will do things his fathers and grandfathers never did. He will give stolen goods, treasure, and wealth to his followers. He will plan attacks on strong cities, but only for a time.

He will use his power and courage against the king of the south with a big army. The king of the south will fight with a very big and strong army. But he will not stand, because they will make plans against him.
The people who eat at his table will destroy him. His army will be swept away. Many will be killed.
The two kings will sit at the same table. Both will have evil in their hearts. They will tell lies to each other. But it will not work, because the end is still to come at the set time.
Then he will go back to his land with much wealth. But his heart will be against the holy agreement. He will do something and then go back to his land.
At the set time he will come back and go south. But it will not be like before.
Ships from Kittim will come against him. He will be afraid and go back. Then he will be angry at the holy agreement and do something. He will go back and help the people who leave the holy agreement.
His soldiers will rise up. They will make the holy place unclean. They will stop the daily offering. They will set up the terrible thing that causes ruin.
He will use smooth words to turn against him the people who break the agreement. But the people who know their God will be strong and do great things.
The wise people will help many understand. But they will fall by sword and fire. They will be captured and robbed for a time.
When they fall, they will get a little help. Many will join them with smooth words.
Some wise people will stumble. This will make them clean and pure until the end comes. The end will come at the set time.

Then the king will do what he wants. He will lift himself up above every god. He will say amazing things against the God of gods. He will succeed until God's anger is finished, because what is decided will be done.
He will not care about the gods of his fathers. He will not care about the one women desire. He will not care about any god. He will make himself greater than all of them.
Instead, he will honor a god of strong places. It is a god his fathers did not know. He will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and costly things.
He will attack the strongest forts with the help of a foreign god. He will give great honor to those who follow him. He will make them rulers over many. He will give out land for money.

At the time of the end, the king of the south will fight him. The king of the north will attack him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will invade countries and sweep through them like a flood.
He will also enter the Beautiful Land. Many countries will fall. But Edom, Moab, and the leaders of Ammon will escape from his hand.
He will reach out his hand against the countries. Even the land of Egypt will not escape.
He will take control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the riches of Egypt. The Libyans and Cushites will follow him.
But rumors from the east and the north will alarm him. He will go out in a great rage to destroy many people.
He will set up his royal tents between the sea and the beautiful holy mountain. But he will come to his end, and no one will help him.

At that time, Michael will stand up. He is the great leader who watches over your people. There will be a hard time. No time has ever been that hard since nations began. But at that time, your people will be saved. Everyone whose name is in the book will be saved.
Many people who sleep in the dust of the earth will wake up. Some will live forever. Others will be shamed forever.
The wise people will shine like the bright sky. The ones who help many people do right will shine like the stars forever and ever.
But you, Daniel, keep these words secret. Seal the book until the end time comes. Many people will go here and there. Knowledge will grow.
Then I, Daniel, looked. I saw two other people standing there. One stood on this side of the river. The other stood on the other side.
One of them said to the man in linen clothes, who was above the river water, "How long until these amazing things end?"

I heard the man in linen clothes, who was above the river water. He raised his right hand and his left hand to heaven. He made a promise by Him who lives forever. He said, "It will be for a time, times, and half a time. When the power of the holy people is broken, all these things will end."
I heard it, but I did not understand. So I asked, "My lord, what will happen at the end?"
He said, "Go your way, Daniel. These words are secret and sealed until the end time."
Many people will be made clean and pure. But bad people will keep doing bad things. None of the bad people will understand. But wise people will understand.
From the time the daily offering is stopped and the terrible thing that brings ruin is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
Happy is the person who waits and reaches the end of the 1,335 days.
But you, go your way until the end. Then you will rest. You will stand up and get your reward at the end of the days.

This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea. Hosea was the son of Beeri. It came in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. They were kings of Judah. It also came in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash. He was king of Israel.

When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to him, "Go, marry a woman who is not faithful. Have children with her. The people in this land have turned away from the LORD. They are not faithful to Him."
So Hosea went and married Gomer. She was the daughter of Diblaim. She became pregnant and had a son.
Then the LORD said to Hosea, "Name him Jezreel. In a little while I will punish Jehu's family. This is because of the blood spilled at Jezreel. I will end the kingdom of Israel.
On that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."
Gomer became pregnant again. She had a daughter. The LORD said to Hosea, "Name her 'No Mercy.' I will not show mercy to Israel anymore. I will not forgive them at all.
But I will be kind to Judah. I will save them. I will not do it with bows, swords, or war. I will not do it with horses or horsemen. I will save them by the LORD their God."
After Gomer stopped nursing 'No Mercy,' she became pregnant again. She had a son.
The LORD said, "Name him 'Not My People.' You are not My people. I am not your God."

But the people of Israel will be many. They will be like the sand by the sea. No one can count them. In the place where people said, "You are not My people," they will say, "You are children of the living God."
The people of Judah and Israel will come together. They will choose one leader. They will go up from the land. The day of Jezreel will be great.
"Tell your brothers, 'You are My people.' Tell your sisters, 'You are shown mercy.'"
"Argue with your mother. Argue with her. She is not My wife, and I am not her husband. Tell her to stop looking and acting like a prostitute. Tell her to stop cheating.
If she does not stop, I will take off her clothes. I will leave her bare, like the day she was born. I will make her like an empty desert. I will make her like dry land. I will let her die of thirst.
I will not show mercy to her children, because they are children born from cheating.

Their mother was not faithful. The one who had them acted in a shameful way. She said, 'I will follow my lovers. They give me my bread and water. They give me my wool and cloth. They give me my oil and drinks.'"
"So I will block her path with thorns. I will build a wall so she cannot find her way.
She will chase her lovers, but she will not catch them. She will look for them, but she will not find them. Then she will say, 'I will go back to my first husband. Things were better for me then.'"
"She did not know that I gave her grain, new wine, and oil. I gave her much silver and gold. But she used them to honor Baal.
So I will take back My grain when it is time. I will take back My new wine when it is ready. I will take away the wool and cloth that cover her.
Now I will show her shame to her lovers. No one will save her from My hand.
I will stop all her joy. I will stop her feasts, her new moon parties, and her Sabbath days. I will stop all her special days."
"I will ruin her grapevines and fig trees. She said, 'These are gifts my lovers gave me.' I will turn them into a forest. Wild animals will eat them.
I will punish her for the days she worshiped Baal. She burned incense to them. She put on rings and jewels. She went after her lovers and forgot Me, says the the LORD."
"So I will win her back. I will lead her into the desert. I will speak kindly to her.
There I will give her vineyards. I will make the Valley of Trouble a door of hope. There she will answer Me like when she was young. It will be like the day she left Egypt.
In that day, says the the LORD, you will call Me 'my Husband.' You will not call Me 'my Baal' anymore.
I will take the names of the Baals out of her mouth. No one will remember those names again."
"On that day I will make a promise with the wild animals, the birds, and the small animals that crawl. I will take away bows, swords, and war from the land. I will let them rest safely."
"I will promise to marry you forever. I will promise to marry you with what is right and fair. I will do it with love and mercy.
I will promise to marry you with faithfulness. Then you will know the the LORD."
"In that day, says the the LORD, I will answer. I will answer the sky, and the sky will answer the earth.
The earth will give grain, wine, and oil. They will give them to Jezreel.
I will plant her for Myself in the land. I will show mercy to the one called 'No Mercy.' I will say to the one called 'Not My People,' 'You are My people.' And he will say, 'You are my God.'"

The LORD said to me, "Go and love a woman who is loved by someone else and is not faithful in marriage. Love her the way the LORD loves the people of Israel. They turn to other gods and like cakes given to false gods."
So I bought her for fifteen pieces of silver. I also gave a big basket and a smaller basket of barley.
I said to her, "You will stay with me for many days. You must not be unfaithful, and you must not be with any other man. I will be faithful to you, too."
The people of Israel will live many days without a king, without a leader, without offerings, without stone pillars, without the priest's special vest, and without small idols.
Later, the people of Israel will come back. They will look for the LORD their God and for David their king. They will respect the LORD and His goodness in the last days.
Children of Israel, hear the word of the the LORD, for the the LORD has a case against the people who live in the land. He says, "There is no truth, no kindness, and no knowing God in the land.
People curse, lie, kill, steal, and are not faithful in marriage. One killing comes right after another."
So the land is sad. Everyone who lives there grows weak. The wild animals, the birds, and even the fish are dying.
"Do not let anyone argue. Do not let anyone blame. Your people are like people who fight with the priest.
You will trip and fall today. The prophet will trip and fall with you at night. I will destroy your mother.
"My people are destroyed because they do not know Me. Because you did not want to know Me, I will not let you be My priest. You forgot the law of your God, so I will forget your children.
The more they grew, the more they sinned against Me. I will turn their honor into shame.
"They feed on the sin of My people. They set their hearts on doing wrong.
The people and the priest will be the same. I will punish them for what they do. I will pay them back for their deeds.
"They will eat but not be full. They will be unfaithful but not have more children, because they left the the LORD to be unfaithful.
Wine and new wine take away good sense.
"My people ask a piece of wood for answers. Their stick tells them what to do. A spirit of unfaithfulness has led them the wrong way. They are unfaithful to their God.

"They sacrifice on the tops of mountains. They burn incense on hills. They do this under oak, poplar, and other trees, because the shade is good. So your daughters will be unfaithful, and your brides will cheat on their husbands.

I will not punish your daughters when they are unfaithful. I will not punish your brides when they cheat. This is because the men go off with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with temple prostitutes. People who do not understand will be ruined.
"Israel, even if you are unfaithful, let Judah not be guilty. Do not go to Gilgal. Do not go up to Beth Aven. Do not swear by the life of the the LORD.
Israel is stubborn, like a stubborn young cow. Now the the LORD will feed them like a lamb in a wide field.
Ephraim is joined to idols. Leave him alone.
"Their wine is gone. They keep being unfaithful. Their leaders love shame.
A wind has wrapped her in its wings. They will be ashamed because of their sacrifices."
Hear this, priests! Pay attention, people of Israel! Listen, king! For judgment is on you, because you have been a trap at Mizpah and a net spread on Tabor.
The rebels have gone deep into killing, but I will punish them all.
I know Ephraim. Israel is not hidden from Me. Now, Ephraim, you have been unfaithful. Israel is made unclean.
Their bad actions keep them from coming back to their God. A spirit of unfaithfulness is in them, and they do not know the LORD.
Israel's pride shows they are guilty. Israel and Ephraim trip because of their sin. Even Judah trips with them.
They will go with their sheep and cows to look for the LORD, but they will not find Him. He has left them.
They have not been true to the LORD. They have had children who are not their own. Now one month will destroy them and their land.
Blow the horn in Gibeah! Blow the trumpet in Ramah! Shout the war cry in Beth-aven! "Look behind you, Benjamin!"
Ephraim will be ruined on the day I correct them. Among Israel's tribes, I tell what is sure to happen.
Judah's leaders are like people who move boundary stones. I will pour out My anger on them like water.
Ephraim is crushed and treated unfairly, because he chose to follow worthless idols.
So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like rot to Judah.
When Ephraim saw he was sick and Judah saw his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot heal you or cure your wound.
I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to Judah. I will tear them apart and go away. I will carry them off, and no one will save them.
Then I will go back to My place until they admit they are guilty and seek Me. In their trouble they will look for Me.
"Come, let us go back to the LORD. He hurt us, but He will heal us. He hit us, but He will fix our hurts.
In two days, He will make us live again. On the third day, He will lift us up. Then we will live with Him.
Let us learn about the LORD. Let us keep trying to know Him. He will come like the sunrise. He will come to us like rain, like spring rain that wets the ground."
"What can I do with you, Ephraim? What can I do with you, Judah? Your love is like morning mist. It is like early dew that goes away.
So I spoke through My prophets. My words struck you down. My decisions came out like light.
"I want kindness, not sacrifices. I want people to know God, not just burnt gifts.
But they broke My agreement, like Adam did. They were not faithful to Me.
"Gilead is a town full of bad people. It is stained with blood.
Robbers wait to attack a man. Priests do the same. They kill people on the road to Shechem. They carry out evil plans.
"I have seen a terrible thing in Israel. Ephraim acts like a prostitute. Israel is made dirty.
Judah, you also have a harvest coming. I will bring My people back."
When I wanted to heal Israel, Ephraim's sin showed. Samaria did bad things too. They told lies. A thief came in, and robbers took things outside.
They do not think about all their wrongs. Now their bad deeds surround them. They are right in front of Me.
They make the king happy with their bad deeds. They make the leaders happy with their lies.
They all burn with sin, like a hot oven. The baker stops tending the fire while the dough rises.
On our king's day, the leaders got sick from wine. The king shook hands with men who mock.
They get ready in their hearts like a hot oven. They lie in wait all night. In the morning, it burns like a blazing fire.
They are all hot like an oven. They eat up their judges. All their kings have fallen. None of them calls to Me.
Ephraim mixes with other nations. Ephraim is like bread cooked on only one side.
Strangers eat his strength, and he does not know it. Gray hair shows on him, and he does not know it.
Israel's pride speaks against him. Yet they do not turn back to the LORD their God. They do not look for Him, even after all this.
Ephraim is like a silly dove with no sense. It calls to Egypt and goes to Assyria.
When they go, I will spread My net over them. I will pull them down like birds in the sky. I will punish them as their people hear.
Trouble for them, because they ran from Me! Ruin for them, because they turned against Me! I wanted to save them, but they tell lies about Me.
They do not cry to Me from their hearts. They only wail on their beds. They gather for grain and new wine, and they turn away from Me.
I trained and strengthened their arms, but they plan bad things against Me.
They turn, but not to God above. They are like a bad bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword because of their proud words. This will make them a joke in Egypt.
Blow the trumpet! Put the trumpet to your lips! An eagle flies over the the LORD's house. Israel broke My agreement and turned away from My rules.
Israel cries out to Me, "Our God, we know You!"
But Israel turned away from what is good. An enemy will chase him.
They chose kings, but not by Me. They made leaders, but I did not pick them. They used silver and gold to make idols for themselves. That will destroy them.
I rejected your calf, Samaria. I am angry with them. How long until they are clean?
It came from Israel. A worker made it. It is not God. Samaria's calf will be broken into pieces.
They plant wind and get a storm. The grain does not stand. What sprouts makes no flour. Even if it does, strangers eat it.
Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations. No one wants them, like a broken pot.
They went to Assyria. They are like a wild donkey alone. Ephraim paid other nations to be on their side.
Even if they hire nations to help them, I will gather them now. They will start to grow weak under the heavy rule of the great king.
Ephraim made many altars for sin, but the altars became places for more sin.
I wrote ten thousand of My rules for him, but he thought they were strange.
They offer gifts to Me and eat the meat, but the the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their wrongs and punish their sins. They will go back to Egypt.
Israel forgot his Maker and built palaces. Judah built many strong cities. But I will send fire on their cities, and it will burn their strong buildings.
Do not be happy, Israel. Do not cheer like other nations. You have turned away from your God. You love pay from selling yourself on every grain floor.
The grain floor and wine press will not feed them. The new wine will not help them.
They will not stay in the the LORD's land. Ephraim will go back to Egypt. They will eat food that is not clean in Assyria.

They will not pour wine for the the LORD. Their gifts will not make Him happy. Their gifts will be like food for people in mourning. Everyone who eats them will become unclean. Their bread will only fill their stomachs. It will not go into the the LORD's house.
He asked, "What will you do on the special day? What will you do on the the LORD's feast day?"
Look, they are running from trouble. Egypt will gather them. Memphis will bury them. Thorns will take their silver. Weeds will grow in their tents.
The days to punish have come. The days to pay back have come. Israel will know. The prophet is a fool. The man with God's Spirit is crazy. This is because your sin is great, and your hate is great.
The prophet watches over Ephraim for my God. But traps are on all his paths. There is hate in the house of his God.
They have sinned deeply, like in the days of Gibeah. God will remember their wrong. He will punish their sins.

I found Israel like grapes in the desert. I saw your fathers like the first figs on a fig tree. But they went to Baal Peor. They gave themselves to Shame. They became as awful as the thing they loved.
Ephraim's honor will fly away like a bird. There will be no babies born, no one pregnant, and no baby started.
Even if they raise children, I will take their children away. How sad for them when I leave them!
I have seen Ephraim like Tyre, planted in a nice place. But Ephraim will bring his children out to be killed.
Hosea prayed, "Give them, O the LORD—what will You give? Give them mothers who lose their babies and cannot feed them."
All their wrong is in Gilgal. There I hated them. Because of their bad deeds, I will push them out of My house. I will not love them anymore. All their leaders are against Me.
Ephraim is hit hard. Their root is dry. They will make no fruit. Even if they have children, I will kill the babies they love.
My God will reject them because they did not obey Him. They will wander among the nations.
Israel is like a grapevine that grows well and makes fruit. The more fruit he had, the more altars he built. The better his land was, the more stone pillars he set up.
Their hearts are not true. Now they must pay for their wrong. the LORD will break their altars and smash their stone pillars.
Now they will say, "We have no king. We did not fear the LORD. What can a king do for us?"
They say empty words. They make deals with false promises. So God's punishment grows like bad weeds in the rows of a field.
The people of Samaria will be afraid for the calf idol at Beth-aven. Its people will be sad for it. Its false priests will cry over it, over its glory, because it was taken away.
It will be taken to Assyria as a gift to the king. Ephraim will be ashamed. Israel will be ashamed of its own plans.
Samaria and her king will be destroyed. They will be like foam on the water.

The hilltop worship places at Aven will be destroyed. That is Israel's sin. Thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, "Fall on us!" and to the hills, "Cover us!"
Israel, you have sinned since the days of Gibeah. You stayed there. Will the battle at Gibeah not catch the bad people?
I will punish them as I choose. Nations will gather against them and put them in chains for their double sin.
Ephraim is like a young cow that has been trained and likes to crush grain. So I will put a heavy yoke on her neck. I will make Ephraim pull. Judah will plow. Jacob will break up the ground.
Plant what is right for yourselves. Reap love. Break up your hard ground. It is time to seek the LORD, until He comes and sends good like rain on you.
You planted wrong and reaped unfairness. You ate the fruit of lies. You trusted in your own plans and in your many strong men.
So the noise of war will rise against your people. All your forts will be destroyed. It will be like Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel in battle, when mothers were killed along with their children.
So Bethel will do this to you because of your great wrong. At dawn, the king of Israel will be destroyed.
"When Israel was a little child, I loved him. I called My son out of Egypt.
The more I called them, the more they walked away. They gave gifts to Baal. They burned smoke to idols.
"I taught Ephraim to walk. I held him in My arms. But he did not know I made him well.
I led them with kind ropes and love. I was like one who lifts a heavy load off their jaw. I bent down and fed them.
"They will not go back to Egypt. Assyria will be their king, because they would not come back to Me.
A sword will sweep through their cities. It will break their gates. It will destroy them because of their bad plans.
My people want to turn away from Me. They call to the Most High, but He will not lift them up.
"How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart turns inside Me. My love grows warm.
I will not pour out My hot anger. I will not destroy Ephraim again. I am God, not a man. I am the Holy One among you. I will not come in anger.
"They will follow the the LORD. He will roar like a lion. When He roars, His children will come shaking from the west.
They will come shaking like birds from Egypt and like doves from Assyria. I will settle them in their homes.
Ephraim has surrounded Me with lies. Israel's people have surrounded Me with tricks. But Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One," says the the LORD.
Ephraim wastes all day chasing empty things. He keeps lying and hurting people. He makes a deal with Assyria and sends oil to Egypt.
The LORD also has a complaint against Judah. He will punish Jacob for the way he lives. He will pay him back for what he has done.
Even before he was born, he grabbed his brother’s heel. When he was a man, he wrestled with God.
He fought with the angel and won. He cried and begged God to be kind. He found God at Bethel, and there God spoke to us.
The LORD is the God of armies. The LORD is His name.
But you must come back to your God. Keep love and fairness. Always wait for your God.
A trader likes to cheat with false scales.
And Ephraim brags, “I am very rich. I found wealth for myself. With all my work, they can’t find any sin in me.”
“But I am the LORD your God from the time you were in Egypt. I will make you live in tents again, like in the days of the special feast.
I spoke to the prophets. I gave them many dreams. I taught with stories through the prophets.”
Is there sin in Gilead? The people there are worthless. They kill bulls in Gilgal. Their places of worship are like piles of rocks in the fields.
Jacob ran away to Aram. Israel worked for a wife. Yes, he watched sheep for a wife.
But the LORD used a prophet to bring Israel out of Egypt. He also used a prophet to keep Israel safe.
Ephraim made his Lord very angry. So his Lord will leave his guilt on him. He will pay him back for his shame.
When Ephraim spoke, people shook with fear. He became great in Israel. But he sinned by worshiping Baal, and he died.

Now they sin more and more. They make metal idols for themselves. They make them just the way they want, all from silver. Skilled workers make them. They say, "Men who kill people kiss the calf idols."
So they will be like a morning cloud. They will be like dew that goes away. They will be like straw blown away from grain. They will be like smoke from a chimney.
"I am the LORD your God. I brought you out of Egypt. You must know that I am the only God. No one else can save you.
I knew you in the desert, in the dry land."
They ate until they were full. Their hearts became proud. So they forgot Me.
"So I will be like a lion to them. I will watch for them like a leopard on the road.
I will meet them like a bear that lost her cubs. I will tear open their hearts. I will eat them there like a lion. Wild animals will tear them apart.
You are destroyed, Israel, because you are against Me. You are against the One who helps you."
Where is your king now? Can he save you in all your cities? Where are your judges? You said, "Give me a king and leaders."
"I gave you a king when I was angry. I took him away when I was full of wrath."
Ephraim's guilt is saved up. His sin is not forgotten.
Pain like a woman in labor will come to him. He is not a wise son, because he does not come when it is time to be born.
"I will save them from the grave. I will buy them back from death. Death, where are your hurts? Grave, where is your sting? I will not show pity."

He grows well among his brothers. But an east wind will come. The wind of the LORD will rise from the desert. His spring will dry up. His well will dry up. His storehouse will be robbed of every treasure.
Samaria will be punished because she turned against her God. They will fall by the sword. Their babies will be smashed to pieces. Their pregnant women will be cut open.
Israel, come back to the LORD your God. You have tripped because of your sin.
Take words with you and come back to the LORD. Say to Him, "Take away all our wrongs. Accept what is good. We will praise You with our words."
Assyria will not save us. We will not ride on horses. We will not say, "This is our God," to things we made with our hands. You care for children with no parents.
I will heal them from turning away. I will love them for free. My anger has left them.
I will be like dew to Israel. They will bloom like a flower. They will put down roots like the trees of Lebanon.
Their new branches will spread out. They will be as pretty as an olive tree. They will smell sweet like Lebanon.
People will come back and rest in his shade. They will grow like grain. They will bloom like a grapevine. They will be as well known as the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim, what do I have to do with idols? I am the One who answers and watches over you. I am like a tree that stays green all year. Your fruit comes from Me.
Who is wise? Let him understand these things. Who can think clearly? Let him know them. The ways of the LORD are right. Good people walk in them. But people who do wrong trip over them.
This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel. Joel was the son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you leaders. Listen, all you people who live in the land. Has anything like this happened in your days? Did it happen in the days of your fathers?
Tell your children about it. Let your children tell their children. Let their children tell the children after them.
What one group of locusts left, the next group ate. What that group left, another group ate. What was left after that, yet another group ate.
Wake up, you people who drink too much, and cry. Wail, all you who drink wine. The sweet wine is taken from your mouths.
A strong group of people came up on My land. They are too many to count. Their teeth are like a lion's teeth. Their jaws are like a lioness's jaws.
They ruined My grapevines. They stripped My fig tree. They threw down its branches. The branches turned white.
Cry like a young woman in rough cloth. She is sad for the husband she had when she was young.
Grain and drink gifts are cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests are sad. The helpers of the LORD are sad.
The field is ruined. The ground is sad. The grain is ruined. The new wine is weak. The oil is dry.
Be upset, you farmers. Cry out, you grape growers. Cry for the wheat and barley. The harvest of the field is gone.
The grapevine is dry. The fig tree is weak. The pomegranate, the palm, and the apple tree are dry. All the trees in the field are dry. Joy is gone from people.

Put on rough cloth and be sad, you priests. Cry out, you workers at the altar. Come and lie down in rough cloth all night, you helpers of my God. Grain and drink gifts are kept from the house of your God.
Set apart a time with no food. Call a special meeting. Bring the leaders and all the people who live in the land to the house of the LORD your God. Cry out to the LORD.
Oh, what a sad day! The Day of the LORD is near. It comes like ruin from the All-Powerful One.
Our food is taken away right in front of us. Joy and gladness are gone from the house of our God.
The seeds dry up under the dirt. The storehouses are ruined. The barns are broken down. The grain is dry.
The animals groan. The herds of cows are confused. They have no grass to eat. Even the flocks of sheep suffer.
I cry to You, the LORD, because fire ate the grass in the wild land. The flame burned all the trees in the field.
Even the animals in the field cry to You, because the streams of water are dry. Fire ate the grass in the wild land.
Blow a trumpet in Zion. Shout on God's holy hill. Let everyone in the land shake with fear. The day of the LORD is coming. It is near.

It will be a day of darkness and gloom. It will be a day of clouds and thick darkness. A huge, strong army will come, like the morning light spreading over the mountains. There has never been an army like it. There will never be one again, not for many years.
Fire burns everything in front of them. Flames burn everything behind them. The land in front of them is like a garden of Eden. The land behind them is a dry, empty desert. Nothing escapes them.
They look like horses. They run like horsemen.
They jump on the mountain tops like chariots. They sound like fire eating dry grass. They are like a strong army lined up for war.
People shake with fear when they see them. Every face turns pale.
They run like strong warriors. They climb walls like soldiers. Each one goes straight ahead. They do not turn from their path.
They do not push each other. Each one stays in his own place. They break through weapons, but they are not stopped.
They run through the city. They climb the walls. They go into houses. They come in through windows like a thief.
The earth shakes before them. The sky trembles. The sun and moon grow dark. The stars stop shining.
The LORD shouts before His army. His camp is very large. The ones who carry out His word are strong. The day of the LORD is great and terrible. Who can live through it?
"Even now," says the LORD, "come back to Me with all your heart. Come with fasting, crying, and sadness."

Be truly sorry in your hearts. Do not just tear your clothes. Come back to the LORD your God. He is kind and full of mercy. He is slow to get angry. He has great love. He may choose not to send the hard times.
Who knows? He may turn back and be kind. He may leave a blessing behind. Then you can bring grain and drink offerings to the LORD your God.
Blow a trumpet in Zion. Set apart a time to fast. Call a meeting.
Bring the people together. Set apart the group. Gather the older people. Bring the children and even babies. Let the groom leave his room. Let the bride leave her tent.

The priests who serve the LORD cry between the porch and the altar. They say, "LORD, please spare Your people. Do not let other nations shame what belongs to You. Do not let them rule Your people. Why should people ask, 'Where is their God?'"
Then the LORD cared deeply for His land. He felt sorry for His people.
The LORD answered His people. He said, "Look, I am sending you grain, new wine, and oil. You will have enough. I will not let other nations shame you again."

The LORD will move the army from the north far away from you. He will push it into a dry and empty land. Its front will go into the eastern sea. Its back will go into the western sea. Its bad smell will rise. Its stink will go up, because the LORD has done great things.
Do not be afraid, land. Be glad and happy, because the LORD has done great things.
Do not be afraid, you wild animals. The dry fields are turning green. The trees are growing fruit. The fig trees and grapevines are strong again.
Children of Zion, be glad. Be happy in the LORD your God. He gave you the early rain at the right time. He sent rain early and late, just like before.
The grain bins will be full of grain. The wine jars will overflow with new wine and oil.
The LORD will give back the years the bugs ate. He sent the big army of bugs that ate your crops.
You will eat plenty and be full. You will praise the name of the LORD your God. He did amazing things for you. His people will never be put to shame again.
You will know that the LORD is with Israel. He is the LORD your God. There is no other. His people will never be put to shame again.
After that, the LORD will pour out His Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will tell God's messages. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
In those days, He will pour out His Spirit on male and female servants too.
He will show wonders in the sky and on the earth. There will be blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
The sun will turn to darkness. The moon will turn to blood. This will happen before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved. On Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be safety. The LORD said some people will survive. He will call them.
For look, in those days and at that time, I will bring back the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
I will bring all the nations down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will judge them for what they did to My people Israel. They scattered My people among the nations and split up My land.
They threw lots for My people. They sold boys to bad women. They sold girls for wine and drank it.
Tyre, Sidon, and all the lands of Philistia, what are you to Me? Are you paying Me back? If you are paying Me back, I will quickly pay you back. You will get what you deserve.
You took My silver and gold. You carried My best things into your temples.
You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks. You sent them far from their home.
But I will bring them back from where you sold them. I will pay you back for what you did.
I will sell your sons and daughters to the people of Judah. They will sell them to faraway people. The LORD has spoken.
Tell this to the nations: Get ready for war! Wake up the strong men. Let all the fighters come near.
Make your plows into swords. Make your garden tools into spears. Let even a weak man say, "I am a strong fighter."
Hurry and come, all nations around. Gather there. The LORD, bring down Your warriors.
Let the nations get ready and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will sit to judge all the nations around.
Cut the grain, because the harvest is ready. Come and crush the grapes, because the winepress is full. The vats spill over. Their wrong is great.
Huge crowds, huge crowds in the Valley of Decision! The day of the LORD is near in the Valley of Decision.
The sun and moon will grow dark. The stars will stop shining.
The LORD will roar from Zion. He will shout from Jerusalem. Heaven and earth will shake. But the LORD will be a safe place for His people. He will be a strong fort for the people of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the LORD your God. I live in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy. Strangers will not walk through it again.

On that day, the mountains will drip with sweet wine. The hills will flow with milk. All the streams of Judah will flow with water. A spring will come from the house of the LORD and water the valley of Shittim.
Egypt will become empty land. Edom will become a dry desert. This is because they hurt the people of Judah. They killed innocent people in their land.
But Judah will live forever. Jerusalem will last for all time.
I will pay them back for the blood they spilled. I did not pay them back before. The LORD lives in Zion.
Amos was a shepherd from Tekoa. He saw these words about Israel. This was in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel. He saw them two years before the earthquake.
The LORD roars from Zion. He shouts from Jerusalem. The green fields where shepherds feed sheep become sad. The top of Mount Carmel dries up.
This is what the LORD says: "Damascus has sinned again and again. I will not take back My punishment. They crushed the people of Gilead with iron tools.
I will send fire on Hazael's house. It will burn Ben-hadad's palaces.
I will break the gates of Damascus. I will remove the people from the Valley of Aven. I will take away the ruler from Beth-eden. The people of Aram will be taken away to Kir," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "Gaza has sinned again and again. I will not take back My punishment. They took whole towns of people away and handed them over to Edom.
I will send fire on Gaza's wall. It will burn its palaces.
I will remove the people from Ashdod. I will take away the ruler from Ashkelon. I will strike Ekron with My hand. The rest of the Philistine people will die," says the Lord, the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "Tyre has sinned again and again. I will not take back My punishment. They sent whole towns of people away to Edom. They forgot their promise to be like brothers.
I will send fire on Tyre's wall. It will burn its palaces," says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: "Edom has sinned again and again. I will not take back My punishment. Edom chased his brother with a sword. He showed no mercy. His anger never stopped. He kept being angry all the time.
I will send fire on Teman. It will burn Bozrah's palaces," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "The Ammonites have sinned again and again. I will not take back My punishment. They cut open pregnant women in Gilead. They did this to take more land.
I will set fire to Rabbah's wall. It will burn its palaces. There will be shouting in battle and a big storm.
Their king will be taken away. His leaders will go with him," says the LORD.
The LORD says, "Moab has done wrong again and again. I will not take back its punishment, because Moab burned the bones of the king of Edom and turned them to powder.
"So I will send fire on Moab. It will burn the forts of Kerioth. Moab will die in the loud noise of battle, with shouts and trumpet blasts.
"I will take away its ruler. I will kill all its leaders with him," says the LORD.

The LORD says, "Judah has done wrong again and again. I will not take back its punishment, because Judah turned away from the law of the LORD and did not keep His rules. They believed lies that their fathers believed.
"So I will send fire on Judah. It will burn the forts of Jerusalem."
The LORD says, "Israel has done wrong again and again. I will not take back its punishment, because they sell good people for silver and poor people for a pair of sandals.
"They walk on the heads of poor people like dust on the ground. They are not fair to people who need help. A man and his father go to the same young woman. They make My holy name unclean.
"They lie down by every altar on clothes they took from poor people. In the house of their God, they drink wine that came from fines.
"Yet I destroyed the Amorites before them. The Amorites were as tall as cedar trees and as strong as oak trees. I destroyed their fruit above and their roots below.
"I brought you up from Egypt. I led you for forty years in the desert. I did this so you could take the land of the Amorites.
"I chose some of your sons to be prophets. I chose some of your young men to be special servants called Nazirites. Isn't this true, children of Israel?" declares the LORD.
The LORD says, "You made the Nazirites drink wine. You told the prophets not to speak God's message.
"So I will crush you where you are. I will crush you like a heavy cart full of grain crushing what is under it.
"Fast runners will not get away. Strong men will lose their strength. Warriors will not save their lives.
"Archers will not stand their ground. Fast runners will not escape. Horse riders will not save their lives.
"Even the bravest warrior will run away with nothing on that day," declares the LORD.
Listen to this word. The LORD spoke it against you, people of Israel. He spoke it against the whole family I brought out of Egypt. He said,
"I chose you alone from all the families on earth. So I will punish you for all your sins."
Can two walk together unless they agree?
Does a lion roar in the woods if it has no food? Does a young lion growl from its den unless it has caught something?
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground if there is no bait? Does a trap spring up from the ground if it has not caught something?
If a trumpet blows in a city, won't the people be afraid? If trouble comes to a city, hasn't the LORD done it?
The Lord the LORD does nothing without telling His secret to His servants, the prophets.
A lion has roared. Who won't be afraid? The Lord the LORD has spoken. Who can keep from speaking His words?
Tell the big houses in Ashdod and in Egypt, "Come together on the hills of Samaria. Look at the big mess inside her. Look at the people being hurt there."
"They do not know how to do right," says the LORD. "They store up hurt and stealing in their big houses."
So the Lord the LORD says, "An enemy will come all around the land. He will take away your strength. He will rob your big houses."

The LORD says, "Like a shepherd saves two legs or part of an ear from a lion's mouth, so the people of Israel who live in Samaria will be saved. They will have only a corner of a bed or a piece of a couch."
Listen and speak against the family of Jacob, says the Lord the LORD, the God of Hosts.
"On the day I punish Israel for their sins, I will also punish the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground."
"I will hit the winter house and the summer house. The houses made of ivory will be gone. Many houses will end," says the LORD.
Listen to this word, you cows of Bashan, who are on the mountain of Samaria. You push down poor people, and you hurt needy people. You say to your masters, “Bring more drinks, and we will drink.”
The Lord, the LORD, has promised by His holy name, “Days are coming when people will drag you away with hooks. They will drag your children away with fishhooks.
You will go out through holes in the wall. Each woman will go straight ahead. You will be thrown out toward Harmon,” says the the LORD.
“Come to Bethel and sin. Sin more and more at Gilgal. Bring your sacrifices every morning. Bring your tithes every three days.
Burn a thank offering with yeast. Announce your gifts. Tell everyone about them. This is what you love to do, people of Israel,” says the Lord, the LORD.
“I let you go hungry in every city. You did not have enough bread in any place. Yet you did not come back to Me,” says the the LORD.
“I also kept rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. I made it rain on one town, but not on another. One field got rain, and another field dried up.
People from two or three towns walked to another town to get water, but they still were thirsty. Yet you did not come back to Me,” says the the LORD.
“I struck you with plant disease and mildew. Locusts ate your many gardens and vineyards. They ate your fig trees and olive trees. Yet you did not come back to Me,” says the the LORD.
“I sent sickness among you like Egypt had. I killed your young men with swords. I took your horses away. I made your camps smell bad. Yet you did not come back to Me,” says the the LORD.
“I destroyed some of you like I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a burning stick pulled from a fire. Yet you did not come back to Me,” says the the LORD.
“So this is what I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this, get ready to meet your God, Israel!”

He is the One who made the mountains and the wind. He tells people what He is thinking. He turns morning into darkness. He walks on the high places of the earth. The The LORD, the God of heaven's armies, is His name.
Listen to this message, people of Israel. I am sad for you.
"Israel has fallen like a young woman. She will not get up again. She lies on her land, and no one helps her up."
The Lord GOD says this: "A city that sends out 1,000 soldiers will have only 100 left. A city that sends out 100 will have only 10 left for Israel."
The LORD says to Israel: "Look for Me, and you will live.
Do not look for help at Bethel. Do not go to Gilgal. Do not travel to Beersheba. Gilgal will be carried away, and Bethel will become a place of trouble.
Look for the LORD, and you will live. If not, He will come like fire through Joseph's family. It will burn, and no one in Bethel can put it out.
"You turn fair choices into something bitter. You throw goodness down to the ground!"
He made the stars called Pleiades and Orion. He turns dark into morning. He makes day dark like night. He calls sea water and pours it on the land. His name is the LORD.
He brings ruin on strong people. He brings trouble to their strong towers.
They hate the person who corrects them at the city gate. They hate the person who tells the truth.
So, because you step on poor people and take grain from them, you built stone houses, but you will not live in them. You planted nice grape fields, but you will not drink their wine.
I know you do many wrong things. You have so many sins. You hurt good people. You take money to be unfair. You turn poor people away at the city gate.
So wise people stay quiet then, because those days are bad.
Look for good, not bad, so you can live. Then the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, like you say.
Hate bad and love good. Make fair choices at the city gate. Maybe the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be kind to the people left from Joseph's family.

So the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord, says: "There will be crying in all the streets. People will say, 'Oh no! Oh no!' in all the open places. Farmers will be called to cry. People who know sad songs will be called to wail.
In all the grape fields, people will cry, because I will walk through your land," says the LORD.
How sad for people who want the Day of the LORD to come! Why do you want it? That day will be dark, not light.
It will be like a man who runs from a lion and meets a bear. Or he goes home, leans on the wall, and a snake bites him.
Will not the Day of the LORD be dark, not light? It will be gloomy, with no bright light.
"I hate your celebrations! I cannot stand the smell of your special meetings.
Even if you bring Me burnt gifts and grain gifts, I will not accept them. I will not even look at your fat animals you give for peace.
Take away your loud songs from Me! I will not listen to your harp music.
But let fair choices roll on like a river, and right living flow like a strong stream."
"Did you bring Me gifts and offerings in the desert for forty years, people of Israel?
You carried Sikkuth, your king, and Kaiwan, your star god, the idols you made for yourselves.
So I will send you away to a land past Damascus," says the LORD. His name is the God of Hosts.
Oh no! People in Zion feel safe. People on the hill in Samaria feel safe too. They are the big leaders of the best nations. Israel goes to them.
Go see Calneh. Then go to big Hamath. Then go down to Gath, where the Philistines live. Are those places better than your kingdoms? Is their land bigger than your land?
You act like trouble is far away. But you bring hurt close.
You lie on fancy beds with ivory. You lounge on your couches. You eat baby sheep from the flock. You eat young cows from the pen.
You sing silly songs with harps. You make up new instruments, like David did.
You drink wine from bowls. You put on the best oils. But you do not care that Joseph is being ruined.
So now you will be the first to go away as captives. Your parties will end.
The Lord, the LORD, promised by His own life. The LORD, the God of armies, says, "I hate the pride of Jacob. I hate his big houses. I will give up the city and everything in it."
If ten men are left in one house, they will die.
A family member will come to take the bones out of the house. He will ask, "Is anyone still with you?" The answer will be, "No." Then he will say, "Hush! We must not say the name of the LORD."
Look, the LORD will give the order. The big house will break into pieces. The little house will crack.
Do horses run on rocks? Do people plow rocks with oxen? But you turned justice into poison. You turned good into something bitter.
You are happy about Lo-debar. You say, "We took Karnaim by our own power."
Look, I will bring a nation against you, people of Israel, says the LORD, the God of armies. They will crush you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.
This is what the Lord the LORD showed me. He was making grasshoppers. It was right after the king's workers cut the first grass. The new grass was just starting to grow.
When the grasshoppers had eaten all the grass, I said, "Please forgive Jacob, Lord the LORD! He is too small to survive this."
The LORD changed His mind. He said, "This will not happen."
This is what the Lord the LORD showed me. He was calling fire to judge. The fire burned the deep water and began to burn the land.
Then I said, "Please stop, Lord the LORD! Jacob is too small to survive this."
The LORD changed His mind again. He said, "This will not happen either."
This is what He showed me. The Lord stood by a wall. He held a weight on a string in His hand.
The LORD asked me, "Amos, what do you see?" I said, "A weight on a string." Then the Lord said, "I am putting this test in the middle of My people Israel. I will not spare them anymore.
The hilltop altars of Isaac will be ruined. Israel's temples will be destroyed. I will fight against Jeroboam's family with a sword."
Then Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, sent a message to Jeroboam, king of Israel. He said, "Amos is plotting against you among the people. The country cannot stand all his words.
He said Amos told you, 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will be taken away from its land.'"
Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go away! Run to Judah. Earn food there and prophesy there.
Do not prophesy at Bethel again. It is the king's holy place and the nation's temple."
Amos answered, "I was not a prophet. I was not from a prophet's family. I was a shepherd and a man who picked sycamore figs.
But the LORD took me from tending sheep. The LORD said to me, 'Go. Give My messages to My people Israel.'
Now listen to the LORD's word. You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel. Do not speak against Isaac's family.'

So the LORD says, 'Your wife will sell herself in the city. Your sons and daughters will die by the sword. Your land will be split up with a measuring rope. You will die in an unclean land. Israel will surely be taken from its land.'"
The Lord the LORD showed me a basket of summer fruit.
He said, "Amos, what do you see?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the Lord the LORD said to me, "The end has come for My people Israel. I will not spare them anymore."
"In that day," says the Lord the LORD, "the songs in the temple will turn to sad cries. Dead bodies will be everywhere. Be quiet!"
Listen to this, you who walk on the poor and wipe out the needy in the land.
You say, "When will the new moon be over so we can sell grain? When will the Sabbath be over so we can sell wheat? We will make the measure small and the price big. We will cheat with false scales."
We will buy poor people with silver and needy people for a pair of shoes. We will even sell the sweepings with the wheat.
The LORD has made a promise by the pride of Jacob: "I will never forget what they have done."
"Will the land not shake because of this? Will not everyone who lives in it cry? The whole land will rise like the Nile. It will be stirred up and then go down again, like the Nile in Egypt."
"In that day," says the Lord the LORD, "I will make the sun go down at noon. I will make the earth dark in the middle of the day.

I will turn your celebrations into sad times. I will turn all your songs into crying. I will make everyone wear rough cloth and shave their heads. I will make it like crying for an only child. The end will be a bitter day."
"The days are coming," says the Lord the LORD, "when I will send hunger to the land. It will not be hunger for bread. It will not be thirst for water. It will be hunger to hear the words of the LORD.
People will wander from sea to sea. They will go from north to east. They will look for the word of the LORD, but they will not find it."
"In that day, the pretty young women and strong young men will faint from thirst.
Those who make promises by the sin of Samaria will say, 'As surely as your god lives, Dan,' or, 'As surely as the way to Beersheba lives.' They will fall and never get up again."

I saw the Lord standing by the altar. He said, "Hit the top of the pillars so the door frames shake. Break them on the heads of all the people. I will kill the rest with a sword. No one will get away. No one will escape.
If they dig down to the place of the dead, My hand will grab them there. If they climb up to heaven, I will bring them down from there.
If they hide on top of Mount Carmel, I will look for them and take them. If they hide from Me at the bottom of the sea, I will tell the snake to bite them there.
If they are taken away as prisoners by their enemies, I will tell the sword to kill them there. I will watch them to hurt them, not to help them."
The Lord GOD of all armies touches the earth, and it melts. Everyone who lives on it cries. The whole land rises like the Nile River and sinks like the Nile in Egypt.
He builds His rooms high in heaven. He sets His foundation on the earth. He calls the sea water and pours it on the land. the LORD is His name.

The LORD says, "Are you not like the people of Cush to Me, people of Israel? Did I not bring Israel up from Egypt? Did I not bring the Philistines from Caphtor? Did I not bring the people of Aram from Kir?"
"Look, My eyes are on the sinful kingdom. I will destroy it from the earth. But I will not completely destroy Jacob's family," says the LORD.
"Look, I will give the command. I will shake the people of Israel among all the nations. It will be like shaking grain in a strainer. Not one small stone will fall to the ground.
All the sinners among My people will die by the sword. They say, 'Trouble will not come near us or find us.'"
"On that day I will raise up David's fallen tent. I will fix its broken walls. I will raise up its ruins. I will build it like in the old days.
Then they will take over what is left of Edom and all the nations that are called by My name," says the LORD, who does this.

"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when the farmer who plows will catch up to the worker who cuts grain. The one who crushes grapes will catch up to the one who plants seed. The mountains will drip sweet wine. All the hills will flow with it.
I will bring back My people Israel. They will rebuild ruined cities and live in them. They will plant grape fields and drink the wine. They will make gardens and eat the fruit.
I will plant them in their land. They will never again be pulled up from the land I gave them," says the LORD your God.
This is what Obadiah saw. My Lord, the LORD, says this about Edom: "We heard news from the LORD. He sent a messenger to the nations. The messenger said to get up and fight Edom.
"I will make you small among the nations. You will be hated a lot.
Your pride tricked you. You live in high rock caves. You say in your heart, 'Who can bring me down?'
Even if you fly like an eagle and make your nest among the stars, I will bring you down," says the LORD.
"If thieves came to you, they would steal only what they want. If grape pickers came to you, they would leave some grapes. But you will be ruined badly.
Esau's hidden things will be found and taken.
Your friends will push you out of your land. Your peaceful friends will trick you and beat you. People who eat your bread will set a trap. You won't know.
"I will destroy the wise men of Edom and the smart men of Esau's mountains that day," says the LORD.
"Your fighters, Teman, will be scared. Everyone from Esau's mountains will be killed.
Because you hurt your brother Jacob, shame will cover you. You will be cut off forever.
You stood by when strangers took his stuff and foreigners entered his gates and drew lots for Jerusalem. You were like one of them.
"Don't be glad in your brother's bad day. Don't be happy when Judah's people are destroyed. Don't brag in their hard time.
Don't enter My people's gate in their bad day. Don't be glad about their trouble. Don't take their stuff in their bad day.
Don't stand where roads meet to kill their running people. Don't hand over their people who got away in their hard time.
"The Day of the LORD is near for all nations. What you did will be done to you. Your pay will come back on your head.
You drank on My holy mountain. So all nations will drink and drink. They will drink and choke. They will be like they never were.
"But on Mount Zion, some will be saved. It will be holy. Jacob's family will get their land back.
Jacob's family will be like fire. Joseph's family will be like a flame. Esau's family will be like dry grass. They will burn it up. No one will be left of Esau's family." For the LORD has spoken.
People from the south will take Esau's mountains. People from the lowlands will take the Philistines' land. They will take Ephraim's and Samaria's fields. Benjamin will take Gilead.
Israel's people who were taken away will take the land of the Canaanites up to Zarephath. Jerusalem's people who were taken to Sepharad will take the south cities.
Helpers will go up Mount Zion to rule Esau's mountains. The kingdom will belong to the LORD.
The word of the the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai.
The The LORD said, “Get up and go to the big city of Nineveh. Tell the people there that I see their bad ways.”

But Jonah ran away from the the LORD. He went to Tarshish. He went to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid the fare and got on. He sailed with them to Tarshish to get away from the the LORD.
Then the the LORD sent a big wind on the sea. A big storm came up. The ship was about to break apart.

The sailors were afraid. Each man cried to his own god. They threw the things on the ship into the sea to make the ship lighter. But Jonah had gone down into the ship. He lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
The captain came to him and said, “How can you sleep? Get up and call to your god! Maybe he will care about us and not let us die.”
The sailors said to each other, “Come, let us draw lots. Then we will know who caused this trouble.” They drew lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
They asked him, “Tell us, who caused this trouble for us? What is your job? Where do you come from? What country are you from? What people are you from?”
He said, “I am a Hebrew. I worship the the LORD, the God of heaven. He made the sea and the dry land.”
The men were very afraid. They said, “What have you done?” They knew he was running away from the the LORD, because he had told them.
The sea was getting rougher and rougher. They asked him, “What should we do to you so the sea will be calm for us?”
He said, “Pick me up and throw me into the sea. Then it will be calm. I know this big storm came on you because of me.”
The men tried hard to row back to land. But they could not. The sea got even wilder.
They cried to the the LORD, “Please, the the LORD, do not let us die because of this man. Do not blame us for killing a good man. You, the the LORD, have done what You wanted.”
Then they picked up Jonah and threw him into the sea. The sea became calm.
The men were very afraid of the the LORD. They gave a gift to the the LORD. They made promises to Him.
The The LORD sent a big fish to swallow Jonah. Jonah was in the fish’s belly for three days and three nights.
Jonah prayed to the the LORD his God from inside the fish.
Jonah said, "I was in trouble, so I called to the the LORD. He answered me. I cried out from the grave, and You heard my voice.
"You threw me deep into the sea. Water was all around me. Your waves rolled over me.
I said, 'I am thrown away from Your sight. But I will look again toward Your holy temple.'
"The water was all around me. It came up to my neck. The deep sea was around me. Seaweed wrapped around my head.
I went down to the bottom of the mountains. The earth closed around me forever. But You, the the LORD my God, brought me up from the grave.
When I was weak and ready to give up, I remembered the the LORD. My prayer came to You in Your holy temple.
"People who worship false gods turn away from Your faithful love.
But I will thank You with a loud voice. I will give You a gift. I will keep my promise to You. The LORD saves."
Then the the LORD spoke to the fish, and it spit Jonah out onto dry land.
The LORD spoke to Jonah again.
He said, "Get up and go to Nineveh, that big city. Tell the people the message I give you."
Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, just as the the LORD said. Nineveh was a very big city. It took three days to walk across it.
Jonah walked one day into the city. Then he called out, "In forty days, Nineveh will be destroyed!"
The people of Nineveh believed God. They did not eat for a while, and they wore rough cloth. Everyone did this, from the most important to the least.
The king of Nineveh heard the news. He got up from his throne. He took off his fancy robe. He put on rough cloth. He sat in ashes.
He sent a message all through Nineveh. He said, "The king and his leaders make this rule: Do not let people or animals eat or drink anything.
Let people and animals wear rough cloth. Let them call out loud to God. Let each person stop doing bad things and stop hurting others.
Maybe God will change His mind. Maybe He will stop being so angry. Then we will not die."
God saw what they did. He saw that they stopped doing bad things. So God changed His mind about the bad thing He had planned to do to them. He did not do it.
Jonah was very angry. He was upset.

He prayed to the LORD: "The LORD, this is what I said before I left home. That is why I ran to Tarshish. I knew You are kind and caring. You are slow to get angry. You love people very much. You change Your mind and do not send trouble.
Now, the LORD, please take my life. It is better for me to die than to live."
The LORD said, "Do you have a good reason to be angry?"
Jonah left the city and sat east of it. He made a small shelter and sat in its shade. He waited to see what would happen to the city.
The LORD God made a plant grow over Jonah. It shaded his head and helped him feel better. Jonah was very happy about the plant.
The next day at dawn, God sent a worm. The worm ate the plant, and the plant died.
When the sun came up, God sent a hot east wind. The sun beat down on Jonah's head. He felt very weak. He wanted to die. He said, "It is better for me to die than to live."
The LORD said, "Do you have a good reason to be angry about the plant?" Jonah said, "I am angry enough to die."
The LORD said, "You cared about the plant. You did not work for it or grow it. It grew in one night and died in one night.
Should I not care about Nineveh, that big city? More than 120,000 people live there. They do not know right from left. There are many animals too."
This is the word of the LORD that came to Micah from Moresheth. It came in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. Micah saw it about Samaria and Jerusalem.
Listen, all you peoples! Listen, earth and everything in it! The Lord the LORD will be a witness against you. He is in His holy temple.
Look! The LORD is coming from His place. He will come down and walk on the high places of the earth.
The mountains will melt under Him. The valleys will split open. They will be like wax in front of fire. They will be like water running down a hill.
All this is because of the sin of Jacob and the sins of Israel. What is the sin of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? What is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
So I will make Samaria a pile of rocks in a field. It will be a place to plant grape vines. I will pour its stones into the valley. I will show its foundations.

All its carved statues will be smashed. All the things it got for sin will be burned in fire. I will destroy all its idols. She got them with money from selling herself, and that money will go back to that kind of life.
Because of this I will cry and wail. I will walk barefoot and with no clothes. I will cry like a wild dog and mourn like an owl.
Her wound will not heal. It has reached Judah. It has reached the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem.
Do not tell this in Gath. Do not cry at all. In Beth-le-aphrah, roll in the dust.
Pass on, people of Shaphir, in shame and with no clothes. The people of Zaanan do not go out. The people of Beth-ezel mourn. He will take away its help from you.
The people of Maroth wait for good. But bad has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
Tie the chariot to the fast horse, people of Lachish. She was the first to lead Zion's people into sin. The wrongs of Israel were found in you.
So you will give goodbye gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will trick the kings of Israel.
I will bring another enemy against you, people of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
Shave your head and cut off your hair for the children you love. Make your bald spot as wide as an eagle's. They have gone far away from you.
Trouble is coming for people who plan bad things and do wrong while they are in bed. When morning comes, they do those bad things because they have the power to do them.
They want fields and take them. They want houses and take them too. They are mean to a man and his home. They take away a man's family land.
So the LORD says, “I am planning trouble for this family. You cannot get out of it. You will not walk with proud heads anymore, because it will be a bad time.”
In that day people will make fun of you. They will cry a sad song: “We are ruined! He has changed the share of my people. How He took it from me! He gave our fields to people who turned against us.”
So you will not have anyone among the LORD's people to divide the land.
They say, “Do not preach!” They say, “Do not preach those things. We will not be shamed.”
Should people say, “House of Jacob, is the Spirit of the LORD angry? Are these His doings?” Do not My words help the person who does right?
But lately My people have stood up like an enemy. You take the nice coat off a peaceful man who walks by, like men coming home from war.
You drive the women of My people out of their nice homes. You take away My blessing from their children forever.
Get up and go! This is not your resting place, because it is not clean. It will destroy you in a terrible way.
If a man who talks empty words comes and lies, “I will preach to you about wine and beer,” he would be just the preacher for these people!
I will surely gather all of you, people of Jacob. I will surely bring together the rest of Israel. I will put them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in a field. There will be many people.
The one who breaks open the way will go up before them. They will break out, go through the gate, and go out. Their King will go before them, and the LORD will lead them.
Then I said, "Listen, leaders of Jacob! You rulers of Israel's people, should you not know what is right?
You hate good and love what is bad. You tear the skin off My people and the meat from their bones.
You eat My people's meat. You pull their skin off. You break their bones and chop them up like meat for a pot, like meat in a big pot."
Then they will cry to the the LORD, but He will not answer them. At that time He will turn away from them, because they did such bad things.
This is what the the LORD says about the prophets who lead My people the wrong way. They say, "Peace," but they bite with their teeth. They start a fight with anyone who does not feed them.
So night will come for you with no visions. It will be dark for you, and you will not be able to tell the future. The sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will turn black over them.
The seers will be ashamed. The people who tell the future will be put to shame. They will all cover their mouths, because God will not answer them.
But I am filled with power by the Spirit of the the LORD. I have justice and strength. I can tell Jacob about his wrongs and Israel about his sin.
Now listen to this, leaders of Jacob's family and rulers of Israel's people. You hate what is right. You twist everything that is good.
You build Zion with blood. You build Jerusalem with sin.

Her leaders decide cases for money. Her priests teach for pay. Her prophets tell the future for silver. Yet they lean on the the LORD and say, "Isn't the the LORD with us? No bad thing will come on us."
So because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field. Jerusalem will become a pile of rocks. The hill of the the LORD's house will become a forest.
In the last days, the mountain where the house of the LORD stands will be higher than all the other mountains. It will stand above the hills. People from many lands will come to it.

Many nations will come. They will say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of Jacob's God. He will teach us His ways, and we will walk in His paths." God's law will go out from Zion. The word of the LORD will go out from Jerusalem.

He will settle fights between many people. He will decide for strong nations far away. They will hammer their swords into farm tools. They will turn their spears into tools to trim trees. One nation will not fight another. They will not learn war anymore.
Each man will sit under his grapevine and fig tree. No one will scare him. The LORD All-Powerful has spoken.
All people follow their own gods. But we will follow the LORD our God forever and ever.
On that day, says the LORD, "I will gather the ones who limp. I will bring together the ones sent away. I will bring back the ones I hurt.
I will make the ones who limp into the people who are left. I will make the ones sent far away into a strong nation. The LORD will rule over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever."
And you, tower near the sheep, hill of Zion's people, your old rule will come back to you. The kingdom will come to Jerusalem's people.
Why do you cry so loud now? Is there no king in you? Has your wise helper died? Pain has grabbed you like a woman having a baby.

Twist and groan, Zion's daughter, like a woman having a baby. Now you will leave the city. You will live in the field. You will go all the way to Babylon. There you will be saved. There the LORD will buy you back from your enemies.
Now many nations have come together against you. They say, "Let her be ruined, and let us look at Zion."
But they do not know what the LORD is thinking. They do not understand His plan. He has gathered them like grain to be beaten.

Get up and beat them, Zion's daughter, for I will make your horn like iron. I will make your feet like bronze. You will crush many people. I will give their gains to the LORD and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
Now, city of soldiers, gather your troops. We are under attack. They hit Israel's leader on the cheek with a stick.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, you are small among Judah's family groups. Yet from you will come for Me a ruler for Israel. His beginnings are from long ago, from days of old.
So He will give them up until she who is in labor gives birth. Then the rest of His brothers will return to the people of Israel.
He will stand and care for His people with the strength of the LORD, and with the glory of the name of the LORD His God. They will live safely, because now He will be great to the ends of the earth.
This One will bring peace. When the Assyrian comes into our land and walks in our palaces, we will raise up seven shepherds and eight leaders against him.
They will rule Assyria with the sword, and they will enter Nimrod's land through its gates. He will save us from the Assyrian when he comes into our land and steps over our border.
