The rest of Jacob's people will be among many nations like dew from the LORD, like rain on the grass. It does not wait for people, and people cannot control it.
Jacob's people left will be among the nations, among many peoples, like a lion among forest animals, like a young lion among sheep. It will crush and tear, and no one will save them.
Your hand will be raised over your enemies, and all your foes will be destroyed.
On that day, says the LORD, I will take away your horses and destroy your chariots.
I will destroy the cities of your land and tear down all your forts.
I will take away your magic, and you will have no more fortune tellers.
I will destroy your carved idols and your stone pillars, and you will not worship what your hands made anymore.
I will pull up your idols from among you and destroy your cities.
I will punish the nations that did not listen, in anger and fury.
The LORD says, "Get up and speak to the mountains. Let the hills hear you."
Mountains, listen to the LORD's case. Strong parts of the earth, listen. The LORD has a case against His people. He will talk with Israel.
"My people, what did I do to you? How did I wear you out? Tell Me if I did wrong.
I brought you up from Egypt. I set you free from being slaves. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead you.

My people, remember what Balak, the king of Moab, planned. Remember what Balaam son of Beor said back to him. Remember the trip from Shittim to Gilgal. Then you will know the good things the LORD has done."
"What should I bring to the LORD? How should I bow to the God of heaven? Should I bring animals burned on the altar? Should I bring calves one year old?
Will the LORD be happy with thousands of rams? Will He be happy with lots of oil? Should I give my first child for my wrongs? Should I give my own child for my sin?"
God has shown you, people, what is good. What does the LORD want from you? He wants you to do what is right. He wants you to love kindness. He wants you to walk with your God in a humble way.
The LORD calls to the city. Wisdom respects Your name. He says, "Listen to the punishment and to the One who sent it."
Is there still stolen money in a bad person's house? Are there short measures that are cursed?
Can I say a person is good if he uses bad scales? Can I say he is good if he uses false weights?
The rich people in the city hurt others. The people who live there tell lies. Their words are tricky.
"So I will punish you. I will make you empty because of your sins.
You will eat but not be full. You will still be hungry inside. You will try to save things, but you will lose them. What you save, I will give to the sword.
You will plant but not pick. You will press olives but not use the oil. You will press grapes but not drink the wine.

You have kept Omri's rules. You have done all the bad ways of Ahab's house. You have followed their plans. So I will make you empty. People will laugh at the people who live there. You will carry the shame of My people."
How sad for me! I am like someone picking summer fruit, like grapes left after harvest. There is no bunch to eat. I am hungry for the first good fruit.
Good people are gone from the land. No one does right. They all wait to hurt others. They trap each other.
They are skilled at doing wrong. The ruler asks for gifts. The judge takes bribes. The powerful man says what he wants. They work together to do wrong.
Even the best of them is like a thorn bush. The most honest one is sharper than thorns. The day you set has come. Now they are confused.
Do not trust a friend. Do not trust a close friend. Watch what you say to the one who lies in your arms.
A son shames his father. A daughter turns against her mother. A wife turns against her mother-in-law. A man's enemies are in his own home.
But I will look to the the LORD. I will wait for God, who saves me. My God will hear me.
Do not laugh at me, my enemy. I may fall, but I will get up. I may sit in the dark, but the the LORD will be my light.
I will take the the LORD's anger because I sinned against Him. He will stand up for me and make things right. He will bring me into the light. I will see that He is right.
My enemy will see it and be ashamed. She said, "Where is the the LORD your God?" My eyes will see her. She will be stepped on like mud in the street.
The day will come when your walls are built again. On that day, your land will get bigger.
In that day, people will come to you from Assyria, from strong cities, from walled cities to the river, from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
But the land will be empty because of the people who live there. It will be because of what they have done.
Take care of your people with your stick. They are your flock. They live alone in the woods, in Carmel. Let them eat in Bashan and Gilead, like in the old days.
Like in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them amazing things.
The nations will see and be ashamed of their strength. They will put their hands over their mouths. Their ears will be deaf.
They will lick the dust like a snake. They will crawl out of their holes like worms. They will shake with fear because of the the LORD our God. They will be afraid of You.
Who is a God like You? You forgive sin. You let go of the wrongs of the people who are left of Your own people. You do not stay angry forever, because You love to show mercy.
He will come back and have mercy on us. He will defeat our sins. You will throw all their sins into the deep sea.
You will keep Your promise to Jacob. You will show mercy to Abraham. You promised this to our fathers long ago.
This is a message about Nineveh. It is the book of Nahum's vision. He was from Elkosh.
The LORD is a jealous God who punishes. The LORD punishes and is full of anger. The LORD punishes His enemies. He keeps His anger for those who hate Him.
The LORD is slow to get angry, but He is very strong. The LORD will not let guilty people go free. He walks in the storm and the wind. The clouds are like dust under His feet.
He tells the sea to dry up, and it does. He dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel dry up. The flowers of Lebanon fade.
The mountains shake before Him. The hills melt away. The earth trembles when He is near. The whole world and everyone in it shakes too.
Who can stand before His anger? Who can live through His hot anger? His anger pours out like fire. Rocks break apart before Him.
The LORD is good. He is a safe place when trouble comes. He takes care of people who trust in Him.
But He will destroy Nineveh with a huge flood. He will chase His enemies into darkness.
What do you plan against the LORD? He will destroy it. Trouble will not come again.
They will get tangled in thorns. They will be drunk with their wine. They will burn up like dry grass.
Someone from you, Nineveh, planned evil against the LORD. He made bad plans.
The LORD says, "Even if they have many friends and are strong, they will be destroyed and disappear. I hurt you, Judah, but I will not hurt you again.
Now I will take their heavy load off your neck. I will break the chains that hold you."
The LORD has given a command about you, Nineveh. He says, "Your name will not last. I will destroy the carved idols and metal gods in your temple. I will dig your grave, because you are worthless."

Look! On the mountains, someone is coming with good news. He brings peace. Celebrate your special days, Judah. Keep your promises. The worthless people will never attack you again. They will be completely destroyed.
An enemy is coming to attack you. Guard your walls. Watch the road. Get ready. Gather all your strength.
For the LORD will make Jacob great again, like Israel. Enemies broke them and ruined their grapevines.
His strong soldiers' shields are red. His brave men wear red. The chariots shine like fire when they are ready. The spears are raised.
The chariots race through the streets. They rush around the squares. They look like torches. They flash like lightning.
He calls his leaders. They trip as they run. They hurry to the wall. A shield is set up.
The river gates open. The palace falls down.
It is decided that the city will be taken away. Its young women cry like doves. They beat their chests.
Nineveh has been like a pool of water for a long time. Now its people run away. "Stop! Stop!" they shout, but no one stops.
Take the silver! Take the gold! There is no end to the riches. There are many precious things.
Empty! Empty and ruined! Hearts melt. Knees shake. Bodies tremble. Every face turns pale.
Where is the lions' den? Where did the young lions eat? The lion and lioness walked there with their cubs. Nothing scared them.
The lion killed enough for his cubs. He caught food for his lionesses. He filled his caves with food. His dens were full of torn meat.

Look, I am against you, says the LORD of Armies. I will burn your chariots in smoke. A sword will eat your young lions. I will cut off your food from the land. No one will hear your messengers anymore.
How terrible for the city of blood! It is full of lies. It is full of stolen things. It never stops hurting people.
Whips crack. Wheels rumble. Horses run fast. Chariots jump.
Horsemen charge. Swords flash. Spears shine. Many people die. Dead bodies pile up. There is no end to them. People trip over the dead.
This will happen because the city acted like a woman who sells herself. She looked pretty. She used magic. She tricked nations and families.
“I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies. “I will show your shame to the nations. I will show your shame to the kingdoms.”
“I will throw garbage on you. I will treat you as worthless. I will make people stare at you.”
Everyone who sees you will turn away. They will say, “Nineveh is destroyed! Who will feel sorry for her? Who will comfort her?”
Are you better than Thebes? Thebes sat by the Nile River. Water was all around it. The sea was like a wall around it.
Cush and Egypt made it strong. Put and Libya helped it. Their help had no end.
But Thebes was taken away. Its people became slaves. Its babies were killed in the streets. Soldiers drew lots for its leaders. Its important men were tied up in chains.
You will be like a drunk person. You will try to hide. You will look for a safe place from your enemies.
Your strong cities are like fig trees with ripe figs. If someone shakes them, the figs fall right into his mouth.
Your people are weak and afraid. Your gates stand open to your enemies. Fire has burned your gate bars.
Store water for the attack. Make your forts strong. Go into the mud and mix clay. Hold the brick mold.
There fire will burn you. The sword will cut you down. It will eat you up like locusts eat plants. Even if you become as many as locusts or grasshoppers, it will not save you.
You have more traders than stars in the sky. But like locusts, they strip everything and fly away.
Your guards are like locusts. Your leaders are like swarms of locusts. They sit in the walls on a cold day. When the sun comes up, they fly away. No one knows where they go.
King of Assyria, your leaders are asleep. Your nobles sleep too. Your people are scattered on the mountains. No one gathers them.
No one can heal your wound. Your injury will kill you. Everyone who hears about you claps their hands. Who has not suffered from your endless cruelty?
This is the hard message that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
"How long, the LORD, must I call and You not hear? I cry to You, 'So much violence!' but You do not save.
Why do You make me see bad things? Why do You look at trouble? Robbery and violence are before me. People fight and argue.
So God's law is weak. Justice does not last. Bad people trap good people. So justice comes out wrong."
"Look at the nations. Watch them. Be very amazed! I will do something in your days that you will not believe, even if someone tells you.
I am bringing the Chaldeans. They are mean and fast. They march across the land to take homes that are not theirs.
They are scary and frightening. They make their own rules and honor.
Their horses run faster than leopards. They are fiercer than wolves at night. Their horse riders spread out. They come from far away. They rush like an eagle that wants to eat.
They all come ready to hurt people. They sweep in like a hot east wind. They gather prisoners like sand.
They laugh at kings and leaders. They make fun of every strong city. They pile up dirt and take the city.
Then they move on. They are guilty. They worship their own strength as a god."
"Have You not been here since the beginning, the LORD? My God, my Holy One, we will not die. You chose them to judge, the LORD. Mighty God, You set them to correct people.
Your eyes are too pure to look at evil. You cannot look at wrong. Why do You look at cheaters? Why are You quiet when bad people destroy people better than them?
You make people like fish in the sea, like crawling things with no leader.
They pull them all up with a hook. They catch them in a net. They gather them in a fishing net. So they are happy and glad.
So they offer gifts to their net. They burn incense to their fishing net. Their net gives them plenty. Their food is rich.
Will they keep emptying their net? Will they keep killing nations and not show mercy?"
I will stand at my watch. I will stay on the wall. I will look to see what He will say to me. I will see how I should answer my complaint.
The LORD answered me. He said, “Write down the vision. Make it clear on tablets. Then a runner can read it as he runs.
The vision will wait for its time. It tells about the end. It will not lie. If it is slow, wait for it. It will come for sure. It will not be late.
See, he is proud. He is not right inside. But a good person will live by faith.
“Wine tricks him. He is proud and never rests. He is as greedy as the grave. Death is never full. He gathers all nations to himself. He collects all peoples.

“Will not all these people make fun of him with mocking words? They will say that trouble is coming to the one who takes things that are not his. They will ask how long he will pile them up. They will say he loads himself with debts.
Will not the people you owe money to rise up suddenly? Then you will be afraid. They will take your things.
You took things from many nations. So the people left will take things from you. This is because you killed people and hurt the land, the city, and the people who live there.
“Trouble is coming to the one who builds his house with stolen gain and puts his home high up to be safe from trouble.
You planned shame for your house when you hurt many peoples. You have sinned against your own life.
The stones in the wall will cry out. The wooden beams will answer them.
“Trouble is coming to the one who builds a city with blood and starts a town with wrong.
Look, the the LORD of Armies has said this: people work only to feed the fire. Nations tire themselves out for nothing.
The earth will be full of people knowing the the LORD's glory. It will be like water covering the sea.
“Trouble is coming to the one who makes his neighbor drink. He pours out his anger and gets them drunk. Then he looks at their shame.
You will be full of shame, not glory. You will drink too, and show your shame. The LORD's cup of punishment will come to you. Your glory will be covered with shame.
The harm you did to Lebanon will cover you. The hurt to the animals will scare you. This is because you killed people and hurt the land, the city, and the people who live there.
“What good is an idol? The one who made it shaped it. It is a metal statue that teaches lies. The maker trusts in what he made. But the idol cannot speak.
Trouble is coming to the one who tells wood to wake up and a silent stone to get up. Can it teach? Look, it is covered with gold and silver. But it has no breath in it.
“But the the LORD is in His holy temple. Let all the earth be quiet before Him.”
This is a prayer by Habakkuk the prophet.
The LORD, I heard Your report. I was afraid. The LORD, make Your work strong again during these years. Show it to people during these years. When You are angry, remember to be kind.
God comes from Teman. The Holy One comes from Mount Paran. His glory covers the sky. The earth is full of His praise.
His light shines like the sun. Rays come from His hand. His power is hidden there.
Sickness goes before Him. Fever follows at His feet.
He stood and measured the earth. He looked and made nations shake. The old mountains broke apart. The old hills bowed down. His ways last forever.
I saw the tents of Cushan in trouble. The curtains of Midian shook.
Were You angry with the rivers, the LORD? Was Your anger against the rivers? Did You ride on Your horses? Did Your chariots bring help?
You took out Your bow. You called for the arrows You promised. You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw You and shook. A flood of water passed by. The deep sea cried out. It raised its hands high.
The sun and moon stood still in the sky. Your arrows shone like light. Your spear flashed brightly.
You marched across the land in anger. You crushed the nations.
You came to save Your people. You came to save Your chosen one. You crushed the head of the wicked house. You laid it open from top to bottom.
You pierced the enemy leaders with their own arrows. They stormed out to scatter me. They were happy, like people who secretly hurt the poor.
You walked through the sea with Your horses. The great waters piled up.

I heard this, and my body shook. My lips trembled at the sound. My bones felt weak. I shook all over. I will rest in the day of trouble. The enemy will come against the people. He will attack them with his army.

Even if the fig tree does not bloom, and the vines have no grapes, and the olive trees give no oil, and the fields grow no food, and the sheep are gone from the pen, and there are no cows in the stalls.
Yet I will be glad in the LORD. I will rejoice in God who saves me.
The LORD God is my strength. He makes my feet like a deer's feet. He makes me walk on high places. For the music leader, with stringed instruments.

This is the message from the LORD that came to Zephaniah. He was the son of Cushi, who was the son of Gedaliah, who was the son of Amariah, who was the son of Hezekiah. This happened when Josiah, son of Amon, was king of Judah.

The the LORD says, "I will take away everything from the earth. I will take away people and animals. I will take away the birds in the sky and the fish in the sea. I will remove the things that make people trip into sin, and I will remove bad people. I will cut people off from the earth," says the the LORD.

The the LORD says, "I will punish Judah and all who live in Jerusalem. I will remove every sign of Baal worship from this place. I will remove the names of the false priests and the other priests. I will remove people who bow on roofs to worship the stars in the sky. I will remove people who bow down and make promises to the the LORD, but also make promises to their false king. I will remove people who turn away from following the the LORD. They do not look for the the LORD or ask Him for help."
Be quiet before the Lord the LORD, because the Day of the the LORD is near. The the LORD has made a special meal ready. He has set it apart for His guests.

The the LORD says, "On the Day of the the LORD's sacrifice, I will punish the leaders and the king's sons. I will punish everyone who wears foreign clothes. On that day, I will punish everyone who jumps over the doorstep. They fill their master's house with hurt and lies."
The the LORD says, "On that day, there will be a loud cry from the Fish Gate. There will be a sad wail from the second part of the city. There will be a loud crash from the hills."
Cry out, people who live in the Hollow! All the traders are gone. Everyone who counted silver is cut off.

The the LORD says, "At that time, I will search Jerusalem with lamps. I will punish the men who sit still and do not care. They say in their hearts, 'The the LORD will not do anything, good or bad.' Their money will be taken. Their houses will be destroyed. They will build houses but not live in them. They will plant grape fields but not drink the wine."
The great Day of the the LORD is near. It is very near and coming fast. Listen! On the Day of the the LORD, there will be a bitter cry. There, the warrior will shout.

That day is a day of anger. It is a day of trouble and pain. It is a day of ruin and empty places. It is a day of darkness and gloom. It is a day of clouds and blackness. It is a day of trumpets and battle cries. It will come against strong cities and high towers.

The the LORD says, "I will bring so much trouble on people that they will walk like blind people, because they sinned against the the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust. Their bodies will be like trash. Their silver and gold will not save them on the Day of the the LORD's anger. The whole earth will be burned up by the fire of His jealousy. He will quickly end the lives of everyone on earth."
Gather together. Gather, people who feel no shame.
Do this before the command takes effect. Do this before the day blows away like straw. Do this before the LORD's hot anger comes on you. Do this before the day of the LORD comes on you.
Look for the LORD, all you humble people of the land who do what He says is right. Look for what is right. Try to be humble. Maybe you will be safe on the day of the LORD.
Gaza will be empty. Ashkelon will be ruins. Ashdod will be pushed out at noon. Ekron will be pulled up.
Oh no, people who live by the sea, nation of the Cherethites! The LORD's word is against you, O Canaan, land of the Philistines: "I will destroy you, and no one will stay."
The land by the sea will become fields. Shepherds will have wells. Sheep will have pens.

The coast will belong to the people left from Judah's family. They will feed their sheep there. In the evening they will lie down in Ashkelon's houses. For the LORD their God will care for them and bring back the ones taken away.
"I have heard Moab make fun of My people. I have heard the Ammonites say mean things. They made fun of My people and bragged about their land."

"So, as sure as I live," says the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, "Moab will be like Sodom. The Ammonites will be like Gomorrah. They will be full of weeds and salt pits. They will be empty forever. My people who are left will take their things. The rest of My nation will own their land."
"This will happen to them because they were proud. They made fun of and bragged against the people of the LORD of Armies."
The LORD will make them afraid. He will make all the gods of the earth weak. Then every nation will bow to Him. Each person will worship in their own place, even by the far seas.
"You too, people of Cush, will be killed by My sword."
He will reach out His hand against the north. He will destroy Assyria. He will make Nineveh an empty, dry place like a desert.

Herds will lie down in the middle of it. Animals from many nations will be there. Owls and screech owls will sleep on its pillars. Their calls will sound from the windows. Broken stones will be in the doorways. He will show the cedar beams.

This is the happy city that lived without fear. It said in its heart, "I am the only one. No one else is like me." Now it is a ruin. Wild animals live there. Everyone who passes by hisses and shakes his fist.
Trouble is coming to the city that hurts people. It fights back and is dirty.
She does not listen. She will not learn. She does not trust the the LORD. She does not come close to her God.
Her leaders roar like lions. Her judges are like hungry wolves at night. They eat everything, so nothing is left by morning.
Her prophets are careless. They cannot be trusted. Her priests make holy things dirty. They break God's law.
But the the LORD is in the city. He does right. He does no wrong. Every morning He judges fairly. He never fails. But bad people are not ashamed.
I have cut down nations. I broke their strong towers. I made their streets empty. No one walks there. Their cities are ruined. No one lives there.
I said, "Surely you will fear Me and learn. Then your home will not be destroyed, and I will not take away all I planned for you." But they were quick to do bad things.

So wait for Me, says the the LORD. Wait for the day I stand up to judge. I have decided to gather nations and kingdoms. I will pour out My anger on them. My hot anger will burn. The whole earth will be eaten by the fire of My jealousy.
Then I will make people speak pure words. All of them will call on the the LORD's name and serve Him together.
People from far away, beyond the rivers of Cush, will worship Me. My scattered people will bring Me gifts.
On that day you will not be ashamed for the bad things you did against Me. I will take away the proud people who brag, and you will never again act proud on My holy mountain.
But I will leave humble and poor people in the city. They will trust in the the LORD's name.
The people left in Israel will not do wrong. They will not lie. No one will find lies in their mouths. They will eat and rest. No one will scare them.
Sing, people of Zion! Shout, Israel! Be happy and glad with all your heart, people of Jerusalem!
The LORD took away your punishment. He turned back your enemy. The LORD, the King of Israel, is with you, and you will not fear bad things anymore.
On that day people will say to Jerusalem, "Do not be afraid, Zion. Do not give up."
The LORD your God is with you. He is strong and saves. He will be glad over you and sing over you. He will calm you with His love.
I will take away those among you who are sad about the special feasts, so you will not be shamed.

Look, at that time I will punish all who hurt you. I will save the people who cannot walk. I will bring back the people who were sent away. I will make them famous and praised in all the earth. They were shamed there.

At that time I will bring you home. I will gather you. I will make you famous and praised among all the people of the earth. I will bring back the people who were taken away, and you will see it, says the the LORD.

On the first day of the sixth month, in the second year that Darius was king, the the LORD spoke through the prophet Haggai. He spoke to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the leader of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
The LORD All-Powerful says, "These people say, 'Now is not the time to build the house of the the LORD.'"
Then the the LORD spoke again through Haggai the prophet.
The LORD asked, "Is it time for you to live in nice houses while My house is still in ruins?
Think about how you are living.

You planted a lot, but you picked a little. You eat, but you are still hungry. You drink, but you are still thirsty. You wear clothes, but you are still cold. You earn money, but it goes into a bag with holes.
Think about how you are living.
Go up the mountain, bring wood, and build My house. Then I will be happy with it, and I will be honored, says the the LORD.
You hoped for a lot, but you got a little. I blew away what you brought home. Why? Because My house is still in ruins, while each of you runs to his own house.
So, because of you, I stopped the dew from the sky, and the ground stopped giving crops.
I called for dry weather on the land and the hills, on the grain, the new wine, the olive oil, and everything the ground grows. I called it on people, animals, and all your hard work."

Then Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the rest of the people listened to the the LORD their God. They also listened to Haggai the prophet, because the the LORD their God had sent him. And the people respected the the LORD.
Then Haggai, the the LORD's messenger, gave the the LORD's message to the people: "I am with you," says the the LORD.
So the the LORD gave Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the rest of the people new energy. They came and worked on the house of the the LORD All-Powerful, their God.
They started on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year that Darius was king.
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the LORD's message came to Haggai the prophet.
The LORD told him to say to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the leader of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the rest of the people,
"Who is left among you who saw this house in its first glory? How does it look to you now? Doesn't it seem like nothing to you?

But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, says the LORD. Get to work, for I am with you, says the LORD of Hosts.
I made this promise to you when you left Egypt. My Spirit is still with you. Do not be afraid."
The LORD of Hosts says, "In a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all the nations. The treasure all nations want will come. I will fill this house with glory.
The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine.
The glory of this house will be greater in the end than it was at first. In this place I will give peace," says the LORD of Hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the LORD's message came to Haggai the prophet.
The LORD of Hosts says, "Ask the priests about the law.
If a man carries holy meat in the fold of his coat, and that fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, will that food become holy?" The priests answered, "No."
Then Haggai said, "If someone who is unclean from touching a dead body touches any of these foods, will it become unclean?" The priests answered, "It will become unclean."
Then Haggai answered, "So it is with these people and this nation before Me, says the LORD. So it is with every work of their hands. What they offer there is unclean."
"Now think about this from today back to before any stone was laid on another stone in the LORD's house.
Before that, when someone came to a pile of grain that should have been twenty baskets, there were only ten. When someone came to the wine vat to get fifty jugs, there were only twenty.
I struck you with disease, mold, and hail in all your work. But you still did not turn to Me, says the LORD."
"Think about this from today on, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the LORD's house was started. Think about it.
Is the seed still in the barn? The vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not given fruit yet. But from today on, I will bless you."
Again on the twenty-fourth day of the month, the LORD's message came to Haggai. He said,
"Tell Zerubbabel, the leader of Judah, 'I will shake the heavens and the earth.'"

"I will turn kingdoms upside down. I will destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will turn over the chariots and their riders. The horses and their riders will fall, each by his brother's sword."
"On that day, says the LORD of Hosts, I will take you, My servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, says the LORD. I will make you like My special ring, for I have chosen you, says the LORD of Hosts."
In the eighth month of the second year of King Darius, the LORD spoke to the prophet Zechariah. Zechariah was the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo. The LORD said:
"The LORD was very angry with your fathers.
So tell them to come back to Me, and I will come back to them. That is what the LORD of Hosts says.
Do not be like your fathers. The old prophets told them to stop their bad ways and bad deeds, but they did not listen or pay attention to Me.
Where are your fathers now? Do the prophets live forever?

But My words and My rules, which I gave to My servants the prophets, caught up with your fathers. They turned back and said that the LORD of Hosts did to them just what He planned, because of their ways and their deeds."
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo.
I saw a vision at night. A man was riding a red horse. He stood among myrtle trees in a low place. Behind him were red, brown, and white horses.
I asked, "What are these, my lord?"The angel who talked with me said, "I will show you what they are."
The man standing among the myrtle trees answered, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to walk through the earth."
They answered the angel of the LORD who stood among the myrtle trees, "We have walked all through the earth. Look, all the earth is sitting still and at rest."
Then the angel of the LORD said, "O the LORD of Hosts, how long will You not show mercy to Jerusalem and the towns of Judah? You have been angry with them for seventy years."
The LORD answered the angel who talked with me. He gave him good and comforting words.
The angel who talked with me said, "Shout this message: The LORD of Hosts says He cares very much for Jerusalem and Zion.
He is very angry with the nations that feel safe. He was only a little angry, but they made things worse.
So the LORD says He has come back to Jerusalem with mercy. His house will be built there, says the LORD of Hosts. A measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.
Shout again: The LORD of Hosts says His towns will grow and do well again. The LORD will comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem again."
I looked up and saw four horns.
I asked the angel who talked with me, "What are these?"He answered, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
Then the LORD showed me four builders.

I asked, "What are these coming to do?"He answered, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, so no one could even lift his head. But these builders have come to scare those nations and knock down their power. They lifted their power against Judah to scatter it."
I looked up and saw a man. He had a measuring stick in his hand.
I asked him, "Where are you going?" He said, "I am going to measure Jerusalem. I want to see how wide and long it is."
Then the angel who was talking with me went out. Another angel came to meet him.
The other angel said, "Run and tell that young man, 'Jerusalem will be a city without walls. So many people and animals will live there.'"
"I will be a wall of fire around it," says the the LORD. "I will be its glory inside."
"Come! Come! Run away from the land in the north," says the the LORD. "I scattered you everywhere," says the the LORD.
"Come, Zion! Escape, you who live with Daughter Babylon!"
The The LORD of Hosts says, "After He has honored Me, He will send Me against the nations that robbed you—for whoever touches you touches what is most precious to Him—"
"I will surely raise My hand against them, so their own servants will take their things. Then you will know that the the LORD of Hosts has sent Me."
"Shout and be glad, Daughter Zion! For I am coming, and I will live among you," says the the LORD.
"In that day, many nations will join the the LORD and become My people. I will live among you, and you will know that the the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you."
The the LORD will take Judah as His part in the holy land, and He will choose Jerusalem again.
Be quiet before the the LORD, all people, because He is coming from His holy home.
The LORD showed me Joshua. He was the high priest. He stood before the angel of the LORD. Satan stood at Joshua's right side to blame him.
The LORD said to Satan, "The LORD says no to you, Satan! The LORD chose Jerusalem, so He says no to you! Isn't Joshua like a stick pulled from a fire?"
Joshua was wearing dirty clothes. He stood before the angel.
The angel said to the men standing there, "Take off his dirty clothes." Then he said to Joshua, "Look, I have taken away your sin. I will dress you in clean, beautiful clothes."
I said, "Put a clean turban on his head." So they put a clean turban on his head. They dressed him in clean clothes. The angel of the LORD stood there.
The angel of the LORD gave Joshua this message from the LORD:
"If you follow My ways and do what I ask, then you will be in charge of My house and My yards. I will let you walk with these who stand here." "
Listen, Joshua the high priest. You and your friends who sit before you are men who show what is coming. I am bringing My Servant, the Branch. "
Look at the stone I put before Joshua. One stone has seven eyes. I will carve writing on it, says the LORD of Hosts. I will take away the sin of this land in one day.
In that day, says the LORD of Hosts, each of you will invite your neighbor to sit under a vine and a fig tree."
The angel who had been talking to me came back. He woke me up like a man waking from sleep.
He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a gold lampstand. It has a bowl on top, and seven lamps on it.
There are seven spouts for the lamps on top, and two olive trees by it. One is on the right of the bowl, and one is on the left."
I asked the angel who was talking to me, "What are these, my lord?"
The angel who was talking to me answered, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
Then he answered, "This is what the LORD says to Zerubbabel: 'Not by strength and not by power, but by My Spirit,' says the LORD of Hosts.
Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel, you will become flat ground. He will bring out the top stone while people shout, 'Grace, grace to it!'"
Then The LORD's message came to me. It said,
"Zerubbabel's hands started this house, and his hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts sent me to you."
"Who looks down on small beginnings? These seven are the LORD's eyes. They look all over the earth. They will be glad when they see the measuring line in Zerubbabel's hand."
I asked him, "What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
I asked again, "What are these two olive branches next to the two gold pipes that pour out golden oil?"
He answered, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
He said, "These are the two men chosen by God. They stand by the Lord of all the earth."
Then I looked up and saw a scroll flying through the air.
The angel asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a flying scroll. It is twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

Then he said, "This is the curse that is going out over the whole earth. On one side it says every thief will be taken away. On the other side it says everyone who lies when they promise to tell the truth will be taken away."

"I will send it out," says the LORD of Hosts, "and it will go into the house of the thief and the house of the one who lies when they promise to tell the truth using My name. It will stay in that house and destroy it, along with its wood and stones."
Then the angel who was talking with me came forward and said, "Lift up your eyes and see what is coming."
I asked, "What is it?" He said, "It is a measuring basket." Then he said, "This is the wrong done all over the land."
Then a lead cover was lifted, and a woman was sitting inside the basket.
He said, "This is Evil." Then he pushed her down into the basket and put the lead cover over the opening.
Then I looked up and saw two women coming out. The wind was in their wings. They had wings like a stork's wings, and they lifted the basket up between heaven and earth.
I asked the angel who was talking with me, "Where are they taking the basket?"
He said, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar. When it is ready, it will be set there on its base."
I looked up again and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains.
The first chariot had red horses. The second had black horses.
The third had white horses. The fourth had spotted horses. All the horses were strong.
I asked the angel who was talking to me, "What are these, my lord?"
The angel said, "These are the four spirits of heaven. They are going out from where they stood before the Lord of all the earth."
The chariot with black horses goes to the north country. The white horses follow them. The spotted horses go to the south country.
The strong horses went out. They wanted to go and walk all over the earth. The LORD said, "Go and walk all over the earth." So they went.
Then He called to me and said, "Look, the ones going to the north country have brought peace to My Spirit there."
The word of the LORD came to me. He said,
"Take a gift from the people who came back from Babylon. Get it from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah. Go that same day to the house of Josiah, son of Zephaniah.
Take silver and gold and make a crown. Put it on the head of Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
Tell him, 'This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Here is a man whose name is the Branch. He will grow where He is and build the temple of the LORD.
Yes, He will build the temple of the LORD. He will be dressed in honor and will sit and rule on His throne. He will be a priest on His throne, and there will be peace between the two.'
The crown will be a reminder in the temple of the LORD. It will be for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen, son of Zephaniah.
People far away will come and build the temple of the LORD. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts sent me to you. This will happen if you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God."
In the fourth year that King Darius ruled, the LORD gave a message to Zechariah. It was on the fourth day of the ninth month, called Kislev.
People from the town of Bethel sent Sharezer, Regem-Melech, and their men. They wanted to ask the LORD to be kind to them.
They asked the priests in the LORD's house and the prophets, “Should I be sad and not eat in the fifth month, like I have done for many years?”
Then the LORD of Hosts gave me this message:
“Ask all the people and the priests: When you did not eat and were sad in the fifth and seventh months for seventy years, was it really for Me that you did it?
When you ate and drank, were you not doing it for yourselves?”

Are these not the words the LORD said through the old prophets? Back then, Jerusalem and the towns around it had people living in them. They were safe. The south country and the low hills also had people.
The LORD gave another message to Zechariah. He said,
“This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Be fair when you judge. Show love and kindness to each other.
Do not hurt widows or children with no parents. Do not hurt strangers or poor people. Do not think bad things about each other in your hearts.”
But they would not listen. They turned away and would not obey. They stopped their ears so they could not hear.
They made their hearts as hard as rock. They would not listen to God's law or to the words the LORD of Hosts sent by His Spirit through the old prophets. So the LORD of Hosts was very angry.
The LORD of Hosts says, “When I called, they did not listen. So when they call, I will not listen.”
“I sent them to live among nations they did not know. The land became empty after them. No one could travel through it or come back. They turned the good land into a waste.”
The word of the LORD of Hosts came to me. He said,
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: I am very jealous for Zion. Yes, I am jealous for her with great anger.
This is what the LORD says: I will come back to Zion and live in Jerusalem. Then Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth. The mountain of the LORD of Hosts will be called the Holy Mountain."
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Old men and old women will sit in the streets of Jerusalem again. Each one will have a walking stick in his hand because he is very old.
The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in them.
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: If this seems amazing to the people left alive, should it also seem amazing to Me?" says the LORD of Hosts.
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Look, I will save My people from the land in the east and from the land in the west.
I will bring them back. They will live in Jerusalem. They will be My people, and I will be their God. I will be true and do what is right."
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Let your hands be strong, you who hear these words now. These words came from the prophets who were there when the house of the LORD of Hosts was started.
Before those days, people and animals did not get paid for their work. There was no peace for anyone who went out or came in. I turned every person against his neighbor.
But now I will not treat the rest of this people the way I did before," says the LORD of Hosts.
"For the seed of peace will grow well. The grapevine will give its fruit. The land will give its food. The sky will give its dew. I will give all these things to the rest of this people.
You have been a curse among the nations, O people of Judah and Israel. In the same way, I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid. Let your hands be strong."
"For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: Just as I planned to hurt you when your fathers made Me angry, and I did not change My mind,
so now I have planned to do good to Jerusalem and the house of Judah. Do not be afraid."
"These are the things you must do: Speak the truth to each other. Give true and fair judgment in your city gates.
Do not plan evil in your hearts against your neighbor. Do not love to make false promises. I hate all these things," says the LORD.
The word of the LORD of Hosts came to me again. He said,

"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: The fasts in the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become times of joy and gladness for the people of Judah. They will be happy feasts. So love truth and peace."
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: People from many cities will still come.
The people of one city will go to another city and say, 'Let us go at once to ask the LORD to be kind to us. Let us seek the LORD of Hosts. I will go too.'
Many strong nations and peoples will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem. They will ask the LORD to be kind to them.
In those days, ten men from all kinds of nations and languages will hold the corner of a Jewish man's coat. They will say, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"
This is a message from the the LORD. His word is against the land of Hadrach. It will rest on Damascus. People everywhere and all the tribes of Israel look to the the LORD.
Hamath is next to it. Tyre and Sidon are very wise, but that will not help them.
Tyre built a strong fort for herself. She piled up silver like dust. She piled up gold like mud in the streets.
Look, the Lord will take her away. He will throw her riches into the sea. Fire will burn her up.
Ashkelon will see it and be afraid. Gaza will shake with pain. Ekron will lose hope. The king of Gaza will die. Ashkelon will be empty.
"People from many nations will live in Ashdod. I will end the pride of the Philistines.
I will take away the blood they eat and the bad things between their teeth. Then they too will belong to our God. They will be like a family group in Judah. Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
I will set up camp around My house to guard it from armies passing by. No one will trouble them again. I have seen this with My own eyes."
Be very happy, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your King is coming to you. He does what is right and saves people. He is gentle. He rides a donkey, a young donkey.

"I will take away war carts from Ephraim and horses from Jerusalem. I will break the war bow. I will speak peace to the nations. His rule will reach from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.
As for you, because of the blood of your promise, I will set your prisoners free from a pit with no water.
Come back to your safe place, prisoners who still have hope. Today I say I will give you twice as much.
I will bend Judah like a bow. I will fill it with Ephraim. I will stir up your sons, Zion, to fight your sons, Greece. I will make you like a strong man's sword."
The The LORD will appear above them. His arrow will shoot out like lightning. The Lord, the the LORD, will blow the trumpet. He will march in the storms from the south.
The The LORD of Hosts will guard them. They will destroy and conquer with sling stones. They will drink and shout like with wine. They will be as full as a bowl, like the corners of the altar.
On that day the the LORD their God will save them like a flock of sheep. They will be like shiny jewels in a crown over His land.
How good and beautiful they will be! Grain will make the young men grow strong. New wine will make the young women grow strong.
Ask the LORD for rain in spring. The LORD makes lightning. He gives rain to everyone. He makes grass grow in the fields.
Idols tell lies. Fortune tellers see false dreams. They say empty words to comfort people. So people wander like sheep. They suffer because they have no shepherd.
“My anger burns against the shepherds. I will punish the leaders. For the LORD of Armies has cared for His flock, the people of Judah. He makes them like His strong horse in war.
From Judah will come the cornerstone, the tent peg, the battle bow, and every ruler.
They will be like strong men in war. They will trample the enemy in the mud of the streets. They will fight because the LORD is with them. They will put the horsemen to shame.

“I will make the people of Judah strong. I will save the people of Joseph. I will bring them home because I care for them. They will be as if I never turned away from them. I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
The people of Ephraim will be like strong men. Their hearts will be glad, like wine makes people glad. Their children will see it and be glad. Their hearts will rejoice in the LORD.
I will whistle for them and gather them, because I have set them free. They will grow in number as they did before.
“I will scatter them among the nations. They will remember Me in faraway lands. They and their children will live and come home.
I will bring them back from Egypt. I will gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon. There will not be room enough for them.
They will pass through a sea of trouble. They will strike the waves of the sea. All the deep parts of the river will dry up. The pride of Assyria will fall. The power of Egypt will go away.
I will make them strong in the LORD. They will live to honor His name,” says the LORD.
Open your doors, Lebanon, so fire can eat your cedar trees.
Wail, cypress, because the cedar fell. The mighty trees are ruined. Wail, oaks of Bashan, because the thick forest came down.
Shepherds cry out, because their good land is gone. Young lions roar, because the Jordan’s thick bushes are ruined.
This is what the LORD my God says: “Shepherd the flock that is set to be killed.”
Their buyers kill them and are not guilty. Their sellers say, “Bless the LORD, I am rich!” Their shepherds do not feel sorry for them.

The LORD says, “I will not feel sorry for the people of this land anymore. Look, I will hand each person over to his neighbor and his king. They will ruin the land, and I will not save it from their hands.”
So I took care of the flock set to be killed, especially the poor sheep. I took two sticks. I called one Favor and the other Union. Then I took care of the sheep.
In one month I got rid of three shepherds. I was tired of them, and they hated me.
Then I said, “I will not be your shepherd. Let the dying die. Let the lost be lost. Let those left eat each other up.”
I took my stick called Favor and broke it. I did this to break the agreement I had made with all the nations.
It broke that day. The poor sheep who watched me knew it was the LORD’s word.
I said to them, “If it seems good to you, give me my pay. If not, keep it.” They weighed out my pay: thirty pieces of silver.
The LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter—the great price they put on me!” So I took the thirty silver coins and threw them to the potter in the LORD’s house.
Then I broke my second stick, Union. I did this to break the bond between Judah and Israel.
The LORD said to me, “Take the tools of a foolish shepherd again.

I am raising up a shepherd in this land. He will not look for lost sheep. He will not help young sheep. He will not heal hurt sheep. He will not feed strong sheep. He will eat the meat of fat sheep and tear off their hooves.
Trouble for the worthless shepherd who leaves the flock! A sword will hit his arm and right eye. His arm will dry up, and his right eye will go dark.”
This is a message from the LORD about Israel. The LORD, who spreads out the sky, lays the earth's base, and makes the human spirit inside a person, says: "
I will make Jerusalem like a cup that makes all the countries around it stumble. Judah will also be attacked. Enemies will surround Jerusalem. "
On that day, all the countries in the world will gather against her. I will make Jerusalem like a heavy stone. Everyone who tries to lift it will hurt themselves. "
On that day," declares the LORD, "I will make every horse panic and its rider go crazy. I will watch over Judah, but I will blind all the horses of the other countries."
Then Judah's leaders will say in their hearts, "The people of Jerusalem are strong. The LORD of Armies is their God." "

On that day I will make Judah's leaders like a fire in a pile of wood and like a torch in dry grain. They will burn up all the countries around them, on every side. But Jerusalem will stay safe in her place."
The LORD will save Judah's homes first. He does this so the honor of David's family and of Jerusalem's people will not be greater than Judah's.
On that day the LORD will protect the people who live in Jerusalem. The weakest among them will be like David. David's family will be like God, like the LORD's angel going before them. "
On that day I will destroy all the countries that come against Jerusalem. "

Then I will pour out on David's family and on the people of Jerusalem a spirit of kindness and prayer. They will look at Me, the One they hurt. They will cry for Him like people cry for an only child. They will be very sad for Him like people are sad for a firstborn son."
On that day the crying in Jerusalem will be as great as the crying at Hadad Rimmon in the valley of Megiddo.
The land will be sad. Each family will be by itself, and their wives by themselves. David's family and their wives will be by themselves. Nathan's family and their wives will be by themselves.
Levi's family and their wives will be by themselves. Shimei's family and their wives will be by themselves.
All the other families will be by themselves, and their wives by themselves.
On that day, a spring will open for David's family and for the people of Jerusalem. It will wash away their sin and make them clean.

On that day, says the LORD of Armies, "I will take away the names of the false gods from the land. People will not remember them anymore. I will also remove the false prophets and the bad spirit from the land."
If a man still says he is a prophet, his father and mother who had him will say, "You will not live, because you lied and said it was from the LORD." Then they will stab him.
On that day, people who say they are prophets will be ashamed of their visions. They will not wear a rough hair coat to trick people.
He will say, "I am not a prophet. I am a farmer. Someone made me a slave when I was young."
If someone asks him, "What are these cuts on your body?" He will answer, "I got them at my friends' house."
"Wake up, sword, against My Shepherd, against the man who is My friend," says the LORD of Armies. "Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will run away. I will punish the little ones too."
In all the land, says the LORD, two-thirds of the people will die, and one-third will be left.

I will bring that third part through the fire. I will make them pure like silver is made pure. I will test them like gold is tested. They will call on My name, and I will answer them. I will say, "They are My people." They will say, "The LORD is my God."
Look, a day for the LORD is coming. Your things will be taken and split up among you.

For I will bring all the nations to fight against Jerusalem. The city will be taken. Homes will be robbed. Women will be hurt. Half the people will be taken away. But the rest will still be in the city.
Then the LORD will go out and fight those nations. He will fight like He does on a day of war.

On that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The mountain will split in two from east to west. A very big valley will open. Half the mountain will move north, and half will move south.

You will run to the valley between My mountains. That valley will reach to Azal. You will run like you ran from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all His holy ones will come with Him.
On that day there will be no light. There will be no cold or frost.
It will be a special day that only the LORD knows. It will not be day or night. But in the evening there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out of Jerusalem. Half will go to the east sea, and half to the west sea. It will flow in summer and in winter.
The LORD will be King over the whole earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and His name will be one.

All the land will become flat from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will stay high where it is. It will stretch from the Benjamin Gate to the old gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's wine presses.
People will live there. There will never again be an order to wipe it out completely. Jerusalem will be safe.
This is the sickness the LORD will send on all the people who fight Jerusalem: Their bodies will rot while they stand. Their eyes will rot in their heads. Their tongues will rot in their mouths.
On that day the LORD will make them very afraid. Each person will grab another person's hand. One person's hand will be raised against another's hand.
Even Judah will fight in Jerusalem. The wealth of all the nations around will be gathered: gold, silver, and clothes in great amounts.
The same sickness will hit the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the animals in those camps.
Then all the people left from the nations that fought Jerusalem will go up every year to worship the King, the LORD of Armies, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
If any family on earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Armies, there will be no rain for them.
If the family of Egypt does not go up, the LORD will send on them the same sickness He sends on nations that do not go to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
This will be the punishment for Egypt and for all nations that do not go to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
On that day the bells on the horses will say, ‘Holy to the LORD.’

Every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Armies. People who bring sacrifices can take them and cook their offerings in them. There will no longer be any sellers in the LORD’s house on that day.
This is the heavy message the LORD gave to Israel through Malachi.
The LORD says, "I have loved you." But you ask, "How have You loved us?" The LORD says, "Was not Esau Jacob's brother? Yet I loved Jacob, and I hated Esau.
I made his mountains a wasteland, and I gave his land to wild animals."

Edom may say, "We have been crushed, but we will rebuild the ruins." But the LORD Almighty says, "They may build, but I will tear it down. People will call them the Wicked Land. They are the people the LORD is angry with forever."
You will see this with your own eyes and say, "Great is the LORD, even beyond Israel's borders!"

The LORD Almighty says, "A son honors his father, and a worker honors his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is My respect?" He says to the priests, "You show no respect for My name." But you ask, "How have we shown no respect for Your name?"
They did this by offering unclean food on My altar. But you ask, "How have we made You unclean?" The LORD says, "You did it by saying the LORD's table is not important."

The LORD Almighty says, "When you offer blind animals, is that not wrong? When you offer lame or sick animals, is that not wrong? Try giving them to your governor! Would he be happy with you? Would he accept you?"
"Now ask God to be kind to us. You caused this. Will He accept you?" says the LORD Almighty.
"I wish one of you would close the doors, so you would not light useless fires on My altar. I am not happy with you," says the LORD Almighty. "I will not accept any offering from your hands."

"My name will be great among the nations. From where the sun rises to where it sets, pure incense and clean offerings will be given to My name. My name will be great among the nations," says the LORD Almighty.
"But you treat it as unclean. You say, 'The Lord's table is unclean, and its food is not good.'"
"You also say, 'What a bother!' and you look down on it," says the LORD Almighty. "When you bring stolen, lame, or sick animals and offer them, should I accept them from your hands?" says the LORD.

"Cursed is the person who cheats. He has a good male animal in his flock and promises to give it, but then gives a sick animal to the Lord. I am a great King," says the LORD Almighty. "My name is feared among the nations."
"Now this command is for you priests.

If you do not listen, and if you do not care to honor My name," says the LORD of Hosts, "I will send a curse on you, and I will curse your blessings. Yes, I have already cursed them, because you do not take it to heart.
Look, I will punish your children. I will smear dung on your faces. It is the dung from your feast offerings. Then you will be thrown away with it.
Then you will know that I sent you this command. I did this so My agreement with Levi will last," says the LORD of Hosts.
"My agreement with him was for life and peace. I gave those to him. He had to respect Me. He did respect Me and honor My name.
He told the truth. He did not lie. He walked with Me in peace and did what was right. He helped many people stop doing wrong.
A priest's lips should keep knowledge. People should learn from him. He is a messenger from the LORD of Hosts."
"But you turned away from the right way. You led many people to do wrong. You ruined the agreement with Levi," says the LORD of Hosts.
"So I made people look down on you. I made you feel small in front of everyone. You did not follow My ways. You were unfair when you taught the law."
"Don't we all have one Father? Didn't one God make us? Why do we break promises to each other and ruin the agreement our fathers made?
Judah has broken promises. A terrible thing happened in Israel and Jerusalem. Judah has ruined the holy place the the LORD loves. Judah married a woman who worships a false god.
The The LORD will remove any man who does this from Jacob's people. Even if he brings an offering to the the LORD of Hosts, he will be cut off."
"Here is another thing you do. You cover the altar of the the LORD with tears. You cry and groan. He does not look at your offerings anymore. He does not accept them from your hands.
You ask, 'Why?' It is because the the LORD has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth. You broke your promise to her. She is your partner and the wife of your agreement.

Didn't the the LORD make them one? He gave them a share of His Spirit. What does God want? He wants children who follow Him. So guard yourselves in your spirit. Do not break your promise to the wife you married when you were young."
"For I hate divorce," says the the LORD, the God of Israel, "and I hate it when a man hurts his wife," says the the LORD of Hosts. "So guard yourselves in your spirit. Do not break your promise."

"You made the the LORD tired with your words. You ask, 'How did we make Him tired?' You say, 'Everyone who does bad things is good to the the LORD. He likes them.' Or you say, 'Where is the God who is fair?'"

"Look, I am sending My messenger. He will clear the way in front of Me. Then the Lord you look for will suddenly come to His temple. The messenger of the promise you want is coming," says the the LORD of Hosts.
"But who can live through the day He comes? Who can stand when He shows Himself? He is like a fire that cleans metal. He is like soap that washes clothes.
He will sit like one who cleans silver and makes it pure. He will make Levi's sons pure. He will clean them like gold and silver. Then they will bring gifts to the the LORD in the right way.
Then the gifts from Judah and Jerusalem will please the the LORD. They will be like they were long ago."

"Then I will come close to you to judge you. I will quickly speak against people who do magic, people who are not faithful in marriage, people who lie under oath, people who are mean to widows and children with no father, people who do not pay workers, and people who treat strangers unfairly. They do not fear Me," says the the LORD of Hosts.
"For I, the the LORD, do not change. That is why you, Jacob's children, are not destroyed."
"For a long time, you have turned away from My rules. You have not obeyed them. Come back to Me, and I will come back to you," says the the LORD of Hosts. "But you say, 'How can we come back?'
Can a person steal from God? But you are stealing from Me. But you ask, 'How are we stealing from You?' You are stealing from Me when you do not give your tithes and gifts.
So you are cursed, because all of you are robbing Me.

Bring all the tithe into the storehouse, so there will be food in My house. Test Me in this, says the the LORD of Hosts. I will open the sky for you and pour out so much blessing that you will not have room enough for it.
I will stop the pests that eat your crops. They will not destroy the food your land grows. Your grapevines in the field will not lose their fruit, says the the LORD of Hosts.
Then all the nations will say you are blessed, because your land will be a land people love, says the the LORD of Hosts."
"Your words have been mean things against Me," says the the LORD. "Yet you say, 'What have we said against You?'
You have said, 'It is useless to serve God. What good is it to obey His rules? Why should we act sad before the the LORD of Hosts?
So now we call proud people blessed. People who do wrong get rich. They even test God and get away with it.'"

Then the people who feared the the LORD talked with each other. The the LORD listened and heard them. A book to remember them was written in front of Him. It was for the people who feared the the LORD and honored His name.
"They will be Mine," says the the LORD of Hosts, "on the day I do this. They will be My special treasure. I will be kind to them, like a father is kind to his son who serves him.
Then you will see again the difference between good people and bad people, between people who serve God and people who do not."

The LORD of Armies says, "A day is coming that will burn like a hot oven. Proud people and people who do wrong will be like dry grass. The day that comes will burn them up. It will not leave a root or a branch.
But you who honor My name will see the sun of goodness rise. It will bring healing. You will go out and jump like young cows let out of a pen.
You will step on the bad people. They will be like ashes under the soles of your feet on the day I get ready," says the LORD of Armies.
"Remember the law that My servant Moses gave. I told him the rules and right ways for all Israel at Mount Horeb."
"Look, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and scary day of the LORD comes.
He will help fathers and children love each other again. Then I will not come and put a curse on the land."
This is the family history of Jesus Christ. He is the son of David. He is also the son of Abraham.
Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac was the father of Jacob. Jacob was the father of Judah and his brothers.
Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah. Their mother was Tamar. Perez was the father of Hezron. Hezron was the father of Ram.
Ram was the father of Amminadab. Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
Salmon was the father of Boaz. Boaz's mother was Rahab. Boaz was the father of Obed. Obed's mother was Ruth. Obed was the father of Jesse.
Jesse was the father of King David. David was the father of Solomon. Solomon's mother had been Uriah's wife.
Solomon was the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam was the father of Abijah. Abijah was the father of Asa.
Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat was the father of Joram. Joram was the father of Uzziah.
Uzziah was the father of Jotham. Jotham was the father of Ahaz. Ahaz was the father of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh. Manasseh was the father of Amon. Amon was the father of Josiah.
Josiah was the father of Jeconiah and his brothers. This was when the people were taken to Babylon.
After they were taken to Babylon, Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud. Abiud was the father of Eliakim. Eliakim was the father of Azor.
Azor was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Achim. Achim was the father of Eliud.
Eliud was the father of Eleazar. Eleazar was the father of Matthan. Matthan was the father of Jacob.
Jacob was the father of Joseph. Joseph was the husband of Mary. Mary gave birth to Jesus, who is called the Christ.
So there were 14 generations from Abraham to David. There were 14 from David to the time the people were taken to Babylon. And there were 14 from that time to the Christ.

This is how Jesus Christ was born. Mary was promised to Joseph to be married. But before they lived together as husband and wife, people learned she was going to have a baby. The baby was from the Holy Spirit.
Joseph was to be her husband. He was a good man. He did not want to shame her in front of people. So he planned to break the engagement quietly.

While Joseph was thinking about this, an angel of the Lord came to him in a dream. The angel said, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The baby in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will have a son. You will call Him Jesus. He will save His people from their sins."
All this happened to make come true what the Lord had said through His prophet.
"The virgin will have a baby. She will have a son. They will call Him Immanuel." Immanuel means "God is with us."
When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had told him. He took Mary as his wife.
But he did not live with her as a husband until she had the baby. He named the baby Jesus.
Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea. This was when King Herod ruled. Wise men came from the east to Jerusalem.
They asked, “Where is the new King of the Jews? We saw His star in the east. We came to worship Him.”
King Herod heard this. He was upset. All Jerusalem was upset too.
He called the chief priests and teachers of the law. He asked them where the Christ would be born.
They said, “In Bethlehem in Judea. This is what the prophet wrote:
‘You, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are not the smallest among Judah’s leaders. A ruler will come from you. He will take care of My people Israel.’”
Then Herod called the wise men in secret. He asked them exactly when the star appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem. He said, “Go and look carefully for the child. When you find Him, tell me. Then I can come and worship Him too.”
The wise men heard the king. They went. The star they had seen in the east went ahead of them. It stopped over the place where the child was.
They were very happy when they saw the star.
They went into the house. They saw the child with His mother Mary. They bowed down and worshiped Him. They opened their gifts. They gave Him gold, incense, and myrrh.
God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod. So they went home another way.

After they left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. He said, “Get up. Take the child and His mother. Run away to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you. Herod is going to look for the child to kill Him.”
Joseph got up. He took the child and His mother at night. They went to Egypt.
They stayed there until Herod died. This happened to make true what the Lord said through the prophet: “I called My Son out of Egypt.”

Herod saw that the wise men had tricked him. He was very angry. He sent soldiers. They killed all the boys in Bethlehem and nearby. The boys were two years old or younger. This matched the time the wise men told him.
Then the words of the prophet Jeremiah came true.
“People heard a voice in Ramah. There was crying and loud sadness. Rachel cried for her children. She would not be comforted, because they were gone.”
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt.
The angel said, “Get up. Take the child and His mother. Go to the land of Israel. The people who wanted to kill the child are dead.”
Joseph got up. He took the child and His mother. They went to Israel.
But he heard that Archelaus was king in Judea. Archelaus took his father Herod’s place. Joseph was afraid to go there. God warned him in a dream. So he went to Galilee.
He came and lived in a town called Nazareth. This made true what the prophets said: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
In those days, John the Baptist came to preach in the desert of Judea.
He said, "Turn from your sins, for God's kingdom in heaven is near."
This was the man Isaiah the prophet talked about when he said, "A voice calls out in the desert, 'Get the LORD's road ready. Make His paths straight.'"
John wore clothes made from camel hair. He had a leather belt around his waist. He ate bugs called locusts and wild honey.
People from Jerusalem, all of Judea, and the land around the Jordan River came to see him.
They told God they were sorry for their sins, and John baptized them in the Jordan River.
John saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to be baptized. He said to them, "You snakes! Who told you to run away from God's coming anger?
Do things that show you have changed your hearts.
Do not think you can say, 'We have Abraham as our father.' I tell you, God can make children for Abraham from these stones.
The axe is already at the roots of the trees. Every tree that does not make good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
I baptize you with water to show you are sorry. But the One coming after me is stronger than I am. I am not good enough to carry His shoes. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
He holds a tool to separate grain. He will clean the place where grain is separated and gather His wheat into the barn. But He will burn the husks with fire that never goes out."
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan River to be baptized by John.
John tried to stop Him. He said, "I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?"
Jesus answered, "Let it be this way now. It is right for us to do all that God wants." Then John let Him be baptized.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, He came up out of the water. Then the sky opened, and He saw God's Spirit coming down like a dove and landing on Him.
A voice from heaven said, "This is My beloved Son. I am very pleased with Him."
Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the desert to be tested by the devil.
He did not eat for forty days and forty nights. Then He was hungry.
The devil came to Him and said, "If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
Jesus answered, "It is written: 'People do not live on bread alone. They live on every word that comes from God's mouth.'"
Then the devil took Him to the holy city. He put Him on the highest part of the temple.

"If You are the Son of God," the devil said, "jump down. The Bible says, 'God will tell His angels to watch over You. They will hold You up with their hands, so You will not hit Your foot on a stone.'"
Jesus said, "It is also written, 'Do not test the Lord your God.'"
Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain. He showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
"I will give all this to You," the devil said, "if You bow down and worship me."
Jesus said, "Go away, Satan! It is written, 'Worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only.'"
Then the devil left Him. Angels came and helped Him.
When Jesus heard that John had been put in jail, He went to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum. That town is by the lake, in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali.
This happened to make true what the prophet Isaiah said:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, by the sea, across the Jordan, Galilee where the nations live.
The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light. Light has come to those who sat in the land of the shadow of death."
From then on, Jesus began to preach. He said, "Turn from your sins, because God's kingdom is near."
Jesus was walking by the Sea of Galilee. He saw two brothers, Simon (called Peter) and his brother Andrew. They were throwing a net into the lake, because they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, "Come, follow Me, and I will send you to fish for people."
Right away they left their nets and followed Him.
Jesus went on and saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, fixing their nets. Jesus called them.
They left the boat and their father right away and followed Him.
Jesus traveled all over Galilee. He taught in their meeting places. He told the good news about God's kingdom. He healed all kinds of sickness and disease among the people.

People all over Syria heard about Him. They brought to Him everyone who was sick. Some had many kinds of diseases. Some were in great pain. Some had demons. Some had seizures. Some could not walk. He healed them all.
Big crowds followed Him from Galilee, the Ten Towns, Jerusalem, Judea, and the land across the Jordan.
When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on a mountain. He sat down, and His followers came to Him.
He opened His mouth and taught them. He said:
"Happy are people who know they need God, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
Happy are people who cry, because they will be comforted.
Happy are people who are gentle, because they will receive the earth.
Happy are people who are hungry and thirsty for what is right, because they will be filled.
Happy are people who show mercy, because they will get mercy.
Happy are people with clean hearts, because they will see God.
Happy are people who make peace, because they will be called God's children.
Happy are people who are hurt for doing right, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
"You are happy when people make fun of you, chase you, and say lies about you because of Me.
Be glad and jump for joy, because your reward in heaven is big. People did the same thing to the prophets before you."
"You are the salt of the earth. But if salt loses its taste, how can it be made salty again? It is not good for anything. It is thrown out and stepped on by people.
You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
People do not light a lamp and put it under a bowl. They put it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
In the same way, let your light shine before people, so they can see your good works and praise your Father in heaven."
"Do not think that I came to destroy the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to destroy them. I came to make them complete.
I tell you the truth: until heaven and earth pass away, not one small letter or part of a letter will pass from the Law until everything happens.

So anyone who breaks one of the least of these commands and teaches people to do that will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But anyone who does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
I tell you that unless your goodness is more than the goodness of the teachers of the law and the Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven."
