"You have heard that it was said to the people long ago, 'Do not murder.' Anyone who murders will be guilty in court.

But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be guilty in court. Anyone who calls his brother 'good-for-nothing' will be guilty before the council. Anyone who calls him 'fool' will be guilty and may be thrown into the fire of hell.
So if you are bringing your gift to the altar and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there in front of the altar. First go and make peace with your brother. Then come back and offer your gift.
Make peace quickly with the one who is against you while you are on the way. If not, he may hand you over to the judge. The judge may hand you over to the guard, and you may be thrown into prison.
I tell you the truth: you will not get out until you have paid the last small coin."
"You have heard that it was said, 'Do not commit adultery.'
But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to want her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
If your right eye makes you sin, take it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than to have your whole body thrown into hell.
If your right hand makes you sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than to have your whole body go into hell.
It was also said, 'Anyone who divorces his wife must give her a paper of divorce.'
But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual sin, causes her to commit adultery. And anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
"You have heard that it was said to the people long ago, 'Do not break your promises to the Lord, but keep your oaths to Him.'
But I tell you not to swear at all. Do not swear by heaven, because it is God's throne.
Do not swear by the earth, because it is His footstool. Do not swear by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.
Do not swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
Let your 'Yes' be 'Yes,' and your 'No' be 'No.' Anything more than this comes from the evil one."
"You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.'
But I tell you not to fight back against an evil person. If someone slaps you on the right cheek, turn the other cheek to him.
If someone wants to sue you and take your shirt, let him have your coat too.
If someone makes you go one mile, go with him two miles.
Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you."
"You have heard that it was said, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who hurt you.
Then you will be children of your Father in heaven. He makes His sun rise on bad people and good people. He sends rain on those who do right and those who do wrong.
If you love only those who love you, what reward do you get? Even tax collectors do that.
If you greet only your brothers, what are you doing more than others? Even people who do not know God do that.
So be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect."
Be careful not to do your good deeds in front of people just to be seen by them. If you do, your Father in heaven will not give you a reward.

So when you give to people in need, do not blow a trumpet before you, like the show-offs do in places of worship and on the streets. They want people to praise them. I tell you the truth, they already have their reward.
But when you give to someone in need, keep it a secret.
Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
And when you pray, do not be like the show-offs. They love to stand and pray in places of worship and on street corners so people can see them. I tell you the truth, they already have their reward.
But when you pray, go into your room, close your door, and pray to your Father, who cannot be seen. Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
When you pray, do not keep saying the same words over and over, like people who do not know God do. They think they will be heard because they use many words.
Do not be like them. Your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
So pray like this: "Our Father in heaven, may Your name be kept holy.
May Your kingdom come. May what You want be done on earth, just as it is in heaven.
Give us today the food we need.
Forgive us for the wrong things we have done, just as we forgive people who have wronged us.
And do not let us be tempted to do wrong. But save us from the evil one."
If you forgive other people when they do wrong to you, your Father in heaven will forgive you too.
But if you do not forgive them, your Father will not forgive your wrongs.
When you fast, do not look sad like the show-offs do. They make their faces look sad so people will see they are fasting. I tell you the truth, they already have their reward.
But when you fast, wash your face and put oil on your head.
Then no one will know you are fasting, except your Father, who cannot be seen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth. Moths and rust can destroy them, and thieves can break in and steal them.
Instead, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven. Moths and rust cannot destroy them there, and thieves cannot break in and steal them.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.
The eye is like a lamp for the body. So if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If the light in you is really darkness, how dark that is!
No one can serve two masters. He will hate one and love the other, or he will be loyal to one and look down on the other. You cannot serve both God and money.
So I tell you, do not worry about your life. Do not worry about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about what you will wear. Is life not more than food? Is the body not more than clothes?
Look at the birds in the sky. They do not plant seeds or gather crops or store food in barns. But your Father in heaven feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they are?
Can any of you add even one hour to his life by worrying?
And why do you worry about clothes? Look at how the wild flowers grow. They do not work or make clothes.
But I tell you, even King Solomon in all his glory was not dressed as well as one of these flowers.
If God dresses the grass of the field so well, and it is here today and gone tomorrow, will He not dress you even better? You have so little faith!
So do not worry. Do not say, "What will we eat?" or "What will we drink?" or "What will we wear?"
People who do not know God chase after all these things. But your Father in heaven knows you need them.
But put God's kingdom and His right way first. Then all these things will be given to you too.
So do not worry about tomorrow. Tomorrow will have its own worries. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
Do not judge, or you will be judged.
The way you judge others is the way you will be judged. The way you measure others is the way you will be measured.
Why do you look at the tiny speck in your brother's eye? You do not see the big board in your own eye.
How can you say to your brother, "Let me take the speck out of your eye," when you have a big board in your own eye?
You hypocrite! First take the big board out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
Do not give holy things to dogs. Do not throw your pearls to pigs. They may step on them, and then turn and hurt you.
Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and the door will be opened to you.
Everyone who asks receives. The one who seeks finds. The door is opened to the one who knocks.
Which of you, if your son asks for bread, would give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, would give him a snake?
If you are sinful but still know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!
So do for others what you want them to do for you. This is what the Law and the Prophets mean.
Go in through the narrow gate. The wide gate and the big road lead to ruin, and many people go that way.
But the small gate and the hard road lead to life, and only a few people find it.
Watch out for false prophets. They come to you looking like gentle sheep, but inside they are wild wolves.
You will know them by what they do. Do people pick grapes from thorn bushes? Do they pick figs from thistles?
In the same way, every good tree makes good fruit, but a bad tree makes bad fruit.
A good tree cannot make bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot make good fruit.
Every tree that does not make good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So you will know them by what they do.
Not everyone who says to Me, "Lord, Lord," will go into the kingdom of heaven. Only the one who does what My Father in heaven wants will go in.
Many will say to Me on that day, "Lord, Lord, did we not speak for You? Did we not drive out demons in Your name? Did we not do many powerful works in Your name?"
Then I will tell them clearly, "I never knew you. Go away from Me, you who do evil!"
So everyone who hears these words of Mine and does them is like a wise man who built his house on rock.
The rain came down, the streams rose, and the wind blew hard against that house. But it did not fall, because it was built on rock.
But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not do them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
The rain came down, the streams rose, and the wind blew hard against that house. It fell with a big crash.
When Jesus finished saying these things, the crowds were amazed at His teaching.
For He taught like one who had authority, not like their teachers of the law.
When Jesus came down from the mountain, many people followed Him.
A man with a skin disease came to Him. He knelt down and said, "Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean."
Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. He said, "I am willing. Be clean!" Right away the man's skin disease was gone.
Jesus said to him, "Do not tell anyone. But go and show yourself to the priest. Offer the gift that Moses told you to bring. This will be proof for them."
When Jesus went into Capernaum, a Roman army officer came to Him. He asked Jesus to help.
He said, "Lord, my servant is at home in bed. He cannot move, and he is in great pain."
Jesus said, "I will come and heal him."
The officer answered, "Lord, I am not good enough for You to come into my house. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed."
He said, "I am a man under orders too. I have soldiers under me. I tell one, 'Go,' and he goes. I tell another, 'Come,' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
Jesus was amazed when He heard this. He said to the people following Him, "I tell you the truth. I have not found faith like this in anyone in Israel.
I tell you, many people will come from east and west. They will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in God's kingdom in heaven.
But some people who should be in the kingdom will be thrown out into the dark. There they will cry and grind their teeth."
Jesus said to the officer, "Go home. It will happen just as you believed." And his servant was healed that same hour.
Jesus went to Peter's house. He saw Peter's mother-in-law in bed with a fever.
Jesus touched her hand. The fever left her. She got up and served Him.
That evening, people brought many who had evil spirits. Jesus spoke, and the spirits left. He healed all who were sick.
This happened to make true what the prophet Isaiah said: "He took our weaknesses and carried our sicknesses."
Jesus saw the crowd around Him. He told His followers to go to the other side of the sea.
A teacher of the law came to Him. He said, "Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go."
Jesus said, "Foxes have holes to live in. Birds have nests. But the Son of Man has no place to rest His head."
Another follower said to Him, "Lord, first let me go and bury my father."
Jesus said, "Follow Me. Let others take care of burying the dead."
Jesus got into a boat. His followers went with Him.
A big storm came up on the sea. The boat was covered by waves. But Jesus was sleeping.
The followers came to Him and woke Him up. They said, "Lord, save us! We are dying!"
Jesus said, "Why are you afraid? You have so little faith!" Then He got up and told the wind and the sea to stop. The sea became very calm.
The men were amazed. They said, "What kind of man is this? Even the wind and the sea obey Him!"
Jesus came to the other side of the sea, to the land of the Gadarenes. Two men with evil spirits came out of the tombs to meet Him. They were so wild that no one could pass that way.
They shouted, "What do You want with us, Son of God? Have You come here to hurt us before it is time?"
Far away, a large herd of pigs was eating.
The evil spirits begged Him, "If You make us leave, send us into the herd of pigs."
Jesus said, "Go!" The spirits left and went into the pigs. The whole herd ran down the hill into the sea and died in the water.
The men who were watching the pigs ran away. They went to the town and told everything. They told about the men with evil spirits too.
The whole town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw Him, they begged Him to leave their area.
Jesus got into a boat. He crossed over and came to His own town.
Some men brought Him a man who could not walk. The man was lying on a bed. Jesus saw their faith. He said to the man, "Be brave, my child. Your sins are forgiven."
Some teachers of the law said to themselves, "He is speaking against God."
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said, "Why do you think bad things in your hearts?
Which is easier to say: 'Your sins are forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'?
But I say this so you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins." Then He said to the man, "Get up, take your bed, and go home."
The man got up and went home.
The crowd saw this. They were afraid. They praised God for giving such power to people.
As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew. Matthew was sitting at the tax booth. Jesus said, "Follow Me." Matthew got up and followed Him.
Later, Jesus was eating in the house. Many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Jesus and His followers.
The Pharisees saw this. They asked His followers, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus heard them. He said, "People who are well do not need a doctor. Sick people do."
He said, "Go and learn what this means: 'I want mercy, not offerings.' I did not come to call good people. I came to call sinners."
John's followers came to Jesus. They asked, "Why do we and the Pharisees go without food, but Your followers do not?"
Jesus said, "Can the friends at a wedding be sad while the groom is with them? No. But the time will come when the groom is taken away. Then they will go without food.
No one puts a new piece of cloth on an old coat. It would tear the coat and make a bigger hole.
And no one puts new wine into old leather bags. The bags would break, and the wine would spill. New wine goes into new leather bags. Then both are safe."
While Jesus was saying these things, a leader came. He bowed down to Jesus and said, "My daughter has just died. But come and put Your hand on her, and she will live."
Jesus went with him. His followers went too.
A woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind Jesus. She touched the edge of His coat.
She thought, "If I just touch His clothes, I will be healed."
Jesus turned and saw her. He said, "Be brave, daughter. Your faith has healed you." The woman was healed right then.
Jesus came to the leader's house. He saw flute players and a noisy crowd.
He said, "Go away. The girl is not dead. She is sleeping." The people laughed at Him.
After the crowd was sent out, Jesus went in. He took the girl by the hand, and she got up.
News of this spread through all that land.
As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed Him. They shouted, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
When Jesus came into the house, the blind men came to Him. Jesus said, "Do you believe that I can do this?" "Yes, Lord," they said.
Jesus touched their eyes. He said, "Let it be done for you as you believe."
Their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them, "Do not tell anyone."
But they went out and told everyone in that whole land.
As they were leaving, some people brought Jesus a man who could not talk and had a demon.
Jesus sent the demon out. The man could talk. The crowd was amazed. They said, "We have never seen anything like this in Israel!"
But the Pharisees said, "He drives out demons by the ruler of demons."
Jesus went through all the towns and villages. He taught in their meeting places. He preached the good news of the kingdom. He healed every sickness and disease.
When He saw the crowds, He felt sorry for them. They were tired and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
Then He said to His followers, "The harvest is big, but the workers are few.
So pray to the Lord of the harvest. Ask Him to send workers into His harvest."
Jesus called His twelve followers to Him. He gave them power over bad spirits. He gave them power to throw the spirits out. He also gave them power to heal every sickness and every weak body.
These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James, the son of Zebedee, and his brother John;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew, the tax man; James, the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot, who later handed Jesus over.
Jesus sent these twelve out. He told them, "Do not go to other nations. Do not go into a Samaritan town.
Go instead to the lost sheep of Israel's people.
As you go, tell people that God's kingdom in heaven is near.
Heal sick people. Raise dead people. Clean people who have a skin disease. Throw out demons. You received these gifts for free. Give them for free. "
Do not get gold, silver, or copper for your belts.
Do not take a bag for the road. Do not take two shirts. Do not take shoes. Do not take a stick. A worker is worth his food. "
When you go into a town or village, find out who is good there. Stay with that person until you leave.
When you go into a house, say hello to the people there.
If the house is good, let your peace come to it. If it is not good, let your peace come back to you. "
If anyone does not take you in or listen to your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that house or town.
I tell you the truth: it will be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah on judgment day than for that town. "
Look, I send you out like sheep among wolves. So be smart like snakes and gentle like doves.
Watch out for people. They will hand you over to courts. They will beat you in their meeting places.
Because of Me, you will be brought before leaders and kings. This will be a witness to them and to the nations. "
When they hand you over, do not worry about what to say. At that time, you will be given what to say.
You are not the ones speaking. The Spirit of your Father speaks through you. "
A brother will hand over a brother to die. A father will hand over a child. Children will turn against their parents and kill them.
Everyone will hate you because of My name. But the one who keeps going to the end will be saved.
When they chase you out of one town, run to the next. I tell you the truth: you will not finish going through all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes. "
A student is not above his teacher. A servant is not above his master.
It is enough for the student to be like his teacher and the servant to be like his master. If they called the owner of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they call the people in his house! "
So do not be afraid of them. Nothing is hidden that will not be shown. Nothing is secret that will not be known.
What I tell you in the dark, say in the light. What you hear whispered, shout from the rooftops.
Do not be afraid of people who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, be afraid of the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell. "
Are not two small birds sold for a penny? Not one of them falls to the ground without your Father knowing.
Even the hairs on your head are all counted.
So do not be afraid. You are worth more than many small birds. "
Everyone who says he is with Me in front of people, I will say he is with Me in front of My Father in heaven.
But anyone who says he is not with Me in front of people, I will say I am not with him in front of My Father in heaven. "
Do not think I came to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace. I came to bring a sword.
I came to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a bride against her mother-in-law.
A man's enemies will be the people in his own house. "
Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not good enough for Me. Anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not good enough for Me.
Anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not good enough for Me.
The one who finds his life will lose it. The one who loses his life for Me will find it. "
Anyone who takes you in takes Me in. Anyone who takes Me in takes in the One who sent Me.
Anyone who takes in a prophet because he is a prophet will get a prophet's reward. Anyone who takes in a good person because he is good will get a good person's reward.
And anyone who gives just a cup of cold water to one of these little ones, because he is My follower, I tell you the truth, he will not lose his reward."
After Jesus finished teaching His twelve disciples, He left there. He went to teach and tell the good news in their towns.
John heard in prison what Christ was doing.
He sent his disciples to ask Jesus, "Are You the One who is coming, or should we wait for someone else?"
Jesus answered, "Go back and tell John what you hear and see.
Blind people can see. People who could not walk can walk. People with skin disease are made clean. Deaf people can hear. Dead people are raised to life. And the good news is told to poor people.
Happy is the person who does not turn away because of Me."
As John's disciples were leaving, Jesus began to talk to the crowd about John. "What did you go out into the desert to see? A tall plant shaking in the wind?
No? Did you go to see a man in soft clothes? People who wear soft clothes live in kings' houses.
Then why did you go? To see a prophet? Yes. I tell you, he is more than a prophet.
He is the one the Bible talks about. The Lord says He will send His helper ahead of You. He will make Your road ready before You. "
I tell you the truth. No one born from a woman is greater than John the Baptist. But even the smallest person in God's kingdom is greater than John.
From the time of John until now, God's kingdom has been pushed hard, and strong people try to take it. "
All the prophets and the Law told God's message until John.
If you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah who was to come.
Anyone who has ears should listen."
"What can I compare this group of people to? They are like children sitting in the town square. They call to their friends.
They say they played a song for them, but the friends did not dance. They say they cried for them, but the friends did not cry with them.
John came. He did not eat or drink like others. People say he has a demon.
The Son of Man came eating and drinking. People say He eats too much and drinks too much. He is a friend of tax collectors and sinners. But wisdom is shown to be right by what it does."
Then Jesus began to speak against the towns where He had done most of His powerful works, because they did not turn from sin.

"It will be bad for you, Chorazin! It will be bad for you, Bethsaida! If the powerful works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned from sin long ago. They would have worn rough clothes and put ashes on themselves to show they were sorry. "
But I tell you, on the day God judges, it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you.

And you, Capernaum, do you think you will be lifted up to heaven? No, you will go down to the place of the dead! If the powerful works done in you had been done in Sodom, that city would still be here today.
But I tell you, on the day God judges, it will be easier for Sodom than for you."
"I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You hid these things from wise and smart people and showed them to little children.
Yes, Father, this is what You wanted.
My Father has given Me all things. No one knows the Son except the Father. No one knows the Father except the Son and anyone the Son chooses to tell. "
Come to Me, all you who are tired and carry heavy loads, and I will give you rest.
Take My yoke on you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For My yoke is easy and My load is light."
At that time, Jesus walked through the grain fields on a Sabbath day. His disciples were hungry. They began to pick heads of grain and eat them.
The Pharisees saw this. They said to Him, "Look! Your disciples are doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath."
He said to them, "Have you not read what David did when he and his men were hungry?
He went into God's house and ate the bread set apart for God. It was not allowed for him or his men to eat it. Only the priests could eat it.
Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple work and are not guilty?
I tell you, something greater than the temple is here.
If you had known what this means, 'I want mercy, not sacrifice,' you would not have blamed innocent people.
For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
Then Jesus left there and went into their synagogue.
A man was there whose hand did not work. The Pharisees wanted to accuse Jesus. They asked Him, "Is it allowed to heal on the Sabbath?"
He said to them, "If one of you has a sheep and it falls into a hole on the Sabbath, won't he grab it and pull it out?
So a man is worth much more than a sheep. It is allowed to do good on the Sabbath."
Then He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man stretched it out. It became well, like the other hand.
The Pharisees went out and planned how to kill Him.
Jesus knew this. He left there. Many crowds followed Him. He healed them all.
He told them not to tell others who He was.
This was to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah said:
"Here is My Servant whom I chose. He is My Beloved. I am pleased with Him. I will put My Spirit on Him. He will tell the nations what is right.
He will not argue or shout. No one will hear His voice in the streets.
He will not break a bent reed. He will not put out a weak flame. He will keep going until He brings justice to victory.
The nations will put their hope in His name."
Then a man who was demon-possessed, blind, and unable to speak was brought to Jesus. Jesus healed him. The man could speak and see.
All the crowds were amazed. They said, "Could this be the Son of David?"
The Pharisees heard this. They said, "This man does not drive out demons except by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons."
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said to them, "Every kingdom that fights against itself is ruined. Every city or house that fights against itself will not stand.
If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So they will be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then God's kingdom has come to you. "
How can anyone go into a strong man's house and take his things, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can rob his house.
Whoever is not with Me is against Me. Whoever does not gather with Me scatters. "
So I tell you, people will be forgiven for every sin and blasphemy. But blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, not in this age or in the age to come.
Make the tree good, and its fruit will be good. Or make the tree bad, and its fruit will be bad. A tree is known by its fruit.
You snakes! How can you speak good things when you are evil? The mouth speaks what the heart is full of.
A good man brings good things out of his good treasure. A bad man brings bad things out of his bad treasure.
I tell you, people will give an account for every careless word they speak on the day of judgment.
For by your words you will be found right, and by your words you will be found wrong."
Then some of the teachers of the law and Pharisees answered Him. They said, "Teacher, we want to see a sign from You."
He answered them, "This is an evil and unfaithful generation. It asks for a sign. But no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the big fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation. They will judge it. For they turned from their sin when Jonah preached to them. And something greater than Jonah is here.
The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation. She will judge it. For she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom. And something greater than Solomon is here.
When an evil spirit leaves a person, it goes through dry places looking for rest. It does not find any.
Then it says, 'I will go back to my house, the place I left.' When it goes back, it finds the house empty, swept, and put in order.

Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits worse than itself. They go in and live there. So the last state of that person is worse than the first. That is how it will be with this evil generation."
While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, His mother and brothers stood outside. They wanted to speak to Him.
Someone told Him, "Look! Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside. They want to speak to You."
He answered the one speaking, "Who is My mother? Who are My brothers?"
He stretched out His hand toward His disciples. He said, "Here are My mother and My brothers.
For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother."
That same day, Jesus left the house and sat by the sea.
Big crowds came to Him. He got into a boat and sat down. All the people stood on the shore.
He told them many stories. He said, "Look! A farmer went out to plant seeds.
As he planted, some seeds fell on the path. Birds came and ate them.
Some fell on rocky ground with little dirt. They sprang up fast because the dirt was not deep.
But when the sun came up, they burned and dried up because they had no roots.
Some fell among thorns. The thorns grew and choked them.
Some fell on good dirt. They grew and gave fruit—some one hundred, some sixty, some thirty.
Whoever has ears, let him listen."
His followers came to Him and asked, "Why do you tell them stories?"
He answered, "You can learn the secrets of God's kingdom. That gift is for you, not for them.
Whoever has something will get more, and have plenty. Whoever has nothing will lose even what he has.
That is why I speak to them in stories. They look, but they do not see. They hear, but they do not hear or understand."
He said, "So the words of the prophet Isaiah come true for them." "You will hear, but you will not understand. You will look, but you will not see.

These people's hearts are hard. Their ears are dull. They have closed their eyes. If they had not, they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, and understand with their hearts. Then they would turn to Me, and I would heal them."
"But your eyes are blessed because they see. Your ears are blessed because they hear.
I tell you for sure: Many prophets and good people wanted to see what you see, but they did not. They wanted to hear what you hear, but they did not."
"So listen to the story of the farmer."
"When anyone hears the word about God's kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes. He takes away the seed that was planted in that person's heart. This is the seed that fell on the path.
The seed on rocky ground is the person who hears the word and takes it with joy.
But he has no root in himself. He lasts only a short time. When trouble or people make fun of him because of the word, he quickly gives up.
The seed among thorns is the person who hears the word. But the worries of this life and the trick of money choke the word. It does not grow fruit.
The seed on good dirt is the person who hears the word and understands it. He gives fruit—some one hundred, some sixty, some thirty."
Jesus told them another story. He said, "God's kingdom is like a man who planted good seed in his field.
While people slept, his enemy came. He planted weeds among the wheat and left.
When the plants grew and made grain, the weeds showed up too."
The man's servants came to him and said, "Sir, didn't you plant good seed in your field? Where did the weeds come from?"
"An enemy did this," he said. The servants asked, "Do you want us to go pull them up?"
"No," he said. "If you pull the weeds, you might pull the wheat too.
Let both grow until harvest time. Then I will tell the workers: First pull the weeds and tie them into bundles to burn. Then gather the wheat into my barn."
Jesus told them another story. He said, "God's kingdom is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
It is the smallest of all seeds. But when it grows, it is bigger than garden plants. It becomes a tree. Birds come and make nests in its branches."
He told them another story. "God's kingdom is like yeast that a woman mixed into a big bowl of flour. She mixed it until all the dough rose."
Jesus told the crowds all these things in stories. He did not tell them anything without a story.
This happened to make true what the prophet said: "I will open my mouth and tell stories. I will speak things hidden since the world began."
Then Jesus left the crowds and went into the house. His followers came to Him and said, "Explain to us the story about the weeds in the field."
He answered, "The one who planted the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world. The good seeds are the people of the kingdom. The weeds are the people of the evil one.
The enemy who planted them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age. The harvesters are angels.
Just as weeds are pulled up and burned, so it will be at the end of the age.
The Son of Man will send His angels. They will take out of His kingdom everything that causes sin and all who do wrong.
They will throw them into a hot fire. There they will cry and grind their teeth.
Then God's good people will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. Whoever has ears, let him listen."
"God's kingdom is like treasure hidden in a field. A man found it and hid it again. He was so happy that he sold everything he had and bought that field."
"Again, God's kingdom is like a man who buys and sells things. He looked for fine pearls.
When he found one pearl worth a lot, he sold everything he had and bought it."
"Again, God's kingdom is like a net that was thrown into the sea. It caught fish of every kind.
When it was full, the fishermen pulled it to shore. They sat down and put the good fish in baskets. They threw the bad fish away."
"So it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come and separate the bad people from the good people.
They will throw the bad people into a hot fire. There they will cry and grind their teeth."
Jesus asked, "Do you understand all this?" "Yes," they said.
He said, "So every teacher of God's Law who becomes a follower of God's kingdom is like a homeowner. He brings out new things and old things from his treasure room."
When Jesus finished these stories, He left that place.
He came to His hometown and taught the people in their meeting place. They were amazed and said, "Where did this man get such wisdom and power?"
"Isn't this the carpenter's son? Isn't His mother Mary? Aren't His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
Aren't all His sisters here with us? Where did He get all this?"
They were upset with Him. Jesus said, "A prophet is respected everywhere except in his hometown and in his own home."
He did not do many miracles there because the people did not believe.
At that time Herod, the ruler, heard about Jesus.
He said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist. He has risen from the dead! That is why these powers work in him."
Herod had arrested John. He tied him up and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.
John had told him, "It is not right for you to have her."
Herod wanted to kill John, but he was afraid of the crowd. They thought John was a man from God.
On Herod's birthday, Herodias's daughter danced for the guests. Herod was pleased.
So he promised to give her whatever she asked.
Her mother told her what to ask. She said, "Give me here on a plate the head of John the Baptist."
The king was sad. But because of his promises and the guests, he ordered it.
He sent men to cut off John's head in prison.
His head was brought on a plate and given to the girl. She brought it to her mother.
John's followers came. They took his body and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard this, He left there in a boat to a quiet place alone. But the crowds heard and followed Him on foot from the towns.
When Jesus came out, He saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them and healed their sick.
In the evening, the followers came to Him and said, "This is a lonely place, and the hour is already late. Send the crowds away so they can go to the villages and buy food."
Jesus said, "They do not need to go. You give them something to eat."
They said, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish here."
He said, "Bring them here to Me."

He told the crowds to sit on the grass. He took the five loaves and two fish. He looked up to heaven and blessed them. He broke the loaves and gave them to the followers. The followers gave them to the crowds.
Everyone ate and was full. They picked up twelve baskets full of leftover pieces.
About five thousand men ate, not counting women and children.
Right away Jesus made the followers get into the boat. He told them to go ahead of Him to the other side while He sent the crowds away.
After sending the crowds away, He went up on a mountain by Himself to pray. When evening came, He was there alone.
The boat was already far from land. The waves were beating it, because the wind was against it.
In the last part of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.
The followers saw Him walking on the sea. They were scared. They said, "It is a ghost!" and cried out in fear.
But Jesus spoke to them right away: "Take heart! It is I. Do not be afraid."
Peter answered Him, "Lord, if it is You, tell me to come to You on the water."
He said, "Come." Peter got out of the boat. He walked on the water and came toward Jesus.
But when he saw the strong wind, he was afraid. He began to sink and cried out, "Lord, save me!"
Right away Jesus reached out His hand and caught him. He said, "You have little faith. Why did you doubt?"
When they got into the boat, the wind stopped.
The men in the boat worshiped Him and said, "Truly You are the Son of God."
They crossed over and came to land at Gennesaret.
The men of that place knew Him. They sent word all around that area and brought all who were sick to Him.
They begged Him to let them just touch the edge of His clothes. Everyone who touched it was healed.
Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came to Jesus from Jerusalem.
They said, "Why do your followers not wash their hands before they eat? They do not follow what our older leaders taught."
Jesus answered, "Why do you break God's command?
God said, 'Honor your father and your mother.' He also said, 'Anyone who curses his father or mother must die.'
But you say a person can tell his father or mother, "I already gave to God what I would have used to help you,"
and then he does not have to take care of them. In this way, you cancel God's word to keep your own rules."
Jesus said, "You pretenders! Isaiah said true words about you:
'These people honor me with their words, but their hearts are far from me.
They worship me, but it means nothing. They teach man-made rules as if they were God's commands.'"
Then Jesus called the crowd to come closer. He said, "Listen and understand.
What goes into a person's mouth does not make him unclean. What comes out of his mouth makes him unclean."
Later, His followers came to Him. They said, "Do you know the Pharisees were upset when they heard what you said?"
Jesus answered, "Every plant my Father in heaven did not plant will be pulled up.
Leave them alone. They are blind leaders of blind people. If a blind person leads another blind person, both will fall into a hole."
Peter said to Him, "Please explain this story to us."
Jesus said, "Are you still not able to understand?
Do you not know that everything that goes into the mouth goes to the stomach and then leaves the body?
But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart. That is what makes a person unclean.
From the heart come bad thoughts, murder, cheating in marriage, sexual sins, stealing, lying about others, and cursing God.
These things make a person unclean. But eating with unwashed hands does not make a person unclean."
Then Jesus left that place and went to the area near Tyre and Sidon.
A woman from Canaan came out. She cried out, "Lord, Son of David, please help me! My daughter is very troubled by a demon."
Jesus did not say a word to her. His followers came to Him and asked, "Please send her away. She keeps shouting behind us."
Jesus answered, "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the family of Israel."
The woman came and knelt before Him. She said, "Lord, help me."
Jesus answered, "It is not right to take the children's bread and give it to the dogs."
She said, "Yes, Lord. But even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their owners' table."
Then Jesus answered her, "Woman, you have great faith! Let it happen for you just as you want." And her daughter was healed at that same time.
Jesus left there and went beside the Sea of Galilee. Then He went up on a hill and sat down.
Many people came to Him. They brought people who could not walk, could not see, had twisted hands, could not speak, and many others. They laid them at His feet. He healed them.

The crowd was amazed when they saw people who could not speak now speaking, people with twisted hands now well, people who could not walk now walking, and people who could not see now seeing. They praised the God of Israel.

Jesus called His followers to Him. He said, "I feel sorry for the crowd. They have been with me three days, and they have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry. They might get too weak on the way."
His followers said to Him, "Where can we get enough bread in this empty place to feed all these people?"
Jesus asked them, "How many loaves of bread do you have?" They said, "Seven, and a few small fish."
Jesus told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
He took the seven loaves and the fish. He gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to His followers. His followers gave them to the crowd.
Everyone ate and was full. They picked up seven baskets full of leftover pieces.
About four thousand men ate, not counting women and children.
Then Jesus sent the crowd away. He got into a boat and went to the area of Magadan.
The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus. They wanted to test Him. They asked Him to show them a sign from heaven.
Jesus answered, "When evening comes, you say, 'The sky is red, so it will be fair weather.'
And in the morning you say, 'The sky is red and dark, so it will rain.' You can read the sky, but you cannot read the signs of the times.
Bad and unfaithful people ask for a sign. But no sign will be given to them except the sign of Jonah." Then He left them and went away.
The disciples went across the lake. They forgot to bring bread.
Jesus said to them, "Watch out! Be careful of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
The disciples talked among themselves. They said, "We did not bring any bread."
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said, "You have so little faith! Why are you talking about having no bread?
Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand? How many baskets did you pick up?
And do you not remember the seven loaves for the four thousand? How many baskets did you pick up?
How can you not understand? I was not talking about bread. I said, 'Be careful of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.'"
Then they understood. He was not warning them about yeast in bread. He was warning them about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Jesus went to the area of Caesarea Philippi. He asked His disciples, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?"
They answered, "Some say John the Baptist. Others say Elijah. Others say Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
Jesus asked them, "But who do you say I am?"
Simon Peter answered, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
Jesus answered him, "You are blessed, Simon son of Jonah. No person told you this. My Father in heaven showed it to you.
I tell you, you are Peter. On this rock I will build My church. The power of death will not beat it.
I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you tie up on earth will be tied up in heaven. Whatever you set free on earth will be set free in heaven."
Then Jesus told His disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ.

From that time on, Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem. He would suffer many things from the older leaders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law. He would be killed, and He would rise again on the third day.
Peter took Jesus aside and began to scold Him. He said, "Never, Lord! This will never happen to You!"
Jesus turned and said to Peter, "Get behind Me, Satan! You are in My way. You are thinking like a person, not like God."
Then Jesus said to His disciples, "If anyone wants to follow Me, he must say no to himself. He must pick up his cross and follow Me.
Anyone who tries to save his life will lose it. But anyone who gives up his life for Me will find it.
What good is it if a person gains the whole world but loses his life? What can a person give to buy back his life?
The Son of Man will come in His Father's glory with His angels. Then He will pay each person for what he has done.
I tell you the truth: some people standing here will not die before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom."
Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John, the brother of James. He led them up a high mountain by themselves.
There Jesus changed. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became white as light.
Then Moses and Elijah appeared. They were talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You want, I will make three tents here. One for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
While Peter was still talking, a bright cloud came over them. A voice from the cloud said, "This is My Son, whom I love. I am pleased with Him. Listen to Him!"
The disciples heard this and fell on their faces. They were very afraid.
Jesus came and touched them. "Get up," He said. "Do not be afraid."
When they looked up, they saw no one but Jesus.
As they went down the mountain, Jesus told them, "Do not tell anyone what you saw until the Son of Man rises from the dead."
The disciples asked Him, "Then why do the teachers of the law say Elijah must come first?"
Jesus answered, "Elijah does come. He will make all things right again.
But I tell you, Elijah has already come. They did not know him. They did to him what they wanted. In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer from them."
Then the disciples understood He was talking about John the Baptist.
When they came to the crowd, a man came to Jesus. He got on his knees before Him.
He said, "Lord, have mercy on my son. He has fits. He gets hurt a lot. He often falls into fire or into water.
I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him."
Jesus answered, "You people do not believe! You are turned around. How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me."
Jesus spoke sternly to the demon. It left the boy. The boy was healed right then.
The disciples came to Jesus alone. They asked, "Why could we not drive it out?"

Jesus said, "Because you have so little faith. I tell you the truth. If you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you."
While they were together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man will be handed over to people.
They will kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again." The disciples were very sad.
When they came to Capernaum, the men who collected the temple tax came to Peter. They asked, "Does your Teacher pay the temple tax?"
"Yes," Peter said. When Peter came into the house, Jesus spoke first. "What do you think, Simon? Do kings of the earth collect taxes from their own sons or from other people?"
"From other people," Peter answered. Jesus said to him, "Then the sons are free."
"But we do not want to upset them. Go to the lake and throw in a hook. Take the first fish you catch. Open its mouth, and you will find a coin. Take it and give it to them for Me and for you."
At that time, the followers of Jesus came to Him. They asked, "Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
Jesus called a little child to Him. He had the child stand among them.
He said, "I tell you the truth. Unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
So anyone who makes himself as humble as this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And anyone who welcomes a child like this in My name welcomes Me."
"If anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to sin, it would be better for him to have a big stone tied around his neck and be drowned in the deep sea.
The world will have trouble because of things that make people sin. Those things must come, but trouble will come to the person who brings them.

If your hand or foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one hand or one foot than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the fire that never ends.
If your eye causes you to sin, take it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell."
"Be careful not to look down on one of these little ones. I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven."
"What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them wanders away, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go look for the one that wandered?
And if he finds it, I tell you the truth, he is happier about that one sheep than about the ninety-nine that did not wander.
In the same way, your Father in heaven does not want any of these little ones to be lost."
"If your brother or sister sins against you, go and talk to them alone. If they listen to you, you have won them back.
But if they will not listen, take one or two others with you. Then everything can be proved by the words of two or three witnesses.
If they still will not listen, tell it to the church. If they will not listen even to the church, treat them like a person who does not know God or a tax collector."
"I tell you the truth, whatever you tie up on earth will be tied up in heaven, and whatever you set free on earth will be set free in heaven.
Again I tell you, if two of you on earth agree about anything you ask for, My Father in heaven will do it for you.
For where two or three come together in My name, there I am with them."
Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, "Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother or sister who sins against me? Up to seven times?"
Jesus said, "I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times."
"So the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to collect what his servants owed him.
As he began to collect it, a man who owed him ten thousand bags of gold was brought to him.
The man could not pay. So the master ordered that the man, his wife, his children, and all he had be sold to pay the debt."
"The servant fell on his knees before the master. He said, 'Be patient with me, and I will pay back everything.'
The master felt sorry for him. He canceled the debt and let the servant go.
"But when that servant went out, he found another servant who owed him a hundred silver coins. He grabbed him and choked him. He said, 'Pay back what you owe me!'
"The other servant fell on his knees and begged him, 'Be patient with me, and I will pay it back.'
"But he would not. He went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay the debt.
"The other servants saw what happened. They were very sad. They went and told their master everything.
Then the master called the servant in. He said, 'You bad servant! I canceled all that debt for you because you begged me.
Should you not have shown kindness to your fellow servant, just as I showed kindness to you?'
In anger, the master handed him over to the jailers to be punished until he paid back all he owed.
"This is how My Father in heaven will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart."
When Jesus finished these words, He left Galilee and went to the area of Judea across the Jordan.
Many crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.
The Pharisees came to Him to test Him. They asked, "Is it right for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?"
He answered, "Haven't you read that from the beginning the Creator made them male and female?
He said, 'For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one body.'
So they are no longer two. They are one body. So what God has joined together, no person should separate."
They said to Him, "Then why did Moses tell us to give a paper that ends a marriage and divorce her?"
He said to them, "Moses let you divorce your wives because you were stubborn. But it was not like that from the start.
I tell you, anyone who divorces his wife, unless she has been unfaithful, and marries another woman, is guilty of adultery."
His disciples said to Him, "If that is how it is between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry."
He said to them, "Not everyone can accept this teaching. Only those God gives it to can.
Some men are born unable to marry. Some are made that way by people. Some choose this for the kingdom of heaven. Anyone who can accept this should accept it."
Then little children were brought to Him so He could put His hands on them and pray. But the disciples told them to stop.
Jesus said, "Let the little children come to Me. Do not stop them. The kingdom of heaven belongs to people like them."
He put His hands on them and left there.
Look, a man came to Him and said, "Teacher, what good thing must I do to have life that never ends?"
He said to him, "Why do you ask Me about what is good? Only One is good. But if you want to enter life, keep the commands."
He said to Him, "Which ones?" Jesus said, "Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not lie about others.
Honor your father and your mother, and love your neighbor as you love yourself."
The young man said to Him, "I have kept all these. What am I still missing?"
Jesus said to him, "If you want to be perfect, go sell your things and give to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. Come and follow Me."
When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he had many things.
Jesus said to His disciples, "Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
When the disciples heard this, they were very amazed. They said, "Who then can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said, "For people this is impossible. But with God all things are possible."
Then Peter answered Him, "Look, we have left everything and followed you. What will there be for us?"

Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, in the new world, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones. You will judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for My name will receive a hundred times as much and will receive life that never ends.
But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first."
For the kingdom of heaven is like a man who owned a vineyard. He went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed to pay them one coin for the day. Then he sent them to work in his vineyard.
About nine in the morning, he went out again. He saw some other people standing in the town square doing nothing.
He said to them, “You go and work in my vineyard too. I will pay you what is right.”
So they went. He went out again at noon and at three in the afternoon and did the same thing.
About five in the afternoon, he went out and found some other people standing there. He asked them, “Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?”
They said, “No one hired us.” He said to them, “You go and work in my vineyard too.”
When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his helper, “Call the workers and pay them. Start with the last ones hired and go to the first.”
The workers who were hired about five in the afternoon came. Each one got one coin.
When the first workers came, they thought they would get more. But each one also got one coin.
When they got their pay, they complained to the owner.
They said, “These last workers only worked one hour. You made them equal to us! We worked hard all day in the hot sun.”
The owner answered one of them, “Friend, I am not cheating you. Didn't you agree to work for one coin?
Take your pay and go. I want to give this last worker the same as I gave you.
Can't I do what I want with my own money? Or are you upset because I am kind?”
So the last will be first, and the first will be last.
Jesus was going up to Jerusalem. On the way, He took the Twelve aside and said to them, “
We are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They will say He must die.
They will hand Him over to people from other nations. They will make fun of Him, beat Him, and put Him on a cross. On the third day, He will rise again.”
Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came to Jesus. She knelt down and asked Him for something.
Jesus said to her, “What do you want?” She said, “Let these two sons of mine sit one at Your right and one at Your left in Your kingdom.”
Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you go through the hard things I will go through?” They said, “We can.”
Jesus said to them, “You will go through hard things too. But sitting at My right or left is not for Me to give. Those places are for the people My Father has chosen.”
When the ten disciples heard this, they were angry with the two brothers.
Jesus called them together and said, “You know that the rulers of other nations boss their people around. Their great leaders push people around.
It will not be like that with you. Anyone who wants to be great among you must be your servant.
Anyone who wants to be first must be your slave.
The Son of Man did not come to be served. He came to serve and to give His life to set many people free.”
As Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.
Two blind men were sitting by the road. They heard that Jesus was passing by. They shouted, “Lord, Son of David, please help us!”
The crowd told them to be quiet. But they shouted even louder, “Lord, Son of David, please help us!”
Jesus stopped and called them. He said, “What do you want Me to do for you?”
They said, “Lord, we want to be able to see.”
Jesus felt sorry for them. He touched their eyes. Right away they could see, and they followed Him.
As Jesus and His disciples got close to Jerusalem, they came to Bethphage. This town is on the Mount of Olives. Jesus sent two disciples.
He said, "Go into the village ahead of you. You will find a donkey tied up. A young donkey will be with her. Untie them and bring them to Me."
If anyone says anything to you, say, "The Lord needs them." He will send them right away.
This happened to make true what the prophet said.
"Tell the people of Zion, 'Look! Your King is coming to you. He is gentle. He rides on a donkey. He rides on a young donkey.'"
The disciples went and did what Jesus told them.
They brought the donkey and the young donkey. They put their coats on the animals. Jesus sat on the coats.
A big crowd spread their coats on the road. Other people cut branches from trees and spread them on the road.
The people in front of Jesus and the people behind Him shouted, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
When Jesus came into Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken. The people asked, "Who is this?"
The crowds said, "This is Jesus. He is the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee."
Jesus went into the temple. He threw out all the people who were buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers. He turned over the chairs of the people selling doves.
He said to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you make it a den for robbers."
Blind people and lame people came to Him in the temple. He healed them.
The chief priests and teachers saw the wonderful things He did. They saw the children shouting in the temple, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" They were angry.
They said to Him, "Do you hear what these children are saying?" Jesus said, "Yes. Have you never read, 'From the mouths of little children and babies, You have made praise perfect'?"
Jesus left them. He went out of the city to Bethany. He stayed there.
In the morning, Jesus was going back to the city. He was hungry.
He saw a fig tree by the road. He went to it. But He found only leaves. He said to it, "May no fruit ever grow on you again." Right away the fig tree dried up.
The disciples saw it. They were amazed. They said, "How did the fig tree dry up so fast?"

Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth. If you have faith and do not doubt, you will do more than this to the fig tree. You can even say to this mountain, 'Move and throw yourself into the sea,' and it will happen.
If you believe, you will get everything you ask for in prayer."
Jesus went back to the temple. He was teaching. The chief priests and the elders came to Him. They said, "By what power do you do these things? Who gave you this power?"
Jesus answered, "I will ask you one question too. If you answer Me, I will tell you by what power I do these things.
Where did John's baptism come from? From heaven or from people?" The chief priests and elders thought to themselves, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Then why did you not believe him?'"
"But if we say, 'From people,' we are afraid of the crowd. All the people think John is a prophet."
So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." Jesus said, "Then I will not tell you by what power I do these things."
Jesus said, "What do you think? A man had two sons. He went to the first son and said, 'Son, go work in the vineyard today.'
The son answered, 'I will not.' But later he changed his mind and went.
The man went to the second son and said the same thing. The second son said, 'I will, sir.' But he did not go."
"Which son did what his father wanted?" The chief priests and elders said, "The first." Jesus said, "I tell you the truth. Tax collectors and prostitutes will go into God's kingdom before you."
"John came to show you the right way. You did not believe him. But tax collectors and prostitutes did believe him. Even after you saw that, you did not change your minds and believe him."

Jesus said, "Listen to another story. A man owned a vineyard. He planted it. He put a wall around it. He dug a place for a wine press. He built a tower. Then he rented it to some farmers. He went away.
When it was time for the fruit, he sent his servants to the farmers to get his share.
The farmers took his servants. They beat one. They killed one. They threw stones at another.
He sent more servants than before. The farmers did the same thing to them.
Last, he sent his son. He thought, 'They will respect my son.'
But the farmers saw the son. They said to each other, 'This is the one who will get everything. Let's kill him and take his land.'
They took him. They threw him out of the vineyard. They killed him."
"So when the owner comes, what will he do to those farmers?"
The chief priests and elders said, "He will destroy those bad men. He will rent the vineyard to other farmers. They will give him the fruit at the right time."
Jesus said, "Have you never read this in the Bible? 'The stone the builders did not want has become the most important stone. The Lord did this. It is wonderful to us.'
So I tell you, God's kingdom will be taken from you. It will be given to people who make good fruit.
Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken. Anyone it falls on will be crushed."
The chief priests and the Pharisees heard Jesus' stories. They knew He was talking about them.
They wanted to arrest Him. But they were afraid of the crowds. The crowds thought Jesus was a prophet.
"God's kingdom in heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast for his son.
He sent his servants to call the people he had invited, but they did not want to come.
He sent other servants and said, 'Tell the invited people, "Look, I have made my dinner ready. My bulls and fat calves are killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast."'
But they did not care. One man went to his farm, and another went to his work.
The rest grabbed his servants, hurt them, and killed them.
The king was very angry. He sent his army and killed those murderers. He burned their city.
Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding feast is ready, but the people I invited were not good enough.
Go to the roads and invite everyone you find to the wedding.'
The servants went out into the streets. They brought in everyone they found, both bad and good. The wedding hall was full of guests.
The king came in to see the guests. He saw a man who was not wearing wedding clothes.
'Friend,' he asked, 'how did you get in here without wedding clothes?' The man said nothing.
Then the king said to his servants, 'Tie his hands and feet. Throw him into the dark place outside. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'
Many are invited, but few are chosen."
The Pharisees went out. They planned to trap Jesus with His words.

They sent their followers to Him with the Herodians. They said, "Teacher, we know You are true. You teach God's way truly. You do not care what people think, because You do not look at how people look.
So tell us, what do You think? Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
Jesus knew their bad plan. He said, "You pretenders! Why are you testing Me?
Show Me the coin for the tax." They brought Him a coin.
He asked, "Whose picture is on this? Whose words are on it?"
They said, "Caesar's." Then Jesus said, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and give to God what is God's."
They heard this and were amazed. They left Him and went away.
That same day, the Sadducees came to Him. They say people do not rise from the dead. They asked Him a question.
"Teacher," they said, "Moses told us that if a man dies with no children, his brother must marry his wife and have children for him.
There were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died. He had no children, so he left his wife to his brother.
The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, all the way to the seventh.
Last of all, the woman died.
So when people rise from the dead, whose wife will she be? All seven had married her."
Jesus answered, "You are wrong. You do not know God's writings or God's power.
When people rise from the dead, they do not marry or get married. They are like angels in heaven.
But about the dead rising, have you not read what God said to you?
'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' He is not the God of the dead, but of the living."
The crowds heard this. They were amazed at His teaching.
When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had made the Sadducees be quiet, they came together.
One of them, a teacher of the law, tested Him with a question.
"Teacher, which command in the law is the greatest?"
Jesus said to him, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.
This is the first and greatest command.
The second is like it: Love your neighbor as yourself.
All the Law and the Prophets depend on these two commands."
While the Pharisees were together, Jesus asked them, "What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?"
Jesus said to them, "Then how does David, with the Spirit's help, call Him Lord? David says,
'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand, until I put Your enemies under Your feet."'
If David calls Him Lord, how can He be David's son?"
No one could answer Him. From that day on, no one dared to ask Him anything else.
Then Jesus talked to the crowds and to His disciples.
He said, "The teachers and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat.
So do what they tell you to do, and obey their words. But do not live the way they live, because they say things and do not do them.
They tie heavy loads that are hard to carry and put them on people's shoulders. But they will not even lift a finger to help.
They do everything so people will see them. They make their prayer boxes big and their robe tassels long.
They like the best seats at dinners and the best seats in meeting places.
They like greetings in the market and being called 'Teacher' by people.
"But you must not be called 'Teacher,' because you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
Do not call anyone on earth 'Father,' because you have one Father in heaven.
Do not be called leaders, because you have one Leader, the Christ.
The greatest among you will be your servant.
Anyone who lifts himself up will be brought low, and anyone who brings himself low will be lifted up.
"How terrible for you, teachers and Pharisees, you pretenders! You shut the door to heaven's kingdom in front of people. You do not go in yourselves, and you stop those who are trying to go in.
How terrible for you, teachers and Pharisees, you pretenders! You travel over land and sea to make one new follower. Then, when he follows, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves.
"How terrible for you, blind guides! You say that if anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing, but if anyone swears by the gold in the temple, he must keep his promise.
You blind fools! Which is greater, the gold or the temple that makes the gold holy?
You also say that if anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing, but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he must keep his promise.
You blind! Which is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy?
So anyone who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
Anyone who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who lives in it.
Anyone who swears by heaven swears by God's throne and by the One sitting on it.

"How terrible for you, teachers and Pharisees, you pretenders! You give a tenth of your mint, dill, and cumin. But you forget the bigger parts of God's law: being fair, showing mercy, and being faithful. You should do these things and not forget the small ones.
You blind guides! You pay attention to tiny things but ignore big things.
How terrible for you, teachers and Pharisees, you pretenders! You wash the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and not controlling yourselves.
You blind Pharisee! First wash the inside of the cup and dish, so the outside can be clean too.
How terrible for you, teachers and Pharisees, you pretenders! You are like graves painted white. They look nice outside, but inside they are full of dead bones and everything unclean.
In the same way, you look good to people outside, but inside you are full of pretending and doing wrong.
"How terrible for you, teachers and Pharisees, you pretenders! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the graves of good people.
And you say that if you had lived back then, you would not have helped kill the prophets.
So you show that you are children of the people who killed the prophets.
Go ahead and finish the bad things your fathers started!
You snakes, you baby snakes! How will you escape being punished in hell?
So I am sending you prophets, wise people, and teachers. Some of them you will kill and put on a cross. Some of them you will beat in your meeting places and chase from town to town.
This is so all the blood of good people spilled on earth will come on you, from the blood of good Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
I tell you the truth, all these things will happen to people living now.
"Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets and stone the people sent to you. How often I wanted to gather your children like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you would not let Me.
Look, your house is left empty.
I tell you, you will not see Me again until you say that the One who comes in the name of the Lord is blessed."
Jesus left the temple. His followers came to Him and showed Him the temple buildings.
He said, "Do you see all these things? I tell you the truth. Not one stone here will be left on another. Every stone will be thrown down."
Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives. His followers came to Him alone. They said, "Tell us, when will this happen? What will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the world?"
Jesus answered, "Be careful. Do not let anyone trick you.
Many people will come using My name. They will say, 'I am the Christ.' They will trick many people.
You will hear about wars and stories of wars. Do not be afraid. These things must happen. But the end is not yet.
One nation will fight another nation. One kingdom will fight another kingdom. There will be times with no food. There will be earthquakes in many places.
All these things are just the start of the hard times."
Then people will hand you over to be hurt. They will kill you. All people will hate you because of My name.
Then many people will turn away from their faith. They will turn against each other. They will hate each other.
Many fake prophets will come. They will trick many people.
Because bad things will grow, the love of many people will grow cold.
But the one who keeps going to the end will be saved.
This good news about God's kingdom will be told in all the world. It will be a witness to all nations. Then the end will come.
So when you see the terrible thing that ruins standing in the holy place, the one spoken of by the prophet Daniel, the reader should understand.
Then people in Judea should run to the hills.
A person on the roof should not go down to get things from the house.
A person in the field should not go back to get his coat.
It will be very hard in those days for women who are pregnant or feeding babies.
Pray that you will not have to run away in winter or on the Sabbath day.
For then there will be great trouble. It will be worse than any trouble since the world began. It will never be that bad again.
If those days were not made shorter, no one would live. But for the sake of God's chosen people, those days will be made shorter.
At that time, if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ!' or 'There He is!' do not believe it.
Fake Christs and fake prophets will come. They will do big miracles and amazing things. They will try to trick even God's chosen people if they can.
See, I have told you before it happens.
So if anyone tells you, 'He is out in the desert,' do not go out. If they say, 'He is in the back rooms,' do not believe it.
The coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning. It flashes from the east and shines to the west.
Where there is a dead body, vultures gather.
Right after the trouble of those days, the sun will become dark. The moon will not give its light. The stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the sky will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. All the people of the earth will cry. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
He will send His angels with a loud trumpet sound. They will gather His chosen people from every direction, from one end of the sky to the other.
Learn this lesson from the fig tree. When its branches get soft and leaves grow, you know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see all these things, you know that it is very close.
I tell you the truth. The people living then will not all die before all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away. But My words will never pass away.
But no one knows about that day or hour. The angels in heaven do not know. The Son does not know. Only the Father knows.
It will be like in Noah's time when the Son of Man comes.
In those days before the flood, people were eating and drinking. They were getting married. This went on until Noah went into the ark.
They did not know what was coming. The flood came and took them all away. It will be like that when the Son of Man comes.
Two men will be in the field. One will be taken. The other will be left.
Two women will be grinding grain with a hand mill. One will be taken. The other will be left.
So stay awake. You do not know the day your Lord will come.
But know this. If the owner of a house had known what time at night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake. He would not have let the thief break in.
So you too must be ready. The Son of Man will come at a time you do not expect.
Who is the faithful and wise servant? His master put him in charge of the other servants. He gives them food at the right time.
That servant is blessed if his master comes back and finds him doing this.
I tell you the truth. The master will put him in charge of everything he owns.
But if that servant is bad, he may think, 'my master is taking a long time.'
He may start to beat the other servants. He may eat and drink with drunk people.
His master will come on a day he does not expect. He will come at a time he does not know.
He will cut him to pieces. He will put him with the pretenders. There, people will cry and grind their teeth.
"The kingdom of heaven is like ten young women. They took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.
Five of them were silly, and five were wise.
The silly ones took their lamps but did not take extra oil.
The wise ones took oil in jars with their lamps.
The groom was late. So all the young women got sleepy and fell asleep.
"At midnight someone shouted, 'Look! The groom is coming! Go out to meet him!'
Then all the young women woke up and fixed their lamps.
The silly ones said to the wise ones, 'Give us some of your oil. Our lamps are going out.'
But the wise ones answered, 'No. There may not be enough for us and you. Go buy some for yourselves.'
