While they were gone to buy oil, the groom came. The ready ones went in with him to the wedding. Then the door was shut.
"Later the other young women came and said, 'Lord, Lord, open the door for us!' But he answered, 'I do not know you.'
So stay awake. You do not know the day or the hour.
"It is like a man who went on a trip. He called his servants and gave them his money to use.
He gave five bags of money to one, two bags to another, and one bag to another. He gave each one what he could handle. Then he left.
"The servant who got five bags went right away and worked with the money. He made five more bags.
The one with two bags did the same. He made two more bags.
But the servant who got one bag went and dug a hole in the ground. He hid his master's money there.
"After a long time, the master came back. He settled accounts with his servants.
The servant who had five bags came and brought five more. He said, 'Sir, you gave me five bags of money. Look, I made five more.'
His master said, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful with a little. I will put you in charge of much. Come and share your master's joy.'
"The servant with two bags also came. He said, 'Sir, you gave me two bags of money. Look, I made two more.'
His master said, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful with a little. I will put you in charge of much. Come and share your master's joy.'
"Then the servant who had one bag came. He said, 'Sir, I knew you are a hard man. You harvest where you did not plant, and you gather where you did not scatter.
I was afraid. So I hid your money in the ground. Here is your money.'
"His master answered, 'You wicked, lazy servant! You knew that I harvest where I did not plant and gather where I did not scatter.
Then you should have put my money with the bankers. When I came back, I would have gotten my money with interest.'
'Take the money from him and give it to the servant who has ten bags.
For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have plenty. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
Throw that useless servant out into the dark. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'
"When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit on His glorious throne.
All the nations will be gathered before Him. He will separate the people, like a shepherd separates sheep from goats.
He will put the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.
"Then the King will say to those on His right, 'Come, you who are blessed by My Father. Take your place in the kingdom that was made ready for you since the world began.
For I was hungry, and you gave Me food. I was thirsty, and you gave Me drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed Me.
I was naked, and you clothed Me. I was sick, and you visited Me. I was in prison, and you came to Me.'
"Then the good people will answer Him, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You? Or thirsty and give You drink?
When did we see You as a stranger and welcome You? Or naked and clothe You?
When did we see You sick or in prison and come to You?'
The King will answer them, 'Truly I tell you, when you did it for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did it for Me.'
"Then He will say to those on His left, 'Go away from Me, you who are cursed, into the fire that lasts forever. It was made ready for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry, and you did not give Me food. I was thirsty, and you did not give Me drink.
I was a stranger, and you did not welcome Me. I was naked, and you did not clothe Me. I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit Me.'
Then they will answer, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and not help You?'
He will answer them, 'Truly I tell you, when you did not do it for one of the least of these, you did not do it for Me.'
And these will go away to punishment that lasts forever, but the good people will go to life that lasts forever."
When Jesus finished all these words, He said to His followers,
“You know that the Passover is in two days. Then the Son of Man will be handed over to be killed on a cross.”
Then the chief priests and the elders of the people met in the yard of Caiaphas, the high priest.
They planned to catch Jesus by a trick and kill Him.
But they said, “Not during the feast, or the people may make trouble.”
Jesus was in Bethany. He was at the house of Simon the leper.
A woman came to Him. She had a jar of costly perfume. She poured it on His head while He sat at the table.
The followers saw this. They were upset. They said, “Why waste this?
It could have been sold for a lot of money. The money could have been given to poor people.”
Jesus knew this. He said to them, “Why bother this woman? She did a good thing for Me.
You will always have poor people with you. But you will not always have Me.
She poured this perfume on Me to get My body ready to be buried.
I tell you the truth. Wherever this good news is told in the whole world, what she did will be told too. People will remember her.”
Then one of the twelve, Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests.
He said, “What will you give me if I hand Him over to you?” They paid him thirty silver coins.
From then on, Judas looked for a good time to hand Him over.
On the first day of the bread with no yeast, the followers came to Jesus. They said, “Where do you want us to get ready for you to eat the Passover?”
He said, “Go into the city to a certain man. Tell him the Teacher says His time is near. He will eat the Passover with His followers at that man's house.”
The followers did what Jesus told them. They got the Passover ready.
When evening came, Jesus sat at the table with the twelve followers.
While they were eating, He said, “I tell you the truth. One of you will hand Me over.”
They were very sad. They began to say to Him, one after another, “Lord, is it I?”
He answered, “The one who dips his hand in the bowl with Me will hand Me over.
The Son of Man will go, just as it is written about Him. But it will be bad for the man who hands Him over. It would be better for that man if he had never been born.”
Judas, who would hand Him over, said, “Rabbi, is it I?” Jesus said to him, “You have said so.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread. He gave thanks and broke it. He gave it to His followers. He said, “Take and eat. This is My body.”
Then He took a cup. He gave thanks. He gave it to them. He said, “Drink from it, all of you.
For this is My blood of the agreement. It is poured out for many people. It brings forgiveness of sins.
I tell you, I will not drink wine again. I will not drink until that day. Then I will drink it new with you in My Father's kingdom.”
They sang a hymn. Then they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, “This very night you will all turn away from Me. For it is written, ‘I will hit the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
But after I rise, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
Peter answered, “Even if all the others turn away from You, I never will.”
Jesus said to him, “I tell you the truth. This very night, before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know Me.”
Peter said to Him, “Even if I must die with You, I will never say I do not know You.” All the followers said the same thing.
Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane. He said to His followers, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with Him. He began to feel very sad and troubled.
Then He said to them, “My soul is very sad, even to death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”
He went a little farther. He fell with His face to the ground. He prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this suffering pass from Me. Yet not what I want, but what You want.”
He came back to His followers. He found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Could you not keep watch with Me for one hour?
Keep watch and pray. Then you will not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
He went away again. He prayed, “My Father, if I must suffer, let Your will be done.”
He came back. He found them sleeping again. Their eyes were heavy.
He left them. He went away again. He prayed the same words a third time.
Then He came back to His followers. He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the time is near. The Son of Man is handed over to sinners.
Get up. Let us go. Look, the one who hands Me over is near.”
While He was still speaking, Judas came. He was one of the twelve. A big crowd came with him. They had swords and clubs. They came from the chief priests and elders of the people.
The man who would hand Him over had given them a sign. He said, “The one I kiss is the man. Grab him.”
Right away Judas went to Jesus. He said, “Greetings, Rabbi.” He kissed Him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you came to do.” Then the men came up. They put their hands on Jesus and took Him.
One of the men with Jesus reached for his sword. He pulled it out. He struck the servant of the high priest. He cut off his ear.
Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back in its place. All who take the sword will die by the sword.
Do you think I cannot ask My Father? He would send Me more than twelve armies of angels right now.
But how would the holy writings come true? They say it must happen this way.”
At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Did you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me, as if I were a robber? Every day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not arrest Me.
But all this has happened so the writings of the prophets would come true.” Then all the followers left Him and ran away.
Those who seized Jesus took Him to Caiaphas the high priest. The teachers of the law and elders were gathered there.
Peter followed Him far away. He went to the yard of the high priest. He went in and sat with the guards. He wanted to see what would happen.
The chief priests and the whole council tried to find false witness against Jesus. They wanted to put Him to death.
They did not find any, even though many false witnesses came forward. At last two came forward.
They said, “This man said he could destroy God's temple and build it again in three days.”
The high priest stood up. He said to Jesus, “Do you have no answer? What are these men saying against you?”
But Jesus was quiet. The high priest said to Him, “I make you swear by the living God. Tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus said to him, “You have said so. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power. You will see Him coming on the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes. He said, “He has spoken against God! Why do we need more witnesses? Look, you have now heard the evil words.”
“What do you think?” They answered, “He is guilty and should die.”
Then some spit in His face. They hit Him with their fists. Others slapped Him.
They said, “Christ, prophesy for us. Who hit you?”
Peter was sitting outside in the yard. A servant girl came to him. She said, “You also were with Jesus, the man from Galilee.”
But he denied it in front of everyone. He said, “I do not know what you mean.”
He went out to the gate. Another servant girl saw him. She said to the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth.”
Again he denied it. He swore, “I do not know the man.”
After a little while, the people standing there came up to Peter. They said, “Surely you are one of them. Your accent gives you away.”
Then he began to curse and swear. He said, “I do not know the man!” Right away a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had said: “Before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know Me.” He went outside and cried bitterly.
Early in the morning, all the top priests and the leaders of the people met. They planned how to kill Jesus.
They tied Jesus up and took Him to Pilate, the governor.
Judas was the one who had handed Jesus over. When he saw that Jesus was found guilty, he felt sorry. He took the thirty silver coins back to the top priests and leaders.
He said, "I sinned. I handed over an innocent man." The leaders answered, "That is not our problem. You deal with it."
Judas threw the money into the temple and left. Then he went and hanged himself.
The top priests picked up the coins. They said, "We cannot put this money into the temple treasury. It is money paid for a man's death."
They talked about it and used the money to buy a field from a potter. It was for burying strangers.
So that field has been called the Field of Blood ever since.
Then what the prophet Jeremiah said came true. He said, "They took the thirty silver coins, the price for the One the people of Israel set a price on.
They used them to buy the potter's field, just as the LORD told me."
Jesus stood in front of the governor. The governor asked Him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" Jesus said, "You said it."
While the top priests and leaders accused Him, Jesus said nothing.
Pilate said to Him, "Don't you hear all the things they are saying against you?"
Jesus did not answer even one word. This surprised the governor.
At the feast, the governor was used to letting one prisoner go free. The crowd could choose.
At that time they had a well-known prisoner named Barabbas.
When the people gathered, Pilate asked them, "Which one do you want me to set free: Barabbas or Jesus, who is called the Christ?"
Pilate knew they had handed Jesus over because they were jealous.
While Pilate was sitting on the judge's seat, his wife sent him a message. She said, "Stay away from that good man. I had a bad dream today because of Him, and it troubled me a lot."
The top priests and leaders talked the crowd into asking for Barabbas and having Jesus killed.
Pilate asked, "Which of the two do you want me to set free?" The people said, "Barabbas."
Pilate said, "Then what should I do with Jesus, who is called the Christ?" They all said, "Nail Him to a cross!"
Pilate asked, "Why? What bad thing did He do?" But they shouted even louder, "Nail Him to a cross!"
Pilate saw that it was no use. The crowd was getting louder. So he took water and washed his hands in front of them. He said, "I am not guilty of this man's death. You must take the blame."
All the people answered, "Let His death be on us and on our children!"
Then Pilate set Barabbas free. He had Jesus whipped and handed Him over to be nailed to a cross.
The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the governor's house. They called all the soldiers together around Him.
They took off His clothes and put a red robe on Him.
They made a crown from thorns and put it on His head. They put a stick in His right hand. Then they knelt in front of Him and made fun of Him. They said, "Hello, King of the Jews!"
They spit on Him. They took the stick and hit Him on the head with it.
After they made fun of Him, they took off the robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him away to nail Him to a cross.
On the way out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon. They made him carry Jesus' cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which means Place of the Skull.
They gave Him wine mixed with something bitter. He tasted it but did not want to drink it.
After they nailed Him to the cross, they divided His clothes by throwing lots.
Then they sat down and watched Him there.
They put a sign above His head. It said, "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
Two robbers were nailed to crosses with Him. One was on His right and one was on His left.
People walking by insulted Him. They shook their heads.
They said, "You said you could tear down the temple and build it again in three days. Save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!"
The top priests, teachers of the law, and leaders also made fun of Him.
They said, "He saved other people, but He cannot save Himself! He is the King of Israel. Let Him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in Him."
They said, "He trusts in God. Let God save Him now if He wants Him. After all, He said, 'I am the Son of God.'"
The robbers who were nailed to crosses with Him also insulted Him.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.
About three in the afternoon, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" That means, "My God, My God, why have You left Me?"
Some people standing there heard it and said, "He is calling for Elijah."
One of them ran and got a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a stick, and gave it to Jesus to drink.
The others said, "Leave Him alone. Let's see if Elijah comes to save Him."
Jesus cried out again in a loud voice and then gave up His spirit.
The curtain in the temple tore in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.
The tombs opened, and many holy people who had died were raised to life.
After Jesus rose, they came out of the tombs and went into the holy city. Many people saw them.
The army officer and the soldiers with him were guarding Jesus. When they saw the earthquake and everything that happened, they were very afraid. They said, "This man really was the Son of God!"
Many women were there, watching from far away. They had followed Jesus from Galilee and helped Him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
In the evening, a rich man named Joseph came. He was from Arimathea, and he was a follower of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body. Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He put it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out of the rock. He rolled a big stone in front of the tomb door and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there across from the tomb.
The next day was the day after the Preparation Day. The top priests and the Pharisees went to Pilate.
They said, "Sir, we remember that liar said, 'After three days I will rise again.'

So please order the tomb to be guarded until the third day. His followers might come and steal the body and tell the people, 'He has risen from the dead.' Then the last lie would be worse than the first."
Pilate said to them, "You have a guard. Go and make it as safe as you can."
They went and made the tomb safe. They sealed the stone and put guards there.
After the Sabbath day, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the tomb.
Suddenly the ground shook hard. An angel of the Lord came down from heaven. He went to the tomb and rolled the stone away. Then he sat on it.
He looked like lightning, and his clothes were white as snow.
The guards shook with fear. They became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, "Do not be afraid. I know you are looking for Jesus, who was put on a cross.
He is not here. He is alive again, just like He said. Come and see the place where He lay.
Then go quickly and tell His followers that He is alive again. He is going ahead of you to Galilee. You will see Him there. I have told you."
The women hurried away from the tomb. They were afraid, but they were also very happy. They ran to tell His followers.
Suddenly Jesus met them. He said, "Hello." The women came to Him. They held His feet and worshiped Him.
Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go and tell My brothers to go to Galilee. They will see Me there."
While the women were going, some guards went into the city. They told the chief priests everything that had happened.
The chief priests met with the elders. They made a plan. They gave the soldiers a lot of money.
They said, "Say that His followers came at night and stole Him while we were sleeping.
If the governor hears this, we will explain it to him. We will keep you out of trouble."
The soldiers took the money and did what they were told. This story spread among the Jews. It is still told today.
The eleven followers went to Galilee. They went to the mountain Jesus had told them about.
When they saw Him, they worshiped Him. But some doubted.
Jesus came to them and said, "All power in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.
So go and make followers of all nations. Baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
Teach them to obey everything I have told you. And I am with you always, even to the end of time."
This is the start of the good news about Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
The prophet Isaiah wrote, “I am sending My messenger ahead of You. He will get Your road ready.
A voice calls in the desert: ‘Get the Lord’s road ready. Make a straight path for Him.’”
John the Baptist came. He was in the desert. He told people to be baptized. This showed they were sorry for their sins. Then God would forgive them.
People from Jerusalem and all over Judea came to him. They said they were sorry for their sins. John baptized them in the Jordan River.
John wore clothes made of camel hair. He had a leather belt. He ate locusts and wild honey.
John told people, “Someone is coming after me. He is stronger than I am. I am not good enough to even untie His shoes.
I baptize you with water. But He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee. John baptized Him in the Jordan River.
As Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the sky open. The Holy Spirit came down on Him like a dove.
A voice came from heaven. It said, “You are My Son, whom I love. I am very happy with You.”
Right away, the Holy Spirit sent Jesus into the desert.
He stayed there 40 days. Satan tempted Him. Wild animals were there too. Angels took care of Him.
After John was put in jail, Jesus went to Galilee. He told people the good news from God.
He said, “The time has come. God’s kingdom is near. Be sorry for your sins and believe the good news.”
Jesus walked by the Sea of Galilee. He saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were fishing with nets.
Jesus said, “Come follow Me. I will teach you to fish for people.”
Right away, they left their nets and followed Him.
Jesus walked a little farther. He saw James and his brother John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in a boat fixing their nets.
Jesus called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men. Then they followed Jesus.
Jesus and His friends went to Capernaum. On the Sabbath, Jesus went into the meeting place and taught.
The people were amazed. He taught like someone with power. He did not teach like the teachers of the law.
In the meeting place, a man with an evil spirit shouted,
“What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Did you come to destroy us? I know who You are. You are the Holy One of God!”
Jesus said, “Be quiet! Come out of him!”
The evil spirit shook the man. It shouted loudly. Then it came out of him.
Everyone was amazed. They asked each other, “What is this? He teaches with power! He even tells evil spirits what to do, and they obey Him!”
Right away, news about Jesus spread all over Galilee.
Jesus left the meeting place. He went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.
Simon’s mother-in-law was in bed with a fever. They told Jesus about her.
He went to her. He took her hand and helped her up. The fever left her. Then she began to serve them.
That evening, after the sun went down, people brought Jesus everyone who was sick or had evil spirits.
The whole town came to the door.
Jesus healed many sick people. He also forced out many evil spirits. He did not let the spirits talk, because they knew who He was.
Very early in the morning, before daylight, Jesus got up. He went to a quiet place and prayed.
Simon and his friends went to look for Him.
They found Him and said, “Everyone is looking for You.”
Jesus said, “Let us go to the nearby towns. I want to preach there too. That is why I came.”
So He traveled all over Galilee. He preached in the meeting places and drove out evil spirits.
A man with a skin disease came to Jesus. He begged Him. He knelt down and said, “If You want to, You can make me clean.”
Jesus felt sorry for him. He reached out His hand and touched him. He said, “I want to. Be clean!”
Right away, the skin disease left the man.
Then Jesus sent him away with a strong warning.
He said, “Do not tell anyone about this. Go show yourself to the priest. Give the offering Moses told people to give when they are made clean. This will show everyone what happened.”
But the man went out and told everyone. He talked about it so much that Jesus could not go into a town openly. He stayed outside in quiet places. But people still came to Him from everywhere.
After a few days, Jesus came back to Capernaum. People heard He was home.
So many people came that there was no room left, not even by the door. Jesus told them God's word.
Some men brought a man who could not walk. Four men carried him.
They could not get close to Jesus because of the crowd. So they took off the roof where Jesus was. They made a hole and lowered the mat with the man on it.
Jesus saw their faith. He said to the man, "My child, your sins are forgiven."
Some teachers of the law were sitting there. They thought in their hearts,
"Why does this man talk like that? He is speaking against God. Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
Jesus knew right away in His spirit what they were thinking. He said to them, "Why do you think this in your hearts?
Which is easier to say to the man who cannot walk: 'Your sins are forgiven,' or 'Get up, take your mat, and walk'?
But I want you to know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins." Then He said to the man,
"I tell you, get up, take your mat, and go home."
The man got up right away. He took his mat and walked out in front of everyone. They were all amazed. They praised God. They said, "We have never seen anything like this!"
Jesus went out again by the sea. A big crowd came to Him, and He taught them.
As He walked by, He saw Levi, son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax booth. Jesus said, "Follow me." Levi got up and followed Him.
Later, Jesus was eating at Levi's house. Many tax collectors and sinners ate with Jesus and His followers. Many people followed Him.
The teachers of the law who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with sinners and tax collectors. They asked His followers, "Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus heard it. He said to them, "Healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do. I did not come to call good people, but sinners."
John's followers and the Pharisees were fasting. They came to Jesus and asked, "Why do John's followers and the Pharisees' followers fast, but your followers do not fast?"
Jesus said to them, "Can the friends of the groom fast while the groom is with them? As long as they have the groom with them, they cannot fast.
But the days will come when the groom is taken away from them. Then they will fast on that day."
No one sews a new patch on an old coat. If they do, the new piece pulls away from the old, and the tear gets worse.
No one puts new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the wine breaks the skins. The wine and the skins are lost. New wine goes into new wineskins.
On a Sabbath day, Jesus was walking through the grain fields. His followers began to pick grain as they walked.
The Pharisees said to Him, "Look! Why are they doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath?"
Jesus said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he and his men were hungry and needed food?
He went into God's house when Abiathar was high priest. He ate the bread that was set apart. Only priests were allowed to eat it. He also gave some to the men with him.
The Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
Another time Jesus went into the meeting house. A man there had a hand that was all dried up.
Some people watched Jesus. They wanted to find a reason to say He did wrong. They wanted to see if He would heal the man on the Sabbath.
Jesus said to the man with the bad hand, “Stand up in front of everyone.”
Then Jesus asked them, “Is it right on the Sabbath to do good or to do bad? Is it right to save a life or to kill?” But they did not say a word.
Jesus looked around at them. He was angry. He was sad because their hearts were hard. He said to the man, “Hold out your hand.” The man held it out. His hand was made well again.
The Pharisees left right away. They made a plan with the Herodians to kill Jesus.
Jesus went away with His followers to the lake. A big crowd from Galilee followed Him.
Many people came to Him from Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, and the lands across the Jordan River. People also came from around Tyre and Sidon. They came because they heard what He was doing.
Jesus told His followers to have a small boat ready for Him. He did not want the crowd to push Him.
He had healed many people. So sick people pushed in to touch Him.
When bad spirits saw Jesus, they fell down in front of Him. They cried out, “You are the Son of God!”
But Jesus told them again and again not to tell who He was.
Jesus went up on a hill. He called the people He wanted. They came to Him.
He chose twelve men to be with Him. He would send them out to tell the good news.
He gave them power to send bad spirits away.
These were the twelve: Simon, whom He named Peter;
James, the son of Zebedee, and his brother John, whom He named Boanerges, which means “sons of thunder”;
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot;
and Judas Iscariot, who later turned Jesus over to His enemies.
Jesus went into a house. Again a crowd came. It was so big that Jesus and His followers could not even eat.
When His family heard this, they came to take Him home. They said, “He has lost His mind.”
Teachers of the law came down from Jerusalem. They said, “He has Beelzebul! He sends out bad spirits by the power of the ruler of bad spirits.”
Jesus called them to Him. He spoke to them in stories. He said, “How can Satan send out Satan?
If a kingdom fights against itself, that kingdom cannot last.
If a family fights against itself, that family cannot last.
If Satan fights against himself, he cannot last. His end has come.
No one can go into a strong man’s house and take his things unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can take what he wants.”
“Truly I tell you, people will be forgiven for all their sins and for every bad thing they say.
But anyone who says bad things about the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven. They are guilty of a sin that lasts forever.”
Jesus said this because they were saying, “He has a bad spirit.”
Jesus’ mother and brothers came. They stood outside and sent someone to call Him.
A crowd was sitting around Jesus. They told Him, “Look, Your mother and brothers are outside. They are looking for You.”
“Who are My mother and My brothers?” Jesus asked.
Then He looked at the people sitting around Him. He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!
Anyone who does what God wants is My brother, My sister, and My mother.”
Again Jesus began to teach by the sea. A very big crowd came to Him. So He got into a boat and sat on the water. The whole crowd stood on the shore.
He taught them many things with stories. In His teaching He said to them:
"Listen! A farmer went out to plant seeds.
As he planted, some seeds fell by the path. Birds came and ate them.
Other seeds fell on rocky ground with little soil. They sprang up fast because the soil was not deep.
When the sun came up, they burned and dried up because they had no roots.
Other seeds fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them, and they gave no fruit.
Other seeds fell on good soil. They grew up and got bigger and gave fruit: one gave thirty, one gave sixty, and one gave one hundred.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."
When He was alone, the people around Him, with the twelve, asked Him about the stories.
He said to them, "The secret of God's kingdom is given to you. But to people outside, everything is in stories.
They look, but they do not really see. They listen, but they do not understand. Then they will not turn and be forgiven."
He said to them, "Do you not know this story? How will you know all the stories?"
These people are like the seed by the path. The message is planted, but as soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes the message away from them.
These people are like the seed on rocky ground. When they hear the message, they take it with joy.
But they have no root in themselves. They do not last long. When trouble or people hurt them because of the message, they give up.
Others are like the seed among thorns. They hear the message.
But the worries of this life, the lies of money, and wanting other things come in and choke the message. It does not grow.
These people are like the seed on good soil. They hear the message, take it in, and grow fruit: thirty, sixty, or one hundred."
He said to them, "Does a lamp come to be put under a basket or under a bed? No, it is put on a lamp stand.
Nothing is hidden that will not be shown. Nothing is kept secret that will not come into the light.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear."
He said to them, "Pay attention to what you hear. The way you measure will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.
Whoever has will be given more. Whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away."
He said, "God's kingdom is like this: a man throws seed on the ground.
Night and day he sleeps and wakes. The seed sprouts and grows, but he does not know how.
The ground makes fruit on its own: first a green stem, then a head of grain, then full grain in the head.
As soon as the fruit is ready, he cuts it down, because harvest time has come."
He said, "How can we show God's kingdom? What story can we use?
It is like a mustard seed. When it is planted in the ground, it is the smallest seed on earth.
But when it is planted, it grows up and becomes the biggest plant in the garden. It makes big branches, so the birds of the sky can rest in its shade."
He spoke the message to them with many stories like these, as much as they could understand.
He did not speak to them without a story. But when He was alone, He explained everything to His own followers.
That day, when evening came, He said to them, "Let us go to the other side."
They left the crowd and took Him in the boat, just as He was. Other boats were with Him.
A big storm with wind came up. The waves splashed into the boat, so the boat was already filling with water.
Jesus was in the back of the boat, sleeping on a pillow. They woke Him and said, "Teacher, don't you care that we are dying?"
He woke up and told the wind and the sea, "Quiet! Be still!" The wind stopped, and it became very calm.
He said to them, "Why are you afraid? Do you still not trust Me?"
They were very afraid and said to each other, "Who is this? Even the wind and the sea obey Him!"
Jesus and His followers went across the sea to the land of the Gerasenes.
As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, a man with a bad spirit came from the graves to meet Him.
The man lived among the graves. No one could tie him up, not even with chains.
People had often tied him with chains and foot chains. He broke the chains and smashed the foot chains. No one was strong enough to control him.
Night and day he was in the graves and in the hills. He cried out and hurt himself with stones.
The man saw Jesus from far away. He ran to Jesus and bowed down to Him.
He shouted, "What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You by God, don't hurt me!"
Jesus had said to the spirit, "Come out of this man, you bad spirit."
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" The spirit answered, "My name is Legion, because we are many."
The spirits begged Jesus not to send them out of that land.
A big herd of pigs was eating on the hillside.
The spirits begged, "Send us into the pigs, so we can go into them."
Jesus let them. The bad spirits came out of the man and went into the pigs. The herd, about two thousand pigs, ran down the hill into the sea and drowned.
The men who fed the pigs ran away. They told the people in the town and in the fields. The people came to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been controlled by demons. He was sitting down, wearing clothes, and thinking clearly. The people were afraid.
The people who had seen it told them what happened to the man and to the pigs.
The people began to beg Jesus to leave their land.
As Jesus got into the boat, the man who had been controlled by demons begged to go with Him.
Jesus did not let him. He said, "Go home to your people. Tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how He has been kind to you."
The man went away. He began to tell people in the Ten Towns what Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.
Jesus crossed back over the sea in the boat. A big crowd gathered around Him by the sea.
A man named Jairus came. He was a leader of the synagogue. He saw Jesus and fell at His feet.
He begged Jesus, "My little daughter is very sick. Please come and put Your hands on her. Then she will be healed and live."
Jesus went with him. A big crowd followed and pressed around Jesus.
A woman had been bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered much from many doctors. She had spent all her money. She was not better. She was worse.
She heard about Jesus. She came through the crowd from behind and touched His clothes.
She thought, "If I just touch His clothes, I will be healed."
Right away her bleeding stopped. She felt in her body that she was healed.
Jesus knew that power had gone out of Him. He turned around in the crowd and said, "Who touched My clothes?"
His followers said to Him, "You see the crowd pressing You. Why do You ask who touched You?"
Jesus looked around to see who had done it.
The woman knew what had happened to her. She came and fell down before Jesus. She was shaking with fear. She told Him the whole truth.
Jesus said to her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace. Be well and free from your sickness."
While Jesus was still speaking, some people came from the house of the synagogue leader. They said, "Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher anymore?"
Jesus paid no attention to what they said. He told the synagogue leader, "Don't be afraid. Just believe."
He let no one go with Him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James.
They came to the house of the synagogue leader. Jesus saw a lot of noise. People were crying loudly.
He went in and said to them, "Why are you making so much noise and crying? The child is not dead. She is only sleeping."
They laughed at Him. Jesus made them all leave. He took the child's father and mother and the followers who were with Him. They went into the room where the child was.
Jesus took the child by the hand. He said to her, "Talitha koum." This means, "Little girl, I say to you, get up!"
Right away the girl stood up and walked around. She was twelve years old. The people were completely amazed.
Jesus told them strongly not to let anyone know about this. He also said to give the girl something to eat.
Jesus left that place and went to His hometown. His disciples went with Him.

On the Sabbath, He began to teach in the synagogue. Many people heard Him and were amazed. They asked, "Where did this man get these things? What wisdom was given to Him? How can He do such big miracles?"
"Isn't this the carpenter? Isn't He Mary's son? Aren't James, Joses, Judas, and Simon His brothers? Aren't His sisters here with us?" They were upset with Him.
Jesus said, "A prophet is honored everywhere except in his hometown, with his relatives, and in his own home."
He could not do any big miracle there. He only put His hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He was amazed because they did not believe. Then He went around the villages and taught.
Jesus called the twelve disciples. He began to send them out two by two. He gave them power over evil spirits.
He told them to take nothing for the trip but a walking stick. They could not take bread, a bag, or money in their belts.
They could wear sandals, but they could not wear two shirts.
He said, "When you go into a house, stay there until you leave that place.
If a place will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave. That will be a warning to them."
So they went out and told people to turn from sin.
They forced out many evil spirits. They put oil on many sick people and healed them.
King Herod heard about Jesus. His name was known everywhere. Some people said, "John the Baptist has come back to life! That is why these powers work in Him."
Others said, "He is Elijah." Others said, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets."
But Herod said, "John, the man I killed, has come back to life!"
Herod had sent men to arrest John. They tied him up and put him in jail. Herod did this because of Herodias. She was the wife of his brother Philip, but Herod had married her.
John had told Herod, "It is not right for you to have your brother's wife."
Herodias hated John and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
Herod was afraid of John, because he knew John was a good and holy man. He liked to listen to John, even though John's words confused him, and he listened with joy.
On Herod's birthday, he gave a dinner for his leaders, army officers, and the important people of Galilee.
His wife's daughter came in and danced. She pleased Herod and his guests. The king said to the girl, "Ask me for anything you want, and I will give it to you."
He promised her, "I will give you whatever you ask, up to half of my kingdom."
She went out and asked her mother, "What should I ask for?" Her mother said, "Ask for the head of John the Baptist."
Right away, the girl hurried to the king and asked, "I want you to give me John the Baptist's head on a plate right now."
The king was very sad. But because of his promise and his guests, he did not want to say no.
Right away, he sent a soldier to bring John's head. The soldier went and cut off John's head in the jail.
He brought the head on a plate and gave it to the girl. Then the girl gave it to her mother.
When John's disciples heard about it, they came and took his body and put it in a tomb.
The disciples came back to Jesus. They told Him everything they had done and taught.
Jesus said, "Come with me to a quiet place and rest for a while." Many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
So they went away in a boat to a quiet place by themselves.
But many people saw them leave. They knew who they were. People ran there on foot from all the towns and got there first.
When Jesus got out of the boat, He saw a big crowd. He felt sorry for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So He began to teach them many things.
It was getting late. The disciples came to Jesus and said, "This is a lonely place, and it is already late.
Send the people away so they can go to the nearby farms and villages and buy food for themselves."
Jesus answered, "You give them something to eat." The disciples said, "Should we go buy bread for two hundred coins and feed them?"
Jesus said, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." They found out and said, "Five loaves and two fish."
Jesus told them to make everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
They sat down in rows of hundreds and fifties.
Jesus took the five loaves and two fish. He looked up to heaven and blessed them. He broke the loaves and gave them to His disciples to pass out. He also divided the two fish among everyone.
The disciples picked up twelve baskets of leftover bread and fish.
Five thousand men ate the bread.
Right away, Jesus made His disciples get into the boat. He told them to go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida. He would send the crowd away.
After He said goodbye, He went up on a mountain to pray.
That evening, the boat was in the middle of the sea. Jesus was alone on land.
He saw His disciples working hard to row. The wind was against them. Late at night, Jesus came to them. He was walking on the sea. He was going to pass by them.
When they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out. They thought He was a ghost.
They all saw Him and were scared. Right away, Jesus spoke to them: "Be brave! It is I. Do not be afraid."
He got into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were very amazed.
They had not understood about the loaves. Their hearts were hard.
They crossed over and came to land at Gennesaret. They tied up the boat.
As soon as they got out, people recognized Jesus.
People ran through that whole area. They carried sick people on beds to wherever they heard Jesus was.
Wherever Jesus went, in villages, cities, or farms, people put sick people in the town squares. They begged Him to let them touch the edge of His coat. Everyone who touched it was healed.
Some Jewish leaders and teachers of the law came from Jerusalem. They gathered around Jesus.
They saw some of His followers eating bread with hands that were not washed.
The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands first. They follow old rules passed down by leaders.
Even after coming from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. They also wash cups, bowls, pots, and even couches. They follow many rules like these.
The Pharisees and teachers of the law asked Jesus, "Why do your followers not follow the old rules? Why do they eat bread with unwashed hands?"
Jesus said to them, "Isaiah was right about you pretenders. He wrote that these people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
They worship Me for nothing. They teach rules made by people.
You leave God's command and hold to people's rules."
Jesus also said, "You do a good job of setting aside God's command so you can keep your own rules.
Moses said to honor your father and mother, and that anyone who curses his father or mother must die.
But you say that if a man tells his parents this help is a gift to God, then he does not have to help them.
You stop him from doing anything for his parents.
You cancel God's word with your own rules. You do many things like this."
Then Jesus called the crowd to Him. He said, "Listen to Me and understand.
Nothing that goes into a person from the outside can make that person unclean. What comes out of a person is what makes that person unclean."
When Jesus went into a house away from the crowd, His followers asked Him what the story meant.
He said to them, "Are you so slow to understand? Don't you see that food from outside cannot make a person unclean?
It does not go into the heart. It goes into the stomach and then out of the body. This makes all foods clean."
Jesus said, "What comes out of a person is what makes that person unclean.
Bad thoughts come from inside a person's heart. So do sexual sins, stealing, murder, and cheating in marriage.
Greed, meanness, lies, wrong wants, jealousy, saying bad things about God, pride, and foolish acts also come from inside.
All these bad things come from inside and make a person unclean."
Jesus left there and went to the area of Tyre. He wanted to stay hidden, but He could not.
A woman heard about Him. Her little girl had an evil spirit. The woman came and fell at Jesus' feet.
She was from a Greek family in Syria and Phoenicia. She asked Jesus to throw the demon out of her daughter.
Jesus said to her, "First let the children eat all they want. It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
The woman answered, "Yes, Lord. But even the dogs under the table eat the crumbs that fall from the children's food."
Jesus said to her, "Because of your words, go home. The demon has left your daughter."
She went home and found her child lying on the bed. The demon was gone.
Jesus left the area of Tyre again. He went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee. He was in the area of the Ten Towns.
People brought a man to Jesus. The man could not hear and could not speak well. They begged Jesus to put His hand on the man.
Jesus took the man away from the crowd. He put His fingers in the man's ears. He spat and touched the man's tongue.
Then Jesus looked up to heaven and sighed. He said to the man, "Ephphatha," which means "Be opened."
Right away the man could hear. His tongue was freed, and he spoke clearly.
Jesus told them not to tell anyone. But the more He told them, the more they told others.
They were very amazed. They said, "He has done everything well. He makes deaf people hear and people who cannot speak talk."
In those days, a big crowd came again. They had nothing to eat. Jesus called His disciples to Him.
Jesus felt sorry for them. He said, "They have been with Me for three days now. They have nothing to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they may get too weak on the way. Some of them came from far away."
His disciples answered, "Where can anyone find enough bread to feed all these people out here in this empty place?"
Jesus asked, "How many loaves of bread do you have?" "Seven," they said.
Jesus told the crowd to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves. He thanked God for them. Then He broke them. He gave them to His disciples to pass out.
The disciples also had a few small fish. Jesus blessed them and told His disciples to pass them out too.
Everyone ate and was full. The disciples picked up seven baskets of leftover pieces.
About four thousand people were there. Then Jesus sent them home.
Right away, Jesus got into a boat with His disciples. They went to the area of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came out. They began to argue with Jesus. They tested Him. They wanted Him to show a miracle from heaven.
Jesus sighed deeply. He said, "Why does this group of people ask for a miracle? I tell you the truth. No miracle will be given to them."
Then Jesus left them. He got back into the boat. He went to the other side of the lake.
The disciples forgot to bring bread. They had only one loaf with them in the boat.
Jesus warned them. He said, "Be careful. Watch out for the bad teaching of the Pharisees and of Herod."
The disciples talked among themselves. They said, "We do not have any bread."
Jesus knew what they were saying. He said, "Why are you talking about having no bread? Do you still not understand? Are your hearts hard?
You have eyes. Can you not see? You have ears. Can you not hear? Do you not remember?"
Jesus said, "When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets of leftover pieces did you pick up?" "Twelve," they said.
Jesus said, "And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets did you pick up?" "Seven," they said.
Jesus said, "Do you still not understand?"
They came to Bethsaida. People brought a blind man to Jesus. They begged Him to touch the man.
Jesus took the blind man by the hand. He led him out of the town. He spit on the man's eyes. He put His hands on him. Then He asked, "Do you see anything?"
The man looked up. He said, "I see people. They look like trees walking around."
Then Jesus put His hands on the man's eyes again. The man looked hard. His sight came back. He could see everything clearly.
Jesus sent him home. He said, "Do not go into the town."
Jesus and His disciples went to the villages near Caesarea Philippi. On the way, He asked His disciples, "Who do people say I am?"
They answered, "Some say John the Baptist. Some say Elijah. Others say one of the prophets."
Jesus asked them, "Who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Christ."
Jesus told them not to tell anyone about Him.

Then Jesus began to teach them. He said the Son of Man must suffer many things. The leaders, the top priests, and the teachers of the law would not accept Him. They would kill Him. But after three days, He would rise again.
He said this plainly. Peter took Jesus aside and began to scold Him.
Jesus turned around. He saw His disciples. He scolded Peter. He said, "Get away from Me, Satan! You are thinking like people, not like God."
Jesus called the crowd and His disciples to Him. He said, "If anyone wants to follow Me, he must say no to himself. He must carry his cross. Then he must follow Me."
Jesus said, "Anyone who wants to save his life will lose it. But anyone who loses his life for Me and for the good news will save it."
Jesus said, "What good is it if a man gains the whole world but loses his soul?"
Jesus said, "What can a man give to get his soul back?"

Jesus said, "If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this sinful and unfaithful group, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him. This will happen when He comes with His Father's glory and with the holy angels."
Truly, I tell you, some people standing here will not die before they see God's kingdom come with power.
Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with Him. He led them up a high mountain. They were alone.
There Jesus changed. His clothes became very white. They were whiter than any person on earth could make them.
Elijah and Moses appeared and talked with Jesus.
Peter said, "Teacher, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
They were very scared. Peter did not know what to say.
Then a cloud came over them. A voice came from the cloud: "This is My Son, whom I love. Listen to Him!"
Suddenly they looked around. They saw no one but Jesus.
As they came down the mountain, Jesus told them, "Do not tell anyone what you saw until the Son of Man rises from the dead."
They kept this to themselves. They asked each other what "rising from the dead" meant.
They asked Jesus, "Why do the teachers of the law say Elijah must come first?"
Jesus said, "Elijah does come first. He makes all things ready. It is also written that the Son of Man will suffer many things and be treated like nothing.
But I tell you, Elijah has already come. People did to him what they wanted, just as it is written about him."
When they came to the other disciples, they saw a big crowd around them. Teachers of the law were arguing with them.
As soon as the crowd saw Jesus, they were amazed. They ran to greet Him.
Jesus asked, "What are you arguing about with them?"
A man from the crowd said, "Teacher, I brought my son to You. He has a spirit that makes him unable to speak.
Wherever it takes him, it throws him down. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and his body gets stiff. I asked Your disciples to drive it out, but they could not."
Jesus said, "You people do not believe! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me."
They brought the boy. When the spirit saw Jesus, it shook him. he fell on the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked the father, "How long has this been happening to him?"
The father said, "Since he was a little child. It has often thrown him into fire and water to kill him. If You can do anything, have pity on us and help us."
Jesus said, "If You can? All things are possible for the one who believes."
Right away the father cried out, "I believe! Help me not to doubt!"
Jesus saw the crowd running together. He spoke firmly to the evil spirit. "You spirit that makes him unable to hear or speak, I command you to come out of him and never go back in."
The spirit screamed and shook him hard. Then it came out. The boy looked like he was dead. Many people said, "He is dead."
But Jesus took his hand and helped him up. he stood up.
Later, when Jesus went into a house, His disciples asked Him privately, "Why could we not drive it out?"
Jesus said, "This kind can come out only by prayer."
They left there and traveled through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know.
He was teaching His disciples. He said, "The Son of Man will be handed over to men. They will kill Him. After three days He will rise again."
But they did not understand what He meant. They were afraid to ask Him.
They came to Capernaum. When Jesus was in the house, He asked them, "What were you arguing about on the road?"
They said nothing. On the road they had argued about who was the greatest.
Jesus sat down and called the Twelve. He said, "If anyone wants to be first, he must be last of all and servant of all."
He took a little child and stood the child in the middle of them. He hugged the child and said,
"Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me. Whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me."
John said to Him, "Teacher, we saw a man driving out demons in Your name. He does not follow us. We tried to stop him."
Jesus said, "Do not stop him. No one who does a miracle in My name can soon speak badly about Me.
Whoever is not against us is for us.
Truly I tell you, anyone who gives you a cup of water because you belong to Christ will not lose his reward."
Jesus said, "If anyone leads one of these little ones who believe in Me to sin, it would be better for him to have a heavy stone tied around his neck and be thrown into the sea."
Jesus said, "If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life with one hand than to go into hell with two hands, into the fire that never goes out."
"If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to be thrown into hell with two feet."
"If your eye causes you to sin, throw it out. It is better for you to enter God's kingdom with one eye than to be thrown into hell with two eyes.
There the worms do not die, and the fire is never put out."
For everyone will be tested by fire.
Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, how can you make it salty again? Keep your salt, and live in peace with each other.
Jesus left that place. He went to the land of Judea. He went across the Jordan River. Again, big crowds came to Him. He taught them, like He always did.
Some Pharisees came to test Him. They asked, "Is it right for a man to send his wife away?"
Jesus answered, "What did Moses tell you to do?"
They said, "Moses let a man write a paper to send his wife away. Then he could send her away."
Jesus said, "Moses wrote that rule for you because your hearts were hard.
But from the start, God made them male and female.
That is why a man leaves his father and mother. He joins his wife.
The two become one body. So they are not two anymore. They are one body.
So what God joined together, no person should split apart."
Later, in the house, the followers asked Him about this.
Jesus said, "If a man sends his wife away and marries another woman, he is not faithful to her.
If a woman sends her husband away and marries another man, she is not faithful either."
People brought little children to Jesus. They wanted Him to touch them. But the followers told them to stop.
Jesus saw this. He was upset. He said, "Let the little children come to Me. Do not stop them. God's kingdom belongs to people like them.
I tell you the truth. Anyone who does not receive God's kingdom like a little child will not go in."
Jesus hugged the children. He put His hands on them. He blessed them.
As Jesus started on His way, a man ran up to Him. He knelt down. He said, "Good Teacher, what must I do to have life that lasts forever?"
Jesus said, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good but God alone.
You know the rules. Do not murder. Do not be unfaithful in marriage. Do not steal. Do not lie about others. Do not cheat. Respect your father and mother."
The man said, "Teacher, I have kept all these since I was young."

Jesus looked at him. Jesus loved him. Jesus said, "You are missing one thing. Go and sell what you have. Give the money to poor people. Then you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow Me."
The man became sad. He went away sad. He had many things.

Jesus looked around. He said to His followers, "How hard it is for rich people to enter God's kingdom!" The followers were surprised at His words. Jesus said again, "Children, how hard it is to enter God's kingdom!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom."
The followers were even more surprised. They said to each other, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them. He said, "People cannot do this. But God can do all things."
Peter said, "Look, we left everything and followed You."
Jesus said, "I tell you the truth. Anyone who leaves home, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children, or fields for Me and for the good news

will get a hundred times more now in this life. He will get homes, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields, along with hard times. And in the world to come, he will have life that never ends.
But many who are first will be last. And many who are last will be first."

They were on the way up to Jerusalem. Jesus was walking ahead of them. The followers were amazed. The people who followed were afraid. Again, Jesus took the twelve aside. He began to tell them what would happen to Him.

He said, "We are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and teachers of the law. They will say He must die. Then they will hand Him over to people who are not Jews.
They will make fun of Him. They will spit on Him. They will whip Him. Then they will kill Him. But after three days, He will rise again."
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus. They said, "Teacher, we want You to do something for us."
Jesus said, "What do you want Me to do for you?"
They said, "Let one of us sit at Your right hand. Let the other sit at Your left hand when You are king."
Jesus said, "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup I will drink? Can you be baptized the way I will be baptized?"
They said, "We can." Jesus said, "You will drink the cup I drink. You will be baptized like I am baptized.
But I cannot choose who sits at My right or left. That is for those God has prepared."
The other ten followers heard this. They were angry with James and John.
Jesus called them together. He said, "You know that rulers of other lands rule over their people. Their leaders order them around.
But it is not like that with you. Whoever wants to be great among you must be your servant.
Whoever wants to be first must be the servant of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served. He came to serve. He came to give His life to set many people free."
They came to Jericho. As Jesus and His followers were leaving Jericho, a blind man sat by the road. His name was Bartimaeus. He was the son of Timaeus. He begged for money.
He heard that Jesus of Nazareth was there. He began to shout, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Many people told him to be quiet. But he shouted even more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped. He said, "Call him." They called the blind man. They said, "Cheer up! Get up! He is calling you."
The man threw off his coat. He jumped up. He came to Jesus.
Jesus asked him, "What do you want Me to do for you?" The blind man said, "Teacher, I want to see."
Jesus said, "Go. Your faith has saved you." Right away, the man could see. He followed Jesus on the road.
As Jesus and His friends came near Jerusalem, near Bethphage and Bethany by the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His followers.
He said to them, "Go into the village across from you. As soon as you go in, you will find a young donkey tied up. No one has ever sat on it. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone says to you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord needs it. He will send it back soon.'"
They went and found the young donkey outside by the road, tied at a door. They untied it.
Some people standing there asked, "What are you doing? Why are you untying the donkey?"
They told them what Jesus had said, and the people let them go.
They brought the young donkey to Jesus. They put their coats on it, and Jesus sat on it.
Many people spread their coats on the road. Others cut branches from the fields and spread them on the road.
The people walking ahead and behind shouted, "Save us! God bless the One who comes in the name of the Lord!
God bless the kingdom of our father David that is coming! Save us, God in heaven!"
Jesus went into Jerusalem and into the temple. He looked all around. It was already late, so He went out to Bethany with the twelve.
The next day, as they left Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
He saw a fig tree far away with leaves on it. He went to see if it had fruit. But when He got there, He found only leaves. It was not the time for figs.
Jesus said to the tree, "No one will ever eat fruit from you again." His followers heard Him say this.

They came to Jerusalem again. Jesus went into the temple. He began to throw out the people who were buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the chairs of those selling doves.
He did not let anyone carry things through the temple.
He taught them and said, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.' But you have made it a hideout for robbers."
The leading priests and teachers of the law heard this. They looked for a way to kill Him. They were afraid of Him, because all the people were amazed at His teaching.
When evening came, they went out of the city.
The next morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.
Peter remembered and said to Him, "Teacher, look! The fig tree you cursed has dried up."
Jesus said to them, "Have faith in God.
I tell you the truth: If anyone says to this mountain, 'Move and throw yourself into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, it will happen for him.
So I tell you, when you pray and ask for anything, believe that you have received it, and you will have it.
When you stand and pray, if you have anything against anyone, forgive them. Then your Father in heaven will forgive you for your sins."
They came to Jerusalem again. As Jesus was walking in the temple, the leading priests, teachers of the law, and elders came to Him.
They asked Him, "By what right do you do these things? Who gave you this right?"
Jesus said to them, "I will ask you one thing. Answer Me, and I will tell you by what right I do these things.
Was John's baptism from heaven or from people? Answer Me."
They talked among themselves. They said, "If we say it came from heaven, He will ask why you did not believe John.
But if we say it came from people, we are afraid of the crowd. Everyone thinks John was a true prophet."
So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." Jesus said to them, "Then I will not tell you by what right I do these things."
Jesus began to speak to them in stories. A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it. He dug a wine press. He built a tower. He rented the vineyard to farmers. Then he went away.
At harvest time, he sent a servant to the farmers to get some fruit from the vineyard.
The farmers took the servant, beat him, and sent him away with nothing.
Then the man sent another servant. They hit him on the head and treated him badly.
He sent another one, and they killed him. He sent many more. Some they beat. Some they killed.
The man had one son left. He loved his son. He sent him last. He thought, “They will respect my son.”
But the farmers said to each other, “This is the one who will get everything. Come, let’s kill him. Then the vineyard will be ours.”
So they took him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those farmers. Then he will give the vineyard to others.
Haven’t you read this part of the Bible? “The stone the builders said no to has become the most important stone.
The Lord did this, and it is wonderful to us.”
They wanted to arrest Jesus. They knew He told the story against them. But they were afraid of the crowd. So they left Him and went away.
Some Pharisees and some Herodians came to Jesus. They wanted to trap Him with His words.
They said, “Teacher, we know You are honest. You do not care what people think. You teach God’s way truly. Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar, or not? Should we pay, or not?”
Jesus knew they were pretending. He said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a coin. I want to see it.”
They brought a coin. Jesus asked, “Whose picture is this? Whose words are on it?” They said, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus said, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s. Give to God what is God’s.” They were amazed at Him.
Some Sadducees came to Jesus. They do not believe people rise from the dead. They asked Him,
“Teacher, Moses wrote this for us: If a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, the brother should marry her. Then they can have children for the dead brother.
There were seven brothers. The first brother married her. He died and left no child.
The second brother married her and died. He left no child. The third brother did the same.
All seven brothers married her and left no children. Last of all, the woman died.
When people rise from the dead, whose wife will she be? All seven had married her.”
Jesus said, “You are wrong. You do not know the Bible or God’s power.
When people rise from the dead, they do not marry. They are not given in marriage. They are like angels in heaven.
Now, about dead people rising: Have you not read in Moses’ book, at the bush? God said to Moses, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
He is not the God of dead people. He is the God of living people. You are very wrong.”
One of the teachers of the law came. He heard them arguing. He saw that Jesus answered well. He asked Jesus, “Which command is first of all?”
Jesus answered, “The first is this: ‘Hear, Israel. The Lord our God is one Lord.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, all your mind, and all your strength.’
The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other command is bigger than these.”
The teacher said to Jesus, “Teacher, You are right. God is one. There is no other God but Him.
To love God with all your heart, all your understanding, and all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself, is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
Jesus saw that he answered wisely. He said, “You are not far from God’s kingdom.” After that, no one dared ask Him anything.
While Jesus was teaching in the temple, He asked, “How can the teachers of the law say that the Christ is David’s son?”
David himself said by the Holy Spirit, “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.’”
David calls Him Lord. So how can He be David’s son? The crowd listened to Him with joy.

Jesus said in His teaching, “Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk in long robes. They like greetings in the marketplaces. They like the best seats in the places of worship. They like the best places at dinners.
They pray long prayers to show off. These men will be punished even more.”
Jesus sat across from the temple money box. He watched how the crowd put money into it. Many rich people put in a lot.
Then a poor widow came. She put in two small coins. Together they were worth very little.
Jesus called His disciples. He said, “I tell you the truth. This poor widow put in more than all the others who put money into the box.”
They all gave from what they had extra. But she gave from her need. She put in all she had. It was her whole life.
As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look at these big stones and buildings!”
Jesus said, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left on another. They will all be torn down.”
Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, across from the temple. Peter, James, John, and Andrew came to Him alone.
They said, “Tell us, when will these things happen? What sign will show that all these things are about to be finished?”
Jesus began to tell them, “Watch out! Don't let anyone trick you.
Many will come using My name. They will say, ‘I am He,’ and they will trick many people.
“When you hear about wars and news of wars, don't be scared. These things must happen, but the end is not yet.
Nation will rise against nation. Kingdom will rise against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in many places. There will be famines. These are just the start of the hard times.
“Watch out for yourselves. People will hand you over to courts. You will be beaten in meeting places. Because of Me, you will stand before rulers and kings. You will tell them about Me.
The good news must first be told to all nations.
When they arrest you and hand you over, don't worry ahead of time about what to say. Say what is given to you at that time. You will not be the ones speaking. The Holy Spirit will speak.
“Brother will hand over brother to die. A father will hand over his child. Children will turn against their parents and kill them.
Everyone will hate you because of My name. But the one who stays strong to the end will be saved.
“When you see the terrible thing that destroys standing where it should not be—let the reader understand—then people in Judea must run to the mountains.
If someone is on the roof, don't go down into the house to get anything.
If someone is in the field, don't go back to get a coat.
It will be very hard for pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days.
Pray that it won't happen in winter.
“Those days will have worse trouble than any time since God made the world until now. Nothing like it will ever happen again.
If the Lord had not made those days shorter, no one would live. But He made them shorter for the sake of His chosen people.
“If someone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ don't believe it.
False Christs and false prophets will come. They will do signs and wonders to trick God's chosen people. If it were possible, they would trick even them.
So watch out. I have told you everything ahead of time.
“But in those days, after that trouble, the sun will go dark. The moon will not give its light.
The stars will fall from the sky. The powers in heaven will shake.
Then people will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
Then He will send His angels. He will gather His chosen people from all directions, from one end of the earth to the other.
“Learn this lesson from the fig tree. When its branch gets soft and leaves come out, you know summer is near.
So when you see these things happening, you know He is near, right at the door.
I tell you the truth: the people living now will not all die before all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will end, but My words will never end.
“No one knows that day or hour. The angels in heaven don't know. The Son doesn't know. Only the Father knows.
Watch out and stay awake, because you don't know when the time will come.
“It is like a man who went on a trip. He left his house and gave each servant a job. He told the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So stay awake. You don't know when the owner of the house will come. It could be evening, midnight, when the rooster crows, or morning.
Don't let him come suddenly and find you sleeping.
What I say to you, I say to everyone: Stay awake!”
It was two days before Passover and the Feast of Bread Without Yeast. The chief priests and teachers of the law wanted to trick Jesus and kill Him.
They said, "We must not do it during the feast. The people might start a riot."
Jesus was in Bethany at the house of Simon, who had leprosy. A woman came with a stone jar of very costly perfume made from pure nard. She broke the jar and poured the perfume on Jesus' head.
Some people were angry. They said to each other, "Why waste this perfume?
It could have been sold for more than three hundred silver coins and given to poor people." They scolded her.
But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why are you bothering her? She has done a good thing for Me.
You will always have poor people with you. You can help them anytime you want. But you will not always have Me.
She did what she could. She poured perfume on My body to get Me ready for burial.
I tell you the truth: Wherever the good news is told in all the world, people will also tell what she did. They will remember her."
Judas Iscariot was one of the Twelve. He went to the chief priests to hand Jesus over to them.
They were glad to hear it. They promised to give him money. Judas looked for a good time to turn Jesus in.
On the first day of the Feast of Bread Without Yeast, when people killed the Passover lamb, Jesus' followers asked Him, "Where do you want us to go and get ready for you to eat the Passover?"
He sent two of His followers. He said, "Go into the city. You will meet a man carrying a jar of water. Follow him.
Tell the owner of the house he goes into, 'The Teacher asks where His guest room is. He wants to eat the Passover there with His followers.'
He will show you a big room upstairs. It will be ready and furnished. Get things ready for us there."
The followers went into the city. They found everything just as He said. They got the Passover ready.
That evening, Jesus came with the Twelve.
While they were sitting at the table eating, Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: One of you who eats with Me will hand Me over."
They were sad. They asked Him one by one, "It is not me, is it?"
He said, "It is one of the Twelve. It is the one who dips bread in the bowl with Me.
The Son of Man will go just as the Bible says about Him. But it will be very bad for the man who hands the Son of Man over. It would be better for him if he had never been born."
While they ate, Jesus took bread. He thanked God and broke it. He gave it to them and said, "Take this. It is My body."
Then He took a cup. He gave thanks and gave it to them. They all drank from it.
He said, "This is My blood of the new agreement. It is poured out for many people.
I tell you the truth: I will not drink grape juice again until the day I drink it new in God's kingdom."
They sang a song. Then they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus said to them, "All of you will turn away from Me. The Bible says, 'I will hit the shepherd, and the sheep will run away.'
But after I rise from death, I will go ahead of you to Galilee."
Peter said, "Even if everyone else turns away, I will not."
Jesus said to him, "I tell you the truth: Tonight, before the rooster crows two times, you will say three times that you do not know Me."
Peter said even more strongly, "Even if I have to die with You, I will never say I do not know You." All the others said the same thing.
They came to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to His followers, "Sit here while I pray."
He took Peter, James, and John with Him. He began to feel very troubled and upset.
He said to them, "My heart is so sad I could die. Stay here and keep watch."
He went a little farther. He fell to the ground and prayed that, if possible, this hard time would pass.
He said, "Abba, Father, You can do anything. Take this cup away from Me. But do not do what I want. Do what You want."
He came back and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, "Simon, are you asleep? Could you not stay awake one hour?
Stay awake and pray. Then you will not fall into trouble. The spirit wants to do right, but the body is weak."
He went away again and prayed the same words.
He came back and found them sleeping again. Their eyes were heavy. They did not know what to say to Him.
He came the third time and said, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough! The time has come. Look! The Son of Man is being handed over to sinful people.
Get up! Let us go! The one who will hand Me over is here."
While Jesus was still talking, Judas came. He was one of the Twelve. A crowd came with him. They had swords and clubs. The chief priests, teachers of the law, and elders had sent them.
Judas had given them a sign. He said, "The one I kiss is the man. Grab Him and take Him away safely."
Judas went straight to Jesus. He said, "Rabbi!" and kissed Him.
They grabbed Jesus and arrested Him.
One of the men standing there pulled out a sword. He hit the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
