Jesus said to them, "Did you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me like I am a robber?
I was with you every day in the temple teaching, and you did not arrest Me. But this happened so the Bible would come true."
Everyone left Him and ran away.
A young man was following Jesus. He was wearing only a linen cloth. The men grabbed him.
He ran away naked and left the cloth behind.
They led Jesus to the high priest. All the chief priests, elders, and teachers of the law met together.
Peter followed far behind. He went into the courtyard of the high priest. He sat with the guards and warmed himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole council wanted proof against Jesus so they could kill Him. But they could not find any.
Many people lied about Him. Their stories did not match.
Some stood up and lied about Him. They said,
"We heard Him say, 'I will tear down this temple made by people. In three days I will build another one not made by people.' "
But even their stories did not match.
Then the high priest stood up in front of everyone. He asked Jesus, "Do you have no answer? What do these men say against you?"
But Jesus stayed quiet. He did not answer. The high priest asked again, "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
Jesus said, "I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power. He will come with the clouds of heaven."
The high priest tore his clothes. He said, "Why do we need more witnesses?
You have heard the bad words against God. What do you think?" They all said He was guilty and should die.
Some began to spit on Him. They covered His face. They hit Him with their fists. They said, "Tell us what will happen!" The guards took Him and hit Him.
Peter was still in the courtyard below. One of the servant girls of the high priest came by.
She saw Peter warming himself. She looked at him and said, "You were with Jesus from Nazareth too."
But he said no. "I do not know Him. I do not understand what you are talking about." Then he went out to the front yard, and a rooster crowed.
The servant girl saw him again. She began to say to the people standing there, "This man is one of them."
But he said no again. After a little while, the people standing there said to Peter, "You are one of them. You are from Galilee."
Then he began to curse and swear. He said, "I do not know this man you are talking about."
Right away the rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered what Jesus had said: "Before the rooster crows two times, you will say three times that you do not know Me." Then Peter cried.
Early in the morning, the chief priests, older leaders, and teachers of the law met together. The whole Jewish council agreed. They tied Jesus up. They led Him away and handed Him to Pilate.
Pilate asked Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?" Jesus answered, "That's what you say."
The chief priests said many bad things against Him.
Pilate asked Him again, "Won't you answer? Look how many things they say against you."
But Jesus did not answer anymore. Pilate was amazed.
At the feast, Pilate used to let one prisoner go free. The people could choose.
A man named Barabbas was in jail with rebels. They had killed someone during a riot.
The crowd came and asked Pilate to do what he always did.
Pilate asked them, "Do you want me to let the King of the Jews go free for you?"
He knew the chief priests had handed Jesus over because they were jealous.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd. They asked for Barabbas instead.
Pilate asked them again, "What do you want me to do with the man you call the King of the Jews?"
Pilate said, "Why? What bad thing did He do?" But they shouted even louder, "Crucify Him!"
Pilate wanted to make the crowd happy. So he let Barabbas go free. He had Jesus whipped. Then he handed Jesus over to be crucified.
The soldiers led Jesus into the courtyard. This place was called the Praetorium. They called all the soldiers together.
They put a purple robe on Him. They made a crown of thorns and put it on His head.
They began to say to Him, "Greetings, King of the Jews!"
They hit His head with a stick. They spit on Him. They got down on their knees and pretended to worship Him.
After they made fun of Him, they took the purple robe off Him. They put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to be crucified.
A man named Simon was passing by. He was from Cyrene. He was the father of Alexander and Rufus. He was coming from the country. The soldiers forced him to carry Jesus' cross.
They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha. That means "Place of the Skull."
They offered Him wine mixed with a spice called myrrh. But He did not take it.
They hung Him on the cross. They divided His clothes among themselves. They threw dice to see who would get what.
It was nine o'clock in the morning when they crucified Him.
A sign said why He was being killed. It said, "THE KING OF THE JEWS."
They also crucified two robbers with Him. One was on His right side, and one was on His left.
People walking by made fun of Him. They shook their heads and said, "Ha! You said You could tear down the temple and build it again in three days.
Come down from the cross and save Yourself!"
The chief priests and teachers of the law also made fun of Him. They said to each other, "He saved other people, but He can't save Himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down from the cross now. Then we will see and believe." The men crucified with Him also insulted Him.
At noon, darkness came over the whole land. It lasted until three in the afternoon.
At three o'clock, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" That means, "My God, My God, why have You left Me?"
Some people standing there heard it. They said, "Listen! He is calling Elijah."
Someone ran and soaked a sponge in sour wine. He put it on a stick and gave Jesus a drink. He said, "Wait! Let's see if Elijah comes to take Him down."
Jesus cried out with a loud voice and died.
The curtain in the temple tore in two from top to bottom.
A Roman officer was standing in front of Him. He saw how Jesus died. He said, "This man really was the Son of God."
Some women were watching from far away. They included Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome.
They had followed Jesus and helped Him when He was in Galilee. Many other women had also come with Him to Jerusalem.
It was already evening. It was the day before the Sabbath.
Joseph came from the town of Arimathea. He was an important man in the Jewish council. He was also waiting for God's kingdom. He was brave. He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body.
Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. He called the Roman officer and asked if Jesus had been dead for a while.
When he learned from the officer, he gave the body to Joseph.
Joseph bought a linen cloth. He took Jesus down from the cross. He wrapped Him in the cloth. He put Him in a tomb cut out of rock. He rolled a stone in front of the tomb door.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses watched where Jesus was laid.
After the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices. They wanted to put the spices on Jesus' body.
Very early on Sunday, when the sun came up, they went to the tomb.
They asked each other, “Who will roll the stone away from the door of the tomb for us?”
But when they looked up, they saw that the stone was already rolled away. It was very big.
They went into the tomb. There they saw a young man. He wore a white robe. He sat on the right side. The women were amazed.
The young man said to them, “Do not be amazed. You are looking for Jesus from Nazareth. He was put on a cross. But He is alive again. He is not here. Look at the place where they put Him.
Go and tell His followers and Peter that He is going ahead of you to Galilee. You will see Him there, just as He told you.”
The women left the tomb and ran away. They were shaking and shocked. They were afraid. They did not say anything to anyone.
Early on Sunday, after Jesus rose from the dead, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene. He had sent seven demons out of her before.
She went and told the people who had been with Him. They were sad and crying.
They heard that Jesus was alive. They heard that Mary had seen Him. But they did not believe it.
Later, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of His followers. They were walking to the country.
Those two went and told the rest. But the rest did not believe them.
Later, Jesus appeared to the eleven while they were eating. He scolded them for not believing. They had stubborn hearts. They did not believe the people who saw Him alive again.
Jesus said to them, “Go into all the world. Tell the good news to everything God made.
Anyone who believes and is baptized will be saved. But anyone who does not believe will be punished.
These signs will follow those who believe. In My name, they will send demons out. They will speak in new languages.
They will pick up snakes with their hands. If they drink anything deadly, it will not hurt them. They will put their hands on sick people, and the sick people will get well.”
After the Lord Jesus finished speaking to them, He was taken up into heaven. He sat in the place of honor next to God.
The followers went out. They preached everywhere. The Lord worked with them. He made their words sure by the miracles that followed.
Many people have tried to write down the things that happened among us.
They wrote what the first people who saw it and helped teach the good news told us.
I have studied all of this carefully from the start. So I decided to write it down in order for you, Theophilus.
I want you to know that the things you were taught are true.
When Herod was king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah. He was from the priest group of Abijah. His wife was named Elizabeth. She was from Aaron's family.
Both of them did what was right in God's eyes. They followed all the Lord's commands without blame.
But they had no children. Elizabeth could not have a baby. They were both very old.
One day, Zechariah was doing his priest work. His group was on duty.
He was chosen to go into the Lord's temple and burn incense.
The whole crowd of people prayed outside while the incense burned.
Then an angel of the Lord stood on the right side of the incense altar.
Zechariah saw him and was scared. Fear came over him.
The angel said, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah. God has heard your prayer.
Your wife Elizabeth will have a son for you.

You will name him John. he will bring you joy and gladness. Many people will be happy when he is born. he will be great in the Lord's eyes. he will not drink wine or strong drink. he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before he is born.
he will turn many of Israel's people back to the Lord their God.
he will go before the Lord with the spirit and power of Elijah. he will turn fathers' hearts to their children. he will help stubborn people become wise. he will get the Lord's people ready."
Zechariah said to the angel, "How can I know this? I am an old man. My wife is very old too."
The angel answered, "I am Gabriel. I stand in front of God. I was sent to talk to you and bring you this good news.
But you did not believe my words. So you will not be able to speak until these things happen. My words will come true at the right time."
The people were waiting for Zechariah. They were surprised that he stayed in the temple so long.
When he came out, he could not speak to them. They knew he had seen something special in the temple. He made signs to them, but he stayed unable to speak.
When his days of service were over, he went home.
After some days, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant. She stayed hidden for five months. She said, "The Lord has done this for me.
In these days He took away my shame among people."
In the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee named Nazareth.
He was sent to a young woman who was promised to marry a man named Joseph. Joseph was from David's family. The young woman's name was Mary.
The angel came to her and said, "Greetings, Mary. You are very special. The Lord is with you."
Mary was troubled by his words. She wondered what kind of greeting this was.
The angel said, "Do not be afraid, Mary. You have found favor with God.
You will become pregnant and have a son. You will name Him Jesus.
He will be great. He will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David.
He will rule over Jacob's family forever. His kingdom will never end."
Mary said to the angel, "How can this be? I have not been with a man."
The angel answered, "The Holy Spirit will come to you. The power of the Most High will cover you. So the holy child born to you will be called the Son of God."
Look, your relative Elizabeth has also become pregnant with a son in her old age. People called her unable to have children, but now she is in her sixth month.
Nothing is too hard for God.
Mary said, "I am the Lord's servant. Let it happen to me just as you said." Then the angel left her.
Soon after that, Mary got ready and hurried to a town in the hills of Judea.
She went into Zechariah's house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the baby jumped in her belly. Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She cried out in a loud voice, "You are blessed among women! The child you are carrying is blessed too.
Why has this happened to me? The mother of my Lord has come to me!
As soon as I heard your greeting, the baby in me jumped for joy.
You are blessed because you believed. What the Lord said to you will come true."
Mary said, "My soul praises the Lord.
My spirit is happy in God my Savior.
He has looked kindly on me, His humble servant. From now on, all people will call me blessed.
The Mighty One has done great things for me. His name is holy.
He shows mercy to people who honor Him, from one family to the next.
"He has shown His power. He scattered people who were proud in their hearts.
He brought down rulers from their thrones. He lifted up humble people.
He filled hungry people with good things. He sent rich people away with nothing.
He remembered to be kind, just as He promised our fathers and Abraham's family forever."
Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months. Then she went back home.
When it was time for Elizabeth to have her baby, she gave birth to a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had been very kind to her. They were happy with her.
On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child. They wanted to name him after his father, Zechariah.
But his mother said, "No. His name will be John."
They said to her, "No one in your family has that name."
They made signs to his father to ask what he wanted to name the child.
He asked for something to write on. He wrote, "His name is John." Everyone was surprised.
Right away, Zechariah could speak again. His tongue was freed, and he praised God.
All the neighbors were afraid. People all over the hill country of Judea talked about these things.
Everyone who heard about it thought about it. They said, "What will this child become? The Lord's hand is with him."
Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke: "Praise the Lord, the God of Israel!
He has come to help His people and set them free.
He has raised up a strong Savior for us from the family of His servant David.
This is what He promised long ago through His holy prophets.
He promised to save us from our enemies and from everyone who hates us.
He promised to be kind to our fathers and remember His holy promise.
He promised Abraham that we could serve Him without fear.
We have been rescued from our enemies.
We can serve Him in a holy and right way all our days.
"And you, my child, will be called a prophet of the Most High.
You will go before the Lord to make His paths ready.
You will tell His people how they can be saved by having their sins forgiven.
Because our God is so kind, a new day will shine on us from heaven. It will give light to people who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. It will guide our feet into the way of peace."
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He lived in the desert until he was shown to Israel.
At that time, Caesar Augustus sent out an order. Everyone in the world had to be counted.
This was the first time people were counted while Quirinius was governor of Syria.
Everyone went to his own town to be counted.
Joseph went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea. He went to Bethlehem, the town of David. He went because he was from David's family.
He went to be counted with Mary. She was promised to marry him, and she was going to have a baby.
While they were there, the time came for her baby to be born.
She had her first son. She wrapped Him in cloths and laid Him in a feeding box. There was no room for them in the place to stay.
There were shepherds in the fields nearby. They were watching their sheep at night.
An angel of the Lord stood by them. The glory of the Lord shone around them. They were very afraid.
"Do not be afraid. I bring you good news. It will bring great joy to all people.
Today in David's town a Savior is born for you. He is Christ the Lord.
This is how you will know Him. You will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a feeding box."
Suddenly a great crowd of angels from heaven was with the angel. They praised God and said,
"Glory to God in the highest. Peace on earth to people He is pleased with."
When the angels went back to heaven, the shepherds said to each other, "Let's go to Bethlehem. Let's see this thing the Lord has told us about."
They hurried and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby. The baby was lying in the feeding box.
When they saw Him, they told what had been said about this child.
Everyone who heard it was amazed at what the shepherds said.
Mary kept all these things in her heart. She thought about them.
The shepherds went back. They praised and thanked God for all they had heard and seen. It was just as they had been told.
When the baby was eight days old, He was circumcised. He was named Jesus. That was the name the angel gave before Mary was pregnant with Him.
When the time came for Mary and Joseph to be made clean, they brought Him to Jerusalem. They brought Him to give Him to the Lord.
It is written in the law of the Lord, "Every first baby boy belongs to the Lord."
They also gave an offering, as the law of the Lord says. They gave two doves or two young pigeons.
In Jerusalem there was a man named Simeon. He was good and loved God. He was waiting for God to comfort Israel. The Holy Spirit was on him.
The Holy Spirit had told him he would not die before he saw the Lord's Christ.
The Spirit led him to the temple. When the parents brought in the child Jesus, Simeon came too. They were doing what the law said.
Simeon took the baby in His arms. He praised God and said,
"Now, Lord, You can let Your servant go in peace.
I have seen Your salvation with my own eyes.
You made it ready for all people.
It is a light to show the way to the nations. It brings glory to Your people Israel."
Jesus' father and mother were amazed at what was said about Him.
Simeon blessed them. Then he said to Mary, "This child will cause many in Israel to fall and to rise. He will be a sign people speak against.
Then the secret thoughts of many hearts will be shown. And a sword will go through your own soul too."
There was also a prophet named Anna. She was the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She was very old. She had lived with her husband seven years after she got married.
Then she was a widow until she was 84. She stayed at the temple. She worshiped God night and day. She fasted and prayed.
At that time she came up to them. She thanked God. She talked about the baby to all who were waiting for Jerusalem to be set free.
When Joseph and Mary had done everything the law of the Lord said, they went back to Galilee. They went to their own town, Nazareth.
The child grew strong. He was filled with wisdom. God's grace was on Him.
Every year Jesus' parents went to Jerusalem for the Passover feast.
When He was twelve years old, they went up as usual for the feast.
After the feast days were over, they started home. But the boy Jesus stayed in Jerusalem. His parents did not know it.
They thought He was with the group. They traveled one day. Then they looked for Him among family and friends.
They did not find Him. So they went back to Jerusalem to look for Him.
After three days they found Him in the temple. He was sitting with the teachers. He was listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard Him was amazed at His understanding and His answers.
When His parents saw Him, they were surprised. His mother said, "Child, why did You do this to us? Your father and I have been looking for You. We were very worried."
Jesus said, "Why were you looking for Me? Did you not know I had to be in My Father's house?"
They did not understand what He said.
He went down to Nazareth with them. He obeyed them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
Jesus grew in wisdom and in years. He grew in favor with God and with people.
In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar's rule, Pontius Pilate was the ruler of Judea. Herod ruled Galilee. His brother Philip ruled Iturea and Trachonitis. Lysanias ruled Abilene.
Annas and Caiaphas were high priests. God's word came to John, Zechariah's son, in the desert.
John went all around the land near the Jordan River. He told people to be baptized. This showed they were sorry for their sins. God would forgive them.
This is what the prophet Isaiah wrote: "A voice calls out in the desert, 'Get the Lord's road ready. Make straight paths for Him.'
Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be made low. Crooked roads will become straight. Rough roads will become smooth.
And all people will see God's saving power."
John said to the crowds coming to be baptized, "You snakes! Who warned you to run away from God's coming anger?
Do things that show you are truly sorry. Do not start saying to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' I tell you, God can make children for Abraham from these stones.
The ax is already at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not make good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
The crowds asked him, "What should we do?"
John answered, "If you have two shirts, give one to someone who has none. If you have food, do the same."
Tax collectors also came to be baptized. They asked, "Teacher, what should we do?"
John said, "Do not collect more money than you are told to."
Some soldiers asked him, "What should we do?" He said, "Do not rob anyone. Do not lie about people. Be happy with your pay."
The people were waiting. They wondered in their hearts if John might be the Christ.
John answered everyone, "I baptize you with water. But someone stronger than me is coming. I am not good enough to untie His sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

"He has a tool in His hand to separate grain. He will clean the place where grain is threshed. He will gather the good grain into His barn. But He will burn the worthless husks with fire that cannot be put out."
John said many other things too. He told the people the good news.
But John spoke against Herod the ruler. Herod had married his brother's wife, Herodias. John also spoke against all the other bad things Herod did.
So Herod added one more wrong. He locked John in prison.
When all the people were being baptized, Jesus was baptized too. As He prayed, heaven opened.
The Holy Spirit came down on Him in a body like a dove. A voice from heaven said, "You are My Son, whom I love. I am very pleased with You."
Jesus was about thirty years old when He began His work. People thought He was Joseph's son. Joseph was Heli's son.
Heli was the son of Matthat. Matthat was the son of Levi. Levi was the son of Melchi. Melchi was the son of Jannai. Jannai was the son of Joseph.
Joseph was the son of Mattathias. Mattathias was the son of Amos. Amos was the son of Nahum. Nahum was the son of Esli. Esli was the son of Naggai.
Naggai was the son of Maath. Maath was the son of Mattathias. Mattathias was the son of Semein. Semein was the son of Josech. Josech was the son of Joda.
Joda was the son of Joanan. Joanan was the son of Rhesa. Rhesa was the son of Zerubbabel. Zerubbabel was the son of Shealtiel. Shealtiel was the son of Neri.
Neri was the son of Melchi. Melchi was the son of Addi. Addi was the son of Cosam. Cosam was the son of Elmadam. Elmadam was the son of Er.
Er was the son of Joshua. Joshua was the son of Eliezer. Eliezer was the son of Jorim. Jorim was the son of Matthat. Matthat was the son of Levi.
Levi was the son of Simeon. Simeon was the son of Judah. Judah was the son of Joseph. Joseph was the son of Jonam. Jonam was the son of Eliakim.
Eliakim was the son of Melea. Melea was the son of Menna. Menna was the son of Mattatha. Mattatha was the son of Nathan. Nathan was the son of David.
David was the son of Jesse. Jesse was the son of Obed. Obed was the son of Boaz. Boaz was the son of Salmon. Salmon was the son of Nahshon.
Nahshon was the son of Amminadab. Amminadab was the son of Admin. Admin was the son of Arni. Arni was the son of Hezron. Hezron was the son of Perez. Perez was the son of Judah.
Judah was the son of Jacob. Jacob was the son of Isaac. Isaac was the son of Abraham. Abraham was the son of Terah. Terah was the son of Nahor.
Nahor was the son of Serug. Serug was the son of Reu. Reu was the son of Peleg. Peleg was the son of Eber. Eber was the son of Shelah.
Shelah was the son of Cainan. Cainan was the son of Arphaxad. Arphaxad was the son of Shem. Shem was the son of Noah. Noah was the son of Lamech.
Lamech was the son of Methuselah. Methuselah was the son of Enoch. Enoch was the son of Jared. Jared was the son of Mahalalel. Mahalalel was the son of Cainan.
Cainan was the son of Enosh. Enosh was the son of Seth. Seth was the son of Adam. Adam was the son of God.
Jesus was full of the Holy Spirit. He left the Jordan River, and the Spirit led Him into the desert.
There the devil tested Him for forty days. Jesus ate nothing during those days. When the days ended, He was hungry.
The devil said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
Jesus answered, "It is written, 'A person does not live by bread alone.'"
The devil led Him up high and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment.
The devil said to Him, "I will give You all this power and glory. It has been given to me, and I give it to anyone I want.
So if You bow down and worship me, it will all be Yours."
Jesus answered, "It is written, 'Worship the LORD your God and serve Him only.'"
The devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the highest part of the temple. He said, "If You are the Son of God, jump down from here.
For it is written, 'He will command His angels to take care of You.
They will lift You up in their hands so You will not hit Your foot on a stone.'"
Jesus answered, "It is also written, 'Do not test the LORD your God.'"
When the devil finished all his testing, he left Him for a while.
Jesus went back to Galilee in the power of the Spirit. News about Him spread through all the nearby land.
He taught in their meeting places, and everyone praised Him.
He went to Nazareth, where He grew up. On the day of rest He went into the meeting place, as He usually did, and stood up to read.
Someone gave Him the book of the prophet Isaiah. He opened the book and found the place where these words were written:

"The Spirit of the LORD is on Me. He has chosen Me to tell good news to the poor. He has sent Me to tell prisoners they are free. He has sent Me to help blind people see again. He has sent Me to set free people who are hurt.
He has sent Me to tell about the year when the LORD will show His kindness."
Then He closed the book, gave it back to the helper, and sat down. Everyone in the meeting place stared at Him.
He began to say to them, "Today these words from God have come true while you listen."
Everyone spoke well of Him. They were amazed at the kind words from His mouth. They said, "Isn't this Joseph's son?"
Jesus said to them, "Surely you will say this to Me: 'Doctor, heal yourself!' And you will say, 'Do here in your hometown what we heard You did in Capernaum.'"
He said, "I tell you the truth, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
I tell you the truth, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah. It did not rain for three and a half years, and there was a great hunger over all the land.
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them. He was sent to a widow in Zarephath in Sidon.
And there were many people with skin disease in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet. None of them was healed except Naaman the Syrian."
When all the people in the meeting place heard this, they were very angry.
They got up, threw Him out of the town, and took Him to the edge of the hill where the town was built. They wanted to throw Him down the cliff.
But He walked right through the crowd and went on His way.
He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and taught them on the day of rest.
They were amazed at His teaching, because He taught with power.
In the meeting place there was a man with an evil spirit. He cried out in a loud voice,
"Go away! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!"
Jesus said to him, "Be quiet! Come out of him!" The evil spirit threw the man down in the middle and came out of him without hurting him.
Everyone was amazed. They said to each other, "What is this teaching? He gives orders to evil spirits with power, and they come out!"
News about Him spread everywhere in the area.
Jesus left the meeting place and went to Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was sick with a high fever, and they asked Him about her.
He stood over her and told the fever to go away. It left her right away, and she got up and served them.
When the sun went down, all who had sick people with different diseases brought them to Him. He put His hands on each one and healed them.
Demons also came out of many people. They shouted, "You are the Son of God!" But He told them to be quiet because they knew He was the Christ.
When day came, He went to a quiet place. The crowds looked for Him and came to Him. They tried to keep Him from leaving them.
But He said to them, "I must tell the good news of God's kingdom to other towns too. That is why I was sent."
And He kept preaching in the meeting places of Judea.
One day, Jesus stood by Lake Gennesaret. The crowd pushed in to hear God's word.
He saw two boats by the lake. The fishermen had gotten out and were washing their nets.
Jesus got into one of the boats. It was Simon's boat. He asked Simon to push out a little from land. Then Jesus sat in the boat and taught the crowd.
When He finished speaking, He said to Simon, "Put out into the deep water. Let down your nets to catch fish."
Simon answered, "Master, we worked all night and caught nothing. But at your word I will let down the nets."
They did this, and they caught a lot of fish. Their nets began to break.
They signaled to their friends in the other boat to come help. They came and filled both boats. The boats began to sink.
Simon Peter saw this. He fell at Jesus' knees and said, "Go away from me, Lord! I am a sinful man."
He and all his friends were amazed at the catch of fish.
Jesus said to Simon, "Don't be afraid. From now on you will catch people." James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were Simon's fishing friends. They were amazed too.
They pulled their boats onto the shore. They left everything and followed Him.
In one town, a man was full of leprosy. He saw Jesus. He fell on his face and begged, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Jesus reached out His hand and touched him. He said, "I am willing. Be clean!" Right away the leprosy left him.
Jesus told him, "Don't tell anyone. But go and show yourself to the priest. Offer what Moses told you to offer. This will be a sign to them."
News about Him spread even more. Big crowds came to hear Him and to be healed from sickness.
But Jesus often went to quiet places to pray.
One day Jesus was teaching. Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from Jerusalem and from every town in Galilee and Judea. The Lord's power was with Him to heal people.
Some men carried a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him in and lay him before Jesus.
They could not get through the crowd. So they went up on the roof. They lowered him through the roof tiles into the middle, right in front of Jesus.
Jesus saw their faith. He said, "Man, your sins are forgiven."
The teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to think, "Who is this man? He speaks against God! Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He answered them, "Why do you question this in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so you may know the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins." Then He said to the paralyzed man, "I tell you, get up, take your mat, and go home."
Right away the man stood up in front of them. He picked up what he had been lying on and went home. He praised God.
Everyone was amazed. They praised God. They were filled with fear and said, "We saw amazing things today!"
After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. Jesus said to him, "Follow Me."
Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
Levi gave a big dinner for Jesus at his house. Many tax collectors and other people were eating with them.
The Pharisees and their teachers of the law complained to His disciples. They said, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered, "Healthy people don't need a doctor, but sick people do.
I did not come to call good people. I came to call sinners to turn to God."
They said to Him, "John's disciples often fast and pray. So do the Pharisees' disciples. But your disciples eat and drink."
Jesus said to them, "Can you make the wedding guests fast while the groom is with them?
But the days will come when the groom is taken away from them. Then they will fast."
He told them this story: "No one tears a patch from a new coat and puts it on an old coat. If he does, the new coat will tear. The patch from the new coat will not match the old coat.
No one puts new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins. The wine will spill out, and the skins will be ruined.
New wine must be put into new wineskins.
No one who drinks old wine wants new wine. He says, 'The old is better.'"
On a Sabbath day, Jesus was walking through grain fields. His followers picked grain heads and rubbed them in their hands to eat.
Some Pharisees said, "Why are you doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered, "Have you not read what David did when he and his men were hungry?
He went into God's house. He took the holy bread. He gave it to his men, and they ate it. Only priests were allowed to eat that bread.
The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
On another Sabbath, Jesus went into the meeting place and taught. A man was there. His right hand was weak and dry.
The teachers of the law and the Pharisees watched Jesus. They wanted a reason to accuse Him. They watched to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said to the man with the weak hand, "Get up and stand in the middle." The man got up and stood there.
Jesus said to them, "I ask you: Is it right to do good on the Sabbath or to do bad? Is it right to save a life or to destroy it?"
Jesus looked at all of them. He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did it, and his hand was made well.
They were very angry. They talked with each other about what to do to Jesus.
In those days, Jesus went up on a mountain to pray. He prayed to God all night.
When day came, He called His followers. He chose twelve of them and named them apostles.
They were Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon called the Zealot,
Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who later turned against Jesus.
Jesus came down with them and stood on a flat place. A large crowd of His followers was there. Many people came from Judea, Jerusalem, and the seashore near Tyre and Sidon.
They came to hear Him and to be healed from their sicknesses. People troubled by evil spirits were healed.
Everyone in the crowd tried to touch Him, because power came from Him and healed them all.
Jesus looked at His followers and said, "Blessed are you poor, because God's kingdom is yours.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, because you will be filled. Blessed are you who cry now, because you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, push you away, say mean things to you, and say your name is bad because of the Son of Man.

Be glad on that day. Jump for joy! You have a big reward in heaven. Their fathers did the same things to the prophets." "But trouble is coming for you rich people, because you already have your good things.
Trouble is coming for you who are full now, because you will be hungry. Trouble is coming for you who laugh now, because you will be sad and cry.
Trouble is coming for you when all people say good things about you. Their fathers did the same to the false prophets."
"But I say to you who listen: Love your enemies. Do good to those who hate you.
Say good things about people who curse you. Pray for those who are mean to you.
If someone hits you on the cheek, let him hit the other cheek too. If someone takes your coat, do not stop him from taking your shirt.
Give to everyone who asks you. If someone takes your things, do not ask for them back.
Do to others what you want them to do to you."
"If you love people who love you, what good is that? Even sinners love people who love them.
If you do good to people who do good to you, what good is that? Even sinners do that.
If you lend to people you hope will pay you back, what good is that? Even sinners lend to sinners to get the same back.

But love your enemies. Do good. Lend, and do not hope to get it back. Then your reward will be big. You will be children of the Most High, because He is kind to people who are not thankful and to bad people.
Be kind, just like your Father is kind."
"Do not judge others, and you will not be judged. Do not blame others, and you will not be blamed. Forgive others, and you will be forgiven.

Give, and it will be given to you. People will give you a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over. They will pour it into your lap. The way you measure for others is the way it will be measured to you."
Jesus also told them a story: "Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a hole?
A student is not above his teacher. But when a student is fully trained, he will be like his teacher."
"Why do you see the tiny piece in your brother's eye, but you do not see the big stick in your own eye?

How can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the tiny piece out of your eye,' when you do not see the big stick in your own eye? You faker! First take the stick out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly to take the piece out of your brother's eye."
"A good tree does not make bad fruit. A bad tree does not make good fruit.
Each tree is known by its own fruit. People do not pick figs from thorn bushes. They do not pick grapes from a briar bush.
A good man brings good things out of the good stored in his heart. A bad man brings bad things out of the bad stored in his heart. What a person says shows what is in his heart."
"Why do you call Me 'Lord, Lord,' but you do not do what I say?
I will show you what everyone is like who comes to Me, hears My words, and does them.
He is like a man who builds a house. He digs down deep and sets the base on rock. A flood comes. The river hits that house. But it cannot shake it, because it was built well.
But the one who hears and does not do is like a man who builds a house on the ground with no base. The river hits it. It falls right away. And the house is badly broken."
When Jesus finished saying all these things to the people, He went into Capernaum.
An army leader had a servant he cared about very much. The servant was sick and about to die.
When the leader heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to Him. He asked Jesus to come and heal his servant.
They came to Jesus and begged Him hard. They said, "He deserves for you to do this for him,
because he loves our people and built our meeting place for us."
Jesus went with them. When He was not far from the house, the army leader sent friends to Him. They said, "Lord, please do not trouble Yourself. I am not good enough for You to come into my house.
That is why I did not think I should come to You myself. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
I am a man under orders too. I have soldiers under me. I tell one, 'Go,' and he goes. I tell another, 'Come,' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
When Jesus heard this, He was amazed at the man. He turned to the crowd following Him and said, "I tell you, I have not found faith like this, even in Israel."
The men who were sent went back home. They found the servant well.
Soon after, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, and a big crowd too.
As He came near the town gate, a dead man was being carried out. He was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. A big crowd from the town was with her.
The Lord saw her. He felt sorry for her. He said to her, "Do not cry."
He came up and touched the coffin. The men carrying it stopped. He said, "Young man, I say to you, get up."
The dead man sat up and began to talk. Jesus gave him back to his mother.
Everyone was afraid. They praised God. They said, "A great prophet has come among us," and "God has come to help His people."
News about Jesus spread all over Judea and the nearby places.
John's disciples told him about all these things.
John called two of his disciples. He sent them to the Lord to ask, "Are You the One who is to come, or should we look for someone else?"
The men came to Jesus. They said that John the Baptist had sent them to ask if You are the One who is to come, or if they should look for someone else.
At that time, Jesus healed many people of sickness and pain. He also forced out bad spirits. He made many blind people see.

He answered them, "Go and tell John what you have seen and heard. Blind people see. Lame people walk. People with skin disease are made clean. Deaf people hear. Dead people are raised. Poor people hear good news."
"Happy is the person who does not lose faith in Me."
After John's messengers left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John. He said, "What did you go out into the desert to see? A weak person blown about by the wind?
What did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothes? People in fancy clothes who live in comfort are in kings' houses.
What did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes. I tell you, he is more than a prophet.
This is the one the Bible talks about. It says that God is sending His messenger ahead of You to get Your way ready.
I tell you, no one born of a woman is greater than John. But the least person in God's kingdom is greater than he."
All the people, even tax collectors, heard this. They agreed that God was right, because they had been baptized by John.
But the strict Jewish leaders and the teachers of the law did not accept God's plan for themselves. They were not baptized by John.
Jesus said, "What are the people of this time like? What can I compare them to?
They are like children sitting in the market. They call to each other that they played a happy song but the others did not dance, and that they sang a sad song but the others did not cry.
John the Baptist came. He did not eat bread or drink wine. You say he has a demon.
The Son of Man came. He eats and drinks. You say He eats too much and drinks too much and is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!
But wisdom is shown to be right by all she does."
One of the strict Jewish leaders asked Jesus to eat with him. Jesus went into his house and sat down to eat.
A woman in the town who had sinned much heard that Jesus was eating there. She brought a small bottle of perfume.
She stood behind Him at His feet. She cried. She began to wet His feet with her tears. She dried them with her hair. She kissed His feet. She put perfume on them.

The strict Jewish leader who invited Jesus saw this. He said to himself, "If this man were a prophet, he would know who this woman is and what kind of woman she is. She is a sinner, and she is touching him."
Jesus answered him, "Simon, I have something to say to you." "Say it, Teacher," he said.
"A man who lent money had two people who owed him money. One owed 500 silver coins. The other owed 50.
Neither could pay. So the man forgave both. Which one will love him more?"
Simon answered, "I think the one who owed more." Jesus said, "You are right."

Then Jesus turned to the woman. He said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I came into your house. You did not give Me water for My feet. But she wet My feet with her tears and dried them with her hair.
You did not kiss Me. But she has not stopped kissing My feet since I came in.
You did not put oil on My head. But she put perfume on My feet.
So I tell you, her many sins are forgiven. She loved much. But a person who is forgiven little loves little."
He said to her, "Your sins are forgiven."
The other people eating with Him began to say to themselves, "Who is this man who even forgives sins?"
He said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace."
Soon after this, Jesus went from town to town and village to village. He told people the good news about God's kingdom. The Twelve went with Him.
Some women who had been healed from bad spirits and sicknesses also went. Mary, called Magdalene, was one. Seven demons had gone out of her.
Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's manager, was another. Susanna and many other women helped them with the things they had.
When a big crowd came together, and people from many towns came to Him, He told them a story.
"A farmer went out to plant his seed. As he planted, some seed fell by the road. People walked on it, and birds ate it.
Some fell on rock. It grew, but it dried up because it had no water.
Some fell among thorns. The thorns grew with it and choked it.
Some fell on good soil. It grew and made a hundred times more." Then He said, "Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."
His disciples asked Him, "What does this story mean?"
He said, "You have been given to know the secrets of God's kingdom. But other people are told in stories, so they look but do not really see, and listen but do not understand."
"This story means: The seed is God's word.
The seeds by the road are people who hear it. Then the devil comes and takes the word from their hearts, so they may not believe and be saved.
The seeds on rock are people who hear the word and take it with joy. But they have no root. They believe for a while, then turn away when trouble comes.
The seeds among thorns are people who hear it. But as they go, worries, money, and fun things in life choke the word, and it does not grow fruit.
The seeds in good soil are people who hear the word with a good and honest heart. They hold on to it and grow fruit with patience."
"No one lights a lamp and covers it with a bowl or puts it under a bed. They put it on a stand, so people coming in can see the light.
Nothing is hidden that will not be shown. Nothing is kept secret that will not come out and be seen.
So listen well to how you hear. Whoever has will be given more. Whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away."
Then Jesus' mother and brothers came to Him. They could not reach Him because of the crowd.
Someone told Him, "Your mother and brothers stand outside. They want to see You."
He answered, "My mother and brothers are those who hear God's word and do it."
One day He said to His disciples, "Let's go across the lake." He got into a boat with His disciples, and they sailed.
While they sailed, He fell asleep. A strong windstorm came down on the lake. The boat filled with water, and they were in danger.
They came and woke Him, saying, "Master, Master, we are dying!" He woke up and told the wind and the waves to stop. They stopped, and it became calm.
He said to them, "Where is your faith?" They were afraid and amazed. They said to each other, "Who is this? He tells even the winds and the water what to do, and they obey Him."
They sailed to the country of the Gerasenes, across from Galilee.
When He stepped onto the land, a man from the town met Him. The man had demons. For a long time he wore no clothes and did not live in a house, but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell at His feet. He said with a loud voice, "What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You, do not hurt me."

Jesus had told the bad spirit to come out of the man. For a long time it had seized him. He was kept under guard, chained with chains and leg irons. But he broke the chains and was driven by the demon into the wild places.
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" He said, "Legion," because many demons had gone into him.
They begged Him not to order them to go into the deep.
A large herd of pigs was feeding on the hill. They begged Him to let them go into the pigs. He let them.
The demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. The herd rushed down the bank into the lake and drowned.
The men who fed the pigs saw what happened. They ran and told it in the town and country.
People came out to see what happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out. He was sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind. They were afraid.
The people who saw it told how the man who had demons was saved.
All the people in the area asked Jesus to leave, because they were very afraid. He got into the boat and went back.
The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to go with Him.
But Jesus sent him away and said, "Go back home and tell how much God has done for you." He went and told the whole town how much Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus came back, the crowd welcomed Him, because they were all waiting for Him.
A man named Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, came. He fell at Jesus' feet and begged Him, "Please come to my house, because my only daughter, about twelve years old, is dying."
As Jesus went, the crowds pressed around Him.
A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years had spent all she had on doctors. No one could heal her.
She came behind Him and touched the edge of His cloak. Right away her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, "Who touched Me?" Everyone said no. Peter said, "Master, the crowds are pressing and crowding You."
Jesus said, "Someone touched Me. I felt power go out from Me."
The woman saw she could not hide. She came trembling and fell before Him. In front of all the people, she told why she touched Him and how she was healed right away.
He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace."
While He was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue ruler's house and said, "Your daughter has died. Do not bother the Teacher anymore."
Jesus heard it and answered, "Do not be afraid. Just believe, and she will be saved."
When He came to the house, He let no one go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child's father and mother.
Everyone was crying and mourning for her. He said, "Do not cry. She is not dead; she is sleeping."
They laughed at Him, knowing she was dead.
He took her by the hand and called out, "Child, get up."
Her spirit came back, and right away she got up. He told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were amazed. He told them not to tell anyone what happened.
Jesus called the twelve disciples together. He gave them power over all demons. He also gave them power to heal sick people.
He sent them to tell people about God's kingdom. He sent them to heal sick people too.
He said, "Take nothing with you for the trip. Do not take a walking stick, a bag, bread, money, or two shirts.
When you go into a house, stay there until you leave that town.
If people do not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave. This will warn them."
The disciples went out. They traveled from village to village. They told the good news. They healed people everywhere.
Herod the ruler heard about all that was happening. He was confused. Some people said John had come back from the dead.
Some said Elijah had appeared. Others said a prophet from long ago had come back to life.
Herod said, "I cut off John's head. Who is this man I hear about?" He wanted to see Jesus.
The apostles came back. They told Jesus what they had done. He took them away to a town called Bethsaida.
The crowds found out. They followed Him. He welcomed them. He talked to them about God's kingdom. He healed people who needed healing.
Late in the day, the twelve came to Him. They said, "Send the people away. They can go to nearby villages and farms. They can find food and a place to stay. We are in a lonely place here."
Jesus said, "You give them something to eat." The disciples said, "We have only five pieces of bread and two fish. Should we go buy food for all these people?"
There were about five thousand men. Jesus said to His disciples, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty."
Jesus took the five pieces of bread and two fish. He looked up to heaven. He blessed them. He broke them. He gave them to the disciples to give to the crowd.
Everyone ate and was full. The disciples picked up twelve baskets of leftover pieces.
One day Jesus was praying alone. His disciples were with Him. He asked them, "Who do the crowds say I am?"
They answered, "Some say John the Baptist. Some say Elijah. Others say a prophet from long ago has come back to life."
He asked, "But who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Christ of God."
Jesus told them not to tell anyone.
He said, "The Son of Man must suffer many things. The leaders, chief priests, and teachers of the law will not accept Him. They will kill Him. On the third day He will rise again."
He said to all, "If anyone wants to follow Me, he must say no to himself. He must take up his cross every day. He must follow Me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it. But whoever loses his life for Me will save it.
What good is it for a person to gain the whole world but lose himself?
If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him. This will happen when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and the holy angels.
I tell you the truth. Some people standing here will not die before they see God's kingdom."
About eight days later, Jesus took Peter, John, and James up a mountain to pray.
While He prayed, His face changed. His clothes became bright white.
Two men, Moses and Elijah, talked with Him.
They appeared in glory. They talked about His leaving. He was about to do this in Jerusalem.
Peter and the others were very sleepy. But they woke up. They saw His glory and the two men with Him.
As the men were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents. One for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He did not know what he was saying.
While Peter was speaking, a cloud came and covered them. They were afraid as they went into the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud. It said, "This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him."
When the voice stopped, Jesus was alone. They kept quiet. In those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen.
The next day, they came down the mountain. A large crowd met Him.
A man in the crowd shouted, "Teacher, I beg You, look at my son. He is my only child.
A spirit takes him. He screams. It throws him down. He foams at the mouth. It hurts him badly. Then it leaves him.
I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they could not."
Jesus answered, "You people who do not believe and are mixed up in your thinking! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring your son here."
While the boy was coming, the evil spirit threw him down and shook him. Jesus spoke sternly to the spirit. He healed the boy. He gave him back to his father.
Everyone was amazed at God's great power. While everyone was wondering about all Jesus did, He said to His disciples,
"Listen to these words. The Son of Man is going to be handed over to people."
But they did not understand. It was hidden from them. They were afraid to ask Him about it.
The disciples argued about who was the greatest.
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He took a little child and stood the child by His side.
He said, "Whoever welcomes this child in My name welcomes Me. Whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. The least one among you is the greatest."
John said, "Master, we saw a man driving out demons in Your name. We tried to stop him because he does not follow us."
Jesus said, "Do not stop him. Whoever is not against you is for you."
As the time came for Him to be taken up to heaven, Jesus decided to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead. They went into a Samaritan village to get things ready for Him.
But the people there did not welcome Him, because He was heading to Jerusalem.
When James and John saw this, they said, "Lord, do You want us to call fire down from heaven to burn them up?"
Jesus turned and spoke sharply to them.
They went on to another village.
As they walked along the road, a man said to Him, "I will follow You wherever You go."
Jesus said, "Foxes have holes. Birds have nests. But the Son of Man has no place to rest His head."
He said to another man, "Follow Me." The man said, "Lord, first let me go bury my father."
Jesus said, "Let the dead bury their own dead. You go and tell about God's kingdom."
Another man said, "I will follow You, Lord. But first let me say goodbye to my family."
Jesus said, "No one who starts to plow and looks back is ready for God's kingdom."
After this, the Lord chose seventy-two other people. He sent them out two by two. They went ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.
He said to them, "The harvest is big, but the workers are few. So ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers into His harvest.
Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a money bag, a travel bag, or extra shoes. Do not stop to greet anyone on the road."
"When you enter a house, first say, 'Peace to this house.'
If someone there wants peace, your peace will stay with them. If not, it will come back to you.
Stay in that house. Eat and drink what they give you. A worker is worth his pay. Do not move from house to house."
"When you go into a town and they welcome you, eat what is set before you.
Heal the sick people there. Tell them, 'God's kingdom has come near to you.'"
"But if you go into a town and they do not welcome you, go out into the streets and say, '
Even the dust from your town that sticks to our feet, we wipe off to show we are done with you. But know this: God's kingdom has come near.'
I tell you, on that day it will be easier for Sodom than for that town."
"Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If the big miracles done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have been sorry long ago. They would have sat in rough cloth and ashes.
But it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon when God judges everyone than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will go down to the place of the dead.
Whoever listens to you listens to Me. Whoever turns you away turns Me away. And whoever turns Me away turns away the One who sent Me."
The seventy-two came back happy. They said, "Lord, even the demons obey us in Your name!"
He said to them, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
Look, I have given you power to walk on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will hurt you.
But do not be glad just because spirits obey you. Be glad because your names are written in heaven."

At that same hour Jesus was full of joy through the Holy Spirit. He said, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You hid these things from wise and smart people and showed them to little children. Yes, Father, this is what You wanted to do.
All things have been handed over to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father. And no one knows who the Father is except the Son and anyone the Son chooses to tell."
Then Jesus turned to His followers and spoke to them alone. He said, "Happy are the eyes that see what you see."
"For I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see, but they did not see it. They wanted to hear what you hear, but they did not hear it."
Then a man who knew God's law stood up to test Jesus. He said, "Teacher, what must I do to have life that never ends?"
Jesus said to him, "What is written in the Law? How do you read it?"
The man answered, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind. And love your neighbor as yourself."
Jesus said to him, "You have answered right. Do this and you will live."
But the man wanted to make himself look right. So he asked Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?"
Jesus answered, "A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho. Robbers attacked him. They took his clothes, beat him, and left him almost dead."
A priest happened to be going down that road. He saw the man and passed by on the other side.
A Levite also came by. He saw the man and passed by on the other side.
But a Samaritan who was traveling came to where the man was. He saw him and felt sorry for him.
He went to him and bandaged his wounds. He poured oil and wine on them. Then he put the man on his own donkey and took him to an inn. He took care of him.
The next day he took out two silver coins and gave them to the innkeeper. He said, "Take care of him. When I come back, I will pay you for anything else you spend."
"Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell among robbers?"
The man said, "The one who showed mercy to him." Jesus said to him, "Go and do the same."
As they traveled, Jesus went into a village. A woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
She had a sister named Mary. Mary sat at the Lord's feet and listened to what He said.
But Martha was busy with much serving. She came to Jesus and said, "Lord, don't You care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me."
The Lord answered her, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things."
But only one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, and it will not be taken away from her.
One day Jesus was praying in a place. When He finished, one of His followers said, "Lord, teach us to pray. John taught his followers too."
He said to them, "When you pray, say: Father, may Your name be holy. Let Your kingdom come.
Give us the bread we need today.
Forgive us our sins. We forgive everyone who does wrong to us. And do not lead us into trouble."
Then He said, "Suppose one of you goes to a friend at midnight and asks for three loaves of bread.
You say a friend is visiting and you have no food to give him.
The friend inside says the door is locked and his children are in bed, so he cannot get up to give you anything.
I tell you, even if he will not get up because you are friends, he will get up because you keep asking. He will give you all you need."
"So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and the door will be opened to you.
Everyone who asks receives. The one who seeks finds. The door is opened to the one who knocks."
"Which of you fathers, if your son asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
If you are not good, but you know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!"
One day Jesus was sending out an evil spirit that made a man unable to talk. When the spirit left, the man talked, and the crowd was amazed.
But some said, "He sends out demons by Beelzebul, the boss of demons."
Others tried to test Him. They asked for a sign from heaven.
Jesus knew their thoughts. He said, "Every kingdom that fights against itself is ruined. A home that fights against itself falls.
If Satan fights against himself, how can his kingdom last? You say I send out demons by Beelzebul.
If I send them out by Beelzebul, who do your people use to send them out? So they will judge you.
But if I send them out by God's power, then God's kingdom has come to you."
"When a strong man with weapons guards his house, his things are safe.
But when a stronger man attacks and beats him, he takes the strong man's weapons and shares his stuff.
Anyone who is not with Me is against Me. Anyone who does not gather with Me scatters."
"When an evil spirit leaves a person, it goes through dry places looking for rest. It does not find any. Then it goes back to the house it left.
It finds the house clean and neat.
Then it brings seven other spirits worse than itself. They go in and live there. That person ends up worse than before."
As Jesus said these things, a woman in the crowd called out, "How happy is the mother who gave birth to You, and how happy are the breasts that fed You!"
He said, "Even more, happy are those who hear God's word and do what it says."
As the crowd grew, Jesus began to say, "This is a bad generation. It wants a sign, but no sign will be given except the sign of Jonah.
Just as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation."

"The Queen of the South will stand up on judgment day with the people of this generation and judge them. She came from far away to hear Solomon's wise words. And now someone greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up on judgment day with this generation and judge it. They turned from their sins when Jonah preached to them. And now someone greater than Jonah is here."
"No one lights a lamp and hides it. No one puts it under a bowl. They put it on a stand, so people who come in can see the light.
Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body is full of light. When they are bad, your body is full of darkness."
"So be careful that the light in you is not darkness.
If your whole body is full of light, with no dark part, then it will be all light. It will be like a lamp shining its light on you."
While Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee asked Him to eat with him. Jesus went in and sat down.
The Pharisee was surprised that Jesus did not wash before the meal.
The Lord said to him, "You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish. But inside you are full of greed and evil.
You fools! Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
But give what you have to the poor, and everything will be clean for you."
"But shame on you Pharisees! You give a tenth of your mint, rue, and every herb. But you forget justice and the love of God. You should do these things and not forget the others.
Shame on you Pharisees! You love the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.
Shame on you! You are like hidden graves. People walk over them and do not know it."
One of the teachers of the law said, "Teacher, when you say these things, you insult us too."
Jesus said, "Shame on you teachers of the law too! You put heavy loads on people. But you do not help them with even one finger.
Shame on you! You build tombs for the prophets, but your fathers killed them.
So you show that you agree with what your fathers did. They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs."
"Because of this, God said He would send them prophets and apostles, and some of them would be killed and chased.
So the blood of all the prophets, spilled since the world began, will be blamed on this generation.
From Abel's blood to Zechariah's blood, who died between the altar and the temple. Yes, I tell you, it will be blamed on this generation.
Shame on you teachers of the law! You took away the key of knowledge. You did not go in yourselves, and you stopped those who were trying to go in."
As Jesus left there, the teachers of the law and Pharisees became very angry with Him. They asked Him many hard questions.
They watched Him closely, hoping to catch Him in something He said.
Many thousands of people came together. They pushed each other. Jesus first spoke to His disciples. He said, "Watch out for the hypocrisy of the religious leaders.
Nothing is hidden that will not be shown. Nothing is secret that will not be known.
What you say in the dark will be heard in the light. What you whisper in a room will be shouted from the roof.
"I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of people who kill the body. After that, they can do nothing more.
I will show you whom to fear. Fear God. After He kills, He has power to throw people into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him.
Five sparrows are sold for two small coins. But God does not forget even one of them.
Even the hairs on your head are all counted. Do not be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
"I tell you, everyone who says he follows Me in front of people, the Son of Man will say he follows Him in front of God's angels.
But anyone who says he does not know Me in front of people will be turned away in front of God's angels.
Everyone who speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
"When people bring you to meeting places, rulers, or leaders, do not worry about how to answer or what to say.
The Holy Spirit will teach you in that hour what you should say."
Someone in the crowd said to Him, "Teacher, tell my brother to share the family money with me."
Jesus said to him, "Man, who made Me judge or divider over you?"
Then He said to them, "Watch out! Guard yourselves from wanting too much. A person's life is not made full by having many things."
Then He told them a story. A rich man's land grew a big crop.
He thought, "What should I do? I have no place to store my crops."
He said, "I will do this. I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones. There I will store all my grain and goods."
"Then I will say to myself, 'You have many good things saved for many years. Rest now. Eat, drink, and be happy.'"
But God said to him, "You fool! Tonight your life will be taken from you. Then who will get the things you saved?"
This is what happens to people who save up for themselves but are not rich toward God.
Then Jesus said to His disciples, "So I tell you, do not worry about your life and what you will eat. Do not worry about your body and what you will wear.
"Life is more than food. The body is more than clothes.
Look at the ravens. They do not plant seeds. They do not gather crops. They have no barns. But God feeds them. You are worth much more than birds.
"Which of you can add even a little bit to your life by worrying?
If you cannot do such a small thing, why worry about the rest?
"Look at how the flowers grow. They do not work or make cloth. But I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed as nicely as one of these.
If God dresses the grass of the field so well, and it is here today and gone tomorrow, how much more will He take care of you? You have so little faith.
"So do not keep looking for what to eat or drink. Do not worry.
People of the world look for all these things. But your Father knows you need them.
Instead, look for God's kingdom. Then these things will be given to you too.
Do not be afraid, little flock. Your Father is happy to give you the kingdom.
"Sell what you own and give to people in need. Make money bags that do not wear out. Save treasure in heaven that does not run out. Thieves cannot get near it. Moths cannot ruin it.
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.
"Be ready. Keep your belts tied and your lamps lit.
Be like people waiting for their master to come home from a wedding. When he comes and knocks, they open the door right away.
"Those servants are happy. The master finds them awake when he comes. I tell you the truth, he will dress himself to serve. He will have them sit down. Then he will serve them.
Even if he comes in the middle of the night or near morning, those servants are happy if he finds them ready.
"You know this: if the owner of a house knew when a thief was coming, he would not let his house be broken into.
So you must be ready too. The Son of Man is coming at a time you do not expect."
Peter said, "Lord, are you telling this story to us or to everyone?"
The Lord said, "Who is the faithful and wise manager? The master puts him in charge of the other servants. He gives them their food at the right time.
That servant is happy if the master finds him doing this when he comes.
I tell you the truth, the master will put him in charge of all he owns.
"But suppose that servant says to himself, 'My master is taking a long time to come.' Then he starts to hit the other servants. He eats and drinks and gets drunk.
The master will come on a day the servant does not expect. He will come at a time the servant does not know. Then he will punish him badly. He will put him with people who do not believe.
"That servant knew what his master wanted. But he did not get ready or do it. He will be punished with many blows.

But a servant who did not know, and did things that should be punished, will get only a few blows. Everyone who is given much will have much asked of them. More will be asked from the one who was trusted with more."
"I came to bring fire to the earth. I wish it were already burning!
I have a baptism to go through. I am very troubled until it is finished.
Do you think I came to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you. I came to bring division.
"From now on, five people in one house will be divided. Three will be against two, and two will be against three.
They will be divided: father against son, son against father, mother against daughter, daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."
Jesus also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rise in the west, you say, 'Rain is coming.' And it happens.
When the south wind blows, you say, 'It will be hot.' And it happens.
"You fakers! You know how to read the sky and the earth. Why can you not read this time?
Why do you not judge what is right for yourselves?
"When you go with your enemy to a ruler, try hard to settle on the way. If you do not, he may drag you to the judge. The judge may hand you to the officer. The officer may throw you into jail.
I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid the very last small coin."
At that time, some people were there. They told Jesus about some people from Galilee. Pilate had killed them and mixed their blood with the gifts they gave to God.
Jesus answered, "Do you think those Galileans were worse sinners than all other Galileans, so this happened to them?
No, I tell you. But unless you turn from your sin, you will all die the same way.
What about the eighteen people the tower in Siloam fell on and killed? Do you think they were worse sinners than all the people in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you. But unless you turn from your sin, you will all die the same way."
Then Jesus said, "A man had a fig tree in his grape field. He came looking for fruit on it, but he did not find any.
So he said to the man who cared for the field, 'Look, for three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree. I never find any. Cut it down. Why should it take up the ground?'
But the man answered, 'Sir, leave it alone for one more year. I will dig around it and put plant food on it.
Maybe it will make fruit next year. If not, then cut it down.'"
Jesus was teaching in one of the meeting places on the Sabbath day.
A woman was there who had been sick for eighteen years. An evil spirit had bent her over, and she could not stand up straight.
When Jesus saw her, He called to her. He said, "Woman, you are free from your sickness."
He put His hands on her. Right away she stood up straight. She praised God.
The leader of the meeting place was angry because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath day. He said to the crowd, "There are six days for work. Come and be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath day."
The Lord answered him, "You hypocrites! On the Sabbath day, doesn't each of you untie his ox or donkey and lead it to water?
This woman is a daughter of Abraham. Satan had tied her up for eighteen years. Should she not be set free from this on the Sabbath day?"
When Jesus said this, all His enemies were ashamed. But all the people were happy about the wonderful things He did.
Then Jesus said, "What is God's kingdom like? What can I compare it to?
It is like a mustard seed. A man took it and planted it in his garden. It grew and became a tree. The birds of the sky made nests in its branches."
Again He said, "What can I compare God's kingdom to?
It is like yeast. A woman took it and mixed it into a big bowl of flour. It spread until all the dough was ready."
Jesus traveled through towns and villages. He taught the people. He was on His way to Jerusalem.
Someone asked Him, "Lord, will only a few people be saved?"
He said to them, "Work hard to go through the narrow door. I tell you, many people will try to go in, but they will not be able to.
Once the owner of the house gets up and locks the door, you will stand outside. You will knock and say, 'Lord, open the door for us.' But he will answer, 'I do not know where you come from.'
Then you will say, 'We ate and drank with you. You taught in our streets.'
But he will say, 'I tell you, I do not know where you come from. Go away from Me, all you who do wrong.'
There will be crying and grinding of teeth. You will see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in God's kingdom. But you will be thrown out.
People will come from east and west, and from north and south. They will sit down to eat in God's kingdom.
Some who are last will be first. Some who are first will be last."
At that time, some Pharisees came to Jesus. They said, "Leave here and go away. Herod wants to kill You."
Jesus said to them, "Go tell that fox I am forcing out demons and healing people today and tomorrow. On the third day, I will finish My work.
But I must travel today, tomorrow, and the next day. A prophet cannot die outside Jerusalem."
"Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets and stone those sent to you. How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you were not willing.
Look, your house is left to you empty. I tell you, you will not see Me again until you say, 'Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
One Sabbath day, Jesus went to eat at the home of a leader of the Pharisees. The people there were watching Him closely.
A man whose body was swollen with water stood in front of Him.
Jesus asked the law experts and the Pharisees, "Is it allowed to heal someone on the Sabbath day, or not?"
They said nothing. So Jesus took the man, healed him, and let him go.
Then Jesus said to them, "If your son or your ox falls into a well on the Sabbath day, won't you pull him out right away?"
Jesus saw that the guests were picking the best seats. So He told them this story.
"When someone invites you to a wedding, do not sit in the best seat. A more important guest may have been invited too.
