Then the host will come and say, 'Give this person your seat.' You will feel ashamed and have to take the last seat.
Instead, when you are invited, go sit in the last seat. Then the host may say, 'Friend, move up to a better seat.' Then you will be honored in front of everyone there.
For everyone who makes himself great will be brought low, and everyone who makes himself small will be lifted up."

Jesus also said to the man who had invited Him, "When you make a lunch or a dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your family, or rich neighbors. They may invite you back, and that will be your pay.
Instead, when you give a feast, invite poor people, crippled people, lame people, and blind people.
You will be happy because they cannot pay you back. You will be paid back when God raises good people to life."
One of the guests heard this and said to Jesus, "How happy is the person who will eat bread in God's kingdom!"
Jesus said to him, "A man made a big dinner and invited many people.
When it was time to eat, he sent his servant to tell the invited guests, 'Come, everything is ready.'
But they all began to make excuses. The first one said, 'I bought a field. I must go see it. Please excuse me.'
Another said, 'I bought five pairs of oxen. I am going to test them. Please excuse me.'
Another said, 'I just got married, so I cannot come.'

The servant came back and told his master. The master was angry. He said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the town. Bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.'
The servant said, 'Sir, I did what you said, but there is still room.'
The master said, 'Go out to the roads and country lanes. Make people come in, so my house will be full.
I tell you, none of those invited men will taste my dinner.'"
Large crowds were traveling with Jesus. He turned and said to them,
"If anyone comes to Me and does not love Me more than his father, mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be My follower.
Whoever is not ready to suffer for Me and follow Me cannot be My follower.
"Think about it. If you want to build a tower, you first sit down and count the cost. You make sure you have enough money to finish it.
If you do not, people who see it will laugh at you.
They will say, 'This man started to build, but he could not finish.'
"Or what king, going to fight another king, does not first sit down and think if he can win with ten thousand men against twenty thousand?
If he cannot, he sends messengers while the other king is still far away. He asks for peace.
"In the same way, none of you can be My follower unless you give up everything you own."
"Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, how can it be made salty again?
It is no good for the soil or the manure pile. People throw it away. Whoever has ears to hear, let him listen."
Now all the tax collectors and sinners came close to listen to Jesus.
But the Pharisees and teachers of the law grumbled. They said, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
So Jesus told them this story:
"Suppose one of you has one hundred sheep and loses one. Won't he leave the ninety-nine sheep in the field and go look for the lost one until he finds it?
"When he finds it, he puts it on his shoulders and is happy.
"Then he goes home and calls his friends and neighbors together. He says, 'Be happy with me! I found my lost sheep.'
"I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who turns from sin than over ninety-nine good people who do not need to turn.
"Or suppose a woman has ten silver coins and loses one. Won't she light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?
"When she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together and says, 'Be happy with me! I found the coin I lost.'
"In the same way, I tell you, there is joy before God's angels over one sinner who turns from sin.
Jesus also said, "A man had two sons.
The younger son said to his father, 'Father, give me my share of what you own.' So the father divided his things between them.
"After a few days, the younger son packed up all he had and went to a far country. There he wasted his money on wild living.
When he had spent everything, a terrible food shortage hit that country, and he began to go hungry.
"So he went and worked for a man from that country. The man sent him to the fields to feed pigs.
He wanted to eat the bean pods the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
"Then he thought clearly. He said, 'How many of my father's workers have plenty of food, but here I am starving to death!
I will go back to my father and say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
I am not worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your workers."'
"So he got up and went to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and felt sorry for him. He ran to him, hugged him, and kissed him.
The son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am not worthy to be called your son.'
"But the father said to his servants, 'Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fat calf and kill it. Let us eat and celebrate.
For this son of mine was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.' So they began to celebrate.
"Now the older son was in the field. As he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.
He called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
"The servant said, 'Your brother has come home. Your father killed the fat calf because your brother is back and well.'
"The older son got angry and would not go in. So his father went out and begged him to come in.
"But he answered his father, 'Look! All these years I have worked for you. I never disobeyed you. But you never gave me even a young goat so I could have a party with my friends.
But when this son of yours came back, who wasted your money on bad women, you killed the fat calf for him!'
"The father said, 'My son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.
But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.'"
"There was a rich man. He had a worker who took care of his things. Someone said the worker was wasting the rich man's stuff.
So the rich man called the worker in. He said, 'Tell me how you used my things. You cannot be my worker anymore.'
The worker said to himself, 'What will I do now? My boss is taking my job from me. I am not strong enough to dig, and I am too proud to beg.
I know what I will do. Then, when I lose my job, people will let me stay in their homes.'
So he called in each person who owed money to his boss. He asked the first one, 'How much do you owe my boss?'
The man said, 'A hundred jars of olive oil.' "The worker said, 'Take your bill. Sit down fast, and write fifty.'
Then he asked another man, 'And you, how much do you owe?' "The man said, 'A hundred baskets of wheat.' "The worker said, 'Take your bill and write eighty.'
The boss praised the dishonest worker because he had acted smartly. People in this world are smarter with their own people than people who follow the light.
"I tell you, use money in this world to make friends for yourselves. Then, when the money is gone, they will welcome you into homes that last forever.
"A person who is faithful with a little is faithful with a lot. A person who is dishonest with a little is dishonest with a lot.
"So if you have not been faithful with money in this world, who will trust you with true riches?
"And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what is your own?
"No servant can serve two bosses. He will hate one and love the other, or he will stay with one and look down on the other. You cannot serve both God and money."
The Pharisees loved money. They heard all this and made fun of Jesus.
"You say you are good in front of people. But God knows your hearts. What people think is great is very bad to God.
"God's Law and the Prophets were taught until John. Since then, the good news about God's kingdom is being told. Everyone is trying hard to get into it.
"It is easier for the sky and the earth to pass away than for one little mark of God's Law to be lost.
"Anyone who sends away his wife and marries another sins. And anyone who marries a woman who was sent away sins."
"There was a rich man. He wore fine purple clothes and soft linen. He lived in great comfort every day.
"A poor man named Lazarus lay at the rich man's gate. His body was full of sores.
He wanted to eat the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table. Even dogs came and licked his sores.
"The poor man died. Angels carried him to be with Abraham. The rich man also died and was buried.
"In the place of the dead, the rich man was in pain. He looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus by his side.
"He called out, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me. Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. I hurt in this fire.'
"Abraham said, 'Child, remember that in your life you got your good things. Lazarus got bad things. Now he is comforted here, and you are in pain.
And besides all this, a big gap is fixed between us and you. People cannot cross from here to you, and no one can cross from there to us.'
"The rich man said, 'Then I beg you, father, send him to my father's house.
I have five brothers. Warn them so they will not come to this place of pain.'
"Abraham said, 'They have Moses and the Prophets. Let them listen to them.'
"The rich man said, 'No, father Abraham. But if someone goes to them from the dead, they will change their hearts.'
"Abraham said, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not believe even if someone comes back to life.'"
Then Jesus said to His disciples, "Things that make people sin will happen. But it will be very bad for the person who makes them happen.
It would be better for him to have a big stone tied to his neck and be thrown into the sea than to make one of these little ones sin."
"Watch out for yourselves. If your brother sins, tell him he is wrong. If he says sorry, forgive him.
Even if he sins against you seven times in one day, and seven times comes back to you and says, 'I am sorry,' you must forgive him."
The apostles said to the Lord, "Give us more faith!"
The Lord replied, "If you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, 'Be pulled up and planted in the sea,' and it would listen to you."
"Which of you has a servant who comes in from plowing or watching sheep in the field? Would you tell him, 'Come and sit down to eat right now'?"
"No. He will tell him, 'Get my dinner ready. Put on your work clothes and serve me while I eat and drink. After that, you can eat and drink.'"
"Does he thank the servant for doing what he was told?"
"So you also, when you have done everything you were told to do, should say, 'We are not good servants. We only did our job.'"
While Jesus was going to Jerusalem, He passed between Samaria and Galilee.
As He entered a village, ten men with a bad skin disease met Him. They stood far away.
They called out, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
When He saw them, He said, "Go, show yourselves to the priests." As they went, they were healed.
One of them, when he saw he was healed, came back. He praised God with a loud voice.
He fell on his face at Jesus' feet and thanked Him. He was a Samaritan.
Jesus asked, "Were not all ten healed? Where are the other nine?
Was no one found to come back and give glory to God except this foreigner?"
He said to the man, "Get up and go. your faith has made you well."
The Pharisees asked Him when the kingdom of God would come. He replied, "The kingdom of God will not come in a way you can see.
People will not say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'There it is!' For the kingdom of God is among you."
Then He said to His disciples, "Days are coming when you will want to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
People will say to you, 'Look, there He is!' or 'Look, here He is!' Do not go out or run after them.
For as lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one side to the other, so will the Son of Man be in His day.
But first He must suffer many things and be turned away by the people of this time.
"Just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
People were eating and drinking, getting married, up to the day Noah went into the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
It was the same in the days of Lot. People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and burning sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
It will be the same on the day the Son of Man is shown.
"On that day, no one on the roof should go down to get things from inside the house. No one in the field should go back.
Whoever tries to keep his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will keep it.
I tell you, on that night two men will be in one bed. One will be taken, and the other will be left.
Two women will be grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left."
They asked, "Where, Lord?" He replied, "Where the body is, there the birds of prey will gather."
Jesus told His followers a story. He wanted them to pray all the time and not give up.
He said, "In one town there was a judge. He did not fear God. He did not care what people thought.
A widow lived there. She kept coming to him and asking for fair help against the man who hurt her.
For a while he said no.
But then he said to himself that he did not fear God and did not care what people thought. Still, the widow kept bothering him. So he would help her, so she would stop bothering him."
The Lord said, "Listen to what the bad judge said.
Will not God help His chosen people? They cry to Him day and night. Will He wait too long to help them?
I tell you, He will help them soon. But when the Son of Man comes, will He find people who trust Him?"
Jesus told this story to some people who thought they were good and looked down on others.
Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee. The other was a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood alone and prayed, "God, I thank You that I am not like other people. I am not a thief. I am not unfair. I am not a cheater in marriage. I am not even like this tax collector.
I go without food two days each week. I give one tenth of all I get."
But the tax collector stood far away. He would not even look up to heaven. He hit his chest and said, "God, be kind to me. I am a sinner."
Jesus said, "I tell you, this man went home right with God. The other man did not. Everyone who lifts himself up will be brought down. Everyone who puts himself down will be lifted up."
People brought babies to Jesus. They wanted Him to touch them. The followers saw this. They told the people to stop.
But Jesus called the children to Him. He said, "Let the little children come to Me. Do not stop them. God's kingdom belongs to people like them.
I tell you the truth. Anyone who does not accept God's kingdom like a little child will never enter it."
A leader asked Him, "Good Teacher, what must I do to have life that never ends?"
Jesus said, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the rules. Do not cheat in marriage. Do not kill. Do not steal. Do not lie about others. Honor your father and mother."
The man said, "I have kept all these since I was young."
When Jesus heard this, He said to him, "You still need one thing. Sell all you have. Give it to poor people. Then you will have treasure in heaven. Come, follow Me."
When the man heard this, he became very sad. He was very rich.
Jesus looked at him and said, "It is hard for rich people to enter God's kingdom.
It is easier for a camel to go through the tiny hole in a needle than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom."
The people who heard this asked, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus said, "What people cannot do, God can do."
Peter said, "Look, we left everything to follow You!"
Jesus said, "I tell you the truth. No one who leaves home, wife, brothers, sisters, parents, or children for God's kingdom
will get much more in this life. In the life to come, they will get life that never ends."
Jesus took the twelve followers aside. He said, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem. Everything God's helpers wrote about the Son of Man will come true.
He will be handed over to people who are not Jews. They will make fun of Him. They will say mean things to Him. They will spit on Him.
They will beat Him. They will kill Him. On the third day, He will rise again."
The followers did not understand any of this. Its meaning was hidden from them. They did not know what He was talking about.
As Jesus came near Jericho, a blind man sat by the road. He was begging.
He heard the crowd going by. He asked what was happening.
People told him, "Jesus of Nazareth is passing by."
He called out, "Jesus, Son of David, be kind to me!"
The people in front told him to be quiet. But he shouted even more, "Son of David, be kind to me!"
Jesus stopped. He told them to bring the man to Him. When the man came near, Jesus asked him,
"What do you want Me to do for you?" The man said he wanted to see.
Jesus said, "Now you can see. Your faith has healed you."
Right away the man could see. He followed Jesus. He praised God. All the people saw it. They praised God too.
Jesus went into Jericho. He was passing through.
A man named Zacchaeus was there. He was the head tax man. He was rich.
He wanted to see who Jesus was. He could not see because of the crowd. He was short.
So he ran ahead and climbed a tree. He wanted to see Jesus, because Jesus was coming that way.
When Jesus came to that place, He looked up. He said, "Zacchaeus, come down fast. I must stay at your house today."
Zacchaeus came down fast. He welcomed Jesus with joy.
All the people saw it. They grumbled. They said, "Jesus went to stay with a sinner."
Zacchaeus stood up. He said to the Lord, "Lord, I give half of what I have to poor people. If I cheated anyone, I will pay back four times."
Jesus said, "Today this house is saved, because he is also a son of Abraham.
The Son of Man came to look for lost people and save them."
The people were listening. Jesus told a story. They were near Jerusalem. The people thought God's kingdom would come right away.
Jesus said, "A rich man went to a far country. He went to get a kingdom for himself. Then he would come back.
He called ten servants. He gave each one a coin. He told them to do business until he came back.
But his people hated him. They sent a message that said they did not want him to rule them."
When he came back as king, he called the servants he had given money to. He wanted to know what they had earned.
The first servant came. He said, "Lord, your coin made ten more coins."
The master said, "Good job, good servant. You were faithful with a little. So you will rule ten cities."
The second servant came. He said, "Lord, your coin made five more coins."
The master said to him, "You will rule five cities."
Another servant came. He said, "Lord, here is your coin. I kept it in a cloth.
I was afraid of you. You are a hard man. You take what you did not put down. You harvest what you did not plant."
The master said, "You bad servant, I will judge you by your own words. You knew I am a hard man. I take what I did not put down. I harvest what I did not plant.
Why did you not put my money in the bank? Then I could have collected it with interest."
He said to the people standing by, "Take the coin from him. Give it to the one who has ten coins."
They said, "Lord, he already has ten coins."
He said, "I tell you, everyone who has will get more. But from the one who has nothing, even what he has will be taken.
But bring my enemies here. They did not want me to rule them. Kill them in front of me."
After Jesus said this, He went on ahead. He was going up to Jerusalem.
As He came near Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent two disciples.
He said, "Go into the village ahead. You will find a young donkey tied there. No one has ever ridden it. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks why you are untying it, say that the Lord needs it."
The men went. They found it just as He had said.
As they untied the young donkey, its owners asked, "Why are you untying the young donkey?"
They brought it to Jesus. They put their coats on the young donkey. They helped Jesus sit on it.
As He went, people spread their coats on the road.
As He came near the place where the road goes down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples began to praise God with joy. They shouted about all the miracles they had seen.
They said, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"
Some Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, "Teacher, tell Your disciples to stop."
Jesus answered, "I tell you, if they keep quiet, the stones will cry out."
As He came near, He saw the city. He cried over it.
He said, "If you had known today what brings peace. But now it is hidden from your eyes.
Days will come when your enemies will build a wall around you. They will surround you. They will trap you on every side.
They will knock you down. They will destroy your children in you. They will not leave one stone on another. This is because you did not know the time God came to help you."
Jesus went into the temple. He began to throw out the sellers.
He said, "It is written, 'My house will be a house of prayer,' but you made it a den of robbers."
He taught in the temple every day. The chief priests, teachers of the law, and leaders of the people tried to kill Him.
But they could not find a way, because all the people were listening to Him.
One day, while Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and sharing the good news, the chief priests, teachers of the law, and elders came to Him.
They said, "Tell us, by what power are You doing these things? Who gave You this power?"
Jesus said, "I will ask you a question too. Tell Me.
Was John's baptism from heaven or from people?"
They thought to themselves, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will ask, 'Why didn't you believe him?'
But if we say, 'From people,' all the people will throw stones at us, because they believe John was a prophet."
They answered, "We don't know where it was from."
Jesus said, "Then I won't tell you by what power I do these things either."
Then He began to tell the people this story: "A man planted a grape field. He rented it to some farmers and went away for a long time.
At harvest time, he sent a servant to the farmers to get some of the fruit. But the farmers beat him and sent him away with nothing.
"He sent another servant. They beat him too, treated him badly, and sent him away with nothing.
He sent a third servant. They hurt him and threw him out.
"The owner of the grape field said, 'What should I do? I will send my dear Son. Maybe they will respect Him.'
"But when the farmers saw Him, they said to each other, 'This is the one who will get everything. Let's kill Him so it will be ours.'
They threw Him out of the grape field and killed Him. What will the owner do to them?
"He will come and kill those farmers and give the grape field to others." When the people heard this, they said, "No, that must not happen!"
Jesus looked at them and said, "Then what does this mean? 'The stone the builders did not want has become the most important stone.'
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken. And the stone will crush anyone it falls on."
The teachers of the law and chief priests knew He was talking about them. So they wanted to arrest Him right then, but they were afraid of the people.
They watched Him closely. They sent spies who pretended to be good. They wanted to catch Him in His words so they could hand Him over to the governor's power.
They said, "Teacher, we know You speak and teach what is right. You don't favor anyone. You truly teach God's way.
Is it right for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
Jesus saw their trick. He said to them,
"Show Me a coin. Whose picture and name are on it?" "Caesar's," they said.
He said, "Then give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and give to God what is God's."
They could not catch Him in His words in front of the people. They were amazed at His answer and said nothing.
Some Sadducees came to Him. They say there is no rising from the dead.
They said, "Teacher, Moses wrote this for us: If a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the brother should marry her and have children for his brother.
There were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died without children.
The third married her too. All seven married her and died without children.
Last of all, the woman died.
So in the rising from the dead, whose wife will she be? All seven were married to her."
Jesus said, "People in this world get married.
But those who are chosen to take part in that world and in the rising from the dead do not get married.
They cannot die anymore. They are like angels. They are God's children, because they belong to the rising from the dead.
Even Moses showed that the dead rise. He said at the bush, 'The Lord is the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. To Him, all are alive."
Some teachers of the law said, "Teacher, You spoke well."
They did not dare ask Him anything else.
Then Jesus said to them, "How can people say the Christ is David's Son?
David himself says in the Book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord,
"Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet."'
David calls Him 'Lord.' So how can He be David's Son?"
While all the people were listening, Jesus said to His disciples, "Watch out for the teachers of the law.
They like to walk around in long robes. They love greetings in the marketplaces. They love the best seats in the meeting places and the best places at feasts.
They take widows' houses and pray long prayers to look good. They will be punished even more."
Jesus looked up. He saw rich people putting their gifts into the temple money box.
He also saw a poor widow put in two small coins.
He said, "I tell you the truth. This poor widow gave more than all of them.
They all gave from the extra they had. But she gave from what she needed. She gave everything she had to live on."
Some people were talking about the temple. They said it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts given to God.
Jesus said, "Look at these things you see. Days will come when not one stone will be left on another. Every stone will be thrown down."
They asked Him, "Teacher, when will these things happen? What sign will show that they are about to happen?"
He said, "Be careful so you are not fooled. Many will come using My name. They will say, 'I am he,' and, 'The time is near.' Do not follow them.
When you hear about wars and fighting, do not be scared. These things must happen first, but the end will not come right away.
"Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be big earthquakes, times with no food, and sickness in many places. There will be scary things and great signs from heaven.
"But before all this, people will arrest you. They will chase you because of My name. They will hand you over to places of worship and prisons. They will bring you before kings and rulers.
This will give you a chance to tell about Me.
So do not worry ahead of time about what you will say.
I will give you words and wisdom. None of your enemies will be able to stand against you or argue with you.
"You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. Some of you will be put to death.
Everyone will hate you because of My name.
But not one hair on your head will be lost.
By standing firm, you will save your lives.
"When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, know that it will soon be destroyed.
Then those in Judea should run to the mountains. Those in the city should leave. Those in the country should not go into the city.
"These are the days of punishment. Everything written will come true.
How sad it will be for women who are pregnant or nursing babies in those days! There will be great trouble on the earth and anger against this people.
They will die by the sword. They will be taken captive to all nations. Jerusalem will be walked on by other nations until their time is up.
"There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars. On earth, nations will be worried and not know what to do. They will hear the roaring of the sea and the waves.
People will faint from fear and from waiting for what is coming to the world. The powers of heaven will be shaken.
"Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift your heads. Your rescue is near."
He told them this story: "Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they sprout leaves, you see it and know that summer is near.
So also, when you see these things happening, you know that God's kingdom is near.
I tell you the truth, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
"Watch yourselves so your hearts are not weighed down with partying, drinking, and worries of life. That day will come on you suddenly, like a trap.
For it will come on all who live on the face of the whole earth.
So stay awake at all times. Pray that you may have strength to escape all these things that are going to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."
During the day, Jesus taught in the temple. At night, He went out and stayed on the Mount of Olives.
Early in the morning, all the people came to Him in the temple to listen to Him.
Now the Feast of Bread Without Yeast, called Passover, was near.
The chief priests and teachers of the law wanted to kill Jesus. They were afraid of the people.
Satan entered Judas, called Iscariot. He was one of the Twelve.
Judas went and talked with the chief priests and leaders. He told them how he could hand Jesus over to them.
They were glad. They agreed to give him money.
He said yes. He looked for a good time to hand Jesus over when no crowd was there.
The day of Bread Without Yeast came. On that day the Passover lamb had to be killed.
Jesus sent Peter and John. He said, "Go and get the Passover meal ready for us."
They asked, "Where do You want us to get it ready?"
He said, "When you go into the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him to the house he goes into.
Tell the owner of the house that the Teacher asks where the room is where He can eat the Passover with His friends.
He will show you a big room upstairs. It will be ready. Get the meal ready there."
They went and found it just as He said. They got the Passover ready.
When the time came, Jesus sat down. His followers sat with Him.
He said to them, "I have really wanted to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
He took a cup, gave thanks, and said, "Take this and share it among yourselves.
I tell you, I will not drink wine until God's kingdom comes."
He took bread, gave thanks, and broke it. He gave it to them and said, "This is My body. It is given for you. Do this to remember Me."
In the same way, after the meal, He took the cup. He said, "This cup is the new promise. It is sealed with My blood, which is poured out for you."
He said, "But look, the hand of the one who is handing Me over is with Me at the table.
The Son of Man will go as it has been set. But it will be terrible for the man who hands Him over."
They began to ask each other who would do this.
A fight started among them. They argued about who seemed to be the greatest.
Jesus said to them, "The kings of the nations rule over them. Their leaders are called helpers.
But you must not be like that. The greatest among you should be like the youngest. The one who leads should be like the one who serves.
Who is greater? The one who sits at the table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits? But I am among you as one who serves."
He said, "You are the ones who stayed with Me in My hard times.
I am giving you a kingdom, just as My Father gave one to Me.
You will eat and drink at My table in My kingdom. You will sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel."
He said, "Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to test you all.
But I have prayed for you. I pray that your faith will not fail. When you turn back, help your brothers."
Peter said, "Lord, I am ready to go with You to jail and to death."
Jesus said, "Peter, I tell you, the rooster will not crow today until you say three times that you do not know Me."
Jesus asked them, "When I sent you out without a money bag, a bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?" They said, "Nothing."
He said, "But now, whoever has a money bag should take it. Take a bag too. Whoever does not have a sword should sell his coat and buy one."
He said, "I tell you, this must come true in Me: 'He was counted with those who broke the law.' What is written about Me is coming to an end."
They said, "Lord, here are two swords." Jesus said, "That is enough."
Jesus went out and went to the Mount of Olives, as He usually did. His followers followed Him.
When He got there, He said, "Pray so you will not be tested."
He went a short way from them. He knelt down and prayed.
He said, "Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. But not My will. Let Your will be done."
An angel from heaven appeared to Him and made Him strong.
He was in great pain. He prayed harder. His sweat fell like drops of blood to the ground.
He got up from praying and went to His followers. He found them sleeping because they were sad.
He said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray so you will not be tested."
While He was still speaking, a crowd came. Judas, one of the Twelve, led them. He came near Jesus to kiss Him.
Jesus said to him, "Judas, are you handing over the Son of Man with a kiss?"
Those with Jesus saw what was going to happen. They said, "Lord, should we strike with a sword?"
One of them hit the servant of the high priest. He cut off the servant's right ear.
Jesus said, "Stop! That is enough." He touched the ear and healed it.
Jesus said to the chief priests, temple guards, and elders who came for Him, "Did you come out with swords and clubs as if I were a robber?"
He said, "Every day I was with you in the temple. You did not grab Me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness is here."
They seized Him and led Him away. They took Him to the high priest's house. Peter followed far behind.
They lit a fire in the middle of the yard. Peter sat among them.
A servant girl saw him sitting by the fire. She looked at him and said, "This man was with Him too."
Peter said, "Woman, I don't know Him."
A little later, someone else saw him and said, "You are one of them too." Peter said, "Man, I am not."
About an hour later, another man said strongly, "This man was with Him. He is from Galilee too."
Peter said, "Man, I don't know what you are talking about." While he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Peter remembered what the Lord had said: 'Before the rooster crows today, you will say three times that you do not know Me.'
Peter went outside and cried hard.
The men holding Jesus made fun of Him. They hit Him.
They covered His eyes and said, "Tell us who hit You."
They said many bad things about Him.
When day came, the elders of the people, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law met together. They took Him to their council. They said,
"If You are the Christ, tell us." Jesus said, "If I tell you, you will not believe.
If I ask you, you will not answer.
From now on, the Son of Man will sit at the right hand of God's power."
They all said, "Are You the Son of God then?" Jesus said, "You say that I am."
They said, "What more do we need? We heard it from His own mouth."
The whole crowd stood up and led Jesus to Pilate.
They began to blame Him. They said, “We found this man turning our people against us. He stops us from paying taxes to Caesar. He says He is the Christ, the King.”
Pilate asked Him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “You say so.”
Pilate said to the leading priests and the crowd, “I see no wrong in this man.”
But they kept saying, “He stirs up the people all over Judea. He started in Galilee and has come here.”
When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was from Galilee.
He learned that Jesus was in Herod’s area. So he sent Jesus to Herod, who was in Jerusalem at that time.
Herod was very glad to see Jesus. He had wanted to see Him for a long time. He had heard about Him and hoped to see Him do a miracle.
He asked Jesus many questions, but Jesus did not answer.
The leading priests and teachers of the law stood there. They spoke against Him.
Herod and his soldiers made fun of Jesus. They put a bright robe on Him and sent Him back to Pilate.
That day Herod and Pilate became friends. Before, they had been enemies.
Pilate called the leading priests, the rulers, and the people together.
He said to them, “You brought this man to me. You say he turns people away. I have questioned him in front of you. I see no wrong in him for the things you say he did.
Herod did not find wrong either. He sent him back to us. See, he has done nothing that should get him killed.
So I will punish him and let him go.”
But they all shouted, “Take this man away! Let Barabbas go free!”
Barabbas was in prison for a riot and murder.
Pilate wanted to let Jesus go. He spoke to them again.
But they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
A third time he said to them, “What wrong has this man done? I see no reason to kill Him. So I will punish Him and let Him go.”
But they kept shouting loudly to crucify Him. Their shouting won.
Pilate gave in to what they wanted.
He let the man they asked for go free. That man was in prison for riot and murder. He handed Jesus over to them.
As they led Him away, they grabbed Simon from Cyrene. He was coming from the country. They put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
A large crowd followed Him. Women were there too. They cried and mourned for Him.
Jesus turned to them and said, “Women of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me. Weep for yourselves and your children.
Days are coming when people will say, ‘Happy are women who never had children, who never fed babies.’
Then they will say to the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us!’
If they hurt Me while I am innocent, what will happen to you?”
Two other criminals were led out to be killed with Him.
When they came to the place called Skull, they nailed Him to a cross there. They also nailed the criminals to crosses, one on His right and one on His left.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them. They do not know what they are doing.” They divided His clothes and drew straws.
The people stood and watched. The rulers laughed at Him. They said, “He saved others. Let Him save Himself, if He is God’s chosen Christ.”
The soldiers also made fun of Him. They came and offered Him sour wine.
They said, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!”
A sign above Him said, “This is the King of the Jews.”
One of the criminals hanging there insulted Him. He said, “Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us!”
The other criminal answered and told him to stop. He said, “Don’t you fear God? We are under the same punishment.
We deserve it. We are getting what we deserve for what we did. But this man did nothing wrong.”
Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”
Jesus said to him, “I tell you the truth, today you will be with Me in Paradise.”
It was about noon. Darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon.
The sun stopped shining. The curtain in the temple tore in two.
Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Father, I put My spirit in your hands.” Then He breathed His last.
The army officer saw what happened. He praised God and said, “Surely this man was innocent.”
All the crowds who came to see this sight saw what happened. They went home beating their chests.
All His friends and the women who had followed Him from Galilee stood far away and watched.
There was a man named Joseph. He was a good and fair man. He was a member of the council.
He had not agreed with their plan and action. He was from the Jewish town of Arimathea. He was waiting for God’s kingdom.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
He took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid it in a tomb cut in rock. No one had ever been laid there.
It was the day before the Sabbath. The Sabbath was about to begin.
The women who had come with Him from Galilee followed. They saw the tomb and how His body was laid.
Then they went home and prepared spices and perfumes. They rested on the Sabbath, as the law said.
On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women went to the tomb. They brought the spices they had prepared.
They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
They went in, but they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
While they were wondering about this, two men in shining clothes stood beside them.
The women were afraid. They bowed their faces to the ground. The men said to them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
He is not here. He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee.
He said the Son of Man must be handed over to sinful men. He must be nailed to a cross. He will rise again on the third day.”
Then the women remembered His words.
They went back from the tomb. They told all these things to the eleven and to all the others.
The women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and others with them. They told this to the apostles.
But their words seemed like nonsense to the apostles. They did not believe the women.
Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and looked in. He saw only the cloths. Then he went home, wondering what had happened.
That same day, two of Jesus’ followers were walking to a village called Emmaus. It was about seven miles from Jerusalem.
They talked with each other about all these things that had happened.
While they talked and asked questions, Jesus came near and walked with them.
But they did not know it was Jesus. Their eyes were kept from seeing Him.
He said to them, “What are you talking about as you walk?” They stopped and looked sad.
One of them, named Cleopas, answered, “Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there in these days?”
“What things?” He asked. “About Jesus of Nazareth. He spoke for God. He was strong in what He said and did before God and all the people.
Our chief priests and rulers handed Him over to be killed. They nailed Him to a cross.
We hoped He was the one who would save Israel. But now it is the third day since all this happened.
Some women among us surprised us. They went to the tomb early.
They did not find His body. They came back and said they saw angels. The angels said He is alive.
Some of us went to the tomb. We found it just as the women said. But we did not see Him.”
He said to them, “You foolish people! You are so slow to believe all that God’s prophets said!
Did not the Christ have to suffer these things and then enter His glory?”
Starting with Moses and all the prophets, He explained to them what was said about Himself in all the holy writings.
They came near the village where they were going. He acted as if He would go farther.
But they urged Him, “Stay with us. It is almost evening. The day is almost over.” So He went in to stay with them.
When He was at the table with them, He took bread. He blessed it. He broke it. He gave it to them.
Then their eyes were opened. They knew Him. He disappeared from them.
They said to each other, “Did not our hearts feel warm inside us while He talked with us on the road? Did He not open the holy writings to us?”
That same hour they got up and went back to Jerusalem. They found the eleven and those with them gathered together.
They were saying, “The Lord has truly risen! He has appeared to Simon!”
Then the two told what had happened on the road. They told how they knew Jesus when He broke the bread.
While they were talking about this, Jesus stood among them. He said, “Peace be with you.”
They were scared and frightened. They thought they saw a spirit.
He said to them, “Why are you troubled? Why do you have doubts in your hearts?
Look at My hands and My feet. It is I, Myself. Touch Me and see. A spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”
After He said this, He showed them His hands and His feet.
They still did not believe because of joy and wonder. He said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave Him a piece of cooked fish.
He took it and ate it in front of them.
He said to them, “These are My words that I spoke to you while I was still with you. Everything must come true that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”
Then He opened their minds so they could understand the holy writings.
He said, “This is what is written: The Christ will suffer. He will rise from the dead on the third day.
People will be told to turn from sin. Their sins will be forgiven in His name. This will be preached to all nations. It will start at Jerusalem.
Look, I am sending you what My Father promised. But stay in the city until you are given power from heaven.”
He led them out as far as Bethany. He lifted up His hands and blessed them.
While He was blessing them, He left them. He was taken up into heaven.
They worshiped Him. Then they went back to Jerusalem with great joy.
They were always in the temple, praising God.
In the beginning was the Word. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
All things were made through Him. Without Him, nothing was made.
In Him was life, and that life was the light of people.
The light shines in the dark, and the dark did not overcome it.
A man named John was sent from God.
He came to tell about the light. He came so all people could believe through him.
He was not the light. He came to tell about the light.
The true light was coming into the world. It gives light to everyone.
He was in the world. The world was made through Him, but the world did not know Him.
He came to His own people, but they did not welcome Him.
Yet to all who did welcome Him, who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God.
They were born not from blood, not from a man's desire, and not from a man's will, but from God.
The Word became a man and lived among us. We saw His glory. It was the glory of the only Son from the Father. He was full of grace and truth.
John told about Him. He cried out, "This is the One I meant when I said, 'The One coming after me is greater than me, because He was before me.'"
From all He has, we all received grace. It was grace on top of grace.
The law was given through Moses. Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God. The only Son, who is God and is at the Father's side, has made Him known.
This is John's story. The Jewish leaders in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, "Who are you?"
He did not say no. He said clearly, "I am not the Christ."
They asked, "Are you Elijah?" He said, "No." They asked, "Are you the Prophet?" He said, "No."
They said, "Who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"
John said what Isaiah the prophet said: "I am a voice calling in the desert, 'Make a straight road for the Lord.'"
They asked him, "Why do you baptize if you are not the Christ, not Elijah, and not the Prophet?"
John answered, "I baptize with water. But among you stands One you do not know.
He is coming after me. I am not worthy to untie His sandal strap."
This happened in Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
The next day John saw Jesus coming to him. He said, "Look! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
This is the One I meant when I said, 'A man who comes after me is greater than me, because He was before me.'
I did not know Him. But I came baptizing with water so He would be shown to Israel."
John also said, "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove. It stayed on Him.
I did not know Him. But the One who sent me to baptize with water told me that the One I see the Spirit come down and stay on is the One who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.
I have seen this. I tell you, He is the Son of God."
The next day John was there again with two of his followers.
He looked at Jesus walking by and said, "Look! The Lamb of God!"
The two followers heard him and followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following. He said, "What do you want?" They said, "Rabbi, where are you staying?" Rabbi means Teacher.
Jesus said, "Come and see." They came and saw where He stayed. They stayed with Him that day. It was about four in the afternoon.
Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was one of the two who heard John and followed Jesus.
First he found his brother Simon and said, "We found the Messiah!" Messiah means Christ.
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, "You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas." Cephas means Peter.
The next day Jesus wanted to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said, "Follow Me."
Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said, "We found the One Moses wrote about in the Law. The prophets wrote about Him too. He is Jesus from Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
Nathanael said, "Can anything good come from Nazareth?" Philip said, "Come and see."
Jesus saw Nathanael coming to Him. He said, "Here is a true Israelite. There is no trick in him."
Nathanael said, "How do you know me?" Jesus said, "Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree."
Nathanael said, "Rabbi, You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"
Jesus said, "Do you believe because I said I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.
I tell you the truth, you will see heaven open. You will see God's angels going up and coming down on the Son of Man."
On the third day there was a wedding in Cana in Galilee. Jesus' mother was there.
Jesus and His disciples were also invited to the wedding.
When the wine ran out, Jesus' mother said to Him, "They have no more wine."
Jesus said to her, "Woman, what does that have to do with Me? My time has not come yet."
His mother said to the servants, "Do whatever He tells you."
There were six stone water jars there. The Jews used them to wash. Each jar held about 20 to 30 gallons.
Jesus said to them, "Fill the jars with water." So they filled them to the top.
Then He said, "Now draw some out and take it to the man in charge of the feast." So they took it.
The man in charge of the feast tasted the water. It had become wine. He did not know where it came from. But the servants who had drawn the water knew. He called the bridegroom.
He said, "Everyone serves the best wine first. Then they serve the cheaper wine after people have had enough to drink. But you have kept the best wine until now."
This was the first sign Jesus did in Cana in Galilee. It showed His glory. His disciples believed in Him.
After this, He went down to Capernaum. His mother, His brothers, and His disciples went with Him. They stayed there for a few days.
The Passover of the Jews was near. Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple He found people selling cows, sheep, and doves. He also found money changers sitting there.
He made a whip out of cords. He drove everyone out of the temple. He drove out the sheep and cows too. He poured out the money changers' coins. He turned over their tables.
He said to the dove sellers, "Take these things away! Do not make My Father's house a place for selling things."
His disciples remembered that it is written, "I care so much for Your house that it eats Me up."
The Jews answered Him, "What sign do You show us? Why do You do these things?"
Jesus answered them, "Destroy this temple. I will raise it up in three days."
The Jews said, "It took forty-six years to build this temple. Will You raise it up in three days?"
But He was talking about the temple of His body.
Later, when He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered what He had said. They believed the Scripture and His words.
While He was in Jerusalem for the Passover feast, many people believed in His name. They saw the signs He did.
But Jesus did not trust Himself to them. He knew all people.
He did not need anyone to tell Him about a person. He knew what was in a person's heart.
There was a man named Nicodemus. He was one of the Pharisees, a religious group, and a leader of the Jews.
He came to Jesus at night and said, "Teacher, we know you are a teacher from God. No one can do these miracles unless God is with him."
Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: No one can see God's kingdom unless they are born again."
Nicodemus asked, "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he go back into his mother's body and be born a second time?"
Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: No one can enter God's kingdom unless they are born of water and the Spirit.
What is born from people is people, and what is born from the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be amazed that I told you, 'All of you must be born again.'
The wind blows where it wants. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. It is the same with everyone born from the Spirit."
Nicodemus asked, "How can these things happen?"
Jesus answered, "Are you the teacher of Israel, and you do not understand these things?
I tell you the truth: We speak about what we know, and we tell about what we have seen. But you do not accept our words.
If I told you about things on earth and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about things in heaven?
No one has gone up to heaven except the One who came down from heaven, the Son of Man.
Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the desert, so the Son of Man must be lifted up.
Then everyone who believes in Him will have life that lasts forever.
"For God loved the world so much that He gave His only Son, so that everyone who believes in Him will not die but will have life that lasts forever.
God did not send His Son into the world to judge the world. He sent Him so the world could be saved through Him.
The one who believes in Him is not judged. But the one who does not believe is already judged, because that person has not believed in the name of God's only Son.
This is the judgment: The light came into the world, but people loved the dark more than the light, because their deeds were evil.
Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so their deeds will not be shown.
But the one who does what is true comes to the light, so it may be seen that their deeds are done in God."
After this, Jesus and His disciples went to the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and baptized people.
John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there. People came and were baptized.
John had not yet been put in prison.
John's disciples and a Jewish man argued about washing to make people clean.
They came to John and said, "Teacher, the man who was with you across the Jordan, the one you told about, is baptizing now, and everyone is going to Him."
John answered, "A man can receive only what is given to him from heaven.
You yourselves know I said, 'I am not the Christ. I was sent ahead of Him.'
The bride belongs to the groom. The friend of the groom stands and listens to him. He is very happy because of the groom's voice. So my joy is now full.
He must become greater, and I must become less."
The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks like someone from the earth. The One who comes from heaven is above all.
He tells what He has seen and heard, but no one accepts His words.
The one who accepts His words shows that God is true.
The One God sent speaks God's words, because God gives the Spirit without limit.
The Father loves the Son and has put everything in His hand.
The one who believes in the Son has life that lasts forever. But the one who does not obey the Son will not see life. God's anger stays on that person.
The Pharisees heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more followers than John.
But Jesus did not baptize people Himself. His followers did.
So He left Judea and went back to Galilee.
He had to go through Samaria.
He came to a town in Samaria called Sychar. It was near the field Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
Jacob's well was there. Jesus was tired from the trip. He sat by the well. It was about noon.
A woman from Samaria came to get water. Jesus said to her, "Give Me a drink."
His followers had gone to town to buy food.
The Samaritan woman said to Him, "Why do You ask me for a drink? I am a Samaritan woman. Jews do not share things with Samaritans."
Jesus answered her, "If you knew God's gift and who is asking you for a drink, you would ask Him. He would give you living water."
"Sir," the woman said, "You have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. Where do You get this living water?
Are You greater than our father Jacob? He gave us this well. He drank from it. His sons and his animals drank from it too."
Jesus said, "Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
But whoever drinks the water I give will never be thirsty. The water I give will become a spring in him. It will give life that never ends."
The woman said, "Sir, give me this water. Then I will not be thirsty. I will not have to come here to draw water."
Jesus said, "Go call your husband and come back."
She answered, "I have no husband." Jesus said, "You are right to say, 'I have no husband.'
You have had five husbands. The man you have now is not your husband. You spoke the truth."
The woman said, "Sir, I see that You are a prophet.
Our fathers worshiped on this mountain. But you Jews say the place to worship is in Jerusalem."
Jesus said, "Believe Me, woman. The time is coming when you will not worship the Father on this mountain or in Jerusalem.
You worship what you do not know. We worship what we know. The way to be saved comes from the Jews.
But the time is coming, and it is now here, when true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. The Father wants people like that to worship Him.
God is Spirit. His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and truth."
The woman said, "I know that the Messiah is coming. He is called the Christ. When He comes, He will tell us everything."
Jesus said, "I am He. I am talking to you."
Just then His followers came back. They were surprised that He was talking to a woman. But no one asked, "What do You want?" or "Why are You talking to her?"
The woman left her water jar. She went into town and said to the people,
"Come see a man who told me everything I did. Could this be the Christ?"
Many people came out of town and went to Him.
Meanwhile His followers said, "Rabbi, eat something."
Jesus said, "I have food to eat that you do not know about."
The followers asked each other, "Did someone bring Him food?"
Jesus said, "My food is to do what God sent Me to do. I want to finish His work.
You say, 'There are four more months until harvest.' But I tell you, look up. Look at the fields. They are already ready for harvest.
The worker who harvests gets paid. He gathers fruit for life that never ends. Then the one who plants and the one who harvests can be glad together.
This saying is true: 'One person plants, and another person harvests.'
I sent you to harvest what you did not work for. Others worked hard, and you get to share in their work."
Many Samaritans in that town believed in Him. They believed because of what the woman said. She said, "He told me everything I did."
The Samaritans asked Him to stay with them. He stayed there two days.
Many more people believed because of His words.
They said to the woman, "We believe now. We do not believe just because of what you said. We have heard Him for ourselves. We know that He is truly the Savior of the world."
After two days, He left for Galilee.
Jesus had said, "A prophet is not honored in his own hometown."
When He got to Galilee, the people there welcomed Him. They had seen all He did in Jerusalem at the feast. They had gone to the feast too.
He went to Cana in Galilee again. That was where He had turned water into wine. A royal official was there. His son was sick in Capernaum.
The official heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee. He went to Jesus and asked Him to come down and heal his son. The boy was about to die.
Jesus said to him, "Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe."
The official said, "Sir, come down before my child dies."
Jesus said, "Go. Your son lives." The man believed what Jesus said and went.
While he was going down, his servants met him. They said his son was alive.
He asked what time the boy got better. They said, "The fever left him yesterday at one o'clock."
The father knew that was the same hour Jesus said, "Your son lives." He and his whole family believed.
This was the second sign Jesus did after coming from Judea to Galilee.
After this, there was a Jewish feast. Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, there is a pool called Bethesda in Hebrew. It has five porches.
Many sick people lay there. Some were blind. Some could not walk. Some could not move well.
One man had been sick for 38 years.
Jesus saw him lying there. He knew the man had been sick a long time. Jesus said, "Do you want to get well?"
The sick man said, "Sir, I have no one to put me in the pool when the water moves. By the time I get there, someone else goes in first."
Jesus said, "Get up. Pick up your mat and walk."
Right away the man was well. He picked up his mat and walked. That day was a Sabbath.
The Jewish leaders said to the healed man, "It is the Sabbath. You may not carry your mat."
He said, "The man who made me well told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
They asked him, "Who told you, 'Pick up and walk'?"
The healed man did not know who it was. Jesus had slipped away because many people were there.
Later Jesus found him in the temple. He said, "See, you are well. Stop sinning, so nothing worse happens to you."
The man went away. He told the Jewish leaders that Jesus had made him well.
Because of this, the Jewish leaders were against Jesus. He had done these things on the Sabbath.
Jesus said to them, "My Father is working even now. I am working too."
This made the Jewish leaders want to kill Him even more. He did not just break the Sabbath. He also said God was His own Father. That made Him equal with God.
Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth. The Son cannot do anything by Himself. He only does what He sees the Father doing. What the Father does, the Son does too.
The Father loves the Son. He shows Him everything He does. He will show Him even greater things than these. Then you will be amazed." "
Just as the Father raises dead people and gives them life, the Son gives life to anyone He wants.
The Father does not judge anyone. He gave all judging to the Son.
He did this so everyone will honor the Son, just as they honor the Father. Anyone who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him." "
I tell you the truth. Anyone who hears My words and believes the One who sent Me has life that never ends. That person will not be judged. He has moved from death to life.
I tell you the truth. A time is coming, and it is here now, when dead people will hear the voice of the Son of God. Those who hear will live.
The Father has life in Himself. He gave the Son the power to have life in Himself too.
He gave the Son the right to judge, because He is the Son of Man." "
Do not be surprised at this. A time is coming when all people in the graves will hear His voice.
They will come out. People who did good will rise to life. People who did wrong will rise to be judged.
I cannot do anything by Myself. I judge as I hear. My judgment is fair. I do not do what I want. I do what the One who sent Me wants." "
If I say good things about Myself, that is not enough proof.
Someone else speaks for Me. I know His words about Me are true.
You sent people to John. He told the truth.
I do not need people to say good things about Me. I say this so you can be saved." "
John was like a lamp that burned and gave light. For a while, you were happy to enjoy his light.
But I have proof bigger than John's. The Father gave Me work to do. The work I am doing shows that the Father sent Me." "
The Father who sent Me has spoken for Me. You have never heard His voice. You have never seen what He looks like.
You do not keep His words in your hearts. You do not believe the One He sent." "
You study the Holy Books. You think they give you life that never ends. Those books tell about Me.
But you do not want to come to Me to have life." "
I do not look for praise from people.
But I know you. You do not have God's love in your hearts.
I came in My Father's name, and you do not receive Me. If someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.
How can you believe? You accept praise from each other. You do not look for praise from the only God." "
Do not think I will accuse you before the Father. Moses is the one who accuses you. You put your hope in him.
If you believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.
If you do not believe his writings, how will you believe My words?"
After this, Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias.
A big crowd followed Him because they saw the miracles He did for sick people.
Jesus went up on a mountain and sat there with His disciples.
The Jewish Passover feast was near.
Jesus looked up and saw the big crowd coming to Him. He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread so these people can eat?”
He said this to test Philip, because He already knew what He was going to do.
Philip answered Him, “Two hundred silver coins would not buy enough bread for each person to get a little.”
One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him,
“Here is a boy who has five barley loaves and two small fish. But what are these for so many people?”
Jesus said, “Have the people sit down.” There was much grass in that place, so the men sat down. There were about five thousand of them.
Jesus took the loaves. After giving thanks, He gave them to the people sitting there. He did the same with the fish. Everyone had as much as they wanted.
When they were full, He said to His disciples, “Gather the pieces that are left over so nothing is lost.”
So they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with pieces from the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.
The people saw the miracle He had done. They said, “This is truly the Prophet who is coming into the world.”
Jesus knew they were about to come and make Him king, so He went away again to the mountain by Himself.
When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea.
They got into a boat and started across the sea to Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.
A strong wind was blowing, and the sea was getting rough.
After they had gone about three miles, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat. They were afraid.
But He said to them, “It is I. Don’t be afraid.”
Then they wanted to take Him into the boat, and right away the boat was at the land where they were going.

The next day, the crowd that stayed on the other side of the sea saw that there was only one small boat there. They saw that Jesus had not gone with His disciples in the boat, but His disciples had gone alone.
But other small boats from Tiberias came near the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
When the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor His disciples, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they said to Him, “Teacher, when did you come here?”
Jesus answered them, “I tell you the truth, you are looking for Me not because you saw miracles, but because you ate the loaves and were filled.
Do not work for food that spoils, but for food that lasts for life that never ends, which the Son of Man will give you. For God the Father has put His stamp on Him.”
Then they said to Him, “What must we do to do the works of God?”
Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in Him whom He sent.”
So they said to Him, “What miracle will you do, so we may see and believe you? What will you do?
Our fathers ate the manna in the desert, as it is written, ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
Jesus said to them, “I tell you the truth, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but My Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”
Then they said to Him, “Lord, give us this bread always.”
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in Me will never be thirsty.
But I said to you that you have seen Me and still do not believe.”
“All that the Father gives Me will come to Me, and whoever comes to Me I will never turn away.
For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
This is the will of Him who sent Me, that I lose none of all He has given Me, but raise them up on the last day.
For this is the will of My Father, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him may have life that never ends, and I will raise him up on the last day.”
Then the Jews complained about Him because He said He is the bread that came down from heaven.
They said, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How can He now say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”
Jesus answered them, “Stop complaining among yourselves.
No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me brings him, and I will raise him up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets, ‘They will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to Me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the One who is from God; He has seen the Father.”
“I tell you the truth, whoever believes has life that never ends.
I am the bread of life.”
“Your fathers ate the manna in the desert, and they died.
This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that one may eat of it and not die.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. The bread that I will give for the life of the world is My body.”
Then the Jews argued with each other, saying, “How can this Man give us His body to eat?”
Jesus said to them, “I tell you the truth, unless you eat the body of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you.
Whoever eats My body and drinks My blood has life that never ends, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For My body is real food, and My blood is real drink.”
“Whoever eats My body and drinks My blood stays in Me, and I in him.
As the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever feeds on Me will live because of Me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven, not like your fathers ate and died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.”
He said these things while teaching in the meeting place in Capernaum.
When many of His disciples heard it, they said, “This is a hard teaching. Who can listen to it?”
Jesus knew in Himself that His disciples were complaining about this. He said to them, “Does this upset you?
Then what if you see the Son of Man go up to where He was before?
The Spirit gives life. The body is no help at all. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
But there are some of you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray Him.
He went on to say, “That is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless it is given to him by the Father.”
From that time many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.
So Jesus said to the Twelve, “Do you also want to go away?”
Simon Peter answered Him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of life that never ends.
We have believed and come to know that you are the Holy One of God.”
Jesus answered them, “Did I not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.”
He was speaking of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, for he, one of the Twelve, was going to betray Him.
After this, Jesus walked in Galilee. He did not want to walk in Judea, because the Jewish leaders wanted to kill Him.
Now the Jewish Festival of Shelters was near.
So His brothers said to Him, "Leave here and go to Judea. Then your followers can see the things you do.
No one does a thing in secret if he wants people to know him. If you do these things, show yourself to the world."
His brothers did not believe in Him.
Jesus said to them, "My time has not come yet. But your time is always ready.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me. It hates Me because I tell it that its works are bad.
You go up to the festival. I am not going up to this festival yet, because My time is not full."
After He said this, He stayed in Galilee.
But when His brothers went up to the festival, He went up too. He did not go openly. He went in secret.
The Jewish leaders looked for Him at the festival. They said, "Where is He?"
The crowd talked a lot about Him. Some said, "He is good." Others said, "No, He leads the crowd the wrong way."
But no one spoke openly about Him. They were afraid of the Jewish leaders.
When the festival was about half over, Jesus went up to the temple. He taught there.
The Jewish leaders were amazed. They said, "How does this man know so much? He has not studied."
Jesus answered them, "My teaching is not Mine. It comes from the One who sent Me.
If anyone wants to do God's will, he will know if My teaching comes from God or if I speak on My own.
A person who speaks on his own wants his own praise. But a person who wants praise for the One who sent him is true. There is no wrong in him."
"Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why do you want to kill Me?"
The crowd answered, "You have a demon! Who wants to kill you?"
Jesus answered them, "I did one thing, and all of you are amazed.
That is why Moses gave you circumcision. Circumcision did not start with Moses. It came from the fathers. And you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.
If a man is circumcised on the Sabbath so the law of Moses is not broken, why are you angry at Me? I made a whole man well on the Sabbath.
Do not judge by how things look. Judge with right judgment."
Some people from Jerusalem said, "Is this not the man they want to kill?
Look! He speaks openly, and they say nothing to Him. Have the rulers really decided that this is the Christ?
But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from."
Jesus cried out as He taught in the temple, "Yes, you know Me, and you know where I am from. But I have not come on My own. The One who sent Me is true. You do not know Him.
I know Him, because I am from Him, and He sent Me."
They tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him. His time had not come yet.
Many in the crowd believed in Him. They said, "When the Christ comes, will He do more signs than this man has done?"
The Pharisees heard the crowd talking about Him. The Pharisees and chief priests sent guards to seize Him.
Jesus said, "I will be with you a little longer. Then I go to the One who sent Me.
You will look for Me and not find Me. Where I am, you cannot come."
The Jewish leaders said to each other, "Where will this man go? We will not find Him. Will He go to the Jews scattered among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?
What does He mean by saying, 'You will look for Me and not find Me. Where I am, you cannot come'?"
On the last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood up. He cried out, "If anyone is thirsty, come to Me and drink.
If anyone believes in Me, rivers of living water will flow from inside him. This is what the Bible says."
Jesus said this about the Spirit. People who believed in Him were going to receive the Spirit. The Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been shown His glory.
When some in the crowd heard this, they said, "This is truly the Prophet."
Others said, "This is the Christ." But some said, "Does the Christ come from Galilee?"
"Does not the Bible say the Christ will come from David's family and from Bethlehem, the town where David was?"
So the crowd was split because of Him.
Some of them wanted to seize Him. But no one laid hands on Him.
The guards went to the chief priests and Pharisees. They said, "Why did you not bring Him?"
The guards answered, "No man has ever spoken like this man."
The Pharisees answered them, "Have you been fooled too?
Has any ruler or Pharisee believed in Him?
But this crowd does not know the law. They are under a curse."
Nicodemus was one of them. He had gone to Jesus before. He said to them,
"Does our law judge a man before it hears him and knows what he does?"
They answered, "Are you from Galilee too? Look into it. You will see that no prophet comes from Galilee."
Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
At dawn He came back to the temple. All the people came to Him, and He sat down and taught them.
The teachers of the law and the Pharisees brought a woman to Him. She had been caught cheating on her husband. They made her stand in the middle.
They said to Him, "Teacher, this woman was caught cheating on her husband.
Moses told us in the Law to stone women like this. What do You say?"
They said this to test Him. They wanted a reason to accuse Him. But Jesus bent down and wrote on the ground with His finger.
They kept asking Him. He stood up and said, "Let the one among you who has no sin throw the first stone at her."
Then He bent down again and wrote on the ground.
When they heard this, they went out one by one. The older men left first. Jesus was left alone with the woman. She was still standing there.
Jesus stood up and said to her, "Woman, where are they? Did no one say you are guilty?"
She said, "No one, Lord." Jesus said, "I do not say you are guilty either. Go, and do not sin again."
Jesus spoke to them again. He said, "I am the light of the world. Anyone who follows Me will not walk in the dark. He will have the light that gives life."
The Pharisees said to Him, "You speak for Yourself. Your words are not true."
Jesus answered, "Even if I speak for Myself, My words are true. I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
You judge by human ways. I do not judge anyone.
But if I do judge, My judgment is true. I am not alone. The Father who sent Me is with Me.
It is written in your Law that the words of two people are true.
I speak for Myself, and the Father who sent Me speaks for Me too."
They asked Him, "Where is Your Father?" Jesus said, "You do not know Me or My Father. If you knew Me, you would know My Father."
He said these things while He taught in the temple, near the money box. No one arrested Him, because His time had not yet come.
He said to them again, "I am going away. You will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I go, you cannot come."
The Jews said, "Will He kill Himself? He says, 'Where I go, you cannot come.'"
He said to them, "You are from below. I am from above. You are of this world. I am not of this world.
That is why I told you that you will die in your sins. If you do not believe that I am He, you will die in your sins."
