They asked Him, "Who are You?" Jesus said, "I am who I have been telling you from the start.
I have much to say and judge about you. But the One who sent Me is true. I say to the world what I heard from Him."
They did not understand that He was talking about the Father.
Jesus said to them, "When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He. I do nothing on My own. I speak just as the Father taught Me.
The One who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him."
As He said these things, many people believed in Him.
Jesus said to the Jews who believed in Him, "If you stay in My word, you are truly My followers.
You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
They answered Him, "We are Abraham's children. We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be free?"
Jesus answered them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave of sin.
A slave does not stay in the house forever. A son stays forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you are free indeed.
I know you are Abraham's children. But you want to kill Me, because My word has no room in you.
I speak what I saw with My Father. And you do what you heard from your father."
They said to Him, "Abraham is our father." Jesus said to them, "If you were Abraham's children, you would do Abraham's works.
But now you want to kill Me, a man who told you the truth I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
You do the works of your father." They said, "We were not born from sexual sin. We have one Father, God."
Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love Me. I came from God, and I am here. I did not come on My own. He sent Me.
Why do you not understand My words? You cannot hear My word.

You are from your father the devil. You want to do what your father wants. He was a murderer from the start. He does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his own words, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
Because I tell the truth, you do not believe Me.
Which of you can show that I have sinned? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe Me?
The person who is from God hears God's words. You do not hear them, because you are not from God."
The Jews answered Him, "Are we not right to say You are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon. I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
I do not look for My own glory. There is One who looks for it and judges.
Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death."
The Jews said to Him, "Now we know You have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets died. Yet You say if anyone keeps Your word, he will never taste death.
Are You greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died too. Who do You make Yourself?"
Jesus answered, "If I bring glory to Myself, My glory is nothing. My Father brings glory to Me. You say He is your God.
You do not know Him. But I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I know Him, and I keep His word.
Your father Abraham was glad to see My day. He saw it and was glad."
The Jews said to Him, "You are not even fifty years old. Have You seen Abraham?"
Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am."
They picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus hid and left the temple.
As Jesus walked by, He saw a man who had been blind since birth.
His followers asked Him, "Teacher, who sinned? Did this man sin, or did his parents sin? Why was he born blind?"
Jesus answered, "This man did not sin, and his parents did not sin. He was born blind so that God's power could be seen in him.
We must do the work of the One who sent Me while it is still day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
While I am in the world, I am the light of the world."
After He said this, He spit on the ground. He made mud with the spit. Then He put the mud on the man's eyes.
He told him, "Go wash in the pool of Siloam." (Siloam means "Sent.") The man went and washed. He came back seeing.
The neighbors and people who had seen him beg before said, "Isn't this the man who used to sit and beg?"
Some said, "Yes, he is." Others said, "No, but he looks like him." The man said, "I am the one."
They asked him, "Then how were your eyes opened?"
He answered, "The man called Jesus made mud. He put it on my eyes. He told me, 'Go to Siloam and wash.' So I went and washed. Then I could see."
They asked him, "Where is He?" He said, "I don't know."
They brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees.
It was a Sabbath day when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
So the Pharisees asked him again how he could see. He said to them, "He put mud on my eyes. I washed. Now I see."
Some of the Pharisees said, "This man is not from God. He does not keep the Sabbath." Others said, "How can a sinner do such signs?" They did not agree.
They asked the blind man again, "What do you say about Him? He opened your eyes." He said, "He is a prophet."
The Jews did not believe that he had been blind and now could see. They called his parents.
They asked them, "Is this your son? You say he was born blind. How does he see now?"
His parents answered, "We know this is our son. We know he was born blind.
But we do not know how he sees now. We do not know who opened his eyes. Ask him. He is old enough. He can speak for himself."
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. The Jews had already agreed that anyone who said Jesus was the Christ would be thrown out of the place where Jews worship.
That is why his parents said, "He is old enough. Ask him."
So they called the man who had been blind a second time. They said to him, "Give glory to God. We know this man is a sinner."
He answered, "I don't know if He is a sinner. One thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see."
Then they said to him, "What did He do to you? How did He open your eyes?"
He answered, "I already told you. You did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you want to be His disciples too?"
They yelled at him and said, "You are His disciple. We are disciples of Moses.
We know God spoke to Moses. But we do not know where this man comes from."
The man answered, "That is amazing! You don't know where He comes from, but He opened my eyes.
We know God does not listen to sinners. But God listens to anyone who worships Him and does what He wants.
No one has ever heard of anyone opening the eyes of a person born blind.
If this man were not from God, He could not do anything."
They answered him, "You were born in sin! Are you trying to teach us?" Then they threw him out.
Jesus heard that they had thrown him out. He found him and said, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
He answered, "Who is He, Lord? Tell me so I can believe in Him."
Jesus said to him, "You have seen Him. He is the one talking with you."
He said, "Lord, I believe." And he worshiped Him.
Jesus said, "I came into this world to judge. I came so that people who do not see may see, and people who see may become blind."
Some Pharisees who were with Him heard this. They said to Him, "Are we blind too?"
Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now you say, 'We see.' So your sin stays."
"I tell you the truth. Anyone who does not go into the sheep pen through the door, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
But the one who comes in through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
The man at the gate opens it for Him. The sheep hear His voice. He calls His own sheep by name and leads them out.
When He has brought out all His own sheep, He walks ahead of them. The sheep follow Him because they know His voice.
They will not follow a stranger. They will run away from him because they do not know the voice of strangers."
Jesus told them this story, but they did not understand what He was saying.
Jesus said again, "I tell you the truth. I am the door for the sheep.
All who came before Me are thieves and robbers. But the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the door. If anyone comes in through Me, he will be saved. He will go in and out and find good grass.
The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came so they can have life, and have it more than enough."
"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives up His life for the sheep.
The hired man is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf grabs them and scatters them.
he runs away because he is paid to work and does not care about the sheep.
"I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep, and My sheep know Me.
The Father knows Me, and I know the Father. I give up My life for the sheep.
I have other sheep that are not in this sheep pen. I must bring them too. They will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
"That is why the Father loves Me. I give up My life so I can take it back again.
No one takes it from Me. I give it up by My own choice. I have the right to give it up, and I have the right to take it back. My Father gave Me this command."
Again, the Jews were divided because of what He said.
Many of them said, "He has an evil spirit and is crazy! Why listen to Him?"
Others said, "These are not the words of a man with an evil spirit. Can an evil spirit open the eyes of a blind man?"
Then it was time for a special feast in Jerusalem. It was winter.
Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon's porch.
The Jewish leaders gathered around Him and said, "How long will You keep us waiting? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly."
Jesus answered, "I told you, and you do not believe. The works I do in My Father's name speak for Me.
But you do not believe because you are not My sheep.
My sheep listen to My voice. I know them, and they follow Me.
I give them life that never ends. They will never be lost. No one will snatch them out of My hand.
My Father gave them to Me. He is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of My Father's hand.
I and the Father are one."
Again, the Jewish leaders picked up stones to stone Him.
Jesus answered them, "I showed you many good works from the Father. For which one are you going to stone Me?"
The Jewish leaders answered, "We are not stoning You for a good work. We are stoning You because You speak against God. You are only a man, but You make Yourself God."
Jesus answered them, "It is written in your law, 'I said, you are gods.'
If He called them gods, and God's Word cannot be changed,
then why do you say I speak against God? I am the One the Father set apart and sent into the world. You say I speak against God because I said, 'I am the Son of God.'
If I do not do My Father's works, do not believe Me.
But if I do them, even if you do not believe Me, believe the works. Then you will know and understand that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father."
They tried again to grab Him, but He escaped from them.
Jesus went back across the Jordan River to the place where John first baptized. He stayed there.
Many people came to Him. They said, "John did no miracle, but everything John said about this Man was true."
Many people there believed in Him.
A man named Lazarus was sick. He was from Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.
Mary was the one who put perfume on the Lord and wiped His feet with her hair. Lazarus was her brother.
So the sisters sent word to Jesus. They said, "Lord, the one You love is sick."
Jesus heard this. He said, "This sickness will not end in death. It is for God's glory. The Son of God will get glory through it."
Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
When He heard Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two more days.
Then He said to His followers, "Let us go back to Judea."
"Teacher," they said, "the Jews just tried to stone You. Are You going there again?"
Jesus answered, "There are twelve hours of light in a day. If someone walks in the day, he does not trip. He sees the light of this world.
But if someone walks at night, he trips. There is no light."
After this, He said, "Our friend Lazarus is asleep. But I am going to wake him up."
His followers said, "Lord, if he is asleep, he will get better."
They thought He meant real sleep. But Jesus meant Lazarus had died.
Then Jesus said plainly, "Lazarus is dead.
I am glad I was not there, so you may believe. But let us go to him."
Thomas, called the Twin, said to the other followers, "Let us go too, so we can die with Him."
When Jesus arrived, He found Lazarus had been in the tomb four days.
Bethany was near Jerusalem, about two miles away.
Many Jews had come to Martha and Mary. They came to comfort them about their brother.
Martha heard Jesus was coming. She went to meet Him. Mary stayed home.
Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
But I know God will give You whatever You ask Him."
Jesus said, "Your brother will rise again."
Martha said, "I know he will rise again in the last day."
Jesus said, "I am the one who brings people back to life and gives life. The one who believes in Me will live, even if he dies.
Everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?"
"Yes, Lord," she said. "I believe You are the Christ, the Son of God, the One who comes into the world."
After she said this, she went back. She called her sister Mary quietly. She said, "The Teacher is here. He is calling you."
Mary got up quickly and went to Him.
Jesus had not yet come into the town. He was still where Martha met Him.
The Jews in the house were comforting Mary. They saw her get up fast and leave. They followed her. They thought she was going to the tomb to cry there.
Mary came to where Jesus was. She saw Him and fell at His feet. She said, "Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died."
Jesus saw her crying. He saw the Jews with her crying too. He was very upset in spirit. He was troubled.
He asked, "Where have you laid him?" They said, "Lord, come and see."
The Jews said, "See how He loved him!"
But some said, "He opened the eyes of the blind man. Could He not have kept this man from dying?"
Jesus was still very upset. He came to the tomb. It was a cave. A stone was over it.
Jesus said, "Take away the stone." Martha said, "Lord, he smells bad now. He has been dead four days."
Jesus said, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see God's glory?"
So they took away the stone. Jesus looked up and said, "Father, I thank You that You heard Me.
I know You always hear Me. But I said this for the crowd standing here. I said it so they will believe You sent Me."
After He said this, He called in a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!"
The dead man came out. His hands and feet were wrapped in strips of cloth. His face was wrapped in a cloth. Jesus said, "Take off the grave clothes and let him go."
Many Jews who had come to Mary saw what Jesus did. They believed in Him.
But some went to the Pharisees. They told them what Jesus had done.
The chief priests and Pharisees called a meeting. They said, "What are we doing? This man does many miracles.
If we let Him go on, everyone will believe in Him. Then the Romans will come and take away our place and our nation."
Caiaphas, the high priest that year, said, "You do not know anything. You do not see that it is better for you that one man die for the people.
Then the whole nation will not die."
He did not say this on his own. As high priest that year, he spoke a message from God. He said Jesus would die for the nation.
He also said Jesus would die to bring together God's scattered children into one family.
From that day on, they planned to kill Him.
So Jesus did not walk openly among the Jews anymore. He left there. He went to a town called Ephraim, near the desert. He stayed there with His followers.
The Jewish Passover feast was near. Many people went up from the country to Jerusalem. They went to make themselves clean before Passover.
They looked for Jesus. They talked with each other in the temple. They said, "What do you think? Will He not come to the feast?"
The chief priests and Pharisees had given orders. If anyone knew where Jesus was, he must tell them. They wanted to arrest Him.
Six days before Passover, Jesus went to Bethany. That was where Lazarus lived. Jesus had raised Lazarus from the dead.
There they made a dinner for Him. Martha served. Lazarus was one of the people at the table with Jesus.
Mary took a pound of very costly perfume. It was pure nard. She put it on Jesus' feet. She wiped His feet with her hair. The whole house smelled like the perfume.
One of His disciples spoke. It was Judas Iscariot. He was the one who would hand Jesus over. He said,
"Why wasn't this perfume sold? It could have brought a lot of money. We could have given it to poor people."
He said this, but not because he cared about poor people. He was a thief. He kept the money bag and stole from it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She saved this perfume for the day I will be buried.
You will always have poor people with you. But you will not always have Me."
A big crowd of Jews found out Jesus was there. They came not only to see Jesus, but also to see Lazarus. Jesus had raised Lazarus from the dead.
The chief priests made a plan to kill Lazarus too.
Many Jews left and believed in Jesus because of Lazarus.
The next day, a big crowd came to the feast. They heard Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
They took palm branches and went out to meet Him. They shouted, "Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! He is the King of Israel!"
Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it. This happened just as it was written:
"Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion. Look! Your King is coming. He is sitting on a donkey's colt."

At first, His disciples did not understand this. But after Jesus was honored, they remembered these things. They remembered that these things were written about Him and that they had done them for Him.
The crowd that was with Him kept telling about Lazarus. Jesus had called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead.
That is why the crowd went to meet Him. They had heard He did this sign.
The Pharisees said to each other, "Look! You are not getting anywhere. See, the whole world has gone after Him."
Some Greeks were there. They came up to worship at the feast.
They came to Philip. He was from Bethsaida in Galilee. They asked him, "Sir, we want to see Jesus."
Philip went and told Andrew. Then Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, "The time has come for the Son of Man to be honored.
I tell you the truth. Unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it stays alone. But if it dies, it makes much fruit.
Anyone who loves his life will lose it. Anyone who hates his life in this world will keep it for life that lasts forever.
If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me. Where I am, My servant will be too. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
Now My soul is troubled. What should I say? 'Father, save Me from this hour'? But that is why I came to this hour.
Father, make Your name great." Then a voice came from heaven. It said, "I have made it great, and I will make it great again."
The crowd standing there heard it. Some said it thundered. Others said an angel spoke to Him.
Jesus answered, "This voice came, not for Me, but for you.
Now this world is judged. Now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to Myself."
He said this to show what kind of death He would die.
The crowd answered Him, "We heard from the Law that the Christ stays forever. So how can you say the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?"

Jesus said to them, "You still have the light with you for a little while. Walk while you have the light. Then darkness will not catch you. The one who walks in darkness does not know where he is going.
Believe in the light while you have it. Then you will be children of light." After Jesus said this, He went away and hid from them.
Even though He had done so many signs in front of them, they did not believe in Him.
This happened so the word of Isaiah the prophet would come true. He said, "Lord, who has believed our message? Who has seen the Lord's power?"
That is why they could not believe. Isaiah also said,
"He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts. Then they will not see with their eyes or understand with their hearts. They will not turn, and I will not heal them."
Isaiah said this because he saw His glory and spoke about Him.
Even so, many leaders believed in Him. But they did not say so because of the Pharisees. They were afraid they would be put out of the synagogue.
They loved praise from people more than praise from God.
Jesus cried out, "The one who believes in Me does not believe in Me only. He believes in the One who sent Me.
The one who sees Me sees the One who sent Me.
I came into the world as a light. Then everyone who believes in Me will not stay in darkness.
If anyone hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
The one who rejects Me and does not take My words has a judge. The word I spoke will judge him on the last day.
I did not speak on My own. The Father who sent Me told Me what to say and what to speak.
I know His command is life that lasts forever. So I speak just as the Father told Me."
Before the Passover feast, Jesus knew His time had come. He would leave this world and go to the Father. He loved His own people in the world. He loved them to the very end.
It was supper time. The devil had already put it in Judas's heart to turn Jesus in. Judas was Simon's son.
Jesus knew the Father had given Him power over all things. He knew He had come from God and was going back to God.
So Jesus got up from supper. He took off His outer clothes. He wrapped a towel around Himself.
Then He poured water into a bowl. He began to wash His followers' feet. He dried them with the towel.
"Lord, are You washing my feet?" Peter asked.
Jesus answered, "You do not know now what I am doing. But later you will know."
Peter said, "You will never wash my feet!" Jesus answered, "If I do not wash you, you have no part with Me."
Peter said, "Lord, not just my feet. Wash my hands and my head too."
Jesus said, "A person who has had a bath is clean all over. He only needs his feet washed. You are clean, but not all of you."
Jesus knew who would turn Him in. That is why He said, "Not all of you are clean."
After Jesus washed their feet, He put His clothes back on. He sat down again. He asked, "Do you know what I have done for you?"
"You call Me Teacher and Lord. You are right. That is what I am.
"I am your Lord and Teacher. I washed your feet. So you should wash one another's feet.
I gave you an example. Do as I did for you.
"I tell you the truth. A servant is not greater than his master. A messenger is not greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things, you are happy if you do them.
"I am not talking about all of you. I know the ones I chose. But this must happen to make the Holy Writings come true: 'The one who eats My bread has turned against Me.'
I am telling you now, before it happens. Then when it happens, you will believe that I am the one.
I tell you the truth. Anyone who welcomes the one I send welcomes Me. Anyone who welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me."
After Jesus said this, He was very upset in His spirit. He said, "I tell you the truth. One of you will turn Me in."
His followers looked at each other. They did not know who He meant.
One follower sat next to Jesus. Jesus loved him. He leaned against Jesus.
Simon Peter nodded to him. He wanted him to ask who Jesus meant.
So that follower leaned back against Jesus' chest. He asked, "Lord, who is it?"
Jesus answered, "It is the one I give this piece of bread to after I dip it." Then Jesus dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, Simon's son.
As soon as Judas took the bread, Satan came into him. Jesus said to him, "Do quickly what you are going to do."
No one at the table knew why Jesus said this to him.
Some thought Jesus told Judas, "Buy what we need for the feast," or "Give something to the poor." Judas kept the money box.
Judas took the bread and left right away. It was night.
After Judas left, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is honored. And God is honored in Him.
If God is honored in Him, God will honor Him in Himself. He will do it right away."
"My dear children, I will be with you a little longer. You will look for Me. I told the Jews this, and now I tell you: Where I am going, you cannot come.
I give you a new command: Love one another. Love one another the way I loved you.
Everyone will know you are My followers if you love one another."
Peter said, "Lord, where are You going?" Jesus answered, "Where I am going, you cannot follow now. But you will follow later."
Peter said, "Lord, why can't I follow You now? I will give my life for You."
Jesus answered, "Will you give your life for Me? I tell you the truth. Before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know Me."
Jesus said, "Don't let your hearts be worried. Trust in God. Trust in Me too.
My Father's house has many rooms. If that were not true, I would have told you. I am going there to get a place ready for you.
After I go and get a place ready for you, I will come back. I will take you to be with Me. Then you can be where I am.
You know the way to where I am going."
Thomas said to Him, "Lord, we don't know where You are going. How can we know the way?"
Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one goes to the Father except through Me.
If you knew Me, you would know My Father too. Now you know Him and have seen Him."
Philip said to Him, "Lord, show us the Father. That is all we need."
Jesus said, "Philip, I have been with you a long time. Don't you know Me yet? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, 'Show us the Father'?
Don't you believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you are not My own. The Father who lives in Me does His work.
Believe Me when I say I am in the Father and the Father is in Me. Or at least believe because of the things I do.
"I tell you the truth: Anyone who believes in Me will do the same things I do. He will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
Whatever you ask in My name, I will do it. Then the Father will be honored through the Son.
If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it.
"If you love Me, you will obey My commands.
I will ask the Father. He will give you another Helper. This Helper will be with you forever.
He is the Spirit of truth. The world cannot accept Him. The world does not see Him or know Him. But you know Him. He lives with you and will be in you.
"I will not leave you alone. I will come to you.
In a little while, the world will not see Me anymore. But you will see Me. Because I live, you will live too.
On that day, you will know that I am in My Father. You are in Me, and I am in you.
"Whoever has My commands and obeys them is the one who loves Me. The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father. I will love him too. I will show Myself to him."
Judas, not Judas Iscariot, said to Him, "Lord, why will You show Yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered, "If anyone loves Me, he will obey My word. My Father will love him. We will come to him and make our home with him.
Anyone who does not love Me does not obey My words. The word you hear is not Mine. It is from the Father who sent Me.
"I have told you these things while I am still with you.
But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, will come. The Father will send Him in My name. He will teach you everything. He will remind you of everything I said to you.
"I give you peace. It is My peace I give you. I do not give it the way the world gives. Don't let your hearts be worried or afraid.
You heard Me say, 'I am going away, and I will come back to you.' If you loved Me, you would be glad I am going to the Father. That is because the Father is greater than I am.
I have told you this now, before it happens. Then when it happens, you will believe.
"I will not talk with you much longer. The ruler of this world is coming. He has no power over Me.
But I do what the Father told Me. Then the world will know I love the Father. Get up. Let's go from here."
I am the true vine. My Father takes care of the vine.
He cuts off every branch in Me that does not make fruit. He trims every branch that does make fruit, so it can make more fruit.
You are already clean because of the words I said to you.
Stay in Me, and I will stay in you. A branch cannot make fruit by itself. It must stay in the vine. You can't make fruit unless you stay in Me." "
I am the vine. You are the branches. The one who stays in Me and I in him makes lots of fruit. Without Me, you can't do anything.
If someone does not stay in Me, he is thrown out like a branch. He dries up. People pick up the dry branches and throw them in the fire. They burn.
If you stay in Me, and My words stay in you, ask for what you want. It will be done for you.
This makes My Father glad, because you make lots of fruit. Then you will be My followers." "
The Father loved Me. I loved you too. Stay in My love.
If you obey My rules, you will stay in My love. I obeyed My Father's rules, and I stay in His love.
I told you these things so My joy can be in you. Then your joy will be full.
This is My rule: Love each other like I loved you." "
No one has greater love than this. A person gives his life for his friends.
You are My friends if you do what I tell you.
I don't call you servants now. A servant doesn't know what his master is doing. I call you friends, because I told you everything I heard from My Father.
You didn't choose Me. I chose you. I put you here so you can go and make fruit. Your fruit will last. Then whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
I tell you these things so you love each other." "
If the world hates you, remember it hated Me first.
If you were from the world, the world would love you. But you are not from the world. I chose you out of the world. So the world hates you.
Remember what I told you: 'A worker is not greater than his master.' If they hurt Me, they will hurt you too. If they listened to My words, they will listen to yours too.
But they will do all these things to you because of My name. They don't know the One who sent Me." "
If I had not come and talked to them, they would not have sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
The one who hates Me hates My Father too.
If I had not done works among them that no one else did, they would not have sin. But now they have seen them, and they hate Me and My Father.
This happened so the words in their law would come true: 'They hated Me for no reason.'" "
When the Helper comes, I will send Him to you from the Father. He is the Spirit of truth. He comes from the Father. He will tell about Me.
You will tell about Me too, because you have been with Me from the start."
I have told you these things so you won't give up.
They will throw you out of your places of worship. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think they are helping God.
They will do these things because they don't know the Father or Me.
I have told you this so that when the time comes, you will remember I told you. I didn't tell you at first because I was with you.
But now I'm going to the One who sent Me. None of you asks Me, "Where are You going?"
Instead, you are sad because I said these things.
But I tell you the truth: It is good for you that I go away. If I don't go, the Helper won't come to you. But if I go, I will send Him to you.
When He comes, He will show the world it is wrong about sin, about God's right way, and about judgment.
He will show it is wrong about sin, because people don't believe in Me.
He will show it is wrong about God's right way, because I'm going to the Father, and you won't see Me anymore.
He will show it is wrong about judgment, because the ruler of this world has already been judged.
I still have many things to say to you, but you can't understand them now.
But when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. He won't speak on His own. He will speak what He hears and tell you what is coming.
He will make Me known, because He will take what is Mine and tell it to you.
Everything the Father has is Mine. That's why I said He takes what is Mine and tells it to you.
In a little while, you won't see Me. Then after a little while, you will see Me.
Some of His followers said to each other, "What does He mean by, 'In a little while, you won't see Me, and then after a little while, you will see Me'? And by, 'I'm going to the Father'?"
They kept asking, "What does 'a little while' mean? We don't know what He is saying."
Jesus knew they wanted to ask Him. So He said, "Are you asking each other about this? I said, 'In a little while, you won't see Me, and then after a little while, you will see Me.'
I tell you the truth: You will cry and be sad, but the world will be happy. You will be sad, but your sadness will turn into joy.
A woman has pain when she has a baby because her time has come. But when the baby is born, she forgets the pain because she is happy a person has come into the world.
So you have sadness now. But I will see you again, and your heart will be glad. No one will take your joy from you."
On that day, you won't ask Me anything. I tell you the truth: The Father will give you whatever you ask in My name.
Until now, you haven't asked for anything in My name. Ask, and you will get it, so your joy will be full.
I have told you these things in stories. A time is coming when I won't use stories anymore. I will speak clearly about the Father.
On that day, you will ask in My name. I'm not saying I will ask the Father for you.
The Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and believed I came from God.
I came from the Father into the world. Now I'm leaving the world and going to the Father.
His followers said, "Look, now You speak plainly! You are not using stories now.
Now we know You know everything. You don't need anyone to ask You questions. We believe You came from God."
Jesus answered them, "Do you believe now?
Look, a time is coming, and it is already here, when you will all run away. Each of you will go to your own home. You will leave Me alone. But I'm not alone, because the Father is with Me.
I told you these things so you can have peace in Me. In the world, you will have trouble. But be brave! I have beaten the world."
Jesus said these things. He looked up to heaven and said, “Father, the time has come. Make Your Son great, so Your Son can make You great.
You gave Him power over all people. He gives them life that lasts forever. He gives this life to all the people You gave Him.
This is the life that lasts forever: that they know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, the One You sent.
I made You great on earth. I finished the work You gave Me to do.
Now, Father, make Me great beside You. Give Me the greatness I had with You before the world began. “
I showed Your name to the people You gave Me from the world. They were Yours. You gave them to Me. They have kept Your word.
Now they know that everything You gave Me comes from You.
I gave them the words You gave Me. They took them and knew they were true. They knew I came from You. They believed You sent Me. “
I pray for them. I do not pray for the world. I pray for the ones You gave Me, because they are Yours.
All I have is Yours, and all You have is Mine. I am made great in them.
I am not in the world anymore, but they are in the world. I am coming to You, Holy Father. Keep them safe by Your name, the name You gave Me. Keep them together as one, just like We are one.
While I was with them, I kept them and watched over them by Your name, the name You gave Me. None of them was lost, except the one who was set to be lost. This happened so God’s Word would come true.
Now I am coming to You. I say these things in the world so they can have My joy. I want their joy to be full. “
I gave them Your word. The world hated them, because they do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world.
I do not ask You to take them out of the world. I ask You to keep them safe from the evil one.
They do not belong to the world, just as I do not belong to the world. “
Make them holy by Your truth. Your word is truth.
You sent Me into the world. I also sent them into the world.
I set Myself apart for them, so they can be set apart by the truth. “
I do not pray for these alone. I also pray for those who will believe in Me through their words.
I pray that all of them may be one. Father, just as You are in Me, and I am in You, I pray that they may be in Us. Then the world will believe that You sent Me.
I gave them the greatness You gave Me. I did this so they may be one, just as We are one.
I am in them, and You are in Me. I pray they may be made complete as one. Then the world will know that You sent Me, and that You love them, just as You love Me. “
Father, I want the people You gave Me to be with Me where I am. I want them to see My greatness, the greatness You gave Me. You loved Me before the world began.
Good Father, the world did not know You. But I knew You, and these knew that You sent Me.
I made Your name known to them, and I will keep making it known. I do this so the love You have for Me may be in them, and I may be in them.”
After Jesus said these things, He went out with His followers. They crossed the Kidron Valley. There was a garden there. Jesus and His followers went into it.
Judas, who betrayed Him, knew the place. Jesus often met there with His followers.
Judas came there. He brought soldiers and guards from the top priests and religious leaders. They had lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Jesus knew all that was going to happen. He went out and said to them, "Who are you looking for?"
They answered, "Jesus of Nazareth." Jesus said, "I am He." Judas, who betrayed Him, was standing with them.
When Jesus said, "I am He," they stepped back. They fell to the ground.
He asked them again, "Who are you looking for?" They said, "Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus answered, "I told you that I am He. If you are looking for Me, let these men go."
This happened so Jesus' words would come true. He had said, "I have not lost one of those You gave Me."
Simon Peter had a sword. He pulled it out. He hit the top priest's servant. He cut off the servant's right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
Jesus said to Peter, "Put your sword away! Should I not accept the suffering the Father has given Me?"
Then the soldiers, the commander, and the Jewish guards arrested Jesus. They tied Him up.
They led Him first to Annas. Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas. Caiaphas was the top priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who told the Jewish leaders this. He said it was better for one man to die for the people.
Simon Peter and another follower went with Jesus. That follower knew the top priest. So he went with Jesus into the top priest's courtyard.
Peter stood outside by the door. The other follower knew the top priest. He came out. He spoke to the girl who watched the door. He brought Peter in.
The girl at the door said to Peter, "Aren't you one of this man's followers?" He said, "No, I am not."
It was cold. The servants and guards stood around a fire of coals. They warmed themselves. Peter also stood with them. He warmed himself.
The top priest asked Jesus about His followers and His teaching.
Jesus answered him, "I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in the meeting place and in the temple. All the Jews meet there. I said nothing in secret.
Why do you ask Me? Ask the people who heard Me. They know what I said."
When Jesus said this, one of the guards standing nearby hit Jesus. He said, "Is that how You answer the top priest?"
Jesus answered him, "If I said something wrong, tell what was wrong. But if I said what is right, why did You hit Me?"
Then Annas sent Him, still tied up, to Caiaphas the top priest.
Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said to him, "Aren't you one of His followers?" He denied it. He said, "No, I am not."
One of the top priest's servants was there. He was a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off. He said, "Didn't I see you with Him in the garden?"
Peter denied it again. Right away a rooster crowed.
They led Jesus from Caiaphas to the ruler's house. It was early morning. The Jewish leaders did not go into the house. They did not want to become unclean. They wanted to eat the Passover meal.
Pilate went out to them. He said, "What charge do you bring against this man?"
They answered, "If He were not a bad man, we would not have handed Him over to you."
Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves and judge Him by your law." The Jewish leaders said, "We are not allowed to put anyone to death."
This happened so Jesus' words would come true. It showed what kind of death He would die.
Pilate went back into the house. He called for Jesus. He asked Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?"
Jesus answered, "Are you asking this on your own? Or did others tell you about Me?"
Pilate answered, "Am I a Jew? Your own people and top priests handed You over to me. What have You done?"

Jesus answered, "My kingdom is not of this world. If My kingdom were of this world, My servants would fight. They would keep Me from being handed over to the Jewish leaders. But My kingdom is not from here."
Pilate said to Him, "So you are a king?" Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. I was born for this. I came into the world to tell the truth. Everyone who is from the truth listens to My voice."
Pilate said to Him, "What is truth?" Then he went out again to the Jewish leaders. He said, "I find no fault in Him."
Pilate said to them, "You have a custom. I release one prisoner for you at the Passover. Do you want me to release the King of the Jews for you?"
They shouted, "Not Him! Give us Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a robber.
Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him whipped.
The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown. They put it on His head. They put a purple robe on Him.
They came to Him again and again. They said, "Hello, King of the Jews!" They hit Him in the face.
Pilate went out again. He said to the Jews, "Look, I bring Him out to you. I want you to know I find no fault in Him."
Jesus came out wearing the thorn crown and purple robe. Pilate said, "Here is the man!"
When the chief priests and helpers saw Him, they shouted, "Crucify Him! Crucify Him!" Pilate said, "Take Him and crucify Him yourselves. I find no fault in Him."
The Jews answered, "We have a law. By that law He must die. He said He is the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid.
He went back into his office. He asked Jesus, "Where are You from?" Jesus did not answer.
Pilate said, "Won't You talk to me? Don't You know I have power to free You and power to kill You on a cross?"
Jesus answered, "You would have no power over Me if it were not given to you from above. So the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of a worse sin."
From then on, Pilate tried to free Him. But the Jews shouted, "If you free this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who says he is a king fights against Caesar."
When Pilate heard this, he brought Jesus out. He sat on the judge's seat. The place was called Stone Pavement. In Hebrew it is Gabbatha.
It was the day to get ready for Passover. It was about noon. Pilate said to the Jews, "Here is your King!"
They shouted, "Take Him away! Take Him away! Crucify Him!" Pilate said, "Should I crucify your King?" The chief priests answered, "We have no king but Caesar."
Then Pilate handed Him over to be killed on a cross. The soldiers took Jesus away.
Jesus carried His own cross. He went out to the Place of the Skull. In Hebrew it is called Golgotha.
There they nailed Him to a cross. Two other men were with Him. One was on each side. Jesus was in the middle.
Pilate wrote a sign. He put it on the cross. It said, "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews."
Many Jews read the sign. The place where Jesus was killed was near the city. The sign was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
The chief priests said to Pilate, "Do not write, 'The King of the Jews.' Write, 'He said, I am the King of the Jews.'"
Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."
When the soldiers nailed Jesus to the cross, they took His clothes. They made four parts. Each soldier got one part. They also took His long shirt. It had no seams. It was woven all in one piece.

They said to each other, "Let's not tear it. Let's throw dice to see who gets it." This happened to make God's Word come true. It says, "They split My clothes among them. They threw dice for My shirt." So the soldiers did this.
Near Jesus' cross stood His mother. His mother's sister stood there too. Mary, the wife of Clopas, stood there. Mary Magdalene stood there.
Jesus saw His mother. He saw the follower He loved standing near. He said to His mother, "Woman, here is your son."
Then He said to the follower, "Here is your mother." From that time, the follower took her into his home.
After this, Jesus knew everything was done. He said this to make God's Word come true: "I am thirsty."
A jar of sour wine was there. They soaked a sponge in the wine. They put it on a plant branch. They held it to His mouth.
When Jesus drank the sour wine, He said, "It is finished." Then He bowed His head. He gave up His spirit.

It was the day to get ready. The next day was a special Sabbath. The Jews did not want the bodies to stay on the crosses on the Sabbath. So they asked Pilate to break the men's legs and take them down.
The soldiers came. They broke the legs of the first man. They broke the legs of the other man too. Both were killed with Jesus.
But when they came to Jesus, they saw He was already dead. They did not break His legs.
Instead, one soldier poked His side with a spear. Blood and water came out right away.
The one who saw this has told about it. His story is true. He knows he tells the truth. He tells it so you may believe.
This happened to make God's Word come true: "None of His bones will be broken."
Another writing says, "They will look at the One they poked."

After this, Joseph from Arimathea asked Pilate for Jesus' body. Joseph was a follower of Jesus, but he kept it secret because he was afraid of the Jews. Pilate said yes. So Joseph came and took His body.
Nicodemus came too. He was the man who came to Jesus at night before. He brought about 75 pounds of sweet-smelling spices.
So they took Jesus' body. They wrapped it in cloth strips with spices. This is how the Jews bury their dead.
There was a garden where Jesus was killed. In the garden was a new tomb. No one had been put there yet.
Because it was the Jewish day to get ready, and the tomb was close, they put Jesus there.
Early on Sunday, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb. She saw that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb.
So she ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one Jesus loved. She said, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they put Him."
Peter and the other disciple went out and started for the tomb.
They both ran, but the other disciple ran faster than Peter and got there first.
He bent down and looked in. He saw the cloth strips lying there, but he did not go in.
Then Simon Peter came, following him. He went into the tomb and saw the cloth strips lying there.
He also saw the cloth that had been on His head. It was not with the other cloths. It was folded up by itself.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. He saw and believed.
They did not yet know that He had to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back home.
But Mary stood outside the tomb, crying. As she cried, she bent down to look into the tomb.
She saw two angels in white. They were sitting where His body had been. One was at the head, and one was at the feet.
The angels said to her, "Woman, why are you crying?" She said to them, "They took my Lord, and I do not know where they put Him."
After she said this, she turned around. She saw Jesus standing there, but she did not know it was Jesus.
Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for?" She thought He was the gardener. She said, "Sir, if you carried Him away, tell me where you put Him, and I will get Him."
Jesus said to her, "Mary." She turned and said in Hebrew, "Rabboni!" This means "Teacher."
Jesus said to her, "Do not hold on to Me. I have not yet gone up to the Father. But go to My brothers and tell them, 'I am going up to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.'"
Mary Magdalene went and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord. She also told them what He had said to her.
That evening, on Sunday, the disciples were together. The doors were locked because they were afraid of the Jews. Jesus came and stood among them. He said, "Peace be with you."
After He said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The disciples were glad when they saw the Lord.
Jesus said to them again, "Peace be with you. As the Father has sent Me, I am sending you."
After He said this, He breathed on them and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven. If you hold on to anyone's sins, they are not forgiven."
Thomas, also called the Twin, was one of the Twelve. He was not with them when Jesus came.
The other disciples told him, "We have seen the Lord." But he said, "Unless I see the nail holes in His hands and put my finger in the holes, and put my hand in His side, I will not believe."
A week later, the disciples were in the house again. The doors were locked. Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them. He said, "Peace be with you."
Then He said to Thomas, "Put your finger here. Look at My hands. Put your hand into My side. Stop doubting and believe."
Thomas answered Him, "My Lord and my God!"
Jesus said to him, "Because you have seen Me, you believe. Happy are the people who have not seen and still believe."
Jesus did many other miracles in front of His disciples. They are not written in this book.
But these things are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God. By believing, you will have life in His name.
After this, Jesus showed Himself again to His followers by the Sea of Tiberias. This is how He showed Himself:
Simon Peter, Thomas (called Didymus), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other followers were together.
Simon Peter said, “I am going fishing.” They said, “We will go with you.” They went out and got into the boat. But they caught nothing that night.
Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore. But the followers did not know it was Jesus.
Jesus said to them, “Children, do you have any fish?” They answered, “No.”
He said, “Throw your net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they threw it in. Now they could not pull the net in because there were so many fish.
The follower Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his coat, because he had taken it off. Then he jumped into the sea.
The other followers came in the boat. They pulled the net full of fish. They were not far from land, only about 100 yards away.
When they got to land, they saw a fire of hot coals. Fish was on it, and bread.
Jesus said, “Bring some of the fish you just caught.”
Simon Peter got into the boat and pulled the net to land. It was full of big fish, 153 of them. Even with so many, the net did not break.
Jesus said, “Come and eat breakfast.” None of the followers dared ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them. He did the same with the fish.
This was the third time Jesus showed Himself to His followers after He was raised from the dead.
After they ate, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?” Peter said, “Yes, Lord. You know I love You.” Jesus said, “Feed My lambs.”
Jesus said to him again, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” Peter said, “Yes, Lord. You know I love You.” Jesus said, “Take care of My sheep.”

A third time Jesus said, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was sad because Jesus asked him a third time, “Do you love Me?” Peter said, “Lord, You know everything. You know I love You.” Jesus said, “Feed My sheep.”

Jesus said, “I tell you the truth. When you were young, you put on your own clothes and went where you wanted. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands. Someone else will dress you and take you where you do not want to go.”
Jesus said this to show how Peter would die and honor God. Then He said, “Follow Me.”
Peter turned around. He saw the follower Jesus loved coming behind them. This was the one who had leaned on Jesus at dinner and asked, “Lord, who will turn against You?”
Peter saw him and said to Jesus, “Lord, what about him?”
Jesus said, “If I want him to stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow Me.”
So people said the follower would not die. But Jesus did not say he would not die. He said, “If I want him to stay until I come, what is that to you?”
This is the follower who tells about these things. He wrote them down. We know what he says is true.
Jesus did many other things too. If all of them were written down, one by one, I think the whole world would not have room for the books.
Dear Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about all the things Jesus began to do and teach.
He kept teaching until the day He was taken up to heaven. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, He told the apostles He had chosen what to do.
After He suffered, He showed Himself alive to them in many ways. For forty days He appeared to them and talked about God's kingdom.
While He was eating with them, He told them not to leave Jerusalem. He said, "Wait for what the Father promised. You heard Me talk about it."
John baptized with water, but in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
So they asked Him, "Lord, are you going to make Israel a kingdom again now?"
He said to them, "It is not for you to know the times or dates the Father set by His own power.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you. Then you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth."
After He said this, He was lifted up while they watched. A cloud hid Him from their sight.
They were looking up into the sky as He went. Suddenly two men in white clothes stood by them.
They said, "Men of Galilee, why are you standing here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you saw Him go."
Then they went back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives. It was near Jerusalem, not far away.

When they arrived, they went upstairs to the room where they were staying. Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James were there.
They all prayed together. The women were there too, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and His brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the believers. There were about 120 people. He said,
"Brothers, the Holy Spirit said through David long ago that this had to happen. David spoke about Judas, who led the men who arrested Jesus.
He was one of us. He shared in this work.
He used the money he got for his wrong to buy a field. He fell headfirst, his body broke open, and his insides spilled out.
Everyone in Jerusalem heard about it. They called the field in their own language Akeldama, which means Field of Blood. "
For it is written in the book of Psalms: 'Let his home be empty. Let no one live in it.' And, 'Let someone else take his job.'
So we need to choose one of the men who were with us the whole time the Lord Jesus was with us.
He was with us from John's baptism until the day He was taken up to heaven. This man must be a witness with us that Jesus rose from the dead."
They put forward two men: Joseph called Barsabbas (also called Justus) and Matthias.
They prayed, "Lord, You know everyone's heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen
to take this job as an apostle, since Judas left it to go where he belonged."
They cast lots, and Matthias was chosen. So he was added to the eleven apostles.
On the day called Pentecost, they were all together in one place.
Suddenly a sound like a strong wind came from heaven. It filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw what looked like flames of fire. The flames separated and rested on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit. They began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit helped them.
Jews who worshiped God were living in Jerusalem. They came from every nation under heaven.
When this sound happened, a large crowd came together. The people were confused because each person heard them speaking in their own language.
They were amazed. They asked, "Aren't all these speakers from Galilee?
Then how is it that each of us hears them in our own language?
We are Parthians, Medes, and Elamites. Some of us live in Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia.
Some live in Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near Cyrene. Some of us are visitors from Rome.
We are Jews and people who turned to the Jewish faith. We are Cretans and Arabs. We hear them telling the great things God has done, and they are using our own languages!"
They were all amazed and confused. They asked each other, "What does this mean?"
But others made fun of them. They said, "They have had too much new wine!"
Then Peter stood up with the eleven apostles. He raised his voice and spoke to them: "Men of Judea and all who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you. Listen to my words.
These men are not drunk, as you think. It is only nine in the morning!
No, this is what the prophet Joel said: "
'In the last days, God says, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will speak God's message. Your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
In those days I will pour out My Spirit on My servants, both men and women, and they will speak God's message.
I will show wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below: blood, fire, and smoke.
The sun will turn dark, and the moon will turn to blood, before the great and wonderful day of the Lord comes.
And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.' "

People of Israel, listen to this: Jesus of Nazareth was a man God sent to you. God showed who He was by miracles, wonders, and signs. God did these things among you through Him, as you yourselves know.
God planned this and knew it ahead of time. Yet you handed Him over, and sinful men killed Him by nailing Him to a cross.
But God raised Him from the dead. He set Him free from the pain of death, because death could not hold Him. "
David said about Him: 'I saw the Lord always before me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
So my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices. My body will also rest in hope.
You will not leave me in the grave. You will not let Your Holy One rot.
You have shown me the paths of life. You will fill me with joy in Your presence.' "
Brothers, I can tell you plainly that David died and was buried. His tomb is still here with us today.
He was a prophet. He knew God had promised him that a child from his family would sit on his throne.
He saw what was coming. He spoke about the Christ being raised from the dead. He said the Christ would not be left in the grave, and His body would not rot.
God raised this Jesus to life. We are all witnesses of this.
God lifted Him up to His right hand. He received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father. He has poured out what you now see and hear.
David did not go up to heaven. But he said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "
Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your control."'
So let all the people of Israel know for sure: God made this Jesus, whom you killed on a cross, both Lord and Christ."
When they heard this, they were deeply moved. They asked Peter and the other apostles, "Brothers, what should we do?"
Peter said to them, "Turn from your sins and be baptized, each of you, in the name of Jesus Christ. Then your sins will be forgiven, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
This promise is for you and your children. It is also for all who are far away, for everyone the Lord our God calls to Himself."
With many other words he warned them and begged them, "Save yourselves from these sinful people."
Those who accepted his message were baptized. About three thousand people joined them that day.
They stayed faithful to the apostles' teaching. They spent time together, broke bread, and prayed.
Everyone felt awe. The apostles did many wonders and signs.
All the believers were together and shared everything they had.
They sold their land and belongings. They gave the money to anyone who needed it.
Every day they met together in the temple. They broke bread in their homes and ate with glad and honest hearts.
They praised God and were liked by all the people. The Lord added to their group every day those who were being saved.
One day Peter and John went to the temple to pray at three in the afternoon.
A man who could not walk since he was born was carried to the temple gate called Beautiful. People put him there every day to beg from those going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to go in, he asked them for money.
Peter and John looked at him and said, "Look at us!"
So the man looked at them. He thought he would get something from them.
But Peter said, "I don't have silver or gold. But what I have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ from Nazareth, get up and walk!"
Peter took him by the right hand and helped him up. Right away his feet and ankles became strong.
He jumped up and stood. Then he began to walk. He went into the temple with them, walking and jumping and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God.
They knew he was the man who used to sit and beg at the Beautiful Gate. They were full of wonder and surprise at what had happened to him.
The man who was healed held on to Peter and John. All the people were amazed. They ran to them in the part of the temple called Solomon's Porch. "
Men of Israel, why are you amazed at this? Why do you stare at us? It was not by our own power or goodness that this man walks.
The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has honored His Servant Jesus. You handed Him over and said no to Him in front of Pilate, even though Pilate wanted to let Him go. "
You said no to the Holy and Good One. You asked for a killer to be set free for you.
You killed the One who gives life. But God raised Him from the dead. We saw it happen. "
This man you see and know was made strong by faith in His name. It is the name of Jesus and faith that comes through Him that gave him this full healing in front of your eyes. "
Now, brothers, I know you did this without knowing. Your leaders did too.
But this is how God kept His word. He said long ago through all the prophets that His Christ would suffer. "
So change your hearts and turn to God. Then your sins will be wiped away.
Times of rest will come from the Lord. He will send Jesus, the Christ He chose for you.
Jesus must stay in heaven until the time comes for God to make all things new. God promised this long ago through His holy prophets. "
Moses said that the Lord your God will raise up for you a Prophet like Moses from among your own people. You must listen to Him in everything He tells you.
Anyone who does not listen to this Prophet will be cut off from his people. "
All the prophets from Samuel on spoke about these days.
You are children of the prophets. You share in the promise God made with your fathers. God said to Abraham that through his family all the families of the earth will be blessed. "
God raised up His Servant and sent Him first to you. He sent Him to bless you by turning each of you from your evil ways."
Peter and John were talking to the people. The priests, the temple guard leader, and the Sadducees came to them.
They were upset because Peter and John taught the people. They also said that Jesus rose from the dead.
They grabbed Peter and John and put them in jail until the next day. It was already evening.
But many people who heard the message believed. The number of men grew to about 5,000.
The next day, the rulers, elders, and teachers of the law met in Jerusalem.
Annas the high priest was there. Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and others from the high priest’s family were there too.
They made Peter and John stand in the middle. They asked, “By what power or by what name did you do this?”
Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit. He said to them, “Leaders and elders of the people,
today we are being checked because we did a good thing for a sick man. You want to know how he was healed.

Let all of you and all of Israel know this. This man stands healthy in front of you. He was healed by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. You nailed Him to a cross. But God raised Him from the dead.
Jesus is the stone that you builders did not want. Now He is the most important stone.
No one else can save us. There is no other name that God has given to people. We must be saved by Jesus.”
The leaders saw that Peter and John were brave. They also saw that Peter and John were not trained in school. They were amazed. They knew Peter and John had been with Jesus.
They saw the healed man standing with them. They could not say anything against them.
The leaders told Peter and John to leave the meeting. Then the leaders talked with each other.
They said, “What should we do with these men? Everyone in Jerusalem knows they did a big miracle. We cannot say it did not happen.
But we do not want this to spread to more people. Let us warn them not to talk to anyone using that name.”
They called Peter and John back in. They told them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Peter and John answered them, “You decide if it is right for us to listen to you instead of God.
We cannot stop talking about what we saw and heard.”
The leaders threatened them more. Then they let them go. They could not punish them because the people praised God for what happened.
The man who was healed was more than 40 years old.
Peter and John went back to their own people. They told them what the high priests and elders said.
When the believers heard this, they prayed to God together. They said, “Lord and Master, You made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
You spoke through Your servant David by the Holy Spirit. David said, ‘Why do the nations get angry? Why do the people make useless plans?
The kings of the earth stand ready. The rulers join together against the LORD and against His Christ.’
In this city, Herod and Pontius Pilate joined with the non-Jewish people and the people of Israel. They stood against Your holy servant Jesus, whom You chose to be the Christ.
They did what Your hand and Your plan had already decided would happen.
Now, Lord, look at their threats. Give Your servants power to speak Your word bravely.
Stretch out Your hand to heal people. Do signs and wonders through the name of Your holy servant Jesus.”
After they prayed, the place where they were meeting shook. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit. They spoke God’s word bravely.
The group of believers were of one heart and mind. No one said that their things were their own. They shared everything.
The apostles told people about the rising of the Lord Jesus with great power. God’s grace was on all of them.
There were no poor people among them. People who owned land or houses sold them. They brought the money from the sales.
They put the money at the apostles’ feet. Then it was given to each person who needed it.
Joseph was a Levite from Cyprus. The apostles called him Barnabas. That name means “son who gives comfort.”
He sold a field he owned. He brought the money and put it at the apostles’ feet.
Now a man named Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold some land.
His wife knew about it. He kept back part of the money. He brought only part of it and put it at the apostles' feet.
Peter said, "Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart? You lied to the Holy Spirit. You kept back part of the money from the land.
Before it was sold, was it not yours? After it was sold, was the money not yours to use? Why did you plan this in your heart? You did not lie to people. You lied to God."
When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. Great fear came on everyone who heard it.
The young men got up, wrapped him, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later, his wife came in. She did not know what had happened.
Peter asked her, "Tell me, did you sell the land for this much?" She said, "Yes, for that much."
Peter said to her, "Why did you two agree to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look! The men who buried your husband are at the door. They will carry you out too."
Right away she fell at his feet and died. The young men came in and found her dead. They carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came on the whole church and on everyone who heard these things.
The apostles did many amazing miracles among the people. All the believers were together in Solomon's Porch.
The people praised them, but no one else dared to join them.
More and more men and women believed and joined the Lord.
People brought sick people into the streets. They laid them on beds and mats. They hoped even Peter's shadow would fall on some of them as he walked by.
Crowds came from the towns around Jerusalem. They brought sick people and people bothered by evil spirits. All of them were healed.
The high priest and all his friends, who were Sadducees, became very jealous. They got up
and grabbed the apostles. They put them in the public jail.
But at night an angel of the Lord opened the jail doors and led them out.
The angel said, "Go and stand in the temple. Tell the people all the words of this life."
At daybreak they went into the temple and taught. The high priest and his friends came. They called the council and all the elders of Israel. They sent to the jail to bring the apostles.
The officers went to the jail, but they did not find them. They went back and reported,
"We found the jail locked tight. The guards were standing at the doors. But when we opened it, no one was inside."
The temple guard and the chief priests heard this. They did not know what to think.
Someone came and told them, "Look! The men you put in jail are standing in the temple and teaching the people."
Then the temple guard went with the officers. They brought the apostles without force. They were afraid the people might throw stones at them.
They brought them and stood them before the council. The high priest asked them,
"We told you not to teach in this name. But you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching. You want to blame us for this man's death."
Peter and the apostles answered, "We must obey God instead of people.
The God of our fathers raised Jesus. You killed Him by hanging Him on a tree.
God lifted Him up to His right hand. He made Him Leader and Savior. He gives people a chance to turn from sin and have their sins forgiven. He gives this to Israel.
We tell what we have seen and heard. The Holy Spirit does too. God gave Him to people who obey Him."
When they heard this, they were very angry. They wanted to kill the apostles.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up in the council. He was a teacher of the law. All the people respected him. He told the men to go outside for a little while.
He said to them, "Men of Israel, be careful. Think about what you are about to do to these men.
Before now, Theudas rose up. He said he was someone important. About four hundred men joined him. He was killed. All who followed him scattered. They did not amount to anything.
After him, Judas the Galilean rose up. This was when the people were counted. He led people away after him. He died too. All who followed him scattered.
So now I tell you: Leave these men alone. Let them go. If this plan or work comes from people, it will fall apart.
But if it comes from God, you cannot stop it. You might even be found fighting against God."
They listened to him. They called the apostles in. They beat them. They told them not to speak in the name of Jesus. Then they let them go.
The apostles left the council. They were happy to suffer shame for the Name.
Every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not stop. They taught and preached that Jesus is the Christ.
In those days, more and more people became followers. The Greek-speaking followers were upset with the Hebrew-speaking followers. They said the widows were left out when food was given out each day.
The twelve called all the followers together. They said, "It is not right for us to stop teaching God's word so we can serve food.
Brothers, pick seven men from among you. They should be known as men full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will put them in charge of this work.
We will keep praying and teaching God's word."

This pleased everyone. They chose Stephen. He was full of faith and the Holy Spirit. They also chose Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas. Nicolas was from Antioch and had become a follower.
They brought these men to the apostles. The apostles prayed and put their hands on them.
God's word grew. Many more people in Jerusalem became followers. Many priests also believed.
Stephen was full of God's kindness and power. He did great miracles among the people.
Some men from the meeting place of the freed slaves stood up. Other men from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia stood up too. They argued with Stephen.
But they could not beat his wisdom and the Spirit that helped him speak.
Then they secretly found men to say, "We heard him speak bad words against Moses and God."
They made the people, the elders, and the teachers of the law angry. They rushed up, grabbed Stephen, and took him to the council.
They brought false witnesses. The witnesses said, "This man never stops speaking against this holy place and the law.
We heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses gave us."
Everyone in the council looked at Stephen. They saw his face looked like an angel's face.
The high priest asked Stephen, "Are these things true?"
Stephen said, "Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory showed Himself to our father Abraham. This was in Mesopotamia, before Abraham lived in Haran."
God said, "Leave your country and your family. Go to the land I will show you."
Stephen said, "So Abraham left the land of Chaldea and lived in Haran. After his father died, God moved him to this land, where you live now."
God did not give him any land here. He did not even get a small piece of ground. But God promised to give the land to him and to his children after him. Abraham had no child yet.
God said, "Your children will live in a foreign land. They will be slaves and be treated badly for 400 years."
God said, "I will judge the nation they serve. After that, they will come out and worship Me in this place."
Stephen said, "God gave Abraham the agreement of circumcision. Then Abraham had Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac had Jacob. Jacob had the twelve family leaders."
Stephen said, "The family leaders were jealous of Joseph. They sold him to Egypt. But God was with Joseph."
God saved him from all his troubles. God gave him grace and wisdom before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Pharaoh made Joseph ruler over Egypt and over his whole house.
A big famine and much trouble came over Egypt and Canaan. Our fathers could not find food.
Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt. He sent our fathers there first.
The second time, Joseph made himself known to his brothers. Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.
Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his family. There were 75 people.
Jacob went down to Egypt. He and our fathers died there.
Their bodies were moved to Shechem. They were buried in the tomb that Abraham bought from the sons of Hamor in Shechem. He paid silver for it.
The time was getting close for God's promise to Abraham. The people in Egypt grew and became many.
Then a new king came to power in Egypt. He did not know Joseph.
He tricked our people. He was cruel to our fathers. He made them leave their baby boys outside so they would die.
Stephen said, "At that time Moses was born. He was a beautiful child to God. He was cared for in his father's house for three months."
When he was put outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him. She raised him as her own son.
Moses learned all the wisdom of the Egyptians. He was strong in what he said and did.
When he was 40 years old, he decided to visit his brothers, the people of Israel.
He saw an Israelite being wronged. Moses defended him and punished the Egyptian by hitting him.
Moses thought his brothers would understand that God was giving them freedom through him. But they did not understand.
The next day he saw two of them fighting. He tried to make peace. He said, "Men, you are brothers. Why are you hurting each other?"
The man who was wronging his neighbor pushed Moses away. He said, "Who made you our ruler and judge?
Do you want to kill me the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?"
Stephen said, "When Moses heard this, he ran away to Midian. He lived there as a stranger. He had two sons."
After 40 years, an angel appeared to him in a burning bush. This was in the wilderness near Mount Sinai.
Moses saw it and was amazed. When he went to look, the voice of the LORD came to him.
God said, "I am the God of your fathers. I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." Moses was so afraid that he did not dare to look.
The LORD said, "Take off your sandals. The place where you are standing is holy ground."
He said, "I have seen how My people suffer in Egypt. I have heard their groaning. I have come down to set them free. Now come, I am sending you to Egypt."
Stephen said, "This is the Moses they refused. They said, 'Who made you our ruler and judge?' But God sent him as ruler and rescuer, with the angel who appeared to him in the bush."
He led them out. He did wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for 40 years in the wilderness.
Stephen said, "This is Moses, who said to the people of Israel, 'God will raise up a prophet for you like me. He will come from your own brothers.'"
This is the man who was with our people in the desert. He was with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai. He received living words to give to us.
Our fathers did not want to obey him. They pushed him away. In their hearts they turned back to Egypt.
Stephen said, "They said to Aaron, 'Make us gods to go before us. We do not know what happened to Moses, who led us out of Egypt.'"
So in those days they made a calf. They offered a sacrifice to the idol. They were happy with what their hands had made.

Stephen said, "But God turned away from them. He let them worship the stars in the sky. This is what the prophets wrote: 'Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings for 40 years in the wilderness, O people of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan. You made these images to worship them. I will send you beyond Babylon.'"
Stephen said, "Our fathers had the tent of witness in the wilderness. They made it just as God told Moses. They followed the pattern Moses had seen.
