Our fathers brought it with Joshua when they took the land from the nations God drove out before them. They used it until the time of David.
David found favor with God. He asked to find a home for the God of Jacob.
But Solomon built a house for God."

Stephen said, "But the Most High does not live in houses made by hands. The prophet says, 'Heaven is My throne. The earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me? says the LORD. Where is the place where I can rest?
Did not My hand make all these things?'"
Stephen said, "You are stubborn people. Your hearts and ears are not right with God. You always fight against the Holy Spirit, just like your fathers did.
Which prophet did your fathers not hurt? They killed the men who told about the coming of the Righteous One. Now you have become traitors and murderers.
You received God's law, which angels gave, but you did not obey it."
When they heard this, they were very angry. They ground their teeth at him.
Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit. He looked up to heaven and saw God's glory. He saw Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Stephen said, "Look! I see heaven open. I see the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
They covered their ears and shouted loudly. They all rushed at him.
They dragged him out of the city and threw stones at him. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They stoned Stephen as he called out, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
Stephen knelt down and cried out loudly, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." Then he died.
Saul was glad Stephen died. That day, people hurt the church in Jerusalem very much. All the believers, except the apostles, ran away to towns in Judea and Samaria.
Good men carried Stephen and cried loudly for him.
Saul tried to ruin the church. He went into homes. He dragged out men and women. He put them in jail.
The believers who ran away told people the good news as they went.
Philip went down to a city in Samaria. He told the people about Christ.
The crowds listened to Philip. They heard his words and saw the signs he did.
Bad spirits cried out loud and left many people. Many who could not walk or move were healed.
The whole city was very happy.
A man named Simon had done magic in that city. He amazed the people of Samaria. He said he was a great man.
Everyone, from small to big, listened to him. They said, "This man is God's power. People call it Great."
They listened to him because his magic had amazed them for a long time.
But when the people believed Philip's good news about God's kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, men and women were baptized.
Simon believed too. He was baptized. He stayed close to Philip. He was amazed when he saw the big signs and powerful things Philip did.
The apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted God's word. They sent Peter and John to them.
Peter and John came down and prayed for the people. They prayed that the people would receive the Holy Spirit.
The Holy Spirit had not yet come on any of them. They had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John put their hands on them. The people received the Holy Spirit.
Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given when the apostles put their hands on people. He offered them money.
He said, "Give me this power too. Then anyone I put my hands on will receive the Holy Spirit."
Peter said to him, "May your money be lost with you! You thought you could buy God's gift with money.
You have no part in this. Your heart is not right with God.
So turn away from your bad ways. Pray to the Lord. Maybe He will forgive the bad thoughts in your heart.
I see that you are full of bitter anger. You are trapped in wrong."
Simon answered, "Pray to the Lord for me. Ask Him that none of the bad things you said will happen to me."
After Peter and John told people about the Lord and spoke God's word, they went back to Jerusalem. On the way, they told the good news in many Samaritan towns.
An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip. He said, "Get up and go south. Take the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. It is a desert road."

So Philip got up and went. He saw a man from Ethiopia. The man was an important worker. He worked for Candace, the queen of Ethiopia. He was in charge of all her money. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship.
Now he was going home. He sat in his chariot and read from the book of Isaiah the prophet.
The Holy Spirit said to Philip, "Go to that chariot and stay near it."
Philip ran to the chariot. He heard the man reading from Isaiah the prophet. He asked, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
The man said, "How can I understand unless someone shows me the way?" Then he asked Philip to get in and sit with him.
The part he was reading said, "He was led like a sheep to be killed. He was quiet like a lamb before the one who cuts its wool. He did not open His mouth.
When He was hurt, no one was fair to Him. Who can tell about His family? His life was taken from the earth."
The official asked Philip, "Who is the prophet talking about? Is it about himself or someone else?"
Then Philip began with that part of the Bible. He told the man the good news about Jesus.
As they traveled down the road, they came to some water. The official said, "Look! There is water. What stops me from being baptized?"
He told the chariot to stop. Both Philip and the official got down into the water. Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord took Philip away. The official did not see him again. The official went on his way, happy.
Philip was found in the city of Azotus. He traveled through and told the good news in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
Saul was still very angry. He wanted to hurt the Lord's followers. He went to the high priest.
He asked for letters to the Jewish meeting houses in Damascus. The letters would let him take any men or women who followed the Way. He would tie them up and bring them to Jerusalem.
On the way to Damascus, a bright light from heaven suddenly shone around him.
He fell to the ground. He heard a voice say, "Saul, Saul, why do you hurt Me?"
Saul asked, "Who are You, Lord?" The voice said, "I am Jesus. You are hurting Me.
Get up and go into the city. Someone will tell you what to do."
The men with Saul stood still. They heard the voice, but they saw no one.
Saul got up. His eyes were open, but he could not see. They led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he could not see. He did not eat or drink.
In Damascus there was a follower named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision. The Lord said, "Ananias!" Ananias said, "Here I am, Lord."
The Lord said, "Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street. Ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying.
In a vision he saw a man named Ananias come in and put his hands on him. Then he could see again."
Ananias said, "Lord, I have heard many bad things about this man. He hurt Your holy people in Jerusalem.
He came here with power from the chief priests. He wants to tie up everyone who calls on Your name."
The Lord said, "Go. This man is My chosen tool. He will tell My name to people of other nations, to kings, and to the people of Israel.
I will show him how much he must suffer for My name."

Ananias went to the house. He went in. He put his hands on Saul. He said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus appeared to you on the road. He sent me so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
Right away something like scales fell from Saul's eyes. He could see again. He got up and was baptized.
After he ate some food, Saul got strong again. He stayed with the followers in Damascus for a few days.
Then he began to preach in the Jewish meeting houses. He said that Jesus is the Son of God.
The people who heard him were surprised. They said, "Isn't this the man who hurt people in Jerusalem who call on this name? Didn't he come here to take them to the chief priests?"
But Saul became stronger and stronger. He confused the Jews who lived in Damascus. He proved that Jesus is the Christ.
After many days, the Jews made a plan to kill Saul.
Saul learned about the plan. They watched the city gates day and night to kill him.
But at night his followers put him in a basket. They lowered him through a hole in the wall.
Saul went to Jerusalem. He tried to join the followers. But they were all afraid of him. They did not believe he was a follower.
Barnabas took him to the apostles. He told them how Saul saw the Lord on the road. He told how the Lord spoke to him. He told how Saul spoke bravely in Damascus in the name of Jesus.
Saul stayed with them. He went in and out of Jerusalem. He spoke boldly in the name of the Lord.
He talked and argued with the Greek-speaking Jews. They tried to kill him.
When the believers found out, they took him to Caesarea. Then they sent him to Tarsus.
The church in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace. It was built up. It grew in number. The people lived in fear of the Lord. The Holy Spirit gave them comfort.
Peter traveled around. He went to visit the Lord's people in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas. Aeneas could not walk. He had stayed in bed for eight years.
Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed." Right away Aeneas got up.
All the people in Lydda and Sharon saw him. They turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a follower named Tabitha. In Greek her name was Dorcas. She did many good things and helped poor people.
About that time she got sick and died. The people washed her body. They put her in an upstairs room.
Lydda was near Joppa. The followers heard that Peter was there. They sent two men to him. They asked him, "Please come to us right away."
Peter went with them. When he arrived, they took him upstairs. All the widows stood around him. They were crying. They showed him the coats and clothes Dorcas had made.
Peter sent everyone out of the room. He knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes. She saw Peter. She sat up.
He took her hand and helped her stand. Then he called the believers and the widows. He showed them that she was alive.
News of this spread all over Joppa. Many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for many days. He stayed with Simon, a man who worked with animal skins.
In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius. He was an army officer in the Italian group.
He and his whole family worshiped God and respected Him. He gave many gifts to the people. He prayed to God all the time.
One day, about three in the afternoon, he saw an angel from God in a vision. The angel came to him and said, "Cornelius."
Cornelius looked at the angel. He was scared. He said, "What is it, Lord?" The angel said, "Your prayers and your gifts have come up to God. He remembers them.
"Now send men to Joppa. Bring back a man named Simon. People call him Peter.
"He is staying with another Simon. That Simon works with leather. His house is by the sea."
When the angel finished talking, Cornelius called two of his servants and one soldier who loved God. The soldier stayed close to him.
Cornelius told them everything. Then he sent them to Joppa.
The next day, the men were near the city. Peter went up on the roof to pray.
He was hungry and wanted to eat. While they made food ready, he had a vision.
He saw heaven open. Something like a big sheet came down. It was held by four corners and lowered to the ground.
In it were all kinds of animals with four feet. There were also things that crawl on the ground and birds from the sky.
A voice said to him, "Get up, Peter. Kill and eat."
Peter said, "No, Lord! I have never eaten anything that is not allowed or unclean."
The voice said to him again, "Do not call unclean what God has made clean."
This happened three times. Then the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
Peter was wondering what the vision meant. Just then, the men from Cornelius reached Simon's house. They stood at the gate.
They called out and asked if Simon, called Peter, was staying there.
Peter was still thinking about the vision. The Holy Spirit said to him, "Look, three men are looking for you.
"Get up, go down, and go with them. Do not doubt. I sent them."
Peter went down to the men. He said, "Look, I am the one you are looking for. Why are you here?"

They said, "Cornelius is an army officer. He does what is right and respects God. All the Jewish people speak well of him. A holy angel told him to send for you. He wants you to come to his house and hear your words."
Peter invited them in and let them stay. The next day he got up and went with them. Some brothers from Joppa went too.
The next day they came to Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them. He had called his family and close friends together.
When Peter was about to go in, Cornelius met him. He fell at Peter's feet and worshiped him.
Peter lifted him up. He said, "Stand up. I am a man too."
They talked together. Then Peter went in. He saw many people gathered there.
He said to them, "You know it is against our law for a Jewish man to be close to a person from another nation. But God showed me that I should not call any person common or unclean.
"So when you sent for me, I came without arguing. Now tell me, why did you send for me?"
Cornelius said, "Four days ago I was in my house praying. It was about this same hour, the ninth hour. Then a man in bright clothes stood in front of me.
"He said, 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard. Your gifts are remembered before God.
"'Send to Joppa and call for Simon, called Peter. He is staying in the house of Simon the leather worker by the sea.'
"So I sent for you right away. You did well to come. Now we are all here before God. We want to hear everything the Lord has told you to say."
Then Peter spoke. He said, "I now see that God treats everyone the same.
"In every nation, the person who respects Him and does what is right is accepted by Him.
"God sent His word to the people of Israel. He told them the good news of peace through Jesus Christ. Jesus is Lord of all.
"You know the message that spread through all Judea. It started in Galilee after John preached about baptism.
"You know how God poured His Holy Spirit and power on Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus went around doing good. He healed all the people the devil had hurt. God was with Him.
"We are witnesses of everything He did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed Him by hanging Him on a tree.
"God raised Him on the third day. God let Him be seen.
"He was not seen by all the people. He was seen by witnesses God chose ahead of time. We are those witnesses. We ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
"He told us to preach to the people. He told us to say that Jesus is the One God chose to judge the living and the dead.
"All the prophets say this about Him: Everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name."
While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit came down on all who heard the message.
The Jewish believers who came with Peter were amazed. The gift of the Holy Spirit was poured out on people from other nations too.
They heard them speaking in different languages and praising God. Then Peter said,
"Can anyone stop these people from being baptized with water? They received the Holy Spirit just like we did."
Peter told them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.
The apostles and the brothers in Judea heard that people who were not Jews had accepted God's word.
When Peter went to Jerusalem, some Jewish believers argued with him.
They said, "You went into the homes of men who were not circumcised and ate with them."
Peter began to explain. He said, "I was in the city of Joppa. I was praying.
I saw a vision. A big sheet came down from heaven. It was held by four corners. It came close to me.
I looked at it. I saw animals, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds.
"I heard a voice say, 'Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.'
I said, 'No, Lord! Nothing dirty or unclean has ever gone into my mouth.'
The voice from heaven answered, 'Do not call unclean what God has made clean.'
This happened three times. Then everything went back up to heaven.
"Right then, three men from Caesarea came to the house where we were.
The Spirit told me to go with them and not doubt. Six brothers came with me. We went into the man's house.
"He told us how he saw an angel standing in his house. The angel said, 'Send to Joppa and bring Simon, who is called Peter.
He will tell you words that will save you and your whole family.'
"As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came on them, just like He came on us at first.
Then I remembered what the Lord had said: 'John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to stop God?"
When they heard this, they became quiet. They praised God. They said, "Then God has given even the people who are not Jews a chance to turn to Him and live."
Some believers had been scattered because of the trouble after Stephen died. They traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They told God's word only to Jews.
But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene. They came to Antioch and spoke to Greek-speaking people. They told them the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord's power was with them. Many people believed and turned to the Lord.
The church in Jerusalem heard about this. They sent Barnabas to Antioch.
He came and saw God's grace. He was glad. He told everyone to stay true to the Lord with all your heart.
Barnabas was a good man. He was full of the Holy Spirit and faith. Many people were added to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to find Saul.
He found him and brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met with the church. They taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
In those days, some prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them was Agabus. He stood up and, through the Spirit, said a big famine would come over the whole world. This happened during the time of Claudius.
The disciples decided that each one would send help to the brothers living in Judea.
They did this. They sent the gift to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
About that time, King Herod began to hurt some people in the church.
He killed James, John's brother, with a sword.
When Herod saw that this pleased the Jews, he also arrested Peter. This was during the feast when people ate bread with no yeast.
After he caught Peter, he put him in prison. He gave him to four groups of four soldiers to guard him. He planned to bring Peter out to the people after the Passover feast.
So Peter was kept in prison. But the church prayed hard to God for him.
The night before Herod was going to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers. He was tied with two chains. Guards watched the door.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood there. A light shone in the room. The angel hit Peter on the side and woke him up. He said, "Get up fast!" The chains fell off Peter's hands.
"Put on your belt and sandals," the angel said. Peter did. "Put on your coat and follow me," he said.
Peter followed him out. He did not know it was really happening. He thought he was seeing a vision.
They passed the first and second guards. They came to the iron gate that led to the city. It opened by itself. They went out and walked down one street. Then the angel left him.
Then Peter knew it was real. He said, "Now I know for sure that the Lord sent His angel. He saved me from Herod's hand and from what the Jewish people hoped would happen."
When he understood this, he went to Mary's house. She was the mother of John, also called Mark. Many people were gathered there and were praying.
He knocked at the gate. A servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
She knew Peter's voice. She was so happy that she did not open the gate. Instead, she ran in and said Peter was standing at the gate.
"You are crazy!" they said to her. But she kept saying it was true. They said, "It must be his angel."
But Peter kept knocking. When they opened the door, they saw him and were amazed.

Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet. He told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. "Tell these things to James and the brothers," he said. Then he left and went to another place.
When morning came, the soldiers were very upset. They did not know what had happened to Peter.
Herod looked for him but could not find him. He questioned the guards and had them killed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

Herod was angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him together. They won over Blastus, the king's trusted helper. They asked for peace, because their land got food from the king's country.
On the set day, Herod put on royal clothes, sat on his throne, and gave a speech to them.
The people shouted, "This is the voice of a god, not a man!"
Right away an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give God the glory. He was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of God kept growing and spreading.
Barnabas and Saul finished their work and went back to Jerusalem. They took John, called Mark, with them.
In the church at Antioch, there were prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon (called Niger), Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen (who grew up with Herod the ruler), and Saul.
While they worshiped the Lord and went without food, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart Barnabas and Saul for Me. I have called them to do My work.”
Then they went without food and prayed. They put their hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them out.
So the Holy Spirit sent them out. They went down to Seleucia. Then they sailed to Cyprus.
When they came to Salamis, they told God's message in the Jewish meeting places. John helped them.
They went all over the island to Paphos. There they met a Jewish man who used magic. He was a false prophet named Bar-Jesus.
He was with Sergius Paulus, the Roman leader. Sergius was a wise man. He sent for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God's message.
But Elymas the magician (that is what his name means) tried to stop them. He wanted to turn the Roman leader away from believing.
But Saul, also called Paul, was full of the Holy Spirit. He looked hard at Elymas.
Paul said, “You son of the devil! You hate what is right. You are full of tricks and bad plans. Will you never stop twisting the Lord's right ways?”
“Now the Lord's hand is on you. For a while, you will be blind and not see the sun.” Right then, a dark mist came over Elymas. He walked around looking for someone to lead him by the hand.
The Roman leader believed when he saw what happened. He was amazed at the Lord's teaching.
Paul and the men with him sailed from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
They traveled from Perga and came to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath, they went into the meeting place and sat down.
After the Law and the Prophets were read, the leaders of the meeting sent word to them. They said, “Brothers, if you have a helpful message for the people, please speak.”
Paul stood up and motioned with his hand. He said, “Men of Israel and you who respect God, listen.
The God of Israel chose our fathers. He made His people strong while they lived in Egypt. With great power, He led them out.
He was patient with them for about forty years in the desert.
He destroyed seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to His people.
All this took about 450 years. After that, He gave them leaders until Samuel the prophet. “
Then they asked for a king. God gave them Saul, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin. He ruled for forty years.
Then God removed Saul and made David their king. God said about David, ‘I have found David, son of Jesse. He is a man who wants what I want. He will do all I ask.’
From David's family, God brought a Savior to Israel. It is Jesus, just as He promised.
Before Jesus came, John told all the people of Israel to be baptized and turn from sin.
As John finished his work, he said, ‘Do you think I am the one you are waiting for? I am not. But someone is coming after me. I am not even good enough to untie His shoes.’
Brothers, children of Abraham and all of you who respect God, this message of salvation was sent to us. “
The people in Jerusalem and their leaders did not know Jesus. They did not understand the prophets' words that are read every Sabbath. But by killing Him, they made those words come true.
They found no reason to kill Him. But they asked Pilate to have Him put to death.
When they had done all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the cross and put Him in a tomb.
But God raised Him from the dead.
For many days, He appeared to the people who came with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now His witnesses to the people. “
We bring you good news. God made a promise to our fathers.
He has kept that promise for us, their children, by raising Jesus. It is written in Psalm 2: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’
God raised Jesus from the dead so He would never die again. God said, ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’
So God says in another psalm, ‘You will not let Your Holy One rot in the grave.’
David served God in his time. Then he died and was buried with his fathers. His body decayed.
But Jesus, whom God raised, did not decay. “
So I want you to know, brothers, that through Jesus, forgiveness of sins is announced to you.
Everyone who believes in Him is made right with God. The law of Moses could not make you right.
Be careful, then, so the prophets' words do not happen to you.
‘Look, you who make fun of God! Be amazed and be destroyed. I am doing something in your time that you will not believe, even if someone tells it to you.’”
As Paul and Barnabas left, the people asked them to say these things again the next Sabbath.
When the meeting ended, many Jews and people who worshiped God followed Paul and Barnabas. Paul and Barnabas talked with them and urged them to keep trusting God's grace.
The next Sabbath, almost the whole city came to hear the Lord's message.
But when the Jews saw the crowds, they became jealous. They argued against Paul and said bad things about him.
Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly: “God's message had to be told to you first. But you push it away. You show you are not worthy of eternal life. So we are going to the people who are not Jews.
The Lord commanded us, ‘I have made you a light for the nations, so you can bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
When the non-Jewish people heard this, they were glad. They praised the Lord's message. All who were chosen for eternal life believed.
The Lord's message spread through the whole area.
But the Jews stirred up the respected women and the city leaders. They started trouble against Paul and Barnabas and made them leave the area.
Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet to show they were done with that place. Then they went to Iconium.
The believers were full of joy and the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went into the Jewish meeting place. They spoke so well that many Jews and Greeks believed.
But some Jews did not believe. They got the other people angry. They made trouble for the believers.
Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time. They spoke boldly about the Lord. The Lord showed that His grace was true. He let them do signs and wonders.
The people in the city were split. Some stood with the Jews. Some stood with the apostles.
Then the other people and the Jews, with their leaders, tried to hurt Paul and Barnabas. They wanted to throw stones at them.
Paul and Barnabas found out. They ran away to the cities of Lystra and Derbe in Lycaonia. They also went to the area around them.
There they told the good news.
In Lystra, a man sat there. He could not use his feet. He had been crippled since he was born. He had never walked.
He listened to Paul speak. Paul looked at him. Paul saw that the man had faith to be healed.
Paul said in a loud voice, "Stand up on your feet!" The man jumped up and walked.
The crowd saw what Paul did. They shouted in their own language, "The gods have come down to us like men!"
They called Barnabas Zeus. They called Paul Hermes. This was because Paul was the main speaker.
The priest of Zeus had a temple just outside the city. He brought bulls and flower crowns to the city gates. He wanted to offer a sacrifice with the crowd.
When Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their clothes. They ran into the crowd and shouted.

"Men, why are you doing this? We are men just like you. We bring you good news. Turn away from these useless things. Turn to the living God. He made the sky, the land, the sea, and everything in them.
In the past, He let all nations go their own way.
But He did not leave Himself without proof. He does good. He sends rain from the sky. He gives good times for crops. He fills your hearts with food and joy."
Even with these words, they could barely stop the crowd from offering sacrifices to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium. They won the crowd over. They stoned Paul. They dragged him out of the city. They thought he was dead.
The believers gathered around him. He got up and went back into the city. The next day, he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
They told the good news in that city. They made many disciples. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
They made the believers strong. They told them to stay true to the faith. They said, "We must go through many hard times to enter God's kingdom."
In each church, they chose leaders. They prayed and did not eat for a time. Then they gave the leaders to the Lord. They trusted Him.
They traveled through Pisidia. Then they came to Pamphylia.
They spoke God's word in Perga. Then they went down to Attalia.
From there, they sailed to Antioch. That was the city where believers had sent them out with God's help. They had finished the work.
When they arrived, they gathered the church. They told all that God had done with them. They said God had opened a door of faith to the non-Jewish people.
They stayed there a long time with the believers.
Some men came from Judea. They taught the believers, "You must be circumcised the way Moses taught, or you cannot be saved."
This caused a big argument between Paul and Barnabas and them. So the church chose Paul, Barnabas, and some others to go to Jerusalem. They would ask the apostles and elders about this question.
The church sent them on their way. They went through Phoenicia and Samaria. They told how people who are not Jews were turning to God. This made all the believers very happy.
When they reached Jerusalem, the church, the apostles, and the elders welcomed them. Paul and Barnabas told them all that God had done through them.
But some believers who were Pharisees stood up. They said, "People who are not Jews must be circumcised. They must also be told to obey Moses' law."
The apostles and elders met to talk about this.
After much talk, Peter stood up. He said, "Brothers, you know that long ago God chose me to tell the Good News to people who are not Jews. They heard it and believed.
God knows what is in hearts. He showed He accepted them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as He did for us.
He made no difference between us and them. He made their hearts clean by faith.
So why are you testing God? Why put a heavy load on the disciples' necks? We and our fathers could not carry that load.
We believe we are saved by the grace of the Lord Jesus. They are saved the same way."
Everyone became quiet. They listened as Barnabas and Paul told about the signs and wonders God had done among people who are not Jews through them.
When they finished, James spoke. "Brothers, listen to me.
Simon has told how God first helped people who are not Jews. He chose some of them to be His people.
The prophets' words agree with this. It is written:
'After this I will come back. I will rebuild David's fallen tent. I will fix its broken parts. I will make it stand again.
So the rest of the people may seek the LORD. All the nations I have called by My name may seek Him, says the LORD, who does these things.'
He has known these things from long ago.
So I think we should not make it hard for people who are not Jews who turn to God.
But we should write to them. They should stay away from things offered to idols, from sexual sin, from meat of animals killed by strangling, and from blood.
For Moses has people in every city who read his law in the synagogues every Sabbath."

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, thought it was good to choose men from among them. They would send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, called Barsabbas, and Silas. These men were leaders among the brothers.
They sent this letter by them: "The apostles and elders, your brothers, to the brothers among people who are not Jews in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Hello.
We heard that some men from us, whom we did not send, upset you with their words. They troubled your minds.
We all agreed to choose men and send them to you with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul.
These men risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we send Judas and Silas. They will tell you the same things in person.
The Holy Spirit and we think you should not have any heavy load, except these needed things:
Stay away from food offered to idols, from blood, from meat of strangled animals, and from sexual sin. If you keep away from these, you will do well. Good-bye."
So the men were sent off. They went down to Antioch. They gathered the church and gave them the letter.
The people read it and were glad because of the comfort.
Judas and Silas, who were also prophets, spoke a lot. They encouraged and strengthened the brothers.
After spending some time, they were sent off in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them.
Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. They taught and preached the word of the Lord with many others.
After some days, Paul said to Barnabas, "Let's go back and visit the brothers in every city where we preached the word of the Lord. Let's see how they are doing."
Barnabas wanted to take John, called Mark, with them.
But Paul did not think it was good to take him, because he had left them in Pamphylia and did not go with them to the work.
They had a sharp disagreement. So they parted. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.
Paul chose Silas. The brothers sent him off, trusting him to the Lord's grace.
He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
Paul came to Derbe and Lystra. There, he met a follower named Timothy. Timothy's mother was a Jewish woman who believed in God. His father was a Greek man.
The believers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy.
Paul wanted Timothy to travel with him. So Paul had Timothy circumcised. He did this because of the Jews who lived there. Everyone knew Timothy's father was Greek.
Paul and his friends went through the cities. They gave the people the rules the church leaders in Jerusalem had decided. They told them to keep these rules.
The churches became strong in faith. More people joined them every day.
The Holy Spirit kept them from telling God's word in Asia. So they went through Phrygia and Galatia.
They came to Mysia and tried to go to Bithynia. But the Spirit of Jesus did not let them.
They passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
At night, Paul had a vision. He saw a man from Macedonia standing there. The man begged him, "Come over to Macedonia and help us."
After Paul saw the vision, we quickly tried to go to Macedonia. We knew God had called us to tell the good news there.
We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace. The next day we went to Neapolis.
From there we went to Philippi. Philippi is the main city in that part of Macedonia. We stayed there for some days.
On the Sabbath day, we went outside the city gate by the river. We thought people prayed there. We sat down and talked to the women who came together.
A woman named Lydia listened. She sold purple cloth and was from Thyatira. She worshiped God. The Lord opened her heart so she could listen to Paul's words.
She and her family were baptized. Then she begged us, "If you think I am faithful to the Lord, come and stay at my house." She made us stay.
One day we were going to pray. A slave girl met us. She had a spirit that told the future. She made much money for her owners.
She followed Paul and us. She shouted, "These men are servants of the Most High God. They tell you how to be saved."
She did this for many days. Paul got upset. He turned and said to the spirit, "In the name of Jesus Christ, I tell you to leave her." The spirit left her right away.
Her owners saw their hope of money was gone. They grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them to the leaders in the market.
They brought them to the city rulers and said, "These men are Jews. They are troubling our city.
They teach customs that we Romans are not allowed to accept or do."
The crowd joined against them. The city rulers ordered Paul and Silas to be stripped and beaten with rods.
After many blows, they threw them into prison. They told the jailer to guard them carefully.
The jailer put them in the inner prison. He locked their feet in chains.
At midnight, Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God. The other prisoners listened to them.
Suddenly a big earthquake shook the prison. The doors opened, and everyone's chains came off.
The jailer woke up. He saw the doors open. He pulled out his sword to kill himself. He thought the prisoners had run away.
Paul shouted in a loud voice, "Do not hurt yourself! We are all here."
The jailer called for a light. He ran in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
He brought them out and said, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
They said, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your family."
They told him and everyone in his house about the Lord.
That same hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. He and his whole family were baptized right away.
He brought them to his house and set food before them. His whole family was very happy because they believed in God.
When day came, the city rulers sent officers with a message: "Let those men go."
The jailer told Paul, "The rulers sent to release you. Now go in peace."

But Paul said to them, "They beat us in public. We were not guilty, but they threw us in prison. We are Romans. Now they want to send us away in secret. No! Let them come here and lead us out themselves."
The officers told the rulers what Paul said. The rulers were afraid when they heard Paul and Silas were Romans.
They came and said they were sorry. They led Paul and Silas out and asked them to leave the city.
Paul and Silas left the prison. They went to Lydia's house. They saw the believers there and encouraged them. Then they left.
They traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia. Then they came to Thessalonica, where the Jews had a meeting place.
As was his way, Paul went into the meeting place. For three Sabbath days he talked with them from the Scriptures.
He explained and showed that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. He said, "This Jesus I am telling you about is the Christ."
Some of them believed and joined Paul and Silas. Many Greeks who worshiped God believed too, and quite a few leading women.
But the Jews were jealous. They got some bad men from the market. They made a crowd and upset the city. They came to Jason's house and looked for Paul and Silas, to bring them out to the crowd.
When they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some other believers to the city leaders. They shouted, "These men have caused trouble all over the world. Now they are here too!
Jason has taken them in. They all break Caesar's rules. They say there is another king, Jesus."
Hearing this, the crowd and the city leaders were upset.
They took money from Jason and the others, then let them go.
That night the believers sent Paul and Silas to Berea. When they arrived, they went to the Jewish meeting place.
The people in Berea were more willing to listen than the people in Thessalonica. They gladly received the message. They checked the Scriptures every day to see if these things were true.
Many of them believed. Many respected Greek women and men believed too.
When the Jews in Thessalonica heard that Paul was telling God's word in Berea, they came there too. They stirred up the crowds and caused trouble.
Then the believers quickly sent Paul away to the sea. Silas and Timothy stayed there.
The men who traveled with Paul took him to Athens. Then they returned with a message for Silas and Timothy to come to him as soon as they could.
While Paul waited for them in Athens, he was very upset to see that the city was full of idols.
So he talked in the meeting place with the Jews and with people who worshiped God. He also talked every day in the market with anyone who was there.

Some Epicurean and Stoic thinkers talked with him. Some said, "What is this talker trying to say?" Others said, "He seems to be telling about strange gods," because he was telling the good news about Jesus and the rising from the dead.
They took him to a place called the Areopagus. They said, "Can we know what this new teaching is that you are telling?
You are bringing strange things to our ears. We want to know what they mean."
All the Athenians and visitors there spent their time talking about and listening to the newest ideas.
Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, "Men of Athens, I see that you are very religious in every way.
"As I walked around and looked at the things you worship, I found an altar with these words: 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.' You worship something you do not know. I am telling you about it.
"The God who made the world and everything in it is Lord of heaven and earth. He does not live in temples made by hands.
He is not served by human hands, as if He needed something. He gives life and breath and everything to all people.
"From one man He made every nation of people to live on all the earth. He set their times and the places where they would live.
He did this so people would look for God. Maybe they would reach for Him and find Him. He is not far from each one of us.
"In Him we live and move and exist. Some of your own poets have said, 'We are His children.'
Since we are God's children, we should not think that God is like gold or silver or stone. He is not an image made by human skill and thought.
"In the past God did not punish people for not knowing. But now He tells all people everywhere to turn from their sins.
He has set a day when He will judge the world fairly. He will do this through a Man He chose. He proved this to everyone by raising Him from the dead."
When they heard about the dead rising, some made fun of Paul. Others said, "We will hear you again about this."
But some men joined him and believed. Among them were Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
There he found a Jewish man named Aquila. Aquila was from Pontus. He had just come from Italy with his wife Priscilla. Claudius had told all Jews to leave Rome.
Paul stayed with them and worked. They made tents.
Every Sabbath day, Paul talked in the meeting place. He tried to convince Jews and Greeks.
When Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, Paul gave all his time to telling God's message. He told the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
But they argued and said bad things. Paul shook his clothes and said, "You are to blame for what happens to you! I am not to blame. From now on, I will go to people who are not Jews."
Paul left that place and went into the house of a man named Justus. Justus worshiped God. His house was next to the meeting place.
Crispus was the leader of the meeting place. He believed in the Lord. His whole family believed too. Many people in Corinth heard Paul. They believed and were baptized.
One night, the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision. He said, "Do not be afraid. Keep speaking. Do not stop. I am with you.
No one will hurt you. I have many people in this city."
Paul stayed there for a year and a half. He taught God's word to the people.
When Gallio was the Roman governor of Achaia, the Jews came together against Paul. They took him to court.
They said, "This man teaches people to worship God in a way that breaks the law."
Paul was about to speak. But Gallio said to the Jews, "If this were a real crime, I would listen to you.
But these are questions about words, names, and your law. You take care of them. I do not want to be the judge."
He sent them away from the court.
Then everyone grabbed Sosthenes, the leader of the meeting place. They beat him in front of the court. Gallio did not care.
Paul stayed many more days. Then he said goodbye to the believers. In Cenchreae he had cut his hair because he had made a promise to God. Then he sailed to Syria. Priscilla and Aquila went with him.
They came to Ephesus. Paul left Priscilla and Aquila there. He went into the meeting place and talked with the Jews.
They asked him to stay longer. He said no.
He said goodbye and said, "I will come back to you if God wants." Then he sailed from Ephesus.
He landed at Caesarea. He went up and greeted the church. Then he went down to Antioch.
After some time, he left. He traveled through Galatia and Phrygia. He helped all the followers be strong.
A Jew named Apollos came to Ephesus. He was from Alexandria. He was a good speaker and knew the Scriptures well.
He had learned the way of the Lord. He was excited in spirit. He spoke and taught true things about Jesus. But he only knew John's baptism.
He began to speak boldly in the meeting place. Priscilla and Aquila heard him. They took him aside and explained God's way better.
Apollos wanted to go to Achaia. The believers encouraged him. They wrote to the followers there to welcome him. When he arrived, he helped many people. They had believed by God's grace.
He proved to the Jews in public that Jesus is the Christ. He used the Scriptures.
While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland regions and came to Ephesus. There he found some followers.
He asked them, “Did you get the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said, “No. We have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
Paul asked, “Then what baptism did you have?” They said, “John’s baptism.”
Paul said, “John baptized people to show they were turning from sin. He told them to believe in the One who would come after him. That One is Jesus.”
When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
When Paul put his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them. They spoke in new languages and told God’s messages.
There were about twelve men in all.
Paul went into the synagogue. He spoke boldly for three months. He talked with people and tried to convince them about God’s kingdom.

But some people were stubborn. They did not believe. They spoke badly about the Way in front of the crowd. So Paul left them. He took the followers with him. He talked every day in the school of Tyrannus.
This went on for two years. So everyone who lived in Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the Lord’s word.
God did amazing things through Paul’s hands.
Even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched his skin were taken to sick people. Their sickness left them, and evil spirits went out of them.

Some Jewish men traveled around and tried to make evil spirits leave people. They tried to use the name of the Lord Jesus over people who had evil spirits. They said, “I command you to leave by Jesus, whom Paul preaches.”
Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, did this.
But the evil spirit answered, “I know Jesus, and I know Paul, but who are you?”
The man with the evil spirit jumped on them. He overpowered them and hurt them. They ran out of the house naked and wounded.
Everyone in Ephesus, both Jews and Greeks, heard about this. They were afraid. The name of the Lord Jesus was honored.
Many believers came. They admitted their sins and told what they had done.
Many who had done magic brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. They counted the cost. It came to fifty thousand pieces of silver.
So the Lord’s word grew strong and won.
After this, Paul decided, led by the Spirit, to go to Jerusalem. He would pass through Macedonia and Achaia. He said, “After I go there, I must see Rome too.”
He sent two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. He stayed in Asia for a while.
About that time, there was a big uproar about the Way.
A man who worked with silver named Demetrius made silver temples of Artemis. This gave much work to the workers.
He called the workers and others who did this kind of work together. He said, “Men, you know that we make our money from this work.
You see and hear that not only in Ephesus but almost all Asia, this Paul has convinced many people and turned them away. He says gods made by hands are not gods.
So our business is in danger. Also, the temple of the great goddess Artemis may be counted as nothing. Her greatness, which all Asia and the world worship, may be destroyed.”
When they heard this, they were full of anger. They shouted, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
The whole city was confused. They rushed together into the theater. They grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s travel friends from Macedonia.
Paul wanted to go in to the crowd, but the followers would not let him.
Some of the city leaders who were his friends sent a message. They begged him not to go into the theater.
The crowd was confused. Some shouted one thing, and some shouted another. Most did not know why they had come together.
The Jews pushed Alexander forward. He motioned with his hand. He wanted to explain things to the crowd.
But when they knew he was a Jew, they all shouted the same thing for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
The city clerk quieted the crowd. He said, “Men of Ephesus, who does not know that the city of Ephesus guards the temple of the great Artemis and the stone that fell from the sky?
Since these things cannot be denied, you should be calm. Do not do anything quick and foolish.
You brought these men here. But they did not rob temples. They did not speak against our goddess.
If Demetrius and the workers with him have a charge against anyone, the courts are open. There are judges. Let them bring charges against each other.
If you want anything more, it will be settled in the lawful meeting.
We are in danger of being blamed for a riot today. There is no reason for this. We cannot explain this crowd.”
After he said this, he sent the crowd away.
After the trouble ended, Paul called the followers to him. He cheered them up and said goodbye. Then he left to go to Macedonia.
He went through those places. He talked a lot to cheer the people. Then he came to Greece.
He stayed three months. The Jews made a plan to hurt him. He was about to sail to Syria. So he decided to go back through Macedonia.
Sopater from Berea went with him. Aristarchus and Secundus were from Thessalonica. Gaius was from Derbe. Timothy went too. Tychicus and Trophimus were from Asia.
These men went ahead and waited for us at Troas.
After the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi. It took five days to reach them at Troas. We stayed there seven days.
On the first day of the week, we met to break bread. Paul was going to leave the next day. He talked with the people. He kept talking until midnight.
There were many lamps in the upstairs room where we were meeting.
A young man named Eutychus was sitting in the window. He was very sleepy. Paul talked for a long time. Eutychus fell into a deep sleep. He fell from the third floor. They picked him up. He was dead.
Paul went down. He fell on him. He hugged him. He said, "Don't worry. He is alive."
Paul went back upstairs. He broke bread and ate. He talked with them until morning. Then he left.
The people were very comforted. They took the boy home alive.
We went ahead to the ship. We sailed to Assos. We were going to pick up Paul there. He had planned it that way. He wanted to walk.
When he met us at Assos, we took him on board. We came to Mitylene.
We sailed from there. The next day we were across from Chios. The next day we stopped at Samos. The day after that, we came to Miletus.
Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus. He did not want to spend time in Asia. He was in a hurry to get to Jerusalem for Pentecost, if he could.
From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus. He called for the church leaders.
When they came to him, he said, "You know how I lived with you. I was with you the whole time from the first day I came to Asia.
I served the Lord with a humble heart. I served with tears. I served through hard times when the Jews made plans against me.
I did not hold back anything good for you. I taught you in public and in your homes.
I told Jews and Greeks to turn to God. I told them to have faith in our Lord Jesus Christ. "
Now I am going to Jerusalem. The Holy Spirit is sending me. I do not know what will happen to me there.
I only know this: in every city, the Holy Spirit tells me that chains and troubles are waiting for me.
But I do not care about my own life. I want to finish my race. I want to finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me. That work is telling people the good news of God's grace. "
Now I know that none of you will see me again. I preached God's kingdom to all of you.
So I tell you today: I am clean from the blood of all people.
I did not keep back any of God's plan from you.
Watch yourselves and all the sheep. The Holy Spirit made you leaders to take care of God's church. He bought it with His own blood. "
I know that after I leave, fierce wolves will come among you. They will not spare the sheep.
Even some of your own men will stand up. They will say wrong things. They will try to pull followers away to themselves.
So stay awake. Remember that for three years, I never stopped warning each of you. I did it night and day, and I cried.
Now I give you to God. I give you to His word of grace. It can build you up. It can give you a share with all God's holy people. "
I did not want anyone's silver, gold, or clothes.
You know these hands worked for my needs. They worked for the people with me.
In everything, I showed you that we must help weak people. We must remember the words of the Lord Jesus. He said, 'It is better to give than to get.'"
After he said this, he knelt down with all of them. He prayed.
They all cried a lot. They hugged him. They kissed him.
They were very sad. They were sad most because he said they would not see his face again. Then they walked with him to the ship.
After we left them, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we went to Rhodes. Then we went to Patara.
There we found a ship going to Phoenicia. We got on it and sailed.
We saw Cyprus, but we left it on our left side. We sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre. The ship was there to unload its cargo.
We found some followers of Jesus there. We stayed with them for seven days. Through the Spirit, they told Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
When the week was over, we left. Everyone, with their wives and children, walked with us out of the city. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
We said goodbye to each other. Then we got on the ship, and they went home.
After we finished our trip from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.
The next day we left and went to Caesarea. We went into the house of Philip. He was the man who told the good news. He was one of the seven. We stayed with him.
He had four daughters who were not married. They told what God would do.
We stayed there many days. A prophet named Agabus came from Judea.

He came to us. He took Paul's belt. He tied his own feet and hands. Then he said, "The Holy Spirit says, 'The Jews in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will hand him over to people who are not Jews.'"
When we heard this, we and the people there begged Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
Paul answered, "Why are you crying? Why are you breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be tied up, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
He would not listen. So we stopped. We said, "The Lord's will be done."
After these days, we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.
Some followers from Caesarea went with us. They took us to stay with Mnason. He was from Cyprus. He was an old follower.
When we got to Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us with joy.
The next day Paul went with us to see James. All the leaders were there.
Paul greeted them. He told them one by one what God had done among people who are not Jews. He did this through his work.
When they heard it, they praised God. Then they said to Paul, "Brother, you see how many thousands of Jews believe. They all care deeply about the law.
They have heard that you teach Jews who live among people who are not Jews to turn away from Moses. They say you tell them not to circumcise their sons and not to follow our customs.
What should we do? They will hear that you have come.
"So do what we tell you. We have four men who made a promise to God.

Take them with you. Make yourself clean with them. Pay for them so they can shave their heads. Then everyone will know that what they heard about you is not true. They will know that you keep the law too.

As for the people who are not Jews and believe, we wrote to them. We said they should stay away from food offered to false gods, from blood, from meat of animals that were strangled, and from sexual sin."
The next day Paul took the men. He made himself clean with them. Then he went into the temple. He told when the days of cleaning would end. This was until an offering was brought for each man.
The seven days were almost over. Some Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd. They grabbed him.
They shouted, "Men of Israel, help! This man teaches everyone everywhere against our people, our law, and this place. He even brought Greeks into the temple. He made this holy place unclean."
They had seen Trophimus from Ephesus with Paul in the city. They thought Paul had brought him into the temple.
The whole city was upset. People ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. The doors were shut.
They were trying to kill him. The leader of the soldiers heard that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
He quickly took soldiers and officers. He ran down to them. When the people saw the leader and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
The leader came near. He took Paul and ordered him tied with two chains. He asked who Paul was and what he had done.
Some people shouted one thing. Others shouted something else. The leader could not learn the truth because of the noise. So he ordered Paul taken to the army camp.
When Paul got to the steps, the soldiers had to carry him. The crowd was so rough.
The crowd followed and shouted, "Take him away!"
As Paul was about to be taken into the camp, he said to the leader, "May I say something to you?" The leader asked, "Do you know Greek?
Are you not the Egyptian who started trouble before this? Did you not lead four thousand men with daggers into the desert?"
Paul said, "I am a Jew. I am from Tarsus in Cilicia. It is not a small city. Please let me speak to the people."
The leader said yes. Paul stood on the steps. He waved his hand. When the people were very quiet, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language.
"Brothers and fathers, please listen to me now. I want to speak for myself to you.
When the people heard him speak in Hebrew, they became very quiet. Then Paul said,

"I am a Jew. I was born in Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in this city. I learned from Gamaliel. I followed our fathers' law very carefully. I was very eager for God, just like all of you are today.
I hurt people who followed the Way. I had men and women put in jail. I kept doing it until some died.

The high priest and all the elders can tell you this is true. They gave me letters to take to our Jewish brothers in Damascus. I was going there to bring back the followers of Jesus who were in chains. I would take them to Jerusalem to be punished.
"About noon, I was on my way to Damascus. Suddenly a bright light from heaven shone all around me.
I fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say, 'Saul, Saul, why are you hurting Me?'
I asked, 'Who are You, Lord?' He said, 'I am Jesus from Nazareth. You are hurting Me.'
The men with me saw the light. But they did not hear the voice of the One who spoke to me.
I said, 'Lord, what should I do?' The Lord said, 'Get up and go to Damascus. There you will be told all the things you must do.'
I could not see because the light was so bright. So the men with me led me by the hand into Damascus.
"A man named Ananias lived there. He obeyed God's law and was respected by all the Jews who lived there.
He came to me and stood by me. He said, 'Brother Saul, see again.' Right then I could see him.
Then he said, 'The God of our fathers chose you to know His will. He chose you to see the Righteous One and hear His voice.'
You will tell all people what you have seen and heard.
And now, why wait? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins. Call on His name.
"Later, I came back to Jerusalem. While I was praying in the temple, I had a vision.
I saw the Lord. He said, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem fast. The people here will not listen to your words about Me.'
I said, 'Lord, they know I used to put people in jail. I beat people in every synagogue who believed in You.'
When Stephen, who told the truth about You, was killed, I was there. I agreed with it. I watched the coats of the men who killed him.
Then the Lord said to me, 'Go! I will send you far away to the nations.'"
The people listened until Paul said this. Then they shouted, "Take this man away! He should not live!"
They yelled and threw off their coats. They threw dust into the air.
The commander ordered Paul to be brought into the fort. He said Paul should be whipped to find out why the people were shouting at him.
As they tied Paul up to whip him, Paul said to the officer standing there, "Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen who has not been found guilty?"
When the officer heard this, he went to the commander. He said, "What are you going to do? This man is a Roman citizen."
The commander came to Paul. He asked, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" Paul said, "Yes."
The commander said, "I paid a lot of money for my citizenship." Paul said, "But I was born a citizen."
Right away, the men who were going to question Paul stepped back. The commander was afraid because he had learned Paul was a Roman citizen. He had tied him up.

The next day, the commander wanted to know for sure why the Jews were accusing Paul. So he set Paul free. He called the chief priests and all the council to meet. Then he brought Paul down and stood him in front of them.
Paul looked straight at the council and said, "Brothers, I have served God and tried to do right up to today."
The high priest Ananias told the men near him, "Hit him on the mouth!"
Then Paul said to him, "God will hit you, you pretender! You judge me by the law, but you break the law when you order me hit."
The men near him said, "Do you insult God's high priest?"
Paul said, "Brothers, I did not know he was the high priest. The Bible says, 'Do not say bad things about a ruler of your people.'"
Then Paul saw that one group was Sadducees and the other was Pharisees. He called out, "Brothers, I am a Pharisee and the son of Pharisees. I am on trial because I hope in the rising of the dead."
When he said this, the Pharisees and Sadducees started to argue, and the crowd split.
The Sadducees say there is no rising of the dead, no angels, and no spirits. But the Pharisees believe in all three.
Then a loud shout came. Some teachers of the law from the Pharisees' side stood up and argued, "We find nothing wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel spoke to him."
The argument grew big. The commander was afraid Paul would be torn apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go down, take Paul by force from them, and bring him into the army camp.
That night the Lord stood near Paul and said, "Be brave. You spoke for me in Jerusalem. In the same way, you must speak for me in Rome."
The next day some Jews made a plan. They promised not to eat or drink until Paul was dead.
More than forty men joined this plot.
They went to the chief priests and elders and said, "We have promised not to eat anything until we kill Paul.
Now you and the council must tell the commander to bring Paul down to you. Pretend you want to ask more about him. But we are ready to kill him before he gets near."
But Paul's sister's son heard about the trap. He went into the army camp and told Paul.
Paul called one of the army officers and said, "Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him."
So the officer took him to the commander and said, "The prisoner Paul called me and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to say to you."
The commander took the young man by the hand and stepped aside. He asked, "What do you have to tell me?"
The young man said, "The Jews agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the council tomorrow. They will pretend they want to ask more about him.
Do not listen to them. More than forty men are waiting to kill him. They promised not to eat or drink until he is dead. They are ready now, waiting for your promise."
The commander let the young man go. He told him, "Do not tell anyone that you told me these things."
Then he called two army officers and said, "Get ready two hundred soldiers, seventy men on horses, and two hundred soldiers with spears. They will go to Caesarea at nine o'clock at night.
Give them horses so they can take Paul safely to Governor Felix."
He also wrote a letter. It said this:
"Claudius Lysias to the Most Excellent Governor Felix: Greetings.
The Jews seized this man and were about to kill him. I came with the soldiers and saved him, because I learned he is a Roman citizen.
I wanted to know why they accused him, so I brought him to their council.
I found that he was accused about questions of their law. He has done nothing that deserves death or chains.
When I heard about the plot against him, I sent him to you right away. I told his accusers to speak against him in front of you."
So the soldiers did what they were told. They took Paul by night to Antipatris.
The next day they went back to the army camp. They let the men on horses go on with Paul.
The men on horses came to Caesarea. They gave the letter to the governor and brought Paul to him.
After reading the letter, the governor asked where Paul was from. He learned Paul was from Cilicia.
The governor said, "I will listen to you when your accusers come." He ordered Paul to be kept in Herod's palace.
After five days, the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus. They told the governor about Paul.
When Paul was called, Tertullus began to accuse him. He said, "Because of you, we have much peace. Because of your care, good things have happened for this nation.
In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we are very thankful.
But I do not want to take too much of your time. I ask you to listen to us for a short time, because you are kind.
We found this man to be a troublemaker. He stirs up fights among all the Jews all over the world. He is a leader of the group called the Nazarenes.
He also tried to make the temple unclean. We caught him.
If you ask him, you can learn about all these things we say against him."
The Jews agreed. They said, "Yes, that is true."
The governor nodded for Paul to speak. Paul answered, "I know you have been a judge for this nation for many years. So I speak for myself with confidence.
You can learn that I went to Jerusalem to worship less than twelve days ago.
They did not find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I did not stir up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.
They cannot prove to you the things they say against me now.
But I tell you this: I worship the God of my fathers by following the Way, which they call a group. I believe everything in the Law and the Prophets.
I have hope in God, just like they do. I hope that good people and bad people will rise from the dead.
So I always try to keep my heart clear toward God and people.
After many years, I came to bring gifts to help my people and to offer sacrifices.
They found me in the temple. I had made myself clean. I was not with a crowd, and I was not making noise. Some Jews from Asia
should be here before you to accuse me if they have anything against me.
Or let these men say what wrong they found when I stood before the council.
Or let them tell about the one thing I shouted while I stood with them: 'I am judged before you today because of the hope of rising from the dead.'"
Felix knew a lot about the Way. He delayed their case. He said, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case."
He told the captain to keep Paul safe. He said Paul could have some freedom, and no one should stop his friends from helping him.
Some days later, Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jew. He sent for Paul and heard him talk about faith in Christ Jesus.
As Paul talked about doing right, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix became afraid. He said, "Go away for now. When I have time, I will call for you."
At the same time, Felix hoped Paul would give him money. So he sent for Paul often and talked with him.
After two years, Porcius Festus took Felix's place. Felix wanted to do the Jews a favor, so he left Paul in chains.
Three days after Festus came to the area, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
The chief priests and Jewish leaders told him their case against Paul. They asked Festus to do them a favor.
They asked him to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They planned to kill Paul on the road.
Festus answered that Paul was being kept in Caesarea. He said he would go back soon.
So he said, "If there is anything wrong with this man, let the leaders among you go down and charge him."
Festus stayed with them no more than eight or ten days. Then he went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judge's seat and ordered Paul to be brought in.
When Paul came, the Jews from Jerusalem stood around him. They brought many serious charges, but they could not prove them.
Paul said in his defense, "I have done nothing wrong against the Jewish law, the temple, or Caesar."
Festus wanted to do the Jews a favor. So he asked Paul, "Do you want to go up to Jerusalem and be judged there by me about these things?"
Paul said, "I am standing before Caesar's judge's seat. I must be judged there. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you know very well.
If I have done wrong and deserve death, I will not ask to be saved from death. But if none of these charges is true, no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar."
Festus talked with his council. Then he said, "You have appealed to Caesar. You will go to Caesar."
After some days, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.
While they stayed there many days, Festus told the king about Paul. He said, "There is a man here who was left as a prisoner by Felix.
When I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and Jewish elders told me about him. They asked me to judge him guilty.
I told them it is not the Roman way to hand over a man before he has a chance to face his accusers and answer the charge.
So when they came here, I did not wait. The next day I sat on the judge's seat and ordered the man to be brought in.
"His accusers stood up, but they did not bring any charge of the bad things I thought they would.
Instead, they had questions about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus. Paul said Jesus was alive.
I did not know what to do with these questions. So I asked if he wanted to go to Jerusalem and be judged there.
But Paul appealed to be kept for Caesar's decision. So I ordered him to be kept until I send him to Caesar."
Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear the man myself." Festus said, "Tomorrow you will hear him."
The next day, Agrippa and Bernice came with great show. They went into the meeting hall with the army leaders and important men of the city. Festus ordered Paul to be brought in.
Festus said, "King Agrippa and all the men here with us, you see this man. All the Jewish people came to me about him, both here and in Jerusalem. They shouted that he should not live any longer.
But I found that he did nothing that deserves death. Since he appealed to Caesar, I decided to send him.

But I do not have anything sure to write to Caesar about him. So I brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa. Then, after we ask him questions, I may have something to write.
It does not make sense to send a prisoner without also telling what he is charged with."
Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and made his defense. “
King Agrippa, I am happy to stand before you today. I will answer all the charges the Jewish people bring against me.
You know a lot about Jewish ways and questions. So I ask you to listen to me patiently. “
All the Jewish people know how I lived from the start. They know I grew up among my own people in Jerusalem.
They have known me for a long time. If they wanted, they could say I lived as a Pharisee. I followed the strictest part of our religion. “
Now I stand here because I hope in God's promise. God made this promise to our fathers.
Our twelve tribes hope to reach that promise. They serve God day and night. King Agrippa, the Jewish people accuse me because of this hope.
Why would any of you think it is hard to believe that God raises the dead? “
I thought I should do many things against the name of Jesus from Nazareth.
I did this in Jerusalem. I got power from the chief priests. I put many of God's people in jail. When they were killed, I voted against them.
I punished them many times. In every synagogue I tried to make them speak against Jesus. I was very angry at them. I even chased them to cities far away. “
I was on my way to Damascus with power from the chief priests.
About noon, King Agrippa, I saw a light from heaven. It was brighter than the sun. It shone around me and the men with me.
We all fell to the ground. I heard a voice say to me in the Hebrew language, “‘Saul, Saul, why do you hurt Me? It is hard for you to fight against Me.’ “
I said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ The Lord said, “‘I am Jesus, whom you are hurting.’ “
‘But get up and stand on your feet. I have shown Myself to you for a reason. I chose you to be My helper and witness. You will tell about the things you have seen and the things I will show you.
I will save you from your people and from the other nations. I am sending you to them.

You will open their eyes. You will turn them from darkness to light. You will turn them from Satan's power to God. Then they can receive forgiveness of sins. They can receive a place among God's holy people by faith in Me.’ “
So, King Agrippa, I did not disobey the vision from heaven.

First I told people in Damascus and Jerusalem. I told all the area of Judea and the other nations too. I told them to turn from sin and turn to God. I told them to do good things that show they are sorry. “
Because of this, the Jewish people grabbed me in the temple. They tried to kill me.
But God helped me. So I am still here today. I tell small and great people the same thing. I say nothing except what Moses and the prophets said would happen.
They said the Christ would suffer. They said He would be the first to rise from the dead. They said He would bring light to His people and to the other nations.”
While Paul was saying this, Festus shouted, “Paul, you are crazy! Too much learning has made you mad!”
Paul said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus. I speak true and sensible words.
The king knows about these things. I speak openly to him. I am sure nothing has been hidden from him. These things did not happen in a corner.
King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
Agrippa said to Paul, “In a short time you think you can make me a Christian?”
Paul said, “I pray to God that soon or late, not only you but everyone hearing me today would become like me, except for these chains.”
Then the king, the governor, Bernice, and the others stood up.
They left and talked to each other. They said, “This man has done nothing that deserves death or chains.”
Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been set free if he had not asked to go to Caesar.”
It was decided that we would sail to Italy. They handed Paul and some other prisoners to a Roman officer named Julius. He led soldiers from the Augustan group.
We got on a ship from Adramyttium. It was going to ports in Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia came with us.
The next day we landed at Sidon. Julius was kind to Paul. He let Paul go to his friends to get care.
We left there and sailed under Cyprus. The wind was against us.
We sailed across the sea near Cilicia and Pamphylia. Then we came to Myra in Lycia.
There the officer found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. He put us on it.
We sailed slowly for many days. It was hard to get near Cnidus because the wind would not let us. So we sailed under Crete near Salmone.
We moved along the coast and barely reached a place called Fair Havens. It was near the city of Lasea.
A long time passed. Sailing was now dangerous because the special fast day had already gone by. Paul warned them.
He said, "Men, I see that this trip will bring trouble and great loss. We could lose the ship and the cargo, and even our lives."
But the officer listened to the pilot and the ship's owner more than to Paul.

The harbor was not a good place to stay for winter. Most of the men wanted to sail from there. They hoped to reach Phoenix, a harbor in Crete that faced southwest and northwest, and stay there for winter.
A south wind began to blow. They thought their plan had worked. They raised the anchor and sailed close along Crete.
But soon a strong wind called Euraquilo hit us.
The ship could not face the wind. It was caught and driven.
We sailed under a small island called Cauda. We barely got the lifeboat under control.
They pulled it up. They used ropes to hold the ship together. They were afraid the ship would run aground on the sandbars called Syrtis. So they lowered the sail gear and let the wind push us.
The storm hit us hard. The next day they threw cargo overboard.
On the third day they threw the ship's gear overboard with their own hands.
The sun and stars did not show for many days. The storm kept hitting us. At last we gave up all hope of being saved.

After they had gone a long time without food, Paul stood among them and said, "Men, you should have listened to me. You should not have sailed from Crete. Then you would not have had this trouble and loss.
But now I tell you to be brave. No one will die. Only the ship will be lost.
Last night an angel of God stood by me. I belong to God, and I serve Him.
The angel said, 'Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. God has given you everyone sailing with you.'
So be brave, men. I trust God. It will happen just as He told me.
But we must run aground on an island."
On the fourteenth night, we were driven in the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors thought land was near.
They measured the water and found it was about 120 feet deep. A little later they measured again and found it was about 90 feet deep.
